verdict.rationale: Accommodation Place is a spatial/physical location (subclass of Place) where conference attendees stay, while Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal concept (subclass of Deadline) representing the cutoff date for booking hotel rooms. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Place vs Time) and denote different kinds of entities.

Both properties express the authorship relation: cmt:hasAuthor links Paper to Author, and iasted:is_writen_by links Item to Person. In the conference domain, Paper/Item and Author/Person are closely corresponding concepts, and both properties express the same relation direction (document -> author/person who wrote it). Despite the passive voice 'is writen by' in B, the domain/range show it goes from Item to Person, matching A's direction from Paper to Author.

Committee member in Conference denotes a person serving on a committee (domain of has members/was a member of, parent of Chair/Co-chair). Scholar in confOf denotes a price-category registration class for academics studying at a university (comment: 'price category - scholar', domain of study At -> University). These are completely different concepts despite sharing the parent Person.

These properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person who is a member of the conference). In edas, belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event (an event within the conference). The domains (Conference vs Programme), ranges (Conference Member vs Conference Event), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman > Person). In confOf, 'Conference' is an event (subclass of Working event > Event). These denote completely different categories of entities—a person versus an event—so they are unrelated.

Property A relates a Program committee to a Conference volume, expressing that a PC serves a conference. Property B is a mereological relation between Events (an Event is part of another Event). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings; neither subsumes the other.

These properties operate in completely different domains. printHardcopyMailingManifests relates an Administrator to a Conference (printing hardcopy mailing manifests for a conference). follows relates one Administrative event to another (temporal/sequence relation between events). They share no common domain or range types, and their semantics are entirely different.

The two properties relate different concepts in different directions. In cmt, 'write Review' links a Reviewer to a Review they author. In confOf, 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author who wrote it. They involve different domain/range types (Reviewer/Review vs Contribution/Author) and even if viewed as authorship relations, 'written By' is the inverse direction of a writing relation, so they are not equivalent.

The edas 'for Event' property links a Call to an Academic Event (e.g., a call for papers associated with a conference event), while the sigkdd 'presentation' property links a Speaker to a Document (the document being presented). They relate completely different domain entities in different directions and serve different purposes.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract, whereas 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material). They do not share the same domain or range, and neither is a more general version of the other.

An Attendee in edas is a general conference participant (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.), whereas a PC Chair in ekaw is a specific leadership role within the Programme Committee (child of PC Member). These denote different concepts: a general attendee vs. a specific committee chair. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clearly intended way.

edas:WithdrawnPaper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been withdrawn from the conference process), while ekaw:Paper is the general Paper class under Document. ekaw:Paper subsumes WithdrawnPaper because every withdrawn paper is a paper, but not vice versa.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. `maxChoice` in confOf relates Social/Working events to a positive integer (likely a maximum number of choices), while `End_of_conference` in sigkdd relates a Conference to a dateTime (the end date/time of the conference). They do not denote the same relation.

confOf's Event is a broad top-level class covering Administrative, Social, and Working events, whereas edas's Academic Event is a specific subtype of Conference Event restricted to academic gatherings (Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop). edas also has a sibling Non Academic Event, showing that Academic Event is not the most general event class. Therefore confOf Event is more general than edas Academic Event, so A is subsumed_by B.

Cryptography Topic is a subject-matter topic under Topic in edas, denoting a research area. Audiovisual equipment is a physical item under Item in iasted, with children like Computer, LCD projector, etc. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to its title (a string), while the sigkdd 'City of conference' property relates a Conference to the city where it is held (a string). They have completely different domains (Paper vs Conference) and denote unrelated attributes in the conference domain.

The cmt 'date' property assigns a date to a Conference, while the Conference ontology 'has a name' property assigns a name (string) to various entities (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic). They have different domains, different ranges (date vs string), and denote completely different attributes.

Review in Conference is a document containing a review of a contribution, while Web_Site in ekaw is a web-based document that lists events. They are siblings under Document in ekaw, not the same concept.

hasFirstName relates a Person to their first name (a string), while hasBiography relates a Person to their biography text (a string). These are clearly different attributes of a person despite sharing the same domain and range types.

These properties connect completely different domains and ranges. `hasSubjectArea` links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic), while `is_held_in` links an Activity to a Place or Time (location/temporal). They share no semantic overlap.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: hasHomePage points to a URL/home page string for a person, while hasFirstName points to the person's first name. No reference alignment would equate these.

hasPhone is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's phone number), while locationOf is an object property from Location to Event (relating a location to an event held there). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

IASTED's 'One day presenter' is a specific kind of delegate who presents on a single day, while sigkdd's 'Speaker' is a more general class of person who gives a presentation (with subtypes Author and Invited Speaker). The sigkdd Speaker class is broader, subsuming various kinds of presenters, making One_day_presenter a narrower, subsumed concept.

The property 'employed By' in confOf relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while 'can stay in' in sigkdd relates a Person to a Place they can stay at (e.g., a hotel or accommodation). These are entirely different relations: employment vs. lodging/accommodation. They share only the Person domain, but the ranges differ (Organization vs. Place) and the semantics are unrelated.

has_the_last_name is a datatype property mapping Person to string (a person's surname), while obtain is an object property mapping Person to Item (a person acquiring an item). They differ in type, range, and meaning; no alignment relation holds.

The two properties operate in completely different domains and ranges. 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to a string (the ISBN code), while 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They share no common semantics.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a kind of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while ekaw:Tutorial_Abstract is a document (a kind of Abstract, sibling of Invited Talk Abstract). One denotes an organized meeting/event, the other a written text/artefact; they are disjoint categories in the conference domain.

confOf's Social event is a specific kind of event (banquet, reception, trip) under Event, alongside Working and Administrative events. edas's Non Academic Event is a broader category under Conference Event that includes Break Event, Meal Event, and Social Event as children. Thus confOf:Social_event is subsumed by edas:NonAcademicEvent, since a social event is one type of non-academic event, but not all non-academic events are social events.
Excursion is a social event (a subclass of Non Academic Event), while Speaker is a person who gives a presentation. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In edas, 'Accept Rating' is a subclass of 'Review Rating' — it represents a rating value (a recommendation to accept) assigned during the review process, not a full review document. In ekaw, 'Negative Review' is a subclass of 'Review' (itself under Document), meaning it is an entire review document with negative content. The edas class is a rating/evaluation value, while the ekaw class is a document. They are at different levels of abstraction and different ontological categories, so they are not equivalent. They are also not in a subsumption relationship since one is a rating and the other a document.

Written contribution (e.g., papers, articles) and Form (e.g., registration forms, hotel forms, author information forms) are distinct document types in the conference domain. Written contribution has children like Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, while Form has children like Author information form, Hotel registration form, and Registration form. These are disjoint categories of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties operate at different levels and have different domains and ranges. In cmt, 'addProgramCommitteeMember' is an administrative action property with domain Administrator and range Program Committee Member, representing the act of adding an individual PC member. In the Conference ontology, 'has_a_program_committee' is a structural/compositional property with domain Conference volume and range Program committee, indicating that a conference volume has an associated program committee. The domains (Administrator vs Conference volume) and ranges (Program Committee Member vs Program committee) are different kinds of entities, and the properties serve fundamentally different purposes: one is an action of adding a member, the other is a structural relationship denoting committee existence.

In cmt, Program Committee Chair is a specific role (a chair of the program committee), whereas in Conference, Committee member is a general class whose children include Chair and Co chair. Thus Program Committee Chair is a more specific concept subsumed by Committee member.

Entity A is a topic class about computer networks and sensor technology, a subject area for papers/contributions. Entity B is a physical computer device, a subclass of audiovisual equipment. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

The property hasDecision in cmt relates a Paper to a Decision (the acceptance/rejection outcome of a submitted paper), while studyAt in confOf relates a Scholar to a University (the institution where the scholar studies). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no overlap in meaning.

confOf:writes relates an Author to a Contribution (paper) that the author has written. ekaw:technicallyOrganisedBy is a sub-property of organisedBy and concerns the technical organisation of an event by some agent or organisation. These are completely different relations in the conference domain: one is about authorship of a paper, the other about event organisation.

Extended abstract and Demo Paper denote different types of conference contributions. An extended abstract is a short summary of work (typically 1-2 pages), while a demo paper describes a system demonstration. They have distinct purposes, lengths, and roles in conference organization. Neither subsumes the other; they are disjoint categories of conference documents.

These properties denote different relations. In cmt, 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria (a meta-level administrative relation about the conference setup). In edas, 'isReviewedBy' relates a Paper to the people who reviewed it (a direct paper-reviewer assignment). They differ in domain (Conference vs Paper), range (Administrator vs Reviewer/Chair roles), and meaning: one is about who configured review criteria for the conference, the other is about who reviewed a specific paper.

Non Academic Event in edas is a conference event type (parent: Conference Event; children: Break Event, Meal Event, Social Event) denoting social/non-academic activities at a conference. Registration Non Member in sigkdd is a fee category (parent: Registration fee) denoting the registration fee for non-members. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'has Conference Member' property links a Conference to its Conference Member (i.e., membership relation). The Conference ontology 'gives presentations' property links an Active conference participant to a Presentation (i.e., a presentation-giving relation). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics; they share no common meaning in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a broad superclass covering all persons who contribute to a conference (including active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors). Plenary lecture speaker in ontology B is a specific type of author who gives a plenary lecture. Since a plenary lecture speaker is a kind of conference contributor but not all conference contributors are plenary lecture speakers, A subsumes B.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'has parts' links a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (a mereological relation). In ontology B, 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (an authorship relation). They share no common domain or range types and express fundamentally different relationships.

The two properties operate in entirely different parts of the conference domain. `is Reviewed By` links a Paper to reviewer roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), capturing the peer-review relationship. `is equipped by` links a Place to an Item, capturing what equipment a venue has. They have disjoint domains (Paper vs Place) and disjoint ranges (reviewer roles vs Item), so they cannot denote the same relation.

confOf's 'Social event' is a subclass of Event with children like Banquet, Reception, and Trip — it denotes social activities at a conference. edas's 'Conference' is the top-level academic event container with properties like paper deadlines, topics, and members. These are completely different concepts: one is a social sub-event, the other is the conference itself.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific chair role (a Chairman, sibling of Conference Chair and PC Chair) for co-chairing the conference. OC Member in ekaw is a member of the Organizing Committee, a participant role that subsumes OC Chair. These are different committee structures: Associated Chair is a top-level conference co-chair, not an organizing committee member. Their intended instances do not coincide.

Workshop Chair in ekaw is a person who chairs a workshop, while Webmaster in sigkdd is a person responsible for the conference website. These are distinct organizational roles with different responsibilities, and neither subsumes the other.

A is a subclass of Person denoting a human contributor (author, speaker, etc.) at a conference. B is the conference event itself, with properties like start/end dates, city, name, and being held by ACM SIGKDD. These are completely different concepts: a person who contributes vs. the conference event.

A Workshop Session is a session within a workshop, typically comprising multiple talks or presentations. A Plenary lecture is a single lecture given to all conference attendees. They are different types of conference activities: one is a session (a grouping event), the other is an individual lecture. Neither subsumes the other, and their instances do not coincide.

The property markConflictOfInterest in CMT marks a conflict of interest between a reviewer/author/chairman and a paper, explicitly preventing the reviewer from being assigned to or reviewing that paper. The property hasReviewer in EKAW associates a paper with a possible reviewer. These are semantically opposite relations: one indicates a reviewer should NOT review the paper, while the other indicates a reviewer is (or may be) assigned to review it. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only loosely related by both involving reviewers and papers.

Both properties relate a document-like entity to a person who authored it, but the direction is opposite: cmt:writePaper has domain Author and range Paper (author -> paper), while iasted:is_prepared_by has domain Item and range Person (item -> person). A property and its inverse are not equivalent. They are related as inverse-like relations but not equivalent.

The two properties denote completely different concepts. `contactEmail` in confOf relates a Contribution to a contact email address (string), while `paperDueOn` in edas relates a Conference to a paper submission deadline (dateTime). They differ in domain (Contribution vs. Conference), range (string vs. dateTime), and meaning (contact information vs. deadline).

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., welcome reception) held during a conference, while iasted:Receiving_manuscript is an administrative activity before the conference where manuscripts are received/submitted. They share the word 'reception/receiving' but denote entirely different concepts: a social gathering vs. a manuscript-handling activity. Their paths, siblings, and parent contexts confirm no overlap in intended instances.

These properties are unrelated. In edas, 'initiates' has domain {Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member} and range Call, meaning a chair or committee member initiates/sends a call (for papers/participation). In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' has domain Document and range Speaker, meaning a document (e.g., a presented paper) is presented by a speaker. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different: one relates committee roles to calls, the other relates documents to speakers. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only weakly related at best.

confOf:Country is a geographic country entity used as the range of a 'has Country' property for organizations and persons. iasted:State is a generic spatial/administrative-area concept whose children are Conference state, Presenter state, and Sponsor state—clearly not countries but rather status/role or locale categories in the iasted ontology. The intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other in a clear direction.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length submission document in cmt (Document > Paper > PaperFullVersion), while SecurityTopic is a subject-area classification in edas (Topic > SecurityTopic). They denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are social events associated with a conference, but a Conference Trip is a broader category (e.g., an excursion or outing) while a Dinner banquet is a specific type of social gathering (a meal). They overlap in being non-academic conference activities, but neither subsumes the other and their intended instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In edas, 'for Event' links a Call (e.g. call for papers) to the Academic Event it is issued for. In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g. a presentation or lecture). The domains (Call vs Person) and ranges (Academic Event vs Activity/Item) do not overlap in the intended usage, so the properties are unrelated.

Both are conference presentation events, but they are not equivalent: a Contributed Talk is a non-invited paper presentation, while a Plenary lecture is a high-level lecture addressed to all conference participants (often invited/keynote). They overlap only in being lectures/presentations, so 'related' is the best fit.

Published Paper is a document (an actual paper artefact that has been published), while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a temporal entity (a deadline for submitting the final version of a manuscript). They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (Document vs Time) and denote entirely different kinds of things.

hasLastName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's surname), while authorOf is an object property from Person to Document (relating a person to a paper they wrote). They have different ranges (string vs Document), different property types (datatype vs object), and denote completely different relations.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference, representing a type of conference event (as opposed to a Two Level Conference). In the IASTED ontology, 'Conference state' is a subclass of State, representing a state or status that a conference can be in. These are entirely different concepts: one is a conference event itself, the other is a state/status of a conference.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs the conference, sitting under Person > Chairman. Mailing list (iasted) is a document artifact sitting under Item > Document. These are completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Abstract in cmt denotes the abstract content of a paper (a document part), while Accepted Paper in edas denotes a paper that has been accepted for the conference (a review-state subclass). They share the parent Paper but have disjoint intended instances and different semantics.

In ontology Conference, Review is a document (subclass of Conference document) that contains the actual review content of a contribution, as shown by properties 'has a review' (Reviewed contribution -> Review) and 'reviews' (Review -> Reviewed contribution). In EDAS, ReviewForm is a form used to collect review input, not the review document itself. A review form is a template or instrument for gathering reviews, whereas a review is the substantive output. These are structurally and semantically distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (has_a_committee_co-chair) links a Committee to its Co-chair (a person role), while property B (reviewes) links a Member PC to a Contribution (a paper). They relate completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

Proceedings Publisher is an organization (a kind of entity/agent) that publishes proceedings, while Receiving manuscript is an activity (an action/event) that occurs before a conference. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies (Organisation vs. Activity) and denote fundamentally different categories of things: one is a corporate body, the other is a process. There is no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:Conference denotes the academic conference event itself (an organizational entity with members, dates, paper submissions, administrators), while iasted:Conference_restaurant is a physical building/venue where conference-related dining occurs. These are completely different kinds of entities: one is the conference as an event/organization, the other is a restaurant location. No subsumption relationship holds between them.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. In ontology A, 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (indicating a reviewer's preference for reviewing papers on a given topic). In ontology B, 'hasReview' links a Paper to a Review (indicating that a paper has received a review). The domains (Topic vs Paper) and ranges (Review preference vs Review) are disjoint concepts, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

In ekaw, Conference Trip is a Social Event (a happening/excursion associated with a conference). In iasted, Trip day is a subclass of Time (a temporal unit). One is an event, the other is a time interval; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The cmt 'paper ID' is a datatype property from Paper to unsignedLong, representing a numeric identifier for a paper. The edas 'related To Paper' is an object property from Paper Presentation to Accepted Paper, linking a presentation to the paper it presents. They have different domains, ranges, property types, and meanings; no alignment relation holds.

confOf:Workshop denotes a whole working event (a meeting with its own programme, co-located with a conference), whereas ekaw:Regular_Session denotes a single session within a conference programme. They occupy different positions in their respective hierarchies (Working event vs Session) and their intended instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent; nor is one a generalisation of the other.

Property A links a Committee to its Chair (person role), while property B links an Event to the Location where it is held. They relate completely different kinds of entities and have no overlap in domain or range.

Associated Chair is a specific conference leadership role (a type of Chairman in cmt), while Regular in confOf is a general participant category (distinguished from Member and Student). These denote completely different concepts: one is a specialized organizational role, the other is a broad participant type. They do not overlap in intended instances.

A's `memberOfProgramCommittee` denotes general membership in a Program Committee (domain: Program Committee Member, range: Program Committee). B's `was_a_committee_chair_of` is a subproperty of `was a member of` and specifically denotes the chair role (domain: Chair, range: Committee). Being a committee chair is a special kind of committee membership, so B is more specific than A; A is subsumed by B in the sense that B's relation is a specialization of the membership relation A represents. They are not equivalent because A covers all members while B covers only chairs.

A Tutorial is a teaching/instructional event, while a Workshop is a collaborative working session. Though both are academic events, they are distinct types of conference events with different purposes and structures. The labels and paths confirm they denote different concepts.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event (alongside Social_event and Administrative_event) representing conference, tutorial, and workshop events. edas:ComputerNetworksSecurityTopic is a subclass of Topic representing a specific subject area. These are completely different domain concepts: one is a type of event/activity, the other is a topic/subject classification. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

In ekaw, OC Member is a Conference Participant who serves on the Organizing Committee, a specific role. In sigkdd, Organizator is a broad class covering all organizing roles (General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster). The sigkdd Organizator is more general, subsuming the ekaw OC Member concept.

The property 'is used by' in iasted relates an Item to a Person (an item is used by a person), while 'can stay in' in sigkdd relates a Person to a Place (a person can stay in a place). They have different domains, different ranges, and express completely different relationships with no overlap.

Invited talk (A) is a subclass of Conference contribution/Presentation, denoting a type of presentation/document delivered at a conference. Invited Speaker (B) is a subclass of Person > Presenter, denoting the person who gives the talk. One is an event/presentation artefact, the other is a person role; they are disjoint kinds of entities and not equivalent.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs a conference, sitting under Person > Chairman. Presenter house (iasted) is a building/place where a presenter stays, sitting under Place > Building. One is a person role, the other is a physical location; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference contribution is a document-like artefact (subclass of Conference document) with children such as Poster, Presentation, and Written contribution. Participant is a person role (subclass of Person) with children such as Member, Regular, and Student. These denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Entity A is a person role (Tutorial Chair under Conference Participant/Person), while entity B is a monetary fee (Member registration fee under Money/Fee/Registration fee). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

confOf:Workshop is a type of event (a meeting/conference track where papers are presented), while iasted:Speaker_lecture is a specific lecture session given by a single speaker. These are different concepts in the conference domain: a workshop is an event type, whereas a speaker lecture is an individual presentation activity.

confOf Member is a person (subclass of Participant) who is a member of the conference, while sigkdd Registration_Non-Member is a fee category for non-member registrants. These are completely different concepts: one denotes a person, the other a registration fee. They share no semantic overlap.

hasVAT is a datatype property mapping social/working events to a string (VAT value), while listsEvent is an object property mapping programme brochures/web sites to events. Different domains, different ranges (string vs Event), different semantics.

The cmt 'assigned To' property links a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper), while the sigkdd 'award' property links something (likely a paper or person) to an Award. These are completely different relations in the conference domain: one is about review assignment, the other about bestowing an award. They share no semantic overlap.

Conference participant is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person), while Activity before conference is a pre-conference activity/event (subclass of Activity). One denotes a person, the other an activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Although both are datatype properties on Person with range string, they denote different attributes: 'has the last name' captures a person's surname/family name, while 'has First Name' captures the given/first name. They are distinct slots of a person's name, not the same relation, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent.

Associated Chair in cmt is a person role (a kind of Chairman involved in conference organization), while Welcome address in iasted is a conference activity/event. They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

confOf Student is a participant who is a student (a person attending the conference), whereas sigkdd Platinum Supporter is a sponsor at the highest support level. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Person/Participant vs. Sponzor) and denote entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Document' and represent the same concept in the conference domain: a written artifact such as an abstract, paper, or review. They share key subclasses (Abstract, Paper, Review) and serve as the domain/range for authorship and related properties. The broader set of subclasses in ekaw (e.g., Flyer, Programme Brochure) reflects a slightly more comprehensive modeling but does not change the core denotation of the class.

Both properties relate to the transfer of an item/award to a person/author, but they differ in directionality and domain/range. 'is given to' (Item -> Person) describes the act of giving an item to a person, while 'obtain' (Author -> Award) describes an author obtaining an award. They are semantically related (inverse-like) but not equivalent due to different domain/range and perspective.

maxChoice is a confOf datatype property whose domain is Social event / Working event and range is positiveInteger, representing a maximum number of choices. hasEndDateTime is an edas datatype property whose domain is ConferenceEvent and range is dateTime, representing an end timestamp. They relate different kinds of entities to different datatypes and have no semantic overlap.

confOf:Member_PC is a person who serves on the programme committee and reviews papers (a subclass of Person with properties like expertOn and reviewes). edas:AccpetIfRoomRating is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a rating value assigned to a review. One is an agent (a person), the other is a rating artefact; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'enter Review Criteria' has domain Administrator and range Conference, describing an administrator entering review criteria for a conference. In ekaw, 'has Review' has domain Paper and range Review, describing a paper having a review. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or overlapping.

Publisher is an organization that issues conference proceedings, while Time is a temporal concept with children like Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Author in edas is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person, domain of has Related Paper). Value added tax in iasted is a monetary tax (subclass of Tax under Money). These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

The property 'reviews' in the Conference ontology relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution (i.e., it captures the relationship between a review and the paper being reviewed). The property 'award' in the sigkdd ontology relates something (unspecified domain) to an Award. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain: one is about reviewing a paper, the other is about receiving or bestowing an award. They share no semantic overlap.

confOf's Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster, Short paper) representing any paper submitted. edas's Pending Paper is a specific workflow state of a paper (sibling of Accepted, Rejected, Published, etc.), denoting only papers still awaiting decision. Thus Pending Paper is a strict subset of the general Paper concept, so A is subsumed_by B's parent Paper but not equivalent to Pending Paper.

In cmt, Person is a human agent (parent of Chairman, Reviewer, User, etc., with conflict-of-interest and email properties). In edas, Contact Information is a data object holding address fields (city, street, postal code, phone, email). They denote completely different kinds of entities: a person vs. a contact record. Although edas Person has an email property whose range includes Contact Information, the two classes themselves do not overlap.

Accommodation Place in edas denotes a place where conference participants stay (e.g., hotels, lodgings), a subclass of Place. Shuttle bus in iasted denotes a transport vehicle used to move people, a subclass of Transport vehicle. One is a static lodging location, the other a means of transportation; their instances do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

These properties denote completely different relations. `markConflictOfInterest` in CMT relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to declare a conflict of interest, preventing the reviewer from bidding on or being assigned to that paper. `has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution` in Conference relates a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic, indicating what a review preference is about. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different: one is about declaring conflicts, the other about linking review preferences to topics or contributions. They share no semantic overlap.

WirelessCommunicationsTopic is a specific subject-area Topic (e.g., antennas, communication theory, mobile computing) used to classify papers, whereas Program_Committee is a committee responsible for reviewing papers. They belong to entirely different parts of the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'has a commtitee' in ontology Conference relates a Conference volume to a Committee, denoting that a conference has an associated committee. The property 'initiates' in edas relates conference roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call, denoting that a person in a chair role initiates a call (e.g., call for papers). These properties have completely different domains and ranges, and they express entirely different relationships in the conference organization domain. They are unrelated.

A Published Paper is a specific academic document (a paper that has been published), while a Cd proceening is a physical medium (a CD containing conference proceedings). One is a document/content type, the other is a publication medium/format. Their instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

The cmt Author is a person who writes and submits papers, sitting under Person > Conference Member. The ekaw Academic Institution is an organization (with children University and Research Institute) that scientifically organises conferences. One is a human role, the other an organisational entity; they share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

These properties are completely different. 'has Submission Instructions' is a datatype property from Call to string, describing textual instructions for a call. 'submit' is an object property from Author to Paper, representing the action of an author submitting a paper. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Submitted contribution is a written document (paper) that has been submitted to a conference, while Possible Reviewer is a person who could serve as a reviewer. One is a document, the other is a person; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Conference applicant is a person who applies to attend a conference, while Committee is an organizational body composed of members. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair in cmt is a specific leadership role (a Chairman responsible for the conference), whereas Member PC in confOf denotes a program-committee member who reviews papers and has expertise on topics. A conference chair is not the same concept as a PC member; they occupy different organizational positions. The classes are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

Free Time Break in edas is a specific kind of break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break) occurring during a conference, denoting a scheduled period of free time. Conference activity in iasted is a broad top-level class subsuming many conference activities including receptions, lectures, registrations, and social programs. These are at very different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept; Free Time Break is not equivalent to the broad Conference activity class, nor is it straightforwardly subsumed by it since the two ontologies model the domain differently (edas places breaks under Non Academic Event, not under a general activity class).

Property A (is_used_by) is an object property relating an Item to a Person, while property B (Name) is a datatype property relating a Person to a string. They have different domains, different range types (object vs datatype), and represent completely different relations.

These properties are completely different. 'has_the_first_name' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's first name. 'is_visited_by' is an object property from locations (Building, City, State) to Person, indicating that a person visits a location. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

The property 'invited by' in Conference relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the one who invited them), while 'send' in iasted relates a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings: one is about invitation between reviewers, the other about sending items by persons.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member, presumably setting a paper limit for that PC member. In confOf, expertOn relates a Member PC to a Topic, indicating the topics on which the member has expertise. They connect different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

cmt:User is a generic superclass for any person who uses the system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), whereas confOf:Scholar denotes a specific price-category attendee who studies at a university. Their intended instances do not coincide: a Scholar is not necessarily a system user, and a cmt User (e.g., an Administrator or Reviewer) is not necessarily a scholar. They share only the common ancestor Person, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or subsumed.

Invited_speaker in Conference is a speaker (a contributor who gives a talk), while Worker_non_speaker in iasted is explicitly a non-speaker (a delegate who does not present). They are mutually exclusive categories: one speaks, the other does not. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

The two properties have opposite directions: confOf's hasTopic goes from Working event to Topic, while ekaw's topicCoveredBy goes from Research Topic to Event/Paper. A property and its inverse are not equivalent. Moreover, the domains and ranges differ: confOf restricts the domain to Working event and range to Topic, whereas ekaw's domain is Research Topic and range is Event or Paper. Given these structural and directional differences, the properties are not equivalent, and without clearer evidence of an exact inverse correspondence, they are best treated as unrelated rather than related.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision (alongside Rejection), representing the outcome of a paper review process. Tip in iasted is a subclass of Money (alongside Fee, Sponzorship, Tax), representing a monetary amount. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Demo Chair is an organizational role (a person who chairs demo sessions), while Tutorial speaker is a presenter who gives a tutorial. These are distinct concepts: one is an administrative/chairing role for demonstrations, the other is a speaking/presenting role for tutorials. They share no clear overlap in intended instances.

Paper Full Version in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a document), representing the full-length version of a submitted paper. Antennas Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject-area classification for papers. These are completely different concepts: one is a document type, the other is a research topic category. They share no instances and have no overlap.

Both represent the final, camera-ready version of a paper that has been accepted and is ready for publication. However, 'Published Paper' in edas is defined by publication status (a sibling of Accepted, Rejected, etc.), while 'Final manuscript' in iasted is a submission document type (sibling of Initial manuscript). The two ontologies model the lifecycle differently: one by review decision state, the other by submission iteration. They overlap significantly in intended instances but are not strictly equivalent due to differing ontological context.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., welcome reception), while iasted:Registration is a conference activity representing the registration process (with Delegate as a child). They denote different concepts despite both being conference-related events/activities.

In cmt, 'Meta Review' is a specific kind of review document (a meta-review written by a meta-reviewer), sitting under Review > Document. In the Conference ontology, 'Reviewed contribution' is a contribution (i.e., a paper) that has been reviewed, sitting under Conference contribution > Written contribution > Submitted contribution. One is a review artifact; the other is the paper being reviewed. They are different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Entity A is a document class (a brief introduction for a session chair) under Document in the iasted ontology, while entity B is a deadline class (the paper submission deadline) under Deadline in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A's Author is a person who writes a paper (subclass of Person/Conference Member). B's Multi-author Volume is a document type (subclass of Document) such as proceedings or a book with multiple authors. They are disjoint kinds of entities: a person vs. a publication artefact.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while University is an academic institution/organisation in ekaw. These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf 'Chair PC' denotes the chair of the Programme Committee (a PC leadership role, sibling of Member PC), whereas ekaw 'Demo Chair' denotes the person responsible for demo sessions (a conference participant role). They are different conference organisation roles with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. setMaxPapers (cmt) relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member, likely setting a paper-assignment limit. isMemberOf (edas) relates a Person to a Conference, indicating membership. They connect different entity types in different directions with no semantic overlap.

confOf:Social_event is a subclass of Event with children like Banquet, Reception, and Trip, denoting social activities at a conference. sigkdd:Organizator is a subclass of Person with children like General Chair and Program Chair, denoting people who organize the conference. These are completely different categories of entities (events vs. persons) with no overlap in intended instances.

Committee member is a subclass of Person, denoting a person serving on a committee. Place is a spatial location with subclasses like Building, Conference hall, and Hotel room. These are completely disjoint domains with no overlap in intended instances.

Review_expertise in Conference denotes the expertise/preference of a reviewer regarding a submitted contribution, while Review in iasted is a document (subclass of Document) that is a review artifact. They are different concepts: one is about reviewer expertise/preference, the other is a review document.

Invited Talk Abstract is a subclass of Document/Abstract, denoting a written text. Invited Speaker is a subclass of Person/Speaker, denoting a human role. They belong to disjoint branches of the ontology hierarchy and denote completely different kinds of entities.

Camera Ready event is a specific administrative event in the conference workflow (the stage where final camera-ready papers are prepared), whereas ekaw:Conference denotes a whole conference edition (a scientific event). They are at different levels of granularity and serve different purposes: one is a sub-event within a conference lifecycle, the other is the conference itself.

These properties relate entirely different kinds of things. 'is Initiated By' connects a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the people/roles who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). 'held In' connects an Event to the Location where it takes place. The domains (Call vs Event), ranges (person roles vs Location), and meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Program Committee Chair is a leadership role (a Chair who manages the reviewing process, with the power to end reviews), sitting under Chairman and above Program Committee Member. In iasted, Reviewer is a sub-role of Speaker (itself under Delegate), with no chairing or administrative authority. A PC Chair is not a Reviewer and a Reviewer is not a PC Chair; they are distinct roles in the conference organisation, so they are unrelated.

A 'Call For Reviews' is an event/action soliciting reviewers or review submissions, while 'Reviewer' is a person role (a delegate/speaker who reviews papers). They denote completely different categories of entities (an event vs. a person role) and share no meaningful semantic relationship.

The two properties are completely different in meaning, domain, range, and type. cmt:endReview is an object property relating a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the action of ending/submitting a review). confOf:ends_on is a datatype property relating an Event to a string (the end date of an event). They share the word 'end' but denote entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Committee member denotes a person serving on a committee (with subtypes Chair, Co-chair; linked to Committee via has-members/was-a-member-of). Author denotes a person who writes a Contribution (linked via writes/writtenBy). These are distinct roles in the conference domain: a committee member need not author any paper, and an author need not be on any committee. Their extensions do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The property `name` in cmt denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while `E mail` in sigkdd denotes the email address of a Person. These are distinct attributes with different meanings, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Conference is a large-scale working event (a whole conference), whereas ekaw:Individual Presentation is a single presentation slot within a conference (parent: Scientific Event; children: Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). They occupy different levels of the event hierarchy and their intended instances do not coincide.

Operating Topicsystems is a subclass of Topic (a subject area like antennas, cryptography, mobile computing), while Program Committee is a subclass of Committee (a group of people organizing paper reviews). These denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The property 'sign' in iasted relates a Person to an Item (e.g., signing a document or artefact), while 'pay' in sigkdd relates a Person to a Registration fee (paying a fee). These are distinct relations with different ranges and different semantics; signing is not paying.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. confOf:studyAt has domain Scholar and range University, describing where a scholar studies. edas:isWrittenBy has domain Paper and range Author, describing the authorship of a paper. They share no common domain or range types and denote entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

Property A (is_a_full_paper_submission_date) is a datatype property from Important_dates to a date value, representing the concrete date by which full papers must be submitted. Property B (submit_until) is an object property from Document to a Deadline object, linking a document to its deadline entity. They differ in type (datatype vs object property), domain (Important_dates vs Document), and range (date literal vs Deadline class). Although both relate to submission deadlines, they model different relationships and are not equivalent.

Meta Review is a type of review document in the cmt ontology, while Company is a type of organization in the confOf ontology. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'abstract' property relates a Contribution to a string (its textual abstract), while the iasted 'has amount of' property relates Money to an integer (a monetary amount). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference itself. edas:ConferenceChair is a person role (subclass of Person, sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.) who chairs the conference. One is an event, the other is a person; they share only the word 'Conference' and are otherwise unrelated.

Call for participation is a conference document (an announcement/invitation), while Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal deadline for booking accommodation. They are different kinds of entities: one is a document artefact, the other is a time point. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds between them.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a person or conference, while the confOf 'has Email' property denotes an email address. These are distinct attributes with no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated.

Property A is a specific abstract submission deadline date with domain Important dates and range date. Property B is a general dating property with domain Activity and range dateTime. They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings; one is a specific deadline while the other is a general activity date.

Pending Paper in edas is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper awaiting review/decision), while Paper in ekaw is the general class of all papers, with subclasses like Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc. Pending Paper's instances are a subset of ekaw:Paper's instances, so Pending Paper is subsumed by ekaw:Paper, not equivalent.

A 'Passive conference participant' is someone who attends a conference without an active role (e.g., audience member), while an 'Organizing Committee member' is an active organizer with specific responsibilities. These are distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Co-author is a specific subclass of Author denoting a person who co-writes a paper (implying multiple authors). In ekaw, Paper_Author is the general class of any person who authored a paper, whether sole or co-author. Thus Co-author is strictly narrower than Paper_Author.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. In EDAS, belongsToEvent links a Programme (the schedule of items) to a Conference Event, indicating that a programme item is part of an event. In EKAW, listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event, indicating that a document or web resource lists an event. The domains are distinct (a schedule vs. a brochure/website), and the relations are not the same kind of association: one is about membership/belonging, the other about listing/publishing. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Dining Place is a venue/location where meals are served (a subclass of Place), while Taxi is a transport vehicle (a subclass of Item). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Document (a written summary of a paper/talk), while Tax in iasted is a subclass of Money (a financial charge such as departure tax or VAT). These denote entirely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Entity A is an event class representing the reviewing results announcement (a temporal occurrence in the conference workflow), while entity B is a committee class representing the group of people organizing the conference. These are fundamentally different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Paper is a written document submitted for review (with authors, bids, decisions, reviewers), while in Conference, Presentation is an oral/spoken event at the conference (given by an active participant, with invited talks as a subclass). They are different kinds of entities: a written submission vs. a live talk. No subsumption holds between them.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), denoting a type of conference event. edas:MobileComputingTopic is a subclass of Topic, denoting a specific subject area. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (events vs. topics) and share no domain overlap.

The cmt property 'member Of Conference' links a Conference Member to a Conference, denoting membership of a person in a conference. The Conference property 'was a steering committee of' links a Steering committee to a Conference volume, denoting that a committee organizes a conference volume. The domains (Conference Member vs Steering committee), ranges (Conference vs Conference volume), and the nature of the relations (individual membership vs committee-to-event) are different, so these properties are unrelated.

Review preference in the Conference ontology denotes a preference object related to reviewing (with degree, topic, reviewer, submitted contribution), while Person in iasted denotes a human participant (with children Delegate and Sponsor). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In EKAW, Person is the top-level class for all people (including authors, reviewers, participants, staff, students). In SIGKDD, Author is a specific subclass of Person > Speaker, denoting only people who author papers. EKAW's Person therefore subsumes SIGKDD's Author.

Submitted contribution is a written work submitted to a conference (e.g., a paper), while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance. These denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Attendee in edas denotes a person who attends the conference (a general participant), whereas OC Member in ekaw denotes a member of the Organizing Committee, a specific organizational role. An attendee is not necessarily an OC member, nor is an OC member necessarily an attendee in the same sense. The concepts do not coincide and neither subsumes the other in the given hierarchies.

In cmt, Acceptance is a subclass of Decision representing the positive decision outcome (accepting a paper), sibling to Rejection. In the Conference ontology, Rejected contribution is a subclass of Reviewed contribution representing the actual paper that was rejected. These are different kinds of entities: one is a decision/event, the other is a document. Moreover, they are on opposite ends of the acceptance spectrum (acceptance vs rejection), so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and not meaningfully related.

reviewsPerPaper is a count of how many reviews each paper receives (range int), while manuscriptDueOn is a submission deadline (range dateTime). They share the domain Conference but denote completely different concepts.

The two properties are completely different in domain, range, and meaning. has_an_ISBN is a datatype property from Conference proceedings to a string (an ISBN code), while listsEvent is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event (listing events in a programme). They share no semantic relationship.

The property 'has gender' in Conference denotes a person's gender, while 'has First Name' in edas denotes a person's first name. These are semantically distinct attributes of a Person, not the same relation, and neither subsumes the other.

Session Chair in edas is a person role (subclass of Person) who chairs sessions and can review papers. Demo Session in ekaw is a type of event/session (subclass of Session > Scientific Event > Event) where demonstrations are presented. One is a person, the other is an event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Registration of participants event is an administrative event concerning participant registration, while Workshop is a scientific event where presentations and discussions occur. They are disjoint concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both TPC Member (edas) and SC Member (ekaw) are subclasses of Person that serve on a conference committee and can act as reviewers. However, they occupy different positions in the committee hierarchy: in ekaw, SC Member is a subclass of PC Member, whereas in edas TPC Member is a direct subclass of Person with no corresponding superclass. The two ontologies model committee structure differently, so the classes overlap (both denote committee members who can review) but are not equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a public announcement document inviting people to attend or participate in a conference, while an 'Invitation letter' is a personal document (e.g., for visa or travel purposes) sent to an individual. They serve different communicative purposes in the conference domain: one is a broadcast solicitation, the other a targeted personal letter. Their sibling classes also confirm distinct document categories, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully overlapping.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person role—the chair of a conference—while Session (iasted) is a scheduled activity/event (a lecture session). They belong to completely different branches of the ontology (Person vs Activity) and denote entirely different kinds of things.

Rejected_Paper in EKAW is a highly specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been evaluated and rejected), whereas Paper in SIGKDD is the general class of all papers. Every rejected paper is a paper, but not vice versa, so Rejected_Paper is subsumed by Paper.

Both properties link a reviewer to a paper they are assigned to read/review. The cmt 'readPaper' has domain Reviewer and range Paper, while ekaw 'reviewerOfPaper' has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper. In the conference domain, these denote the same relation: a reviewer being assigned a paper to review. The slight domain difference (Reviewer vs Possible Reviewer) does not change the intended meaning of the relation itself.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document intended for attendees, while 'Computer Architecture Topic' in edas is a subject-topic for classifying papers. They share no instances and no meaningful overlap.

Both classes denote the same top-level concept of a conference in the conference-organisation domain. They share the same label and both represent the main event entity with properties such as name and topics. The differences in their property sets and subclasses reflect modelling granularity rather than divergent intended extensions.

In EDAS, PersonalHistory is a broad category capturing a person's history (with children Personal Publication History and Personal Review History), i.e. a biographical/record aggregate about a person. In EKAW, Review is a specific document written by a reviewer evaluating a paper (child of Document, with subtypes Negative/Neutral/Positive Review). These denote completely different kinds of entities: a personal history record vs. an individual review document. They share no overlap in intended instances.

Conference volume in ontology Conference denotes the overall conference edition/publication (it has committees, important dates, contributions, tracks, parts, location), i.e. the whole conference event. Conference_Session in EKAW is a specific session within a conference (sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop sessions, child of Session). These are at very different granularity levels: a conference volume contains many sessions, so they are not equivalent, not in a direct subsumption relation, and only loosely related.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Silver Supporter is a type of sponsor. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'read By Reviewer' property relates a Paper to a Reviewer (who reads/reviews the paper). The iasted 'give' property relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person gives a presentation or an item). These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and describe different actions in the conference domain.

The confOf 'early Registration' property indicates whether a Participant has registered early (boolean), while the sigkdd 'Currency' property specifies the currency of a Registration fee (string). They have different domains, different ranges, and denote entirely different concepts.

Property A captures the abstract submission deadline (a date), while property B captures textual submission instructions (a string). They denote different relations: one is a temporal deadline, the other is a set of instructions. No subsumption holds.

The property 'adjusted By' in cmt relates a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it, while 'payed by' in sigkdd relates a Registration fee to the Person who paid it. These are entirely different domain relationships with different domains and ranges, and no overlap in meaning.

In edas, Review is a subclass of Document (a specific kind of document: a review of a paper). In iasted, Document is a broad class whose children include Review, Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc. Thus iasted:Document is more general than edas:Review, making edas:Review subsumed_by iasted:Document.

Entity A is an activity/event that occurs after a conference (e.g., Departure, Full day tour), a subclass of Activity. Entity B is a physical place/venue (Conference hall), a subclass of Place. These denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Conference denotes the organisational event itself (with date, members, administrators, paper assignments, etc.). In the Conference ontology, Conference_contribution is a document/artefact (child of Conference_document) with subtypes like Written_contribution, Poster, Presentation. One is the event, the other is a contribution artefact; they share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different things.

The property 'issues' in Conference relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publication relationship), while 'searched by' in sigkdd relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (a sponsorship/search relationship). The domains (Publisher vs. Sponzor) and ranges (Conference proceedings vs. ACM SIGKDD) are entirely different concepts, and the two properties describe unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document, while in edas, Document is a general class with Paper as one of its children (alongside Meal Menu, Programme, Review, Slide Set). Thus cmt:Paper is strictly narrower than edas:Document; edas:Document subsumes cmt:Paper.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document subclass representing the abstract of a paper, while Performance Topic in edas is a topic subclass representing a subject area (performance-related). They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Document vs Topic) and denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In edas, hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a record of reviews they have authored). In sigkdd, presentation links a Speaker to a Document they present. The domains (Reviewer vs Speaker), ranges (Personal Review History vs Document), and overall semantics (review history vs presentation document) are disjoint, so no equivalence or subsumption holds.

Conference document in ontology A is a class whose instances are documents (Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review, etc.), with properties like has authors and has a date of issue. Activity in ontology B is a class whose instances are activities/events (Conference activity, Activity before/after conference), with properties like is held in, is given by, is paid for. These are fundamentally different categories of things: documents vs. activities. They share no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Building is a specific kind of Place (path: Place > Building) with concrete subclasses like Conference hotel, Conference building, etc. In sigkdd, Place is the general spatial concept with children Conference hall, Hotel, Main office. Thus iasted:Building is strictly narrower than sigkdd:Place; the two are not equivalent.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Best Paper Awards Committee is a committee that selects award-winning papers. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The property `write` in iasted relates a Person to an Item they author (e.g., a paper or document), while `presentation` in sigkdd relates a Speaker to a Document they present. Authoring and presenting are distinct roles in the conference domain: a person writes a paper, whereas a speaker gives a presentation of a document. The domains (Person vs Speaker) and the intended semantics differ, so these properties are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

An Invited speaker is a specific conference contributor who delivers an invited talk, whereas an Attendee is any person who attends the conference. These are distinct concepts: an invited speaker is not necessarily an attendee (they may only come to give their talk), and an attendee is not necessarily an invited speaker. They share the common parent Person but neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way, and they are not equivalent.

confOf:writes relates an Author to a Contribution they have authored. ekaw:partOf is a generic mereological relation indicating that one entity is part of another. These are fundamentally different relations: one denotes authorship, the other denotes parthood. They do not share domain/range overlap and no contextual evidence suggests equivalence.

Session Chair (ekaw) is a person who chairs a session, a specific role within a conference. Conference Hiker (iasted) is a type of Delegate (person attending the conference) who moves between sessions. These are distinct concepts: one is a leadership role, the other is an attendee behavior pattern. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A's paperID is a datatype property mapping a Paper to a numeric identifier (unsignedLong), while B's write is an object property mapping a Person to an Item they author. They differ in type, domain, range, and meaning; one denotes identification, the other authorship.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (paper -> decision). In sigkdd, submit links an Author to a Paper (author -> paper). They have different domains (Paper vs Author) and different ranges (Decision vs Paper), and represent conceptually different relations (assigning a decision to a paper vs an author submitting a paper).

Review Question in edas is a specific question item in a review form (numerical or textual), while Document in sigkdd is a general document artefact (abstract, paper, review). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties associate a paper with a subject area / research topic, but they differ in direction and generality. In cmt, hasSubjectArea goes from Paper to Subject Area. In ekaw, topicCoveredBy goes from Research Topic to Event or Paper, i.e. the inverse direction and with a broader range (Event or Paper). They are therefore not equivalent; they are related (overlapping) but not inverse-equivalent in the strict alignment sense.

Week Reject Rating is a review rating value (a subclass of Review Rating alongside Accept/Reject ratings), while Abstract is a document type (subclass of Document alongside Paper and Review). These are completely different concepts: one is a rating/score for a review, the other is a type of document. No overlap in intended instances.

Conference contributor in ontology Conference is a broad superclass covering all persons who contribute to a conference (including active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors). General Chair in sigkdd is a specific type of organizer who leads the conference. A General Chair is a conference contributor, but not vice versa, so Conference contributor subsumes General Chair.

Conference applicant is a person who applies to attend/register for a conference (a prospective participant). Organizator is a person who organizes the conference (with subtypes like General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). These are distinct roles: one seeks to attend, the other runs the event. They share only the common parent Person.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference part' denotes structural subdivisions of a conference such as Track, Tutorial, and Workshop—constituent parts of a conference volume/proceedings. In the EDAS ontology, 'Conference Event' is a top-level class for events (academic or non-academic) with properties like start/end dates, location, attendees, and a programme. These are different concepts: one is a structural component of a conference, the other is an event entity. Their children, properties, and intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property from Conference to int that records how many reviews each paper should receive, whereas hasReview is an object property from Paper to Review that links a paper to its individual review instances. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Paper), range (int vs Review), and meaning (a count vs a relation to review objects).

Conference document in the Conference ontology is a broad top-level class covering all conference-related documents (call for papers, announcements, contributions, reviews, web pages, etc.). Abstract in ekaw is a specific subclass of Document denoting a summary of a presentation. The two do not share the same instances: a Call for Paper or Conference WWW is not an Abstract, and an Abstract is not a Conference document in the broad sense. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

Reception in edas is a social event (a gathering/social function), while Welcome address in iasted is a conference activity (a speech/programmatic item). They denote different kinds of things: a social event vs. an opening speech. The iasted ontology even has a separate sibling 'Coctail reception' which is closer to edas Reception, confirming that Welcome address is not the same concept.

Both classes denote the same concept: a person involved in the conference domain. They share identical labels and both serve as a general superclass for conference-related roles (Attendee/Listener, Author/Speaker, Chair/Organizator, etc.). Their properties overlap in capturing personal information (email, name) and conference-related activities (attending, paying registration). The children and properties are consistent with the same intended extension of 'Person' in the conference organization domain.

Accepted Paper is a document (paper) accepted for publication, while Best Student Paper Supporter is a sponsor type. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Document vs Sponzor) and denote completely different domain concepts.

A Conference Member in cmt is a person who belongs to a conference (parent: Person; subclasses include Author, Reviewer, Chair). A Social Event in edas is a non-academic event such as a reception or excursion (parent: Non Academic Event > Conference Event). One denotes a person/role, the other an event/activity; they share no domain overlap.

A Program Committee Member (cmt) is a person who reviews papers, distinct from an Organizing Committee member (sigkdd) who handles logistics. The sigkdd ontology has a separate 'Program Committee member' class, confirming these are different roles. Their parent hierarchies also differ: cmt's Program Committee Member descends from Conference Member, while sigkdd's Organizing Committee member descends from Organizator.

Both are datatype properties that indicate when an event/conference begins. The confOf 'starts_on' has domain Event and range string, while sigkdd 'Start_of_conference' has domain Conference and range dateTime. A Conference is a subtype of Event, and both string and dateTime represent temporal values; the difference in datatype representation is a modeling choice rather than a semantic distinction. The intended meaning—recording the start date/time of a conference event—coincides.

The property 'issues' in Conference ontology relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issuing proceedings). The property 'presentation' in sigkdd ontology relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presenting a document). These are entirely different relations with different domains (Publisher vs Speaker) and different ranges (Conference proceedings vs Document), denoting different relationships in the conference domain.

Author Not Reviewer in cmt is a specific subclass of Author (a person who authored a paper but is not assigned as a reviewer), whereas Attendee in edas is a general Person who attends the conference. These are disjoint concepts: an Author Not Reviewer is not necessarily an attendee, and an Attendee is not necessarily an author. They share only the distant ancestor Person.

Non speaker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate, i.e. a person who attends the conference but does not present. Registration Non Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee, i.e. a monetary fee paid by a non-member. One denotes a person role, the other a fee; they are unrelated.

Property A (has_a_location) is a datatype property from Conference volume to string, capturing where a conference volume is located. Property B (is_equipped_by) is an object property from Place to Item, capturing what items a place is equipped with. They have different domains, different ranges (string vs Item), different directions of meaning, and no overlap in the relation they express.

Cryptography Topic is a subject-area topic (sibling of Communication Theory, Computer Networks, etc.) under Topic in edas. Tutorial Abstract is a document type (a kind of Abstract) in ekaw. They denote completely different concepts: a research subject area vs. a textual document artefact. No subsumption or overlap.

`is an ending date` is a datatype property whose domain is `Important dates` (e.g., conference deadlines) and range is `date`; it denotes the end of a deadline period. `is dated on` is a datatype property whose domain is `Activity` (e.g., conference sessions/events) and range is `dateTime`; it denotes when an activity occurs. They relate to different kinds of entities (deadline periods vs. scheduled activities) and capture different semantics (ending date vs. occurrence date), so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract document of a paper, not the paper itself. In Conference, 'Paper' is a full regular contribution.
