The cmt equivalent of Conference's Paper would be cmt's Paper (or Paper Full Version), not Paper Abstract. These denote different levels of artefact: an abstract vs. a complete paper.

Sponsorship in edas is a class representing financial support arrangements (with cost amount, currency, provider organization, and a child Travel Grant). Currency in iasted represents a monetary currency unit. These are completely different concepts: one is the act/arrangement of sponsoring, the other is the unit of money. They share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

In edas, Call is a top-level class representing an announcement soliciting submissions (papers, manuscripts, reviews), with properties like submission instructions, deadlines, and event associations. In iasted, Deadline is a temporal entity (subclass of Time) representing specific due dates (camera ready, notification, hotel reservation, registration, submission). A Call is a document/announcement artifact that may have a deadline, while a Deadline is a point in time. These are structurally and semantically different concepts despite both being related to the submission process.

A Rated Paper in edas is a paper that has received a review rating, sitting under Active Paper > Paper > Document. A Card in iasted is a physical item (with a child Credit card and siblings like Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle, Publication, Document). These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Registeered applicant is a person who has registered for a conference (a subclass of Conference applicant under Person), whereas Travel Grant is a kind of sponsorship award. These denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Review in the Conference ontology denotes a complete review document of a contribution, whereas Textual Review Question in edas denotes a specific question (with a textual/free-form answer) within a review form. They are at different levels of granularity: one is the review artefact itself, the other is a component question of a review. Their intended instances do not coincide.

confOf:Paper is a scholarly contribution (a document submitted to a conference), while sigkdd:Deadline_Paper_Submission is a temporal deadline (a date by which papers must be submitted). They share the word 'Paper' but denote entirely different concepts — a document artefact vs. a temporal milestone — with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a Chairman responsible for organizing the conference), while Hotel presenter is a delegate who presents at a hotel venue. These are completely different concepts: one is an organizational/committee role, the other is a presentation role tied to a venue type. Their paths, parents, and siblings confirm no overlap in intended instances.

Invited Speaker is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, while Reviewer is a person who evaluates submitted papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for people involved in a conference. Ontology A's children (Conference participant, Reviewer, Committee member, etc.) and Ontology B's children (Delegate, Sponsor) are all subtypes of people in the conference domain. The properties differ in granularity but all relate persons to conference activities, items, documents, and contact information. The intended instances coincide: both denote any human actor in the conference setting.

In cmt, Document is a general superclass whose children are Paper and Review (i.e., any written artefact produced in the reviewing system). In the Conference ontology, Review is a specific kind of Conference document (a review of a contribution). These are at different levels of abstraction and denote different concepts: a generic document container vs. a specific review artefact. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the differing ontology scopes.

`reviewsPerPaper` in cmt captures the number of reviews each paper receives during the reviewing process (domain Conference, range int). `City_of_conference` in sigkdd captures the location/city where the conference takes place (domain Conference, range string). They relate to completely different aspects of a conference (review workload vs. geographic location), so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair in cmt is a conference leadership role (a type of Chairman/Conference Member responsible for chairing the conference). Author cd proceedings included in iasted is a specific type of author whose paper is included in the CD proceedings. These are completely different concepts: one is an administrative/organizational role, the other is a contributor role distinguished by publication medium. They share no semantic overlap.

Paper Abstract is a short summary of a research paper (a scientific contribution artifact), while Registration form is an administrative form for conference registration. They serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain and share no meaningful overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, 'Program committee' is a specific committee type (sibling of Organizing committee and Steering committee under Committee). In ontology B, 'Committee' is the general class with children including Best Paper Awards Committee, Organizing Committee, and Program Committee. Thus A's Program committee is a subtype of B's Committee, not equivalent to it.

logoURL points to a logo image (anyURI) for the conference, while Name_of_conference provides the textual name (string) of the conference. These are completely different attributes with no semantic overlap.

Regular author in Conference is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, denoting a person who authors a paper. Participant in confOf is a subclass of Person, denoting any conference attendee. They are disjoint in intended instances: an author is not necessarily a participant (e.g., non-attending author), and a participant is not necessarily an author. No subsumption holds either way.

These properties relate completely different entities. 'has_a_steering_committee' links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (organizational governance), while 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Different domains, different ranges, different semantics — no alignment relationship exists.

These properties have different meanings and different domains/ranges. 'is given by' in Conference relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it (a presenter). 'is given to' in iasted relates an Item to a Person who receives it (a recipient). They are not the same relation, nor inverses of each other in this context, and their domains (Presentation vs. Item) and ranges (Active conference participant vs. Person) differ. They denote different concepts in the conference domain.

Reject Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating, i.e. a specific evaluation outcome/score assigned to a paper. Review in sigkdd is a subclass of Document, i.e. the textual review artefact itself. One is a rating value, the other is a document; they denote completely different kinds of entities.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'is Written By' links a Paper to its Author, while 'designed by' links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD. They share no common domain or range types and denote entirely different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'member Of Conference' links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation). In the Conference ontology, 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (who presents). The domains (Conference Member vs Presentation), ranges (Conference vs Active conference participant), and semantic relations (membership vs presentation authorship) are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Conference:Topic is a general class for conference topics, with properties linking topics to conference parts, reviews, and submitted contributions. edas:CryptographyTopic is a specific subclass of Topic representing only cryptography-related subjects. The general Topic class in Conference does not correspond to the specialized CryptographyTopic in edas; they are at different levels of generality and the Conference ontology has no counterpart to the specific cryptography topic.

confOf Member is a participant category (alongside Regular and Student), while iasted IASTED_member is a delegate subcategory (alongside Listener, Speaker, etc.). The iasted class is oddly placed under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate, suggesting a modelling artefact rather than a genuine membership concept. The two classes occupy different hierarchies and have different intended instances, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different things: A maps an Important dates entity to a date (camera-ready submission deadline), while B maps a Social/Working event to a string (where the event is held). Different domains, different ranges, different meanings.

Both are datatype properties recording a paper-submission deadline, but they differ in domain (Important dates vs Conference) and range (date vs dateTime). The Conference ontology models deadlines as entities with their own date slot, while edas attaches the deadline directly to the Conference. They overlap in meaning but are not equivalent.
Van is a transport vehicle in iasted, while Listener is a person (audience member) in sigkdd. They denote completely unrelated categories with no domain overlap.

confOf:Conference is a class denoting an academic event (a kind of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). iasted:Tutorial speaker is a class denoting a person who gives a tutorial (a kind of Author/Speaker/Delegate). These are completely different categories—an event versus a person role—so they are unrelated.

Conference document in the Conference ontology is a class whose instances are documents (Call for paper, Review, Conference contribution, etc.), with properties like has authors and has a date of issue. Organization in edas is a class whose instances are organizations (Academia, Government, Industry, NGO) that provide sponsorships. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A is a specific deadline property (abstract submission deadline) while B is a general deadline-completion property applicable to any deadline. A's relation is a specific instance of B's general relation, so A is subsumed by B.

Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/trip that attendees participate in during a conference), while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (a physical means of transportation). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote different categories of things: one is an event, the other is a vehicle.

These properties relate entirely different kinds of things. 'has a submitted contribution' connects a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (i.e., the paper being reviewed in an expertise area). 'give' connects a Person to an Activity or Item (i.e., a person giving a presentation or item). The domains (Review expertise vs. Person) and ranges (Submitted contribution vs. Activity/Item) do not overlap, and the relations denote different concepts in the conference domain.

Entity A is a class denoting a person who registered early and paid (a subtype of Person/Conference applicant), while entity B is a class denoting a monetary fee charged to non-members for registration (a subtype of Money/Fee). One denotes a person, the other a fee amount; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Review in the Conference ontology is a document class whose instances are individual review documents (siblings include Call for paper, Conference contribution, etc.). Personal Review History in edas is a history/record object associated with a reviewer, summarizing that reviewer's reviewing activity over time (sibling is Personal Publication History). One is a single review artefact; the other is an aggregated personal record. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author (the person who wrote the paper), while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (someone assigned to review it). These are distinct roles in the conference domain, relating different kinds of people to the paper, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Conference Banquet is a social event during the conference (e.g., a dinner), while Full day tour is a post-conference activity (a day-long excursion). They are different kinds of events occurring at different times with different purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Reviewer is a specific role (a Conference Member who reviews papers, with properties like assignExternalReviewer, readByReviewer, markConflictOfInterest). In the Conference ontology, Conference_contributor is a broader class subsuming Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author—i.e., someone who contributes content to the conference, not necessarily a reviewer. Notably, the Conference ontology has a separate sibling class 'Reviewer', confirming that Conference_contributor is not intended to cover reviewers. These classes denote different concepts with non-coinciding intended instances.

confOf Reception is a specific social event, while iasted Social program is a broader category of conference activities that includes Dinner banquet, Coctail reception, Coffee break, etc. Reception is thus a narrower concept subsumed by Social program.

The iasted property 'is needed for' is a generic relation from Item to Person (e.g., an item such as a registration or document is needed for a person to participate). The sigkdd property 'presentationed by' specifically links a Document to a Speaker who presents it. The domains differ (Item vs Document), the ranges differ (Person vs Speaker), and the intended meanings are distinct: one denotes a requirement/need relation, the other denotes authorship/presentation of a document. They do not denote the same relation.

Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference, while Webmaster is a person serving as an organizer. They belong to entirely different ontological categories (activity vs. person) and share no domain overlap.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they capture completely different information: email stores a person's electronic mail address, while hasBiography stores a free-text biographical description. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

hasFirstName is a datatype property from Person to string representing a person's first name. Price is a datatype property from Registration fee to int representing a monetary amount. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings with no overlap.

These properties have different meanings and different ranges. 'employed By' relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place or Time where they are present. Employment and physical/temporal presence are distinct relations in the conference domain.

These properties are completely different. earlyRegistration is a datatype property from Participant to boolean indicating whether a participant registered early. locationOf is an object property from Location to Event indicating where an event takes place. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Invited speaker is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, whereas Author of paper is a person who authored a paper. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: an invited speaker need not have a paper, and an author need not be an invited speaker. The class hierarchies also differ (Conference contributor vs Author), and there is no evidence of overlap or subsumption between these two specific roles.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. In edas, 'relates To' goes from a Document to an Academic Event/Conference/Session/Person (i.e., a document is related to the event or person it concerns). In iasted, 'give' goes from a Person to an Activity/Item (i.e., a person gives a presentation or item). They are not inverses of each other either, since one is about documents being associated with events/persons and the other about persons presenting activities/items. The domains and ranges do not align, so they are unrelated.

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs a committee or conference (subclass of Person with children like Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair). Power Point presentation in iasted is a type of presentation/activity at a conference. These denote completely different categories of entities—a person role versus a presentation artifact—so they are unrelated.

Conference Venue Place in edas is a general class for places where conference events are held (e.g., meeting rooms, dining places, accommodations). Conference building in iasted is a specific kind of Building where the conference takes place. The iasted ontology models Conference building as a specific Building with subtypes like Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, etc., while edas treats venue places more broadly. Conference building is a more specific concept (a building) within the broader category of conference venue places, so Conference Venue Place subsumes Conference building.

Both properties relate a conference document/paper to its authors/persons, but they are inverses of each other: 'has_authors' goes from document to person, while 'isWrittenBy' goes from paper to author. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, the best relation is 'related'.

Conference Participant in EKAW is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference (with children like Presenter, Session Chair, etc.). Activity before conference in IASTED is a subclass of Activity, denoting organizational activities that occur before a conference (such as Accepting manuscript, Renting, Research). These are completely different categories: one is about people, the other about activities. They share no instances and are unrelated.

Administrative event in confOf is a temporal event in the conference lifecycle (submission, reviewing, registration, camera ready). Signal Processing Topic in edas is a subject-area classification for papers. They share no instances and belong to disjoint domain partitions (events vs topics).

Tutorial in iasted is a subclass of Lecture under Activity > Conference activity, denoting an educational event or session. Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person > Speaker, denoting a person who gives a talk. One is an event/activity, the other is a person; they are disjoint categories with no meaningful alignment.

cmt:User is a subclass of cmt:Person, restricted to users of the CMT system (Administrator, Author, Reviewer). confOf:Person is the top-level person class covering all conference-related people including non-users like Scholar, Volunteer, Participant, etc. Therefore cmt:User is more specific than confOf:Person, making it subsumed_by.

In ontology A, 'Conference fees' denotes a monetary charge or fee concept, whereas in ontology B, 'Conference' is an event class (a subtype of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). These are entirely different kinds of entities: one is about financial charges, the other about academic events. They share the word 'Conference' in their labels but denote unrelated concepts.

A's 'is the 1th part of' is a specific part-whole relation restricted to Abstract being the first part of Paper/Poster/Presentation. B's 'part Of' is a general meronymic relation with no domain/range restrictions. The specific relation is subsumed by the general one, but they are not equivalent since A is much more constrained.

In ekaw, Document is a general artefact (Abstract, Paper, Review, Flyer, etc.) written/authored by persons. In sigkdd, Deadline is a temporal point (with a dateTime) by which submissions must be received, and it has specific subclasses like abstract/paper submission and notification deadlines. Although sigkdd has a 'submit until' property whose domain happens to be Document, the two classes themselves denote completely different categories of entities (artefact vs. temporal deadline), so they are unrelated.

confOf:Volunteer is a subclass of Person representing a person who volunteers at a conference. edas:TwoLevelConference is a subclass of Conference (and oddly also listed under Person/TPC Member in the provided hierarchy) representing a type of conference event. These denote completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is a conference type. They share no semantic overlap.

The two properties are completely different in meaning and structure. 'has the first name' is a datatype property from Person to string, representing a person's first name. 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item, representing a person obtaining some item. They have different ranges (string vs Item), different types (datatype vs object property), and no semantic overlap.

A cmt ProgramCommitteeMember is a specific role (PC member who reviews papers, assigned to a Program Committee, with maxPapers etc.), whereas ekaw Conference_Participant is a broad superclass for anyone attending the conference (including demo chairs, presenters, early/late registered participants, OC members, etc.). Every PC member is a conference participant, but not vice versa, so cmt:ProgramCommitteeMember is subsumed_by ekaw:Conference_Participant.

The two properties relate completely different entities in the conference domain. In cmt, 'hasBid' links a Paper to a Bid (an offer to review the paper). In the Conference ontology, 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings. The domains (Paper vs Publisher) and ranges (Bid vs Conference proceedings) are disjoint, so the properties are unrelated.

Property A links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation that publishes proceedings). Property B links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (a temporal/ordering relation between events). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings with no overlap.

A is a subclass of Person (a conference participant who is passive), while B is a subclass of State (a phase or status of a conference). They denote completely different kinds of entities: people vs. temporal/organizational states.

The cmt 'assigned By Reviewer' property links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (a person-to-person assignment relation). The iasted 'give' property links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person-to-event/artefact relation). These are completely different relations: one is about reviewer assignment, the other about giving presentations or items. They share no semantic overlap.

The property isMenuOf in edas specifically relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (i.e., which meal event a menu belongs to), while hasEvent in ekaw is a general part-whole relation between an Event and its sub-events. They operate on completely different domain/range types and express different relations (menu-to-meal-event vs. event-to-sub-event), so they are unrelated.

In Conference ontology, Tutorial is a specific kind of conference part (a tutorial event), sibling to Track and Workshop. In confOf, Conference is the main conference event itself, with Tutorial and Workshop as siblings under Working event. These denote completely different concepts: a tutorial session vs. the conference as a whole.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person participating in the conference). In the Conference ontology, is_a_topis_of_conference_parts links a Topic to a Conference part (a subject area to a session/event part). The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, so the properties are unrelated.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Contributed Talk is a type of presentation event. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The ekaw property 'volumeContainsPaper' relates a volume (proceedings container) to the papers it contains, while the iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or item). They connect completely different domain and range types and describe unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and express different relations. confOf:writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper). iasted:send relates a Person to an Item (e.g., someone sending an item). The direction and semantics differ: writtenBy points from document to author, while send points from person to item. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

Although both properties relate a conference-event holder to an event/programme, the domains differ significantly: edas:hasProgramme has domain Conference Event and range Programme, while ekaw:listsEvent has domain Programme Brochure or Web Site and range Event. The direction and the nature of the relationship differ: hasProgramme attaches a programme to a conference event, whereas listsEvent enumerates events within a published programme brochure or website. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other.

These two properties are fundamentally different. confOf:ends_on is a datatype property that maps an Event to a string representing its end date. ekaw:partOfEvent is an object property that relates an Event to another Event (part-whole relation). They have different ranges (string vs Event), different types (datatype vs object), and different semantics (temporal endpoint vs mereological relation).

Camera Ready Paper (ekaw) is a class of document—a finalized paper accepted for publication at a conference. Deadline hotel reservation (iasted) is a temporal class representing a deadline date for booking hotel accommodations. These are completely different domain concepts: one is a document artifact, the other is a time point. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Author is a person who writes/submits papers in the cmt ontology, while Building is a physical place in the iasted ontology. They share no common instances and are from completely different domains (person vs. place).

Invited speaker is a person invited to speak at a conference. Author cd proceedings included is a specific author role tied to having work included in CD proceedings. One is about being an invited speaker, the other about authorship of CD proceedings; they denote different concepts with no clear overlap.

In the iasted ontology, Fee is a general class covering various monetary charges (registration fees, hotel fees, extra trip fees, etc.), with Sponzorship as a sibling. In the sigkdd ontology, Sponzor fee is a specific subtype of Fee. Thus iasted:Fee is strictly more general than sigkdd:Sponzor fee, making this a subsumes relationship rather than equivalence.

Entity A is a class denoting a written work that has been accepted (a contribution/artefact), while entity B is a class denoting a temporal deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies (document vs. time) and their instances do not coincide.

A 'Conference Chair' in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (a role under Person > Chairman), while 'Conference building' in iasted is a physical place/building where a conference is held (under Place > Building). They denote completely different categories of entities—a human role versus a physical location—so they are unrelated.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'enter Conference Details' (cmt) relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of an admin entering conference details), while 'has Topic' (edas) relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (assigning a topic to a conference or paper). They share no semantic overlap.

Submitted Paper (ekaw) is a class representing a document type—a paper that has been submitted for review. Deadline Paper Submission (sigkdd) is a class representing a temporal deadline (a date/time point) by which papers must be submitted. One is a document artifact, the other is a temporal event/deadline. They share the word 'submission' but denote completely different categories of entities (document vs. deadline), so they are unrelated.

Company is a type of organization (e.g., a corporate entity), while Conference_hall is a physical place where conference events are held. They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies (Organization vs Place) and denote completely different kinds of things in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. confOf:hasCountry links Organizations and Persons to a Country, while iasted:is_designed_for links Activity, Money, and Time to Activity or Person. They share no domain or range overlap, and their labels and intended meanings are completely different.

These properties differ in both domain/range and meaning. 'relatedToEvent' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (a specific presentation event for that paper), while 'partOfEvent' is a general mereological relation linking any Event to another Event it is part of. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since one is a paper-to-presentation relation and the other is a general event-to-event part-whole relation.

Hotel fee (iasted) is a fee for hotel accommodation, while Registration fee (sigkdd) is a fee for conference registration. They are distinct types of fees with different purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. In cmt, 'hasConferenceMember' links a Conference to its Conference Member (organizational membership relation). In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or item). The domains (Conference vs Person), ranges (Conference Member vs Activity/Item), and intended meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

Written contribution in Conference is a document (subclass of Conference document > Conference contribution), with children like Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, meaning it denotes written papers/articles. Contributed Talk in ekaw is an event (subclass of Event > Scientific Event > Individual Presentation), meaning it denotes a talk/presentation session at a conference. One is a document, the other is an event/activity; they are disjoint kinds of things.

Property A (is_a_topis_of_conference_parts) links a Topic to a Conference part, expressing that a topic is associated with a conference part. Property B (partOf) in EKAW is a generic mereological relation expressing that something is part of something else. They operate in opposite directions and relate entirely different kinds of entities: A's domain is Topic and range is Conference part, while partOf is a general part-whole relation. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only weakly related at best.

Conference contributor (Person > Conference contributor) denotes a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker). Conference state (State > Conference state) denotes a state or status associated with a conference, not a person. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Person vs. State) and have no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in opposite conceptual directions. `has_a_program_committee` links a Conference volume to its Program committee (an organizational body). `belongsToEvent` links a Programme (a document/schedule) to a Conference Event. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so they are unrelated.

Information for participants is a conference document providing logistical information to attendees, while Computer Networks Topic is a subject classification for paper submissions. They share no instances and belong to completely different parts of the conference domain.

Bid in cmt is a bid placed by a Reviewer on a Paper (part of the paper assignment process), while Country in confOf is a geographic country associated with organizations and persons. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:Author is a broad class covering any person who authors a paper (with children like Co-author). Conference:Regular_author is more specific, sitting under Conference_contribution and further partitioned into Contribution_1th_author and Contribution_co_author. The cmt Author class subsumes the Conference Regular_author concept, as the latter is a more structured/specific representation of authors within that ontology.
Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Cryptography Topic is a subject-area topic. They share no instances and belong to unrelated parts of the domain.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a subtype of Chairman/Person), while Modelling is a research activity performed before a conference. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

confOf:Submission_event is an event class (subclass of Administrative event) representing the submission process/activity. iasted:Brief_introduction_for_Session_chair is a document class (subclass of Document) representing a specific artefact given to session chairs. One is an event, the other is a document; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (i.e., who added that PC member to the system). In ekaw, 'organised By' links an Event to an Organisation or Person (i.e., who organises an academic event). The domains (PC Member vs Event) and ranges (Administrator vs Organisation/Person) do not overlap, and the intended meanings are unrelated.

confOf:Workshop is a type of event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), denoting an academic meeting activity. iasted:Session_room is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room), denoting a room where sessions are held. One is an event/activity, the other is a physical location; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf:Conference is an event (a conference occurrence), whereas ekaw:OC_Chair is a person who chairs the Organizing Committee. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In the iasted ontology, 'Viza' (visa) is a travel document for conference attendees, distinct from academic submissions. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is an academic document that can be submitted by an author. Despite sharing the parent 'Document', their intended instances are completely different: a visa is an immigration/travel artefact, whereas a Paper is a scholarly contribution. They are unrelated.

edas:AcademicEvent is a specific subclass of ConferenceEvent whose children are Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop. ekaw:Event is the top-level event class with children Scientific Event and Social Event. ekaw:Event is more general: it includes both scientific and social events, whereas edas:AcademicEvent is restricted to academic events (with a sibling NonAcademicEvent). Thus edas:AcademicEvent is subsumed by ekaw:Event rather than equivalent.

cmt:Author is a specific subclass of Person (a conference member who writes/submits papers), while sigkdd:Person is the general person class with subclasses Listener, Organizator, Speaker. Author is more specific than Person, so Author is subsumed_by Person.

These properties differ in both domain and range: confOf's hasCity links Organization or Person to a City object, while sigkdd's City_of_conference links Conference to a string literal. They relate different kinds of entities and use different range types (object vs datatype), so they do not denote the same relation.

The cmt property hasConflictOfInterest specifically denotes a conflict of interest between a Person and a Document (e.g., a reviewer having a conflict with a paper). The iasted property is_connected_with is a much more generic relation whose domain includes Activity and Person and whose range includes Item and Place. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same way, and the iasted property does not capture the specific notion of conflict of interest.

Research Topic in EKAW denotes a subject area covered by events and papers (e.g., a research field or theme), while Currency in IASTED denotes a monetary unit (e.g., for registration fees). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'assigned To' property links a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper), while the sigkdd 'awarded by' property links an Award to some unspecified entity that grants the award. These are completely different relations in the conference domain: one concerns review assignment, the other concerns award attribution.

confOf:Scholar is a person (a scholar/student attending the conference), while iasted:Author_attendee_book_registration_fee is a monetary fee charged for registration. They belong to completely different branches of the ontology (Person vs Money/Fee) and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Computer in iasted is a piece of audiovisual equipment used in conference presentations, while Listener in sigkdd is a person who attends talks. They share no instances and belong to entirely different domains (equipment vs. person).

Both relate to the manuscript submission process in a conference, but they are not equivalent. 'Call For Manuscripts' in edas is a Call (an announcement/invitation for submission), while 'Receiving manuscript' in iasted is an Activity (the act of accepting/receiving submissions). A call for manuscripts precedes and triggers the receiving of manuscripts, but they denote different concepts: one is an announcement, the other is an action/activity. They are related as part of the same workflow but not equivalent.

confOf 'Social event' is a broad class covering banquets, receptions, and trips, while ekaw 'Conference Trip' is a specific kind of social event (child of ekaw 'Social Event'). Thus confOf:Social_event is strictly more general than ekaw:Conference_Trip.

cmt:Conference Member is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs). iasted:Conference hall is a subclass of Place, denoting a physical location where conference sessions are held. One is a person, the other is a physical venue; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a Person who contributes to a conference (parent is Person; children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author). Conference Hiker in ontology B is a subclass of Delegate under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate, i.e. a type of conference attendee/participant, not a contributor of papers or talks. The two classes denote different concepts (contributor vs. participant/hiker), and their hierarchies confirm they are not equivalent, nor is one clearly more general than the other.

Radio Communications Topic is a subject-matter topic (e.g., antennas, communication theory, mobile computing) under Topic in the edas ontology, whereas Card is a physical item (with a child Credit card) under Item in the iasted ontology. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

A Demo Chair is a specific conference role responsible for organizing demos, while a Program Committee member is a reviewer/committee role for paper selection. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have different domains (Conference vs Conference proceedings), different ranges (boolean vs int), and completely different meanings: one indicates whether a conference accepts hardcopy submissions, while the other records the number of volumes in conference proceedings. They share no semantic relationship.

confOf's 'ends on' is a datatype property from Event to a string (representing an end date), while ekaw's 'has Event' is an object property from Event to Event (linking an event to sub-events). They have different ranges, different property types, and different semantics; they are not equivalent.

Property A (has_members) relates a Committee to its Committee members, capturing the membership relation of a committee. Property B (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution they authored. These are entirely different relations: one is about committee composition, the other about authorship of a paper. They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. `has parts` connects a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (e.g., tracks, sessions, or sub-events within a volume), while `has Location` connects a Conference Event to a Place where it is held. The domains (Conference volume vs Conference Event) and ranges (Conference part vs Place) are disjoint concepts, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

Rejection is a decision outcome for a submitted paper (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), while Banquet is a social event (sibling of Reception and Trip under Social event). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both entities concern individual presentations at a conference, but they are modeled at different levels of generality and in different hierarchies. In the Conference ontology, Poster is a specific kind of Conference contribution (a document/artefact), sibling to Regular contribution, Written contribution, Presentation, etc. In EKAW, Individual Presentation is a Scientific Event (an occurrence/activity), with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial. A poster is a type of individual presentation event, but Poster (a specific contribution type) is narrower than Individual Presentation (a general event category that subsumes talks and tutorials). The two ontologies also place them under different root categories (document vs. event), so they are not equivalent; they overlap conceptually but neither cleanly subsumes the other given the artefact/event distinction.

Agency Staff Member in ekaw denotes personnel from a sponsoring or partner agency (a staff member, not necessarily a conference participant or author), whereas Author of paper in sigkdd is a specific kind of person who authored a paper. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other: an agency staff member need not be an author, and an author need not be agency staff.

The iasted Reviewer is a person who reviews papers (subclass of Speaker, sibling of Author). The sigkdd Author is a person who writes and submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: a reviewer evaluates papers while an author produces them. They share the parent Speaker but denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference gathering itself. ekaw:Early Registered Participant is a person (subclass of Conference Participant), denoting an individual who registered early. One is an event, the other is a person; they share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Location in EKAW denotes a physical or virtual place where an Event is held (domain/range of heldIn/locationOf). Money in IASTED denotes a monetary amount, with children Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip and properties like has_amount_of, is_paid_by, is_paid_for. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'invited by' (Conference) relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the one who invited them), while 'has Reviewer' (ekaw) relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer assigned to review it. They describe fundamentally different relationships: one is about invitation between reviewers, the other about paper-reviewer assignment.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and express different relations. In ontology A, 'is the 1th part of' links an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation, indicating a part-whole relationship between a document and its abstract. In ontology B, 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker, indicating who presented the document. These are semantically distinct relations with incompatible domains and ranges.

Co author in cmt is a subclass of Author (a Person) who co-writes a paper. Poster in Conference is a subclass of Conference contribution (a Document). One denotes a person, the other a document type; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Student lecturer in iasted is a person who is both a student and a lecturer (a speaker presenting at the conference), situated under Lecturer. Author of paper in sigkdd is a person who authored a paper. A student lecturer is not necessarily an author, and an author of paper is not necessarily a lecturer. The two concepts denote different roles in the conference domain and do not overlap in intended instances.

Organizational Meeting in edas is a meeting for organizational/administrative purposes (e.g., committee or planning meetings), situated under Academic Event alongside Paper Presentation, Talk Event, and Workshop. Poster Session in ekaw is a session where posters are presented, situated under Session alongside Conference Session, Demo Session, Regular Session, and Workshop Session. These are distinct concepts: one is an administrative/organizational gathering, the other is a scientific presentation format for posters. They share no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Working_event is a kind of event (Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) with properties like topics, titles, and administrative events. sigkdd:Main_office is a physical place (sibling of Conference hall, Hotel). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair is a leadership role (a person who chairs the conference), while Listener is a passive attendee who only listens. They are distinct roles in a conference with no overlap in intended instances.

hasCity is a datatype property from Contact Information to a string (a city name), while heldIn is an object property from Event to Location (a place object). They have different domains, different ranges (literal vs. object), and different semantics: one records a city string for contact info, the other records where an event is held.

Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a published document (a multi-author volume of conference papers), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place where a conference is held. They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely unrelated categories (document vs. place).

Conference Chair in cmt is an active leadership role (a Chairman responsible for accepting/rejecting papers and assigning reviewers), sitting under Chairman > Conference Member. Passive conference participant in Conference denotes someone who attends but does not actively participate (e.g., audience member), sitting under Conference participant with sibling Active conference participant. A chair is an active participant, not a passive one, so the two classes are disjoint rather than equivalent or overlapping.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel (same time slot), while the ekaw 'event On List' property relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (i.e., where the event is listed). They connect entirely different kinds of entities and express completely different relationships.

Property A (has_a_publisher) relates Conference proceedings to Publisher, indicating the publisher of proceedings. Property B (write) relates Person to Item, indicating authorship. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

A's 'Information for participants' is a broad conference document category covering general participant information (sibling to Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.), while B's 'Author information form' is a specific form for authors (sibling to Hotel registration form, Registration form). They serve different purposes at different granularity levels, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'has a submitted contribution' links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (i.e., the paper being reviewed). In confOf, 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (i.e., the paper authored). These are distinct relations with different domains and ranges, and they are not inverses of each other either.

confOf:Assistant denotes a person serving as an assistant in conference organization (a staff/support role), while ekaw:Student denotes a person who is a student (an academic status). These are different concepts: an assistant is not necessarily a student, and a student is not necessarily an assistant. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Individual Presentation in EKAW is a subclass of Scientific Event (an event/activity where a paper is presented), whereas Paper in SIGKDD is a subclass of Document (the written artefact submitted by an author). One denotes a presentation event, the other a document; they are disjoint kinds of entities.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to attend/register for a conference, while a 'PC Chair' is the chair of the Programme Committee. These are distinct roles: one is an applicant seeking participation, the other is a leadership role in the programme committee. They share the parent 'Person' but have no meaningful overlap in intended instances.

co-writePaper in cmt relates a Co-author to a Paper they co-authored, i.e. it expresses authorship of a paper. hasRelatedPaper in edas relates an Author to a Paper that is related (e.g., a related/follow-up paper), not necessarily one authored by that person. The domains (Co-author vs Author) and the intended semantics differ: authorship vs relatedness, so they are not equivalent.

Presenter city is a city where a presenter is located (subclass of City), while Conference hall is a physical venue/place where a conference is held (subclass of Place). One denotes a geographic location (city), the other a building/facility. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Rejection in cmt is a Decision (acceptance/rejection of a paper), while Renting in iasted is an Activity before conference (e.g., renting equipment or facilities). These are completely different domain concepts despite both being subclasses of a generic event/activity class.

In edas, 'Call For Reviews' is a Call (an invitation/request action) for reviewers to submit reviews, sibling to Call For Papers and Call For Manuscripts. In ekaw, 'Review' is a Document (the review artefact itself), with subtypes like Positive/Neutral/Negative Review. One is a request/event soliciting reviews; the other is the review document produced. They denote completely different things.

The two properties have different domains and ranges that do not align. Property A (has_a_date_of_issue) has domain Conference document and range date, indicating when a document was issued. Property B (is_dated_on) has domain Activity and range dateTime, indicating when an activity is dated. Since Conference document and Activity are distinct concepts (one is a document, the other is an event/activity), and the properties relate to different kinds of entities, they are not equivalent. They are also not in a subsumption relationship since neither domain subsumes the other in a way that would make one property more general than the other.

In the Conference ontology, Workshop is a top-level conference part (a scientific event focused on a theme), whereas in ekaw, Workshop Session is a specific session within a workshop (a time slot containing talks). The Conference Workshop corresponds more to the ekaw Workshop event itself, not to an individual session within it. Thus Workshop (Conference) is narrower/more specific than a generic session but is not equivalent to Workshop Session; rather, a Workshop Session is a part of a Workshop, making the Conference Workshop subsumed_by the broader ekaw Workshop concept, not equivalent to Workshop Session.

Property A (has_the_last_name) relates a Person to their surname (a string), while property B (hasVAT) relates a Social event or Working event to a value-added tax value (a string). They have disjoint domains (Person vs. events) and completely unrelated meanings, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise related.

Conference days in iasted represents the time period during which a conference takes place (a temporal entity with children like Delegate and One conference day). Deadline Abstract Submission in sigkdd represents a specific submission deadline date. These are fundamentally different concepts: one denotes conference event days, the other a deadline for abstract submission. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The property 'written By' in ekaw relates a Document to the Person who authored it, while 'is needed for' in iasted relates an Item to a Person who needs it. These are semantically distinct relations: authorship vs. requirement/need. They share the same range (Person) but their domains differ (Document vs. Item) and their intended meanings do not coincide.

In cmt, User is a broad superclass covering Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—any person who interacts with the conference management system. In sigkdd, Speaker is a specific role for a person who gives a presentation, with children Author and Invited Speaker. A Speaker is not a superclass of all system users (e.g., administrators or reviewers who do not present), nor is a User necessarily a Speaker. The two classes have different intended extensions with only partial overlap, and neither subsumes the other in a clear direction, so they are unrelated.

Time zone is a geographic/temporal region concept, while Deadline Author notification is a specific conference deadline for notifying authors of acceptance. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop, denoting academic/working events in a conference. iasted:Conference_building is a subclass of Building under Place, denoting a physical venue/building. These are completely different categories (event vs. physical place), with no overlap in intended instances.

The EKAW property 'technicallyOrganisedBy' (a subproperty of 'organisedBy') relates an event to the entity that technically organises it (e.g., an organisation or committee). The SIGKDD property 'awarded_by' relates an Award to the entity that grants the award. These are distinct relations: one concerns the technical organisation of events, the other concerns the conferral of an award. They do not share a common domain or range, and neither subsumes the other.

In ekaw, Document is a specific class whose instances are textual artefacts (Abstract, Paper, Review, Flyer, etc.). In iasted, Item is a broad superclass encompassing physical objects and documents (Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). Since iasted has Document as a child of Item, ekaw:Document is a specific kind of iasted:Item, making ekaw:Document subsumed_by iasted:Item.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In ekaw, 'paperPresentedAs' links a Paper to its Individual Presentation (the presentation slot/event). In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they give. One connects a document to a presentation event; the other connects a person to an activity/item. They do not share domain or range types, nor do they denote the same relation.

Property A links a Conference volume to its constituent Workshops (a part-whole relation). Property B links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). They have different domains, different ranges, and express entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, 'hardcopyMailingManifestsPrintedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who printed hardcopy mailing manifests. In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker who presented it. The domains (Conference vs Document), ranges (Administrator vs Speaker), and the underlying semantics (printing manifests vs presenting a paper) are completely different, so these properties are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different entities in the conference domain. In cmt, hasBid links a Paper to a Bid (a reviewer's bid to review a paper). In sigkdd, obtain links an Author to an Award. The domains (Paper vs Author), ranges (Bid vs Award), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

These properties relate entirely different entities. In ontology A, 'is the 1th part of' links an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (an abstract is a part of a paper). In ontology B, 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the document/presentation associated with a speaker). The domains (Abstract vs. Speaker), ranges (Paper/Poster/Presentation vs. Document), and the nature of the relationship (part-of vs. has/associated-with) are all different, so these properties are unrelated.

maxChoice is a datatype property from Social_event/Working_event to positiveInteger, while obtain is an object property from Person to Item. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings; they share no semantic overlap.

The ekaw Presenter is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant, with child Invited Speaker). The iasted Presenter_city is a city where a presenter is located (subclass of City, sibling of Conference_city, Sponsor_city, Trip_city). One denotes a person role, the other a geographic location; they share only the word 'Presenter' but denote completely different things.
Chair is a person who leads a committee, while Building is a physical place; they share no instances and occupy disjoint regions of the domain.

The property 'related To Paper' in edas links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (i.e., the paper being presented). The property 'write' in iasted links a Person to an Item (i.e., an author writing a document). These properties have completely different domains and ranges, and express different relationships (presentation-to-paper vs. author-to-document). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

EKAW Multi-author_Volume is a specific kind of document (a volume authored by multiple people, with Proceedings as a child). IASTED Publication is a broader category of published items that includes Book proceeding, Cd proceeding, and Document. While a Multi-author Volume is a type of publication, IASTED Publication is more general and also covers single-author works and other published formats, so Multi-author_Volume is subsumed by Publication.

The two properties relate different kinds of subjects to a Conference. In cmt, memberOfConference links a Conference Member (a person) to a Conference, indicating participation/membership. In sigkdd, hold links ACM SIGKDD (an organization/sponsor) to a Conference, indicating the organization hosts the conference. The domains differ (person vs. organization) and the intended relations differ (membership vs. hosting), so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' denotes the abstract component of a paper (a summary text), as indicated by its sibling 'Paper Full Version' — together they partition a paper into its abstract vs. full text. In ekaw, 'Conference Paper' denotes a paper presented at a conference (a whole document), with siblings like 'Regular Paper', 'Demo Paper', 'Poster Paper' classifying papers by presentation type. An abstract is a part of a paper, not a kind of conference paper; the two concepts do not share instances.

Associated Chair in cmt is a person role (a chairman assisting in conference organization), while Viza in iasted is a document type (a visa document under Item > Document). They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Author in edas is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person, domain of has Related Paper). Registration fee in iasted is a monetary amount charged for conference registration (subclass of Fee > Money). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'Working event' is a kind of academic/scientific event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) that is part of a conference programme, whereas edas's 'Radio Communications Topic' is a subject-area topic within a taxonomy of research topics. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Event vs. Topic) and denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a full paper document in cmt (Document > Paper > Paper Full Version), while Computer Networks Measurements Topic is a subject topic in edas (Topic > Computer Networks Topic). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

The two properties relate completely different domains and ranges. confOf:employedBy links a Person to the Organization that employs them, while iasted:is_paid_with links Money to an Item being purchased. They denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Co chair is a committee co-chair (a role within an organizing/program committee), while Session chair is a delegate who chairs a conference session. These are distinct roles: one is a committee-level position, the other is a session-level position held by a conference delegate. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Administrative event in confOf is a kind of conference event (e.g., registration, camera ready, reviewing), while Computer Networks Switching Topic in edas is a subject topic classification for papers. They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

An Excursion is a social event during a conference (e.g., a trip or outing), whereas a Departure is an activity occurring after the conference ends (e.g., leaving the venue). They represent different temporal phases and different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Venue Place in edas denotes the general location where a conference takes place (a venue), whereas Session room in iasted denotes a specific room where individual sessions are held. They are at different levels of granularity: a conference venue typically contains many session rooms. Although both are subclasses of Place, their intended instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

In EDAS, Paper is a full conference paper (with subclasses like Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper, authored, reviewed, etc.). In EKAW, Abstract is a short summary document (with subclasses Invited Talk Abstract, Tutorial Abstract) that is presented as an individual presentation. These are distinct document types in the conference domain: a full paper vs. an abstract of a talk/tutorial. They share the parent Document but denote different kinds of artefacts, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. In ekaw, authorOf links a Person to a Document they authored. In iasted, is_paid_with links Money to an Item it is used to pay for. They share no common domain or range types and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Both classes are subclasses of Organization and represent non-academic, commercial/corporate entities. confOf's Company and edas's Industry Organization occupy the same position under Organization, with Company being the natural confOf counterpart for an industry/commercial organization. Their intended instances (companies, firms, industry organizations) coincide in the conference domain.

Both classes denote the same concept of a conference event in the conference-organisation domain. confOf models Conference as a type of Working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop, while edas models it with subtypes like Single/Two Level Conference and properties such as dates, topics, and members. Despite structural differences, the intended instances coincide.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. `hasFirstName` relates a Person to a string (a person's first name), while `done_till` relates a Deadline to a date (the date by which a deadline is completed). They share no conceptual overlap.

In cmt, Conference is the main conference object with properties like date, logo URL, and members, while in confOf, Event is a broad superclass with children Administrative event, Social event, and Working event. A Conference is a specific kind of Event, so cmt:Conference is subsumed by confOf:Event.

The two properties relate entirely different domains and ranges. In ekaw, publisherOf connects an Organisation to the items it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). In sigkdd, obtain connects an Author to an Award they receive. There is no conceptual overlap between publishing artefacts and obtaining awards.

Both properties relate an event/activity to where it takes place, but they differ in direction and scope. 'location Of' in EKAW has domain Location and range Event (location -> event), while 'is held in' in IASTED has domain Activity and range Place/Time (activity -> place/time). They are inverses in direction and IASTED's property additionally covers time, so they are related but not equivalent.

In Conference ontology, 'Information for participants' is a subclass of Conference document—a document/artefact providing information to participants. In confOf, 'Conference' is a subclass of Working event—an actual event. One is a document, the other is an event; they share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

Call for paper is a document type (a conference announcement soliciting submissions), while Conference in confOf is an event type (a working event like a conference itself). One is a document artefact, the other is an event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Early paid applicant is a person who registered early and paid for conference attendance; Author is a person who writes and submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in their intended instances.

A's 'Passive conference participant' is any conference participant who is not active (e.g., audience members), with no restriction to students. B's 'Student non speaker' is specifically a student delegate who does not speak. The student restriction in B makes these non-overlapping rather than one subsuming the other, since A could include non-student passive participants and B is limited to students.

Property A denotes a person's first name, while property B denotes a person's fax number. They share the same domain (Person) and range (string), but they capture completely different attributes of a person. There is no semantic overlap that would justify equivalence, subsumption, or even a related relation.

Associated Chair is a person role (a kind of conference chairman) in the cmt ontology, while Conference Banquet is a social event in the ekaw ontology. They belong to completely different branches of their respective hierarchies (Person/Chairman vs Event/Social Event) and denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

The cmt property addProgramCommitteeMember relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (the act of adding someone to a committee). The ekaw property organises relates an Organisation or Person to an Event. They have different domains, different ranges, and denote completely different relations in the conference domain.

Refusing manuscript is an activity (rejecting a paper), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Both classes denote the same role in the conference domain: the chair of the Program Committee. In cmt, 'Program Committee Chair' is a specialization of Chairman and a sibling of Conference Chair, and it is the domain of the 'end Review' property, confirming its PC-chair role. In confOf, 'Chair PC' is a direct subclass of Person and a sibling of 'Member PC', which is the typical confOf modeling for the PC chair. The labels are synonymous ('Program Committee Chair' = 'Chair PC'), and the context (siblings, properties) supports that the intended instances coincide.

cmt:Review is a document artefact (a written review of a paper), whereas edas:PersonalReviewHistory is a history object aggregating a reviewer's past review activity. They denote different kinds of things: one is an individual review document, the other is a personal record/history of reviews. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Both properties relate a person/author to a document/contribution they author in the conference domain. 'contributes' (Person -> Conference document) and 'writes' (Author -> Contribution) denote the same authorship relation, with Conference document and Contribution being equivalent concepts in this domain.

These properties differ in both domain and range and direction. In cmt, readByMeta-Reviewer has domain Paper and range Meta Reviewer, meaning a paper is read by a meta-reviewer. In confOf, reviewes has domain Member PC and range Contribution, meaning a PC member reviews a contribution. The domains (Paper vs Member PC) and ranges (Meta Reviewer vs Contribution) are different concepts, and the property directions are reversed. A meta-reviewer reading a paper is a distinct relationship from a PC member reviewing a contribution.

TextualReviewQuestion in edas is a type of review question (a question posed to reviewers, with a textual answer), sibling to NumericalReviewQuestion. Final_manuscript in iasted is a submitted document (the final version of a manuscript), sibling to Initial_manuscript. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain: one is a review question, the other is a document artifact. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In cmt, Paper is a concrete document artefact (a submission with authors, reviews, bids, decisions, etc.). In iasted, Activity_before_conference is a temporal activity/event class whose instances are things like Accepting manuscript, Receiving manuscript, Refusing manuscript, Renting, Research. These are disjoint kinds of entities: a document vs. an activity, with no overlap in intended instances.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference part' denotes structural subdivisions of a conference such as Track, Tutorial, and Workshop. In the EDAS ontology, 'Conference Session' is a temporal event-like entity (a session where papers are presented), not a structural subdivision. The two concepts do not have coinciding intended instances: a workshop or tutorial is not a session, and a conference session is not a conference part in the structural sense. They are therefore unrelated rather than equivalent or subsumed.

A is a document/information artefact for participants (child of Conference document), while B is a social event/activity (child of Conference activity). They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

confOf 'Submission event' is an administrative event representing the act/process of submitting contributions, while sigkdd 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a specific deadline temporal point for paper submission. They overlap in topic (paper submission) but denote different things: one is an event/activity, the other is a deadline. They are related but not equivalent.

These properties are completely different. `siteURL` is a datatype property from Conference to anyURI, representing the website of a conference. `obtain` is an object property from Person to Item, representing a person obtaining an item. They have different domains, ranges, and meanings.

In edas, 'Computer Networks Topic' is a subject-area topic under Topic, used to classify papers (e.g., networks, security, sensors). In iasted, 'Computer' is a physical piece of audiovisual equipment under Item > Audiovisual equipment, alongside LCD projector and Overhead projector. They denote completely different kinds of entities—a conceptual topic vs. a physical device—so they are unrelated.

Committee_member in Conference is a generic class for any member of a committee (with children Chair and Co_chair, and linked to Committee via has_members/was_a_member_of). ConferenceChair in edas is a specific role: the chair of a conference, who can initiate calls, review papers, etc. A Conference Chair is a specific kind of committee member (at best a subclass), not equivalent. Moreover, edas has a separate TPC Member sibling, suggesting ConferenceChair is not the same as the generic Committee member. The two classes do not have coinciding intended instances.

paperID is a numeric identifier for a Paper; has_an_ISBN is a string-valued ISBN identifier for Conference proceedings. They have different domains, different ranges, and denote different real-world identifiers.

In ekaw, Presenter is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant, with child Invited Speaker). In iasted, Delegate is a much broader category covering all conference attendees (including Listener, Non speaker, Sponsor, etc.), and it is oddly placed under Conference building. The iasted Delegate subsumes the ekaw Presenter concept, since every Presenter is a Delegate but not vice versa. They are not equivalent.

Conference proceedings in ontology A is a published document (with ISBN, volume, publisher), while Conference in ontology B is an event (with start/end dates, city). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In ekaw, Regular Session is a specific kind of session (a sibling of Demo Session, Poster Session, Workshop Session, etc.), i.e. a non-special, regular parallel session. In iasted, Session is a general class (under Activity > Conference activity > Lecture) that subsumes various session types including Speaker lecture. Thus iasted:Session is more general than ekaw:Regular Session; the ekaw class is subsumed by the iasted class, not equivalent.

Both properties link a paper-like entity to a review-related entity, but they differ in meaning: A's range is 'Review preference' (a preference for who should review), while B's range is 'Review' (the actual review document). They are related but not equivalent.
University is an organization where scholars study, while Departure tax is a type of tax/monetary amount. These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Person is a top-level class subsuming all human roles (Chairman, Conference Member, Reviewer, PC Member, User). In sigkdd, Speaker is a subclass of Person specifically denoting someone who gives a presentation. These are not the same concept: Person is far more general than Speaker. They are not in a direct subsumption relationship across ontologies (cmt's Person is a root, sigkdd's Speaker is a specialized role), and their instance sets do not coincide, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent.

Subject Area in cmt denotes a research topic or category used to classify papers (domain of hasSubjectArea is Paper). City in confOf denotes a geographical location where organizations or persons reside (domain of hasCity is Organization/Person). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
City is a geographic location where organizations and persons are located, while Time zone is a temporal region for time reckoning. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Property A (contributes) relates a Person to a Conference document (a paper, abstract, etc.), indicating authorship or contribution to a document. Property B (isMemberOf) relates a Person to a Conference, indicating organizational membership. They connect Person to completely different ranges (document vs. conference event) and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

The property 'write Review' in cmt relates a Reviewer to a Review (writing a review of a paper), while 'presentation' in sigkdd relates a Speaker to a Document (presenting a document). These are fundamentally different relations in the conference domain: one is about reviewing a submission, the other about presenting at the conference. Their domains (Reviewer vs Speaker) and ranges (Review vs Document) are also distinct concepts.

hasCity relates an Organization or Person to a City (a location), while organises relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (an activity they organize). Despite sharing the same domain, the ranges differ entirely (City vs Event), so these properties denote completely different relations.

Property A relates a Co-chair to a Committee they co-chaired, while property B relates a Contribution to the Author who wrote it. These are completely different relations in the conference domain with disjoint domains and ranges.

Both Reception and Conference Banquet are social events at a conference, but they are distinct subtypes: a banquet is a formal dinner, while a reception is a more general welcome/gathering event. They overlap (a banquet may include a reception) but are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Submitted contribution is a specific subclass of Written contribution in the Conference ontology, representing works that have been submitted for review. Paper in sigkdd is a broader document type (sibling of Abstract and Review). While every submitted contribution could be considered a Paper, Paper also encompasses other forms and is not restricted to submitted works, so Submitted contribution is subsumed by Paper rather than equivalent.

Both are subclasses of Deadline, but they denote completely different deadlines: one is for hotel reservations (accommodation logistics) and the other is for paper submission (academic process). Their sibling sets confirm distinct deadline categories, and there is no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a person who is a member of a conference (parent: Person; children include Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair, etc.). Travel Grant in edas is a type of sponsorship (parent: Sponsorship). One denotes a person, the other a financial grant; they share no semantic overlap.

The cmt property 'memberOfProgramCommittee' links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (expressing committee membership).
