The confOf property 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (expressing that the member reviews a paper). These are fundamentally different relations: one denotes organizational membership in a committee, the other denotes a reviewing activity on a specific contribution. They share no common relational semantics despite both having a PC member as domain.

Accommodation Place in edas denotes lodging (hotels, dorms, etc.) for conference attendees, as indicated by its siblings (Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) and the word 'accommodation'. Conference hall in sigkdd denotes a physical room/hall where conference sessions take place, not lodging. They share the parent Place but refer to disjoint categories of places; an accommodation place is not a conference hall and vice versa.

In cmt, Paper is a document submitted to a conference, with authors, reviews, decisions, etc. In edas, Topic is a subject area (e.g., Antennas, CAD, Cryptography) that papers and conferences can be associated with. These are completely different concepts: one is a document/artifact, the other is a subject classification. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Rejected Paper is a document (a paper that was not accepted), while Submissions deadline is a temporal event (the deadline for submitting papers). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies (Document vs. Time) and share no semantic overlap.

Extended abstract is a specific contribution type based on document nature (a short summary/abstract), while Active Paper is a workflow/review-status state of a paper. They classify papers along orthogonal dimensions and their instances do not coincide.

Dining Place is a venue/location where meals are served (a subtype of Place), while Car is a means of transport (a subtype of Transport vehicle). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

`has a name` is a datatype property whose domain includes Publisher and whose range is string, i.e. it assigns a textual name to an entity. `publisher Of` is an object property from Organisation to various publication artefacts (Flyer, Multi author Volume, etc.), i.e. it relates an organisation to the things it publishes. They have different domains, different ranges (string vs. publication artefacts), and different semantics; neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome). In iasted, is_present links a Person to a Time (indicating when someone is present). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different, so they are not equivalent, subsumed, or otherwise related.

Conference volume in the Conference ontology is a broader concept: it represents a particular edition/volume of a conference series and aggregates many parts (tracks, contributions, committees, important dates, location). The sigkdd Conference class is a concrete conference event with start/end dates, name, and city. A sigkdd Conference is an instance of a Conference volume, but Conference volume also subsumes other conference editions, so the relation is subsumes (A more general than B).

In cmt, 'Program Committee' denotes the committee of reviewers that evaluates paper submissions, as evidenced by its properties linking it to Program Committee Members. In iasted, 'Social program' is a subclass of Conference activity whose children include Dinner banquet, and whose siblings include Cocktail reception and Coffee break; it denotes the social events organized at a conference. These are completely different concepts despite both being conference-related.

Both properties relate a Person to a written document (Conference document / Item) in the conference domain. 'contributes' and 'write' both describe the authorship relation where a person produces a paper or document. The domain (Person) and range (Conference document / Item) align closely, and in the conference-organisation context these denote the same authorship relation.

Both classes denote the same conference-domain concept: a welcome talk/address given at the start of a conference. 'Welcome Talk' in edas (path: Conference Event > Academic Event > Talk Event > Welcome Talk) and 'Welcome address' in iasted (path: Activity > Conference activity > Welcome address) are clearly synonyms referring to the same event type, despite differences in the surrounding taxonomy.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person). In ekaw, Conference Trip is a social event (subclass of Event). One denotes a human role, the other an activity/excursion; they share only the word 'Conference' and have no semantic overlap.

In EKAW, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. In IASTED, Worker non speaker is a subclass of Non speaker under the Delegate branch, denoting a delegate who is a worker and does not give a presentation. These are disjoint concepts: a student is not necessarily a worker or a delegate, and a worker non speaker is not necessarily a student. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference volume in the Conference ontology denotes a concrete conference event/publication with committees, contributions, tracks, and important dates. Conference state in iasted is a subclass of State (alongside Presenter state and Sponsor state), representing a state or status value, not a conference event or volume. These are completely different concepts despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

In edas, 'Rejected Paper' is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper whose submission was rejected), while in sigkdd 'Paper' is the general class of all papers. The sigkdd Paper class is strictly more general, so edas:RejectedPaper is subsumed_by sigkdd:Paper.

Reception in edas is a social event (a non-academic conference event like a banquet or gathering), while Invited_Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives an invited talk. One is an event, the other is a person; they share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

A Conference Session is a scheduled event/session within a conference (e.g., a talk or panel session), whereas an Abstract in EKAW is a type of document (child of Document, sibling of Paper, Review, Flyer, etc.) representing the abstract text of a presentation. These denote completely different categories of entities—an event vs. a document—so they are unrelated.

A Published Paper in edas is a specific kind of academic paper that has been published, sitting under Paper > Document. A Record of attendance in iasted is an administrative document certifying someone attended an event, sitting under Document alongside forms, invitation letters, and payment documents. These are completely different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: 'has an email' captures a person's electronic mail address, while 'has Surname' captures a person's family name. They do not relate the same kind of information and are therefore unrelated.

Conference in edas denotes the academic event itself (with properties like dates, country, topics, paper deadlines), while Committee in sigkdd denotes a group of people organizing or reviewing for a conference (with children like Organizing Committee, Program Committee). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference denoting an event type (a conference with a single organizational level, sibling to 'Two Level Conference'). In sigkdd, 'Conference hall' is a subclass of Place denoting a physical location (sibling to Hotel and Main office). One is an event, the other is a physical venue; they share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different concepts.

confOf:Administrator is an administrative role (a kind of Person who manages the conference tool), while iasted:Reviewer is a scientific role (a Delegate > Speaker who reviews papers). They occupy very different positions in their respective hierarchies and denote distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while Event in ekaw is a conference-related occurrence (scientific or social). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In ekaw, Review is a document written by a reviewer about a Paper, with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review and properties reviewOfPaper and reviewWrittenBy. In sigkdd, Abstract is a sibling of Review under Document, representing a summary document. These are distinct concepts: a Review is an evaluation document, while an Abstract is a summary document. They share the parent Document but denote different things.

confOf:Contribution (with children Paper, Poster, Short paper) denotes the intellectual work submitted to a conference, while iasted:Submission (a subclass of Document, with children Final manuscript and Initial manuscript) denotes the concrete document artefact handed in at a particular stage. The two are closely related but not equivalent: a Contribution is the abstract content that a Submission (document) instantiates, so Contribution is subsumed_by Submission only in a loose sense; in the reference alignment they are best treated as Contribution being the more specific concept relative to the document-oriented Submission hierarchy.

`has title` relates events to their title (a string), while `start Date` relates a conference to its start date and time (a dateTime). They denote completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and model different aspects of the conference domain. In cmt, 'has Been Assigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. In Conference, 'has a topic or a submission contribution' links a Review preference to either a Submitted contribution or a Topic, indicating what the preference is about. They relate different kinds of entities and express different relationships.

These properties are completely different. 'is a starting date' is a datatype property mapping an Important dates instance to a date value, while 'held In' is an object property mapping an Event to a Location. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

Property `hasAuthor` in cmt relates a Paper to its Author (domain: Paper, range: Author). Property `paperInVolume` in ekaw relates a paper to the volume/proceedings in which it appears. These are entirely different relations: one connects a paper to a person who wrote it, the other connects a paper to a publication venue containing it. No subsumption or overlap exists between them.

A Neutral Review is a specific kind of review (a sentiment/value judgment of a paper), while an Abstract is a summary component of a document. They occupy different positions in the document hierarchy and denote unrelated concepts.

A Meta Review is a specific type of review document written by a meta-reviewer summarizing the paper's reviews. B Numerical Review Question is a type of review question (e.g., a rating scale item) used within a review form. They are completely different concepts: one is a document/artefact, the other is a question element of a review form. No subsumption or overlap in intended instances.

Paper Full Version is a conference document (a full paper submission), while Trip day is a temporal entity (a day during a trip). They share no instances and belong to completely unrelated parts of the domain.

In cmt, 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person). In edas, 'Conference' is the event itself (with subclasses like Single Level Conference, properties like has Country, paper Due On, etc.). These are completely different concepts: a person role vs. the conference event.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person representing people who are members of a conference (authors, chairs, reviewers, etc.). In ekaw, Conference Session is a subclass of Session under Event, representing a scheduled session/event at a conference. One is about people/persons, the other is about events/sessions. There is no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. confOf:parallel_with relates Administrative events to other Administrative events (indicating events running in parallel), while edas:relatesTo relates Documents to Academic Events, Conferences, Conference Sessions, or Persons. They connect different types of entities and serve different purposes, so they are unrelated.

Rejection in cmt is a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome of a paper), while WeekRejectRating in edas is a Review Rating (a rating value assigned by a reviewer). These are different kinds of entities: one is a final decision on a paper, the other is a rating score used during the review process. They share the word 'reject' but denote different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'contributes' in the Conference ontology relates a Person to a Conference document (a paper or similar contribution), whereas 'occupy' in the iasted ontology relates a Person to a Building, City, or State (a physical location). These properties connect completely different kinds of objects and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.
Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while MedicineTopic is a subject-area topic under Topic. They share no domain overlap.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a type of Chairman/Person), while Invited Talk is a type of event/presentation. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

minChoice is a datatype property from Social/Working event to positiveInteger, while organisedBy is an object property from Event to Organisation/Person. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Conference Dinner in edas is a social event (a meal event) that occurs during a conference, whereas Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place/location where conference activities happen. One is an event, the other is a venue; they denote completely different kinds of entities.

The two properties relate completely different entities. 'has_a_review' links a Reviewed contribution to a Review (a paper being reviewed points to its review), while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (a person authoring a paper). They have different domains and ranges and express different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'has Been Assigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper (paper assignment for review). In sigkdd, 'payed by' links a Registration fee to a Person (who paid the fee). They share no common domain or range types and denote entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes or submits a paper (subclass of Person/Conference Member). In iasted, Activity is an event or occurrence (e.g., conference activity, activity before/after conference) with temporal and spatial properties. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

`reject Paper` in cmt relates an Administrator to a Paper that is being rejected, whereas `writes` in confOf relates an Author to a Contribution they authored. The domains (Administrator vs Author), ranges (Paper vs Contribution), and intended meanings (rejection decision vs authorship) are completely different, so the two properties are unrelated.

Reception is a social event (e.g., welcome reception) held during a conference, while Departure is an activity after the conference (e.g., leaving/departing). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Conference Trip in EKAW is a subclass of Social Event, denoting an organised excursion or outing associated with a conference. Conference airport in IASTED is a subclass of Building under Place, denoting the physical airport used for travel to a conference. One is an event/activity, the other is a physical location; they share the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different categories of things.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference announcement inviting people to participate in an event, while 'Viza' (Visa) is an official travel document. They share no semantic overlap despite both being subclasses of document-like entities.

Paid applicant in Conference is a specific subclass of registered applicant who has paid registration fees. Conference Participant in ekaw is a broader category encompassing all kinds of conference participants including organizers, chairs, presenters, and registered participants. While a paid applicant is certainly a conference participant, the reverse is not true: many ekaw Conference_Participant subclasses (e.g., PC Chair, Session Chair, Demo Chair) are not necessarily registered/paid applicants. Thus Paid_applicant is strictly more specific than Conference_Participant.

The two properties relate completely different entities. 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a record of reviews they have authored), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Reviewer vs Document) and ranges (Personal Review History vs Speaker) are disjoint, and the relations describe unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

In the iasted ontology, Fee is a monetary amount (subclass of Money) with concrete subtypes like registration fee and hotel fee. In sigkdd, Silver Supporter is a sponsor category/role (subclass of Sponzor) alongside Gold, Bronze, etc. These denote completely different things: a monetary charge vs. a sponsorship tier. No overlap in intended instances.

The property 'has a degree' in the Conference ontology relates a Review preference to an integer (likely indicating the degree or strength of a reviewer's preference), while 'Nation' in the sigkdd ontology relates a Person to a string (representing their nationality). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) denoting a kind of conference event, whereas edas:CADTopic is a subclass of Topic denoting a specific subject area (CAD). They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote completely different concepts.

In cmt, Paper is a conference paper submitted for review, with authors, reviewers, bids, decisions, and subject areas. In iasted, Viza is a type of administrative document (a visa) under Item > Document, sibling to forms, invitation letters, payment documents, etc. These denote completely different things in the conference domain: a submitted paper vs. a visa document. They share only the word 'document' as an ancestor, which is insufficient for equivalence or even a meaningful relation.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables a virtual meeting). In sigkdd, 'hold' relates an ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference (that it holds). They connect different entity types in different directions and express unrelated relationships.

confOf:Regular is a subclass of Participant (a person who is a regular, non-student, non-member participant at a conference). edas:TwoLevelConference is a subclass of Conference (an event with two levels, e.g., main conference plus workshops). One denotes a type of person, the other a type of conference event; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Conference participant is a broad superclass for all people who participate in a conference (including active and passive participants), while Conference Chair is a specific role. A Conference Chair could be considered a participant, but the two classes are not equivalent; one is much more general than the other. Given the specific role-based properties of Conference Chair in edas and the broad categorization in Conference, they are not equivalent, and the relationship is best characterized as unrelated at the alignment level since Conference participant does not subsume the specific role in the other ontology's structure.

An Excursion in edas is a social event (a non-academic activity such as a trip or outing), whereas an Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives an invited talk. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies (events vs. persons) and share no instances.

The property 'written By' in ekaw relates a Document to the Person who wrote it, while 'design' in sigkdd relates an ACM SIGKDD conference to a Deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a subclass of Chairman (a Person role), representing an individual who co-chairs the conference. In sigkdd, 'Organizing Committee' is a subclass of Committee (a group/committee entity), representing the organizing body. One is a person role, the other is a committee group; they are structurally and semantically different types of entities.

Meal Event in edas is a general class covering any meal-based non-academic event (with a child Conference Dinner), while Dinner banquet in iasted is a specific kind of social-program activity. A dinner banquet is a meal event, but not every meal event is a dinner banquet, so Meal Event is subsumed_by Dinner banquet is incorrect; rather Dinner banquet is subsumed_by Meal Event. The correct relation is that the iasted Dinner banquet is subsumed_by the edas Meal Event, meaning from A's perspective A subsumes B.

Entity A is a class denoting a document (a camera-ready paper), while entity B is a class denoting a temporal concept (a deadline for submitting such papers). They belong to disjoint branches (Document vs. Time) and do not share instances.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing a short version or abstract of a conference paper. Computer Architecture Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area within computer architecture. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Active_conference_participant is a person (subclass of Person > Conference contributor) who actively participates in a conference, e.g., gives presentations. Individual_Presentation is an event (subclass of Event > Scientific Event) such as a contributed talk or invited talk. One denotes a person, the other denotes an event; they are disjoint kinds of things.

In ekaw, Conference Trip is a Social Event (a trip organized as part of a conference). In iasted, Conference days is a subclass of Time, representing the temporal span of the conference. One denotes an event/activity, the other a time period; they are disjoint categories despite superficial label similarity.

Organization in the Conference ontology denotes an organizational entity (e.g., a university, company, or institution), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd denotes a person who serves on the organizing committee. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an institution/organization, the other is an individual person. They share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference document in ontology Conference is a document class (with children like Call for paper, Review, Conference contribution, etc. and properties like has authors, has a date of issue). Event in confOf is a temporal occurrence class (with children like Administrative event, Social event, Working event and properties like starts on, ends on). These are fundamentally different concepts: one represents documents associated with a conference, the other represents events/activities that happen at a conference. There is no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Session chair is a specific Delegate role (a person chairing a session), a leaf class with no children. In sigkdd, Organizator is a broad superclass subsuming General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc. The two concepts do not overlap: a session chair is not necessarily an organizer, and an organizer is not necessarily a session chair. They denote different roles in the conference domain.

Conference Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion or outing) in the ekaw ontology, while Main office is a physical place (a building or office location) in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective hierarchies (Event vs. Place) and denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper they submit, while studyAt relates a Scholar to a University they study at. These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no overlap in meaning.

confOf:Conference is a top-level event (the conference itself), sibling to Workshop and Tutorial. iasted:Introduction is a conference activity (like a welcome address or coffee break), with a child 'Introduction of speaker'. These denote completely different things: one is the conference event, the other is a social/activity program item within a conference.

The cmt 'assignedTo' property assigns a Reviewer to a Paper (domain: Paper, range: Reviewer), representing the reviewer-assignment relation in a paper-review system. The iasted 'sign' property has domain Person and range Item, indicating that a person signs an item (e.g., a document or registration). These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event under Event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas edas:CADTopic is a subject-area topic (a Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, Communication Theory Topic, etc.). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain—an event versus a research topic—so they are unrelated.

OC Member in ekaw is a person who is a member of the Organizing Committee (subclass of Conference Participant, with child OC Chair). Registration in iasted is an activity (subclass of Conference activity, with child Delegate). One denotes a person/role, the other an activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Regular contribution in Conference is a written document (subclass of Conference contribution, with children Extended abstract and Paper), whereas Regular Session in ekaw is a temporal event (subclass of Session under Scientific Event). They denote completely different categories of entities—a publication artefact versus a scheduled session—so they are unrelated.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, Author is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person, with properties linking to Paper). In iasted, Memeber registration fee is a monetary fee (subclass of Registration fee > Fee > Money) for member registration. There is no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. In Conference, 'was a committe co chair of' connects a Co chair (a person role) to a Committee. In sigkdd, 'hold' connects the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference. The domains (Co chair vs. ACM SIGKDD) and ranges (Committee vs. Conference) are different, and the relations denote different real-world relationships (chairing a committee vs. an organization hosting a conference). They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only weakly related at best.

These properties are completely different. `hasStartDateTime` is a datatype property from Conference Event to a dateTime, recording when an event starts. `listsEvent` is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event, indicating that a document or website lists events. They have different domains, different range types (datatype vs object), and express unrelated relationships.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. In Conference, 'reviews' goes from Review to Reviewed contribution (the review points to the paper it reviews). In edas, 'isReviewedBy' goes from Paper to reviewer roles (the paper points to its reviewers). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent, and since inverse relations are explicitly not considered equivalent, they are classified as unrelated.

The cmt 'paper ID' is a datatype property mapping a Paper to an unsignedLong identifier, while the ekaw 'presentation Of Paper' is an object property linking an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract. They operate in completely different directions and relate different kinds of entities; one assigns an ID number, the other associates a presentation with the paper being presented.

In cmt, Chairman is a general superclass with three subclasses: Associated Chair, Conference Chair, and Program Committee Chair. In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a specific role under Organizator. The sigkdd class corresponds to the cmt subclass Program Committee Member/Chair, not to the general Chairman superclass. Therefore Chairman (cmt) is strictly more general than Program Committee member (sigkdd).

cmt:User is a broad superclass covering Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—any person who interacts with the CMT system. sigkdd:Organizing_Committee_member is a specific role under Organizator, alongside General Chair, Program Chair, etc. The two classes do not share instances: an Organizing Committee member is not a generic 'user' in the CMT sense, and a CMT User is not necessarily an organizing committee member. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

Hotel fee is a fee for accommodation at a hotel, while Sponzor fee is a fee paid by a sponsor. These are distinct types of fees covering different things (lodging vs. sponsorship), so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

cmt:email is a datatype property from Person to string (an email address), while iasted:obtain is an object property from Person to Item (a person obtaining an item). They have different ranges, different property types, and different semantics; they do not denote the same relation.

Withdrawn Paper is a document (a paper that has been withdrawn from submission), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They share no instances and belong to unrelated ontology branches (documents vs. deadlines).

Both classes denote the same conference-domain concept: a Tutorial event. In Conference, Tutorial is a Conference part (sibling of Workshop, Track) and is the range of 'has tutorials'. In confOf, Tutorial is a Working event (sibling of Workshop, Conference). Both ontologies model it as a session/event that occurs as part of a conference, and the identical label with consistent sibling structure (especially Workshop) strongly supports equivalence.

confOf:Member_PC is a subclass of Person denoting a PC member/reviewer, with properties like reviewing contributions. edas:PersonalPublicationHistory is a subclass of Personal History tracking a person's publication record. They denote completely different kinds of entities (a person vs. a history object) and share no meaningful semantic relationship.

In the edas ontology, 'Conference' denotes the conference event/organization itself, with properties like dates, topics, members, and papers. In the iasted ontology, 'Conference airport' is a physical building (a place where conference attendees travel through), a subclass of Building. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

AccpetIfRoomRating is a subclass of Review Rating (a rating value for paper reviews, sibling to Accept/Reject ratings) in the edas ontology. Abstract is a subclass of Document (a conference document type, sibling to Paper and Review) in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different domain concepts: one is a review rating value, the other is a document type. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Co chair is a generic committee co-chair role (sibling of Chair, under Committee member), while Demo Chair is a specific conference role responsible for demonstrations (sibling of PC Chair, Tutorial Chair, etc., under Conference Participant). A Demo Chair is not a generic co-chair, and a generic co-chair is not necessarily a Demo Chair. They are different roles with different scopes and no overlap in intended instances.

Camera ready contribution is a document (the final version of an accepted paper), while Submissions deadline is a temporal entity (a deadline date). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote entirely different kinds of things.

These properties have different domains and different intended meanings. 'is a starting date' in the Conference ontology has domain 'Important dates' and represents the starting date of an important deadline period. 'startDate' in edas has domain 'Conference' and represents the conference start date and time. They relate to different kinds of entities (deadline periods vs. the conference event itself), so they are not equivalent.

startDate in edas denotes the start date/time of a Conference, whereas done_till in iasted denotes a deadline date. They have different domains (Conference vs Deadline) and different ranges (dateTime vs date), and they represent conceptually distinct temporal notions: an event start time versus a submission/completion deadline.

Conference applicant (Person > Conference applicant) denotes a person who applies to attend/register for a conference. Two Level Conference (Conference > Two Level Conference) denotes a type of conference event (one with two review levels). They are in entirely different branches of their ontologies and refer to different categories of things (person vs. event), so they are unrelated.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates one Administrative event to another (temporal/sequential ordering), while 'has Menu' in edas relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (part-whole relation between an event and its menu). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings.

Both concern negative review outcomes, but they are different kinds of entities: WeekRejectRating is a rating value within a rating taxonomy (siblings include Accept Rating, Reject Rating), while Negative_Review is a document type (subclass of Review with siblings Neutral Review, Positive Review). They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

The property 'hasMember' in edas relates a Conference to a Person (i.e., a person who is a member/participant of the conference), while 'writtenBy' in ekaw relates a Document to a Person (i.e., the author of a document). These are entirely different relations with different domain and range types, so they are unrelated.

Conference in ontology A denotes the academic event (with a name, proceedings, parts, etc.), while Conference building in ontology iasted denotes a physical place (under Place > Building) where a conference is held. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference proceedings is a published document (with ISBN, volume, publisher), while Activity is a temporal event/action (held in places, dated, given by people). These are fundamentally different categories with no overlap in instances.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person, representing a person who is a member of a conference (with subclasses like Author, Reviewer, Chair). In iasted, Conference building is a subclass of Building under Place, representing a physical location where a conference takes place. One denotes a person/role, the other a physical structure; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Administrator in cmt is a person who manages the conference system (subclass of Person > User), while Review in the Conference ontology is a document (subclass of Conference document). They denote completely different things: a human role vs. a review artefact.

Non Academic Event in edas denotes social/break/meal events occurring during a conference (e.g., banquets, coffee breaks). Activity before conference in iasted denotes preparatory administrative activities such as accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts, renting, and research. These are completely different kinds of things: one is a social gathering event, the other is a pre-conference organizational activity. No overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, 'Conference www' is a subclass of 'Conference document' and represents a web page (URL) about a conference, alongside siblings like Call for paper, Review, etc. In ontology B, 'Conference' is the main event class with properties like dates, country, members, and topics, and children like Single Level Conference. One is a web document/resource, the other is the actual academic event. They denote completely different concepts.

The two properties denote completely different attributes: 'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'has Email' captures an electronic mail address. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they relate to semantically unrelated facets of a person. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Committee member denotes a person serving on a committee (with subtypes Chair, Co-chair), while Speaker denotes a person who gives a presentation (with subtypes Author, Invited Speaker). Their intended instances do not coincide: a committee member need not speak, and a speaker need not be on a committee. They are sibling subclasses of Person but otherwise unrelated.
Paper Abstract in cmt is a document type (a short version of a paper), while CAD Topic in edas is a subject-area topic for classifying papers. They share no instances and no semantic relationship.

Conference Venue Place in edas denotes a place where a conference is held (a venue), while Main office in iasted denotes the administrative office of an organization. They share the parent Place but have different intended instances and no overlap in the conference domain.

Conference Banquet is a social event that occurs during a conference, whereas Hotel is a physical place where people might stay. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Administrative event in confOf is a temporal organizational event (submission, reviewing, registration, etc.), while Computer Networks Topic in edas is a subject-area classification for papers. They share no instances and belong to disjoint parts of the conference domain.

A's Paper is a document (the written contribution submitted to a conference), while B's Camera ready manuscript deadline is a temporal deadline by which the final version must be submitted. They denote completely different kinds of entities (document vs. time point), so they are unrelated.

The two properties operate in completely different domains and directions. 'detailsEnteredBy' in cmt relates a Conference to an Administrator (who entered conference details), while 'parallel_with' in confOf relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (co-occurring parallel events). They share no common domain, range, or semantic relationship.

The edas 'has Menu' property relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (food menu at a meal), while the sigkdd 'presentation' property relates a Speaker to a Document (the document being presented). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain: one is about catering/meals, the other about a speaker's presentation document. No subsumption or overlap exists.

In EDAS, Reviewer is a concrete role for someone who actually reviews a paper (domain of is Reviewing, range of is Reviewed By). In EKAW, Possible Reviewer is a more general class denoting anyone who could potentially review a paper, and it has PC Member as a subclass. Every actual Reviewer is a Possible Reviewer, but not vice versa, so Reviewer is subsumed by Possible Reviewer.

The property 'invited by' in the Conference ontology relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the one who invited them to review), while 'write' in the iasted ontology relates a Person to an Item (a document/artefact they authored). These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and express fundamentally different relationships: one is about invitation between reviewers, the other is about authorship of items. They are unrelated.

Active_conference_participant in the Conference ontology is a specialized subclass of Conference_participant that specifically gives presentations, making it narrower than confOf's Participant, which is a general conference attendee with subclasses like Member, Student, and Regular. The Conference ontology distinguishes Active from Passive participants, so Active_conference_participant denotes only the active subset of all participants.

These properties are completely different. `hasLastName` is a datatype property from Person to string, representing a person's surname. `obtain` is an object property from Person to Item, representing a person obtaining some item. They share the same domain (Person) but differ in range type (string vs Item) and denote entirely different relations.

The confOf 'writes' property relates an Author to a Contribution (an author writes a paper). The sigkdd 'search' property relates an ACM SIGKDD entity to a Sponzor (sponsor). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no indication they denote the same concept.

Regular Paper in EKAW is a specific type of academic paper (a full-length contribution submitted to a conference), whereas Document in IASTED is a broad administrative category encompassing forms, invitation letters, payment documents, records of attendance, reviews, submissions, etc. The two classes do not share instances: a Regular Paper is not an administrative document, and the IASTED Document children are not papers. They are at different levels of granularity and in different conceptual spaces, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or subsumed.

In cmt, 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a member of a conference (with children like Author, Reviewer, etc.). In ekaw, 'Conference' is a subclass of Scientific Event, denoting one edition of a conference event itself. These are completely different concepts: one is a person/role, the other is an event. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both properties relate a person to a document in a conference context, but they are not equivalent. 'submit Paper' specifically denotes the act of an Author submitting a Paper, while 'contributes' is broader, relating a Person to any Conference document (which could include reviews, proceedings, etc.). The domain (Author vs Person) and range (Paper vs Conference document) differ in generality, indicating an overlap but not identity.

In ekaw, Research Institute is an organization (a kind of academic institution, sibling of University). In iasted, Research is an activity performed before a conference (sibling of Accepting manuscript, Renting, etc., with children Modelling and Simulating). One is an institutional entity, the other is a research activity; they share only the word 'research' and denote completely different concepts.

Both classes are subclasses of Person and represent authors who write papers/contributions in the conference domain. The confOf Author writes Contribution, while the edas Author has Related Paper (and is the inverse of is Written By). Both denote the same concept: a person who authors a paper submitted to a conference.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, 'memberOfConference' links a Conference Member to a Conference, indicating membership of a person in a conference. In the Conference ontology, 'has_a_steering_committee' links a Conference volume to a Steering committee, indicating that a conference volume has a steering committee as a sub-part. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so the properties are unrelated.

Meal Menu (under Document) is a menu listing for a meal event, while Tip (under Money) is a monetary gratuity. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and domains with no overlap in intended instances.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is the chair/leader of the PC, a specialized role above PC members. Member PC (confOf) is a regular PC member/reviewer. The chair role and a regular member role are distinct: a chair oversees the review process while a member just reviews papers. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since confOf has a separate 'Chair PC' class for the chair role.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a specific document type representing the abstract portion of a paper, sibling to 'Paper Full Version'. In ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' denotes a paper that has been submitted to a conference (a status/stage in the workflow), with subtypes like 'Assigned Paper'. These are different concepts: one is a document component (abstract vs. full version), the other is a submission status category. Their instances do not coincide—a submitted paper typically contains both an abstract and a full version, and an abstract alone is not a submitted paper.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and express different relations. In EDAS, hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of activities). In EKAW, technicallyOrganises is a sub-property of organises, with domain Organisation, expressing that an organisation technically organises something. The domains (Conference Event vs Organisation) and the intended semantics (possessing a programme vs organising) do not coincide, so the properties are unrelated.

confOf Short_paper is a specific subtype of Contribution (a short paper), whereas edas Paper is the general class for all papers (with subtypes like Accepted, Rejected, etc.). Short_paper instances would be a subset of Paper instances, so Short_paper is subsumed_by Paper.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event representing academic/professional gatherings (conferences, tutorials, workshops). sigkdd:Organizator is a subclass of Person representing people who organize events (chairs, committee members, webmaster). One is an event, the other is a person role; they denote completely different categories of entities.

Member PC in confOf is a Program Committee member (reviewer), with properties like reviewes (Contribution) and expert On (Topic). OC Member in ekaw is an Organizing Committee member, a distinct role from PC member. The two committees handle different conference responsibilities: the PC handles paper review and scientific program, while the OC handles logistics and organization. Their instances do not coincide.

Paper Abstract denotes the abstract of a paper (a short summary component), whereas Regular Paper denotes a full paper accepted in a regular conference track. They share the parent Paper but represent fundamentally different concepts: one is a document component/summary, the other is a paper type based on submission category.

Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Paper Author is a person who writes a paper. They belong to disjoint branches (document vs person) and share no instances.

confOf 'Submission event' is a temporal/administrative event (subclass of Event > Administrative event) representing the submission phase of a conference. iasted 'Initial manuscript' is a document artefact (subclass of Item > Document > Submission) representing the actual paper file submitted. One is an event, the other is a physical/document entity; their instances do not coincide.

These properties operate at completely different levels. 'has an expertise' (domain: Review expertise) describes the expertise level or topic associated with a review-expertise entity, while 'reviewes' (domain: Member PC, range: Contribution) links a PC member to the paper they review. They have different domains, different ranges (unspecified datatype vs. Contribution object), and express different relationships.

The property writePaper in cmt relates an Author to a Paper (the act of authoring a document). The property coversTopic in ekaw relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (the subject matter covered). These are fundamentally different relations with different domains and ranges, and they do not overlap in meaning.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings: 'has an email' applies to Person and records an email address, while 'hasPostalCode' applies to Contact Information and records a postal code. They denote different attributes and do not overlap.

Chair is a person who leads a committee in the Conference ontology, while Registration fee is a monetary amount paid for conference attendance in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to completely different domains (people vs. fees) and share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, listsEvent connects a Programme Brochure / Web Site to an Event (a document or site listing events). In iasted, is_given_by connects an Activity / Item to a Person (an activity or item being presented or authored by a person). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so the properties are unrelated.

The confOf hasCountry property links an Organization or Person to a Country, while the iasted is_present property links a Person to a Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Property A (`has a location`) maps a Conference volume to a string representing its physical/geographic location (e.g., city, venue). Property B (`Name of conference`) maps a Conference to a string representing the conference's name/title. These are semantically distinct attributes: one denotes where the conference takes place, the other denotes what the conference is called. Despite both being datatype properties with domain Conference volume/Conference and range string, they relate different kinds of information and would not be considered equivalent in a reference alignment.

Both classes are named 'Person' and represent the top-level class for people involved in a conference. They share core properties such as email/name, and their subclasses (Chairman/Conference Chair, Program Committee Member/TPC Member, External Reviewer/Reviewer, etc.) are clear correspondences. Both serve as the general person class in the conference-organisation domain, so their intended instances coincide.

These properties denote different relations. 'speak in' (iasted) relates a Person to a Place or Time where they give a talk/presentation, while 'can stay in' (sigkdd) relates a Person to a Place where they can lodge/stay. Speaking at a venue and staying at a venue are distinct activities with different semantics, so these properties are unrelated.

In ekaw, Proceedings is a subclass of Multi author Volume (a Document), denoting a published volume of conference papers. In iasted, 'Author book proceedings included' is a subclass of Author (under Person > Delegate > Speaker > Author), denoting a person who authored a book included in proceedings. One is a document/artifact, the other is a person/role; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The cmt 'acceptedBy' property links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it, indicating acceptance of the paper. The sigkdd 'presentationed_by' property links a Document to the Speaker who presented it. These are fundamentally different relations: one concerns the acceptance decision made by an administrator, the other concerns the act of presenting by a speaker. The domains (Paper vs Document) and ranges (Administrator vs Speaker) also differ, confirming these are unrelated properties in the conference domain.

The two properties denote different relations. In cmt, 'addedBy' records which Administrator added a Program Committee Member (an administrative creation/assignment action). In Conference, 'was_a_member_of' records the committee that a Committee member belonged to (a membership relation). The domains overlap (PC member vs Committee member) but the ranges differ (Administrator vs Committee) and the intended semantics are distinct: one is about who added the person, the other is about which committee the person was a member of.

These two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. readByReviewer has domain Paper and range Reviewer (Paper -> Reviewer), while reviewerOfPaper has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper (Reviewer -> Paper). They describe the same relationship but in opposite directions. A reference alignment would not mark inverse properties as equivalent.

Microelectronics Topic is a subject-area classification (a Topic) in the EDAS ontology, while Contributed Talk is a type of presentation event (an Individual Presentation) in EKAW. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion) in confOf, while Listener is a person who attends talks in sigkdd. They denote completely different categories of entities (event vs. person) with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations. `has parts` in the Conference ontology links a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (a mereological part-whole relation). `isLocationOf` in edas links a Place to a Conference Event (a spatial location relation). The domains (Conference volume vs. Place) and ranges (Conference part vs. Conference Event) are disjoint concepts, and the intended meanings (part-of vs. located-at) are semantically distinct, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only trivially related by both being binary object properties.

Possible Reviewer in ekaw denotes a person who can review papers (a potential reviewer), while Author in sigkdd denotes a person who writes/submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: a reviewer evaluates papers, while an author produces them. There is no indication that these classes share instances or that one subsumes the other.

confOf:Contribution is a general work submitted to a conference (with children Paper, Poster, Short paper), while ekaw:Abstract is a specific document type (a textual abstract, sibling of Paper, Review, Flyer, etc., with children Invited Talk Abstract, Tutorial Abstract). They denote different concepts: one is the contribution itself, the other is the abstract document associated with a presentation.

confOf Author is a broad class of persons who write contributions, while edas Presenter is a subclass of Author specifically denoting authors who present their work. Every Presenter is an Author, but not every Author is a Presenter, so confOf Author is subsumed_by edas Presenter in the sense that Presenter is the more specific concept.

The confOf property 'reviewes' relates a PC Member to a Contribution they review, whereas the iasted property 'is made from' relates an Item to another Item it is made from. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The two properties operate in entirely different domains. In cmt, 'has Decision' links a Paper to a Decision (e.g., accept/reject) made during the review process. In iasted, 'is equipped by' links a Place to an Item (physical equipment). They share no common domain, range, or semantic relationship in the conference-organisation domain.

These properties have different domains and ranges that do not align. In cmt, hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to a Conference Member (a person who is a member of the conference, likely an author or participant). In the Conference ontology, has_a_commtitee relates a Conference volume to a Committee (an organizational body). A Conference Member (individual person) is not the same as a Committee (a group/organizational entity), so the properties relate fundamentally different kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Conference announcement is a document that announces a conference (a sibling of Call for paper, Call for participation, etc.), whereas Cd proceening is a publication medium (a CD containing conference proceedings, sibling to Book proceeding). One is an announcement document, the other is a proceedings publication format; their intended instances do not coincide.

hasTitle (confOf) is a datatype property from Contribution to string representing the title of a contribution. Nation (sigkdd) is a datatype property from Person to string representing a person's nationality. They relate to completely different domains and concepts, so they are unrelated.

Paper Abstract is a document subclass (a short summary of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Full day tour is an activity (a post-conference excursion) in the iasted ontology. They belong to completely different domains and share no conceptual overlap.

In cmt, Preference is a class used to model review preferences (e.g., a reviewer's bid on a paper). In iasted, Currency is a class representing monetary currency (e.g., for registration fees). These are entirely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Registeered applicant is a person who has applied to register for a conference, whereas Registration in iasted is an activity (sibling of Cocktail reception, Lecture, etc.) that a delegate participates in. One denotes a person role, the other an event/activity, so they are not equivalent.

The property 'is Provider Of' in edas relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (an organization provides a sponsorship), while 'written By' in ekaw relates a Document to a Person (a document is authored by a person). These properties connect entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

A 'Tutorial Chair' (ekaw) is a person who chairs/organizes a tutorial, while a 'Tutorial speaker' (iasted) is a person who speaks/presents at a tutorial. These are distinct roles: a chair organizes and moderates, while a speaker delivers content. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

Property A ('is given by') relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it. Property B ('is used by') relates an Item to a Person who uses it. The domains (Presentation vs Item), ranges (Active conference participant vs Person), and the underlying relations (delivering/presenting vs using) are distinct, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

Both properties concern the authorship relation between a written item and a person, but they are inverses of each other: confOf:writes has domain Author and range Contribution (Author -> Contribution), while iasted:is_sent_by has domain Item and range Person (Item -> Person). A property and its inverse are not equivalent; they are related.

A Presenter is a conference participant who presents a paper/talk, while a Sponsor is a person or organization that provides financial support to the conference. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a person who is a member of a conference (parent: Person, with subclasses like Author, Reviewer, Chair). Activity after conference in iasted is an event/activity (parent: Activity, with subclasses like Departure, Full day tour). These denote completely different concepts: a person vs. an organized activity.

Publication in iasted is a subclass of Item with children like Book proceeding and Cd proceeding, denoting published artefacts. Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited Speaker, denoting people who present. One is a document/artefact, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Chairman in cmt is a person role (a kind of Person) that includes Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, etc. Scientific Event in ekaw is a kind of Event (with children like Conference, Session, Workshop). One denotes a human role in conference organization; the other denotes an event/activity. They share no instances and are from entirely different parts of the domain hierarchy.

An Attendee in edas is a person who attends the conference (a participant), while a Program Committee member in sigkdd is an organizer who serves on the program committee (responsible for reviewing papers and selecting the program). These are distinct roles: an attendee is not necessarily an organizer, and a PC member is not merely an attendee. Their intended instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate completely different entities. cmt:assignedTo has domain Paper and range Reviewer, capturing which reviewer is assigned to review a paper. edas:hasRelatedPaper has domain Author and range Paper, capturing which papers are associated with an author. They differ in both domain and range and express different relationships.

Invited talk is a type of conference contribution/presentation (an invited speaker giving a talk), while Demo Session is a type of session/event where demonstrations are held. They are at different levels of granularity and serve different purposes in the conference domain: one is a contribution type, the other is an event/session type. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties have different meanings and different ranges. In edas, 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (a conference member/participant). In sigkdd, 'holded by' relates a Conference to ACM SIGKDD (the organization that holds the conference). One denotes membership of people in a conference, the other denotes the organizing body that holds a conference. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), denoting a kind of conference event. edas:MedicineTopic is a subclass of Topic, denoting a subject area. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and domains of discourse.

In ekaw, Neutral_Review is a specific subclass of Review (a review with neutral sentiment, sibling to Positive_Review and Negative_Review). In sigkdd, Review is the general review class. Thus ekaw:Neutral_Review is subsumed by sigkdd:Review.

Co author is a person (subclass of Author/Person) who co-writes papers; Multi author Volume is a document (subclass of Document) with multiple authors, e.g. proceedings. One is a person, the other a document, so they are unrelated.

Accommodation Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where conference attendees stay, while Author information form is a document (subclass of Form > Document > Item) for collecting author information. These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts: `has_the_first_name` captures a person's first name (domain Person), while `hasCity` captures a city as part of contact information (domain Contact Information). Despite both being datatype properties with range string, their domains and intended meanings are disjoint, so they are unrelated.

These properties are completely unrelated. Property A is a datatype property mapping 'Important dates' to a 'date' value, specifically capturing the submission deadline for full papers. Property B is an object property mapping 'Research Topic' to 'Event' or 'Paper', indicating which events or papers cover a given research topic. They have different domains, different ranges (datatype vs. object), and represent entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

These properties have different domains and ranges and serve different purposes. 'for Event' in EDAS links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the Academic Event it is associated with. 'has Event' in EKAW links an Event to a sub-Event (part-of relation between events). They relate different entity types in different directions and are not equivalent.
Invited talk is a type of conference presentation/contribution, while Radio Communications Topic is a subject-area topic. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Associated Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person) in cmt, while Best Paper Awards Committee is a committee (a group/body) in sigkdd. They denote completely different kinds of entities: an individual person vs. an organizational committee.

Both classes denote speakers at a conference, but they are distinct roles: an 'Invited speaker' is someone invited to give a talk (often a plenary or keynote), while a 'Tutorial speaker' specifically presents a tutorial. They overlap (a person could be both) but their intended instances do not coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In Conference, 'Committee member' is a specific subclass of Person restricted to people who serve on committees (with children Chair, Co chair). In sigkdd, 'Person' is the general class of all people (with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker). Every committee member is a person, but not every person is a committee member, so Committee member is subsumed by Person.

confOf's 'parallel with' is a symmetric relation indicating two administrative events occur in parallel (same time slot, different tracks). ekaw's 'part Of' is a mereological relation indicating a part-whole relationship. These are fundamentally different relations: parallel events are not parts of each other, and part-whole relations are not about temporal concurrency. No meaningful overlap exists between these two properties.

Meal Event is a non-academic social event (e.g., conference dinner) in the event hierarchy, while Speaker is a person who gives a presentation in the person hierarchy. They belong to completely different domains (events vs. people) and share no instances.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Topic' is a subject-area topic under the Topic hierarchy, with children like security, switching, and sensor topics. In EKAW, 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a document type under Abstract. There is no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote a place where conference participants dine/eat. 'Dining Place' in EDAS and 'Conference restaurant' in IASTED are sibling concepts under a general Place/Building hierarchy and both refer to the same kind of facility in the conference organization domain.

The property 'assigned To' in cmt relates a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assigned to reviewer for review), while 'location Of' in ekaw relates a Location to an Event (the location where an event takes place). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

The property 'issues' in the Conference ontology relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings), whereas 'write' in the iasted ontology relates a Person to an Item (a person writes an item). The domains (Publisher vs Person) and ranges (Conference proceedings vs Item) are disjoint, and the relations describe completely different actions in the conference domain.

The two properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges. 'is given by' relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the person delivering the talk), whereas 'is Initiated By' relates a Call (e.g., a call for papers) to committee roles such as Conference Chair, Session Chair, or TPC Member. The domains (Presentation vs. Call) and ranges (Active conference participant vs. committee roles) do not coincide, so the properties denote different relations in the conference domain.

Attendee denotes a person who attends a conference session/event, whereas Session Chair denotes a person who chairs a specific session. These are distinct roles: an attendee is a general participant, while a session chair is a specific leadership role. They share the common parent Person/Conference Participant but are sibling-level concepts with different intended instances.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a kind of Chairman), while Book proceeding is a publication artifact (a kind of Item/Publication). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Tip in iasted is a monetary amount given as a tip (a gratuity), sibling to Fee, Sponsorship, and Tax under Money. Sponzor fee in sigkdd is a specific kind of fee paid by a sponsor, sibling to Registration fee under Fee. A tip is not a sponsor fee; they denote different financial concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in opposite conceptual directions. 'has parts' links a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (a whole-to-part relation), while 'holded by' links a Conference to the organization ACM SIGKDD that holds it (an event-to-organizer relation). They differ in domain, range, and the kind of relation they express, so they are unrelated.

Multimedia Topic in edas is a subject area for conference papers (a Topic), while Overhead projector in iasted is a physical audiovisual equipment item. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion or outing), whereas iasted:Hotel_presenter is a person role (a delegate who presents at a hotel venue). They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies (events vs. persons) and share no instances.

The EKAW property 'inverse of partOf 7' is a structural mereological relation whose range is Event, relating parts to their containing events. The SIGKDD 'award' property relates something (e.g., a person or paper) to an Award it receives. These denote completely different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in intended meaning.

In EDAS, Textual Review Question is a specific type of review question (a question posed to reviewers, with a free-text answer), sibling to Numerical Review Question. In SIGKDD, Review is a document (the actual review artefact of a paper), sibling to Abstract and Paper. These denote different things: one is a question item, the other is a review document. They are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

cmt's writeReview has domain Reviewer and range Review, while iasted's write has domain Person and range Item. Reviewer is a kind of Person and Review is a kind of Item, so writeReview is a more specific property than write. They are not equivalent because write can relate any Person to any Item (e.g., writing a paper, abstract, or other document), whereas writeReview specifically relates a Reviewer to a Review.

Property `is Reviewing` in edas specifically denotes the act of a reviewer (or related committee role) reviewing a Paper, with domain restricted to Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member and range Paper. Property `write` in iasted denotes a Person writing an Item (a more general document/artefact). Reviewing and writing are distinct relations in the conference domain, so these properties are neither equivalent nor subsumed by one another.

The two properties have different domains and ranges. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person who is a member of the conference). In the Conference ontology, has_members links a Committee to its Committee member (a person serving on a specific committee). A conference membership and a committee membership are distinct relationships in the conference domain, so these properties are not equivalent.

These properties have different meanings and different ranges. 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization they work for, while 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place/Time where they give a presentation. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

confOf:Tutorial is a type of event (a working event under Event), while sigkdd:Conference_hall is a physical place (under Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

These properties operate on completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated meanings. 'updated Version Of' (ekaw) relates a Document to a prior Document it is an updated version of. 'give' (iasted) relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give/present. No semantic overlap exists between a document-versioning relation and a person-to-activity/item action relation.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for people in the conference domain. confOf's Person has children like Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc., while sigkdd's Person has children like Listener, Organizator, Speaker. These are complementary specializations of the same general concept (a person involved in a conference). Both have similar contact properties (email, name, address-related). The intended instances coincide at the general level: any person in the conference organization domain.

In ekaw, PC Member is a general program committee member (subclass of Possible Reviewer), with PC Chair as one of its subclasses. In sigkdd, Program Chair is the head of the program (a specific leadership role, sibling of General Chair and Program Committee member). These are different roles: a PC Member is an ordinary committee member, while a Program Chair is the committee's chair. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties operate at different levels of granularity and have non-equivalent domains and ranges. In edas, hasProgramme links a Conference Event to a Programme (the schedule of sessions/activities at an event). In sigkdd, hold links an ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference (the event itself). The domains (Conference Event vs ACM SIGKDD) and ranges (Programme vs Conference) do not coincide, and the relations denote different things: one associates an event with its programme, the other associates an organization with the conference it holds.

contactEmail is a datatype property from Contribution to string (an email address), while listsEvent is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event. They relate completely different kinds of entities and have no semantic overlap.

The two properties operate in completely different domains and directions. In EDAS, 'hasCall' links an AcademicEvent to a Call (e.g., a call for papers issued by a conference). In IASTED, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or distributing an item). The domains (AcademicEvent vs Person) and ranges (Call vs Activity/Item) do not overlap, and the relations they express are conceptually distinct.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In confOf, 'study At' links a Scholar to a University (a person studies at an institution). In iasted, 'is given to' links an Item to a Person (an item is given to a person). The domains (Scholar vs Item), ranges (University vs Person), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Conference participant in ontology A is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference. Conference in ontology B denotes the event itself, with properties like start/end dates, city, and name, and it is held by ACM SIGKDD. These are fundamentally different concepts: a person vs. an event.

Non Academic Event in EDAS denotes events like breaks, meals, and social activities—non-scholarly parts of a conference. Scientific Event in EKAW denotes scholarly events such as conferences, sessions, tracks, workshops, and presentations. These are disjoint categories: one is explicitly non-academic, the other is explicitly scientific/academic. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

Conference volume in the Conference ontology is a top-level organizational entity (a conference edition) that has committees, contributions, tracks, parts, and important dates. Conference days in iasted is a temporal entity (subclass of Time) that has delegates and individual conference days as children. One denotes the conference as an organizational whole, the other a time span; their intended instances do not coincide.

The property 'is Menu Of' in EDAS relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event, indicating which meal event a menu belongs to. The property 'part Of Event' in EKAW relates an Event to an Event, indicating mereological parthood between events. These are structurally and semantically different: one connects menus to events, the other connects events to events. They do not share domain/range types and do not denote the same relation.

Both entities share the same two children (Acceptance/Accepted contribution and Rejection/Rejected contribution), indicating they model the same decision outcome space in the conference domain. However, they are fundamentally different kinds of entities: cmt:Decision is an abstract class representing the decision itself (the outcome of reviewing), while Conference:Reviewed_contribution is a written artifact (a paper that has been reviewed). The children in cmt are decision types, whereas in Conference they are contribution types distinguished by the decision. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

Conference participant in ontology A is a broad class covering all participants (with children Active/Passive), while Late Registered Participant in ekaw is a specific kind of participant who registered late. A subsumes B because every late-registered participant is a conference participant, but not vice versa.

An Attendee is a general conference participant who is present at the event, while an Invited Speaker is a specific role for someone delivering an invited talk. Attendees are not necessarily speakers, and invited speakers are a specialized subset of speakers rather than a kind of attendee. The two classes denote different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to a conference (subclass of Person), while 'Registration' in iasted is an activity (subclass of Conference activity). One is a person, the other is an event/activity; they denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

confOf:remark is a datatype property from Contribution to string (a textual comment/remark on a contribution), whereas ekaw:reviewWrittenBy is an object property from Review to Possible Reviewer (linking a review to its author). They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning; one is a comment field and the other an authorship relation.

In ekaw, Research Institute is an organization (a kind of academic institution, sibling of University). In iasted, Modelling is an activity (a research activity performed before the conference). One is an institution, the other is a research activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are subclasses of Person involved in reviewing, but they are not equivalent. In the Conference ontology, Reviewer is the specific class for persons who write reviews.
