They share only the domain (Person) but differ in range type (object vs. datatype) and denote entirely different relations.

Trip city is a subclass of City representing a city where a trip occurs (sibling to Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city). Conference hall is a subclass of Place representing a physical venue/building (sibling to Hotel, Main office). One is a geographic location (city), the other is a built structure/venue. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Session Chair is a person role (a Person who chairs a session), while Sponzor fee is a monetary fee paid by a sponsor. They belong to completely different branches of the ontology (Person vs. Fee) and share no domain overlap.

Committee member is a person who serves on a committee, while Money is a financial entity with subtypes like Fee, Tax, Tip. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties are completely different in meaning and structure. `hasEmail` is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's email address. `writtenBy` is an object property from Document to Person, capturing authorship of a document. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

confOf:Conference is an academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas iasted:Conference_airport is a physical location (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel and Conference restaurant). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a kind of Chairman), while Track is a scientific event subdivision. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Conference Chair (edas) is the person chairing the entire conference, while Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is the person chairing a tutorial event. These are distinct organizational roles with different scopes and responsibilities; neither subsumes the other.

The iasted 'is given to' is an object property relating an Item to a Person (e.g., an award or item given to someone), while the sigkdd 'Name' is a datatype property relating a Person to a string (the person's name). They have different types, domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

The property hasPhone in edas relates Contact Information to a string (a phone number), while has_amount_of in iasted relates Money to an int (a monetary amount). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

These properties relate completely different entities. The cmt property 'hardcopyMailingManifestsPrintedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (who printed mailing manifests), while the ekaw property 'presentationOfPaper' links an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract (the paper being presented). They have different domains, different ranges, and describe unrelated aspects of conference organization.

The edas 'Session Chair' is a subclass of Person, denoting the role of a person who chairs a conference session. The iasted 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a subclass of Document, denoting a textual artefact. Despite the shared phrase 'Session chair', these entities denote completely different categories of things (a person/role vs. a document), so they are unrelated.

confOf:Tutorial is a type of working event (a session/activity where tutorials are presented), while iasted:One_conference_day is a temporal entity representing a single day within the conference period. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Event vs. Time) and denote fundamentally different concepts in the conference-organization domain.

Trip in confOf is a social event (e.g., excursion, banquet, reception), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives a presentation. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and run in different directions. In edas, isMemberOf links a Person to a Conference (membership relation). In iasted, is_sent_by links an Item to a Person (authorship/sending relation). The domains (Person vs Item), ranges (Conference vs Person), and overall semantics are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Paper Abstract is a textual document (a short version of a paper), while Best Research Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Decision (cmt) represents the outcome of a paper review process (Acceptance/Rejection), while Fee (sigkdd) represents a monetary charge (Registration fee/Sponzor fee). These are entirely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference applicant in ontology A is a subclass of Person, denoting someone who applies to attend a conference. Conference in ontology B is an event with properties like start/end dates, city, and name, and is held by ACM SIGKDD. These are completely different concepts: a person vs. an event.
PC Member is a person who serves on a programme committee, while Fee is a monetary charge for registration or sponsorship. They denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Accommodation Place in edas is a broad class covering any place of accommodation (siblings include Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). Double hotel room in iasted is a specific type of hotel room (a single or double room). A double hotel room is an instance/subtype of an accommodation place, not equivalent to it. The edas class is more general, so iasted's Double hotel room is subsumed_by Accommodation Place.

Organization in edas denotes an organizational entity (academia, government, industry, NGO) that can sponsor conferences, while Place in iasted denotes a physical location (building, conference hall, hotel room, etc.) where activities are held. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Medicine Topic is a subclass of Topic in the edas ontology, representing a subject area for conference papers (e.g., alongside Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). Invited Talk Abstract is a subclass of Abstract > Document in the ekaw ontology, representing a specific type of document produced for an invited talk. These are completely different concepts: one is a topic/subject classification, the other is a document artifact. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

ekaw:Document is a broad superclass covering abstracts, papers, reviews, flyers, brochures, web sites, etc. iasted:Payment_document is a specific subclass of iasted:Document (under Item) with children Bank_transfer and Cheque—i.e., concrete payment instruments. A payment document is not an instance of the ekaw:Document notion (which is about conference artefacts like papers and reviews), and the broad ekaw:Document is not a payment document. The two concepts occupy different parts of the domain with no clear overlap, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or in a subsumption relation.

Rejection in cmt is a subclass of Decision representing the outcome of a paper submission being declined. Listener in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who attends a conference to listen. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

In ontology Conference, 'Important dates' is a class that groups deadline-related dates (abstract submission, full paper submission, camera-ready, acceptance announcement, start/end dates) for a conference volume. In sigkdd, 'Conference' is the actual conference event itself with properties like city, start/end, and name. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a collection of temporal deadline markers, the other is the conference event. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

In ekaw, Social Event is a specific kind of Event (e.g., Conference Banquet, Conference Trip) — purely non-scientific social occasions. In iasted, Conference activity is a broad class covering all conference activities including lectures, presentations, registrations, technical activities, and social programs. Thus Social Event is a strict subset of Conference activity, not equivalent.

confOf Participant is a broad superclass covering all conference attendees (with children like Member, Regular, Student), whereas ekaw OC Member is a specific role for members of the Organizing Committee. The two classes do not share instances: a general participant is not necessarily an OC member, and an OC member is not a subclass of the generic Participant in confOf. They are therefore unrelated rather than equivalent or subsumed.

confOf:Scholar is a subclass of Person (a human participant/scholar), while iasted:Author_attendee_cd_registration_fee is a monetary fee. They denote completely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Talk Event in edas is a subclass of Academic Event (an event/activity), whereas Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Document > Abstract (a written artefact). One denotes the talk event itself, the other denotes the abstract document associated with an invited talk. They are different kinds of entities (event vs document), so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document and denotes the written submission itself, with properties like hasAuthor, hasDecision, assignedTo. In sigkdd, Author is a subclass of Person (via Speaker) and denotes a human agent who submits papers and can obtain awards. These are disjoint concepts (document vs. person), so they are unrelated.

confOf:follows relates one Administrative event to another Administrative event (e.g., one event following another in sequence), while edas:hasCall relates an Academic Event to a Call (a call for papers/submissions). They have different domains and ranges, and denote entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

In Conference, Topic is a subject area (e.g., research topic) assigned to conference parts and used in review preferences. In confOf, Contribution is a written work submitted to the conference (parent of Paper, Poster, Short paper) that deals with topics. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a subject matter, the other is a submitted document/artifact.

hasCo-author relates a Paper to its Co-author (a Person), while contributes relates a Person to a Conference document they contributed to. Different domains, different ranges, and different relational semantics: one links a document to an author, the other links a person to a document.

The two properties relate different concepts: 'has important dates' links a conference volume to its important dates (e.g., submission deadlines), while 'has Programme' links a conference event to its programme (schedule of sessions/events). Their domains and ranges differ, and they denote distinct relationships in the conference domain.

In Conference, Presentation is a broad class covering any spoken or shown contribution (it has child Invited talk and siblings Poster, Written contribution, etc.). In ekaw, Contributed Talk is a specific kind of Individual Presentation, distinct from Invited Talk and Tutorial. Thus ekaw's Contributed Talk is narrower than Conference's Presentation, which also includes invited talks and posters.
Committee member is a person who serves on a committee, while Fee is a monetary charge. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Invited_speaker in Conference is a subclass of Person/Conference_contributor, denoting a person who gives an invited talk. Conference in confOf is a subclass of Event/Working_event, denoting the conference event itself. These are completely different categories of entities (person vs. event) with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Member_PC is a person who is a PC member and reviewer (subclass of Person, domain of reviewes/expertOn). ekaw:Review is a document (subclass of Document) that is a review artifact written by a reviewer. One denotes the reviewer (a person), the other denotes the review document itself. They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Preference represents a reviewer's bid on a paper (e.g., values like 'want to review', 'do not want to review'), while Organization in the Conference ontology denotes an institution such as a university or company involved in the conference domain. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Author Not Reviewer is a conference member who authored a paper but is not assigned as a reviewer (a role-based restriction class under Author). Student is a person who is a student (an academic/occupational status). The intended instances do not coincide: an author-not-reviewer need not be a student, and a student need not be an author. No subsumption holds in either direction.

confOf:Person is a broad class covering all people involved in the conference (authors, chairs, participants, volunteers, etc.), while edas:Author is a specific subclass of Person restricted to authors of papers. confOf:Person therefore subsumes edas:Author.

The two properties relate entirely different domains and ranges and go in opposite directions. 'is equipped by' links a Place to an Item it contains, while 'can stay in' links a Person to a Place they can occupy. They are not inverses of each other (Place/Item vs Person/Place) and share no common relational semantics in the conference domain.

Paper Presentation is an academic event (a talk/session where a paper is presented), while Programme Brochure is a document listing events. They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Document) and denote fundamentally different kinds of entities.

A 'Conference applicant' is someone who applies to attend a conference, while an 'Early Registered Participant' is someone who has already registered early. Application precedes registration, and these are distinct stages with different instances. The ontologies model them under separate hierarchies (applicant vs. participant), and there is no evidence of overlap or subsumption.

Review in cmt is a document written by a reviewer about a paper, while Transport vehicle in iasted denotes a physical vehicle (car, shuttle bus, taxi, van). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and in different directions. In EDAS, 'is Member Of' links a Person to a Conference (person is a member of a conference). In EKAW, 'written By' links a Document to a Person (document is written by a person). They share no common domain or range types and are not inverses of each other.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of setting review criteria for a conference). In edas, 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to various reviewer roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), indicating who reviewed a paper. They connect different entity types in different directions and represent different relations.

The property 'rejected By' in cmt relates a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it, while 'has Review' in ekaw relates a Paper to a Review. They connect different kinds of entities (Administrator vs. Review) and express different relationships (who rejected the paper vs. what reviews the paper has). A paper can have reviews without being rejected, and rejection is an administrative decision unrelated to the existence of reviews.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a structural role-assignment relation), while 'initiates' links conference/session/TPC chairs to a Call (e.g., a call for papers/participation). They relate different kinds of entities and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, sitting under Person > Conference Member. Track in Conference is a conference part (like Tutorial or Workshop) that a conference volume has. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Workshop Chair (ekaw) is the chair of a workshop, a satellite event, while Program Chair (sigkdd) is the chair of the entire conference program. These are distinct organizational roles: a Workshop Chair oversees a single workshop, whereas a Program Chair oversees the whole conference's paper selection and program. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since they are coordinate roles at different scopes.

Chairman is a person who leads a conference committee (subclasses include Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Fee for extra trip is a monetary charge for an additional trip. They belong to entirely different domains (person vs. money) with no semantic overlap.

Subject Area in cmt denotes a research topic or category that a Paper belongs to (domain of has Subject Area is Paper -> Subject Area). Money in iasted denotes a monetary amount with children Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment, amounts, and currency. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The EKAW 'Invited Speaker' is a Person (subclass of Presenter), i.e. the human who delivers an invited talk. The IASTED 'Speaker lecture' is an Activity (subclass of Session/Lecture), i.e. the talk event itself. They denote different categories of entities (agent vs. event), so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalisation of the other.

Committee in the Conference ontology denotes a group of people organized for a specific conference role (e.g., Organizing committee, Program committee), with properties for chairs, co-chairs, and members. Person in the iasted ontology denotes an individual human (with subtypes Delegate and Sponsor) who performs actions like giving, being connected with, or being present. A committee is not an individual person; these are disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities in opposite directions. In cmt, assignExternalReviewer links a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (a reviewer assigning an external co-reviewer). In edas, isReviewHistoryOf links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (a history record belonging to a reviewer). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

The property 'invites co reviewers' specifically relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (co-reviewing invitation), while 'send' relates a Person to an Item (sending an item). They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning.

cmt:Paper is a general class for all papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties covering bidding, assignment, decisions, etc.), while ekaw:Assigned Paper is a specific subclass of Submitted Paper restricted to papers that have been assigned to reviewers. Every Assigned Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is an Assigned Paper, so cmt:Paper subsumes ekaw:Assigned Paper.

Both properties relate a document to its author(s): Conference's 'has authors' (Conference document -> Person) and ekaw's 'written By' (Document -> Person) share the same domain and range types and the same intended meaning of linking a written artefact to the person who authored it.

Coffee break is a conference activity/event in the iasted ontology, while Conference hall is a place/location in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Activity vs Place) and denote different types of entities with no overlap in instances.

confOf's 'Working event' groups substantive academic events (Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) as a sub-type of Event, contrasted with Administrative and Social events. iasted's 'Registration' is a specific conference activity (a registration process/record) that has Delegate children. These are structurally and semantically different: one is a broad category of academic events, the other is a specific administrative activity. They share no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, enableVirtualMeeting connects Administrator to Conference (an administrator enabling a virtual meeting for a conference). In edas, hasMember connects Conference to Person (listing members of a conference). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different, so they are not equivalent, subsumed, or overlapping.

Conference activity in iasted denotes an event or activity during a conference (e.g., reception, lecture, registration), a subclass of Activity. Organizator in sigkdd denotes a person who organizes the conference (e.g., chairs, committee members), a subclass of Person. These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Author is a Person who submits and writes papers, a standard conference-paper author role. In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Author under Speaker/Delegate, with children like Student lecturer and Worker lecturer, denoting a person who delivers a lecture at the conference. Despite the label 'Author' appearing in iasted's hierarchy, Lecturer is specifically a speaker/lecturer role, not a paper author. The two concepts denote different roles in the conference domain and do not overlap in intended instances.

Both are datatype properties associating a deadline/important-date entity with a temporal value, but they are not equivalent. A's 'is an ending date' is a specific sub-property capturing the end boundary of an important date interval (sibling to 'is a starting date'), while B's 'Date' is a generic deadline date property. The sigkdd 'Date' property is more general (any deadline date), subsuming the more specific 'is an ending date' relation.

Review preference in the Conference ontology represents a reviewer's preference for reviewing a particular topic or submission, with properties like degree, topic, and reviewer. Document in sigkdd is a general container for textual artefacts (Abstract, Paper, Review) with properties about presentation and submission deadlines. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad grouping of all people who belong to a conference (including authors, chairs, reviewers, etc.), whereas Session Chair in edas is a specific role for someone who chairs a session. They share the parent Person, but their intended instances do not coincide: a Conference Member is not necessarily a Session Chair, and a Session Chair is a specific role rather than a general membership class. No subsumption holds either, since Conference Member is a generic membership concept and Session Chair is a concrete functional role.

Both relate a written work to its author(s), but they differ in scope and direction. cmt's hasCo-author specifically links a Paper to a Co-author (a person who co-authored the paper), while iasted's is_writen_by links an Item to a Person (the author). The cmt property is narrower (only co-authors, not sole authors) and the iasted property is broader (any author relationship). They overlap in meaning but are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract in cmt is the abstract of a paper (a research contribution submitted for review), while Tutorial Abstract in ekaw is the abstract of a tutorial (an instructional event). These are different kinds of documents describing different types of conference content, so they do not coincide in intended instances.

In the Conference ontology, 'Review expertise' is a class representing the expertise or qualification level a reviewer has for reviewing a particular submitted contribution (it is linked to Reviewer, Submitted contribution, and Review preference). In edas, 'Reviewer' is a subclass of Person — a human role. One is an attribute/qualification concept, the other is a person role; they do not share instances and are not hierarchically related.

employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment affiliation), while providedBy relates a Sponsorship to an Organization (sponsor provision). Different domains (Person vs Sponsorship) and different semantics; no overlap in intended meaning.

Presenter in EKAW is a conference participant who presents (parent: Conference Participant, under Person). Technical commitee in IASTED is a delegate (under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate), denoting a committee member, not a presenter. The two classes denote different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. Property A is a datatype property linking an Important dates instance to a date value, recording the camera-ready paper submission deadline. Property B is an object property linking a Research Topic to the Events or Papers that cover it. They have disjoint domains, disjoint ranges, and no semantic overlap.

Track workshop chair is a specific role for chairing a track or workshop within a conference, while General Chair is the overall chair of the entire conference. These are distinct organizational roles with different scopes and responsibilities, neither subsuming the other.

In confOf, Tutorial is a standalone class (sibling of Conference and Workshop under Working event). In iasted, Tutorial is a child of Lecture, making Lecture strictly more general. The two Tutorial classes are not equivalent to each other, and confOf's Tutorial is subsumed by iasted's Lecture.

A Web Site in ekaw is a general web resource (sibling to Paper, Review, Flyer, etc.) that can list events and be published by organisations. A Registration form in iasted is a specific form for conference registration (sibling to Author information form, Hotel registration form). These are distinct document types with different purposes; neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate different kinds of subjects to a Person. In edas, hasMember connects a Conference to its members (people who are part of the conference). In iasted, is_signed_by connects an Item (a document/artefact) to the Person who signed it. The domains (Conference vs Item) and the intended semantics (membership vs authorship/signature) are distinct, so these are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Accommodation Place in edas is a physical location (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) where people stay during a conference. Hotel registration form in iasted is a document (subclass of Form under Document) used to register for hotel accommodation. One is a place, the other is a form/document. They are completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a subclass of Document > Paper, denoting the textual abstract artefact of a paper. In edas, Paper Presentation is a subclass of Conference Event > Academic Event, denoting the presentation event at which a paper is presented. One is a document, the other is an event; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

confOf Member is a general participant category (sibling of Regular and Student), whereas ekaw Student specifically denotes a student person. These classes do not share the same intended instances: a Member could be any non-student/non-regular participant, and an ekaw Student is not necessarily a confOf Member (it may be a Paper Author or Possible Reviewer instead). They are neither equivalent nor in a clear subsumption relation given their disjoint sibling structures.

Property A (has_tracks) links a Conference volume to its constituent Tracks (a part-whole relation at the sub-event level). Property B (hold) links an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference it organizes (an agent-event relation). The domains, ranges, and relation semantics differ entirely, so they are not equivalent.

These properties denote completely different relations. 'referenced In' in ekaw relates a document/paper to something it is cited or referenced in, while 'sign' in iasted relates a Person to an Item (e.g., a person signing a document). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; there is no overlap in meaning.

hasKeyword is a datatype property from Contribution to string (assigning keywords to a paper), while obtain is an object property from Person to Item (a person receiving an item). Different domains, different ranges, different property types, and different semantics.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Best Applications Paper Award is a specific award given to a paper. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document type (a short version/summary of a paper), while Mobile Computing Topic in edas is a subject topic classifying papers by research area. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Document vs Topic) and denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A relates Important dates to a date (a starting date), while property B relates Person to a string (a first name). They have disjoint domains and unrelated ranges, so they denote completely different relations.

Conference document in the Conference ontology is a specific class of documents produced for or associated with a conference (call for papers, reviews, conference contributions, etc.). Item in the iasted ontology is a broad top-level class encompassing physical objects and documents (audiovisual equipment, cards, transport vehicles, publications, documents). Conference document is a narrower concept focused on conference-specific artefacts, while Item is a general class of items. Some instances of Conference document (e.g., Conference contribution, Review) may correspond to instances of Document or Publication under Item, but the scopes differ significantly. Thus Conference document is subsumed by Item.

Performance Topic in EDAS is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area (performance) that a paper or presentation can cover. Contributed Talk in EKAW is a subclass of Individual Presentation under Event, representing a type of conference presentation. These are completely different concepts: one is a topic/subject classification, the other is a type of event/activity.

Entity A is a person who registered early and paid for conference attendance; entity B is an activity of receiving manuscripts before the conference. They belong to completely different domains (person vs. activity) and share no semantic relationship.

Multi-author_Volume in ekaw is a kind of Document (a publication with multiple authors, e.g., proceedings). Author in sigkdd is a kind of Person who writes papers. One is a document/artefact, the other is a person role; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Both classes represent written scholarly works submitted to a conference. In Conference, 'Written contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution' with children like Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, covering papers and similar written artefacts. In confOf, 'Contribution' has children Paper, Poster, and Short paper, and is the range of 'writes'/'written By' linking authors to their written works. The slight label difference (Written contribution vs Contribution) reflects naming convention, but the intended instances—written scholarly submissions—coincide. The broader 'Conference contribution' in ontology A also includes non-written items like Invited talk and Presentation, making 'Written contribution' the proper match for confOf's Contribution.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. cmt:assignExternalReviewer links a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (the act of assigning an external reviewer to help), while ekaw:reviewerOfPaper links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (indicating which paper a reviewer reviews). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics differ entirely.

confOf's hasTitle is a datatype property from Contribution to string (assigning a paper title), while ekaw's hasEvent is an object property from Event to Event (linking events to sub-events). They relate entirely different domain/range types and serve unrelated purposes.

In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Topic' is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area within computer networks. In EKAW, 'Paper' is a subclass of Document, representing a written academic document. These are completely different concepts: one is a topic/subject classification, the other is a document type. They share no instances and have no hierarchical relationship.

Both classes denote a person who chairs a committee in a conference, but they are not equivalent: A's 'Co chair' is a generic committee co-chair (sibling of Chair under Committee member), whereas B's 'OC Chair' is specifically the chair of the Organizing Committee (under OC Member). They overlap in role but differ in scope and specificity.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations. In iasted, 'is designed for' links Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person, suggesting something is intended for an activity or person. In sigkdd, 'designed by' links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD, indicating authorship or design origin of a deadline. They are not the same relation, nor is one a generalization of the other.

confOf's Event is a broad top-level class covering Administrative, Social, and Working events (e.g., conferences, talks, social activities). edas's MealEvent is a specific Non Academic Event subtype (e.g., conference dinners, meals). Event subsumes MealEvent, but they are not equivalent since MealEvent is a narrow specialization.

The cmt 'date' property has domain Conference and range date, representing a general date associated with a conference. The Conference ontology's 'is a date of camera ready paper submission' has domain Important dates and represents a specific deadline date for camera-ready paper submission. These are different relations: one is a generic conference date, the other is a specific submission deadline. They do not share the same domain (Conference vs. Important dates) and the cmt 'date' is not a generalization of the camera-ready submission date specifically; it is a different kind of date property altogether.

The confOf 'abstract' property relates a Contribution to its abstract text (string), while the sigkdd 'Nation' property relates a Person to their nation (string). They have completely different domains (Contribution vs Person) and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with range string, but they have different domains: confOf:contactEmail has domain Contribution (a paper/submission artefact), while sigkdd:E-mail has domain Person (any person). The sigkdd property is more general: any person can have an e-mail, whereas contactEmail is specifically the contact e-mail attached to a contribution. Thus contactEmail is subsumed_by E-mail (the Person-level e-mail property is the broader relation).

In ontology Conference, 'Conference document' is a class for documents produced for or during a conference (call for papers, reviews, contributions, etc.), with properties like has authors and date of issue. In edas, 'Conference' is the event itself (the academic gathering), with properties like has Country, has Member, start/end dates, and paper due dates. These are completely different concepts: one is a document/artefact, the other is the event/organization. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated entities.

Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman under Person) in cmt, while Reviewing results event is a temporal/administrative event (under Event > Administrative event) in confOf. They denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. an event—and share no meaningful overlap.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote unrelated relations. In cmt, 'detailsEnteredBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details. In the Conference ontology, 'is_a_topis_of_conference_parts' relates a Topic to a Conference part it belongs to. There is no overlap in meaning, direction, or the kinds of entities involved.

confOf 'Chair PC' is a subclass of Person and, given its sibling 'Member PC', denotes the chair of the Programme Committee. ekaw 'OC Chair' is a subclass of 'OC Member' under 'Conference Participant', i.e. the chair of the Organising Committee. These are distinct committee roles in conference organisation, so the classes do not coincide; they are not in a subsumption relation either.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper) authored by an Author and reviewed by PC members. Document in sigkdd is a broader artefact that includes Abstract, Paper, and Review. They overlap on the notion of a paper, but Contribution does not subsume Review or Abstract as a submitted work, and Document is broader than just authored contributions. The two classes are related but not equivalent.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities and express different relations. `is situated in` (iasted) has domain Building/City/Place and range Building/City/Place/State, expressing a spatial-location relation between physical entities and their containing places. `can stay in` (sigkdd) has domain Person and range Place, expressing where a person can lodge or reside. The domains (physical structures vs. persons) and the intended meanings (being located in vs. being able to stay in) are distinct, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully overlapping.

confOf Workshop is a specific kind of working event (a workshop session/event), whereas edas TalkEvent is a superclass of talks (closing talk, welcome talk, paper presentation) and has Workshop as a sibling. They occupy different positions in their respective hierarchies and do not denote the same concept.

Review (ekaw) is a document evaluating a paper, with subclasses like Positive/Negative Review and properties linking it to papers and reviewers. Tax (iasted) is a monetary amount with subclasses like Departure tax and Value added tax, sibling to Fee and Tip under Money. These denote completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Chair is a person who leads a committee in the Conference ontology, while Country is a geographic entity used as the range of a hasCountry property in confOf. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent non-academic social activities within a conference. 'Social Event' in edas (child: Reception, Excursion) and 'Social program' in iasted (child: Dinner banquet, sibling: Cocktail reception) cover the same intended instances of conference social gatherings, despite slight naming differences.

Computer Architecture Topic is a subject-area classification for conference submissions, while Program Committee is an organizational body responsible for reviewing papers. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Preference is a class used to express a reviewer's bidding preference for papers (e.g., values like 'very high', 'high', 'low'). In edas, ReviewForm is a document/artefact used to collect review content. These denote completely different concepts: a preference value vs. a review template/form. No subsumption or meaningful overlap.

The two properties relate completely different domains and ranges. In cmt, 'has Decision' links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection). In iasted, 'is present in' links a Person to a Place or Time (physical/temporal presence). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Property A (has parts) relates a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts, expressing a part-whole relationship. Property B (parallel with) relates Administrative events to other Administrative events, expressing a co-occurrence/scheduling relationship. They have different domains, different ranges, and express fundamentally different relations.

In edas, 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference denoting a conference with a single organisational level (as opposed to a Two Level Conference). In iasted, 'One conference day' is a subclass of Conference days under Time, denoting a single day within a conference. One is a conference type, the other is a temporal unit; their intended instances do not coincide.

hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (geographic location of the conference), while is_equipped_by relates a Place to an Item (equipment available at a place). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while ekaw:Demo_Chair is a person role (subclass of Conference Participant, sibling of PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization representing a corporate entity (e.g., a company involved in conference organization). edas:MicroelectronicsTopic is a subclass of Topic representing a specific subject area for conference papers. These classes denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The ekaw 'paper In Volume' property relates a paper to the volume/proceedings it appears in, while the sigkdd 'presentation' property relates a Speaker to a Document (their presentation document). These are different relations with different domain/range types and different semantics: one is about publication venue, the other about authored presentation materials.

Camera ready contribution is a specific stage in the lifecycle of a contribution: it has been submitted, reviewed, accepted, and then finalized as camera-ready. Conference Paper in ekaw is a more general class encompassing all papers presented at a conference, including submitted, accepted, and camera-ready variants (as evidenced by siblings like 'Camera Ready Paper', 'Submitted Paper', etc.). Thus Camera ready contribution is a strict subset of Conference Paper, making the relation subsumed_by.

`end Review` is an object property in cmt whose domain is Program Committee Chair and range is Review, denoting the action of a chair ending/submitting a review. `end Date` is a datatype property in edas with domain Conference and range dateTime, denoting the date and time a conference ends. They share the lexical token 'end' but denote completely different relations (review management vs. conference scheduling), operate on disjoint domains/ranges, and are of different property types (object vs. datatype).

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic' is a subject-area classification for conference topics (a subclass of Topic, alongside other research areas like Cryptography, Mobile Computing, etc.). In iasted, 'Modelling' is a type of pre-conference research activity (subclass of Research, sibling of Simulating). One is a topic/subject category; the other is a research activity. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Both denote post-conference social/leisure activities, but they are not strictly equivalent: edas Excursion is a specific kind of social event, while iasted Activity after conference is a broader category that includes Departure and Full day tour, so they overlap without coinciding.

partOfEvent relates an Event to another Event it is part of, while award relates something (unspecified domain) to an Award. They connect entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and express different relations. In EKAW, 'written By' links a Document to the Person who authored it (domain Document -> range Person). In IASTED, 'need' links a Person to an Item they require (domain Person -> range Item). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so the properties are unrelated.

defaultChoice is a confOf datatype property from Social event / Working event to positiveInteger, representing some numeric choice value. hasStartDateTime is an edas datatype property from ConferenceEvent to dateTime, representing when an event starts. They have different domains, different ranges (positiveInteger vs dateTime), and completely different semantics.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'relatedToEvent' in EDAS links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (the event where the paper is presented). 'technicallyOrganisedBy' in EKAW is a sub-property of 'organisedBy' indicating that something is technically organised by some agent/organisation. They relate different kinds of entities in different ways: one connects papers to presentation events, the other connects things to their technical organisers.

The EKAW 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a Document (an abstract text artefact of an invited talk), while the IASTED 'Tutorial' is an Activity/Lecture (the event itself). They are different categories of entity entirely, so they are not equivalent.

confOf:Banquet is a social event (an activity/occasion where participants dine together), while edas:DiningPlace is a physical place where dining occurs. One is an event, the other is a location; they do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

cmt's `name` applies to both Conference and Person and represents a full name, while Conference's `has_the_first_name` applies only to Person and captures just the first name. The cmt property is broader in domain and scope, so it subsumes the Conference property, but they are not equivalent.

confOf's 'has title' applies to Social event and Working event (e.g., naming a conference session or social event), while edas's 'hasName' applies specifically to Conference entities to capture the conference's full name. The domains are disjoint (Social event/Working event vs. Conference), so these properties relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

These properties are completely different. `endReview` is an object property in cmt with domain Program Committee Chair and range Review, modeling the action of a chair ending/submitting a review. `End_of_conference` is a datatype property in sigkdd with domain Conference and range dateTime, recording the date/time when a conference ends. They differ in arity (object vs datatype), domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'reject Paper' relates an Administrator to a Paper that is being rejected. In edas, 'related To Paper' relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. There is no overlap in the kinds of things they connect or the relations they express.

Programme Brochure (ekaw) is a document listing events of a conference, while Registration form (iasted) is a form for registering attendees. They are different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Conference Chair' in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (a role held by a human, under Person > Chairman). B 'Introduction of speaker' in iasted is an activity/event (under Activity > Conference activity > Introduction) where a speaker is introduced. One is a person/role, the other is an activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Both classes denote the same concept of a person who authors/writes a paper in the conference domain. In cmt, Author is a Conference Member who submits/writes papers and is the domain of 'write Paper' and 'submit Paper'. In iasted, Author is a Speaker (a Delegate role) whose children include various author/presenter subtypes. Despite different ontology structures (cmt models authors as conference members; iasted models them as delegates/speakers), the intended instances—people who author conference papers—coincide. The iasted hierarchy appears to conflate authoring with presenting, but the core denotation of 'Author' as a paper author is the same in both ontologies.

Organising Agency in EKAW is a kind of Organisation (an agent that organises a conference), whereas Book proceeding in IASTED is a kind of Publication (a physical artefact/document). One denotes an organising entity, the other a published item; they share no intended instances.

In the Conference ontology, 'Organizer' denotes a person or committee member who organizes a conference (an agent/role). In EKAW, 'Organisation' denotes an institutional entity (e.g., Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher). These are different kinds of things: an individual organizer vs. an organization. They share a lexical stem but do not have overlapping instances.

Entity A is a person who registered early and paid for conference attendance; entity B is a document (a published paper). They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (Person hierarchy vs Document hierarchy) and denote entirely different things.

Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee (organizing/reviewing body), while property B links a Contribution to an Author. They relate completely different domain and range types and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

Administrative event in confOf is a kind of Event (e.g., camera ready, registration, reviewing, submission events), while Organizing Committee in sigkdd is a kind of Committee (a group of people). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, 'date' is a datatype property with domain Conference and range date, representing the date of the conference itself. In sigkdd, 'Date' has domain Deadline and range dateTime, representing the date of a deadline. These properties relate to completely different subjects (conference vs. deadline) and thus do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

`has Member` (edas) links a Conference to a Person who is a member of that conference, while `is needed for` (iasted) links an Item to a Person who needs that item. The domains (Conference vs. Item) and the intended meanings (membership vs. necessity) are completely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Entity A is a Conference Paper, a written document submitted to a conference, while entity B is a Conference building, a physical place where a conference is held. They belong to completely different domains (documents vs. places) and share no semantic overlap despite the word 'Conference' appearing in both labels.

The property hasReview in ekaw relates a Paper to a Review (a written evaluation of the paper). The property presentation in sigkdd relates a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material/slides). These are different relations connecting different domain and range types, with no overlap in meaning.

These properties are inverses, not equivalent. `isReviewedBy` in EDAS relates a Paper to the person who reviewed it (domain Paper -> range Reviewer/Chair roles). `reviewOfPaper` in EKAW relates a Review document to the Paper being reviewed (domain Review -> range Paper). They connect different entity types in opposite directions: one goes Paper->Reviewer, the other goes Review->Paper. A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent.

A Conference Paper is a written document submitted to a conference, while a Main office is a physical place (sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has_a_commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee (an organizational body associated with the conference). 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (something a person gives, such as a presentation or lecture). The domains (Conference volume vs Person) and ranges (Committee vs Activity/Item) are disjoint, and the relations denote completely different semantics in the conference domain.

In edas, AcceptedPaper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been accepted), while in sigkdd Paper is the general class of all papers. AcceptedPaper is strictly narrower than sigkdd's Paper, so the relation is subsumed_by.

Co chair is a committee role (a person who co-chairs a committee), while Sponsor is a person or organization that provides financial support. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (is_held_in) relates an Activity to the Place/Time where it is held, while property B (submit) relates an Author to a Paper they submit. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

confOf Event covers administrative, social, and working events during a conference, while iasted Conference_activity is a broader category under Activity that includes presentations, lectures, registration, social programs, and technical activities. Conference_activity subsumes Event because it encompasses a wider range of conference-related activities, including those that may occur before or after the main conference events.

The two properties have different domains, ranges, and directions. cmt:assignedByReviewer relates an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (indicating assignment of an external reviewer by a regular reviewer), while ekaw:reviewerOfPaper relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (indicating which paper a reviewer reviews). They do not connect the same kinds of entities in the same direction, so they are not equivalent; nor is one a generalization of the other.
A Steering committee is a committee of people organizing a conference; a Building is a physical place. They share no instances and occupy entirely different parts of the domain.

These two properties denote different temporal milestones in the conference lifecycle. 'is a date of acceptance announcement' marks when paper acceptance decisions are communicated to authors, while 'Start of conference' marks when the conference itself begins. They have different domains (Important dates vs. Conference) and different ranges (date vs. dateTime), and they serve distinct organizational purposes with no overlap in meaning.

confOf:Paper is a written contribution (subclass of Contribution, sibling of Poster and Short paper), whereas ekaw:Paper_Author is a person who writes a paper (subclass of Person, sibling of Conference Participant and Student). One denotes the document/artefact, the other denotes the human author; they are disjoint kinds of entities.

confOf's Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster, Short paper) representing any paper submitted to the conference. EKAW's Camera_Ready_Paper is a specific final-stage paper (child of Paper, sibling of Submitted_Paper, Regular_Paper, etc.). The confOf Paper is more general and is subsumed_by the broader EKAW Paper class, but is not equivalent to the specific Camera_Ready_Paper.

In ontology A, Track is a conference part (sibling of Workshop and Tutorial) and is the range of 'has tracks' from Conference volume. In ontology B, Workshop is a scientific event (sibling of Conference, Session, Track, etc.). These are different concepts: A's Track denotes a thematic division of a conference, while B's Workshop denotes a type of event. They are not the same entity, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

Review preference in Conference ontology denotes a reviewer's preference/assignment for reviewing a topic or submission (with properties linking to reviewers, topics, submitted contributions, and a degree value). Review Rating in edas is a rating assigned to an active paper (with children like Accept Rating, Reject Rating). These are fundamentally different concepts: one captures review assignment preferences, the other captures review outcome ratings.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'belong to a conference volume' links Important dates to a Conference volume, indicating which conference volume a set of deadlines belongs to. In ontology B, 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event, indicating which event a programme belongs to. The domains (Important dates vs Programme) and ranges (Conference volume vs Conference Event) are distinct concepts, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

Conference www is a web document (URL) about a conference, while Conference hotel is a physical building where a conference is held. They share no instances and are unrelated concepts despite both containing the word 'Conference'.

Person in the Conference ontology denotes an individual human being (with first name, last name, email, gender, etc.), while Organization in edas denotes an institutional entity (with subtypes like Academia, Government, Industry, NGO). These are disjoint categories in the conference domain; neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Workshop is an event where work is presented and discussed, sitting under Working event alongside Conference and Tutorial. iasted:Power Point presentation is a specific type of presentation artefact/activity (a slide deck), sitting under Presentation alongside Video presentation. One denotes an organisational event; the other denotes a presentation medium/format. Their intended instances do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'is Written By' relates a Paper to its Author (authorship relation), while 'pay' relates a Person to Money (payment relation). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Invited_speaker is a person (a conference participant who gives an invited talk), while Speaker_lecture is an activity/event (the lecture itself). One is an agent, the other is an event, so they are not equivalent.

Property A (`has a URL`) captures the web address (URL) of a Conference www entity, while property B (`City of conference`) captures the city where a Conference takes place. They denote completely different attributes of a conference, so they are unrelated.

Workshop in edas is an academic event (a type of conference session where papers are presented), while Program Committee in sigkdd is a committee (a group of people reviewing papers). These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement soliciting paper submissions), while Paper Presentation is an academic event where an accepted paper is presented. They are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, 'Program Committee' is a specific committee handling paper reviews, with members linked via hasProgramCommitteeMember. In sigkdd, 'Committee' is a general class with children Best Paper Awards Committee, Organizing Committee, and Program Committee. Thus cmt's Program Committee corresponds to a subclass of sigkdd's Committee, making it subsumed_by.

Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or review preference, capturing the expertise/preferences a reviewer brings to the review process. Property B links a Person to an Item they write (e.g., a paper or document). These are fundamentally different relations: A is about reviewer expertise/preference, while B is about authorship of written items. They do not share the same domain, range, or meaning.

In cmt, Person is a human agent (parent of Chairman, Conference Member, Reviewer, User) with properties like email and name. In iasted, State is a geographic/political region (parent of Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state) that can be occupied by or visited by persons. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties relate different kinds of things in different directions. In EDAS, 'belongsToEvent' links a Programme to a Conference Event (a programme is part of / belongs to an event). In SIGKDD, 'hold' links an ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference (an organization holds a conference). The domains differ (Programme vs. ACM SIGKDD organization), the ranges differ (Conference Event vs. Conference), and the semantic direction is different (belonging-to vs. holding). They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, writePaper specifically relates an Author to a Paper (i.e., the act of authoring a paper). In the Conference ontology, contributes relates a Person to a Conference document, which is a broader category that can include papers, reviews, programs, etc. Since Author is a kind of Person and Paper is a kind of Conference document, writePaper is a more specific property than contributes, making it subsumed_by contributes.

These two properties connect entirely different kinds of things. In edas, 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History (a record of a reviewer's past reviewing activity) to a Reviewer. In ekaw, 'review Of Paper' links a Review (an individual review document) to the Paper being reviewed. The domains differ (Personal Review History vs. Review), the ranges differ (Reviewer vs. Paper), and the direction of the relationship is fundamentally different: one points from a history record to the person who reviewed, the other from a review to the document being reviewed. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The property `need` in iasted relates Person to Item, indicating a person needs some item. The property `design` in sigkdd relates ACM_SIGKDD (an organization/conference entity) to Deadline, indicating the organization designs/sets a deadline. They have different domains (Person vs ACM_SIGKDD), different ranges (Item vs Deadline), and different semantics (needing an item vs designing a deadline). There is no meaningful overlap or subsumption between these two properties.

These properties differ in both structure and semantics. In edas, 'has Submission Deadline' is a datatype property from Call to dateTime, directly capturing a deadline's timestamp. In sigkdd, 'submit until' is an object property from Document to Deadline, linking a document to a Deadline object. The domains differ (Call vs Document), the ranges differ (dateTime vs Deadline), and the property types differ (datatype vs object). They are not equivalent.

`Paper Full Version` in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a document submitted to a conference), while `Departure` in iasted is a subclass of Activity after conference (a post-conference event). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain: one is a written document, the other is a logistical activity. No overlap in intended instances.

University (academic institution where scholars study) and Industry Organization (commercial/industrial entity) are disjoint kinds of organizations. They share only the common parent Organization, but their intended instances do not overlap.

confOf:Person denotes a human being involved in the conference (with subclasses like Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.). iasted:State denotes a geographic/political state with subclasses like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state, and properties like 'is occupied by' and 'is situated in'. These are completely different concepts despite both being able to relate to Person in some properties.
Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while TravelGrant in edas is a type of sponsorship funding. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (is an ending date) relates Important dates to a date, capturing a deadline's end date. Property B (has First Name) relates Person to a string, capturing a person's first name. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs a conference, sitting under Person > Chairman. Conference Proceedings (ekaw) is a published document containing conference papers, sitting under Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings. One is a person role, the other is a document artefact; they share only the word 'Conference' and have no semantic overlap.

Conference announcement is a document type (a conference-related publication artefact), while Computer Networks Sensor Topic is a subject classification under the Topic hierarchy. They belong to completely different parts of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.

In ekaw, 'Social Event' is a broad class covering social activities like Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. In iasted, 'Dinner banquet' is a specific kind of social program activity. The ekaw ontology even has a child class 'Conference Banquet' which would be equivalent to iasted's 'Dinner banquet'. Therefore, 'Dinner banquet' is a specific instance/subclass of the more general 'Social Event' category, making this a subsumed_by relationship.

Both classes denote an organization in the conference domain. In Conference, Organization is a top-level class with subclasses Company and University, and in confOf it has the same subclasses Company and University. The shared label, identical subclass structure, and common domain context strongly indicate the same intended concept.

The property `rejected By` in cmt relates a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, capturing a review decision in the conference management process. The property `has a publisher` in Conference relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher, capturing the publication relationship of proceedings. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types (Paper/Administrator vs. Conference proceedings/Publisher) and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

Presenter university (iasted) is a Building where a presenter's university is located, while Conference hall (sigkdd) is a Place where conference events are held. They denote different kinds of locations with different purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

A Published Paper in edas is an individual accepted/published paper (a specific document with authors, abstract, etc.), whereas a Book proceeding in iasted is a collection/compilation of many papers published as a book. One is a single paper, the other is a whole proceedings volume; neither subsumes the other.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Academia Organization in edas is an organization (subclass of Organization). One denotes a person/role, the other an institution; they share no instances.

In Conference, 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members. In edas, 'hasMember' links a Conference to a Person (e.g., conference attendee/participant). The domains differ (Committee vs Conference) and the ranges differ (Committee member vs Person), so they do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Property A links a Reviewer to a review expertise or preference (a qualification/topic), while property B links a Member PC to a Contribution (the paper being reviewed). They relate entirely different kinds of objects and do not denote the same relation.

Associated Chair in cmt is a leadership role in the conference committee hierarchy (Person > Chairman > Associated Chair), distinct from Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair. Session chair in iasted is a type of Delegate (Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Session chair), i.e., a person attending the conference who chairs a session. These are different concepts: one is a conference-wide organizational role, the other is a delegate-level session role. They do not share a common parent or overlapping instance sets in a way that would make them equivalent or subsuming.

Invited speaker is a conference contributor who delivers an invited talk, while Webmaster is an organizer responsible for the conference website. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties are inverses of each other: cmt:hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (domain Committee -> range Member), while Conference:was_a_member_of relates a Committee member to the Committee (domain Member -> range Committee). They describe the same relationship but in opposite directions, so they are related (inverse) but not equivalent.

cmt:Document is a general class whose children are Paper and Review, representing written artefacts in the reviewing process. iasted:Payment_document is a leaf-level subclass of a general Document hierarchy, with children Bank transfer and Cheque, representing payment-related records. The two classes occupy very different positions in their respective ontologies and denote different kinds of entities; they share only the generic word 'document'.

A Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference, while a Best Paper Awards Committee is a committee that selects best papers. One is an individual role/position, the other is a collective body. They share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relationship.

A is a subject-area topic (Powerline Transmission) under Topic, while B is a type of conference presentation event (Contributed Talk) under Individual Presentation. They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Property A (hasProgramme) links a Conference Event to a Programme (a schedule/document of activities), while property B (is_given_by) links an Activity/Item to a Person (who presents or gives it). They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships: one associates an event with its programme, the other attributes an activity/item to a person. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap exists.

The property 'has Postal Code' in confOf captures the postal code of an Organization or Person, while 'Name' in sigkdd captures the name of a Person. These are completely different attributes with no semantic overlap.

Chair is a committee leadership role (a Committee member who chairs a committee), whereas Sponsor is a Person who provides financial support. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In edas, 'relatedToEvent' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (the event where the paper is presented). In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving a presentation or item). The domains (Accepted Paper vs Person) and ranges (Paper Presentation vs Activity/Item) do not coincide, and the direction of the relation is fundamentally different: one connects a paper to its presentation event, the other connects a person to what they give. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to its title string, while the sigkdd 'Name_of_sponsor' property relates a Sponsor to its name string. These are completely different relations applying to different domain entities (Paper vs. Sponsor) with no overlap in meaning.

Tutorial in ekaw is a type of scientific event / individual presentation (a session where a tutorial is given), while Cd_proceening in iasted is a type of publication (a CD-ROM containing conference proceedings). One is an event, the other is a physical publication artefact; they denote completely different concepts.

confOf Administrator is a system/tool administrator role (sibling to Volunteer, Assistant, etc.), while sigkdd General Chair is the top-level conference organizer. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:Paper is a scholarly document (with authors, reviewers, bids, decisions, subject areas) sitting under Document with sibling Review. iasted:Card is a physical item type (parent Item, sibling Document/Publication/Audiovisual_equipment/Transport_vehicle, child Credit_card) representing things like credit cards or identification cards. They share no domain overlap: one is an academic submission artifact, the other a physical card object. No subsumption holds either.

In cmt, Review is a document (subclass of Document) that is a review of a paper, written by a reviewer. In Conference, Review_expertise is not a review document but rather a property/attribute representing a reviewer's expertise level or area, linked to reviewers and submitted contributions. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a document artefact, the other is an expertise assessment attribute.

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), denoting a type of conference event. edas's 'Operating Topicsystems' is a subclass of Topic, denoting a subject area. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Workshop Chair in ekaw is a person who chairs a specific workshop, sitting under Conference Participant and PC Member. Program Committee member in sigkdd is a person who serves on the program committee of the conference (reviewing papers, accepting/rejecting). These are distinct organizational roles: a workshop chair organizes a workshop, while a PC member reviews submissions for the main conference. Neither subsumes the other in the conference domain.

confOf:Reviewing_event is a temporal/administrative event (a phase in the conference lifecycle when reviewing takes place), whereas sigkdd:Program_Committee is a group of people (a committee). One denotes an event, the other a committee; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

confOf Paper is a general contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short paper), whereas ekaw Demo Paper is a specific subtype of ekaw Paper. The confOf Paper class is more general than the specific Demo Paper, so it is subsumed by the broader ekaw Paper hierarchy rather than being equivalent to Demo Paper.

Entity A is a specific subject topic (Computer Networks Security) under the Topic hierarchy in the edas ontology, while Entity B is a Program Committee, a type of organizational committee in the sigkdd ontology. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Call For Manuscripts in edas is a type of Call (an event/announcement soliciting submissions), while Review in sigkdd is a type of Document (a written evaluation of a paper). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The iasted property 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place or Time (indicating attendance/presence at a location or time), whereas the sigkdd property 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (indicating the act of submitting a paper). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no meaningful overlap in the conference domain.

The cmt Author is a person who writes or submits papers, sitting in the hierarchy Person > Conference Member > Author. The confOf Administrative event is a kind of event (e.g., registration, reviewing, submission events) with temporal/event properties such as follows and parallel with. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (a document/schedule artefact), while hasEvent links an Event to a constituent sub-Event. They relate different kinds of things (Programme vs Event) and represent different relationships (event-to-programme vs event-to-subevent).

These two classes denote entirely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and also Person/TPC Member due to multiple inheritance), representing a type of conference event with two levels (e.g., with a TPC and a secondary review level). In the IASTED ontology, 'One day presenter' is a subclass of Delegate, representing a person who presents at a one-day event. One is a conference/event type, the other is a person/role type. They share no common instances and are unrelated.

Conference_part in ontology Conference denotes structural divisions of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) with properties like has_parts and is_part_of_conference_volumes. Activity in iasted denotes temporal/social activities (Activity_before_conference, Conference_activity) with properties like is_dated_on, is_held_in, is_paid_for. These are different concepts: one is a structural component, the other a temporal/social event. No subsumption holds either, as their extensions do not overlap in the intended domain.

Both are calls in the conference domain, but they are not equivalent. In the Conference ontology, 'Call for paper' is a sibling of 'Call for participation' and other conference documents, denoting a specific call for paper submissions. In edas, 'Call For Manuscripts' is a sibling of 'Call For Papers' and 'Call For Reviews', suggesting that 'Call For Manuscripts' is a distinct concept from 'Call For Papers'. Since the Conference ontology's 'Call for paper' most closely corresponds to edas' 'Call For Papers' (a different sibling), the two entities in this pair overlap conceptually but are not the same intended instances.

Meal Event in edas is a specific Non Academic Event (a meal during a conference, with a menu), a leaf-level subclass. Event in ekaw is the top-level class for all events (scientific, social, etc.). Meal Event is therefore a specialized kind of ekaw:Event, not equivalent.

Paper Author is a person who writes academic papers (subclass of Person in ekaw). Platinum Supporter is a sponsor at the highest sponsorship tier (subclass of Sponzor in sigkdd). These are completely different concepts: one is an author of a paper, the other is a financial sponsor of the conference. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Slide Set denotes a set of presentation slides (a visual aid used during a talk), whereas Review denotes a review document evaluating a submission. They share the parent Document, but their intended instances are disjoint and neither subsumes the other.
hasRelatedDocument relates events/persons to documents, while partOfEvent relates events to events (mereological). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Country in confOf denotes a geographical nation, used as the range of properties linking organizations and persons to their country. Time zone in iasted denotes a temporal region used for scheduling. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person (e.g., authors, reviewers, chairs), while University in confOf is a subclass of Organization (an institution). They denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt Associated Chair is a conference leadership/management role (a Chairman responsible for paper assignment and conference administration), while the iasted Author book proceedings included is a specific type of author whose paper is included in the book (printed) proceedings. These are completely different concepts: one is an organizational role, the other is an author subcategory based on publication medium. They share no instances in common.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and do not denote the same relation.
