Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person (a human participant in a conference), while Conference city in iasted is a subclass of City (a geographic location). These denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

A Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference session), whereas a Student lecturer is a person (a delegate/speaker who is a student). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology hierarchy and denote completely different kinds of entities.

The cmt property hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (people participating in the conference), whereas the confOf property parallel_with links two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Workshop Chair (ekaw) is a person who chairs a whole workshop, whereas Session chair (iasted) is a delegate who chairs a single session. These are distinct organisational roles in a conference, neither subsuming the other.

confOf:Member_PC is a person who serves on a programme committee and reviews papers (subclass of Person, domain of reviewes/expertOn). edas:NumericalReviewQuestion is a review question with a numerical answer (subclass of Review Question, sibling of TextualReviewQuestion). One denotes a human role, the other a questionnaire item; they share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Paper, representing the abstract portion of a paper. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a top-level document class representing the full paper. The cmt Paper Abstract is a more specific concept (a part/aspect of a paper) and is subsumed by the sigkdd Paper class, which represents the complete paper entity.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a type of Chairman/Conference Member), while Accommodation Place is a physical location where people stay. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and domains with no overlap in intended instances.

Contribution 1th author is the first author of a conference contribution (a writing credit), whereas Presenter is someone who presents at a conference (a speaking role). First authors may or may not present, and presenters may not be authors at all (e.g., invited speakers). These are distinct roles in the conference domain, not equivalent and not in a subsumption relation.

Organization in edas denotes an organizational entity (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. Money in iasted denotes a monetary amount with subtypes like Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, Tip. These are completely different concepts: one is an agent/organization, the other is a financial instrument. No overlap in intended instances.

hasReviewHistory connects a Reviewer to their PersonalReviewHistory (a record of past review assignments), while write connects a Person to an Item (a written document). These are different relations: one tracks review history, the other denotes authorship of a document. The domains and ranges differ (Reviewer vs Person, PersonalReviewHistory vs Item), and the intended semantics do not coincide.

Preference in cmt is a class representing a reviewer's bid/preference on a paper, while ACM_SIGKDD in sigkdd is the organizing body (ACM SIGKDD group) that holds conferences, designs deadlines, and searches for sponsors. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Review is a document written by a reviewer about a paper. In Conference, Review preference is a data object representing a reviewer's preference for reviewing a particular topic or submission, with properties like 'has a degree' (int) and 'has a review reference or expertise'. These are completely different concepts: one is the review artifact itself, the other is a preference value associated with the review-assignment process.

These properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges. Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (i.e., associating a conference part with its track/workshop/tutorial chair). Property B links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the person(s) who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). The domains (Conference part vs. Call) and ranges (Track workshop chair vs. Conference Chair/Session Chair/TPC Member) do not correspond, and the relations they express—having a chair vs. being initiated by someone—are semantically distinct. They are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issuing proceedings). In edas, 'is Topic Of' links a Topic to a Conference or Paper (a topic being associated with a conference or paper). The domains (Publisher vs Topic) and ranges (Conference proceedings vs Conference/Paper) are disjoint, and the intended meanings share no overlap.

The confOf 'employed By' property links a Person to the Organization that employs them, a standard employment relation. The iasted 'is designed for' property links an Activity, Money, or Time to an Activity or Person it is intended for. These have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

In ekaw, Person denotes a human being (authors, reviewers, participants, students). In iasted, State denotes a geographic/political entity (with subclasses like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state) that can be occupied, visited, or situated in. These are completely disjoint concepts despite both being top-level classes.
Author is a person who writes papers; Nonmember registration fee is a monetary fee for non-member conference registration. They share no semantic overlap.

A Contributed Talk in EKAW is a scientific event—an individual presentation at a conference. Conference State in IASTED is a state or status of a conference (e.g., preparing, active, post-conference), not an event or talk. They share no instances and belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies.

In the iasted ontology, Card is a physical item (sibling of Publication, Document, Audiovisual equipment, with child Credit card), denoting a tangible object like a credit card. In the sigkdd ontology, Speaker is a subclass of Person (sibling of Listener, Organizator) denoting a human role at a conference. These entities belong to completely different hierarchies (Item vs. Person) and denote entirely different things, so they are unrelated.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'run Paper Assignment Tools' relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of running paper assignment tools), while 'is Written By' relates a Paper to an Author (authorship). They share no semantic overlap.

Presenter (ekaw) is a person who presents at a conference, a subclass of Conference Participant. Listener (iasted) is a Delegate who attends but does not present. These are disjoint categories of conference participants: a Presenter actively gives a talk/presentation, while a Listener is in the audience. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In edas, Attendee is a subclass of Person, denoting a human participant who attends a conference. In iasted, Technical_commitee is a subclass of Delegate, which is itself nested under Place > Building > Conference building, indicating a very different structural context. Despite the label 'Technical commitee' suggesting a committee role, its placement under Delegate (and ultimately under Place) makes its intended meaning unclear and certainly not equivalent to a general Attendee class. The two classes are unrelated.

The edas 'is Topic Of' property links a Topic to a Conference or Paper, indicating the subject matter of those entities. The sigkdd 'presentation' property links a Speaker to a Document, indicating the document presented by that speaker. These are fundamentally different relations: one concerns topic classification, the other concerns a speaker's presented document. They have different domains (Topic vs Speaker) and different ranges (Conference/Paper vs Document), and no meaningful overlap in the conference domain.

Non speaker is a Delegate who does not present (e.g., Student non speaker, Worker non speaker), while Organizator is a Person who organizes the conference (e.g., General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). These are disjoint roles: a non-speaker is an attendee, whereas an organizator is an organizer. No subsumption holds either.

Both are subclasses of Organization/Organisation, but they denote different categories: 'Industry Organization' is a for-profit company, while 'Organising Agency' is an entity that organizes a conference. An industry organization could act as an organising agency, and an organising agency could be an industry organization, so they overlap without being equivalent.

A is a conference document providing information for participants, while B is a type of sponsor (Bronze Supporter). They belong to completely different parts of the ontology hierarchy and denote unrelated concepts.

In iasted, 'Conference city' is a subclass of City, denoting a geographical location where a conference takes place. In sigkdd, 'Conference' is an event with properties like start/end dates, name, and a holding organization. These are completely different concepts: a place vs. an event.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while Workshop Paper is a specific type of paper submitted to a workshop. These are completely different concepts: one is an announcement/invitation document, the other is a research paper artifact.

Written_contribution in the Conference ontology is a specific subclass of Conference contribution (e.g., papers, articles), whereas Document in iasted is a broad superclass encompassing many kinds of documents (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, reviews, transparencies, etc.). Written_contribution is thus a narrower concept subsumed by the more general Document class.

Both classes denote a person who authors a paper in the conference domain. Despite different ontology structures (edas places Author under Person, iasted under Speaker), both share the same label, have Reviewer as a sibling, and represent the same concept of a paper author. The differing hierarchy paths reflect modeling choices rather than different intended meanings.

Submitted Paper is a document type (a paper submitted to a conference), while Committee is a group of people organizing or reviewing for a conference. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'has City' links an Organization or Person to a City (a location attribute). sigkdd's 'can stay in' links a Person to a Place (lodging/accommodation). These are semantically distinct relations: one denotes a location/address property, the other denotes where a person can lodge. They do not share the same domain (confOf includes Organization), range (City vs Place), or intended meaning.

In iasted, 'Conference hotel' is a physical building/place where conference participants stay, subclass of Building. In sigkdd, 'Conference' is an event with start/end dates, a name, and a city, held by an organization. A hotel building and a conference event are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasSubjectArea links a Paper to a Subject Area (topic classification of a paper). In iasted, is_present_in links a Person to a Place or Time (where/when a person is present). The domains (Paper vs Person) and ranges (Subject Area vs Place/Time) are disjoint, so these properties denote unrelated relations.

cmt:User is a person who interacts with the system (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while ekaw:Conference_Session is a scheduled event within a conference (parent Session, siblings Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

A's Reviewer is a subclass of Person, denoting the human agent who performs reviews. B's Review is a subclass of Document, denoting the written review artefact itself. They are disjoint kinds of entities (person vs document), so they are unrelated.

In EDAS, Conference is the event itself (with children like Single/Two Level Conference, properties like dates, topics, country). In EKAW, Conference Participant is a subclass of Person (people who attend a conference). These denote completely different categories of entities: an event vs. a person.
Conference www is a web document (URL) about a conference, while Computer Networks Measurements Topic is a subject classification topic. They share no instances and no semantic relationship.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers (domain of writePaper, submitPaper). In ekaw, Possible_Reviewer is a person who can review papers (range of hasReviewer, domain of reviewerOfPaper). These are distinct roles: an author produces papers, a reviewer evaluates them. The ontologies even separate these roles (ekaw has a distinct 'Paper_Author' sibling under Person). They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In Conference, 'was a program committee of' links a Program committee (the group of reviewers) to a Conference volume (the proceedings/event). In edas, 'hasProgramme' links a Conference Event to a Programme (the schedule of sessions/activities). The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, and the relations denote different things: committee membership vs. having a schedule.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. cmt:markConflictOfInterest relates authors, chairmen, or reviewers to papers to declare a conflict of interest. confOf:parallel_with relates administrative events to other administrative events that run in parallel. They share no domain or range types and express entirely different relations.

Dining Place in edas denotes a location for eating (e.g., restaurants, banquet halls), as indicated by its label and sibling structure under Place. Hotel room in iasted denotes a lodging accommodation within a hotel, with children Single hotel room and Double hotel room. These are distinct concepts: a dining place is not a hotel room, and a hotel room is not a dining place. They share only the generic parent Place, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties have opposite directions: cmt's 'written By' goes from Review to Reviewer (review is written by the reviewer), while confOf's 'reviewes' goes from Member PC to Contribution (PC member reviews the contribution). They are not equivalent. They are also not inverses in a strict sense because the domain/range types differ (Reviewer vs Member PC, Review vs Contribution), so the best classification is unrelated rather than inverse-equivalent.

In ontology A, 'Conference participant' is a direct subclass of Person, denoting any person who participates in a conference. In ontology B, 'Delegate' is a much broader class that has multiple parents including Person, Registration, Conference building, and Conference days, and it has many specialized child classes (Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc.). The iasted Delegate class appears to be a complex modeling construct that encompasses the entire conference participation role including registration and logistical aspects, making it more general than the straightforward 'Conference participant' class in ontology A. The A class is subsumed by the B class.

Both are datatype properties with domain Paper/Contribution (equivalent conference paper concepts) and range string, representing the title of a paper. Same name, same domain, same range, same intended meaning.

In ontology A, 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person, specifically someone who applies to register for a conference (its child is 'Registered applicant'). In ontology B, 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker under a path rooted at Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Speaker, denoting a person who presents/authors a paper at the conference. A conference applicant is someone seeking to register/attend, not necessarily an author of a paper, and an author is not necessarily an applicant. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In ekaw, Regular_Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper accepted for a regular conference track), whereas in sigkdd Paper is the general class of all papers (siblings include Abstract and Review). Thus ekaw:Regular_Paper is strictly narrower than sigkdd:Paper, so it is subsumed_by it.

The iasted 'give' property has domain Person and range Activity or Item, denoting a person giving an activity or item. The sigkdd 'award' property has range Award, denoting the act of conferring an award. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no clear overlap or subsumption between them.

confOf:Regular denotes a non-student, non-member participant (a regular conference attendee), whereas ekaw:Student denotes a person who is a student. These are disjoint concepts: a regular participant is explicitly not a student, and a student is not a regular participant. They do not coincide, nor does one subsume the other.

In ekaw, Person is a general class for all people (authors, reviewers, participants, staff, students). In sigkdd, Sponzor is a class of sponsoring organizations/entities (with subclasses like Gold Supporter, Exhibitor, etc.) that support the conference. These are disjoint concepts: Person denotes individual human beings, while Sponzor denotes organizational entities that provide sponsorship. There is no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event representing conferences, tutorials, and workshops—i.e., scheduled activities in the conference program. ekaw's 'Multi-author Volume' is a subclass of Document representing published collections such as proceedings. One is an event/activity, the other is a physical or digital document; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate different kinds of things in different directions. In Conference, 'belongs to reviewers' has domain Review expertise / Review preference and range Reviewer, i.e., it links a review-expertise or preference record to the reviewer it belongs to. In ekaw, 'hasReviewer' has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer, i.e., it links a paper to its assigned/possible reviewer. They are not the same relation (different domains, different meanings), and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

`has title` relates a social/working event to a string title, while `has End Date Time` relates a conference event to a dateTime end timestamp. They differ in both meaning and range, so they are unrelated.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad superclass of all conference participants (active/passive), while B's 'Demo Chair' is a specific role for chairing demos. They are at different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept; A subsumes B in a general sense, but the reference alignment would not equate them.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a Chairman who assists the Conference Chair in running the conference), while Webmaster is a technical/organizational support role responsible for the conference website. These are distinct roles in conference organization with different responsibilities, not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Property A (has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution) links a Review preference to either a Submitted contribution or a Topic, capturing what a reviewer's preference is about. Property B (isReviewHistoryOf) links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer, indicating which reviewer the history belongs to. They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships: one is about the subject matter of a review preference, the other about ownership of a review history by a reviewer. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap exists.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), whereas Presenter state in iasted is a state/status value (subclass of State), not a person. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote different kinds of entities.

Paper in edas is a document (subclass of Document) representing an academic paper submitted to a conference, with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc. Departure tax in iasted is a monetary tax (subclass of Tax > Money) related to travel costs. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

ekaw:Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while iasted:Conference_Hiker is a subclass of Delegate (a person who attends). Despite sharing the word 'Conference', they denote entirely different things: an event vs. a person.

Property A (has parts) goes from Conference volume to Conference part, while property B (part Of) is the inverse direction (part to whole). A property and its inverse are not equivalent. They are also not in a subsumption relation since they relate things in opposite directions. Thus they are unrelated as an alignment pair.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person restricted to people who are members of a Conference (via member_of_conference). In the Conference ontology, Person is the top-level class for all people involved in the conference (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers, etc.). Thus cmt:ConferenceMember is more specific than Conference:Person, since every Conference Member is a Person but not every Person is necessarily a Conference Member.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote different relations. In edas, 'has Call' links an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., a call for papers). In iasted, 'need' links a Person to an Item (e.g., something a person needs). There is no overlap in intended meaning.

Conference announcement in ontology Conference is a document (subclass of Conference document), while Industrial Session in ekaw is an event (subclass of Conference Session under Event). One is a written artefact, the other is a scheduled session at a conference. They denote completely different kinds of entities.

The two properties relate completely different entities and in different directions. `has_contributions` links a Conference volume to the Conference contributions it contains, whereas `writtenBy` links a Contribution to its Author. They do not share domain or range types, nor do they express the same relation.

Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (assigning a chair role), while property B links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (listing an event on a publication venue). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Participant in confOf is a person who attends the conference (subclass of Person, with children Member, Regular, Student). Fee in sigkdd is a monetary charge (with children Registration fee, Sponsor fee). These are completely different domain concepts: one denotes a person, the other a financial obligation. No subsumption or overlap relationship exists.

Paper Abstract is a short summary/abstract of a paper, whereas Camera Ready Paper is the final, accepted version of a paper ready for publication. These are distinct artefacts in the conference workflow with different content and purpose, so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties that associate a start date with something in the conference domain, but their domains differ: A's domain is Important dates (a container for deadlines), while B's domain is Event. They overlap conceptually in denoting a starting date, but are not equivalent because they apply to different kinds of entities and have different structural roles.

These classes denote entirely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in ontology A is a conference document providing information to participants (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.). 'Review' in ontology B is a review document (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Submission, etc.). Despite both being documents, their intended instances do not coincide: one is informational material for participants, the other is a review of a submission.

Invited talk in Conference is a type of conference contribution/presentation (an event where someone speaks), whereas Invitation letter in iasted is a type of document (a written letter inviting someone). Despite the shared word 'invit-', these are fundamentally different concepts: one is a talk/presentation event, the other is a physical document. They are unrelated.

confOf:Reviewing_event is an administrative event representing the reviewing procedure itself, whereas edas:CallForReviews is a call (announcement) soliciting reviewers or reviews. One is the process/event of reviewing; the other is a communication artifact requesting reviews. They do not share instances.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a leadership role (a Chairman responsible for the conference), whereas in iasted, Reviewer is a Delegate who reviews papers. These are completely different roles in the conference organization, with no overlap in intended instances.

Registration form is a document/form that participants fill out to register for a conference, whereas Author is a person who writes and submits papers. One is an inanimate artefact (a form), the other is a human role. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.
Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Communication Theory Topic is a subject-area classification under Topic. They share no domain overlap.

In the Conference ontology, 'Committee member' is a specific role: a Person who is a member of a Committee, with children Chair and Co chair, and linked by properties 'has members' and 'was a member of' to Committee. In confOf, 'Member' is a broader category under Participant, alongside Regular and Student, representing any conference participant who is a member (e.g., of the conference or organization). Committee member is a specific kind of member, so A is subsumed by B.

These properties are completely different. `location Of` is an object property from Location to Event, indicating where an event takes place. `Name of sponsor` is a datatype property from Sponzor to string, representing the name of a sponsor. They have different domains, different ranges (object vs. datatype), and represent entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (an offer to review), while hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a person). They connect different kinds of entities and represent different relationships in the conference domain.

Both properties concern the reviewing relationship between a paper and a reviewer, but they are inverses of each other: confOf:reviewes goes from reviewer (Member PC) to paper (Contribution), while edas:isReviewedBy goes from paper to reviewer. A property and its inverse are not equivalent; they are related.

confOf Administrative event is a broad category of conference workflow events (camera ready, registration, reviewing, submission, etc.), while edas Call is a document-like artifact (call for papers, call for manuscripts, call for reviews) issued by organizers to solicit submissions. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one is an event/activity, the other is a call document. Their properties and children confirm no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Reviewer is a person who writes reviews (a subclass of Person > Conference Member). In the Conference ontology, Review is a document (subclass of Conference document) that is the output of a review. These are completely different entities: one is the agent (reviewer), the other is the artefact (review). They are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate fundamentally different kinds of entities in different directions. `hasRelatedDocument` (edas) links various entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person) to a Document, capturing a broad 'related document' association. `paperPresentedAs` (ekaw) links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation, capturing how a paper is presented at a conference. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics differ substantially: one is about document association, the other about presentation form. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

Video presentation is a type of presentation/activity in the iasted ontology, while Organizator is a person role in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to completely different hierarchies (Activity vs Person) and denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Administrator is a person role (a subclass of Person responsible for administration), while edas:TwoLevelConference is a kind of conference/event. They belong to completely different parts of the domain hierarchy and denote unrelated concepts.

In ekaw, Review is a document containing a review of a paper, with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review and properties linking it to Paper and Possible Reviewer. In iasted, Form is a broader category of administrative documents (author info form, hotel registration form, registration form). Although both are subclasses of Document, Form is about registration/author information forms, not reviews. The iasted ontology already has a separate Review class as a sibling of Form, confirming they are distinct concepts.

Presentation in the Conference ontology is a specific conference contribution (talk/poster/invited talk) given by an active participant. Item in iasted is a broad top-level class covering physical objects (equipment, cards, documents, publications, vehicles). A Presentation is an event/activity, not a physical item, and their instance sets do not overlap.

Both properties have domain Topic, but their ranges differ: A's range is Conference part (e.g., sessions, tracks, or sub-events of a conference), while B's range is Conference or Paper. The two properties relate Topics to different kinds of entities, so they do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

A's 'Conference document' is a narrower concept than B's 'Document'. A's children (Call for paper, Conference announcement, Conference www, etc.) are all specific kinds of documents produced for a conference, whereas B's 'Document' is a broader class that includes any document (abstracts, flyers, multi-author volumes, papers, etc.). The properties are similar (authors/written by), but A is restricted to conference-related documents while B is more general.

A Conference Banquet is a social/dining event, while a Welcome address is a speech/programmatic activity opening the conference. They are different kinds of conference activities with distinct purposes.

hasCostAmount (domain Sponsorship, range int) captures the numeric monetary amount of a sponsorship, whereas Currency (domain Registration_fee, range string) captures the currency unit (e.g., USD, EUR) of a registration fee. They describe different facets of money (amount vs. currency) and attach to different entities (Sponsorship vs. Registration_fee), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully overlapping.

Entity A is the class Paper (a conference document / contribution), while entity B is the class Author of paper (a person who authored a paper). These are disjoint kinds of entities: one is a document, the other is a person. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

confOf:Volunteer is a person who assists with conference logistics (a helper), placed under Person alongside Administrator, Assistant, Participant, etc. iasted:Author is a delegate who writes a paper and presents it, placed under Speaker > Delegate. The two classes denote completely different roles in the conference domain: a volunteer is not an author and vice versa. They share no instances by definition, so they are unrelated.

`has the first name` is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's given name), whereas `is present in` is an object property from Person to Place/Time (where/when a person is present). They relate completely different kinds of values and have no semantic overlap.

confOf:Member PC is a subclass of Person denoting a reviewer (a committee member who reviews papers), while ekaw:Negative Review is a subclass of Review denoting a specific type of review document with a negative recommendation. One is a person role, the other is a document artefact; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In iasted, 'go through' links an Item to an Activity (e.g., an item undergoing some process/activity). In sigkdd, 'obtain' links an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). The domains (Item vs Author) and ranges (Activity vs Award) are disjoint in the conference domain, and the intended meanings (undergo a process vs receive an award) are unrelated.

Entity A is a Conference (an academic event/organization with volumes, proceedings, publishers, and topics), while entity B is a Speaker (a type of Person who gives presentations). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Registration form in iasted is a document/form that a participant fills out (subclass of Form, sibling of Hotel registration form). Registration Student in sigkdd is a fee category for student registration (subclass of Registration fee, sibling of Registration Non Member, Registration SIGKDD Member). One is a document, the other is a monetary fee; they denote completely different kinds of entities despite sharing the word 'registration'.

The cmt 'name' property applies to Conference and Person entities, denoting their names. The confOf 'has_short_title' applies to Social event and Working event entities, denoting a short title for events. The domains are disjoint (people/conferences vs. events), and the properties denote different concepts (a full name vs. a short event title), so they are unrelated.

confOf:Paper is a Contribution (a written academic submission) with siblings Poster and Short_paper, while ekaw:Flyer is a Document (promotional material) with siblings like Abstract, Review, Programme_Brochure, Web_Site. They denote completely different things: an academic paper vs. a promotional flyer. No subsumption holds between them.

Both properties concern where an event is held, but they differ in type and range: confOf:location is a DatatypeProperty with range string, while iasted:is_held_in is an ObjectProperty with range Place or Time. The iasted property is broader (it can also relate to Time), and the value types are disjoint (literal string vs. Place/Time individuals). They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

Performance Topic is a subject-matter topic (sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), whereas Plenary lecture is a conference activity/event type (a kind of lecture). They denote completely different categories in the conference domain.

Coffee Break is a social/refreshment event in a conference schedule, while Program Committee is an organizational body responsible for paper review. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
A is an object property linking Important dates to a Conference volume, while B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime. They differ in type, domain, range, and meaning.

confOf:Member is a person who is a participant (a human being), while sigkdd:Registration_SIGKDD_Member is a registration fee category (a monetary amount). They belong to completely different hierarchies (Person vs Fee) and denote different kinds of entities.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to a Co chair (a person role). In sigkdd, 'hold' links an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference (an event). They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Workshop (Conference ontology) and Tutorial (iasted ontology) are distinct concepts in the conference domain. A Workshop is a collaborative event, often with its own papers and sessions, while a Tutorial is an instructional/educational session. They are siblings in the Conference ontology (both under Conference part), and Tutorial in iasted is a subclass of Lecture, indicating an educational activity. These are different types of conference activities with different purposes.

Review in Conference is a document produced by evaluating a contribution, while Reviewer in iasted is a person (a kind of Delegate/Speaker) who performs reviews. They denote completely different categories of entities (document vs. person), so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level event representing the entire conference gathering (sibling of Workshop and Tutorial). In ekaw, Conference is similarly the whole conference, while Track is a sub-event within a conference (a session/track of the conference program). These are different concepts: a Track is a part of a Conference, not the same thing. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

The ekaw property 'location Of' is an object property with domain Location and range Event, indicating where an event takes place. The sigkdd property 'Currency' is a datatype property with domain Registration fee and range string, indicating the currency of a registration fee. They relate entirely different concepts in different directions with different types and ranges.

confOf:Contribution is a written scholarly artefact (paper, poster, short paper) submitted to a conference, with properties like abstract, title, keywords, and authored/reviewed relations. edas:ReviewQuestion is a question used within a review form, with subclasses for numerical and textual questions. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A specifically relates a Steering committee to the Conference volume it oversees, whereas property B relates an Organisation or Person to an Event it organises. The domains (Steering committee vs Organisation/Person) and ranges (Conference volume vs Event) differ, and the relations themselves denote different roles (steering/oversight vs general organisation).

The two properties have opposite domain/range directions and are not inverses in a formal sense. In ekaw, 'written By' relates a Document to the Person who authored it (Document -> Person). In iasted, 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item they prepare (Person -> Item). Even if 'prepare' could loosely cover authoring, the direction is reversed, and the properties are not declared as inverse relations. A reference alignment would not treat them as equivalent.

`Conference Chair` in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Person > Chairman), while `Technic activity` in iasted is a kind of conference activity (e.g., a lecture or presentation). One denotes a human role and the other an event/activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate different concepts in different directions. `hasMember` links a Conference to a Person who is a member/participant of that conference. `organisedBy` links an Event to an Organisation or Person that organises it. The domains differ (Conference vs Event), the ranges differ (Person vs Organisation or Person), and the intended relations are distinct: being a member of a conference is not the same as organising an event.

markConflictOfInterest records a conflict of interest between a reviewer/author/chairman and a paper, explicitly preventing the reviewer from being assigned to or bidding on that paper. reviewerOfPaper is a generic relation indicating that a possible reviewer is assigned to or reviews a paper. They are semantically distinct: one denotes a prohibition/conflict, the other a reviewing assignment. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Conference fees in ontology A is a specific category of monetary charges associated with attending a conference. Fee in ontology B is a broader class covering all kinds of fees (hotel fees, registration fees, extra trip fees, etc.), with siblings like Tax and Tip under Money. Since conference fees are a subset of all fees, A is subsumed by B.

Personal Review History in edas is a record of a reviewer's past review activity, while ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd is an organization that holds conferences and designs deadlines. These are completely different concepts with no overlap.

These properties have different domains (Important dates vs Item), different ranges (date datatype vs Time object), and different meanings: one marks the end date of a deadline period, the other indicates a temporal ordering after which an item is sent. They do not denote the same relation.

The two properties have opposite directions: ekaw:authorOf has domain Person and range Document (Person -> Document), while iasted:is_prepared_by has domain Item and range Person (Item -> Person). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. A property and its inverse are not equivalent in the reference alignment.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'hasMember' relates a Conference to a Person (conference membership), while 'send' relates a Person to an Item (sending an item). They connect different entity types in different directions and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

These properties have different domains (cmt:Conference vs confOf:Social_event/Working_event) and different meanings: reviewsPerPaper specifies how many reviews each paper receives in a conference, while defaultChoice is a positive integer associated with social/working events. They do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent.

In edas, Place is a general spatial/location concept with children like Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, and Meeting Room Place, and it serves as the range of hasLocation for Conference Event. In iasted, State is a geopolitical/administrative entity (a subdivision of a country) with children like Conference state, Presenter state, and Sponsor state, and it participates in relations like is_occupied_by, is_situated_in, is_visited_by, and occupy with Person, Building, and City. These are different concepts: one is a general physical location, the other is a political/geographic administrative unit. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear, intended way.

Conference contributor is a broad superclass for anyone who contributes to a conference (authors, speakers, active participants), whereas Workshop Chair is a specific organizational role for a workshop. A workshop chair is not necessarily a contributor in the authorship/presentation sense, and a contributor is not necessarily a workshop chair. The two classes denote disjoint role categories in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a conference paper. In confOf, Paper is a subtype of Contribution (a written contribution to a conference), and in EKAW it is a subtype of Document. The EKAW Paper has many subtypes (Conference Paper, Regular Paper, etc.) and is linked to reviews, reviewers, presentations, and topics, which is consistent with the confOf Paper being a conference contribution alongside posters and short papers. The different parent (Contribution vs Document) reflects modelling style rather than a different intended extension, so the two classes are equivalent.

Property A assigns a name (string) to various entities (Conference, Publisher, Topic, etc.), while property B records the end date/time (dateTime) of a Conference. They relate different kinds of values to different aspects of the domain and do not denote the same relation.

Author in edas is a subclass of Person, denoting someone who writes a paper. Nonauthor registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee charged to non-author registrants. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference www in ontology Conference is a subclass of Conference document, representing a web page/document with a URL. Conference Session in ekaw is a subclass of Session under Event, representing a scheduled session at a conference. One is a document/artefact, the other is an event/activity; they denote completely different concepts.

Both classes represent events in the conference domain. confOf:Event has children Administrative event, Social event, Working event, while edas:ConferenceEvent has children Academic Event, Non Academic Event. Both serve as top-level event classes in their respective ontologies with similar properties (start/end dates). The term 'Conference Event' in edas is the general event concept for the conference domain, matching confOf's 'Event'. Their intended instances overlap significantly as the root event classes covering all conference-related activities.

A's Paper is a document submitted for review (subclass of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions). B's Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline by which authors are notified (subclass of Deadline, sibling of abstract/paper submission deadlines). They denote completely different concepts—a document vs. a date/deadline—with no overlap in instances.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Conference' denotes the academic event (the conference itself), as evidenced by its properties (has Country, has Topic, paper Due On, manuscript Due On) and its children (Single Level Conference, Two Level Conference). In the IASTED ontology, 'Conference building' is a physical place (path: Place > Building > Conference building) where a conference is held, with siblings like Conference airport, Conference hotel, and Conference restaurant. These are entirely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a physical venue. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only weakly related (a conference event happens in a conference building), so 'unrelated' is the appropriate verdict.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing that papers are being solicited, while 'Deadline' in iasted is a temporal entity representing a point in time by which something must be done. They belong to completely different hierarchies (document vs. time) and denote different concepts.

In ontology Conference, 'Invited talk' is a subclass of Conference contribution and Presentation, denoting a type of academic presentation or document. In sigkdd, 'Author' is a subclass of Person > Speaker, denoting a person who writes papers. These are completely different concepts: one is a talk/presentation artifact, the other is a person role. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

cmt:Review is the general concept of a review (with a subclass Meta_Review), while ekaw:Positive_Review is a specific kind of review (a sibling of Negative_Review and Neutral_Review under ekaw:Review). The cmt:Review class is strictly more general, subsuming ekaw:Positive_Review.

Associated Chair is a person/role in the conference committee hierarchy (Person > Chairman > Associated Chair), while Meal Break is a non-academic event during the conference (Conference Event > Non Academic Event > Break Event > Meal Break). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

In cmt, Administrator is a system/organizational role (manages conference details, enables virtual meetings, assigns reviewers) under Person > User, sibling to Author and Reviewer. In sigkdd, Author is a contributor who submits papers and obtains awards, under Person > Speaker. These are distinct domain roles with no overlap in intended instances; an Administrator manages the conference system while an Author writes/submits papers.

Conference Chair in edas is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Person, sibling of Attendee, Author, Reviewer). Conference hall in iasted is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Building, Hotel room). One denotes a human role, the other a location; they share only the word 'conference' and are unrelated.

Dinner banquet is a social event/activity in the conference program, while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. They are completely different types of entities (event vs. person) with no semantic overlap.

In ekaw, Assigned_Paper is a specific stage in the paper workflow: a Submitted_Paper that has been assigned to reviewers (child of Submitted Paper, parent of Evaluated Paper). In iasted, Submission is a broad class covering any submission document, with children like Initial manuscript and Final manuscript, and siblings including Review, Form, Invitation letter, etc. Assigned_Paper is a specialized submission that has entered the review-assignment phase, so it is strictly more specific than the general Submission class.

Property A (writes) has domain Author and range Contribution, expressing the direction author -> paper. Property B (is writen by) has domain Item and range Person, expressing the inverse direction paper -> author. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other (they relate the same types of entities but in opposite directions), the correct relation is unrelated.

A's hasEndDateTime is a datatype property from Conference Event to a dateTime value, representing when an event ends. B's hasEvent is an object property from Event to Event, linking an event to its sub-events. They differ in type, range, and meaning.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. confOf:dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic (what the paper is about), while iasted:is_sent_before links an Item to a Time (a temporal/deadline relation). They share no semantic overlap in domain, range, or intended meaning.

In the EDAS ontology, Document is a broad superclass whose children include Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, and Meal Menu. In the SIGKDD ontology, Paper is a specific subclass of Document. Therefore EDAS Document is strictly more general than SIGKDD Paper, so the relation is subsumes.

confOf:University is an organization where scholars study, while edas:PersonalReviewHistory is a record of a reviewer's review history. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In confOf, 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel. In sigkdd, 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (the presented document). They do not denote the same relation.

The cmt 'name' property applies to Conference and Person entities and returns a string (a name), whereas the edas 'hasCostAmount' property applies to Sponsorship entities and returns an integer (a monetary amount). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Pending Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document submitted but not yet reviewed/decided), while Deadline Paper Submission is a subclass of Deadline (a temporal entity marking the end of the paper submission period). They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Document vs Deadline) and denote completely different kinds of things.

The cmt 'email' is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's email address), while the iasted 'is used by' is an object property from Item to Person (indicating which person uses an item). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; they do not denote the same relation.

Both classes denote the person who chairs the Program Committee in a conference. 'Chair PC' in confOf is a direct child of Person alongside Member PC, and 'Program Chair' in sigkdd is a child of Organizator alongside General Chair and Program Committee member. The labels are synonymous (Chair PC = Chair of the Program Committee = Program Chair), and both ontologies model conference organizational roles, so their intended instances coincide.

edas:Attendee is a person who attends the conference (a general participant). ekaw:SC_Member is a member of the Steering Committee, a specific organizational role under PC_Member. An attendee is not necessarily a steering committee member, nor vice versa; their intended instances do not coincide.

Both are object properties with domain involving money/payment and range Person, expressing the same relationship that a monetary amount/fee is paid by a person. The domain difference (Money vs Registration fee) reflects ontology granularity, but the intended relation is the same.

Property A (has_workshops) relates a Conference volume to its Workshop parts, going from a container to a specific kind of part. Property B (partOfEvent) relates an Event to the Event it is part of, going from a part to its whole (the inverse direction). They differ in both direction and specificity: has_workshops is a specialised has-part relation for workshops, while partOfEvent is a generic part-of relation between events. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

These properties denote completely different relations. 'referenced In' (ekaw) indicates that something (e.g., a paper) is referenced/cited in another work, while 'awarded by' (sigkdd) indicates that an Award is granted by some agent or organization. They have different domains, different meanings, and no overlap in the conference domain.

Both properties link a conference document/contribution to its authors. 'has authors' (Conference document -> Person) and 'written By' (Contribution -> Author) express the same relationship in the same direction, with closely aligned domains and ranges (Conference document ≈ Contribution, Person ≈ Author). The only minor mismatch is generality of Person vs. Author, but the intended relation between a paper and its authors is the same.

The confOf property hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their home page URL), while the ekaw property authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document they authored. They relate a Person to completely different kinds of values and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

Conference announcement is a document type (subclass of Conference document) used to publish information about a conference, while Meal Break is a scheduling event (subclass of Break Event under Non Academic Event). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

A Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while a Proceedings Publisher is an organisation that publishes proceedings (subclass of Organisation in ekaw). One is a person, the other an organisation; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are places under a common Place parent. 'Conference Venue Place' in edas denotes the general venue where a conference is held, while 'Conference hall' in iasted is a specific room/hall within the venue (sibling of Session room, Hotel room, etc.). Thus Conference Venue Place is more general than Conference hall.

The two properties have incompatible domains and ranges. In ekaw, 'scientificallyOrganises' has domain Academic Institution and relates an institution to an event/activity it organizes. In iasted, 'give' has domain Person and range Activity or Item, denoting a person giving (e.g., a presentation or lecture). An institution organizing an event is a fundamentally different relation from a person giving an activity or item, so these properties are unrelated.

Both classes represent the registration activity/event at a conference. confOf's 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event covering participant registration, while iasted's 'Registration' is a conference activity (with Delegate as a child). Both denote the same conference-domain concept of registering participants for an event, despite minor structural differences in how each ontology organizes events vs. activities.

Short_paper in confOf is a type of conference contribution (a short paper submitted/presented), while Best_Research_Paper_Award in sigkdd is a type of award given to a paper. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Contribution vs Award) and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Both classes denote abstract-like textual artefacts associated with papers, but they occupy different positions in their respective hierarchies. In cmt, Paper Abstract is a direct subclass of Paper (a sibling of Paper Full Version), suggesting it is a specific kind of paper artefact. In the Conference ontology, Abstract is a distinct part of a contribution (via 'is the 1th part of'), not a subclass of Paper itself. The extensional overlap is partial: a cmt Paper Abstract instance is a paper-like document, whereas a Conference Abstract is a component of a paper/poster/presentation. They are related but not equivalent.

In cmt, Acceptance is a Decision about a paper being accepted. In confOf, Reception is a Social event (e.g., a reception at a conference). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Paper under Document, but they classify papers along different dimensions. 'Published Paper' denotes a paper that has been published (a status/lifecycle stage), while 'Conference Paper' denotes a paper written for and presented at a conference (a type/category by venue). A published paper could be a conference paper, and a conference paper could be published, but neither subsumes the other: some published papers are not conference papers (e.g., journal papers), and some conference papers are not yet published (e.g., submitted or accepted-but-not-published). The sibling sets confirm different taxonomic axes: edas uses acceptance/status states (Accepted, Rejected, Pending, Withdrawn, Active), while ekaw uses presentation/track types (Demo, Poster, Regular, Workshop, Industrial). Thus they overlap without equivalence or subsumption.

Organisation in EKAW denotes an organisational entity (academic institution, agency, publisher) that organises events and publishes materials. Committee in SIGKDD denotes a specific group of people entrusted with a particular function (awards, organising, programme). A committee is not itself an organisation but rather a body within an organisation; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In the Conference ontology, 'Committee member' is a broad class covering members of any committee (with children such as Chair, Co-chair, and siblings like Track workshop chair). In EKAW, 'PC Member' is specifically a member of the Programme Committee, a particular kind of committee. Since a PC Member is a Committee member but not every Committee member is necessarily a PC Member, A is subsumed by B.

confOf:Banquet is a specific social event (a meal-based gathering), while iasted:Social_program is a broader category of conference activities that includes Dinner banquet, Cocktail reception, Coffee break, etc. The iasted ontology has a child 'Dinner banquet' under Social_program, which corresponds more closely to confOf:Banquet. Therefore, confOf:Banquet is subsumed by iasted:Social_program.

Committee member is a person who serves on a committee, while Meal Event is a non-academic event involving meals. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and share no instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a class denoting a person who is a member of a conference (parent: Person; children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member). Conference_fees in the Conference ontology denotes fees paid for conference attendance, not a person. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Co-author is a specific subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a paper), whereas in sigkdd Author is the general class of authors who submit papers. Thus cmt:Co-author is narrower than sigkdd:Author.

confOf:Assistant is a general helper role (sibling of Volunteer, Administrator) under Person, while sigkdd:Organizing_Committee_member is a specific committee role under Organizator. They do not share the same intended instances: an Assistant is not necessarily an organizing committee member, and vice versa. The labels and hierarchy positions indicate distinct concepts.

In edas, PublishedPaper is a specific paper status (a paper that has been published), sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper. In iasted, Submission is a general document type under Item > Document, with children like Final manuscript and Initial manuscript, and siblings including Form, Invitation letter, Review, etc. A published paper is not the same concept as a submission document; a submission is typically pre-publication, and the iasted Submission class is a broad document category rather than a paper-publication status.

These two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. cmt:assignReviewer has domain Administrator and range Reviewer, representing the action of an administrator assigning a reviewer to a paper. ekaw:reviewerOfPaper has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper, representing the relationship of a reviewer being assigned to a paper. The domains and ranges are swapped (Administrator vs. Possible Reviewer, Reviewer vs. Paper), confirming they describe the same assignment relationship from opposite directions. A property and its inverse are not equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different domain and range types. `detailsEnteredBy` links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered conference details), while `forEvent` links a Call to an Academic Event. They describe different relationships in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

The cmt 'title' property maps a Paper to a string (the paper's title), while the Conference 'is an ending date' property maps an Important dates entity to a date (a deadline end date). They relate completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated concepts.

The ekaw 'organised By' property links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. The sigkdd 'presentationed by' property links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. These are different relations: one concerns who organises an event, the other concerns who presents a document. They have different domains (Event vs Document) and different ranges (Organisation/Person vs Speaker), and there is no indication they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but they operate at different levels of generality. In edas, 'registration Due On' is a specific deadline property whose domain is Conference, denoting the registration deadline. In sigkdd, 'Date' is a more general property whose domain is Deadline, representing the date of any deadline. The sigkdd 'Date' property subsumes 'registration Due On' because registration due date is one specific kind of deadline date, but they are not equivalent since 'Date' applies to all deadlines, not just registration.

Administrative event in confOf is a temporal organizational event (submission, reviewing, registration, etc.), while Computer Networks Sensor Topic in edas is a subject classification topic for papers. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

In ekaw, Conference Session is a scientific event/session where presentations occur (sibling of Demo Session, Poster Session, etc.). In iasted, Conference days is a temporal entity (child of Time, sibling of Deadline and Trip day) representing the time period of the conference. One denotes a scheduled meeting/event session, the other a time interval. They are structurally and semantically distinct concepts despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

confOf:Student is a class denoting a person (a student participant) under Person > Participant, while iasted:Student_registration_fee is a class denoting a monetary amount (a fee) under Money > Fee > Registration fee. They represent completely different categories of entities (a person vs. a monetary fee) and share no semantic relationship.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a kind of Chairman), while Dinner banquet is a social event/activity. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The two properties have different domains (Administrator vs Publisher) and different ranges (Conference vs Conference proceedings), and they denote different actions in the conference domain: printing hardcopy mailing manifests is an administrative task, while issues relates a publisher to the proceedings it publishes. They share no common semantics.

confOf:Company is an organization (a corporate entity, sibling of University), while iasted:Sponzorship is a monetary concept (child of Money, sibling of Fee/Tax/Tip). One denotes an organization, the other a financial transaction/amount; they share no intended instances.

Topic in the Conference ontology denotes a subject area of a conference (e.g., a research topic assigned to conference parts, submissions, and review preferences). Time in the iasted ontology denotes a temporal entity, with children such as Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day, and is used in properties like 'is held in' and 'is present'. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties operate in completely different domains. 'assigned To' in cmt links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper-reviewer assignment). 'topic Covered By' in ekaw links a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (topic coverage). They have different domains (Paper vs Research Topic), different ranges (Reviewer vs Event/Paper), and express entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while the confOf 'hasStreet' property denotes the street address of an Organization or Person. These are completely different attributes despite sharing the string range and overlapping Person domain.

Meeting Room Place in edas is a physical location (a Place) where meetings are held, while Conference Banquet in ekaw is a social event. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities: a place vs. an event. They share no meaningful semantic relationship in the conference domain.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events (e.g., sessions running in parallel), while the edas 'has Related Document' property relates events or persons to Documents. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Student is a person who is a participant attending a conference, while sigkdd:Gold_Supporter is a sponsor at a sponsorship level. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Person/Participant vs. Sponzor) and denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties have domain Reviewer, but their ranges differ fundamentally. cmt's hasBeenAssigned assigns a Reviewer to a Paper (the paper to review). edas's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a record of past reviews). These are different relations: one is about assignment to a paper, the other about a reviewer's review history record. They are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor for a student paper award. They share no instances and belong to entirely different parts of the domain.
confOf Organization denotes an institution (Company, University) with address properties; sigkdd Award denotes a prize (Best Paper Awards). No overlap in intended instances.

Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is a person role - a conference participant who chairs a tutorial. Author attendee cd registration fee (iasted) is a monetary fee for a specific registration type. These are completely different concepts: one is a person, the other is a fee amount. No alignment relation holds.

Both properties share domain Paper and express that a paper is read/reviewed by someone, but the ranges differ in specificity. cmt:readByMeta-Reviewer has range Meta Reviewer (a specialized reviewer role), while edas:isReviewedBy has a broader range including Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, and TPC Member. The cmt property is thus a specialization (subproperty) of the edas property: every paper read by a meta-reviewer is reviewed by someone, but not vice versa. They are not equivalent.

The EKAW 'Accepted Paper' is a document (an artefact) that has been accepted for publication, while the IASTED 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity (an event/action) of accepting a manuscript. One is a document, the other is an activity; they denote fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing that papers are being solicited, while Active Paper is a paper in the submission/decision workflow. They denote completely different things despite both being under a Document hierarchy.

confOf:Person denotes a human agent (with children such as Author, Chair PC, Participant) and is the domain of personal properties like hasFirstName and hasHomePage. edas:ContactInformation is a data object holding address fields (city, street, email, phone, postal code) and is not itself a person. Despite sharing several datatype properties, their intended instances are disjoint, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two properties are completely different in domain, range, and meaning. 'has_the_last_name' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's surname. 'go_through' is an object property from Item to Activity, indicating that an item undergoes some activity. They share no semantic overlap.

A 'Single hotel room' is a type of accommodation for sleeping/lodging, while a 'Conference hall' is a venue for holding conference sessions. They are disjoint kinds of places with no overlap in instances.

Computer Architecture Topic is a subject-area topic (sibling of various technical topics under Topic), while Tutorial Abstract is a document type (subclass of Abstract under Document). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The property 'was a member of' in ontology Conference relates a Committee member to a Committee, capturing membership in a committee. The property 'is signed by' in ontology iasted relates an Item to a Person, capturing authorship or signing of an item. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships (committee membership vs. signing a document/item). They are unrelated.

confOf:Scholar is a subclass of Person (a human attendee such as a student), while sigkdd:Registration_fee is a subclass of Fee (a monetary amount). They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

Published Paper in edas is a document artefact (a paper that has been published), while Research in iasted is an activity performed before a conference (with children like Modelling and Simulating). One is a tangible document, the other is a research activity; they share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Test Only Topic is a subclass of Topic in the edas ontology, representing a subject area for conference submissions (alongside Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). Card in iasted is a subclass of Item, representing a payment card (with child Credit card), alongside siblings like Audiovisual equipment, Document, Publication, and Transport vehicle. These are completely different concepts: one is a conference topic/subject area, the other is a physical payment card. No overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. Property A (has_a_review_reference_or_expertise) relates a Reviewer to their review expertise or preferences, capturing what a reviewer is knowledgeable about or prefers. Property B (hasReview) relates a Paper to a Review written about it. They connect different entity types in different directions and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

Associated Chair in cmt is a conference leadership/administrative role (a Chairman who assists in running the conference), while Regular author in the Conference ontology is a type of conference contributor who writes papers. One is an organizational/committee role, the other is an authorship role. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In EKAW, 'Conference Banquet' is a specific social event (a leaf class under Social Event). In IASTED, 'Social program' is a broad category of conference activities that subsumes multiple social sub-events including 'Dinner banquet' (the IASTED counterpart to EKAW's Conference Banquet). Thus EKAW's Conference Banquet is narrower than IASTED's Social program, so it is subsumed_by it.

Entity A is a person who registered early and paid for a conference; entity B is an activity of accepting a manuscript before a conference. One is a person, the other is an activity — they share no common instances and are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions. In edas, hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper has a rating assigned to it). In iasted, write links a Person to an Item (a person writes an item such as a paper). The domains (Active Paper vs Person) and ranges (Review Rating vs Item) are disjoint, and the relations are conceptually distinct: one is about assigning a rating to a paper, the other about authorship of a document.

Both are non-academic social events at a conference, but a Conference Dinner (a meal event) and a Conference Trip (an excursion) are distinct kinds of social events; they overlap only at the broader Social Event level.

Both relate a person to a written artifact (Person/Author -> Item/Paper), but 'write' denotes authorship while 'submit' denotes the act of sending a paper to a conference. Writing and submitting are distinct activities: one can write without submitting and submit without being the writer. They overlap in the common scenario where an author writes and then submits a paper, but they are not equivalent relations.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'endReview' (cmt) relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review, representing the action of ending/submitting a review. 'presentation' (sigkdd) relates a Speaker to a Document, representing a presentation document associated with a speaker. They connect different entity types in different directions with no overlap in meaning.

Property 'reviews' in Conference relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution (a reviewer reviewing a paper), while 'pay' in iasted relates a Person to Money (a person paying money). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

In the edas ontology, 'Rated Papers' is a subclass of Active Paper, meaning it is a full paper that has received reviews. In the sigkdd ontology, 'Abstract' is a sibling of Paper and Review under Document, representing a short summary document distinct from a full paper. A rated full paper and an abstract are different types of documents and do not share instances.

The cmt 'accept Paper' property relates an Administrator to a Paper, representing the administrative action of accepting a paper for the conference. The ekaw 'paper Presented As' property relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation, representing how a paper is presented at the conference. These are completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

A 'Conference Chair' in cmt is a person who chairs the conference, sitting under Chairman > Person. B 'Two Level Conference' in edas is a type of conference event (a two-level conference structure), not a person. Despite both appearing under a Conference-related hierarchy in edas, they denote completely different things: one is a human role, the other is a conference event type.

Both properties link Author to Paper, but 'hasRelatedPaper' in EDAS denotes a broader association (an author may be related to a paper in various capacities, e.g., co-authorship, reference, etc.), while 'submit' in SIGKDD specifically denotes the act of an author submitting a paper. 'submit' is a narrower action than 'hasRelatedPaper', so they overlap but are not equivalent.

Property A is a datatype property from Person to string capturing a person's first name. Property B is an object property from Item to Item describing what an item is made from. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'topic Covered By' links a Research Topic to Events or Papers, indicating which topics are covered by those events or papers. 'designed by' links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD, indicating who designed a deadline. They have different domains (Research Topic vs Deadline), different ranges (Event/Paper vs ACM SIGKDD), and no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Both classes sit under Paper and represent the final, accepted, camera-ready version of a paper that has been published/included in the conference proceedings. In the conference domain, 'Published Paper' in EDAS and 'Camera Ready Paper' in EKAW denote the same concept: the paper that has gone through acceptance and final revision and is now part of the published record. The sibling structure of EDAS (Accepted, Active, Pending, Rejected, Withdrawn) and EKAW (Submitted, Conference, Demo, etc.) is compatible with this equivalence, as both ontologies partition papers by status/type at the same level.

Property A links a Steering committee to a Conference volume (indicating which conference volume a steering committee oversees). Property B links an Item to a Person (indicating who signed an item). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

Tutorial is a type of conference part/event (a session where a topic is taught), while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies and share no domain overlap.

These properties have different domains and ranges and serve different purposes. `hasAdministrativeEvent` links a Working event to an Administrative event (e.g., a conference containing administrative sub-events). `forEvent` links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to an Academic Event it pertains to. The direction and semantics differ: one is a part-of/containment relation, the other is an about/applies-to relation. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Property A links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee, while property B links a Person to a Building, City, or State. They have disjoint domains and ranges and denote completely different relations in the conference domain.
