The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (paper) they have authored. The sigkdd 'awarded by' property links an Award to some entity that grants it. These are entirely different relations with different domains and different semantics; they share no overlap in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Conference_Banquet is a subclass of Social_Event, denoting a dinner/social gathering held during a conference. In sigkdd, Conference is the main academic event itself, with properties like start/end dates, city, name, and held by ACM SIGKDD. A banquet is a sub-activity within a conference, not the conference itself; the two classes denote completely different kinds of entities.

confOf:Social_event is a subclass of Event with children Banquet, Reception, Trip — it denotes social activities at a conference. sigkdd:Fee has children Registration_fee and Sponzor_fee — it denotes monetary charges. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Committee in the Conference ontology denotes an organizational body (e.g., Program committee, Organizing committee) with members and chairs. State in the iasted ontology denotes a geographic/political state (with children like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state) that can be occupied or visited by persons and situated in places. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'abstract' property links a Contribution to a string (the abstract text of a paper), while the iasted 'done till' property links a Deadline to a date (the date by which a deadline is completed). They relate completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

A is a person role (Presenter under Conference Participant under Person), while B is a physical building (Sponsor company house under Building under Place). They are in completely different hierarchies and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing the call for submissions, while Industrial Paper is a specific type of paper (industrial track). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties relate a person-type entity to a written document in the conference domain, but they differ in scope and direction of generality. cmt:co-writePaper has domain Co-author (a specific sub-type of person) and range Paper (a specific document type), while Conference:contributes has domain Person (more general) and range Conference_document (also more general, potentially including papers, posters, abstracts, etc.). Neither subsumes the other cleanly: co-writePaper is narrower on the domain side but also narrower on the range side, while contributes is broader on both. They overlap (a co-author writing a paper is a person contributing a conference document) but are not equivalent.

These properties are inverses, not equivalents. confOf's 'written By' has domain Contribution and range Author (paper -> author), while iasted's 'write' has domain Person and range Item (person -> paper). They describe the same relationship but in opposite directions. A reference alignment would not equate a property with its inverse.

Organizing committee is a committee of people responsible for organizing a conference volume, while Academic Institution is an organization like a university or research institute. They are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in the conference domain. In cmt, 'has Been Assigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. In sigkdd, 'searched by' links a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. The domains (Reviewer vs Sponsor) and ranges (Paper vs ACM SIGKDD) are disjoint concepts, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a type of working event with Conference and Tutorial as siblings), whereas iasted:One_day_presenter is a person/role (a Delegate subclass, with siblings like Speaker, Listener, Session chair). They denote completely different categories of entities—an event vs. a person—so they are unrelated.

Conference www in ontology Conference is a subclass of Conference document representing a conference website (it has a URL property). Conference hall in sigkdd is a subclass of Place representing a physical location where a conference is held. These are completely different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

In confOf, 'Short paper' is a type of Contribution (a full submission category alongside Paper and Poster), while in sigkdd 'Abstract' is a type of Document (a preliminary summary, sibling to Paper and Review). A short paper is a complete submitted contribution, not merely an abstract/summary document; the two concepts denote different things in the conference domain.

A Program Committee Member is a specific role in a conference (serving on the PC, reviewing papers), while a Conference contributor is a broader category of person who contributes to a conference in various ways (including active participants, invited speakers, and authors). A PC member could be considered a contributor, but the two classes do not have the same intended instances: many contributors (e.g., authors, invited speakers) are not PC members, and the ontologies model these roles differently. They overlap but are not equivalent.

Property A (abstract) has domain Contribution and range string, representing the abstract text of a conference contribution. Property B (Name) has domain Person and range string, representing the name of a person. They relate different kinds of entities (documents vs. people) and denote completely different concepts, so they are unrelated.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Regular Session is a type of session/event at a conference. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

A's 'Conference participant' is a broad superclass covering all participants (with children Active/Passive conference participant), while B's 'OC Member' is a specific role: a member of the Organising Committee (with child OC Chair and siblings like Demo Chair, PC Chair, etc.). They are at different levels of generality and OC Member is not a subclass of Conference participant in ontology A (A has no OC-specific class). The concepts do not coincide, and neither clearly subsumes the other in a way a reference alignment would record.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. In ontology A, 'has_an_expertise' is a datatype property with domain 'Review expertise' (likely denoting an area or topic of expertise). In ontology B, 'hasReview' is an object property with domain 'Paper' and range 'Review', denoting the relation that a paper has a review. They relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is there a subsumption or overlap relationship.

Entity A is a topic class under a taxonomy of conference subject areas (Computer Networks Applications), while entity B is a physical equipment item (a Computer as audiovisual equipment). They belong to entirely different domain hierarchies and share no conceptual overlap.

Both classes represent the subject matter of conference papers and events. confOf:Topic is linked to contributions, PC members, and working events, while ekaw:Research_Topic is linked to papers and events via covers/topicCoveredBy. The properties show the same functional role: topics that papers and events cover. The only difference is the 'Research' qualifier in ekaw, but in the conference domain 'Topic' and 'Research Topic' are used interchangeably to denote the subject area of a paper or event.

The cmt 'Associated Chair' is a person role (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member) responsible for conference organization tasks. The iasted 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a document artifact (under Item > Document) that provides introductory information for a session chair. One is a person, the other is a document; they share only the word 'chair' but denote completely different entities.

confOf:Conference and ekaw:Workshop are distinct types of events. In confOf, Conference is a sibling of Workshop under Working event, while in ekaw, Workshop is a sibling of Conference under Scientific Event. The two ontologies use different taxonomic structures, but the concepts themselves are distinct: a conference is a broader academic meeting, while a workshop is a smaller, more focused event typically associated with a conference. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a way that would be recorded in a reference alignment.

Committee in Conference ontology denotes an organizational body (with subtypes like Organizing committee, Program committee, Steering committee) that has chairs and members. Participant in confOf is a subclass of Person who attends a conference (with subtypes Member, Regular, Student). These are completely different concepts: one is an organizational entity, the other is a person role. No overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Workshop is an academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas iasted:Conference_hotel is a physical place/building where a conference is hosted. They denote completely different categories of entities (event vs. venue), so they are unrelated.

In EKAW, Conference Participant is a subclass of Person, covering all kinds of conference attendees (chairs, presenters, reviewers, etc.). In IASTED, Non speaker is a subclass of Delegate, which is itself a subclass of Building/Conference building, making it a place-based rather than person-based entity. The ontological contexts are fundamentally different, so these classes do not denote the same concept.

Co chair is a generic committee co-chair role (sibling of Chair under Committee member), while Organizing Committee member is a specific role within the organizing committee. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relation: a co-chair could be of any committee (program, organizing, etc.), and an organizing committee member is not necessarily a co-chair. The ontologies model different role granularities with no clear overlap.

These properties have different domains and ranges and represent different relationships. In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to its Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome). In ekaw, reviewOfPaper links a Review to the Paper it reviews. They connect different entity types in different directions and represent conceptually distinct relationships.

The two properties have completely different meanings and ranges. In edas, 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership relation). In iasted, 'is present' relates a Person to a Time (temporal presence). Despite sharing the domain Person, the ranges (Conference vs Time) and intended semantics differ entirely, so they are unrelated.

Free Time Break is a non-academic event during a conference (a scheduled break with free time), while Trip day is a temporal unit (a day on which a trip occurs). One is an event, the other is a time period; they do not share instances.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Conference Event' is a class whose instances are events (academic or non-academic) that have attendees, locations, start/end dates, and programmes. In the EKAW ontology, 'Conference Proceedings' is a subclass of Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings, i.e. a published artefact. One denotes an event/activity, the other a document. They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different categories of entity.

Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing a paper submission deadline, while SignalProcessingTopic is a subject-area taxonomy node. They share no instances and occupy unrelated branches of their ontologies.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Call' denotes a call for papers/manuscripts/reviews (an announcement soliciting submissions to an academic event), while in the EKAW ontology, 'Abstract' denotes a textual abstract document (e.g., an invited talk abstract or tutorial abstract). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Travel Grant in edas is a subclass of Sponsorship, denoting a financial award or grant, whereas Sponsor in iasted is a subclass of Person, denoting an individual or organization that sponsors. One is an award/artefact, the other is a person/agent; they are disjoint kinds of entities.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Best Research Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Coffee Break is a short refreshment break during the academic program, while Conference Trip is an organized excursion/social outing. They are distinct kinds of social/non-academic events with no overlap in intended instances.

In EKAW, Tutorial is a type of Individual Presentation (an event where someone presents at a conference), sibling to Contributed Talk and Invited Talk. In IASTED, Modelling is a Research activity performed before the conference, sibling to Simulating. One is a presentation event; the other is a pre-conference research activity. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In EDAS, 'Conference Session' is a class denoting a scheduled block of events at a conference (an event/session). In EKAW, 'Session Chair' is a class denoting a person who chairs a session. One is an event, the other is a person/role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Property A (has_the_last_name) maps Person -> string, representing a person's surname. Property B (Price) maps Registration fee -> int, representing a monetary amount. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Conference Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion) in ekaw, while Single hotel room is a type of accommodation/place in iasted. They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Attendee in edas is a class of persons (subclass of Person) who attend a conference. Nonauthor registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee charged for non-author registration (subclass of Registration fee under Money). One denotes a person role, the other a financial amount; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in opposite directions. cmt:hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review, while confOf:writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author. The domains (Reviewer vs. Contribution) and ranges (Paper vs. Author) do not correspond, and the relations themselves denote different concepts (review assignment vs. authorship).

These properties describe different relationships. In ekaw, 'volumeContainsPaper' relates a volume (e.g., proceedings) to the papers it contains. In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it. They differ in both domain/range and meaning: one is a containment relation, the other is a presentation/authorship relation.

Paper Full Version is a document (a full-length paper submission), while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a temporal entity (a deadline). They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

In ekaw, Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents (a role). In iasted, Hotel presenter is a Delegate who is specifically presenting at a hotel venue—a more specialized subclass of presenter tied to a particular place/type of event. The iasted Hotel presenter is thus a narrower concept, subsumed by the more general ekaw Presenter.

In confOf, Conference is a kind of event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference event itself. In sigkdd, Program Committee is a kind of committee (sibling of Best Paper Awards Committee and Organizing Committee), denoting a group of people who review papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Co-author is a person who co-writes a paper (subclass of Author in cmt), while Co-chair is a committee member who co-chairs a committee (subclass of Committee member in Conference). They belong to different branches of the Person hierarchy and have different roles: one is an author of a paper, the other is a chair of a committee. No subsumption relation holds between them.

In cmt, 'Conference' denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, accepts hardcopy submissions, has conference members). In iasted, 'Conference activity' is a subclass of Activity whose instances are specific activities during a conference (e.g., Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Registration). These are completely different concepts: one is the conference as a whole, the other is a type of activity that occurs at a conference. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated entities.

Both classes denote members of the (technical) programme committee. In EDAS 'TPC Member' is a Person who can review papers and initiate calls, and in EKAW 'PC Member' is a Possible Reviewer under Person. The labels TPC and PC are standard synonyms for the programme committee in the conference domain, and both ontologies place the class as a reviewing-capable person beneath Person.

The property 'reviews' in the Conference ontology relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution, capturing the paper-reviewing activity. The property 'search' in the sigkdd ontology relates an ACM SIGKDD conference to a Sponsor, capturing a sponsorship-related relation. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

The edas property 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (person membership in a conference), while the sigkdd property 'hold' relates the organization ACM SIGKDD to a Conference it organizes. They have different domains (Person vs. ACM SIGKDD) and different semantics (membership vs. organization/holding), so they are not equivalent.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and capture unrelated information. 'has an expertise' (domain: Review expertise) records the expertise area of a reviewer or review-expertise entity, while 'Name' (domain: Person, range: string) records a person's name. They share no conceptual overlap in the conference domain.

Renting in iasted is an activity (e.g., renting a room or equipment before a conference), situated under Activity > Activity before conference. Author of paper in sigkdd is a person role, situated under Person > Speaker > Author. These denote completely different concepts: an organizational activity vs. a human author role. No overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent happenings in a conference setting, but their scopes differ. confOf's Event is a broad umbrella for administrative, social, and working events (e.g., talks, sessions, receptions), while iasted's Activity is more specifically about conference-related activities (before, during, after the conference) and is heavily tied to logistics like items, money, places, and times. They overlap in the conference domain but their intended instances do not clearly coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Property A (issues) relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings it publishes. Property B (hasUpdatedVersion) relates a Document to another Document that is an updated version of it. They connect entirely different kinds of entities (Publisher→Proceedings vs. Document→Document) and express different relations (publication vs. versioning).

confOf's hasCountry relates Organizations and Persons to a Country (geographic location), while iasted's obtain relates Persons to an Item (something acquired). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; there is no overlap in meaning.

The two properties relate different entities and express different relationships. In cmt, hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its Members (the committee has members). In Conference, was_a_program_committee_of links a Program committee to a Conference volume (the committee served a conference). The domains and ranges differ, and the intended relations are distinct, so they are not equivalent.

The property `relatedToEvent` in edas links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (the event at which the paper is presented), while `write` in iasted links a Person to an Item (a person authoring a written item). They relate completely different kinds of entities and express different relations (presentation-of vs. authorship), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

These two properties are fundamentally different in both type and meaning. In cmt, 'memberOfConference' is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference (expressing that a person is a member of a conference). In sigkdd, 'City_of_conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (expressing the city where a conference takes place). They have different domains, different ranges (object vs. string), and different semantics; they are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

Sponsorship in edas is a specific concept representing a sponsorship arrangement (with a provider organization, cost amount, and currency). Money in iasted is a general monetary amount concept that has subclasses like Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, and Tip. These are different kinds of entities: Sponsorship is an arrangement/relationship, while Money is a monetary value. Although iasted has a subclass 'Sponzorship' under Money, the edas Sponsorship class itself is not equivalent to the general Money class, nor is there a clear subsumption relationship between them.

confOf:Banquet is a social event (e.g., a dinner or reception during a conference), while sigkdd:Speaker is a person who gives a presentation. One is an event, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Entity A is a class representing a written document (a Paper) in the ekaw ontology, with siblings like Abstract, Flyer, and Review. Entity B is a subclass of Person representing a human role (an Author of a paper) in the sigkdd ontology. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a document, the other is a person. They are not equivalent, nor is there a subsumption or overlap relationship.

Conference participant in ontology Conference is a broad superclass of all people who participate in a conference (including active and passive participants). Workshop Chair in ekaw is a specific role under Conference Participant. Thus Conference participant subsumes Workshop Chair.

confOf:Regular is a subclass of Participant (a Person) denoting a regular (non-student, non-member) conference participant. sigkdd:Registration_Student is a subclass of Registration_fee, i.e., a monetary fee amount for student registration. One is a person, the other is a fee; they are disjoint kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of things in different directions. `hasReviewHistory` in edas links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (the history of reviews a person has produced), while `hasReview` in ekaw links a Paper to a Review (a review written about that paper). The domains (Reviewer vs Paper) and ranges (Personal Review History vs Review) are disjoint concepts, so these are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully overlapping relations.

Entity A is an event (a happening or activity in the conference workflow, under Event > Administrative event), while entity B is a deadline (a point in time, under Time > Deadline). They share the phrase 'camera ready' but denote fundamentally different categories: one is the administrative event/process of collecting camera-ready papers, the other is the temporal deadline by which such manuscripts must be submitted. Their positions in disjoint hierarchies (Event vs. Time) confirm they are not the same concept.

Publisher in the Conference ontology denotes an organization that issues conference proceedings, while Money in the iasted ontology denotes a monetary amount with subtypes like Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, and Tip. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, Attendee is a subclass of Person, representing a human participant who attends a conference. In iasted, Record of attendance is a subclass of Document, a physical artefact recording that someone attended. One is a person, the other is a document; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption hierarchy.

The cmt 'email' property captures a person's email address, while the Conference 'has the last name' property captures a person's surname. These are distinct attributes with no overlap in meaning despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string).

Submitted Paper is a document (an academic paper submitted for review), while Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal event (a date by which acceptance decisions are communicated). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies (Document vs. Time) and share no domain overlap.

The confOf 'has Keyword' property links a Contribution to a string representing its keyword(s), while the sigkdd 'Name' property links a Person to a string representing their name. They have different domains (Contribution vs. Person) and denote entirely different relations (paper keywords vs. person names), so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, 'Event' denotes a conference-domain event (scientific event, social event) held at a location and organized by persons/organizations. In iasted, 'State' denotes a geographic/political state (a place), with children like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state, and properties like 'is situated in' and 'is visited by'. These are completely different concepts: one is an occurrence/activity, the other is a geographic entity. No overlap in intended instances.

Social event (e.g., Banquet, Reception, Trip) is an event/activity, while Building is a physical place (e.g., Conference hotel, Conference airport). They are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Poster Paper in ekaw is a specific type of paper (a poster presentation artifact), while Abstract in sigkdd is a document type sibling to Paper and Review. These are different kinds of documents: a poster paper is a full paper category, whereas an abstract is a summary document. They share no overlap in intended instances.

In EKAW, Session is a scientific event (a scheduled block of presentations such as conference sessions, demo sessions, poster sessions). In IASTED, Main office is a physical place (a building/office location), sibling to Conference hall, Hotel room, and Session room. These denote completely different categories—an event versus a physical location—so they are unrelated.

ekaw:Event denotes a conference-domain event (scientific event, social event) with properties like being held in a location, organised by organisations/persons, covering topics, and being part of other events. iasted:City denotes a geographic location/city, with subclasses like Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city, and properties about being situated in or occupied by persons. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In Conference, 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (the expertise level assigned to a review). In edas, 'isReviewHistoryOf' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (the person who performed the reviews). The domains (Submitted contribution vs. Personal Review History) and ranges (Review expertise vs. Reviewer) are entirely different concepts, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

Conference proceedings in ontology Conference is a published volume with ISBN, publisher, and volume number. Topic in confOf is a subject matter that contributions deal with, PC members are experts on, and working events cover. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. 'was a track workshop chair of' links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a chairing role over a conference part), while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the document/slides presented). The domains (Track workshop chair vs Speaker) and ranges (Conference part vs Document) are disjoint, and the relations describe different aspects of the conference domain.

The two properties operate in completely different domains and ranges. 'has Member' (edas) links a Conference to a Person (i.e., conference membership/attendance). 'need' (iasted) links a Person to an Item (i.e., a person needing some item). They share no common domain or range types and express entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs). Hotel room in iasted is a subclass of Place, denoting a physical lodging room. These are completely disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Computer Networks Aapplications Topic' is a subclass of 'Topic' (specifically under 'Computer Networks Topic'), representing a subject area for conference papers. In iasted, 'Trip day' is a subclass of 'Time', representing a temporal concept related to conference trips. They share no common instances, no overlapping semantics, and belong to entirely different parts of their respective ontologies.

In edas, Conference Session is an academic event/session within a conference (e.g. a talk or panel session), with properties relating it to documents and academic events. In iasted, Conference days is a temporal concept under Time, with children like Delegate and One conference day, siblings like Deadline and Trip day. These denote completely different things: a session/event vs. a time period/measurement of conference days.
Contribution co-author is a role for a person who co-authored a conference contribution, while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation/place. They share no domain overlap.

The cmt property 'site URL' (domain Conference, range anyURI) denotes the web address/URL of the conference website, while the sigkdd property 'Name of conference' (domain Conference, range string) denotes the human-readable name/title of the conference. These are fundamentally different attributes: one is a URL locator, the other is a textual name. They share only the same domain (Conference) but express completely different information about that domain.

Extended abstract is a specific type of conference contribution (a short summary or extended abstract of work), while Submitted Paper is a paper that has been submitted for review. These are different concepts: one is defined by its format/length, the other by its submission status. An extended abstract could be submitted or not, and a submitted paper could be a full paper or other type. Their instance sets do not coincide.

In iasted, 'Registation deadline' is a specific subclass of Deadline (sibling to camera-ready, notification, hotel reservation, and submission deadlines). In sigkdd, 'Deadline' is the general class with subclasses for abstract submission, author notification, and paper submission. Thus iasted's Registation_deadline is a specific kind of deadline that is subsumed by sigkdd's general Deadline class; they are not equivalent since one is a leaf specialization and the other is the broader category.

Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (parent Person, siblings Reviewer, Committee member), while Social program is an activity/event during a conference (parent Conference activity, siblings Cocktail reception, Coffee break). They denote completely different categories of entities.

Paper Full Version is a document (a complete paper submitted for review), while Submissions deadline is a temporal entity (a deadline date). They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies (Document vs Time) and share no domain overlap.

Reviewing event in confOf is a subclass of Administrative event under Event, denoting a reviewing procedure/activity in the conference workflow. Conference Participant in ekaw is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference. One is an event/activity, the other is a person role; their intended instances are disjoint and they share no meaningful overlap.

logoURL is a datatype property from Conference to anyURI (a web address for a conference logo image). locationOf is an object property from Location to Event (indicating which event is held at a location). They have completely different domains, ranges, types (datatype vs object), and meanings. No overlap.

The property 'issues' in the Conference ontology relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'is Menu Of' in the edas ontology relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event. These properties connect entirely different domain concepts (publishing vs. meal planning) and share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate different concepts in the domain. `providedBy` connects a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it (financial or material support), while `organisedBy` connects an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. The domains (Sponsorship vs Event) and the intended semantics (providing sponsorship vs organising an event) are distinct, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

In the Conference ontology, Chair is a general committee chair (with a sibling Co-chair, and a property was a committee chair of relating to any Committee). In ekaw, PC_Chair is specifically the chair of the Programme Committee, a single committee type among many chair roles (Demo Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair, Session Chair, etc.). Thus PC_Chair denotes a narrower role: every PC_Chair is a Chair, but not every Chair is a PC_Chair.

Both are non-academic/social events at a conference, but they are not equivalent. In edas, Excursion is a specific kind of social event (sibling to Reception), while in iasted, Social program is a broader category encompassing Dinner banquet, Cocktail reception, Coffee break, etc. An excursion is one type of social program activity, so the two classes overlap but are not equivalent; edas:Excursion is arguably subsumed by iasted:Social_program, but the iasted class also includes things like coffee breaks and registration that are not social events in the edas sense, making 'related' the safest verdict.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of finalizing paper assignments for a conference), while relatedToEvent relates an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (associating a paper with its presentation event). They connect entirely different kinds of entities and serve different purposes.

In ekaw, Session Chair is a person who chairs a session, placed under Conference Participant/PC Member. In iasted, Technical commitee is a Delegate (and notably under Place > Building > Conference building in the path), with siblings like Listener, Speaker, Session chair, etc. The iasted Technical commitee denotes a committee/body or a delegate role, not the same concept as an individual Session Chair. They are not equivalent; no clear subsumption holds either.

submitPaper is an object property relating an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper), while is_an_abstract_submission_date is a datatype property relating Important dates to a date (the deadline for abstract submission). They are different types of property with different domains, ranges, and meanings: one captures an action by an author, the other captures a temporal deadline value.

These properties denote completely different relations. markConflictOfInterest links an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to declare a conflict of interest, preventing the reviewer from bidding on or reviewing that paper. has_been_assigned_a_review_reference links a Submitted contribution or Topic to a Review preference, expressing a review preference reference. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics with no overlap.

The cmt property 'hardcopyMailingManifestsPrintedBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator (indicating who printed hardcopy mailing manifests), while the confOf property 'parallel with' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (indicating scheduling parallelism). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

The property 'is Written By' in edas relates a Paper to its Author (authorship relation), while 'referenced In' in ekaw relates something to where it is referenced (citation/reference relation). These are fundamentally different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

In iasted, Lecturer is a highly specific role in a deep hierarchy (Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer), denoting someone who gives a lecture at the conference. In sigkdd, Speaker is a broad class (child of Person) that subsumes both Author and Invited Speaker, covering anyone who presents. Thus sigkdd:Speaker is more general than iasted:Lecturer; the latter is a specialized kind of speaker (one who delivers a lecture), so the relation is subsumed_by.

confOf Member is a person who is a participant in a conference (subclass of Participant, sibling of Regular and Student). edas Two Level Conference is a type of conference event (subclass of Conference). They denote completely different concepts: a person vs. a conference structure.

cmt's PaperFullVersion is a specific subclass of Paper (a full version as opposed to just an abstract), while ekaw's Paper is the general class of all paper types (regular, demo, poster, etc.). PaperFullVersion denotes a subset of the instances covered by ekaw:Paper, so cmt:PaperFullVersion is subsumed by ekaw:Paper.

Meal Break is a specific non-academic break event during a conference where attendees eat, while Trip day is a temporal concept representing a day associated with a trip. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (event vs. time) and share no instances.

has_title is a datatype property from Social event/Working event to string, assigning a name. listsEvent is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event, listing events in a publication. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

CAD Topic is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area within the EDAS ontology (siblings include various technical topics like Antennas, Cryptography, Mobile Computing, etc.). Best Applications Paper Award is a subclass of Award representing a specific prize given at a conference. These are completely different concepts: one denotes a subject classification, the other denotes an award. No subsumption or overlap relationship exists between them.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'detailsEnteredBy' (cmt) relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while 'hasRelatedDocument' (edas) relates various entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person) to a Document. They share no common meaning in the conference domain.

cmt:readByMeta-Reviewer is a subrelation of ekaw:hasReviewer. Both are object properties with domain Paper, relating a paper to a reviewer. However, cmt's range is Meta Reviewer (a specialized reviewer role), while ekaw's range is Possible Reviewer (the general reviewer class). A meta-reviewer is a kind of reviewer, so every paper read by a meta-reviewer is also a paper that has a reviewer, but not vice versa. Thus readByMeta-Reviewer is subsumed_by hasReviewer.

Accommodation Place in edas denotes a lodging venue (hotel, etc.) where conference participants stay, sibling to Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place. Trip city in iasted denotes a city associated with a trip, sibling to Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city. One is a type of place/building for lodging; the other is a city role in a trip context. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, topicCoveredBy links a Research Topic to the Events or Papers that cover it. In sigkdd, design links an ACM SIGKDD conference to a Deadline. The domains (Research Topic vs ACM SIGKDD), ranges (Event/Paper vs Deadline), and intended meanings are completely disjoint, so no equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap exists.

The edas class 'Accpet If Room Rating' is a subclass of Review Rating (a rating value such as accept/reject), while the sigkdd class 'Review' is a subclass of Document (the review artefact itself). These are completely different kinds of entities: one is a rating category, the other is a document. They share no intended instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In Conference, 'reviews' links a Review to the Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed). In edas, 'isReviewHistoryOf' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (the person who performed the reviews). The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning: Review vs Personal Review History, and Reviewed contribution vs Reviewer. These are not the same relation.

Entity A is a topic (subject area) about computer networks measurements, sitting under Topic > Computer Networks Topic. Entity B is a conference session (a scheduled event) sitting under Event > Scientific Event > Session. These are completely different kinds of things: one is a subject matter, the other is a temporal event. There is no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a type of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Worker_lecturer is a person role (a lecturer, under Speaker > Author > Lecturer). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In iasted, 'One conference day' is a temporal unit (a single day within a conference), placed under Time > Conference days. In sigkdd, 'Conference' is the conference event itself, with properties like start/end dates, city, and name, and it is held by an organization (ACM SIGKDD). A single day is not equivalent to the entire conference event; they are different concepts at different granularity levels.

Paper Abstract is a short summary of a paper, while Poster Paper is a paper presented as a poster. They are sibling subclasses of Paper but denote different artefacts with no overlap in intended instances.

These are different conference-organisation properties. cmt:reviewsPerPaper counts how many reviews are assigned per paper (domain Conference, range int). confOf:minChoice is a scheduling preference setting for social/working events (domain Social_event/Working_event, range positiveInteger). They have different domains, different ranges, and different meanings; they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

confOf Organization is a general class whose children are Company and University, covering all kinds of organizations. edas GovernmentOrganization is a specific subclass of Organization (alongside Academia, Industry, NGO). Thus confOf:Organization is strictly more general than edas:GovernmentOrganization.

Review in Conference is a document (subclass of Conference document) representing a review artifact, while Conference Chair in edas is a person role (subclass of Person) for a conference chair. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'title' in cmt denotes the name of a paper, while 'abstract' in confOf denotes the summary of a contribution. These are distinct attributes of a document and do not denote the same relation.

Conference announcement in ontology Conference is a document (subclass of Conference document) that announces a conference, while Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event (subclass of Event > Social Event). One is a document/artifact, the other is an event/activity. They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Review expertise in Conference denotes a reviewer's expertise level or area, while Money in iasted denotes monetary amounts (fees, sponsorships, taxes, tips). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Conference participant is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person), while Conference activity is an event or activity that happens during a conference (subclass of Activity). One denotes a human participant, the other denotes an occurrence; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Program committee is a committee (a group of people who review papers), while Social program is an activity/event (like a dinner banquet or cocktail reception). They belong to completely different branches of the ontology hierarchy and denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property 'has authors' in Conference relates a Conference document to a Person (authorship), while 'has City' in confOf relates an Organization or Person to a City (location). They connect completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated relationships.

Test Only Topic is a subject-area topic (sibling to Antennas Topic, Communications Topic, etc.) under Topic in edas, denoting a conference subject category. Transport vehicle in iasted is a physical item (child of Item, with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). These denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (hasKeyword) links a Contribution to its keywords (string), while property B (Nation) links a Person to their country/nationality (string). They relate completely different domain entities (Contribution vs. Person) and denote different concepts (keywords vs. nationality), so they are unrelated.

Cheque is a payment document (a financial instrument used to pay for conference items), while Abstract is a scholarly document summarizing a paper. They share only the distant ancestor Document and denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, paperAssignmentFinalizedBy links a Conference to an Administrator, indicating who finalizes paper assignments. In the Conference ontology, issues links a Publisher to Conference proceedings, indicating what a publisher issues. They share no common semantics.

Invited speaker is a conference contributor who delivers an invited talk, while Administrator is a person with administrative responsibilities in the conference tool. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Paper/Regular contribution representing written submission artifacts, but they denote different categories: a full version paper is a complete paper, while an extended abstract is a shorter contribution type. They overlap as conference document types but are not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person, representing a human participant in a conference (with children such as Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member). In iasted, Presentation is a subclass of Conference activity, representing a talk or presentation event (with children such as Power Point presentation, Video presentation). One denotes a person, the other an activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and go in opposite conceptual directions. cmt:assignedByAdministrator has domain Reviewer and range Administrator, expressing that a reviewer is assigned by an administrator. ekaw:hasReviewer has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer, expressing that a paper has a reviewer. They relate different entity types (Reviewer-Administrator vs. Paper-Reviewer) and are not inverses of each other either, since one is about administrative assignment and the other about the paper-reviewer relationship.

cmt:Document is a general artefact class whose direct children are Paper and Review (i.e. conference documents). edas:PersonalHistory is a history/record class whose children are PersonalPublicationHistory and PersonalReviewHistory (i.e. biographical records about a person). The children overlap thematically (publications/reviews) but the classes themselves denote different kinds of entities: a document artefact vs. a personal history record. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other.

These properties have different domains (Deadline vs Conference) and different semantics: 'done till' indicates a deadline date by which something must be completed, while 'Start of conference' marks when a conference begins. They are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

A 'Presenter' in ekaw is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant, a Person). B 'Sponsor state' in iasted is a state (a temporal/phase concept) with siblings like 'Presenter state' and 'Conference state', not a person. These are completely different ontological categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Track workshop chair in Conference is a Person role (a chair of a track/workshop), while Track in ekaw is a Scientific Event (the track itself). One denotes a person, the other an event, so they are unrelated.

Published Paper (edas) classifies a paper by its publication status (accepted/published), while Demo Paper (ekaw) classifies a paper by its presentation type (demo). These are orthogonal dimensions: a demo paper could be published or not, and a published paper could be a demo, regular, poster, etc. Neither subsumes the other, and they are not equivalent.

Conference Dinner is a specific meal event (a single dinner), while Social program is a broader category of conference activities that includes Dinner banquet as a child along with receptions, coffee breaks, lectures, etc. They overlap in topic but are not equivalent: a Conference Dinner would be an instance/sub-concept of a Social program, not the same concept.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs a conference, sitting under Person > Chairman. Coffee break (iasted) is a scheduled activity during a conference, sitting under Activity > Conference activity. One is a human role, the other is an event/activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Property A (is_the_1th_part_of) relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation, indicating that the abstract is a part of the larger work. Property B (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution, indicating authorship. These are entirely different relations: part-whole vs. authorship, with disjoint domains (Abstract vs. Author) and ranges (Paper/Poster/Presentation vs. Contribution).

Both properties connect a Person to a document-like entity they authored/signed, but 'author of' specifically denotes authorship of a scholarly document (Paper, Contribution, etc.), while 'sign' in the IASTED ontology denotes the act of signing an Item, which is broader and may include signing registration forms, agreements, or other items beyond authored papers. They overlap when a person signs a paper they authored, but the intended semantics differ: authorship vs. signing. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

In ontology A, 'Invited talk' is a subclass of Conference contribution and Presentation, denoting the talk event itself. In ontology B, 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a subclass of Abstract under Document, denoting the written abstract document associated with an invited talk. These are related but not equivalent: one is the presentation/activity, the other is the document artefact.

Conference Venue Place is a spatial/location concept (subclass of Place, sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place), denoting where a conference takes place. Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal concept (subclass of Deadline under Time, sibling of various submission/registration deadlines), denoting a date by which hotel reservations must be made. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Country is a geographic entity (domain of hasCountry, range Conference->Country), while Money is a financial entity with children Fee, Sponzorship, Tax, Tip and properties about payment amounts and transactions. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Committee in Conference is a class whose instances are committees (groups/organizations), with children like Organizing committee, Program committee, Steering committee. Organizing_Committee_member in sigkdd is a subclass of Person/Organizator, whose instances are individual people who serve on an organizing committee. One denotes a collective body, the other denotes an individual person; they are at different levels of granularity and do not share instances.

The cmt Author class denotes a person who writes and submits papers, situated under Person > Conference Member. The iasted Student registration fee denotes a monetary fee paid by students for conference registration, situated under Money > Fee > Registration fee. These entities belong to completely different domains (person vs. monetary amount) and share no semantic overlap.

Track in the Conference ontology is a conference part (like Tutorial, Workshop) representing a thematic track within a conference volume. Tutorial in iasted is a specific type of lecture/activity. These are different concepts: a Track is a session/section grouping, while a Tutorial is an instructional event. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

PaperFullVersion in cmt denotes a paper that includes its full content (as opposed to just an abstract), describing the completeness of the document. AcceptedPaper in edas denotes a paper that has been accepted (as opposed to rejected, withdrawn, etc.), describing its review status. These are orthogonal dimensions: a full version paper could be accepted or rejected, and an accepted paper could be a full version or an abstract. Neither subsumes the other and their intended instances do not coincide.

The two properties have different domains: cmt:email applies to Person (an individual's email address), while confOf:contactEmail applies to Contribution (a contact email for a paper/contribution). They relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

The two properties relate to completely different domains and meanings. In cmt, 'title' is a datatype property with domain Paper and range string, representing the title of a paper. In confOf, 'location' is a datatype property with domain Social_event/Working_event and range string, representing where an event is held. They share no semantic overlap despite both being string-valued datatype properties.

Author Not Reviewer is a subclass of Author (a person who wrote a paper but is not assigned as a reviewer), while Invited Speaker is a subclass of Speaker (a person invited to give a talk). These are disjoint roles in the conference domain: one concerns paper authorship, the other concerns delivering an invited presentation. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Both classes concern abstract-like conference artefacts, but they occupy different positions in their respective ontologies. In Conference, 'Extended abstract' is a subtype of Regular contribution (a sibling of Paper), denoting a short contribution submitted to the conference. In ekaw, 'Abstract' is a direct subtype of Document and has specialised children such as Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, making it a broader document category. The ekaw Abstract subsumes more specific abstract types, whereas the Conference Extended abstract is a specific kind of contribution. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

In EDAS, Workshop is an academic event (a standalone workshop event), whereas in EKAW, Workshop Session is a session within a conference (a subdivision of the program). They overlap in topic but denote different concepts: one is an event, the other is a session slot.

A Conference Chair (cmt) is the chair of the entire conference, sitting under Chairman and Conference Member. A Session Chair (ekaw) is the chair of a single session within the conference, sitting under Conference Participant and PC Member. These are distinct roles: a conference chair oversees the whole event, while a session chair manages one session. Neither subsumes the other, and they are not equivalent.

The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (i.e., the author writes a paper). The sigkdd 'presentation' property links a Speaker to a Document (i.e., the speaker gives a presentation based on a document). These are different relations: authorship of a written contribution versus delivery of a presentation. The domains (Author vs Speaker) and ranges (Contribution vs Document) differ, and the intended semantics do not coincide.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of finalizing paper assignments), while relatedToPaper relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (linking a presentation to the paper it presents). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relations.

Conference Venue Place in edas denotes a physical place where conference events are held (a subtype of Place alongside accommodation, dining, and meeting rooms). Sponsor city in iasted denotes a city that provides sponsorship (a subtype of City alongside conference city, presenter city, trip city). These are different concepts: one is a venue/facility, the other is a city acting as a sponsor. They do not share instances or a common intended meaning.

Although both properties have domain Person, their ranges and intended meanings differ. 'contributes' (range: Conference document) denotes authorship or intellectual contribution to a paper, while 'send' (range: Item) denotes the act of transmitting or submitting an item. A person contributing a paper is not the same relation as a person sending an item; sending is a broader, different action that may include submitting but is not equivalent to contributing.

In Conference ontology, 'Information for participants' is a document type (a subclass of Conference document) providing information to conference attendees. In sigkdd, 'Exhibitor' is a type of sponsor (subclass of Sponzor) — an organization or entity that exhibits at the conference. These are completely different concepts: one is an informational document, the other is a sponsor role. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Review preference in the Conference ontology denotes a reviewer's preference or expertise regarding a topic/submission (with properties like degree, review reference, reviewer). Review Form in EDAS denotes a form used to collect review content. These are structurally and semantically different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Written_contribution in the Conference ontology is a document (subclass of Conference document > Conference contribution), denoting a written paper or contribution. Conference in confOf is an event (subclass of Event > Working event), denoting the conference gathering itself. These are completely different categories (document vs. event) with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf Poster is a type of contribution (a presentation format, sibling of Paper and Short paper), while iasted Final_manuscript is a document submission stage (sibling of Initial_manuscript). One denotes a presentation type, the other a final version of a submitted document; their instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate completely different entities and express different relations. In cmt, assignExternalReviewer links a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (assigning someone to review a paper). In sigkdd, presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). The domains (Reviewer vs Document), ranges (External Reviewer vs Speaker), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

edas:Author is a general class for any person who authors a paper, sitting directly under Person with properties like has Related Paper. sigkdd:Author_of_paper_student is a specialized subclass of sigkdd:Author denoting specifically a student author of a paper. The edas Author class is strictly more general than the student-author subclass, so edas:Author subsumes sigkdd:Author_of_paper_student.

Review Rating in edas is a class representing the rating outcome of a paper review (e.g., Accept, Reject), while Time in iasted is a temporal concept (e.g., Conference days, Deadline, Trip day). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, 'Bank transfer' is a kind of Payment document (a financial/payment artefact), whereas in sigkdd 'Abstract' is a scholarly document (a summary of a paper). They belong to completely different parts of the conference domain (payment vs. document) and share no instances.

The property `adjusted By` in cmt relates a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it, capturing a specific action on a bid. The property `has Reviewer` in ekaw relates a Paper to its assigned Possible Reviewer, capturing the assignment of reviewers to papers. They have different domains (Bid vs Paper), different ranges (Reviewer vs Possible Reviewer), and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

In cmt, External Reviewer is explicitly NOT a Reviewer: it is a person assigned to assist another Reviewer, subordinate to and distinct from the Reviewer role. In edas, Reviewer is the primary reviewer role that reviews papers. These are different concepts: cmt's External Reviewer is a helper/assistant reviewer, while edas's Reviewer is the main reviewer. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way given the different modeling of the reviewer hierarchy.

Property A links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a specific type of committee), while property B links a Conference to a Person (a member). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and do not denote the same relation.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Author Not Reviewer' in cmt is a person who authored a paper but is not assigned as a reviewer, sitting under Author > Conference Member > Person. 'Student non speaker' in iasted is a delegate (attendee) who is a student and not giving a talk, sitting under Non speaker > Delegate > Conference building > Building > Place. One is about authorship/reviewing roles; the other is about student status and speaking at a conference. They share no domain overlap.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a Person role - the individual chairing the conference, sitting under Chairman/Person. Organizing Committee (sigkdd) is a Committee - a group of people organizing the conference. One is a single person role, the other is a collective body; they are different kinds of entities at different levels of granularity with no direct overlap.

Conference contributor (Person > Conference contributor) denotes someone who contributes to a conference by authoring papers or presenting, with subclasses like Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author. Listener (Delegate > Listener) denotes a passive attendee who listens but does not present. A listener is specifically a non-contributor, so these are disjoint rather than equivalent or overlapping.

The two properties have opposite directions. In cmt, 'write Review' has domain Reviewer and range Review (a reviewer writes a review). In the Conference ontology, 'reviews' has domain Review and range Reviewed contribution (a review is about a contribution). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not the same relation.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while iasted:Conference_restaurant is a place/building (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel and Conference airport). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

A Published Paper is a paper that has been accepted and published, whereas an Initial manuscript is the first version of a submission before review. They represent opposite ends of the publication lifecycle and do not share instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (a person authoring or contributing a paper). In edas, 'providedBy' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (an organization providing sponsorship). The domains (Person vs Sponsorship) and ranges (Conference document vs Organization) are disjoint, so these properties denote different relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) denoting a kind of conference activity, whereas edas:CommunicationTheoryTopic is a subclass of Topic denoting a specific subject area. They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote completely different concepts.

Conference participant in ontology Conference is a broad class covering all persons who participate in a conference (including active and passive participants, committee members, reviewers, etc.). Program Committee member in sigkdd is a specific type of organizer responsible for reviewing papers. A Program Committee member is a conference participant, but not vice versa, so Conference participant subsumes Program Committee member.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Invited talk in Conference is a type of conference contribution/presentation (a document or event). They denote completely different categories of entities—a role vs. a contribution type—with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, 'Rated Papers' is a subclass of Active Paper under the Paper hierarchy, denoting papers that have received ratings. In sigkdd, 'Review' is a sibling of Paper under Document, denoting a review document written about a paper. These are fundamentally different entities: one is a paper that has been rated, the other is a review artifact. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are object properties with domain Person, but authorOf specifically denotes authorship of a Document (e.g., a paper), while prepare is a broader relation meaning a Person prepares an Item, which could include presentations, documents, or other materials. Authorship is a specific kind of preparation, but not all preparation is authorship, so they overlap without being equivalent.

confOf's 'Submission event' is an administrative event representing the submission of contributions (a process/event), while iasted's 'Deadline hotel reservation' is a specific temporal deadline for hotel booking. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Event vs. Time/Deadline) and denote different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have different domains: A's domain is Sponsorship (a relationship between a sponsor and a conference), while B's domain is Money (a monetary amount). They model different aspects of the conference domain: A captures the cost amount of a sponsorship, while B captures the numeric value of a money object. Since their domains are disjoint concepts, the properties cannot be equivalent.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (the admin who finalizes paper-to-reviewer assignments). In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a lecture or handing out an item). The domains (Conference vs. Person), ranges (Administrator vs. Activity/Item), and intended meanings are completely disjoint.

Microelectronics Topic is a subject-area classification for conference topics (sibling to Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), while Organizing Committee is a committee responsible for organizing a conference. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

ekaw:Paper Author is a subclass of Person denoting someone who authors a paper. iasted:Student lecturer is a very specific subclass of Person (via Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer > Student lecturer) denoting a student who gives a lecture. The iasted hierarchy treats Author as a role of a Delegate at a conference building, and Student lecturer is a narrow specialization of Lecturer, not a general paper author. The two classes do not share the same intended instances: a Paper Author need not be a student or a lecturer, and a Student lecturer is defined by giving a lecture, not by authoring a paper. They are therefore unrelated rather than equivalent or subsuming.

Both are subclasses of Person, but they denote different concepts. cmt:User is a system-level role (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer) covering anyone who interacts with the reviewing system, whereas ekaw:Conference Participant is a domain-level role for people who attend the conference (parent of Demo Chair, Presenter, Session Chair, etc.). A Reviewer is a cmt:User but need not be a Conference Participant, and a Demo Chair is a Conference Participant but need not be a cmt:User. The classes overlap (e.g., an Author who presents) without one subsuming the other.

Both Presenter (edas) and Lecturer (iasted) are subclasses of Author and relate to presenting at a conference. However, iasted's Lecturer is more specific: it has specialized subclasses (Student lecturer, Worker lecturer) and specific sibling types (Plenary lecture speaker, Tutorial speaker), suggesting it covers a particular kind of speaker/presenter. Edas's Presenter is a broader concept for any author who presents, without such fine-grained distinctions. Thus Presenter subsumes Lecturer (Lecturer is subsumed_by Presenter).

Paper Abstract in cmt denotes the abstract content of a paper (a document component), sibling to Paper Full Version. Pending Paper in edas denotes a paper whose review status is pending, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn papers. These are orthogonal classifications: one is about document granularity, the other about review workflow state. Their instances do not coincide.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas iasted:IASTED_member is a person (subclass of Delegate, sibling of Speaker, Listener, etc.). These denote completely different categories—an organizational event versus a conference attendee/member—and share no meaningful overlap.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), representing the conference itself as an occurrence. iasted:IASTED_non_member is a person (subclass of Delegate under Place > Building > Conference building), representing a non-member attendee. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A ('invited by') relates a Reviewer to the Reviewer who invited them, capturing the invitation relationship between committee members. Property B ('presentation') relates a Speaker to the Document they present. They have completely different domains (Reviewer vs Speaker), ranges (Reviewer vs Document), and meanings (invitation vs presentation). There is no overlap or subsumption between these two relations.

Both classes denote the top-level conference chair role. In the conference domain, 'Conference Chair' and 'General Chair' are commonly used interchangeably for the person who oversees the entire conference. In sigkdd, 'General Chair' is a sibling of 'Program Chair' (the head of the program), which aligns with edas where 'Conference Chair' is distinct from 'Session Chair' and 'TPC Member'. The structural positions are compatible: both are the most senior organizer role under Person/Organizator.

Conference www is a web document (a URL/resource) under Conference document, whereas Plenary lecture is an activity/event (a lecture) under Activity > Conference activity > Lecture. They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

Conference participant is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person), while Dining Place is a physical location (subclass of Place). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

Both are conference leadership roles under Person, but Chair PC in confOf is specifically the chair of the Program Committee (sibling of Member PC), while General Chair in sigkdd is the overall conference chair (sibling of Program Chair). These are distinct organizational roles that overlap in being conference leadership positions but do not denote the same concept.

A Tutorial is a hands-on instructional session, while a Plenary lecture is a keynote-style lecture delivered to the entire conference. They are sibling-level concepts under different hierarchies (Individual Presentation vs Lecture) and denote different kinds of activities; neither subsumes the other.

In edas, DiningPlace is a specific subclass of Place (alongside AccommodationPlace, ConferenceVenuePlace, MeetingRoomPlace), representing locations where dining occurs. In iasted, Place is a general top-level class with children like Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, etc. Thus edas:DiningPlace is a more specific concept than iasted:Place, making it subsumed_by iasted:Place.

In ekaw, Session is a broad scientific event category with children like Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session, and Workshop Session. In iasted, Session is a narrower concept: a subtype of Lecture (under Activity > Conference activity > Lecture), with child 'Speaker lecture' and siblings 'Plenary lecture' and 'Tutorial'. The iasted Session corresponds more closely to a specific kind of session (a lecture-like session) rather than the general ekaw Session. Thus ekaw:Session is more general and subsumes iasted:Session.

In edas, Conference is a class representing the conference event itself, with properties like dates, country, topics, and members. In sigkdd, Document is a class for textual artefacts (Abstract, Paper, Review) with properties like submission deadlines and presentations. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. 'is held in' connects an Activity (e.g., a conference event) to the Place or Time where it occurs, whereas 'can stay in' connects a Person to a Place where they can lodge. They share the Place range, but the domains (Activity vs Person) and the intended semantics (event venue vs accommodation) are distinct, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

cmt:User is a person (parent Person) who interacts with the conference management system, with subclasses Administrator, Author, Reviewer. ekaw:Proceedings is a document (parent Multi author Volume) that collects accepted papers. One denotes a human agent, the other a published volume; they share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

Conference Chair is a specific organizational role (the chair of the entire conference), while Late Registered Participant is a person who registered late for the event. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker), while Banquet is a social event. They share no instances and are from entirely different parts of the hierarchy.

The two properties have completely different meanings. In cmt, 'hasConflictOfInterest' indicates that a Person has a conflict of interest with respect to a Document (e.g., a paper they should not review). In the Conference ontology, 'contributes' indicates that a Person contributes a Conference document. These are distinct relations in the conference domain, not synonyms or sub-relations.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In EDAS, 'is Initiated By' links a Call (e.g., a call for papers) to the committee members who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). In IASTED, 'is used by' links an Item to a Person who uses it. The domains (Call vs Item), ranges (committee roles vs Person), and intended meanings (initiating a call vs using an item) do not coincide, so the properties are unrelated.

The two properties have opposite directions. In Conference, 'has_authors' goes from a Conference document to a Person (document -> person). In iasted, 'sign' goes from a Person to an Item (person -> item). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. A reference alignment would not equate a property with its inverse.

The cmt `email` is a datatype property mapping Person to a string email address, while ekaw `authorOf` is an object property mapping Person to Document. They relate different kinds of things (contact info vs authorship) and have incompatible ranges, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (subclass of Person/Chairman), while Hotel is a physical place (subclass of Place). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length submission document in the cmt ontology (Document > Paper > PaperFullVersion), while ComputerArchitectureTopic is a subject-area classification in the edas ontology (Topic > ComputerArchitectureTopic). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote completely different concepts: one is a type of conference paper artifact, the other is a research topic category. No alignment relation holds between them.

Academia Organization is a subclass of Organization, denoting an institution such as a university or research body. Simulating is a subclass of Research under Activity, denoting a research activity (simulation). One is an organization, the other is an activity; they share no domain overlap.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers. In Conference, Presentation is a conference document (an artefact/event), not a person. These are disjoint kinds of entities with no meaningful overlap.

In cmt, Author is a person role (subclass of Conference Member/Person/User) who submits or writes papers. In the Conference ontology, Poster is a type of conference contribution/document (subclass of Conference contribution), not a person. These are completely different categories of entities: one denotes an agent/role, the other denotes an artefact/document type. There is no overlap in intended instances.
