Both properties relate a topic to something it covers, but the ranges differ: A's range is Conference part, while B's range is Event or Paper. These are overlapping but not identical categories, so the properties are related rather than equivalent.

These properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. In cmt, 'hasBeenAssigned' goes from Reviewer to Paper (reviewer -> paper they must review). In edas, 'isReviewedBy' goes from Paper to Reviewer (paper -> reviewer who reviews it). They describe the same review-assignment relationship but in opposite directions, so they are related (inverse) rather than equivalent.

Both properties link a conference event/part to a Topic, with identical range (Topic). The domains (Conference part vs Working event) are closely related conference entities. Both express the same relationship of an event having a topic, making them equivalent in the conference domain.

Property A (has_a_review_expertise) links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise, capturing the expertise level assigned during the review process. Property B (is_given_by) links an Activity/Item to a Person, indicating who presents or delivers the activity. They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference, indicating membership of a person in a conference. In the Conference ontology, has_a_commtitee links a Conference volume to a Committee, indicating that a conference volume has an associated committee. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so they are unrelated.

Conference announcement is a document type (subclass of Conference document) used to announce a conference, while Sponsor company house is a physical building (subclass of Building > Place) where a sponsor company is located. They belong to entirely different domains (documents vs. physical places) and share no semantic relationship.

Paper Full Version is a conference document (a full paper submitted for review), while Overhead projector is an audiovisual equipment item. They belong to completely different domain categories with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties operate in completely different domains and directions. In edas, 'isProviderOf' links an Organization to a Sponsorship (i.e., an organization provides/is a provider of a sponsorship). In sigkdd, 'payed_by' links a Registration fee to a Person (i.e., a registration fee is paid by a person). The domains (Organization vs. Registration fee), ranges (Sponsorship vs. Person), and the underlying semantics (providing sponsorship vs. paying a fee) are entirely different. There is no overlap in what these properties relate.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'has Event' links an Event to another (sub-event relationship). In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person presenting or distributing something). They share no common domain or range types and do not denote the same relation.

The cmt property 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper assignment tools), while the sigkdd property 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Paper is a subclass of Document and has specific subtypes (Accepted, Rejected, etc.), while in sigkdd, Document is a broader class that includes Abstract, Paper, and Review as children. Thus edas:Paper is a specific document type, whereas sigkdd:Document is the general container. The edas:Paper is subsumed by sigkdd:Document.

confOf's Paper is a broad class for any paper contribution (sibling of Poster, Short_paper under Contribution). ekaw's Evaluated_Paper is a specific stage in a paper lifecycle: a paper that has been assigned and evaluated, with children Accepted_Paper and Rejected_Paper. Thus every Evaluated_Paper is a Paper, but not vice versa, so confOf:Paper is subsumed_by ekaw:Evaluated_Paper in the sense that the ekaw class is more specific.

cmt:Person is a broad class covering all people in the system (reviewers, authors, users, conference members, etc.), while sigkdd:Organizator is a specific subclass of Person restricted to organizing roles (chairs, committee members, webmaster). They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since cmt:Person is more general but in a different ontology context, while sigkdd:Organizator is narrower. They overlap only in that both are persons, so the most accurate relation is unrelated (no direct alignment).

Associated Chair is a person who co-chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while Presenter city is a geographic city associated with a presenter (subclass of City in iasted). These are completely different categories - a human role vs. a location - with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Submitted contribution' in the Conference ontology is a document/artefact (a written paper that has been submitted), while 'Reviewing event' in confOf is an event (the reviewing procedure/process). They belong to disjoint branches (document vs. event) and denote fundamentally different kinds of entities, despite the comment of B mentioning 'submitted contributions'.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'startReviewerBidding' in cmt is an action property where an Administrator initiates reviewer bidding for a Conference. 'presentationed_by' in sigkdd relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

The cmt property 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who enables a virtual meeting, while the iasted property 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item they prepare. These are completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes denote members of the Programme Committee. confOf's 'Member PC' is explicitly commented as 'Reviewer' and is a subclass of Person, while ekaw's 'PC Member' is a subclass of Possible Reviewer under Person. The confOf class has roles such as reviewing contributions and expertise on topics, consistent with being a PC member who can serve as a reviewer. ekaw's PC Member has subclasses for various chair roles (PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.), which are committee roles. The labels are near-identical ('Member PC' vs 'PC Member') and both represent the same concept of a Programme Committee member in the conference domain.

confOf:Conference is a class denoting a conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). edas:Presenter is a class denoting a person who presents (subclass of Author, under Person). One is an event, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Bid (cmt) is a bid placed by a reviewer on a paper indicating willingness to review it, while Research_Topic (ekaw) is a subject area covered by events or papers. They share no instances and occupy entirely different parts of the conference-organization domain.

The cmt 'date' property assigns a date to a Conference, while the Conference ontology 'has a volume' assigns an integer volume number to Conference proceedings. They differ in domain, range, and meaning.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Hotel is a place where conference attendees stay. They share no instances and are in completely different branches of their ontologies.

Organizing committee is a committee (a group body) responsible for organizing a conference volume, while Session Chair is a person who chairs a session. One is an organizational entity, the other a role held by an individual person; their instances do not coincide and they are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. In edas, hasMember connects a Conference to a Person (the members/participants of the conference). In iasted, occupy connects a Person to a Building, City, or State (the places a person occupies/stays at). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; there is no overlap or subsumption between them.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (a paper under review for which the person has a conflict), whereas hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country (geographic location). They connect completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

The edas 'is Provider Of' is an object property linking an Organization to a Sponsorship instance, while the sigkdd 'Name_of_sponsor' is a datatype property linking a Sponzor to a string value. They differ in both arity/type and semantic role: one denotes a relationship between organizational entities, the other denotes a name attribute. They are unrelated.

coversTopic relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (what subject matter the paper/event covers), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (the document a speaker presents). They connect different entity types in different directions and express different relationships.

These properties differ in both domain and range and express different relationships. Property A links an Organizing committee (a group/committee entity) to a Conference volume, expressing that the committee organizes that conference volume. Property B links a Person to a Conference, expressing that the person is a member of (e.g., attends or participates in) the conference. The domains (Organizing committee vs. Person) and ranges (Conference volume vs. Conference) are distinct, and the semantics differ: one is about a committee organizing a conference, the other about a person being a member of a conference. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Entity A is a class denoting a person who passively attends a conference (a sub-type of Conference participant under Person), while entity B is a class denoting an academic event (a sub-type of Working event under Event). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

The two properties denote different concepts. 'has Submission Deadline' in edas relates a Call to a dateTime representing the deadline for paper submissions. 'notification until' in sigkdd relates an Author to a 'Deadline Author notification' object, representing the deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance/rejection. They differ in domain (Call vs Author), range (dateTime vs Deadline object), and semantics (submission deadline vs notification deadline).

Entity A is a class denoting a written contribution that has been accepted (a document/artifact), while entity B is a class denoting a deadline for submissions (a time point). These are completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.
Workshop is a conference part/event where papers are presented, while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle. They share no domain overlap.

Accepted_contribution denotes contributions that passed review and were accepted, while Rejected_Paper denotes papers that were rejected. These are disjoint categories of reviewed submissions; they do not overlap, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only trivially related as disjoint siblings under reviewed/evaluated contributions.

Fee for extra trip is a fee for an optional excursion/trip at a conference, while Sponzor fee is a fee paid by a sponsor. These are distinct concepts with different payers and purposes; they only share the generic parent Fee.

Session in ekaw is a type of scientific event (e.g., conference session, demo session, poster session), whereas Program Committee in sigkdd is a type of committee responsible for reviewing papers. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties concern the authorship relationship between papers and authors, but they are inverses of each other: co-writePaper goes from Co-author to Paper, while isWrittenBy goes from Paper to Author. Inverses are not equivalent; they are related.

hasFax is a datatype property relating Person to a string (fax number), while authorOf is an object property relating Person to Document. They share only the domain Person; their ranges and intended meanings are completely different.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and express different relations. 'invited by' in Conference links a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the one who invited them onto a committee/review process), whereas 'written By' in confOf links a Contribution to the Author who wrote it. The domains (Reviewer vs Contribution), ranges (Reviewer vs Author), and semantics (invitation vs authorship) are completely distinct, so they are unrelated.

Conference announcement is a document type (subclass of Conference document) that announces a conference, while Activity after conference is a post-conference event/activity (subclass of Activity with children like Departure and Full day tour). One is a document, the other is an activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated semantics. 'rejectedBy' in cmt links a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while 'parallel_with' in confOf links two Administrative events that occur in parallel. There is no overlap in meaning.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision (alongside Rejection), representing the outcome of accepting a paper. Car in iasted is a subclass of Transport vehicle, representing a physical vehicle. These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes denote web-based resources in a conference context, but they are not equivalent. In ontology A, 'Conference www' is a specific conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) that merely has a URL property. In ekaw, 'Web Site' is a broader document type that can list events and be published by an organisation. The ekaw Web Site is more general and has richer relational properties, while Conference www is a narrower conference-specific web document. They overlap but do not denote the same set of instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In EKAW, presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to the Paper/Abstract being presented (presentation -> paper). In IASTED, give links a Person to an Activity or Item they give (person -> activity/item). The domains differ (presentation vs. person), the ranges differ (paper vs. activity/item), and the relational semantics are distinct: one denotes what a presentation is about, the other denotes what a person gives. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Conference participant is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person), while Research is an activity performed before a conference (subclass of Activity). They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies and denote completely different kinds of entities.

edas:Presenter is a general class for any author who presents a paper, sitting under Author > Person. iasted:One_day_presenter is a specific subtype of Delegate (a conference attendee) who presents for only one day, with siblings like Hotel presenter and Session chair. The iasted class is a narrower concept: every One day presenter is a Presenter, but not vice versa. Thus Presenter subsumes One_day_presenter.

Short_paper in confOf is a type of academic contribution (a short research paper), a sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution. Deadline_Paper_Submission in sigkdd is a temporal deadline (a date) by which papers must be submitted. One denotes a written scholarly artefact, the other a point in time. They share no instances and are unrelated.

The two properties denote completely different actions. In cmt, 'startReviewerBidding' is an administrative action where an Administrator initiates the reviewer bidding process for a Conference. In confOf, 'reviewes' is the relation between a Member PC and a Contribution indicating that the PC member reviews (writes a review for) that contribution. They have different domains (Administrator vs Member PC), different ranges (Conference vs Contribution), and different semantics (starting a bidding phase vs performing a review).

Property A (writePaper) relates an Author to a Paper they author. Property B (is_the_1th_part_of) relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation it is part of. Different domains (Author vs Abstract), different ranges (Paper vs Paper/Poster/Presentation), and different semantics (authorship vs mereological part-of). These are unrelated relations.

Accepted contribution and Rejected Paper are mutually exclusive states of a paper in the review process. One represents contributions that have been accepted, the other those that have been rejected. They are disjoint categories, not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

registrationDueOn is the deadline by which attendees must register for the conference, whereas Start_of_conference is the date/time the conference begins. They are distinct temporal concepts with different semantics, so they are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties that assign a temporal value to a deadline-related entity, but they are not equivalent: A's 'is a starting date' specifically captures the start date of an important date, whereas B's 'Date' is a generic date property on a Deadline. They overlap in the conference domain but neither subsumes the other.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address), while authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document (paper they authored). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and share no semantic overlap.

In the Conference ontology, 'Paper' is a broad class covering regular contributions (including submitted papers). In ekaw, 'Evaluated_Paper' is a specific subclass of Assigned_Paper that has gone through evaluation (with children Accepted_Paper and Rejected_Paper). Thus ekaw's Evaluated_Paper is strictly more specific than Conference's Paper.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and in the relation they express. In iasted, 'is prepared by' links an Item to the Person who prepared it (agent/author relation). In sigkdd, 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the document associated with a presentation). The domains (Item vs Speaker) and ranges (Person vs Document) are disjoint, and the semantic direction is fundamentally different: one is an authorship/preparation relation, the other associates a speaker with a presentation document. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference' is a relatively specific class representing a conference entity that has conference volumes/parts as children. In EDAS, 'Conference Event' is a broad superclass subsuming both Academic Event and Non Academic Event, with properties for attendees, location, programme, and dates. The Conference ontology's 'Conference' denotes a particular conference (an academic event), while EDAS 'Conference Event' is a more general category covering any event associated with a conference, including non-academic ones. Thus Conference is subsumed by Conference Event, not equivalent.

Possible Reviewer is a person who can review a paper (subclass of Person in ekaw), while Departure tax is a monetary tax (subclass of Tax in iasted). These are completely unrelated concepts in different domain areas.

Extended abstract in the Conference ontology is a specific type of conference contribution (a short summary of a paper), situated under Conference document > Conference contribution > Regular contribution. Document in the iasted ontology is a broad top-level class covering many administrative and logistical artefacts (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, mailing lists, visa, etc.). The two classes do not share instances: an extended abstract is not the same concept as the iasted Document category. They are not in a subsumption relation either, since Extended abstract is a contribution type, not a subclass of the broad iasted Document hierarchy.

Entity A is a class denoting a person (a late paid applicant) in a hierarchy of conference applicants and registrants. Entity B is a class denoting a monetary fee (a nonauthor registration fee) in a hierarchy of money/fees. One is a person who registers late and has paid; the other is the fee amount charged to a non-author. They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

In confOf, Conference is the main conference event (parent of Workshop, Tutorial), while in edas, Workshop is a specific type of academic event (sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event). These are different concepts: one is the overarching conference, the other is a workshop event within a conference. They do not share the same intended instances.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Tutorial is an academic activity/event; they denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different domains and ranges. `written By` links a Document to the Person who authored it, while `is paid for` links Money to an Activity or Item it pays for. There is no overlap in the kinds of things related or the relation expressed.

Property A specifically relates a Chair to a Committee they chair, and is a subproperty of 'was a member of'. Property B relates a Person to a Conference they are a member of. They differ in domain (Chair vs Person), range (Committee vs Conference), and meaning (chairing vs general membership). They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since A's range (Committee) is disjoint from B's range (Conference).

cmt:Conference denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, members, logo URL, paper submissions), while iasted:Conference_state is a subclass of State representing the lifecycle state of a conference (e.g., active, ended). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the conference entity, the other is a state attribute of a conference.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In EDAS, 'has Name' is a datatype property from Conference to string, giving the full name of a conference. In IASTED, 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item, indicating that a person obtains an item. They share no semantic relationship.

minChoice in confOf is a datatype property whose domain is Social event / Working event and range is positiveInteger, representing some numeric choice/limit. hasStartDateTime in edas is a datatype property whose domain is ConferenceEvent and range is dateTime, representing a start timestamp. They relate different kinds of entities to completely different datatypes and have no semantic overlap.

Pending Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document submitted for review), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a subclass of Deadline (a temporal entity for abstract submission). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (i.e., a person belonging to the conference). In the Conference ontology, issues links a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a published volume). The domains (Conference vs. Publisher), ranges (Conference Member vs. Conference proceedings), and the nature of the relation (membership vs. publication) are entirely different, so the properties are unrelated.

In ekaw, Track is a scientific event (a thematic session of a conference, e.g., an AI track), whereas in iasted, One conference day is a temporal entity (a day on which the conference occurs). They belong to different ontological categories (event vs. time period) and do not share instances.

In the Conference ontology, Track is a subdivision of a conference volume (a thematic session grouping), with siblings Tutorial and Workshop under 'Conference part'. In confOf, Conference is the top-level event itself (path: Event > Working event > Conference), also with siblings Tutorial and Workshop. Despite the shared siblings, Track denotes a part/session of a conference, while Conference denotes the whole conference event. They are at different levels of granularity and do not share instances.

cmt:ConferenceMember is a subclass of cmt:Person whose instances are people registered with a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). edas:Person is the top-level person class in edas and includes Attendee, Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member, etc. Thus cmt:ConferenceMember is more specific than edas:Person: every conference member is a person, but not every person (e.g., a mere contact or non-registered person) is necessarily a conference member. The children/properties overlap significantly, indicating relatedness, but cmt:ConferenceMember is strictly narrower.

A Workshop is a collaborative academic event with multiple presentations, papers, and sessions, typically a full-day or half-day event. A Tutorial is an individual presentation, a single teaching session. They are sibling-level concepts under different branches of the event hierarchy and do not share instances.

confOf:Topic denotes a subject area of a conference (papers, working events, PC expertise), while iasted:Place denotes a physical location (buildings, rooms, halls). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Written_contribution in Conference ontology is a broad class covering all written contributions to a conference (including regular, submitted, and other types), positioned as a direct child of Conference contribution alongside non-written items like posters and presentations. Conference_Paper in ekaw is a specific subtype of Paper. Written_contribution is more general: it encompasses all written forms of conference contributions, while Conference_Paper refers specifically to papers. The two are not equivalent because Written_contribution includes types that may not be classified as 'Conference Paper' in ekaw's taxonomy, and ekaw's Paper hierarchy has its own broader Paper class that is not aligned with Written_contribution.

Active conference participant is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., gives presentations), while City is a geographic location. These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Regular contribution is a written document type (parent: Conference contribution / Written contribution; children: Extended abstract, Paper), while Talk Event is an event/activity (parent: Academic Event; children: Closing Talk, Welcome Talk). One is a document artefact, the other is a scheduled event, so they do not share instances.

Both classes represent registration fees for conference attendance, sharing the same label, parent class (Fee), and analogous child classes for different attendee categories (author/non-author, member/non-member, student). The sigkdd ontology adds properties (Currency, Price, pay, payed by) that describe how registration fees work, but the core concept—the fee charged to register for the conference—is identical across both ontologies.

In ontology A, 'Conference www' is a subclass of 'Conference document' (a document published on the web about a conference, with a URL property). In ekaw, 'Conference' is a subclass of 'Scientific Event' representing one edition of a conference as an event. One is a document/artefact, the other is an event; they denote completely different categories of things.

Co-author in cmt is a specific kind of author who co-writes a paper, sitting under Author in the hierarchy. Member_PC in confOf is a Program Committee member who reviews papers and has expertise on topics. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one is a paper author, the other is a reviewer/PC member. They share no direct hierarchical or functional relationship.

`hasBiography` is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's biographical text. `writtenBy` is an object property from Document to Person, indicating authorship of a document. They relate different types of entities in different directions and have incompatible signatures, so they are unrelated.
Welcome address is a conference activity (an event/action), while Main office is a place. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

Both are subclasses of Paper, but they represent different classification dimensions. 'Paper Full Version' in cmt contrasts with 'Paper Abstract', distinguishing the complete document from its abstract. 'Regular Paper' in ekaw is one of several paper types by venue/category (alongside Demo, Industrial, Poster, Workshop papers). A full version of a paper could be a regular paper, demo paper, etc., and a regular paper could exist as either a full version or an abstract. They overlap but are not equivalent.

Sponsor (iasted) denotes a person or organization that provides financial support for the conference, while Listener (sigkdd) denotes a person who attends the conference to listen to presentations. These are distinct roles: a sponsor funds the event, whereas a listener is an audience member. Despite both being subclasses of Person, their intended instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who provides sponsorship), while 'is paid in' links Money to a Building (where payment is made). They have different domains, different ranges, and express different relationships in the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference is the conference event/organization itself (with administrators, members, paper assignments, review criteria, etc.). In iasted, Conference_city is a subclass of City, denoting the geographic location where a conference takes place. These are completely different concepts: an event/organization vs. a city. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated entities.

These properties denote completely different relations. In cmt, 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who initiated the reviewer bidding process. In edas, 'isReviewing' links a reviewer role (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to a Paper they are reviewing. The domains (Conference vs. reviewer roles), ranges (Administrator vs. Paper), and semantics (administrative action of starting bidding vs. active reviewing relationship) are entirely different.

confOf:Banquet is a specific kind of social event (a banquet). edas:NonAcademicEvent is a broad superclass covering Break Event, Meal Event, and Social Event. A banquet is a non-academic event, so Banquet is subsumed by NonAcademicEvent, but they are not equivalent since NonAcademicEvent has many other instances besides banquets.

confOf:Workshop is a top-level working event (a whole workshop), whereas ekaw:Workshop_Session is a session within a conference programme (a sub-part of a workshop or conference). The confOf class is strictly more general than the ekaw class, so it subsumes it.

A's Conference is the top-level conference organisation/event, with child Conference volume; B's Conference Dinner is a specific social meal event (Non Academic Event > Meal Event > Conference Dinner). They denote completely different concepts.

These properties denote completely different relations. 'added By' in cmt relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (a social/administrative relation between people). 'occupy' in iasted relates a Person to a Building, City, or State (a spatial/location relation between a person and a place). They have different domains, different ranges, and no semantic overlap.

The property 'is Menu Of' in edas relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (catering domain), while 'presentation' in sigkdd relates a Speaker to a Document (academic presentation domain). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics with no overlap.

The two properties relate completely different things: 'has_tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts, while 'dealsWith' links a Contribution to the Topic it covers. They have different domains, different ranges, and no semantic overlap.

Both are subclasses of Person, but a Conference applicant is specifically someone who applies to attend a conference, whereas a Participant is a broader category covering anyone who participates (including members, regular attendees, students, and potentially chairs, authors, etc.). There is overlap—registered applicants would be participants—but the concepts are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other since applicants may not yet be accepted participants.

In edas, Document is a broad superclass encompassing Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, and Meal Menu—academic-event artefacts. In iasted, Payment document is a specific subclass of Document whose instances are Bank transfer and Cheque (financial instruments). The iasted Payment document is a leaf-level financial concept with no overlap with the edas Document's academic artefact children. They do not denote the same concept, and neither subsumes the other in a way a reference alignment would record.

Conference volume in the Conference ontology denotes a proceedings volume or conference edition that contains contributions, tracks, committees, and important dates. Conference hall in the iasted ontology is a physical place (a room/building) where conference sessions are held, sibling to Building, Hotel room, and Session room. These are completely different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

Acceptance is a subclass of Decision in cmt, representing the outcome of accepting a paper. Company is a subclass of Organization in confOf, representing a corporate entity. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Program Committee Member in cmt is a conference member who serves on the program committee (reviewing papers, etc.), while Speaker in iasted is a delegate who presents at the conference. These are distinct roles: a PC member reviews submissions and is not necessarily a presenter, while a speaker presents work. Their hierarchies and sibling structures confirm they model different concepts. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference 'gives_presentations' specifically relates Active_conference_participant to Presentation, while iasted 'give' relates Person to Activity or Item. The iasted property is more general: its range includes Activity (a superclass subsuming Presentation) and Item, and its domain Person is broader than Active_conference_participant. The Conference property is thus a specialization (subsumed_by) of the iasted property.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference Banquet in ekaw is a social event. They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different things: a person vs. an event.

The two properties have different domains and ranges of application. confOf's 'has title' applies to Social events and Working events (e.g., conferences, sessions, social events), while sigkdd's 'Name_of_conference' is specifically about naming a Conference. Although both map to string, 'has title' is a general titling property for events, whereas 'Name_of_conference' is a narrower property restricted to conference names. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since 'has title' covers non-conference events and 'Name_of_conference' is conference-specific.

In EDAS, Break Event is a specific kind of non-academic event covering coffee breaks, free time, and meal breaks. In EKAW, Social Event denotes organized social activities like banquets and trips. A break event is not the same concept as a social event; they are distinct subcategories of non-scientific conference events with different intended instances.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document (a textual artefact providing information to conference attendees). 'Simulating' in the iasted ontology is a research activity performed before a conference. One is a document/information resource, the other is a scientific activity. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Both classes represent non-author/non-member registration fees under a common parent 'Registration fee'. However, 'Nonauthor registration fee' in iasted is specifically for non-authors (which could still be members), while 'Registration Non Member' in sigkdd is for non-members (who could still be authors). These are distinct categories that overlap (a non-author who is also a non-member) but are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who is an author of a paper. In ekaw, 'Paper Author' is a direct subclass of Person, while in sigkdd 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author (under Speaker under Person). Despite the different hierarchy depths, the intended instances coincide: people who authored a paper. The sigkdd hierarchy places Author under Speaker (a domain-specific modeling choice), but 'Author of paper' specifically captures paper authorship, matching ekaw's 'Paper Author'.

These properties operate on different domains and ranges with different semantics. 'is Initiated By' has domain Call (e.g., call for papers, call for reviews, call for participation) and range persons who initiate that call (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). 'organised By' has domain Event and range Organisation or Person. A Call is not the same as an Event, and initiating a call (e.g., sending out a call for papers) is a different relation than organising an event (managing its logistics/execution). The relations are semantically distinct.

The property 'initiates' in edas relates conference roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call (e.g., call for papers/participation), while 'presentation' in sigkdd relates a Speaker to a Document they present. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and they do not overlap in meaning.

A is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant in ekaw). B is a building/place (subclass of Building in iasted) where a presenter stays. Despite sharing the word 'Presenter', they denote completely different categories: a person vs. a physical location.

The two properties relate completely different entities. `hasAuthor` links a Paper to its Author (a person who wrote the paper), while `hasTopic` links a Paper (or Conference) to a Topic (a subject area). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

confOf's Working event is a specific kind of event (parent Event, siblings Social event and Administrative event), covering Conference, Tutorial, Workshop. ekaw's Event is the top-level event class with children Scientific Event and Social Event. Working event is a specialization of the general Event concept, not equivalent to it.

confOf 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper) they have authored. ekaw 'reviewWrittenBy' relates a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote that review. These are different relations: one is about authoring a paper, the other about writing a review. They connect different domain and range types and are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

Contribution in confOf denotes a scholarly submission (Paper, Poster, Short paper) authored and reviewed in the conference, while Sponzor in sigkdd denotes a financial sponsor (Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor). Their instances, properties, and children are completely disjoint; there is no overlap or subsumption.

confOf:Social_event is a subclass of Event with children like Banquet, Reception, Trip, denoting social activities in a conference. iasted:Form is a subclass of Document with children like Author information form, Hotel registration form, Registration form, denoting administrative documents. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Numerical Review Question is a type of review question (a question asked in a review form, with sibling Textual Review Question), whereas Negative Review is a review document with a negative verdict (sibling of Positive/Neutral Review). One is a question item, the other is a review document; they denote completely different things.

The cmt 'hasConferenceMember' links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person who is a member of the conference). The Conference ontology 'has_parts' links a Conference volume to a Conference part (a structural component/sub-event of a publication volume). One relates a conference to people/members; the other relates a conference volume to its constituent parts. They operate on different domain and range types and express fundamentally different relationships.

An Organizational Meeting is an administrative/coordination meeting for conference organizers, while a Tutorial is an instructional lecture teaching attendees a specific topic. They serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain: one is for planning and coordination, the other is an educational academic event. Their positions in their respective hierarchies confirm this distinction—Organizational Meeting is a sibling of Paper Presentation and Workshop under Academic Event, while Tutorial is a sibling of Plenary lecture under Lecture.

Property A links a conference volume to its program committee (a specific committee role), while property B links an event to the organisation or person that organises it. They relate different kinds of subjects to different kinds of objects and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event involving travel to/from the conference venue, while Coffee break in iasted is a short break activity during the conference program. They denote different kinds of things: one is a trip, the other is a brief refreshment pause. No subsumption holds between them.

Rejected_Paper is a specific outcome class (a paper that has been evaluated and rejected), sitting deep in a review-process hierarchy (Document > Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper > Evaluated Paper > Rejected Paper). Initial_manuscipt is the initial version of a submission document, a sibling of Final_manuscript, with no evaluation or acceptance/rejection semantics. A rejected paper is not the same concept as an initial manuscript; they occupy different positions in the document lifecycle and neither subsumes the other.
A is a person who registered early and paid for conference attendance; B is a paper awaiting a decision. Different domains (person vs document) and no overlap.

confOf:Paper is a specific type of contribution (a written paper submitted to a conference), while iasted:Submission is a broader document category encompassing various submitted items (final manuscripts, initial manuscripts, reviews, forms, etc.). They overlap in the conference domain since a Paper is a kind of Submission, but iasted:Submission includes many non-paper documents. The relationship is related (or possibly subsumed_by), not equivalent.

In edas, Author is a subclass of Person, representing a person who writes papers. In iasted, Student registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, representing a monetary amount charged for student registration. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Reviewing results event is an event where review outcomes are announced to authors, while Program Committee is a committee body. They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies (Event vs Committee) and denote completely different concepts.

Review in cmt is a document written by a reviewer about a paper, situated under Document with properties like write Review and written By. Value added tax in iasted is a monetary tax under Money > Tax, a sibling of Departure tax. These denote completely different domain concepts (a review document vs. a tax type) with no overlap.

confOf:Participant is a subclass of Person (a human participant in a conference, with children Member, Regular, Student). iasted:Author_attendee_cd_registration_fee is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount). These denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. a fee—so they are unrelated.

The property 'is Written By' in edas relates a Paper to its Author, expressing authorship. The property 'updated Version Of' in ekaw relates a Document to another Document, expressing that one document is an updated version of another. These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and they share no conceptual overlap.

The cmt property 'has Decision' links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while the iasted property 'is visited by' links a geographic/location entity (Building, City, State) to a Person. These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve completely different purposes in the conference domain.

Review in the Conference ontology is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a contribution. ReviewQuestion in edas is a question item within a review form (numerical or textual), not the review itself. They denote completely different concepts.

Invited speaker is a person (a conference contributor who gives an invited talk), while Reception is a social event. They belong to completely disjoint branches of the ontology hierarchy and denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

confOf:Topic is a general class for conference subjects, used as the range of properties like 'deals With' and 'has Topic'. edas:SecurityTopic is a specific subclass of edas:Topic, representing only the security subject area. Therefore confOf:Topic subsumes edas:SecurityTopic.

cmt:writePaper relates an Author to a Paper they author. ekaw:volumeContainsPaper relates a Volume (container) to the Papers it contains. These are fundamentally different relations with different domain/range types and different semantics (authorship vs. containment).

confOf:Conference is an event (a gathering such as a conference, workshop, or tutorial), whereas ekaw:Conference_Paper is a document (a paper presented at a conference). They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (Event vs Document) and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

In ontology A, 'Conference proceedings' is a published artefact (with publisher, volume, ISBN) — the collected papers of a conference. In ontology B, 'Conference' is the event itself (with dates, country, members, topics, paper deadlines). These denote entirely different kinds of things (a document vs. an event), so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Presenter is a subclass of Conference Participant (a Person who presents). In iasted, Presenter university is a subclass of Building (a Place/venue). These denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. a building—so they are unrelated.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. In Conference, 'has_an_email' has domain Person and represents a person's email address. In confOf, 'contactEmail' has domain Contribution and represents the contact email for a paper/contribution. They relate different kinds of entities (people vs. documents) and are not equivalent.

Invited speaker is a conference contributor invited to give a talk, whereas Volunteer is a person assisting with conference logistics. They denote disjoint roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt property 'enter Conference Details' has domain Administrator and range Conference, describing an administrative action of entering conference details. The iasted property 'write' has domain Person and range Item, describing a person writing an item (e.g., a document or paper). These properties relate entirely different kinds of things in different contexts and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other in a meaningful way.

hasStreet is a datatype property from Organization/Person to a string (a street address), while organisedBy is an object property from Event to Organisation/Person (who organises the event). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

The two properties have opposite domains and ranges and different semantics. In Conference, 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (expressing a reviewer's preference for reviewing a topic). In confOf, 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (expressing the subject matter of a paper). They are not inverses of each other either, since one involves review preferences and the other involves paper topics.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In confOf, 'has Topic' links a Working event to a Topic (subject matter). In iasted, 'go through' links an Item to an Activity (process/workflow). The domains (Working event vs. Item), ranges (Topic vs. Activity), and intended meanings are disjoint, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.
confOf:Assistant is a person role (assistant), while edas:TwoLevelConference is a conference type. They share no instances and are unrelated concepts despite both being under Person in edas.

The cmt 'email' property relates a Person to a string (an email address), while the iasted 'has amount of' property relates Money to an int (a monetary quantity). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings; they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. 'review Of Paper' links a Review to the Paper being reviewed, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document presented. They differ in domain (Review vs Speaker), range (Paper vs Document), and semantic meaning (reviewing vs presenting).

Conference Event in edas is a temporal event (with start/end dates, location, attendees, programme) that includes academic and non-academic events. Organisation in ekaw is a corporate entity (academic institutions, organising agencies, publishers). One is an event, the other is an organisation; they are disjoint kinds of things.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas ekaw:PC_Chair is a person role (subclass of Person > Conference Participant). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a document submitted to a conference (a full paper or abstract), with properties like hasAuthor, hasDecision, assignedTo reviewers, etc. In edas, WirelessCommunicationsTopic is a subject-area classification (a Topic), sibling to Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc. These denote completely different kinds of entities: a paper artefact vs. a topic/subject area. They share no instances and are unrelated.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In ekaw, 'held In' has domain Event and range Location, meaning an event is held in a location. In sigkdd, 'hold' has domain ACM_SIGKDD (an organization) and range Conference, meaning the organization holds a conference. They are not the same relation: different domains, different ranges, and different semantics. They are not inverses of each other either, since one relates events to locations and the other relates organizations to conferences.

confOf's Paper is a general class for all papers (a sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), whereas edas's Rejected Paper is a specific subclass of Paper denoting only papers that have been rejected. The confOf Paper class is strictly more general, so it subsumes edas's Rejected Paper.

defaultChoice is a datatype property from Social/Working event to positiveInteger (likely a default quantity/choice count), while organisedBy is an object property from Event to Organisation/Person (who organises the event). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Both classes are top-level (or near-top-level) containers for conference-related written artefacts. They share key children (Paper, Review, Programme/Programme Brochure) and both serve as the range/target of authorship and relation properties involving Person and conference entities. The differences in specific child types (e.g., Meal Menu vs. Flyer) reflect ontology coverage variation rather than a fundamental difference in intended meaning. Both denote the general concept of a document in the conference domain.

These properties relate entirely different entities. 'hardcopy Mailing Manifests Printed By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who printed mailing manifests), while 'paper Presented As' links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (how a paper is presented). No overlap in domain, range, or meaning.

Paper Abstract is a document subclass (a written textual artefact: abstract of a conference paper), while Computer is a physical audiovisual equipment item (a piece of hardware used at a conference venue). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no common instances.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a person who attends a conference without an active role, while a 'Full day tour' is a post-conference social activity. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies (Person vs Activity) and share no instances in common.

Both classes denote persons who registered early for the conference. In the Conference ontology, 'Early paid applicant' is a paid applicant who registered early, while in EKAW, 'Early Registered Participant' is a conference participant who registered early. The key difference is that A requires payment status (paid) while B does not explicitly require it. However, in the conference domain, early registration typically implies payment, and both ontologies distinguish early vs. late registration as parallel concepts. The intended instances largely coincide: people who registered early and paid. The slight difference in explicit payment requirement is minor enough that a reference alignment would likely consider these equivalent.

confOf:Member_PC is a Program Committee member who reviews papers (comment says 'Reviewer', has properties expertOn and reviewes). iasted:Author is a Speaker subclass (path: Delegate > Speaker > Author), i.e., a person who presents at the conference. A PC reviewer and a presenting author are distinct roles; neither subsumes the other and they are not equivalent.

confOf:Paper is a general class of submitted documents (a sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), denoting any paper. sigkdd:Best_Student_Paper_Award is a specific award given to a student paper, a child of Award. One denotes the paper itself; the other denotes an award honouring a paper. They share the word 'Paper' but refer to completely different entities, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. `authorOf` (ekaw) links a Person to a Document they authored, while `is_used_by` (iasted) links an Item to a Person who uses it. They describe fundamentally different relationships (authorship vs. usage) and are not inverses of each other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person participating in the conference). In the Conference ontology, has_tutorials links a Conference volume to a Tutorial (an event/session that is part of the conference). The domains (Conference vs Conference volume), ranges (Conference Member vs Tutorial), and overall semantics (membership relation vs part-of relation) are completely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Invited speaker denotes a person invited to give a talk at a conference, whereas Chair PC denotes the chair of the programme committee. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Sponsorship in edas denotes a financial sponsorship arrangement (with cost amount, currency, provider organization, and subtypes like Travel Grant). Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a subclass of Person who can review papers (with properties like hasReviewer, reviewWrittenBy, reviewerOfPaper). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Track is a conference part (like Tutorial or Workshop) that a conference volume has tracks of, while Fee is a monetary amount (under Money) with children like Registration fee and Hotel fee. These denote completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Conference contributor is a broad superclass of all persons who contribute to a conference (authors, invited speakers, active participants). Chair PC is a specific role for the PC chair. Neither subsumes the other: a PC Chair is not necessarily a 'conference contributor' in the sense of authoring/presenting, and a contributor is not a chair. They share only the parent Person.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things in different directions. confOf:writes links an Author to a Contribution (the authorship relation). edas:relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (an event associated with the paper). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

The cmt 'accepted By' property links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it, denoting the acceptance decision process. The sigkdd 'payed by' property links a Registration fee to the Person who paid it, denoting a financial payment relation. These are entirely different relationships in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties concern authorship of a written work, but they differ in direction and granularity. The cmt property co-writePaper relates a Co-author to a Paper (author -> work), whereas the iasted property is_writen_by relates an Item to a Person (work -> author). They are inverses in spirit, not equivalent. Additionally, the domains and ranges differ: Co-author is more specific than Person, and Paper may be narrower than Item. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

confOf:Regular is a regular (non-student, non-member) participant who presumably can speak/present, while iasted:Student_non_speaker is specifically a student delegate who does not speak. The intended instances do not coincide: one excludes students and implies normal participation, the other requires being a student and a non-speaker. They are disjoint rather than equivalent or subsuming.

In EKAW, Possible Reviewer is a subclass of Person restricted to those who can review papers (with properties like reviewerOfPaper, reviewWrittenBy). In SIGKDD, Person is the general class of all people (with subclasses Listener, Organizator, Speaker). Possible Reviewer is thus a more specific concept subsumed by Person.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. In Conference, 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (a document part). In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or item). The domains (document vs. person) and ranges (abstract vs. activity/item) do not overlap, so these are not the same relation.

These classes denote disjoint categories of conference participants. 'Invited speaker' in ontology A is a person invited to give a talk at a conference (a speaker). 'Student non speaker' in ontology B is a student delegate who does not speak at the conference. They are mutually exclusive roles: one is a speaker, the other is explicitly a non-speaker. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

Conference Banquet in ekaw is a social event (an activity/occasion), while Conference restaurant in iasted is a physical place/building. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Event vs Place) and denote different categories of entities.

Both classes represent social trips associated with a conference, situated under the same hierarchy (Event > Social Event) with analogous siblings (Banquet/Reception). The labels 'Trip' and 'Conference Trip' denote the same intended concept in the conference domain.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific conference leadership role (a Chairman who assists in chairing the conference), while Attendee in edas is a general participant who attends the conference. These are distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances: an associated chair is not necessarily an attendee (they have organizational duties), and an attendee is not necessarily a chair. They share only the common parent Person.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'is designed for' in iasted relates Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person, while 'can stay in' in sigkdd relates Person to Place. They share no common relational semantics.

Computer Architecture Topic is a subject-area classification under Topic (alongside Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), whereas Card is a physical item type under Item (with siblings like Audiovisual equipment, Document, Publication). They denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'is present' in iasted relates a Person to a Time (indicating when someone is present), while 'submit' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper (indicating the act of submitting a paper). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In ekaw, Conference Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion or outing associated with a conference). In iasted, Technic activity is a conference activity whose siblings include lectures, presentations, introductions, and welcome addresses—i.e., technical/academic sessions. A conference trip is not a technical/academic activity; the two classes denote different kinds of conference events with no overlap in intended instances.

In EKAW, PC Member is a subclass of Possible Reviewer and has children such as PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc., indicating it is a broad committee role. In EDAS, Reviewer is a specific role under Person (distinct from Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) that is the agent actually performing paper reviews. Thus EDAS Reviewer is narrower than EKAW PC Member: every EDAS Reviewer corresponds to an EKAW PC Member, but not vice versa (EKAW PC Members include chairs who may not review).

Talk Event in EDAS is a broad class for oral presentations (including closing/welcome talks and paper presentations), while Regular Session in EKAW is a scheduled session block within a conference program. They overlap—paper presentations occur in regular sessions—but neither subsumes the other: a Talk Event is about the type of academic event, while a Regular Session is about the scheduling container. They are related but not equivalent.

IASTED member is a person (subclass of Delegate) who is a member of IASTED, while Conference hall is a physical place where conference events occur. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (person vs. place) and share no semantic overlap.

The ekaw 'references' property denotes a relation where one document references another (e.g., a paper citing another paper), while the iasted 'sign' property denotes a Person signing an Item (e.g., a delegate signing a document). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no indication they overlap in meaning.

These properties are fundamentally different in type and semantics. 'has important dates' is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates object (a container for multiple deadlines/dates), while 'start Date' is a datatype property linking a Conference directly to a single dateTime value. They differ in arity/type (object vs datatype), range (class vs dateTime), and meaning (a collection of important dates vs one specific start timestamp). They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The property `has a name` in Conference applies to organizational entities (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic) and denotes their name. The property `hasLastName` in edas applies to Person and denotes a person's family name. They have disjoint domains and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event under Event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). edas:RadioCommunicationsTopic is a subject topic (under Topic, sibling of various technical topics like Antennas, Cryptography, etc.). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain: an event type vs. a research subject area.

confOf:Paper is a general contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short_paper) covering all papers regardless of acceptance status. ekaw:Rejected_Paper is a highly specific subclass of Evaluated_Paper, denoting only papers that were rejected. Thus confOf:Paper is strictly more general than ekaw:Rejected_Paper, so confOf:Paper is subsumed_by ekaw:Rejected_Paper's parent hierarchy; more precisely, ekaw:Rejected_Paper is a proper subclass of confOf:Paper, making confOf:Paper subsumed_by the more specific ekaw class in the alignment direction.

confOf's 'Submission event' denotes the act of submitting contributions (a paper-submission deadline/event), while edas's 'Organizational Meeting' denotes a meeting held for organizational purposes during a conference. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

The cmt 'email' property relates a Person to their email address (string), while the edas 'hasPhone' property relates Contact Information to a phone number (string). These are distinct contact fields (email vs. phone) with different domains (Person vs. Contact Information), so they are unrelated.

Student registration fee is a fee for students, while Registration SIGKDD Member is a fee for SIGKDD members. These are distinct categories of registration fees targeting different groups; neither subsumes the other and they are not equivalent.

Both are registration fees for conference attendees, but they target different categories: A is specifically for an author who is also an attendee and registers with a book, while B is for a student registrant. Neither subsumes the other since an author-attendee-with-book is not necessarily a student, and a student is not necessarily an author. They overlap (some individuals could be both) but are distinct fee categories.

Both classes denote the same concept: a person involved in the conference domain. They share the same label and similar children (Author/Paper Author, Reviewer/Possible Reviewer, Attendee/Conference Participant, etc.), and both serve as domain/range for authorship, organisation, and document-related properties. The children in each ontology are comparable specialisations of the same general notion of a Person.

Submitted Paper is a document (a paper submitted to a conference), while Deadline is a temporal entity (a date by which something must be done). They belong to disjoint branches (documents vs. time) and share no instances.

siteURL points to the conference web address (anyURI), while startDate marks when the conference begins (dateTime). They share the domain Conference but denote completely different attributes, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Conference denotes the overall conference event (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while edas:CoffeeBreak denotes a short social break during a conference (a Break Event sibling of Free Time Break and Meal Break). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A Steering committee is an organizational body (a committee) responsible for overseeing a conference volume, whereas a Session Chair is a person who chairs a session and participates in reviewing and initiating calls. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Committee vs Person) and have no overlapping instances.

Both are object properties linking a sponsorship/award entity to an organization that provides or grants it, but Sponsorship and Award are distinct concepts (sponsorship is financial support, an award is a prize/honor), so the properties are related but not equivalent.

Invited speaker in the Conference ontology is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, a specific role for distinguished speakers. Student lecturer in iasted is a student who lectures, nested under Author > Lecturer, indicating a student presenting authored work. These are distinct concepts: one is defined by invitation status, the other by student status. Their instance sets do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

A Conference in confOf is a working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), i.e. an organised meeting/event. B Simulating in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference (sibling of Modelling). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain: an event vs. a pre-conference research activity.

confOf Administrator is a system/tool administrator role (comment 'confTool'), while edas Attendee is a person who attends the conference. These are distinct concepts: an administrator manages the tool/system, whereas an attendee participates in the event. Their sibling structures confirm this—Administrator groups with volunteer/assistant roles, Attendee groups with author/chair/reviewer participant roles.

Both classes denote the same high-level concept of an organization in the conference domain. The labels are spelling variants (American vs British English), and the ekaw Organisation's children (Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher) and associated properties (organisedBy, organises, publisherOf, technicallyOrganises) are all coherent subtypes and relations that a general Organization class in a conference ontology would subsume. No evidence suggests a different intended meaning.

In confOf, Workshop is a specific kind of working event (a meeting/event where papers are presented), whereas in ekaw, Track is a thematic grouping within a conference (e.g., a research track). They are distinct concepts in the conference domain: a workshop is an event, while a track is a subdivision of a conference program. They do not share instances.

In ekaw, 'Proceedings Publisher' is a subclass of Organisation, denoting the organisation that publishes proceedings (e.g., Springer). In iasted, 'Cd proceening' is a subclass of Publication, denoting a physical artefact (a CD containing proceedings). One is an agent/organisation, the other is a document/item; they are disjoint kinds of entities and not equivalent.

Review_expertise in the Conference ontology denotes the expertise or qualification level of a reviewer (linked to Reviewer, Review preference, Submitted contribution), not a review document. Review in sigkdd is a subclass of Document (sibling of Paper and Abstract), i.e. the actual written review artefact. The two classes denote completely different things: one is a property-like expertise descriptor, the other is a document.

Written contribution in the Conference ontology is a broad class covering any written conference artefact (including regular and submitted contributions), whereas Final manuscript in iasted is a specific submission document type (the final version, as opposed to the initial manuscript). Written contribution subsumes Final manuscript, but they are not equivalent since Final manuscript is a narrower concept.

Both properties share the domain Person and involve a person producing/delivering something at a conference. However, A's 'contributes' specifically relates a Person to a Conference document (a written artefact), while B's 'give' relates a Person to either an Activity or an Item (e.g., giving a presentation or lecture). Contributing a paper and giving a talk/activity are overlapping but distinct relations in the conference domain, so they are related but not equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote unrelated relations. printHardcopyMailingManifests relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of printing hardcopy mailing manifests), while relatesTo relates a Document to various entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person). They share no common domain or range types and express different relationships in the conference domain.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Enterprise Topic' is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area within computer networks. In EKAW, 'Contributed Talk' is a subclass of Individual Presentation representing a type of academic event/presentation. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The cmt 'assigned To' relation links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper is assigned to a reviewer for review). The iasted 'send' relation links a Person to an Item (a person sends an item). These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and they serve different purposes in the conference domain.

Published Paper (a paper that has been published) and Rejected Paper (a paper that was rejected) are mutually exclusive categories of papers in the conference domain. They share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to a Co chair (a role within a committee), while 'prepare' links a Person to an Item (e.g., a document or artefact). They share no common domain or range and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Item > Audiovisual equipment > Overhead projector), whereas Listener is a person who attends a conference (Person > Listener). One is a physical device, the other a human role; their intended instances are completely disjoint.

The two properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (expressing how a topic relates to a reviewer's preference), while 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (tracking a reviewer's past review activity). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

Reception (confOf) is a social event, a sibling of Banquet and Trip. Welcome address (iasted) is a conference activity, a sibling of Coctail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Presentation, etc. A welcome address is a speech/talk, not a reception. The iasted ontology has a separate sibling 'Coctail reception' which would be the counterpart of confOf Reception. These two classes denote different things.

Organisation in ekaw denotes an organisation (e.g., academic institution, organising agency, publisher), while Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who gives a presentation. These are disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Poster in the Conference ontology is a type of conference contribution (a research poster presented at a conference), while Invitation letter in iasted is a type of document (a letter inviting someone to attend or participate). These are completely different concepts: one is an academic contribution artifact, the other is an administrative correspondence document. They share no meaningful semantic relationship in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different things. In EDAS, 'relatedToPaper' links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (i.e., which paper is being presented). In EKAW, 'volumeContainsPaper' links a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. The domains and ranges are disjoint concepts, and the relations describe different aspects of the conference domain.

edas:Author is a general class of person who writes a paper (subclass of Person, with properties linking to Paper). iasted:Author book proceedings included is a very specific subclass of Author (under Place > Building > ... > Delegate > Speaker > Author) denoting an author whose work is included in a book proceedings. The edas Author is a broad role class, while the iasted entity is a narrow publication-medium-specific author category; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither properly subsumes the other given the divergent ontology structures.

Conference contributor (A) denotes a person who contributes a paper or presentation to the conference, with subclasses like Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author. OC Chair (B) is a specific organizational role: the chair of the Organizing Committee, a subclass of OC Member. A conference contributor is not the same concept as the chair of the organizing committee; they occupy different roles in the conference domain. There is no subsumption relationship either: an OC Chair is not necessarily a contributor, and a contributor is not necessarily an OC Chair.

Property A (has_a_date_of_issue) has domain Conference document and range date, representing the date a document was issued. Property B (startDate) has domain Conference and range dateTime, representing when a conference starts. They relate to different entities (documents vs. conferences) and capture different notions (issue date vs. start date), so they are not equivalent.

The cmt property 'write Paper' specifically relates an Author to a Paper they author, while the iasted property 'need' relates a Person to an Item they need (e.g., equipment, services). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (concerning topic preferences in the review process), while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the document/slides presented by a speaker). They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings.

Paper Full Version is a full-length submission (a kind of Paper) in cmt, whereas Review is a referee's evaluation document in sigkdd. They are distinct document types in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A specifically relates a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract, while property B is a generic mereological relation (hasPart) with no specified domain or range. They denote different relations: having an abstract is not the same as having a part.

Both properties concern the assignment of reviewers to authored work, but they differ structurally: in EDAS 'isReviewedBy' links a Paper directly to a reviewer (or chair/TPC member), whereas in EKAW 'reviewWrittenBy' links a Review artefact to a Possible Reviewer. The domain entities (Paper vs Review) are distinct, so the relations are not equivalent, though they are semantically related in the reviewing workflow.
