Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Accommodation Place is a physical location for lodging. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are subclasses of Document with the label Review, representing the same concept in the conference domain: a review of a submitted paper. The sibling sets differ slightly (edas includes Meal Menu, Programme, Slide Set; sigkdd includes Abstract, Paper), but both ontologies place Review as a document type alongside Paper, indicating the same intended instances.

cmt's `name` is a general datatype property whose domain includes both Conference and Person, capturing the full name (or title) of either entity. edas's `hasFirstName` is a narrower property with domain Person, specifically denoting only the first/given name of a person. A first name is a part of (and thus more specific than) a full name, so `hasFirstName` is subsumed by `name`; they are not equivalent because `name` can apply to conferences and represents the complete name rather than just the first name.

hasStreet and hasCity are different datatype properties capturing different address attributes (street vs. city). They have different domains (Organization/Person vs. Contact Information) and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Both are datatype properties that associate an event with its end time. confOf 'ends on' has domain Event and range string, while edas 'has End Date Time' has domain ConferenceEvent and range dateTime. The slight datatype difference (string vs dateTime) is a common modeling variation across independently developed conference ontologies, and the underlying semantics—recording when an event ends—is the same.

Property A relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (the committee was the PC of that volume), whereas property B relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives a presentation or item). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

Review in ekaw is a document evaluating a paper (subclass of Document, with children like Positive/Neutral/Negative Review, linked to Paper and Possible Reviewer). Money in iasted represents financial concepts (fees, sponsorship, taxes, tips) with properties about payment amounts and payers. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Short paper and Demo Paper denote different categories of conference submissions. A short paper is a contribution distinguished by its length or brevity, whereas a Demo Paper is a paper describing a system demonstration. These are orthogonal classification dimensions (length vs. presentation type), and neither subsumes the other.

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) representing a type of conference activity. edas's 'Computer Networks Optical Topic' is a leaf-level subclass of Topic representing a specific subject area. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation that publishes the proceedings), while 'covers Topic' links Events or Papers to Research Topics (the subject matter they cover). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Reviewing event is a temporal/administrative event (a reviewing procedure for submitted contributions), while Organizing Committee is a group of people. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Powerline Transmission Topic is a subject-area Topic (sibling of Antennas, Cryptography, Mobile Computing, etc.), whereas Program Committee is a committee organizing a conference. They denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Author in edas is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person). Multi-author Volume in ekaw is a document type (subclass of Document) for works with multiple authors like proceedings. They are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is a document artefact.

Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers), while Break Event is a non-academic event like a coffee break or meal. One is a person role, the other is an event type; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Paper in cmt is a document (with subclasses Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version) that is authored, reviewed, and accepted/rejected. Working_event in confOf is an event (with subclasses Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) that has a location, title, and VAT. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain: one is a written scholarly artifact, the other is an organized gathering. No overlap in intended instances.

The property 'is Written By' in edas relates a Paper to its Author (who wrote the paper), while 'payed by' in sigkdd relates a Registration fee to the Person who paid it. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain: one concerns authorship of a document, the other concerns payment of a fee. Their domains and ranges are different, and they share no semantic overlap.

Week Reject Rating in edas is a rating value within a review-rating taxonomy (siblings: Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc.), i.e. a discrete score used to evaluate a paper. Refusing manuscript in iasted is an organisational activity performed before the conference (siblings: Accepting manuscript, Receiving manuscript, Renting). One is a rating/score, the other is an action/activity; their instances do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad superclass encompassing all conference participants including authors, reviewers, chairs, and program committee members. In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a specific subclass of Organizator. Since cmt's Conference Member includes Program Committee Member as a child, it is strictly more general than sigkdd's Program Committee member, so the relation is subsumes.

The cmt property 'hardcopyMailingManifestsPrintedBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who printed hardcopy mailing manifests). The confOf property 'follows' relates one Administrative event to another (temporal/sequence ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings; no subsumption or overlap exists.

A Poster Session is a session where posters are presented, while a Plenary lecture is a lecture given to all conference attendees. They are different types of conference activities with distinct formats and purposes.

Conference contributor in ontology Conference is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers, active participants). Science Worker in confOf is a broader category under Person that includes scholars, authors, PC members, chairs, etc. Science Worker appears to be a more general class that encompasses various roles including those who contribute scientifically, while Conference contributor is specifically about contribution roles. The sibling structure suggests Science Worker covers a wider range of roles than just contributors.

Property A links papers/posters/presentations to their abstracts, while property B links an ACM SIGKDD conference to a deadline. These relate entirely different kinds of things and have no semantic overlap.

Meta-Reviewer is a specialized reviewer who consolidates reviews, while Author is a person who writes contributions. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'has Decision' property links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while the confOf 'has Administrative Event' property links a Working event to an Administrative event (a scheduling/organisational sub-event). They relate different kinds of things in the conference domain and do not denote the same relation.

edas Talk Event (Conference Event > Academic Event > Talk Event) is a broad class covering any talk-type event including closing/welcome talks, while iasted Speaker lecture (Activity > Conference activity > Lecture > Session > Speaker lecture) is a specific lecture session delivered by a speaker. Talk Event is more general than Speaker lecture, so subsumed_by.

The two properties are completely different in meaning and structure. `hasPhone` is a datatype property from Contact Information to a string (phone number), while `heldIn` is an object property from Event to Location (where an event takes place). They share no conceptual overlap in the conference domain.

In edas, Paper is a scholarly contribution submitted to a conference, with children like Accepted/Rejected Paper and properties like isWrittenBy and isReviewedBy. In iasted, Transparency is a presentation slide set (a visual aid), sibling to Review, Submission, Form, etc. They share the parent Document but denote entirely different artefacts in the conference domain.

In cmt, writtenBy specifically relates a Review to a Reviewer, whereas in ekaw, writtenBy is a more general property relating any Document to a Person. Since Review is a kind of Document and Reviewer is a kind of Person, the cmt property is a specialization (subsumed_by) of the ekaw property, not equivalent.

In the iasted ontology, 'Conference airport' is a physical building (subclass of Building under Place) where conference participants arrive or stay. In the sigkdd ontology, 'Conference' is an event with start/end dates, a name, a city, and a holding organization (ACM SIGKDD). One is a physical location/building, the other is a temporal event; they share the word 'conference' but denote entirely different things.

NGO in edas is a subtype of Organization (alongside Academia, Government, Industry), denoting a non-governmental organization that may sponsor or participate. Sponsor in iasted is a subtype of Person (alongside Delegate), denoting an individual person who sponsors. These are disjoint: one is an organization, the other a person. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'invited by' in Conference relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them to review), while 'writes' in confOf relates an Author to a Contribution (paper). They have different domains, different ranges, and express entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'belongs to reviewers' in Conference links Review expertise/Review preference to Reviewer, while 'belongsToEvent' in edas links Programme to Conference Event. They share no common domain or range types and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing a person's email address. The labels 'email' and 'E mail' are surface variants of the same concept, and the structural context (Person > email/E mail > string) is identical across the two ontologies.

A 'Nonauthor registration fee' in iasted is a fee for non-author attendees, while 'Registration Student' in sigkdd is a registration fee for students. These are distinct categories of registration fees; neither subsumes the other (a student could be an author or non-author, and a non-author could be a student or non-student), and they are not equivalent.

Both properties point to Document, but hasRelatedDocument has a broad domain (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person) and denotes any related document, whereas presentation has domain Speaker and specifically denotes the document presented by that speaker. hasRelatedDocument is strictly more general than presentation.

Contribution co-author is a specific author role for a co-authored conference contribution, while Invited Speaker is a person invited to give a talk. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different entities. In cmt, hasBid connects a Paper to a Bid (a bidding action by a reviewer expressing interest in reviewing that paper). In edas, hasRelatedPaper connects an Author to a Paper (indicating a paper related to/associated with an author). The domains (Paper vs Author), ranges (Bid vs Paper), and the underlying semantics (reviewer bidding vs authorship association) are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing the same concept of a person's last name/surname. The labels 'has Surname' and 'has Last Name' are synonyms in this context, and both ontologies use them in the same way (Person -> string).

Presentation in the Conference ontology is a spoken/talk event (given by an active participant, has an abstract, has child 'Invited talk'), not a document. Document in iasted is a broad container for administrative and textual artefacts (forms, letters, reviews, submissions, transparencies, etc.). A presentation is an activity/event, while Document denotes physical or digital items; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different domains and ranges. 'is Initiated By' links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to conference roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), while 'is paid by' links Money to a Person. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Conference_www is a class representing a conference website/web document (a document with a URL), while Tutorial is a class representing a type of working event at a conference. One is a document/information resource, the other is an event. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Paper in the Conference ontology denotes a written scholarly contribution (a document), whereas Best Student Paper Award in sigkdd denotes an award given to a paper. These are completely different kinds of entities: one is the artefact itself, the other is a prize. They share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Review Question' is a class whose instances are individual questions used in a review form (with subclasses Numerical Review Question and Textual Review Question). In the IASTED ontology, 'Review' is a subclass of Document representing the entire review document written by a reviewer. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a question item within a review form, the other is the complete review artefact. They share no subsumption relationship and are not equivalent.

In edas, Conference Chair is a leadership role (person who chairs the conference, initiates calls, reviews papers). In iasted, Session chair is a subtype of Delegate (a conference attendee) who chairs a single session. These are different roles at different levels of the conference hierarchy: a Conference Chair oversees the entire conference while a Session chair is a regular delegate responsible for one session. The iasted ontology has no Conference Chair equivalent, and the edas ontology has a separate Session Chair class. The two entities denote different concepts.

The two properties operate in opposite directions and connect entirely different entity types. `has_the_first_name` is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's first name), while `writtenBy` is an object property from Document to Person (the author of a document). They share no domain, range, or semantic overlap.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event under Event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Technical_commitee is a type of person/delegate (under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate, sibling of Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc.). One denotes an event, the other a person role; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document subtype (a short summary of a paper), while Best Student Paper Supporter in sigkdd is a sponsor subtype (an organization/individual providing financial support). They share no instances and belong to completely different parts of the domain hierarchy.

Both classes sit below Author in their respective hierarchies and share the conference-domain notion of a person who authored a paper. However, iasted's 'Worker lecturer' is reached through a chain involving Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer, suggesting a lecturer who is also an author (and possibly employed/non-student), whereas sigkdd's 'Author of paper' is simply an author of a paper. The iasted class carries additional lecturer/worker connotations not present in the sigkdd class, so they overlap but are not equivalent.

Property A (has_a_committee_co-chair) links a Committee to a Co-chair, while property B (organisedBy) links an Event to an Organisation or Person. They have different domains, different ranges, and express different relationships in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a subclass of Person, denoting people who contribute to a conference (authors, speakers, participants). Conference building in ontology B is a subclass of Building under Place, denoting a physical location where a conference is held. These are completely different concepts: a person role vs. a physical structure.

Publisher denotes an organization that publishes conference proceedings, while Contact Information denotes a set of contact details (city, email, phone, postal code, street) for a person or entity. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. In cmt, 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who runs the paper assignment tools (a management/administrative role). In confOf, 'parallel_with' links two Administrative events that are scheduled in parallel. They have different domains (Conference vs. Administrative event), different ranges (Administrator vs. Administrative event), and express unrelated relationships.

Session in iasted is a subclass of Lecture (an event/activity where talks are delivered), while Organizator in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (a human role in the conference). These are completely different categories: an event vs. a person. No alignment relation holds.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, indicating who finalized paper assignments. In ekaw, 'paperPresentedAs' links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation, indicating how a paper is presented. They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap.

The confOf 'abstract' property relates a Contribution to its textual abstract, while the sigkdd 'Name_of_sponsor' property relates a Sponsor to its name. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended meaning.

The two properties operate in completely different domains. confOf:dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic (what subject a paper covers), while iasted:is_paid_with links Money to an Item (payment instrument to purchased item). They have different domains, different ranges, and no semantic overlap in the conference-organisation domain.

Conference document is a class for conference-related documents (papers, reviews, announcements, etc.), while State in iasted is a geographic/administrative entity (with children like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state). They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'organises' has domain Organisation or Person and range Event, denoting who organises an event. In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' has domain Document and range Speaker, denoting the speaker who presents a document. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

Acceptance in cmt is the positive decision outcome (sibling of Rejection under Decision), whereas Refusing manuscript in iasted is the negative decision activity (sibling of Accepting manuscript). They are opposites, not the same concept.

In iasted, Money is a broad class covering all monetary amounts (fees, sponsorships, taxes, tips), while in sigkdd Fee is a specific kind of money charged for registration or sponsorship. Thus iasted:Money subsumes sigkdd:Fee rather than being equivalent.

In iasted, Submission is a subclass of Document representing the submitted artefact (paper/manuscript), with children like Final manuscript and Initial manuscript. In sigkdd, Deadline Paper Submission is a subclass of Deadline representing a temporal date/deadline for paper submission, with siblings like Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Author notification. One is a document, the other is a temporal entity; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

submitPaper has domain Author and range Paper, representing an author submitting a paper. writtenBy has domain Document and range Person, representing a document being written by a person. These are different relations in opposite directions (author->paper vs document->person), and neither subsumes the other since their domains and ranges differ.

In cmt, 'name' applies to both Conference and Person, while in edas 'hasName' is specifically for Conference (commented as 'Conference Full Name'). Thus cmt:name is more general, subsuming edas:hasName, so cmt:name is subsumed_by edas:hasName is incorrect—rather edas:hasName is subsumed_by cmt:name. Correct relation: cmt:name subsumes edas:hasName.

Both classes represent an Organizing Committee in the conference domain. They share the same label, the same parent class (Committee), and appear in analogous positions within their respective ontology hierarchies. The Conference ontology explicitly links it to Conference volume via 'has an organizing committee' and 'was an organizing committee of', confirming it denotes the committee that organizes a conference. The sigkdd ontology places it as a sibling of Program Committee under Committee, consistent with the same concept. No contextual differences suggest divergent intended meanings.

These properties denote completely different relations. 'has an ISBN' is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to a string (the ISBN identifier). 'publisher Of' is an object property linking an Organisation to published items such as Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, and Web Site. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Conference proceedings vs Organisation), range (string vs document-like objects), and meaning (identifier assignment vs publication authorship).

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event like a conference or tutorial), while iasted:Presenter_city is a subclass of City representing the city where a presenter is located. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Rejected contribution is a class whose instances are written contributions (papers) that were rejected after review. Reviewing event is a class whose instances are events in the conference timeline representing the reviewing procedure. One denotes a document/artefact, the other an administrative event; they share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different entities. 'issues' connects a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'designed by' connects a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD. They have different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

edas:Presenter is a subclass of edas:Author, denoting authors who specifically present their work. iasted:Author is a broader class encompassing all authors (including those who only author proceedings, lecturers, tutorial speakers, etc.). Thus Presenter is subsumed by Author rather than equivalent.

Conference's Topic is a general class for conference topics, with properties linking it to conference parts, reviews, and submitted contributions. EDAS's CommunicationsTopic is a specific subclass of Topic (a child of the general EDAS Topic), representing a narrow subject area (communications) alongside siblings like AntennasTopic, CADTopic, etc. Thus CommunicationsTopic is strictly more specific than Conference's Topic, making this a subsumed_by relation.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Tutorial is a type of event/presentation (subclass of Individual Presentation/Event). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In Conference, Person is the top-level human class with children including Conference participant, Reviewer, Committee member, etc. In confOf, Participant is a subclass of Person, with siblings such as Author, Chair PC, Member PC, Volunteer, etc. Thus confOf:Participant is narrower than Conference:Person, covering only those who register/participate, whereas Conference:Person encompasses all persons in the conference domain.

ekaw:Paper_Author is a general class for any person who authors a paper, sitting directly under Person. sigkdd:Author_of_paper_student is a specific subclass of Author restricted to student authors. The ekaw class therefore subsumes the sigkdd class, but they are not equivalent because the sigkdd class is narrower.

hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (the score/evaluation assigned to the paper), while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (the person assigned to review it). These are different relations connecting different kinds of objects, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Chairman is a general superclass with three distinct subclasses (Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), making it a broad role category. In the Conference ontology, Chair is a specific leaf-level class under Committee member, representing the specific role of a committee chair. Since Chairman in cmt encompasses multiple chair roles (including program committee chairs and conference chairs), it is strictly more general than the Conference ontology's Chair, which denotes only one specific kind of chair role.

In edas, Conference is the main conference event/organization with properties like dates, topics, members, and papers. In ekaw, Conference Banquet is a specific social event (a dinner) that occurs during a conference, a child of Social Event. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In EDAS, Social Event is a broad category of non-academic conference events with children Excursion and Reception. In IASTED, Dinner banquet is a specific kind of social program activity. A dinner banquet is a type of social event, but not all social events are dinner banquets, so Social Event subsumes Dinner banquet.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. In ontology A, 'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (author/contributor relationship). In ontology B, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (presenter relationship). They differ in domain, range, and the underlying relationship they model (authorship vs. presentation).

confOf's writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author (who wrote it), while ekaw's paperPresentedAs links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the form in which it is presented). These are different relations with different domains and ranges and no overlap in meaning.

These properties operate in completely different domains and directions. `technicallyOrganises` in ekaw has domain Organisation and describes an organisation's role in organising (likely a conference/event). `is_occupied_by` in iasted has domain Building/City/State and range Person, describing physical occupancy of a place by a person. They share no semantic relationship in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a broad class covering any person who contributes to a conference (authors, speakers, active participants). Student lecturer in ontology B is a highly specific subclass of Lecturer (itself under Author under Speaker under Delegate), denoting a student who gives a lecture. A student lecturer is at most a very specific kind of contributor, but the two classes are at very different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept. They are not equivalent, and the relationship is too tenuous (a student lecturer could be considered a contributor, but the ontologies model them in fundamentally different hierarchies) to assert a clean subsumption in either direction.

The two properties operate in opposite directions and connect completely different entities. `has_a_review_reference_or_expertise` links a Reviewer to their review expertise/preferences (reviewer -> expertise), while `hasReviewer` links a Paper to its possible reviewers (paper -> reviewer). They are not inverses in a formal sense either, since the domains/ranges do not line up (Reviewer vs Paper, Review expertise vs Possible Reviewer). They denote different relations in the conference domain.

A Program Committee Chair (cmt) is the person who leads the program committee and oversees the paper-review process (end Review property). A Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a conference session/event. These are distinct roles in conference organization: one manages reviewing, the other manages a presentation session. They share no parent beyond Person and have different associated properties, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise overlapping.

Important dates in Conference ontology is a class representing the set of key dates (submission, acceptance, camera-ready, start/end) associated with a conference volume. Conference in edas is the conference event itself, with properties like name, country, members, topics, and due dates. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a collection of temporal milestones, the other is the organizational event. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Both are subclasses of Place in their respective ontologies and both concern rooms where conference activities occur. However, 'Meeting Room Place' in EDAS is a broader concept encompassing any room used for meetings (including committee meetings, conference venue rooms, etc.), while 'Session room' in IASTED specifically denotes a room where conference sessions (paper presentations, talks) are held. A session room is a type of meeting room, but not all meeting rooms are session rooms. The sibling structures also differ: EDAS distinguishes accommodation, dining, and conference venue places, while IASTED lists building, conference hall, hotel room, and main office. The concepts overlap but are not coextensive.

These properties have different domains and ranges and represent different relationships. 'provided By' in edas links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who provides the sponsorship), while 'is paid for' in iasted links Money to an Activity or Item (what the money pays for). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships: one is about the source/provider of sponsorship, the other about what money is used to pay for. They are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption relationship.

Paper Abstract is a document (a short version of a paper) in cmt, while Silver Supporter is a type of conference sponsor in sigkdd. They belong to completely different parts of the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different things. In Conference, 'reviews' links a Review to the Reviewed contribution it evaluates (Review -> Reviewed contribution). In edas, 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (Reviewer -> Personal Review History). The domains (Review vs Reviewer) and ranges (Reviewed contribution vs Personal Review History) are disjoint concepts, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

The EKAW 'part Of' property is a general mereological relation indicating that something is part of something else, with no specified domain or range. The SIGKDD 'presentationed by' property specifically relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. These are fundamentally different relations: one denotes parthood, the other denotes presentation authorship/delivery. They do not share the same domain/range types or the same relational semantics.

Written_contribution in the Conference ontology is a class whose instances are documents (papers, submissions, regular contributions), sitting under Conference document > Conference contribution. Author in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (Speaker > Author) whose instances are people who submit papers and receive awards. These are disjoint categories (document vs person), so they are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings. `hasVAT` in confOf applies to Social event and Working event, capturing value added tax. `Name` in sigkdd applies to Person, capturing a person's name. They relate different kinds of entities to different kinds of information, so they are unrelated.

edas RatedPapers is a narrow subclass of papers that have been rated (under Active Paper under Paper), whereas ekaw Paper is the broad class of all papers (including submitted, accepted, camera-ready, etc.). Thus every rated paper is a Paper, but not vice versa, so RatedPapers is subsumed_by ekaw Paper.

Property A (has_an_abstract) links a paper/poster/presentation to its Abstract (document -> abstract text). Property B (paperPresentedAs) links a paper/abstract to an Individual Presentation (document -> presentation event). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions: one connects a paper to its abstract, the other connects a paper to its presentation. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

Accepted_contribution is a written work that has passed peer review (a paper), whereas Review is the evaluation document written about a paper. They are different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Contact Information (edas) is a class for contact details (city, email, phone, postal code, street) associated with persons or locations. Time (iasted) is a temporal class with children like Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day, used in properties like 'is held in' (Activity -> Place, Time). These denote completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

ekaw:Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. sigkdd:Registration_Student is a subclass of Registration_fee, denoting a fee category for student registrations. One is a person, the other is a fee/registration type; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties operate in different domains and directions. In Conference, 'has a review reference or expertise' links a Reviewer to review expertise or preference objects, capturing what a reviewer brings to a review assignment. In ekaw, 'referenced In' is a generic relation indicating that something is referenced in something else (e.g., a paper referenced in a proceedings). They do not share the same domain/range types, nor do they express the same relationship.

Submitted Paper is a research paper submitted for review at a conference, while Transparency is a presentation slide/overhead used during a talk. They are different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, Communications Topic is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference papers (e.g., antennas, CAD, communication theory). In iasted, Card is a subclass of Item, with a child Credit card and siblings like Audiovisual equipment, Document, Publication, and Transport vehicle, indicating it denotes a physical or financial item. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is a class representing an accepted paper/contribution (a document artifact), while entity B is a class representing a registration deadline (a temporal entity). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad role class subsuming chairs, authors, PC members, and reviewers—anyone with a formal conference role. Student in confOf is a specific registration/participant category (a reduced-fee delegate). Neither subsumes the other (a student can be an author or reviewer without being a general conference member, and a conference member need not be a student), and their intended instances do not coincide.

A Sponsor is a person or organization that provides financial support for a conference, whereas a Program Chair is an organizer responsible for the scientific program. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'email' property captures a person's electronic mail address, while confOf 'hasFirstName' captures a person's first name (with the comment noting middle name involvement). These are distinct attributes of a person, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

Speaker in iasted is a person (subclass of Delegate) who gives a presentation at a conference. Conference_hall in sigkdd is a physical location (subclass of Place) where conference events are held. These are completely different categories of entities—a person vs. a venue—so they are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. confOf:follows relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (e.g., one event following another in a sequence), while edas:attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (indicating that a person attends an event). They connect different types of entities and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document providing information to attendees, while 'Book proceeding' in the iasted ontology is a publication type (a book containing conference papers). They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Scientific Event in ekaw is a subclass of Event with children like Conference, Session, Workshop, etc., denoting academic gatherings. Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited Speaker, denoting a person who presents. These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a person role.

confOf:Conference is a specific kind of working event (a conference), whereas edas:AcademicEvent is a broader class that includes workshops, paper presentations, talks, and organizational meetings. The edas class subsumes the confOf class, but they are not equivalent because AcademicEvent has children that are not conferences.

Invited talk in Conference is a type of Conference contribution/Presentation, denoting a talk given by an invited speaker. Workshop Session in ekaw is a Session within a Workshop event. An invited talk is not a workshop session; they are different kinds of conference entities with no clear overlap in intended instances.

These properties relate entirely different domains and ranges. 'is given by' connects a Presentation to an Active conference participant (who delivers the presentation), while 'is paid by' connects Money to a Person (who pays). They describe different relationships in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

confOf:Member PC is a general PC member who reviews papers (comment says 'Reviewer', domain of reviewes->Contribution). ekaw:PC Chair is the specific chair of the PC, a sub-class of PC Member. A PC Chair is a special PC member, not equivalent to the general Member PC class. The two ontologies model different granularity: confOf has separate 'Member PC' and 'Chair PC' siblings, while ekaw has 'PC Chair' as a sub-class of 'PC Member'. They are not equivalent, not in a clean subsumption across ontologies, and not clearly related enough to warrant a 'related' verdict.

In Conference ontology, Abstract is a specific document class representing the abstract text of a paper/poster/presentation, sitting deep in the hierarchy under Extended abstract. In confOf, Contribution is a top-level class representing any submitted work (paper, poster, short paper). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a component/part of a contribution, the other is the contribution itself. The confOf 'abstract' property (Contribution -> string) maps to the content that the Conference 'Abstract' class represents, but the class Abstract is not equivalent to the class Contribution.

Co-author in cmt is a specific role: a Person who co-writes a paper, sitting under Author. Possible_Reviewer in ekaw is a Person who could be assigned to review a paper, with PC Member as a sub-role. The two concepts address different conference roles (authorship vs. reviewing) and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'has gender' captures a person's gender, while 'has Last Name' captures a person's surname/family name. These are semantically distinct attributes with no overlap in meaning, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person.

The cmt 'date' property applies to a Conference and denotes its date, whereas the Conference ontology 'is a full paper submission date' applies to an Important dates entity and specifically denotes the full paper submission deadline. They have different domains and different intended meanings (a conference date vs. a submission deadline), so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

These properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. 'invited by' (domain: Reviewer, range: Reviewer) captures the invitation relationship between reviewers, while 'has Review History' (domain: Reviewer, range: Personal Review History) associates a reviewer with their review history record. They relate reviewers to entirely different kinds of objects and represent semantically distinct relationships.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings. `has_the_first_name` applies to Person and captures a person's first name, while `hasKeyword` applies to Contribution and captures a keyword of a paper. They are unrelated.

Both classes sit under Author in their respective hierarchies, but iasted's Lecturer is a specialized subclass of Author (further down a chain through Speaker) with its own subclasses (Student lecturer, Worker lecturer), while sigkdd's Author_of_paper is a direct subclass of Author. Lecturer is more specific than Author_of_paper, so the best relation is subsumed_by.

The two properties have different domains and denote different attributes: 'has the first name' applies to Person and captures a person's given name, while 'has Title' applies to Contribution and captures the title of a paper/contribution. They relate different kinds of entities and represent semantically distinct attributes, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote people who review papers in the conference domain, so they overlap. However, they are not equivalent: ekaw:Possible_Reviewer is a broad class of any person who could be assigned as a reviewer (a role under Person, with PC_Member as a subclass), while iasted:Reviewer is a narrow subclass chain under Delegate > Speaker > Reviewer, implying the reviewer is a delegate/speaker at the venue. The iasted hierarchy also places Reviewer under Place/Building/Conference_building, which is an unusual modeling that further differentiates it. Thus they share instances but neither subsumes the other cleanly.

The confOf 'reviewes' property relates a PC Member to a Contribution they review, whereas the iasted 'is sent before' property relates an Item to a Time before which it is sent. These are completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property `name` in cmt denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while `has Phone` in confOf denotes a telephone number of a Person. These are completely different attributes with no semantic overlap.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'organised By' relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it, while 'is used for' relates an Item to an Activity or Money it is used for. There is no semantic overlap between these two relations.

Radio Communications Topic is a subject-area Topic (sibling of Antennas Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.), while Invited Talk Abstract is a Document/Abstract subtype (a written artefact for an invited talk). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote completely different things.

These classes denote completely different concepts in the conference domain. cmt:Author is a person who writes and submits papers, situated under Person > Conference Member. edas:MealEvent is a non-academic event during a conference involving meals, situated under Conference Event > Non Academic Event. They share no instances, no common ancestry, and no semantic overlap.

The two properties are completely different in meaning, domain, and range. 'has_the_first_name' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's first name. 'is_used_for' is an object property from Item to Activity or Money, describing what an item is used for. They share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In edas, 'is Topic Of' links a Topic to a Conference or Paper (indicating the subject matter of a paper or conference). In iasted, 'write' links a Person to an Item (indicating authorship). They have different domains (Topic vs Person), different ranges (Conference/Paper vs Item), and express entirely different relationships with no overlap.

Talk Event in edas is a conference event where someone gives a talk (e.g., closing talk, welcome talk, paper presentation). Modelling in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference. These are completely different concepts: one is a scheduled event during a conference, the other is a pre-conference research activity. No meaningful overlap.

cmt:name applies to Conference and Person (naming entities), while confOf:hasTitle applies to Contribution (giving a paper its title). They relate different kinds of things and are not the same relation.

The two properties relate completely different things. In edas, 'has Rating' links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (the score assigned to a paper). In ekaw, 'reviewWrittenBy' links a Review to a Possible Reviewer (the person who wrote the review). One connects papers to ratings; the other connects reviews to reviewers. They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

These properties denote completely different relations. cmt:maxPapers is a datatype property from Program Committee Member to int, recording how many papers a PC member can be assigned. ekaw:paperPresentedAs is an object property from Paper/Abstract to Individual Presentation, linking a paper to its presentation. They share no domain, range, or meaning.

`writePaper` in cmt relates an Author to a Paper they have authored, with domain Author and range Paper. `paperInVolume` in ekaw relates a paper to a volume/proceedings it appears in. These are fundamentally different relations: one connects authors to their papers, the other connects papers to their publication venue. No overlap in meaning.

Both are datatype properties with domain involving deadlines/dates and range date, but they denote different temporal concepts. 'is a starting date' marks the beginning of an event or period, while 'done till' marks a deadline by which something must be completed. These are semantically distinct relations (start vs. end) and would not be considered equivalent in a reference alignment.

These classes denote completely different concepts. Communications Topic in edas is a subject-area topic (a specialization of Topic, alongside other technical domains like Antennas, Cryptography, Mobile Computing, etc.). Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a document type—a kind of abstract written for an invited talk, subclass of Abstract under Document. One is a topic/subject classification, the other is a concrete document artifact. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The property `parallel with` in confOf relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel (same domain and range: Administrative event). The property `covers Topic` in ekaw relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic it covers. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; one is about temporal/structural parallelism between events, the other about subject-matter coverage. They are unrelated.

startReviewerBidding is an action property where an Administrator initiates a reviewer bidding process for a Conference. write is a generic authorship relation where a Person creates/produces an Item (e.g., a paper). They have completely different domains (Administrator vs Person), ranges (Conference vs Item), and meanings (triggering a bidding phase vs authoring a document).

The cmt 'site URL' property holds the web address (anyURI) of the conference, while the sigkdd 'City of conference' property holds the city name (string) where the conference takes place. These are completely different attributes of a conference with no overlap in meaning.

The two properties relate completely different entities and go in opposite directions. `has_a_committee_chair` links a Committee to its Chair (a specific leadership role within a committee), while `isMemberOf` links a Person to a Conference (general membership). They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning; neither subsumes the other.

These properties relate entirely different entities. Property A (belongs_to_a_review_reference) has domain Topic and range Review_preference, indicating it links a Topic to a Review preference. Property B (reviewWrittenBy) has domain Review and range Possible_Reviewer, indicating it links a Review to its author/reviewer. They connect different kinds of things in different directions and serve different purposes.

Presenter city is a subclass of City, denoting the city where a presenter is located or presents. Hotel is a subclass of Place, denoting accommodation. These are distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'adjustedBy' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it. In edas, 'hasReviewHistory' links a Reviewer to their Personal ReviewHistory. They relate different entity types in opposite directions and denote different relations in the conference domain.

In Conference ontology, Abstract is a document class representing the abstract part of a paper/poster/presentation, sitting under Extended abstract in the document hierarchy. In edas, Conference is the event class representing the conference itself, with subclasses like Single Level Conference and Two Level Conference, and properties such as endDate, hasCountry, paperDueOn. These denote completely different things: a document artefact vs. the conference event.

In ontology A, Steering committee is a specific subclass of Committee (alongside Organizing committee and Program committee). In ontology B, Committee is the general class with children Best Paper Awards Committee, Organizing Committee, and Program Committee. Thus A's Steering committee is a specific committee type subsumed by B's general Committee class, not equivalent to it.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'end Review' (cmt) relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review, denoting the action of ending/terminating a review. 'expert On' (confOf) relates a Member PC to a Topic, indicating the reviewer's area of expertise. They connect different entity types (Chair/Review vs. MemberPC/Topic) and express unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

In ekaw, SC Member is a sub-committee member (a PC Member role, under Person), while in iasted, IASTED member is a type of Delegate (under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate). The two ontologies model very different concepts: ekaw's SC Member is a committee role for reviewing/organizing, whereas iasted's IASTED member is a conference attendee who holds membership in the IASTED organization. Their intended instances do not coincide.

In cmt, Author is a person who submits and writes papers, sitting under Person > Conference Member. In sigkdd, Award is a prize (e.g., Best Paper Award) given at the conference. They share no instances and occupy completely different parts of the domain hierarchy.

confOf:Company is a type of organization (e.g., a sponsoring or employing company), while iasted:Conference_restaurant is a physical place/building where conference-related dining occurs. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Organization vs Place/Building) and denote completely different kinds of entities.

These properties operate at different levels of abstraction and have different domains. 'manuscript Due On' is a direct property of Conference with range dateTime, representing the manuscript submission deadline for an entire conference. 'done till' is a property of Deadline (a separate class) with range date, representing when any arbitrary deadline task must be completed. They do not share the same domain type, the same range type, or the same structural position. A reference alignment would not equate them.

A is a document/artefact: the written contribution that has been accepted (path: Conference document > ... > Accepted contribution). B is an activity/event: the act of accepting a manuscript (path: Activity > Activity before conference > Accepting manuscript). They share the word 'accept' but denote fundamentally different categories (product vs. process), so they are unrelated.

A TPC Member is a committee member responsible for reviewing papers and initiating calls, while a Speaker is a delegate who presents at the conference. These are distinct roles; a TPC member need not present, and a speaker need not be on the programme committee.

Administrative event in confOf covers organizational tasks (registration, reviewing, submission, camera ready), while Scientific Event in ekaw covers academic gatherings (conference, session, track, workshop, presentation). They are disjoint subtypes of Event with no instance overlap.

confOf Student is a specific subclass of Participant denoting a student attendee, whereas ekaw Conference Participant is the general class of all conference participants (including chairs, presenters, OC members, etc.). Student is a narrower concept subsumed by Conference Participant.

Both classes represent social events within a conference: confOf's 'Social event' (child of Event, with children Banquet, Reception, Trip) and edas's 'Social Event' (child of Non Academic Event under Conference Event, with children Excursion, Reception). They share the same intended instances (banquets, receptions, excursions, trips) and occupy the same conceptual niche in the conference-organisation domain. The near-identical labels, overlapping children (Reception appears in both), and parallel position as the social/non-academic event category confirm equivalence.

A 'Registered applicant' is a person who has registered (applied) to attend a conference, while a 'Presenter' is a participant who presents a paper. Registration and presentation are orthogonal concerns: one can register without presenting, and presenters are typically a subset of registered participants. The two classes do not denote the same concept, and neither subsumes the other in the given ontologies.

The confOf 'reviewes' property links a Member PC to a Contribution (a PC member reviews a paper), while the sigkdd 'obtain' property links an Author to an Award (an author obtains an award). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: 'has the last name' captures a person's surname, while 'has Biography' captures a free-text biographical description. They do not share instances or meaning, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Computer Architecture Topic' is a subject classification for conference papers, a subclass of Topic. In the IASTED ontology, 'Video cassette player' is a physical piece of audiovisual equipment, a subclass of Item > Audiovisual equipment. They share no instances and have no semantic relationship.

These properties differ in both type and meaning. 'has Cost Amount' is a datatype property from Sponsorship to int, representing the monetary amount of a sponsorship. 'is paid in' is an object property from Money to Building, indicating where money is paid. They relate different domains and ranges and express different relations.

Conference volume in ontology A represents the conference event/edition itself (it has committees, tracks, parts, important dates, and contributions), while Proceedings in ekaw is a document (a multi-author volume of published papers). They are related—a conference volume produces proceedings—but they denote different kinds of entities (event vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

Both properties have domain Paper, but they relate the paper to different things: 'is Reviewed By' points to the reviewer (a person/role), while 'has Review' points to the review document/artifact itself. They are related (a paper that is reviewed by someone also has a review), but they are not equivalent because their ranges differ in kind.

Entity A is a conference document providing information for participants (e.g., logistics, venue details), while entity B is a subject-area topic within the domain of wireless communications research. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (documents vs. topics) and share no semantic overlap.

The two properties are completely different: A is an object property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume, while B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (the city name). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings.

cmt's PaperFullVersion is a specific subclass of Paper (a full version, as opposed to an abstract), while confOf's Paper is the general class of papers (a sibling of Short paper and Poster). Thus PaperFullVersion is subsumed by confOf's Paper rather than equivalent to it.

Administrative event in confOf covers organizational workflow events (submission, reviewing, registration, camera ready), while Academic Event in edas covers scholarly content events (paper presentations, talks, workshops, organizational meetings). They are disjoint branches under their respective Event hierarchies with no overlap in intended instances.

These two datatype properties denote completely different attributes. 'has an ISBN' assigns an International Standard Book Number to Conference proceedings (a bibliographic identifier), while 'Name of conference' assigns the human-readable name of a Conference. They have different domains (Conference proceedings vs. Conference), different semantics, and no overlap in meaning.

Both classes denote a workshop event in the conference domain. In ontology A, Workshop is a part of a conference (sibling to Track, Tutorial) and is the range of 'has workshops' from Conference volume. In ontology B, Workshop is a Scientific Event (sibling to Conference, Track, Session, etc.). Despite slightly different structural positions, both represent the same real-world concept of a workshop held as part of a conference.

In ontology Conference, 'Topic' denotes a subject area or theme of conference parts, reviews, and contributions (e.g., it is the range of 'has a track workshop tutorial topic' and relates to review preferences). In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a document authored and submitted by an Author, sitting under Document alongside Abstract and Review. These are fundamentally different concepts: a Topic is a subject classification, while a Paper is a concrete written artefact. There is no subsumption relationship between them either.

The property 'has gender' in Conference denotes the gender of a Person, while 'has Surname' in confOf denotes the surname (family name) of a Person. These are completely different attributes of a person and share no semantic relationship.

These properties connect different things: 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to the Conference volume (event/venue) where it is submitted, while 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (subject area). They have different ranges (Conference volume vs. Topic) and express fundamentally different relationships (submission venue vs. subject matter).

hasFirstName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's first name). is_given_to is an object property from Item to Person (indicating an item is given to a person). They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Signal Processing Topic is a subject-area topic (sibling of Communication Theory, Computer Networks, etc.) denoting a research domain, while Program Committee is an organizational committee responsible for paper selection. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

In confOf, Author is a specific role under Person whose instances write contributions. In sigkdd, Speaker is a broader role under Person (with Author as a subclass) whose instances give presentations. The sigkdd Speaker subsumes the sigkdd Author, but the confOf Author and sigkdd Speaker are distinct concepts with different intended instances: confOf Author denotes paper authors, while sigkdd Speaker denotes anyone who presents (including invited speakers and authors who present). They overlap (authors who present) but are not equivalent, and the cross-ontology subsumption is not clean enough to assert directly.

Conference contribution is a document-like artefact (paper, poster, presentation) submitted to a conference volume, whereas Administrative event is a temporal event in the conference workflow (registration, reviewing, submission). They belong to disjoint branches (documents vs events) and share no instances.

Paper Abstract is a document component (a short summary of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Platinum Supporter is a top-tier sponsor category in the sigkdd ontology. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote unrelated relations. In cmt, 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrator entering review criteria for a conference). In sigkdd, 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (a speaker presenting a document). There is no overlap in meaning, direction, or the kinds of entities related.

Organizer in the Conference ontology denotes a person or committee member who organizes a conference, whereas Organization in confOf denotes an institutional entity (with subclasses Company and University) that has an address and employs people. These are disjoint kinds of entities: an organizer is an agent role, not an institution.

Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution (paper-writing relation), while property B (pay) relates a Person to Money (payment relation). They connect entirely different domain and range types and denote completely different relations in the conference domain.

edas:hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (its member/participant), whereas ekaw:hasPart is a generic mereological relation (whole-to-part). They differ in both domain/range and meaning: membership of a person in a conference is not the same as a part-of relationship.

cmt's AuthorNotReviewer is a subclass of Author (a Person who writes a paper but is not a reviewer), while iasted's Author is a broad class under Delegate > Speaker that includes lecturers, tutorial speakers, and plenary speakers. The cmt class is a narrower, role-specific concept subsumed by the more general iasted Author class.

Conference applicant is a subclass of Person, denoting someone who applies to attend a conference. Registration Non Member is a subclass of Registration fee, denoting a fee category for non-members. One is a person role, the other is a fee type; they denote completely different kinds of entities.

Tutorial Abstract is a document type (a written abstract for a tutorial), while Nonauthor registration fee is a monetary fee for non-author registration. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.
Bid in cmt is an offer by a reviewer to review a paper, while City in confOf is a geographic location. These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Workshop is an event where work is presented/discussed (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Worker non speaker is a person—a delegate who does not give a speech (subclass of Non speaker under Delegate). One is an event, the other a person role; they share no instances and are not hierarchically related.

Property 'issues' in Conference ontology relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher publishes proceedings). Property 'presentationed_by' in sigkdd relates a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no overlap in meaning.

Track workshop chair (a Person who chaired a track/workshop) and Session chair (a Delegate who chaired a session) denote different organizational roles in a conference. They are not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Social event is a non-academic event (Banquet, Reception, Trip) under Event, while iasted:Submission is a document type (Final/Initial manuscript) under Item > Document. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings, while hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person attending it. They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but they differ in domain and scope. paperDueOn (domain: Conference) specifically denotes the deadline for paper submissions in a conference, while is_dated_on (domain: Activity) is a more general property that assigns a date to any Activity. Since a Conference deadline is a specific kind of date assignment to a conference-scoped activity, paperDueOn is subsumed by the more general is_dated_on relation.

In the Conference ontology, Track is a subdivision of a conference volume (e.g., a research track within a conference), sibling to Tutorial and Workshop. In confOf, Workshop is a type of working event (an event itself), sibling to Conference and Tutorial. A Track is a session/category within a conference, while a Workshop is a standalone event. They denote different concepts despite both being subtypes of conference parts/events.

In ekaw, 'Proceedings Publisher' is a subclass of Organisation, denoting the entity that publishes proceedings (e.g., Springer, IEEE). In iasted, 'Book proceeding' is a subclass of Publication > Item, denoting the physical/volume output itself. One is an agent/organisation, the other is a document/artefact; they are disjoint categories.

In ekaw, Session Chair is a subclass of Person/Conference Participant, denoting a person who chairs a session. In iasted, Viza is a subclass of Document, denoting a visa document. These are completely different categories (person vs. document) with no overlap in intended instances.

Medicine Topic in edas is a subject-area topic (a research topic like Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), while Simulating in iasted is a type of research activity performed before a conference. One is a topic/subject classification, the other is an activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

hasEndDateTime applies to Conference Event (the end time of an event like a talk or session), while done_till applies to Deadline (the date by which a task must be completed). They have different domains (Conference Event vs Deadline) and different semantics: one marks when an event ends, the other marks a deadline cutoff date.

Co chair in Conference is a committee co-chair (e.g., of an organizing or program committee), whereas Session Chair in edas is a person who chairs a conference session and also reviews papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one co-chairs a committee, the other chairs a session. They do not share a common parent in their respective ontologies (Committee member vs Person), and their associated properties differ entirely.

The two properties differ in domain, range, and direction. Property A (has_a_committee_co-chair) goes from Committee to Co-chair, while property B (isMemberOf) goes from Person to Conference. They are not inverses of each other (A's range is Co-chair, not Person; B's range is Conference, not Committee), and they relate entirely different kinds of entities. There is no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Both are object properties linking a written document to its author. In edas, the domain is Paper (a specialization of Document) and the range is Author (a specialization of Person); in ekaw, the domain is Document and the range is Person. The slight difference in generality of domain/range is typical of the Conference track and reference alignments treat these as equivalent.

Author_cd_proceedings_included is a subclass of Author (a delegate who wrote a paper included in conference proceedings on CD). Invited_Speaker is a subclass of Speaker (a person invited to give a talk). One is an author distinguished by the publication medium of their paper; the other is a speaker distinguished by invitation status. They denote different roles and neither subsumes the other.

Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing a paper submission deadline, while Abstract is a short summary document of a paper. They are different document types with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:follows relates one Administrative event to another (e.g., an event following another in a sequence), while ekaw:listsEvent relates a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event it lists. They have completely different domains and ranges, and denote different relations (temporal/sequential ordering vs. listing/publishing).

The two properties relate completely different entities. 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee, while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution they authored. They share no domain, range, or semantic overlap.

Industrial Session in EKAW is a conference session characterized by industrial (non-academic) content, while Speaker lecture in IASTED is a lecture delivered by a speaker. They are different kinds of entities: one classifies sessions by content type, the other by presentation format. Their positions in the respective hierarchies do not suggest overlap, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. `has Member` links a Conference to a Person (its member), while `is held before` links an Activity to a Time (when it occurs). They share no domain, range, or semantic overlap.

confOf:abstract is a datatype property from Contribution to string (the abstract text of a contribution), while ekaw:writtenBy is an object property from Document to Person (the authorship relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings—one maps a contribution to its textual abstract, the other maps a document to its author. No alignment relation holds.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Published Paper' is a class representing a document artefact—a paper that has been published—situated under Document > Paper. In the IASTED ontology, 'Accepting manuscript' is a class representing an activity or event (under Activity > Activity before conference), not a document. One denotes a concrete artefact, the other denotes a process/action in the conference timeline. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference, but cmt:date is a generic conference date while edas:manuscriptDueOn specifically denotes the manuscript submission deadline. manuscriptDueOn is a more specific subproperty of date.

These properties are completely different. In cmt, 'write Review' is an object property with domain Reviewer and range Review, meaning a reviewer writes a review. In the Conference ontology, 'has an expertise' is a datatype property with domain Review expertise, representing some expertise attribute as a data value. They have different domains, different ranges (object vs datatype), and different semantics: one relates a reviewer to a review document, the other assigns a data value to an expertise entity.

Property A ('was a track workshop chair of') relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part, expressing a chairing role over a conference track/workshop. Property B ('is given by') relates an Activity/Item to a Person, expressing who presents or gives an activity/item. The domains (chair vs. activity/item), ranges (conference part vs. person), and directions are entirely different, and the relations denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Rejection in cmt is a Decision (the act of rejecting a paper), while Accepted contribution in Conference is the written contribution itself that has been accepted. They are different categories of entity (decision vs. artefact), and they even represent opposite outcomes, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document (e.g., logistics, travel, accommodation info) intended for conference attendees. 'Computer Networks Optical Topic' in the EDAS ontology is a subject topic used to classify papers (a subtopic of Computer Networks). They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

These properties denote different relationships. 'rejected By' links a Paper to the Administrator who made the rejection decision, while 'has Reviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer assigned to review it. They have different domains/ranges (Administrator vs Possible Reviewer) and capture semantically distinct aspects of the paper workflow: rejection decision vs review assignment.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'start Reviewer Bidding' (domain: Administrator, range: Conference) is an administrative action that initiates the reviewer bidding phase for a conference. 'invites co-reviewers' (domain: Reviewer, range: Reviewer) is a peer-to-peer action where a reviewer invites another reviewer to collaborate. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and denote different relations. In Conference, 'invited by' links a Reviewer to the Reviewer who invited them (reviewer-to-reviewer invitation). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presented it (document-to-speaker presentation relation). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint.

confOf:City denotes a geographic location (a city), used as the range of a 'has City' property for Organization and Person. sigkdd:Person denotes a human participant in a conference (with subclasses Listener, Organizator, Speaker). These are completely disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are subclasses of Document and represent the central concept of a conference paper submitted for review. They share core properties: authorship (has Author / is Written By), review assignment (assigned To / is Reviewed By), and topic/subject area (has Subject Area / has Topic). The differences in children (Paper Abstract/Paper Full Version vs. Accepted/Active/Pending/Published/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper) reflect different modelling choices for paper states and versions, not different intended extensions of the Paper class itself. Both denote the same concept: a document that is a paper in the conference domain.

A Session Chair is a person who chairs a specific conference session, while a Program Committee member is an organizer who reviews papers and helps decide the program. These are distinct roles in conference organization; neither subsumes the other (a session chair need not be a PC member, and a PC member need not chair a session).

In the iasted ontology, Transparency is a specific conference document type (e.g., overhead transparency for presentations), sitting alongside forms, invitation letters, visas, etc. In sigkdd, Abstract refers to the summary of a paper. These are distinct document types with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Abstract in cmt denotes the abstract component of a paper (a document part), while Active Paper in edas denotes a paper in a particular workflow state (active, as opposed to accepted, rejected, pending, etc.). They share the parent Paper but represent fundamentally different concepts: one is a document sub-type, the other is a review-process status classification. Their instances do not coincide.

Both classes denote the same concept: a member of a conference's Program Committee. They share identical labels (modulo case), occupy structurally parallel positions in their respective hierarchies (cmt: Person > Conference Member > Program Committee Member; sigkdd: Person > Organizator > Program Committee member), and the cmt comment explicitly describes the Program Committee membership role. The surrounding properties in cmt (has Program Committee Member, member Of Program Committee) further confirm the intended semantics match.

Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, sitting under Person > Conference Member > Author. Student registration fee is a monetary amount for student registration, sitting under Money > Fee > Registration fee. They denote completely different domain concepts (a person vs. a fee) with no overlap.

These properties have different domains and different meanings. `has_a_date_of_issue` applies to Conference documents and records when a document was issued. `manuscriptDueOn` applies to a Conference itself and records the deadline for manuscript submission. One is about a document's issue date, the other is about a submission deadline for the conference. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two properties relate entirely different domains and ranges. 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee, while 'lists Event' links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in the kinds of things they connect.

Reviewing_results_event is an administrative event where authors receive reviewing results, while Author_information_form is a document/form that authors fill in. One is an event, the other is a document; they share no common instances.
