Meeting Room Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where meetings occur, while Hotel registration form is a document (subclass of Form > Document > Item) used for hotel registration. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Demo Session is a type of conference session where demonstrations are presented, while Program Committee is a committee responsible for reviewing papers. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Sponsor (under Person in iasted) denotes a person or entity that provides financial sponsorship, while Webmaster (under Organizator in sigkdd) denotes a person responsible for managing the website. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In the Conference ontology, 'Call for paper' is a conference document—an announcement soliciting paper submissions—sibling to items like 'Conference announcement' and 'Information for participants'. In confOf, 'Poster' is a type of Contribution (a submitted artefact), sibling to 'Paper' and 'Short paper'. One is an announcement document, the other is a presentation artefact; they share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who enables a virtual meeting. In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker who presents it. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

Short_paper in confOf is a specific type of contribution (a track/category of submission), whereas Initial_manuscript in iasted is a stage in the document lifecycle (initial vs. final version). They classify submissions along different dimensions (type vs. lifecycle stage), so their intended instances do not coincide.

confOf:University is an academic institution (subclass of Organization, domain of studyAt from Scholar), while iasted:Value_added_tax is a financial charge (subclass of Tax > Money). They share no domain overlap whatsoever.

A Presenter is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant), while an Introduction is a conference activity/event (subclass of Conference activity). They denote completely different categories of entities: a person vs. an activity.

In ontology A, 'Conference document' is a broad top-level class covering many kinds of conference-related documents (call for papers, announcements, contributions, reviews, web pages, etc.). In ontology B, 'Conference Proceedings' is a very specific class — a published volume of collected papers, deeply nested under Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings. The two do not coincide: A's class is far more general and includes items that are not proceedings at all, while B's class is a narrow publication type. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way (A's class is a sibling-level grouping, not a superclass of proceedings).

confOf:Company is a kind of Organization (e.g., a sponsoring or affiliated company), while sigkdd:Main_office is a kind of Place (a physical location). They belong to disjoint branches of their respective hierarchies and denote different categories of entities: an organization vs. a physical venue/location. No reference alignment would equate them.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document (e.g., logistics, travel, accommodation info for attendees), while 'Computer Networks Sensor Topic' in the edas ontology is a subject taxonomy topic for paper classification. They share no domain overlap.

Both are object properties linking an event/activity to its location. EKAW's 'held In' has domain Event and range Location; IASTED's 'is held in' has domain Activity and range Place (among others). In the conference domain, Event and Activity are closely aligned, as are Location and Place. The properties share the same label meaning and direction (event -> location), making them equivalent.

Entity A is a subclass of Person denoting a human contributor to a conference (authors, speakers, participants). Entity B is the conference event itself, with properties like dates, country, topics, and members. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties differ in domain, range, and intended meaning. 'has an expertise' (Conference) is a datatype property with domain Review expertise, capturing the topic/area of expertise a reviewer brings to a review. 'has Review History' (edas) is an object property from Reviewer to Personal Review History, capturing a reviewer's accumulated review records. They relate different entities (review-expertise objects vs. reviewers) and connect to different kinds of values (expertise data vs. review-history objects), so they are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumer of the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'reviewer Of Paper' links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the reviewer reviews the paper). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (the document is presented by the speaker). The domains (Possible Reviewer vs Document) and ranges (Paper vs Speaker) do not overlap, and the relations denote different real-world associations (reviewing vs presenting).

Chairman in cmt is a person role (a type of Person who can mark conflicts of interest), while Computer Networks Security Topic in edas is a subject topic under the Topic hierarchy. They denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Conference announcement in the Conference ontology is a subclass of Conference document, i.e. a written artefact announcing a conference. Conference Event in edas is a superclass of Academic Event and Non Academic Event, i.e. an actual event with attendees, locations, dates and programmes. A document is not the same kind of thing as an event, so the two classes are unrelated.

Property A captures the date of issue of a conference document, while property B captures the title of a social or working event. They differ in both domain and range (date vs string) and denote completely unrelated attributes.

Entity A is a person role (Tutorial Chair) who organizes/chairs a tutorial, while entity B is the tutorial event/activity itself. They are completely different concepts: one is a person, the other is an activity.

A is a topic about optical computer networks (a subject-area classification under Topic > Computer Networks Topic), while B is a state/role (Sponsor state) under State, with siblings like Conference state and Presenter state. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In ekaw, 'Web Site' is a subclass of Document representing an online web resource (e.g., conference website), with properties like 'event On List' and 'publisher Of'. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a subclass of Document representing an academic paper submitted by an author. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances and no overlap.

Rejected_Paper in EKAW is a document (an evaluated paper that was rejected), while Accepting_manuscript in IASTED is an activity (the act of accepting a manuscript). They belong to disjoint branches (Document vs Activity) and denote fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Active_conference_participant in ontology Conference is a specific subclass of Conference contributor (and Conference participant) that actively contributes, e.g. gives presentations. ekaw Conference_Participant is a broad class covering any participant, including chairs, registered participants, presenters, etc. Thus A is more specific than B; A is subsumed_by B.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad superclass encompassing authors, reviewers, and various committee roles—anyone who is a member of a conference. In the Conference ontology, Track workshop chair is a specific role limited to chairing tracks, workshops, or tutorials. The cmt Conference Member is far more general and does not specifically denote a track/workshop chair. The two classes do not share the same intended instances, and neither subsumes the other in a clearly aligned hierarchy.

Accommodation Place in edas denotes lodging (hotels, dorms, etc.) as indicated by its label and sibling structure (Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). Conference hall in iasted denotes a meeting/presentation space, not lodging. Their intended instances do not coincide; they are disjoint categories of Place.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level event (a whole conference gathering), sibling to Tutorial and Workshop under Working event. In iasted, Session is a specific lecture-type activity within a conference (child of Lecture, sibling to Plenary lecture and Tutorial), with a child 'Speaker lecture'. These denote very different things: a Conference is the entire event, while a Session is a sub-activity/session within a conference. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

In EDAS, 'Paper' is an individual academic submission authored by researchers, reviewed by reviewers, and classified by acceptance status (Accepted, Rejected, etc.). In EKAW, 'Multi-author Volume' is a collection-type document (e.g., proceedings) published by an organisation, with 'Proceedings' as a subclass. An individual paper is not a multi-author volume; they are sibling-level document subtypes with different intended instances.

cmt:Review is a review document written by a reviewer for a paper, while edas:TextualReviewQuestion is a question (e.g., 'What are the strengths?') within a review form. One is the review artefact itself; the other is a component of a review form. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Reviewer and Speaker denote distinct roles in a conference. A Reviewer evaluates submitted papers (domain of review-related properties), while a Speaker gives presentations at the conference (domain of presentation properties). Although both are subclasses of Person, their intended instances do not coincide: a reviewer need not present, and a speaker (e.g., an invited speaker) need not review. They are not in a subsumption relation either, so they are unrelated.

These properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. 'hasRelatedDocument' links events/persons to documents, while 'presentationed_by' links documents to speakers. They are not equivalent, not inverse-equivalent (inverse would be 'presented by' linking document to person, not 'has related document'), and do not share a subsumption relationship.

A 'Talk Event' in edas is a kind of academic event (e.g., a talk, presentation, or session) occurring at a conference, with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk. B 'Committee' in sigkdd is an organizational body (e.g., Program Committee, Organizing Committee) responsible for running the conference. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Author is a person who submits/writes papers. In Conference, Topic is a subject area associated with conference parts and review preferences. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

edas:hasEndDateTime applies to any Conference Event (a broad class covering conferences, sessions, talks, etc.), while sigkdd:End_of_conference applies specifically to a Conference. Thus hasEndDateTime is more general, subsumed by End_of_conference in the sense that the sigkdd property is the narrower one; however the sigkdd property is more specific, so hasEndDateTime is subsumed_by End_of_conference only if we view the sigkdd property as the more specific relation. Correctly: hasEndDateTime (broader domain) is subsumed_by End_of_conference (narrower domain) is not standard; rather End_of_conference is subsumed_by hasEndDateTime. So the relation is that hasEndDateTime subsumes End_of_conference.

Break Event in EDAS is a non-academic event (coffee break, free time, meal break) — a pause in the programme. Presentation in IASTED is an academic activity where a speaker presents work (PowerPoint, video). These are disjoint kinds of conference entities, not equivalent.

Property A (has_important_dates) links a Conference volume to its Important dates (e.g., submission deadlines), while property B (heldIn) links an Event to its physical Location. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain: one concerns temporal deadlines, the other concerns the physical venue where an event takes place. They do not share domain or range types, and neither subsumes the other.
A is the registration fee for a non-member of the organizing society; B is the registration fee for a SIGMOD member. They are disjoint categories under Registration fee, not the same concept.

The cmt property hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to its Subject Area, while the sigkdd property obtain relates an Author to an Award. They connect completely different domain and range entities and describe unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

Meeting Room Place in EDAS denotes a room where meetings/sessions take place, a fine-grained facility inside a venue. Conference building in IASTED is a broader physical building that hosts a conference (and oddly has Delegate as a child). One is a room-level place, the other a building-level place; neither subsumes the other in a clear, intended way, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent.

Information for participants is a conference document providing logistical details to attendees, while Slide Set is a document consisting of presentation slides. They are sibling document types under different document hierarchies but denote clearly different artefacts with no overlap in intended instances.

The edas Conference class denotes an academic conference event (with children like Single Level Conference, properties like paper Due On, has Topic, etc.). The iasted Conference_restaurant is a physical place/building where conference participants dine, a subclass of Building. These are completely different concepts despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

hasEmail is a datatype property from Person to string (an email address), whereas obtain is an object property from Person to Item (a physical or abstract item). They differ in type, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to a string (its title), while the sigkdd 'Price' property relates a Registration fee to an int (its monetary price). They have different domains, different ranges, and denote completely unrelated attributes in the conference domain.

These properties have opposite domains and ranges and denote different relations. In ekaw, 'written By' relates a Document to the Person who authored it (Document -> Person). In iasted, 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they present or provide (Person -> Activity/Item). They are not inverses of each other either, since writing a document is not the same act as giving/presenting an activity or item. The concepts and relation directions are fundamentally different.

The property 'initiates' in edas specifically relates conference roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call (e.g., call for papers), while 'give' in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., giving a presentation or distributing an item). These denote different relations in the conference domain: initiating a call vs. giving/delivering something. They do not share the same domain, range, or semantic intent.

Sponzorship in iasted is a monetary concept (subclass of Money, sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip), representing the financial transaction/amount of sponsorship. Platinum Supporter in sigkdd is a specific sponsor role/category (subclass of Sponzor, sibling of Gold/Bronze/Silver Supporter), representing an entity that provides sponsorship at a particular tier. One is the financial contribution itself; the other is the contributing entity at a specific level. These are fundamentally different concepts with no direct equivalence or subsumption relationship.
`deals With` relates a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while `is sent after` relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap.

has_the_first_name is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's first name), while speak_in is an object property from Person to Place/Time (where/when a person speaks). They have completely different ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

Conference building (iasted) denotes a building where a conference takes place (e.g., convention center), while Hotel (sigkdd) denotes lodging accommodation. They are distinct types of places in the conference domain: one hosts the academic sessions, the other provides overnight stay. Although both are subclasses of Place, their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Paper Full Version is a conference document (a full paper submission) in the cmt ontology, while Single hotel room is a physical accommodation place in the iasted ontology. They belong to completely different domains (documents vs. places) and share no semantic overlap.

Committee member is a subclass of Person denoting people who serve on a committee (with children Chair, Co chair). Registration fee is a subclass of Fee denoting monetary charges for conference registration (with children like Registration Student, Registration Non Member). These are entirely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference, while Talk Event in edas is an event (a talk). One is a person/role, the other is an event/activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Important dates in the Conference ontology represents a container of deadline-related dates (abstract submission, full paper submission, acceptance announcement, etc.) for a conference volume. Accepted Paper in the edas ontology is a subclass of Paper/Document representing a paper that has been accepted for publication/presentation. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A is a class denoting a person who authors papers (subclass of Person/Conference Member in cmt). B is a class denoting a published volume of conference papers (with ISBN, publisher, volume). They share no instances and no subsumption relationship; they are unrelated.

Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion) in confOf, while Hotel fee is a monetary fee for accommodation in iasted. They belong to completely different domains (events vs. money) and share no conceptual overlap.

In ontology A, 'Conference fees' is a broad category covering all fees associated with attending a conference (registration, banquet, etc.). In ontology B, 'Registration fee' is a specific subclass of 'Fee' with particular subtypes (member, non-member, student). Registration fees are one type of conference fee, so A is subsumed by B's broader Fee concept, but A is more general than B's Registration_fee specifically.

Contribution 1th author is a class representing a person who is the first author of a conference contribution, while Proceedings is a class representing a published multi-author volume of papers. They denote completely different categories of entities (person vs. document) and share no meaningful relationship.

A Submitted Paper in EKAW is a specific paper under review (child of Paper, sibling of Camera Ready Paper, etc.), whereas a Publication in IASTED is a published item (child of Item, parent of Book proceeding and Cd proceeding). A submitted paper is not yet published, so these denote different stages and different concepts; they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties are completely different in meaning and type. 'event On List' in ekaw is an object property linking an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (i.e., the event is listed on that document/site). 'End of conference' in sigkdd is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime value representing when the conference ends. They share no semantic overlap.

Associated Chair is a person role (a kind of conference committee member under Chairman in cmt), while Contributed Talk is a scientific event/presentation in ekaw. One denotes a person, the other an event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In the iasted ontology, Document is a broad superclass encompassing many artefacts (forms, invitation letters, mailing lists, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc.), while in the sigkdd ontology Review is a specific subclass of Document. The two entities are at different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept: one is a general document container, the other is a particular kind of document (a review). They are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption relation across the two ontologies.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Registration deadline is a temporal deadline for registration. They belong to disjoint branches (documents vs. time points) and denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'held In' (Event -> Location) indicates where an event takes place. 'is held after' (Activity -> Time) indicates a temporal relation. They relate different kinds of things (spatial vs. temporal) and are not equivalent.

These properties have different meanings in the conference domain. 'assigned To' relates a Paper to a Reviewer who is assigned to review it, while 'is Written By' relates a Paper to its Author. Reviewers and Authors are distinct roles, so these properties denote different relations.

Multimedia Topic is a subject area for conference papers (subclass of Topic), while Video cassette player is a physical piece of audiovisual equipment. They denote completely different concepts despite both being in conference-domain ontologies.

The property 'contributes' in Conference relates a Person to a Conference document they author or contribute to, while 'notification until' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Deadline for author notification. These are entirely different relations: one denotes authorship/contribution to a document, the other denotes a temporal deadline associated with notifying an author. Their domains and ranges are also disjoint in meaning (Conference document vs. Deadline Author notification).

Reviewer in the Conference ontology is a class denoting a person who reviews papers (subclass of Person, with properties for review expertise, review preference, and inviting co-reviewers). PersonalPublicationHistory in the edas ontology is a class denoting a record of a person's publication history (subclass of PersonalHistory, sibling of PersonalReviewHistory). These are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is a history/record object. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Member PC in confOf is a Program Committee member who reviews papers (comment says 'Reviewer', has reviewes property linking to Contribution). Webmaster in sigkdd is a technical role under Organizator responsible for web infrastructure. These are distinct conference roles with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference 'Paper' is a general class for regular conference contributions (papers, with siblings like Extended abstract). Edas 'RatedPapers' is a specific subclass of Active Paper that has received reviews/ratings. Every Rated Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is a Rated Paper (unrated or pending papers exist). Thus Paper subsumes RatedPapers.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'hasBeenAssigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer assigned to review a paper). In sigkdd, 'designed_by' links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (a deadline created/designed by the SIGKDD organization). The domains (Reviewer vs Deadline) and ranges (Paper vs ACM SIGKDD) are entirely disjoint, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

In EDAS, Workshop is a standalone academic event (a meeting with its own theme, organizers, etc.). In EKAW, Conference_Session is a time-slot block within a conference, and Workshop is not a session but rather appears as a sibling (Workshop_Session) under Session. Thus EDAS Workshop is not equivalent to EKAW Conference_Session; they overlap in the conference domain but denote different kinds of entities.

Both are conference chair roles under Person, but cmt's Associated Chair is a specialized sub-role of Chairman (alongside Conference Chair, PC Chair, etc.), while confOf's Chair PC is a top-level role under Person. They overlap conceptually as chair-type roles but are not equivalent: Associated Chair is more specific (a sub-kind of Chairman), and Chair PC may encompass PC chair duties more broadly. The structural positions differ and the labels are not synonymous, so 'related' is the safest verdict.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Track is a scientific event/session within a conference. They share no instances and are from entirely different parts of the hierarchy (person vs. event).

These classes denote completely different concepts. In EKAW, Conference_Proceedings is a publication artifact (a document/volume of collected conference papers), while in IASTED, Conference_state is a temporal or organizational state of a conference (sibling to Presenter_state and Sponsor_state). No overlap in intended instances.

In ontology Conference, 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person denoting people who participate in a conference (with children Active/Passive conference participant). In edas, 'Conference' is the event itself (with properties like end Date, has Country, paper Due On, and children Single/Two Level Conference). These are completely different concepts: a person vs. an event.

The property 'written By' in ekaw relates a Document to the Person who authored it, while 'payed by' in sigkdd relates a Registration fee to the Person who paid it. These are entirely different relations with different domains (Document vs. Registration fee) and different semantics (authorship vs. payment). They share only the range (Person), which is insufficient for equivalence.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. In edas, hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating. The domains (Reviewer vs Active Paper), ranges (Paper vs Review Rating), and intended meanings (assignment vs rating) are completely different, so they are unrelated.

The two properties have opposite directions: cmt:readPaper has domain Reviewer and range Paper (reviewer reads paper), while ekaw:hasReviewer has domain Paper and range Possible_Reviewer (paper has reviewer). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. Since the task specifies that a property and its inverse are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other, the correct relation is unrelated.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. `reviewCriteriaEnteredBy` (cmt) relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria, while `hasReviewer` (ekaw) relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer assigned to review it. They connect different entity types and express different relationships.

Conference www is a web document about a conference (subclass of Conference document, with a URL property), while Computer Networks Security Topic is a subject topic within the Computer Networks domain hierarchy. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Subject Area in cmt denotes a research topic or domain category for a Paper, while Country in confOf denotes a geographical nation associated with Organizations and Persons. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. In cmt, 'addedBy' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (committee management). In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to the Speaker who presented it (presentation attribution). The domains (Program Committee Member vs Document), ranges (Administrator vs Speaker), and semantics are entirely distinct, so they are unrelated.

confOf:location denotes the physical/geographic location where an event is held (e.g., a city or venue), while sigkdd:Name_of_conference denotes the name/title of the conference itself. Despite both being datatype properties with range string, they express completely different attributes of a conference event.

`provided By` in edas links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it, while `pay` in iasted links a Person to Money. They have different domains (Sponsorship vs Person), different ranges (Organization vs Money), and express fundamentally different relationships: one identifies the sponsor of a sponsorship, the other records a monetary payment by a person. No subsumption or overlap holds.

Entity A is a Reviewer (a Person who reviews papers), while entity B is a Personal Review History (a record/document tracking a reviewer's past reviews). They are completely different kinds of things: one is a person, the other is a history object associated with a person. The edas ontology even has a separate 'Reviewer' class, confirming that PersonalReviewHistory is not meant to represent a reviewer.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria. In sigkdd, 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material). They relate different kinds of entities and express different relationships with no overlap.

These properties operate at different levels and have different domains and ranges. In Conference ontology, 'has a program committee' links a Conference volume (a specific edition of a conference) to its Program committee (the committee handling paper reviews). In sigkdd, 'hold' links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference (an event it organizes). The domains differ (Conference volume vs. ACM SIGKDD organization), the ranges differ (Program committee vs. Conference), and the relationships are fundamentally different: one assigns a committee to a conference edition, the other associates an organization with the conferences it holds.

These two classes denote entirely different concepts. In ekaw, Conference Session is a specific type of session within a conference (e.g., a regular session, demo session, poster session) where papers are presented. In iasted, Activity before conference refers to preparatory activities that occur before the conference takes place, such as accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts, renting, and research. One is a scheduled time-slot during the conference event itself; the other is a pre-conference organizational activity. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Paper Full Version (cmt) is a subclass of Document > Paper, denoting a written artefact (the full-length version of a paper). Author of paper (sigkdd) is a subclass of Person > Speaker > Author, denoting a human role. One is a document, the other is a person; they share no instances and are unrelated.

A is a person role (Conference Chair) in the cmt ontology, sitting under Person > Chairman, while B is an event (Camera Ready event) in confOf, sitting under Event > Administrative event. One denotes a human role, the other a temporal administrative event in the conference lifecycle; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference participant (A) is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference (with children like Active/Passive conference participant). Scientific Event (B) is a subclass of Event, denoting events such as conferences, sessions, workshops, and tracks. One is a person, the other is an event; they share no instances and are completely unrelated.

In cmt, Review is a document written by a reviewer about a paper (an artefact). In ekaw, Evaluated_Paper is a paper that has been assigned and gone through evaluation, i.e. the paper itself, not the review. They are disjoint kinds of entities: one is the review document, the other is the paper being evaluated.

The property 'written By' in confOf relates a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper), while 'awarded by' in sigkdd relates an Award to the entity that granted it. These are completely different relations in the conference domain: one concerns authorship of a paper, the other concerns the bestowal of an award. They do not share a domain or range overlap, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf: Tutorial is a subclass of Working event, i.e., an event/session at a conference. ekaw: Tutorial Abstract is a subclass of Abstract under Document, i.e., the written abstract text for a tutorial. One denotes an event, the other a document; they are not the same kind of entity.

Both are conference-preparation activities dealing with manuscripts, but they denote different stages: confOf 'Submission event' is the act of authors submitting contributions, while iasted 'Accepting manuscript' is the committee's act of accepting a submitted manuscript. They are temporally and functionally distinct events that overlap in topic but do not share the same instances.

confOf:Organization represents an organizational entity (e.g., Company, University) with address-related properties, while edas:ReviewRating represents a rating value for a paper review (e.g., Accept, Reject). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee, while property B links a Building, City, or State to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

A 'Paper' in cmt is a document submitted to a conference, with authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions. B 'Call For Reviews' in edas is a type of Call (sibling of Call For Papers, Call For Manuscripts) that solicits reviews, not a paper or document. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs conference roles (Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, etc.), a subclass of Person. Card in iasted is a physical item (subclass of Item, sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). These denote completely different things with no overlap in the conference domain.

The property hasCountry in edas relates a Conference to a Country (the country where the conference is held). The property is_visited_by in iasted relates a Building, City, or State to a Person (a person visiting that place). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

In the Conference ontology, Topic is a broad concept that covers any subject area used to classify conference parts, tracks, workshops, tutorials, and submitted contributions. In EKAW, Research Topic is specifically a topic covered by events and papers, implying a narrower, research-focused scope. Since every Research Topic is a Topic but not every Topic (e.g., administrative or logistical topics) is necessarily a Research Topic, Topic is subsumed by Research Topic in the sense that Research Topic is the more specific, research-oriented subclass.

The cmt 'date' property has domain Conference (the event itself), indicating the date the conference takes place. The Conference ontology 'has a date of issue' has domain Conference document, indicating when a document was issued. These relate to fundamentally different entities (an event vs. a document) and represent different relations, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Person/Chairman), while Sponsor city is a geographic location (subclass of City) that sponsors a conference. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person). In the Conference ontology, 'Conference' is the event/organization itself, which has conference volumes as parts. A person role and an event are disjoint kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In CMT, markConflictOfInterest records a conflict of interest between a person (Author/Chairman/Reviewer) and a Paper, explicitly preventing the reviewer from bidding on, being assigned to, or viewing reviews for that paper. In confOf, reviewes is the relation stating that a Member PC reviews a Contribution. One marks a conflict (exclusion from reviewing), while the other assigns a review task; they are semantically unrelated.

Committee member is a subclass of Person (a human who serves on a committee), while Place is a spatial location with subclasses like Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, etc. These are completely disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Reception is a social event (a gathering/venue activity) in confOf, while Listener is a person who attends a talk in sigkdd. They share no instances and belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies (Event vs Person).

Information for participants is a general conference document providing logistical or programmatic details to attendees, whereas an Invitation letter is a specific formal document (often for visa or attendance purposes). They serve different functions and do not share the same intended instances.

cmt's Paper is a specific kind of document (a submitted paper with reviews, bids, decisions, authors), whereas Conference's Conference_document is a broad superclass covering calls for papers, announcements, WWW pages, reviews, and contributions. Paper falls under the Conference contribution branch, so it is strictly more specific than Conference_document.

The iasted 'speak in' property relates a Person to a Place or Time (where/when they speak), while the sigkdd 'presentation' property relates a Speaker to a Document (the presentation artefact). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and do not denote the same relation.

In cmt, Document is a general class whose children are Paper and Review, so it covers any conference document. In sigkdd, Paper is a specific subclass of Document. Thus cmt:Document is strictly more general than sigkdd:Paper, so the relation is subsumes.

The cmt 'title' is a datatype property mapping a Paper to its title string, while the sigkdd 'submit' is an object property mapping an Author to a Paper they submit. They have different domains, different ranges (string vs Paper), and completely different semantics (attribute vs submission action).

confOf Participant is a broad class covering all conference attendees (with subclasses Member, Regular, Student), while iasted Speaker is a specialized Delegate who presents. Every Speaker is a Participant, but not every Participant is a Speaker (e.g., listeners, students). Thus Participant subsumes Speaker.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different ways. Property A links a 'Track workshop chair' to a 'Conference part' (expressing the chairing relationship of a conference part/track). Property B links roles like 'Conference Chair', 'Session Chair', or 'TPC Member' to a 'Call' (expressing initiation of a call, e.g., call for papers). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are distinct: one is about chairing a conference part, the other about initiating a call. There is no equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

confOf:Organization is a general class for organizations (with children Company and University). edas:IndustryOrganization is a specific subclass of edas:Organization, sibling to AcademiaOrganization, GovernmentOrganization, and NGO. The confOf Organization is more general, so confOf:Organization is subsumed_by edas:Organization (the parent), while IndustryOrganization is a narrower concept. They are not equivalent.

These properties are unrelated. confOf:abstract is a datatype property with domain Contribution and range string, representing the abstract text of a contribution. edas:manuscriptDueOn is a datatype property with domain Conference and range dateTime, representing the deadline date and time for manuscript submission. They have different domains (Contribution vs Conference), different ranges (string vs dateTime), and different semantics (content text vs deadline timestamp).

These two datatype properties have completely different domains and meanings. `reviewsPerPaper` (domain: Conference, range: int) captures the number of reviews assigned per paper in a conference-reviewing context. `has_amount_of` (domain: Money, range: int) captures a monetary quantity associated with a Money entity. They relate different kinds of things (Conference vs. Money) and denote unrelated attributes in the conference-organisation domain, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Reception and Conference Trip are both social events, but they denote different kinds of events: a reception is a welcome/gathering event, while a conference trip is an excursion. They are siblings under the same parent but not the same concept.

In cmt, User is a broad superclass encompassing Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—any person who uses the system. In confOf, Administrator is a specific role (a confTool administrator). The cmt Administrator is the counterpart of confOf Administrator, not cmt User. cmt User is far more general than confOf Administrator, and since the reference alignment treats these as distinct levels of granularity with no direct equivalence, the appropriate relation is unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document artifact (a short summary of a paper), while Wireless Communications Topic in edas is a subject-area classification topic. They share no instances and no semantic overlap.

Rejected_Paper in EKAW is a class denoting a paper whose submission has been evaluated and rejected (a document/artefact). Deadline_for_notification_of_acceptance in IASTED is a temporal deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance/rejection decisions. One is a document, the other is a time point; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The confOf 'written By' property links a Contribution to its Author, while the sigkdd 'search' property links an ACM SIGKDD conference to a Sponzor. These are completely different domain relations with different domain and range types, so they are unrelated.

Active Paper in EDAS is a specific subclass of Paper denoting papers that are currently active (with children like Rated Papers and siblings like Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn). EKAW Paper is the general class of all papers. Active Paper is thus a narrower concept subsumed by EKAW's Paper.

Conference contribution is a document type (subclass of Conference document) representing a paper, poster, or talk. Speaker is a person who gives a presentation. These are completely different categories: one is a document/artifact, the other is a person role. No overlap in intended instances.

hasCostAmount is a datatype property from Sponsorship to int (the numeric cost amount of a sponsorship). is_paid_with is an object property from Money to Item (the item with which money is paid). They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Sponsorship vs Money), range (int vs Item), and meaning (a numeric cost amount vs a payment instrument/item). They do not denote the same relation.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper (a Document) and is a sibling of Paper Full Version, indicating it represents the abstract portion of a paper. In confOf, Poster is a type of Contribution (alongside Paper and Short paper), representing a poster presentation at a conference. These are distinct concepts: one is a document component (the abstract of a paper), the other is a presentation format. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'is Menu Of' connects a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (indicating which event a menu belongs to), while 'presentationed by' connects a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presented a document). The domains (Meal Menu vs Document), ranges (Meal Event vs Speaker), and semantic meanings are completely different, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and not meaningfully related.

PaperFullVersion in cmt denotes a paper submitted in its complete/full form (as opposed to a Paper Abstract), describing the submission format. Accepted_Paper in ekaw denotes the acceptance status of a paper after evaluation. These are orthogonal dimensions: a full version paper could be accepted or rejected, and an accepted paper could be a full version or an abstract. Neither subsumes the other, and their instances do not coincide.

Conference participant in ontology Conference is a broad class covering all people who participate in a conference, including both active participants (e.g., presenters) and passive participants (e.g., audience members). Attendee in edas is a specific kind of conference participant—one who attends the conference. Since attendees are a subset of all conference participants, Conference participant subsumes Attendee.

The property 'has the first name' applies to a Person and captures a person's given name, while 'Name of sponsor' applies to a Sponzor and captures the name of a sponsoring organization. They have disjoint domains and denote unrelated attributes in the conference domain.

The two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. 'has authors' in Conference goes from Conference document to Person (document -> person), while 'author Of' in ekaw goes from Person to Document (person -> document). A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent; they relate the same kinds of things but in opposite directions.

Accommodation Place in edas is a general class covering any lodging venue (siblings include various place types under Place). Single hotel room in iasted is a specific type of accommodation (a single room within a hotel). Accommodation Place subsumes Single hotel room as the more general concept.

confOf:Organization denotes an entity (e.g., a company or university) that has an address and employs people. edas:Sponsorship denotes a financial arrangement (e.g., a travel grant) with a cost amount and currency, provided by an organization. They are disjoint kinds of things: an organization is an agent/entity, while a sponsorship is an event/arrangement. There is no subsumption relation between them.

hasFax is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's fax number), while writtenBy is an object property from Document to Person (indicating authorship). They relate completely different entities in different directions with different ranges, so they are unrelated.

Conference's 'has authors' specifically links a Conference document to a Person (author). edas' 'relates To' is a broad relation from Document to multiple entity types including Person, Academic Event, Conference, and Conference Session. 'has authors' is a specific case of 'relates To' where the range is restricted to Person and the relation denotes authorship. Thus 'has authors' is subsumed by the more general 'relates To'.

In iasted, Person is a broad superclass with children Delegate and Sponsor, covering all people involved in the conference. In sigkdd, Sponzor is specifically a sponsor entity with subclasses like Gold/Bronze/Platinum Supporter, Exhibitor, etc. Thus iasted:Person subsumes sigkdd:Sponzor, since every sponsor is a person but not every person is a sponsor.

CMT's 'assigned To' means a Paper is assigned to a Reviewer for peer review. IASTED's 'is needed for' means an Item is needed for a Person (e.g., an item required by a person at a conference). These are different relations: one is about review assignment, the other about item-person necessity. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The cmt property rejectPaper has domain Administrator and range Paper, representing the action of an administrator rejecting a paper. The iasted property write has domain Person and range Item, representing a person writing an item. These are completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings; they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Paper Full Version is a concrete document type (a full-length paper submission) in the cmt ontology, while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject-area classification for papers in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Document vs. Topic) and share no domain overlap.

In cmt, Conference denotes the event/organisation itself (with properties like date, logo URL, accepts hardcopy submissions, has conference members). In the Conference ontology, Conference contributor is a subclass of Person denoting people who contribute to a conference (authors, speakers, participants). These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a person.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. confOf:parallel_with links two Administrative events that occur in parallel (domain and range both Administrative event), whereas ekaw:listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event it lists. They do not share the same domain, range, or intended meaning.

Both are object properties linking a reviewed paper/contribution to its Review, with identical range (Review) and semantically equivalent domains (Reviewed contribution vs Paper in the conference domain). The labels 'has a review' and 'has Review' are synonymous, and the relation direction is the same in both ontologies.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract component of a paper. In iasted, Transparency is a subclass of Document representing presentation slides/overheads used at a session. These are distinct artefacts: one is a textual summary of a paper, the other is a visual presentation aid. They share no common intended instances.

Agency Staff Member in ekaw denotes a person affiliated with an agency (e.g., a sponsoring or funding agency) involved in the conference organization, sitting under Person alongside authors, reviewers, and participants. Student lecturer in iasted is a specialized type of lecturer (a speaker/author who presents at the conference), sitting deep in a hierarchy under Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer. These are entirely different concepts: one is about agency affiliation, the other about a student who lectures. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domain/range types. `hasReviewer` (ekaw) relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (paper -> reviewer), while `write` (iasted) relates a Person to an Item (author -> written item). They are not equivalent, and since one is not a generalization of the other, they are unrelated.

The property `parallel with` in confOf relates two Administrative events (indicating they occur in parallel), while `has Call` in edas relates an Academic Event to a Call (a call for papers/submissions). They have different domains and ranges and denote entirely different relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception), whereas iasted:Speaker is a person (a delegate who gives a talk). They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain—an event versus a person—so they are unrelated.

Contribution in confOf denotes a submitted scholarly work (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like abstract, keyword, title, and author relations. Sponsorship in edas denotes financial support (e.g., Travel Grant) provided by an Organization with cost amount/currency properties. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. In cmt, 'assignedTo' connects a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper). In the Conference ontology, 'has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution' connects a Review preference to either a Submitted contribution or a Topic (expressing what a preference is about). The domains (Paper vs Review preference), ranges (Reviewer vs Submitted contribution/Topic), and intended semantics (reviewer assignment vs preference target) are completely different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Invited speaker is a person role (subclass of Conference contributor, under Person) denoting someone invited to speak at a conference. Presenter state is a subclass of State, a temporal phase or status, not a person. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Person vs. State) and denote different categories of entities.

Both classes are documents in the conference domain, and they overlap (e.g., Review appears under both). However, Conference document is a broad category covering calls for papers, announcements, contributions, web pages, and reviews, whereas Form is specifically a document to be filled out (registration forms, author information forms, etc.). Neither subsumes the other: Conference document includes items that are not forms (e.g., Conference www, Call for paper), and Form includes items (e.g., Registration form, Hotel registration form) that are not Conference documents in the Conference ontology's sense. They are related but not equivalent.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'was a member of' links a Committee member to a Committee. In ontology B, 'hasMember' links a Conference to a Person. The domains (Committee member vs Conference) and ranges (Committee vs Person) differ, so they do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Pending Paper is a paper awaiting review/decision in the conference submission workflow, while Mailing list is a type of document used for communication. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

A 'Conference announcement' in the Conference ontology is a document (a publication/notice such as a call for papers or information for participants), while a 'Free Time Break' in the EDAS ontology is a non-academic event (a scheduled break like a coffee or meal break). They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies and denote entirely different things.

The cmt property assigns an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (reviewer-management relation), while the sigkdd property links a Speaker to a Document they present (presentation relation). Different domains, ranges, and semantic roles; no overlap.

confOf:Country denotes a geographic country (domain of has Country for Organization and Person), while sigkdd:Conference denotes a conference event with properties like start/end dates, city, and name. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. 'invited by' connects a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the person who invited them), while 'has Review' connects a Paper to a Review. They have different domains and ranges and describe different relationships in the conference domain.

An Organizational Meeting is a specific administrative/business meeting (a kind of academic event in EDAS), whereas a Scientific Event in EKAW is a broad superclass covering conferences, sessions, tracks, workshops, and presentations. These are different concepts: one is a narrow meeting type, the other a general category of scholarly events. They do not coincide in intended instances, and neither clearly subsumes the other.

Meal Event in edas is specifically about meals (has Menu property, range Meal Menu), with child Conference Dinner. Social program in iasted is a broader category of non-academic conference activities including Dinner banquet, Coctail reception, Coffee break, etc. Meal Event is a narrower concept focused on meal-related events, while Social program encompasses various social activities. The sibling structure of Social program (including non-meal events like Registration, Introduction, Welcome address) confirms it is more general than Meal Event.

Both classes denote the same core concept of a conference paper. They share the same path (Document > Paper), have Review as a sibling, and are the subject of review-related properties. The differences in children (Paper Abstract/Full Version vs. Conference Paper/Regular Paper) reflect different subcategorizations of the same concept, not different concepts.

These properties denote completely different relations. In cmt, 'startReviewerBidding' is an administrative action where an Administrator initiates the reviewer bidding process for a Conference. In edas, 'isReviewing' relates a reviewer role (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Paper they are reviewing. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different: one is about initiating a bidding phase, the other about the actual reviewing relationship.

Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (parent: Person; siblings include Committee member, Reviewer, etc.), while Session is a scheduled event/activity (parent: Lecture under Activity). One denotes a human role, the other a temporal activity; they share no instances.

partOf is a meronymic relation (part-whole), while sign relates a Person to an Item they sign (e.g., a document). These are fundamentally different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Review Question in edas is a question item in a review form (with numerical and textual subtypes), not a review document. Review in sigkdd is a Document subclass representing the review artifact itself. These are different concepts: one is a question posed during reviewing, the other is the review output document.

confOf:Company is a type of organization (e.g., a corporate entity involved in conference organization), whereas edas:WirelessCommunicationsTopic is a subject-area topic within a conference taxonomy. They belong to entirely different parts of the domain and share no instances.

The two properties operate in completely different domains: 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'has Menu' links a Meal Event to a Meal Menu. They share no common domain or range types and denote unrelated relationships in the conference organization domain.

Entity A (Committee member) is a person who serves on a committee, while entity B (Committee) is the committee itself. These are disjoint kinds of entities: one is a person/role, the other is an organizational body. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for people in the conference domain. They share the email property (Person -> string) and have comparable subclasses covering conference roles (authors, committee members, chairs, etc.). The additional properties in confOf (address, phone, fax, homepage) are natural contact details for a person, and 'employedBy' is a reasonable extension. The intended instances—people involved in conference organization—coincide.

Performance Topic in edas is a subject-area Topic (a research theme like antennas, CAD, cryptography), whereas Simulating in iasted is a Research Activity (an action performed before a conference). One is a topic/subject, the other is an activity; they denote completely different kinds of things.

Social program is a conference activity (e.g., dinner banquet, cocktail reception) in the iasted ontology, while Program Committee is a committee (a group of people) in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different concepts: one is an event/activity, the other is an organizational body. No alignment relationship exists between them.

The property `reviews` in Conference relates a Review to the Reviewed contribution it evaluates, while `write` in iasted relates a Person to an Item they author. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

Both classes denote the deadline for submitting papers to a conference. They share the same parent (Deadline) and their labels are synonymous: 'Submissions deadline' and 'Deadline Paper Submission'. The sibling deadlines in each ontology cover the same typical conference timeline events (notification of acceptance, camera-ready, etc.), confirming that the intended instances coincide.

cmt:User is a generic system-user superclass covering Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—anyone who can log into the CMT system—whereas edas:Attendee denotes a person who physically attends the conference. The intended instances differ: a CMT Administrator is a User but not necessarily an Attendee, and an Attendee who never logs into CMT is not a User. They share the parent Person but represent distinct concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, User is a broad superclass subsuming Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—i.e. any person who logs into the conference management system. In sigkdd, Listener is a specific kind of conference participant who attends presentations. The extension of User (all system users) does not coincide with the extension of Listener (audience members), nor is one clearly more general than the other in a way the reference alignment would record.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to its title (a string), while the edas 'hasPostalCode' property relates Contact Information to a postal code (a string). These are entirely different attributes of different domain entities with no semantic overlap.

Company is an organization (e.g., a sponsoring or exhibiting company), while Taxi is a transport vehicle used to move people. They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies and share no domain overlap.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a person who registered late and paid, while a 'Cheque' is a payment document/instrument. They are completely different categories of entities (person vs. document) with no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, Paper is a conference contribution (a full written work), whereas in ontology B, Abstract is a sibling of Paper and Review under Document, denoting the summary text of a paper. These are different concepts: one is the full paper itself, the other is its abstract. They do not coincide in intended instances, and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has applied to attend a conference (and may or may not have paid yet, as indicated by the 'Paid applicant' subclass). A 'Conference Participant' in EKAW is a broader category covering anyone who participates in the conference, including organizers, chairs, presenters, and attendees. The EKAW hierarchy shows Conference Participant has many specialized subclasses (Demo Chair, PC Chair, Presenter, etc.) that are not merely applicants but actual participants with roles. A registered applicant is a subset of conference participants (specifically those who registered/applied to attend), so A is subsumed by B.

In Conference, Tutorial is a conference part (an event/session where tutorials are given), sibling of Track and Workshop. In edas, Programme is a Document (the printed programme booklet), sibling of Meal Menu, Paper, Review, Slide Set. One denotes an event/activity, the other a physical document artefact; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract of a conference paper. Flyer in ekaw is a promotional document (sibling of Abstract, Paper, Review, etc.) with a publisherOf property linking organisations to it. These denote completely different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote a review document in the conference domain. In Conference, Review is a subclass of Conference document and is linked to Reviewed contribution via the reviews/has_a_review properties. In sigkdd, Review is a subclass of Document alongside Abstract and Paper. Despite the different document hierarchies, the intended instances coincide: documents that review a conference submission.

These properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. confOf:earlyRegistration is a datatype property from Participant to boolean, indicating whether a participant registered early. iasted:is_held_before is an object property from Activity to Time, indicating temporal ordering of an activity. They share no semantic overlap.

Both are meronymic (whole-to-part) properties, so they overlap in meaning. However, A is specifically between Conference volume and Conference part, while B is an inverse-of-partOf with range Event (domain unspecified). The restricted domain/range of A to conference-volume/part versus B's apparent generality over events means they do not coincide exactly; a reference alignment would likely treat them as related rather than equivalent.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person representing a person who is a student (e.g., a student volunteer or participant). In sigkdd, Author is a subclass of Speaker > Person, specifically representing an author of a paper who submits papers and can receive awards/notifications. These are distinct concepts: being a student and being an author are orthogonal dimensions. An author need not be a student, and a student need not be an author. The sigkdd Author class is specifically about paper authorship (with properties like submit, obtain Award, notification), while ekaw Student is about academic status. There is no subsumption relationship in either direction.

Property A ('is a date of camera ready paper submission') is a specific deadline property whose domain is the class 'Important dates' and whose range is 'date'. It denotes the particular deadline for camera-ready paper submission. Property B ('done till') is a more general deadline property whose domain is 'Deadline' and range is 'date', applicable to any task or activity that must be completed by a certain date. Thus A is a specialization of B: every camera-ready submission deadline is a 'done till' deadline, but not vice versa. The relation is subsumed_by.

In ekaw, 'Paper Author' is a direct subclass of Person, denoting any author of a paper. In iasted, 'Lecturer' is a highly specific role nested deep under Person via Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer, with specialized subclasses like Student lecturer and Worker lecturer. A Lecturer is a person who gives a lecture at the conference, which is a much narrower and different concept from a generic paper author. The two classes do not share the same intended instances: a paper author may never lecture, and a lecturer (e.g., a plenary or tutorial speaker) may not have authored a paper. They are not equivalent, and neither cleanly subsumes the other across these two ontologies' modeling choices.

An Organizational Meeting is a type of academic event (a meeting that takes place), whereas a Best Paper Awards Committee is a group of people serving on a committee. They are disjoint kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The property rejectPaper in cmt relates an Administrator to a Paper that is being rejected, while hasReviewer in ekaw relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer assigned to review it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Company is a general commercial organization (sibling of University under Organization), while ekaw:Proceedings_Publisher is a specific role—an organization that publishes conference proceedings. A company could be a proceedings publisher, but the two classes do not denote the same set of instances, nor is one clearly more general than the other in the conference ontology context.

Mobile Computing Topic is a subject-area classification (a Topic) in the EDAS ontology, while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award given at a conference. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote a Workshop in the conference domain. They share the same label and occupy analogous positions in their respective hierarchies (as a subtype of a working/scientific event, sibling to Conference). The structural context aligns well, indicating the same intended concept.

confOf:Working_event is a kind of conference event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) that has administrative events, topics, and titles. edas:MultimediaTopic is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area like antennas, CAD, or mobile computing. One denotes an event/activity, the other a subject domain; they share no instances and are unrelated.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), denoting a meeting where papers are presented. iasted:Conference_airport is a physical place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference restaurant), denoting an airport associated with a conference. Despite both containing the word 'Conference' in their context, one is an event and the other is a physical location; their intended instances do not coincide at all.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while the confOf 'has Fax' property denotes a fax number for a Person. These are completely different attributes with no semantic overlap, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

The cmt property 'has Decision' links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject), while the iasted property 'is designed for' links an Activity, Money, or Time to an Activity or Person. These are completely different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in domain or range.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes or submits a paper (subclass of Person/Conference Member). In Conference, Abstract is a document type (subclass of Extended abstract/Conference document) representing a summary part of a paper. One is a person role, the other is a textual artefact; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate completely different entities. In edas, 'has Call' links an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., a call for papers). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. The domains (Academic Event vs Document), ranges (Call vs Speaker), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

Both classes represent written scholarly papers submitted to a conference. cmt's Paper is a Document with authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions, covering the full lifecycle of a conference paper. Conference's Written contribution sits under Conference document > Conference contribution and has children like Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, also representing written papers submitted for review. Their intended instances (conference papers) coincide despite different labels.

These properties relate different entities in opposite directions. 'has_a_review' links a Reviewed Contribution to its Review (contribution -> review), while 'reviewWrittenBy' links a Review to its author (review -> reviewer). They share no common domain or range types and are not inverses of each other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'event On List' connects an Event to publication artefacts (Programme Brochure, Web Site), indicating where an event is listed. In iasted, 'is given by' connects an Activity or Item to a Person, indicating who presents or provides it. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or even meaningfully related.

These properties are fundamentally different. 'organised By' is an object property linking an Event to its organising Organisation or Person, while 'City of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string naming the city. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have incompatible property types (object vs datatype).

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), denoting an academic/work event in a conference. iasted's 'Delegate' is a person role (subclass of Person, with children Speaker, Listener, etc.). One is an event, the other a person; no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:Paper is a general class for all papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version), while ekaw:Industrial Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw:Paper denoting papers written by industrial practitioners. Thus cmt:Paper is strictly more general than ekaw:Industrial Paper.

Organization is a class denoting an organizational entity (e.g., a conference, university, or company) in the Conference ontology, while Time zone is a class denoting a geographical time region in the iasted ontology. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In EKAW, locationOf maps a Location to the Event held at that location (a spatial relation). In IASTED, is_held_before maps an Activity to a Time, expressing a temporal precedence relation. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics, so they are unrelated.

Although both are subclasses of Document, they denote entirely different artefacts. In ekaw, Flyer is a promotional document (sibling to Programme Brochure, Web Site) and is the range of publisherOf. In sigkdd, Paper is a scholarly submission (sibling to Abstract, Review) and the range of submit. A flyer is not a paper, and the two classes share no instance overlap.

registrationDueOn denotes the deadline for conference registration (a date before or at the start of the conference), while End_of_conference denotes the date the conference ends. They are temporally distinct concepts with different semantics; one is a deadline, the other is a closing date. Neither subsumes the other.

Entity A is a class denoting the first author of a conference contribution (a person/role), while entity B is a class denoting a specific monetary registration fee for an author attendee who also books something. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (document/author vs. money/fee) and denote completely unrelated concepts.

Positive Review is a document/artefact (a review with positive content), whereas Reviewer is a person (a delegate/speaker who writes reviews). They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'location Of' in ekaw relates a Location to an Event (a location hosts an event). 'is occupied by' in iasted relates a Building, City, or State to a Person (a place is occupied by a person). They connect different kinds of entities in different ways and are not equivalent.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Workshop' is a subclass of Academic Event, i.e., it denotes a type of conference event (an academic gathering). In the EKAW ontology, 'Workshop Paper' is a subclass of Paper, i.e., it denotes a document (a paper presented at a workshop). These are completely different categories of entities in the conference domain: one is an event, the other is a document. They share the word 'Workshop' but denote unrelated concepts.

hasLastName relates a Person to their family name (string), while Nation relates a Person to their country/nationality (string). Despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string), they denote completely different attributes of a person and are unrelated.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event under Event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas edas:MultimediaTopic is a subject classification (a Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

cmt:User is a subclass of Person, representing people who interact with the conference management system (Administrator, Author, Reviewer). iasted:Lecture is a subclass of Conference activity, representing a type of event/presentation at a conference. One denotes a person role, the other an activity; they share no instances and are completely different concepts.

The property 'has Review' in EKAW relates a Paper to its Review, whereas 'presentationed by' in SIGKDD relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it. These are entirely different relations connecting different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Lecture in iasted is a conference activity/event (a talk or session), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives a presentation. They denote completely different categories of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

Social Event in edas denotes social gatherings during the conference (e.g., Excursion, Reception, Meal Event, Break Event) that are part of the conference program. Activity after conference in iasted denotes activities occurring after the conference ends (e.g., Departure, Full day tour). These are temporally and conceptually distinct: social events happen during the conference, while post-conference activities happen after it concludes. Their instance sets do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference Hiker in iasted is a sub-type of Delegate (a conference attendee/participant), while Organizator in sigkdd is a sub-type of Person who organizes the conference (with children like General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). One is an attendee, the other is an organizer; they are distinct roles in the conference domain.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization, denoting a corporate entity (e.g., a sponsoring or employing company). iasted:Van is a subclass of Transport vehicle under Item, denoting a physical vehicle used for transportation. These classes have disjoint intended instances and no subsumption relationship.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Management Topic' is a specific subject-area topic (a subclass of Topic) used to classify papers. In EKAW, 'Contributed Talk' is a type of scientific event/presentation (a subclass of Individual Presentation). They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate different kinds of subjects to Person. In edas, hasMember connects a Conference to its members (people participating in the conference). In iasted, is_occupied_by connects a Building, City, or State to a Person, indicating occupancy of a place. The domains are disjoint concepts (Conference vs. spatial entities), so the properties do not denote the same relation.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member, indicating the action of setting the maximum number of papers. In Conference, has_a_program_committee relates a Conference volume to a Program committee, indicating that a conference has a certain committee. They connect different types of entities and express different relations.
