cmt:Conference denotes the overall conference event/organization (with administrators, members, paper assignments, submission settings), while ekaw:Conference_Banquet is a specific social gathering during a conference (a subclass of Social Event). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Person in the conference domain, but Chairman in cmt is a leadership role (parent of Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair) while Committee member in Conference is a general committee participant (parent of Chair, Co chair). A chairman is typically a committee member but not vice versa, so they overlap without being equivalent.

These properties operate in completely different domains. 'details Entered By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who entered conference details), while 'is Menu Of' relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event. They share no conceptual overlap in the conference organization domain.

confOf:Reception is a social event (a gathering/entertainment activity like a banquet or trip) that typically occurs during or around a conference. iasted:Activity_before_conference is a pre-conference organizational activity (accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts, renting, research). They are temporally and semantically disjoint: a reception is a social gathering, not a manuscript-handling or logistical task, and it is not specifically a pre-conference activity.

In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member, i.e. someone who is a member of the conference committee/organisation. In edas, hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person who attends the event. A conference member (organisational role) and an attendee (participant) are different concepts, and the domains (Conference vs Conference Event) also differ, so the properties do not relate the same kinds of things.

Conference in cmt denotes the conference event/organization itself, with properties like accepting submissions, having members, and a logo URL. Deadline in sigkdd denotes a temporal deadline (e.g., abstract submission, paper submission, author notification). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Speaker is a broad class covering all delegates who speak (including authors, reviewers, session chairs, etc.), whereas in sigkdd Invited_Speaker is a specific subtype of Speaker for those delivering invited talks. The iasted Speaker is more general, so it subsumes the sigkdd Invited_Speaker; they are not equivalent.

confOf:Conference is the main conference event itself (a working event with siblings like Tutorial and Workshop), while edas:FreeTimeBreak is a specific non-academic break event (a free time break, sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

hasDecision links a Paper to its acceptance/rejection Decision, while hasTopic links a Paper (or Conference) to a Topic it covers. They relate completely different kinds of objects and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

confOf:Workshop is a kind of event (a working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), whereas ekaw:Programme_Brochure is a kind of document (sibling of Paper, Review, Flyer, etc.). One denotes an academic gathering, the other a printed/publication artefact describing a programme. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In ontology A, 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all participants (with children Active and Passive conference participant). In ontology B, 'Non speaker' is a specific subclass of Delegate, covering only non-speaking attendees (with children Student non speaker and Worker non speaker). 'Non speaker' is thus a narrower concept, corresponding roughly to A's 'Passive conference participant', and is subsumed by A's 'Conference participant'.

Rejection in cmt is a Decision outcome for a paper submission, while Invited Talk in ekaw is a type of scientific event/presentation. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, 'Conference part' is a constituent component of a conference (e.g., Track, Tutorial, Workshop), whereas in ontology B, 'Conference' is the top-level event itself (subclass of Working event). These denote entirely different concepts: a part of a conference versus the whole conference event.

Conference hotel (iasted) denotes a hotel building where conference participants stay, a lodging facility. Conference hall (sigkdd) denotes a room or venue space where conference sessions take place. These are different concepts: one is accommodation, the other is an event space. They share the word 'conference' but refer to distinct entities in the conference-organization domain.

hasCity relates Contact Information to a city name (string), while Name relates Person to a person's name (string). They have different domains (Contact Information vs Person) and denote different attributes (city vs person name), so they are not equivalent.

In cmt, User is a person who uses the conference management system (parent Person; children Administrator, Author, Reviewer). In sigkdd, Registration Non Member is a fee category for non-member registration (parent Registration fee; siblings are other registration fee types). One denotes a person/role, the other a monetary fee. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) denoting a kind of conference event, whereas edas:SecurityTopic is a subclass of Topic denoting a specific subject area. They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote entirely different concepts.

iasted's Conference_hotel is a specific hotel used for a conference (child of Building under Place), while sigkdd's Hotel is a general hotel (direct child of Place). Every conference hotel is a hotel, but not vice versa, so Conference_hotel is subsumed_by Hotel.

Registeered applicant in Conference is a subclass of Person/Conference applicant, denoting a person who has registered for a conference. Working event in confOf is a subclass of Event, denoting a type of conference event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop). These are completely different domain concepts: one is a person, the other is an event. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Both classes are named 'Document' and serve as top-level containers for conference-related written artifacts. IASTED's Document has children like Submission, Review, Form, etc., while SIGKDD's Document has children like Abstract, Paper, Review. Both represent the general concept of a document in the conference domain, with overlapping child types (Review appears in both). Despite IASTED having a broader set of administrative document subtypes, the intended extension of the class — any conference-related document — coincides sufficiently for equivalence.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. hasEndDateTime is a datatype property from Conference Event to dateTime, capturing when an event ends. listsEvent is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event, capturing which events are listed in a publication. They share no semantic relationship.

Student is a subclass of Person (a human participant in a conference), while Van is a subclass of Transport vehicle (a physical item used for transportation). These classes denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.
Rejected contribution is a written paper that was rejected after review, while Review is the review document itself. They are different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Company in confOf is a for-profit commercial organization (sibling of University), while Academia Organization in edas represents academic institutions. They are disjoint categories of Organization: a Company is an Industry Organization, not an Academia Organization. Their instances do not coincide.

Paper Full Version is a full research paper submitted for review in a conference management system, while Hotel registration form is an administrative form for booking hotel accommodation. They share no domain overlap despite both being subclasses of Document/Form.

In ontology A, 'Conference part' is a subdivision of a conference (e.g., Track, Tutorial, Workshop) - it is a component part of a conference event. In ontology B (edas), 'Conference' is the top-level event itself (with subclasses like Single Level Conference, Two Level Conference, and properties like has Country, paper Due On, etc.). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a part/section of a conference, the other is the conference as a whole. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a person who registered late and paid for conference attendance, while a 'Pending Paper' is a document (paper) awaiting a decision. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Person vs Document) and denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Meta Reviewer is a specialized subclass of Reviewer with additional responsibilities (overseeing all reviews, submitting a meta-review). In edas, Reviewer is a general reviewer class. Thus cmt's Meta Reviewer is subsumed by edas's Reviewer, not equivalent.

addProgramCommitteeMember is an action performed by an Administrator on a Program Committee Member (adding someone to a committee), while organisedBy relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. In ekaw, 'organises' connects an Organisation or Person to an Event (e.g., a committee organises a conference). In sigkdd, 'presentation' connects a Speaker to a Document (the slides/paper being presented). They differ in domain (Organisation/Person vs. Speaker), range (Event vs. Document), and meaning (organising an event vs. presenting a document). No subsumption holds either, as the domains and ranges are disjoint categories.

Technic activity is a subclass of Conference activity (alongside Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Presentation, etc.), making it an event/activity in the conference program. Organizator is a subclass of Person whose instances are roles like General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc. One is an activity, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a type of Chairman), while Welcome Talk is a type of academic event/talk. They belong to completely different categories (person vs. event) and share no semantic overlap.

`has Decision` links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while `is sent after` links an Item to a Time (temporal relation). Different domains, ranges, and semantics; no alignment relationship.

In the iasted ontology, 'Time zone' denotes a geographical region with a uniform standard time (e.g., UTC+1). In the sigkdd ontology, 'Deadline' denotes a temporal point or date by which a submission or notification must occur (with children like Abstract Submission, Author notification, Paper Submission). These are fundamentally different concepts: a time zone is a spatial/geographical division of time-keeping, while a deadline is a specific temporal event in a conference schedule. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

These properties are completely different. `hasBid` is an object property relating a Paper to a Bid (a bidding action by a reviewer for reviewing a paper). `has_amount_of` is a datatype property relating Money to an integer (the monetary amount). They differ in type (object vs datatype), domain (Paper vs Money), range (Bid vs int), and domain semantics (conference paper bidding vs monetary quantity).

Both classes are named 'Organization' and represent the same high-level concept in the conference-organisation domain. In the Conference ontology, Organization is a top-level class (sibling of Person, Document, etc.) that can sponsor conferences. In edas, Organization has subclasses like Academia Organization, Government Organization, Industry Organization, and NGO, and is linked to Sponsorship via 'is Provider Of' / 'provided By'. The intended instances (organizations involved in conference organisation, especially sponsors) coincide, so a reference alignment would mark them equivalent.

Trip day is a temporal unit during a conference trip (sibling of Conference days), whereas Deadline Paper Submission is a specific submission deadline. They share the parent Time/Deadline but denote entirely different concepts.

Sponsorship in edas is a financial arrangement (with cost amount, currency, provider organization) that may include Travel Grants. Sponsor_city in iasted is a subclass of City, representing a geographical location associated with a sponsor. These are completely different concepts: one is an abstract financial/organizational entity, the other is a geographic place.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion organized as part of a conference), whereas iasted:Shuttle_bus is a transport vehicle (a concrete means of transport). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs. Item/Transport vehicle) and denote different categories of things.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a broad superclass encompassing all conference participants (Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.), while in edas, Reviewer is a specific role under Person. cmt's ConferenceMember includes Reviewer as a child, so it is strictly more general than edas's Reviewer.

Chairman is a person who leads a committee or conference (subclasses include Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Hotel fee is a monetary charge for accommodation. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

submitPaper is an object property relating an Author to the Paper they submit, whereas is_a_full_paper_submission_date is a datatype property relating Important dates to a date value. They differ in type, domain, range, and meaning.

The two classes denote entirely different concepts. 'Passive conference participant' in the Conference ontology is a subclass of Person representing attendees who do not actively participate (e.g., audience members). 'Single Level Conference' in the edas ontology is a subclass of Conference representing a conference without sub-conferences. One is about people, the other about events, so they are unrelated.

Invited_speaker is a person (a conference contributor who gives an invited talk), while Presenter_city is a city (a geographic location associated with a presenter). They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies (Person vs City) and denote completely different kinds of entities.

Both properties relate conference-domain entities to Topic, but their domains differ: A's domain is 'Conference part' (broader, covering tracks, workshops, tutorials), while B's domain is specifically 'Conference Paper'. A's property is more general (applies to any conference part), so A is subsumed by B in the sense that B is a more specific version. They are not equivalent because their intended domains do not coincide.

Conference announcement is a document issued before or during a conference (child of Conference document), whereas Departure is a post-conference activity (child of Activity after conference). They denote completely different kinds of things with no overlap in instances.

In ekaw, Abstract is a subclass of Document representing the textual content of a paper or talk (e.g., Invited Talk Abstract, Tutorial Abstract). In sigkdd, Deadline Abstract Submission is a subclass of Deadline representing a temporal deadline for submitting abstracts. These are completely different concepts: one is a document artifact, the other is a temporal milestone. They share the word 'abstract' but denote unrelated entities.

In ekaw, Conference Participant is a broad superclass covering any person who participates in a conference (chairs, presenters, attendees, committee members). In sigkdd, Author is a narrow subclass of Speaker restricted to people who submit papers and receive notifications/awards. The two classes do not share instances: an Author in sigkdd is a paper author, while a Conference Participant in ekaw may be any participant (e.g., a Session Chair or Demo Chair) who is not necessarily an author. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relation, so unrelated is the best fit.

confOf:Reception is a social event (alongside Banquet and Trip), i.e., a hospitality/gathering occasion. iasted:Introduction is a conference activity that has a child 'Introduction of speaker' and siblings like 'Welcome address' and 'Coctail reception', indicating it refers to the act of introducing speakers, not a reception event. The sibling 'Coctail reception' in iasted corresponds more closely to confOf:Reception, confirming these are distinct concepts.
hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to its Subject Area (topic classification), while obtain relates a Person to an Item they receive. Different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. cmt's hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. edas's isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author. They connect different entities (reviewer vs. author) and express different relationships (review assignment vs. authorship).

Co-author in cmt is a person who co-writes a paper, sitting under Person > Conference Member > Author. Nonmember registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee for non-member registration, sitting under Money > Fee > Registration fee. These denote completely unrelated concepts (a person vs. a monetary amount).

In EDAS, Reception is a specific kind of social event (a subclass of Social Event, sibling to Excursion). In EKAW, Social Event is the general class whose children include Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. Thus EDAS Reception is strictly more specific than EKAW Social Event, so the relation is subsumed_by.

Associated Chair is a person role in a conference committee (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Main office is a physical place (subclass of Place). They denote completely different categories of entities.

Signal Processing Topic is a subject-area classification under Topic in the EDAS ontology, representing a research topic for paper categorization. Simulating is a type of Research activity (an activity before a conference) in the IASTED ontology. These denote completely different concepts: one is a topic/subject category, the other is a research activity. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf's 'Social event' is a specific kind of event (e.g., Banquet, Reception, Trip) that is a child of confOf's Event. ekaw's 'Event' is the top-level event class with children including both Scientific Event and Social Event. Thus confOf's Social event is strictly more specific than ekaw's Event, making this a subsumed_by relationship.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing the call for papers, while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for paper submission. They are different kinds of entities: one is a document/artefact, the other is a date/time event. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a reception gathering), while iasted:Cheque is a payment document. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person, representing a specific kind of person who interacts with the system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer). In the Conference ontology, Person is the top-level class for all people in the domain (parent of Committee member, Conference applicant, etc.). Thus cmt:User is a narrower concept than Conference:Person: every User is a Person, but not every Person (e.g., a mere applicant or committee member) is necessarily a cmt:User. The relation is subsumed_by.

The property 'has Topic' in edas relates Papers/Conferences to Topics, denoting the subject matter of a paper. The property 'paper In Volume' in ekaw relates papers to volumes/proceedings, denoting the publication container of a paper. These are fundamentally different relations: one concerns subject classification, the other concerns publication venue. No subsumption or overlap exists between them.

confOf:Conference is a conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while edas:Mobile Computing Topic is a subject topic (subclass of Topic, sibling of various technical topics). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

In EDAS, 'Paper' is a broad class (parent of Accepted, Rejected, Published, etc.) denoting any paper in the conference system. In EKAW, 'Demo Paper' is a specific subtype of Paper (a sibling of Regular Paper, Poster Paper, Industrial Paper, etc.). EDAS Paper is strictly more general than EKAW Demo Paper, so the relation is subsumes.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion, banquet, reception) that occurs during a conference. iasted:IASTED_member is a person who is a member of the IASTED organization and a delegate attending the conference. These are completely different categories: one is an event/activity, the other is a person/role. There is no overlap in their intended instances.

Session chair (iasted) is a Delegate who chairs a specific session, a role tied to attending and presiding over a talk session. General Chair (sigkdd) is an Organizator, a top-level conference organizer responsible for the overall conference. These are distinct roles: one is a session-level presiding attendee, the other is a conference-level organizer. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Both denote short summary-like contributions in a conference, but they are not equivalent. In Conference, Extended_abstract is a subtype of Regular_contribution (a concrete submission type) and has a child Abstract, whereas in sigkdd Abstract is a direct child of Document alongside Paper and Review. The sigkdd Abstract is more broadly positioned as a document type, while Extended_abstract is a specific kind of regular contribution. They overlap in intended instances but differ in scope and ontological role, so related is the best fit.

Both properties denote the act of a committee member reviewing a paper. confOf:reviewes has domain Member PC and range Contribution, while edas:isReviewing has domain (including TPC Member) and range Paper. Member PC corresponds to TPC Member, and Contribution corresponds to Paper in this domain. The direction is identical (reviewer -> paper), so the properties are equivalent.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (Administrator, Author, Reviewer). In sigkdd, Registration_SIGKDD_Member is a subclass of Registration fee, representing a monetary fee for SIGKDD member registration. One is a person/role concept, the other is a fee/financial concept. They share no common instances and are unrelated.

In Conference, Chair is a generic committee chair (with a sibling Co-chair) covering any committee, whereas in ekaw OC_Chair is specifically the chair of the Organizing Committee (a child of OC_Member). Thus OC_Chair is a specific kind of Chair, making Chair more general (A subsumed_by B is incorrect; rather B subsumes A in specificity, so A is subsumed_by B).

readByReviewer relates a Paper to the Reviewer who reads/reviews it, while writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author. These are distinct relations involving different roles (reviewer vs author) and different activities (reading/reviewing vs authoring).

SC Member in ekaw is a member of the Steering Committee (a committee role under PC Member), while Author in iasted is a Delegate who writes papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one is a governance/committee role, the other is a contribution author. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

Chairman in cmt is a generic superclass of various chair roles (Associated Chair, Conference Chair, PC Chair), not a regular PC member. Member_PC in confOf is a reviewer (per comment) who reviews contributions and has expertise on topics. A Chairman is a leadership/oversight role, while Member_PC is a regular PC member/reviewer; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

hasBiography is a datatype property from Person to string (a textual biography), while authorOf is an object property from Person to Document (relating a person to the documents they authored). They relate different kinds of things (string vs. Document) and represent entirely different relations.

In ekaw, Negative_Review is a subclass of Review, a specific type of review with a negative evaluation. In sigkdd, Abstract is a subclass of Document, representing a summary of a paper. These are distinct concepts: one is a review outcome, the other is a document component. They share only the common ancestor Document, and there is no subsumption relationship between them.

Entity A is a class representing the first author of a conference contribution (a person/role), while entity B is a class representing a conference event (an academic gathering). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (has_members) relates a Committee to its Committee member (people who serve on the committee). Property B (hasPart) is a generic mereological relation indicating that something is part of something else (e.g., an event has parts, an organization has parts). These are fundamentally different relations: committee membership is not a parthood relation. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same way.

Both classes denote conference participants who give talks, but they are not equivalent. In ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a direct subclass of 'Conference contributor' (a Person), representing any person invited to speak at a conference. In ontology B, 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a highly specific subclass of 'Author' (which is itself a subclass of 'Speaker' and 'Delegate'), denoting specifically a speaker who delivers a plenary lecture and is also modeled as an author. The iasted hierarchy imposes additional constraints (being an Author, a Delegate, and specifically a plenary-level speaker), whereas the Conference ontology's 'Invited speaker' is broader, covering any invited talk type. They overlap (a plenary lecture speaker is often an invited speaker) but neither subsumes the other cleanly due to differing structural assumptions, so 'related' is the most accurate relation.

The iasted `write` property relates a Person to an Item they author (e.g., a paper or document). The sigkdd `presentationed_by` property relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. Authoring a written item is a different relation from presenting a document; the domains and ranges differ (Person/Item vs Document/Speaker), and the two relations denote distinct roles in the conference domain.

Track is a session/topic division of a conference (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while Sponzor fee is a monetary charge for sponsors (sibling of Registration fee). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Organization denotes an organizational entity (e.g., Company, University) with address-related properties, while iasted:Item denotes a physical or informational object (e.g., Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). Their intended instances do not overlap at all; they are completely different domain concepts.

confOf:Scholar is a subclass of Person representing a conference attendee in a 'scholar' price category, with a 'studyAt' property linking to University. edas:MealMenu is a subclass of Document representing a menu for a meal event, with properties linking it to MealEvent. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Reception in confOf is a social event (e.g., a conference reception/banquet), while Travel Grant in edas is a type of sponsorship award. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad superclass encompassing all conference participants (chairs, authors, PC members, reviewers), whereas in the Conference ontology Reviewer is a specific role under Person concerned with reviewing papers and inviting co-reviewers. Conference Member is far more general than Reviewer, but since cmt already has a dedicated Reviewer subclass, the two concepts do not align as equivalent, subsumption, or overlap in a reference alignment.

A's Paper is a general conference contribution (sibling of Extended abstract, parent Regular contribution), while B's Demo Paper is a specific subtype of Paper in ekaw. A's Paper is more general than B's Demo Paper, so A is subsumed by B's broader Paper hierarchy, but not equivalent to the specific Demo Paper.

Reception is a social event during a conference (e.g., welcome reception), while Departure is an activity after the conference ends. They denote different kinds of things occurring at different times and serve different purposes; neither subsumes the other.

In Conference, 'Committee member' is a subclass of Person denoting people who serve on a committee. In edas, 'Person' is the broad top-level class for all people involved in a conference, with children such as Attendee, Author, Reviewer, and TPC Member. Thus every Committee member is a Person, but not every Person is a Committee member, so Committee member is subsumed by Person.

confOf:Poster is a type of academic contribution (a poster presentation), a sibling of Paper and Short paper under Contribution. sigkdd:Best_Student_Paper_Supporter is a type of sponsor (a person or organization that financially supports the best student paper award), a sibling of Bronze/Gold/Platinum/Silver Supporter and Exhibitor under Sponzor. These are completely different concepts: one is a presentation artifact/type, the other is a sponsor role. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

In ontology A, Review is the general class of all reviews (a sibling of Conference contribution, Call for paper, etc., under Conference document). In ontology B, Positive_Review is a specific subclass of Review (a sibling of Negative Review and Neutral Review). Thus A's Review is strictly more general than B's Positive_Review, so A is subsumed_by B's broader hierarchy position; more precisely, B's Positive_Review would be subsumed by A's Review. Since the pair is A=Review and B=Positive_Review, the relation is subsumed_by (A is narrower than B's parent, but B itself is narrower than A).

has_an_email is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's email address), while writtenBy is an object property from Document to Person (indicating authorship). They have different domains, different ranges, and completely different semantics.

Property A (has_the_last_name) has domain Person and range string, representing a person's surname. Property B (remark) has domain Contribution and range string, representing a remark about a contribution. They relate to completely different domains (people vs. contributions) and carry entirely different semantics, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a broad class subsuming Author, Conference Chair, Program Committee Member, Reviewer, etc. In ekaw, SC_Member is a specific kind of committee member (under PC_Member), sibling to PC Chair, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair. SC_Member instances would be ConferenceMember instances, but not vice versa. Thus ConferenceMember subsumes SC_Member.

In edas, 'has Last Name' is a datatype property with domain Person and range string, specifically denoting the surname/family name of a person. In sigkdd, 'Name' is a datatype property with domain Person and range string, representing the full name of a person. A last name is a part of (subsumed by) the full name, so 'has Last Name' is subsumed_by 'Name'.

In confOf, Tutorial is a distinct type of working event (a tutorial event), while in iasted, Session is a container/slot activity that has Tutorial as a sibling and Speaker lecture as a child. They are at different levels of the event hierarchy and serve different purposes: Tutorial denotes a specific kind of event, whereas Session denotes a scheduled block containing lectures. They do not share the same intended instances.

Entity A is a Person (an invited speaker), while entity B is a Document (the abstract of an invited talk). They are completely different kinds of entities — one is a person, the other is a document — so they are unrelated.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., a published announcement), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline date for submitting papers. They denote completely different kinds of entities (document vs. date), so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'is part of conference volumes' links a Conference part to a Conference volume (part-whole relation between documents/publications), while 'parallel with' links two Administrative events (scheduling relation between events). They share no common domain or range and denote different relations in the conference domain.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a person who attends but does not actively participate (e.g., audience member), while a 'Conference Trip' is a social event. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Regular author is a person who writes a conference contribution (paper, poster, etc.), situated under Conference contribution/contributor hierarchies. Presenter is a conference participant who presents at the conference, situated under Person > Conference Participant. While some authors may also present, the concepts are distinct: an author writes a paper while a presenter delivers a talk/demo. Their ontological contexts (document vs. participant hierarchies) and intended instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Short_paper in confOf is a type of contribution distinguished by length/format, whereas PendingPaper in edas is a paper in a pending review/decision state. They classify papers along orthogonal dimensions (format vs. workflow status), so their intended instances do not coincide.

In confOf, Tutorial is a subclass of Working event, denoting an event/session type. In iasted, Tutorial speaker is a person role (subclass chain through Delegate > Speaker > Author), i.e. someone who gives a tutorial. One is an event, the other is a person; they are disjoint kinds of entities and not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

Both classes are called 'Abstract' and relate to conference documents, but they denote different concepts. In Conference ontology, Abstract is a specific part/component of a paper (an abstract section), as shown by 'is the 1th part of' and 'has an abstract' properties. In ekaw, Abstract is a document type with subclasses like Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract, sibling to Paper and Review. One is a document component, the other is a document category; they overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

The edas Attendee is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who attends a conference. The iasted Author attendee cd registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, denoting a monetary fee for an author attendee registering with a CD. These are completely different concepts: a person vs. a monetary amount.

In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person, covering any person who attends a conference. In iasted, Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate (which itself sits under Place > Building > Conference building), making it a narrower category of conference participant. The iasted hierarchy distinguishes Conference Hiker from siblings such as Listener, Speaker, Session chair, etc., so it denotes a specific kind of delegate rather than the general notion of attendee. Thus edas:Attendee is more general than iasted:Conference Hiker, giving a subsumed_by relation.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person — a human participant in a conference (authors, chairs, reviewers, committee members). In the Conference ontology, Conference volume is a subclass of Conference — an event/occurrence of a conference series that has committees, tracks, contributions, locations, and dates. One denotes a person, the other an event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

setMaxPapers in cmt is a property from Administrator to Program Committee Member, likely representing an administrative action of setting paper limits for PC members. has_members in Conference is a property from Committee to Committee member, representing the membership relation between a committee and its members. These are fundamentally different relations: one is an administrative assignment action, the other is a structural membership relation. Their domains and ranges differ (Administrator vs Committee, and the semantics are unrelated).

In ontology Conference, 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person — it denotes a person who applies to attend a conference. In ekaw, 'Conference' is a subclass of Scientific Event — it denotes the conference event itself (one edition of a conference). These are completely different categories of entities (a person vs. an event), so they are unrelated.

Publisher is an organization that publishes conference proceedings, while Research Topic is a subject area covered by papers and events. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are conference call-type documents, but they are not equivalent: 'Call for participation' invites people to attend a conference, while 'Call For Papers' invites paper submissions. They overlap as subtypes of a general 'Call' concept but denote different artefacts.

Entity A is a class denoting a document (an accepted paper), while entity B is a class denoting a temporal deadline (the date by which acceptance notifications are due). They belong to entirely different ontological categories—document vs. time point—and share no instances in common.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings: 'has_the_last_name' applies to Person and captures a person's surname, while 'hasKeyword' applies to Contribution and captures a keyword associated with a paper. They relate different kinds of entities and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

The property enableVirtualMeeting in cmt relates an Administrator to a Conference, denoting the act of enabling a virtual meeting for a conference. The property prepare in iasted relates a Person to an Item, denoting the act of preparing some item. These differ in domain (Administrator vs Person), range (Conference vs Item), and meaning (enabling virtual meeting vs preparing an item). They do not denote the same relation.

In the edas ontology, Author is a subclass of Person, representing a human who writes papers. In the iasted ontology, Form is a subclass of Document, representing a type of document or artefact (e.g., registration form, author information form). These are completely different categories of entities (person vs. document), so they are unrelated.

These properties have different domains and different meanings. 'has_a_date_of_issue' applies to Conference documents and records when a document was issued/published. 'done_till' applies to Deadlines and indicates the date by which something must be completed. One is about document publication dates, the other about deadline expiry dates; they relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion, banquet, reception) that occurs during a conference, whereas iasted:Sponsor_city is a geographic location (a city) that sponsors the conference. They belong to completely different ontological categories (event vs. place) and share no instances.

confOf:Company is a kind of Organization (e.g., a sponsoring or hosting company in the conference domain), while iasted:Credit_card is a financial instrument (a Card used for payment). They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Published Paper is a document (a paper that has been published), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting abstracts. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf Member is a general participant role (sibling of Regular and Student under Participant), while iasted Student_non_speaker is a specific subclass of Non_speaker under Delegate. They are at very different levels of generality and occupy different positions in their respective taxonomies. Member is a broad category of conference participant; Student_non_speaker is a narrowly defined delegate type. There is no evidence their intended instances coincide, and neither subsumes the other in a clearly intended way.

Entity A is a person role (an invited speaker, subclass of Conference contributor under Person), while entity B is a state/status concept (subclass of State, sibling to Presenter state and Sponsor state). They denote completely different kinds of things: a person vs. a conference state, so they are unrelated.

The two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. A's 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (committee -> conference), while B's 'organised By' links an Event to an Organisation or Person (event -> organiser). They describe the same real-world relationship but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent. An inverse relationship is not considered equivalent in reference alignments.

In confOf, Company is a specific kind of Organization (a sibling of University under Organization). In edas, Organization is the general top-level class with subtypes like Academia, Government, Industry, and NGO. Thus confOf:Company is a narrower concept than edas:Organization, making it subsumed_by.

The property 'has an email' is a datatype property from Person to string (an email address), while 'author Of' is an object property from Person to Document (relating a person to a paper they wrote). They relate completely different kinds of values and have no semantic overlap.

confOf:Social event is a subclass of Event with children like Banquet, Reception, and Trip, denoting social activities in a conference. iasted:Time is a temporal concept with children like Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day, serving as a range for temporal relations (e.g., 'is held before', 'is sent after'). These are fundamentally different categories: one is a social activity, the other is a temporal entity. They share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Paid applicant is a person who has paid registration fees, while Travel Grant is a sponsorship funding mechanism. They belong to completely different conceptual categories (person vs. financial award) with no overlap in intended instances.

These two datatype properties have different domains (Conference vs Conference_volume), different ranges (anyURI vs string), and different intended meanings: siteURL captures the web address of a conference, while has_a_location captures a physical/venue location string. They relate different kinds of things and are not the same relation.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes or submits a paper. In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author, specifically an author who also presents the paper. Thus Presenter is a narrower concept than cmt's Author: every Presenter is an Author, but not every Author is a Presenter.

In the Conference ontology, 'Active conference participant' is a sub-class of both 'Conference contributor' and 'Conference participant', and it is a sibling of 'Regular author' and 'Passive conference participant'. Its defining property is 'gives presentations' (range Presentation), indicating that an active participant is someone who actively presents at a conference. In confOf, 'Author' is simply a sub-class of Person whose defining property is 'writes' (range Contribution). An Author writes a paper but need not present it, whereas an Active conference participant is someone who gives a presentation. Thus Active_conference_participant is a narrower, more specific role than Author: every active participant who contributes a paper is an author, but not every author is an active participant. Hence Active_conference_participant is subsumed_by Author.

Conference in ontology A denotes an academic conference event (with conference volumes, names, proceedings, etc.), while Conference_hall in ontology B is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). They share the word 'conference' but denote completely different concepts: an event vs. a location.

cmt:Person is a broad superclass covering all people in the system (Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User). confOf:Member_PC is a specific subclass of confOf:Person restricted to PC members who act as reviewers (domain of reviewes and expertOn). Thus cmt:Person is strictly more general than confOf:Member_PC.

Paper in edas is a document submitted to a conference, with subclasses like Accepted/Rejected Paper and properties like isWrittenBy and isReviewedBy. Fee in iasted is a monetary amount, with subclasses like Registration fee and Hotel fee. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

hasCo-author (cmt) specifically relates a Paper to its Co-author, while writtenBy (ekaw) relates a Document to a Person (author). Since Paper is a kind of Document and Co-author is a kind of Person, hasCo-author is a more specific property than writtenBy, making it subsumed_by writtenBy.

Chairman in cmt is a person role (a type of Person) that includes conference chairs and program committee chairs. Administrative event in confOf is a type of Event (e.g., registration, reviewing, submission events). One is a person, the other is an event; they share no domain overlap.

In ekaw, Presenter is a general class of conference participants who present, and it has Invited Speaker as a subclass. In the Conference ontology, Invited speaker is a specific subclass of Conference contributor. Thus A's Invited speaker is strictly more specific than B's Presenter, which subsumes it.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In cmt, 'run Paper Assignment Tools' relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of running paper-assignment software for a conference). In iasted, 'write' relates a Person to an Item (the act of writing a document/item). The domains (Administrator vs Person), ranges (Conference vs Item), and intended meanings are entirely distinct, so they are unrelated.

Conference contribution in the Conference ontology is a document/artefact (subclass of Conference document) with children like Written contribution, Poster, Presentation, etc. Activity in iasted is a temporal event/happening (with properties like is dated on, is held in, is held before/after). A contribution is a document produced for a conference, while an activity is an event or action; they are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

In ekaw, Location is the direct range of 'held In' (Event -> Location), making it a general class for where events take place. In iasted, Place is the range of 'is held in' (Activity -> Place, Time) and has specific subclasses like Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, etc. Place is a broader concept that includes physical venues with equipment and spatial relationships, while ekaw's Location is more narrowly the place where an event is held. Place subsumes Location.

Credit_card in iasted is a payment instrument (Item > Card > Credit card), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives a presentation (Person > Speaker). They belong to completely different domains and share no instances.

Both classes represent papers that have been accepted for a conference. They share the same label and position in the document hierarchy (Document > Paper > ... > Accepted Paper). The ekaw ontology provides a more granular submission lifecycle (Submitted > Assigned > Evaluated > Accepted), while edas has a flatter structure under Paper, but both denote the same concept: a paper whose review outcome is acceptance. The ekaw comment clarifies that camera-ready papers are distinct, which is consistent with edas where 'Published Paper' is a separate sibling. The sibling 'Rejected Paper' appears in both, further confirming the intended equivalence.

Both classes represent reviews of conference papers. They share the same path (Document > Review), have similar domain-range properties (written by reviewers, associated with papers), and the label 'Review' is used consistently in the conference domain. The differences in children (Meta Review vs. Negative/Neutral/Positive Review) reflect different sub-categorizations of the same concept, not different concepts.

Reviewing results event is an administrative event where authors access review results, while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a temporal deadline for submitting final manuscripts. They are different kinds of entities (event vs. deadline) at different points in the conference workflow.

Both classes represent the initial/abstract version of a paper submitted to a conference. In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Paper (with sibling 'Paper Full Version'), representing the abstract version of a paper. In iasted, 'Initial manuscript' is a subclass of Submission (with sibling 'Final manuscript'), representing the first version of a submitted document. Both denote the preliminary/abstract form of a submission before the full version, and in the conference domain these concepts are used interchangeably to refer to the initial abstract submission.

The two properties relate fundamentally different kinds of entities. ekaw:heldIn has domain Event and range Location, describing where an event takes place. iasted:is_present_in has domain Person and range Place or Time, describing where/when a person is present. Since their domains (Event vs. Person) and ranges (Location vs. Place/Time) do not overlap, these properties do not denote the same relation.

Lecture in iasted is a conference activity/event (subclass of Activity > Conference activity), with children like Plenary lecture, Session, Tutorial. Organizator in sigkdd is a person role (subclass of Person), with children like General Chair, Program Chair, etc. One denotes an event/activity, the other a person. They share no semantic overlap.

Review Rating in edas is a rating value for a reviewed paper (children: Accept, Reject, etc.; range of has Rating). Place in sigkdd is a physical location (children: Conference hall, Hotel, Main office; range of can stay in). These denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

Property A (has parts) relates a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (e.g., tracks, sessions, or sections of a proceedings volume). Property B (hasEvent) relates an Event to a sub-Event (e.g., a conference has a session, a session has a talk). Although both express mereological relations, their domains and ranges differ: Conference volume vs. Event, and Conference part vs. Event. A Conference part is not necessarily an Event, and a Conference volume is not necessarily an Event. The properties therefore do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction, so they are not equivalent.

The property `hasTopic` in edas links a Conference/Paper to a Topic (subject classification of a paper). The property `scientificallyOrganises` in ekaw links an Academic Institution to some unspecified entity, expressing that an institution scientifically organizes a conference or event. These are entirely different relations: one assigns a topic to a paper, the other denotes an institution's role in organizing an event. They share no domain, range, or semantic overlap.

confOf:Conference is a top-level conference event (sibling of Tutorial, Workshop under Working event), representing the entire conference or a conference-type event. edas:Closing Talk is a specific talk event occurring at the end of a conference (sibling of Welcome Talk under Talk Event). These are completely different concepts: one is the conference itself (or a conference-type working event), the other is a specific session/talk within a conference program. No subsumption relationship holds between them.
Review is a document written by a reviewer about a paper, while Departure tax is a monetary tax. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract is a document artefact (a short version of a paper) in cmt, while Security Topic is a subject classification in edas. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Document vs Topic) and share no domain overlap.

Property A (was a committee chair of) relates a Chair to a Committee, indicating committee leadership. Property B (reviewes) relates a Member PC to a Contribution, indicating paper reviewing. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

In ekaw, Web Site is a subclass of Document (a digital artefact), sibling to Paper, Review, Flyer, etc. In sigkdd, Webmaster is a subclass of Organizator under Person, sibling to General Chair and Program Committee member. One denotes an inanimate document/resource; the other denotes a human role. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Both Presenter (ekaw) and Speaker (iasted) denote a conference participant who presents at the conference. In ekaw, Presenter is a Conference Participant with child Invited Speaker. In iasted, Speaker is a Delegate with children Author and Reviewer. Despite the different hierarchy placement, the core meaning of a person who gives a presentation at a conference aligns. The terms Presenter and Speaker are near-synonyms in the conference domain, and both are subclasses of a participant/delegate class, indicating the same intended instances.

Contribution in confOf denotes a submitted scholarly work (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like abstract, keywords, title, and author relationships. Award in sigkdd denotes a prize/honor given to authors (Best Paper Award, Best Research Paper Award, etc.). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the work itself, the other is a recognition bestowed upon a work or its authors. There is no subsumption relationship between them.

Paper Full Version is a full-length manuscript document (subclass of Paper > Document), while Best Student Paper Award is an award given to a student paper. One is a document, the other is an award; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Both are object properties with domain Paper that relate a paper to the person(s) reviewing it. The edas range is a union of reviewer-related roles (Reviewer, Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), while the ekaw range is Possible Reviewer; these cover the same set of potential reviewers in the conference domain. The relation direction is identical (Paper -> Reviewer), so the properties denote the same relation.

maxChoice is a datatype property on Social event/Working event with range positiveInteger, representing a maximum number of choices. endDate is a datatype property on Conference with range dateTime, representing the conference end date and time. They have different domains, different ranges, and completely different meanings.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (organization-to-person). In edas, attendeeAt links a Person to a Conference Event (person-to-event). They are not inverses of each other either, since the ranges differ (Conference Member vs Conference Event).

Both properties relate a Paper to the reviewer(s) who are assigned to review it. 'assigned To' in cmt and 'is Reviewed By' in edas share the same domain (Paper) and both have Reviewer in their range, expressing the same relationship direction from paper to reviewer. The edas range is broader (including chair roles), but the core intended relation—linking a paper to its assigned reviewers—coincides.

IASTED member denotes a general membership status in the IASTED organization, sitting under Delegate alongside non-members and various participant roles. Organizing Committee member denotes a specific functional role on the organizing committee for a conference, sitting under Organizator alongside chairs and webmaster. These are distinct concepts: one is about organizational membership, the other about a committee role. Their instances do not coincide.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a broad superclass covering authors, reviewers, and committee members—essentially any person with a role in the conference. In sigkdd, Organizing_Committee_member is a specific kind of organizer (under Organizator) responsible for logistical arrangements, distinct from program chairs or committee members. The cmt ontology has no separate organizing-committee hierarchy, and ConferenceMember is far more general. The two concepts do not coincide: one is a broad role category, the other a specific logistical role. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the different organizational structures.

cmt:assignedTo assigns a Reviewer to a Paper for reviewing purposes (domain Paper, range Reviewer). ekaw:referencedIn indicates that something is referenced in something else (e.g., a paper is referenced in another paper or publication). These are fundamentally different relations: one is about assigning reviewers to papers, the other is about citation/reference relationships between documents. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Both classes denote the same concept: a contribution/paper that has been submitted to a conference. 'Submitted contribution' in the Conference ontology is a written contribution that has been submitted (and can be reviewed), while 'Submitted Paper' in EKAW is a paper that has been submitted. The sibling and child structures align (both can lead to reviewed/assigned papers), and the domain context confirms they refer to the same stage in the submission lifecycle. The slight terminological difference (contribution vs. paper) is a common synonym in this domain.

Paper Abstract is a textual document (a written summary of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical device) in the iasted ontology. They belong to completely different domains and hierarchies with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Document > Paper, representing a textual document (the abstract of a paper). In ekaw, 'Poster Session' is a subclass of Event > Scientific Event > Session, representing a scheduled event type at a conference. These are completely different domain concepts: one is a document artefact, the other is a session/event. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different ways. confOf:parallel_with links two Administrative events (e.g., conference tracks/sessions running in parallel), while edas:relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (associating a paper with its presentation event). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; neither subsumes the other.

In EDAS, Social Event is a broad category of non-academic events with children Excursion and Reception. In EKAW, Social Event is also a broad category, and Conference Banquet is a specific subtype of it. Thus EDAS Social Event is more general than EKAW Conference Banquet, so the relation is subsumed_by.

In EKAW, 'Conference Trip' is a subclass of Social Event, denoting a social/excursion activity associated with a conference. In SIGKDD, 'Conference' is the main academic event itself, with properties like start/end dates, city, and name, and it is held by ACM SIGKDD. These denote completely different concepts: a social trip vs. the conference event. They share the word 'Conference' but their intended instances do not coincide.

Research Institute (ekaw) is an organization (subclass of Organisation > Academic Institution), while Simulating (iasted) is an activity (subclass of Activity > Activity before conference > Research). One denotes an institution and the other a research activity; they share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Entity A is a committee (a group/body), while entity B is a person who is a member of an organizing committee. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one is an organizational body, the other is an individual person. Additionally, A refers to a steering committee specifically, while B refers to organizing committee members, so even the committee type differs.

Entity A is a topic about computer network applications within a topic hierarchy, while entity B is a type of presentation event (Contributed Talk) within an event hierarchy. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Poster Session is a type of scientific event/session where posters are presented, while Program Committee is a committee responsible for reviewing papers. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Test Only Topic is a subclass of Topic (a subject area for conference papers), while Invited Talk Abstract is a subclass of Abstract (a document). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

An Organizing committee handles the overall logistics and organization of a conference, while a Best Paper Awards Committee is a specialized committee responsible for selecting the best paper award. They are sibling committees under a common Committee parent but denote distinct concepts with different responsibilities; neither subsumes the other.
Acceptance is a Decision about a paper being accepted; Banquet is a Social event. They share no domain overlap.

The property 'written By' in EKAW relates a Document to the Person who authored it, while 'speak in' in IASTED relates a Person to a Place or Time where they speak. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties operate in entirely different domains. `invited by` links a Reviewer to another Reviewer (e.g., a reviewer invited by a chair or meta-reviewer), while `is sent by` links an Item (e.g., a document or submission) to a Person who sent it. They have different domains (Reviewer vs. Item), different ranges (Reviewer vs. Person), and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Computer Networks Sensor Topic' is a subclass of 'Computer Networks Topic' under 'Topic', representing a subject area within computer networks (specifically sensor networks). In the IASTED ontology, 'Sponsor state' is a subclass of 'State', representing a state related to sponsorship (likely a workflow or organizational state). These classes share no semantic overlap—one is a domain topic, the other is an organizational state.

These properties are completely different. 'has the first name' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's first name. 'is used by' is an object property from Item to Person, indicating which person uses an item. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics with no overlap.

Meal Menu denotes a menu for a meal event at a conference, while Web Site denotes a web page/site associated with an event or published by an organisation. Although both are subclasses of Document, their intended instances are completely disjoint and they participate in unrelated property networks.

These two datatype properties denote completely different attributes of a Person: one captures a person's last name (family name), the other captures an email address. Despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string), they relate to semantically unrelated concepts. A reference alignment would not consider them equivalent, nor is there a subsumption relationship between them.

Both properties link a Person to a document they authored/contributed, with matching domain (Person) and range (Conference document / Document). In the conference domain, 'contributes' and 'author Of' are used synonymously to denote authorship of a paper or document.

Both classes are named Document and serve as a general super-class for conference artefacts such as Paper and Review. In cmt, Document subsumes Paper and Review and is the range of hasConflictOfInterest (Person -> Document). In sigkdd, Document subsumes Abstract, Paper and Review and is the domain/range of presentation/submit-until relations. The shared children (Paper, Review) and the role as a generic container for conference artefacts indicate the same intended concept, despite sigkdd being slightly broader by also including Abstract.

In EDAS, TPC Member is a specific role: a member of the programme committee who can initiate calls and review papers. In EKAW, Possible Reviewer is a broader class (parent of PC Member) denoting anyone who could potentially review a paper. Since EKAW's Possible_Reviewer subsumes EDAS's TPCMember (a TPC member is a possible reviewer, but not every possible reviewer is a TPC member), the relation is subsumed_by.

These are two distinct deadline types in the conference timeline. 'Deadline for notification of acceptance' is when authors are notified of acceptance decisions, while 'Deadline Paper Submission' is when full papers must be submitted. They occur at different stages and denote different concepts, despite sharing the parent class Deadline.

Conference participant (A) is a subclass of Person, denoting people who attend a conference (with children Active/Passive conference participant). Social event (B) is a subclass of Event, denoting social activities like banquets, receptions, and trips. One is a person role, the other is an event type; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (adjusting a paper bidding preference), while pay relates a Person to Money (making a payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Paper is a scholarly document submitted for review, with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties linking it to authors, reviewers, bids, decisions, etc. In iasted, Tip is a monetary concept (path Money > Tip) with siblings Fee, Sponzorship, Tax. These denote completely unrelated domain concepts—a conference paper versus a monetary tip/gratuity.

In the Conference ontology, Topic is a general class for conference topics, with properties linking it to conference parts, reviews, and submitted contributions. In the edas ontology, SecurityTopic is a specific subclass of Topic (a sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), denoting only security-related topics. Thus SecurityTopic is strictly narrower than the general Topic class, so the Conference Topic subsumes edas SecurityTopic.

confOf:Event denotes a temporal occurrence (conference event with start/end dates, children like Social event, Working event). iasted:Item denotes a physical or informational object (equipment, documents, publications, transport). Their instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In ekaw, Negative_Review is a specific subclass of Review (alongside Positive and Neutral reviews). In sigkdd, Review is the general class for reviews. Thus ekaw:Negative_Review is strictly more specific than sigkdd:Review, so it is subsumed_by it.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Powerline Transmission Topic is a technical subject domain. They share no instances and belong to entirely different parts of the conference ontology.

Conference airport (iasted) denotes an airport used for conference travel, a specific type of Building. Hotel (sigkdd) denotes lodging accommodation. These are distinct types of places with different functions; an airport is not a hotel and vice versa. They share only the general parent Place, which is insufficient for equivalence or even a close relation.

Conference document is a class of documents (papers, reviews, announcements, etc.) in the Conference ontology, while Participant is a subclass of Person in confOf. They denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.
Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while ComputerArchitectureTopic is a subject-area topic. They share no domain overlap.

A Social event is an event (e.g., banquet, reception, trip) in confOf, while a Hotel room is a place/accommodation in iasted. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Event vs Place) and share no domain overlap.

In cmt, Document is a superclass whose children are Paper and Review, making it a broad artefact class. In edas, Paper is a specific subclass of Document with various status-based subtypes (Accepted, Rejected, etc.). Thus cmt:Document is strictly more general than edas:Paper, so the relation is subsumes.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing a person's email address. The labels 'email' and 'has an email' are synonymous in this context, and the structural positions (Person > property > string) match exactly.

confOf:City is a general class for any city (it is the range of properties on Organization and Person). iasted:Sponsor_city is a specific subclass of iasted:City, restricted to cities that sponsor the conference. Thus confOf:City is strictly more general than iasted:Sponsor_city, so the relation is subsumed_by.

A is a subclass of Conference participant (a person who attends but does not actively contribute), while B is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference/event). They denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. an event—so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject outcome), while in confOf, dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic (subject area). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

In the Conference ontology, 'Topic' is a general class for conference topics, serving as the domain/range for several general topic-related properties (e.g., being a topic of conference parts). In the EDAS ontology, 'CAD Topic' is a specific subclass of 'Topic' (a sibling alongside Antennas Topic, Communication Theory Topic, etc.), denoting topics specific to CAD (Computer-Aided Design). Therefore, CAD Topic is strictly narrower than the general Topic class, making A subsumed_by B.

cmt:Author is specifically a person who writes/submits papers, evidenced by properties like submitPaper and writePaper. Conference:Active_conference_participant is broader, covering any participant who actively contributes (e.g., gives presentations), with Regular author as a more specific subclass. The two classes overlap (authors are active participants) but are not equivalent; Active_conference_participant subsumes Author in intent, but the structural and property differences suggest a related/overlap relation rather than clean subsumption.

In ekaw, Presenter is a subclass of Person > Conference Participant, denoting a person who presents at a conference. In iasted, Conference building is a subclass of Place > Building, denoting a physical venue. These are completely different categories (person vs. physical location) with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In cmt, 'readByReviewer' links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper -> reviewer who reads it). In confOf, 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (author -> paper they authored). They involve different domain/range types and different semantic relations (reading vs. authoring), so they are not equivalent, not subsumed, and only weakly related as both connect persons to documents.

The iasted class 'Author book proceedings included' is a specialized author role (an author whose paper is included in book proceedings), nested under Author. The sigkdd 'Invited Speaker' is a speaker invited to present. These denote different roles: one is about authorship in a proceedings book, the other about being an invited speaker. They do not share a common direct parent in their respective hierarchies (Author vs Speaker) and their intended instances do not coincide.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference hotel in iasted is a physical place/building where the conference is held. They denote completely different categories of entities.

Reception in confOf is a social event (e.g., a conference reception), whereas Transport vehicle in iasted is a physical item used for transportation (car, taxi, van, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and share no domain overlap.

cmt:Document is a general artefact (parent of Paper and Review) that can be subject to conflicts of interest, whereas edas:ReviewQuestion is a question item used in reviewing (parent of Numerical/Textual Review Question). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Poster in the Conference ontology is a specific kind of conference contribution (a poster presentation), while Document in iasted is a broad super-class covering many artefact types (forms, letters, reviews, submissions, transparencies, etc.). A Poster is not equivalent to the broad Document class, nor is it clearly subsumed by it since the ontologies model different aspects (contribution vs. artefact). They share no clear instance overlap.

These two datatype properties have completely different meanings. 'reviewsPerPaper' (cmt) captures the number of reviews assigned per paper in a conference (range: int), while 'hasName' (edas) captures the full name of a conference (range: string). They share the same domain (Conference) but denote entirely different attributes with different ranges and semantics.

A is a Conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while B is a person role (a student delegate who does not speak, subclass of Non speaker under Delegate). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

The cmt property 'hasProgramCommitteeMember' relates a Program Committee to its Program Committee Members, while the iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. `hasConflictOfInterest` links a Person to a Document (the paper for which there is a conflict), whereas `hasCity` links an Organization or Person to a City (a geographic location). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

These properties relate entirely different kinds of things. 'invites co reviewers' connects a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the act of one reviewer inviting another to help review). 'isReviewHistoryOf' connects a Personal Review History object to a Reviewer (linking a review-history record to the reviewer it belongs to). The domains differ (Reviewer vs Personal Review History), the ranges differ in role, and the semantics are unrelated.

Invited Talk Abstract is a document (an abstract text for an invited talk), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline (a date for abstract submission). One is a written artefact, the other is a deadline event; they share no instances.

The two properties relate completely different things: cmt:memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while confOf:reviewes links a Member PC to a Contribution (reviewing relation). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

Tutorial is a specific type of conference part where a tutorial is given, distinct from a Paper Presentation which is an academic event where an accepted paper is presented. They denote different kinds of conference activities with different purposes.

Paper Full Version in cmt is a full-length paper document submitted to a conference, while Best Research Paper Award in sigkdd is an award given to a paper. They are completely different concepts: one is a document type, the other is an award. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Invited Talk Abstract is a document (an abstract of an invited talk), while Nonmember registration fee is a monetary fee for non-member registration. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Author Not Reviewer in cmt is a subclass of Author (a person who authored a paper but is not a reviewer). Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Subject Area denotes a topic or research area that a Paper can be classified under (cmt ontology), while Time zone denotes a geographical time offset (iasted ontology). These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Workshop in the Conference ontology is a conference part/event (a scientific meeting session), while Video cassette player in iasted is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

submit Paper (domain Author, range Paper) models an author submitting a paper to a conference. is paid in (domain Money, range Building) models money being paid in a building. These relate entirely different domain and range types with no semantic overlap.

Conference proceedings in the Conference ontology is a published document (with ISBN, publisher, volume), while Conference Session in edas is a temporal/organizational event within a conference. They denote completely different kinds of things (publication artefact vs. scheduled session), so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate different domain entities in different directions. cmt:writeReview has domain Reviewer and range Review, capturing the action of a reviewer writing a review. ekaw:hasReview has domain Paper and range Review, capturing a paper being associated with a review. They are not inverses of each other (an inverse of writeReview would be something like 'writtenBy' with domain Review and range Reviewer), and they do not share the same domain or direction, so they are unrelated.
