confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion) under Event > Social event, while iasted:Trip_day is a temporal entity (a day on which a trip occurs) under Time. One denotes an event/activity, the other a time period; they are different kinds of things.

cmt:Document is a general document class with children Paper and Review, representing written artefacts in the conference domain. Conference:Review_expertise represents the expertise level or area of a reviewer, not a document at all. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event specifically about participant registration during a conference. edas's 'Organizational Meeting' is an academic event like a workshop or paper presentation. These are different kinds of conference events with no clear overlap in intended instances.

Property A (was_a_committee_of) links a Committee to a Conference volume, indicating which conference a committee served. Property B (writtenBy) links a Contribution to an Author, indicating authorship. They connect entirely different entity types in different directions and serve unrelated functions in the conference domain.

In the EDAS ontology, Document is a broad superclass that subsumes Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, and Meal Menu. In the EKAW ontology, Review is a specific subclass of Document. Thus EDAS Document is strictly more general than EKAW Review, so the relation is subsumes.

Paper Full Version is a document (a full paper submission), while Registration deadline is a temporal entity (a deadline for registration). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no instances.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. 'has an expertise' is a datatype property whose domain is 'Review expertise' (linking a review-expertise object to some expertise value), while 'speak in' is an object property whose domain is Person and whose range is Place/Time (indicating where/when a person gives a presentation). They share no common domain or range and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Although both properties have range Person, their domains and meanings differ: has_authors links a Conference document to the Person(s) who authored it, while hasAttendee links a Conference Event to the Person(s) who attend it. These are distinct relations in the conference domain with no overlap in the kinds of things they relate.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. cmt:assignedTo has domain Paper and range Reviewer, expressing that a paper is assigned to a reviewer. ekaw:reviewOfPaper has domain Review and range Paper, expressing that a review is of a paper. They are not inverses of each other (the inverse of assignedTo would be a property from Reviewer to Paper, not from Review to Paper), and they do not share the same domain or range types. Therefore they denote different relations and are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is a subclass of Document denoting the written article itself, while ekaw:Paper_Author is a subclass of Person denoting the author of a paper. They are disjoint kinds of entities (document vs person), so they are unrelated.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person, representing people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Place in edas represents physical locations such as accommodation, venues, dining places, and meeting rooms. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is the person who chairs the entire program committee, overseeing paper review and acceptance decisions for the conference. Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is the person who organizes and chairs tutorials, a specific session/event type. These are distinct conference roles with different responsibilities and scopes; neither subsumes the other.

In Conference ontology, 'Regular contribution' is a broad class covering various written contribution types (it has children Extended abstract and Paper, plus siblings like Poster, Presentation). In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a specific document type (child of Document, sibling of Abstract and Review). The sigkdd Paper corresponds to the more specific 'Paper' child under Regular_contribution in Conference, not to Regular_contribution itself. Thus Regular_contribution subsumes Paper.

Invited_speaker in the Conference ontology is a subclass of Person (specifically a Conference contributor), denoting the human role of a person invited to give a talk. Invited_Talk in ekaw is a subclass of Individual Presentation (under Event), denoting the presentation event itself. One is a person, the other is an event; they are disjoint kinds of entities and not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

Sponsor (iasted) is a person or organization that provides financial support for the conference, while Organizing Committee member (sigkdd) is a person who serves on the organizing committee. These are distinct roles: a sponsor funds the event, whereas an organizing committee member handles logistical organization. There is no indication that their instances coincide, and neither concept subsumes the other.

The cmt property 'hasProgramCommitteeMember' relates a Program Committee to its members (people serving on the committee), while the edas property 'isProviderOf' relates an Organization to a Sponsorship it provides. These are completely different domain relationships with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Paper is a document submitted for review (subclass of Document, with authors, reviews, bids, decisions). In iasted, Deadline is a temporal concept (subclass of Time) representing submission or notification deadlines. These denote completely different entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Subject Area in cmt denotes a topic or research area that a Paper can be associated with (via hasSubjectArea). Review preference in Conference denotes a reviewer's preference for reviewing a particular topic or submitted contribution, including a degree of preference and an assignment to a reviewer. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a subject classification for papers, the other is a bidding/preference mechanism for reviewers. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers, distinct from reviewers and PC members. In confOf, Member PC is explicitly a reviewer (per rdfs:comment) who reviews contributions and has expertise on topics. The cmt ontology separates Author from Reviewer/Program Committee Member as distinct sibling roles, so these two classes denote different conference roles with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and represent different concepts. confOf:hasTitle applies to Contribution and captures the title of a paper or contribution. sigkdd:Name applies to Person and captures a person's name. They do not share the same domain or range semantics, and neither subsumes the other.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string postal code, while writtenBy is an object property linking Document to Person. They relate completely different entities in different directions with different ranges, so they are unrelated.

`invites co reviewers` relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (inviting a co-reviewer), while `writes` relates an Author to a Contribution (writing a paper). They have different domains, different ranges, and denote completely different relations in the conference domain.

These properties connect entirely different entities in opposite directions. Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (indicating a topic's association with a review preference), while property B links a Member PC to a Topic (indicating a PC member's expertise area). The domains (Topic vs Member PC) and ranges (Review preference vs Topic) are completely disjoint, so these are unrelated relations.

confOf:writes relates an Author to a Contribution (a person writes a paper). ekaw:hasPart is a generic mereological relation indicating that something has a part. These are fundamentally different relations: one connects a person to a document they authored, the other expresses part-whole structure. They do not share the same domain/range types or semantics.

Both classes represent a paper/contribution that has undergone review/evaluation, sitting at the same position in their respective hierarchies (submitted -> assigned -> evaluated/reviewed) and sharing the same children (Accepted/Rejected). The only difference is terminology (Reviewed vs Evaluated), which in the conference domain denotes the same concept.

Both are datatype properties recording when an event starts, with closely aligned domains (Event vs ConferenceEvent). However, they differ in range type (string vs dateTime), so they are not strictly equivalent; they are related/overlapping.

Both classes denote authors of conference papers/contributions, so their intended instances overlap. However, they are not equivalent: A's Contribution_co-author is a specific co-author role nested under Regular author within a document/contribution hierarchy, whereas B's Paper_Author is a broad subclass of Person covering any author of a paper. B is more general in its ontology's structure, but because A is a role-based subclass rather than a direct subclass of Person, a reference alignment would likely mark them as related rather than strict subsumption.

Government Organization in edas is a type of organization (e.g., a government body that might sponsor or participate in a conference). Sponsor state in iasted is a geographic/political state that sponsors a conference. One is an organization, the other is a geographic region; they denote fundamentally different kinds of entities despite both being connected to the notion of sponsorship.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Activity in iasted denotes events or actions (e.g., conference activities, activities before/after conference) with properties like being held in a place, dated, given by someone. These are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is an event/activity. No overlap in intended instances.

Conference announcement is a document type (a conference-related publication/notice), while Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a subject domain for conference papers. They share no instances and belong to completely different hierarchies (documents vs. topics).

A 'Plenary lecture' is a type of academic presentation/activity at a conference, while 'Program Committee' is a committee of people who review papers. They share no instances and are from entirely different parts of the ontology hierarchy (Activity vs. Committee).

Poster is a conference contribution artefact (subclass of Conference contribution, sibling of Paper, Presentation), while Speaker is a person role (subclass of Person, with children Author and Invited Speaker). They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote completely different things.

The two properties relate completely different entities and express different relations. In cmt, 'rejected By' links a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it. In the Conference ontology, 'issues' links a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes. The domains (Paper vs Publisher), ranges (Administrator vs Conference proceedings), and meanings (rejection vs publication) are entirely disjoint.

Property A links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract. Property B links a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and share no common semantics.

In EKAW, Event is a broad class covering both scientific and social events, with children like Scientific Event and Social Event. In IASTED, Activity is a broader class that includes pre-conference activities, post-conference activities, and conference activities. While every EKAW Event could be considered an IASTED Activity (since conferences, sessions, and social events are types of activities), the reverse is not true: IASTED Activity includes things like 'Activity before conference' and 'Activity after conference' that may not be events in the EKAW sense (e.g., preparation tasks, payment activities). Thus EKAW Event is subsumed by IASTED Activity, but they are not equivalent.

Property A relates a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (assigning a chair role), while property B relates a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event (listing events in a programme). They have different domains, different ranges, and express fundamentally different relationships: role-assignment vs. event-listing.

The iasted 'Author cd proceedings included' is a specific subclass of Author whose work is included in CD proceedings, while the sigkdd 'Author' is a general author class with subtypes like 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student'. The iasted class is a narrower concept subsumed by the general sigkdd Author class.

Conference Venue Place in edas is a physical venue (building, room, etc.) where conference sessions take place, sibling to accommodation, dining, and meeting-room places. Conference city in iasted is a city associated with a conference, sibling to presenter/sponsor/trip cities. One denotes a venue/place, the other a city; they are different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent and not in a subsumption relation.

These properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. 'has_tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a whole-part relationship). 'presentationed_by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (a document-to-presenter relationship). They share no common domain or range types and express fundamentally different relationships.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges and express different actions. In cmt, 'enter Review Criteria' links an Administrator to a Conference, representing the act of setting review criteria for a conference. In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution, representing the act of reviewing a specific paper/contribution. They differ in domain (Administrator vs. Member PC), range (Conference vs. Contribution), and meaning (entering review criteria vs. performing a review).

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. In edas, 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it, whereas in iasted, 'need' links a Person to an Item they need. The domains (Sponsorship vs Person), ranges (Organization vs Item), and intended meanings are entirely disjoint, so they are unrelated.

These properties go in opposite directions and relate different things. cmt's 'written By' has domain Review and range Reviewer, meaning it links a review to the person who wrote it. Conference's 'has a review reference or expertise' has domain Reviewer and range (Review expertise, Review preference), meaning it links a reviewer to their expertise or preferences. They are not the same relation, nor is one the inverse of the other (the ranges differ entirely).

A's Conference is the top-level conference entity with children like Conference volume and properties linking to proceedings/publishers/topics. B's Conference Banquet is a specific social event (a meal/gathering) occurring within a conference, subsumed by Social Event > Event. They share the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different things: the overall conference vs. a banquet event at a conference.
A Reviewer is a person who reviews papers, while a Submitted contribution is a document/paper that has been submitted. They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in instances.

Possible Reviewer (ekaw) is a person who could review a paper (child of Person, domain/range of review-related properties). Sponzor (sigkdd) is a sponsor entity with subclasses like Gold/Bronze Supporter and Exhibitor, and properties for sponsor name and search relationships. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain: a potential reviewer vs. a financial/material sponsor. No overlap in intended instances.

Final manuscript is a specific stage of submission (the final version after acceptance), while Paper in sigkdd is a general document type that can be submitted. Final manuscript is more specific than Paper, so it is subsumed by it.

In ontology A, Abstract is a specific class (a kind of conference contribution, a leaf under Extended abstract). In ontology B, Document is a general superclass whose children include Abstract, Paper, and Review. Thus A's Abstract is a specific document type subsumed by B's Document; they are not equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference, capturing how a topic is valued in the review process. 'is present in' links a Person to a Place or Time, capturing attendance/presence. They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relations in the conference domain.

A 'Call for paper' is a document announcing that papers are being solicited for a conference, while a 'Record of attendance' is a document certifying that someone attended an event. These are completely different types of conference documents with no overlap in intended instances.

Individual Presentation in EKAW is a broad superclass encompassing Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, and Tutorial—any single oral/academic presentation event. Video presentation in IASTED is a specific medium-based presentation type (sibling of Power Point presentation). A video presentation is not an instance of the EKAW Individual Presentation class (which models live conference talks), and the EKAW class does not subsume the IASTED video presentation concept since they belong to disjoint categorizations (event-type vs. delivery-medium). They share only the word 'presentation'.

The cmt 'adjusted By' property relates a Bid to a Reviewer (a reviewer adjusts a bid in the paper-bidding process). The iasted 'give' property relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives a presentation or item at a conference). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Viza (visa) is a travel/immigration document for conference attendance, while Abstract is a summary of a paper. Despite both being subclasses of Document, they denote completely different artefacts with no overlap in intended instances.

manuscriptDueOn is a datatype property from Conference to dateTime representing a manuscript submission deadline, while topicCoveredBy is an object property from Research Topic to Event/Paper indicating which events or papers cover a topic. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Both are object properties with domain Author and range a paper/contribution concept (cmt:Paper and confOf:Contribution are commonly aligned in the Conference track). They both express the relation that an author writes a paper, with the same direction (Author -> Paper/Contribution).

The property 'was a member of' in the Conference ontology relates a Committee member to a Committee (indicating committee membership), while 'hold' in sigkdd relates the organization ACM SIGKDD to a Conference (indicating the organization holds/organizes a conference). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and different semantics.

These two entities denote completely different concepts. In the iasted ontology, 'Conference Hiker' is a subclass of Delegate, meaning it represents a type of person (a conference attendee/participant). In the sigkdd ontology, 'Conference hall' is a subclass of Place, meaning it represents a physical location where a conference takes place. Despite the superficial lexical similarity, one is a person role and the other is a venue; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Entity A is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area about computer networks sensors, while entity B is a subclass of Committee representing a program committee. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent authors of conference papers, but they are not equivalent. 'Contribution 1th author' is a specific subclass of 'Regular author' denoting the first author of a contribution, whereas 'Paper Author' is a general class for any author of a paper. The first author is a kind of paper author, but not vice versa, so they overlap without being equivalent.
Organizer is a person or entity that organizes a conference, while Currency is a monetary unit (e.g., used for registration fees). These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Organizational Meeting' is a type of academic event (a meeting held to organize conference affairs), sitting alongside Paper Presentation, Workshop, etc. In iasted, 'Author book proceedings included' is a sub-type of Author (a person who has a book proceedings publication included), sitting alongside other author/speaker types. One is an event, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are unrelated.

cmt:Author is a specific role (a person who writes/submits papers) sitting under Person > Conference Member, whereas ekaw:Person is the general class of all people, with Paper Author among its children. Thus cmt:Author is subsumed by ekaw:Person rather than equivalent to it.

confOf:Scholar is a price-category role (a participant who qualifies for a discounted registration fee, with a 'studyAt' property linking to a University). edas:ConferenceChair is the person who chairs the entire conference, with properties like initiating calls and reviewing papers. These are completely different concepts: one is a registration fee category, the other is an organizational leadership role. Their instances do not coincide.

Entity A is a specific research topic about computer networks management, a subclass of Topic. Entity B is a Program Committee, a type of organizing committee for a conference. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'belongs to reviewers' in Conference relates review expertise or review preference to a reviewer, indicating which reviewer a preference or expertise belongs to. The property 'references' in ekaw is a generic object property with unspecified domain and range, likely denoting a reference relation between documents or entities. These properties denote completely different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

hasEmail relates a Person to their email address (string), while Name relates a Person to their name (string). These are distinct attributes with no overlap in meaning; one is not a subproperty of the other.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is the chair of the entire conference program committee, overseeing paper reviews for the conference. Workshop Chair (ekaw) is the chair of a specific workshop within a conference. These are distinct organizational roles: one oversees the conference-level review process, the other manages a single workshop. They share the parent PC Member but denote different responsibilities and scopes.

In edas, Sponsorship is a specific concept representing a sponsorship arrangement (with provider organization, cost amount, currency, and subtypes like Travel Grant). In iasted, Sponzorship is placed under Money alongside Fee, Tax, and Tip, making it a monetary amount or financial concept rather than the relational sponsorship arrangement. The iasted Money hierarchy is broader and more general, treating Sponzorship as a kind of money/financial value, while edas Sponsorship is a specific organizational relationship. Thus edas Sponsorship is subsumed by the broader iasted Sponzorship concept, but they are not equivalent.

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs conference roles (Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Author in iasted is a delegate who writes papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Paper Presentation' is a subclass of Academic Event (a Conference Event), i.e., the act/session of presenting a paper. In the EKAW ontology, 'Paper' is a subclass of Document, i.e., the written artefact itself. These are disjoint categories (event vs. document), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or even related in the alignment sense.

The two properties relate different entities and in opposite directions. `has_a_review` links a Reviewed contribution to its Review (paper -> review), whereas `isReviewing` links a Reviewer (or chair/TPC member) to the Paper they are reviewing (reviewer -> paper). They are not inverses of each other either, since one connects a paper to a review document and the other connects a reviewer to a paper. They denote different relations in the conference domain.

confOf Member is a broad participant role (sibling to Regular, Student) covering any conference member, while sigkdd Organizing_Committee_member is a specific organizing-committee role. Member is more general, so Member is subsumed_by Organizing_Committee_member is not right; rather Organizing_Committee_member is a specialization of Member, making Member subsume it. The correct relation is subsumes (A subsumes B).

In ekaw, Event is a broad class covering scientific and social events (conferences, sessions, etc.), with properties for location, organization, topics, and part-whole relations. In sigkdd, Award is a specific kind of recognition given to authors for papers (e.g., Best Research Paper Award). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Programme Brochure (ekaw) is a document listing conference events/programme, with properties like 'lists Event' and 'event On List'. Hotel registration form (iasted) is a form for hotel registration. They are different kinds of documents serving entirely different purposes in the conference domain, with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, 'Non Academic Event' is a conference event category (e.g., meals, breaks, social events), whereas in sigkdd 'Author' is a person role for someone who submits papers and receives awards. They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. In cmt, 'enter Review Criteria' links an Administrator to a Conference (an action of setting review criteria for a conference). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presented a document). They have different domains (Administrator vs Document), different ranges (Conference vs Speaker), and different meanings. There is no overlap in what they relate.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and are not inverses. In cmt, hasCo-author links a Paper to a Co-author (a Person who co-authored that paper). In ekaw, authorOf links a Person to a Document (the authored document). The cmt property is a co-authorship relation from document to person, while the ekaw property is an authorship relation from person to document. They are not inverses because hasCo-author is specifically about co-authors, not the primary author, and the ekaw authorOf is a general authorship relation. No reference alignment would equate these.

In ekaw, 'Assigned Paper' is a submitted paper that has been assigned to reviewers (a workflow state in the reviewing process, parent 'Submitted Paper', child 'Evaluated Paper'). In sigkdd, 'Abstract' is a document type that is a summary of a paper, sibling to 'Paper' and 'Review'. These denote completely different concepts: one is a paper in a specific review-assignment state, the other is a summary document. They share only the distant ancestor 'Document'.

cmt:Conference Member is a subclass of Person (a human participant in a conference, with subclasses like Author, Reviewer, etc.), while sigkdd:Conference_hall is a subclass of Place (a physical location/venue). They belong to completely disjoint hierarchies (people vs. places) and share no instances in common.

A 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a specific type of presenter/author who gives a plenary lecture, while a 'Program Chair' is an organizer responsible for overseeing the conference program. These are distinct roles: one is a content contributor/speaker, the other is an administrative/organizational leader. Their paths and siblings confirm they belong to different hierarchies (speakers/authors vs. organizers/committee members).

A Meta Review is a second-level review written by a meta-reviewer about a paper's reviews, whereas an Abstract is a summary of a paper's content. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain despite both being subclasses of Document.

confOf:Conference is an event (a conference gathering), while iasted:Author_book_proceedings_included is a sub-role of Author (a person whose book proceedings are included). They denote completely different concepts: an event vs. a person/role.

Communication Theory Topic is a subject-area classification (a Topic) in the EDAS ontology, while Invited Talk is a type of presentation event in the EKAW ontology. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A is a Conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop), while B is a CD proceeding (subclass of Publication, sibling of Book proceeding). One denotes an event, the other a physical publication medium; they share no instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'belongs to reviewers' links Review expertise/Review preference to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer a preference or expertise belongs to). 'hasReviewHistory' links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (indicating the review history record of a reviewer). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Main office in iasted is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room). One is a human role, the other is a location; they share no instances and are unrelated.

In the iasted ontology, Activity is a broad class encompassing conference-related events and actions (e.g., Conference activity, Activity before/after conference), with properties about scheduling, venues, and payments. In the sigkdd ontology, Document is a class for textual artefacts (Abstract, Paper, Review) with properties about presentations and submission deadlines. These are fundamentally different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have opposite directions and relate different entity types. In Conference, 'gives presentations' links an Active conference participant (person) to a Presentation (event). In ekaw, 'presentationOfPaper' links an Individual Presentation (event) to a Paper/Abstract (document). One is person→presentation, the other is presentation→paper; they are not inverses of each other either, since the participants and the papers are different kinds of things.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. `has tracks` links a Conference volume to a Track (a topical session division of a conference), while `has City` links an Organization or Person to a City (a geographical location). They share no domain or range overlap and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Both are object properties linking a written artefact to its author/sender, but the domains differ: confOf:writtenBy has domain Contribution (a paper/contribution) and range Author, while iasted:is_sent_by has domain Item (which may include non-paper items) and range Person. The broader domain/range of the iasted property makes it more general, but the two properties overlap significantly in the conference submission context, so 'related' is the safest reference-alignment choice rather than strict equivalence or subsumption.

Property A (has_an_abstract) links a paper/poster/presentation to its Abstract, while property B (relatedToPaper) links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and express different relationships (abstract ownership vs. association with an accepted paper).

Conference participant in ontology A is a broad class covering all people who participate in a conference (including active and passive participants), sitting as a sibling of Committee member, Reviewer, etc. Organizing Committee member in ontology B is a specific role within the organizing committee (a subtype of Organizator), alongside chairs and webmaster. An organizing committee member is not a conference participant in the general sense intended by A, and a conference participant is not necessarily an organizing committee member. The two classes have largely disjoint intended instances, so they are unrelated.

Both properties relate persons to documents/items in the conference domain, but they are inverses of each other: 'contributes' goes from Person to Conference document, while 'is writen by' goes from Item to Person. A property and its inverse are not equivalent.
A is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while B is a city where a conference takes place. They denote completely different kinds of entities (event vs. place), so they are unrelated.

cmt:Review is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a paper, with properties like written By (Review -> Reviewer) and write Review (Reviewer -> Review). edas:PersonalPublicationHistory is a personal history record tracking an individual's publications, sibling to Personal Review History under Personal History. These denote completely different concepts: one is a review document, the other is a publication history aggregate. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.

In ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' is a specific subclass of Paper denoting papers that have been submitted (but not yet accepted), with siblings like 'Camera Ready Paper' indicating different stages/types. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general top-level paper class under Document, with siblings Abstract and Review. Thus ekaw:Submitted_Paper is a narrower concept subsumed by sigkdd:Paper.

Both classes represent activities/events occurring during a conference, but they are not equivalent. 'Non Academic Event' in edas is specifically restricted to non-academic events (breaks, meals, social events), excluding academic events. 'Conference activity' in iasted is a broader concept encompassing all conference activities including academic ones (Lecture, Presentation, Introduction) as well as non-academic ones (Coffee break, Social program, Coctail reception). The iasted class subsumes the edas class extensionally, but the labels and structural positions suggest different intended scopes, so 'related' is the safest verdict.

Entity A is a class denoting a written academic paper presented at a conference (a document), while entity B is a class denoting a city in which a conference takes place (a location). Despite the shared word 'Conference', these are completely different concepts with disjoint intended instances.

cmt:User is a broad superclass encompassing Administrator, Author, and Reviewer — essentially any person who logs into the CMT system. edas:TPC Member is a specific committee role (a member of the Technical Program Committee) that can review papers, initiate calls, and chair sessions. A TPC Member would be a kind of user of the system, but the two classes do not denote the same concept: User is a system-access category, while TPC Member is a functional conference role. They are not equivalent, and neither cleanly subsumes the other in the intended modeling, so they are best treated as unrelated.

Abstract in the Conference ontology is a document type (a written summary of a paper/poster/presentation), whereas Activity in iasted denotes an event or action (e.g., conference activity, activity before/after conference) with temporal and spatial properties. These are completely different domain concepts despite both appearing in a conference ontology.
cmt:name denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while confOf:ends_on denotes the end date of an Event. They have disjoint domains and completely different semantics.

confOf:Author is a subclass of Person denoting a human author who writes contributions. iasted:Author_information_form is a subclass of Form (under Document > Item), i.e. a bureaucratic document/form. They share the word 'Author' but denote completely different entities (a person vs. a form), so they are unrelated.
Accommodation Place is a lodging venue (e.g., hotel) under Place, while Taxi is a transport vehicle under Item. They denote completely different categories with no overlap in instances.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (the act of a reviewer adjusting their bid on a paper), while hasReviewHistory relates a Reviewer to their Personal ReviewHistory (a record of past reviewing activity). These are distinct relations with different ranges and meanings; one is about bidding and the other about review history.

These properties go in opposite directions and have different semantics. cmt's hasAuthor relates Paper -> Author (paper has an author). edas's hasRelatedPaper relates Author -> Paper (author has a related paper). They are not the same relation, nor is one the inverse of the other in a way that would make them equivalent. hasAuthor is about authorship attribution; hasRelatedPaper is about papers associated with an author. They are unrelated.

confOf:Member_PC is a subclass of Person denoting a PC member/reviewer, while edas:RejectRating is a subclass of Review Rating denoting a rating value. They belong to completely different parts of the conference domain (people vs. review ratings) and share no instances.

Short_paper in confOf is a type of conference contribution (a short paper submission), while Best_Applications_Paper_Award in sigkdd is a type of award given for a paper. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Contribution vs Award) and denote entirely different concepts.

Conference volume (A) is a conference event/publication volume with committees, tracks, contributions, and important dates. Organizing Committee member (B) is a person who serves on an organizing committee. These are completely different kinds of entities: an event/artefact vs. a person/role.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In Conference, 'belongs to reviewers' links review expertise/preference to a reviewer (indicating which reviewer an expertise or preference belongs to). In iasted, 'write' links a person to an item they author. The domains (Review expertise/Review preference vs Person) and ranges (Reviewer vs Item) do not coincide, and the intended relations are distinct: one is about reviewer assignment of expertise/preference, the other about authorship of an item.

locationOf is an object property relating a Location to an Event, while Price is a datatype property relating a Registration fee to an integer value. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics with no overlap.

confOf:Topic denotes a subject area that contributions, working events, and PC members are associated with (via deals With, expert On, has Topic). iasted:Activity denotes a temporal event or happening (with subclasses like Conference activity, Activity before/after conference) that is held in places, dated, paid for, etc. These are completely different concepts: a topic/subject area vs. an organized activity/event. No overlap in intended instances.
Decision (accept/reject a paper) and Money (financial amounts) are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in instances.

A Conference Chair in cmt is a specific leadership role (a person who chairs the conference), while a Conference contributor in the Conference ontology is a broad superclass covering anyone who contributes (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors). These are very different concepts: one is a specific organizational role, the other is a general category of contribution. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

Test Only Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference submissions (alongside siblings like Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). Tutorial Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Abstract under Document, representing a summary document for a tutorial. These are completely different concepts: one is a topic/subject classification, the other is a type of document abstract.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a human who contributes to a conference, e.g., author or speaker), while Lecture is a subclass of Activity (an event/presentation). They denote entirely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

These properties operate in completely different domains and directions. In ekaw, 'scientifically Organises' has domain Academic Institution and relates an institution to something it scientifically organizes (likely a conference or event). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' has domain Document and range Speaker, relating a document/presentation to the speaker who presented it. They connect different entity types (institution vs. document) and represent different relationships (organizing an event vs. being presented by a speaker). No overlap in intended meaning.

Dining Place in edas is a subclass of Place, representing a physical location where dining occurs. Conference Trip in ekaw is a subclass of Social Event, representing an organized social activity/event. One is a spatial location, the other is a temporal event. They are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology Conference, 'Information for participants' is a subclass of Conference document, i.e. a written artefact providing information to conference attendees. In ekaw, 'Conference' is a subclass of Scientific Event denoting one edition of a conference itself. One is a document/information resource, the other is an event; their intended instances do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

Property A (is an ending date) is a datatype property with domain Important dates and range date, capturing when a deadline ends. Property B (location Of) is an object property with domain Location and range Event, capturing where an event is located. They relate entirely different kinds of entities (temporal vs. spatial) and have no semantic overlap.

hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person who attends it, while organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person that organises it. These are distinct relations (attending vs. organising) with different semantics, and neither subsumes the other.

Workshop Chair in ekaw is a committee/organizational role (a PC Member who chairs a workshop), while Tutorial speaker in iasted is a type of Author/Speaker who presents a tutorial. One is an administrative chair role, the other is a presenter/author role; their intended instances do not coincide.

In the edas ontology, Conference represents the conference event itself (with properties like has Country, has Name, paper Due On, etc.). In the iasted ontology, Activity is a general class for activities (with subtypes like 'Activity after conference', 'Activity before conference', 'Conference activity'), meaning things people do at or around a conference, not the conference event. These are disjoint concepts: a Conference is not an Activity. The iasted ontology would represent the conference event elsewhere (e.g., as a Conference activity or Conference), not as the general Activity class.

Conference announcement is a document type (a written notice about a conference), while Power Point presentation is a presentation format/activity. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (document vs. activity) and denote different concepts in the conference domain.

The property hasMenu in edas relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (catering context), while need in iasted relates a Person to an Item (personal requirement context). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the same conference-domain artefact: a formal announcement inviting paper submissions. 'Call for paper' in Conference and 'Call For Papers' in edas are synonymous labels, and both are situated under a document/announcement hierarchy (Conference document vs Call) alongside sibling calls (participation, manuscripts, reviews). Their intended instances coincide.

In Conference ontology, 'Information for participants' is a document/artefact (child of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.) — a piece of written information. In iasted, 'Technic activity' is an event/activity (child of Conference activity, sibling of Cocktail reception, Registration, Presentation) — a scheduled happening. A document and an activity are disjoint kinds of things; no subsumption holds.
Both properties link a Review to the paper it reviews. Domain is Review in both; range (Reviewed contribution vs Paper) denotes the same artefact in the conference domain. Direction is identical.

Property A (issues) relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings it publishes. Property B (eventOnList) relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site where the event appears. Different domains (Publisher vs Event), different ranges (Conference proceedings vs Programme Brochure/Web Site), and different semantics (publishing proceedings vs listing an event on a brochure/website). No overlap in meaning.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a type of working event/conference activity), while ekaw:Session_Chair is a person (a conference participant role). These are completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Scientific Event in ekaw is a broad class covering conferences, sessions, tracks, workshops, and individual presentations—i.e., the academic/scientific program of a conference. Social program in iasted is a Conference activity whose instances are dinners, cocktail receptions, coffee breaks, and welcome addresses—i.e., the social/leisure side of a conference. These are disjoint categories of conference activities; neither subsumes the other.

Industrial Session (a conference session focused on industrial presentations) and Plenary lecture (a lecture delivered to all conference attendees) are distinct concepts with different scopes and structures. An industrial session is a session that may contain multiple talks, while a plenary lecture is a single lecture. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Both properties have domain Author and range Paper, and both express the relationship of an author producing/submitting a paper. In the conference domain, 'write Paper' and 'submit' are used synonymously to denote an author contributing a paper, and the matching domain and range strongly support equivalence.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Call' is a specific document-like entity (with children like Call For Papers, Call For Manuscripts, Call For Reviews, and properties like has Submission Deadline, has Submission Instructions) that announces the invitation to submit papers or reviews to an academic event. In the IASTED ontology, 'Activity' is a broad category encompassing things people do at or around a conference (with children like Activity before conference, Conference activity, and properties like is held in, is given by, is paid for). A Call is not itself an Activity; it is a document/announcement that may initiate or relate to activities. Their instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

PaperFullVersion in cmt is a full-length submission document (subclass of Paper under Document), while CADTopic in edas is a subject-area classification (subclass of Topic). They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the same concept of a conference paper. In Conference ontology, Paper is a Regular contribution (subclass of Conference contribution), while in confOf it is a subclass of Contribution. Both are sibling to Poster and represent full-length conference papers. The hierarchies converge on the same intended instances: regular conference papers as opposed to posters or short papers/extended abstracts.

These classes denote entirely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and the listed parents include Person/TPC Member likely due to ontology modeling peculiarities), representing a conference with two review levels. In EKAW, 'Late Registered Participant' is a subclass of Conference Participant, representing a person who registered late for a conference. One is a conference/event type, the other is a person/participant type. They share no instances and are unrelated.

confOf Working event groups collective events like Conference, Workshop, and Tutorial, contrasting with Social/Administrative events. ekaw Individual Presentation groups single-speaker talks (Contributed/Invited Talk, Tutorial) and is a sibling of Conference/Workshop. The two groupings are disjoint in scope: Working event is about the nature of the event (work vs social), while Individual Presentation is about the presentation format (single talk vs multi-event). Their children/siblings overlap only incidentally (Tutorial), so they are unrelated.

`reviewsPerPaper` is an integer count of reviews per paper associated with a Conference, while `paperDueOn` is a dateTime deadline for paper submission. They have different ranges (int vs dateTime) and denote completely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while property B is an object property linking Working event to an Administrative event. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain, range, and meaning; they share only the word 'has' in their labels.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs a conference, under Person > Chairman. Trip day (iasted) is a temporal concept under Time, representing a day during a trip. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
Rejection is a decision outcome for a paper submission, while Shuttle bus is a type of transport vehicle. These classes denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper Full Version is a specific subclass of Paper representing the complete/full version of a paper, distinct from the Paper Abstract. In the Conference ontology, Paper is the general class for regular paper contributions. Thus cmt's Paper Full Version is a more specific concept (a full version of a paper) than Conference's Paper, which denotes papers in general. The Conference ontology also distinguishes Extended abstract as a sibling of Paper, whereas cmt distinguishes Paper Full Version from Paper Abstract under Paper. This indicates Paper Full Version is subsumed by Paper.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference. Administrative event is a subclass of Event, denoting organizational events such as registration, reviewing, or submission events. One denotes a person role, the other denotes an event; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Coffee break is an activity/event during a conference, while Main office is a physical place. They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies (Activity vs Place) and share no domain overlap.

A Meta Review in cmt is a specific kind of review document written by a meta-reviewer, sitting under the Review class. A Review Form in edas is a structural template or schema used to collect reviews, not a review itself. These denote fundamentally different things—one is an authored document, the other is a form/template—so they are unrelated.

Conference document in the Conference ontology is a broad class of textual artefacts (call for papers, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc.) produced for or about a conference. Conference Session in edas is a temporal session/event slot within a conference program. One is a document/artefact, the other is an event; their intended instances do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. printHardcopyMailingManifests relates an Administrator to a Conference (printing hardcopy mailing manifests for a conference), while relatedToPaper relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. They connect entirely different entity types and serve unrelated purposes in the conference domain.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person who is a member of the conference). In the Conference ontology, was_a_committee_of links a Committee to a Conference volume (an event/instance of a conference). The domains (Conference vs Committee) and ranges (Conference Member vs Conference volume) are distinct, and the relations themselves denote different things: one assigns members to a conference, the other associates a committee with a conference volume. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote different relationships. In cmt, 'assignedByAdministrator' links a Reviewer to an Administrator who assigned them (administrator assigns reviewer to paper). In edas, 'isReviewHistoryOf' links a Personal Review History to the Reviewer it belongs to. The domain/range pairs are disjoint (Reviewer->Administrator vs PersonalReviewHistory->Reviewer) and the semantics are unrelated.

Entity A is a topic within the subject taxonomy (a research area like signal processing), while entity B is a type of scientific event (a contributed talk/presentation at a conference). They belong to completely different parts of the ontology hierarchy and denote entirely different kinds of things.

In ekaw, Conference Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion organized during a conference), subclass of Social Event. In iasted, Conference city is a city where a conference takes place, subclass of City. One denotes an event/activity, the other a geographic location. They share the word 'conference' but denote completely different categories of things.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person and has subclasses Administrator, Author, and Reviewer, denoting people who interact with the conference management system. In iasted, Research is a subclass of Activity before conference with subclasses Modelling and Simulating, denoting a research activity performed prior to the conference. These are completely different concepts: one is a person/role, the other is an activity. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf:Member_PC is a person who serves on the program committee (a reviewer), while sigkdd:Review is a document containing a review of a paper. One is an agent, the other is an artefact; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Contribution 1th author is a specific author role (first author of a conference contribution) in the Conference ontology, whereas Participant in confOf is a general class of people attending the conference (with subclasses Member, Regular, Student). They denote different concepts: one is an authorship role, the other is a participation category. There is no subsumption relationship between them.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different temporal notions. 'has a date of issue' applies to a Conference document (e.g., when a paper or proceedings item was issued) and ranges over date, whereas 'Start of conference' applies to a Conference and ranges over dateTime, marking when the conference begins. They relate different kinds of entities and are not the same relation.

Both classes are named 'Document' and serve as a common superclass for Paper and Review. In cmt, Document has children Paper and Review; in edas, Document has children including Paper and Review (plus Meal Menu, Programme, Slide Set). The edas ontology simply models a broader set of conference documents, but the core concept of a Document as a written artefact in the conference domain coincides. The additional subclasses in edas do not make the concepts disjoint; they indicate edas is more detailed. The shared core subclasses (Paper, Review) and the role of Document as a general written artefact support equivalence.
Meal Break is a temporal event (a break during a conference for meals), while Conference hall is a physical place. They share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In EKAW, 'organised By' connects an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it (Event -> Organisation/Person). In IASTED, 'give' connects a Person to an Activity or Item that the person gives (Person -> Activity/Item). They do not share the same domain, range, or direction, and 'give' is not the inverse of 'organised By' either, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Decision is an abstract outcome of paper review (with children Acceptance and Rejection, range of hasDecision from Paper). In iasted, Person is a human agent (with children Delegate and Sponsor) involved in many conference activities. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Person, but they denote different roles. cmt:User is a broad class covering anyone who uses the conference management system (including Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while sigkdd:Organizator is specifically an organizer of the conference (General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.). A regular Author or Reviewer in cmt is a User but not an Organizator, and conversely the two ontologies partition the Person hierarchy differently. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other since cmt:User includes non-organizers (authors, reviewers) while sigkdd:Organizator includes roles like Webmaster that may not be considered Users in cmt's system-usage sense. They are best considered unrelated.

Property A (has_an_abstract) links a paper/poster/presentation to its Abstract (the document part). Property B (writtenBy) links a Contribution to its Author (a person). They relate completely different kinds of objects (abstract vs. author) and express different relations (having an abstract vs. being authored by someone).

Both classes denote the same role in the conference domain: the person who chairs the conference. In cmt, Conference Chair is a specialization of Chairman (under Person), while in edas it is a direct subclass of Person. The cmt hierarchy is more fine-grained (Chairman is an intermediate role class), but the intended instances of Conference Chair coincide across both ontologies. The edas properties (initiates calls, reviews papers) are consistent with the conference chair role and do not contradict the cmt definition. The structural difference (extra intermediate parent in cmt) reflects modeling granularity, not a semantic mismatch.

The cmt 'assigned To' property assigns a Reviewer to a Paper (domain Paper, range Reviewer), denoting the reviewer-to-paper assignment relation. The Conference 'has a review expertise' property links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (domain Submitted contribution, range Review expertise), denoting the expertise area associated with a contribution. These are fundamentally different relations: one connects a paper to a person (reviewer), the other connects a paper to a topic/expertise category. They do not share the same range type or semantic meaning.

Talk Event is a subclass of Conference Event/Academic Event in edas, representing a scheduled academic activity (e.g., Welcome Talk, Closing Talk). Audiovisual equipment in iasted is a subclass of Item, representing physical equipment like computers and projecters. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Review and Abstract are distinct document types in the conference domain. In the sigkdd ontology, Abstract and Review are explicitly siblings under Document, meaning they are different kinds of documents. A Review is an evaluation of a paper, while an Abstract is a summary of the paper's content. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Property A relates a Topic to a Conference part (indicating which conference parts a topic belongs to), while property B relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (indicating parallel scheduling between events). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics with no overlap.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Organizational Meeting in edas is an event (subclass of Academic Event/Conference Event). One denotes a role held by a person, the other denotes a meeting/activity; they are completely different kinds of entities.

In ekaw, 'Tutorial Abstract' is a subclass of Document > Abstract, i.e., a written text summarizing a tutorial. In iasted, 'Plenary lecture' is a subclass of Activity > Conference activity > Lecture, i.e., an event/activity. One is a document artefact, the other is a scheduled activity; they denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

A's Paper is a general conference contribution (sibling of Extended abstract, parent Regular contribution), while B's Industrial Paper is a specific subtype of Paper in ekaw (sibling of Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). A's Paper is more general and is subsumed by B's broader Paper hierarchy, but they are not equivalent since Industrial Paper denotes only industrial papers, not all papers.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'is Written By' in edas relates a Paper to its Author, while 'is occupied by' in iasted relates a Building, City, or State to a Person. These are completely different domain/range pairs and different relations in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, representing when a conference starts. The labels 'start Date' and 'Start of conference' are synonymous in this context, and the edas comment confirms it denotes the conference start date and time.

confOf:Short_paper is a type of academic contribution (a short written paper submitted to a conference), sibling to Paper and Poster under Contribution. iasted:Bank_transfer is a type of payment document (a financial transaction record), sibling to Cheque under Payment document. These denote completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Meal Menu is a food menu for meal events (domain/range of has Menu/is Menu Of linking to Meal Event), while Review is a document evaluating a paper. They share only the generic parent Document but denote completely different things.

Entity A is a conference document type (an announcement publication), while entity B is a specific subject topic about computer networks management. They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Submitted Paper is a document type (a paper under review), while Program Committee is a committee organizing peer review. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:follows relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (e.g., one event following another in a sequence), while edas:forEvent relates a Call to an Academic Event (e.g., a call for papers is issued for a particular event). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; they do not denote the same relation.

A is a Topic (subject area) in the EDAS ontology, while B is an Invited Talk Abstract (a type of Document) in the EKAW ontology. They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Entity A is a conference document providing information for participants, while entity B is a specific topic about computer network applications. They belong to entirely different parts of the domain hierarchy and share no semantic relationship.

A 'Working event' in confOf is a kind of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while 'Computer Networks Enterprise Topic' in edas is a specific Topic within the Computer Networks domain. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Invited Talk is an event (a type of Individual Presentation), while Speaker is a person who gives a presentation. These are disjoint categories in the conference domain: one denotes the talk itself, the other denotes the person delivering it.

In cmt, Decision is an outcome of reviewing a paper (with children Acceptance and Rejection). In sigkdd, Document is a physical/informational artefact (with children Abstract, Paper, Review). One denotes a verdict, the other a document; they share no instances.
Workshop in ekaw is a scientific event (a meeting/conference activity), while Conference_hall in sigkdd is a physical place. They denote completely different categories of entities.

hasFirstName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's given name), while authorOf is an object property from Person to Document (relating a person to a paper they wrote). They have completely different ranges and meanings.

Property A (has_a_review) links a Reviewed contribution to a Review, capturing the peer-review process. Property B (award) links something to an Award, capturing the best-paper award. These are distinct relations in the conference domain: one concerns reviewing, the other concerns awarding. They share no common domain/range overlap and are not synonyms.

A Conference restaurant is a dining venue associated with a conference, whereas a Conference hall is a meeting/lecture venue. They are distinct types of places with different functions, and neither subsumes the other.

Both properties relate a reviewer to a paper they are reviewing. In cmt, readPaper has domain Reviewer and range Paper, representing the act of a reviewer reading/reviewing a paper. In edas, isReviewing has domain including Reviewer (among other committee roles) and range Paper, representing the same relationship of a reviewer reviewing a paper. The core semantics coincide: a reviewer reading/reviewing a paper. The broader domain in edas (also including Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) is a generalization, but the central intended relation is the same.

The two properties operate on different domains and express different relations. In cmt, 'adjusted By' links a Bid to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer adjusted a bid). In the Conference ontology, 'invited by' links a Reviewer to a Reviewer (indicating who invited a reviewer to join the program committee or review process). These are distinct relations with different domain types and different semantics.

confOf's Topic is a general class for conference topics, used as the range of properties like dealsWith, expertOn, and hasTopic. edas's MicroelectronicsTopic is a specific subclass of Topic (a child of the general Topic class in edas, alongside AntennasTopic, CADTopic, etc.). Therefore, MicroelectronicsTopic is a specific kind of Topic, making it subsumed_by the general confOf Topic class.

Property A (`has a name`) is a datatype property with domain Conference/Conference part/Conference proceedings/Publisher/Topic and range string, denoting the name of various conference-related entities. Property B (`covers Topic`) is an object property with domain Event/Paper and range Research Topic, denoting which research topics a paper or event covers. They have completely different domains, ranges (string vs Research Topic), and semantics (naming vs topic coverage), so they are unrelated.

The confOf 'follows' property relates two Administrative events (e.g., one event following another in a schedule), while the edas 'has Attendee' property relates a Conference Event to a Person who attends it. They connect completely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a specific subclass of Abstract (it is the abstract of an invited talk, sibling to Tutorial Abstract). In sigkdd, 'Abstract' is the general Abstract class (child of Document, sibling to Paper and Review). The sigkdd Abstract is more general, so ekaw's Invited Talk Abstract is subsumed by sigkdd's Abstract.

confOf:Workshop is a multi-presenter working event (a mini-conference with multiple papers/sessions), while ekaw:Tutorial is an individual presentation by a single presenter. They are different kinds of conference events, so they are not equivalent.

Simulating is a research activity (e.g., running simulations), while Organizing Committee member is a person who serves on the organizing committee. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a short version of a paper) in cmt, while Computer Networks Optical Topic is a subject-area classification in edas. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Paper Abstract is a document (subclass of Paper in cmt), whereas Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline (subclass of Deadline in sigkdd). One denotes a textual artefact, the other a date; their instances cannot coincide.

`accept Paper` in cmt relates an Administrator to a Paper, representing the action of accepting a paper. `parallel with` in confOf relates two Administrative events, indicating they occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.
Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement/publication), while Main office is a physical place. They share no instances and belong to completely different domains.
Slide Set denotes a set of presentation slides, while Review denotes a review of a paper. These are distinct document types in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have opposite domain/range directions and different semantics. In Conference, 'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (person contributes a document). In edas, 'relatesTo' links a Document to various entities (events, conferences, sessions, persons), expressing a generic association from the document to related entities. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In EKAW, Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), whereas in IASTED, Conference days is a temporal concept (subclass of Time) that groups delegates and individual conference days. They denote completely different categories of things (an event vs. a time period), so they are unrelated.

The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (paper they authored), while the edas 'isReviewHistoryOf' property links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer. These are fundamentally different relations: one concerns authorship of papers, the other concerns the association between a review history record and a reviewer. The domains and ranges are completely different, and they serve unrelated purposes in the conference domain.

An Attendee is a person who attends a conference session, whereas an Agency Staff Member is a person employed by an agency (e.g., a conference organizing agency). These are disjoint intended extensions: an attendee participates in the event, while agency staff provide organizational services. They share only the common parent Person.

A Passive conference participant is someone who attends but does not actively organize (sibling of Active conference participant under Conference participant), whereas a Program Committee member is an organizer who reviews papers. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Program Committee Member is a broad class covering all PC members (with Program Committee Chair as a subclass). In sigkdd, Program Chair is a specific organizer role, distinct from the more general Program Committee member class. The cmt class subsumes the sigkdd Program Chair role, since a chair is a specialized PC member, but they are not equivalent.

Workshop in edas is a type of academic conference event (a meeting/session where papers are presented), whereas Modelling in iasted is a research activity performed before a conference. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

Reviewer (Conference ontology) denotes a person who reviews papers, with properties like review expertise, review preference, and inviting co-reviewers. Conference Participant (EKAW) denotes any person attending the conference, with children including Demo Chair, PC Chair, Presenter, etc. A reviewer is not necessarily a conference participant (e.g., external reviewers may not attend), and a conference participant is not necessarily a reviewer. The two concepts have distinct intended instances with no clear overlap in this context.

Entity A is a class denoting a document (a camera-ready paper/contribution), while entity B is a class denoting a temporal deadline for submitting such a manuscript. They are completely different kinds of entities (document vs. time point), so they are unrelated.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events (e.g., sessions running in parallel), while the ekaw 'volumeContainsPaper' property relates a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. They connect completely different kinds of entities and serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain.

The cmt 'name' property captures the name of a Conference or Person, while the confOf 'hasPostalCode' property captures the postal code of an Organization or Person. These are completely different attributes with no overlap in meaning.

These classes denote completely different things. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document providing logistical information to attendees, sibling to Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc. 'Review' in edas is a review of a paper, sibling to Paper, Programme, Slide Set. Despite both being subclasses of a Document-like parent, their intended instances do not coincide at all.

Property A (has_workshops) relates a Conference volume to its constituent Workshops (a part-whole relation). Property B (speak_in) relates a Person to a Place or Time where they speak. They have different domains, different ranges, and express entirely different relationships.

A Conference applicant is someone who applies to attend a conference (a prospective registrant), whereas an Attendee is someone who actually attends the conference. These are distinct concepts: an applicant may or may not become an attendee, and an attendee may have applied or been invited. They share the parent Person but denote different roles in the conference lifecycle, so they are not equivalent, nor is one clearly more general than the other in a way that a reference alignment would record.

confOf:Person denotes a human being involved in the conference (with children such as Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), while iasted:Place denotes a physical location (with children such as Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). They share no instances and are unrelated concepts despite both appearing as domain/range in various properties.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing a person's email address. The labels 'has Email' and 'E mail' are synonymous in the conference domain, and the structural context (Person -> email -> string) is identical.

A 'Late paid applicant' is a person who registered late and paid, while 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity before the conference. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Person vs Activity) and denote unrelated concepts.

A 'Welcome Talk' is a formal opening address at a conference, whereas 'Introduction of speaker' is the act of introducing a specific speaker before their presentation. These are distinct conference activities with different purposes and scopes.

Registration in iasted is a conference activity (e.g., attendee registration for the conference), a subclass of Activity > Conference activity, with Delegate as a child. Committee in sigkdd is an organizational body (e.g., Program Committee, Organizing Committee, Best Paper Awards Committee). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, a Chairman under Person) in cmt, while B is an administrative event (Registration of participants event) in confOf. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Both classes are subclasses of Person and represent people who participate in a conference. The labels are near-identical (differing only by a space), and both sit under the same parent (Person). The children differ—A distinguishes active vs. passive participants, B distinguishes by role/registration timing—but these are just different subcategorizations of the same overarching concept. The intended extension (all people participating in a conference) coincides.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'locationOf' maps a Location to an Event (i.e., where an event takes place). In iasted, 'go_through' maps an Item to an Activity (i.e., an item undergoes or passes through some activity such as review or selection). The domains (Location vs. Item) and ranges (Event vs. Activity) are distinct, and the intended meanings are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a written work to its author. confOf's 'written By' has domain Contribution and range Author, while edas's 'is Written By' has domain Paper and range Author. In the conference domain, Contribution and Paper are typically equivalent or closely overlapping, and both properties express the same relation (work -> author) in the same direction. The labels are synonymous, and the domain/range structure matches.

Property A (has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution) has domain Review preference and range Submitted contribution / Topic, expressing what a review preference is about. Property B (write) has domain Person and range Item, expressing authorship of a written item. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and share no common semantics.

Short paper in confOf is a type of Contribution (a short written paper submission), whereas Poster Paper in ekaw is a type of Paper (a document) representing a poster. They denote different artefacts in the conference domain: a short paper is a written contribution, while a poster paper is a poster presentation/document. The labels and sibling contexts indicate distinct concepts, so they are not equivalent.
