Attendee in edas denotes any person who attends a conference, while Demo Chair in ekaw is a specific conference participant role responsible for demonstration sessions. An attendee is not necessarily a demo chair, and a demo chair is a specialized role rather than a general attendee concept. These classes do not share equivalent instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In Conference, 'Review preference' denotes a reviewer's preference for reviewing a particular topic or submission (it has properties like degree, review reference, topic/submission contribution, and reviewer). In sigkdd, 'Review' is a subclass of Document, i.e., the actual review document written about a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a preference/assignment entity, the other is a review artefact. They share the word 'review' but do not denote the same thing.

Property A captures a person's first name, while property B captures a person's nation (country). Despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes of a person.

Property A ('has the last name') has domain Person and relates a person to their surname/family name. Property B ('has Street') has domain Contact Information and relates contact info to a street address. They connect different domains to different kinds of data (personal name vs. postal address), so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only trivially related as both being string-valued datatype properties.

In EDAS, AcceptedPaper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been accepted), while in EKAW, Paper is the general class for all papers (including submitted, accepted, camera-ready, etc.). Thus EDAS AcceptedPaper is subsumed by EKAW Paper.

Country in confOf denotes a geographical entity (domain of Organization and Person locations), while Money in iasted denotes a financial amount with children like Fee, Tax, Tip. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Entity A is a class denoting a person (a late-paid conference applicant) under the Person hierarchy, while Entity B is a class denoting a monetary fee (member registration fee) under the Money hierarchy. They are completely different kinds of things—a person vs. a fee—and share no conceptual overlap.

Written contribution is a scholarly work (paper, article, etc.) submitted or presented at a conference, while Payment document is a financial instrument (bank transfer, cheque) used to pay registration fees. They share no instances and belong to completely different domains of the conference organization.

Reviewed contribution is a document (a paper that has been reviewed), while Possible Reviewer is a person who could review a paper. They are disjoint categories (document vs person) in the conference domain.

Although both are subclasses of Document, they denote different artefacts: Flyer is a promotional document (with publisherOf from Organisation), while Abstract is a summary of a paper. They are disjoint document types, not equivalent.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization representing corporate entities (e.g., companies involved in conference organization). edas:PersonalPublicationHistory is a subclass of PersonalHistory representing a person's publication record. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These two properties are inverses, not equivalents. In cmt, co-writePaper has domain Co-author and range Paper, meaning it points from the author to the paper. In confOf, writtenBy has domain Contribution and range Author, pointing from the paper to the author. A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent; they relate the same entities but in opposite directions.

Conference announcement is a document type (child of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while Excursion is a social event type (child of Social Event under Non Academic Event). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

These properties differ in both domain and range. 'was a program committee of' links a Program committee to a Conference volume, while 'organised By' links an Event to an Organisation or Person. The relations are also conceptually distinct: one denotes PC membership/oversight of a conference volume, the other denotes general organisation of an event by an agent. The domains (Program committee vs Event) and ranges (Conference volume vs Organisation/Person) do not align, so these are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. `lists Event` connects a Programme Brochure/Web Site to the Events it lists, whereas `presentationed by` connects a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Programme Brochure/Web Site vs Document) and ranges (Event vs Speaker) do not coincide, so the properties are unrelated.

Programme Brochure is a specific conference document listing events, while Abstract is a summary of a paper. They share the parent Document but denote clearly different artefacts in the conference domain.

Session Chair in edas is a person role (subclass of Person, sibling of Attendee, Author, Reviewer, etc.), while Session room in iasted is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). They denote completely different concepts: a person who chairs a session vs. a room where sessions are held.

NumericalReviewQuestion in edas is a type of review question used in the reviewing process (sibling of TextualReviewQuestion), while Final_manuscript in iasted is a document submitted as the final version of a paper. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'addProgramCommitteeMember' connects an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (the act of adding a PC member). In sigkdd, 'hold' connects ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (the act of holding/organizing a conference). The domains (Administrator vs. ACM SIGKDD) and ranges (Program Committee Member vs. Conference) are disjoint concepts, so these properties cannot be equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

Review in Conference is a document containing a review of a contribution, while Slide Set in edas is a set of presentation slides. They are sibling document types with different purposes and no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'co-writePaper' in cmt relates a Co-author to a Paper, representing the act of co-authoring (writing) a paper. The property 'submit' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper, representing the act of submitting a paper. Co-authoring and submitting are distinct relations in the conference domain: a co-author writes the paper while submission is the act of sending it to the conference system. They have different domains (Co-author vs Author) and different meanings, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only loosely related at best.

The cmt property addProgramCommitteeMember is an administrative action where an Administrator adds a Program Committee Member. The confOf property reviewes is a reviewing relation where a Member PC reviews a Contribution. They have different domains (Administrator vs Member PC), different ranges (Program Committee Member vs Contribution), and denote entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a broad class covering any paper (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version) and is the subject of reviewing, bidding, and decisions. In Conference, Camera ready contribution is the most specific stage in a chain (Submitted -> Reviewed -> Accepted -> Camera ready), i.e. the final, accepted, publication-ready version. Thus cmt:Paper is more general and is subsumed by Conference:Camera_ready_contribution (equivalently, Camera ready contribution is a narrower concept).

Property A (has_important_dates) relates a conference volume to its important dates (e.g., submission deadlines), while property B (hold) relates an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a conference it holds. These are fundamentally different relations: one connects a conference to its temporal milestones, the other connects an organizing body to the event it organizes. Their domains and ranges differ accordingly.

Both classes denote a student in the conference domain. In confOf, Student is a subclass of Participant (which is a subclass of Person), while in ekaw it is a direct subclass of Person. The difference in hierarchy depth does not change the intended instances: both refer to persons who are students. The ekaw hierarchy places various person roles directly under Person, whereas confOf introduces an intermediate Participant class, but this structural difference does not imply a different meaning for Student itself.

Administrator in cmt is a person (User subclass) who manages conference tasks such as accepting papers, assigning reviewers, and entering conference details. Mailing list in iasted is a Document subclass (an artefact/item), sibling to Review, Submission, Invitation letter, etc. These denote completely different categories of entities—a human role versus a document type—with no overlap in intended instances.

Industrial Paper (ekaw) is a specific kind of paper written by or for industry practitioners, sitting under Paper. Abstract (sigkdd) is a summary document, a sibling of Paper and Review under Document. They denote completely different concepts: one is a type of paper, the other is a document type (summary). No subsumption holds between them.

These properties relate completely different entities in different directions. 'is Reviewing' connects reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to Papers they review, while 'presentationed by' connects Documents to the Speaker who presents them. Reviewing a paper and presenting a document are distinct activities with different participants and artifacts.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception during a conference), while iasted:Payment document is a financial document (bank transfer, cheque) under Item > Document. They denote completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'accept Paper' property relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of accepting a paper), while the sigkdd 'presentationed by' property relates a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presents a document). These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and represent different relationships in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a person affiliated with a conference (parent Person, with sub-roles like Author, Reviewer, Chair). Sponzor in sigkdd is an external entity that provides financial or material support (with tiers like Gold/Silver/Bronze Supporter, Exhibitor). These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (has_the_first_name) relates a Person to their first name, while property B (starts_on) relates an Event to its start date. They have different domains (Person vs Event) and denote completely different relations in the conference domain.

Both classes denote the same role in the conference domain: the chair of the Programme Committee. 'Chair PC' and 'PC Chair' are simply word-order variants of the same label. Both are subclasses of Person (with ekaw adding an intermediate Conference Participant parent) and both have a sibling 'PC Member' / 'Member PC', confirming they refer to the same organizational role.

hasPhone is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's phone number), while is_used_by is an object property from Item to Person (indicating which person uses an item). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

These properties are fundamentally different in type, domain, and range. Property A is an object property with domain Review preference and range Submitted contribution/Topic, relating review preferences to contributions or topics. Property B is a datatype property with domain Call and range string, capturing submission instructions text for a call for papers. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers, distinct from reviewers and committee members. In edas, TPC Member is a committee member who reviews papers and initiates calls, explicitly listed as a sibling of Author. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: an author writes papers, while a TPC member serves on the program committee and reviews papers. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

These properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. 'is Reviewed By' relates Papers to reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), indicating who reviewed a paper. 'is paid by' relates Money to Person, indicating who paid money. They share no semantic overlap despite both being object properties with a similar syntactic pattern ('is X by').

Personal Review History is a record/history artifact associated with a reviewer's reviewing activity, while Reviewer is a person role (a delegate who reviews papers). One is a document-like history object, the other is a person. They share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In EDAS, Conference is a top-level organizational entity with properties like hasCountry, hasName, paperDueOn, etc., representing the conference as a whole. In EKAW, Individual_Presentation is a specific type of scientific event (a talk/presentation), a child of Scientific_Event with siblings like Conference, Session, Track, and Workshop. These denote completely different things: one is the conference itself, the other is an individual presentation within a conference.

logoURL points to a logo image (anyURI) for a conference, while startDate records when the conference begins (dateTime). They share the same domain (Conference) but denote completely different attributes with no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Bid is a specific concept denoting a reviewer's bid on a paper, with properties like 'has Bid' (Paper -> Bid) and 'adjusted By' (Bid -> Reviewer). In iasted, Person is a general class for people (with children Delegate, Sponsor) involved in activities, items, and places. These are completely different concepts: a Bid is an action/artifact in the reviewing process, while Person is a human actor. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document they have a conflict with, while employedBy relates a Person to an Organization that employs them. These are entirely different relations with different ranges (Document vs Organization) and different semantics.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. `hasUpdatedVersion` in EKAW links a Document to another Document (an updated version of it), whereas `presentation` in SIGKDD links a Speaker to a Document (the document/slides they present). They relate different kinds of entities and express different semantics, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

confOf's 'Submission event' is an event (subclass of Administrative event > Event) representing the act or period of submitting contributions. iasted's 'Submissions deadline' is a temporal entity (subclass of Deadline > Time) representing the cut-off date for submissions. One is an event/activity, the other is a point in time; they denote different categories of things and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

confOf:Contribution represents a submitted conference artefact (paper, poster, short paper) with properties like abstract, keyword, title, and author/reviewer relationships. edas:PersonalHistory represents a person's historical record (publication history, review history) — a biographical/organisational concept, not a conference submission. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

SC Member in ekaw is a person role (a committee member under PC Member, alongside chairs). Registration Student in sigkdd is a fee category (a type of registration fee, alongside other fee types). One is a person, the other is a monetary fee; they share no domain overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. confOf:expertOn connects a Member PC to a Topic (indicating which subject areas a PC member is expert in), while edas:hasMember connects a Conference to a Person (indicating who is a member/participant of the conference). They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning.

Property 'issues' in Conference ontology relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher publishes/issues proceedings). Property 'hold' in sigkdd ontology relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (an organization holds/hosting a conference event). These are different relations: one is about publishing proceedings, the other about organizing/hosting a conference. The domains and ranges are different types of entities, and the semantics of the properties do not coincide.

confOf:Conference is an academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas iasted:Presenter_university is a physical place/building where a presenter is affiliated. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Topic in edas denotes a subject area (e.g., Antennas, CAD, Cryptography) associated with conferences and papers. Person in sigkdd denotes a human participant (Listener, Organizer, Speaker) with attributes like email, name, and nation. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Invited speaker is a person (subclass of Conference contributor), while Tutorial is an event (subclass of Individual Presentation). One denotes a person who gives a talk, the other denotes the type of event/session itself. They are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. confOf's writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while edas's hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; there is no overlap or subsumption between them.

Property A links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the committee organizes the conference). Property B links a Building, City, or State to a Person (a person occupies a location). They relate completely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

The two properties describe opposite relationships. In edas, 'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to the people who review it (domain Paper -> range Reviewer/Chair/TPC Member). In iasted, 'write' links a Person to an Item they author (domain Person -> range Item). They connect different entities and run in opposite directions; one denotes authorship, the other the reviewing relation, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.
A is a person who writes a paper; B is a monetary fee charged to non-members for conference registration. They share no domain overlap.

Social Event in edas denotes gatherings like excursions and receptions, whereas Registration in iasted denotes the activity of registering for a conference. These are entirely different concepts despite both being non-academic conference activities.

confOf:Participant is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person, with children Member, Regular, Student). iasted:Nonmember_registration_fee is a monetary fee charged to non-members for registration (subclass of Registration fee > Fee > Money). One is a person, the other is a fee — completely disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Activity in iasted is a broad class covering conference activities (before, during, after conference) with properties about being held in places, dated, given by persons, etc. Deadline in sigkdd is a specific temporal milestone for submissions and notifications, with children like Abstract Submission, Author Notification, Paper Submission deadlines. A deadline is not an activity but a point in time; these denote fundamentally different concepts.

The cmt 'assigned To' property links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment to reviewers for review), while the iasted 'pay' property links a Person to Money (a person paying money). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

These properties relate completely different kinds of things. In cmt, 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered conference details). In edas, 'isTopicOf' links a Topic to a Conference or Paper (indicating the topic of that conference or paper). The domains (Conference vs. Topic), ranges (Administrator vs. Conference/Paper), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Conference is an event/organization with properties like dates, country, members, topics, and paper deadlines. In iasted, Conference_hall is a physical place (child of Place, sibling of Building, Hotel_room, etc.). These are completely different concepts: one is a conference event, the other is a physical venue/room.

These properties go in opposite directions and have incompatible domains/ranges. In Conference, 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to Publisher (proceedings -> publisher). In ekaw, 'publisher Of' links Organisation to published items like Flyer, Multi author volume, Programme brochure, Web site (publisher -> published item). They are inverses of each other in spirit, not equivalent. Moreover, the ranges differ significantly: ekaw's range includes flyers, brochures, and web sites, not just proceedings, so even the inverse relationship is not exact. A reference alignment would not mark them as equivalent.

A Conference Session in EDAS is a scheduled session/block within a conference program (a grouping of multiple talks or presentations). An Individual Presentation in EKAW is a single presentation by an individual (e.g., a contributed talk, invited talk, or tutorial). These are different concepts: one is a session container, the other is an individual talk. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

Property A (reviews) links a Review to the Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed), i.e. Review -> Paper. Property B (reviewWrittenBy) links a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it, i.e. Review -> Reviewer. They relate the same domain class (Review) to completely different ranges (paper vs. reviewer), so they are not equivalent; they are also not in a subsumption relation. They are simply different relations (one points to the reviewed artifact, the other to the author of the review).

A 'Presenter house' in iasted is a building where a presenter resides or is housed (sibling of Conference hotel, Presenter university, Sponsor company house), while a 'Conference hall' in sigkdd is a venue/place where conference events are held (sibling of Hotel, Main office). One is lodging for a presenter, the other is a meeting/event venue; their intended instances do not coincide.

Paper Full Version is a document (a full paper submitted to a conference), while Registration SIGKDD Member is a registration fee paid by a SIGKDD member. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person). In edas, Government Organization is a type of organization (e.g., a government body). One denotes a human role, the other an organizational entity; they share no common superclass and have completely different intended instances.

confOf's 'Chair PC' is a PC chair (sibling of Member PC, Administrator, etc.), while ekaw's 'Workshop Chair' is specifically a workshop chair (sibling of Demo Chair, Tutorial Chair, Session Chair). A PC chair and a workshop chair are distinct conference roles; neither subsumes the other in the given hierarchies.

Both are object properties with domain Person relating a person to a document/item they authored. 'authorOf' (Person -> Document) and 'write' (Person -> Item) express the same authorship relation in the conference domain, with Document/Item being the written artefact. They are not inverses (both go Person -> Document).

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and have different domains and ranges. `contributes` links a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution relation), while `organised By` links an Event to an Organisation or Person (event-organisation relation). They share no common semantics.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In cmt, 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person representing people who are members of a conference (with subclasses like Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair). In iasted, 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time representing temporal periods of a conference (with children like Delegate, One conference day). One is a person role, the other is a time period. They share no semantic overlap despite both containing the word 'Conference'.

The property `added By` in cmt relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator who added them (an administrative/meta relationship about committee management). The property `reviewes` in confOf relates a Member PC to a Contribution they review (the actual reviewing action on a paper). These are entirely different relations: one is about who added a PC member, the other is about which paper a PC member reviews. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Meeting Room Place in EDAS denotes a place where meetings are held (a room for sessions or gatherings), whereas Hotel room in IASTED denotes lodging/accommodation rooms in a hotel (with children Single/Double hotel room). They share the parent Place but represent different kinds of locations: one is for meetings, the other is for sleeping accommodation. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Conference denotes the conference event itself (an organizational/academic event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop under Working event). iasted:Conference_days denotes a time period (under Time, sibling of Deadline and Trip day) during which the conference takes place, with children like Delegate and One conference day. One is an event, the other is a temporal interval; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

confOf:Workshop is a type of working event (a mini-conference with sessions, papers, etc.), while ekaw:Contributed_Talk is an individual presentation (a single talk by a presenter). They are at different granularity levels and denote different kinds of events: a workshop is a multi-session event, whereas a contributed talk is a single presentation within a session.

ekaw:Possible_Reviewer is a subclass of Person restricted to those who can review papers (it has child PC Member and is the domain/range of review-related properties). iasted:Person is the top-level person class with children Delegate and Sponsor and is involved in many general conference-organisation properties. Possible Reviewer is thus a narrower concept subsumed by iasted:Person, not equivalent.

Non Academic Event in edas denotes social/non-academic conference activities (breaks, meals, social events), while Conference in ekaw denotes one edition of a scientific conference. They are at different levels of granularity and serve entirely different purposes in the conference organization domain.

In ekaw, PC Member is a specific role (member of the Program Committee, a possible reviewer), whereas in sigkdd, Organizator is a broader concept covering all organizing roles including General Chair, Webmaster, and Organizing Committee members. PC Member is thus a kind of Organizator, but Organizator includes roles beyond the Program Committee. The sigkdd hierarchy (with Program Committee member as a child of Organizator) confirms that PC Member is subsumed by Organizator.

Rejected_Paper in ekaw is a specific evaluated paper that was not accepted for publication, sitting deep in a submission/evaluation hierarchy. Abstract in sigkdd is a document type sibling to Paper and Review, representing a summary or preliminary text. These denote entirely different concepts: one is a publication decision outcome, the other is a document category. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two properties have different domains and ranges. `hasLocation` in edas relates a Conference Event to a Place (where the event is held), while `is_present_in` in iasted relates a Person to a Place or Time (where/when a person is present). They describe different relationships between different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

In EDAS, 'Call For Manuscripts' is a kind of Call (an announcement soliciting submissions), whereas in SIGKDD, 'Abstract' is a kind of Document (a written summary of a paper). These denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A Conference airport is a transportation hub (airport) associated with a conference, while B Conference hall is a venue space where conference sessions take place. Despite the shared word 'Conference', these denote entirely different kinds of places with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (invites_co-reviewers) relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (a reviewer inviting a co-reviewer to help review a paper). Property B (presentationed_by) relates a Document to a Speaker (a document being presented by a speaker). The domains (Reviewer vs. Document), ranges (Reviewer vs. Speaker), and overall semantics (inviting co-reviewers vs. being presented by a speaker) are entirely different. These properties denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. confOf's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (e.g., registration, reception), while iasted's obtain links a Person to an Item they receive. The domains (Working event vs. Person) and ranges (Administrative event vs. Item) are disjoint, and the relations themselves denote different things: associating an administrative sub-event with a working event vs. a person obtaining a physical item.

These properties denote completely different relations. In cmt, 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to the Administrator who initiated the reviewer bidding process. In ekaw, 'reviewerOfPaper' links a Possible Reviewer to the Paper they are reviewing. The domains (Conference vs. Possible Reviewer), ranges (Administrator vs. Paper), and semantics (administrative action vs. reviewing assignment) are entirely different.

A Reviewer is a person who reviews papers in a conference, with properties like assigning reviewers, adjusting bids, and reading papers. A Paid applicant is a person who has paid registration fees for attending a conference. These are completely different roles: one evaluates submissions, the other registers to attend. They share no functional overlap in the conference domain.

Submitted Paper is a document type (a paper submitted for review), while Best Paper Awards Committee is a committee that selects best papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology hierarchy (Document vs. Committee) and denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Cryptography Topic is a subject area within the Topic hierarchy of edas, while Best Research Paper Award is a specific award type in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different parts of the conference domain (research topics vs. awards) and share no instances.

In the edas ontology, Person is a broad superclass covering all people involved in the conference (attendees, authors, chairs, reviewers, etc.). In sigkdd, Speaker is a subclass of Person that specifically denotes people who give presentations. Every Speaker is a Person, but not every Person is a Speaker (e.g., attendees, reviewers, committee members may not present). Thus Person subsumes Speaker.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document intended for attendees, while 'Medicine Topic' in the edas ontology is a subject topic used to classify papers. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Both properties link a conference entity to a subject/topic classification, but they differ in domain: cmt:hasSubjectArea applies to Paper while confOf:hasTopic applies to Working_event. The ranges (Subject Area vs Topic) are conceptually similar but the different domains mean they do not relate the same kinds of things in the same way. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and in the relationship they express. In cmt, hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (Program Committee -> Program Committee Member). In Conference, was_a_committee_chair_of relates a Chair to a Committee (Chair -> Committee). The domains and ranges are disjoint, and the direction of the relationship is different: one assigns members to a committee, the other assigns a chair to a committee. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

Personal Publication History is a history/record class (sibling of Personal Review History under Personal History), not a document itself. ekaw Paper is a concrete document with children like Camera Ready Paper, Submitted Paper, etc. These denote completely different concepts: a publication history record vs. an actual paper document.

PC Chair is the chair of the Programme Committee, responsible for the scientific programme and paper acceptance decisions. Webmaster is a technical role responsible for the conference website. These are distinct roles in conference organisation with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties are completely different in meaning and structure. 'is_a_full_paper_submission_date' is a datatype property mapping an Important dates individual to a date value, representing when a full paper is due. 'paperPresentedAs' is an object property mapping a Paper to an Individual Presentation, representing how a paper is presented at the conference. They have different domains, ranges, and types, and share no semantic relationship.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In iasted, 'is used for' connects an Item to an Activity or Money (e.g., an item used for some activity or monetary purpose). In sigkdd, 'obtain' connects an Author to an Award (an author obtaining an award). The domains (Item vs Author), ranges (Activity/Money vs Award), and intended meanings are disjoint, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

TPC Member in edas denotes a member of the Programme Committee (a reviewer/decision-maker for paper selection), while Conference Participant in ekaw denotes anyone who participates in/attends the conference. A TPC member is a kind of conference participant, but the two classes do not denote the same concept: TPC Member is a specific role, Conference Participant is a broad category. They are not equivalent. However, they are also not in a clean subsumption relationship within these ontologies (edas has no generic 'participant' class, and ekaw's Conference Participant does not subsume the specific role of TPC member as modeled). The most accurate relation for a reference alignment is 'unrelated' (no direct equivalence or subsumption), though one could argue 'related' due to domain overlap.

These properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. In cmt, readPaper has domain Reviewer and range Paper (Reviewer reads Paper). In edas, isReviewedBy has domain Paper and range Reviewer/Chair roles (Paper is reviewed by Reviewer). The domain and range are swapped, making them inverse relations. A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent.

In ekaw, Paper Author is a direct subclass of Person, denoting any person who authors a paper. In sigkdd, Author is more specific: it is a subclass of Speaker (which is a subclass of Person), and has subclasses such as 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student'. The sigkdd Author class is a more specialized role (tied to presenting/speaking and specific author categories), so ekaw's Paper Author is more general and is subsumed by sigkdd's Author in terms of role specificity.

confOf:Student is a person who is a participant in a conference (path Person > Participant > Student), denoting a student attendee. sigkdd:Silver_Supporter is a type of sponsor (path Sponzor > Silver Supporter), denoting an organization or entity providing silver-level sponsorship. These are completely different concepts: one is a human participant role, the other is a sponsorship tier. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

cmt:User is a broad superclass covering Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—any person who interacts with the CMT system. ekaw:SC_Member is a specific kind of PC Member (a member of the Steering Committee, alongside PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.). The two classes are at very different levels of generality and do not share the same intended instances: a typical Author or Administrator would not be an SC Member, and an SC Member is not necessarily a CMT User. They are therefore unrelated rather than equivalent or in a subsumption relation.

In EKAW, Conference Participant is a broad class covering any person who participates in a conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, committee members, etc.). In IASTED, Lecturer is a very specific role: a subclass of Author, which is itself a subclass of Speaker, under Delegate. A Lecturer in IASTED is a specific kind of speaker/author who delivers a lecture, not a general conference participant. The two classes are at very different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept; nor is one clearly a sub/superclass of the other across these independently modeled ontologies.

A CAD Topic is a subject-area classification (a Topic) in the EDAS ontology, while Program Committee is an organizational committee in the SIGKDD ontology. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Coctail reception is a social event/activity in the iasted ontology, while Organizator is a person role in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to completely different conceptual categories (activity vs person) and share no instances.

Contribution in confOf denotes a submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper) authored by someone and reviewed by a PC member. Review in ekaw denotes a review document written by a reviewer about a paper. These are disjoint concepts in the conference domain: one is the artefact being reviewed, the other is the review itself.

Workshop Paper is a document (academic paper) in the ekaw ontology, while Car is a transport vehicle in the iasted ontology. These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the chair of the entire conference, the top organizer role, sitting under Chairman. SC Member (ekaw) is a member of the Scientific Committee, a sub-role of PC Member under Possible Reviewer. These are distinct organizational roles: one is a conference-level leadership position, the other is a committee member role focused on scientific/program review. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Short paper is a type of academic contribution (a document submitted to a conference), while Sponzor fee is a financial charge paid by a sponsor. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:User is a person who interacts with the conference management system (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while ekaw:University is an academic institution (parent Organisation > Academic Institution). They denote completely different categories of entities.

Trip day is a temporal division of a conference trip (a day during which trips or conference activities occur), whereas Deadline Abstract Submission is a specific submission deadline for abstracts. They share only the distant ancestor Time/Deadline and denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Rejection is a subclass of Decision, representing the outcome of a paper review process (paper rejected). In confOf, Reception is a subclass of Social event, representing a social gathering at a conference. These are completely different concepts despite superficial label similarity.

Both classes denote a paper submitted to a conference. In iasted, 'Initial manuscript' is a subclass of Submission (itself under Document), representing the initial version of a paper submitted for review. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a subclass of Document and is the object of the 'submit' property (Author -> Paper), also representing a submitted paper. The siblings and properties confirm both are concrete document types representing submitted papers. The term 'Initial manuscript' specifies the stage (initial submission) but the intended instances coincide with sigkdd's 'Paper' as the submitted document. They are equivalent in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'has short title' assigns a string title to social and working events, while 'done till' assigns a date deadline to a Deadline entity. They do not denote the same relation.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things: `has Topic` links a Working event to a Topic (subject classification), while `obtain` links an Author to an Award (prize received). Different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; no overlap in intended meaning.

confOf:Workshop is a type of event (subclass of Working event), while ekaw:Invited_Speaker is a type of person (subclass of Presenter under Conference Participant). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain—an event versus a person—so they are unrelated.

Country denotes a nation/geographic entity, while Currency denotes a monetary system (e.g., Euro, Dollar). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain despite both appearing as range classes for location-related properties.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Best Research Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Money in iasted is a class representing monetary amounts (fees, taxes, tips, sponsorships) paid by persons for activities/items. ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd is an organization that holds conferences, designs deadlines, and searches for sponsors. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Single Level Conference is a type of academic conference (a subclass of Conference), while Presenter state is a subclass of State representing the status of a presenter. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Associated Chair is a committee role (a person who co-chairs a conference), while Coffee Break is a scheduled non-academic event during a conference. They share no instances and are from completely different branches of the conference-organisation domain.

The property 'assigned To' in cmt relates a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper), while 'payed by' in sigkdd relates a Registration fee to a Person (indicating who paid the fee). These properties connect completely different domain and range types and represent unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

Organizational Meeting in edas is a subclass of Academic Event / Conference Event, i.e. an event (a meeting that takes place). Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a subclass of Organizator / Person, i.e. a person who serves on the organizing committee. One is an event, the other is a person; they share the word 'organizational/organizing' but denote completely different categories of entities.

The property 'adjusted By' in cmt relates a Bid to a Reviewer who adjusted it, while 'pay' in iasted relates a Person to Money. These are completely different relations in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The confOf 'abstract' property has domain Contribution and range string, representing the abstract text of a paper or contribution. The sigkdd 'Name_of_conference' property has domain Conference and range string, representing the name of a conference. These are completely different attributes of different entities (a paper's abstract vs. a conference's name), so they are unrelated.

These properties have different meanings and different ranges. 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership in the conference organization), while 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (signing a document/artifact). The domains overlap (Person) but the ranges differ (Conference vs Item) and the intended semantics are distinct.

Both are lecture-style presentations at a conference, but an Invited Talk is specifically given by an invited speaker, whereas a Plenary lecture is defined by its plenary (whole-conference) session scope. The two notions overlap (an invited talk can be plenary) but are not equivalent.

Talk Event in edas is a kind of academic event (e.g., closing talk, welcome talk), while Document in iasted is a physical or digital item (e.g., forms, letters, reviews, submissions). These are completely different categories in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

A Meta Review in cmt is a specific kind of review document written by a meta-reviewer for a paper, whereas a Personal Publication History in edas is a history object tracking an individual's publications. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference www in the Conference ontology is a document (subclass of Conference document) that has a URL, i.e. a web page or web resource about a conference. Academic Event in edas is an event (subclass of Conference Event) with children like Workshop, Talk Event, Paper Presentation, i.e. an actual happening/activity. A document and an event are disjoint kinds of things, so these classes are unrelated.

Organising Agency in ekaw is an organization (subclass of Organisation) that coordinates a conference, while Receiving manuscript in iasted is an activity (subclass of Activity before conference) describing the action of receiving paper submissions. One is an agent/organization, the other is an event/activity; they denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings. 'has_the_last_name' applies to Person and captures a person's surname, while 'hasCostCurrency' applies to Sponsorship and captures the currency of a sponsorship cost. They relate different kinds of entities and denote unrelated concepts.

confOf Administrator is a person who administrates the conference tool/organisation, while ekaw Agency Staff Member is a person working for a funding or sponsoring agency. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: an administrator manages the conference system/organisation, whereas an agency staff member represents an external funding/sponsoring body. Their intended instances do not coincide.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing that papers are being solicited, while 'Computer Networks Topic' is a subject-area topic used to classify papers. They share no instances and occupy entirely different positions in their respective ontologies (document vs. topic taxonomy).

Free Time Break in edas is a specific kind of break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break) denoting unstructured free time during a conference. Coffee break in iasted is a specific scheduled activity for refreshments. These are distinct concepts: a free time break is not the same as a coffee break, and neither subsumes the other in the given ontologies.

Both classes denote members of an organizing committee for a conference. 'OC Member' is an abbreviation of 'Organizing Committee member'. In ekaw, OC Member is a Conference Participant specialized as an organizing committee role (with a child OC Chair). In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is under Organizator (a person involved in organizing the conference). The intended instances coincide: people who serve on the organizing committee. The slightly different hierarchy placement reflects different modeling choices but does not change the core meaning.

These two datatype properties have completely different meanings. 'acceptsHardcopySubmissions' (boolean) indicates whether a conference accepts hardcopy paper submissions, while 'City_of_conference' (string) specifies the city where a conference takes place. They share only the same domain (Conference) but denote entirely different attributes.

confOf Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster and Short paper), whereas ekaw Submitted Paper is a specific phase/status of a paper (child of Paper, sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc.). confOf Paper is more general and is subsumed by the narrower ekaw Submitted Paper in the sense that the ekaw class denotes a specific submission-stage document, though the two ontologies model paper taxonomy differently.

writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (who wrote it), while hasReview relates a Paper to a Review (a review of the paper). These are different relations connecting different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Conference denotes the conference as an organizational entity (with administrators, members, paper submissions, review criteria, etc.), while iasted:Conference_days is a temporal concept (subclass of Time) representing the days on which a conference takes place. They are at different levels of abstraction and belong to different ontological categories (event/organization vs. time period), so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The cmt property 'hasBeenAssigned' relates a Reviewer to a Paper they have been assigned to review, whereas the confOf property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution they have authored. These are distinct relationships involving different domain and range concepts (reviewer vs author, reviewing vs authoring), so they are unrelated.

Paper Full Version is a subclass of Paper under Document, denoting a full-length conference paper. Gold Supporter is a subclass of Sponsor, denoting a top-tier financial sponsor of the conference. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt property hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to its Subject Area (topic), while the ekaw property publisherOf relates an Organisation to the documents it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Early Registered Participant is a person who registered early for a conference (a temporal/administrative category of participant), while Tutorial speaker is a specific role for someone presenting a tutorial. These are orthogonal dimensions: an early-registered participant could be any role (including a tutorial speaker), and a tutorial speaker could register early or late. Neither subsumes the other and their intended instances do not coincide.

Conference Chair is a person role in the cmt ontology (a kind of Chairman/Person), while Demo Session is a type of session/event in the ekaw ontology. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties relate a reviewer to a paper they have been assigned to review. The domain in cmt is Reviewer, in ekaw is Possible Reviewer, and both have range Paper. The direction is the same (reviewer -> paper). The slight domain difference (Reviewer vs Possible Reviewer) does not prevent equivalence, as both denote the assignment relationship between a reviewer and a paper in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a person who authors a paper. CMT's Author is a ConferenceMember with properties like submitPaper and writePaper, and is the range of hasAuthor (Paper -> Author). EKAW's Paper_Author is a Person who is an author of a paper. The intended instances coincide: people who write papers in the conference domain.

Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper are mutually exclusive outcomes of paper evaluation. In edas, Accepted Paper is a sibling of Rejected Paper under Paper; in ekaw, Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper are likewise disjoint siblings under Evaluated Paper. They denote opposite acceptance decisions, so they are not equivalent, not subsumed, and not related.

A 'Two Level Conference' in edas is a type of conference (or conference-related person role), while 'Sponsor' in iasted is a person who sponsors the event. These are entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Conference is a class denoting a conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). ekaw:Late-Registered_Participant is a class denoting a person who registered late (subclass of Conference Participant, sibling of DemoChair, Presenter, etc.). One is an event, the other is a person; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are subclasses of Person and both denote a person who chairs a session/track at a conference. However, in ontology A, 'Track workshop chair' is specifically linked to conference parts (tracks/workshops/tutorials), while in ontology B, 'Session Chair' is associated with initiating calls, reviewing papers, and broader session-level activities. The scope and associated properties differ: A's entity is tied to 'Conference part' via chair-of relations, whereas B's entity participates in review and initiation processes. They overlap conceptually (both are chairs of sub-events) but are not clearly equivalent given the differing property contexts and granularity.

The cmt 'title' property has domain Paper and range string, denoting the title of a paper. The sigkdd 'Name_of_conference' property has domain Conference and range string, denoting the name of a conference. These are different properties relating to different entities (Paper vs. Conference) in the conference domain, so they are not equivalent.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges. A's 'memberOfConference' links a Conference Member to a Conference (person-to-conference membership). B's 'was_a_committee_of' links a Committee to a Conference volume (committee-to-conference-venue relationship). They denote different relations in the domain.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers, distinct from Reviewer (a sibling class). In iasted, Reviewer is a person who reviews papers, and Author is its sibling. These are distinct roles in the conference domain; they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

A 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a meal/gathering) that occurs during a conference, while a 'Trip city' is a city visited during a conference trip. One is an event, the other is a geographic location (a city). They share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

cmt:Chairman is a general role whose subclasses include Associated Chair, Conference Chair, and Program Committee Chair, covering multiple kinds of chair roles in a conference. edas:SessionChair is a specific chair role for a session. Chairman is strictly more general than Session Chair, so the relation is subsumes.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: 'email' captures a person's electronic mail address, while 'Nation' captures a person's nationality/country. They do not coincide as relations.

Both are datatype properties with range string and relate to names. However, Conference.has_a_name has a broader domain (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), while edas.hasName is specifically for Conference (comment: 'Conference Full Name'). Thus has_a_name subsumes hasName.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a type of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while iasted:Conference_hall is a physical place (child of Place, sibling of Building and Hotel room). One denotes an academic gathering, the other a physical location; they share only the word 'conference'/'workshop' context but are completely different concepts.

Paper Full Version in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a Document) representing the full version of a written paper. Author of paper student in sigkdd is a subclass of Author (a Person) representing a student who authored a paper. One is a document, the other is a person; they denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In ekaw, 'Proceedings Publisher' is a subclass of Organisation — it represents the entity (e.g., Springer, IEEE) that publishes conference proceedings. In iasted, 'Author cd proceedings included' is a subclass of Author (under Person > Delegate > Speaker > Author) — it represents a person who authored a paper included in the CD proceedings. One is an organisation that publishes; the other is a person who writes. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

A's 'has tracks' is a specific part-whole relation linking a Conference volume to its Track components. B's 'has Event' is a general part-whole relation linking any Event to its constituent sub-Events. A track is a kind of event (or sub-event) within a conference volume, so 'has tracks' is a specialization of the more general 'has Event' relation. They are not equivalent because the domain/range of A is narrower (Conference volume -> Track) than B's (Event -> Event).

An 'Invited speaker' is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, while a 'Conference Hiker' in the iasted ontology is a type of Delegate (a conference attendee). These are distinct concepts: an invited speaker is a specific role with an invitation to present, whereas a conference hiker is an attendee who moves between sessions. They share no clear subsumption relationship and are not equivalent.

Record_of_attendance in iasted is a subclass of Document (Item > Document), denoting a physical/administrative artefact issued to track attendance. Author in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (Person > Speaker > Author), denoting a human role. One is a document, the other is a person; they share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

The property hasRelatedPaper in edas relates an Author to a Paper they have authored or are associated with. The property referencedIn in ekaw relates a paper to a venue or collection where it is referenced. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'is held before' (domain Activity, range Time) expresses a temporal relation between an activity and a time point. 'submit' (domain Author, range Paper) expresses an action where an author submits a paper. They share no domain, no range, and no semantic overlap.

A Conference Paper in EKAW is a scholarly paper submitted/presented at a conference, while a Mailing list in IASTED is an administrative document type. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The property hasEmail in edas relates a Person/Contact Information to a string (an email address), while locationOf in ekaw relates a Location to an Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.
Associated Chair is a person role in the conference organization (a chairman), while Sponsor company house is a physical building/place. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and domains.

ConferenceVenuePlace in edas is a general venue for a conference (parent Place, siblings Accommodation/Dining/Meeting Room), while Conference_hotel in iasted is specifically a hotel building used for a conference (parent Building, siblings Conference airport/restaurant/building). A conference hotel is one possible conference venue place, but the two classes are not equivalent: ConferenceVenuePlace is broader (includes non-hotel venues) and Conference_hotel is tied to the Building hierarchy. They overlap but are not the same concept.
Author is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person), while Fee is a monetary amount (subclass of Money). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

edas:Place is a general spatial location with subclasses like Conference Venue Place, Accommodation Place, Dining Place, and Meeting Room Place. iasted:City is specifically a city with subclasses like Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city, and Trip city. A city is a kind of place, but Place is broader (includes venues, rooms, accommodations). However, the iasted ontology also has a separate Place class, suggesting City and Place are distinct concepts in iasted. The two classes do not have coinciding instances: Place includes non-city locations, and City is a specific geographic/administrative entity. They are not equivalent, and the relationship is not clean subsumption since iasted treats Place and City as separate classes with City potentially being a subclass of Place rather than equivalent.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a Chairman responsible for organizing the conference), whereas Late Registered Participant is a person who registered for the conference after a deadline. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties differ in both domain and range. A's 'has a location' links a Conference volume to a string (a textual location), while B's 'is held in' links an Activity to a Place or Time object. A conference volume is a publication, not an activity, and a string is not an object Place/Time, so the properties do not relate the same kinds of entities in the same way.

In ontology Conference, Poster is a subclass of Conference contribution, i.e. a written document/artifact submitted to a conference. In edas, Paper Presentation is a subclass of Academic Event, i.e. a scheduled event where a paper is presented. One is a document, the other is an event; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

`hasCo-author` (cmt) relates a Paper to a Co-author (a person who co-authored the paper), while `writes` (confOf) relates an Author to a Contribution. These are different relations with different domains and ranges: one captures the paper-to-coauthor link, the other the author-to-contribution link. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting people to participate, while 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a specific temporal deadline for abstract submissions. They denote entirely different concepts—one is a document type, the other is a date/deadline—with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are subclasses of Document, share the same label 'Paper', and have siblings Abstract and Review. They both represent the concept of a paper submitted/published in a conference. The ekaw Paper has more specialized subclasses and richer properties, but the core denotation is the same: a written document submitted to a conference. The additional structure in ekaw reflects greater modeling detail, not a different intended meaning.

confOf:Trip is a subclass of Social event (an event/activity), whereas iasted:Trip_city is a subclass of City (a location). They denote completely different kinds of entities: an organized excursion vs. the city where a trip occurs.

The edas 'is Reviewed By' property links a Paper to the person/role reviewing it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). The sigkdd 'presentation' property links a Speaker to a Document (the presentation artefact). They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships: one is a review assignment, the other is a presentation document association. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. 'has important dates' links a conference volume to its important dates (e.g., submission deadlines), while 'holded by' links a conference to the organization that holds it (ACM SIGKDD). Their domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. `updated Version Of` links a Document to another Document (a newer version to its prior version), while `write` links a Person to an Item (author to authored artefact). They differ in domain, range, and meaning; neither subsumes the other.

Rejection is a decision outcome for a paper submission (sibling of Acceptance under Decision), while Sponzorship is a monetary concept (sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip under Money). They belong to entirely different domains and share no semantic overlap.

In iasted, Building is a general class covering many venue types (airport, hotel, restaurant, university, etc.), while in sigkdd Hotel is a specific kind of place. They are not equivalent: Building is far broader than Hotel. They are also not in a direct subsumption relation because they come from different ontologies with different hierarchies, and Building's intended instances (all buildings) do not overlap with Hotel's intended instances (hotels) in a way that would make them related. The most accurate verdict is unrelated.

Both properties relate an author to the document they have written. cmt's writePaper has domain Author and range Paper; ekaw's authorOf has domain Person and range Document. Author is a sub-class of Person and Paper is a sub-class of Document, so the properties operate at different levels of generality but denote the same relation (authorship of a paper). The broader domain/range in ekaw is consistent with typical ontology modeling differences; the intended relation is the same.

In Conference ontology, 'Information for participants' is a specific kind of conference document providing information to participants (sibling to Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.). In iasted, 'Form' is a document subclass for fillable forms (children: Author information form, Hotel registration form, Registration form). These are different concepts: one is informational content, the other is a structured fillable document type. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

hasCountry in confOf links organizations and persons to a Country (a geographic/political entity). is_connected_with in iasted links activities and persons to Items or Places, which are much broader targets. The ranges differ substantially (Country vs Item/Place), and the intended semantics are different: one is a specific geographic relation, the other a broad association. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other.

Extended abstract is a type of conference document/contribution (a written artefact submitted to a conference), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline (a date/event marking when something is due). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
Both properties relate a written item to its author, but they are inverses: cmt:hasAuthor goes Paper -> Author, while iasted:write goes Person -> Item. A property and its inverse are not equivalent.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. 'gives presentations' links an active conference participant (a person) to a presentation they deliver, whereas 'related To Paper' links a paper presentation to an accepted paper. One is about a person presenting, the other about associating a presentation with a paper; they do not denote the same relation.

Personal Publication History (edas) is a history/record of a person's publications, sitting under Personal History alongside Personal Review History. Final manuscript (iasted) is a concrete document artefact, a submission document that is the final version of a paper, sitting under Submission alongside Initial manuscript. One is a historical record of publications; the other is a specific document file. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties are completely different in kind and meaning. listsEvent is an object property relating a Programme Brochure/Web Site to an Event it lists, while Start_of_conference is a datatype property relating a Conference to a dateTime value. They share no common domain, range, or semantics.

cmt:Paper is a general class for all papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version), while ekaw:Demo Paper is a specific subtype of paper (a sibling of Regular Paper, Industrial Paper, etc.). cmt:Paper is strictly more general than ekaw:Demo Paper, so the relation is subsumes.

A.reviews links a Review to the Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed). B.referencedIn in EKAW indicates that a paper is referenced/cited in another paper. These are different relations: one connects a review to the paper it reviews, the other indicates a citation/reference relationship between documents. They relate different kinds of entities in different ways.

Both are non-academic/social conference events, but a Meal Break is a short refreshment break during the program (sibling of Coffee Break, Free Time Break), while a Conference Banquet is a major social event (sibling of Conference Trip). They overlap conceptually as social/meal-related events but are not equivalent; a banquet is not a meal break and vice versa.

The edas property 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership in the conference organization), while the iasted property 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place or Time (physical/temporal presence). These are distinct relations with different ranges and different semantics.

Property A ('was a member of') relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation), while property B ('writes') relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship relation). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

The cmt 'title' property represents the title of a Paper, while the edas 'has Submission Instructions' property represents submission instructions for a Call. These are completely different attributes: one is the name/title of a paper, the other is a set of instructions for submitting to a call. Despite both being datatype properties with string ranges, their domains (Paper vs Call) and intended meanings are entirely different.

These properties relate completely different entities. `covers Topic` links Events/Papers to Research Topics (what subject matter is covered). `presentationed by` links Documents to Speakers (who presents a document). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different with no overlap in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In EDAS, belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event (a document/artefact belonging to an event). In EKAW, technicallyOrganises links an Organisation to an event it technically organises. The domains (Programme vs Organisation) and the intended semantics (belonging vs organising) are distinct, so the properties are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other in a meaningful way.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, assignExternalReviewer links a Reviewer to an External Reviewer they have assigned (an action of delegation). In Conference, belongs_to_reviewers links a Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer holds that expertise or preference). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are disjoint.

confOf:University is an academic institution (subclass of Organization, with Scholar studyAt University), while iasted:Tip is a monetary amount (subclass of Money, sibling of Fee, Sponzorship, Tax). These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different things: 'author Of' links a Person to a Document they authored, while 'pay' links a Person to Money. They share only the domain (Person) but differ entirely in range and meaning.

Co chair is a committee role (a person who co-chairs a committee), while Author is a person who writes contributions. They occupy different positions in the conference organization domain: one is an administrative/leadership role, the other is a scholarly contribution role. Their paths, siblings, and associated properties all indicate distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent authors of a paper, but they are not equivalent. In Conference ontology, 'Contribution 1th author' is a subclass of 'Regular author' and specifically denotes the first author of a contribution, with a sibling 'Contribution co author'. In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a subclass of 'Author' (under Person > Speaker > Author) and denotes any author of a paper, with a sibling 'Author of paper student'. The sigkdd class is more general (any author), while the Conference class is more specific (first author only). However, the hierarchy structures differ significantly (Conference has Regular author as both parent and child, suggesting possible modeling issues), making a precise subsumption relationship uncertain. They are related as overlapping author concepts but not equivalent.

Van in iasted is a transport vehicle (a physical means of transportation), while Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes a conference. These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document providing general information to attendees (e.g., logistics, schedule). B's 'Transparency' is a physical document type (like an overhead projector slide) used for presentations. Despite both being subclasses of a document-related class, they denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The two properties operate in completely different domains. 'location Of' (ekaw) relates a Location to an Event (where an event takes place), while 'is made from' (iasted) relates an Item to an Item (what material/item something is made from). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

A Program Committee is a specific committee of reviewers for a conference paper review process, not an organisation. Organisation in ekaw is a broad class including academic institutions, organising agencies, and publishers. A PC is neither a sub- nor super-class of Organisation; they are disjoint kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Conference document in the Conference ontology is a class of documents (e.g., Call for paper, Review, Conference contribution) produced for or associated with a conference. Organisation in ekaw is a class of organisations (e.g., Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher) that organise or publish conference-related things. These are completely different categories: one denotes documents/artefacts, the other denotes institutional entities. There is no subsumption or overlap relationship between them.

In ekaw, Conference_Paper is a specific kind of paper (a document that is a conference paper), sitting under Document > Paper. In iasted, Document is a broad class covering many artefacts (forms, reviews, submissions, transparencies, etc.). Thus ekaw:Conference_Paper is a much narrower concept than iasted:Document, so it is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

Contribution co-author in the Conference ontology is a specialized kind of author (a co-author of a conference contribution, situated under Regular author). Author in edas is the general class of all authors. The co-author class is thus a narrower concept subsumed by the general Author class.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different ways. In EDAS, 'relatedToEvent' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (a specific presentation event for that paper). In EKAW, 'hasEvent' links a general Event to a sub-Event (a part-of / containment relation between events). The domains and ranges differ (Accepted Paper vs. Event, Paper Presentation vs. Event), and the intended semantics are distinct: one connects a paper to its presentation, the other decomposes an event into sub-events.

These properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. Property A links an Active conference participant (a person) to a Presentation they give. Property B links an Accepted Paper (a document) to a Paper Presentation associated with it. The domains (person vs. document) and the nature of the relationship (a person giving a presentation vs. a paper being related to a presentation event) are fundamentally different, so the properties are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption or overlap.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a written academic document), while Card in iasted is a physical item (sibling to Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle, etc.) with Credit card as a child. These denote completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Organizing_committee in Conference is a committee (a group/organization), while Organizing_Committee_member in sigkdd is a person who is a member of the organizing committee. One is the collective entity, the other is an individual member. They are at different levels of granularity and do not denote the same concept.

In edas, Conference is the top-level event organising the whole conference (with subtypes Single/Two Level Conference, deadlines, topics, members). In iasted, One_conference_day is a temporal subdivision—a single day within the conference—placed under Time > Conference days. These denote completely different things (the overall event vs. one day of the event), so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person (A's domain also includes Contact Information, which is closely related to Person) and range string, representing a person's email address. The labels 'has Email' and 'E mail' are synonymous in the conference domain, and the property paths and types match.

The edas Attendee is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person). The iasted Author_attendee_book_registration_fee is a monetary fee charged for registration (subclass of Registration fee under Money). They denote completely different concepts: a person vs. a monetary amount.

Submitted Paper is a research paper submitted for review at a conference, while Cheque is a payment instrument. They belong to completely different domain contexts despite both being subclasses of Document.
