They share the notion of manuscript rejection/receipt but denote different categories of entities (document vs. activity), so they are not equivalent. They are related by domain proximity but not subsumed by one another.

cmt:writePaper specifically relates an Author to a Paper (a conference document being authored for submission). iasted:prepare relates a Person to an Item, which is more general—Item can be any artefact a person prepares (e.g., a presentation, a manuscript, equipment), and Person is more general than Author. Thus writePaper is a specialisation of prepare: every author writing a paper is a person preparing an item, but not vice versa.

confOf Workshop is a type of working event (a conference session where papers are presented), while edas Paper Presentation is a specific academic event where an accepted paper is presented. Although both relate to conference events, Workshop denotes a session/event type, whereas Paper Presentation denotes the act of presenting a paper. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain.
Review is a conference document (peer review of a paper), while Departure tax is a monetary tax on travel. They share no domain overlap whatsoever.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Sponsor company house in iasted is a building/location (subclass of Place > Building). They denote completely different categories of entities—a person role vs. a physical venue.

In cmt, Paper is a submitted manuscript under review (children: Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version; properties: hasBid, hasDecision, assignedTo reviewers, acceptedBy administrator). In iasted, Publication is a physical/produced item (child of Item, siblings: Audiovisual equipment, Card, Transport vehicle; children: Book proceeding, Cd proceeding). These denote different things: a paper under review vs a published proceedings artifact. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other.

Chair in the Conference ontology is a general committee chair role (with siblings like Co-chair and properties linking to any Committee), whereas Workshop_Chair in ekaw is a specific chair role restricted to workshops. A Workshop Chair is a kind of Chair, so Workshop_Chair is subsumed by Chair; they are not equivalent because Chair covers all committee chairs, not only workshop chairs.

confOf:Conference is a conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas iasted:Technical_commitee is a person/role (subclass of Delegate, sibling of Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc.). One denotes an academic event, the other a committee member role; they share no instances and are not hierarchically related.

confOf:Event denotes a temporal occurrence (Administrative/Social/Working event) with start/end dates, while sigkdd:Speaker is a subclass of Person who gives presentations. They share no common instances and are from disjoint conceptual categories.

The two properties are completely different: `hasCountry` is an object property linking a Conference to a Country, while `Name_of_conference` is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (the conference name). They relate to different aspects of a conference and have different ranges (Country vs. string), so they are unrelated.

Call_for_paper in the Conference ontology is a conference document announcing a call for papers, while Exhibitor in sigkdd is a type of sponsor (a person or organization that exhibits at the conference). These are completely different concepts: one is a document, the other is a sponsor role. They share no semantic overlap.

confOf:follows relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event it follows (e.g., temporal/causal succession between events), whereas edas:hasProgramme relates a Conference Event to a Programme (a document/artefact describing the event's schedule). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and express different relations, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In EDAS, 'is Initiated By' links a Call (e.g., a call for papers) to the committee member(s) who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). In IASTED, 'is writen by' links an Item (e.g., a paper or document) to the Person who authored it. The domains (Call vs. Item) and the intended relations (initiation of a call vs. authorship of a document) are distinct, so the properties are not equivalent.

In confOf, Conference is a concrete type of working event (sibling of Workshop, Tutorial). In edas, SingleLevelConference is a specific subclass of the general Conference class (sibling of TwoLevelConference). The confOf Conference corresponds to the edas Conference superclass, not to the more specific SingleLevelConference. Thus confOf:Conference is subsumed_by edas:SingleLevelConference.

The property 'issues' in Conference relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings). The property 'updatedVersionOf' in ekaw relates a Document to another Document (a newer version pointing to an older version). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (has_workshops) relates a Conference volume to its constituent Workshops (a mereological part relation in the event domain). Property B (is_equipped_by) relates a Place to an Item it is equipped with (a facility/equipment relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

These properties are completely unrelated. 'has_the_first_name' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's first name. 'is_held_after' is an object property from Activity to Time, capturing a temporal ordering relation between activities. They have different domains, different ranges, different types, and different semantics.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'was a committee chair of' connects a Chair person to a Committee they chaired, while 'held In' connects an Event to the Location where it takes place. They have different domains (Chair vs Event), different ranges (Committee vs Location), and no semantic overlap.

These properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. 'written By' relates a Document to the Person who authored it, while 'is paid by' relates Money to the Person who paid it. They connect entirely different kinds of entities and express different relationships with no overlap.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. hasCity (confOf) links Organizations/Persons to a City (a location), while organisedBy (ekaw) links Events to Organisations/Persons (who organize the event). They connect different entity types in different directions and represent different relations.

A 'Submissions deadline' is a temporal deadline by which papers must be submitted, while a 'Best Applications Paper Award' is an award given for a paper. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

submit Paper (domain Author, range Paper) denotes the act of an author submitting a paper to a conference system. obtain (domain Person, range Item) denotes a person receiving/acquiring an item. These are different relations with different semantics and different directions of transfer; they are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

paperDueOn is a datatype property from Conference to dateTime representing a paper submission deadline, while presentationOfPaper is an object property from Individual Presentation to Abstract/Paper linking a presentation to the paper it presents. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings with no overlap.

Property A 'has the first name' denotes a person's given/first name, while property B 'has Surname' denotes a person's family/last name. These are distinct attributes of a person, not the same relation, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

Reviewer in Conference is a person who reviews papers (subclass of Person), while Numerical Review Question in edas is a type of review question (subclass of Review Question). They denote completely different concepts: a human role vs. a question item in a review form.

The two properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges. EKAW's 'inverse of partOf 7' relates some entity to an Event (suggesting a part-whole relationship where the range is an Event), while SIGKDD's 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker. There is no overlap in the kinds of things they connect or the relationship they express.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, authorOf links a Person to a Document they authored. In iasted, is_paid_for links Money to an Activity or Item it pays for. They have disjoint domains (Person vs Money) and disjoint ranges (Document vs Activity/Item), and express entirely different relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Submission_event is an administrative event representing the deadline/period during which contributions are submitted, while edas:Workshop is an academic event that is a type of conference gathering. They share no instances: a submission event is a temporal/administrative occurrence, whereas a workshop is a meeting/venue for presentations. Their positions in the hierarchy and their siblings confirm they are different kinds of things.

Antennas Topic is a subject-matter topic (sibling of CAD Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.) under Topic in edas, denoting a research area. Invited Talk Abstract is a kind of document/abstract in ekaw, denoting a written text. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The ekaw `has Event` property links an Event to a sub-Event (domain Event, range Event), modeling events containing other events. The sigkdd `presentationed by` property links a Document to a Speaker (domain Document, range Speaker), modeling who presents a document. They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

Active Paper in edas is a subclass of Paper (a document under review/active in the conference process), while Card in iasted is a subclass of Item with siblings like Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle, and Publication, denoting a physical or financial item such as a credit card. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'assigned To' in cmt relates a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper), while 'designed by' in sigkdd relates a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (indicating who designed/created the deadline). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel (same time, different tracks), while the ekaw 'technicallyOrganisedBy' property indicates the organising entity responsible for an event's technical organisation. These denote completely different relations: temporal/track parallelism vs. organisational responsibility.

Call For Manuscripts is an event/action (a Call) soliciting submissions, while Conference Paper is a document type (a Paper). They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

Both properties concern the relationship between a review and a paper/contribution, but they are inverses of each other. In ontology A, 'reviews' has domain Review and range Reviewed contribution (Review -> Paper). In ontology B, 'hasReview' has domain Paper and range Review (Paper -> Review). Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, the correct relation is 'related'.

A is a specific datatype property linking Important dates to a date, specifically for camera-ready paper submission. B is a generic datatype property linking Deadline to a dateTime, covering any kind of deadline date. A is thus a more specific property than B: every camera-ready submission date is a deadline date, but not vice versa. The ranges (date vs dateTime) are compatible, and the domains (Important dates vs Deadline) overlap, but A is strictly narrower in meaning.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In EKAW, 'paperInVolume' relates a paper to the volume (e.g., proceedings or collected volume) in which it appears. In IASTED, 'write' relates a Person to an Item they author. They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships (publication containment vs. authorship), so they are unrelated.

Conference announcement is a document type (subclass of Conference document) used to announce a conference, while Tutorial is an event type (subclass of Working event) representing a tutorial session. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote different kinds of entities.

Paper Abstract in cmt denotes the abstract component of a paper (a short summary artefact), whereas Workshop Paper in ekaw denotes a complete paper submitted to and presented at a workshop. They share the parent Paper, but their intended instances are disjoint: an abstract is not a full workshop paper. The sibling sets also differ (Paper Full Version vs. Conference Paper, Demo Paper, etc.), confirming distinct partitionings of the Paper concept.

Accommodation Place is a general category of lodging (hotels, dormitories, etc.), while Hotel is a specific type of accommodation. Both are subclasses of Place, but Hotel is narrower than Accommodation Place, so Accommodation Place is subsumed_by Hotel's broader category—i.e., Hotel would be a subclass of Accommodation Place if aligned.

Property 'issues' in Conference relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issuing proceedings). Property 'writes' in confOf relates an Author to a Contribution (an author writing a paper). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and they do not overlap in meaning.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. In ontology Conference, 'Information for participants' is a subclass of 'Conference document' — it represents a document containing information for conference participants. In confOf, 'Reviewing event' is a subclass of 'Administrative event' — it represents the reviewing procedure/event for submitted contributions. One is a document/information artefact, the other is an administrative event/process. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (e.g., an item required by a person), while 'search' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Sponzor (e.g., a conference searching for sponsors). There is no semantic overlap between these relations.

In Conference ontology, Chair is a committee chair (e.g., program committee chair), a leadership role for an organizational committee. In iasted, Session chair is a delegate who chairs a single conference session (presentation block). These are distinct roles: a committee chair leads a committee, while a session chair manages a session of talks. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In edas, hasCountry links a Conference to a Country (the location of the conference). In iasted, obtain links a Person to an Item (a person obtaining an item). The domains (Conference vs Person), ranges (Country vs Item), and overall meaning are completely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a leadership role responsible for overseeing the conference, sitting under Chairman > Person. Author book proceedings included (iasted) is a specific subtype of Author (under Speaker > Delegate) indicating an author whose paper appears in book proceedings. These are completely different concepts: one is an administrative/leadership role, the other is a specific author classification based on publication medium. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

hasCountry relates a Conference to its Country, while is_made_from relates an Item to another Item it is made from. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no overlap in meaning.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In edas, 'relatedToPaper' links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (presentation -> paper). In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (person -> activity/item). The domains and ranges are disjoint, and the intended semantics differ: one associates a presentation with a paper, the other associates a person with something they give (e.g., a presentation/activity). They are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption.

cmt:Preference denotes a reviewer's bid/preference value for a paper (an int-valued preference), whereas confOf:Participant is a person who attends the conference (subclass of Person with children Member, Regular, Student). They share no instances and no semantic relationship.

The cmt property 'read By Meta Reviewer' has domain Paper and range Meta Reviewer, modeling the relationship that a meta-reviewer reads a paper. The iasted property 'write' has domain Person and range Item, modeling that a person writes an item (e.g., a paper or document). These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and they are not inverses of each other (reading vs. writing are distinct activities). Therefore they are unrelated.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different attributes: `email` captures a person's electronic mail address, while `Name` captures a person's display name. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain and would not be considered equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise related in a reference alignment.

Card in iasted is a subclass of Item with a child Credit card, denoting a physical or financial artefact. Author in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (via Speaker) with roles such as submitting papers and obtaining awards. These denote completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.
University is an academic institution (organization), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

confOf:Conference is a top-level conference event (the whole conference), while ekaw:Invited_Talk is a specific individual presentation within a conference. They are at completely different levels of granularity and do not overlap.

Conference participant (A) is a person who attends a conference, while Conference Session (B) is a scheduled event/session within a conference. One is a person, the other is an event — they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate different entities and run in opposite directions. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (organization-level membership). In the Conference ontology, was_a_member_of links a Committee member to a Committee (committee-specific membership). The domains and ranges differ, and even if one considered an inverse relationship, the underlying concepts (Conference vs Committee, Conference Member vs Committee member) are distinct, so they are not equivalent.

Organizer in the Conference ontology denotes a person or committee that organizes a conference, whereas Organizational Meeting in edas is a subclass of Academic Event (a meeting/event). One is an agent/role, the other is an event; they do not share instances.

confOf:hasCountry links an Organization or Person to a Country, denoting nationality or location of the actor. iasted:is_situated_in links a spatial entity (Building, City, Place) to another spatial entity (Building, City, Place, State), denoting physical containment of one place within another. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings differ: one is an actor-to-country relation, the other is a place-to-place spatial relation, so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

The property 'email' in cmt captures a person's email address, while 'has the first name' in Conference captures a person's first name. These are distinct attributes with no semantic overlap, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

The two properties have different meanings in the conference domain. `detailsEnteredBy` in cmt relates a Conference to the Administrator who entered its details, capturing an administrative data-entry relationship. `holded_by` in sigkdd relates a Conference to the organization that hosts it (ACM SIGKDD), capturing an organizational hosting/ownership relationship. The domains coincide (Conference), but the ranges differ (Administrator vs. ACM SIGKDD) and the intended semantics are distinct: one is about who entered conference metadata, the other about which body holds/organizes the conference. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Country denotes a nation/state (domain of Organization/Person locations), while sigkdd:Place denotes a physical venue or facility (Conference hall, Hotel, Main office) where a Person can stay. A country is not a kind of place in the venue sense, nor vice versa; the two classes have disjoint intended instances.

Both are datatype properties with domain Deadline, relating a deadline to its date/time value. 'done till' and 'Date' both express the temporal point by which a deadline must be met. The range difference (date vs dateTime) is a minor modeling variation rather than a semantic distinction.

A 'Sponsor company house' in iasted is a building where a sponsor company is located (a specific type of building, sibling to conference hotels, airports, etc.). A 'Conference hall' in sigkdd is a place where conference events are held (sibling to Hotel and Main office). These are different concepts: one denotes the premises of a sponsoring organization, the other denotes a venue for conference sessions. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.
One property captures a person's email address, the other captures a person's phone number. They are distinct contact details, not the same relation, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In cmt, memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (person→conference). In the Conference ontology, has_members links a Committee to a Committee member (committee→person). They are not inverses of each other either, since one involves Conference and the other involves Committee. The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, so the properties are unrelated.

The property 'has Event' in ekaw relates an Event to a sub-Event (e.g., a conference has sessions or workshops), establishing a part-whole hierarchy among events. The property 'awarded by' in sigkdd relates an Award to the entity that grants it (e.g., a committee or organization). These properties connect entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and express different relationships (part-of vs. awarded-by), so they are unrelated.

In iasted, `obtain` links Person to Item (a broad category including awards, certificates, etc.), while in sigkdd it links Author to Award specifically. The sigkdd property is a specialization of the iasted property: every Author-obtains-Award triple is an instance of Person-obtains-Item, but not vice versa. They are not equivalent because the domains and ranges differ in generality.

Regular author in the Conference ontology is a broad class covering any author of a conference contribution (it subsumes Contribution 1th author and Contribution co author). Author of paper in sigkdd is a narrower class specifically for authors of papers, sitting under Person > Speaker > Author. Regular author is more general, covering authors of any written contribution (papers, posters, etc.), so it subsumes Author of paper.

Person in edas is a broad class covering all people involved in the conference (attendees, authors, chairs, reviewers, committee members). Speaker in iasted is a specific role: a delegate who presents, sitting under Delegate > Speaker with siblings like Non speaker and Listener. Every Speaker is a Person, but not every Person is a Speaker (e.g., attendees who do not present, committee members who do not present). Thus edas:Person is strictly more general than iasted:Speaker.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract of a paper, while Review (sigkdd) is a subclass of Document representing a review of a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a summary of the paper itself, the other is an evaluation of the paper by a reviewer. They share no instance-level overlap.

Both properties relate a person who writes/prepares a document to the document itself, but they differ in direction: confOf:writes has domain Author and range Contribution, while iasted:is_prepared_by has domain Item and range Person. They are inverse relations rather than equivalent. They are related because they describe the same underlying association between authors and their papers.

Both denote the subject domain or topic of a paper in the conference domain. In cmt, Subject Area is the range of 'has Subject Area' (Paper -> Subject Area). In edas, Topic is the range of 'has Topic' (Paper -> Topic). The edas ontology enumerates specific instances (Antennas, CAD, etc.), but the class itself represents the same concept: a categorization of papers by subject matter.

Conference Chair (edas) is the person chairing the entire conference, while Demo Chair (ekaw) chairs the demo/demo-session track. They are distinct organizational roles at different scopes; neither subsumes the other.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Trip day is a temporal concept representing a day during a conference trip. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (documents vs. time) and share no domain overlap.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'has Updated Version' (ekaw) relates a Document to another Document (a newer version of the same document). 'give' (iasted) relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or distributing an item). There is no overlap in intended semantics.

Workshop (ekaw) is a scientific event where participants present and discuss papers on a topic, typically involving submitted and reviewed contributions. Tutorial (iasted) is a lecture/teaching session, an educational activity with no paper submissions or reviews. They are distinct types of conference activities: a workshop is a mini-conference with its own program; a tutorial is instructional. Neither subsumes the other.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'has_gender' is a datatype property from Person to an unspecified value (gender), while 'is_needed_for' is an object property from Item to Person. They share no semantic relationship in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with range string that associate a location (city) with an entity, but their domains differ: hasCity applies to Contact Information (a general contact/location holder) while City_of_conference applies specifically to a Conference. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent since one is more broadly applicable to contact information and the other is scoped to conferences.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and express different relations. 'was a committee of' links a Committee to a Conference volume (the conference/event it serves), while 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (a person participating in the conference). The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, and neither property subsumes the other.

hasLastName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's surname). is_given_to is an object property from Item to Person (an item is given to a person). They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings.

In the EDAS ontology, Conference Session is a temporal/organizational event within a conference (a session where papers are presented), while in the SIGKDD ontology Document is an information artefact (abstract, paper, review). These are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one is an event/activity, the other is a written document. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference Member in cmt is a person who is a member of a conference (parent is Person, with sub-classes like Author, Reviewer, Chair). State in iasted is a geographic/political entity (with sub-classes like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state) that can be occupied by or visited by persons. These are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is a geographic region.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings. 'ends_on' applies to Event and captures when an event ends, while 'hasLastName' applies to Person and captures a person's surname. They share only the datatype range (string), which is not sufficient for equivalence.

Review expertise in Conference denotes a reviewer's area of expertise or qualification for reviewing a contribution, as shown by its properties linking it to reviewers and submitted contributions. Review Question in edas denotes a question item in a review form (numerical or textual), i.e., a field to be answered during review. These are fundamentally different concepts: one captures reviewer competence, the other captures review-form structure. They share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

Property A (has_authors) links a conference document to its authors (Person), indicating who wrote the paper. Property B (presentationed_by) links a document to a Speaker, indicating who presented it. Authorship and presentation are distinct roles in the conference domain; the same person may be an author but not a presenter, or vice versa. The domains (Conference document vs Document) and ranges (Person vs Speaker) also differ, confirming these are unrelated relations.

Both properties relate a document-like entity (Conference document / Item) to a Person, but 'has authors' specifically denotes authorship of a conference document, while 'is sent by' is a broader relation indicating the sender of an item. The domain of A (Conference document) is more specific than the domain of B (Item), and the semantics differ: authorship vs. sending. They overlap in cases where a paper author sends their paper, but they are not equivalent relations.

In cmt, Program Committee is a committee of reviewers for a conference, with members (Program Committee Members). In edas, Sponsorship is a financial sponsorship arrangement with cost amount/currency and a provider organization, having Travel Grant as a subtype. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent the same real-world concept of a university. In confOf, University is a subclass of Organization with a sibling Company, and is the range of the 'study At' property (Scholar -> University). In ekaw, University is a subclass of Organisation > Academic Institution with sibling Research Institute. Despite slightly different hierarchy positions, both denote the same entity: a university as an academic institution/organization. The ekaw hierarchy is more fine-grained (adding an intermediate Academic Institution class), but the leaf concept University is identical in both ontologies.

Abstract in Conference is a document/artefact (a textual summary that is part of a Paper, Poster, or Presentation), whereas Author in confOf is a person who writes contributions. They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations. In EDAS, hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of activities). In IASTED, give links a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a presentation or lecture). They do not denote the same relation.
Country denotes a nation (domain of a conference location), while Currency denotes a monetary unit. These are disjoint concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

hasLocation relates a Conference Event to its Place (venue/location), while hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event (part-of event hierarchy). They connect different kinds of things in different directions and serve different purposes.

In ontology A, 'Conference' denotes the overall conference entity (with conference volumes, proceedings, publishers, and topics), whereas in ekaw 'Conference_Session' is a specific session within a conference (a child of Session, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop sessions). These are different levels of granularity: one is the whole conference, the other is a session held at a conference. They are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption relation between the two ontologies' conceptualizations.

Late paid applicant is a highly specific subclass of Person in the Conference ontology, denoting someone who registered late and paid. Participant in confOf is a broad subclass of Person covering all conference participants. The confOf Participant class is far more general, so Late paid applicant is subsumed by Participant rather than equivalent.

confOf's 'written By' relates a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper). iasted's 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they present/give. These are different relations with different domains and ranges: one is about authorship of a written work, the other about presenting or giving something at an event. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

edas NonAcademicEvent is a broad class covering all non-academic conference events (breaks, meals, social events), while iasted Social_program is a specific kind of conference activity that includes dinner banquets and sits alongside other non-academic activities like cocktail receptions and coffee breaks. NonAcademicEvent subsumes Social_program as a more general category of non-academic events.

Review and Paper are distinct concepts in the conference domain. In ekaw, Review is a sibling of Paper under Document, and the property hasReview explicitly maps Paper -> Review, confirming they are disjoint. In Conference, Review is a document written about a contribution, with reviews pointing back to Reviewed contribution. The two classes do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In ontology A, 'Information for participants' is a conference document providing general information to participants (sibling to Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.). In ontology B, 'Registration form' is a specific form for registration (sibling to Author information form, Hotel registration form). These are different types of documents: one is informational material, the other is a fillable form for registration. They do not denote the same concept.

Session room in iasted denotes a room where conference sessions are held, a sub-part of a venue. Hotel in sigkdd denotes an entire lodging establishment. Despite sharing the parent Place, these are different concepts: a session room is a space within a building/venue, while a hotel is a complete accommodation facility. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. confOf:earlyRegistration is a boolean flag indicating whether a Participant has registered early, while iasted:done_till is a date-valued property on a Deadline indicating the date until which something is completed. They do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent.

Review (ekaw) is a document class representing an evaluation of a paper, situated under Document with children like Negative/Neutral/Positive Review and properties linking it to papers and reviewers. Value added tax (iasted) is a monetary concept under Money > Tax, representing a type of tax. These denote completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A Late Registered Participant is a conference participant who registered late (a temporal/administrative category of attendee). A Tutorial speaker is a person who presents a tutorial (a role-based category). These are orthogonal dimensions: a tutorial speaker could register late or early, and a late-registered participant could be any role. No subsumption holds in either direction.

Conference announcement is a document type (child of Conference document), while LCD projector is a physical audiovisual equipment item. They share no instances and are from completely different branches of their respective ontologies.

The two properties are inverses, not equivalent. In cmt, writePaper has domain Author and range Paper (Author -> Paper). In ekaw, writtenBy has domain Document and range Person (Document -> Person). They relate the same kinds of entities but in opposite directions. A reference alignment treats a property and its inverse as distinct (not equivalent), and since neither subsumes the other in the same direction, they are unrelated.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Powerline Transmission Topic' is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference papers (alongside other topics like Antennas, Cryptography, etc.). In iasted, 'Transport vehicle' is a subclass of Item, representing physical vehicles (with children like Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). Despite the superficial lexical overlap on 'transmission/transport', these are unrelated: one is an abstract topic for categorizing papers, the other is a concrete physical item.

Property A denotes the date on which acceptance decisions are announced (a post-review, post-decision deadline), while property B denotes the submission deadline (the date by which papers must be submitted). These are distinct temporal milestones in the conference lifecycle with different domains (Important dates vs. Call) and different semantics; they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a type of Chairman in cmt), while Late paid applicant is a registration status for a person who paid late. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair in EDAS is a leadership role (a Person who initiates calls, reviews papers, etc.), while Conference Hiker in IASTED is a subtype of Delegate (a Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate path), i.e., a type of attendee. They denote completely different concepts despite the superficial label similarity.

In cmt, User is a broad superclass covering all system users (Administrator, Author, Reviewer). In iasted, Author is a specific subclass of Delegate > Speaker, denoting a person who authors proceedings. cmt's User is strictly more general than iasted's Author, so the relation is subsumes.

confOf:Scholar is a price-category/registration role for conference participants (e.g. students/scholars) who study at a university, while sigkdd:Speaker is a functional role for persons who give presentations. Their intended instances do not coincide: a Scholar need not present, and a Speaker need not be a scholar. They share only the parent Person.

These properties denote completely different relations. `reviewerBiddingStartedBy` (cmt) links a Conference to the Administrator who initiated the reviewer bidding process, with domain Conference and range Administrator. `isReviewedBy` (edas) links a Paper to the person(s) who reviewed it (Reviewer, Chair, etc.), with domain Paper and range various reviewer roles. They have disjoint domains, disjoint ranges, and describe different stages of the review workflow (bidding initiation vs. actual reviewing).

The property 'has Email' in edas captures a person's email address, while 'Name' in sigkdd captures a person's name. These are distinct attributes of a person with no semantic overlap; they are not equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise related.

Both classes denote the published proceedings of a conference. In the Conference ontology, 'Conference proceedings' is a top-level concept with properties like publisher, volume, and ISBN, which are characteristic of proceedings. In ekaw, 'Proceedings' sits under Document > Multi-author Volume and has a child 'Conference Proceedings'. The ekaw hierarchy suggests 'Proceedings' may be a slightly broader concept (potentially including workshop proceedings), but in the conference-organisation domain the two are used interchangeably to refer to the published volume of papers from a conference. The strong overlap in intended instances and the domain context support equivalence.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference (with children like Active/Passive conference participant). MeetingRoomPlace is a subclass of Place, denoting a physical room where meetings occur. These are completely different categories of entities (people vs. physical locations) with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman and Conference Member). In iasted, Conference days is a temporal concept (subclass of Time) representing days on which the conference occurs, with children like Delegate and One conference day. These are completely different concepts: one is a human role, the other is a time period. No meaningful alignment relation exists between them.

`authorOf` in ekaw relates a Person to a Document they have authored (e.g., a paper or contribution). `need` in iasted relates a Person to an Item they require (e.g., equipment or materials for a presentation). Despite sharing the domain Person, the relations are semantically distinct: authorship vs. needing an item. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

confOf:Company is an organization (sibling of University) that represents a corporate entity in the conference domain. iasted:Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (sibling of Car, Taxi, Van) used for logistical purposes. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:University denotes an academic institution where scholars study, while ekaw:Proceedings_Publisher denotes an organisation that publishes conference proceedings. Despite both being subclasses of an organisation class, their intended instances are disjoint: a university is not the same kind of entity as a proceedings publisher.

These properties have different meanings and different ranges. 'is Member Of' links a Person to a Conference (organizational membership), while 'can stay in' links a Person to a Place (accommodation). The domains coincide (Person) but the ranges and intended semantics are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person participating in the conference). In edas, isProviderOf links an Organization to a Sponsorship (financial or material support). The domains (Conference vs Organization), ranges (Conference Member vs Sponsorship), and intended meanings are disjoint, so no equivalence or subsumption holds.

Extended abstract is a type of conference document/contribution (a written document), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented (subclass of Conference Event > Academic Event), while Best Student Paper Award is an award given to a student paper (subclass of Award). They are completely different concepts: one is an event/activity, the other is an award/honor. No subsumption relationship exists between them.

A Conference contributor is a person who contributes a paper or presentation to the conference (parent Person, children include Regular author, Invited speaker). B SC Member is a member of the Steering Committee, a governance role (path Person > Possible Reviewer > PC Member > SC Member). A contributor is not a committee/governance role, and an SC Member is not defined by contributing a paper. The two classes denote disjoint kinds of roles in the conference domain.

Published Paper is a document (a paper that has been published), while Best Student Paper Award is an award given for a student paper. They are completely different kinds of entities: one is a written document, the other is a recognition/honor. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds between them.

In edas, Industry Organization is a subclass of Organization (a corporate entity, sibling to Academia/Government/NGO organizations). In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person (a human individual who sponsors, sibling to Delegate). These are fundamentally different categories: one is an organization/company, the other is a person. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

In iasted, 'Hotel fee' is a specific kind of fee (subclass of Fee, sibling of Registration fee and Fee for extra trip). In sigkdd, 'Fee' is the general class with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee. Thus iasted's Hotel fee is a specific fee subsumed by sigkdd's general Fee class; they are not equivalent.

confOf University is an organization (subclass of Organization) that scholars study at, while sigkdd Main office is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). A university institution and a main office building denote different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different things. In Conference, 'belongs to reviewers' links a Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer has that expertise/preference). In ekaw, 'hasReview' links a Paper to a Review (indicating that a paper has a review). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or even meaningfully related.

LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Item > Audiovisual equipment), while Organizator is a person role (Person > Organizator) with subclasses like General Chair and Program Chair. These denote completely unrelated categories of entities in the conference domain.

Both classes denote the same concept in the conference domain: a written research paper submitted to a conference. In Conference ontology, Paper is a Regular contribution (a document) with an abstract. In sigkdd ontology, Paper is a Document that an Author submits. Despite different positions in the class hierarchy, the intended instances coincide—both represent the same kind of entity (a conference paper).

confOf:Working_event is a kind of event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) in the Event branch, while edas:WirelessCommunicationsTopic is a specific subject topic in the Topic branch. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'maxPapers' property limits how many papers a Program Committee Member can review (domain: Program Committee Member, range: int). The confOf 'abstract' property holds the abstract text of a Contribution (domain: Contribution, range: string). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to attend/register for a conference (a prospective attendee), while an 'SC Member' (Steering Committee Member) is a senior committee member in the program committee hierarchy. Their instances do not coincide: an applicant is someone seeking to register, whereas an SC Member holds an organizational governance role. They share only the distant ancestor 'Person' but denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In Conference, 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to its Review (paper -> review). In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (reviewer -> paper). They are not inverses of each other either, because the domain/range types do not line up (Review vs Member PC, Reviewed contribution vs Contribution). They denote different relations in the conference domain.

Property A (abstract) has domain Contribution and range string, representing the textual abstract of a paper. Property B (Date) has domain Deadline and range dateTime, representing a deadline date. They relate entirely different entities (papers vs. deadlines) and have different ranges (string vs. dateTime), so they are unrelated.
Industrial Session is a scientific event/session in a conference, while Hotel is a physical place. They share no instances and are unrelated.

A Steering committee is a committee that oversees a conference volume, whereas a Sponsor is a person who provides financial support. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The cmt Author is a person who writes or submits a paper, while the sigkdd Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline by which authors are notified. They denote completely different kinds of entities (person vs. date/deadline), so they are unrelated.

In EDAS, Conference is an event (the conference itself, with subtypes like Single/Two Level Conference, properties like dates, country, topics). In EKAW, Conference_Paper is a document (subclass of Paper under Document). These denote completely different categories of entities—an event vs. a written artefact—so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the subject matter covered by conferences and papers. They occupy the same structural position: each is the range of a property linking papers/events to topics (edas: has Topic; ekaw: covers Topic) and the domain of the corresponding inverse relation (is Topic Of; topic Covered By). The only difference is that ekaw qualifies the label with 'Research', while edas lists concrete research areas (Cryptography, Mobile Computing, etc.) as children. In the conference domain these are the same concept.

In iasted, State is a geographic/administrative entity (with children like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state, and properties involving buildings, cities, places, and persons occupying/visiting states). In sigkdd, Speaker is a subclass of Person (with children Author and Invited Speaker, and properties relating speakers to presentations/documents). These are completely different concepts: a geographic region vs. a person who gives a presentation. No alignment relation holds.

In edas, 'Rejected Paper' is a subclass of Document > Paper, i.e., the paper artefact that has been rejected. In iasted, 'Refusing manuscript' is a subclass of Activity, i.e., the action/event of rejecting a manuscript. One is a document, the other is an activity; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'was a steering committee of' links a Steering committee (an organizational body) to a Conference volume. In edas, 'is Member Of' links a Person to a Conference. The domains (Steering committee vs Person) and the intended semantics (a committee chairing/overseeing a conference vs a person belonging to a conference) are distinct, so these properties are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

In ekaw, 'Conference Paper' is a subclass of Paper under Document, denoting a written academic paper. In iasted, 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time, denoting a temporal period during which a conference takes place. One is a document, the other is a time interval; they share no domain overlap.

The cmt 'assigned To' property links a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper), while the iasted 'is_occupied_by' property links a Building, City, or State to a Person (indicating a person occupies a physical location). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in domain, range, or meaning.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In confOf, 'study At' links a Scholar to a University (where they study). In sigkdd, 'obtain' links an Author to an Award (that they receive). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so there is no equivalence or subsumption between these properties.

Single hotel room is a specific type of accommodation unit within a hotel, while Hotel is the entire lodging establishment. These are disjoint kinds of entities: a single hotel room is not a hotel, and a hotel is not a single hotel room. They share only the distant ancestor Place, which is too generic to imply any alignment.

Both classes denote the same concept in the conference domain: a person who presents (a paper, demo, etc.) at a conference. They share the same label and both are subclasses of Person (via Author in edas, via Conference Participant in ekaw). The differing intermediate parents reflect modelling choices in the two ontologies rather than a genuine semantic difference. The ekaw class has an Invited Speaker child, but this does not make the parent class narrower; it simply makes explicit a specialisation that edas leaves implicit. The intended instances coincide.

A's Abstract is a general abstract that can be part of a Paper, Poster, or Presentation, sitting under Extended abstract. B's Invited Talk Abstract is a specific kind of abstract for an invited talk, a sibling of Tutorial Abstract under a general Abstract class. The two do not share instances: A's Abstract is a broad category of contribution abstract, while B's is narrowly scoped to invited talks. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

OC Chair is a person who chairs the Organizing Committee (a role/person), while Introduction of speaker is an activity/event. They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (Person vs Activity) and denote entirely different things.

These properties operate in completely different domains and directions. 'technicallyOrganises' in EKAW has domain Organisation and relates an organisation to something it technically organises (e.g., an event or session). 'presentation' in SIGKDD has domain Speaker and range Document, relating a speaker to the document (e.g., slides or paper) they present. They connect different entity types (Organisation vs. Speaker) and express different relationships (organising an event vs. presenting a document), so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'has parts' links a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (e.g., tracks or sessions within a proceedings/volume). In sigkdd, 'hold' links the organization ACM SIGKDD to a Conference it organizes. The domains (Conference volume vs. ACM SIGKDD) and ranges (Conference part vs. Conference) are distinct, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

In ekaw, Workshop Paper is a specific kind of paper (subclass of Paper > Document), denoting a paper submitted to or presented at a workshop. In iasted, Document is a broad superclass whose children include Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission, Transparency, etc. Thus iasted:Document is far more general than ekaw:Workshop_Paper; the latter is a specific document type, so Workshop_Paper is subsumed by Document.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. Property A captures the date by which a camera-ready paper must be submitted, with domain Important dates and range date. Property B captures whether a participant has registered early, with domain Participant and range boolean. They share no conceptual overlap in the conference domain.

Both classes are subclasses of Document and represent the conference programme. In EDAS, 'Programme' is linked to Conference Event via hasProgramme/belongsToEvent, and in EKAW, 'Programme Brochure' is linked to Event via listsEvent/eventOnList. Both denote the same artefact: the document listing the events of a conference.

The cmt property relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (membership relation), while the sigkdd property relates a Speaker to a Document (presentation material). They connect entirely different domain and range types with no semantic overlap.

ekaw:Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while iasted:Conference_airport is a physical place/building (an airport associated with a conference). They denote completely different categories of entities: an event vs. a location.

The edas 'has Topic' property links a Paper (or Conference) to a Topic, representing the subject matter of a paper. The sigkdd 'presentation' property links a Speaker to a Document, representing the document a speaker presents. These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

confOf:Company is an organization (a company/corporate entity), while iasted:Presenter_university is a physical building (a place) where a presenter is housed. They denote completely different things: an organization vs. a building.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a type of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while sigkdd:Conference_hall is a physical place (child of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). One denotes an academic meeting/event, the other a physical room/venue. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference announcement in ontology Conference is a document (child of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while Organizational Meeting in edas is an event (child of Academic Event, sibling of Paper Presentation, Workshop). One is a textual artefact, the other is a scheduled gathering; they share no common instances.

These properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. Property A ('was a program committee of') relates a Program committee to a Conference volume, indicating that the committee served for that volume. Property B ('hold') relates an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference, indicating that the organization holds the conference. The domains (Program committee vs. ACM SIGKDD) and the intended meanings (committee service vs. organization hosting) are distinct, so the properties are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who registers late for a conference. In ontology A, 'Late paid applicant' is a paid applicant who registered late (distinguished from 'Early paid applicant'), while in ontology B, 'Late Registered Participant' is a conference participant who registered late (distinguished from 'Early Registered Participant'). The 'paid' aspect in A's hierarchy is an additional classification dimension, but the core concept of a late-registered conference attendee coincides. The sibling structures (late vs early) and the position under Person/Participant confirm they are intended to capture the same notion.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing the email address of a person in the conference domain. The additional domain Contact Information in edas does not conflict, as Person is the shared domain and both properties capture the same relation.

These two properties denote completely different concepts. In cmt, 'reviewsPerPaper' is a datatype property with domain Conference and range int, representing the number of reviews assigned per paper (a count). In ekaw, 'reviewerOfPaper' is an object property with domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper, linking a reviewer to the paper they review. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Conference vs Possible Reviewer), range (int vs Paper), and meaning (a numeric count vs a reviewer-paper assignment relation). No alignment relation holds.

Chair (Conference ontology) is a committee leadership role, a subclass of Committee member, with properties tying it to committees. Author (confOf) is a person who writes contributions, a direct subclass of Person. These denote distinct roles in the conference domain: a chair presides over a committee, while an author writes papers. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

In iasted, Listener is a subclass of Delegate, which is the general class for conference participants. In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person and represents any person attending the conference. The iasted hierarchy places Delegate above Listener, suggesting Listener is a more specific concept (a delegate who listens rather than speaks). Thus edas:Attendee is subsumed by iasted:Delegate, and Listener is a narrower role than a general Attendee.

In Conference, 'Reviewed contribution' is a written contribution (a paper) that has been reviewed, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution and a property 'has a review' pointing to Review. In edas, 'Review' is a Document (the review artefact itself), a sibling of Paper, Slide Set, etc. These are different concepts: one is the paper being reviewed, the other is the review document. They are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption or overlap relation.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a kind of chairman), while One conference day is a temporal entity representing a day during a conference. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (Person hierarchy vs. Time hierarchy) and share no semantic overlap.

These properties denote different relations. 'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. Reviewing and presenting are distinct activities with different participants, so the properties are unrelated.

In cmt, Conference is the conference event itself (the academic gathering being administered), with properties like date, logo URL, has Conference Member, accepts Hardcopy Submissions, and administrators entering details. In iasted, Conference building is a physical place (subclass of Building under Place) where the conference is held, with siblings like Conference hotel, Conference airport, Conference restaurant. These are fundamentally different concepts: an event vs. a physical venue. They share the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different things.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of objects. cmt:assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (the person assigned to review it), while ekaw:coversTopic links a Paper or Event to a Research Topic (the subject matter covered). They share no common domain/range semantics and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Program Committee Chair is a person who chairs the review process (a leadership role in the PC), while Author is a delegate who writes papers. These are distinct conference roles with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have different domains and different meanings. `hasKeyword` links a Contribution to its keywords (topics/terms describing the paper), while `hasSubmissionInstructions` links a Call to textual submission instructions. They relate different kinds of entities and carry different semantics, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise related.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document intended for attendees, while 'Microelectronics Topic' in the EDAS ontology is a subject-area topic for papers. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

cmt:Paper is a document submitted to a conference (with authors, reviewers, decisions, bids, etc.), while edas:CallForPapers is a call/announcement soliciting paper submissions. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Poster Paper is a type of academic paper (a document presented at a conference as a poster), while Bank transfer is a type of payment document. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties have different domains and ranges representing different relationships. In cmt, assignReviewer has domain Administrator and range Reviewer, representing the action of an administrator assigning a reviewer to a paper. In ekaw, hasReviewer has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer, representing the relationship between a paper and its reviewer. These are structurally and semantically different relations: one is an assignment action by an administrator, the other is a paper-to-reviewer association. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (assigning a chair to a conference part), while property B links a Person to an Item (expressing that a person needs an item). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a broad superclass covering all persons who contribute to a conference (authors, invited speakers, active participants), whereas Program Chair in ontology B is a specific organizational role. A Program Chair is an organizer, not a contributor in the authorship/participation sense, and a Conference contributor is not necessarily a chair. The two classes do not share instances, so they are unrelated rather than subsuming one another.

In confOf, Conference is the top-level event that encompasses the whole conference (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). In ekaw, Contributed Talk is a specific kind of individual presentation given by a speaker. These denote completely different levels of granularity: one is the conference itself, the other is a single talk within a conference. They share no instance overlap.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to attend/register for a conference (a prospective attendee), while a 'Program Committee member' is an organizer who reviews submissions and helps select papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one is an applicant seeking participation, the other is an appointed committee member with reviewing duties. Their hierarchies confirm this—A sits under Person alongside participants and reviewers, while B sits under Organizator alongside chairs and webmasters. They share no instance overlap.

In the edas ontology, Paper is a document submitted by an author and reviewed by reviewers, with subclasses like Accepted/Rejected/Pending Paper. In the ekaw ontology, Review is a document written by a reviewer about a paper, with subclasses like Positive/Negative/Neutral Review. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain: a Paper is the work being reviewed, while a Review is the evaluation of that work. They share the parent Document but have different roles, properties, and subclasses.

In confOf, 'Short paper' is a specific contribution type (a short paper submission, distinct from full Paper and Poster). In ekaw, 'Regular Paper' denotes a standard-length paper as opposed to other paper categories (demo, industrial, workshop, etc.). These are different classification dimensions: short vs. regular length in confOf vs. paper-category in ekaw. A confOf Short paper would not be an instance of ekaw Regular Paper (since it is explicitly short, not regular), and vice versa. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

Reviewing results event is an administrative event where authors access review results, while Submissions deadline is a temporal deadline for paper submission. They are different kinds of entities (event vs. deadline) representing different aspects of the conference process.

The cmt 'paper ID' property has domain Paper and range unsignedLong, serving as a unique identifier for a paper. The sigkdd 'Name' property has domain Person and range string, representing the name of a person. These properties relate to completely different entities (papers vs. persons) and serve different purposes (identifier vs. personal name), so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate fundamentally different entities and in different directions. In edas, 'relatedToEvent' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (the event/session where the paper is presented). In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents it). The domains differ (Accepted Paper vs. Document), the ranges differ (Paper Presentation/event vs. Speaker/person), and the semantics are distinct: one connects a paper to its presentation event, the other connects a document to its presenter. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only weakly related at best.

Property A ('is given by') relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the person delivering the talk). Property B ('awarded by') relates an Award to some entity that grants the award. These are fundamentally different relations in the conference domain: one concerns who presents a talk, the other concerns who bestows an award. Their domains (Presentation vs. Award) and intended meanings are distinct, so they are unrelated.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, setMaxPapers is an action performed by an Administrator on a Program Committee Member (likely setting a paper assignment limit). In edas, hasMember relates a Conference to a Person who is a member of it. They connect entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.
Country denotes a nation, while City denotes a municipality. They are disjoint geographic concepts; neither subsumes the other.

In iasted, 'Presenter state' is a subclass of 'State' (a temporal/role phase, alongside 'Conference state' and 'Sponsor state'), not a person. In sigkdd, 'Speaker' is a subclass of 'Person' with children 'Author' and 'Invited Speaker'. A state-phase of being a presenter is structurally and ontologically different from the person who is a speaker, so they are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

edas:PublishedPaper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been published), while ekaw:Paper is the general class of all papers (including submitted, accepted, camera-ready, etc.). PublishedPaper is strictly more specific than the general ekaw:Paper concept.

Both are datatype properties representing end dates, but they have different domains: A's domain is 'Important dates' (e.g., submission deadlines, notification dates) while B's domain is 'Conference Event' (e.g., conference sessions, talks). An important date's end date and a conference event's end date are related concepts but apply to different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

hasProgramCommitteeMember (domain: Program Committee, range: Program Committee Member) is a specific membership relation restricted to program committee members, while hasMember (domain: Conference, range: Person) is a more general membership relation covering any person associated with a conference. The cmt property is strictly more specific than the edas property, so it is subsumed_by hasMember.

The cmt property 'assignExternalReviewer' specifically relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (i.e., a reviewer assigns an external reviewer to a paper). The iasted property 'give' is a generic relation from Person to Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or item). These denote different relations in the conference domain: one is about assigning external reviewers, the other is a broad 'give' relation. They do not share the same domain, range, or meaning.

The property 'prepare' in iasted has domain Person and range Item, suggesting a broad relation where a person prepares some item (e.g., a manuscript, a presentation artifact). The property 'presentation' in sigkdd has domain Speaker and range Document, specifically linking a speaker to the document they present. These differ in both domain (Person vs. Speaker) and range (Item vs. Document), and the intended semantics differ: 'prepare' is about preparation of any item, while 'presentation' is about the act/document of presenting. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the different scopes and contexts.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. confOf:hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (e.g., associating administrative tasks with a working event), while sigkdd:submit links an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper). They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning; neither subsumes the other.

Tutorial is a conference part/event type (sibling of Track and Workshop), while Meal Menu is a document artefact describing meals (sibling of Paper, Programme, Review). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In Conference, 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (the author of the document). In edas, 'has Related Document' links an Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, or Person to a Document (a related document). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different: one assigns authors to documents, the other associates related documents with events or persons. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

Both classes denote the same conference artefact: a poster presentation submitted to a conference. In confOf, Poster is a subtype of Contribution alongside Paper and Short paper, representing a type of conference contribution. In ekaw, Poster Paper is a subtype of Paper (under Document), representing a poster paper document. Despite the slightly different structural positions (Contribution vs. Document/Paper), both refer to the same real-world entity in the conference domain—a poster paper. The term 'Poster' in confOf and 'Poster Paper' in ekaw are synonymous in this context, as a poster contribution is effectively a poster paper.

Paper Abstract is a document (a written summary of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment in the iasted ontology. They belong to completely different domains and share no conceptual overlap.

Industrial Paper is a type of academic document (a paper written by industry practitioners), while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment used for presentations. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (Document vs. Item/Audiovisual equipment) and share no semantic overlap.

The two properties have different domains and different intended semantics. 'is a starting date' has domain 'Important dates' (e.g., submission or notification deadlines) and range 'date', while 'has Start Date Time' has domain 'Conference Event' (e.g., when a session or conference begins) and range 'dateTime'. One captures the start date of an important deadline; the other captures the start date-time of a conference event. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'is signed by' (domain Item, range Person) denotes authorship or endorsement of a document/item by a person, while 'payed by' (domain Registration fee, range Person) denotes who paid a registration fee. They relate different kinds of entities (documents vs. fees) and express fundamentally different relationships (signing/authoring vs. payment). No reference alignment would equate these.

The cmt property 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper-assignment tools), whereas the confOf property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper they author). The domains (Conference vs. Author), ranges (Administrator vs. Contribution), and intended meanings (tool administration vs. authorship) are entirely different, so the two properties are unrelated.

In ontology A, 'Conference announcement' is a subclass of 'Conference document'—a document/artefact such as an announcement. In ekaw, 'Conference' is a subclass of 'Scientific Event'—one edition of a conference event. One is a document, the other is an event; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The property `has a name` in the Conference ontology assigns a string name to entities such as Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic. The property `manuscript Due On` in the edas ontology assigns a dateTime deadline for manuscript submission to a Conference. These are fundamentally different relations: one denotes naming/labeling, the other denotes a temporal deadline. They share no semantic overlap despite both being datatype properties with Conference in the domain.

Camera ready contribution is a document (the final version of an accepted paper), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal event (a deadline date). They share no instances and belong to entirely different categories.

Individual Presentation in ekaw is a scientific event where a paper is presented (e.g., Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). Time in iasted is a temporal entity (Conference days, Deadline, Trip day). These denote completely different concepts: one is an event/activity, the other is a time point or period. No overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person role - the chair of a conference, situated under Person > Chairman. Workshop (confOf) is a type of event - a working event under Event. One is a person, the other is an event; they share no instances and are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference Banquet (ekaw) is a specific social event—a meal/gathering event. Technic activity (iasted) is a technical conference activity (e.g., presentations, lectures). They belong to disjoint categories: one is social, the other technical. No overlap in intended instances.

These properties operate in completely different domains. 'assignedTo' in cmt relates a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper), while 'providedBy' in edas relates a Sponsorship to an Organization (indicating which organization provides a sponsorship). They connect different entity types with different semantics and have no overlap in the conference domain.

These two datatype properties operate on completely unrelated domains and serve different purposes. 'has_a_degree' in Conference has domain Review preference and range int, capturing the degree of preference in a review. 'maxChoice' in confOf has domain Social event / Working event and range positiveInteger, capturing a maximum choice count for events. They share no conceptual overlap.

In edas, TPC Member is a person who participates in the program committee, initiates calls, and reviews papers. In sigkdd, Author is a person who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. These are distinct conference roles: a TPC member evaluates submissions, while an author creates submissions. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

These classes denote completely different concepts.
