In Conference, 'Reviewed contribution' is a written document (a paper that has been submitted and reviewed), sitting in a hierarchy from Conference document down through Written contribution and Submitted contribution. In edas, 'Review Rating' is an evaluation score/decision category (with children like Accept Rating, Reject Rating, etc.) assigned to active papers via the hasRating property. One is the paper being reviewed; the other is the rating/decision value assigned during review. They share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relationship.

A is a person role (Conference Chair, subclass of Chairman/Person) in cmt, while B is a document type (Brief introduction for Session chair, subclass of Document) in iasted. They denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. a document—so they are unrelated.

In EDAS, Talk Event is a broad class covering any talk-type academic event (including closing talks, welcome talks, paper presentations, workshops). In EKAW, Tutorial is a specific kind of Individual Presentation focused on instructional/educational content, sibling to Contributed Talk and Invited Talk. A tutorial is a specific type of talk, but the EDAS Talk Event class is much broader and includes organizational and social events that are not tutorials. The two classes do not share the same intended instances, and neither subsumes the other in a clear hierarchy across ontologies.

In cmt, Administrator is a system-level user role (path Person > User > Administrator) responsible for conference management tasks like entering details, enabling virtual meetings, and assigning reviewers. In edas, Reviewer is a person who reviews papers (path Person > Reviewer). These are distinct domain roles: an Administrator manages the conference system, while a Reviewer performs paper reviews. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

Conference participant in ontology Conference is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference (with children like Active/Passive conference participant). Non Academic Event in edas is a subclass of Conference Event, denoting events such as breaks, meals, and social events. One is a person, the other is an event; they share no instances and are unrelated.
Paper Full Version in cmt is a full paper submitted for review, while Slide Set in edas is a presentation slide document. They are different kinds of documents with no overlap in instances.

hasEndDateTime applies to Conference Event (when an event ends), while Date applies to Deadline (a submission deadline date). Different domains, different semantics: one is the end timestamp of a conference event, the other is a deadline date. They are not equivalent.

Chair is a person who leads a committee in the Conference ontology, while City is a geographic location used as the range of a has City property in confOf. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class covering all persons affiliated with a conference (authors, chairs, committee members, reviewers), while Possible Reviewer in ekaw is specifically someone who can review a paper. The only structural overlap is that both are subclasses of Person and PC Member appears under both, but their intended instances do not coincide: not every conference member is a potential reviewer, and a possible reviewer need not be a conference member. The classes are therefore not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clearly documented direction.

confOf:Conference denotes the academic/scientific conference event itself (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas ekaw:Conference_Trip denotes a social excursion associated with a conference (child of Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet). They are completely different kinds of events with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Decision is an abstract class representing the outcome of the review process (with children Acceptance and Rejection), serving as the range of the 'hasDecision' property from Paper. In ekaw, Evaluated_Paper is a subclass of Paper representing a document that has gone through evaluation, with children Accepted_Paper and Rejected_Paper. While both have children corresponding to accept/reject outcomes, one is a decision/outcome concept and the other is a paper artifact. They are disjoint in type: Decision instances are verdicts, Evaluated_Paper instances are documents.

In EDAS, Workshop is a subclass of Academic Event (under Conference Event), representing an academic event where papers are presented. In EKAW, Tutorial Abstract is a subclass of Abstract (under Document), representing a document type. One is an event, the other is a document; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf:City is a geographic location class (domain of has City points Organization and Person to City). edas:ContactInformation is a composite data-structure class aggregating address fields (street, postal code, city, email, phone). They share no instances: a city is a place, while contact information is a record about how to reach someone. The shared property name 'has City' is coincidental and has different ranges (City object vs string literal).

In cmt, Paper is a document (subclass of Document) representing a conference paper submitted for review, with properties like hasAuthor, hasDecision, assignedTo, etc. In confOf, Organization is an entity like a Company or University with address properties (hasCity, hasCountry, etc.). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.
Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different attributes: a home page URL versus a biographical text. They are not the same relation.

`addedBy` in cmt relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator who added them (an administrative action on a person). `isMemberOf` in edas relates a Person to a Conference they are a member of (membership in an event/organization). They connect different entity types in different directions and denote different relations.

These properties relate entirely different things. cmt:assignedTo assigns a Reviewer to review a Paper, while ekaw:scientificallyOrganisedBy indicates an Academic Institution that scientifically organises an event. The domains (Paper vs. unspecified event), ranges (Reviewer vs. Academic Institution), and semantics (review assignment vs. scientific organisation) share no overlap.

The property 'reviews' in Conference relates a Review to the Reviewed contribution it evaluates, whereas 'give' in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a lecture or item). They have different domains (Review vs Person) and different ranges (Reviewed contribution vs Activity/Item), and they denote different relations in the conference domain.

The edas Author is a subclass of Person denoting a person who writes a paper. The iasted Author_attendee_book_registration_fee is a subclass of Registration fee denoting a monetary amount charged for an author attending with a book. These are completely different concepts (a role/person vs. a fee amount), so they are unrelated.

Travel Grant in EDAS is a kind of Sponsorship (financial support for travel), whereas Conference Trip in EKAW is a kind of Social Event (an activity/excursion during a conference). They denote entirely different concepts despite both being conference-related.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person, representing people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Fee under Money, representing a monetary charge for conference registration. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'is Menu Of' in edas relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (indicating which event a menu belongs to), while 'need' in iasted relates a Person to an Item (indicating something a person needs). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics with no overlap in meaning.

The two properties relate completely different entities and have different meanings. In cmt, enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference (the admin enables a virtual meeting for the conference). In sigkdd, presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (the document is presented by the speaker). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

In EDAS, 'Review Form' is a structured document/template used to collect review content (rating questions, text fields), while in sigkdd 'Review' is the actual review artefact (path Document > Review, sibling of Paper). The form is a template/structure that is filled in to produce a review; it is a more specific kind of document than the review output itself. They are not equivalent, and Review Form is subsumed by the broader Review/Document concept.

Accommodation Place in edas is a subclass of Place denoting a location where people stay (e.g., hotels, lodging). Student lecturer in iasted is a person role (a type of Lecturer/Author/Speaker/Delegate), not a place. These entities are of completely different semantic categories — one is a spatial location, the other is a human role — so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to the Conference contributions it contains, whereas 'prepare' links a Person to an Item they prepare. The domains (Conference volume vs Person) and ranges (Conference contribution vs Item) are disjoint, and the relations themselves denote different things (containment vs authorship/preparation).

Both Reception and Dinner banquet are social events at a conference, but they are not the same concept: a Reception is a welcome/networking gathering (often at the start of a conference), while a Dinner banquet is a formal sit-down dinner. They are sibling-level social activities that overlap in being social program items, but their intended instances do not coincide.

Property A (is_the_1th_part_of) relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation, expressing that the abstract is a constituent part of the larger work. Property B (paperInVolume) relates a paper to a volume/proceedings containing it. These are structurally different relations: one connects an abstract to its full work, the other connects a paper to a published volume. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction, so they are unrelated.

startDate is a datatype property from Conference to dateTime (a conference's start date/time), while listsEvent is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event (documents listing events). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

In cmt, 'Program Committee' is a specific committee responsible for paper review, with its own members. In the Conference ontology, 'Committee' is a general class with children Organizing committee, Program committee, and Steering committee. Thus cmt's Program Committee is a specific kind of Committee, making it subsumed by the Conference ontology's Committee.

These properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. 'was_a_steering_committee_of' links a Steering committee to a Conference volume, while 'hold' links an ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference. The domains (Steering committee vs. ACM SIGKDD) and ranges (Conference volume vs. Conference) are distinct concepts, and the relations themselves denote different things: one is about a committee's role over a volume, the other about an organization hosting a conference. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

These properties operate in entirely different domains. `written By` in ekaw relates a Document to the Person who authored it. `designed by` in sigkdd relates a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (the organizing committee). The domains (Document vs Deadline), ranges (Person vs ACM SIGKDD), and semantics (authorship vs deadline creation) are all different, so these are unrelated.

Regular contribution in the Conference ontology is a type of written document (a paper or extended abstract), while Conference Session in EKAW is a scheduled event/session. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one is a document artefact, the other is a temporal event. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Entity A is a person who authors a paper (subclass of Person/Conference Member in cmt). Entity B is a monetary fee for an author attendee who registers with a book (subclass of Registration fee in iasted). One is a person role, the other is a fee amount; they share the word 'author' but denote completely different concepts.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. A's 'was a steering committee of' links a Steering committee to a Conference volume, denoting the committee that oversaw the conference. B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker, denoting who presented the document. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so they are not equivalent, subsumed, or meaningfully related.

confOf:Company is a kind of organization (e.g., a corporate entity that might sponsor a conference), while iasted:Conference_state is a kind of State (likely representing a geopolitical or organizational state associated with a conference). These are entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Registration is an activity (subclass of Conference activity) with siblings like Cocktail reception, Coffee break, and Presentation, and it has Delegate as a child—denoting the act of registering for a conference. In sigkdd, Registration Student is a subclass of Registration fee with siblings like Registration Non Member and Registration SIGKDD Member—denoting a specific fee amount for student registration. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an activity/event, the other is a monetary fee category. They are unrelated.

A is a person role (SC Member under PC Member under Possible Reviewer under Person), while B is a registration fee category (Registration Non Member under Registration fee under Fee). They denote completely different concepts: a committee member vs. a fee paid by non-members.

Both are datatype properties that capture an ending date, but their domains differ: A's domain is 'Important dates' (e.g. submission or registration deadlines) while B's domain is 'Event' (e.g. a conference session). They overlap conceptually in denoting when something ends, but they do not relate the same kinds of things, so they are related rather than equivalent.

The cmt 'name' property names conferences and persons, while the edas 'hasSubmissionInstructions' property gives submission instructions for a Call. They relate to completely different entities and carry different semantics; they only share the string range.

The property hasRelatedPaper in edas relates an Author to a Paper they authored, while design in sigkdd relates the ACM SIGKDD conference to a Deadline. These properties connect completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

Trip in confOf is a social event (a happening/activity), while Double hotel room in iasted is a physical place (a type of hotel room). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

confOf:Conference is a top-level conference event (the main conference itself), sibling to Workshop and Tutorial under Working event. edas:Organizational Meeting is a specific sub-event within an academic conference (like a business or committee meeting), sibling to Paper Presentation and Talk Event. They denote different concepts at different levels of granularity: one is the main conference event, the other is a specific organizational sub-event. No subsumption holds between them.

Property A (has_the_first_name) is a datatype property from Person to string, recording a person's first name. Property B (is_sent_before) is an object property from Item to Time, recording when an item is sent. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings; they are unrelated.

Contribution 1th author is a specific role: the first (primary) author of a conference contribution, sitting under Regular author in the Conference ontology. The iasted Author class is a broader class covering all authors (including various speaker types, book/cd proceedings authors, lecturers, etc.), situated under Speaker > Delegate. A first author is an author, but not every author is a first author, so Contribution 1th author is subsumed by Author.

Both classes have identical labels 'Conference hall', sit under the same parent 'Place', and represent the same concept in the conference domain: a physical hall where conference events take place. The sibling differences (iasted has more siblings like Building, Hotel room, Session room) reflect granularity differences in the ontologies, not a difference in the meaning of Conference hall itself.

confOf's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event/process (a reviewing procedure for submitted contributions), while iasted's 'Transparency' is a physical document item. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote different categories of things in the conference domain.

Entity A is a class representing a contribution (paper) that has been accepted, while entity B is a class representing a specific review rating value ('weak reject'). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a document/artifact status, the other is a rating score used in a review. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a subclass of Person representing people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs). In sigkdd, Conference represents the conference event itself, with properties like start/end dates and location. These are completely different concepts: one denotes a person, the other an event.

Both are non-academic conference events, but they denote different concepts: confOf Trip is a specific social event (an excursion), while edas Break Event is a category of events that includes coffee breaks, free time, and meals. A Trip is not a Break Event, and a Break Event is not a Trip; they overlap only in being non-academic events.

Program Committee and Organizing Committee are distinct concepts in conference organization. The Program Committee handles paper reviews and acceptance decisions, while the Organizing Committee handles logistics, venue, registration, and local arrangements. In the sigkdd ontology, Organizing_Committee is explicitly a sibling of Program_Committee under Committee, confirming they are distinct roles. The cmt ProgramCommittee is specifically tied to reviewing via hasProgramCommitteeMember/memberOfProgramCommittee properties, further distinguishing it from an organizing committee.

In ekaw, Conference Session is a scientific event/session (a scheduled gathering like a talk, demo, or poster session). In iasted, One conference day is a temporal entity representing a single day within the conference period. One is an event/activity, the other is a time interval; they do not share instances.

Entity A is a class denoting a person who registered late and paid (a kind of conference applicant/attendee), while entity B is a class denoting a temporal deadline for paper submission. They belong to completely different domains (people vs. temporal events) and share no instances.

A is an object property linking an Event to the Location where it is held; B is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a date value. They relate entirely different domain/range types and express different relations (venue vs. deadline date), so they are not equivalent.

The two properties relate entirely different things: ekaw:eventOnList links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (i.e., the event is listed on those media), while sigkdd:presentation links a Speaker to a Document they present. The domains (Event vs Speaker), ranges (Programme Brochure/Web Site vs Document), and the nature of the relationship (being listed on a publication vs giving a presentation) are all different, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

confOf's writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author (authorship), while ekaw's references links a document to another document it cites (citation). These are fundamentally different relations in the conference domain, with different domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

The property 'parallel with' in confOf relates two Administrative events (indicating they run in parallel), while 'has Programme' in edas relates a Conference Event to a Programme object. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings; one expresses a temporal/scheduling relationship between events, the other associates an event with its programme document.

The two properties operate in entirely different parts of the conference domain. 'issues' links a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes (domain: Publisher, range: Conference proceedings), while 'parallel with' links two Administrative events that run in parallel (domain: Administrative event, range: Administrative event). They relate different kinds of entities and express different relationships, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and at best only weakly related.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, 'member Of Conference' links a Conference Member to a Conference (expressing membership). In the Conference ontology, 'has_contributions' links a Conference volume to a Conference contribution (expressing that a volume contains contributions). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

Both are social events at a conference, but Reception (a welcome/gathering event) and Conference Trip (an excursion/outing) are distinct kinds of social events. They share the parent Social Event but denote different activities, so they are related rather than equivalent.

confOf:Conference is an academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas iasted:Conference_hotel is a physical venue (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference airport and Conference restaurant). One denotes the conference event itself, the other the hotel where it is held; they share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different things.

The cmt 'email' is a datatype property from Person to string (an email address), whereas the iasted 'send' is an object property from Person to Item (the act of sending an item). They have different ranges, types, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

Property A (has_an_ISBN) assigns an ISBN identifier to Conference proceedings, while property B (hasTitle) assigns a title to a Contribution. These are semantically distinct attributes: an ISBN is a publication identifier, whereas a title is the name of the work. They share only the superficial similarity of being datatype properties with range string; their domains and intended meanings differ.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and in the direction of the relation. In ekaw, 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (the author who wrote it). In sigkdd, 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (the author submits the paper). These are distinct relations in the conference domain: authorship vs. submission. They are not inverses of each other either, since the domain/range types do not align (Document/Person vs. Author/Paper).

Talk Event in edas is an academic event with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk, Paper Presentation, denoting spoken presentations. Social Event in ekaw has children like Conference Banquet and Conference Trip, denoting non-academic social activities. These are disjoint kinds of conference events.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: 'has Fax' captures a person's fax number, while 'has First Name' captures a person's first name. They are not the same relation.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document subtype (a short version of a paper), while Operating Topicsystems in edas is a topic (subject area) under the Topic hierarchy. These are completely different kinds of entities: one is a document artefact, the other is a conference subject area. No alignment relation holds between them.

confOf:Event denotes a temporal occurrence (Administrative event, Social event, Working event) with start/end dates, while sigkdd:Document denotes a written artefact (Abstract, Paper, Review) that can be presented or submitted. These are disjoint domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Volunteer is a person who volunteers at the conference (logistics, on-site help), sibling to Participant, Administrator, etc. sigkdd:Program_Committee_member is a specific committee role responsible for reviewing papers, nested under Organizator. A volunteer is not a PC member and vice versa; the two roles are distinct in the conference domain.

Personal Publication History is a history/record of a person's publications, while Abstract is a specific document type (sibling of Paper and Review). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference' denotes the overall conference event/organization (with child 'Conference volume' and a name property). In edas, 'Conference Session' is a specific session within a conference (e.g., a time slot where papers are presented), not the conference itself. These are at very different levels of granularity: one is the whole event, the other is a sub-event/session within it. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

hasSubmissionDeadline (domain Call, range dateTime) denotes the deadline by which a paper must be submitted to a conference call, while is_sent_before (domain Item, range Time) denotes that an item (e.g., a document or artefact) is sent before a time point. They have different domains (Call vs Item), different ranges (dateTime vs Time), and different semantics: a submission deadline is a specific temporal boundary for a call, not a relation stating that an item was sent before a time.

In ontology Conference, 'Conference www' is a subclass of 'Conference document' and represents a web page/document about a conference (it has a URL property). In confOf, 'Conference' is a subclass of 'Working event' and represents the actual conference event itself (a happening, not a document). These are completely different kinds of entities: one is a digital document/artifact, the other is an event. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated concepts.

Both properties relate a document (Paper / Conference document) to its author (Author / Person). In the conference domain, Paper is a kind of conference document and Author is a kind of Person, so these properties express the same relation: linking a written contribution to the person(s) who authored it. The direction is identical in both cases.

Demo Paper in ekaw is a specific kind of academic paper (a paper presented as a demo at a conference), sitting under Paper > Document. Document in iasted is a broad administrative/container class whose children include forms, invitation letters, mailing lists, payment documents, reviews, submissions, transparencies, etc. A Demo Paper is not an instance of the iasted Document class (which covers event-management paperwork rather than academic publications), and the iasted Document is far more general than just papers. The two classes do not share instances in the intended domain, so they are unrelated.

Research Topic in ekaw denotes a subject area covered by events and papers (e.g., AI, databases). Time in iasted denotes a temporal entity such as conference days, deadlines, or trip days. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Industrial Session is a type of session/event at a conference. They denote completely different categories of entities (person vs. event).

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. `for Event` in edas links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the Academic Event it is issued for, while `lists Event` in ekaw links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to the Events it lists. A call-for-papers is not the same kind of thing as a programme brochure or web site, and the relations serve different purposes (issuing a call vs. listing events in a programme). Therefore they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

Social program is a conference activity (e.g., dinner, cocktail reception) in the iasted ontology, while Program Chair is a person/organizer role in the sigkdd ontology. They denote completely different categories of entities—an activity vs. a person role—and share no meaningful semantic relationship.

University and NGO are both subclasses of Organization, but they denote disjoint kinds of organizations. confOf:University is the institution where a Scholar studies, while edas:NGO is a non-governmental organization. Neither subsumes the other, and they are not equivalent.

hasBiography relates a Person to a textual biography (string), while Nation relates a Person to their country of nationality (string). These are completely different attributes of a person with no overlap in meaning.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range types. 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract, while 'has Related Paper' links an Author to a Paper. They share no common semantics in the conference domain.

In ontology A, 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' with children such as Written contribution, Poster, Presentation, and Regular contribution, denoting the work itself (a paper or presentation). In ontology B, 'Author' is a subclass of 'Speaker' with children 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student', denoting a person who writes a paper. These are fundamentally different categories: one is a document/artefact, the other is a person/role. They share no common parent or semantic overlap in this context.

The two properties have different domains and ranges that do not align. Property A has domain Review expertise and range Submitted contribution, relating a review-expertise record to the paper it concerns. Property B has domain Member PC and range Contribution, relating a PC member to the contribution they review. These are structurally different relationships (one connects expertise to paper, the other connects reviewer to paper), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully overlapping.

Both classes relate to conference deadlines but are not equivalent. In edas, Call is a broader concept representing a call for submissions (papers, reviews, manuscripts) with associated deadlines, instructions, and an initiating event. In sigkdd, Deadline is specifically a temporal entity marking submission cutoffs (abstract, paper, notification). A Call encompasses more than just a deadline (it includes instructions, event association, initiator), while a Deadline is purely temporal. They overlap in the sense that calls have deadlines, but their instances are of different kinds: one is a call-for-papers artefact, the other is a point in time. Thus they are related but not equivalent, and neither strictly subsumes the other.

In Conference, 'Contribution co author' is a specific role class under 'Regular author', denoting a person who co-authored a conference contribution. In confOf, 'Participant' is a broad superclass for any conference attendee, with subclasses like Member, Regular, Student, and siblings including Author, Chair PC, etc. A co-author is not necessarily a participant (they may not attend), and a participant is not necessarily a co-author. The two concepts do not coincide, and neither clearly subsumes the other in a straightforward way given the role-based vs. attendance-based distinction.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a working event under Event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while ekaw:Conference_Proceedings is a document (a publication volume under Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings). One denotes a scientific meeting/event, the other a published artefact. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In EDAS, 'Call' denotes a call for papers/manuscripts/reviews (a document-like entity issued by organizers, with submission deadlines and instructions). In IASTED, 'Time' is a temporal entity whose instances are conference days, deadlines, or trip days. These are completely different concepts: one is an announcement artefact, the other is a time point or interval. No subsumption or overlap holds.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain. `has Been Assigned` in cmt links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review, while `design` in sigkdd links an ACM SIGKDD conference entity to a Deadline. They share no common domain or range types and denote entirely different relations.

Property A ('is given by') relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the speaker/presenter). Property B ('is Reviewed By') relates a Paper to reviewers/chairs. These are different relations in the conference domain: one is about who presents a paper, the other is about who reviews it. They connect different kinds of entities and serve different purposes, so they are unrelated.

A's Paper is a regular conference contribution (sibling of Extended abstract), while B's Poster Paper is a specific kind of paper (poster presentation). They are at different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept: A's Paper is a general paper class, whereas B's Poster Paper is a specialized paper type. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way given the different ontology structures.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to its title (string), while confOf 'hasStreet' relates an Organization or Person to a street address (string). These are entirely different attributes with disjoint domains and unrelated semantics.

Paper Presentation is an academic event (subclass of Conference Event) where a paper is presented, while Speaker is a person who gives a presentation. One is an event, the other is a person; they denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Property A (has_a_date_of_issue) is a datatype property from Conference document to date, recording when a document was issued. Property B (listsEvent) is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event, recording that a brochure or web site lists events. They have different domains, different ranges (date vs Event), different property types (datatype vs object), and no semantic overlap.

In ontology A, Conference denotes the academic event itself (with a name, proceedings, parts, etc.). In ontology B, Conference restaurant is a physical place (a building) where conference participants dine. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'Chair PC' is a general PC chair role (sibling to Member PC, Administrator, etc.), while ekaw's 'Tutorial Chair' is a specific chair role for tutorials. They are different roles: a PC Chair oversees the program committee, whereas a Tutorial Chair oversees tutorials. Neither subsumes the other in a clear way, and they are not equivalent.

The cmt 'paper ID' property assigns a numeric identifier (unsignedLong) to a Paper, while the confOf 'abstract' property assigns a textual abstract (string) to a Contribution. They denote completely different attributes of a paper and do not coincide.

Both classes denote authors of conference contributions, but they are not equivalent. In ontology A, Regular author is a broad class covering any author of a regular conference contribution, with Contribution 1th author and Contribution co author as subclasses. In ontology B, Lecturer is a subclass of Author specifically for authors who give lectures, with Student lecturer and Worker lecturer as subclasses. The iasted hierarchy (Speaker > Author > Lecturer) indicates a Lecturer is an author who also presents, making it narrower than a general Regular author. The two overlap (a lecturer may be a regular author) but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so related is the best fit.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a meal/gathering) under Event, while Trip day is a temporal entity (a day on which a trip occurs) under Time. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Event vs Time) and denote fundamentally different categories — one is an activity, the other is a time period.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria. In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker who presented it. The domains (Conference vs Document), ranges (Administrator vs Speaker), and semantics (entering review criteria vs presenting a document) are completely different, so these properties are unrelated.

In EDAS, Social Event is a broad category of non-academic events with children Excursion and Reception and siblings Break Event and Meal Event. In EKAW, Social Event is also a broad category, and Conference Trip is a specific kind of social event (sibling to Conference Banquet). Thus EDAS Social Event is more general than EKAW Conference Trip, making the relation subsumed_by.

confOf:Workshop is an event type (a kind of working event alongside Conference and Tutorial), while iasted:Lecturer is a person role (a kind of speaker/author who delivers a lecture). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In cmt, Author is a broad class covering any person who submits or writes a paper, including co-authors. In the Conference ontology, Contribution_1th_author is a specific subclass of Regular_author denoting only the first/primary author of a contribution, with Contribution_co_author as a sibling. Thus A (Author) is more general and B (Contribution_1th_author) is a strict specialization of it.

siteURL is a datatype property from Conference to anyURI (a web address), while heldIn is an object property from Event to Location (a physical place). They relate different subjects to completely different kinds of objects, so they are unrelated.

These properties differ in type, domain, range, and direction. 'done till' is a datatype property from Deadline to a date value, representing the date by which a deadline is reached. 'submit until' is an object property from Document to Deadline, linking a document to its submission deadline object. They connect different entity types in different directions and do not denote the same relation.

These two datatype properties are completely unrelated. 'has a volume' (domain: Conference proceedings, range: int) denotes the volume number of a published proceedings. 'maxChoice' (domain: Social event / Working event, range: positiveInteger) denotes a maximum number of choices for an event. They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings.

The edas property 'is Member Of' specifically relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference). The iasted property 'is connected with' is a much broader relation connecting Activities or Persons to Items or Places. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other in a way that would be recorded as equivalent in a reference alignment.

Both classes represent social/non-scientific conference activities (e.g., banquets, trips), but they are not strictly equivalent. ekaw's Social Event is a top-level partition of Event alongside Scientific Event, while iasted's Social program is a subtype of Conference activity with many siblings (Coffee break, Registration, etc.) that are not social events. The instance sets overlap (banquet, trip) but do not coincide.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In ekaw, locationOf has domain Location and range Event, meaning a location hosts an event. In sigkdd, holded_by has domain Conference and range ACM_SIGKDD, meaning a conference is organized by the ACM SIGKDD entity. The domains and ranges are disjoint concepts, and the relational semantics differ entirely.

In Conference, 'Review preference' denotes a preference record (with a degree, topic, and reviewer) used to assign reviews, not the review document itself. In ekaw, 'Review' is a document (child of Document) with subtypes like Positive/Negative/Neutral Review and properties reviewOfPaper/reviewWrittenBy. These are different concepts: one is a preference/assignment entity, the other is the actual review artefact. They share the word 'review' but their structure, properties, and intended instances do not coincide.

In Conference ontology, 'Invited talk' is a type of Conference contribution / Presentation—a talk or presentation given at a conference. In confOf ontology, 'Conference' is a type of Event / Working event—the conference itself (alongside Workshop and Tutorial). These denote completely different things: a presentation artifact vs. the conference event. They share no meaningful semantic relationship.

Co-author in cmt is a specific kind of author who co-writes a paper, sitting under Author in the hierarchy. Reviewer in edas is a person who reviews papers, sitting directly under Person. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one writes papers, the other reviews them. They share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'title' in cmt relates a Paper to its title string, while 'has Street' in edas relates Contact Information to a street address string. They have completely different domains (Paper vs. Contact Information) and denote entirely different attributes in the conference domain.

The cmt 'assigned To' property relates a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper), while the iasted 'give' property relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving a presentation or item). These are completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Extended abstract in Conference ontology is a regular conference contribution (like a paper but shorter), a document submitted to the conference. Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is the abstract of an invited talk, a specific event abstract. They are different kinds of things: one is a contribution/document type, the other is an abstract tied to an invited talk event. Their paths and siblings confirm distinct intended instances.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person role, a kind of Chairman who leads the conference. Meal Break (edas) is a non-academic conference event, a kind of break for meals. They belong to completely different branches of the conference domain (people vs. events) and share no instances.

The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (paper), whereas the sigkdd 'design' property links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Deadline. They relate completely different kinds of entities and have no semantic overlap.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Document > Paper, representing a full-length conference paper submission. In edas, 'Performance Topic' is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area (like antennas, CAD, communications, etc.) that a paper can cover. These are completely different concepts: one is a document type, the other is a research topic category. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Call For Manuscripts' is a type of Call (an invitation or solicitation for manuscript submissions), whereas in the IASTED ontology, 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' is a type of Deadline (a temporal point by which camera-ready manuscripts must be submitted). One denotes a solicitation/announcement, the other a date/deadline. They are conceptually distinct entities in the conference domain despite both relating to manuscripts.
Personal Review History is a record of a reviewer's past reviews in the conference domain, while Departure tax is a monetary tax concept. They share no semantic overlap.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while Conference in the Conference ontology is an event/organization with a name and conference volumes. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. 'has parts' connects a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (a mereological relation between organizational entities). 'prepare' connects a Person to an Item they prepare (an action/production relation between an agent and an artefact). The domains (Conference volume vs. Person) and ranges (Conference part vs. Item) are disjoint, and the intended semantics (part-whole vs. agent-product) are unrelated.

Property A (has_the_last_name) is a datatype property from Person to string, representing a person's surname. Property B (is_used_by) is an object property from Item to Person, indicating that an item is used by a person. They have different domains, different ranges (string vs Person), different types (datatype vs object), and represent completely different relationships in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Presenter is a person who presents (a conference participant who gives a talk). In iasted, Session chair is a delegate who chairs a session, not necessarily one who presents. The two roles are distinct: a session chair moderates a session while a presenter delivers content. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

hasFirstName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's first name), while obtain is an object property from Person to Item (a person obtaining an item). They have completely different ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

Co author in cmt is a person who co-writes a paper, sitting under Person > Conference Member > Author. Author attendee cd registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee for an author attendee to register with a CD, sitting under Money > Fee > Registration fee. These denote completely different categories of entities (a person vs. a monetary amount) and share no domain overlap.

The Conference property 'has a committee co chair' specifically relates a Committee to a Co chair (a specialized role), while the edas 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (a general participant). They differ in domain, range, and granularity: one is about assigning a co-chair to a committee, the other about listing members of a conference. Neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way given the different domain types (Committee vs Conference).

Active conference participant is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., gives presentations), while Building is a physical place. These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Person in the Conference ontology denotes a human being (with children like Committee member, Reviewer, Conference participant, and properties like email, first name, last name). Sponsorship in edas denotes a financial sponsorship arrangement (with child Travel Grant, cost amount/currency properties, and relationships to Organization). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A's 'is an ending date' is a generic datatype property on the class 'Important dates' (e.g., end of abstract submission, end of paper submission, end of camera-ready), whereas B's 'End of conference' is a specific property on the Conference class denoting the date the conference itself ends. The sigkdd property is a specific instance of the more general Conference ontology property, so A subsumes B (B is subsumed_by A). They are not equivalent because their domains differ (Important dates vs Conference) and B is strictly more specific.

Property A denotes a specific committee membership role (a Co chair was a committee co-chair of a Committee), while property B denotes a Person giving (e.g., presenting or providing) an Activity or Item. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so the two properties are unrelated.

Reception in confOf is a social event (e.g., a conference reception), while Invitation letter in iasted is a document sent to invite someone. They are completely different kinds of entities: one is an event/activity, the other is a document/artefact.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics. A's 'is the 1th part of' links an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (an abstract is part of a larger work). B's 'paperPresentedAs' links an Abstract or Paper to an Individual Presentation (a paper is presented as a talk). One expresses parthood (abstract -> whole document), the other expresses presentation form (paper -> presentation). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

Both classes represent the registration fee charged to students attending a conference. They share the same parent (Registration fee) and occupy the same structural position among sibling fee categories. The labels differ only in word order and phrasing ('Student registration fee' vs 'Registration Student'), but denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Call for participation is a conference document announcing an event and inviting people to participate, while Deadline Paper Submission is a specific temporal deadline for submitting papers. They are different kinds of things: one is a document/announcement, the other is a date/deline. No subsumption relationship exists between them.

Security Topic is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area in the conference domain (e.g., security as a research topic). Invited Talk Abstract is a subclass of Abstract under Document, representing a written summary of an invited talk. These are completely different concepts: one is a topic/subject classification, the other is a document type. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Track in the Conference ontology is a conference part (like Tutorial or Workshop), while Tip in the iasted ontology is a monetary concept (sibling of Fee, Sponzorship, Tax). They denote completely different things.

Review expertise (Conference) denotes the expertise/qualification level of a reviewer for a specific submitted contribution, linked to both a Reviewer and a Submitted contribution. Personal Review History (edas) denotes a reviewer's accumulated review history record, a personal history item. The former is about expertise for a particular paper; the latter is a historical record of reviews done. They are structurally and semantically distinct concepts.

edas:Author is a subclass of Person (a person who writes a paper), while sigkdd:Person is the general person class in the conference domain (with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker). Author is thus a specific kind of Person, so Author is subsumed_by Person.

Both classes are subclasses of Person and denote a reviewer in the conference domain. confOf's 'Member PC' has the rdfs:comment 'Reviewer' and is the domain of reviewes (Member PC -> Contribution), while edas's 'Reviewer' is the domain of is Reviewing (Reviewer -> Paper). These properties relate the same kinds of entities in the same direction, confirming that both classes are intended to denote the same concept: a person who reviews papers.

In EDAS, Attendee is a direct child of Person, covering any person attending the conference (including speakers, session chairs, etc.). In IASTED, Non_speaker is a child of Delegate, specifically denoting delegates who do not present, with subtypes like Student non speaker and Worker non speaker. Attendee is thus more general than Non_speaker, since speakers and other presenting attendees are Attendees but not Non_speakers.

Entity A is an accepted paper/contribution (a document), while entity B is a deadline (a temporal entity) for submitting camera-ready manuscripts. They are completely different kinds of things with no overlap in instances.

Associated Chair is an administrative/organizing role (a Chairman who assists the Conference Chair), while Invited Speaker is a person invited to give a talk at the conference. They are distinct conference roles with no overlap in intended instances.

Invited speaker is a person who gives an invited talk at a conference, while University is an academic organisation. They belong to disjoint branches of the hierarchy (Person vs Organisation) and share no instances.

Both classes denote the person who chairs the programme committee (the body responsible for paper selection) of a conference. In EDAS 'Conference Chair' is a sub-role of Person and participates in initiating calls and reviewing papers, which are PC-level responsibilities; in EKAW 'PC Chair' is a sub-role of Conference Participant and PC Member. The labels differ but the intended instances coincide: the chair of the conference's programme committee. The EKAW hierarchy also distinguishes OC Member (organising committee) from PC Member, so PC Chair is specifically the programme-committee chair, matching EDAS's Conference Chair in the conference-organisation domain.

hasLastName relates a Person to their surname (string), while E-mail relates a Person to their email address (string). They denote different attributes of a person and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

In the edas ontology, 'Call For Manuscripts' is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting manuscript submissions), whereas in the iasted ontology, 'Final manuscript' is a specific document artifact (a final version of a submitted manuscript). One is a call/announcement event, the other is a document. They denote completely different concepts despite both relating to manuscripts.

The property 'is visited by' in iasted relates a location (Building, City, State) to a Person who visits it, while 'submit' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper they submit. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and describe unrelated activities in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Conference is a scientific event representing one edition of a conference (an event/activity). In iasted, Conference hall is a physical place/room where conference activities occur. These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a location. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.

The cmt Author class represents a person who writes/submits papers, sitting under Person > Conference Member. The iasted Author_attendee_cd_registration_fee is a monetary fee charged for an author attendee's CD registration, sitting under Money > Fee > Registration fee. One is a person role, the other is a financial charge; they share only the word 'author' and denote completely different concepts.

Both classes denote a conference paper. In the Conference ontology, Paper is a concrete contribution type (a leaf under Conference contribution > Regular contribution, sibling to Extended abstract). In edas, Paper is the base class for various paper states (Accepted, Rejected, etc.) and is a child of Document. Despite edas having subclasses that represent workflow states, the core denotation of both classes is the same: a written academic contribution submitted to a conference. The structural difference (leaf vs. parent of state subclasses) reflects modeling granularity, not a difference in the fundamental concept.

Both are social/non-academic meal events at a conference, but Meal Event is a broader category (with Conference Dinner as a child) while Conference Banquet is a specific kind of banquet event. They overlap in denotation but are not equivalent.

In the Conference ontology, 'Paper' is a document class (a written contribution), sitting under 'Conference document' > 'Conference contribution' > 'Regular contribution', with siblings like 'Extended abstract'. In the EDAS ontology, 'Paper Presentation' is an event class (an academic event where a paper is presented), sitting under 'Conference Event' > 'Academic Event', with siblings like 'Organizational Meeting', 'Talk Event', and 'Workshop'. One is the written artefact itself; the other is the presentation event. They are disjoint kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and at best only loosely related.

Entity A is a Topic (research subject area) about satellite and space communications, while Entity B is a Contributed Talk, a type of scientific event/individual presentation. They are completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Associated Chair is a leadership role under Chairman (alongside Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), responsible for paper assignment and reviewer acceptance at the conference level. In edas, Session Chair is a Person who chairs a specific session and also participates in reviewing. These are different organizational roles: Associated Chair is a conference-wide co-chair, while Session Chair manages individual sessions. Their intended instances do not coincide.

In cmt, Reviewer is a specific role: a conference member who reviews papers (child of Conference Member, with review-related properties). In ekaw, Conference Participant is a broad superclass for anyone participating in the conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, organizers). A Reviewer is not a kind of Conference Participant in the cmt taxonomy, and Conference Participant includes many non-reviewer roles. The two classes have different intended instances and no clear overlap in the given hierarchies.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference city in iasted is a geographic location (subclass of City). They denote completely different categories of entities.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. In edas, hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (the schedule of activities). In sigkdd, presentationed_by links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Conference Event vs Document), ranges (Programme vs Speaker), and overall semantics are disjoint, so no equivalence or subsumption holds.

Property A is an object property linking papers/posters/presentations to an Abstract entity (a class), while property B is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string. They differ in both property type (object vs datatype) and range (class vs string), so they do not denote the same relation.

These two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. 'updated Version Of' links a Document to another Document (its prior version), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (the person presenting it). They share only the Document domain; their ranges differ entirely and the semantic relationships they express are unrelated.

Invited_speaker is a specific role (a person invited to give a talk at a conference), whereas Member in confOf is a general participant category (sibling of Regular and Student). An invited speaker is not the same concept as a general member/participant, and neither clearly subsumes the other in the given hierarchies.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'detailsEnteredBy' (cmt) relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered conference details, while 'gives_presentations' (Conference) relates an Active conference participant to a Presentation they give. They connect different entity types in different directions for different purposes.

confOf Student is a person who is a participant in a conference (subclass of Participant, sibling of Member and Regular). sigkdd Best_Student_Paper_Supporter is a sponsor (subclass of Sponzor, sibling of Bronze/Gold/Platinum/Silver Supporter and Exhibitor). One denotes a student attendee; the other denotes a sponsor of a best student paper award. They share the word 'Student' but denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
A is a type of academic document (a paper presented at a workshop), while B is a type of road vehicle used for transport. They belong to completely unrelated domains and share no instances.

A Workshop is an academic event type (a meeting/session on a topic), whereas a Speaker lecture is a specific lecture given by a speaker within a session. They denote different concepts at different granularity levels in the conference domain.

confOf's Trip is a specific kind of social event (a sibling of Banquet and Reception under Social event), whereas edas's Social Event is the broader class whose children include Excursion and Reception. Trip corresponds more closely to edas:Excursion than to the entire Social Event category, so Trip is subsumed by Social Event.

Sponsorship in edas denotes a grant or financial support arrangement (e.g., Travel Grant) provided by an Organization to support attendance, with properties like cost amount, currency, and provider. Fee in sigkdd denotes a monetary charge collected from participants (e.g., Registration fee, Sponsor fee). These are conceptually distinct: a sponsorship is funding given to someone, while a fee is a charge paid by someone. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

A is a person role (Associated Chair, a kind of Chairman/Conference Member in cmt), while B is a conference event type (Closing Talk, a kind of Talk Event in edas). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

These two datatype properties are completely unrelated. Property A captures the submission deadline date for full papers (domain: Important dates, range: date). Property B captures whether a participant has registered early (domain: Participant, range: boolean). They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning — one is a deadline date, the other is a boolean flag on a participant.

Property A (has_a_committee_chair) relates a Committee to its Chair, while property B (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution. They have completely different domains and ranges and denote entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

Workshop in the Conference ontology is a conference part/event (sibling of Track and Tutorial), while Session room in iasted is a physical place (sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a person role (a kind of chairman/conference member) in the cmt ontology, while Conference hall is a physical place (a kind of Place) in the sigkdd ontology. They denote completely different categories of entities: a human role vs. a location. No alignment relationship holds.

confOf:Submission_event is a temporal Event (subclass of Administrative event) denoting the submission phase/period during conference organization. iasted:Submission is a Document artifact (subclass of Document) with children like Final manuscript and Initial manuscript, i.e., the submitted paper itself. One is an event/occurrence, the other is a physical/document object; they do not share instances.

Closing Talk is a specific talk event that occurs at the end of a conference (sibling of Welcome Talk), whereas Plenary lecture is a general lecture delivered to all conference participants. They denote different concepts: a closing talk is defined by its temporal/functional role, while a plenary lecture is defined by its audience scope. Neither subsumes the other.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and express different relations. In EDAS, belongsToEvent links a Programme (a document/schedule artefact) to a Conference Event, indicating that the programme belongs to or covers an event. In EKAW, partOfEvent links an Event to an Event, expressing a mereological part-whole relation between events (e.g., a session is part of a conference). Since one relates a programme artefact to an event and the other relates events to events, they do not denote the same relation, nor is there a clear subsumption between them.

In ontology A, Conference denotes the conference event itself (with a name, proceedings, publisher, topics), while in ontology B, Conference activity denotes activities that occur during a conference (cocktail reception, coffee break, lecture, registration, etc.). These are completely different concepts: one is the conference as an entity, the other is an activity taking place at a conference. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated things in the domain.

Publisher is a general class for publishing entities (issues Conference proceedings). ACM SIGKDD is a specific conference organizer that holds conferences, designs deadlines, and searches for sponsors. They are different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties are completely different. 'obtain' in iasted is an object property relating Person to Item (a person obtaining an item). 'City_of_conference' in sigkdd is a datatype property relating Conference to string (the city where a conference takes place). They have different domains, different ranges, different property types, and entirely different meanings.

cmt:Conference denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, members, administrators), while ekaw:Conference_Paper is a subclass of Paper representing a written document submitted to a conference. One is an event, the other is a document; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations. `partOfEvent` in EKAW links an Event to another Event (part-whole relation between events). `presentationed_by` in SIGKDD links a Document to a Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). They share no common domain or range types and no semantic overlap.

The property 'rejectedBy' in cmt relates a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while 'writes' in confOf relates an Author to a Contribution they authored. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics; they do not denote the same relation.

Chairman in cmt is a role-based class for people who chair committees or the conference (Associated Chair, Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), whereas Conference Participant in ekaw is a participation-based class for anyone attending the conference (including Early/Late Registered Participant, Presenter, Student, etc.). Although both are subclasses of Person, their intended instances do not coincide: a Chairman is not necessarily a participant, and a Conference Participant is not necessarily a chair. They are disjoint role vs. participation categories, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or subsuming.

confOf:Member is a person who is a participant and member (e.g., of a committee or organization), sitting under Person > Participant alongside Regular and Student. sigkdd:Registration_Student is a fee category for student registration, sitting under Fee > Registration_fee alongside other registration fee types. One denotes a person role; the other denotes a monetary fee. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Workshop in edas is a type of academic event (a conference session where papers are presented), while Organizing Committee in sigkdd is a committee responsible for organizing the conference. These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a group of people.

Organizer denotes a person or organization that organizes a conference, while Listener (a subclass of Delegate in iasted) denotes a conference attendee who listens to presentations. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: an organizer runs the event, a listener merely attends it. No subsumption relationship holds between them.

Chairman in cmt is a general role whose children include Associated Chair, Conference Chair, and Program Committee Chair. PC Member in ekaw is a Possible Reviewer whose children include PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, Tutorial Chair, and Workshop Chair. The two classes overlap (e.g., PC Chair is a child of both), but Chairman includes non-PC roles like Conference Chair, while PC Member includes roles like Session Chair and Tutorial Chair that are not chairmen. Neither class subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related but not equivalent.

cmt's Paper is a broad class covering all papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties like hasDecision linking to Decision). Conference's Accepted contribution is a specific subclass in a deep hierarchy (Submitted > Reviewed > Accepted), representing only papers that have been accepted. Paper subsumed_by Accepted contribution is incorrect direction; rather, Paper is more general (includes submitted, under-review, accepted, rejected), while Accepted contribution is the narrow set of accepted ones. So Paper is subsumed_by... actually Paper is MORE general, so Accepted_contribution is subsumed_by Paper. Correct relation: subsumes (A subsumes B). But given options, A=Paper is more general than B=Accepted contribution, so relation is 'subsumes'.

Property A (has_tracks) relates a Conference volume to a Track (a topical subdivision of the conference). Property B (heldIn) relates an Event to a Location (a physical or virtual place). They connect entirely different domain and range types and denote different relations, so they are unrelated.

Organization in edas denotes an organizational entity (with subclasses like Academia, Government, Industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who gives presentations (with subclasses Author and Invited Speaker). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (has_parts) relates a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (mereological/compositional relation). Property B (presentationed_by) relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it. They connect entirely different kinds of entities and express different relationships (part-whole vs. presenter-of-document), so they are unrelated.

Meal Break is a catering/rest break during the conference schedule (siblings: Coffee Break, Free Time Break), while Conference Trip is a social event like a banquet or excursion. They are different kinds of non-academic conference events with no overlap in intended instances.

Social Event in edas is a non-academic conference event such as an excursion or reception, whereas Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes the conference. These denote completely different categories of entities (an event vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its Program Committee Members (people). In ekaw, listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a specific subpart of a Paper (a sibling of 'Paper Full Version' under Paper), representing the abstract document of a paper. In edas, 'Paper' is the top-level class for submitted papers with various status-based subclasses (Accepted, Rejected, etc.) and properties like being reviewed by reviewers. A paper abstract is a component of a paper, not the paper itself, so these classes denote different concepts with no direct alignment relationship.

Web Site and Abstract are both subclasses of Document, but they denote different artefacts: a web site (online resource) versus a textual abstract of a paper. They are sibling-level document types with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but they differ in domain and meaning. In EDAS, hasSubmissionDeadline applies to Call (for papers) and denotes a submission deadline. In IASTED, is_dated_on applies to Activity and denotes a general date. A submission deadline is a kind of date, but the properties relate to different subject types and are not equivalent.

confOf:employedBy relates a Person to an Organization they work for, while iasted:obtain relates a Person to an Item they receive. The domains (Person) coincide but the ranges differ (Organization vs Item) and the intended relations are semantically distinct (employment vs acquisition).

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. `hasReviewHistory` links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (reviewer -> history), while `reviewWrittenBy` links a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it (review -> reviewer). They are not inverses in a strict sense either, since the range of one (Personal Review History) is not the domain of the other (Review). They denote different relations in the conference domain.

Author (cmt) is a person who writes/submits papers, sitting under Person > Conference Member. Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a session, initiates calls, and can review papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain; neither subsumes the other, and their intended instances do not coincide.

These properties have different domains and ranges and denote different concepts. `has_a_date_of_issue` relates a Conference document to a date (when the document was issued), while `registrationDueOn` relates a Conference to a dateTime (the registration deadline). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract version of a conference paper. Gold Supporter in sigkdd is a subclass of Sponzor representing a gold-level sponsor of the conference. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

A Paper Full Version is a conference document (full paper manuscript) under Document > Paper, while a Computer is physical audiovisual equipment under Item > Audiovisual equipment. They share no instances and occupy unrelated branches of their ontologies.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference participant' is a direct subclass of Person with children Active/Passive conference participant, covering anyone who participates in the conference. In confOf, 'Member' is a subclass of Participant (itself under Person) with siblings Regular and Student, suggesting it denotes a specific registration category (e.g. a member of an organization/society) rather than any participant. Thus Member is narrower than Conference participant, and the two are not equivalent.

Contact Information is a composite data structure (with city, email, phone, postal code, street) while City is a geographic location with subtypes like Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city, Trip city. They are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a conference reception), whereas iasted:Card is a physical item (with a child Credit card and siblings like Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes or submits a paper, sitting under Person > Conference Member. In the Conference ontology, Organizer denotes a person who organizes the conference event (logistics, committee work). An author and an organizer are distinct roles in the conference domain; neither subsumes the other.

In EDAS, Paper Presentation is a specific kind of academic event where an accepted paper is presented. In EKAW, Individual Presentation is a broader scientific event category that subsumes Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, and Tutorial. A paper presentation corresponds to a contributed talk, which is a child of Individual Presentation, so EDAS Paper Presentation is subsumed by EKAW Individual Presentation rather than equivalent.

writePaper relates an Author to a Paper they author, while has_an_abstract relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract. They connect completely different domain and range types and express different relationships.

Chairman in cmt is a person role (parent: Person) with sub-roles like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair. Presentation in iasted is an activity (parent: Conference activity) with sub-types like Power Point presentation and Video presentation. These denote completely different concepts: a person vs. an event/activity.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Computer Networks Enterprise Topic' is a specific subject topic (a subclass of 'Topic' under 'Computer Networks Topic'), representing a research subject area. In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Program Committee' is a committee (a subclass of 'Committee') responsible for reviewing papers and organizing the conference program. There is no overlap in intended instances between a topic and a committee.

Workshop in edas is an academic event (a kind of conference event), while Workshop Chair in ekaw is a person who chairs a workshop. These are completely different categories of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

Both properties relate a review-related object to a Reviewer, but the domains differ: cmt:writtenBy has domain Review (the review itself), while edas:isReviewHistoryOf has domain Personal Review History (a history/record of reviews). A Review and a Personal Review History are distinct concepts, so the properties are not equivalent, though they are related by a shared pattern of linking review artefacts to reviewers.

`has authors` links a Conference document to a Person (the author of the document), while `occupy` links a Person to a Building, City, or State (a location the person occupies). They relate completely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

The two properties have opposite domain/range orientations. In cmt, hasAuthor links Paper -> Author (paper has an author). In sigkdd, submit links Author -> Paper (author submits a paper). They are not the same relation, nor is one a subrelation of the other; they describe different actions (authorship attribution vs. submission), so they are unrelated.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Call for participation' in ontology Conference is a conference document (a publication/announcement artifact), sibling to 'Call for paper', 'Conference announcement', etc. 'Modelling' in iasted is a research activity performed before a conference, sibling to 'Simulating'. One is a document/announcement, the other is a research activity. They share no semantic relationship in the conference domain.

Both denote a cocktail reception social event at a conference. EDAS places Reception under Social Event (a non-academic event), and IASTED places Coctail reception as a conference activity. The labels are near-synonymous (Reception / Coctail reception) and both refer to the same kind of social gathering common at conferences.
