ekaw:PC Member is a committee member (under Possible Reviewer, with specialized chairs as children), while iasted:IASTED member is a delegate attending a conference (under Delegate). They denote different concepts: programme-committee membership vs conference-organisation membership/attendance.

In iasted, 'Introduction of speaker' is a subclass of Activity > Conference activity > Introduction, meaning it denotes an event/activity where a speaker is introduced. In sigkdd, 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Person > Speaker, meaning it denotes a person who gives an invited talk. One is an activity, the other is a person; they are disjoint kinds of entities and are unrelated.

Both are roles held by a Person responsible for overseeing a conference, but they come from different organizational models. In cmt, Conference Chair is a sub-role of Chairman (alongside Associated Chair and Program Committee Chair), whereas in sigkdd, General Chair is a sub-role of Organizator (alongside Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, Webmaster). The labels and sibling structures suggest they are analogous leadership roles rather than exactly the same concept; a reference alignment would typically treat them as related (overlapping) rather than equivalent.

Conference participant in ontology Conference is a broad class covering all persons who participate in a conference, with children Active conference participant and Passive conference participant. PC Chair in ekaw is a specific role (a PC Member who chairs the programme committee). Every PC Chair is a conference participant, but not vice versa, so Conference participant subsumes PC Chair.

Both properties express membership, but they differ in domain and range. In Conference, 'was a member of' links Committee member to Committee. In edas, 'is Member Of' links Person to Conference. The edas property is more general: its domain (Person) is broader than Committee member, and its range (Conference) is broader than Committee. Thus 'was a member of' is subsumed by 'is Member Of'.

Both are object properties linking a written document/artefact to the person who authored it: in edas, Paper isWrittenBy Author; in iasted, Item is_prepared_by Person. 'Item' in iasted denotes a conference paper/contribution and 'Person' subsumes authors, so the two properties relate the same kinds of entities in the same direction. The labels differ but the intended relation (document authored by a person) coincides.
has_a_URL is a datatype property from Conference www to string, while hasEvent is an object property from Event to Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

These properties relate entirely different things. In Conference, 'has_a_steering_committee' links a Conference volume to its Steering committee (a specific subcommittee). In sigkdd, 'hold' links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference it organizes. The domains (Conference volume vs. ACM SIGKDD), ranges (Steering committee vs. Conference), and the nature of the relationship (having a subcommittee vs. organizing an event) are all different, so these properties are unrelated.

These properties differ in both structure and semantics. Property A (is_an_abstract_submission_date) is a datatype property with domain Important_dates and range date, representing the date value itself. Property B (submit_until) is an object property with domain Document and range Deadline, linking a document to a deadline entity. They operate at different modeling levels and relate different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

In ontology Conference, 'Conference document' is a class for documents such as calls for papers, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc. In ontology sigkdd, 'Conference' is a class for the conference event itself, with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. These are completely different concepts: one is a document/artefact, the other is an event. They share the word 'conference' but denote unrelated entities in the domain.

Call_for_paper in the Conference ontology is a conference document announcing a paper submission deadline, while CommunicationsTopic in edas is a subject-area topic (a technical category like Antennas or Computer Networks). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Review in the Conference ontology is the general class of all reviews, while Negative_Review in ekaw is a specific subclass of Review denoting only negative reviews. Thus Review is strictly more general than Negative_Review, so Review is subsumed_by Negative_Review's parent (ekaw Review), making the relation subsumed_by.
A is a type of presentation (an activity/artefact), while B is a type of person who organizes a conference. They belong to disjoint domains and share no instances.

confOf:hasEmail is a datatype property from Person to string (an email address), whereas iasted:send is an object property from Person to Item (sending an item such as a document). They differ in type, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

confOf's Paper is a Contribution (a document submitted to a conference), while sigkdd's Best Applications Paper Award is an Award given to a paper. They are completely different kinds of entities: one is the paper itself, the other is a prize/award. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap exists between them.

The cmt 'assign Reviewer' property relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (the act of assigning someone as a reviewer), while the iasted 'write' property relates a Person to an Item (the act of authoring a document). These are completely different relations: one is about assigning reviewers to papers, the other about authoring items. They have different domains, different ranges, and denote different actions in the conference organization domain.

Property A (is_made_from) relates Item to Item, describing composition or material origin. Property B (can_stay_in) relates Person to Place, describing accommodation. Different domains, ranges, and semantics; no overlap.

A is a person role (Associated Chair under Chairman/Person in cmt), while B is a conference document (Call for participation under Conference document). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

Paper in edas is a document submitted to a conference (subclass of Document, with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.), while Credit card in iasted is a financial payment card (subclass of Card > Item). These denote completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A is a rating value (a subclass of Review Rating) used to classify a review's recommendation, whereas B is a concrete document (a paper that has been evaluated and rejected). One denotes an evaluation verdict/code, the other denotes the paper artefact itself; their instances do not coincide.
Reception is a social event in the conference domain, while Credit card is a financial item/card; they share no domain meaning.

Both classes denote the general concept of a person involved in a conference. They share the same label, overlapping children (Author, Chair/Session Chair, Member PC/TPC Member, Participant/Attendee), and common properties such as hasEmail and hasFirstName. The structural position and intended instances coincide across the two ontologies.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document (e.g., logistical information for attendees), while 'Antennas Topic' in the edas ontology is a subject topic for paper classification. They share no instances and no semantic relationship.

Property A (is_the_1th_part_of) relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation, indicating that an abstract is a part of a paper or presentation. Property B (volumeContainsPaper) relates a proceedings volume to a paper, indicating that a volume contains a paper. These properties connect completely different domain and range entities (Abstract->Paper vs. Volume->Paper) and express different relationships (part-of vs. containment). They are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In confOf, 'follows' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal/sequential ordering). In sigkdd, 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (receiving an award). There is no overlap in the types of things they connect or the relation they express.

Property A (has_an_abstract) links papers/posters/presentations to their abstracts, while property B (writes) links authors to the contributions they write. They relate entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships.

Academic Institution in ekaw is an organization (parent Organisation, children University and Research Institute), whereas Author in sigkdd is a person (parent Speaker, parent chain Person). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.
A 'Call For Papers' is an announcement soliciting submissions, while a 'Conference Paper' is the written document itself. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria). In confOf, 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (a paper). The domains (Conference vs. Author) and ranges (Administrator vs. Contribution) are disjoint, and the intended meanings share no overlap.

The property 'is Written By' in edas relates a Paper to its Author, while 'pay' in sigkdd relates a Person to a Registration fee. These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no overlap or subsumption between them.

Both properties relate a presented/published item to a person, but the domains and ranges differ: A links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the speaker), while B links a Contribution (written paper) to an Author (the writer). A presentation being given by a participant is not the same relation as a contribution being written by an author, though the concepts overlap in the conference domain.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person and represents a registered user of the conference management system (with subclasses Administrator, Author, Reviewer). In edas, Person is the top-level class for all people in the conference domain (with children Attendee, Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member, etc.). The edas Person class is more general: it includes attendees and other conference participants who may not be registered system users. cmt's User is a narrower concept (system users) subsumed by edas's Person, but the two are not equivalent since their intended instances do not coincide.

Property A (issues) relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings it publishes. Property B (topicCoveredBy) relates a Research Topic to Events or Papers that cover that topic. They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships (publication vs. topic coverage).

Conference Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion or outing organized as part of a conference), while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation/place. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different kinds of entities.

confOf:Reception is a social event (a banquet-like gathering) that occurs during a conference, while iasted:Accepting_manuscript is an administrative activity before the conference involving accepting/rejecting submitted manuscripts. They share no instances and belong to completely different parts of the conference-organisation domain.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. `has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution` links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic, capturing what a reviewer is willing or prefers to review. `hasReviewHistory` links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History, recording the reviewing track record of a person. The domains (Review preference vs Reviewer), ranges (Submitted contribution/Topic vs Personal Review History), and intended semantics are disjoint, so they are unrelated.

In edas, 'Single Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference denoting a conference with a single organisational level. In iasted, 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time and has children such as Delegate and One conference day, indicating it represents a temporal period during a conference rather than the conference event itself. These are structurally and semantically different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties connect entirely different domain and range types. 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (where a paper is submitted), while 'hasMember' links a Conference to a Person (organizational membership). They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap.

The two properties relate completely different entities and express different relations. In cmt, 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (a meta-reviewer assignment relation). In confOf, 'writes' links an Author to the Contribution they author. The domains (External Reviewer vs Author), ranges (Reviewer vs Contribution), and intended meanings (reviewer assignment vs authorship) are disjoint, so these properties are unrelated.

confOf 'Submission event' is an event (a temporal occurrence of submitting contributions), while ekaw 'Accepted Paper' is a document (the paper artefact that has been accepted). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Document) and denote fundamentally different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Scholar is a subclass of Person (a human role, with a 'study At' property linking to University), while iasted:Memeber_registration_fee is a subclass of Registration fee under Money (a monetary amount charged for registration). One denotes a person, the other a fee; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption hierarchy.

In cmt, 'Co author' is a specific subclass of Author denoting a person who co-writes a paper (a secondary contributor, distinct from the primary author). In iasted, 'Author' is a broad class under Speaker encompassing various presenter/lecturer types (e.g., plenary speakers, tutorial speakers, lecturers). The iasted Author is about conference presenters who may have authored proceedings, while cmt's Co author is narrowly a co-writer of a paper. These are different concepts at different levels of generality and with different intended instances, so they are not equivalent. Given the specificity mismatch and different domain context, they are best considered unrelated rather than in a subsumption relation.

Active conference participant is a person (subclass of Person > Conference contributor) who participates in a conference, e.g. gives presentations. Conference activity is an event/activity (subclass of Activity) such as a cocktail reception, lecture, or registration. One denotes a person, the other an activity; they share no instances and are unrelated.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion, banquet, reception) organised as part of a conference, while iasted:Departure is an activity occurring after the conference (e.g., leaving/departing from the venue). Although both are sub-events/activities, their intended instances do not coincide: a Trip is a social outing, whereas a Departure refers to the act of leaving. They are not synonyms, and neither subsumes the other in a clear, reference-alignment sense.

Conference city (iasted) is a subclass of City, denoting the city where a conference takes place. Hotel (sigkdd) is a subclass of Place, denoting accommodation. These are distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In confOf, Conference is a kind of event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the academic meeting itself. In sigkdd, Hotel is a place (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference hall and Main office), denoting accommodation. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In edas, 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (the person whose review history it is). In iasted, 'write' links a Person to an Item (the artefact they authored). The domains and ranges differ (Personal Review History vs Person; Reviewer vs Item), and the intended semantics are distinct: one records a review history belonging to a reviewer, the other records authorship of a document/item. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

Property A (isWrittenBy) relates a Paper to its Author, expressing authorship. Property B (presentationed_by) relates a Document to a Speaker, expressing who presented the document. These are distinct relations: authorship vs. presentation. The domains (Paper vs. Document) and ranges (Author vs. Speaker) differ, and the intended semantics are unrelated.

finalizePaperAssignment is a CMT-specific action where an Administrator finalizes paper assignments for a Conference. technicallyOrganises is an EKAW property where an Organisation technically organises some event. The domains (Administrator vs Organisation), ranges (Conference vs unspecified event), and semantics (finalizing paper assignment vs technical organization of an event) are entirely different.

hasPostalCode relates organizations and persons to their postal (zip) code, while E-mail relates persons to their email address. These are completely different attributes of a person/organization with no semantic overlap.

In iasted, Money is a broad superclass covering Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, and Tip. In sigkdd, Registration_fee is a specific subclass of Fee. Thus Registration_fee is a specific kind of monetary amount, making it strictly narrower than the general Money class. The relation is subsumed_by.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges and express different relations. In cmt, addProgramCommitteeMember relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (the act of adding a PC member). In sigkdd, presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presented the document). There is no overlap in intended meaning.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a short version of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject-area classification under Topic in the edas ontology. They belong to completely different hierarchies (documents vs. topics) and share no domain overlap.

These properties operate in completely different domains. 'relatedToEvent' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (associating a paper with its presentation event). 'awarded_by' links an Award to some entity that grants the award. They have different domains (Accepted Paper vs. Award), different ranges, and express fundamentally different relationships in the conference domain.

A 'Double hotel room' is a lodging accommodation for guests (a subtype of Hotel room), while a 'Conference hall' is a meeting/event space within a conference venue. They serve entirely different purposes and share no instance overlap. Both are subclasses of Place, but they are sibling-level concepts with no meaningful semantic relationship in the conference domain.

Personal Publication History is a history/record of an individual's publications, while Cd proceening is a concrete publication artefact (a CD-ROM containing conference proceedings). They denote entirely different kinds of things: one is a biographical record, the other a physical/digital publication medium.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a subclass of Social Event, denoting an organized trip activity during a conference. Conference hall in iasted is a subclass of Place, denoting a physical location where conference sessions are held. One is an event/activity, the other is a physical space; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Active Paper (edas) denotes a paper that has been reviewed and assigned a rating (has Rating -> Review Rating), indicating it is in the review/evaluation phase. Assigned Paper (ekaw) denotes a paper that has been assigned (likely to reviewers for evaluation), a prerequisite step before evaluation. These overlap in practice—assigned papers that have received ratings are active—but they are not equivalent: an Assigned Paper may not yet have ratings (so not yet Active), and an Active Paper has ratings (so it must have been assigned). Neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related.

Review_expertise in Conference denotes the expertise/qualification level of a reviewer for a particular submitted contribution, linked to Reviewer and Submitted_contribution. Review in edas is a subclass of Document representing the actual review document written about a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts: one captures reviewer qualification/preference metadata, the other captures the review artefact itself. They share no instance overlap.

Paper in the Conference ontology is a regular conference contribution (a scholarly paper), situated under Conference contribution. Programme Brochure in ekaw is a document listing events, situated under Document alongside Paper. They are disjoint kinds of things: one is an academic contribution, the other a printed programme. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

In EDAS, 'Talk Event' is a broad class for spoken events at a conference, with children such as Closing Talk, Welcome Talk, and Paper Presentation. In IASTED, 'Tutorial' is a specific kind of Lecture (an instructional session), sibling to Plenary lecture and Session. A tutorial is a pedagogical event, not equivalent to the general notion of a talk event, and neither clearly subsumes the other since EDAS Talk Event includes non-instructional talks (welcome/closing) while IASTED Tutorial is specifically instructional.

Volunteer in confOf is a person who assists with conference logistics (a helper), while Reviewer in iasted is a delegate who reviews papers. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific conference-level chair role (a Chairman, sibling of Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), whereas SC Member in ekaw is a member of the (Senior) Program Committee, a reviewer role under Possible Reviewer. These are distinct organizational roles: one is a chair/co-chair position, the other a committee member/reviewer. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Acceptance is a subclass of Decision, i.e., the outcome of deciding to accept a paper (an information artefact). In iasted, Accepting manuscript is a subclass of Activity before conference, i.e., the physical/administrative process of receiving and accepting manuscripts. One is a decision record, the other is an organizational activity; they do not share instances.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) denoting a kind of conference event, while edas:SatelliteAndSpaceCommunicationsTopic is a subclass of Topic denoting a specific subject area. They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote completely different concepts.

Both properties relate a Paper to its authors, but they differ in scope: cmt's hasCo-author specifically links a Paper to a Co-author (a collaborator distinct from the primary author), while edas's isWrittenBy links a Paper to any Author (including sole or primary authors). Thus isWrittenBy is broader and subsumes hasCo-author in principle, but since the ranges (Co-author vs. Author) are not themselves confirmed equivalent, the safest reference alignment relation is 'related' rather than strict subsumption.

Camera Ready event in confOf is a subclass of Administrative event, representing a stage in the conference workflow (preparing camera-ready papers). Program Committee in sigkdd is a subclass of Committee, representing a group of people who review papers and make acceptance decisions. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document/artefact (child of Conference document) such as a call for papers or review. A 'Welcome address' is an activity/event (child of Conference activity) occurring during a conference. They belong to disjoint branches (documents vs activities) and denote completely different kinds of things.

Property A captures a person's first name, while property B captures a postal code for organizations and persons. They denote completely different attributes despite both being datatype properties with range string.

Invited Talk (ekaw) is a subclass of Individual Presentation under Event > Scientific Event, so it denotes an event/activity. Invited Speaker (sigkdd) is a subclass of Speaker under Person, so it denotes a person. These are disjoint categories (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

Property A (has_members) relates a Committee to its Committee member, i.e. it denotes membership in a committee. Property B (reviewes) relates a Member PC to a Contribution, i.e. it denotes the act of reviewing a paper. They have different domains and ranges and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Participant is a subclass of Person, representing a specific role (someone who participates in the conference, with subtypes like Member, Regular, Student). In ekaw, Person is the top-level class for all people, with children including Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student, and Agency Staff Member. Thus confOf:Participant is narrower than ekaw:Person; it corresponds more closely to ekaw:Conference Participant than to ekaw:Person itself.

The two properties operate in opposite directions and connect fundamentally different entity types. In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC (reviewer) to a Contribution (paper being reviewed). In edas, 'isReviewHistoryOf' links a Personal Review History (a record/artifact of reviewing activity) to a Reviewer (the person who performed the review). The confOf property is reviewer->paper, while the edas property is review-history-record->reviewer. They do not share the same domain, range, or direction, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties have different domains and model different aspects of the conference domain. In cmt, 'readByReviewer' links a Paper to the Reviewer(s) who read it. In the Conference ontology, 'belongs_to_reviewers' links a Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer, indicating which reviewer an expertise/preference belongs to. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction.

PC Chair in ekaw denotes the chair of the Programme Committee, while General Chair in sigkdd denotes the overall conference chair. These are distinct organizational roles in conference organization, with different responsibilities and scopes, so they are not equivalent.

Property A (reviews) relates a Review to the Reviewed contribution it evaluates. Property B (updatedVersionOf) relates a Document to another Document of which it is an updated version. They connect entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to its acceptance/rejection Decision. In the Conference ontology, belongs_to_a_review_reference links a Topic to a Review preference (i.e., a reviewer's preference for reviewing papers on that topic). They share no common domain, range, or semantics.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a manuscript for review), whereas speak_in relates a Person to a Place or Time (the act of giving a presentation at a location/time). These are different relations with different domains and ranges, denoting different activities in the conference domain.

These properties are completely different. 'reviewsPerPaper' is a datatype property from Conference to int, representing the number of reviews assigned per paper. 'write' is an object property from Person to Item, representing the act of a person writing an item. They have different domains, different ranges, and different meanings.

The two properties have different domains and ranges: 'is present' relates a Person to a Time (indicating when someone is present), while 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (indicating where someone can stay). They denote different relations in the conference domain and do not overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'belong to a conference volume' links Important dates to a Conference volume, whereas 'organised By' links Events to an Organisation or Person (the organiser). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so they do not denote the same relation.

Both are datatype properties with range string capturing an email address, but their domains differ: confOf:contactEmail applies to Contribution (the paper's contact email) while edas:hasEmail applies to Person or Contact Information (a person's email). They overlap in the conference domain but do not relate the same kinds of things, so they are related rather than equivalent.

The cmt property 'has Decision' links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while the iasted property 'go through' links an Item to an Activity (a process the item undergoes). These are fundamentally different relations: one captures a decision outcome about a paper, the other captures an item participating in an activity/process. Their domains and ranges differ in meaning, and they do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In cmt, hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (Program Committee -> Program Committee Member). In Conference, has_a_program_committee links a Conference volume to a Program committee (Conference volume -> Program committee). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other; they operate at different levels of granularity and connect different kinds of things.

Rejected contribution is a document/artefact (a paper that was reviewed and rejected), while Accepting manuscript is an activity (the act of accepting a manuscript). They are different kinds of entities entirely, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Rejection is a Decision (an outcome of the paper review process, alongside Acceptance). In edas, Reject Rating is a Review Rating (a score assigned by a reviewer to a paper, alongside Accept Rating, Accept If Room Rating, Weak Reject Rating). A decision and a rating are different kinds of things: a rejection is a final decision made by a chair/committee, while a reject rating is a reviewer's assessment score. They do not denote the same concept.

These properties denote completely different relations. In cmt, 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who initiated the reviewer bidding process (a meta/administrative action on the conference itself). In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution, meaning the PC member reviews (writes a review for) a specific paper. They have different domains (Conference vs Member PC), different ranges (Administrator vs Contribution), and express unrelated concepts: one is about who started a bidding phase, the other is about who reviews which paper.

The two properties operate in completely different domains. 'location Of' is an object property relating a Location to an Event, while 'has amount of' is a datatype property relating Money to an integer value. They share no semantic overlap.

The cmt 'email' property associates a Person with a string email address, while the iasted 'is dated on' property associates an Activity with a dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Conference contributor (A) is a Person who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker, participant), while IASTED non member (B) is a Delegate who is not an IASTED member. The former is defined by contribution role, the latter by membership status. Their instances do not necessarily coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Late paid applicant is a person who registered late and paid (a registration status under Person), while Published Paper is a document (a paper that has been published). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Document) and share no instances.

confOf:Reception is a social event (a gathering/activity), while iasted:Registration_fee is a monetary amount charged for conference registration. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (Event vs Money) and share no semantic overlap.

These properties denote different deadlines in the conference lifecycle. `manuscriptDueOn` in edas relates a Conference to a dateTime representing the manuscript submission deadline, while `notification_until` in sigkdd relates an Author to a Deadline object representing the author notification deadline. They differ in domain (Conference vs. Author), range (dateTime vs. Deadline Author notification), and semantics (manuscript submission deadline vs. notification deadline). They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only weakly related as both concern conference deadlines.

In ontology Conference, 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' with children like Paper, Poster, Presentation, and Written contribution—it denotes a scholarly artefact (a paper or talk) submitted to a conference. In edas, 'Conference' denotes the event/organisation itself, with properties like hasCountry, paperDueOn, and subtypes Single/Two Level Conference. These are completely different concepts: a contribution (document) vs. the conference (event). No subsumption or overlap.

The property 'has Surname' in confOf denotes the family name of a Person, while 'Nation' in sigkdd denotes the nationality/country of a Person. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they capture completely different attributes of a person and are not semantically related.

In ekaw, Presenter is a person who presents at a conference (a Conference Participant). In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker and is specifically a person who writes papers (with children like 'Author book proceedings included', 'Author cd proceedings included'). While a presenter may also be an author, the two concepts are distinct: Presenter focuses on the act of presenting, while Author focuses on authorship of publications. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way given the different ontological structures.

Property A (hasTitle) maps a Contribution to a string (its title), while property B (has_amount_of) maps Money to an int (a monetary amount). They have different domains, different ranges, and denote completely different relations.

Entity A is a specific conference topic about satellite and space communications, a subclass of Topic. Entity B is a Tutorial, a type of lecture/conference activity. These are completely different concepts: one denotes a subject area for papers/sessions, the other denotes an instructional event at a conference. No overlap in intended instances.

The edas Workshop is a type of academic event (a conference event where papers are presented), while the iasted Plenary lecture speaker is a person who delivers a plenary lecture. One is an event, the other is a person/role; they share no instances and are not related.

Multimedia Topic in edas is a subject area (a Topic) under which conference papers can be classified, while Computer in iasted is a physical piece of audiovisual equipment used at a conference venue. They denote completely different categories of things with no overlap in intended instances.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a document), while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. 'author Of' (ekaw) has domain Person and range Document, expressing that a person authored a document. 'is given to' (iasted) has domain Item and range Person, expressing that an item is given to (e.g., awarded to) a person. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other; they are unrelated.

Pending Paper in edas is a paper whose review decision has not yet been made, a specific review-state subclass of Paper. Submission in iasted is a broader document category covering submitted items including initial and final manuscripts. They overlap (a pending paper is a kind of submission) but are not equivalent: Submission includes final manuscripts and is not restricted to the pending-review state, while Pending Paper is specifically about review status.

In cmt, Reviewer is a person (subclass of Person > Conference Member) who reviews papers. In confOf, Reviewing_event is an event (subclass of Event > Administrative event) representing the reviewing procedure. These are completely different types of entities: a person vs. an event.

These properties operate at different levels of abstraction. In EDAS, 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History (an aggregate/record of a reviewer's reviewing activity) to a Reviewer, essentially tracking who has a given review history. In EKAW, 'review Written By' links an individual Review to the person who wrote it. The domains differ (Personal Review History vs. Review) and the semantics are distinct: one associates a history record with a reviewer, the other associates a single review artifact with its author. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different entities. `belongs to a review reference` links a Topic to a Review preference, capturing topic-reviewer preference information. `belongsToEvent` links a Programme to a Conference Event, capturing which event a programme belongs to. They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relations in the conference domain.

confOf:hasCity is an object property whose range is the class City, while edas:hasCity is a datatype property whose range is the string literal type. They differ in both the kind of property (object vs datatype) and the nature of the value (an individual of class City vs a plain string), so they cannot be equivalent.

Paper Abstract is a short summary of a research paper (path: Document > Paper > Paper Abstract), while Cheque is a payment instrument (path: Item > Document > Payment document > Cheque). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In confOf, Conference is the main conference event (parent Working event, siblings Tutorial and Workshop). In iasted, Tutorial is a specific lecture/session type (path Activity > Conference activity > Lecture > Tutorial, siblings Plenary lecture and Session). These denote completely different kinds of things: a whole conference versus a tutorial session within a conference.

hasSurname denotes a person's family/last name, while hasFirstName denotes a person's given/first name. These are distinct attributes of a person and not the same relation, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

hasStreet relates Contact Information to a street name string, while Name relates Person to a person's name string. They describe different attributes of different entities and do not denote the same relation.

logoURL points to a logo image (anyURI) for the conference, while City_of_conference gives the city name (string) where the conference is held. These are completely different attributes of a conference with no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. In EKAW, 'hasReview' links a Paper to a Review (a document written about the paper). In IASTED, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a lecture or presenting an item). The domains (Paper vs Person) and ranges (Review vs Activity/Item) do not overlap, and the relations describe different actions in the conference domain.

Country is a geographic entity (domain of hasCountry, range Conference->Country), while Person is a human agent with subtypes Listener, Organizator, Speaker and properties like E_mail, Name, Nation, pay. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Review Question in edas is a question in a review form (with numerical and textual subtypes), while Submission in iasted is a document submitted to a conference (with final/initial manuscript subtypes). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'author Of' in ekaw links a Person to a Document they authored, while 'is paid in' in iasted links Money to a Building. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a person (subclass of Person) who is a member of a conference, with subclasses like Author, Reviewer, Chair. Organizing committee in Conference ontology is a committee (a group/body, subclass of Committee), not an individual person. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one denotes individual people, the other denotes an organizational body. No equivalence or subsumption relationship holds.

Property A 'issues' has domain Publisher and range Conference proceedings, describing a publisher issuing proceedings. Property B 'prepare' has domain Person and range Item, describing a person preparing an item. The domains (Publisher vs Person), ranges (Conference proceedings vs Item), and semantics (issuing/publishing vs preparing/creating) are all different, so these properties are unrelated.

confOf:Organization denotes an institution (company, university) with address properties, while sigkdd:Document denotes a textual artefact (abstract, paper, review) with submission/presentation properties. Their intended instances are disjoint and they share no common domain semantics.

The property 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to a Review, capturing the peer-review process. The property 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document, capturing what a speaker presents. These are entirely different domain relationships with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Banquet is a sibling of Trip under Social event, meaning it denotes a banquet specifically. In ekaw, Conference Trip denotes a trip/excursion, and Conference Banquet is its sibling. Thus these two classes denote different kinds of social events (a banquet vs. a trip), so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Information for participants is a conference document providing logistical details to attendees, while Publication is a published item such as proceedings or CDs. They denote completely different kinds of things in the conference domain.

Conference Session in edas denotes a temporal event/session within a conference (a subclass of Academic Event), while Session room in iasted denotes a physical place (subclass of Place) where sessions are held. They are completely different concepts despite the shared word 'Session'.

Information for participants is a general informational document for conference attendees (e.g., logistics, program details), whereas Record of attendance is a specific document certifying that someone attended. They share the broad parent of conference document but denote different artefacts with different purposes.

hasFirstName relates a Person to their first name (a string), while Nation relates a Person to their nationality/country (also modeled as a string). These are completely different attributes of a person; neither subsumes the other.

Performance Topic is a subclass of Topic in the edas ontology, representing a subject area for conference submissions (e.g., performance-related technical topics). Organizing Committee is a subclass of Committee in the sigkdd ontology, representing a group of people who organize a conference. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Steering committee is a type of committee responsible for overseeing a conference volume, while University is a type of organization where scholars study. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. `locationOf` in ekaw relates a Location to an Event (indicating where an event takes place), while `is_used_for` in iasted relates an Item to an Activity or Money (indicating the purpose or use of an item). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Person/Chairman), while Conference activity in iasted is an event/activity during the conference (subclass of Activity, with children like Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Presentation). One is a person role, the other is an event type — completely different categories with no overlap.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. In Conference, 'is_a_topis_of_conference_parts' links a Topic to a Conference part (Topic -> Conference part). In edas, 'hasTopic' links a Conference or Paper to a Topic (Conference/Paper -> Topic). They are not inverses of each other either, since the domains and ranges do not align (Conference part vs Conference/Paper).

cmt:User is a person who interacts with the system (parent Person; children Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while ekaw:Proceedings_Publisher is an organisation that publishes proceedings (parent Organisation; siblings Academic Institution, Organising Agency). They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Organisation) and denote completely different kinds of entities.

The property 'has a publisher' in Conference links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organization that publishes the proceedings). The property 'relatesTo' in edas links a Document to various entities like Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, or Person, indicating a general relationship between a document and other conference entities. These are different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics; one is specifically about publication and the other is a generic association.

confOf:Short_paper is a type of contribution (a paper category, sibling of Paper and Poster), while iasted:Final_manuscript is a document artifact (a submission stage, sibling of Initial_manuscript). One classifies the nature of a contribution; the other denotes a specific document version. Their intended instances do not coincide.

In the edas ontology, 'Call' represents a call for papers/manuscripts/reviews—an announcement soliciting submissions, with properties like submission deadlines and instructions. In the sigkdd ontology, 'Document' is a general document class with children Abstract, Paper, and Review—actual artefacts produced for the conference. A Call is not itself a document but a solicitation for documents; their instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Signal Processing Topic is a subject-area topic under Topic in the edas ontology, representing a research domain. Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment under Item in the iasted ontology, representing a physical device. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Plenary lecture in iasted is a subclass of Lecture under Activity > Conference activity, denoting an event/activity (a talk given at a conference). Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Speaker under Person, denoting a person who gives an invited talk. One is an event, the other is a person; they are disjoint kinds of entities.

confOf:Author is a specific subclass of Person (a person who writes contributions), while ekaw:Person is the general class of all people, with children including Paper Author, Conference Participant, etc. Author is strictly narrower than Person, so it is subsumed_by ekaw:Person.

The cmt 'assignedTo' property assigns a Paper to a Reviewer (for peer review), while the sigkdd 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). These are distinct conference-domain relations: one concerns review assignment, the other concerns presentation delivery. The domains (Paper vs Document) and ranges (Reviewer vs Speaker) are different concepts, so the properties do not relate the same kinds of things in the same way.

Conference's 'Conference contribution' is a specific subclass of 'Conference document' covering contributions like papers, posters, and presentations. Edas's 'Document' is a broader class including Meal Menu, Programme, Slide Set, etc. 'Conference contribution' is strictly more specific than 'Document'.

Contributed Talk in ekaw is an event (a talk/session where a paper is presented), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives a presentation. One is a scientific event, the other is a person role; they are disjoint categories in the conference domain.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a type of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while iasted:Author_information_form is a document/form (a bureaucratic artefact, sibling of Hotel registration form and Registration form). These are completely different categories of entities in the conference domain: one is an organized gathering/session, the other is a paper or digital form to be filled in. No overlap in intended instances.

hasPhone is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's telephone number), while hasCall is an object property from Academic Event to Call (an event has a call for papers). They relate completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated concepts.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to attend a conference (pre-registration), while a 'Late Registered Participant' is a participant who registered after the normal deadline. An applicant has not yet been accepted/registered; a late-registered participant has already been accepted and registered (just late). These are different stages of the conference participation lifecycle and do not denote the same concept.

belongsToEvent relates a Programme to the Conference Event it belongs to, while organisedBy relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. They connect different entity types in different directions and express fundamentally different relationships (membership vs. agency).

cmt:writePaper has domain Author and range Paper, while iasted:write has domain Person and range Item. Since Author is a subconcept of Person and Paper is a subconcept of Item (as a conference paper is a kind of item), cmt:writePaper is more specific than iasted:write. The cmt property is subsumed by the more general iasted property.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. confOf:employedBy links a Person to an Organization (employment affiliation), while iasted:is_used_by links an Item to a Person (usage of an item by a person). The domains (Person vs Item) and ranges (Organization vs Person) are disjoint, and the intended meanings (employment vs usage) are unrelated.

Workshop is a type of conference part/event (e.g., a workshop session at a conference), while Program Committee is a committee of reviewers. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. The cmt property links a Conference to an Administrator (who printed hardcopy mailing manifests), while the edas property links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation. They share no common domain or range types and describe unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

Poster Paper is a type of academic paper (a document submitted/presented at a conference), while Cheque is a payment instrument. They share no domain overlap despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.

Conference's 'Committee member' is a general class for any member of any committee (with children Chair, Co chair, and siblings including Reviewer, Track workshop chair), covering all committee types. EKAW's 'OC Member' is specifically a member of the Organizing Committee, a single committee type. Thus 'Committee member' is strictly more general than 'OC Member'.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to the Conference contributions it contains, while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a presentation or lecture). The domains (Conference volume vs Person) and ranges (Conference contribution vs Activity/Item) do not overlap, and the relations denote fundamentally different associations in the conference domain.

Active Paper in EDAS denotes a paper that is currently under review (not yet accepted or rejected), as shown by its siblings (Accepted, Rejected, Pending, Published, Withdrawn) and its child Rated Paper. Rejected Paper in EKAW denotes a paper that has been evaluated and turned down. These are disjoint statuses: an active paper is still in process, while a rejected paper has reached a terminal negative decision. They do not overlap in intended instances.

Property A is a sub-property of 'was a member of' that specifically relates a Co-chair to a Committee they co-chaired. Property B relates a Person to a Conference they are a member of. They differ in both domain/range types and the specific relation they express (co-chairing a committee vs. being a member of a conference).

Individual Presentation in ekaw is a scientific event where a paper is presented (e.g., Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). Award in sigkdd is a prize given to authors (e.g., Best Paper Award). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and in meaning. `was a committee chair of` relates a Chair to a Committee (a leadership role), while `has Member` relates a Conference to a Person (general membership). They connect different kinds of entities and are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

Conference announcement is a document that announces a conference, while Book proceeding is a published collection of papers. They are different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Tutorial in the Conference ontology is a conference part/event (a session where tutorials are given), sibling to Track and Workshop, and the range of 'has tutorials'. Tutorial speaker in the iasted ontology is a person (a subclass of Author/Delegate) who speaks at a tutorial. One is an event, the other is a person; they are completely different concepts despite sharing the word 'Tutorial'.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In ekaw, SC Member is a person who serves on the Steering Committee (subclass of PC Member, sibling of various chair roles). In sigkdd, Registration SIGKDD Member is a fee category for SIGKDD members registering for the conference (subclass of Registration fee, sibling of other fee types). One is a person/role, the other is a monetary fee; they share no instances and are unrelated.

In edas, 'isWrittenBy' specifically relates a Paper to its Author. In iasted, 'is_signed_by' relates an Item (a more general document/artefact) to a Person (a more general agent). The iasted property is more general in both domain and range, so edas:isWrittenBy is subsumed by iasted:is_signed_by rather than being equivalent.

Property A (was_a_member_of) relates a Committee member to a Committee, expressing membership in a committee. Property B (give) relates a Person to an Activity or Item, expressing that a person gives (e.g., a presentation or lecture). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no overlap in meaning.

Workshop in EDAS is a distinct academic event type (a mini-conference with its own theme, organizers, and papers), whereas Poster Session in EKAW is a session within a conference where posters are presented. These are different kinds of conference activities; a workshop is not a poster session and vice versa. They share only the broad ancestor of 'Event'.

Personal Review History in edas is a history record associated with a reviewer (their past review activity), not an individual review. Review in iasted is a concrete document (child of Document) containing the actual review content. These are different kinds of entities: one is a personal history/record about reviewing activity, the other is a document artifact. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, representing a person who is a student (e.g., eligible for student awards or registration). In sigkdd, Gold Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor, representing a sponsor at the gold level. These are entirely different concepts: one is a person by academic status, the other is a sponsorship tier. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Technical commitee in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a conference attendee), placed among roles like Listener, Speaker, Session chair — it denotes a person who attends the conference in a technical-committee capacity. Organizator in sigkdd is a subclass of Person whose children are General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster — it denotes an organizer of the conference. An organizer is not necessarily an attendee (delegate), and a technical-committee delegate is not necessarily an organizer. The two concepts have different intended instances and no clear overlap, so they are unrelated.

Multi author Volume in EKAW denotes a collective work with multiple authors (e.g., proceedings, edited volumes), whereas Abstract in SIGKDD denotes a summary of a paper. They share the parent Document but represent distinct document types with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, Conference is the main conference entity with properties like hasCountry, hasName, paperDueOn, etc. In iasted, Conference_days is a subclass of Time representing the days on which the conference occurs, with children like Delegate and One_conference_day. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the conference event/organization itself, the other is a temporal period associated with the conference.

Pending Paper denotes a paper awaiting a decision, whereas Rejected Paper denotes a paper that has been evaluated and turned down. These are mutually exclusive states in the paper lifecycle, so they are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

Conference Participant in EKAW is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference (with children such as Presenter, Session Chair, PC Chair). Conference activity in IASTED is a subclass of Activity, denoting events or happenings during a conference (with children such as Registration, Lecture, Coffee break). One denotes a person role, the other an event/activity; they share no instances and are not related.

A is a topic within a subject taxonomy (Radio Communications Topic, sibling to Communication Theory Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.), while B is a type of conference presentation event (Contributed Talk, sibling to Invited Talk and Tutorial). They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Both classes describe people who contribute to a conference, but they are not equivalent. 'Conference contributor' in ontology A is a subclass of Person whose children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author—i.e., people who contribute content or participation. 'Delegate' in ontology B is a broad class (with multiple parents including Person, Registration, Conference building, and Conference days) whose children include Listener, Non speaker, Session chair, Speaker, and various member types. A Delegate is a registrant at a conference, which is a broader category than a contributor; some delegates (e.g., Listener, Non speaker) may not contribute at all, while contributors may not be formal delegates. The classes overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the best fit.

The two properties relate completely different domain and range types and describe unrelated aspects of the conference organization process. 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to the Administrator who started reviewer bidding, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present. There is no overlap in meaning, direction, or the kinds of entities involved.

Workshop in EDAS is an academic event (a conference session type, sibling of Paper Presentation and Talk Event). Renting in IASTED is a pre-conference logistical activity (sibling of Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). They share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

An Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a Chairman who assists in running the conference), whereas a Sponsor is an entity or person that provides financial support. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A links a reviewed contribution to its review, while property B links a document to an updated version of that document. They relate different kinds of things and express different relations.

Conference contribution is a document/artefact (paper, poster, presentation) submitted to a conference volume, while Registration fee is a monetary amount charged for attending a conference. They belong to entirely different ontological categories (document vs. money) with no overlap in intended instances.

AccpetIfRoomRating is a subclass of Review Rating, representing a rating value used in paper review decisions. Speaker is a subclass of Delegate, representing a person who presents at a conference. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, 'Conference fees' denotes the monetary charges associated with attending a conference (a fee/cost concept). In ontology B, 'Conference' denotes the conference event itself, with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. These are entirely different kinds of entities (a financial artifact vs. an event), so they are unrelated.

In iasted, Registration is an activity/event (subclass of Conference activity, sibling of Cocktail reception, Coffee break, etc.) representing the act of registering for a conference. In sigkdd, Registration Non Member is a fee (subclass of Registration fee, sibling of various member/student registration fees) representing a monetary amount charged to non-members. These denote fundamentally different concepts: an activity vs. a fee, so they are unrelated.

These properties are inverse in direction: 'has an organizing committee' links a conference volume to its organizing committee, while 'technically Organised By' links an event to the organization that organizes it. They are not equivalent (a property and its inverse are never equivalent), and their domains/ranges differ (conference volume vs. event, organizing committee vs. organizing organization), so they are not merely inverse but also operate on different entity types.

These properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. `relatedToEvent` in EDAS goes from Accepted Paper to Paper Presentation (paper -> presentation/event), while `presentationOfPaper` in EKAW goes from Individual Presentation to Paper (presentation -> paper). They connect similar entities but in opposite directions. A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent.
Paid applicant is a person who has paid a registration fee, while Social event is an event like a banquet or trip. They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and share no instances.

The iasted property 'has amount of' maps a Money instance to an integer monetary amount, whereas the sigkdd property 'Currency' maps a Registration fee to a string currency code/name. They relate to different aspects of a monetary value (numeric amount vs currency unit), have different domains (Money vs Registration fee) and different ranges (int vs string), so they do not denote the same relation.

Invited_speaker is a person (a conference contributor who gives an invited talk), while Introduction_of_speaker is an activity (the act of introducing a speaker). One denotes a person, the other an event/activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Property A 'is given by' relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it (oral delivery). Property B 'is writen by' relates an Item (written document) to the Person who authored it (authorship). These are distinct relations: one concerns presenting at a conference, the other concerns authoring a written item. They connect different domain/range pairs and denote different real-world relationships, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range types. 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members, while 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. They describe different relationships in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

Both are datatype properties named 'hasStreet' with range xsd:string, but their domains differ: confOf's hasStreet applies to Organization or Person, while edas's applies to Contact Information. Since Contact Information is a distinct concept (an information object) rather than a Person or Organization, the properties do not relate the same kinds of entities. They overlap conceptually (both capture a street address as a string) but are not equivalent.

Entity A is an event (a registration activity that occurs during a conference), while entity B is a deadline (a point in time by which camera-ready manuscripts must be submitted). They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies (Event vs Time) and denote fundamentally different concepts: one is an administrative activity, the other is a temporal milestone.

`is occupied by` relates a Building, City, or State to a Person who occupies it (physical/spatial occupancy). `payed by` relates a Registration fee to a Person who pays it (financial transaction). The domains (physical locations vs. fees) and the nature of the relationship (occupancy vs. payment) are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Committee in the Conference ontology is a group/organization body (with children Organizing committee, Program committee, Steering committee, and properties like has members, has committee chair). OC_Member in ekaw is a person who is a member of an organizing committee, sitting under Conference Participant > Person. One denotes the committee itself; the other denotes a person belonging to such a committee. They are disjoint kinds of entities.

Break Event in edas denotes a non-academic pause event (coffee break, meal break, free time) during a conference, whereas Lecture in iasted denotes an academic instructional/presentational activity (plenary lecture, tutorial, session). They occupy different branches of their respective event hierarchies and have disjoint intended instances.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). In iasted, Conference activity is a subclass of Activity, denoting events/activities that occur during a conference (cocktail reception, coffee break, lecture, presentation, etc.). One is a person, the other is an activity; they share no instances and are completely unrelated.

Reject Rating is a rating value used to classify a review's verdict as a rejection, while Negative Review is a review document whose content/conclusion is negative. They overlap in the sense that a review with a reject rating would typically be a negative review, but they are different kinds of entities: one is a rating/evaluation category, the other is a document. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

Chair PC in confOf is a specific role for the Program Committee chair, whereas Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a member of the Organizing Committee. These are distinct organizational roles in conference organization: the PC chair oversees the program/peer-review process, while an organizing committee member handles logistics. They do not share the same intended instances, and neither subsumes the other.

Break Event in edas denotes a rest/pause period (coffee break, meal break, free time) during a conference, whereas Technic activity in iasted denotes a technical session/activity (e.g., presentations, lectures). They are conceptually distinct: one is a non-academic intermission, the other an academic/technical program item. Their sibling sets overlap only superficially (Coffee break appears under both), but the intended classes do not coincide.

One conference day is a temporal concept (a day on which a conference takes place), while Conference hall is a spatial concept (a physical room/building where a conference is held). They belong to disjoint categories (Time vs Place) and share no instances.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer they were assigned by (an assignment relationship between people). In the Conference ontology, 'has a review reference or expertise' links a Reviewer to their review expertise or review preference (a relationship between a person and their expertise/preference). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so no equivalence or subsumption holds.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers, active participants), while Student in confOf is a participant who is a student. These are distinct concepts: a contributor is not necessarily a student, and a student participant is not necessarily a contributor. They share no clear overlap in intended instances.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: 'has an email' captures a person's email address, while 'has First Name' captures a person's given name. They do not overlap in meaning and neither subsumes the other.

Meal Event (edas) is a non-academic event like a conference dinner or banquet, characterized by having a menu. Scientific Event (ekaw) is an academic event such as a conference, session, or workshop. They are disjoint categories of events: one is social/catering, the other is academic/scientific. Neither subsumes the other.

Both classes denote the social banquet event of a conference. EKAW places 'Conference Banquet' under Social Event, while IASTED places 'Dinner banquet' under Social program (a sub-activity of Conference activity). The labels are near-synonyms and both are leaf classes representing the same real-world event in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In confOf, 'follows' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (e.g., one event following another). In iasted, 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item (e.g., a person obtaining an item). There is no overlap in the kinds of things related or the direction of the relation.

Pending Paper is a document (a paper awaiting review/decision), while Registation deadline is a temporal entity (a deadline for registration). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different domain concepts.

The property 'written By' in ekaw relates a Document to the Person who authored it, while 'submit until' in sigkdd relates a Document to a Deadline by which it must be submitted. They connect Documents to completely different kinds of objects (Person vs. Deadline) and express different relationships (authorship vs. submission deadline).

The cmt 'setMaxPapers' property relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member, likely setting a limit on papers assigned to a PC member. The iasted 'obtain' property relates a Person to an Item, indicating that a person obtains an item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

The property 'need' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they need, while 'presentation' in sigkdd relates a Speaker to a Document they present. These are different relations: needing an item vs. giving a presentation of a document. The domains (Person vs. Speaker) and ranges (Item vs. Document) also differ, and there is no indication that these properties denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Technical_commitee in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a conference attendee role), while Organizing_Committee_member in sigkdd is a subclass of Organizator (a person who organizes the conference). A technical committee member is a participant/delegate, not an organizer. These are distinct roles in conference organization with no direct subsumption relationship.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Conference proceedings is a published volume with ISBN, publisher, and volume number. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Signal Processing Topic is a subject-area topic (child of Topic, siblings are technical domains like Antennas, Cryptography, Mobile Computing). Invited Talk Abstract is a document type (child of Abstract under Document, sibling of Tutorial Abstract). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote completely different things: a research topic vs. a kind of conference document. No alignment relation holds.

In cmt, Paper is a document submitted for review with properties like hasAuthor, hasDecision, assignedTo reviewers, etc. In sigkdd, Registration fee is a monetary fee for conference registration with properties like price and currency. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'enterConferenceDetails' relates an Administrator to a Conference (the administrator enters conference details). In the Conference ontology, 'has_parts' relates a Conference volume to a Conference part (meronymy / part-whole relation). They do not denote the same relation.

A's 'Call for participation' is a document (subclass of Conference document), i.e. a textual artefact inviting participation. B's 'Reviewing event' is an event (subclass of Administrative event) representing the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions. One is a document, the other is an event/process; their instances do not coincide and they share no meaningful overlap.

Both properties express the same relationship: a written artefact (Paper / Item) is authored/sent by a person (Author / Person). In the conference domain, an Item submitted to a conference is a Paper, and the Author is a Person. The direction is identical (document -> author), and the labels 'is written by' and 'is sent by' are synonymous in this context.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'relatesTo' in edas links a Document to various entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person), indicating a general association between a document and things it relates to. 'scientificallyOrganisedBy' in ekaw links an event (implicitly) to an Academic Institution that scientifically organizes it, and is a subproperty of 'organisedBy'. They connect different types of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

The property 'isMemberOf' in edas relates a Person to a Conference (membership in the conference), while 'need' in iasted relates a Person to an Item (something the person needs). These are completely different relations with different ranges (Conference vs. Item) and different semantics (membership vs. need).

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has_tutorials' connects a Conference volume to Tutorial instances (i.e., the tutorials that are part of a conference). 'presentation' connects a Speaker to a Document (i.e., the document/presentation material associated with a speaker). They have different domains (Conference volume vs. Speaker), different ranges (Tutorial vs. Document), and different meanings. There is no overlap in what these properties express.

Departure in iasted is an activity that occurs after a conference (subclass of Activity after conference), while Conference_hall in sigkdd is a physical place (subclass of Place). One is an event/activity, the other is a location; they share no instances.

The two properties denote different attributes of a person: 'has an email' captures a person's email address, while 'has First Name' captures a person's first name (and possibly middle name per the comment). Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they relate Person to semantically distinct kinds of information, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Entity A is a class denoting a person (an early paid applicant) in the Conference ontology, while entity B is a class denoting a monetary amount (a member registration fee) in the iasted ontology. They belong to completely different branches of their respective hierarchies (Person vs. Money) and have no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (membership relation). In confOf, writes links an Author to a Contribution (authorship relation). The domains (Conference vs Author), ranges (Conference Member vs Contribution), and the nature of the relations (membership vs authorship) are all different, so these are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only very loosely related at best.

The two properties have different meanings and different ranges. In cmt, 'hasConferenceMember' links a Conference to its Conference Member (i.e., a person who is a member/participant of the conference). In sigkdd, 'holded_by' links a Conference to the organization that holds it (ACM SIGKDD), indicating the organizing body, not a member. These are distinct relations: one associates members with a conference, the other associates an organizer/holder organization with a conference.

In ekaw, 'Tutorial Abstract' is a specific subclass of Abstract (sibling of 'Invited Talk Abstract'), denoting the abstract of a tutorial talk. In sigkdd, 'Abstract' is a general class directly under Document, alongside Paper and Review. The sigkdd Abstract is more general and corresponds to the ekaw Abstract parent class, not specifically to tutorial abstracts. Thus ekaw's Tutorial_Abstract is subsumed_by sigkdd's Abstract.

Withdrawn Paper in edas is a specific paper status (a paper that has been withdrawn from the review process), a sibling of Accepted/Rejected/Published papers.
