Submission in iasted is a general document category representing submitted manuscripts, with children like Final manuscript and Initial manuscript. A withdrawn paper is not equivalent to a submission; it is a specific outcome/status of a paper, while submission denotes the act/artefact of submitting. They do not share the same intended instances.

The cmt 'date' property has domain Conference and denotes the date of the conference itself. The Conference ontology's 'is a starting date' has domain Important dates and denotes the starting date of some event or deadline. They apply to different subject types (Conference vs. Important dates) and represent different concepts: a general conference date vs. a specific starting date of an important date item. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

The two properties relate entirely different things: `has_contributions` links a Conference volume to the Conference contributions (papers/articles) it contains, while `hasMember` links a Conference to the Person members of that conference. The domains overlap (Conference volume vs Conference) but the ranges are disjoint (Conference contribution vs Person), so the properties cannot be equivalent or subsumed by one another.

Important dates in the Conference ontology is a composite class that groups all key dates of a conference volume (acceptance announcement, camera-ready, full paper submission, abstract submission, start/end dates). Deadline in iasted is a more general temporal class under Time, with children covering specific deadlines (camera ready, notification, hotel reservation, registration, submissions). Important dates is narrower: it bundles conference-paper-related dates and also includes start/end dates that are not deadlines. Thus Important dates is subsumed_by Deadline rather than equivalent.

A Conference Chair is the person chairing the conference (a leadership role), while a Sponsor is a person or entity that provides financial support. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things: 'is Written By' links a Paper to its Author, while 'is paid by' links Money to a Person. They share no domain or range overlap and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference gathering itself. iasted:Conference_state is a subclass of State, sibling of Presenter_state and Sponsor_state, denoting a status or phase of a conference rather than the conference event. These are disjoint kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are named Review, subclass of Document, and represent the concept of a review document in the conference domain. In ekaw, Review has children (Negative/Neutral/Positive Review) and properties linking it to Paper and Possible Reviewer, confirming it is a conference paper review. In iasted, Review is a subclass of Document with siblings like Submission, Form, etc. Despite iasted not providing additional structural detail, the label, parent hierarchy, and conference-domain context strongly indicate these denote the same concept: a review of a submission.

Regular Paper in EKAW is a type of academic paper submitted to a conference, while Mailing list in IASTED is a type of document (e.g., correspondence or communication artifact). These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion) in confOf, while Single hotel room is a type of accommodation/place in iasted. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. In iasted, Nonmember registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee (under Money > Fee), denoting a monetary fee for non-member registration. These are completely different concepts: one is a person, the other is a financial charge. There is no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Poster is a type of conference contribution (a poster paper), sibling to Paper and Short paper under Contribution. sigkdd:Bronze_Supporter is a type of conference sponsor (a bronze-level supporter), sibling to Gold/Platinum/Silver supporters and Exhibitor under Sponzor. These denote completely different domain concepts—a presentation artefact versus a sponsorship level—with no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties associate a conference entity with a location, but they differ in type and structure: 'has a location' is a datatype property with range string (a literal location name), while 'held In' is an object property with range Location (a class). They also have different domains (Conference volume vs. Event). They overlap semantically in capturing where something takes place, but are not equivalent due to the datatype/object property distinction and differing domains.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'need' connects Person to Item (a person needing some item), while 'searched by' connects Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (a sponsor being searched by the ACM SIGKDD organization). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are completely different, so these properties are unrelated.

The cmt property 'assignExternalReviewer' has domain Reviewer and range External Reviewer, modelling the act of a reviewer assigning an external reviewer. The confOf property 'writes' has domain Author and range Contribution, modelling an author writing a contribution. These are different relations between different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair and Program Chair are distinct conference roles. In cmt, Associated Chair is a subordinate chairman role (sibling of Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), not the head of the program. In sigkdd, Program Chair is the top program organizer (sibling of General Chair). They denote different organizational positions with no clear equivalence or subsumption.

A 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a meal/gathering) under the Event hierarchy in ekaw, while a 'Conference airport' is a physical location (a building) under the Place hierarchy in iasted. They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different kinds of entities: an event vs. a place. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.

A 'Paper Full Version' in cmt is a full research paper submitted to a conference, while 'Bank transfer' in iasted is a payment document (a financial instrument). They belong to completely different domains (academic publications vs. payment methods) despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.

IASTED non member is a person (a Delegate who is not an IASTED member), while Conference hall is a physical place where conference events occur. They belong to completely different domains (person vs. location) despite both being descendants of Place in their respective ontologies.

Reviewing_event in confOf is an administrative event (a happening/activity during the conference where reviewing of papers takes place), while Submissions_deadline in iasted is a temporal deadline (a point in time by which submissions must be received). One is an event/activity, the other is a deadline/time-point; they share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

Camera ready contribution is a written document (a finalized, accepted paper) in the Conference ontology, while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline for abstract submissions in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to completely different categories (document vs. temporal entity) and share no domain overlap.

Registration of participants event is an event (a temporal occurrence in the conference workflow), while Organizing Committee is a committee (a group of people). They belong to disjoint branches of the ontology and denote completely different kinds of entities.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. In Conference, 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (expressing a reviewer's preference for reviewing a topic). In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (expressing that a PC member reviews a paper). They have different domains (Topic vs Member PC), different ranges (Review preference vs Contribution), and different semantics.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Author of paper student is a person who is a student author of a paper. One is an event, the other is a person role; they share no instances.

In the edas ontology, 'Call For Papers' is a kind of Call (an announcement soliciting paper submissions), while in the sigkdd ontology, 'Paper' is a kind of Document (the actual submitted artefact). One is a request/announcement, the other is the artefact being requested. They are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent authors who are students, but they are modeled differently. 'Worker lecturer' in iasted is a student who is also a worker/lecturer, while 'Author of paper student' in sigkdd is specifically a student author of a paper. They overlap (a student author could be a worker lecturer) but neither subsumes the other, as one requires being a worker and the other requires authoring a paper.

A Call in edas denotes a call for papers/manuscripts/reviews with submission deadlines and instructions, initiated by committee members. A Fee in sigkdd denotes a monetary charge (registration fee, sponsor fee). These are entirely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property `name` in cmt denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while `hasEmail` in edas denotes the email address of Contact Information or Person. These are distinct attributes with different meanings and no overlap in intended use.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to a conference, e.g., authors, speakers). Registration is a subclass of Conference activity (the act of registering for a conference). One denotes a person role, the other an activity; they share no instances.

Property A captures the submission deadline date for full papers (domain: Important dates, range: date), while property B captures a person's first name (domain: Person, range: string). They relate entirely different entities and have no semantic overlap.

Topic in the Conference ontology denotes a subject area of conference parts and submissions, with properties linking it to reviews, conference parts, and submitted contributions. Place in sigkdd denotes a physical location (conference hall, hotel, main office) where people can stay. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:User is a subclass of Person, denoting human users such as Administrator, Author, and Reviewer. confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event, denoting conference events such as Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop. These are disjoint domains (people vs. events) with no overlap, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Person is a broad top-level class covering all people in the conference domain (authors, chairs, participants, volunteers, etc.), while sigkdd:Speaker is a specific subclass of Person denoting someone who gives a presentation. These are not equivalent: Person is far more general than Speaker. They are also not in a direct subsumption relation across these two ontologies because confOf:Person is a root class and sigkdd:Speaker is a leaf-level specialization; the alignment task asks whether they denote the same concept, and they do not. Hence unrelated.

confOf:Conference is a subclass of Working_event, representing the conference event itself (a happening/activity). ekaw:Programme_Brochure is a subclass of Document, representing a physical or digital brochure listing the conference programme. One is an event, the other is a document artefact; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

cmt's Document is a broad class covering any conference artefact (children: Paper, Review). confOf's Contribution is specifically a submitted item (children: Paper, Poster, Short paper) with author/contact/abstract properties. A Contribution is a kind of Document, but not every Document (e.g., a Review) is a Contribution, so Document subsumes Contribution.

Conference participant (A) denotes any person who participates in a conference (including active and passive participants), while Student (B) denotes a person who is a student. These are orthogonal concepts: a student may or may not be a conference participant, and a conference participant may or may not be a student. They share the parent Person but have no necessary instance overlap.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a type of Chairman), while Meeting Room Place is a physical location (a type of Place). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Co-author in cmt is a person who co-writes a paper, sitting under Person > Conference Member > Author. Nonauthor registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee charged to non-authors for registration, sitting under Money > Fee > Registration fee. One is a person role, the other is a financial charge; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Organizing committee in Conference is a committee that organizes a conference volume, with siblings like Program committee and Steering committee. Government Organization in edas is a type of organization (alongside Academia, Industry, NGO). These denote completely different concepts: one is a conference organizing body, the other is a governmental entity. No subsumption relationship exists between them.

Hotel fee in iasted is a monetary amount charged for lodging (subclass of Fee > Money), whereas Hotel in sigkdd is a physical place (subclass of Place). They denote completely different categories of entities—a cost versus a location—so they are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings. In cmt, maxPapers is a property of Program Committee Member indicating the maximum number of papers a PC member can review, with range int. In iasted, has_amount_of is a property of Money indicating a monetary amount, with range int. They relate to entirely different concepts (paper assignment limits vs. monetary quantities) and share no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Chairman is a general role whose subclasses include Conference Chair, Associated Chair, and Program Committee Chair. In sigkdd, General Chair is a specific organizer role. General Chair corresponds to one of the specific chair roles under cmt's Chairman, not to the general Chairman superclass. Therefore cmt:Chairman subsumes sigkdd:General Chair.

The two properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. confOf:follows relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (e.g., one event following another in a sequence), while iasted:is_sent_after relates an Item to a Time (e.g., an item being sent after a particular time point). They do not connect the same kinds of entities in the same way, so they are unrelated.

cmt:Conference denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, members, administrators, paper assignments), while iasted:Conference_airport is a physical place—a building where conference attendees arrive—located under Place > Building. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In EDAS, 'Personal History' is a container class for an individual's activity records (personal publication history, personal review history). In SIGKDD, 'Review' is a document produced by a reviewer about a submitted paper. These are completely different concepts: one is a profile/history aggregate, the other is a specific review document. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.
hasHomePage points to a URL/home page string for a Person, while Name points to the person's name; they denote different attributes, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, locationOf maps a Location to an Event (where an event takes place). In iasted, is_sent_after maps an Item to a Time (when an item is sent). They share no domain/range overlap and denote unrelated relations.

In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (Person > Author > Presenter), denoting a person who presents a paper. In iasted, Hotel presenter is oddly placed under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate, suggesting a very different modelling perspective or possibly a modelling error in iasted. The iasted siblings (Conference Hiker, Listener, Speaker, etc.) are delegate subtypes, but the path hierarchy rooted in Place/Building makes the intended semantics diverge significantly from edas Presenter. The two classes do not reliably denote the same set of instances.

In confOf, Chair PC is a specific role (the person who chairs the PC), a sibling of Member PC. In ekaw, PC Member is a broad class covering all PC members including chairs (PC Chair is a child of PC Member). Thus confOf's Chair PC is a specific kind of ekaw PC Member, making it subsumed_by.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization representing a corporate entity (sibling of University). edas:MedicineTopic is a subclass of Topic representing a subject-matter topic for conference papers (sibling of AntennasTopic, CADTopic, etc.). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Full Version in cmt denotes the full-length version of a paper (as opposed to a Paper Abstract), distinguishing by content completeness. Published Paper in edas denotes a paper that has been published, distinguishing by publication status. These are orthogonal classification dimensions: a full version may be unpublished, and a published paper could be an abstract. Their sibling sets confirm different axes (abstract vs. full; accepted/active/pending/rejected/withdrawn), so they do not coincide.

The two properties operate on different domains and ranges with different semantics. In cmt, 'has Been Assigned' links a Reviewer directly to a Paper they are assigned to review. In the Conference ontology, 'has a submitted contribution' links a 'Review expertise' (an abstract entity representing a reviewer's area of expertise) to a 'Submitted contribution'. The Conference property models the relationship between a reviewer's expertise profile and contributions submitted in that area, not a direct reviewer-to-paper assignment. The domains (Reviewer vs Review expertise) and the intended meaning differ sufficiently that these are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption relationship.

Abstract in the Conference ontology is a document class representing the textual summary of a paper/poster/presentation (a written artefact). Deadline Abstract Submission in sigkdd is a temporal class representing a date/deadline for submitting abstracts. One is a document, the other is a deadline; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Paper in the Conference ontology is a regular conference contribution (a written academic paper), while Web Site in ekaw is a web-based document. They share no instances: a Paper is a scholarly contribution, whereas a Web Site is an online document. They are not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other.

Entity A is a subclass of Person (a registered applicant who is a conference participant), while entity B is the Conference event itself with properties like dates, country, topics, and members. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

In cmt, Preference represents a numerical value assigned by a reviewer to express interest in reviewing a particular paper. In the Conference ontology, Organizer is a person who organizes a conference event. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference www is a web document/resource identified by a URL, subclass of Conference document. Main office is a physical place, subclass of Place, sibling to Conference hall and Hotel. A web page and a physical office are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in instances.

Although both properties share the domain Person, their semantics differ substantially. In Conference, 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (something the person authored or submitted). In iasted, 'need' relates a Person to an Item (something the person requires, e.g. equipment or registration items). These are different relations: contributing/producing a document vs. needing an item. No subsumption holds between them, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Conference is the main conference event (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while in ekaw, Tutorial is a specific type of individual presentation. These are disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are object properties linking a conference document/item to a Person who authored/prepared it. The domains (Conference document vs Item) and ranges (Person vs Person) align, and 'has authors' and 'is prepared by' express the same authorship relation in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties named hasFirstName with domain Person and range string, denoting the same relation from a person to their first name. The confOf comment 'involved middle name' is a minor modeling note and does not indicate a different intended relation.

The ekaw 'references' property denotes a relation where a document or paper references another document, while the sigkdd 'awarded by' property denotes a relation where an Award is given by some agent or organization. These are entirely different relations with different domains and meanings; they share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Workshop and Tutorial are distinct types of conference events. In ontology A, Workshop is a sibling of Tutorial under Conference part, while in ontology B, Tutorial is a sibling of Workshop under Working event. The two entities denote different concepts (a workshop vs. a tutorial), so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and not otherwise related.

These properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. `reviewCriteriaEnteredBy` (cmt) has domain Conference and range Administrator, indicating who entered review criteria for a conference. `reviewWrittenBy` (ekaw) has domain Review and range Possible Reviewer, indicating who wrote a specific review. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Conference announcement is a document type (child of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while Presenter house is a physical building (child of Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference restaurant). One is an informational artefact, the other a physical place; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The property 'writes' in confOf has domain Author and range Contribution (Author -> Contribution), while 'isWrittenBy' in edas has domain Paper and range Author (Paper -> Author). These are inverse relations: 'writes' goes from author to paper, 'isWrittenBy' goes from paper to author. A property and its inverse are not equivalent, and since they have opposite directions they are not in a subsumption or overlap relation either.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it. In sigkdd, 'designed by' links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (the organization that designed the deadline). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (indicating membership in a conference). In edas, hasLocation links a Conference Event to a Place (indicating where an event takes place). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

PaperFullVersion is a full submission of a research paper (Document > Paper > Paper Full Version), whereas Registration_form is an administrative form for conference registration (Item > Document > Form > Registration form). They serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain and share no instance overlap.

Entity A is a topic about computer networks and sensors, a subclass of Topic. Entity B is a type of scientific event (a contributed talk/presentation). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Call for participation is a conference document (e.g., an announcement or invitation for event participation), while Industry Organization is a type of organization (e.g., a company). They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Non Academic Event' is a subclass of Conference Event covering social activities like breaks, meals, and social events. In iasted, 'Student non speaker' is a subclass of Non speaker (under Delegate > Person), representing a person who is a student and does not give a presentation. One is an event, the other is a person role; they share no instances.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes and submits papers. In iasted, Registration fee is a monetary amount charged for conference registration. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

hasFirstName relates a Person to their given name (string), while Nation relates a Person to their country/nationality (string). They connect the same domain and range types but denote completely different attributes of a person, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or even meaningfully related.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (cmt), while Free Time Break is a type of non-academic event/break (edas). They belong to completely different parts of the domain hierarchy with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. confOf:dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic (what subject the paper is about), while iasted:is_given_to links an Item to a Person (who receives or is awarded the item). The domains (Contribution vs Item) and ranges (Topic vs Person) are disjoint, and the intended semantics are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Program Committee Chair' is a specific role: the chair of the Program Committee (a committee that handles paper reviews/assignments), sitting under Chairman and parallel to 'Conference Chair'. In edas, 'Conference Chair' is the person who chairs the entire conference (initiates calls, can review papers, etc.). These are distinct roles: a Program Committee Chair manages the reviewing process, while a Conference Chair manages the conference as a whole. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other across the two ontologies.

The two properties relate completely different domain and range concepts. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Members (general conference participants). In edas, isInitiatedBy links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to specific chair roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) that initiate it. The domains (Conference vs. Call) and ranges (Conference Member vs. chair/TPC roles) do not overlap, and the relations denote different real-world associations.

`updated Version Of` in ekaw relates a Document to a prior Document it is a revision of, while `presentation` in sigkdd relates a Speaker to the Document they present. They have different domains (Document vs Speaker), different meanings, and different argument structures, so they are not equivalent.

Dining Place is a location where meals are served (subclass of Place), while Van is a transport vehicle (subclass of Item > Transport vehicle). They share no instances and are from disjoint hierarchies with no overlap in meaning.

Invited speaker is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, while Hotel presenter is a delegate who presents at a hotel venue. They are different concepts: one is defined by the invitation status, the other by the presentation location. Their paths and siblings confirm distinct modeling purposes, and neither subsumes the other.
Property A links a Conference volume to its Program committee, while property B links two Administrative events that run in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The property 'issues' in Conference ontology relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings). The property 'forEvent' in edas relates a Call to an Academic Event (a call for papers is for an event). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no meaningful overlap in the conference domain.

Student non speaker in iasted is a delegate who does not give a presentation (a non-speaking attendee who is a student). Author of paper student in sigkdd is a student who authored a paper and is classified under Speaker/Author, implying they do present. One is a non-speaker, the other is a speaker/author; their intended instances do not coincide.

Both are datatype properties with domain covering deadlines/submission dates and range date, but A is specifically about the full paper submission deadline while B is a generic deadline date property. They overlap in usage but are not equivalent.

In ontology A, 'Regular contribution' is a specific subclass of 'Conference contribution' (distinguished from posters, invited talks, etc.), while in ontology B, 'Contribution' is the top-level class for all contribution types including Paper, Poster, and Short paper. B's Contribution corresponds more closely to A's Conference contribution. A's Regular contribution is thus a narrower concept, subsumed by B's Contribution.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates Administrative events to Administrative events (indicating events running in parallel), while the iasted 'give' property relates Persons to Activities/Items (indicating a person gives a presentation or item). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

cmt:User is a broad superclass covering Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—any person who uses the conference management system. confOf:Student is a specific kind of Participant (a student attendee). A Student is not a general system user, and a User (e.g., Administrator or Reviewer) is not necessarily a Student. The two classes have disjoint intended instances and no subsumption relationship in either direction.

Decision (cmt) represents the outcome of a paper review process (Acceptance/Rejection), while Organization (confOf) represents institutions like companies and universities. These are entirely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a person role in the CMT ontology (a kind of Chairman/Conference Member involved in organizing the conference), whereas Conference Trip is a social event/activity in the EKAW ontology. These denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Value added tax is a tax (a government levy on goods/services) under Money > Tax, while Registration fee is a conference attendance fee under Fee, with subtypes for member/non-member/student registration. They are distinct financial concepts: one is a tax, the other a conference service fee. They share no subsumption relationship and are not equivalent.

The cmt 'memberOfConference' property links a Conference Member to a Conference (expressing membership/affiliation), while the confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (expressing authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote different relations. In EDAS, 'isMemberOf' links a Person to a Conference they are a member of. In IASTED, 'is_needed_for' links an Item to a Person who needs it. There is no overlap in meaning or in the types of entities they relate.

The property 'employedBy' in confOf relates a Person to an Organization that employs them, while 'organises' in ekaw relates an Organisation or Person to an Event they organize. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

These properties go in opposite directions and relate different entities. In cmt, 'hasBeenAssigned' goes from Reviewer to Paper, meaning a reviewer is assigned a paper to review. In the Conference ontology, 'has_a_review' goes from Reviewed contribution to Review, meaning a paper has a review attached. The cmt property is about the assignment relationship (reviewer -> paper), while the Conference property is about the output relationship (paper -> review). They are not inverses either, since the cmt property connects reviewers to papers (not to reviews), and the Conference property connects papers to reviews (not to reviewers).

Both classes denote the same concept of a research subject area in a conference domain. In ontology A, Topic is linked to conference parts, submitted contributions, and review preferences. In ontology B, Topic is linked to conferences and papers. Both represent thematic classification areas for conference content, with B providing concrete examples (Antennas, CAD, etc.) and A describing the structural role topics play in conference organization. The intended instances coincide as subject-area categories.

In ekaw, 'Invited Speaker' is a specific subclass of Presenter under the path Person > Conference Participant > Presenter > Invited Speaker, denoting only speakers who were invited. In sigkdd, 'Speaker' is a broader class (parent of both 'Author' and 'Invited Speaker') covering anyone who presents. Thus ekaw's Invited Speaker is a strict subclass of sigkdd's Speaker.

confOf Short_paper is a specific type of contribution (short paper) whereas ekaw Paper is the general class of papers (with children such as Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). Short_paper is narrower than ekaw Paper, so it is subsumed by it.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., a conference excursion or outing), sitting under Event > Social event alongside Banquet and Reception. iasted:Van is a transport vehicle (a physical conveyance) sitting under Item > Transport vehicle alongside Car, Shuttle bus, and Taxi. One denotes an organised social activity, the other a physical vehicle; their intended instances do not overlap at all.

Both denote social activities associated with a conference, but they are not equivalent. In EKAW, Conference Trip is a specific kind of social event (a trip/excursion), whereas in IASTED, Social program is a broader category of conference activity that subsumes various social events such as Dinner banquet, Cocktail reception, and Coffee breaks. The IASTED Social program is more general than the EKAW Conference Trip, but because the ontologies frame social activities differently (EKAW has a dedicated Social Event branch, IASTED mixes social and administrative activities under Conference activity), a strict subsumption is not clearly intended. They overlap as conference social activities, so related is the safest alignment.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' (domain Conference, range Administrator) denotes an administrator starting the reviewer bidding process. 'invites_co-reviewers' (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer) denotes a reviewer inviting other co-reviewers. They describe different actions involving different participants.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members (PC members reviewing papers). In Conference, was_a_track-workshop_chair_of links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (track/workshop). The domains (Program Committee vs Track workshop chair), ranges (Program Committee Member vs Conference part), and the nature of the relations (membership vs chairing) are all different, so these properties are unrelated.

In ontology A, 'Organizing committee' is a specific committee subclass (sibling of Program committee and Steering committee under Committee). In ontology B, 'Committee' is the general superclass with children including Organizing Committee, Program Committee, and Best Paper Awards Committee. Thus A's Organizing committee is a strict subclass of B's Committee.

Both pertain to the paper submission process, but they denote different concepts. 'Receiving manuscript' is an activity (an action performed by organizers), while 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a temporal deadline (a date by which submission must occur). They are related aspects of the submission workflow but not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties on Person with string ranges, but hasSurname denotes specifically a surname/family name, while Name denotes a full name. They overlap in being name-related properties of persons but are not equivalent: a surname is a proper part of a full name, not the same concept. Name could be seen as more general, but since it may also be a structured or full-name field rather than a strict supertype of surname, related is the safest verdict.

Author and Reviewer are distinct roles in the conference domain. An Author writes papers (writes -> Contribution), while a Reviewer reviews papers (is Reviewing -> Paper). Although both are subclasses of Person, they denote different concepts with different properties and responsibilities. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and not meaningfully related beyond being person roles.

Property A (has_a_volume) links Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while property B (abstract) links a Contribution to its textual abstract string. They relate different domain classes to different range types and denote entirely different attributes.

Co chair is a committee leadership role (a person who co-chairs a committee), while Possible Reviewer is a person who could review a paper. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain: a co-chair is about committee organization, whereas a possible reviewer is about the paper-review assignment. Neither subsumes the other, and their intended instances do not coincide.

A 'Paid applicant' is a person who has paid registration fees for a conference, sitting under Person > Conference applicant > Registered applicant. B 'Credit card' is a physical item (a payment card), sitting under Item > Card. These are completely different concepts — a person vs. a financial instrument — with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different entities. Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (a committee/organisational role), while property B links a Document to a Speaker (a person presenting). The domains (Conference part vs Document) and ranges (Track workshop chair vs Speaker) are disjoint concepts, and the relations themselves denote different things: chairing a track/workshop versus presenting a document.

Communications Topic is a subject-matter topic (a specialization of Topic, alongside Antennas, Cryptography, etc.), whereas Organizing Committee is a committee responsible for organizing a conference. They belong to completely different conceptual hierarchies and share no instances.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. In sigkdd, Registration SIGMOD Member is a subclass of Registration fee, denoting a registration fee category for SIGMOD members. These are completely different concepts: one is a person, the other is a fee. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

markConflictOfInterest in CMT denotes a conflict-of-interest relationship between a person (author/reviewer/chairman) and a paper, explicitly preventing the reviewer from bidding on, being assigned to, or viewing reviews for that paper. isReviewing in EDAS denotes the act of a reviewer (or chair role) reviewing a paper. These are fundamentally different relations: one declares a conflict that blocks review, the other indicates active review. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The confOf property 'reviewes' relates a Member PC to a Contribution (a PC member reviews a paper/contribution), whereas the iasted property 'is paid in' relates Money to a Building (a monetary amount is paid in a building/venue). They connect completely different domain and range types and express unrelated relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Conference is a top-level conference event (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while iasted:Video_presentation is a specific kind of presentation activity. They denote completely different concepts at different levels of granularity with no overlap in intended instances.

Payment document in iasted denotes financial transaction records (Bank transfer, Cheque), while Paper in sigkdd denotes a scholarly submission. They share only the distant ancestor Document; their intended instances are disjoint.

confOf's 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event (a happening/activity during the conference where participants register), while iasted's 'Submissions deadline' is a temporal entity (a point in time by which paper submissions must be received). They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs. Time) and denote fundamentally different things: one is an activity, the other is a deadline. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

These properties operate in completely different directions and relate different entities. In ontology A, 'has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution' links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic (i.e., a preference is about a topic or contribution). In ontology B, 'hasReviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (i.e., a paper is reviewed by a reviewer). The domains (Review preference vs. Paper) and ranges (Submitted contribution/Topic vs. Possible Reviewer) do not align, and the relations they express are fundamentally different.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events (e.g., conference sessions running in parallel), while the edas 'is Menu Of' property relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event. These properties connect entirely different domain entities and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

In iasted, City is a geographic/administrative area (with children like Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city) that can be occupied, situated in, or visited by persons. In sigkdd, Place is a physical facility or venue (with children Conference hall, Hotel, Main office) where a person can stay. City denotes a geographic location, while Place denotes a building/facility; neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way, and they are not equivalent.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'was a committee of' links a Committee to a Conference volume, indicating which conference a committee serves. 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution, indicating authorship of a paper. They have different domains (Committee vs. Author), different ranges (Conference volume vs. Contribution), and denote completely different relationships in the conference domain.

Rejected Paper is a class denoting a paper whose submission was rejected, sitting under Document > Paper. Registation deadline is a temporal deadline for conference registration, sitting under Time > Deadline. These denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, Attendee is a broad class covering any person who attends a conference (sibling to Author, Reviewer, etc.). In iasted, Author is a specialized subclass of Speaker (itself under Delegate), representing a person who presents/authorship of specific publication types. An Attendee is more general than an Author, but the iasted Author is a narrow authorial/presenting role, not a general attendee. The intended instances do not coincide, and neither class subsumes the other across ontologies (edas Attendee includes non-authors; iasted Author includes only authorial speakers). Thus they are unrelated in a reference alignment.

A is a person role (SC Member under PC Member under Possible Reviewer under Person), while B is a monetary fee (Sponzor fee under Fee, sibling of Registration fee). They denote completely different domain entities with no overlap.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a subclass of Document/Proceedings, denoting a published volume of conference papers. These are completely different categories (person vs. document) with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In ontology A, 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee (the conference has an organizing/program committee). In ontology B, 'is Initiated By' links a Call (e.g., a call for papers) to the persons who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). The domains (Conference volume vs. Call), ranges (Committee vs. Chair/TPC Member), and the nature of the relationship (possessing a committee vs. being initiated by a person) are all different, so these properties are unrelated.

cmt:Conference denotes the conference event/organisation itself (with properties like date, logo URL, members, administrators), while ekaw:Conference_Proceedings is a document subclass (Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings > Conference Proceedings) representing the published proceedings volume. One is an event/organisation and the other is a document artefact, so they are unrelated.

These properties denote different concepts. 'has Submission Instructions' is a datatype property from Call to string, representing textual instructions for how to submit. 'submit until' is an object property from Document to Deadline, representing a deadline date by which a document must be submitted. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Call vs Document), range (string vs Deadline), and meaning (instructions text vs deadline entity).

The two properties relate completely different entities. `has_a_review_expertise` links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (capturing the expertise level assigned to a review of that contribution), while `writes` links an Author to a Contribution (capturing authorship). They have different domains (Submitted contribution vs. Author), different ranges (Review expertise vs. Contribution), and express semantically unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

In ontology Conference, 'Regular author' is a subclass of Conference contribution and Conference contributor, with children Contribution 1th author and Contribution co author — it denotes a person who authors a paper. In confOf, 'Regular' is a subclass of Participant (under Person), with siblings Member and Student — it denotes a regular (non-student, non-member) participant at the conference. These are different concepts: one is about authorship of contributions, the other about registration/participant type. They share the word 'regular' but denote unrelated things.

The two properties relate completely different domains and ranges. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a general participant/member of the conference). In the Conference ontology, was_a_track-workshop_chair_of links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a specific section of the conference). The domains (Conference vs. Track workshop chair) and ranges (Conference Member vs. Conference part) are entirely different, and the relations themselves are conceptually distinct: general membership vs. a chair's association with a conference part.

These two properties are completely different in domain, range, and meaning. 'has_the_first_name' is a datatype property from Person to string (representing a person's first name), while 'go_through' is an object property from Item to Activity (representing an item undergoing some activity). They share no semantic overlap.

Paper Full Version is a full-length conference paper (a document) in cmt, while Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a subject-area topic in edas. They belong to entirely different parts of the domain hierarchy (documents vs. topics) and share no instances.

In cmt, Preference is a value class representing a bid/assignment preference for paper reviewing (e.g., want/neutral/don't want), not a person. In sigkdd, Person is a human agent with subtypes like Listener, Organizator, Speaker. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (an event with two levels, e.g., dual-track or multi-tier). In iasted, 'Reviewer' is a person who reviews papers, placed under Speaker > Delegate > Conference building. One is a conference event type, the other is a person role; they share no intended instances.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a broad role class (parent of Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.) representing any person who is a member of a conference. In the Conference ontology, Steering_committee is a specific committee (a group/organization, not a person) that steers a conference. One denotes individual members; the other denotes a committee body. They are structurally and semantically distinct.

ekaw:Accepted_Paper is a highly specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has passed review and been accepted for publication). sigkdd:Paper is the general class of all papers. Every accepted paper is a paper, but not every paper is accepted, so Accepted_Paper is subsumed_by Paper.

cmt:Paper is a scholarly contribution submitted to a conference, with authors, reviews, bids, decisions, and subject areas. iasted:Invitation letter is an administrative document sent to invite participants or speakers. Despite sharing the parent 'Document', their intended instances are completely disjoint: a Paper is an academic submission, while an Invitation letter is a logistical/administrative artefact. No subsumption holds either, so they are unrelated.

Departure tax is a tax on leaving a location (e.g., airport tax), while Registration fee is a fee paid to attend a conference. They are different kinds of charges in the conference domain, with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A links a Track workshop chair (person/role) to a Conference part, expressing that someone chaired a track or workshop. Property B links an Administrative event to another Administrative event, expressing that two events run in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings; they are unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a broad class (parent of Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version) representing any paper submitted to the conference. In ekaw, Poster_Paper is a specific subclass of Paper, denoting only poster papers. Thus cmt:Paper is strictly more general than ekaw:Poster_Paper, so the relation is subsumes.

Entity A is an event (a happening during a conference where participants register), while entity B is a deadline (a point in time by which registration must be completed). They are fundamentally different concepts: one is an administrative event, the other is a temporal deadline. They share the word 'registration' but denote different things entirely.

Submitted Paper in ekaw is a specific academic paper submitted for review at a conference, with siblings like Camera Ready Paper, Regular Paper, etc. Form in iasted is an administrative document type whose children include Author information form, Hotel registration form, and Registration form. These are completely different kinds of things: one is a research paper artifact, the other is an administrative form. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. 'has a topic or a submission contribution' links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic, encoding which paper/topic a reviewer preference applies to. 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker, encoding who presents a document. They have disjoint domains (Review preference vs Document) and disjoint ranges (Submitted contribution/Topic vs Speaker), so they do not denote the same relation.

In iasted, Person is a top-level class with children Delegate and Sponsor, covering all people involved in the conference. In sigkdd, Speaker is a subclass of Person (alongside Listener and Organizator), specifically denoting someone who gives a presentation. Thus iasted:Person is strictly more general than sigkdd:Speaker: every Speaker is a Person, but not every Person is a Speaker.

Both classes are named 'Conference' and represent the same core concept of an academic conference in the conference-organisation domain. They share properties like date/start/end and are both used as the main event entity in their respective ontologies. The differences in attached properties (administrative details in cmt vs. location/name in sigkdd) reflect different modelling emphases, not different concepts.

The property 'addedBy' in cmt relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator who added them, while 'hold' in sigkdd relates the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference it holds. These are entirely different domain relations with different domain and range types, sharing no conceptual overlap.

Tutorial is a conference part (an educational session at a conference), while Sponzor fee is a monetary fee paid by a sponsor. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Review in Conference is a document containing a review of a contribution, while Paper in sigkdd is a document submitted by an author. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain; sigkdd even has Review as a separate sibling of Paper, confirming they are not the same thing.

maxChoice is a datatype property from Social event/Working event to positiveInteger, while organisedBy is an object property from Event to Organisation/Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Conference document is a broad class encompassing various conference-related documents (call for papers, contributions, reviews, announcements, etc.), while Deadline is a specific temporal entity representing submission/notification dates. Their instances do not coincide: a conference document is an artefact, a deadline is a date. They share no overlap in intended instances.
hasCountry relates Organizations and Persons to Countries, while hasReview relates Papers to Reviews. Different domains, ranges, and semantics; no overlap.

The property 'contributes' in the Conference ontology relates a Person to a Conference document (the paper or artefact they author), whereas 'pay' in the iasted ontology relates a Person to Money (a monetary amount). These are entirely different relations with disjoint ranges and unrelated semantics in the conference domain.

The two properties connect entirely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, `written By` links a Document to the Person who authored it. In sigkdd, `notification until` links an Author to a Deadline (notification). They share no domain or range overlap and express different relations (authorship vs. notification deadline), so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate different concepts in different directions. 'has a submitted contribution' links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (the paper being reviewed), while 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a record of past reviews). The domains (Review expertise vs Reviewer), ranges (Submitted contribution vs Personal Review History), and intended semantics are distinct, so they are not equivalent.

In EKAW, Abstract is a specific kind of document (a summary of a paper/talk), a sibling of Paper and Review under Document. In IASTED, Document is a broad superclass covering many administrative and logistical artefacts (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, visas, etc.). The two entities are at completely different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept. Abstract is not a subclass of the IASTED Document either, since the IASTED Document is a broad administrative/container notion rather than a scholarly publication artefact hierarchy. They are therefore unrelated.

Associated Chair is a conference-level chair role in cmt (sibling to Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Demo Chair in ekaw is a specialized role responsible for demo sessions. These are distinct conference organisation roles with different responsibilities; neither subsumes the other.

Property A (has_a_commtitee) links a Conference volume to a Committee, while property B (hasMember) links a Conference to a Person. They relate different kinds of entities (committees vs. persons) and thus denote different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. 'read By Meta Reviewer' links a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (the person who reads it), while 'has Rating' links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a score/value). The domains overlap (Paper vs Active Paper) but the ranges are entirely different: a person vs a rating value. These are not the same relation.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In Conference, 'issues' connects a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issuing proceedings). In edas, 'relatesTo' connects a Document to various entities like events or persons (a document being related to something). There is no overlap in the types of things they relate or in the nature of the relationship.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. `hasReviewer` links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (paper reviewed-by reviewer), while `submit` links an Author to a Paper (author submits paper). They share no domain, no range, and no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. In edas, 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (i.e., listing members/organizers of the conference). In iasted, 'is present' links a Person to a Time (i.e., indicating when a person is present). They share no common domain or range types and express different relations.

confOf:location denotes the physical place where an event is held (range string, domain Social/Working event), whereas edas:registrationDueOn denotes a deadline date/time for conference registration (range dateTime, domain Conference). They describe completely different aspects of the conference domain.

Student lecturer in iasted is a person role: a student who gives a lecture, placed in the hierarchy under Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer. Registration Student in sigkdd is a fee category: a registration fee paid by students, placed under Registration fee with siblings like Registration Non Member, Registration SIGKDD Member. One is a person/role, the other is a monetary fee type. They do not denote the same concept.

The property 'issues' in the Conference ontology relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes, while 'location Of' in the ekaw ontology relates a Location to the Event held at that location. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relations (publication vs. spatial location), so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the same role: the chair of the program committee. In cmt, 'Program Committee Chair' is a Chairman and a Program Committee Member, with the power to end reviews. In ekaw, 'PC Chair' is a PC Member and Conference Participant. The labels are synonymous ('Program Committee Chair' = 'PC Chair'), and both occupy the same structural position as the head of the program committee in the conference organization domain.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a gathering/activity), while Sponzorship is a kind of money/financial arrangement. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

confOf:Conference is a class denoting a conference event (an event/activity), while ekaw:Presenter is a class denoting a person who presents at a conference. These are completely different categories: one is an event, the other is a person role. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both classes are subclasses of Person and relate to conference participation, but they denote different concepts. In cmt, Conference Member is a role-based class covering organizers and authors (Associated Chair, Author, Conference Chair, Program Committee Member, Reviewer) linked to a Conference via has/memberOfConference. In the Conference ontology, Conference participant is split into Active/Passive participants, covering attendees rather than organizational roles. The extension of these classes overlaps (e.g., an author may also be a participant) but does not coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. A's 'was a committe co chair of' links a Co-chair to a Committee (a person to a committee they co-chaired). B's 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (a conference to its members). They have different domains (Co-chair vs Conference), different ranges (Committee vs Person), and different semantics (co-chairing vs general membership).

Conference www is a conference document with a URL (e.g., a conference website), while Powerline Transmission Topic is a subject-domain topic for categorizing papers. They belong to completely different parts of the domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These are inverse relations. `writtenBy` goes from Contribution to Author (document -> person), while `authorOf` goes from Person to Document (person -> document). They relate the same kinds of entities but in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent. In OAEI alignment, a property and its inverse are not considered equivalent.

Wireless Communications Topic is a subject-area topic under Topic in the edas ontology, while Card is a physical item (with child Credit card) under Item in the iasted ontology. They denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings. In the Conference ontology, 'gives_presentations' relates an Active conference participant to a Presentation they give. There is no overlap in the kinds of things being related or the direction of the relation.

Conference:Topic is a general class for any conference topic, while edas:MicroelectronicsTopic is a specific subclass of edas:Topic (a particular subject area). The Conference ontology's Topic corresponds to the general edas:Topic, not to the specialized MicroelectronicsTopic. Thus MicroelectronicsTopic is strictly more specific than (subsumed_by) the general Topic class.

Entity A is a class representing a talk event (a type of academic event such as a welcome or closing talk), while entity B is a class representing an organizer (a person who organizes a conference). These are completely different domain concepts: an event vs. a person role. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference, while Camera ready contribution in Conference is a document (the final version of an accepted paper). One is a person role, the other is a document artifact - completely different concepts in the conference domain.

`name` in cmt denotes the name of a Conference or Person (a label/identifier), while `has Home Page` in confOf denotes the URL of a person's home page. These are semantically distinct properties with different meanings, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

These properties differ in both domain and meaning. In cmt, 'end Review' is an action property with domain Program Committee Chair and range Review, denoting the chair ending/submitting a review. In edas, 'isReviewedBy' has domain Paper and range various reviewer roles, denoting which reviewers reviewed a paper. They relate different entities in different directions and are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Camera_Ready_Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper accepted and in final form for the proceedings). In sigkdd, Paper is the general class of all papers (submitted, accepted, etc.). Thus every Camera Ready Paper is a Paper, but not vice versa, so ekaw:Camera_Ready_Paper is subsumed_by sigkdd:Paper.

In the iasted ontology, Sponzorship is a subclass of Money, sitting alongside Fee, Tax, and Tip, which suggests it denotes a monetary amount or financial concept related to sponsorship. In sigkdd, Best Student Paper Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor, sitting alongside various supporter types (Bronze, Gold, Platinum, Silver, Exhibitor), which denotes an entity (person or organization) that provides sponsorship for a best student paper award. One is a monetary value/financial concept; the other is an agent/organization role. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both classes denote the same concept in the conference domain: a Program Committee responsible for reviewing papers. In cmt, it is a top-level class with members linked via hasProgramCommitteeMember. In sigkdd, it is a subclass of Committee alongside other committee types. The intended instances coincide: the committee that oversees paper reviews for a conference.

submit Paper (cmt) has domain Author and range Paper, representing an author submitting a paper. is visited by (iasted) has domain Building/City/State and range Person, representing a place being visited by a person. These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

In the Conference ontology, Workshop is a specific kind of conference part (a sibling of Track and Tutorial). In confOf, Working_event is a broad superclass that subsumes Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop. Thus Workshop is a strict subclass (more specific) than Working_event, which is a general category of events involving work rather than a single workshop.
confOf:Reception is a social event (a gathering like a banquet or trip), while iasted:Mailing list is a document item. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The two properties relate very different things: edas:initiates has domain (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) and range Call, meaning a chair/TPC member initiates a call (e.g., call for papers). iasted:sign has domain Person and range Item, meaning a person signs an item (e.g., a document). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different; there is no overlap in what these properties express.

These properties are fundamentally different. confOf's 'starts on' is a datatype property mapping an Event to a string (representing a start date/time), while ekaw's 'partOfEvent' is an object property mapping an Event to another Event (representing a part-whole relationship between events). They have different ranges (string vs Event), different semantic meanings (temporal vs structural), and no overlap in the relation they express.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and have different meanings. In EDAS, isMemberOf links a Person to a Conference (membership relation). In SIGKDD, presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

The cmt 'has Conference Member' links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person participating in the conference). The Conference ontology 'has tracks' links a Conference volume to its Track (a structural part/session of the conference). These are fundamentally different relations: one associates people with a conference, the other associates organizational sub-units (tracks) with a conference volume. No subsumption or overlap exists between them.

Industry Organization is a type of organization (e.g., a company), while Organizing Committee member is a person who serves on the organizing committee. One is an organization, the other is a person; they share no instances and are unrelated.

In cmt, Program Committee is a committee of reviewers managing paper reviews, while in edas, Organization is a sponsoring organization (academia, government, industry, NGO). These are structurally and semantically unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. detailsEnteredBy in cmt relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details. relatesTo in edas relates a Document to various entities (AcademicEvent, Conference, ConferenceSession, Person). They connect different types of entities and express different relationships with no overlap in intended semantics.

These properties operate in completely different domains. 'has_tutorials' links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts (a mereological/part-of relation between conference and its tutorial sessions). 'expertOn' links a Member PC to a Topic they have expertise in (an expertise/competence relation between a committee member and a subject area). They have different domains (Conference volume vs Member PC), different ranges (Tutorial vs Topic), and different relational semantics (part-of vs expertise). There is no equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. `written By` (domain Document, range Person) indicates authorship of a document by a person, while `send` (domain Person, range Item) indicates a person sending an item. They are not inverses (sending is not the same as writing), and their domains and ranges differ, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, representing a person who is a student. In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Author (under Speaker > Delegate), representing a person who gives a lecture at a conference and has authored a paper. These are distinct concepts: a student is not necessarily a lecturer, and a lecturer is not necessarily a student. Their paths, parents, and siblings confirm they model different roles in the conference domain.

Money in iasted is a monetary amount/financial resource (with children Fee, Tax, Tip, Sponzorship), while Sponzor in sigkdd is an organization or person that sponsors the conference (with children like Gold Supporter, Exhibitor). One denotes money itself; the other denotes the sponsoring agent. They are disjoint concepts.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion organized during a conference), subclass of Social event, sibling to Banquet and Reception. edas:TravelGrant is a type of sponsorship (financial support for travel), subclass of Sponsorship. These are completely different concepts: one is an event/activity, the other is a monetary grant. They share the word 'travel' only coincidentally.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while Time in iasted is a temporal concept with children like Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Positive_Review in ekaw is a subclass of Review denoting a review with positive evaluation, while Abstract in sigkdd is a subclass of Document denoting a paper abstract. They are sibling-level document types under different hierarchies and share no instances.

Workshop in confOf is a type of academic event (a working event under Event, sibling to Conference and Tutorial). LCD projector in iasted is a piece of audiovisual equipment (under Item > Audiovisual equipment). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are named 'Paper' and represent the core concept of a conference paper. In confOf, Paper is a subtype of Contribution (alongside Poster and Short_paper), while in sigkdd it is a subtype of Document (alongside Abstract and Review). Despite different sibling structures, both denote the same intended concept: a written paper submitted to a conference. The confOf ontology models it as a type of contribution, and sigkdd models it as a type of document, but the Paper class itself in both cases refers to the same entity in the conference domain.

In confOf, Administrative event is a sibling of Social event under Event, covering organizational tasks like registration, reviewing, submission, and camera-ready events. In edas, Social Event is a specific Non Academic Event (excursions, receptions, meals, breaks). These are distinct concepts: one is about administrative/organizational activities, the other about social/leisure activities. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. setMaxPapers (cmt) relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member, likely setting the maximum number of papers a PC member can handle. submit_until (sigkdd) relates a Document to a Deadline, indicating the submission deadline for a document. They connect entirely different entity types and serve unrelated purposes in the conference domain.

Security Topic is a specific subtopic of research (a kind of Topic in EDAS with siblings like Cryptography Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.), whereas Research Topic in EKAW is the general class of topics covered by events and papers. Security Topic is thus a specialization of Research Topic, not equivalent to it.

A is a topic about powerline transmission (a subject area under Topic), while B is an award for best applications paper (under Award). They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (invites_co-reviewers) relates Reviewer to Reviewer, capturing the act of a reviewer inviting another reviewer. Property B (write) relates Person to Item, capturing the act of a person writing an item (e.g., a document). They have different domains, different ranges, and denote completely different relations in the conference domain.

Steering committee is a type of committee responsible for overseeing a conference volume, while Author is a person who writes contributions. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.
Committee member is a person who serves on a committee, while Hotel room is a physical place. They share no instances and occupy entirely different branches of their ontologies.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria. In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution they review. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and denote different relations.

These two properties relate different entities in opposite conceptual directions. cmt:writtenBy has domain Review and range Reviewer (a Review is written by a Reviewer), while ekaw:hasReview has domain Paper and range Review (a Paper has a Review). They connect different pairs of entity types and are not inverses of each other either. They are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. 'was a committee chair of' links a Chair person to a Committee they lead, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present. The domains (Chair vs Speaker) and ranges (Committee vs Document) are disjoint concepts, and the relations describe structurally different associations (leadership role vs presentation artefact).

Both classes are named 'Conference' and represent the same core concept in the conference-organisation domain. They share structurally similar properties (name, end date) and are clearly intended to denote the same entity: a conference event. The differences in additional properties (e.g., topics, submission deadlines in edas vs. city, start date, and holding relationship in sigkdd) are complementary details rather than indicators of different concepts.

Short_paper in confOf is a type of academic contribution (a short research paper), whereas Best_Paper_Awards_Committee in sigkdd is a committee responsible for selecting best paper awards. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Item is a broad superclass encompassing Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle, etc. In sigkdd, Document is a specific class with children Abstract, Paper, Review. Since iasted already has Document as a child of Item, Item is strictly more general than sigkdd's Document. The two are not equivalent.

Both classes represent collections of important conference deadlines. 'Important dates' in the Conference ontology aggregates various deadline dates (abstract submission, full paper submission, camera-ready, acceptance announcement, start/end dates), while 'Deadline' in sigkdd has children for abstract submission, author notification, and paper submission deadlines. Both serve as containers for the set of key temporal milestones of a conference, and the specific date types they enumerate substantially overlap.

hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to a Subject Area (topic/field the paper covers), while has_tracks relates a Conference volume to a Track (organisational subdivision of a conference). These are structurally and semantically different relations: one classifies a document by topic, the other decomposes a conference volume into tracks. They do not share domain or range types, and their intended meanings do not coincide.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a broad superclass under Person encompassing authors, reviewers, chairs, and committee members—essentially any person affiliated with the conference. In iasted, IASTED_member is a specific subclass of Delegate (itself under Person via Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate), distinguishing members from non-members among conference delegates. The iasted IASTED_member is a narrower concept (a delegate who is an IASTED member) and is not equivalent to the broad cmt ConferenceMember. They are also not in a clean subsumption relation because the iasted hierarchy places IASTED_member under Delegate rather than under a general conference-member concept, and the cmt ConferenceMember covers roles (e.g., Author, Reviewer) not necessarily tied to IASTED membership status.
Author is a person who writes/submits papers, while Workshop is a type of conference event/session. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In EKAW, 'scientificallyOrganises' relates an Academic Institution to some scientific event or activity it organizes. In IASTED, 'occupy' relates a Person to a spatial location (Building, City, State) they occupy.
