In EDAS, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and also Person/TPC Member due to multiple inheritance), representing a type of conference event. In IASTED, 'Technical commitee' is a subclass of Delegate, representing a person who serves on a technical committee. One is a conference/event type, the other is a person/role type. They share no intended instances and are unrelated.

The cmt 'date' property captures a temporal value (a date) for a Conference, whereas the confOf 'has title' property captures a string label (a title) for Social events and Working events. They denote completely different attributes of conference-related entities, so they are unrelated.

The cmt property 'max Papers' specifies the maximum number of papers a Program Committee Member can review (domain: Program Committee Member, range: int). The iasted property 'done till' specifies the end date of a Deadline (domain: Deadline, range: date). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both classes represent a Program Committee in the conference domain. They share the same label, the same parent class (Commitute), and appear in sibling sets with other conference committee types (e.g., Organizing Committee). The sigkdd ontology's Program Committee is a well-known conference entity, and the Conference ontology's 'Program committee' has properties linking it to Conference volume, confirming it is the standard PC. No contextual differences suggest distinct meanings.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Person/Conference Member, denoting a human role. In Conference, Conference contribution is a subclass of Conference document, denoting a written artefact (with children like Poster, Presentation, Written contribution). Despite the superficial label similarity ('contribution' vs 'author'), these entities denote fundamentally different categories: a person vs a document. They are unrelated.

Invited speaker in Conference is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, a role defined by selection/invitation. Worker lecturer in iasted is a lecturer who is a worker (as opposed to a student lecturer), defined by employment status. These are orthogonal classifications: an invited speaker could be a worker or a student, and a worker lecturer need not be invited. The hierarchies and siblings confirm different classification axes, so the concepts do not coincide.

Person in iasted denotes a human participant (with children Delegate, Sponsor and properties like give, is present, is occupied by). Deadline in sigkdd denotes a temporal point in a conference schedule (with children like Deadline Abstract Submission and properties Date, submit until). These are completely disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Program committee (reviewing/accepting papers) and Organizing committee (logistics of the event) are distinct roles in conference organization. They are sibling committees under a common Committee parent but denote different concepts with different responsibilities.

confOf Member is a broad participant category (sibling of Regular and Student), while sigkdd Program_Committee_member is a specific organizer role under Organizator. A Member is not necessarily a PC member, but a PC member could be considered a type of Member/participant, making Member more general (subsumed_by the narrower PC member concept in the alignment sense).

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. In ekaw, 'technicallyOrganisedBy' (subproperty of 'organisedBy') links an event to the entity that technically organises it (e.g., a committee or organisation). In iasted, 'occupy' links a Person to a spatial location (Building, City, State) they occupy. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so the properties are unrelated.

The property 'is Member Of' in edas relates a Person to a Conference they are a member of, while 'send' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they send. These are completely different relations with different ranges (Conference vs Item) and different semantics (membership vs sending).

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. 'inverse of part Of 7' in ekaw is a mereological (part-whole) relation whose range is Event, meaning it connects something to an Event that it is part of. 'is given by' in iasted connects an Activity or Item to a Person who gives or presents it. They share no common domain or range types and express fundamentally different relationships (part-of vs. agent-of).

In confOf, 'Short paper' is a specific subtype of Contribution (a sibling of Paper and Poster), denoting a short-format submission. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class of documents submitted by authors. A short paper is a kind of paper, so the two are not equivalent: sigkdd's Paper is broader. However, they are not in a clean subsumption relation across ontologies because confOf already has a separate 'Paper' sibling, making the exact correspondence unclear. They overlap conceptually but are not the same concept.

cmt:Paper is a general class for any paper submitted to the conference (with subclasses Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties like hasBid, hasDecision, assignedTo that apply to all submissions). ekaw:Workshop_Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw:Paper, sibling to Conference Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, etc., denoting papers specifically submitted to a workshop. cmt:Paper is strictly more general than ekaw:Workshop_Paper.

Meta Reviewer is a specialized Reviewer who consolidates reviews for a paper, while Author is a Person who writes papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

A Reviewer is a person who evaluates submitted papers, while an Invited Speaker is a person invited to give a talk at the conference. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances; a reviewer is not necessarily an invited speaker and vice versa.

markConflictOfInterest relates Authors/Chairmen/Reviewers to Papers to indicate a conflict of interest, preventing reviewer assignment. notification_until relates Authors to a Deadline for author notifications. They connect different entities and serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a physical location/place in the conference domain. They share identical labels and overlapping children (Conference hall, Main office). The iasted Place is broader, covering buildings, rooms, and halls where conference activities occur, while sigkdd Place covers conference halls, hotels, and offices where people stay. The core intended instances—physical venues associated with conference events—coincide, making them equivalent as a reference alignment would record.

edas Published Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (one that has been published), while sigkdd Paper is the general class of papers submitted by authors. Published Paper is strictly more specific than sigkdd Paper, so edas Published Paper subsumes sigkdd Paper in the sense that every published paper is a paper but not vice versa. They are not equivalent because sigkdd Paper includes all papers (submitted, accepted, rejected, etc.), not only published ones.

Property A 'is a date of acceptance announcement' specifically denotes the date when acceptance decisions are announced, a particular milestone in the conference lifecycle. Property B 'done till' is a generic deadline-completion property on the Deadline class, indicating the time by which a deadline-related task must be completed. They have different semantics: A is a specific announcement date, while B is a generic deadline completion property. Their domains differ (Important dates vs Deadline) and they do not share the same intended meaning in the conference domain.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a meeting that takes place), while ekaw:Proceedings is a document (a multi-author volume of published papers). They are in disjoint branches of their respective ontologies (Event vs Document) and denote completely different kinds of things.

The two properties are completely different in meaning, domain, range, and type. A's 'is an abstract submission date' is a datatype property mapping an Important dates instance to a date value, representing a deadline. B's 'paperPresentedAs' is an object property mapping a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation, representing how a paper is presented at a conference. They share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. 'has_a_steering_committee' links a Conference volume to a Steering committee, while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution. They share no common domain or range types and denote entirely different relationships in the conference organization domain.

The two properties relate completely different entities and express different relations. Property A links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a chairing/organizing role over a conference part). Property B links a Document to a Speaker (a presentation authorship relation). The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, so the properties are unrelated.

Conference Trip is a social event (a trip organised as part of a conference), whereas Fee is a monetary amount charged for services. They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Organization in edas denotes an organizational entity (with subtypes Academia, Government, Industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. Person in iasted denotes an individual human (with subtypes Delegate, Sponsor). An organization is not a person; these are disjoint categories in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a document (a complete version of a submitted paper) in the cmt ontology, while Main office is a physical place in the iasted ontology. They belong to entirely different domains (document vs. place) and share no conceptual overlap.

In cmt, Rejection is a Decision (the outcome of reviewing a paper, rejecting it). In iasted, 'Receiving manuscript' is an Activity before conference — a logistical action of receiving submitted manuscripts. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a review decision outcome, the other is a pre-conference administrative activity. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

confOf:Workshop is a class representing a type of event (a workshop session at a conference), situated under Event > Working event. iasted:Author_cd_proceedings_included is a class representing a specific kind of person/author (one whose paper is included in CD proceedings), situated under Person/Delegate > Speaker > Author. These are completely different categories of entities in the conference domain: one is an event, the other is a person role. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are subclasses of Person, but they denote different roles. Committee member in Conference is a general committee role (with Chair and Co-chair as subclasses, linked to Committee via has members / was a member of). Member PC in confOf is specifically a program-committee member whose function is reviewing (comment says 'Reviewer'; properties expert On and reviewes). A Member PC is a committee member, but not every Committee member is a PC member (e.g., organizing committee members, track/workshop chairs). Thus they overlap without being equivalent.

Conference contribution is a scholarly work (paper, poster, presentation) submitted to a conference volume, while Payment document is a financial record (bank transfer, cheque). They share no instances and occupy completely different parts of the domain.

The property rejectPaper in cmt relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of rejecting a paper), while has_a_publisher in Conference relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

confOf Member sits under Participant > Person with siblings Regular and Student, suggesting it denotes any conference participant who is a member (a broad category). ekaw PC Member is specifically a Programme Committee member, a narrower role that is also a Possible Reviewer. A confOf Member could be any participant, not necessarily a PC member, so confOf Member is more general and is subsumed_by ekaw PC Member.

The two properties relate completely different entities and have different meanings. In cmt, 'acceptedBy' links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it. In confOf, 'writes' links an Author to the Contribution they wrote. They have different domains (Paper vs Author), different ranges (Administrator vs Contribution), and different semantics (acceptance decision vs authorship).

A Program Committee Chair oversees the reviewing process and assigns reviews, while a Session Chair moderates a presentation session. These are distinct roles in conference organization with different responsibilities, instances, and hierarchies.

Demo Chair and Program Chair are distinct organizational roles in a conference. A Demo Chair oversees demonstrations, while a Program Chair oversees the technical program (paper acceptance, sessions). They are not synonyms, neither subsumes the other, and they do not overlap in intended instances.

Both are datatype properties that associate a conference-related entity with a URL, but they differ in specificity and domain. A's 'logo URL' (domain Conference, range anyURI) points specifically to the URL of the conference logo, whereas B's 'has a URL' (domain Conference www, range string) is a generic property for any URL associated with a conference website. The generic property subsumes the specific one conceptually, but the domains (Conference vs Conference www) may not coincide, so 'related' is the safest verdict.

PC Chair is an administrative/organizational role (chair of the Programme Committee), while Tutorial speaker is a presenter who gives a tutorial. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain: one manages the review process, the other delivers content. They share no organizational or functional overlap.

Reception is a social event (e.g., a banquet or gathering) in the confOf ontology, while Research is an academic activity performed before a conference in the iasted ontology. Their intended instances, paths, and siblings show no overlap; they denote completely different concepts.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Best Applications Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'has Call' in edas relates an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., call for papers), while 'award' in sigkdd relates something (likely a person or paper) to an Award. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain: one concerns the call-for-papers process, the other concerns awarding honors. They share no semantic overlap.

A Welcome Talk is a specific ceremonial/organisational talk opening or greeting a conference, whereas a Plenary lecture is a substantive academic lecture delivered to all conference participants. They are different kinds of conference events with distinct purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

Programme in edas denotes a conference programme document (schedule of events), linked to Conference Event via hasProgramme/belongsToEvent. Review in iasted denotes a review document of a submission. Despite sharing the parent Document, they denote completely different artefacts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In the edas ontology, Workshop is a specific kind of academic event (a workshop, with siblings like Paper Presentation and Talk Event). In the ekaw ontology, Track is a different kind of scientific event (a conference track/session), and Workshop is explicitly listed as a sibling of Track under Scientific Event. Since Workshop and Track are distinct sibling concepts in ekaw, they denote different things: a workshop is a standalone academic event, while a track is a thematic session within a conference. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different entities. `forEvent` links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the Academic Event it is issued for, whereas `scientificallyOrganisedBy` links an event to the Academic Institution that scientifically organises it. Their domains and ranges differ (Call -> Academic Event vs. unspecified -> Academic Institution), and they express orthogonal relationships in the conference domain.

A's 'has a name' is a generic datatype property applicable to multiple classes (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), while B's 'Name of conference' is specifically scoped to Conference. Thus B is a narrower, more specific property than A, making A subsumed_by B in the sense that B's domain is a subset of A's domains. They are not equivalent because A applies to many entity types beyond conferences.

Entity A is a topic within the subject taxonomy of wireless communications, a subclass of Topic. Entity B is a document type, specifically an abstract for an invited talk, a subclass of Abstract under Document. One denotes a subject area, the other a concrete document artefact; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

A's 'Accepted contribution' is a document (a paper that passed review), while B's 'Refusing manuscript' is an activity (the act of rejecting a manuscript). They are not the same kind of entity: one is a document artefact, the other is an action/process. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasSubjectArea links a Paper to a Subject Area (classifying the paper's topic). In sigkdd, can_stay_in links a Person to a Place (indicating accommodation). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a type of Chairman), while Conference Dinner is a social event (a type of Meal Event). They denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

MeetingRoomPlace in edas is a physical location (a type of Place) where meetings are held, sibling to accommodation, venue, and dining places. Conference_Trip in ekaw is a social event (a type of Event), sibling to Conference_Banquet. One is a spatial location, the other is an event/activity. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both classes denote the same concept: a paper/contribution that has been accepted and is in its final, camera-ready form. The labels are near-synonymous ('Camera ready contribution' vs 'Camera Ready Paper'), and both sit at the terminal end of a document/publication workflow (Accepted contribution -> Camera ready contribution in Conference; Paper -> Camera Ready Paper in ekaw). The slight terminological difference (contribution vs paper) is a common synonym in this domain and does not indicate a different intended extension.

ekaw:University is an academic institution (organisation), while iasted:Student_lecturer is a person who is a student giving a lecture. They denote completely different categories of entities (organisation vs. person/role), so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In iasted, 'is equipped by' connects a Place to an Item (a place is equipped by some item). In sigkdd, 'obtain' connects an Author to an Award (an author obtains an award). The domains (Place vs Author) and ranges (Item vs Award) are disjoint, and the intended meanings share no overlap.

LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Item > Audiovisual equipment), while Listener is a person who attends a conference (Person > Listener). They denote completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Administrator is an administrative role (a kind of Person who manages the conference tool), while iasted:Author is a subkind of Speaker/Delegate who writes papers. An administrator is not an author, and an author is not an administrator; the two classes have disjoint intended instances.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas iasted:Non_speaker is a person role (subclass of Delegate, sibling of Speaker and Listener). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

edas RatedPapers is a highly specific subclass of Paper (papers that have been rated), sitting under Active Paper under Paper. sigkdd Paper is the general concept of a paper (a document submitted by an author). Thus every Rated Paper is a Paper, but not vice versa, so RatedPapers is subsumed_by sigkdd Paper.

confOf:Member PC is a person who is a reviewer (a committee member), while ekaw:Neutral Review is a document (a review with neutral sentiment). One is an agent, the other is an artefact; they share no intended instances.

In edas, 'Microelectronics Topic' is a subject/topic of a conference paper (a subclass of Topic alongside Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). In iasted, 'Transport vehicle' is a physical item (subclass of Item) with concrete children such as Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, and Van. These denote completely different kinds of entities—an academic subject area versus a physical vehicle—so they are unrelated.

The cmt property hasProgramCommitteeMember is a specific relation linking a Program Committee to its Program Committee Members, while the Conference property has_members is a general relation linking any Committee to its Committee members. Since Program Committee is a subtype of Committee and Program Committee Member is a subtype of Committee member, hasProgramCommitteeMember is a specialization (subproperty) of has_members. They are not equivalent because has_members applies to all committees, not just program committees.

Industry Organization in EDAS denotes a for-profit commercial company, sibling to Academia/Government/NGO organizations. University in EKAW is an academic degree-granting institution. These are disjoint categories of organization; neither subsumes the other.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person denoting individuals who contribute to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers). Presenter state is a subclass of State, a temporal or modal state, not a person. They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Call for participation is a conference document (e.g., an announcement or informational document), while Government Organization is a type of organization. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in their intended instances.

These properties relate entirely different things. In Conference, 'has_been_assigned_a_review_reference' links a Submitted contribution/Topic to a Review preference (about assigning review preferences to papers/topics). In edas, 'isReviewHistoryOf' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (about a reviewer's review history). Different domains, different ranges, different semantics — no alignment relation holds.

The two properties relate completely different entities. 'was a steering committee of' links a Steering committee to a Conference volume, while 'expert On' links a Member PC to a Topic. They share no common domain or range types and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

Regular author in Conference ontology is a subclass of Conference contribution and Conference contributor, denoting a person who authors a paper. Regular Paper in ekaw is a subclass of Paper, denoting a document type. One is a person/role, the other is a document artefact; they share the word 'regular' but denote completely different entities.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (under Person > Chairman), while Trip city is a geographic location (under City). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote the same concept of a conference event in the conference-organisation domain. In confOf, Conference is a subclass of Working event, distinguishing it from Tutorial and Workshop, which matches the typical conference-track usage. In cmt, Conference is the central entity managed by administrators with properties like date, logo URL, and conference members. The intended instances coincide: both represent the academic conference itself, not a more general event or a different artefact.

Conference www is a digital document (a web page with a URL) under Conference document, while Session room is a physical place under Place. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Both classes share children such as Tutorial and Workshop, indicating overlap in the conference domain. However, Conference_part in ontology A is a broad organizational division of a conference (including Track, Tutorial, Workshop) and is not itself a presentation event. Individual_Presentation in ontology B is a Scientific Event where a paper is presented (including Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). The extensional overlap is partial (e.g., Tutorial appears in both), but the intended instances do not coincide, so the relation is related rather than equivalent.

Entity A is a person who registered early and paid (subclass of Person > Conference applicant), while entity B is a monetary fee for hotel accommodation (subclass of Money > Fee). They belong to completely disjoint hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Associated Chair is a person role (a kind of chairman who helps run the conference), while Submission event is an administrative event representing the act of submitting contributions. One is a person, the other is an event; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Conference Trip in EKAW is a subclass of Social Event, denoting an excursion or social outing associated with a conference. Trip city in IASTED is a subclass of City, denoting a geographical location. These are completely different kinds of entities (an event vs. a place), so they are unrelated despite the shared word 'Trip'.

contactEmail is a datatype property from Contribution to string (an email address), while writtenBy is an object property from Document to Person (authorship). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

These classes denote entirely different concepts. In ontology A, 'Information for participants' is a subclass of 'Conference document' — a static informational artefact (like a call for papers or conference announcement). In ontology B, 'Reviewing results event' is a subclass of 'Administrative event' — a temporal event representing the reviewing outcome phase. A document and an event are disjoint categories, and the specific meanings (general participant information vs. reviewing results) do not overlap.

The cmt 'name' property assigns a string-valued name to a Conference or Person, whereas the edas 'hasCountry' property links a Conference to a Country object. They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning.

The two properties denote different temporal relations. `is sent after` (domain Item, range Time) describes when an item is sent after a point in time, while `submit until` (domain Document, range Deadline) specifies a deadline by which a document must be submitted. They differ in directionality, domain/range types, and meaning (post-sending vs. pre-deadline submission).

A's 'Registration fee' is a general class covering all registration fee types (author, non-author, member, nonmember, student). B's 'Registration SIGMOD Member' is a specific leaf class for SIGMOD-member registration. They sit at different levels of generality and are not equivalent. Moreover, B is a sibling of 'Registration SIGKDD Member', indicating it is a conference-specific member category, not a generic registration fee. Since A's children are iasted-specific fee types and B is a sigkdd-specific member fee, there is no direct subsumption relation between the two ontologies' class hierarchies; they are unrelated.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person representing people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). In the Conference ontology, Conference represents the conference event itself, which has Conference volume as a child and is the subject of properties like 'has a name'. These are completely different concepts: one is a person/role, the other is an event/organization. They share no semantic overlap.

These properties are completely different. 'location Of' is an object property relating a Location to an Event (indicating where an event takes place), while 'done till' is a datatype property relating a Deadline to a date (indicating the deadline date). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Property A (has_a_committee_co-chair) links a Committee to a Co-chair, denoting committee membership/leadership. Property B (writes) links an Author to a Contribution, denoting authorship. They relate entirely different domain and range types and represent different relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different entities in opposite directions. In cmt, `assignedTo` links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assigned to reviewer for review). In confOf, `writes` links an Author to a Contribution (author writes a paper). The domains (Paper vs Author), ranges (Reviewer vs Contribution), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

cmt:co-writePaper is restricted to Co-author -> Paper, while confOf:writes is the more general Author -> Contribution relation. A co-author writing a paper is a specific case of an author writing a contribution, so co-writePaper is subsumed by writes rather than equivalent.
Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while SecurityTopic is a subject-area topic. They share no domain overlap.

Both are subclasses of Deadline in the conference domain, but they denote different kinds of deadlines: 'Registation deadline' refers to the deadline for registering for the conference, while 'Deadline Paper Submission' refers to the deadline for submitting papers. They are sibling-like concepts under a common Deadline parent, not equivalent.

The cmt property printHardcopyMailingManifests relates an Administrator to a Conference (printing hardcopy mailing manifests for a conference), while the ekaw property paperPresentedAs relates a Paper to an Individual Presentation (indicating how a paper is presented). They connect completely different domain and range types and describe unrelated activities in the conference domain.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (organizational/committee membership). In the Conference ontology, is_given_by links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it. The domains (Conference vs Presentation), ranges (Conference Member vs Active conference participant), and intended meanings (membership vs authorship/delivery) are distinct, so the properties are unrelated.

Both classes denote a Workshop in the conference domain. In Conference it is a Conference part (sibling of Track, Tutorial) and the range of has_workshops; in confOf it is a Working event (sibling of Conference, Tutorial). Despite slightly different taxonomic positions, the intended instances coincide: workshops as organisational sub-events of a conference. The shared label, overlapping siblings (Tutorial), and domain context strongly support equivalence.

An Organizing committee is a committee responsible for organizing a conference volume, while an Industry Organization is a type of organization (alongside Academia, Government, NGO) representing an industry entity. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In EDAS, ConferenceEvent is a broad top-level class covering any event associated with a conference (academic or non-academic, with subtypes like talks, meals, social events). In EKAW, Conference_Session is a narrow subtype of Session under Scientific Event, denoting a specific scheduled session within a conference programme. EDAS ConferenceEvent therefore subsumes EKAW Conference_Session.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference, but `date` in cmt denotes the date of the conference (likely the start or overall date), while `End of conference` in sigkdd specifically denotes the end date. They overlap in being conference date properties but are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Conference is a specific scientific event (one edition of a conference), while in iasted, Conference activity is a kind of Activity encompassing things like cocktail receptions, coffee breaks, lectures, and registration. They denote completely different concepts: a conference event vs. activities that occur at a conference.

Mobile Computing Topic is a subject-area classification under Topic in the EDAS ontology, while Tutorial Abstract is a document type (a kind of abstract) in the EKAW ontology. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Talk Event in edas is a presentation/lecture event during a conference (with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk, siblings like Paper Presentation). Activity before conference in iasted covers pre-conference activities such as accepting/receiving/refusing manuscripts, renting, research. These are temporally and conceptually distinct: one is a talk event at the conference, the other is preparatory activity before it. No overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer it was assigned by (a meta-relationship about assignment delegation). In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to the Contribution they review (the actual reviewing relationship). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Call for paper is a document type (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Paper is a contribution type (the submitted work itself). They are different kinds of entities in the conference domain: one is a call/announcement document, the other is the actual academic paper submitted.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference Venue Place in edas is a physical location (subclass of Place). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Industrial Paper is a type of academic document (a paper written for an industrial track at a conference), while Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'assigned To' property links a Paper to a Reviewer (i.e., a paper is assigned to a reviewer for review). The Conference 'has_a_submitted_contribution' property links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (i.e., a review-expertise record references the submitted contribution being reviewed). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not equivalent.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. In cmt, 'assignReviewer' relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (the act of assigning a reviewer to a paper). In edas, 'hasReviewHistory' relates a Reviewer to a PersonalReviewHistory (a reviewer's past review record). They connect different entity types in different directions and represent different relationships.

confOf:Conference denotes the overall conference event (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while iasted:Speaker_lecture denotes a specific lecture given by a speaker within a session. These are completely different levels of granularity and different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Banquet is a sit-down meal/social event, while Coffee break is a short refreshment pause between sessions. They are distinct kinds of conference activities with different purposes and durations; neither subsumes the other.

Submitted contribution is a written document submitted to a conference (a paper), while Author is a person who writes a paper. They are disjoint categories (document vs person) and share no domain overlap.

In confOf, City is a top-level class representing any city (it is the range of hasCity for both Organization and Person). In iasted, Trip_city is a subclass of City specifically denoting a city associated with a trip (e.g., where a presenter or sponsor travels). Thus iasted's Trip_city is a narrower concept, subsumed by confOf's general City.

Conference document in ontology A is a broad class encompassing call for papers, conference contributions, reviews, announcements, etc. Payment document in ontology B is a specific subclass of Document whose instances are Bank transfer and Cheque—financial payment instruments. The two classes have no instance overlap: one covers conference-related documents generally, the other covers payment records specifically. They are unrelated rather than subsuming one another, since Payment document is not a kind of Conference document and vice versa.

The two properties have opposite directions and relate different entities. In cmt, 'read By Meta Reviewer' goes from Paper to Meta Reviewer (a meta-reviewer reads a paper). In Conference, 'reviews' goes from Review to Reviewed contribution (a review document is about a contribution). They are not the same relation, nor is one a subrelation of the other; they connect different domain and range types in different directions.

hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country (a geographic location), while organises relates an Organisation or Person to an Event. Despite sharing the same domain, the ranges (Country vs Event) are completely different, so the properties denote unrelated relations.

In the Conference ontology, Presentation is a broad class covering any oral or visual presentation of a conference contribution, with children including Invited talk, Poster, Regular contribution, and Written contribution. In the edas ontology, Paper Presentation is a specific kind of academic event for presenting an accepted paper. Paper Presentation is thus a narrower concept (a specific presentation event tied to an accepted paper), while Presentation is the more general category. The two are not equivalent; edas:PaperPresentation is subsumed by Conference:Presentation.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. cmt:submitPaper has domain Author and range Paper, modelling the act of an author submitting a paper. confOf:dealsWith has domain Contribution and range Topic, modelling the subject matter a contribution addresses. They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Multimedia Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area of a paper (e.g., alongside Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). Program Committee in sigkdd is a subclass of Committee, representing a group of people organizing the conference. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a specific conference leadership role (a Chairman responsible for paper assignment in CMT), while Science Worker in confOf is a broad category of academic/research personnel. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Committee member in Conference is a person serving on a committee (with children Chair, Co-chair; linked to Committee via was-a-member-of). Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a person who could review a paper (with child PC Member; linked to Paper/Review via reviewer-of-paper/review-written-by). A committee member is not necessarily a potential paper reviewer, and a possible reviewer is not necessarily a committee member. The two concepts address different organizational roles, so they are unrelated.

The two properties differ in both domain and meaning. 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee (logistical/administrative body). 'scientifically Organises' links an Academic Institution to some scientific event/activity, denoting scientific sponsorship rather than committee membership. The domains (Conference volume vs Academic Institution) and the intended semantics do not coincide, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

City and State are distinct geographic/administrative concepts. In confOf, City is a location for organizations and persons. In iasted, State has subclasses like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state, and participates in spatial relations. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship; they are different geographic entities.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range types. In Conference, 'has_been_assigned_a_review_reference' links a Submitted contribution/Topic to a Review preference, indicating a review assignment or preference for a paper. In edas, 'hasReviewHistory' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History, tracking a reviewer's past reviewing activity. They connect different entities in different directions and capture different aspects of the review process.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. In cmt, 'readByReviewer' has domain Paper and range Reviewer, meaning a paper is read by a reviewer. In iasted, 'write' has domain Person and range Item, meaning a person writes an item. These are distinct relations: one captures reading/reviewing, the other captures authorship. They are not equivalent, not inverse equivalents, and do not subsume each other.

A Conference Session is a scheduled event during a conference (parent Session, siblings Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop Session). B Research is a pre-conference activity (parent Activity before conference, siblings Accepting/Receiving/Refusing manuscript). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, locationOf maps a Location to an Event (where an event takes place). In iasted, is_present maps a Person to a Time (when a person is present). They share neither domain nor range, and denote different relations in the conference domain.

The property 'has the last name' denotes a person's surname, while 'has Phone' denotes a phone number. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they capture completely different attributes and are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Rejected_contribution represents papers that were rejected after review, while Accepted_Paper represents papers that were accepted for publication. These are disjoint, mutually exclusive outcomes of the review process - a paper cannot be both rejected and accepted. They are sibling concepts under their respective reviewed/evaluated contribution hierarchies, not equivalent.

Property A (has_a_committee_co-chair) relates a Committee to its Co-chair member, while property B (give) relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give. They have different domains (Committee vs Person), different ranges (Co-chair vs Activity/Item), and express completely different relationships in the conference domain.

Both classes denote academic organizations/institutions, situated under a common Organization parent. 'Academia Organization' and 'Academic Institution' are synonymous in the conference domain, referring to universities, research institutes, and similar academic bodies. The structural positions align (both are subclasses of a general Organization class), and the ekaw class's children (Research Institute, University) are exactly the kinds of entities an 'Academia Organization' would cover.

Invited speaker is a specific role of a person who gives an invited talk at a conference, while Two Level Conference appears to be a classification of conference structure/type. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Microelectronics Topic is a subject-area topic under Topic in edas, representing a research domain. Card is a physical item (with child Credit card) under Item in iasted, representing a payment or identification card. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Conference contributor in ontology Conference is a subclass of Person, denoting people who contribute to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers). Scientific Event in ekaw is a subclass of Event, denoting events such as conferences, sessions, workshops, and tracks. These are disjoint categories (person vs. event) with no overlap in intended instances.

Track in EKAW is a session-like subdivision of a conference scientific programme (a set of presentations grouped by theme), whereas Program Committee in SIGKDD is a committee of people responsible for reviewing papers. They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Invited Talk Abstract is a document (an abstract of an invited talk), while Nonauthor registration fee is a monetary fee for non-author registration. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Presentation in the Conference ontology denotes a conference contribution that is presented (e.g., a talk), with properties like 'is given by' an active participant. Audiovisual equipment in iasted denotes physical equipment (computers, projectors, etc.) used at a conference. These are completely different concepts despite both appearing in a conference domain ontology.

In confOf, Workshop is a specific kind of event (a working event sibling to Conference and Tutorial), representing a workshop as a standalone event type. In ekaw, Workshop is also a sibling of Session under Scientific Event, but Session itself is a broader category that groups together conference sessions, demo sessions, poster sessions, regular sessions, and workshop sessions. Thus confOf:Workshop denotes a workshop event, while ekaw:Session denotes a session (a time-slot grouping within an event). They are at different levels of granularity and do not share the same intended instances; a workshop event is not a session, and a session is not a workshop. They are therefore unrelated rather than equivalent or subsumed.

The cmt property hasProgramCommitteeMember relates a Program Committee to its members (people serving on the committee). The ekaw property organisedBy relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. These are different relations: committee membership vs. event organization. They have different domains (Program Committee vs. Event) and different ranges (Program Committee Member vs. Organisation/Person), and no clear subsumption relationship holds between them.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), whereas Activity after conference in iasted is a post-conference event such as a tour or departure (subclass of Activity). They denote completely different categories of entities—a person versus an event—so they are unrelated.

Single Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (an event/organization with a single review or decision level), while Main office in sigkdd is a physical place (sibling of Conference hall and Hotel under Place). They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Closing Talk is a class representing a scheduled conference event (a talk that closes a conference), while Invited Speaker is a class representing a person (a speaker invited to the conference). One is an event/activity, the other is a person/role. They are disjoint categories in the conference domain and share no subsumption relationship.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference, denoting the act of finalizing paper assignments for the conference. paperPresentedAs relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation, denoting how a paper is presented. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a short summary/abstract of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version), while RatedPapers in edas represents papers that have received reviews/ratings. They denote completely different concepts: one is about the document type/length, the other about the review status of a paper.

Call For Reviews is a solicitation/announcement requesting reviewers to submit reviews, while Review is the actual review document itself. They are different types of entities in the conference domain.

These properties denote different relations. 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), capturing the peer-review assignment. 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person who signs it, capturing authorship or endorsement. The domains differ (Paper vs. Item) and the ranges differ in meaning (reviewers vs. any signing person). They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

These properties relate different entities in opposite directions. In edas, 'isMemberOf' links a Person to a Conference (person is a member of the conference). In sigkdd, 'holded_by' links a Conference to ACM SIGKDD (the conference is organized/held by the SIGKDD organization). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Person vs Conference, Conference vs ACM SIGKDD), and the intended semantics are unrelated.

Paper Full Version is a complete version of a conference paper (Document > Paper > Paper Full Version), whereas Full day tour is a post-conference social activity (Activity > Activity after conference > Full day tour). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Workshop is an event where work is presented (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while iasted:Hotel_registration_form is a document/form used to register for hotel accommodation (subclass of Form, sibling of Author information form and Registration form). They denote completely different categories of entities—an event vs. a document—so they are unrelated.

The cmt 'assignReviewer' property specifically relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to a paper). The iasted 'give' property relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving a presentation or item). These are different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Invited_speaker is a person who gives an invited talk at a conference (subclass of Conference contributor / Person), whereas Sponsor_state is a state or role associated with a sponsor (subclass of State). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

The cmt property `hasProgramCommitteeMember` links a Program Committee to its members (domain: Program Committee, range: Program Committee Member), modeling committee composition. The confOf property `parallel_with` links two Administrative events to each other, modeling scheduling concurrency. They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate completely different entities. 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to its Chair (a person role), while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present. They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Submissions deadline is a temporal deadline for submitting papers, while Best Student Paper Award is an award given for a paper. They belong to entirely different categories (Time/Deadline vs Award) and share no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Paper is a class representing a submitted document (a contribution), with properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer, etc. In sigkdd, Deadline is a class representing a temporal deadline (with a Date property), and its children are abstract submission, author notification, and paper submission deadlines. These denote completely different concepts—a document vs. a temporal milestone—so they are unrelated.

Late Registered Participant classifies a conference participant by registration timing, while Organizing Committee member is a specific organizational role. These are orthogonal dimensions of classification with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (hasConferenceMember) links a Conference to individual Conference Members (persons who are members). Property B (has_an_organizing_committee) links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee (a committee body, not an individual person). The ranges differ: Conference Member is a person, while Organizing committee is a committee/organization. They also have different parent structures (A has no parent listed; B is a subproperty of has_a_committee). These are distinct relations in the conference domain.

Reviewer (Conference ontology) denotes a person who performs paper reviews, with properties like review expertise, review preference, and co-reviewer invitation. Conference Chair (edas) denotes the person chairing the entire conference, with properties like initiating calls and being a session/TPC-level organizer. In edas, Reviewer and Conference Chair are explicitly modeled as distinct sibling classes under Person. These are different roles in the conference domain: a reviewer evaluates papers while a conference chair leads the conference. They do not share instances by definition and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'is occupied by' in iasted relates a Building, City, or State to a Person who occupies it, while 'pay' in sigkdd relates a Person to a Registration fee they pay. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relations (occupancy vs. payment), so they are unrelated.

The two properties operate on disjoint domains and ranges and express opposite relations. In cmt, writtenBy links a Review to the Reviewer who authored it. In confOf, writes links an Author to a Contribution (paper). They are not inverses of the same relation because Review/Reviewer and Author/Contribution denote different concepts in these ontologies, so a reference alignment would treat them as unrelated rather than equivalent or inverse.

Attendee (edas) is a Person who attends a conference, while General Chair (sigkdd) is an organizer who chairs the conference. These are distinct roles: an attendee is a participant, whereas the General Chair is the head of the organizing committee. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Tutorial Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Abstract under Document, representing a written summary of a tutorial. Tip in iasted is a subclass of Money, representing a monetary gratuity. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:Conference denotes a conference event/organization (with properties like date, members, administrators, paper assignments), while ekaw:Abstract is a subclass of Document representing textual abstracts of papers/talks. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Review is a Document produced by a Reviewer about a Paper. In Conference, Reviewed contribution is the Paper itself that has undergone review (a subclass of Written contribution). One is the review document, the other is the reviewed paper; they are different entities in the review process.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. `writtenBy` (domain: Review, range: Reviewer) relates a review to the reviewer who wrote it. `invites_co-reviewers` (domain: Reviewer, range: Reviewer) relates a reviewer to other reviewers they invite to help review. They connect different entity types in different directions and represent entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

Chairman in cmt is a person who serves as a conference/program committee chair, while Registration Student in sigkdd is a type of registration fee for students. One is a person/role, the other is a fee category; they share no instances and have no meaningful overlap.

In ekaw, Negative_Review is a subclass of Review (a document artefact expressing a negative evaluation of a paper). In iasted, Reviewer is a subclass of Speaker (a person who writes reviews). One denotes a document, the other a person; they share only the lexical stem 'review' and have no semantic overlap.

A 'Conference applicant' is someone who applies to attend/register for a conference, whereas a 'Conference Participant' is someone who actually participates in the conference. The two concepts denote different roles in the conference lifecycle (applicant vs. participant), and neither subsumes the other: an applicant may not become a participant, and a participant may not have been an applicant (e.g., invited speakers). They share the parent Person but have distinct intended instances.

Co-author in cmt is a person who co-writes a paper, sitting under Person > Conference Member > Author. Author attendee book registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee for an author attending with a book, sitting under Money > Fee > Registration fee. One is a person role, the other is a financial charge; they share no domain overlap.

hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country, while speak_in relates a Person to a Place or Time. They connect different domain/range types and express different relations (nationality/location vs. speaking venue/time).

External Reviewer is a person assigned to review a paper on behalf of another Reviewer, while Scholar is a price-category participant (a student/discounted attendee). They share only the parent Person and denote completely different roles in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings. 'has an expertise' (domain: Review expertise) captures the expertise area associated with a review assignment, while 'Nation' (domain: Person) records a person's country. They relate different kinds of things and share no semantic overlap.

Review in cmt is a document written by a reviewer about a paper, while Tax in iasted is a monetary charge (subclass of Money with children like Departure tax and Value added tax). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:University is an academic institution that scholars study at, a subclass of Organization. sigkdd:Organizing_Committee is a committee responsible for organizing a conference, a subclass of Committee. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

cmt's Paper Abstract is a specific subclass of Paper (a short/abstract version), sibling to Paper Full Version. confOf's Paper is the general paper class under Contribution. The confOf Paper is more general, so Paper Abstract is subsumed_by confOf Paper.

Conference Member in cmt is a person who is a member of a conference (parent: Person; subclasses include Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair, etc.). Meal Event in edas is a non-academic event during a conference such as a dinner or break (parent: Non Academic Event > Conference Event; has a menu). One denotes a person/role, the other denotes a scheduled event. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf's 'Submission event' is a temporal/administrative event denoting the act of submitting contributions, while sigkdd's 'Organizing Committee' is a standing committee (a group of people) responsible for organizing the conference. They belong to completely different branches of the domain (events vs. committees) and share no instance overlap.

In cmt, 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer, denoting the assignment of a paper to a reviewer for review. In iasted, 'is given by' links an Activity/Item to a Person, denoting who presents or gives an activity/item (e.g., a presentation or lecture). The domains and ranges differ: Paper vs. Activity/Item, and Reviewer vs. Person. The relations are distinct: paper-reviewer assignment for reviewing vs. activity-person giving/presenting. They do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Both classes are subclasses of Document and represent the same concept: a summary of a paper. In ekaw, Abstract has specialized subclasses (Invited Talk Abstract, Tutorial Abstract) and is linked to presentations, while in sigkdd it is a simpler taxonomy with siblings Paper and Review. Despite the difference in granularity, the intended instances of Abstract coincide across both ontologies.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and direction of meaning. In ekaw, 'presentationOfPaper' links an Individual Presentation to the Paper/Abstract being presented (presentation -> paper). In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it (document -> speaker). They are not inverses of each other either, since one connects presentations to papers and the other connects documents to speakers. They denote different relations in the conference domain.

Entity A is a research topic in the domain of parallel and distributed computing, a subclass of Topic. Entity B is an award given for the best research paper, a subclass of Award. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Poster Paper' in ekaw is a type of academic document (a paper presented as a poster), while a 'Silver Supporter' in sigkdd is a type of conference sponsor/supporter at a particular tier. They belong to entirely different domain categories (documents vs. sponsors) and share no instances.

In cmt, Reviewer is a Conference Member who reviews papers, with properties like assign External Reviewer, read By Reviewer, mark Conflict Of Interest, etc. In iasted, Reviewer is a Speaker (which is a Delegate) who is also a reviewer. The iasted Reviewer is more specific: it is restricted to delegates/speakers at the conference, while cmt Reviewer is any conference member (including external reviewers who may not attend). The iasted hierarchy (Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Speaker > Reviewer) shows Reviewer is a specialized role of a delegate/speaker, whereas cmt Reviewer is a broader conference member role. Thus cmt Reviewer subsumes iasted Reviewer, meaning iasted Reviewer is subsumed_by cmt Reviewer.

These properties denote completely different relations. EKAW's 'organised By' links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. IASTED's 'is designed for' links Activity, Money, or Time to an Activity or Person it is intended for. Despite both having Person in the range, the domain concepts (Event vs. Activity/Money/Time) and the relational semantics (organization/management vs. design/purpose) are distinct. There is no meaningful overlap in the conference domain.

The two properties run in opposite directions and connect different entity types. confOf:reviewes goes from Member_PC to Contribution (reviewer -> paper), while ekaw:reviewWrittenBy goes from Review to Possible_Reviewer (review -> reviewer). They are not inverses of each other either, since one links a person to a paper and the other links a review document to a person. They denote different relationships in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a conference edition in the conference-organization domain. EKAW defines Conference as a specific edition of a conference (a Scientific Event), while SIGKDD models Conference with properties like name, city, start/end dates, and a relationship to ACM SIGKDD as the organizer. These represent the same concept: a single conference event/edition.

Conference announcement is a document (subclass of Conference document) that announces a conference, while Conference hall is a physical place (subclass of Place) where a conference is held. They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different categories of entities: a document vs. a physical location.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In EDAS, 'relatesTo' has domain Document and range Academic Event/Conference/Conference Session/Person, indicating a document is associated with or mentions those entities. In EKAW, 'organisedBy' has domain Event and range Organisation/Person, indicating an event is organised by an agent. The domains (Document vs Event) and the intended semantics (document-to-entity association vs event-to-organiser) do not coincide, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalisation of the other.

confOf:Conference is an event (a conference as an organisational event), while iasted:Student_lecturer is a person role (a student who lectures). They share the word 'Conference' only incidentally in the path of B; their intended instances are completely disjoint.

The two properties are completely unrelated. 'has_the_last_name' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's surname. 'is_paid_with' is an object property from Money to Item, capturing what item money is paid with. They have different domains, different ranges, different types, and no semantic overlap.

In ekaw, Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), whereas in iasted, Conference building is a physical place/building where a conference is held. These are completely different concepts — an event vs. a physical venue — so they are unrelated.

The property 'title' in cmt has domain Paper and range string, representing the title of a paper. The property 'hasLastName' in edas has domain Person and range string, representing the last name of a person. These properties relate completely different kinds of entities (documents vs. people) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different concepts. `has a date of issue` applies to a Conference document (e.g., when a paper or proceedings was issued) and ranges over a date, whereas `end Date` applies to a Conference itself (the end date and time of the conference event) and ranges over a dateTime. They relate different kinds of entities and capture different temporal notions, so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

A 'Steering committee' and an 'Organizing Committee' are distinct roles in conference organization. A steering committee provides strategic oversight and governance, while an organizing committee handles logistical arrangements. Though both are subclasses of Committee, they denote different kinds of committees with different responsibilities and members.

The two properties are completely different in meaning and structure. `locationOf` in ekaw is an object property linking a Location to an Event (where an event takes place). `Date` in sigkdd is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a dateTime value (when a deadline occurs). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Rejection is a subclass of Decision (the act/decision of rejecting a paper), whereas in edas, Rejected Paper is a subclass of Paper (the document that was rejected). These are different entities at different ontology levels: one is a decision, the other is a document. They are related in the sense that a rejected paper is the subject of a rejection decision, but they are not equivalent.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range types. cmt:memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while edas:isInitiatedBy links a Call (e.g., for papers/reviews) to conference roles such as Conference Chair, Session Chair, or TPC Member (who initiated the call). They share no common semantics, direction, or participant types.

The cmt 'title' property applies to Paper and captures the paper's title, while confOf 'hasSurname' applies to Person and captures a person's surname. They have disjoint domains and denote completely different attributes, so they are unrelated.

Conference contributor in ontology Conference is a subclass of Person (a human who contributes to a conference, e.g., author, speaker, participant). Conference in ekaw is a subclass of Scientific Event (one edition of a conference). These denote completely different categories of entities: a person vs. an event.

The cmt 'name' property gives the name of a Conference or Person, while the Conference 'has a URL' property gives the URL of a Conference www object. They relate different kinds of entities and denote different attributes, so they are unrelated.

Review is a peer-review document written by a Reviewer for a Paper, while Meal Menu is a menu for a Meal Event. They share only the generic Document parent but denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Written_contribution in Conference is a subclass of Conference document/contribution, denoting a document (e.g., a paper). Author in edas is a subclass of Person, denoting a human who writes papers. These are disjoint categories (document vs. person) despite the superficial lexical connection between 'written' and 'Author'.

confOf:Contribution is a written scholarly artefact (paper, poster, short paper) submitted by an author, with properties like abstract, keywords, title, and reviews. edas:Call is an announcement soliciting submissions (Call for Papers, Call for Manuscripts, Call for Reviews), with deadlines and submission instructions, initiated by committee members. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length submission document in the cmt ontology (Document > Paper > PaperFullVersion), while SignalProcessingTopic is a subject-area topic in the edas ontology (Topic > SignalProcessingTopic). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote completely different kinds of entities: one is a document artifact, the other is a research topic. No alignment relationship exists between them.

The cmt 'date' property applies to a Conference entity and denotes the date of the conference itself, whereas the Conference ontology 'is an ending date' applies to an Important dates entity and specifically denotes an ending date (e.g., submission or registration deadline end). They have different domains and different intended meanings; one is not a generalization of the other.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, runPaperAssignmentTools is an administrative action where an Administrator runs paper assignment tools on a Conference. In sigkdd, submit is an authoring action where an Author submits a Paper. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Both properties link a person to a Conference, but cmt:memberOfConference has domain Conference Member (a restricted class of people who are members of the conference programme committee or similar), while edas:isMemberOf has the broader domain Person. Thus cmt:memberOfConference is a more specific case of edas:isMemberOf, making it subsumed_by.

In Conference ontology, Workshop is a part of a conference (sibling of Track, Tutorial), i.e., a sub-event within a conference. In confOf, Conference is a top-level working event (sibling of Workshop, Tutorial), i.e., the whole conference. These are different levels of granularity: a Workshop (sub-event) is not equivalent to a Conference (whole event). They are not in a subsumption relation either, since Workshop in A is a conference part, while Conference in B is the conference itself.

These are unrelated datatype properties. 'reviews Per Paper' (domain Conference, range int) counts how many reviews each paper receives in the CMT system. 'Price' (domain Registration fee, range int) is the monetary cost of a registration fee. They have completely different domains and meanings.

Individual Presentation in ekaw is a scientific event (a talk/session where a paper is presented), while Power Point presentation in iasted is a specific presentation format/medium (a slide deck artifact). They occupy different positions in their hierarchies: one is an event type with children like Contributed Talk and Invited Talk, the other is a sibling of Video presentation under Presentation. The ekaw class denotes the presentation event/activity, not the slide deck artifact, so these are unrelated concepts despite both involving the word 'presentation'.

In ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a specific kind of conference contributor (a proper subclass of speakers). In ontology B, 'Speaker' is the general class of persons who give presentations, and it explicitly has 'Invited Speaker' as a child. Thus A's Invited speaker is strictly more specific than B's Speaker, so A is subsumed_by B.

These properties relate entirely different things. In Conference, 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (indicating how a topic is rated/preferred in reviews). In edas, 'hasRating' links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (the overall rating assigned to a paper). Different domains (Topic vs. Active Paper), different ranges (Review preference vs. Review Rating), and different semantics.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. In cmt, 'hasBeenAssigned' connects a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. In iasted, 'occupy' connects a Person to a Building, City, or State they occupy (e.g., a location). The domains (Reviewer vs. Person) and ranges (Paper vs. Building/City/State) are disjoint in meaning, and the relations themselves denote completely different concepts (assignment for reviewing vs. occupying a physical location).

These properties are fundamentally different in type and meaning. `written By` is an object property linking a Document to the Person who authored it, while `Name` is a datatype property linking a Person to a string representing their name. They have different domains, different range types (object vs. datatype), and express completely different relationships.

Both classes represent people involved in the administrative/organizational side of a conference, but they are not equivalent. confOf:Administrator is a broad administrative role (sibling to Author, Participant, Volunteer, etc.), while sigkdd:Organizing_Committee_member is a specific committee role (sibling to General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). An Administrator may be an Organizing Committee member and vice versa, but the extensions do not necessarily coincide, so the best relation is related.

Regular author in Conference is a subclass of Conference contribution/contributor, denoting a person who authors a paper. Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference, denoting a type of conference event. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are named 'Social Event' and represent non-scientific social activities within a conference. In edas, Social Event is a subclass of Non Academic Event (itself under Conference Event), with children Excursion and Reception. In ekaw, Social Event is a subclass of Event, with children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. The children overlap conceptually (Excursion ~ Conference Trip, Reception ~ Conference Banquet), and both serve as the top-level category for social/non-academic conference activities. The structural difference (edas has an intermediate 'Non Academic Event' layer) reflects modeling granularity, not a semantic distinction. The intended instances coincide.

Conference Event in edas denotes an event (academic or non-academic) with attendees, locations, programmes, and date-times. State in iasted denotes a geographic/political state with subtypes like Conference state, Presenter state, and Sponsor state, and properties relating to being occupied or visited by persons. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Paper is a specific document type representing a submitted academic paper with properties like hasAuthor, hasDecision, assignedTo reviewers, etc. In iasted, Form is a broader category of administrative documents (author info form, hotel registration form, registration form) used for conference logistics. These are completely different concepts: one is an academic paper, the other is a set of bureaucratic forms. They share only the generic parent Document, but their instances do not overlap.

In edas, Conference Event is a broad class encompassing academic and non-academic events (conferences, sessions, etc.) with properties like location, attendees, programme, and date times. In iasted, Conference days is a subclass of Time, sibling to Deadline and Trip day, with children Delegate and One conference day. The iasted class represents a temporal concept (a period/day of the conference), not the event itself. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an event/activity, the other is a time period. They are unrelated.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. `has_a_submitted_contribution` links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (i.e., which paper a reviewer-expertise slot is assigned to), while `hasReviewer` links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (i.e., who reviews a paper). They are not the same relation, nor inverses of each other in a directly aligned sense, and their domains/ranges do not correspond.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception at a conference), while iasted:Record_of_attendance is a document certifying attendance. They share the word 'attendance/reception' only coincidentally; one is an event, the other a document, with no overlap in intended instances.

Wireless Communications Topic is a subject-matter topic for conference papers (a subclass of Topic, alongside Communication Theory, Computer Networks, etc.), while Organizing Committee is a committee responsible for organizing a conference. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (`has a review expertise`) links a submitted contribution to a review expertise (the level or type of expertise a reviewer brings), while property B (`has Reviewer`) links a paper to a possible reviewer (the person who reviews). The ranges differ: Review expertise vs. Possible Reviewer. They denote different relations—one captures expertise associated with a review, the other captures assignment of a reviewer to a paper—so they are not equivalent.

The property 'issues' in Conference ontology relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issues proceedings). The property 'hasTopic' in edas relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (assigning a subject topic). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, denoting unrelated concepts.

Both are object properties linking a document to its author(s), but they differ in granularity and scope. In cmt, hasCo-author specifically links a Paper to a Co-author (a person who co-authored), while in Conference, has_authors links a Conference document to a Person. The cmt property is narrower (domain restricted to Paper, range to Co-author), whereas the Conference property is broader (domain Conference document, range Person).
