They overlap in meaning but are not equivalent; has_authors subsumes hasCo-author in a general sense, but the range mismatch (Co-author vs Person) and the specific co-authoring semantics make 'related' the safest reference alignment choice.

edas:Topic denotes a subject area of a conference or paper (e.g., Antennas, Cryptography, Medicine), with properties hasTopic/isTopicOf linking conferences and papers to topics. sigkdd:ACM_SIGKDD denotes the ACM SIGKDD organization/society that holds conferences, designs deadlines, and searches for sponsors. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Submitted Paper is a document (an artefact: a paper that has been submitted), while Submissions deadline is a point in time (a deadline for submitting). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies (Document vs Time) and share only the word 'submitted/submissions' in their labels. No semantic overlap exists between a document and a temporal deadline.

The cmt property 'assigned By Administrator' relates a Reviewer to an Administrator who assigned them (e.g., to review a paper). The iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a lecture or presentation). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics; they share no meaningful overlap in the conference domain.

Invited speaker is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, while IASTED member is a delegate who is a member of the IASTED organization. These are distinct concepts: one can be an invited speaker without being an IASTED member, and vice versa. Their hierarchies and sibling contexts confirm they model different aspects of conference participation.

Both properties relate a conference speaker to a presentation artifact, but the ranges differ: A's range is Presentation (an event/activity), while B's range is Document (the written artifact). This mismatch in the nature of the object being related makes them overlap without being equivalent.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event under Event), while iasted:Listener is a type of person (a delegate who attends but does not speak). They belong to entirely different ontological categories (event vs. person) and share no instances.

In ekaw, 'Tutorial Abstract' is a subclass of Document > Abstract, i.e., a written summary of a tutorial. In iasted, 'Tutorial' is a subclass of Activity > Conference activity > Lecture, i.e., the tutorial event/session itself. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities (a document vs. an activity), so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic' is a subject-area topic under the Topic hierarchy, representing a research domain. In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Best Applications Paper Award' is a type of award given at a conference. Their instances do not coincide, and they share no meaningful semantic relationship.

In EKAW, Student is a subclass of Person, representing a person who is a student (e.g., a student author or participant). In IASTED, Student lecturer is a highly specialized role: a lecturer at a conference who is also a student, situated under Person > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer. These denote very different things—a general student person vs. a specific conference speaking role—and there is no evidence their intended instances coincide.

A is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates object, while B is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a dateTime value. They operate at different levels of granularity and have incompatible property types (object vs datatype), so they cannot be equivalent.
Reception is a social event (a gathering/activity), while Single hotel room is a physical place/accommodation. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and share no instances.

These properties are completely different. 'has a volume' is a datatype property relating Conference proceedings to an integer (volume number), while 'paperPresentedAs' is an object property relating a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation. They have different domains, different range types (int vs. Individual Presentation), and represent entirely unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

Property A relates a Committee to its Chair (a leadership role), while property B relates a Member PC to a Contribution they review. They connect completely different domain/range pairs and express different relations in the conference domain.

A Government Organization is a type of institution (e.g., a governmental body) in the edas ontology, while an Organizing Committee is a committee that organizes a conference in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property 'title' in cmt maps a Paper to its title string, while 'has an ISBN' in Conference maps Conference proceedings to an ISBN string. They relate to different domains (Paper vs Conference proceedings) and capture different metadata attributes (title vs ISBN). There is no subsumption relationship between them; they are distinct datatype properties.

Conference announcement is a document type (subclass of Conference document) that denotes a notification or announcement about a conference. Proceedings Publisher is an organization (subclass of Organisation) that publishes conference proceedings. One is a document/artifact, the other is an organization/agent. They share no common semantics despite both being in the conference domain.

These properties are completely different in meaning and type. Property A is an object property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume (indicating containment/part-of relationship). Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (indicating when the conference starts). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

The EKAW 'has Part' is an object property for compositional relations (e.g., an event or document having parts), while the IASTED 'has amount of' is a datatype property from Money to int representing a monetary quantity. They differ in type, domain, range, and intended meaning, so they are unrelated.

The confOf 'reviewes' property relates a PC Member to a Contribution (paper reviewing), while the iasted 'is paid with' property relates Money to an Item (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

These properties are completely different: 'has gender' is a datatype property from Person to an unspecified (likely string) range, capturing a person's gender. 'written By' is an object property from Document to Person, capturing authorship. They have different domains, different ranges, different property types, and no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper, representing the abstract component of a paper submission (sibling of Paper Full Version). In sigkdd, Abstract is a direct subclass of Document, a top-level document type alongside Paper and Review. The sigkdd Abstract is more general, denoting any abstract document, while cmt's Paper Abstract is specifically the abstract of a paper. Thus cmt's Paper Abstract is subsumed by sigkdd's Abstract.

Conference contributor (A) denotes a person who contributes a paper or presentation to the conference, with children like Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author. Attendee (B) denotes a person who is present at the conference. A contributor is not necessarily an attendee (e.g., an author who submits but does not attend), and an attendee is not necessarily a contributor (e.g., audience members who present nothing). These are distinct concepts sharing only the parent Person.

In ontology A, Poster is a specific type of conference contribution distinct from regular papers and presentations, typically denoting a poster presentation at a conference. In ontology B, Paper is a general document type submitted by authors, sitting alongside Abstract and Review as siblings under Document. A poster is a different kind of contribution from a paper in the conference domain; they are not equivalent. Nor is there a clear subsumption relationship, since Poster in A is a contribution (not a document per se) while Paper in B is a document. The two concepts overlap only weakly (a poster may be accompanied by a paper), so the best verdict is unrelated.

`Important dates` in Conference is a container for submission/acceptance deadlines (abstract, full paper, camera-ready, acceptance announcement, start/end dates) tied to a Conference volume. `Individual Presentation` in ekaw is a scientific event where a paper is presented (e.g., Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). One denotes a collection of temporal deadlines; the other denotes a presentation event at a conference. They share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

The two classes denote entirely different concepts. In edas, 'Computer Networks Measurements Topic' is a specific subject-area topic under the Topic hierarchy, used to classify papers by research area. In iasted, 'Simulating' is a type of research activity (an activity performed before a conference). One is a topic/subject classification and the other is an activity; their instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, locationOf maps a Location to an Event (indicating where an event takes place). In sigkdd, search maps an ACM_SIGKDD conference to a Sponzor (sponsor). They share no semantic overlap in domain, range, or intended meaning.

Call For Manuscripts in edas is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Review in iasted is a type of Document (a written evaluation artefact). These are completely different concepts: one is a solicitation/announcement, the other is a document produced in response to a submission. No subsumption or overlap relationship exists between them.

Paper Full Version is a full-length paper submission in the cmt ontology, while Bronze Supporter is a sponsor tier in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A ('has a review reference or expertise') connects a Reviewer to their review expertise or review preference, representing the reviewer's competencies or preferences. Property B ('references') in ekaw is a generic citation/reference relation (e.g., a paper referencing another document). Despite the word 'reference' appearing in both, they relate entirely different kinds of things: A captures reviewer expertise/preference, while B captures document-to-document citation. Their domains, ranges, and intended semantics are disjoint.

Active conference participant in the Conference ontology is a broad class covering any participant who actively contributes (e.g., gives presentations), with siblings including Regular author and Invited speaker. Speaker in the iasted ontology is a specific kind of delegate whose defining characteristic is giving a presentation. Every Speaker is an active participant, but not every active participant (e.g., a regular author who does not present) is a Speaker. Thus Active_conference_participant subsumes Speaker.

In ekaw, Demo_Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper presented as a demo at a conference), while sigkdd's Paper is the general class of all papers (a top-level document type). The sigkdd Paper class is more general, subsuming Demo_Paper.

cmt:Conference denotes the conference event/organization (with properties like date, members, paper submissions, administrators), while sigkdd:Conference_hall is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel) where conference sessions are held. They are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas ekaw:Workshop_Paper is a document (subclass of Paper). One denotes a conference event, the other a type of paper; they share no intended instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Review preference in the Conference ontology denotes a reviewer's preference or expertise for reviewing a particular topic or submission (with properties like degree, review reference, reviewer). Review Question in edas denotes a question item in a review form (with subclasses Numerical Review Question and Textual Review Question). These are fundamentally different concepts: one captures reviewer assignment preferences, the other captures the questions asked during review. They share no instance overlap.

Administrator (cmt) is a person role under User > Administrator, denoting a conference management user who performs administrative actions. Paper (sigkdd) is a document type under Document > Paper, denoting a written submission. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are datatype properties that associate a deadline-bearing entity (Call vs Deadline) with a temporal value (dateTime vs date) representing the submission deadline. In the conference domain 'has Submission Deadline' and 'done till' denote the same relation: the date/time by which a submission must be completed. The slight domain difference (Call vs Deadline) reflects modelling granularity rather than a distinct relation, so a reference alignment would treat them as equivalent.

In cmt, Administrator is a person who manages the conference system (subclass of Person > User), with properties like assigning reviewers and entering conference details. In edas, Paper is a document submitted to a conference (subclass of Document), with properties like being reviewed by reviewers and written by authors. These are completely different concepts: one is an administrative person, the other is a paper document. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document subtype (a written summary of a paper), while Workshop Session in ekaw is an event/session subtype. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies (Document vs Event) and denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Regular contribution is a document (Conference contribution > Regular contribution) with children Extended abstract and Paper. Author is a person (Person > Speaker > Author) who submits papers and receives awards. One is a written artefact, the other is a person role; they share no instances.

These classes denote entirely different concepts. 'Call For Reviews' in edas is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting reviews), sibling to Call For Papers and Call For Manuscripts. 'Abstract' in sigkdd is a type of Document (a written summary of a paper), sibling to Paper and Review. One is a solicitation/announcement event; the other is a document artifact. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Property A links a Program committee to a Conference volume (a committee chairing/reviewing a conference volume), while property B links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (events running in parallel). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

The two properties operate in completely different domains. In cmt, 'has Been Assigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewer assigned to review a paper). In iasted, 'is occupied by' links a Building, City, or State to a Person (a person occupying a location). They share no common domain or range types and denote entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'has_workshops' links a Conference volume to its constituent Workshop events (a part-whole relation between a conference and its workshops). In ontology B, 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the document/slides presented by that speaker). The domains (Conference volume vs Speaker), ranges (Workshop vs Document), and the nature of the relation (partitive vs presented-by) are all different, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

confOf 'ends on' has domain Event (a broad superclass covering conferences, social events, etc.) and range string, while edas 'endDate' has domain Conference specifically and range dateTime. The confOf property is more general (applies to all events, not just conferences), so it is subsumed_by the edas property which is restricted to Conference. They are not equivalent because their domains differ in generality and their ranges differ (string vs dateTime).

A Conference Session in ekaw is a scientific event (a scheduled session where papers are presented), while a Hotel room in iasted is a physical place (accommodation). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (Event vs Place) and share no instances.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person). In sigkdd, Conference_hall is a physical place (subclass of Place). They share no instances and are completely different concepts despite the superficial lexical similarity.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference with range int, representing the number of reviews required per paper. remark is a datatype property on Contribution with range string, representing a textual remark/comment on a contribution. They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a broad category of people affiliated with the conference, with subclasses including Author, Conference Chair, Associated Chair, Program Committee Member, and Reviewer. In ekaw, PC_Member is specifically a member of the Program Committee (a Possible Reviewer), with subclasses like PC Chair, SC Member, Session Chair, etc. Every PC_Member is a conference member, but not every conference member (e.g., an Author who is not on the PC) is a PC_Member. Thus cmt:ConferenceMember is more general than ekaw:PC_Member.

The two properties are inverses, not equivalents. In cmt, readByReviewer has domain Paper and range Reviewer (paper -> reviewer). In edas, isReviewing has domain Reviewer (and related chair roles) and range Paper (reviewer -> paper). A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. 'has tracks' links a Conference volume to its constituent Tracks (whole-part relation), while 'holded by' links a Conference to the organization ACM SIGKDD (ownership/affiliation relation). Their domains and ranges are disjoint concepts, and they express semantically unrelated relationships.

Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Item > Audiovisual equipment), while Organizator is a person who organizes a conference (Person > Organizator). These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (who wrote it), while ekaw's 'has Updated Version' links a Document to another Document (an updated version of it). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and serve completely different purposes.

Property A denotes a person's last/family name while property B denotes a person's first/given name (the comment even mentions middle name involvement). They relate to distinct parts of a person's name, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only loosely related as co-attributes of Person.

In Conference ontology, Reviewer is a broad class covering any person who reviews papers, with properties for review expertise, preference, and co-reviewer invitation. In ekaw, PC_Member is a specific subtype of Possible_Reviewer restricted to program committee members, with subtypes like PC_Chair, Session_Chair, etc. Every PC_Member is a reviewer, but not every reviewer is a PC_Member (e.g., external reviewers). Thus Reviewer is more general, making this a subsumed_by relation.

edas:Attendee is a general class for any person attending a conference (subclass of Person, sibling to Author, Reviewer, etc.). iasted:IASTED_non_member is a specific subclass of Delegate, denoting a delegate who is not an IASTED member. Every IASTED non member is an attendee, but not vice versa, so edas:Attendee subsumes iasted:IASTED_non_member.

These properties operate in opposite directions and relate entirely different entities. cmt:writeReview has domain Reviewer and range Review, modeling the act of a reviewer writing a review. edas:isReviewHistoryOf has domain Personal Review History and range Reviewer, linking a review-history record to the reviewer it belongs to. They do not share the same domain, range, or direction, so they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Paper is a subclass of Document and has specific subclasses like Camera Ready Paper, Conference Paper, etc. In sigkdd, Document has children Abstract, Paper, and Review, meaning sigkdd's Document is a general container for written works. Ekaw's Paper is a specific type of document (a scholarly paper), while sigkdd's Document encompasses all written artefacts including abstracts and reviews. Thus ekaw:Paper is strictly more specific than sigkdd:Document, making the relation subsumed_by.

ekaw:organisedBy relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it (e.g. a conference chair or organising committee). iasted:is_given_by relates an Activity or Item to the Person who presents or delivers it (e.g. a lecture given by a speaker). These are different relations: organising an event is not the same as giving/presenting an activity or item. The domains and ranges differ (Event vs Activity/Item; Organisation/Person vs Person), and the intended semantics are distinct.

Computer Architecture Topic is a subject matter topic for conference papers, while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to completely different domains and have no semantic relationship.

Workshop Session is a type of scientific event/session (a temporal session within a conference where workshop papers are presented), while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing a conference. They belong to completely different branches of the ontology (events vs. committees) and share no instances.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Research Institute is an organisation (subclass of Academic Institution/Organisation). They are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:Rejection is a Decision (the outcome of rejecting a paper), while edas:Reception is a Social Event at a conference. Despite the lexical similarity, they denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

`assignedByReviewer` in cmt relates an External Reviewer to the Reviewer who assigned them (i.e., who invited them to review), while `invites_co-reviewers` in Conference relates a Reviewer to co-reviewers they invite. The domains differ (External Reviewer vs. Reviewer), and the semantics differ: one captures an assignment/invitation relationship from the invitee's perspective, the other captures the act of a reviewer inviting co-reviewers. They are not the same relation in the same direction.

Both classes denote the same concept of a conference event in the conference-organisation domain. They share the same label and both represent the central conference entity with properties like dates, members, and administrative details. The differences in properties reflect different modelling granularity rather than different intended extensions.

Accommodation Place in edas denotes lodging facilities (hotels, dormitories, etc.) for conference participants, while Conference airport in iasted denotes an airport associated with a conference location. An airport is a transportation hub, not an accommodation venue; their intended instances do not coincide. They share only the broad ancestor Place, which is too general to imply any meaningful alignment.

In cmt, 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author (a Person) who is explicitly not a reviewer, capturing a role restriction on conference members. In Conference, 'Contribution co author' is a subclass of Regular author (a Conference document author), i.e., a co-author of a contribution. These are different concepts: one is a role-restricted person (author who is not a reviewer), the other is a specific type of document author (co-author vs. first author). They do not share the same intended instances.

Active conference participant is a broad category covering any person who actively participates (gives presentations), including regular authors and invited speakers. Conference Chair is a specific organizational role (chairing the conference, initiating calls, reviewing papers). The Chair is not an instance of the general participant category by definition, and the two classes do not share instances. They are disjoint role/person categories.

confOf:Scholar is a price-category role for a conference participant who studies at a university (a student/scholar attendee), whereas sigkdd:Author_of_paper is a specific sub-type of Author denoting someone who authored a paper. The two classes have disjoint intended instances: a Scholar is not necessarily an author, and an Author_of_paper is not necessarily a scholar/student. They share only the distant ancestor Person, so they are unrelated.

hasName is a datatype property from Conference to string (the full name of a conference), while heldIn is an object property from Event to Location (where an event takes place). They relate different domain/range pairs and express completely different relations, so they are unrelated.

In edas, 'Industry Organization' is a subclass of Organization, denoting a kind of institution (industry/company). In iasted, 'Sponsor state' is a subclass of State, denoting a phase or status of a sponsor (e.g., registered, paid). One is an organization type, the other is a state/status; their intended instances do not coincide.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Security Topic' is a subclass of 'Topic' representing a subject area within computer networks security. In EKAW, 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a subclass of 'Abstract' (and ultimately 'Document') representing a written summary of an invited talk. There is no overlap in intended instances, and neither subsumes the other.

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs a committee or conference (parent Person, children include Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair). Event in confOf is an occurrence such as a social or working event with start/end dates. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' in cmt relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper assignment tools), while 'presentationed_by' in sigkdd relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). One is about administrative tool management, the other about who presents a document. They denote different relations in the conference domain.
A is a datatype property mapping a Person/Organization to a street string; B is an object property mapping an Activity/Person to an Item/Place. Different domain/range and different semantics.

Attendee (Person > Attendee) denotes a conference participant who attends the event, while Webmaster (Person > Organizator > Webmaster) is an organizer responsible for the conference website. They occupy different branches of the person hierarchy with distinct roles; an attendee is not an organizer and a webmaster is not an attendee. No subsumption holds between them.

In cmt, Meta Review is a specialized subclass of Review (a second-level review by a meta-reviewer). In iasted, Review is a general document class covering all reviews. Thus cmt:Meta-Review is strictly narrower than iasted:Review, so it is subsumed_by it.

Poster Paper in ekaw is a specific type of academic paper (a poster presentation submission), while Mailing list in iasted is a type of document used for communication (e.g., email distribution lists). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties relate entirely different entities in opposite directions. `isWrittenBy` connects a Paper to its Author (paper -> author), while `obtain` connects an Author to an Award (author -> award). They share no common domain, range, or semantic relationship.

confOf:University is an academic institution where scholars study, while ekaw:Organising_Agency is an organization that co-organizes a conference (e.g., a professional body or agency). They share the generic parent Organisation but denote completely different kinds of organizations with no instance overlap.

Property A (has_an_ISBN) assigns an ISBN string to Conference proceedings, while property B (done_till) assigns a deadline date to a Deadline. They relate different domain types to different range types and capture unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

Both classes denote the same core conference-domain concept of a written academic paper. Ontology A's Paper is a 'Regular contribution' under 'Conference contribution' (a document), and ontology B's Paper is a subclass of Document. The structural differences (A has a sibling Extended abstract and a part-of relation to Abstract; B has many paper subtypes and review-related properties) reflect modeling granularity rather than different intended meanings. The instances of both classes coincide: academic papers submitted/published at a conference.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference as an occurrence. iasted:Delegate is a person who attends the conference (subclass of Person, with children like Speaker, Listener, Session chair). These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a participant/attendee. No subsumption holds between them.

These properties operate in completely different domains. In edas, 'is Provider Of' links an Organization to a Sponsorship (i.e., who provides sponsorship). In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (i.e., who presents a document). The domains (Organization vs Document), ranges (Sponsorship vs Speaker), and semantic meanings are entirely different.

confOf:Regular is a subclass of Participant (a person who regularly attends a conference), whereas ekaw:Regular_Session is a subclass of Session (a scheduled event/activity). One denotes a type of person, the other a type of conference event; they share no instances and are unrelated.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person denoting a human member of a conference (with subclasses such as Author, Reviewer, Chair). In iasted, Conference state is a subclass of State, representing a role or status (a non-human abstraction), sibling to Presenter state and Sponsor state. The two classes denote completely different kinds of entities (person vs. state/role) and share no domain overlap.

Property A links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the committee organizes the conference). Property B links a Conference to a Person (the conference has a member/person). They relate different entity types in different directions and represent different relationships: one is about which committee organizes a conference, the other is about persons participating in a conference.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. confOf's 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel (same time slot), while ekaw's 'location Of' relates a Location to the Event held there. They share no semantic overlap.

Rejected contribution in Conference ontology denotes a contribution that was reviewed and rejected, i.e., not accepted for publication. Published Paper in edas denotes a paper that has been published. These are mutually exclusive statuses: a rejected contribution is not published, and a published paper is not rejected. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a broad superclass covering any person affiliated with the conference (authors, chairs, PC members, reviewers). In confOf, Participant is specifically a person who attends the conference (with early registration), with subclasses like Member, Regular, and Student. Every Participant is a ConferenceMember, but ConferenceMember includes roles (e.g., reviewers, external reviewers) who may not attend, so ConferenceMember subsumes Participant.

Track workshop chair in Conference ontology is a person who chairs a specific track (workshop/tutorial track) within a conference part, while Program Chair in sigkdd is the overall chair of the conference program committee. These are distinct organizational roles: a track workshop chair oversees a particular track, whereas a program chair oversees the entire program. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since one is track-specific and the other is program-wide.

Property A relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (part-to-volume containment), while property B relates a Person to an Item (a person signing an item). They connect completely different domain and range types and express unrelated relationships.

Free Time Break is a class denoting a scheduled break event during a conference (e.g., free time between sessions), while Registration SIGMOD Member is a class denoting a registration fee category for SIGMOD members. These are completely different domain concepts: one is a temporal event, the other is a fee/payment classification. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

In ontology A, 'Conference participant' is a broad class covering all persons who participate in a conference, with children 'Active conference participant' and 'Passive conference participant'. In ontology B, 'Student' is a specific kind of participant (a sub-class of Participant, alongside Member and Regular). A student is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is a student. Thus A is subsumed by B's broader Participant hierarchy, making A (Conference participant) more specific than B's Student is not correct; rather, Student is more specific than Conference participant. So the relation is that A subsumes B (Conference participant is more general than Student).

Conference Banquet (ekaw) is a social event that occurs during a conference, whereas Conference city (iasted) is a city where a conference takes place. One is an event, the other is a geographic location; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf's Working event is a kind of academic/scientific event (parent Event, siblings Social event and Administrative event, children Conference/Tutorial/Workshop). edas's Computer Networks Topic is a research subject area (parent Topic, with siblings like Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic). They belong to entirely different parts of the conference-organisation domain hierarchy and share no instances.

The property 'has tracks' in Conference relates a Conference volume to its constituent Track (a session/programme division), while 'has Topic' in edas relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (a subject-matter classification). A track is an organisational/programme entity, whereas a topic is a thematic category; the two properties relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalisation of the other.

Invited speaker in Conference is a person invited to give a talk at a conference. Author book proceedings included in iasted is an author whose paper is included in book proceedings. These are different roles: one is about being an invited speaker, the other about having a publication in a proceedings book. They do not share instances or subsume each other.

confOf Scholar is a price category for conference registration (a participant who qualifies for a reduced scholar rate, typically a student or academic), while ekaw Student is a person role. They overlap significantly (students are often scholars) but are not equivalent: Scholar is broader (can include non-student academics) and is fundamentally a pricing/registration category rather than a direct equivalent of the Student role.

Paper in edas is a conference document (academic paper) with subclasses like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc., and properties like isReviewedBy and isWrittenBy. Transport vehicle in iasted is a physical vehicle (Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

These two datatype properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. logoURL (domain Conference, range anyURI) stores the URL of a conference logo, while earlyRegistration (domain Participant, range boolean) indicates whether a participant registered early. They share no semantic relationship.

A 'Main office' in iasted denotes an administrative office (the organizing entity's headquarters), while B 'Conference hall' in sigkdd denotes a physical venue where conference sessions take place. They are sibling classes under Place in their respective ontologies but denote clearly different kinds of places. In iasted, 'Conference hall' is itself a sibling of 'Main office', confirming these are distinct concepts. No subsumption relation holds between an administrative office and a conference hall.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. 'has an abstract' links a paper/poster/presentation to its Abstract (a textual summary), while 'related To Event' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (an event/session). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

Submitted Paper in EKAW is a specific kind of academic paper that has been submitted to a conference, sitting under Paper > Document. Document in IASTED is a broad administrative container covering forms, letters, mailing lists, payment documents, visas, etc. The IASTED Document class is far more general and administratively oriented, while Submitted Paper is a narrow academic artefact. They do not share the same intended instances, and neither cleanly subsumes the other within the conference domain.

The cmt 'name' property assigns a string name to a Conference or Person, while the edas 'hasStartDateTime' property assigns a dateTime to a Conference Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings; one captures a label/name and the other captures a temporal start timestamp.

Paper Full Version is a complete version of an academic paper submitted to a conference, whereas Conference announcement is a document type used to announce conference-related information. They are different kinds of conference documents with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Workshop is a working event (a conference session where work is presented/discussed), while iasted:Modelling is a research activity performed before the conference. They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies and denote different concepts.

Conference volume in the Conference ontology denotes a conference instance/edition (with committees, contributions, tracks, locations, important dates), whereas Participant in confOf denotes a person who participates in a conference. They are completely different kinds of entities: one is an event/organisation concept, the other is a person role.

The confOf 'employed By' property relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while the sigkdd 'submit' property relates an Author to a Paper they submit. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no overlap in meaning.

confOf Author is a broad class covering authors of any Contribution (papers, posters, etc.), while ekaw Paper_Author is restricted to authors of papers specifically. Author subsumes Paper_Author because every paper author is an author, but not vice versa (e.g., poster authors would be confOf Authors but not ekaw Paper_Authors).

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs a committee or conference (subclass of Person with children like Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair). Lecture in iasted is an academic activity/event (subclass of Conference activity with children like Plenary lecture, Tutorial). These denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain: a person vs. an event.

Trip and Reception are distinct kinds of social events. In confOf, Trip is a sibling of Reception (and Banquet), so they are explicitly disjoint concepts. In edas, Reception is a specific social event distinct from Excursion. A Trip denotes an excursion or outing, while a Reception denotes a welcome/gathering event; their instances do not coincide.

Entity A (Reviewer) is a person role—a delegate who reviews papers—situated under Speaker > Delegate in the iasted ontology. Entity B (Review) is a document—the written review artifact—situated under Document in the sigkdd ontology. One denotes the agent who performs reviewing; the other denotes the output document produced. These are fundamentally different categories (person vs. document) and are not equivalent, nor is there a subsumption relationship between them.

confOf's 'Short paper' is a type of academic contribution (a written paper), a sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution. sigkdd's 'Exhibitor' is a type of sponsor (Sponzor) that exhibits at the conference, a sibling of various supporter tiers. These are completely different concepts: one is a scholarly submission type, the other is a commercial sponsor role. No overlap in intended instances.

cmt:Paper is a written contribution submitted to a conference (children: Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version; properties: has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer). ekaw:Review is an evaluation document written by a reviewer about a paper (children: Negative/Neutral/Positive Review; properties: review Of Paper, review Written By). They are distinct concepts in the conference domain despite both being subclasses of Document.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime and relate to conference deadlines, but they have different domains and scopes. In EDAS, paperDueOn is a specific deadline property on Conference denoting when paper submissions are due. In SIGKDD, Date is a general property on Deadline representing the date of any deadline. They overlap in the case of a paper-submission deadline, but Date is more general (applies to any deadline) while paperDueOn is specific to paper due dates, so they are related but not equivalent.

Social program is a conference activity (e.g., dinner, cocktail reception) in the iasted ontology, while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different categories of entities—an activity versus a person role—with no meaningful overlap.

Academic Event in edas is a kind of conference event (e.g., workshop, paper presentation, talk event), while Academic Institution in ekaw is a kind of organization (e.g., university, research institute). These are completely different concepts: one denotes an academic gathering/activity, the other denotes an academic organization. No overlap in intended instances.

Extended abstract is a short summary-type contribution submitted for review/acceptance, while Final manuscript is the camera-ready, final version of an accepted paper. They represent different stages and artefact types in the conference workflow, not the same concept.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and in opposite directions. 'was a committee chair of' links a Chair to a Committee they presided over, while 'written By' links a Document to the Person who authored it. There is no overlap in domain, range, or intended meaning.

Company in confOf denotes a for-profit commercial organization, while NGO in edas denotes a non-governmental, typically non-profit organization. These are distinct categories of organization with different purposes and structures; neither subsumes the other.

In the iasted ontology, Author is a subclass of Speaker and represents a delegate who writes a paper (with subclasses like 'Author book proceedings included', 'Author cd proceedings included'). In the sigkdd ontology, Invited_Speaker is a distinct subclass of Speaker specifically for invited talks, and Author is a separate sibling class. These are different concepts: an Author writes papers, while an Invited Speaker gives invited presentations. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

These properties have different domains and different meanings. 'max Papers' in cmt specifies the maximum number of papers a Program Committee Member can review, while 'has a volume' in Conference indicates the volume number of Conference proceedings. They relate to entirely different aspects of the conference domain.

Although both are datatype properties with range string capturing a currency value, their domains differ: hasCostCurrency applies to Sponsorship (the currency of a sponsorship cost), while Currency applies to Registration fee (the currency of a registration fee). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in the kinds of things they relate, so they are not equivalent.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'organised By' (ekaw) relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. 'go through' (iasted) relates an Item (e.g., a paper) to an Activity (e.g., a review process) that the item undergoes. They connect different types of entities in different directions and express fundamentally different relationships.

confOf:Workshop is a type of working event (a session or meeting), while iasted:Video_presentation is a type of presentation (a delivery format). They are at different levels of the event/activity taxonomy and do not share instances.

In edas, Conference denotes the academic event (with deadlines, topics, members, papers). In sigkdd, Conference_hall is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a room/building.

These properties are completely different. 'hasStreet' is a datatype property from Contact Information to a string (a street address), while 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item (a person obtaining an item). They have different domains, different range types, and different semantics.

Paid applicant is a person who has paid registration, while Registration fee is the monetary amount charged. They are different kinds of entities (person vs. fee), and there is no subsumption relationship between them.

A is a person who uses the CMT system (parent Person, with subclasses Author, Reviewer, Administrator). B is a registration fee category for SIGMOD members (parent Registration fee, siblings are other fee categories). They denote completely different concepts: a person/role vs. a monetary fee type.
A Call For Papers is an announcement soliciting submissions, while an Abstract is a summary document accompanying a paper. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (is_an_abstract_submission_date) is a datatype property with domain Important dates and range date, capturing when an abstract is due. Property B (locationOf) is an object property with domain Location and range Event, capturing where an event takes place. They relate completely different kinds of things in different directions, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, 'adjustedBy' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted that bid (i.e., who modified the bid value a reviewer placed on a paper). In edas, 'isReviewHistoryOf' links a Personal Review History to the Reviewer it belongs to (i.e., it associates a review history record with its owning reviewer). These are structurally similar (domain is a review-related object, range is Reviewer), but they denote different relations: one is about who adjusted a bid, the other is about which reviewer a review history pertains to. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a way a reference alignment would record.

Conference document in ontology Conference denotes written artefacts such as calls for papers, announcements, contributions, reviews, etc. Time in iasted denotes temporal entities such as conference days, deadlines, and trip days. These are completely disjoint domains with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee member, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. They have different domains and ranges and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

In iasted, 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a highly specific class: a Speaker who is an Author who is a Delegate, with siblings like 'Tutorial speaker' and 'Lecturer', denoting someone who gives a plenary (keynote) lecture. In sigkdd, 'Speaker' is a broad class under Person with children 'Author' and 'Invited Speaker'. The sigkdd Speaker is more general, covering any kind of speaker, whereas the iasted class is restricted to plenary lecture speakers. Thus iasted:Plenary_lecture_speaker is subsumed by sigkdd:Speaker, not equivalent.

The property 'is sent before' in iasted relates an Item to a Time (temporal relation indicating when something is sent). The property 'submit' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper (action of an author submitting a paper). They have different domains (Item vs Author), different ranges (Time vs Paper), and represent fundamentally different relations with no overlap in meaning.

Property A (has_important_dates) links a Conference volume to its Important dates (e.g., submission deadlines). Property B (organisedBy) links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. These are entirely different relations: one captures deadline metadata, the other captures agency/ownership of an event. No overlap in meaning.

These properties relate entirely different kinds of things. 'has tracks' connects a Conference volume to its Tracks (organizational sessions/topics), while 'is held in' connects an Activity to a Place or Time where it occurs. They share no semantic overlap in domain, range, or meaning.

Tutorial and Workshop are distinct types of conference events. A Tutorial is an instructional session, while a Workshop is a collaborative scientific event. They are siblings under broader categories in their respective ontologies but do not denote the same concept.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Computer Networks Optical Topic' is a specific subject-area topic (a subclass of 'Computer Networks Topic' alongside siblings like security, sensor, and switching topics). In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Program Committee' is a type of organizational committee (a subclass of 'Committee' alongside best paper awards and organizing committees). There is no overlap in intended instances, no shared parent, and no domain relationship between a research topic and a conference committee.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In EKAW, coversTopic links an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (indicating the subject matter covered). In IASTED, need links a Person to an Item (indicating something a person requires). The domains (Event/Paper vs Person), ranges (Research Topic vs Item), and intended meanings are disjoint, so no equivalence or subsumption holds.

The property 'written By' in cmt relates a Review to its Reviewer (who authored the review). The property 'send' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they send. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other in the conference domain.
confOf:Conference is an event (a conference gathering), while ekaw:Workshop_Chair is a person who chairs a workshop. They are completely different categories: an event vs. a person/role.

confOf Conference is a specific type of working event (a conference), while ekaw Scientific_Event is a broader class encompassing conferences, workshops, sessions, tracks, and individual presentations. Conference is a child of Scientific_Event in ekaw, so confOf Conference is subsumed by ekaw Scientific_Event.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs a conference, a subclass of Chairman/Person. Conference (sigkdd) is the event itself with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. One is a person role, the other is an event; they are completely different concepts.

confOf Working event is a broad category of events (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) covering the substantive/academic portion of a conference, contrasted with Administrative event and Social event. edas Talk Event is a narrow leaf-level class (with children Closing Talk, Welcome Talk) representing specific presentation-like sessions, sitting under Academic Event alongside Paper Presentation and Workshop. The two do not share the same instances: a Conference or Tutorial is a Working event but not a Talk Event, while a Welcome Talk is a Talk Event but not a Working event. They are at different levels of granularity and neither subsumes the other.
Rejected Paper denotes a paper whose submission was turned down, while Abstract denotes a summary document. They occupy different positions in the Document hierarchy and do not share instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. In edas, 'has Topic' links a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject area). In iasted, 'write' links a Person to an Item (a person authoring a written work). They have different domains (Conference/Paper vs Person), different ranges (Topic vs Item), and express completely different relationships (topic assignment vs authorship). No overlap or subsumption exists.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person (range string), while the edas 'has End Date Time' property denotes the end date/time of a Conference Event (range dateTime). They relate completely different kinds of things and have incompatible domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

Talk Event in edas is a type of academic event (e.g., closing talk, welcome talk), while Gold Supporter in sigkdd is a type of conference sponsor/supporter. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Track in the Conference ontology denotes a conference part (e.g., a workshop or tutorial track within a conference volume), while Program Committee in sigkdd denotes a committee of reviewers. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In EDAS, Conference Event is a broad category covering both academic and non-academic events (e.g., conferences, workshops, sessions), with properties for attendees, location, programme, and dates. In IASTED, Conference activity is a subclass of Activity whose children are Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Presentation, Registration, Social program, etc.—i.e., individual activities that occur during a conference. Thus EDAS Conference Event is more general (a conference-level event with location, programme, attendees) and subsumes IASTED Conference activity, which denotes specific activities within a conference.

cmt:Conference denotes the academic conference event itself (with properties like date, members, paper submissions, reviews), while iasted:Conference_hotel is a physical building/place where conference participants stay. They share only the word 'Conference'; one is an event and the other is a venue, so they are unrelated.

Conference applicant is a subclass of Person, denoting someone who applies to attend a conference. Registration Student is a subclass of Registration fee, denoting a fee category for student registration. One is a person role, the other is a fee type; their instances are disjoint kinds of entities.

The two properties relate different things and have different intended meanings. In EKAW, scientificallyOrganisedBy links an event to an Academic Institution that provides scientific organisation, with a parent property organisedBy and range Academic Institution. In SIGKDD, holded_by links a Conference specifically to ACM SIGKDD (the particular organisation that hosts the conference). The EKAW property is about scientific organisation by academic institutions generally, while the SIGKDD property is about being hosted by the ACM SIGKDD organisation specifically. They do not share the same domain/range types, direction of a common relation, or intended meaning.

The two properties are completely different in kind and meaning. In cmt, submitPaper is an object property with domain Author and range Paper, representing the act of an author submitting a paper. In the Conference ontology, is_a_date_of_camera_ready_paper_submission is a datatype property with domain Important dates and range date, representing a date associated with camera-ready paper submission. They relate different types of entities (authors/papers vs. dates/important dates) and one is an object property while the other is a datatype property, so they are unrelated.

edas:Reception is a specific kind of social event (a reception), while iasted:Social_program is a broader category encompassing dinners, cocktail receptions, coffee breaks, and other social activities. Reception is thus subsumed by Social_program rather than equivalent.

confOf's 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event representing the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions, while edas's 'Workshop' is an academic event representing a workshop session at a conference. They are different kinds of conference events with distinct purposes and positions in their respective hierarchies.

hasStreet relates Contact Information to a street name (string), while E-mail relates Person to an email address (string). These are different attributes with different domains and different meanings; they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. In Conference, 'contributes' goes from Person to Conference document (author -> document). In confOf, 'written By' goes from Contribution to Author (document -> author). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. Since inverse relations are explicitly not considered equivalent, and neither subsumes the other, they are unrelated as alignment targets.

Both are object properties named 'pay' with domain Person, relating a person to a monetary amount they pay (Money in iasted, Registration fee in sigkdd). The ranges are closely related: a registration fee is a specific kind of money/fee. The property denotes the same relation (a person paying money) in both ontologies, so they are equivalent.

Property A (hasAuthor) links a Paper to its Author (who wrote the paper). Property B (has_a_publisher) links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organization that publishes the proceedings). These are entirely different relationships: authorship vs. publication. The domains (Paper vs. Conference proceedings) and ranges (Author vs. Publisher) are disjoint concepts. There is no subsumption relationship either; they are simply unrelated properties.

A Workshop is a collaborative academic event where papers are presented and discussed, typically involving multiple presentations and participants. A Plenary lecture is a single lecture given to all conference attendees at once. These are distinct types of conference events with different structures and purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties operate in completely different contexts. In Conference, 'has a degree' is a datatype property from Review preference to int, expressing the degree/strength of a preference. In iasted, 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item, expressing that a person obtains an item. They have different domains, different ranges (datatype vs object), and different semantics.

In cmt, 'Meta Review' is a subclass of Review (a document), representing a meta-review of a paper. In edas, 'Call For Reviews' is a subclass of Call, representing an announcement soliciting reviews. One is a review document; the other is a call for submissions. They denote completely different concepts.

In the iasted ontology, 'State' is a geographic/administrative region (sibling of City, Place) that can be occupied, situated in, and visited by persons. In sigkdd, 'Conference' is an academic event with start/end dates, held by ACM SIGKDD. These are completely different concepts: a geographic entity vs. a conference event. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Associated Chair is a person role (a chair of a conference committee), while Conference is an event (one edition of a conference). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'employed By' in confOf relates a Person to an Organization that employs them, while 'is given to' in iasted relates an Item to a Person who receives it. They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and do not denote the same relation.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges. In cmt, hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to a Conference Member (a general participant/organizer). In the Conference ontology, was_a_steering_committee_of relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume. The relations connect different kinds of entities and do not denote the same relationship.

These properties differ in both domain and range and in meaning. `written By` (ekaw) relates a Document to the Person who authored it (Document -> Person). `obtain` (iasted) relates a Person to an Item they obtain (Person -> Item). The directions are reversed and the semantics (authorship vs. acquisition) are entirely different.

Meeting Room Place in edas is a specific kind of place (a room where meetings occur), sibling to Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, and Dining Place. Building in iasted is a broader category of physical structures including airports, hotels, restaurants, universities, etc. A meeting room is not equivalent to a building; it is typically a space within a building. They share the parent Place but denote different kinds of locations at different granularity levels, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

In the iasted ontology, Time is a broad temporal concept with children including Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day. In sigkdd, Deadline is a specific temporal concept with concrete subtypes like Abstract Submission and Paper Submission deadlines. Since Deadline is a child of Time in iasted, the iasted Time class subsumes the sigkdd Deadline class. They are not equivalent because Time encompasses much more than just deadlines.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'hasCountry' links a Conference to its Country, while 'is_used_for' links an Item to an Activity or Money. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Both properties link a paper to its presentation at an event, but they differ in generality. In ekaw, paperPresentedAs has domain Abstract/Paper and range Individual Presentation, covering any paper-to-presentation relation. In edas, relatedToEvent is restricted to Accepted Paper -> Paper Presentation, a narrower case. Thus edas:relatedToEvent is subsumed_by ekaw:paperPresentedAs rather than equivalent.

In ekaw, Workshop Session is a specific kind of Session (a session within a workshop), sitting alongside Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, and Regular Session. In iasted, Session is a broad class under Lecture that encompasses Speaker lecture and is a sibling of Plenary lecture and Tutorial. The iasted Session is more general, covering lecture-style sessions broadly, while ekaw Workshop Session is a narrow specialization. The two are not equivalent; ekaw Workshop Session is subsumed by iasted Session.

The cmt 'title' property has domain Paper and denotes the title of a paper, while the sigkdd 'Name' property has domain Person and denotes the name of a person. They relate to completely different kinds of entities and denote different concepts, so they are not equivalent.

`has the first name` captures a person's given name, while `has Biography` captures a free-text biographical description. Both are datatype properties on Person with range string, but they denote completely different attributes of a person.

Extended abstract is a type of conference document/contribution (a written academic submission), while Best Student Paper Award is a type of award given for a paper. They belong to completely different categories: one is a document type, the other is an award type. There is no overlap in their intended instances.

In EKAW, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a specific kind of person (a student). In IASTED, Person is the general class with subclasses Delegate and Sponsor. Thus EKAW Student is strictly more specific than IASTED Person, so Student is subsumed_by Person.

confOf Organization denotes an organizational entity (e.g., Company, University) that employs people and has address properties. iasted Building denotes a physical structure/place (e.g., Conference hotel, Presenter house) that is occupied or situated in locations. These are fundamentally different concepts: an organization vs. a building. While a building may house an organization, they are not the same thing.

A's writtenBy is an object property linking a Review to the Reviewer who authored it. B's has_an_expertise is a datatype property on Review expertise with an unspecified (literal) range. They differ in arity type, domain, and meaning: one captures authorship, the other captures an expertise attribute.

Property A (has_an_organizing_committee) relates a Conference volume to its Organizing committee, while property B (hold) relates the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference it holds. They connect different domain/range pairs and express different relationships: one is a part-whole relation between an event and its committee, the other is an organization-hosts-event relation. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Property A (assignedByAdministrator) links a Reviewer to an Administrator who performed the assignment, capturing an administrative/organizational relationship. Property B (has_a_review_reference_or_expertise) links a Reviewer to Review expertise or Review preference objects, capturing the reviewer's subject-matter expertise and reviewing preferences. They have different ranges (Administrator vs. Review expertise/Review preference) and model fundamentally different aspects of the reviewer-assignment process.

cmt:Preference is a class representing a reviewer's preference value regarding a paper assignment, whereas confOf:Regular is a subclass of Participant denoting a regular (non-student, non-member) conference participant. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference Dinner in edas is a social meal event (subclass of Non Academic Event/Meal Event). They denote completely different categories of entities—a person versus an event—with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Document is a top-level class whose children are Paper and Review, representing artefacts produced in the review process. In ekaw, Web_Site is a specific kind of Document (a sibling of Paper, Review, Flyer, etc.), not a general document concept. The two entities are at different levels of generality and denote different things: cmt's Document is a broad category, while ekaw's Web_Site is a specific online resource. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

The property 'writes' in confOf relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), whereas 'initiates' in edas relates committee roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call (e.g., call for papers). These are completely different relations involving different domain and range entities, so they are unrelated.

Submitted Paper is a document type (a paper submitted to a conference), while Audiovisual equipment is a physical item like a projector or computer. They share no domain semantics despite both being subclasses of a generic Item/Document root.

hasSurname is a datatype property from Person to string capturing a person's family name, while authorOf is an object property from Person to Document capturing which documents a person authored. They relate entirely different kinds of things and share no semantic overlap.

Both represent scheduled oral presentation events at a conference, but they are not equivalent. EDAS Talk Event is a broad category encompassing talks (including closing/welcome talks), while IASTED Session is a specific lecture-format session with speakers. They overlap in the conference presentation domain but neither subsumes the other cleanly given their different hierarchies and scopes.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person and has subclasses Administrator, Author, Reviewer—i.e., it denotes people who interact with the conference system in specific roles. In sigkdd, Person is the top-level class for all people involved in the conference (Listener, Organizator, Speaker) and carries general properties like name, email, nation. Thus cmt:User is a narrower notion (system users with roles) than sigkdd:Person (any conference person), so User is subsumed by Person rather than equivalent.

confOf's Science_Worker is a broad category of academic/research personnel (sibling to Author, Scholar, Administrator, etc.), while sigkdd's Program_Chair is a specific organizational role within Organizator. A Science_Worker is not necessarily a Program Chair, and a Program Chair is not necessarily a Science_Worker. The two classes have different intended instances with no clear overlap relationship.

In iasted, Sponsor is a direct subclass of Person, meaning a sponsor is a person. In sigkdd, Gold Supporter is a specific tier of Sponzor (alongside Silver, Bronze, Platinum, etc.), so it is a more specialized concept. The iasted Sponsor is more general than Gold Supporter, making this a subsumed_by relation (iasted Sponsor is subsumed by the broader sigkdd Sponzor hierarchy, and Gold Supporter is a strict subclass of what Sponsor denotes). They are not equivalent because Gold Supporter is a specific sponsorship level, not the general concept of a sponsor.

In ontology A, 'Conference part' denotes a component of a conference such as Track, Tutorial, or Workshop. In ontology B, 'Conference' denotes the conference event itself (with properties like start/end dates, city, and being held by ACM SIGKDD). These are different concepts: one is a part of a conference, the other is the conference as a whole. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Tutorial is a type of academic event (a working event under Event), while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (an item). They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference announcement is a document type (a subclass of Conference document) used to announce a conference, while Organising Agency is an organisation that organises a conference. One is an information artefact, the other is a corporate entity; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

cmt:Person is the top-level human class in CMT (with subclasses like Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member, User), whereas edas:TPCMember is a specific subclass of edas:Person denoting a Technical Program Committee member. They sit at different levels of generality and come from different ontologies, so they are not equivalent. The most precise relation would be subsumed_by (TPCMember is a kind of Person), but since cmt:Person and edas:Person are from different ontologies and not asserted to be the same here, the safest verdict is unrelated rather than equivalent.

Chairman in cmt is a person role (parent: Person) with sub-roles like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair, involved in marking conflicts of interest. BreakEvent in edas is a non-academic conference event (parent: Non Academic Event > Conference Event) with sub-types like Coffee Break and Meal Break. These denote completely different domain concepts: a person role vs. a scheduled event during a conference.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing a short version or abstract of a conference paper. Computer Networks Applications Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic representing a subject classification for computer networks applications. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Industry Organization in edas is a type of organization (subclass of Organization). One denotes a human role, the other an organizational entity; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Both Banquet (confOf) and Excursion (edas) are subclasses of Social Event, but they denote different kinds of social events: a banquet is a formal meal, while an excursion is a trip or outing. They overlap as social events but are not equivalent.

Property A (has a URL) points to a web address/URL string for a conference, while property B (Name of conference) points to the human-readable name of the conference. These are distinct attributes with no overlap in intended meaning.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. In cmt, paperAssignmentFinalizedBy links a Conference to an Administrator (who finalizes paper assignments). In confOf, writes links an Author to a Contribution (paper). They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relations.

Abstract in the Conference ontology is a document class representing a summary text of a paper/poster/presentation, situated under Conference document > Conference contribution > Regular contribution > Extended abstract. Topic in the edas ontology is a subject-area classification (e.g., Antennas, CAD, Cryptography) assigned to conferences and papers. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Industrial Paper in ekaw is a type of academic paper (Document > Paper > Industrial Paper), referring to a paper from industry. Mailing list in iasted is a type of document (Item > Document > Mailing list), referring to a mailing list document. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

rejectPaper is an action property where an Administrator rejects a Paper (a decision outcome). paperPresentedAs relates a Paper to its Individual Presentation (how it is presented at the conference). These are completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, 'Conference' denotes the overall conference event/organization with properties like date, logo URL, accepts hardcopy submissions, and has conference members. In the Conference ontology, 'Conference part' is a generic class for constituent parts of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop), with properties like 'is part of conference volumes'. These are structurally and semantically different: one is the whole conference entity, the other is a part-of decomposition class. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while Sponzor in sigkdd is an organization that provides financial support (with tiers like Gold/Silver/Bronze). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Presentation in edas is a subclass of Academic Event/Conference Event, denoting the event where a paper is presented. Author of paper in sigkdd is a subclass of Person/Speaker/Author, denoting a person who authored a paper. One is an event, the other is a person; they are disjoint categories with no alignment relationship.

confOf Student is a general participant subcategory (a student attending the conference), while sigkdd Author_of_paper_student is a specific author role for students who authored a paper. The confOf Student class is not restricted to authors, and the sigkdd class is specifically about authorship. They share the word 'student' but denote different concepts: one is a participant type, the other an author sub-role. No subsumption holds because not all Students are authors and not all student authors are conference participants in the confOf sense.

In EDAS, Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, Published Paper, and properties such as isReviewedBy, isWrittenBy, hasTopic. In IASTED, Form is an administrative document with children like Author information form, Hotel registration form, Registration form. These denote completely different kinds of things: academic papers vs. bureaucratic forms. They share only the generic parent Document, which is too broad to imply equivalence or subsumption.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. 'belongs to reviewers' links review expertise or review preference to a Reviewer, indicating which reviewer has a certain expertise or preference. 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker, indicating who presented the document. The domains (Review expertise/Review preference vs Document) and ranges (Reviewer vs Speaker) are disjoint, and the relations describe different aspects of the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing a person's email address in the conference domain. Labels are synonymous ('has an email' / 'has Email'), paths match, and no contextual difference suggests distinct meanings.

In ekaw, Abstract is a specific kind of document (a summary of a paper/talk), a child of Document. In sigkdd, Document is the general superclass of Abstract, Paper, and Review. These are at different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept: an Abstract is not equivalent to a Document. They are not in a direct subsumption relation across the two ontologies either, so the appropriate relation is unrelated.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership/organizing role (a Chairman in cmt), whereas IASTED non member is a type of Delegate (attendee) who is not an IASTED member. One is an organizational official, the other is a regular conference attendee; their intended instances do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

In edas, Sponsorship denotes the financial support arrangement itself (with cost amount, currency, provider), and its child is Travel Grant. In sigkdd, Sponzor denotes the agent/organization that provides sponsorship (with children like Gold Supporter, Exhibitor, etc., and properties like name).
