These are different concepts: one is the sponsorship arrangement, the other is the sponsoring organization. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Modelling is a research activity performed before a conference, while Webmaster is a person serving as an organizer. They belong to entirely different ontological categories (activity vs. person) and share no domain overlap.

In EDAS, Conference is a specific academic event with deadlines, topics, documents, and members. In EKAW, Organisation is a general body (e.g., academic institution, agency, publisher) that organises events. A conference is an event, not an organisation; the two ontologies model different aspects of the domain.

The property 'issues' in the Conference ontology relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings it publishes, while 'has Event' in ekaw relates an Event to a sub-Event (e.g., a conference containing workshops). They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relations (publication vs. mereological/event-containment), so they are unrelated.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event with children Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop, denoting the working/academic portion of a conference. edas:MicroelectronicsTopic is a subclass of Topic, denoting a specific subject area (microelectronics). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'has title' is a datatype property giving the name/title of a Social event or Working event (range string). sigkdd's 'End of conference' is a datatype property giving the end date/time of a Conference (range dateTime). They relate different kinds of things to different value types and denote completely different concepts.

Program committee (Conference ontology) is an organizational body/committee, while Conference Chair (edas) is a specific person role. A committee is a group of people, not a single person, so these are disjoint concepts.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'lists Event' connects a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event it lists. In sigkdd, 'presentation' connects a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are disjoint, so they are unrelated.

hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property from Call to string, giving submission instructions text. locationOf is an object property from Location to Event, relating a place to an event held there. They connect completely different domain/range types and have no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate completely different domains and ranges. hasSubjectArea links a Paper to a Subject Area (topic taxonomy), while is_situated_in links spatial entities (Building, City, Place) to other spatial entities (Building, City, Place, State). They share no conceptual overlap.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for people in the conference domain. They share structurally equivalent children (e.g., Conference participant = Conference Participant, Reviewer = Possible Reviewer, Conference contributor = Paper Author) and participate in symmetric authorship relations (A: has authors Document->Person, written By Person->Document; B: written By Document->Person, author Of Person->Document). The intended instances coincide.

The edas 'Two Level Conference' is a conference type (a subclass of Conference), while the sigkdd 'Program Committee member' is a person role (a subclass of Organizator under Person). They denote completely different things: an event vs. a person.

A denotes a person who participates in a conference (subclass of Person), while B denotes the conference event itself (with properties like city, start/end dates, and name). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Medicine Topic in edas is a specific subject-area topic (a sibling of Antennas Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.), denoting the medical domain specifically. Research Topic in ekaw is a general class for any research subject area, covering all topics that papers or events can address. These are not the same concept: one is a particular topic (medicine), the other is the general category of research topics. They are also not in a subsumption relationship since Medicine Topic is not a subclass of Research Topic in the ekaw sense (edas has no generic 'Research Topic' parent), and Research Topic is not a subclass of Medicine Topic. They are unrelated as classes.

Both properties relate a place/organization to a conference event, but they differ in domain and directionality. edas:isLocationOf has domain Place and range ConferenceEvent, meaning any place can be the location of any conference event. sigkdd:hold has domain ACM_SIGKDD (a specific organization) and range Conference, meaning a specific organization holds a conference. The edas property is more general (any Place can be location of any ConferenceEvent), while sigkdd:hold is restricted to a specific organizer holding a conference. Thus isLocationOf is subsumed_by hold in the sense that hold is a more specific relationship, though the domain difference (Place vs ACM_SIGKDD) makes them not directly equivalent.

Acceptance in cmt is a Decision (the outcome of accepting a paper), while Reject Rating in edas is a Review Rating (a score assigned by a reviewer). These are different concepts: one is a final decision, the other is a reviewer's rating. They are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption relation.

Entity A is a topic about computer networks sensors (a subject area), while entity B is a Workshop (a type of scientific event). They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

An Extended abstract is a short summary-type contribution (a sibling of Paper under Regular contribution), whereas a Workshop Paper is a full paper submitted to a workshop. They denote different kinds of documents in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Document is a narrow class covering only Paper and Review (the artefacts authors/reviewers produce). In iasted, Document is a broad superclass under Item with many subclasses (Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance, Submission, etc.), so cmt:Document is subsumed by iasted:Document rather than equivalent.

confOf's Science Worker is a person working in a scientific capacity (e.g., researcher/scientist), as indicated by its sibling Scholar and the broader Person hierarchy. ekaw's Agency Staff Member denotes staff of a sponsoring or partner agency, not a scientist. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Taxi is a transport vehicle (Item > Transport vehicle > Taxi) in the iasted ontology, while Organizator is a person role (Person > Organizator) in the sigkdd ontology. These denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Company denotes a for-profit commercial organization, whereas Research Institute denotes a non-profit academic research organization. Although both are subtypes of Organization, their intended instances do not coincide: a company is not a research institute and vice versa. They are disjoint specializations rather than equivalent or overlapping.

has_the_last_name denotes a person's surname, while hasFax denotes a fax number. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they represent completely different attributes with no semantic overlap.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length written document (a paper artifact) in the cmt ontology, while Regular_Session is a scheduled event/session in the ekaw ontology. One is a document, the other is an event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference Banquet is a social gathering event during a conference, while Departure is an activity occurring after the conference (e.g., leaving). These denote clearly different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Administrative event in confOf is a kind of event (e.g., registration, reviewing, submission, camera-ready), whereas Committee in sigkdd is an organizational body (e.g., Program Committee, Organizing Committee, Best Paper Awards Committee). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A 'is connected with' is an object property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place, while property B 'Name' is a datatype property linking Person to a string. They have different domains, ranges, and types, and denote completely different relations.

The two properties describe the same real-world relationship between a paper and its author, but in opposite directions: cmt:hasAuthor goes Paper -> Author, while confOf:writes goes Author -> Contribution. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent.

Co-author is a person who co-writes a paper (subclass of Author/Person), while Research Topic is a subject area covered by papers or events. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The ekaw 'references' property denotes a relation where one document cites or references another, while the sigkdd 'presentation' property links a Speaker to the Document they present. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

Both classes denote the same real-world role: a person who chairs a conference session. In edas, Session Chair is a subclass of Person (alongside Attendee, Author, etc.), while in iasted it is modeled as a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference). The iasted ontology places Delegate under Place > Building > Conference building, which is an unusual modeling choice, but the intended instances of Session chair are still conference delegates who serve as session chairs. The labels are identical (modulo capitalization), and the sibling classes in iasted (Speaker, Listener, etc.) are all types of conference delegates, confirming that Session chair is a person role, not a place or building. The two classes therefore have the same intended instances and are equivalent.

Property A ('has a degree') has domain Review preference and represents a degree/rating of preference, while property B ('has amount of') has domain Money and represents a monetary amount. They relate to completely different domains and concepts, so they are unrelated.

Security Topic is a subject-matter topic (a research area like cryptography, antennas, etc.) under Topic in the EDAS ontology. Program Committee is an organizational committee responsible for reviewing papers in the SIGKDD ontology. These are completely different concepts: one denotes a research subject area, the other denotes a group of people organizing peer review. They share no instances and have no hierarchical relationship.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is the chair/head of the program committee, a specialized leadership role distinct from a general Program Committee member (sigkdd). The sigkdd ontology separately lists 'Program Chair' as a sibling of 'Program Committee member', indicating it distinguishes the chair role from ordinary members. A chair is not equivalent to a member; nor is it a broader or narrower class of member. The two concepts denote different organizational roles, so they are unrelated.

Organisation in ekaw denotes an organisational entity (academic institutions, agencies, publishers) that organises events or publishes materials. Place in sigkdd denotes a physical location (conference hall, hotel, office) where people can stay. These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is an event (a scheduled activity during a conference where registration takes place), while entity B is a person (a participant who registered late). They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies (Event hierarchy vs. Person hierarchy) and denote fundamentally different categories of things. There is no equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

Property A ('has the last name') captures a person's surname, while property B ('E mail') captures a person's email address. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote completely different attributes of a person. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and not meaningfully related.

Both classes denote a reviewer in the conference domain. In cmt, Reviewer is a person who reviews papers (properties like read_By_Reviewer, assign_External_Reviewer, adjust_Bid). In confOf, Member_PC has the comment 'Reviewer' and the property 'reviewes' (Member_PC -> Contribution), confirming it is a program committee member who serves as a reviewer. The confOf ontology uses Member_PC as its reviewer role, and the comment explicitly states 'Reviewer'. Both are persons who perform reviews, so they are equivalent.

confOf Administrator is a specific administrative role under Person (alongside Author, Chair PC, etc.), while sigkdd Organizator is a broader category that subsumes General Chair, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Webmaster, and other organizing roles. Administrator appears to be a narrower concept than Organizator, which functions as a general organizer category.

These two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. confOf:location has domain Social_event/Working_event and range string (an event has a location string). edas:isLocationOf has domain Place and range ConferenceEvent (a place is the location of an event). They relate events to locations but in opposite directions, and one is a datatype property while the other is an object property. A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent.

In cmt, Conference is the event itself (with date, logo URL, accepts hardcopy submissions, has conference members). In iasted, Conference Hiker is a person (a Delegate subtype) who participates in a conference hike activity. They denote completely different things despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

Property A (writes) relates Authors to Contributions (papers they author), while property B (isReviewedBy) relates Papers to reviewers (chairs, reviewers, TPC members). These are entirely different relations: authorship vs. review assignment. They share no common semantics despite both involving papers as domain/range.

Chair in the Conference ontology is a generic committee chair role (with a sibling Co-chair), covering any committee leadership position. General Chair in sigkdd is a specific type of organizer (sibling to Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc.), denoting the top conference chair. General Chair is thus a specific kind of Chair, making Chair more general.
Co chair is a person role within a conference committee, while Building is a physical location. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Paper Author in ekaw is a person who authors a paper, a straightforward author role. Worker lecturer in iasted is a lecturer who is also a worker, under a deep hierarchy (Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer > Worker lecturer). The iasted class is a very specific sub-type of lecturer/author with a worker dimension, not equivalent to the general Paper Author class. They share the authoring connection but are at very different levels of generality and the iasted class carries additional lecturer+worker semantics.

Both classes are named 'Review' and represent review documents in the conference domain. In ontology A, Review is a Conference document with properties linking it to reviewed contributions. In ontology B, Review is a Document under Item, with siblings like Submission and Record of attendance. Despite different ontology structures, both denote the same concept: a review document written for a conference contribution.

Entity A is a specific research topic about computer networks switching, a subclass of Topic. Entity B is an Organizing Committee, a subclass of Committee. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

confOf:Administrative_event is a subclass of Event covering organizational activities like registration, reviewing, submission, and camera-ready events. edas:ComputerNetworksManagementTopic is a subclass of Topic, specifically a subject area within computer networks. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt property 'memberOfProgramCommittee' relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee, denoting committee membership. The iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item, denoting that a person gives (presents, delivers, etc.) an activity or item. These are entirely different relations: one expresses organizational membership, the other expresses authorship/presentation of an activity or item. Their domains and ranges do not overlap meaningfully, and there is no subsumption relationship between them.

confOf:Paper is a written contribution submitted to a conference (subclass of Contribution, sibling of Poster and Short_paper). edas:TestOnlyTopic is a subject-area topic (subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They denote completely different concepts: a document/artefact versus a conference subject classification.

Both classes involve oral presentations at a conference, but they operate at different levels of generality and in different ontological contexts. 'Invited talk' in the Conference ontology is a specific kind of conference contribution (a document/artefact), sibling to Regular contribution and Poster, denoting the content of an invited presentation. 'Talk Event' in edas is a kind of academic event (an occurrence/activity), with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk that are organizational events rather than research contributions. While an Invited talk could be realized as a Talk Event, the two classes do not have coinciding instances: Talk Event includes non-contribution events (welcome, closing) and Invited talk is framed as a contribution/document rather than an event. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Web Site is a digital document. They belong to disjoint branches (events vs documents) and share no instances.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In Conference, 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (a reviewer inviting a colleague to co-review). In confOf, 'reviewes' relates a Member PC to a Contribution (a PC member reviewing a paper). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; neither subsumes the other.

Both are short-form conference contributions, but they are not the same concept: 'Extended abstract' typically summarizes a paper/talk, while 'Short paper' is a distinct submission type. They overlap in being brief contributions but are not equivalent.

Both classes denote a person who writes papers/contributions in the conference domain. They share the same label and occupy a parallel position under Person in their respective hierarchies. The properties associated with each class are directly parallel: cmt:Author has 'write Paper' (Author -> Paper) and 'submit Paper' (Author -> Paper), while confOf:Author has 'writes' (Author -> Contribution). Since Paper and Contribution are themselves equivalent in this domain, the two Author classes relate the same kinds of entities in the same way, confirming they denote the same concept.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' has domain Conference and range Administrator, indicating who entered review criteria for the conference. In the Conference ontology, 'invited_by' has domain and range Reviewer, indicating which reviewer invited another reviewer. They relate different entities in different directions and are not equivalent.

Both classes represent chair roles in a conference setting, but they are not equivalent. cmt's Conference Chair is a specific person who chairs the entire conference, while Conference ontology's Chair is a committee chair (domain/range links it to Committee -> Chair). The cmt ontology separately has Program Committee Chair, indicating Conference Chair is broader/different from committee-level chairs. They overlap as chair roles but have different scope and granularity.

confOf Science Worker is a professional research role (e.g., scholar/scientist), while ekaw Student is an academic-status role. They are disjoint concepts that merely share the parent Person; a science worker is not necessarily a student and vice versa.

These properties operate on entirely different domains and serve different purposes. confOf's 'starts on' records the start date of an Event (when something begins), while iasted's 'done till' records the deadline date for a Deadline (when something must be completed). One denotes a beginning point, the other a cutoff/deadline. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

cmt:Paper is a scientific paper (a written contribution submitted to a conference), with properties like hasAuthor, hasDecision, assignedTo reviewers, etc. Conference:Conference_www is a web page about a conference (a URL-bearing document), sibling to Call_for_paper, Conference_announcement, etc. They share no instances: one is the article itself, the other is a web page. Not equivalent, not subsumed, merely unrelated.

Government Organization is a type of organization (e.g., government body) in the EDAS ontology, while Organizing Committee member is a type of person who serves on the organizing committee in the SIGKDD ontology. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in their intended instances.

hasProgramme relates a Conference Event to a Programme (the document/artefact listing the event's schedule). organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (the agent that organises the event). These are different relations with different ranges and different semantics: one points to a programme artefact, the other to an organising agent. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

`author Of` relates a Person to a Document they authored, while `send` relates a Person to an Item they send. Authoring and sending are distinct relations in the conference domain; the ranges (Document vs Item) also differ, and there is no indication that these properties coincide or overlap.

The confOf 'writes' property specifically relates an Author to a Contribution (i.e., a written paper). The iasted 'give' property relates a Person to an Activity or Item (i.e., presenting or giving something at an event). Writing a paper and giving a presentation/item are distinct relations in the conference domain, even though both connect a person to a conference artefact.

confOf Participant is a broad superclass of all conference attendees (Member, Regular, Student), while iasted Author is a highly specific subclass of Speaker under Delegate. A Participant is far more general than an Author, but the iasted Author is modeled as a person role nested under Place > Building > Conference building, making the ontological contexts too divergent for a clean subsumption. They are not equivalent.

Active Paper in edas is a Paper that is currently under review/active in the review process (a subclass of Paper with siblings like Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn). Abstract in sigkdd is a Document type representing a submission abstract, a sibling of Paper and Review. These denote completely different concepts: one is a paper status/state, the other is a document type. They share no instance overlap.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a type of academic event with two levels). In iasted, 'Speaker' is a subclass of Delegate (a person who gives a presentation at a conference). Despite both appearing under a hierarchy that includes Person-related entities in edas, the labels and contexts make clear that one is an event type and the other is a person role; they share no instances.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to its title string, while the confOf 'starts_on' property relates an Event to its start date/time string. These are completely different relations in the conference domain: one captures the name of a paper, the other captures when an event begins. They share only the string datatype, which is not sufficient for equivalence.

OC Member in ekaw refers to an Organizing Committee member (responsible for local logistics and conference organization), while Program Committee member in sigkdd refers to a member of the Program Committee (responsible for reviewing papers). These are distinct committee roles in conference organization: the Organizing Committee handles logistics, venue, registration, etc., while the Program Committee handles the scientific program and paper review. The sibling structures confirm this: OC Member is grouped with conference participant roles (Demo Chair, Session Chair, Presenter, etc.), while Program Committee member is grouped with organizer roles (General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). They denote different concepts and neither subsumes the other.

In ontology A, 'Conference announcement' is a sibling of Call for paper, Call for participation, etc., denoting an announcement document. In ontology B, 'Conference Proceedings' is a published volume of papers (a Multi author Volume). These are different kinds of documents: an announcement vs. a collection of accepted papers.

Both classes denote the same high-level concept of an organization in the conference domain. They share the same label (modulo spelling), and both serve as a general superclass for specific organization types (Company/University vs. Academic Institution/Organising Agency/Proceedings Publisher). The differences in children and associated properties reflect ontology-specific modeling choices rather than divergent intended meanings.

confOf:Conference is a conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference itself as an organised event. iasted:Refusing manuscript is an activity that happens before a conference (subclass of Activity before conference, sibling of Accepting manuscript and Receiving manuscript), denoting the act of rejecting a submitted paper. One is an event, the other is an administrative action; they share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.
Review preference is about a reviewer's preference for reviewing a topic or submission, while Time is a temporal concept with children like Deadline and Conference days. They share no domain overlap.

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs a committee or conference (subclass of Person with children like Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair). Session in ekaw is a scientific event (subclass of Event > Scientific Event with children like Conference Session, Demo Session). These denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain: a person role versus a scheduled event.

Call for participation is a conference document (an announcement/invitation), while Submissions deadline is a temporal entity (a deadline date). One is a document artefact, the other is a time point. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges. enterConferenceDetails relates an Administrator to a Conference (an admin action of setting up conference details), while listsEvent relates a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (a document listing events). They connect different kinds of entities and represent different relationships in the conference domain.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Optical Topic' is a specific subject taxonomy topic under 'Computer Networks Topic', used to classify papers by research area. In EKAW, 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a document type—a subclass of Abstract—representing the summary text of an invited talk. They share no instances, no common parent, and no semantic overlap.

Meeting Room Place is a room where meetings/sessions are held, while Main office is an administrative office. Both are subtypes of Place but denote different kinds of locations with different purposes.

confOf Reception is a social event (e.g., banquet, trip) at a conference, while edas AcceptRating is a review rating value indicating a paper should be accepted. They belong to completely different parts of the domain (social activities vs. review decisions) and share no instances.

A Workshop is a working academic event where papers are presented and discussed, whereas a Coffee break is a social/break activity during a conference. They share no instances and occupy different positions in their respective hierarchies.

Property A relates a Committee to a Conference volume (the committee was a committee of that conference). Property B relates a Person to an Item (the person writes the item). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no overlap in meaning.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length paper document in the CMT ontology (Document > Paper > PaperFullVersion), while MultimediaTopic is a subject-area topic in the EDAS ontology (Topic > MultimediaTopic). They denote completely different kinds of entities: a document artifact versus a research topic.

Entity A is a class denoting a person who applies to attend a conference (subclass of Person). Entity B is a class denoting the conference event itself (with properties like has Country, paper Due On, etc.). These are completely different concepts: one is a person/role, the other is an event/organization.

The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper). The ekaw 'has Reviewer' property links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (the paper has someone assigned to review it). These are different relations involving different domain and range types, and neither subsumes the other.

cmt's writePaper relates an Author to a Paper they author (authorship relation). ekaw's paperPresentedAs relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (presentation format relation). These are completely different relations with different domains (Author vs Paper) and different ranges (Paper vs Individual Presentation).

confOf:hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (its title), whereas iasted:obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Contribution vs Person), range (string vs Item), and meaning (assigning a title vs obtaining an item). They are unrelated.

Student in ekaw is a person (subclass of Person) who is a student, while Student registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee (subclass of Registration fee under Money) charged for student registration. One denotes a person, the other a fee amount — completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in the conference domain. cmt:memberOfConference links a Conference Member (a person) to a Conference, expressing that a person is a member of a conference (e.g., on its committee or programme committee). edas:belongsToEvent links a Programme (a document/artefact) to a Conference Event, expressing that a programme belongs to an event. The domains (Conference Member vs Programme) and ranges (Conference vs Conference Event) differ, so the properties do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Both are datatype properties representing deadlines in the conference domain, but they denote different submission stages: A specifically captures the camera-ready paper submission deadline (domain Important dates), while B captures the general paper submission deadline (domain Conference, comment 'Conference Paper Date and Time Deadline'). The camera-ready deadline occurs after acceptance, whereas the paper due date is the initial submission deadline. They overlap in being conference deadlines but are not equivalent.

confOf:Paper is a class denoting a submitted/accepted written contribution (sibling of Poster and Short paper under Contribution), whereas sigkdd:Best_Research_Paper_Award is a kind of Award given to a paper. One denotes the document/artefact itself, the other denotes an honour/prize; their instances do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'is Initiated By' in edas relates a Call to the persons who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). The property 'give' in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Organization denotes institutions like companies and universities with address properties, while iasted:Money denotes monetary amounts with fee/tax/tip subtypes and payment relations. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person (a chairman who leads the conference), while Submission event in confOf is an administrative event representing the act of submitting contributions. They belong to disjoint branches (Person vs Event) and denote completely different kinds of entities.

The property 'has Call' in edas relates an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., call for papers), while 'searched by' in sigkdd relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and denote unrelated relationships in the conference organization domain.

Paper Full Version is a concrete document artifact (a full paper submitted for review), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline (a date by which abstracts must be submitted). They belong to completely different branches of the domain hierarchy (Document vs. Deadline) and share no instances.

A Program Committee Member in cmt is a specific role: a person serving on the program committee (reviewing papers, assigned max papers, member of a PC). B's Participant in confOf is a broad superclass for anyone attending the conference (with children Member, Regular, Student). A PC member is not equivalent to a participant, nor is one clearly more general than the other in the intended alignments: cmt has a separate Person/ConferenceMember hierarchy without a generic Participant class, and confOf has Member PC / Chair PC as the PC-specific roles. The two classes denote different groupings (committee role vs. attendance role), so they are unrelated.

Workshop in EDAS is a standalone academic event (a meeting organized around a theme), whereas Regular Session in EKAW is a time-slot block within a conference containing multiple talks. They are at different levels of granularity: a workshop is not a kind of regular session, nor vice versa. The EKAW sibling 'Workshop Session' further confirms that a workshop and a session are distinct concepts in this ontology.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person belonging to the conference). In edas, isLocationOf links a Place to a Conference Event (indicating where an event takes place). The domains (Conference vs Place), ranges (Conference Member vs Conference Event), and intended meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

iasted:Deadline is a general class covering all kinds of deadlines (camera ready, notification, hotel reservation, registration, submission). sigkdd:Deadline_Paper_Submission is a specific deadline for paper submission, a child of sigkdd:Deadline. The iasted:Deadline class subsumes the more specific paper-submission deadline concept.

confOf:Paper is a written contribution (subclass of Contribution, sibling of Poster and Short paper), whereas sigkdd:Best_Paper_Awards_Committee is a committee that awards a prize (subclass of Committee, sibling of Organizing/Program committees). They denote completely different kinds of things in the conference domain.

confOf's Assistant is a general conference helper role (sibling of Volunteer, Administrator, etc.), whereas sigkdd's Program Committee member is a specific committee role responsible for paper reviews. The two roles are distinct in the conference domain; an Assistant is not a PC member and vice versa.

confOf Member is a participant who is a member (e.g., of the conference organization), whereas iasted IASTED non member is a delegate who is specifically NOT an IASTED member. These are disjoint concepts: one denotes a member, the other a non-member. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only superficially related via membership status.

A Meta Review is a specific kind of review document (subclass of Review under Document), i.e., an artefact produced in the reviewing process. B Member PC is a person who serves on the programme committee and acts as a reviewer (subclass of Person). One is a document, the other is a person; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop — it denotes academic/professional events. iasted:Non_speaker is a subclass of Delegate (under Person-like hierarchy) denoting conference attendees who do not present. They belong to disjoint regions of the taxonomy (events vs. persons) and share no instances.

Workshop in the Conference ontology is an academic conference part where papers are presented, sibling to Track and Tutorial. Coffee Break in edas is a non-academic break event during the conference. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Book_proceeding in iasted is a publication artefact (a book of conference proceedings), whereas Deadline_Paper_Submission in sigkdd is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies (Publication vs Deadline) and denote unrelated kinds of things.

In EDAS, Conference Event is a broad top-level class covering all conference-related events, with children Academic Event and Non Academic Event. In EKAW, Conference Banquet is a specific social event (a banquet), a leaf under Event > Social Event. A banquet is one particular kind of conference event, so Conference Event subsumes Conference Banquet.

Attendee in edas is a class of persons who attend a conference (subclass of Person), while Student registration fee in iasted is a monetary amount charged for student registration (subclass of Money > Fee > Registration fee). These denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. a fee—and share no meaningful relationship.

Both properties relate an author/person to a written work (Contribution/Document) in the same direction. In the conference domain, Contribution and Document are closely aligned, and Author is a subclass of Person. The properties share the same intended meaning of authorship.

In cmt, Paper is a specific subclass of Document (a concrete paper submission with children like Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version). In sigkdd, Document is the general super-class whose children include Abstract, Paper, and Review. Thus cmt:Paper is a narrower concept subsumed by sigkdd:Document, not equivalent.

starts_on is a datatype property from Event to string (a start date), while hasEvent is an object property from Event to Event (relating an event to its sub-events). They have different ranges, types, and meanings.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote different relations. 'has Updated Version' (ekaw) relates a Document to another Document (a newer version of the same document). 'write' (iasted) relates a Person to an Item (the act of authoring). They share no common semantics.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Departure is a post-conference activity (e.g., leaving). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In the Conference ontology, 'Topic' denotes a subject area of a conference (e.g., a research topic assigned to conference parts, submissions, and review preferences). In the iasted ontology, 'Person' denotes a human actor (with children Delegate and Sponsor) who gives items, attends activities, occupies buildings, etc. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a person who is a conference committee member (path: Person > Chairman > Associated Chair), while Trip city is a geographic location (path: City > Trip city). These are completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (organizational membership), while attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (event attendance). These are distinct relations: being a member of a conference organization is not the same as attending a conference event. The domains (Conference Member vs Person) and ranges (Conference vs Conference Event) also differ, confirming they denote different concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'assignedByReviewer' links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (likely indicating which internal reviewer assigned the external one). In edas, 'hasReviewHistory' links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History object. They relate different kinds of entities and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

These properties have completely different meanings, domains, ranges, and types. confOf's 'default Choice' is a datatype property from Social/Working events to a positive integer (likely a configuration/selection value), while iasted's 'is given by' is an object property from Activity/Item to Person (indicating who provides or gives something). They share no semantic overlap.

hasCostCurrency is a datatype property from Sponsorship to string (capturing the currency of a sponsorship cost), while locationOf is an object property from Location to Event (indicating which event a location belongs to). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings with no overlap.

Administrator in cmt is a person role (a user who manages conference details, assigns reviewers, accepts papers), while Review in iasted is a document artefact. They share no instances and belong to completely different branches (Person vs. Document).

The two properties relate different kinds of things. In cmt, readByReviewer links a Paper to a Reviewer who reads it, whereas in ekaw, reviewWrittenBy links a Review (the document/artefact) to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it. The domains differ (Paper vs Review) and the relations are conceptually distinct: reading a paper vs authoring a review. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

Paper (cmt) is a document submitted for review in a conference management system, with children like Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties linking it to authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions. Currency (iasted) is an unrelated concept (likely representing monetary currency for registration fees). These denote entirely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Regular author is a person who writes a conference contribution, while Author attendee cd registration fee is a monetary fee charged for registration. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities in different directions. 'is signed by' connects an Item (e.g., a document or artefact) to a Person who signs it, while 'pay' connects a Person to a Registration fee. The domains and ranges are disjoint, and the relations capture unrelated aspects of the conference domain (authorship/signing vs. payment).

In cmt, User is a broad superclass covering Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—anyone who interacts with the system. In the Conference ontology, Conference applicant is a specific role: a person who applies to register for a conference (with child 'Registered applicant' and siblings like Committee member, Reviewer, Track workshop chair). A cmt User is not necessarily a conference applicant, and a Conference applicant is not necessarily a cmt User (which is system-specific). The intended instances do not coincide, and neither class subsumes the other in a domain-expert reference alignment.

These properties have the same domain (Conference) and range (dateTime), but they denote different deadlines: 'manuscript Due On' is the deadline for submitting manuscripts, while 'Start of conference' is the date/time when the conference begins. They are distinct temporal properties of a conference and are not equivalent.

Entity A is a class denoting a written document (a paper published at a conference), while entity B is a class denoting the conference event itself, with properties like start/end dates, city, and name. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain despite the shared word 'Conference'.

In cmt, 'Conference Chair' is the overall chair of the conference (a sub-class of Chairman, sibling to Associated Chair and Program Committee Chair). In confOf, 'Chair PC' denotes the chair of the Program Committee (sibling to 'Member PC'). These are distinct roles: the conference chair oversees the entire conference, while the PC chair oversees the reviewing/program committee. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

These properties are completely different. confOf:abstract is a datatype property from Contribution to string (the abstract text of a paper). iasted:obtain is an object property from Person to Item (a person obtaining an item). They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Contribution vs Person), range (string vs Item), and meaning.

In ekaw, Conference Session is a broad class covering various session types (industrial, demo, poster, regular, workshop). In iasted, Session is narrower, sitting under Lecture with child Speaker lecture and siblings like Plenary lecture and Tutorial. The ekaw Conference Session is more general, subsuming the iasted Session.

Steering committee is a committee (an organizational body) that oversees a conference volume, while Possible Reviewer is a person who may review a paper. One denotes an organizational entity, the other a person role; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

edas:SingleLevelConference is a specific structural type of conference (distinguished from TwoLevelConference), whereas ekaw:Conference denotes one edition of a conference in general. The ekaw class is more general, so SingleLevelConference is subsumed by ekaw:Conference rather than equivalent.

In the Conference ontology, 'Organization' denotes an organizational entity (e.g., a conference-organizing body, institution, or company). In the iasted ontology, 'Activity before conference' is a temporal/activity subclass of 'Activity' with children like 'Accepting manuscript', 'Receiving manuscript', 'Refusing manuscript', 'Renting', 'Research'. These are completely different kinds of things: an organization is an agent/institution, while an activity-before-conference is a process/event occurring before a conference. There is no overlap in intended instances.

These properties are completely different: cmt:hasDecision is an object property linking a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while Conference:has_a_degree is a datatype property linking a Review preference to an integer value. They have different domains, different ranges (object vs. datatype), and represent entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Participant is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person, with children Member, Regular, Student). iasted:Research is a pre-conference activity (subclass of Activity before conference, with children Modelling, Simulating). One denotes a person, the other a research activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Entity A is a class denoting a person who registered late and paid (a kind of conference applicant/person), while entity B is a class denoting a financial document (a bank transfer as a payment document). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (Person vs Document) and denote unrelated kinds of entities.

confOf:Conference is a class representing the conference event itself (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). iasted:Brief_introduction_for_Session_chair is a document artifact (subclass of Document, sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Review, etc.). One is an event, the other is a document; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf's 'Social event' is a subclass of Event with children like Banquet, Reception, and Trip, denoting social activities in a conference. iasted's 'Payment document' is a subclass of Document with children like Bank transfer and Cheque, denoting financial documents. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid in the context of paper bidding for review assignment, while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item in the context of giving presentations or items. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and have different domains and ranges. In EDAS, 'for Event' links a Call to an Academic Event (the event the call is for). In EKAW, 'event On List' links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (where the event is listed). They do not share the same domain, range, or meaning, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Conference denotes the conference event/organization itself, with properties like date, logo URL, members, and administrators. In iasted, Time is a temporal concept whose children include Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the conference event, the other is a temporal entity. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

These properties differ in both direction and type. A's 'has a location' is a datatype property from Conference volume to a string (a literal location name), while B's 'location Of' is an object property from Location to Event (relating a Location object to the Event held there). They are not inverses of each other either, since one maps to a string literal and the other to an object. They denote fundamentally different relations.

Both classes denote a conference event/edition in the conference-organisation domain. In ontology A, Conference has a child 'Conference volume' (an edition/proceedings) and properties tying it to Conference part, proceedings, publisher and topic, indicating it is the conference event itself. In ontology B, Conference is a Scientific Event with comment 'One edition of a conference'. The intended instances coincide: a specific conference edition. Minor modelling differences (A is flatter, B places it under Event > Scientific Event) do not prevent equivalence.

Review Rating in EDAS is a rating value (Accept/Accept if room/Reject/Weak reject) assigned to a paper, while Negative Review in EKAW is a kind of Review document. They overlap conceptually around negative outcomes, but one is a rating enum and the other is a document class, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties differ in both meaning and technical type. 'held In' (ekaw) is an object property linking an Event to a Location (where it takes place). 'is dated on' (iasted) is a datatype property linking an Activity to a dateTime (when it occurs). They relate to different aspects (place vs. time) and have incompatible property types (object vs. datatype), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise related.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference itself as an occurrence. ekaw:Conference_Participant is a person (subclass of Person) who participates in a conference, with children such as Presenter, PC Chair, Session Chair, etc. These are disjoint categories (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

Fee for extra trip in iasted denotes a fee for an additional excursion/trip, whereas Registration fee in sigkdd denotes the conference registration fee with subtypes for member/student/non-member. They are disjoint kinds of fees; neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Acceptance is a subclass of Decision, representing the act/decision of accepting a paper. In the Conference ontology, Accepted_contribution is a subclass of Reviewed_contribution, representing the paper itself that has been accepted. These are related concepts (one is the decision, the other is the artifact resulting from that decision), but they are not equivalent because they denote different categories of things: a decision event vs. a written contribution.

confOf#writes has domain Author and range Contribution, while iasted#prepare has domain Person and range Item. Since Author is a sub-class of Person and Contribution is a sub-class of Item (Item being a general artefact including papers, slides, etc.), writes is more specific than prepare. They are not equivalent because prepare can relate non-author persons to non-contribution items.

A 'Working event' in confOf is a kind of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) with properties like has Topic, has title, and location. A 'Building' in iasted is a kind of Place (e.g., Conference hotel, Presenter university) with properties like is situated in and is visited by. These are completely different domain concepts—an event/activity versus a physical structure—so they are unrelated.

In iasted, 'Submissions deadline' is a specific subclass of Deadline (sibling to camera-ready, notification, hotel, and registration deadlines). In sigkdd, 'Deadline' is the general class with children such as abstract submission, author notification, and paper submission deadlines. Thus iasted's Submissions_deadline is a specific kind of deadline that is subsumed by sigkdd's general Deadline class.

In iasted, Item is a broad superclass encompassing physical and documentary objects (Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). In sigkdd, Award is a specific kind of recognition given to authors for papers (Best Paper Awards, etc.). An Award is not a subclass of Item in the iasted sense (it is not equipment, a document, or a vehicle), nor does Item subsume Award conceptually within these ontologies' intended scopes. The two classes denote different domain concepts with no clear hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

confOf:follows relates one Administrative event to another (temporal/sequential ordering between events), while ekaw:organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (who organises it). They have different domains, different ranges, and entirely different semantics; there is no overlap or subsumption relationship.

ekaw:Conference denotes one edition of a scientific conference (an event), while iasted:Conference_hotel denotes the hotel building/venue where a conference takes place (a place). These are completely different concepts despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

The two properties relate different kinds of things in different directions. 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to the Conference volume where it appears, whereas 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author. They denote different relations (submission venue vs authorship) and share no common semantics.

Regular author is a person who writes a conference contribution (subclass of Conference contributor), while Contributed Talk is a type of presentation event. One is a person/role, the other is an event; they share no instances.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract portion of a conference paper. Programme Brochure (ekaw) is a document describing the conference programme, with properties linking it to events, publishers, and web sites. These are entirely different artefacts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

hasTitle is a datatype property from Contribution to string (the title text of a paper). heldIn is an object property from Event to Location (where an event takes place). They relate completely different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range types. confOf:follows connects Administrative events to Administrative events (e.g., one event following another), while edas:isMenuOf connects a Meal Menu to a Meal Event. There is no overlap in the kinds of entities they relate, so they are unrelated.

Break Event in edas denotes a scheduled break (coffee break, meal break, free time) during a conference. Introduction in iasted denotes an introductory conference activity such as introducing a speaker. Despite both being non-academic conference activities, their intended instances are disjoint: a break is not an introduction of a speaker and vice versa.

Both classes denote the same real-world role: a person who chairs a conference session. Despite different ontology placements (ekaw places Session Chair under Person > Conference Participant, while iasted places it under Delegate), the intended instances coincide — a conference participant/delegate who serves as session chair. The labels are essentially identical, and the role is a well-defined, unambiguous concept in the conference domain.

In cmt, Author is a broad class covering all authors of papers (with subclasses like Co-author and Author Not Reviewer). In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a more specific subclass of Author, distinguishing authors of papers from other author types. The cmt Author class is more general and would subsume the sigkdd Author_of_paper class, but they are not equivalent since sigkdd has a more specific hierarchy.

Extended abstract is a short summary-style contribution (parent Regular contribution, sibling Paper, child Abstract), while Industrial Paper is a paper category based on author affiliation/topic (industry vs. academic). They classify contributions along different dimensions: length/format vs. source/type. Neither subsumes the other, and their intended instances do not coincide.

In Conference, 'Program committee' is a committee (an organizational body) that has members and is associated with a conference volume. In ekaw, 'Possible Reviewer' is a person who could review a paper, with 'PC Member' as a subtype. One denotes an organizational entity, the other a person; they are disjoint kinds of things.

cmt:name is a datatype property from Conference or Person to a string (the name of the entity). ekaw:writtenBy is an object property from Document to Person (the author of a document). They have different domains, different ranges (string vs Person), and different meanings: one gives a name, the other relates a document to its author.

The property hasDecision in cmt relates a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while hasCall in edas relates an Academic Event to a Call (for papers). These are different domain/range pairs and different relations in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Workshop is a scientific event (a gathering/session within a conference). In iasted, Simulating is a research activity performed before the conference (e.g., running simulations). One is an event, the other is a research activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference in ontology A denotes the academic event (an organization with a name, proceedings, topics, and conference parts/volumes). Conference hall in ontology iasted denotes a physical place (a room/building where conference activities occur), as shown by its parent Place and siblings Building, Hotel room, Session room. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf 'Member PC' is explicitly a reviewer (comment: 'Reviewer') who reviews contributions and has expertise on topics. edas 'Conference Chair' is the person who initiates calls for papers and can review papers, but is a distinct role from a TPC Member (which is the edas equivalent of a PC member). The two ontologies separate these roles: edas has both 'Conference Chair' and 'TPC Member' as siblings, so Conference Chair is not the same as a PC member. Thus the two entities denote different organizational roles and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (a person attends an event), while partOfEvent relates an Event to an Event (an event is part of another event). They have different domains (Person vs Event), different ranges (Conference Event vs Event), and express fundamentally different relationships (attendance vs mereological parthood).

Accepted Paper is a document (a paper that has been accepted for publication/presentation), while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline (a date by which authors are notified). They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (Document vs. Deadline) and denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Both classes represent people who give presentations at a conference, but they are not equivalent. In EDAS, Presenter is a subclass of Author, implying that a presenter is someone who presents their own paper. In SIGKDD, Invited_Speaker is a subclass of Speaker (not Author), denoting someone invited to give a talk, which may or may not be based on an authored paper submission. The two concepts overlap (an invited speaker could also be an author) but their intended instances do not coincide.

Conference:Person is a broad superclass covering all people involved in the conference (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers, chairs). edas:Author is a specific subclass of edas:Person denoting only authors of papers. Thus Conference:Person subsumes edas:Author; they are not equivalent because Author is a proper subset of Person.

Written_contribution in the Conference ontology is a document/artefact (a written paper or contribution), situated under Conference document > Conference contribution. Poster_Session in ekaw is an event/session type, situated under Event > Scientific Event > Session. One is a document, the other is a scheduled event; they denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

In edas, Attendee is a general class for any person attending the conference (sibling to Author, Reviewer, etc.). In iasted, Session_chair is a specific role under Delegate, sibling to Speaker, Listener, etc. A session chair is a specific kind of attendee, not equivalent to the general Attendee class. The iasted ontology has no general Attendee/Delegate equivalent at the same level, so the relation is not subsumption in either direction but rather a partial overlap (related). However, given the structural mismatch and that Session_chair is a narrow role while Attendee is broad, they are best considered unrelated as direct alignment targets.

hasCountry is an object property linking Organization or Person to a Country individual, whereas Nation is a datatype property linking Person to a string literal. They differ in type (object vs datatype), range (Country vs string), and domain (hasCountry also applies to Organization). These are structurally incompatible and not equivalent.

A's Rejection is a Decision (the outcome of a paper submission), while B's Accept Rating is a Review Rating (a reviewer's score). They are at different levels of the workflow and denote different concepts; moreover A is a negative outcome whereas B is a positive rating, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise overlapping.

In ontology Conference, 'Call for participation' is a subclass of Conference document, i.e. a document issued to invite people to participate in a conference. In confOf, 'Conference' is a subclass of Working event under Event, i.e. the actual conference event itself. A document calling for participation and the conference event are completely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception), whereas iasted:Hotel_fee is a monetary fee for hotel accommodation. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (events vs. money/fees) and share no instances.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while Session room is a physical place where sessions are held (subclass of Place in iasted). They denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. a location—with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing a document (the abstract of a paper). Author of paper student in sigkdd is a subclass of Author representing a person (a student who authored a paper). One is a document, the other is a person; they share no instances and are completely different concepts.

The two properties differ in both domain/range and direction. In Conference, 'has a location' is a datatype property from Conference volume to a string (a textual location). In edas, 'isLocationOf' is an object property from Place to Conference Event, relating a Place object to the event held there. They are not inverses of each other either, since one maps to a string literal and the other to an object; they denote fundamentally different relations.

writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper), while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (who reviews it). These are distinct relationships in the conference domain: authorship vs. review assignment. They connect different kinds of entities and have different meanings, so they are unrelated.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated aspects of the conference domain. `hasCostAmount` (edas) is a datatype property from Sponsorship to int, capturing the monetary amount of a sponsorship. `heldIn` (ekaw) is an object property from Event to Location, capturing where an event takes place. There is no overlap in meaning, direction, or related entity types.

Both properties link a conference artefact (Contribution / Paper) to a subject topic (Topic / Research Topic), so they overlap in intended meaning. However, they are not strictly equivalent: confOf's dealsWith has domain Contribution and range Topic, while ekaw's coversTopic has domain {Event, Paper} and range Research Topic. The ekaw property applies to Events as well as Papers, and the confOf property applies to Contributions (which may include non-paper items like posters or demos). The domain/range mismatch means neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the best fit.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. startReviewerBidding relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of initiating reviewer bidding for a conference), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (the document presented by a speaker). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

The two properties denote different relations. In confOf, 'expertOn' links a PC member to a Topic they have expertise in. In iasted, 'obtain' links a Person to an Item they receive or acquire. The domains (Member PC vs Person) and ranges (Topic vs Item) are disjoint, and the intended meanings (expertise vs acquisition) are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is a document submitted for review (subclass of Document, with authors, reviewers, bids, decisions), whereas confOf:Event is a temporal occurrence (with start/end dates, children like Social event, Working event). They denote completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. ekaw:organisedBy links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it, while iasted:is_occupied_by links a Building, City, or State to a Person that occupies it. The domains (Event vs. Building/City/State) and the intended meanings (organising an event vs. occupying a place) are disjoint, so these properties are unrelated.

Although both properties share the label 'written By', they relate different kinds of things. In cmt, writtenBy links a Review to a Reviewer (who writes a review). In confOf, writtenBy links a Contribution to an Author (who writes a paper). These are distinct relations in the conference domain: one concerns the authorship of reviews, the other concerns the authorship of papers/contributions. They do not share the same domain or range types, and neither subsumes the other.

In EDAS, 'Paper' is a subclass of Document representing the written article itself, with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc. In EKAW, 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person representing a human who authored a paper. These are completely different concepts: one is a document, the other is a person. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference www in ontology Conference is a web page (a Conference document with a URL) about the conference, whereas Conference Proceedings in EKAW is a published multi-author volume of accepted papers. One is a website, the other is a proceedings document; their intended instances do not coincide.

The confOf property 'study At' relates a Scholar to a University (where they study), while the ekaw property 'author Of' relates a Person to a Document (that they authored). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with different domains and ranges, and no overlap in meaning.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event under Event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Video_cassette_player is a piece of audiovisual equipment (under Item, sibling of Computer and LCD projector). These denote completely different categories—a conference session type vs. a physical device—with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference participant in ontology A is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference. Conference building in ontology B is a subclass of Building under Place, denoting a physical location where a conference is held. These are completely different concepts (person vs. physical structure) despite sharing the word 'Conference' in their labels.

Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a specific conference session, distinct from a General Chair (sigkdd) who is the top-level organizer of the entire conference. They are different roles in conference organization, neither subsuming the other.

Conference document is a class for conference-related documents (call for papers, reviews, contributions, etc.), while Sponzor is a class for conference sponsors/supporters (gold, silver, bronze, etc.). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different contexts. 'is Initiated By' links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the committee members who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). 'is signed by' links an Item (a document/artefact) to a Person who signs it. The domains (Call vs Item), ranges (committee roles vs Person), and the nature of the relation (initiation vs signing) are distinct, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. confOf:parallel_with links two Administrative events (e.g., sessions running in parallel), while edas:isLocationOf links a Place to a Conference Event (indicating where an event takes place). They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings, so they are not equivalent.

A Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (a role/agent), while Reviewing results event is an administrative event marking when review results are made available to authors. One is a person, the other is an event; they share no domain overlap.

hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person participating in the conference), while has_a_steering_committee links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (an organizational body). The ranges differ: Conference Member is an individual person, Steering committee is a group/committee. These are distinct relations with different domain and range types.

In ekaw, Person is a broad class with children including Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student, etc. In sigkdd, Speaker is a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited Speaker, siblings Listener and Organizator. Thus ekaw:Person is strictly more general than sigkdd:Speaker, since every Speaker is a Person but not every Person is a Speaker.

In cmt, Person is the top-level class for all people (with children like Chairman, Conference Member, Reviewer, etc.). In ekaw, Student is a proper subclass of Person, representing a specific kind of person (a student). The two entities are at different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept. They are not equivalent, nor is there a subsumption relationship between cmt:Person and ekaw:Student specifically; they are simply unrelated as candidate alignment targets.

Property A ('is submitted at') relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (the venue/event where it is submitted). Property B ('writes') relates an Author to a Contribution (the paper they author). They have completely different domains and ranges and express fundamentally different relationships: submission-to-venue vs. authorship-of-paper.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a short summary component of a paper, sibling to 'Paper Full Version' under Paper. In Conference, 'Extended abstract' is a type of regular contribution (a standalone submission type), sibling to 'Paper' and parent of 'Abstract'. These are different concepts: one is a part/summary of a paper, the other is a submission category. They overlap in being short-form textual artefacts related to papers, but their intended instances do not coincide.

These classes denote entirely different things. 'Information for participants' in ontology Conference is a conference document providing logistical information to attendees (sibling to Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.). 'Conference Paper' in ekaw is a type of academic paper (child of Paper, sibling to Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). One is an informational document, the other is a research paper. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The cmt property 'has Been Assigned' connects a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. The ekaw property 'technically Organised By' (a subproperty of 'organised By') relates something to an entity that technically organises it (e.g., an organisation or committee for an event). These properties operate in different domains (paper review assignment vs. event organisation) and even have opposite directions (assignment-to vs. organised-by), so they are unrelated.

Both classes represent activities occurring during a conference, but their scopes differ significantly. Academic Event in edas is a subclass of Conference Event and includes academic content events like Paper Presentation, Workshop, and Talk Event, with properties linking to calls and documents. Conference activity in iasted is a subclass of Activity and includes social and organizational activities like Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Registration, and Welcome address alongside academic ones like Lecture and Presentation. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

In Conference, Reviewed_contribution is a written contribution (a paper/manuscript) that has been reviewed, with children Accepted_contribution and Rejected_contribution. In sigkdd, Review is a Document (the review report itself), a sibling of Abstract and Paper. One is the artefact under review; the other is the review report. They are different kinds of entities, so not equivalent, subsuming, or related.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has_workshops' links a Conference volume to its constituent Workshops (a part-whole relation), while 'expertOn' links a Member PC to a Topic they are expert in (a competence relation). Their domains and ranges are disjoint, so they do not denote the same relation.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things in different directions. 'read By Meta Reviewer' links a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (who reads/reviews the paper), while 'obtain' links an Author to an Award (the author receives an award). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. In sigkdd, Best Research Paper Award is a subclass of Award, denoting an award given for a research paper. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event dealing with participant registration, while edas's 'Workshop' is an academic event (a type of conference session). They belong to different branches of the event hierarchy and denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different meanings. In cmt, 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who enables a virtual meeting. In confOf, 'follows' links one Administrative event to another (temporal/sequence relation). Their domains and ranges are disjoint, and there is no overlap in intended meaning.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions for different purposes. In cmt, hasConflictOfInterest links a Person to a Document (paper) they have a conflict with, indicating the person cannot review that paper. In iasted, is_used_by links an Item to a Person, indicating the person uses the item. The domains (Person vs Item), ranges (Document vs Person), and semantics (conflict of interest vs usage) are entirely different. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only trivially related by both involving Person on one side.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while Session is a scientific event/session within a conference (subclass of Event in ekaw). One is a person role, the other is an event. They share no instances and are from entirely different branches of their respective ontologies.
A is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (their first name). B is an object property mapping an Activity or Person to an Item or Place. They have different domains, ranges, and meanings.

In ekaw, Person is a top-level class for all people in the conference domain, with children including students, authors, reviewers, and staff. In iasted, Lecturer is a highly specific subclass of Author (itself under Delegate under Conference building), with siblings like Tutorial speaker and Plenary lecture speaker, and children like Student lecturer and Worker lecturer. Lecturer denotes a specific role for a person who delivers a lecture, not the general concept of Person.
