The two classes do not share instances: a Person in ekaw is any individual, while a Lecturer in iasted is a specialized conference participant. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

These properties are inverses, not equivalent. 'belongs To Event' (domain Programme, range Conference Event) links a programme to its event, while 'has Event' (domain Event, range Event) links an event to a sub-event. They relate different kinds of entities in opposite directions and do not share the same domain or range types.

confOf's hasCountry links Organizations and Persons to a Country, while iasted's is_present_in links Persons to Place or Time. The ranges differ (Country vs Place/Time) and the domains differ (Organization+Person vs Person only). They are not equivalent; hasCountry is also not a clear super/subproperty of is_present_in since the latter includes Time and a broader Place.

Closing Talk is a conference event/talk (a scheduled academic session), while Listener is a person who attends to listen. They belong to completely different branches of the ontology hierarchy (events vs. persons) and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Both classes are subclasses of Author and represent authors who co-author a paper. In cmt, 'Co author' is linked to Paper via 'co write' and 'has Co author', indicating a person who jointly writes a paper. In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author (under Speaker > Author), denoting an author of a paper. Both denote the same concept: a person who authors (co-authors) a paper in the conference domain. The slight naming difference (co-author vs author of paper) does not indicate a semantic distinction in this context.

A Workshop is a standalone academic event focused on a specific topic, whereas a Demo Session is a session within a conference dedicated to demonstrations. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain: a workshop is not a type of demo session, nor vice versa.

In edas, Conference denotes the academic event itself (with children like Single/Two Level Conference, properties like paperDueOn, hasCountry, hasTopic). In ekaw, Conference Proceedings is a subclass of Proceedings under Document, i.e. the published volume of papers. These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a document artefact.

Author Not Reviewer in cmt is a subclass of Author, denoting authors who are not reviewers. Member PC in confOf denotes a PC member who reviews papers (comment says 'Reviewer', and it has properties expertOn and reviewes). These are distinct concepts: one is an author excluded from reviewing, the other is a reviewing PC member. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

confOf's Social event is a kind of conference event (e.g., Banquet, Reception, Trip) where participants socialize. edas's Place is a physical location (e.g., Accommodation, Conference Venue, Dining Place, Meeting Room). One denotes an activity/event, the other a spatial location; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Although both are subclasses of Place, they denote different concepts. 'Accommodation Place' in edas refers to lodging (hotels, dormitories, etc.) for conference attendees, while 'Main office' in sigkdd refers to the primary organizational office of the conference. Their siblings also differ: Accommodation Place sits alongside Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, and Meeting Room Place, whereas Main office sits alongside Conference hall and Hotel. There is no overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel (e.g., sessions or tracks running simultaneously). The ekaw 'paper In Volume' property relates a paper to the volume/proceedings in which it appears. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

In cmt, Co-author is a strict subclass of Author (a person who co-writes a paper), whereas in edas Author is the general class of all paper authors. The edas Author class therefore subsumes the cmt Co-author class. They are not equivalent because cmt's Author is a separate, broader sibling/parent concept from Co-author.

Rejected contribution is a class denoting a written paper/contribution that was rejected after review (a document artefact). Reject Rating is a class denoting a rating value used in a review (a rating/code). They belong to completely different categories: one is a document, the other is a rating value. They share the word 'reject' but denote unrelated concepts.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and directions. 'author Of' relates Person to Document (who wrote a paper), while 'presentationed by' relates Document to Speaker (who presents it). They connect different entities (author vs. speaker) and point in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent.

Conference www in ontology Conference is a digital document (a conference website/URL) under Conference document, sibling to Call for paper, Review, etc. Conference building in iasted is a physical place under Building, with children like Delegate and siblings like Conference hotel, Conference airport. These are completely different concepts: one is a web resource, the other is a physical building. No overlap in intended instances.

Poster Paper is a type of academic document (a paper presented as a poster), while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to completely different domains and hierarchies, with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf#writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author (authorship relation), whereas ekaw#presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper being presented (presentation relation). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different semantics; neither subsumes the other.

A `Conference contribution` in the Conference ontology is a document (subclass of Conference document) that encompasses written papers, posters, presentations, and invited talks. B `Individual Presentation` in EKAW is an event (subclass of Event > Scientific Event) where a paper is presented. They overlap (a Regular contribution/Abstract can be presented as an Individual Presentation), but one is a document and the other is a scientific event, so they are not equivalent.

Conference contributor (ontology Conference) is a subclass of Person, denoting a human who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker). Sponsor state (ontology iasted) is a subclass of State, which in iasted is a temporal/phase concept (like Conference state, Presenter state) representing a stage in a workflow. One is a person role, the other is a temporal state; they share no instances and are unrelated.

confOf:Reception is a specific kind of social event (a subclass of Social event), while ekaw:Social Event is the general category whose children include Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. Reception is narrower than Social Event, so it is subsumed_by it.

Talk Event in edas is a subclass of Academic Event representing a presentation/talk session (with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk). Conference days in iasted is a subclass of Time representing temporal periods of the conference (with children like Delegate, One conference day). They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Event vs Time) and denote completely different concepts.

In cmt, ProgramCommittee is a committee (a group body) that has members (Program Committee Members). In edas, ConferenceChair is a specific Person role (an individual who chairs the conference). A committee (group) and an individual chair role are fundamentally different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

Property A relates a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (organizational role to conference component), while property B relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (event to published material/list). They connect entirely different domain and range types and describe different relationships.

Conference participant in ontology Conference is a broad class (parent of Active/Passive conference participant, sibling of Committee member, Reviewer, etc.) denoting anyone who participates in a conference. Session Chair in ekaw is a specific role (a PC Member who chairs a session), making it a narrow subtype of conference participant. Thus Conference_participant subsumes Session_Chair.

A Conference announcement is a public notice about a conference event (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while an Invitation letter is a personal document sent to an individual inviting them to participate. They serve different communicative purposes and target different audiences (public vs. individual), so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

These two datatype properties operate in completely different domains. 'has_a_degree' is about a review preference's degree (an integer rating in the review process), while 'Price' is about a registration fee's monetary price. They have different domains (Review preference vs Registration fee), different meanings, and no overlap in what they relate.

Both are subclasses of Paper under Document, but they partition the paper space differently. In cmt, Paper Full Version is contrasted with Paper Abstract (full text vs. abstract), whereas in ekaw, Conference Paper is one of several venue/type-based paper categories (alongside Workshop Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). A full version of a paper could be any of those venue types, and a conference paper could be either a full version or an abstract. They overlap but are not co-extensive.

OC Chair (Organizing Committee Chair) in EKAW and Program Chair in SIGKDD are distinct committee leadership roles. The OC Chair oversees the Organizing Committee (logistics, local arrangements), while the Program Chair oversees the Program Committee (paper selection, academic content). They are both conference organizer roles under Person, but they denote different responsibilities and are not equivalent.

In iasted, Speaker is a subclass of Delegate (a conference attendee who presents), with children Author and Reviewer. In sigkdd, Organizator is a subclass of Person who organizes the conference, with children General Chair, Program Chair, Committee members, Webmaster. These are distinct roles: a Speaker presents at the conference while an Organizator handles conference organization. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear hierarchy.

hasPhone relates Contact Information to a phone number string, while Name relates Person to a person's name string. They have different domains, different meanings, and no overlap in what they express.

cmt:Administrator is a system administrator who manages conference details, enables virtual meetings, enters review criteria, and accepts papers. confOf:Member_PC is a Program Committee member who reviews papers and has expertise on topics. These are distinct roles: one is an administrative/system-management role, the other is an academic reviewing role. They share no parent-child relationship and their intended instances do not coincide.

These are different concepts: 'early Registration' is a boolean flag indicating whether a participant registered early, while 'Price' is an integer representing the monetary cost of a registration fee. They have different domains (Participant vs Registration fee), different ranges (boolean vs int), and capture entirely different information.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has registered for a conference (a subclass of Conference applicant under Person). B 'Personal History' is a container class for personal publication and review histories. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Conference denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, members, administrators). In the Conference ontology, Important dates is a class representing a collection of key deadlines/dates (abstract submission, camera ready, etc.) associated with a Conference volume. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, 'Conference fees' denotes monetary charges associated with attending a conference (a fee/cost concept), whereas in ekaw 'Conference' denotes a scientific event—one edition of a conference. These are completely different kinds of entities (a financial artefact vs. an event), so they are unrelated.

The two properties are completely different: 'has_the_first_name' captures a person's first name (string), while 'earlyRegistration' is a boolean flag indicating whether a participant registered early. They have different domains, ranges, and intended meanings.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges. In cmt, writePaper relates Author to Paper (an author writes a paper). In edas, relatedToPaper relates Paper Presentation to Accepted Paper (a presentation is associated with a paper). They denote different relations in the conference domain.

Both are subtypes of document artifacts in the conference domain, but they denote different stages: a Paper Abstract is a short summary submitted for review (sibling of Paper Full Version), while a Final manuscript is the completed, camera-ready version submitted after acceptance (sibling of Initial manuscript). They overlap conceptually as conference document artifacts but are not equivalent.

Accepting manuscript is an activity (a process/event of accepting a manuscript for a conference), while Author is a person role. They share no instances and are from entirely different ontological categories (activity vs. person).

Property A links a Conference part to a Topic (categorising content by subject area), while property B links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (indicating events running in parallel). They have different domains, different ranges, and express entirely different relationships in the conference-organisation domain.

Talk Event is a presentation/academic event (e.g., closing talk, welcome talk) in edas, while Platinum Supporter is a top-tier sponsor in sigkdd. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'name' property assigns a name to a Conference or Person, while the Conference 'has a location' property assigns a location to a Conference volume. They relate different domain entities to different kinds of string values (a name vs. a location), so they do not denote the same relation.

Conference www is a digital document (a conference website/URL) under Conference document, while Main office is a physical place under Place. They share no common domain semantics—one is an online resource, the other a physical location.

A Paper in cmt is a scholarly document submitted for review, with children like Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version and properties linking it to authors, reviewers, and decisions. B Tax in iasted is a monetary charge (child of Money, sibling of Fee, Sponsorship, Tip) with subtypes like Departure tax and Value added tax. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a general class covering all papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties for assignment, bidding, decisions, etc.). In edas, Accepted Paper is a specific subclass of Paper whose instances have been accepted (sibling to Rejected Paper, Pending Paper, etc.). Thus cmt:Paper is strictly more general than edas:AcceptedPaper, so the relation is subsumes.

Invited_speaker is a person who gives an invited talk at a conference (subclass of Conference contributor / Person), whereas Sponsor_city is a city that sponsors an event (subclass of City). They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies and denote completely different kinds of entities.
Tutorial is a type of scientific event (an individual presentation), while Memeber registration fee is a monetary fee for registration. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

The ekaw property 'event On List' relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (i.e., the event is listed on a brochure or website). The sigkdd property 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (i.e., the document is presented by a speaker). These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships: one is about an event being listed on a publication/website, the other about a document being presented by a person. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

Property A (is Initiated By) relates a Call (e.g., call for papers) to organizers who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). Property B (is prepared by) relates an Item (e.g., a document or publication) to a Person who prepares it. The domains (Call vs. Item) and the nature of the relationship (initiating a call vs. preparing an item) are different, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. `reviewOfPaper` links a Review to the Paper it reviews, while `presentationed_by` links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. They differ in domain, range, and semantic meaning; there is no overlap or subsumption between them.

In cmt, 'assignedByReviewer' relates an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to review a paper). In iasted, 'write' relates a Person to an Item (e.g., a person writing a paper). These are different relations: one is about reviewer assignment, the other about authorship. The domains and ranges differ, and the intended meaning does not coincide.

The confOf 'reviewes' property relates a PC Member to a Contribution they review, whereas the iasted 'is given to' property relates an Item to a Person who receives it (e.g., an award or certificate). These are different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics; one is about reviewing and the other about giving/receiving.

Location in ekaw denotes a physical or virtual place where an Event is held (domain of 'held In' Event -> Location). Currency in iasted denotes a monetary unit (e.g., USD, EUR) used for registration fees or prices. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference contributor in ontology A denotes any person who contributes a paper or presentation to a conference (subtypes include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author). PC Member in ekaw denotes a member of the Programme Committee, a specific role involving paper review and selection. A contributor is not necessarily a PC Member, and a PC Member is not necessarily a contributor (they review rather than author). The two classes have distinct intended instances with no clear overlap relationship.

Research Topic (ekaw) denotes a subject area covered by events and papers, while Money (iasted) denotes a monetary amount with subtypes like Fee, Sponsorship, Tax, and Tip. These are entirely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

ekaw:Document is a broad top-level class covering any conference document (abstracts, papers, reviews, flyers, brochures, web sites). iasted:Form is a narrow subclass of iasted:Document specifically for structured forms (author info form, hotel registration form, registration form). The two classes do not share instances: a Form is a kind of administrative template/form, whereas ekaw:Document denotes scholarly and promotional artefacts. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other because they belong to independent hierarchies with different roots.

Antennas Topic is a specific subject domain (a Topic) for conference papers, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a subtype) in the Item hierarchy. They share no semantic overlap despite both being leaf-level classes in their respective ontologies.

Conference contributor (Person > Conference contributor) is a broad superclass covering all persons who contribute to a conference (authors, invited speakers, active participants). One day presenter (Delegate > One day presenter) is a specific kind of delegate who presents for one day. A one-day presenter is a contributor, but the two classes are at very different levels of generality and live in unrelated taxonomy branches (Person vs. Place > Building > Delegate). They are not equivalent; the broad contributor class and the narrow one-day-presenter delegate class do not coincide in intended instances.

The cmt 'assigned To' property assigns a Paper to a Reviewer for review purposes. The ekaw 'updated Version Of' property links a Document to a prior version of that Document. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics with no overlap.

PaperFullVersion is a full conference paper document (a written contribution), while MedicineTopic is a subject-matter topic classifying papers by research area. They belong to completely different hierarchies (Document vs. Topic) and denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Student is a person who is a participant in a conference (subclass of Person > Participant), while sigkdd:Best_Student_Paper_Award is an award given for a paper. They denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in instances.

These properties are completely different: hasFirstName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's first name), while go_through is an object property from Item to Activity (an item going through some activity). They share no domain, range, or meaning.

The two properties relate Conference to completely different entities: `hasConferenceMember` links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person participating in the conference), while `hasCountry` links a Conference to a Country (a geographical location). These are semantically unrelated relations despite sharing the same domain (Conference).

confOf Reception is a specific social event (a leaf class under Social event), whereas iasted Conference activity is a broad category encompassing all conference activities including receptions, coffee breaks, lectures, presentations, etc. Reception is thus a specific kind of Conference activity, making Reception subsumed_by Conference_activity.

These properties are completely different. setMaxPapers is an object property from Administrator to Program Committee Member, likely setting the maximum number of papers a PC member can handle. maxChoice is a datatype property from Social/Working events to positiveInteger, likely indicating the maximum number of choices for an event. Different domains, ranges, property types, and meanings.

The confOf 'follows' property relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (e.g., one event following another), while the sigkdd 'submit' property relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

confOf Participant denotes conference attendees (with subclasses Member, Regular, Student and an early-registration property), whereas sigkdd Organizator denotes people who organize the conference (with subclasses General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc.). They are disjoint roles under Person, not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.
Committee member is a person who serves on a committee, while Taxi is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different domains (people vs. vehicles) with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are social events associated with a conference, but an Excursion is a trip or outing (e.g., sightseeing), whereas a Conference Banquet is a formal meal/gathering. They are sibling-level concepts under Social Event rather than the same concept.

A Tutorial is a type of scientific event/session focused on teaching a topic, typically longer and with pedagogical intent. A PowerPoint presentation is a medium/format of presentation delivery. They are orthogonal: a tutorial could use a PowerPoint presentation, but the concepts do not overlap as equivalent or subsuming one another.

In ekaw, Abstract is a document type (a written summary of a paper/talk), subclass of Document, with siblings like Paper, Review, Flyer. In sigkdd, Deadline is a temporal entity representing a due date, with children like Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Paper Submission, and properties like Date (-> dateTime). These are completely different concepts: a document artefact vs. a temporal deadline. No subsumption or overlap.

Industrial Paper is a type of academic document (a paper submitted to an industrial track), while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference proceedings is a specific kind of published, edited volume (with ISBN, publisher, volume number) that collects the papers of a conference. Document in sigkdd is a broad super-class whose children include Abstract, Paper, and Review. A proceedings is an artefact that contains documents rather than being a direct sibling of Paper/Abstract/Review, so it is narrower than Document; the two are not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, representing the end date/time of a conference. The labels 'end Date' and 'End of conference' are synonymous in this context, and the structural signatures match exactly.

These properties operate in different directions and relate different entity types. In cmt, 'has Been Assigned' goes from Reviewer to Paper, indicating which paper a reviewer is assigned to review. In Conference, 'has_been_assigned_a_review_reference' goes from Submitted contribution/Topic to Review preference, indicating a preference assignment for reviewing a contribution. The domains (Reviewer vs. Submitted contribution/Topic), ranges (Paper vs. Review preference), and the nature of the relationship are fundamentally different.

Call for participation is a conference document inviting people to participate in a conference, while Conference Proceedings is a multi-author volume containing accepted papers. They are completely different types of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

An Invitation letter is a document sent to invite someone (e.g., a speaker or participant) to a conference, whereas a Paper is a scholarly submission authored and submitted to the conference. Despite sharing the parent Document, their intended instances are disjoint: an invitation letter is not a paper and vice versa.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while the Conference 'has an ISBN' property denotes the ISBN of Conference proceedings. They relate different kinds of entities and express different attributes, so they are unrelated.

These properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges. 'has_an_expertise' is a datatype property from Review expertise (likely capturing a reviewer's expertise level or topic), while 'hasRating' is an object property from Active Paper to Review Rating (assigning a rating value to a paper). They connect different entities in different directions with different types, so they are unrelated.

In the iasted ontology, 'Session chair' is a subclass of Delegate (a person who chairs a session), while in sigkdd, 'Conference hall' is a subclass of Place (a physical venue). These denote completely different categories of entities—a person versus a physical location—so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'Camera Ready event' is an administrative event concerning the camera-ready paper submission phase, while edas's 'Organizational Meeting' is an academic event like a paper presentation or workshop. They denote different kinds of conference activities with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. cmt:hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (the acceptance/rejection outcome of that paper), while iasted:obtain links a Person to an Item (a person obtaining some item). The domains (Paper vs Person) and ranges (Decision vs Item) do not coincide, and the intended relations are semantically distinct.

The cmt `date` property captures when a conference takes place (a calendar date), while the sigkdd `City_of_conference` property captures where a conference takes place (a city name). They describe completely different attributes of a conference, so they are unrelated.

Conference Venue Place in edas is a physical location where a conference is held (a Place). Student non speaker in iasted is a type of person/delegate attending the conference. Despite the unusual iasted path placing it under Building > Conference building, the class hierarchy (Non speaker > Student non speaker, sibling Worker non speaker) and label indicate it is a person role, not a venue. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf Administrator is a general administrative role (sibling to Author, Participant, Volunteer, etc.), while ekaw PC Chair is specifically the chair of the Programme Committee (a sub-role of PC Member and Conference Participant). An Administrator handles logistics and is not necessarily a PC Member or participant, and a PC Chair is not an Administrator. Their intended instances do not coincide.

Social program is a conference activity/event (e.g., dinner banquet, cocktail reception) in the iasted ontology, while Speaker is a person who gives presentations in the sigkdd ontology. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad superclass encompassing Authors, Reviewers, Associated/Conference Chairs, and Program Committee Members—any person who is a member of the conference. In the Conference ontology, Chair is a specific role within a committee (a committee chair), a sibling of Co-chair. The cmt Conference Member is far more general and not specifically about committee chairing, while the Conference Chair is a narrow committee-leadership role. They do not share the same intended instances, and neither subsumes the other in a way that a reference alignment would record as equivalent.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'reject Paper' (cmt) has domain Administrator and range Paper, representing the act of an administrator rejecting a paper. 'related To Event' (edas) has domain Accepted Paper and range Paper Presentation, representing a relationship between an accepted paper and its presentation event. They share no semantic overlap.

Radio Communications Topic is a subject-area topic (a research domain like antennas, cryptography, mobile computing) under Topic in the EDAS ontology. Program Committee is an organizational committee responsible for reviewing papers, under Committee in the SIGKDD ontology. These denote completely different concepts: a research topic vs. an organizational body. No alignment relationship exists.

In EDAS, 'Paper Presentation' is a subclass of Conference Event / Academic Event, i.e., a scheduled session where a paper is presented. In EKAW, 'Abstract' is a subclass of Document, i.e., a written summary of a talk or paper. One is an event/activity, the other is a document artefact; they denote completely different kinds of entities despite both being connected to paper presentations.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. virtualMeetingEnabledBy relates a Conference to an Administrator (who enables virtual meetings). parallel_with relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (events running in parallel). They share no semantic overlap.

Conference announcement is a document type (e.g., a call for papers or participation notice), while Computer Networks Applications Topic is a subject classification under the Topic hierarchy. They belong to completely different parts of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a type of conference gathering), while iasted:Session_chair is a person/role (a delegate who chairs a session). They are completely different categories: one is an event, the other is a person role.

The cmt property 'addProgramCommitteeMember' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (the act of adding a member to a PC). The iasted property 'occupy' relates a Person to a Building, City, or State (a person occupying a location). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

Talk Event is a kind of academic conference event (e.g., closing talk, welcome talk) in the edas ontology, while Transport vehicle is a physical item like a car, taxi, or shuttle bus in the iasted ontology. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length submission document in the CMT ontology (Document > Paper > Paper Full Version), whereas ComputerNetworksSensorTopic is a subject taxonomy node under Topic in the EDAS ontology. They denote completely different kinds of entities—a document artefact versus a conference topic—so they are unrelated.

Tax (Money > Tax) denotes a compulsory levy imposed by a government, with children like Departure tax and Value added tax. Sponzor fee (Fee > Sponzor fee) is a sponsorship-related charge paid to an organization, a sibling of Registration fee. These are categorically different financial concepts: a tax is a government levy, while a sponsorship fee is an organizational charge. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person (a string label), while the sigkdd 'End of conference' property denotes the date/time when a conference ends. They have completely different meanings, domains, and ranges, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a poster presented at a conference. In Conference, Poster is a kind of Conference contribution (sibling of Presentation, Regular contribution, Written contribution). In ekaw, Poster Paper is a kind of Paper (sibling of Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). Despite the slight terminological difference (Poster vs Poster Paper), both refer to the same conference artefact/contribution type: a poster submission. The structural contexts are compatible (contribution/paper document hierarchies), and no evidence suggests a different intended meaning.

In EDAS, 'hasRelatedPaper' connects an Author to a Paper they have authored or contributed to. In EKAW, 'references' is a relation between papers (one paper citing another). These are fundamentally different relations: one links a person to their work, the other links a document to another document it cites. They do not share the same domain/range types or the same semantic meaning.

In cmt, 'Author Not Reviewer' is a specific role: a person who authored a paper but is not assigned as a reviewer. In confOf, 'Scholar' denotes a registration/price category (a student or academic scholar attending the conference), unrelated to authorship or reviewing roles. The two classes have disjoint intended instances and no subsumption relationship.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings. `has Submission Instructions` (domain: Call) captures submission guidelines for a conference call, while `Name` (domain: Person) holds a person's name. They relate different kinds of entities and denote entirely different concepts.

Signal Processing Topic is a subject-area classification under Topic in the edas ontology, while Organizing Committee is a committee type responsible for conference organization in sigkdd. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Volunteer in confOf denotes a person who performs volunteer duties at the conference (a helper/staff role), whereas Attendee in edas denotes a person who attends the conference. An attendee is not necessarily a volunteer, and a volunteer is not necessarily an attendee; the two concepts have distinct intended extensions and neither subsumes the other.

In the iasted ontology, 'Introduction' is a conference activity/event (e.g., an introductory session such as 'Introduction of speaker'), sitting alongside Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, etc. In the sigkdd ontology, 'Organizator' is a person role (a kind of Person) with subclasses like General Chair, Program Chair, etc. One denotes a scheduled activity, the other a person/role; they share no intended instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both classes denote the same concept: a human person involved in the conference domain. They share the same label and are top-level classes covering conference participants, authors, committee members, and other roles. Their children (Author/Paper Author, Participant/Conference Participant, Member PC/Possible Reviewer, etc.) are closely parallel, and the associated properties (contact details, authorship, organisation) all apply to people in the conference setting. No evidence suggests a different intended meaning.

A is a document/form (a hotel registration form) under Item > Document > Form, while B is a physical place (a hotel) under Place. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'startReviewerBidding' (Administrator -> Conference) is an action property where an administrator initiates reviewer bidding for a conference. 'need' (Person -> Item) relates a person to an item they need. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

The property 'written By' in ekaw relates a Document to a Person (its author), while 'presentationed by' in sigkdd relates a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents it). Authorship and presentation are distinct relationships in the conference domain; a paper's author is not necessarily its presenter. The ranges differ (Person vs Speaker) and the semantics are different, so these properties are unrelated.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges. 'has_the_first_name' applies to Person and returns a string (a person's first name), while 'has_amount_of' applies to Money and returns an int (a monetary amount). They denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. confOf:has_short_title applies to Social event and Working event, denoting a short title for those events. edas:hasName applies to Conference and denotes the conference's full name. The domains do not overlap (Conference is not a Social event or Working event in confOf), and the semantics differ (short title vs. full name). They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'reviewOfPaper' in ekaw relates a Review to a Paper (a reviewer or review process associated with a paper). The property 'give' in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or distributing an item). These properties have different domains (Review vs. Person) and different ranges (Paper vs. Activity/Item), and they denote completely different relations in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Document' and serve as the top-level document concept in their respective ontologies. They share key child classes Paper and Review, and both are linked to Person via authorship/conflict-of-interest properties. The broader set of children in ekaw (Abstract, Flyer, etc.) reflects a more detailed subdivision but does not change the intended extension of the Document class itself; both denote the same general category of conference-related documents.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Important dates (a temporal/administrative metadata relation), while property B links an Administrative event to another Administrative event that runs in parallel (a scheduling relation between events). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings with no overlap.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, 'hasConferenceMember' links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person participating in the conference). In edas, 'hasTopic' links a Conference or Paper to a Topic (a subject area). The domains partially overlap (Conference) but the ranges are entirely disjoint (Conference Member vs Topic), and the intended semantics are unrelated.

The two properties operate in different domains and ranges. In edas, 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who is the sponsor). In iasted, 'is paid by' links Money to a Person (who pays). The domain and range types do not coincide, and the relations describe different kinds of transactions in the conference domain.

Pending Paper in EDAS classifies a paper by its review status (pending decision), while Industrial Paper in EKAW classifies a paper by its track/category (industrial vs. academic). These are orthogonal classification dimensions with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair in cmt is a person role (a kind of Chairman involved in conference organisation), whereas Conference in confOf is an event type (a kind of Working event with siblings Tutorial and Workshop). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

confOf Reception is a social event (e.g., a reception/banquet during a conference), whereas iasted Publication is a published item such as a book or CD proceeding. These denote completely different kinds of things in the conference domain.

Talk Event in edas is a subclass of Academic Event (a conference event/activity such as a closing talk or welcome talk), while Proceedings in ekaw is a subclass of Multi author Volume under Document (a published collection of papers). One denotes a scheduled event, the other a document artefact; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf:Author denotes a person who writes a contribution (paper), whereas ekaw:Possible_Reviewer denotes a person who may be assigned to review a paper. In ekaw, the sibling 'Paper Author' is the class for authors, so Possible_Reviewer is a distinct role. The two classes do not share intended instances: an author is not necessarily a reviewer and vice versa.

Conference Paper in ekaw is a written document (subclass of Paper > Document), while Conference hall in iasted is a physical location (subclass of Place). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Reviewed contribution is a written document (paper) that has been reviewed, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution. Activity is a temporal event/action (with children like Conference activity, Activity before/after conference). A document is not an activity; these denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

A Published Paper is a document (a paper that has been published), while Best Applications Paper Award is an award given for a paper. They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (Document hierarchy vs Award hierarchy) and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

In ekaw, Conference is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while in iasted, Conference state is a state (a phase or status), sibling to Presenter state and Sponsor state. These are completely different concepts: one denotes a conference event, the other a state or phase, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person (a person who uses the conference management system). In iasted, Person is the top-level class for people involved in the conference (delegates, sponsors). Thus cmt:User is narrower than iasted:Person, and is subsumed by it rather than equivalent.

The cmt 'date' property maps a Conference to a date (a temporal value), while the edas 'hasName' property maps a Conference to a string representing its full name. These are completely different attributes of a conference with no overlap in meaning.

confOf:Topic is a general conference topic class, used for papers, PC expertise, and events. edas:PerformanceTopic is a specific subclass of edas:Topic covering performance-related subjects, with siblings like AntennasTopic, CADTopic, etc. Thus confOf:Topic is strictly more general than edas:PerformanceTopic, so confOf:Topic is subsumed_by edas:Topic but not equivalent to the narrower PerformanceTopic.

Proceedings Publisher is an organization that publishes conference proceedings, while Organizing Committee member is a person who serves on the organizing committee. They belong to disjoint branches (Organization vs Person) and denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Conference is the main academic conference event itself (a working event sibling of Workshop and Tutorial). iasted:Welcome_address is a specific social/administrative activity within a conference (sibling of Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Registration). They denote completely different concepts at different levels of granularity with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations. 'location Of' (ekaw) relates a Location to the Event held there, whereas 'speak in' (iasted) relates a Person to the Place/Time where they speak. They share no common relational semantics.

Both classes are subclasses of Person and represent the same role in the conference domain: a person who reviews papers. Both ontologies place Reviewer under Person, and both associate Reviewer with review-related properties (review expertise/preferences in Conference, review history and reviewing papers in edas). The sibling terms differ (Conference has more specialized committee roles, edas has Attendee, Author, etc.), but the intended instances of Reviewer coincide across both ontologies.

Reviewer is a person who reviews papers (subordinate of Conference Member in cmt, with review/bid/assignment properties). Speaker is a person who gives a presentation (child of Person in sigkdd, with presentation properties). These are distinct conference roles with no overlap in intended instances.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and Person/TPC Member per the given hierarchy), representing a type of conference event. In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Webmaster' is a subclass of Organizator under Person, representing a person who manages the web. These are completely different concepts: one is a conference event type, the other is a human role. No equivalence or subsumption relationship exists.

In confOf, Conference is a type of event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), representing the conference gathering itself. In sigkdd, Organizing_Committee is a committee (subclass of Committee, sibling of Program Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee), representing the group of people who organize the conference. These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a committee of people. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Property 'has a name' in Conference applies to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic, denoting the name of organizational or topical entities. Property 'has title' in confOf applies to Social event and Working event, denoting the title of events. The domains are disjoint (organizational entities vs. events), and 'name' vs. 'title' carry different semantics. These are different properties with no overlap in intended use.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events to each other (indicating temporal concurrency between events), while the ekaw 'held In' property relates an Event to a Location (indicating where an event takes place). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantic meanings: one is about temporal scheduling between events, the other about spatial location of an event.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Document > Paper, representing the abstract of a conference paper. Computer Networks Enterprise Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic > Computer Networks Topic, representing a subject area for paper classification. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. `hasDecision` links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while `notification_until` links an Author to a Deadline for author notifications. They connect different entity types and represent different relationships in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a broad superclass covering all persons who contribute to a conference (authors, invited speakers, active participants). Author book proceedings included in ontology B is a very specific subclass of Author denoting authors whose work appears in book-format proceedings. The former is strictly more general than the latter.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a short summary of a paper) in the cmt ontology's Document hierarchy, while Signal Processing Topic is a subject-area topic in the edas ontology's Topic hierarchy. They belong to completely different conceptual categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference participant in ontology Conference is a broad class covering all people who participate in a conference (including active participants like speakers and passive participants like attendees). Conference Hiker in iasted is a specific subclass of Delegate, sibling to Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc., denoting a particular kind of delegate. Thus Conference participant is strictly more general than Conference Hiker.

External Reviewer is a person assigned to review a paper on behalf of another Reviewer, but is not themselves a Reviewer. Author is a Speaker who authors a publication. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one reviews papers, the other writes papers. They are siblings in iasted (Reviewer vs Author), confirming they are disjoint role classes. No subsumption holds between them.

confOf's 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event representing the phase when review outcomes are made available to authors. ekaw's 'Conference' is a scientific event representing one edition of a conference. They occupy different branches of their respective hierarchies and denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (paper), whereas the sigkdd 'searched by' property links a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. They relate completely different kinds of entities and describe different relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization, denoting a corporate entity (e.g., a sponsoring or participating company). sigkdd:Author_of_paper is a subclass of Person > Speaker > Author, denoting a person who authored a paper. One is an organization, the other is a person; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

A Conference in confOf is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas a Session room in iasted is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). These denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

confOf Paper is a general contribution type (sibling to Poster and Short paper), whereas ekaw Workshop Paper is a specific subtype of Paper restricted to workshop papers. ekaw's Paper class is the broader counterpart; confOf Paper is subsumed by ekaw Paper, not equivalent to the narrower Workshop Paper.

confOf:Workshop is a specific kind of working event (a smaller meeting within a conference), while ekaw:Conference is an entire conference edition. They are disjoint event types at different levels of granularity; Workshop is even a sibling of Conference in ekaw, so they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

hasCity is a datatype property from Contact Information to string (a city name), while obtain is an object property from Person to Item (a person obtaining an item). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

confOf:follows relates two Administrative events (e.g., one event following another in a sequence), whereas ekaw:inverse_of_partOf_7 is the inverse of a part-of relation, linking an Event to its container/whole. These are structurally and semantically different relations: a temporal/sequential 'follows' vs. a mereological 'has-part'. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same way, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Submission event is a temporal/administrative event (a deadline or phase when contributions are submitted), sitting under Event > Administrative event alongside Registration, Reviewing, and Camera Ready events. iasted:Transparency is a physical document type (e.g., an acetate slide) under Item > Document, with siblings like Form, Invitation letter, and Review. One is an event/occurrence, the other is a document/artefact; they share no instances and are not related.

Regular author in Conference ontology is a broad class covering any author of a conference contribution (with subtypes for first author and co-author). Tutorial speaker in iasted is a specific kind of author who presents a tutorial. A tutorial speaker may be an author, but the two classes do not overlap in intended instances: many regular authors are not tutorial speakers, and tutorial speakers are characterized by their tutorial presentation role rather than by authorship of a paper. The hierarchies and siblings confirm these are distinct concepts with no clear subsumption relationship.

Tutorial is a conference session/event part (sibling of Track and Workshop), while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment (sibling of Computer, LCD projector). They denote completely different things in the conference domain with no overlap.

In the iasted ontology, Lecturer is a subclass of Author (path: ... > Author > Lecturer), making it a more specific concept. The sigkdd Author class is a general author concept (Person > Speaker > Author) with children like 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student'. Since Lecturer is a specialization of Author in iasted, and sigkdd's Author represents the general author concept, Lecturer is subsumed by sigkdd's Author.

Registation deadline is the deadline for registering for the conference, while Deadline Abstract Submission is the deadline for submitting an abstract. These are distinct temporal milestones in the conference organization process with different purposes.

Contribution co-author is a specific author role for a written contribution, whereas Presenter is a conference participant role involving presenting at a session. A co-author need not attend or present, and a presenter need not be a co-author of a paper.

Both are object properties linking a written document/artefact to the person who authored/signed it. In the conference domain, a Contribution (confOf) corresponds to an Item (iasted), and an Author is a Person. 'written By' and 'is signed by' both express the authorship relation from the document to its author, so they are equivalent.

These classes denote entirely different concepts. In edas, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and Person/TPC Member per the hierarchy), representing a type of conference or conference-related role. In iasted, 'Conference state' is a subclass of State, representing a state or status of a conference (e.g., planned, ongoing, completed). They share no common meaning despite both containing the word 'Conference'.

Both Administrator (cmt) and Organizer (Conference) are involved in conference management, but they are not equivalent. The cmt Administrator has specific system-level powers (accepting papers, assigning reviewers, entering review criteria, enabling virtual meetings) that go beyond typical organizing duties, while an Organizer in the Conference ontology typically handles logistical aspects. They overlap in being conference-management roles but denote different sets of responsibilities and instances.

Workshop in the Conference ontology is an academic conference part (a session with talks/papers, sibling of Track and Tutorial). FreeTimeBreak in edas is a non-academic break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The property hasMenu in edas relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (what food items are available at a meal). The property give in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item (what a person presents or gives). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no overlap in meaning.

Conference www is a web document/resource identified by a URL, while University is an academic institution/organisation. They denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Welcome Talk in edas is a specific type of talk event (a talk given to welcome participants), while Introduction in iasted is a broader conference activity that includes introducing speakers. They overlap in the conference welcome/introduction domain but are not equivalent: Welcome Talk is a talk, whereas Introduction encompasses speaker introductions and similar activities. A related relation is most appropriate.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'reviewer Bidding Started By' (cmt) relates a Conference to an Administrator who initiates the reviewer bidding process. 'write' (iasted) relates a Person to an Item they author. There is no semantic overlap between initiating a bidding phase and authoring/writing an item.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions. In edas, 'hasRating' links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper has a rating assigned during review). In sigkdd, 'submit' links an Author to a Paper (an author submits a paper). They have different domains (Active Paper vs. Author), different ranges (Review Rating vs. Paper), and represent different relationships in the conference domain.

In Conference, 'Contribution 1th author' is a specialized subclass of 'Regular author' that denotes the first author of a contribution, whereas in edas, 'Author' is the general class of all authors (a subclass of Person). The edas Author class is more general, encompassing any author, not just first authors. Thus, Contribution 1th author is subsumed by Author.

A's paperID is a datatype property from Paper to unsignedLong (an identifier). B's submit is an object property from Author to Paper (a submission relation). Different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

The confOf 'writes' property relates an Author to a Contribution they author, while the ekaw 'reviewOfPaper' property relates a Review to the Paper it reviews. These are distinct relations with different domains (Author vs Review) and different intended semantics (authorship vs reviewing), so they are unrelated.

Committee in Conference denotes a group of people organizing or reviewing for a conference (e.g., Program committee, Organizing committee), with members, chairs, and co-chairs. Organization in edas denotes an institutional entity (Academia, Government, Industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. These are structurally and semantically different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains and meanings. cmt:maxPapers applies to Program Committee Members and likely represents a paper assignment limit for reviewing. confOf:maxChoice applies to Social events and Working events and represents some choice/option count for events. They share no conceptual overlap in the conference domain.

Conference Chair is an administrative/leadership role responsible for overseeing the conference, while Tutorial speaker is a presenter who gives a tutorial talk. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain: one is a governance role, the other is a presenter role. They share no meaningful overlap in their intended instances.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for human individuals in their respective conference ontologies. EKAW's Person has subclasses like Conference Participant, Paper Author, and Student, while IASTED's Person has subclasses like Delegate and Sponsor. These are complementary specializations of the same universal concept of a person involved in conference activities. The properties in both ontologies consistently treat Person as the human agent who performs actions (giving, writing, organizing) or receives items/payments. The intended instances coincide: any human participant, author, sponsor, or staff member in a conference setting.

The property 'write' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they author, while 'holded by' in sigkdd relates a Conference to the organization (ACM SIGKDD) that holds it. They connect completely different kinds of entities and express different relations (authorship vs. organizational holding), so they are unrelated.

A Conference Banquet is a social event (a gathering/activity), while a Conference hotel is a building/place where conference attendees stay. They are completely different kinds of entities despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

These properties relate completely different entities in different directions. `attendee At` links a Person to a Conference Event they attend, while `presentationed by` links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Person vs Document), ranges (Conference Event vs Speaker), and overall semantics (attendance vs authorship/presentation) are all different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Proceedings in ekaw is a document (a multi-author volume of conference papers), while Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes a conference. These are completely different categories (document vs. person) with no overlap in intended instances.

In EDAS, 'Call' denotes a call for papers/manuscripts/reviews (a solicitation artifact with submission deadlines and instructions, initiated by organizers). In EKAW, 'Event' denotes a scientific or social event (something held in a location, organized by persons/organizations, part of other events). A call for papers is not an event; an event is not a call. They share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relation.

Both are subclasses of Place in the conference domain, but a Meeting Room Place is a room where meetings/sessions are held, while a Conference hall is a larger venue. They overlap in denoting places where conference events occur, but neither clearly subsumes the other and their intended instances do not fully coincide.

The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (the act of authoring a paper). The ekaw 'paperPresentedAs' property links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (the act/event of presenting it at a conference). These are fundamentally different relations: writing a paper versus presenting it. They connect different domain and range types and do not overlap in meaning.

A 'Submission event' in confOf is an event representing the act of submitting contributions, while 'Best Paper Awards Committee' in sigkdd is a committee responsible for selecting best paper awards. These are entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In the Conference ontology, Track is a conference part (like Tutorial and Workshop) that groups sessions or papers within a conference volume. In edas, Programme is a Document (sibling of Paper, Review, Slide Set) associated with a Conference Event via belongsToEvent/hasProgramme. One denotes a structural subdivision of a conference; the other denotes a physical document artefact. They share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

The two properties operate on different domains (Sponsorship vs Registration fee) and capture different information: hasCostCurrency records the currency of a sponsorship cost (range string), while Price records the numeric price of a registration fee (range int). They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Coctail reception is a social activity/event during a conference, while Conference hall is a physical place/location. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Activity vs Place) and denote completely different concepts.

These are different properties with different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'has a volume' (domain: Conference proceedings, range: int) denotes the volume number of a proceedings publication. 'has Name' (domain: Conference, range: string, comment: 'Conference Full Name') denotes the full name of a conference. They relate different entities to different value types and have no semantic overlap.

confOf's Event is a broad top-level class covering Administrative, Social, and Working events. edas's SocialEvent is a specific subclass of Non Academic Event with children like Excursion and Reception. confOf:Event subsumes edas:SocialEvent because SocialEvent is a kind of Event, but they are not equivalent since confOf:Event includes many non-social event types.

confOf Company is a specific kind of organization (a for-profit corporate entity), positioned as a sibling of University under Organization. ekaw Organisation is a broad class covering academic institutions, organising agencies, proceedings publishers, etc. Company is a specific type of organisation, so Company is subsumed by Organisation, but they are not equivalent since Organisation includes many entities that are not companies.

Conference announcement is a document (child of Conference document) that communicates information about a conference, while Coffee break is an activity (child of Conference activity) that occurs during a conference. They belong to completely different ontological categories (document vs. activity) and share no instances.

confOf's 'Short paper' is a type of contribution (a paper format/type, sibling of Paper and Poster), while ekaw's 'Rejected Paper' is a paper that has gone through review and been rejected (sibling of Accepted Paper). They denote completely different concepts: one is a format/type of submission, the other is a review outcome status. Their intended instances do not coincide.

Social Event in edas is a non-academic conference event (e.g., Excursion, Reception), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who presents a document. They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference, while Workshop is an academic event. These are completely different concepts with no overlap.

Conference participant in ontology Conference is a general class for any person participating in a conference, with children Active/Passive conference participant. Early Registered Participant in ekaw is a specific kind of participant who registered early. The former is strictly more general than the latter, so subsumes is the correct relation.

confOf:Company is an organization (e.g., a corporate entity involved in conference organization), while edas:SecurityTopic is a subject matter topic for conference papers. They share no semantic overlap despite both being subclasses of different root concepts.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In cmt, hasBid links a Paper to a Bid (a reviewer's bid to review that paper). In sigkdd, submit links an Author to a Paper (the act of an author submitting a paper). They have different domains (Paper vs Author) and different ranges (Bid vs Paper), and they model entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

These properties are completely different in domain, range, and meaning. 'has short title' is a datatype property from Social event/Working event to a string (a short textual title). 'lists Event' is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event (listing events in a publication/website). They share no semantic overlap.

Committee member (Conference ontology) denotes a person serving on a committee, with children Chair and Co-chair and a membership relation to Committee. Speaker (iasted) denotes a delegate who presents at a conference, with children Author and Reviewer. These are distinct roles: a committee member need not present, and a speaker need not be on any committee. Their hierarchies, siblings, and properties confirm no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, 'Conference announcement' is a kind of conference document such as a call for papers or program announcement—a notification or informational artefact. In ontology B, 'Conference Paper' is an actual academic paper submitted or published at a conference. One is an announcement document, the other is a scholarly paper; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the entity that publishes the proceedings), while 'prepare' links a Person to an Item (something the person prepares). The domains (Conference proceedings vs Person) and ranges (Publisher vs Item) do not overlap, and the relations denote different roles (publishing vs preparing). They are unrelated.

Active Paper in edas is a specific state of a paper in the review/decision workflow (a sibling of Accepted, Rejected, Pending, etc.), while Document in iasted is a broad category of conference items including forms, invitation letters, reviews, submissions, etc. These are at very different levels of abstraction and serve different purposes; an Active Paper is not a kind of Document in the iasted sense, nor vice versa.

Entity A is an administrative event where participants register (an occurrence/activity), while entity B is a temporal deadline by which acceptance notifications must be issued. They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs. Time) and denote fundamentally different concepts: one is an event, the other is a date/deadline.

Conference Venue Place in edas denotes a place where a conference is held (e.g., a building or complex hosting conference events), while Presenter university in iasted denotes the university affiliation of a presenter. These are distinct concepts: one is a venue for the conference itself, the other is the academic institution a presenter belongs to. They share only the generic Place ancestor and have no meaningful overlap in intended instances.
Paper is a document presented at a conference, while Credit card is a payment instrument. They share no domain overlap.

The iasted property 'is writen by' relates an Item to a Person (authorship), while the sigkdd property 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation delivery). These are distinct relations: one concerns who wrote the document, the other concerns who presented it. They are not equivalent.

Property A relates Important dates to a date (datatype property), while property B relates Event to Location (object property). They connect completely different domain/range pairs and describe unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference, but cmt:date denotes a general conference date (likely the start date or a single date), while edas:endDate specifically denotes the conference end date and time. They overlap in being conference-related dates but are not equivalent; a reference alignment would treat them as related rather than the same relation.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'hasConflictOfInterest' relates a Person to a Document they have a conflict with, while 'is_paid_for' relates Money to an Activity or Item it pays for. There is no overlap in intended semantics.

Conference Member in cmt is a person who is a member of a conference (parent: Person, children: Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.). Academic Event in edas is an event (parent: Conference Event, children: Workshop, Talk Event, Paper Presentation). One is a person role, the other is an event type; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Paper Abstract is a document artifact (a short version of a paper) in cmt, while Microelectronics Topic is a subject-area classification in edas. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Personal Publication History in edas is a history/record of a person's publications, sitting under Personal History alongside Personal Review History. Review in iasted is a document type (child of Document, sibling of Submission, Form, etc.). One is a history/record object about a person's publications; the other is a review document itself. They denote completely different concepts.

Submitted contribution in Conference is a written academic paper submitted for review, while Form in iasted is an administrative document type (e.g., registration form, hotel form). They occupy completely different positions in their respective hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

In cmt, Review is a document containing the actual review content written by a reviewer about a paper. In edas, ReviewForm is a template/structure used to collect review input, not the review itself. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain: one is the filled-out artefact, the other is the blank form template.
Call For Papers is a document/event announcing a paper solicitation, while Reviewer is a person who reviews submissions. They share no instances and are completely different domain concepts.

The property 'held In' in ekaw relates an Event to the Location where it takes place. The property 'write' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they author. These have completely different domains (Event vs Person) and ranges (Location vs Item), and express entirely different relations in the conference domain.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Switching Topic' is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area within computer networks. In EKAW, 'Contributed Talk' is a subclass of Individual Presentation representing a type of event/presentation at a conference. They share no instances and have no hierarchical relationship.

In cmt, Review is a specific document written by a Reviewer about a Paper, a child of Document. In confOf, Contribution is a general class of submitted items (Paper, Poster, Short paper) written by an Author. A Review is not a Contribution; it is an assessment of a contribution. Their instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (an event with a two-level structure). In iasted, 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker > Delegate (a person who writes a paper). Despite the shared 'Conference' context, one is an event type and the other is a person role, so they are unrelated.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: 'has an email' captures a person's email address, while 'has Biography' captures a biographical text. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

The cmt 'adjust Bid' property relates a Reviewer to a Bid (a reviewer adjusting their bidding on papers), while the confOf 'writes' property relates an Author to a Contribution (an author writing a paper). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain, with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference Session in ekaw is a type of event/session where presentations occur. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Entity A is a person (an early paid applicant) under the Person hierarchy, while entity B is a monetary fee (a nonauthor registration fee) under the Money > Fee hierarchy. One denotes a human participant, the other a cost amount; they are completely different kinds of things.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a kind of chairman), while Conference airport is a physical place/building. They belong to completely different hierarchies and domains with no overlap.

Rejection is a decision outcome for a submitted paper in the conference review process, while Taxi is a transportation vehicle. These classes denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

`has Menu` relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (a specific catering artifact), while `has Event` relates an Event to a sub/constituent Event. They connect different kinds of things and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime, but their domains differ: A's domain is Activity (a broad class covering all conference activities), while B's domain is Deadline (a specific kind of activity). 'is dated on' applies to any Activity, whereas 'Date' applies specifically to Deadlines. Thus A is subsumed_by B in terms of domain specificity — A is the more general property that could apply to deadlines among other activities, while B is restricted to deadlines only.

confOf's Event is a broad class encompassing Administrative events, Social events, and Working events, covering any scheduled activity. ekaw's Scientific Event is a specific subtype of ekaw's Event, restricted to academic/scientific gatherings like conferences, workshops, sessions, and tracks. Since every Scientific Event is an Event but not every Event (e.g., administrative or social) is a scientific one, confOf Event subsumes ekaw Scientific Event, i.e., Scientific_Event is subsumed_by Event.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, sitting under Person > Conference Member. Registration fee in sigkdd is a monetary fee for conference registration, sitting under Fee. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are named 'Document' and serve as top-level containers for various conference-related written materials. EKAW's Document includes Abstract, Paper, Review, Flyer, Programme Brochure, Web Site, and Multi-author Volume, while IASTED's Document includes Submission, Review, Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, Record of attendance, Transparency, etc. Both represent the general concept of a conference document/artifact. The children differ due to ontology scope but the intended extension (conference-related documents) coincides. The IASTED path 'Item > Document' places it under a slightly more abstract parent, but the class itself denotes the same concept.

Paper in the Conference ontology denotes a written scholarly contribution (a document), while Best Research Paper Award in sigkdd denotes an award given to a paper. These are completely different kinds of entities: one is the artefact itself, the other is a prize. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. enterConferenceDetails relates an Administrator to a Conference (entering conference details), while parallel_with relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (indicating parallel scheduling). There is no overlap in intended usage.
