Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers, active participants), situated under Person. Hotel presenter is a delegate who presents at a hotel venue, situated under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate. While both may involve presenting, their ontological contexts and intended meanings differ significantly: one is about the role of contributing to a conference, the other about a delegate presenting at a hotel location. They do not denote the same concept.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to a string (the title of the paper), while the iasted 'done_till' property relates a Deadline to a date (the date by which a deadline is done). They have completely different domains (Paper vs Deadline) and ranges (string vs date), and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

A's 'was an organizing committee of' is a specific relation: an Organizing committee organizes a Conference volume. B's 'organises' is broader: any Organisation or Person organises any Event. The A property is a specialization of the B property, so A is subsumed_by B.

confOf:Scholar is a subclass of Person representing a scholar (a person who studies at a university), while iasted:Nonauthor_registration_fee is a monetary fee subclass under Money > Fee > Registration fee. They denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. a price/fee—and share no meaningful semantic relationship.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a summary of a paper (a research document), while Bank transfer in iasted is a payment document (a financial instrument). They belong to completely different domains despite both being subclasses of Document.

Both properties express that a reviewer/PC member was added or invited by another agent, but they differ in domain/range structure: cmt:addedBy has domain Program Committee Member and range Administrator (the person who added the member to the PC), while Conference:invited_by has domain Reviewer and range Reviewer (the reviewer who issued the invitation). The direction and the nature of the agent doing the inviting differ (administrator vs. fellow reviewer), so they are not equivalent; they are related by overlapping semantics of being invited/added to a reviewing body.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. Property A links a Topic to a Conference part (indicating that a topic is associated with a conference part), while property B links a Document to a Speaker (indicating the speaker who presented a document). Their domains (Topic vs Document) and ranges (Conference part vs Speaker) are disjoint concepts, and the relations themselves denote different associations in the conference domain.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'enableVirtualMeeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference (the administrator enables virtual meetings for a conference). In confOf, 'parallel_with' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (indicating two events run in parallel). They share no common semantics.

In edas, Slide Set is a specific kind of document (a sibling of Paper, Programme, Review under Document). In iasted, Document is a broad class covering many artefacts (Submission, Review, Form, Invitation letter, Transparency, etc.). Slide Set corresponds to a particular document type (closest to iasted's Transparency), not to the entire Document class. Thus Slide Set is subsumed by iasted's Document.

hasFax and Name are both datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote completely different attributes: a fax number versus a person's name. No reference alignment would equate them.

The cmt 'assignedTo' property assigns a Reviewer to a Paper (domain Paper, range Reviewer), expressing a review-assignment relationship. The ekaw 'partOf' property is a generic mereological relation with unspecified domain and range. These denote completely different relationships: one is about assigning reviewers to papers, the other about parthood. They are unrelated.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' (domain: Conference, range: Administrator) relates a conference to the administrator who runs its paper assignment tools. 'paperPresentedAs' (domain: Paper, range: Individual Presentation) relates a paper to its presentation at the conference. They connect entirely different entity types and describe different aspects of conference organization.

The two properties have incompatible domains and ranges and express different relations. 'relates To' in edas links a Document to various entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person), indicating a broad association between a document and things it is about or connected to. 'write' in iasted links a Person (author) to an Item (written work), expressing authorship. The domains differ (Document vs Person), the ranges differ, and the intended semantics differ: one is a generic relation from a document to other entities, the other is an authorship relation from a person to a written item. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A 'Two Level Conference' in EDAS denotes a type of conference event (a conference with two review levels), whereas 'Presenter' in EKAW denotes a person who presents at a conference. They are disjoint categories (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.
hasDecision relates a Paper to its Decision (acceptance/rejection), while employedBy relates a Person to their employing Organization. Different domains, ranges, and semantics; no overlap.

Invited talk in the Conference ontology is a type of Conference contribution / Presentation — an invited oral presentation. Poster Session in ekaw is a Session (a scheduled event block) where posters are displayed. One is a talk/presentation, the other is a session; they are different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, External Reviewer is a Person who assists another Reviewer but is explicitly not themselves a Reviewer. In iasted, Reviewer is a direct subclass of Speaker (under Delegate > Speaker), making it a full reviewer role. The cmt External Reviewer is by definition not a Reviewer, so these two classes do not denote the same concept; they are distinct roles in different ontology structures with no clear subsumption relationship.

Conference activity in iasted denotes an event or activity during a conference (e.g., Cocktail reception, Lecture, Registration), whereas Speaker in sigkdd denotes a person who gives a presentation. One is an activity/event, the other is a person role; they share no intended instances.

Both classes denote a person who authors a paper in the conference domain. In EDAS, Author is a subclass of Person with properties linking to Paper (has Related Paper, is Written By). In SIGKDD, Author is also a subclass of Person (via Speaker) with a submit property linking to Paper. Despite the different intermediate hierarchy (EDAS places Author directly under Person; SIGKDD places it under Speaker), the intended instances coincide: conference paper authors. The shared label, domain context, and paper-related properties support equivalence.

Both represent reviewer assessments of papers (bids/preferences for assignment), but they are structurally and semantically distinct. A cmt Bid is a simple object linking a Reviewer to a Paper via 'has Bid'. A Conference Review preference is a richer entity with a numeric degree, a topic or submission contribution, and a review reference, modeling a preference for reviewing a topic or contribution rather than a bid to review a specific paper. They overlap in the conference-review domain but are not equivalent.

In the edas ontology, Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, with subclasses like Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper and properties such as isWrittenBy and isReviewedBy. In the iasted ontology, Card is a physical item (subclass of Item) with child Credit card, sibling to Audiovisual equipment and Transport vehicle. These denote completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote the same concept of a poster presentation in the conference domain. They share identical labels, are both subclasses of a contribution class (Conference contribution / Contribution), and their siblings (Paper, Short paper, Presentation, etc.) are consistent with the same domain conceptualization of conference contribution types.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (a role, under Person > Chairman). In confOf, Tutorial is a type of event (under Event > Working event). One denotes a human role, the other an academic event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

A Travel Grant in edas is a type of Sponsorship (financial support awarded to a participant, typically funding their travel). A Fee for extra trip in iasted is a type of Fee (a charge the participant must pay for an extra trip). One is money given to the participant (grant/sponsorship), the other is money owed by the participant (fee/charge). They are conceptually distinct and not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties differ in both domain and range semantics. In edas, hasRelatedDocument links an Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, or Person to a Document, indicating an association with a related document. In iasted, prepare links a Person to an Item, indicating that the person prepares (creates/produces) an item. The domains overlap only on Person, but the ranges (Document vs. Item) and the intended meanings (having a related document vs. preparing an item) are distinct. These are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate different concepts in different directions. 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to the Conference volume (proceedings) where it is published, while 'paperPresentedAs' links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (the talk). The range types (Conference volume vs Individual Presentation) are distinct, and the relations describe different aspects of conference participation (publication venue vs presentation event).

confOf: Tutorial is a type of event (a working event like a conference or workshop), while iasted: Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical item). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf Author is a broad class covering all persons who write contributions, positioned directly under Person with siblings like Scholar, Science Worker, etc. sigkdd Author_of_paper is a more specific subclass under Author > Speaker > Author, denoting specifically an author of a paper. The confOf Author subsumes the sigkdd Author_of_paper because every author of a paper is an author, but not every author is specifically an author of a paper (e.g., could be author of other contribution types).

Multimedia Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference papers. Audiovisual equipment in iasted is a subclass of Item, representing physical equipment like computers and projectors. Despite the loose semantic association with 'multimedia', these classes denote entirely different kinds of entities (abstract topic vs. physical equipment) and share no instances.

Regular Session in EKAW is a temporal event (subclass of Session under Scientific Event), whereas Session room in IASTED is a physical place (subclass of Place). They denote entirely different categories of entities—a scheduled event vs. a location—and share no meaningful overlap.

The two properties relate different kinds of things. In edas, hasMember links a Conference to a Person (i.e., a conference has members/participants). In iasted, is_sent_by links an Item (e.g., a paper or document) to a Person (i.e., the person who sent/submitted the item). The domains (Conference vs Item) and the intended semantics (membership vs authorship/submission) differ, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

In ekaw, SC Member is a Program Committee member (a conference role under PC Member, alongside chairs). In iasted, Reviewer is a sub-concept of Speaker, which is a sub-concept of Delegate — i.e., a person who physically attends the conference and presents, and also reviews. An SC Member in ekaw need not be a delegate or speaker, and an iasted Reviewer is defined through the delegate/speaker hierarchy rather than as a PC role. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Both concern the authorship/reviewer-ship of a written artefact, but they run in opposite directions and have different domains/ranges: ekaw:reviewWrittenBy goes Review -> Possible Reviewer, while iasted:write goes Person -> Item. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership/administrative role (a Chairman responsible for chairing the conference), while Tutorial speaker is a person who presents a tutorial at a conference. These are completely different concepts: one is a governance/organizational role, the other is a presenter/speaker role. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The cmt property 'has Been Assigned' relates a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review, while the sigkdd property 'search' relates the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Sponsor. The domains (Reviewer vs ACM SIGKDD) and ranges (Paper vs Sponzor) are completely different, and the two properties describe unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'run Paper Assignment Tools' (Administrator -> Conference) denotes an administrative action of running paper assignment tools for a conference. 'writes' (Author -> Contribution) denotes an author writing a contribution/paper. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and share no semantic overlap.

Chair is a person who leads a committee in the Conference ontology, while Country is a geographic entity used as the range of a property from Conference in the edas ontology. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The cmt property 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who runs the paper assignment tools, while the iasted property 'write' relates a Person to an Item they write. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, Presenter is a person (subclass of Author > Person) who presents a paper. In iasted, Presenter city is a city (subclass of City) associated with a presenter's location. One is a person role, the other is a geographic location; they share the word 'Presenter' but denote completely different entities.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Bronze Supporter is a type of conference sponsor. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Abstract is a document artifact (a short version of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a subject-area classification in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (a paper having an associated expertise level for reviewing), while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving/presenting something). The domains (Submitted contribution vs Person) and ranges (Review expertise vs Activity/Item) are disjoint, and the intended semantics are unrelated.

confOf:Company is a kind of Organization (e.g., a company that participates in a conference), while edas:MeetingRoomPlace is a kind of Place (a physical room where conference sessions are held). They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

A is 'Nonmember registration fee', a specific subclass of 'Registration fee' in iasted. B is the general 'Registration fee' class in sigkdd, which has children including 'Registration Non Member' (the direct counterpart of A). Thus A is subsumed by B: every nonmember registration fee is a registration fee, but not vice versa.

confOf:Student is a person who is a participant in a conference (a student attendee), while sigkdd:Bronze_Supporter is a sponsor at a particular support level. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Person/Participant vs. Sponzor) and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property 'done till' in iasted relates a Deadline to a date (when a deadline expires), while 'Price' in sigkdd relates a Registration fee to an integer (monetary cost). They connect completely different domain entities and represent different relations (temporal vs. monetary), so they are unrelated.

These two classes denote different kinds of documents. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a general informational document aimed at conference participants (alongside call for papers, announcements, etc.), whereas 'Brief introduction for Session chair' in the iasted ontology is a specific introductory document for session chairs. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Conference denotes the overall conference event (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas edas:WelcomeTalk denotes a specific talk event (a Talk Event sibling of Closing Talk) that occurs within a conference. These are completely different kinds of entities at different levels of granularity, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. In cmt, virtualMeetingEnabledBy links a Conference to an Administrator who enables a virtual meeting. In ekaw, listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event it lists. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'was a member of' links a Committee member to a Committee (organizational membership), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (who presented the document). The domains (Committee member vs. Document) and ranges (Committee vs. Speaker) are disjoint, and the relations denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property hasRating in edas relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper receiving a review score), whereas obtain in sigkdd relates an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). They connect completely different domain and range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Measurements Topic' is a subject classification under the Topic hierarchy, representing a research topic about measurements in computer networks. In EKAW, 'Contributed Talk' is a type of event—an individual presentation given at a conference. They share no instances and no conceptual overlap.

In cmt, Paper is a specific document type (a submitted paper with authors, reviews, bids, decisions). In iasted, Document is a broad superclass covering many artefacts (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc.). cmt's Paper is a strict subclass of iasted's Document, not equivalent.

Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a conference session, while Demo Chair (ekaw) is a person who chairs demos. These are distinct organizational roles in a conference, neither subsuming the other. They share the common ancestor Person/Conference Participant but are sibling-level specializations with different responsibilities.

Poster Paper is a type of academic document (a paper presented as a poster) in the EKAW ontology, while Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment in the IASTED ontology. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has members' connects a Committee to its Committee members (organizational membership), while 'sign' connects a Person to an Item (the act of signing a document/artifact). They have different domains (Committee vs Person), different ranges (Committee member vs Item), and different meanings in the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference denotes the conference event/organization itself (with dates, members, administrators, paper assignments). In edas, Call denotes a call-for-papers/reviews/manuscripts artefact that is initiated by chairs and associated with an academic event via 'for Event'. These are distinct concepts: a conference vs. a call issued for a conference.

Both properties relate something to a spatial location, but they differ in domain and direction. 'held In' has domain Event and range Location, meaning an event takes place at a location. 'is situated in' has domain Building/City/Place and range Building/City/Place/State, meaning a place is geographically situated within another place. The domains are disjoint (events vs. places), so they are not equivalent; they are only loosely related as spatial-location properties.

Conference announcement is a document type (a conference document announcing something), while Video presentation is an activity/presentation type. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote different kinds of entities.

The two classes denote completely different concepts in the conference domain. In the EDAS ontology, 'Computer Networks Optical Topic' is a specific subject-area topic (a subclass of 'Computer Networks Topic') used to classify papers. In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Organizing Committee' is a type of committee responsible for organizing a conference. There is no overlap in intended instances, and neither concept subsumes the other.

Program Committee in cmt denotes a committee of reviewers for a conference, while State in iasted denotes a geographical or administrative state (with children like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state and properties like is situated in, is visited by). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges: finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference (finalizing paper assignments for the conference), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submitting a paper). They describe different actions by different actors on different objects.

Workshop in the Conference ontology denotes a conference part/event (a meeting that is part of a conference volume), while Workshop_Chair in ekaw denotes a person who chairs a workshop. One is an event, the other is a person/role; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person who attends that event, while is_prepared_by links an Item (e.g., a document or artifact) to a Person who prepared it. These are distinct relations: attending an event vs. preparing an item. They have different domains (Conference Event vs. Item) and different semantics, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Conference is a kind of event (a working event like Workshop or Tutorial), i.e., the conference itself. In iasted, Activity_before_conference is a pre-conference activity such as Accepting manuscript, Receiving manuscript, Renting, or Research. These denote completely different things: one is the conference event, the other is preparatory activity before it. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Invited talk is a presentation-type conference contribution (an oral talk given by an invited speaker), whereas Short paper is a written contribution category based on length. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Author (cmt) denotes a person who writes or submits a paper, with properties like submitPaper and writePaper. Track workshop chair (Conference) denotes a person who chairs a track, workshop, or tutorial, with properties relating to conference parts. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution they have authored. Property B (hasUpdatedVersion) relates a Document to another Document that is an updated version of it. They connect entirely different kinds of entities (Author->Contribution vs. Document->Document) and express different relationships (authorship vs. versioning).

Review Rating in edas is a rating/score value assigned to a paper (with children like Accept Rating, Reject Rating), while Review in iasted is a document artifact. They denote completely different concepts: one is an evaluation score, the other is a written review document.

cmt:Paper is a document submitted to a conference (subclass of Document, with authors, reviewers, bids, decisions), while edas:ContactInformation is a data object holding address/email/phone details. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In ontology A, 'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution relation). In ontology B, 'payed by' links a Registration fee to a Person (payment relation). They have different domains and ranges, and even if viewed as inverse directions they do not connect the same kinds of entities.

A 'User' in cmt is a person who interacts with the conference management system (parent: Person; children: Administrator, Author, Reviewer). A 'Session' in iasted is a conference activity/event (parent: Lecture; children: Speaker lecture). They denote completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is a scheduled event.

The two properties have opposite domain/range orientations and different semantics. 'contributes' relates Person -> Conference document (a person authors/contributes a document), while 'is signed by' relates Item -> Person (an item is signed by a person). They are not inverses of each other either: contributing a document is not the same as signing an item. The domains (Person vs Item) and ranges (Conference document vs Person) differ, and the intended relations are distinct in the conference domain.

An Organizational Meeting in EDAS is a meeting for organizational/administrative purposes (e.g., committee or planning meetings), not a scientific event. A Workshop in EKAW is a scientific event where papers are presented and discussed. These are different kinds of conference events with different purposes, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

confOf Paper is a document (subclass of Contribution, sibling of Poster and Short paper) denoting the written article itself. edas Paper Presentation is an event (subclass of Academic Event, sibling of Organizational Meeting and Workshop) denoting the oral presentation session. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one is a document, the other is a scheduled event/activity. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Contribution co-author in the Conference ontology is a specific role: a person who co-authors a conference contribution, sitting under Regular author. Author in confOf is the general class of all authors (domain of writes -> Contribution). Every co-author is an author, but not every author is a co-author (e.g., sole authors or first authors are not co-authors). Thus Contribution co-author is subsumed by Author.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person, denoting a human participant who is a student. Renting in iasted is a subclass of Activity before conference, denoting an action of renting something. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf Member is a broad participant subcategory (sibling of Regular and Student) covering any conference member, while edas TPC Member is specifically a program-committee member with reviewing and call-initiation roles. TPC Member is thus a narrower concept; Member subsumes it, so Member is subsumed_by TPC Member in the sense that every TPC Member is a Member but not vice versa.

hasName is a datatype property from Conference to string (the full name of a conference), while listsEvent is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event (listing events in a brochure or web site). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings.

Organization in edas denotes an organizational body (with subtypes like Academia, Government, Industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. Item in iasted denotes a physical or informational object (audiovisual equipment, documents, publications, transport vehicles). These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. confOf:hasTitle applies to a Contribution (e.g., a paper or abstract) and captures its title, while sigkdd:Name_of_conference applies to a Conference and captures the conference's name. They relate different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

In EKAW, Neutral_Review is a specific subclass of Review (alongside Positive_Review and Negative_Review), representing a review with a neutral verdict. In IASTED, Review is the general class for review documents. Thus EKAW's Neutral_Review is strictly more specific than IASTED's Review, so the relation is subsumed_by.
hasEmail relates a Person to their email address (string), while hasLastName relates a Person to their last name (string). These are distinct attributes with no overlap in meaning.

Property A links a Co-chair to a Committee (a structural/organizational role-holding relation), while property B links a PC Member to a Contribution (a reviewing relation). They involve different domain and range types and express fundamentally different relationships in the conference domain.

`read By Reviewer` relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the reviewer assigned to read/review the paper), while `presentationed by` relates a Document to a Speaker (the person presenting it at the conference). These are different relationships in the conference domain: one concerns the review process, the other concerns the presentation of a document. The domains (Paper vs Document) and ranges (Reviewer vs Speaker) are distinct concepts, and the relations serve different purposes.

The two properties are completely different in meaning and structure. In cmt, 'memberOfConference' is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference (indicating membership). In sigkdd, 'Start_of_conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (indicating when the conference starts). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A Paper in edas is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, with children like Accepted/Rejected Paper and properties like isWrittenBy and isReviewedBy. Value added tax in iasted is a monetary tax concept under Money > Tax. These denote completely unrelated domain concepts.

Written_contribution in ontology Conference is a specific subclass of Conference contribution (alongside invited talks, posters, presentations), denoting written scholarly works. Submission in iasted is a broader document category covering any submitted document (including final manuscripts, initial manuscripts, reviews, transparencies, etc.). Written_contribution is thus a narrower concept, subsumed_by the more general Submission document class.

Paper in the Conference ontology is a scholarly contribution (a research paper submitted to a conference), sitting under Conference contribution > Regular contribution. Form in the iasted ontology is an administrative document type (e.g., Author information form, Hotel registration form, Registration form), sitting under Item > Document. These denote completely different kinds of things: a research paper vs. an administrative form. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution (paper) to its Author, while ekaw's reviewWrittenBy relates a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it. These are different relations over different domain/range pairs: one is about authorship of a paper, the other about authorship of a review. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

`has an email` is a datatype property from Person to string, recording a person's email address. `obtain` is an object property from Person to Item, indicating that a person obtains some item. They differ in property type, range, and meaning; there is no alignment relation between them.

These properties relate entirely different concepts. Property A links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (organizational role to event part), while property B links a Member PC to a Topic (reviewer expertise to subject area). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are disjoint.

Both properties link papers/events to topics, but they run in opposite directions: edas:hasTopic goes from Paper/Conference to Topic, while ekaw:topicCoveredBy goes from ResearchTopic to Event/Paper. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent.

Break Event in edas is a subclass of Non Academic Event representing scheduled breaks (coffee breaks, meals, free time) during a conference. Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who gives presentations. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties relate Person to Place, but A's 'is present in' also has Time in its range, making it broader. B's 'can stay in' is specifically about lodging/accommodation at a Place, a narrower relation. Thus A subsumes B (B is subsumed_by A).

Both classes denote the same concept of an invited speaker at a conference. They share identical labels (modulo case), and both are subclasses of a speaker/contributor hierarchy under Person. The slight structural difference (A has parent 'Conference contributor' while B has parent 'Speaker') reflects different modeling choices, but the intended instances coincide: people invited to give a talk at a conference.

These properties relate completely different entities in different directions. 'reviewWrittenBy' links a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it, while 'obtain' links an Author to an Award they received. They share no semantic overlap in domain, range, or meaning.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person participating in the conference). In the Conference ontology, is_part_of_conference_volumes links a Conference part to a Conference volume (structural/proceedings containment). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so no equivalence or subsumption holds.

A 'Two Level Conference' in edas is a type of Conference (an event with two levels/sections), while 'IASTED non member' in iasted is a type of Delegate (a person who is not an IASTED member). One is an event, the other is a person; they share no common instances and are unrelated.

confOf:Conference is a top-level conference event (sibling of Workshop and Tutorial), while ekaw:Demo_Session is a specific type of session within a conference. These are at completely different levels of the event hierarchy and denote different concepts.

The property 'accepted By' in cmt relates a Paper to an Administrator who accepted it, while 'parallel with' in confOf relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range types. In Conference, 'has_a_track-workshop-tutorial_topic' links a Conference part to a Topic (indicating the topic of a conference part). In iasted, 'need' links a Person to an Item (indicating something a person needs). There is no overlap in the kinds of things being related or the direction of the relation.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing that papers are being solicited for a conference. A 'Microelectronics Topic' is a specific subject-matter topic within the EDAS ontology (a conference management system), representing a technical domain like microelectronics. These are completely different concepts: one is a document type, the other is a subject classification. They share no semantic relationship in the conference organization domain.

In EDAS, Place is a broad top-level spatial concept with subclasses such as Conference Venue Place, Accommodation Place, Dining Place, and Meeting Room Place. In IASTED, Building is a narrower spatial concept (a child of Place) whose instances are specific physical structures (e.g., Conference airport, Conference hotel, Presenter house). Thus EDAS Place is strictly more general than IASTED Building; the two are not equivalent.

confOf Contribution is a broad class covering all submitted works (Paper, Poster, Short paper), while ekaw Evaluated_Paper is a specific stage in the paper lifecycle (a submitted paper that has been assigned and evaluated, with children Accepted_Paper and Rejected_Paper). Contribution subsumes Evaluated_Paper because every evaluated paper is a contribution, but not vice versa.

Property A links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the event it organized), while property B links a Person to a Building, City, or State (a physical location occupied). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Conference is the event itself (with properties like date, members, administrators, paper assignments). In the Conference ontology, Conference_announcement is a document type (a subclass of Conference document) that announces a conference. These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a document about the event.

In cmt, Preference is a class used to encode a reviewer's bid/preference on a paper (e.g., as the range of preferences), whereas in ekaw, Review is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a paper. These are distinct concepts: a preference/bid is not the same as a review document, and there is no subsumption relationship between them.

Administrative event in confOf is a subclass of Event covering organizational activities like registration, reviewing, submission, and camera-ready events. Paper in edas is a subclass of Document representing written scholarly contributions. These are completely different domain categories: one is an event/activity, the other is a document. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

edas:Place denotes a physical location (accommodation, venue, dining, meeting room) where conference events are held, while ekaw:Event denotes an occurrence (scientific or social event) that happens at a location. These are disjoint concepts: Place is the spatial container, Event is the activity. No overlap in intended instances.

A is a datatype property mapping a Person to their last name (string), while B is an object property linking an Activity or Person to an Item or Place. They differ in type, domain, range, and meaning.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (representing a type of conference event with two review levels), despite having Person and TPC Member listed as parents (likely due to ontology modeling peculiarities). In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Speaker under Person, representing a person who gives an invited talk. One is a conference event, the other is a person role; they share no semantic overlap.

Both classes denote the act of rejecting a paper/manuscript in the conference domain. In cmt, Rejection is a subclass of Decision (alongside Acceptance), representing the decision to reject a paper. In iasted, Refusing manuscript is an activity before the conference (alongside Accepting manuscript, Receiving manuscript), representing the act of refusing a manuscript. Despite different modeling contexts (decision vs. activity), both refer to the same concept: the rejection of a submitted paper. The sibling structures are parallel (Rejection/Acceptance vs. Refusing manuscript/Accepting manuscript), confirming they denote the same domain concept.

These properties denote different attributes of a sponsorship/sponsor. 'has Cost Currency' records the currency of a sponsorship cost (e.g., USD, EUR), while 'Name of sponsor' records the name of the sponsor entity. They have different domains (Sponsorship vs. Sponzor) and capture semantically unrelated information, so they are not equivalent.

These properties relate different concepts in different directions. 'has Member' (domain Conference, range Person) connects a conference to its members (people). 'hold' (domain ACM SIGKDD, range Conference) connects the ACM SIGKDD organization to the conferences it holds. The domains (Conference vs ACM SIGKDD), ranges (Person vs Conference), and semantics (membership vs organizing/holding an event) are entirely different.

Conference Event in edas denotes an event (academic or non-academic) with attendees, locations, programmes, and date/times. Time zone in iasted denotes a temporal region for time offset purposes. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event (indicating which event a programme belongs to), while 'is given by' links an Activity/Item to a Person (indicating who presents or gives an activity). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not equivalent.

These properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. In cmt, 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper). In sigkdd, 'pay' links a Person to a Registration fee (a person paying a registration fee). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a Paper distinguished by being the full-length version as opposed to a Paper Abstract (a content/format distinction). In edas, 'Pending Paper' is a Paper in a pending state of the review process, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn Paper (a workflow/status distinction). These are orthogonal classification dimensions: a full version could be pending, accepted, etc. The intended instances do not coincide, and neither concept subsumes the other.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. `parallel with` in confOf relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel (symmetric scheduling relation), while `for Event` in edas relates a Call to the Academic Event it is issued for. They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different entities. In cmt, 'assignedByAdministrator' links a Reviewer to an Administrator who assigned them, while in sigkdd, 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present. They share no common domain, range, or meaning.

The two properties relate entirely different things. In Conference, 'invited by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the one who invited them to review), while in confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (the paper they review). Different domains, different ranges, and different semantics: one is about invitation between reviewers, the other about the act of reviewing a paper.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (an announcement/invitation artefact), whereas a 'Workshop' in edas is an academic event. They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies (document vs. event) and denote completely different kinds of entities.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and in their intended meaning. In cmt, assignExternalReviewer relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer, capturing the assignment of an external reviewer (the range is a person). In confOf, reviewes relates a Member PC to a Contribution, capturing which paper a PC member reviews (the range is a document). They do not connect the same kinds of entities in the same direction, so they are not equivalent; nor is one a generalization of the other.

Both are subclasses of Deadline, but they denote different deadlines in the conference timeline. 'Deadline for notification of acceptance' is when authors are notified of acceptance/rejection decisions, while 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is when abstracts must be submitted. These are distinct events in the conference workflow, not equivalent.

Review expertise in Conference denotes the level or area of expertise a reviewer has for a contribution, linked to reviewers and submitted contributions. ReviewForm in edas denotes a structured form used to collect review content. These are different concepts: one captures reviewer qualification/preference, the other the review artefact template.
Late paid applicant is a person who registered late and paid, while Accepting manuscript is an activity of accepting a manuscript. They are completely different concepts with no overlap.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper they submit for review; publisherOf relates an Organisation to published items such as flyers, multi-author volumes, brochures, and web sites. Different domain (Author vs Organisation), different range (Paper vs published artefacts), and different semantics (submission vs publication).

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. confOf:dealsWith connects a Contribution to a Topic (what the paper is about), while sigkdd:obtain connects an Author to an Award (receiving an award). Different domain, different range, different meaning — no alignment relationship holds.

cmt:Author is a specific role (a person who writes/submits papers) sitting under Conference Member, whereas Conference:Person is the general class of all people involved in the conference (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers, etc.). Author is thus a kind of Person, not equivalent to it.

The two properties have different domains and different meanings. In cmt, 'assignedByReviewer' links an External Reviewer to the Reviewer they were assigned by (an assignment relationship). In Conference, 'belongs_to_reviewers' links a Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer the expertise/preference belongs to). They relate different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are not equivalent.

Information for participants is a conference document (e.g., informational material sent to attendees), while Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment. These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while the confOf 'location' property denotes where a Social event or Working event is held. They relate different kinds of entities and express different attributes (name vs. physical location), so they are unrelated.

cmt:Conference is the actual conference event/organization entity (with properties like date, members, administrators, paper assignments). Conference:Conference_www is a subclass of Conference document, representing a web page about a conference (with a URL property). One is an event, the other is a document artifact; they denote completely different things despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

Tutorial is a type of conference part/event (a session where instruction occurs), while Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document (e.g., logistical information for attendees), sibling to Call for paper, Review, etc. 'Computer Networks Measurements Topic' in edas is a subject topic under the Computer Networks topic hierarchy, used to classify papers by research area. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

confOf's 'Chair PC' is a specific role restricted to the Program Committee chair (sibling of Member PC, Administrator, etc.), whereas sigkdd's 'Organizator' is a broad grouping that subsumes General Chair, Program Chair, Program Committee member, Organizing Committee member, and Webmaster. 'Chair PC' denotes a narrower concept than 'Organizator', so it is subsumed_by it rather than equivalent.

Rejection (cmt) is a Decision, the act/verdict of rejecting a paper. Rejected Paper (ekaw) is a Document, the paper artefact that received a negative decision. They are related (a rejection decision applies to a rejected paper) but denote different entities: one is a decision, the other is a document.

Submitted Paper is a paper submitted for review at a conference, while Mailing list is a document used for communication. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain despite both being subclasses of Document.

Both are object properties linking a written artefact (Document / Item) to a Person who authored it, with the same direction (domain -> range). The labels 'written By' and 'is writen by' are near-synonymous, and both ontologies model authorship of conference documents/items in the same way.

Reception and Conference Banquet are both social events at a conference, but they are distinct types of events. A reception is typically a welcome/registration gathering, while a banquet is a formal dinner. They are sibling-level concepts under Social Event, not equivalent. They share a common parent but do not denote the same concept.

In cmt, Review is a document written by a reviewer about a paper. In edas, Call For Manuscripts is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting submissions). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Workshop is a type of event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), denoting a workshop session at a conference. edas:SlideSet is a type of document (subclass of Document, sibling of Paper, Review, Programme), denoting a set of presentation slides. These are completely different kinds of entities—an event versus a document artefact—so they are unrelated.

PC Chair in ekaw is a Program Committee Chair (a leadership role within the PC, under PC Member), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a member of the Organizing Committee (a distinct body handling local logistics). The two are different organizational roles in different committees, and neither subsumes the other.

hasStreet is a datatype property relating Contact Information to a string (a street address), while heldIn is an object property relating an Event to a Location. They connect different domains and ranges and denote entirely different relations.

Both classes represent committee leadership roles within a conference, but they are not the same concept. confOf's 'Chair PC' is a sibling of 'Member PC', suggesting it denotes the chair of the program committee—a leadership role. sigkdd's 'Program Committee member' is a regular member of the program committee (a sibling of 'Program Chair', which would be the leadership equivalent). The two overlap in the domain of program committee roles but are not equivalent: a Chair PC would typically be a PC member, but not vice versa. They are related but not equivalent.

edas ConferenceEvent is a broad top-level class covering all conference events (academic and non-academic), with properties for attendees, dates, location, and programme. ekaw Conference_Trip is a specific kind of social event (a subclass of Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet). The edas class is strictly more general and subsumes the ekaw class.

The Conference ontology's 'is part of conference volumes' is a highly specific property linking Conference parts to Conference volumes, while EKAW's 'partOf' is a general mereological relation with no specified domain or range. The EKAW property is strictly more general, so the Conference property is subsumed by it.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different attributes: email captures an electronic mail address, while hasHomePage captures a URL to a personal home page. They are distinct relations in the conference domain and do not overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. confOf:employedBy links a Person to an Organization (employment relationship). iasted:is_paid_for links Money to an Activity or Item (payment relationship). Different domains, different ranges, different semantics.

Item in iasted is a broad class covering physical objects (Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle), while Person in sigkdd is a human agent with subtypes Listener, Organizator, Speaker. These are completely disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is a person who registered late and paid (subclass of Person > Conference applicant > Paid applicant). Entity B is a financial concept (subclass of Money) representing sponsorship. One is a human role, the other is a monetary entity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are object properties with domain Paper that relate a paper to the reviewer(s) who read/review it. The cmt property has range Reviewer, while edas has a broader range including Reviewer and related committee roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) who can also serve as reviewers. The core semantics—indicating which reviewer(s) read/reviewed a given paper—coincide, and the range difference reflects edas's more permissive modeling of who can review rather than a fundamentally different relation.

In edas, 'Operating Topicsystems' is a subclass of Topic, i.e., a subject area within the conference taxonomy (siblings include Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.). In iasted, 'Modelling' is a subclass of Research under Activity > Activity before conference, i.e., a research activity performed before the conference. These denote completely different kinds of things: a topic/subject area vs. a research activity. They share no meaningful semantic overlap.

confOf:Topic denotes a subject area of a conference (e.g., a research topic that contributions deal with, PC members are experts on, and working events cover). edas:ConferenceSession denotes a scheduled session/event within a conference (a temporal occurrence, not a subject area). Their intended instances are completely disjoint: a topic is an abstract subject, while a conference session is a concrete event. The properties confirm this: Topic is the range of 'deals With'/'expert On'/'has Topic', whereas ConferenceSession is a domain of 'has Related Document'/'relates To' and is itself a kind of academic event. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion organized during a conference), whereas iasted:IASTED_non_member is a type of delegate/person who is not an IASTED member. They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies (events vs. persons) and share no instances.

Property A links a paper/poster/presentation to its Abstract, while property B (paperInVolume) relates a paper to a volume/proceedings. They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

The cmt `has Bid` property links a Paper to a Bid (a bidding action by a reviewer expressing interest in reviewing that paper), while the ekaw `has Event` property links an Event to a sub-Event (a mereological/hierarchical relation among events). They have completely different domains (Paper vs Event), ranges (Bid vs Event), and meanings; there is no overlap in the conference-organisation domain.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Rated Papers are papers that have received review ratings. These are completely different concepts: one is an announcement document, the other is a category of reviewed papers.

Bid in cmt is an entity representing a reviewer's bid on a paper (domain/range involving Reviewer and Paper). Location in ekaw is a physical place where an event is held (domain/range involving Event). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: 'has Fax' captures a person's fax number, while 'Nation' captures a person's country/nationality. They share no semantic relationship in the conference domain.

The ekaw 'has Event' property relates an Event to a sub-Event (e.g., a conference has sessions or workshops), while the sigkdd 'award' property relates some entity to an Award. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no indication of overlap or subsumption between them.

These two properties denote completely different relations. startReviewerBidding relates an Administrator to a Conference, representing the action of initiating the reviewer bidding process. reviewerOfPaper relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper, indicating that a reviewer is assigned to or reviews a specific paper. They have different domains (Administrator vs Possible Reviewer), different ranges (Conference vs Paper), and capture semantically distinct relationships with no overlap.

In the iasted ontology, 'Audiovisual equipment' is a subclass of Item and has children like Computer, LCD projector, Overhead projector, and Video cassette player, making it a physical equipment category. In the sigkdd ontology, 'Speaker' is a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited Speaker, making it a role for a person who presents. These are completely different concepts: one is an inanimate object/equipment, the other is a human role. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'assignReviewer' has domain Administrator and range Reviewer, meaning an administrator assigns a reviewer to a paper. In the Conference ontology, 'has_a_review_reference_or_expertise' has domain Reviewer and range (Review expertise, Review preference), meaning a reviewer has associated expertise or preference metadata. They connect entirely different entities and serve different purposes.

Conference Participant denotes any person who participates in a conference (including presenters, chairs, committee members, registered attendees), while Sponsor denotes a person or organization that provides financial support. A sponsor is not necessarily a participant, and a participant is not necessarily a sponsor. They share only the common parent Person, but their intended instances are disjoint.

In EDAS, 'Academic Event' is a broad superclass covering Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event, and Workshop. In EKAW, 'Conference' is a specific subclass of Scientific Event representing one edition of a conference. EKAW's Conference is a specific type of academic event, making EDAS's Academic Event more general. Thus, Academic Event is subsumed_by Conference in the sense that Conference is a narrower concept, but the correct relation is that Academic Event subsumes Conference (or equivalently, Conference is subsumed_by Academic Event). Here, A (Academic Event) is more general than B (Conference), so A subsumes B.

Activity_after_conference is a subclass of Activity (e.g., Departure, Full day tour), denoting post-conference events. Main_office is a subclass of Place (sibling of Conference hall, Hotel), denoting a physical location. These are entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Invited_speaker is a specific kind of conference contributor who gives an invited talk. Speaker in iasted is a broad class covering anyone who speaks (it has Author and Reviewer as subclasses, among others). Thus every Invited_speaker is a Speaker, but not vice versa, so Invited_speaker is subsumed_by Speaker.

Property A (has_a_submitted_contribution) links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution, i.e., it records which paper a reviewer-expertise is about. Property B (hasReview) links a Paper to a Review, i.e., it records the reviews attached to a paper. They relate different entity types in different directions (review-expertise -> paper vs. paper -> review), so they are not equivalent, inverse, or subsuming one another.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), whereas Dinner banquet in iasted is a social event/activity. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Short_paper in confOf is a type of academic contribution (a short research paper submitted to a conference), whereas Flyer in ekaw is a promotional document published by an organisation. They belong to disjoint branches of the ontology hierarchy (Contribution vs Document) and denote entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Program Committee' denotes the committee itself (a group/organization), as shown by its property 'has Program Committee Member' relating it to individual members. In sigkdd, 'Program Committee member' denotes an individual person who serves on the committee, placed under Person > Organizator. These are different types of entities (a collective body vs. an individual role), so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Conference announcement is a document type (a child of Conference document) used to announce a conference, whereas Workshop is an academic event (a child of Academic Event). They are completely different kinds of entities: one is an information artefact, the other is an event that takes place at a conference.

Communications Topic is a subject-area classification (a kind of Topic) for papers in the EDAS ontology, while Program Committee is an organizational entity (a kind of Committee) responsible for reviewing papers in the SIGKDD ontology. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:University is a specific type of academic organization (universities), while edas:AcademiaOrganization is a broader category covering all academia organizations. University is subsumed by AcademiaOrganization.

Both properties link a paper/contribution to its author(s), but they are not equivalent. 'hasCo-author' in cmt specifically relates a Paper to a Co-author (a co-author, not the primary author), while 'writtenBy' in confOf is a more general property relating a Contribution to any Author. 'writtenBy' subsumes 'hasCo-author' in a broad sense, but the range and domain differences (Co-author vs Author, Paper vs Contribution) and the specific co-author semantics mean they are related but not equivalent.

A 'Two Level Conference' in EDAS denotes a type of conference event (a conference with two review levels), while 'Tutorial Chair' in EKAW denotes a person who chairs tutorials. These are completely different concepts despite both appearing under Person-related hierarchies in their respective ontologies.

Conference announcement is a document (subclass of Conference document) that communicates information about a conference, while Conference restaurant is a physical place (subclass of Building) where conference-related dining occurs. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (documents vs. places) and share no conceptual overlap despite the common word 'Conference' in their labels.

The two properties relate completely different entities. In ekaw, paperPresentedAs links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (the event where the paper is presented). In iasted, write links a Person to an Item (a document). They have different domains (Paper vs Person) and different ranges (Individual Presentation vs Item), and they express different relations (presentation of a paper vs authorship of a document).

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. 'has_the_first_name' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's given name. 'Price' is a datatype property from Registration fee to int, capturing a monetary amount. They share no conceptual overlap.

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) representing a type of conference activity. edas's 'Computer Networks Switching Topic' is a leaf-level subclass of Topic representing a specific subject area within computer networks. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties go in opposite directions and relate different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'written By' has domain Review and range Reviewer, meaning it points from a review to the person who wrote it. In the Conference ontology, 'reviews' has domain Review and range Reviewed contribution, meaning it points from a review to the paper being reviewed. These are not the same relation: one connects a review to its author, the other connects a review to the artefact it evaluates. They are not inverses of each other either (an inverse of 'written By' would still relate a review to a reviewer, not to a contribution). Therefore they are unrelated.

These two datatype properties are completely unrelated. 'has_the_last_name' has domain Person and range string, representing a person's family name. 'hasSubmissionInstructions' has domain Call and range string, representing instructions for submitting to a call for papers. They have different domains (Person vs Call), different meanings (a person's surname vs submission guidelines for a call), and no overlap in the kinds of things they describe.

In EDAS, 'Review Form' is a document/artefact (the form used to collect a review), while in IASTED 'Review' is a document that is the actual review output. They are both documents in the conference domain and are closely associated, but a review form (the template) is not the same concept as a review (the completed artefact). They overlap in topic but do not denote the same thing, so 'related' is the most accurate relation.

siteURL has domain Conference and range anyURI, denoting the conference website. hasHomePage has domain Person and range string, denoting a person's home page. Different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings; they are not equivalent.

In edas, 'Paper' is a subclass of Document representing the written article submitted to a conference, with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc. In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Person (via Speaker > Author) representing a person who authored a paper. These are completely different concepts: one is a document, the other is a person/role.

confOf:Organization denotes an organizational entity (e.g., Company, University) that employs people, while sigkdd:Place denotes a physical location (e.g., Conference hall, Hotel, Main office) where people can stay. These are disjoint concepts: an Organization is an institution, not a geographic/physical place, and the ontologies provide no indication of overlap.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a short version of a paper submitted for review), while Cryptography Topic is a subject-area classification for papers. They share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'startReviewerBidding' is an action by an Administrator on a Conference (initiating a bidding process), while 'invited_by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who issued the invitation). They share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things: `has_workshops` links a Conference volume to its constituent Workshops, while `hasMember` links a Conference to Person members (e.g., attendees or committee members). Their domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, so they are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers), while Presenter city is a city where a presenter is located. One is a person role, the other is a geographic location; they share no semantic overlap.

Written contribution is a document (subclass of Conference document > Conference contribution) with children like Regular contribution and Submitted contribution, denoting written artefacts such as papers. Talk Event is an event (subclass of Conference Event > Academic Event) with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk, denoting scheduled oral presentations. One is a document, the other is an event; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (paper), whereas the edas 'hasReviewHistory' property links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. These are entirely different relations involving different domain and range types, with no overlap in meaning.

confOf:Reception is a social event (a gathering/activity), while edas:Dining Place is a physical location/place. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Event vs. Place) and denote different kinds of entities: one is an event, the other is a venue/location.

Presentation in iasted is a subclass of Conference activity, denoting an event/activity (with children like Power Point presentation and Video presentation). Organizator in sigkdd is a subclass of Person, denoting a human role (with children like General Chair, Program Chair). These are disjoint categories: an activity vs. a person. No alignment relation holds.

Person in the Conference ontology denotes a human individual (authors, reviewers, committee members, etc.), while State in the iasted ontology denotes a geographic/political region that can be occupied by or visited by persons. They share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. In cmt, 'adjust Bid' connects a Reviewer to a Bid (reviewer adjusting a paper's bid for review assignment). In confOf, 'written By' connects a Contribution to an Author (authorship relation). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Property A (has_the_last_name) has domain Person and range string, representing a person's surname. Property B (ends_on) has domain Event and range string, representing when an event ends. They relate to completely different domains (people vs. events) and denote unrelated attributes.

CMT's `name` is a general datatype property whose domain includes both Conference and Person, capturing the full name or title of either entity. EDAS's `hasLastName` is specifically scoped to Person and captures only the surname portion of a person's name. `name` is broader in both domain (includes Conference) and semantic coverage (full name vs. last name only), so `name` is subsumed_by `hasLastName` is not right; rather `hasLastName` is subsumed_by `name`. The correct relation is subsumed_by (hasLastName is subsumed by name).

The property 'has Part' in ekaw denotes a mereological relation (part-whole), while 'awarded by' in sigkdd denotes the relation between an Award and the entity that grants it. They relate entirely different kinds of things and express different semantics, so they are unrelated.

Committee_member is a subclass of Person (a human committee member), while AccommodationPlace is a subclass of Place (a physical location for lodging). They share no instances and belong to entirely disjoint branches of their respective ontologies.
Paper Full Version is a document (a full paper), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline. They share no instances and are in disjoint branches of their ontologies.

In edas, Conference Event is a class whose instances are events (academic or non-academic) that have start/end dates, locations, programmes, and attendees. In sigkdd, Place is a class whose instances are physical locations (Conference hall, Hotel, Main office) where people can stay. These are disjoint categories: an event is not a physical place. The hasLocation property in edas (Conference Event -> Place) further confirms that Conference Event and Place are distinct entities in a relationship, not equivalent.

Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is the chair of a tutorial, a specific session-type event, while General Chair (sigkdd) is the top-level organizer of the entire conference. These are distinct organizational roles with different scopes and responsibilities; neither subsumes the other.

Property A (has_a_name) is a datatype property with range string, assigning a name to entities like Conference, Publisher, Topic, etc. Property B (hasTopic) is an object property with range Topic, linking a Working event to a Topic. They have different domains, different ranges (string vs Topic), and different semantics (naming vs topic assignment).

Both classes denote the outcome of a paper being rejected in the conference domain. 'Rejected contribution' in the Conference ontology is a subclass of Reviewed contribution, representing a manuscript that was reviewed and not accepted. 'Refusing manuscript' in the iasted ontology is modeled as an activity (subclass of Activity before conference) with siblings Accepting manuscript and Receiving manuscript, indicating it represents the rejection action/outcome. Despite the structural difference (document vs. activity modeling), the intended denotation coincides: a rejected paper. The sibling 'Accepting manuscript' parallels 'Accepted contribution', confirming the parallel semantics. Thus, they are equivalent.

Conference contributor (Person > Conference contributor) denotes a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers). Conference days (Time > Conference days) denotes a temporal period during which a conference takes place. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Person vs Time) and have no conceptual overlap.

The cmt 'hasAuthor' property links a Paper to its Author, while the sigkdd 'presentationed_by' property links a Document to a Speaker. These are fundamentally different relationships: authorship (who wrote the document) vs. presentation (who presents it). The domains and ranges differ (Paper/Author vs. Document/Speaker), and the concepts of author and speaker are distinct roles in the conference domain.

confOf:Organization denotes an institution such as a Company or University (with address properties), whereas sigkdd:Committee denotes a group of people assigned to a specific conference role (e.g., Program Committee, Organizing Committee). These are disjoint concepts in the conference domain: an Organization is an institution, while a Committee is a temporary body of individuals.

The two properties describe different relationships. In cmt, 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer who is assigned to review it. In iasted, 'is sent by' links an Item to a Person who sent/submitted it. These are distinct relations: one is about review assignment, the other about authorship/submission. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

In the Conference ontology, Topic is a general class for conference topics (with properties like having a name, being assigned to conference parts, etc.). In the edas ontology, MultimediaTopic is a specific subclass of Topic, with siblings like AntennasTopic, CADTopic, CommunicationsTopic, etc. Thus MultimediaTopic is a specific kind of topic, making it strictly narrower than the general Topic class. The relation is subsumed_by.

Both are conference talks, but they are not equivalent. In EKAW, 'Invited Talk' is a sibling of 'Contributed Talk' under 'Individual Presentation', meaning it specifically denotes a talk given by an invited speaker. In EDAS, 'Talk Event' is a broader category that includes 'Paper Presentation' and 'Welcome Talk' as siblings, covering various types of talks. An invited talk could be an instance of a Talk Event, but not all Talk Events are invited talks. The concepts overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly given their sibling structures.

Conference announcement is a document (subclass of Conference document) used to announce a conference, while Conference hotel is a physical place/building where a conference is held. They denote completely different categories of entities (information artefact vs. physical location) with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In Conference, 'belongs to reviewers' links Review expertise/Review preference to a Reviewer (i.e., a reviewer is associated with their expertise or preference). In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (i.e., a PC member reviews a paper). They have different domains, different ranges, and express different relationships, so they are not equivalent.

A is a specific submission deadline date (full paper submission date) with domain Important dates and range date, while B is a generic deadline date with domain Deadline and range dateTime. B is more general than A, so A is subsumed by B.

Both are places under a Place superclass, but a Meeting Room Place is a room where meetings/sessions are held, while a Conference hall is a larger venue for conference events. They overlap (a conference hall may contain meeting rooms) but are not equivalent: a meeting room can exist outside a conference hall, and a conference hall is broader than just a meeting room.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. confOf:employedBy links a Person to an Organization that employs them (employment relation). edas:hasMember links a Conference to a Person who is a member of that conference (membership relation). They have different domains (Person vs Conference), different ranges (Organization vs Person), and different semantics, so they are not equivalent.

Dining Place in edas is a specific kind of place (sibling of Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Meeting Room Place) denoting where dining occurs. Building in iasted is a broad class covering many structure types (airports, hotels, restaurants, offices, houses, universities). While a dining place might be located in a building, these concepts operate at different levels of granularity and do not share the same intended instances: a Dining Place is not itself a Building, and most Buildings are not Dining Places. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clearly aligned way.

Associated Chair (cmt) is a conference-level leadership role responsible for the overall conference organization, sitting alongside Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair. Session Chair (ekaw) is a role responsible for chairing a specific session within the conference, sitting alongside Demo Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair, etc. These are distinct roles: one is a high-level conference officer, the other chairs individual presentation sessions. They do not share the same intended instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.
