Conference fees in ontology Conference denotes monetary charges associated with conference attendance, while Conference Session in edas denotes a scheduled session/event within a conference. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are datatype properties that assign a temporal value to an event-like entity (Event in confOf, Activity in iasted), so they overlap in meaning. However, 'starts on' specifically marks the start point of an event and uses xsd:string, whereas 'is dated on' is a more general date assignment using xsd:dateTime. The difference in granularity (start date vs. general date) and range types makes them related rather than equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to the Conference volume where it is submitted, whereas 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they give. The domains (Conference contribution vs Person) and ranges (Conference volume vs Activity/Item) do not overlap, and the intended relations are entirely different.

Both are object properties linking a conference event to its physical location: edas hasLocation (domain Conference Event, range Place) and ekaw heldIn (domain Event, range Location). The domain concepts (Conference Event / Event) and range concepts (Place / Location) are themselves equivalent in the conference domain, and both properties express the same relation of an event being situated at a place.

confOf:Conference is a scientific meeting/event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). ekaw:OC_Member is a person who serves on the Organizing Committee (subclass of Conference Participant, parent of OC Chair). One is an event, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are not related.

Associated Chair is a conference-level leadership role in cmt (sibling of Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), whereas Workshop Chair in ekaw is specifically the chair of a workshop. These are distinct roles with different scopes; one is not more general than the other.

Topic in the Conference ontology denotes a subject area or theme of a conference (e.g., associated with conference parts, submissions, and review preferences). Reviewer in the EDAS ontology is a subclass of Person who reviews papers. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:location denotes the physical place where an event is held (domain: Social event, Working event), while edas:hasName denotes the full name of a conference (domain: Conference). They relate different kinds of things and have completely different meanings, so they are unrelated.

Written contribution is a scholarly document (e.g., paper, article) submitted or published at a conference, while Bank transfer is a payment document representing a financial transaction. They belong to completely different domains (academic content vs. payment method) despite both being subclasses of a document-like hierarchy.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (author contributing a paper), while 'isProviderOf' links an Organization to a Sponsorship (an organization providing sponsorship). The domains (Person vs Organization), ranges (Conference document vs Sponsorship), and the underlying semantics are all different, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Scientific Event in ekaw is an event type (subclass of Event) with children like Conference, Session, Workshop. One is a person role, the other is an event. They share no instances and are completely different concepts.

hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country, while hasMember relates a Conference to a Person. They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships.

Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Item > Audiovisual equipment), while Listener is a person who listens to presentations (Person > Listener). They belong to completely disjoint domains (equipment vs. person) and share no common instances.

Property A links Topic to Conference part (a topic is associated with a conference part such as a session or track). Property B links Event to Event (meronymic part-whole relation between events, e.g., a session is part of a conference). They differ in domain/range types and in meaning: A is a topic-of relation, B is a part-of relation. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In EDAS, Talk Event is a subclass of Academic Event with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk, denoting a talk-type event at a conference. In IASTED, Introduction is a subclass of Conference activity with a child 'Introduction of speaker', denoting the act of introducing a speaker. These are different concepts: one is a talk event, the other is an introduction activity. They share no clear subsumption relationship and are not equivalent.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while Sponsorship in edas is a financial arrangement with cost, currency, and provider. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A Conference Session in edas is an academic event (a scheduled session within a conference where papers are presented), while a Building in iasted is a physical place (with children like Conference building, Conference hotel, Session room). One is an event/activity, the other is a physical structure; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both classes denote the same concept in the conference domain: a tutorial as a type of conference event/presentation. In ontology A, Tutorial is a Conference part (sibling to Track and Workshop), and in ontology B it is an Individual Presentation under Scientific Event. Despite different taxonomic placements, the intended instances coincide—tutorials held at a conference. The identical label and consistent domain usage support equivalence.

Entity A is an event (a temporal occurrence where participants register for a conference), situated under Event > Administrative event. Entity B is a document/form (a physical or digital artefact), situated under Item > Document > Form. One is an event, the other is a document; they denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

A is a Paper (a document submitted for review), while B is a Deadline hotel reservation (a temporal deadline for booking hotels). They share no conceptual overlap despite both appearing under a Document/Time hierarchy in their respective ontologies.

Both classes denote the same social event in a conference: a dinner that is part of the non-academic/social program. In edas, Conference Dinner is a subclass of Meal Event under Non Academic Event; in iasted, Dinner banquet is a subclass of Social program under Conference activity. The labels are near-synonyms and the context (conference social event involving a meal/dinner) confirms they are intended to denote the same concept.

Academic Event in edas is a subclass of Conference Event with children like Workshop, Paper Presentation, and Talk Event — it denotes an academic gathering or session. Author in sigkdd is a subclass of Person > Speaker, denoting a person who writes papers. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A Workshop is a scientific event where papers are presented, typically with its own program committee and accepted papers. A Plenary lecture is a lecture given to all conference attendees (a single talk). They are different kinds of conference activities: a workshop is an event comprising multiple presentations, while a plenary lecture is a single talk. Their paths, siblings, and positions in the respective hierarchies confirm they denote different concepts.

These properties relate entirely different entities. In ekaw, volumeContainsPaper links a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. In sigkdd, 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the presentation/slides they give). The domains (volume vs. speaker) and ranges (paper vs. presentation document) are disjoint, so the properties share no common semantics.

Both are datatype properties associating a date with an entity, but in cmt the domain is specifically Conference while in iasted the domain is the more general Activity class. Since Conference is a kind of Activity, the iasted property is_dated_on is more general (applies to all activities), while cmt's date is restricted to conferences. Thus cmt:date is subsumed_by iasted:is_dated_on.

In edas, Pending Paper is a specific subclass of Paper denoting a paper still under review, with siblings Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc. In sigkdd, Paper is the general class of submitted papers (a direct child of Document). Thus Pending Paper is strictly narrower than sigkdd's Paper, so it is subsumed_by it.

The two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. In cmt, writePaper has domain Author and range Paper (author -> paper). In Conference, has_authors has domain Conference_document and range Person (document -> person). They relate the same concepts but in opposite directions. A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'was a steering committee of' links a Steering committee to a Conference volume, while 'sign' links a Person to an Item. They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

confOf's 'Submission event' is an event marking the submission of contributions, while sigkdd's 'Committee' is a group of people (e.g., Program Committee, Organizing Committee). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a person role (a kind of conference chairman) in cmt, while Single Level Conference is a type of conference event in edas. They denote completely different categories of entities (person vs. event) with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'accepted By' property links a Paper to an Administrator who accepted it, while the iasted 'write' property links a Person to an Item they authored. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

The cmt property co-writePaper has domain Co author and range Paper, representing the relation from a co-author to the paper they co-authored. The ekaw property writtenBy has domain Document and range Person, representing the relation from a document to its author. These are inverse directions: co-writePaper goes author -> paper, while writtenBy goes document -> person. A property and its inverse are not equivalent. They are not subsumption-related either, as they operate in opposite directions.

The two properties are completely different in type, domain, range, and meaning. `is used by` is an object property relating an Item to a Person, while `E mail` is a datatype property relating a Person to a string (email address). They share no semantic relationship.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In confOf, 'expertOn' links a PC Member to a Topic (indicating expertise). In ekaw, 'topicCoveredBy' links a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (indicating coverage). They are not inverses of each other either, since the domains and ranges do not correspond: PC Member expertise is not the same relation as topic coverage of events/papers.

maxPapers is a datatype property from Program Committee Member to int, representing the maximum number of papers a PC member can review. hasName is a datatype property from Conference to string, representing the full name of a conference. They have different domains, different ranges, and completely different meanings.

In the Conference ontology, 'Organization' is a top-level class denoting any organization (e.g., academic institutions, companies, publishers). In the sigkdd ontology, 'Organizing_Committee' is a specific committee responsible for organizing a conference, a subclass of 'Committee' alongside 'Program Committee' and 'Best Paper Awards Committee'. An organizing committee is a group of people, not an organization in the institutional sense. These two classes denote different concepts and share no clear subsumption relationship.

A's Presentation is a broad class covering any spoken/visual conference presentation (subtypes include Invited talk, Poster, Written contribution), while B's Video presentation is a specific kind of presentation medium (sibling of Power Point presentation under iasted's Presentation). A's Presentation is more akin to B's parent Presentation class, not to the specific Video presentation subclass. The two classes do not have coinciding instances.

Extended abstract is a specific type of conference contribution (a short paper or summary), while Submission in iasted is a broad document category covering various administrative items (forms, invitations, mailing lists, payment documents, reviews, visas, etc.). They occupy very different positions in their respective hierarchies and do not share the same intended instances.

Both classes denote members of the conference program committee (TPC = Technical Program Committee). They share the same parent Person, and both are siblings of Author, Reviewer, and Conference Chair. The cmt comment explicitly defines Program Committee Member, and edas uses the standard abbreviation TPC Member for the same role. The surrounding context (Person hierarchy, conference roles) confirms they are intended to denote the same concept.

Conference www in the Conference ontology is a document subclass (a web page with a URL) whose siblings are Call for paper, Review, Conference contribution, etc. Conference activity in iasted is an event/activity subclass whose children are Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Registration, etc. One denotes a web document, the other an activity that occurs during a conference; they share no instances and are unrelated.

`assigned To` in cmt relates a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper), while `held In` in ekaw relates an Event to a Location (where an event takes place). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges and no semantic overlap.

The property hasCostAmount in edas relates a Sponsorship to an integer cost amount, while locationOf in ekaw relates a Location to an Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics with no overlap in meaning.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different actions. In cmt, 'end Review' is used by a Program Committee Chair to end/close a Review, whereas in sigkdd 'submit' is used by an Author to submit a Paper. They relate different kinds of entities in different parts of the conference workflow and do not denote the same relation.

A Conference applicant is someone who applies to attend/register for a conference (a prospective participant), while a Student is a person enrolled in an academic institution. These are distinct concepts: a conference applicant is not necessarily a student, and a student is not necessarily a conference applicant. They share only the common parent Person, which is too general to establish any meaningful relationship.

In ontology A, 'Conference announcement' is a subtype of Conference document (a textual artefact like a call for papers or review). In ontology B, 'Conference Banquet' is a social event that occurs at a conference. One is a document, the other is an event; they share no instances and are unrelated.

In iasted, Activity is a broad superclass covering all conference-related activities (before, during, and after the conference), including things like presentations, sessions, and social events. In sigkdd, Conference is a specific entity representing the conference event itself with properties like start/end dates, city, and name. A Conference is one kind of Activity, but Activity is much broader, so iasted:Activity subsumes sigkdd:Conference (iasted:Activity is more general).

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who finalizes paper assignments, while 'presentationOfPaper' relates an Individual Presentation to the Paper being presented. They connect different entity types in different directions with no semantic overlap.

Industrial Session is a type of conference session (an event), while Conference hall is a physical place. They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

Committee in ontology Conference is a general class with children Organizing committee, Program committee, and Steering committee. Organizing Committee in sigkdd is a specific subclass of Committee. Thus Committee subsumes Organizing Committee, but they are not equivalent.

confOf's Paper is a broad class covering any conference paper submission (with siblings Poster and Short paper), while ekaw's Conference_Paper is a more specific subclass under Paper (which itself is under Document). ekaw further distinguishes Conference_Paper from Regular_Paper, Workshop_Paper, Demo_Paper, etc., so confOf Paper is more general than ekaw Conference_Paper; they are not equivalent.

The cmt `acceptedBy` property links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it, indicating acceptance of a paper by a person/role. The ekaw `paperPresentedAs` property links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation, indicating how a paper is presented at a conference. These are entirely different relations: one is about acceptance by an administrator, the other about presentation form. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

The property 'reviewer Of Paper' in ekaw relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper, indicating the reviewing relationship. The property 'submit' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper, indicating the submission relationship. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain: one denotes who reviews a paper, the other denotes who submits a paper. They have different domains (Possible Reviewer vs. Author) and different semantics, so they are unrelated.

Chairman in cmt is a person role (parent Person, with sub-roles like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), while Fee in sigkdd is a monetary charge (with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee). They denote completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

cmt:User is a broad superclass covering all system users (Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while ekaw:PC_Member is a specific role restricted to program committee members (subordinate to Possible_Reviewer). Their intended instances do not coincide: a cmt:User could be an author or administrator who is not a PC member, and an ekaw:PC_Member is a specific committee role. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

Property A ('has a name') is a generic datatype property that assigns a name to several entity types (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic). Property B ('City of conference') is a specific datatype property that records the city where a conference takes place. They have different meanings, different domains, and different intended semantics; they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.
Early paid applicant is a person who registered early and paid; Cheque is a payment document/instrument. They are disjoint kinds of entities (person vs document).

A Government Organization is an organizational entity (e.g., a government agency) under Organization, while a Main office is a physical place under Place with siblings like Building, Conference hall, Hotel room. They denote different categories of things (an organization vs. a physical location), so they are unrelated.

These properties have different domains and different semantics. 'is a starting date' (domain: Important dates) denotes the start date of a deadline or important date, while 'is dated on' (domain: Activity) denotes when an activity is scheduled. They relate to different kinds of entities (dates/deadlines vs. activities/events) and serve different purposes, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

cmt:User is a generic system-user superclass (Administrator, Author, Reviewer) for the CMT conference-management tool, whereas ekaw:Agency_Staff_Member denotes staff of an external agency involved in organising a conference. Although both are subclasses of Person, their intended instances do not coincide: a CMT User is a conference participant role, not an agency employee. No overlap is asserted, so they are unrelated rather than merely subsumed.

In edas, Country is a geographic nation (domain of hasCountry: Conference -> Country). In iasted, State is a sub-national administrative/political region with children like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state, and participates in spatial relations (is situated in, is visited by, etc.). A country and a state are distinct geographic levels, and the iasted State's children and properties indicate a different concept from a sovereign nation.

Both classes represent papers that have been assigned a rating/evaluation by reviewers. 'Rated Papers' in edas sits between Active Paper and (implicitly) accepted/rejected, while 'Evaluated Paper' in ekaw is the parent of Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper. Both denote the same concept: a paper that has received review evaluations, serving as the stage before acceptance/rejection decision.

Communication Theory Topic is a subject-area topic (sibling of Communications Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.) under Topic in the edas ontology. Card is a physical item type (parent of Credit card, sibling of Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) under Item in the iasted ontology. These denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'hasAuthor' property links a Paper to its Author. The ekaw 'volumeContainsPaper' property links a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. These are entirely different relations: one connects a document to a person (authorship), the other connects a container to its constituent documents (containment). They share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has_tutorials' links a Conference volume to the Tutorial events it contains, whereas 'sign' links a Person to an Item they sign. Their domains (Conference volume vs Person) and ranges (Tutorial vs Item) do not overlap, so they denote different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. In Conference, 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher publishes proceedings). In sigkdd, 'holded by' links a Conference to ACM SIGKDD (an organization that holds the conference). These are different relations in both domain/range and meaning: publishing proceedings vs. organizing/holding a conference.

Poster in the Conference ontology is a type of conference contribution (a document/artefact presented at a conference), situated under Conference document > Conference contribution, with siblings like Presentation, Regular contribution, and Written contribution. Author in the edas ontology is a type of person who writes papers, situated under Person, with siblings like Attendee, Reviewer, and Conference Chair. One denotes a document/artefact, the other denotes a person/role; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Co author in cmt is a Person who co-writes a Paper, sitting under Person > Conference Member > Author. Author book proceedings included in iasted is a Speaker/Delegate whose paper is included in a book proceedings, sitting under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Speaker > Author. Despite sharing the parent name 'Author', these classes belong to entirely different taxonomy contexts and model different concepts: one is a co-authoring role on a paper, the other is a delegate whose work appears in printed proceedings. Their intended instances do not coincide.

Entity A is a class denoting a person (a late-paid conference applicant) in the Person hierarchy of ontology Conference. Entity B is a class denoting a monetary fee (a student registration fee) in the Money/Fee hierarchy of ontology iasted. One is a person, the other is a fee amount; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference www is a web document/resource identified by a URL, sitting under Conference document alongside Call for paper, Review, etc. Tutorial is an academic activity/event (a type of Lecture) under Activity > Conference activity. One is a document artefact, the other is a scheduled activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In EDAS, 'Paper' is a broad class with children like Accepted, Pending, Rejected, Published, etc., covering all paper lifecycle states. In EKAW, 'Submitted Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper' specifically denoting papers that have been submitted. EDAS Paper is more general, encompassing all papers regardless of submission status, so EDAS Paper subsumes EKAW Submitted Paper.

Paper Abstract is a document type (a short version of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
hasFirstName and hasLastName are distinct datatype properties on Person capturing different parts of a person's name. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A is a person role (Associated Chair under Chairman/Person in cmt), while B is a type of conference contribution/presentation (Invited talk under Conference document in Conference ontology). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

Entity A is a Conference (an event/organization with a name, proceedings, publisher, topics, and conference volumes as children). Entity B is a Conference Paper (a document that is a paper presented at a conference, with siblings like Camera Ready Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). One denotes an academic event, the other a written document. They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different things.

Associated Chair is a person role in the conference organization hierarchy (Person > Chairman > Associated Chair), while Conference hall is a physical location (Place > Conference hall). They denote completely different categories of entities.

confOf:Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster, Short_paper) without any publication/acceptance status, whereas edas:PublishedPaper is a specific subtype of edas:Paper that has been published. edas:PublishedPaper is strictly narrower than confOf:Paper, so confOf:Paper is subsumed_by edas:PublishedPaper in the sense that the confOf class is more general than the specific published-paper subclass.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'lists Event' connects a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (a document/web resource listing events). In iasted, 'give' connects a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving a presentation or item). The domains (documents/web sites vs. persons) and ranges (events vs. activities/items) are disjoint, and the semantics of 'listing events in a brochure' versus 'a person giving something' are fundamentally different relations.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in ontology Conference is a document type (a child of Conference document) containing information for conference attendees. 'Silver Supporter' in sigkdd is a type of sponsor (child of Sponzor) representing a sponsorship tier. They share no instances and have no semantic overlap.

confOf:Contribution is a general class for submitted items (with children Paper, Poster, Short paper), whereas edas:ActivePaper is a specific state of a Paper (a sibling of Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, etc.). Contribution subsumes ActivePaper because every Active Paper is a Contribution, but not vice versa.

The property 'held In' (ekaw) relates an Event to the Location where it takes place, while 'is held before' (iasted) relates an Activity to a Time before which it occurs. They connect different kinds of entities (spatial vs temporal) and express fundamentally different relations, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Working_event is a kind of event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) with properties like location, title, and VAT. edas:SignalProcessingTopic is a specific subject area (a Topic) such as signal processing, a sibling of Antennas Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc. These are completely different concepts: one is an event type, the other is a research topic. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In cmt, Meta-Review is a specialized subclass of Review (a second-level review typically written by a meta-reviewer), whereas in edas, Review is the general class of all reviews. Thus cmt:Meta-Review is strictly more specific than edas:Review, so it is subsumed_by it.

Conference proceedings in the Conference ontology is a published document (with ISBN, volume, publisher), while ConferenceEvent in edas is an event (with location, start/end dates, attendees). A proceedings is an artefact produced by a conference, not the event itself; the two classes have disjoint intended instances.
Acceptance is a decision outcome for a paper submission in the conference-review domain, while Shuttle bus is a physical transport vehicle. They share no domain overlap.

In EDAS, 'Published Paper' is a paper that has been published (e.g., in proceedings or otherwise), which is broader than EKAW's 'Accepted Paper' that specifically means a paper accepted to become part of proceedings (but not yet camera-ready). EKAW's comment distinguishes 'accepted' from 'camera-ready', while EDAS 'Published Paper' could include camera-ready or already-published papers. Thus EDAS Published Paper subsumes EKAW Accepted Paper, as every accepted paper (EKAW sense) is on the path to being published, but not every published paper is merely 'accepted' in EKAW's narrower sense.

Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (Item > Transport vehicle > Shuttle bus), while Registration Student is a type of registration fee (Fee > Registration fee > Registration Student). They belong to completely different domains (transportation vs. conference fees) and share no conceptual overlap.

The cmt property 'run Paper Assignment Tools' specifically denotes an administrator running paper-assignment tools for a conference, a very specific administrative action. The iasted property 'give' is a general relation from Person to Activity/Item (e.g., giving a presentation or item). These have different domains (Administrator vs. Person), different ranges (Conference vs. Activity/Item), and denote completely different actions with no overlap in meaning.

Entity A is a class denoting a written contribution that has been accepted (a document/paper artifact in the conference domain). Entity B is a class denoting a rating value assigned to a review (an evaluation score indicating acceptance). Despite the shared word 'Accept', these are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one is the paper itself, the other is a rating used within a review. Their paths, parents, and siblings confirm they belong to disjoint parts of the ontology hierarchy with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'is submitted at' in ontology Conference relates a Conference contribution to the Conference volume where it is submitted (domain: Conference contribution, range: Conference volume). The property 'locationOf' in ekaw relates a Location to an Event (domain: Location, range: Event). These properties connect entirely different kinds of entities: one is about submission of contributions to conference volumes, the other about physical locations of events. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

confOf:Tutorial is a type of academic event (a teaching session held during a conference), whereas iasted:Conference_city is a geographic location (a city where a conference takes place). They belong to entirely disjoint branches of their ontologies (events vs. places) and share no instances.

Both classes denote persons who chair sessions in a conference, but they are not equivalent. In the Conference ontology, Chair is a Committee member (broader organizational role), while in edas, Session Chair is a direct subclass of Person alongside Conference Chair and TPC Member. The Conference ontology's Chair is more aligned with a general committee chair role, whereas edas distinguishes Session Chair from Conference Chair. They overlap in the conference domain but are not the same concept.

In ekaw, Paper is a class representing a written academic document (with subclasses like Conference Paper, Demo Paper, etc.) and is the subject of reviews. In iasted, Review is a specific document type (a review/referee report) under Document, sibling to Submission, Form, etc. These are different concepts: one is the paper itself, the other is a review document. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in the given ontologies.

confOf's 'Reviewing event' is a specific administrative event representing the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions, sitting under Event > Administrative event alongside submission, camera-ready, and registration events. ekaw's 'Event' is the top-level class for all events (scientific events, social events, etc.) with properties like being held in a location, organised by organisations/persons, covering topics, etc. A reviewing event is not a general event in the ekaw sense—it is a procedural/administrative activity, not something that would be held at a location or listed in a programme brochure. The two classes denote different concepts at different levels of granularity with no clear overlap in intended instances.

Both are datatype properties with domain involving money/fees and range int, but the domains differ: A's domain is the general Money class while B's domain is the specific Registration fee. The properties are not equivalent since they attach to different kinds of entities, though they overlap conceptually in representing monetary amounts.

Property A 'has a name' applies to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic, denoting a general name for organizational entities. Property B 'has First Name' applies specifically to Person and captures a person's first name (possibly including middle name). They have disjoint domains and denote different concepts: a general name vs. a person's first name.

Social Event in ekaw is a subclass of Event (e.g., Conference Banquet, Conference Trip), denoting a non-scientific gathering. Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who gives a presentation. These are disjoint categories (event vs. person) with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Conference denotes the overall conference event (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while iasted:Introduction_of_speaker is a specific conference activity introducing a speaker. They are at completely different levels of granularity and denote different concepts.

confOf's Topic is a general class for conference topics, used broadly across contributions, PC members, and working events. edas's MultimediaTopic is a specific subclass of Topic (a child of the general Topic class in edas), representing only multimedia-related subjects. Thus, confOf:Topic is strictly more general than edas:MultimediaTopic.

These two classes denote entirely different concepts. 'Two Level Conference' in EDAS refers to a type of conference (an event), while 'Workshop Chair' in EKAW refers to a person who chairs a workshop. Despite both appearing under Person-related hierarchies in the structural context, their intended instances do not coincide at all.

`presentationOfPaper` in EKAW relates an Individual Presentation to the Paper/Abstract being presented (domain: Individual Presentation, range: Abstract/Paper). `write` in IASTED relates a Person to an Item they author (domain: Person, range: Item). These are entirely different relations: one connects a presentation event to the document presented, the other connects a person to a document authored. They share no common domain or range types and express different relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome). In confOf, hasCountry links an Organization or Person to a Country (geographical location). They share no common domain or range and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Trip and Conference Banquet are both social events, but they are distinct kinds of social events. In ekaw, Conference Trip is a sibling of Conference Banquet, indicating they are different concepts. confOf's Trip corresponds to ekaw's Conference Trip, not to Conference Banquet.

Banquet and Reception are distinct types of social events at a conference. A banquet is a formal dinner, while a reception is a welcoming/gathering event. They are sibling-level concepts under social events but do not denote the same concept.

In edas, Paper is a written scholarly contribution submitted to a conference, with children like Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper and properties such as isWrittenBy and isReviewedBy. In iasted, Review is a review document (a referee's evaluation of a submission), a sibling of Submission under Document. These denote different artefacts in the conference domain: a paper versus a review of a paper. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Departure is an activity (leaving after a conference), while Main office is a place (a physical location). They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

Meal Menu is a menu for a meal event (e.g., dinner menu), while Review is a review of a paper. They share the parent Document but denote completely different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

Co chair in Conference is a committee co-chair (a sub-role of Committee member, sibling of Chair, linked to committees). Chair PC in confOf is the chair of the Program Committee, a direct sub-class of Person with siblings like Member PC, Author, Participant. A committee co-chair is not the same as a PC chair; they are distinct organizational roles, and neither subsumes the other in the given context.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. `employed By` relates a Person to an Organization that employs them, while `go through` relates an Item to an Activity it undergoes. There is no semantic overlap between employment and an item passing through an activity.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference. Break Event is a subclass of Non Academic Event, denoting scheduled breaks such as coffee breaks or meals. These are completely disjoint categories: one is about persons, the other about events.

has VAT (confOf) captures the value-added tax applied to social/working events, while Currency (sigkdd) specifies the currency of a registration fee. They denote different concepts: one is a tax amount, the other is a monetary unit. Their domains also differ (social/working events vs. registration fee), so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

In EDAS, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (distinguishing conference structure levels), whereas in EKAW 'PC Chair' is a person role under Conference Participant. They denote completely different things: a conference type vs. a committee chair role.

reviewOfPaper relates a Review to the Paper being reviewed, while write relates a Person to an Item they authored. These are fundamentally different relations with different domains and ranges, and they express different concepts (reviewing vs. authoring).

Security Topic is a subject-area topic (a subclass of Topic with siblings like Cryptography Topic, Mobile Computing Topic, etc.), denoting a conference topic or theme. Organizing Committee is a committee role/group (a subclass of Committee with siblings like Program Committee, Best Paper Awards Committee), denoting a body of people organizing an event. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the chair of the entire conference, while Workshop Chair (ekaw) is the chair of a specific workshop within a conference. These are distinct organizational roles at different levels of the event hierarchy. Neither subsumes the other: a conference chair is not necessarily a workshop chair, and a workshop chair is not necessarily a conference chair. They share only the common ancestor of Person/Participant.

Although both classes are subclasses of Document, they denote completely different concepts. In ekaw, Abstract is a summary of a paper or presentation (with children like Invited Talk Abstract and Tutorial Abstract). In iasted, Payment document is a financial record (with children Bank transfer and Cheque). They share no instances and are unrelated in the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference is the event/organization itself (has date, members, administrators, accepts submissions). In confOf, Contribution is the submitted artefact (paper/poster/short paper) with abstract, keywords, authors, and reviews. These are completely different concepts with no overlap.

The cmt 'title' is a datatype property from Paper to string (the title text of a paper). The ekaw 'presentationOfPaper' is an object property from Individual Presentation to Abstract/Paper (linking a presentation to the paper it presents). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have different types, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote a person who authors (and submits) a paper in the conference domain. They share the same label, both are subclasses of Person (via intermediate roles), and both are the domain of a submit-paper relation (cmt:submitPaper Author->Paper, sigkdd:submit Author->Paper). The differing intermediate parents (Conference Member vs Speaker) reflect different modelling choices, not a difference in the intended set of instances. A reference alignment would equate these two Author classes.

In cmt, Paper is a conference paper submitted for review, with children like Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties linking it to authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions. In iasted, Transparency is a presentation aid (e.g., slides for a talk), a sibling of Submission, Review, Form, etc. A transparency is not a paper/contribution but a visual aid used during presentation. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a conference event in the conference-organisation domain. In CMT, Conference is a top-level class with properties like date, logo URL, and accepts Hardcopy Submissions, clearly representing a conference edition. In EKAW, Conference is a subclass of Scientific Event with the comment 'One edition of a conference.' The intended instances coincide: both represent a single conference/edition. The structural differences (CMT has it as a root class, EKAW places it under Event > Scientific Event) reflect modeling style, not semantic divergence.

Early Registered Participant is a person who registered early for a conference, while Session chair is a delegate who chairs a session. These are distinct roles/statuses with no overlap in intended instances.

Deadline hotel reservation is a deadline for booking a hotel room (logistical/accommodation), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a deadline for submitting a paper abstract (scientific contribution process). They share the parent Deadline but denote different kinds of deadlines with no overlap in instances.

The cmt property `hasProgramCommitteeMember` relates a Program Committee to its members (Program Committee Member), denoting committee membership. The iasted property `is_given_by` relates an Activity/Item to a Person, denoting who presents or gives an item. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other in the conference domain.

Workshop and Tutorial are distinct types of academic events in the conference domain. A workshop is a collaborative session focused on a specific topic, while a tutorial is an instructional/educational session. Their different positions in the class hierarchies (Workshop under Academic Event vs. Tutorial under Lecture) and their different siblings confirm they are separate concepts, not equivalent.

The two properties are completely different in type and meaning. 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item, representing a person obtaining some item. 'Nation' is a datatype property from Person to string, representing a person's nationality. They share the same domain (Person) but differ in range type (object vs datatype) and express unrelated relationships.

Property A (has_a_committee_chair) specifically relates a Committee to its Chair, a specialized role. Property B (hasMember) relates a Conference to any Person who is a member. They differ in domain (Committee vs Conference), range (Chair vs Person), and meaning (chair role vs general membership). They are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption relation between the two properties themselves.

A denotes the committee as a collective body (a group/organization), while B denotes an individual person who is a member of the program committee. These are different types of entities (group vs. person) and are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

The property authorOf in ekaw relates a Person to a Document they authored, while pay in sigkdd relates a Person to a Registration fee they paid. These are completely different relations with different ranges (Document vs Registration fee) and different semantics (authorship vs payment).
A Presenter is a person who presents at a conference, while Conference state is a state or phase of a conference. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Possible Reviewer is a subclass of Person (someone who can review a paper), while Registration fee is a subclass of Fee (a monetary amount paid for conference registration). They belong to completely different domains (people vs. financial fees) and share no instances.

Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Abstract, representing the abstract text of an invited talk. Invitation letter in iasted is a concrete document type (a letter sent to invite someone), sibling to forms, reviews, submissions, etc. These are different document types: one is an abstract/summary of a talk, the other is an invitation correspondence. They share no conceptual overlap beyond both being documents.

Both classes represent a student/member registration fee under a Registration fee parent. The iasted 'Memeber registration fee' (despite the typo) is a sibling of 'Student registration fee', and the sigkdd 'Registration Student' is a sibling of member and non-member registration fees. Both denote the same concept: a registration fee for a student/member attendee at a conference.

Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a conference session, with properties like reviewing papers and initiating calls. Author (sigkdd) is a person who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. These are distinct roles in conference organization - a session chair moderates a session while an author writes and submits papers. They share no overlap in their intended instances beyond both being persons.

In ontology A, 'Conference' denotes the academic conference event itself (with children like Conference volume and properties linking to proceedings, publishers, topics). In ontology B, 'Conference airport' is a physical building (path: Place > Building > Conference airport) where conference participants arrive. These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a transportation infrastructure facility. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated entities in the domain.

In cmt, Document is a physical artefact (parent of Paper and Review, subject of conflict-of-interest declarations). In confOf, Topic is a subject area that contributions deal with, PCs are experts on, and working events cover. They share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

Property A ('was a program committee of') links a Program committee to a Conference volume, expressing committee membership/service for a conference volume. Property B ('writes') links an Author to a Contribution, expressing authorship of a paper. They relate entirely different entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (a role/committee member), while Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They share no instances and are in completely different branches of their respective ontologies.

confOf:Reviewing_event is an administrative event representing the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions (i.e., the process of conducting reviews). edas:CallForManuscripts is a call (announcement) soliciting manuscript submissions. One is a process/event where reviewing happens; the other is a call for submissions. They denote different concepts with no clear subsumption relationship.

In the EDAS ontology, Workshop is a kind of academic event (a standalone event with its own papers, program, etc.), sibling to Paper Presentation and Talk Event. In the IASTED ontology, Session is a sub-class of Lecture, sibling to Plenary lecture and Tutorial, with child Speaker lecture. A Session here is a time-slot block within a conference program containing talks, not a Workshop. These are structurally and semantically different concepts: a Workshop is a self-contained academic event, while a Session is a scheduling unit inside a conference. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Regular contribution in the Conference ontology is a broad category that subsumes both Extended abstract and Paper, covering all standard-length and short written contributions. Short paper in confOf is a specific type of contribution distinct from Paper and Poster, representing only short-length papers. Since Regular contribution includes full Papers and Extended abstracts, it is strictly more general than Short paper.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics. In cmt, hasCo-author relates a Paper to its Co-author(s). In edas, hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper that is related to them. They connect different entity types in different directions and express different relationships (co-authorship vs. related-paper association).

The two properties operate in completely different domains: 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher, while 'has Menu' links a Meal Event to a Meal Menu. They share no conceptual overlap in the conference-organisation domain.

In EDAS, Workshop is a specific academic event type (a workshop event). In EKAW, Session is a broader grouping concept for conference sessions, and Workshop is actually a sibling of Session under Scientific Event, with Workshop Session being a child of Session. These are structurally and semantically distinct: a Workshop is a standalone event, while a Session is a time-slot container that may contain various presentations. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear, consistent direction.

A Workshop Chair is a person who chairs a specific workshop (a scientific/academic session within a conference), whereas an Organizing Committee member is a person who handles logistical organization of the conference (e.g., local arrangements, webmastering). These are distinct roles in conference organization: one is a scientific/programmatic role for a sub-event, the other is a logistical/administrative role for the whole conference. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

cmt:User is a person who interacts with the conference management system (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), whereas ekaw:Organising_Agency is an organisation that handles conference logistics (parent Organisation, siblings Academic Institution/Proceedings Publisher). One denotes an individual person, the other an organisational entity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision, representing the decision to accept a paper. Excursion in edas is a subclass of Social Event, a non-academic conference event. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

The two properties relate to different concepts: 'has a volume' assigns an integer volume number to Conference proceedings, while 'Name of conference' assigns a string name to a Conference. They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'detailsEnteredBy' (cmt) relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered conference details, while 'is_submitted_at' (Conference) relates a Conference contribution to a Conference volume where it is submitted. They connect different entity types in different directions with different semantics.

Property A (has_important_dates) links a Conference volume to Important dates, capturing submission/deadline information. Property B (writes) links an Author to a Contribution (paper). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap or subsumption exists.

Rejection in cmt is a Decision concerning paper acceptance/rejection, while Car in iasted is a Transport vehicle for conference logistics. They belong to completely different domains and share no conceptual overlap.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime capturing when something starts. However, A (edas) has domain Conference Event, which is more general than B (sigkdd) whose domain is specifically Conference. A conference is a kind of conference event, so A's property applies to a broader set of subjects. Thus A is subsumed_by B in the sense that B is the more specific property; equivalently, B subsumes A. They are not equivalent because their domains differ in generality.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'hasPostalCode' is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (postal code), while 'is_sent_before' is an object property linking Item to Time (a temporal relation). They share no semantic overlap.

Review in Conference is a document type (a review artifact), sibling to Conference contribution. Contribution in confOf is a general class of submitted works (Paper, Poster, Short paper). These are different concepts: one is a review document, the other is the contribution being reviewed. They do not overlap in intended instances.

Property A relates a Co-chair to a Committee (a committee membership role), while property B relates a Document to a Person (authorship). They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

Late paid applicant is a person who registered late and paid for a conference, while Program Committee is a committee that reviews papers. They share no instances and are from entirely different parts of the conference domain.

A 'Two Level Conference' in edas is a type of conference event (a subclass of Conference), whereas 'Program Chair' in sigkdd is a person role (subclass of Organizator/Person). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Document in EKAW denotes written artefacts (papers, abstracts, reviews, etc.) authored by persons, while Money in IASTED denotes monetary amounts (fees, taxes, tips, sponsorships) paid by persons for activities/items. These are completely disjoint domains with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person, denoting people who take part in a conference (with children like Active/Passive conference participant). Working event is a subclass of Event, denoting events such as Conference, Tutorial, Workshop. One denotes people, the other denotes events; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The property 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (capturing the expertise level assigned during review), while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material). They connect entirely different domain and range types and serve unrelated purposes in the conference organization domain.

Both classes denote the same concept: a person invited to speak at a conference. They share nearly identical labels ('Invited speaker' vs 'Invited Speaker') and both are subclasses of Person through conference-participation hierarchies. The slight difference in parent class (Conference contributor vs Presenter) does not affect the intended instances, which coincide exactly.

confOf:Conference is an academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting a conference occurrence. sigkdd:Main_office is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference hall and Hotel), denoting an office location. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (e.g., a paper being part of a proceedings volume), while property B relates a Conference to a Person (a member of the conference). They connect completely different domain and range types and describe different relationships in the conference organization domain.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. In cmt, 'hasBeenAssigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper they have been assigned to review. In edas, 'hasRelatedPaper' links an Author to a Paper they have authored. These are distinct relations in the conference domain, not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Both classes are named 'Fee' and share the same intended meaning: a monetary charge in the conference domain. They have overlapping children (Registration fee), and the iasted Fee has additional subkinds (Hotel fee, Fee for extra trip) while sigkdd has Sponzor fee. The extension of instances (monetary fees associated with conference participation) coincides, so a reference alignment would treat them as equivalent.

A Conference Trip is a social excursion associated with a conference, whereas a Welcome address is an opening speech or introductory activity. They denote different kinds of conference activities and do not share instances.

Both classes denote members of the Program Committee in a conference organization context. 'PC Member' is a standard abbreviation for 'Program Committee member'. In ekaw, PC_Member sits under Possible_Reviewer (a PC member is someone who can review papers), and its children include various chair roles. In sigkdd, Program_Committee_member sits under Organizator alongside Program_Chair and General_Chair. Despite slightly different hierarchy placement, the intended instances coincide: people serving on the program committee. The label match is exact in meaning, and the conference-domain context confirms they refer to the same role.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (the committee that organizes it). Property B links a Conference to ACM SIGKDD (the organization that holds/sponsors it). They relate a conference to different kinds of entities (a committee vs. a parent organization) and express different relationships (organizing vs. ownership/sponsorship), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully overlapping.

Conference Banquet (ekaw) is a social event that takes place during a conference (e.g., a dinner or reception). Sponsor city (iasted) is a city that provides sponsorship for a conference. One is an event/activity, the other is a geographical location/city role. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its Program Committee Members (organizational structure). In sigkdd, presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). The domains (Program Committee vs. Document) and ranges (Program Committee Member vs. Speaker) are disjoint concepts, and the relations capture different aspects of the conference domain.

confOf:Workshop is a type of event (a working event at a conference, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference (sibling of Modelling under Research > Activity before conference). These denote completely different concepts: one is an organized event/session, the other is a pre-conference research activity. No overlap in intended instances.

Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a subclass of Person, denoting someone who can serve as a reviewer (a human agent). Review in sigkdd is a subclass of Document, denoting the written review artefact. These are completely different categories of entities (person vs. document) with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person, representing a human participant in a conference (with subclasses like Author, Reviewer, etc.). In iasted, Conference hotel is a subclass of Building under Place, representing a physical venue where a conference is held. These are completely different concepts: one is a person, the other is a building/location.

Entity A is a class denoting a written document (a camera-ready paper/contribution) in a hierarchy of conference documents. Entity B is a class denoting an administrative event (the camera-ready submission phase) in a hierarchy of events. Despite sharing the words 'Camera ready', one is a document artefact and the other is a temporal/organisational event; their instances do not coincide.

The cmt `email` property relates a Person to their email address (string), while the sigkdd `Currency` property relates a Registration fee to its currency (string). They have completely different domains (Person vs. Registration fee) and denote unrelated attributes in the conference domain.

AccpetIfRoomRating is a rating value for paper reviews (a subclass of Review Rating with siblings Accept Rating, Reject Rating), while Reviewer is a person role (a subclass of Speaker under Delegate). They denote completely different kinds of entities—a review rating category versus a conference participant role—with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (has_a_steering_committee) links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a specific committee type). Property B (organisedBy) links an Event to an Organisation or Person (the agent organising the event). They differ in both domain and range: A's range is a specific committee, while B's range is an organising agent (Organisation/Person). A steering committee is not the same as an organiser, and the relations connect different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalisation of the other.

The cmt 'addedBy' property relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them, while the iasted 'give' property relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics with no overlap in meaning.

In ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' is a specific kind of Paper that has been submitted to a conference (a sibling of Camera Ready Paper, Regular Paper, etc.). In sigkdd, 'Abstract' is a sibling of Paper and Review under Document, denoting a summary document rather than a full paper. These are distinct document types in the conference domain: a submitted paper is a full paper under review, while an abstract is a short summary. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Coffee Break in edas is a specific, concrete kind of break event (a leaf class with siblings Free Time Break and Meal Break). Conference activity in iasted is a broad top-level category whose children include Coffee break, Coctail reception, Introduction, Lecture, Presentation, Registration, etc. The two entities are at very different levels of generality and do not have coinciding intended instances; Coffee Break would be a child of Conference activity rather than equivalent to it.

Accept Rating in edas is a rating value used in the paper review process (subclass of Review Rating, sibling to Reject Rating). Reviewer in iasted is a person who reviews papers (subclass of Speaker > Delegate). One is a rating/score, the other is a person role; they share no semantic overlap.

Cryptography Topic is a subject-area classification (a kind of Topic) in the EDAS ontology, while Invited Talk Abstract is a document type (a kind of Abstract under Document) in the EKAW ontology. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, 'Hotel room' denotes an individual room within a hotel (with subtypes Single/Double hotel room), whereas in sigkdd 'Hotel' denotes the entire building/establishment. These are distinct concepts at different granularity levels, not equivalent.

confOf:Poster is a type of academic contribution (a poster paper presented at a conference), sibling to Paper and Short paper under Contribution. sigkdd:Platinum_Supporter is a type of conference sponsor (a financial supporter at a sponsorship tier), sibling to Gold/Bronze/Silver supporters and Exhibitors under Sponzor. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Full Version is a full-length conference paper (a document artefact) in the cmt ontology, while Radio Communications Topic is a subject-area topic in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Document vs. Topic) and denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology Conference, 'Conference proceedings' is a published document/artefact (it has a publisher, volume, ISBN, and is issued by a Publisher). In ekaw, 'Conference Session' is a kind of event (a session within a conference, with subtypes like Industrial Session, Demo Session, etc.). One is a tangible publication and the other is a scheduled event, so they are unrelated.

Both denote post-conference social/leisure activities, but 'Excursion' is a broader category of social event while 'Full day tour' is a specific activity scheduled after the conference. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent: an excursion could be a half-day trip or reception-adjacent event, and a full day tour is a specific kind of excursion. The hierarchies differ (Social Event vs Activity after conference), suggesting related but not identical concepts.

Associated Chair is a co-chair of the entire conference (a top-level conference role), while Tutorial Chair is the chair of a specific tutorial event. They are distinct roles with different scopes; neither subsumes the other.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document type (a short version of a paper), while Medicine Topic in edas is a subject classification topic. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

A 'Conference Session' in ekaw is a scientific event (a scheduled session where papers are presented), while 'Main office' in iasted is a physical place (a building/office location). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Free Time Break is a non-academic event during a conference (a scheduled break), while Registration Non Member is a fee paid by non-members for registration. One is a temporal event, the other is a monetary fee; they share no semantic overlap.

Reject Rating is a rating value used to evaluate a submission (a child of Review Rating), whereas Abstract is a kind of document (a summary of a paper). They belong to completely different parts of the conference domain hierarchy and denote entirely different things.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, 'addedBy' links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (committee management). In edas, 'providedBy' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provided it (financial sponsorship). Different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings.

Currency in iasted denotes a monetary unit (e.g., USD, EUR), while Registration_fee in sigkdd is a fee amount paid for conference registration. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the type of money, the other is a charge. The sigkdd class has children like Registration_Non_Member and Registration_Student, confirming it represents fee categories, not currencies. No subsumption relationship exists between them.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'forEvent' links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the Academic Event it announces, while 'partOfEvent' links an Event to the Event it is part of (mereological relation). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

The cmt property hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a general participant/committee member of the conference). The Conference ontology property links a Conference part (e.g., a track or workshop) to a Track workshop chair (a specific chair role for that part). The domains differ (whole conference vs. conference part), the ranges differ (general member vs. specific chair role), and the relations are conceptually distinct.

Academia Organization in edas denotes academic institutions (universities, research institutes) as a type of organization. Organising Agency in ekaw denotes an agency that organizes conference events (e.g., professional conference organizers). These are distinct concepts: one is about the academic sector classification of an organization, the other is about the functional role of organizing an event. Their intended instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate fundamentally different things. In EDAS, 'isReviewing' has domain (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) and range Paper, i.e., it links a person/role to the paper they are reviewing. In EKAW, 'reviewOfPaper' has domain Review and range Paper, i.e., it links a review document to the paper it reviews. The domains are disjoint (person/role vs. review document), so the properties do not relate the same kinds of entities in the same direction; they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference contributor (Person who contributes to a conference, e.g. author or speaker) and Member (a Participant sub-type in confOf, alongside Regular and Student) overlap in extension but are not equivalent: a contributor is specifically someone who contributes a paper or talk, whereas a Member is any registered participant who is a member of the organization. Neither subsumes the other cleanly, so related is the best fit.

PaperFullVersion in cmt is a full-length conference paper (a document artefact), while ComputerNetworksSecurityTopic in edas is a subject-area topic under the Topic hierarchy. They belong to completely different parts of the domain (documents vs. topics) and share no instances.

A 'Two Level Conference' in EDAS is a type of conference (a conference event with two review levels), while a 'Demo Chair' in EKAW is a person who chairs demonstrations. One is an event/conference, the other is a person/role; they are completely different concepts despite both appearing under a Person-like hierarchy in EDAS's path listing.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'min Choice' is a datatype property from Social event/Working event to positiveInteger (likely about minimum number of choices for a working event), while 'lists Event' is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event (about listing events in a brochure or website). They share no semantic overlap.

hasReview relates a Paper to its Review (paper -> review). write relates a Person to an Item they author (person -> item). Different domains, different ranges, different semantics: one captures the review relationship on a paper, the other captures authorship by a person. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Microelectronics Topic is a subject-area topic under Topic in the edas ontology, denoting a research area. Program Committee is an organizational committee in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Computer Networks Sensor Topic' is a specific subject-area topic (a subclass of 'Computer Networks Topic') used to classify papers. In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Organizing Committee' is a committee responsible for organizing a conference. There is no overlap in intended instances, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas iasted:Worker_non_speaker is a person role (subclass of Non speaker under Delegate). They denote completely different categories—an event vs. a delegate role—so they are unrelated.

In iasted, Review is a specific document type (a review of a submission), sibling to Submission, Form, Invitation letter, etc. In sigkdd, Paper is the submitted article itself, sibling to Review and Abstract. These denote different concepts: a review document versus a paper. They share the parent Document but are distinct entities in the conference domain.

cmt:Paper is a specific kind of document that has been submitted for review (it has reviewers assigned, bids, decisions, etc.). Conference:Submitted_contribution is a more general class representing any written contribution that has been submitted, which includes both regular and reviewed contributions. Since cmt:Paper represents a submitted paper under review, it is a subtype of Submitted_contribution. The cmt ontology does not distinguish between submitted and accepted papers at the class level, but the properties (assigned to reviewers, has bid, has decision) indicate it is in the review process, making it a submitted contribution. Thus cmt:Paper is subsumed by Conference:Submitted_contribution.

In ontology A, 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. an informational artefact provided to attendees. In ontology B, 'Departure' is a post-conference activity (sibling of Full day tour). One is a document/information resource, the other is an event/activity; they share no domain overlap.

Conference participant is a broad class covering all people who attend a conference (including active and passive participants), while Program Chair is a specific organizational role responsible for the scientific program. A Program Chair is not a general participant concept, and a Conference participant is not an organizer. The two concepts occupy different positions in the domain hierarchy and do not share instances.

Both are datatype properties with range dateTime. 'is dated on' has domain Activity (a broad superclass covering any scheduled event or activity), while 'Start of conference' has domain Conference (a specific kind of activity). Thus 'is dated on' is more general, subsuming 'Start of conference' as a broader temporal-annotation property applicable to all activities rather than just conferences.

`hasKeyword` applies to Contribution and captures paper keywords, while `hasLastName` applies to Person and captures a person's surname. They relate to completely different domains and concepts, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, 'hasBeenAssigned' means a Reviewer has been assigned a Paper to review (Reviewer -> Paper). In edas, 'isReviewing' has domain including Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, and TPC Member, and range Paper. The edas property is more general because it applies to a broader set of roles (not just Reviewer) who may be reviewing a paper. The core relation (a person assigned to review a paper) is the same, but edas covers additional roles beyond cmt's Reviewer, so cmt's hasBeenAssigned is subsumed by edas's isReviewing.

partOfEvent relates an Event to its sub-Event (part-whole relation between events), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item they present. Different domains (Event vs Person), different ranges (Event vs Activity/Item), and different semantics (mereological vs agentive action).

The confOf 'remark' property attaches a textual string to a Contribution, while the sigkdd 'Date' property attaches a dateTime to a Deadline. They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings; there is no overlap or subsumption between them.

confOf:Organization represents an institution (e.g., Company, University) that employs people and has an address; sigkdd:Person represents a human individual (Listener, Organizator, Speaker) with a name, email, and nationality. They are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's hasCity specifically relates an Organization or Person to a City, whereas iasted's occupy relates a Person to a more general location (Building, City, or State). hasCity is thus a more specific relation than occupy, so it is subsumed_by occupy rather than equivalent.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to its title (string), while the edas 'has City' property relates Contact Information to a city (string). They have completely different domains (Paper vs. Contact Information) and denote entirely different attributes of different entities. There is no semantic overlap between a paper's title and a contact's city.

cmt:User is a person who interacts with the conference system (parent Person, children Administrator/Author/Reviewer), while edas:BreakEvent is a non-academic event during a conference such as a coffee break or meal break. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Review Form in EDAS denotes a form/document used to collect review data, while Possible Reviewer in EKAW denotes a person who could serve as a reviewer. These are completely different kinds of entities (artefact vs. person), so they are unrelated.

cmt:Paper is a general class for any submitted paper (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties covering bidding, assignment, decisions, etc.), whereas edas:PublishedPaper is a specific subclass of edas:Paper restricted to papers that have been published. Thus cmt:Paper is strictly more general than edas:PublishedPaper, so cmt:Paper is subsumed_by edas:PublishedPaper.

confOf:City denotes a geographical location (e.g., where an Organization or Person is located), while ekaw:Research_Topic denotes a subject area covered by events or papers. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'addedBy' records which Administrator added a Program Committee Member (an administrative/management relation).
