In the Conference ontology, 'has_a_committee_co-chair' links a Committee to its Co-chair (a structural committee-composition relation). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and serve different purposes.

confOf:University is an organization where scholars study, while edas:NumericalReviewQuestion is a type of review question used in paper reviews. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to a Review (the review document/artefact). In edas, 'isReviewedBy' links a Paper to a person (Reviewer, Conference Chair, etc.) who performs the reviewing. One connects a paper to its review artefact, the other connects a paper to the person who reviews it. These are semantically distinct relations, not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person and has subclasses such as Author, Reviewer, and Program Committee Member, denoting people who participate in a conference. In the Conference ontology, Review is a subclass of Conference document, denoting a written review artefact. One is a person role, the other is a document; they share no instances and are unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document representing the written article submitted for review. In sigkdd, Author_of_paper is a subclass of Person > Speaker > Author, representing a person who authored a paper. These are fundamentally different entities: one is a document, the other is a person/author role.

The cmt 'memberOfConference' property links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation). The Conference ontology 'has_parts' property links a Conference volume to a Conference part (mereological part-whole relation). These are fundamentally different relations: one denotes membership of a person in a conference, the other denotes that a conference volume has a conference part. The domains and ranges are completely different, and the semantics (membership vs. part-of) are unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a document submitted for review with authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions. In iasted, Credit_card is a financial item under Card. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (i.e., assigning a chair to a track/workshop/tutorial). Property B links a Conference Chair, Session Chair, or TPC Member to a Call (i.e., a chair initiating a call for papers). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different: one assigns a chair role to a conference part, the other records a chair initiating a call. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only tangentially related.
Committee member is a person serving on a committee, while Registration SIGMOD Member is a registration fee category. They denote completely different concepts.

cmt's Document is a top-level abstraction whose children are Paper and Review (i.e., any conference artefact). Conference's Reviewed contribution is a specific subclass of Submitted contribution that has undergone review, with children Accepted/Rejected contribution. The two do not share instances: a Document in cmt may be an unreviewed Paper or a Review, while a Reviewed contribution is a particular written contribution that has been reviewed. There is no subsumption either, since cmt's Document is not defined as a contribution and Conference's hierarchy does not make Reviewed contribution a kind of generic Document. They are therefore unrelated.

The two properties have different domains (Contribution vs Conference), different ranges (string vs dateTime), and different intended meanings: 'remark' is a free-text annotation on a contribution, while 'manuscriptDueOn' is a deadline date for a conference. They do not denote the same relation.

The property 'obtain' in iasted is an object property relating Person to Item (a person obtains an item), while 'E mail' in sigkdd is a datatype property relating Person to a string (a person's email address). They have completely different meanings, domains/ranges, and types.

Invited_speaker is a subclass of Person/Conference_contributor, denoting a human role at a conference. Trip_city is a subclass of City, denoting a geographical location. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and denote completely different kinds of entities.

Administrative event in confOf covers organizational workflow events such as submission, reviewing, registration, and camera-ready, whereas Break Event in edas covers rest/social break events such as coffee breaks, meals, and free time. Their intended instances do not overlap, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Science_Worker is a broad category of person (sibling of Author, Participant, Scholar, etc.) denoting any science worker. iasted:Student_lecturer is a highly specific subclass of Lecturer (itself under Speaker/Author/Delegate) denoting a student who lectures. The intended instances do not coincide: a generic science worker is not necessarily a student lecturer, and a student lecturer is a very specific role not captured by the broad Science Worker class. No subsumption holds either, as Science_Worker is not a superclass of Student_lecturer in the iasted taxonomy.

The cmt 'paper ID' is a datatype property mapping a Paper to a numeric unsignedLong identifier, whereas the edas 'is Written By' is an object property linking a Paper to its Author. They share the same domain (Paper) but have completely different ranges and meanings, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Conference denotes the entire academic conference event (a working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). ekaw:Conference_Banquet is a specific social event (a dinner/gala) held during a conference. These are completely different concepts: one is the conference itself, the other is a social sub-event within a conference. No subsumption relation holds between them either.

These properties are completely different. 'has a URL' is a datatype property linking a Conference www object to a string (a web address). 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item they receive or acquire. They have different domains, different ranges, different types, and no semantic overlap.

Property A (has_a_publisher) relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher, while property B (hasTopic) relates Conference/Paper to a Topic. These are completely different relations in the conference domain: one assigns a publishing entity to proceedings, the other assigns a subject topic to a paper or conference. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely disjoint.

The confOf 'employed By' property relates a Person to an Organization they work for, while the iasted 'is made from' property relates an Item to another Item it is constructed from. These are entirely different relations with disjoint domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

In ekaw, Location is the range of 'held In' (Event -> Location), denoting where an event takes place. In sigkdd, Place has children like Conference hall, Hotel, Main office, and is the range of 'can stay in' (Person -> Place), denoting where a person can stay. Place is more general, covering lodging and offices, while Location in ekaw is specifically about event venues. The ekaw Location concept is narrower than sigkdd's Place, so ekaw Location is subsumed_by sigkdd Place.

In the edas ontology, Author is a subclass of Person — it denotes a human being who writes papers. In the iasted ontology, Author information form is a subclass of Form under Document — it denotes a physical/digital form/document that an author fills out. These are completely different categories: a person vs. a document. There is no subsumption relationship between them, and they are not related.

Property A captures the date of issue of a conference document (range date), while property B captures the title of a contribution (range string). They denote completely different attributes of different (though related) entities, so they are unrelated.

Review Rating in edas is a rating value (Accept/Reject/etc.) assigned to a paper, while Document in sigkdd is a document artifact (Paper, Abstract, Review). They are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Contribution is a scholarly work (paper, poster, short paper) authored and reviewed, while iasted:Money is a financial entity (fees, sponsorship, taxes, tips) paid by persons for activities/items. These are completely disjoint domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (is a starting date) is a datatype property with domain Important dates and range date, representing when something starts. Property B (location Of) is an object property with domain Location and range Event, representing the spatial location of an event. They relate completely different kinds of things (dates vs. locations) and have incompatible property types (datatype vs. object property).

A Paper in cmt is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, with authors, reviews, and acceptance decisions. A Transport vehicle in iasted is a physical vehicle (car, taxi, shuttle bus, van) used for conference logistics. These denote completely unrelated concepts despite both being subclasses of a broad Item/Document-like root.

Active_conference_participant in the Conference ontology is a broad class covering any person who actively participates (e.g., gives presentations), with Regular author as a sibling rather than a parent. Author in edas is specifically a person who writes papers. The two classes overlap (authors are active participants, and edas Author has Presenter as a subclass), but neither subsumes the other: Active_conference_participant includes non-author active roles, while edas Author is narrower than the general active-participant concept. They are related but not equivalent.

These properties are completely different. `registrationDueOn` is a datatype property from Conference to dateTime, representing the registration deadline. `eventOnList` is an object property from Event to Programme Brochure/Web Site, relating an event to its published materials. They have different domains, different ranges (literal vs. object), and entirely different semantics.

confOf's Science Worker is a broad scholarly/research professional (sibling to Scholar, Author, etc.), while sigkdd's Organizing Committee member is a specific conference-organisation role under Organizator alongside chairs and webmaster. The former denotes a scientific professional by occupation; the latter denotes a committee role for a specific event. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In confOf, Company is a subclass of Organization, denoting a corporate entity. In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person, denoting an individual human sponsor. These are disjoint kinds of entities (organization vs. person), so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other in a meaningful way for this alignment.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume, whereas 'employedBy' links a Person to an Organization. They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in domain or range.

has_a_URL relates a Conference www to a string representing its web address, while hasEmail relates a Person to a string representing an email address. They have different domains (Conference www vs Person), different intended meanings (URL vs email), and no overlap in the kinds of things they connect.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference management (a kind of Chairman under Person), while Presenter state is a state/status concept under State. They denote entirely different categories of entities: one is a human role, the other is a state value. No overlap in intended instances.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. 'has a location' relates a Conference volume to a string (a textual location), while 'has amount of' relates Money to an integer (a monetary quantity). They share no conceptual overlap in the conference domain.

In cmt, `title` has domain Paper (a written document submitted to the conference). In confOf, `has title` has domain Social event / Working event (gatherings or activities, not documents). The two properties relate titles to completely different kinds of entities, so they do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

The two properties operate on disjoint domains and ranges. In EDAS, 'is Initiated By' links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to specific committee roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) who initiate it. In IASTED, 'is sent by' links an Item (a document/artefact) to a Person who sends it. The domain concepts (Call vs Item) and range concepts (committee roles vs Person) differ, and the relations denote different actions (initiating a call vs sending an item).

These two datatype properties operate in completely different contexts. `has_a_degree` has domain Review preference and range int, capturing the degree or strength of a reviewer's preference for a paper. `defaultChoice` has domain Social event and Working event and range positiveInteger, annotated with 'confTool', and appears to capture a default choice value for events (e.g., a default registration or participation option). They relate to different domain entities (review preferences vs. social/working events) and encode different domain semantics, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and at most only weakly related by both being integer-valued datatype properties.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Program committee (organisational structure of a conference). Property B links a Person to an Activity or Item (someone giving a presentation or item). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

In EDAS, Conference Chair is a specific role (the person chairing the conference), a sibling of Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member, etc. In EKAW, Conference Participant is a broad superclass subsuming many roles including PC Chair, Session Chair, Demo Chair, etc. Thus EKAW's Conference Participant is more general than EDAS's Conference Chair; the chair is one kind of participant. The two are not equivalent.

In iasted, Place is a general class with children Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office, Session room. In sigkdd, Main office is a child of Place (alongside Conference hall, Hotel). Thus iasted:Place is strictly more general than sigkdd:Main_office, which is one of its subtypes.

In ekaw, Negative_Review is a subclass of Review, so the edas Review class is strictly more general than the ekaw Negative_Review class. They are not equivalent because the former covers all reviews while the latter only covers negative ones.
Author is a person who writes/submits papers, while Deadline is a temporal entity representing a submission/notification date. They share no domain overlap.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a document (subclass of Paper) representing the abstract text of a paper. Best Student Paper Award in sigkdd is an award given to a student paper. One is a written document/artifact, the other is an honor/award. They share the word 'Paper' but denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The edas `has Cost Amount` property links a Sponsorship to an integer representing a monetary cost amount, while the sigkdd `Name of sponsor` property links a Sponzor to a string representing the sponsor's name. They have different domains (Sponsorship vs Sponzor), different ranges (int vs string), and denote entirely different attributes (cost amount vs sponsor name).

hasFirstName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's first name), whereas writtenBy is an object property from Document to Person (indicating authorship). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have incompatible ranges (string vs Person), so they are unrelated.

Review preference in Conference denotes a reviewer's preference/expertise assignment for reviewing a topic or submission (with properties like degree, review reference, belonging to reviewers). Paper in sigkdd is a document submitted by an author. These are completely different concepts: one is a review-assignment preference, the other is a written document. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.

The confOf 'writes' property specifically relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), denoting authorship. The iasted 'need' property relates a Person to an Item, denoting a requirement or need. These are different relations with different semantics, domains, and ranges; they do not denote the same concept.

confOf:Contribution denotes a written scholarly artefact (Paper, Poster, Short paper) submitted to a conference, with properties like abstract, keyword, title, and writtenBy. iasted:Activity denotes a temporal occurrence or event (Conference activity, Activity before/after conference) with properties like isHeldIn, isDatedOn, isGivenBy. These are fundamentally different categories: one is a document/artefact, the other is an event/activity. They share no instance overlap and no subsumption relationship holds.

The two properties relate different entities and in opposite directions. `is Reviewing` links a reviewer role (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to a Paper, whereas `has Review` links a Paper to a Review. They are not inverses of each other (a Review is not the same as a Reviewer), and they do not share the same domain or range types, so they are unrelated.

In iasted, Fee is a broad superclass covering Hotel fee, Registration fee, Fee for extra trip, etc. In sigkdd, Registration fee is a specific fee with subclasses for different member categories. Thus iasted:Fee is strictly more general than sigkdd:Registration fee, so the relation is subsumes.

Entity A is a Reviewer (a Person who reviews papers), while entity B is a Positive Review (a Document that is a review with positive evaluation). They are completely different concepts: one is an agent role, the other is a document artefact. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Medicine Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area for conference papers (alongside siblings like Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). Card in iasted is a subclass of Item representing payment cards (with child Credit card and siblings like Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization representing a corporate entity (sibling of University), while sigkdd:Review is a subclass of Document representing a review document (sibling of Abstract and Paper). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

An Attendee in EDAS is any person who attends the conference, regardless of registration timing. An Early Registered Participant in EKAW is specifically a participant who registered early, a narrower concept. The two classes overlap (an attendee may have registered early) but are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since EKAW's hierarchy distinguishes early vs. late registered participants under Conference Participant.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper). In iasted, 'need' links a Person to an Item (expressing that a person needs some item). The domains (Paper vs Person), ranges (Reviewer vs Item), and intended meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

The property 'has gender' in the Conference ontology captures the biological or social gender of a Person, while 'Nation' in the sigkdd ontology captures the nationality or country of a Person. These are entirely different attributes of a person, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person.

Attendee denotes a person who attends a conference, while Paper Author denotes a person who authored a paper. An attendee need not be an author, and an author need not attend the conference. These are distinct concepts that merely share the parent class Person.

confOf Member is a broad participant role (sibling of Regular and Student participants), while ekaw SC Member is specifically a Steering Committee member (a subtype of PC Member). These denote different concepts in the conference organization domain with no clear overlap in intended instances.

A 'Passive conference participant' is a person who attends a conference but does not actively present or organize, while a 'Conference city' is a geographic location where a conference takes place. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Person vs City) and denote completely different kinds of entities.

In ekaw, 'Regular Paper' is a specific kind of Paper (a full-length conference paper, as opposed to Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Industrial Paper, etc.). In sigkdd, 'Abstract' is a sibling of Paper and Review under Document, representing a summary/abstract document. A regular paper is a complete paper, not an abstract; an abstract is not a regular paper. These are distinct document types in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

A Flyer in EKAW is a promotional document published by an organisation (e.g., conference flyer, brochure), whereas an Author information form in IASTED is a specific administrative form that authors fill out. They share only the distant ancestor Document, but their intended instances are disjoint: a flyer is not an author information form and vice versa.
Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Multimedia Topic is a subject-area topic for categorizing papers. They share no instances and no semantic relationship.

Both are conference leadership roles involving persons, but they are distinct positions. cmt's Associated Chair is a specific co-chair role (sibling to Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair), while ekaw's PC Chair is the chair of the Program Committee. An Associated Chair may or may not be the PC Chair, and the sibling structures differ significantly (cmt distinguishes Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, and Associated Chair as separate roles). They overlap in being high-level committee chairs but are not equivalent.

In cmt, ProgramCommitteeMember is a specific role: a conference member who serves on the program committee (with properties like memberOfProgramCommittee, maxPapers, addedBy). In ekaw, Possible_Reviewer is a broader class denoting any person who could potentially review a paper (properties hasReviewer, reviewWrittenBy, reviewerOfPaper all point to it as the reviewer type). The ekaw class PC_Member is a child of Possible_Reviewer, indicating that PC members are a subset of possible reviewers. Thus Possible_Reviewer subsumes ProgramCommitteeMember: every PC member is a possible reviewer, but not vice versa.

Conference Chair in cmt is a leadership role responsible for overseeing the conference, sitting under Chairman/Conference Member. Late paid applicant in Conference ontology is a registration status for someone who paid late, sitting under Paid applicant. These denote completely different concepts: a conference official vs. a late-fee-paying registrant. No overlap in intended instances.

In Conference ontology, 'Passive conference participant' is a specific subclass of 'Conference participant' (distinguished from 'Active conference participant'), denoting attendees who do not actively present or contribute. In confOf, 'Participant' is a broad class covering all kinds of participants (with subclasses like Member, Regular, Student, and siblings like Author, Chair PC, etc.). The confOf Participant is more general, subsuming the narrower Passive conference participant.

Both classes represent reviews of conference papers, sharing the same path (Document > Review) and similar siblings (e.g., Paper, Programme). The ekaw ontology further specifies Review with properties like 'review Of Paper' and 'review Written By', which align with the concept of a paper review in the conference domain. The edas ontology also has a 'hasReview' property relating Paper to Review. These are the same concept in the conference domain.

Talk Event in edas is a specific kind of academic event (a talk/presentation), whereas Scientific Event in ekaw is a broad category encompassing conferences, sessions, tracks, workshops, and individual presentations. A Talk Event is thus a narrower concept subsumed by Scientific Event.

Conference announcement is a document (a notification/announcement about a conference), while Conference airport is a physical place/building (an airport associated with a conference). They belong to entirely different hierarchies (documents vs. places) and share no instances.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In cmt, 'assignedByAdministrator' links a Reviewer to the Administrator who assigned them (reviewer -> administrator). In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to the Contribution they review (reviewer -> paper). These are different relations: one is about an assignment relationship to an administrator, the other is about reviewing a paper. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

The two properties have different domains and different meanings. In cmt, 'assignedByReviewer' links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (indicating assignment of an external reviewer by a regular reviewer). In edas, 'isReviewHistoryOf' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (indicating that a review history record belongs to a reviewer). The domains (External Reviewer vs Personal Review History) are distinct concepts, and the relations capture different aspects of the conference domain.

The cmt `title` property maps a Paper to its title string, while the iasted `has_amount_of` property maps Money to an integer amount. They operate on completely unrelated domains (Paper vs Money) and carry different semantics (a textual title vs a numeric monetary amount), so they are unrelated.

cmt:hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while iasted:is_used_for links an Item to an Activity or Money (what the item is used for). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf Workshop is an academic working event where papers are presented, while edas Free Time Break is a non-academic break event (sibling of Coffee Break and Meal Break). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper, indicating which paper a reviewer reads. In the Conference ontology, reviews is a property whose domain is Review (the review document/artefact) and range is Reviewed contribution, expressing which contribution a review evaluates. The domains differ (Reviewer vs Review) and the semantics differ: one is about a person reading a paper, the other about a review document evaluating a contribution. They are not equivalent.

Property A (has_a_name) assigns a name to entities like Conference, Conference part, Publisher, and Topic. Property B (location) specifies where a Social event or Working event is held. They relate different kinds of entities to different attributes (name vs. physical location), so they are unrelated.

Invited speaker is a specific conference role for a person invited to give a talk, while Science Worker is a broad professional category of persons involved in science. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other in the context of these ontologies.

Social Event in ekaw is a non-scientific gathering such as a banquet or trip, while Fee in iasted is a monetary charge. These are completely different domain concepts with disjoint intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote different relations. cmt's enterConferenceDetails has domain Administrator and range Conference, representing an administrator entering conference details. edas's relatesTo has domain Document and ranges over Academic Event, Conference, ConferenceSession, and Person, representing a document being related to various entities. There is no overlap in the types of things they relate or the meaning of the relation.

confOf:Workshop and iasted:Tutorial denote different kinds of conference events. A Workshop is a collaborative working event, while a Tutorial is an instructional lecture. They are sibling concepts within their respective hierarchies (Workshop is a sibling of Tutorial in confOf), not the same concept.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad superclass encompassing all persons involved in the conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, PC members). In the Conference ontology, Registeered applicant is a specific subclass of Conference applicant, representing someone who has registered (and whose child is Paid applicant). A Conference Member in cmt is not necessarily an applicant who registered, and a Registered applicant is not necessarily a conference member in the cmt organizational sense. These denote different concepts with no clear subsumption relationship.
Tutorial is a scientific event (an individual presentation), while Speaker is a person who gives a presentation. They are disjoint categories (event vs. person) with no alignment relationship.

confOf's Member is a participant who is a member of the conference (e.g., a non-student, non-regular participant), while ekaw's Early-Registered_Participant is specifically a participant who registered early. These are orthogonal classifications: a Member could be early- or late-registered, and an Early-Registered_Participant could be a Member, Regular, or Student. There is no subsumption relationship between them, and they do not denote the same concept.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. In cmt, hasAuthor links Paper to Author (document -> person). In Conference, contributes links Person to Conference document (person -> document). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. An inverse property is not equivalent under standard alignment criteria.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, memberOfConference links a Conference Member (a person) to a Conference they are a member of. In the Conference ontology, belong_to_a_conference_volume links Important dates (temporal/administrative entities) to a Conference volume (a specific edition/proceedings). The domains (Conference Member vs Important dates) and ranges (Conference vs Conference volume) are disjoint, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

An Author (cmt) is a person who writes/submits a paper, while a Presenter (ekaw) is a conference participant who presents at the conference. These are distinct roles: an author need not present (e.g., co-authors, authors of posters/demos), and a presenter need not be an author (e.g., invited speakers). The ontologies define them with different properties and sibling structures, and neither subsumes the other.

The edas property 'is Review History Of' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer, recording who performed a review. The sigkdd property 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document, indicating which document a speaker presents. These relate entirely different domain concepts (review history vs. presentation, reviewer vs. speaker/document) and have no semantic overlap.

confOf:Submission_event is an event (a temporal occurrence of submitting contributions), sitting under Event > Administrative event alongside other events like Registration and Reviewing. iasted:Record_of_attendance is a document/artefact (a physical or digital record), sitting under Item > Document alongside Form, Submission, Review, etc. One is an event, the other is a document; they are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Member_PC is a person who serves on a program committee and reviews papers (subclass of Person, domain of reviewes and expertOn). edas:TextualReviewQuestion is a type of review question (a question item in a review form, sibling of NumericalReviewQuestion). One is a person role, the other is a question artifact; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Although both properties have domain Reviewer, they relate the reviewer to fundamentally different things. In cmt, 'write Review' connects a Reviewer to a Review (the actual review document/artifact produced). In the Conference ontology, 'has a review reference or expertise' connects a Reviewer to Review expertise or Review preference (meta-information about the reviewer's expertise and preferences for paper assignment). The ranges are disjoint concepts, so these properties are unrelated.

These properties operate in completely different domains. Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or review preference, capturing what topics a reviewer is qualified or willing to review. Property B links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. They have different domains (Reviewer vs. Document), different ranges (Review expertise/Review preference vs. Speaker), and serve entirely unrelated functions in the conference organization domain.

Closing Talk and Invited Talk are distinct conference event types. A closing talk is the final talk of a conference, whereas an invited talk is a presentation given by an invited speaker. They share the broader ancestor of a talk/presentation event, but neither subsumes the other and their intended instances do not coincide.

edas:Person is a broad class covering all people in the conference domain (authors, reviewers, attendees, chairs, etc.), while ekaw:Conference_Participant is a narrower subclass of ekaw:Person denoting only those who participate in the conference. edas:Person subsumes ekaw:Conference_Participant because every conference participant is a person, but not every person (e.g., a non-attending author or external reviewer) is necessarily a conference participant.

Conference announcement is a document type (a child of Conference document) used to announce a conference, whereas Tutorial is an academic activity/event (a child of Lecture under Activity). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote different kinds of entities.

Both classes represent reviews of conference papers/contributions. In Conference ontology, Review is a Conference document with properties 'has a review' (Reviewed contribution -> Review) and 'reviews' (Review -> Reviewed contribution), clearly denoting a document containing a paper review. In edas, Review is a Document sibling to Paper, Programme, etc. Both are documents that serve as reviews in the conference domain, and their instances coincide.

confOf's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event, a specific sub-type of event. ekaw's hasEvent links an Event to an Event in general. Since Administrative event is a narrower range than Event, hasAdministrativeEvent is subsumed by hasEvent.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations. `expertOn` in confOf links a Member PC to a Topic (indicating expertise), while `submit` in sigkdd links an Author to a Paper (indicating submission). The domains (Member PC vs. Author), ranges (Topic vs. Paper), and the nature of the relation (expertise vs. submission) are all different, so these properties are unrelated.

Hotel room (a place where attendees sleep/stay) and Conference hall (a place where conference sessions are held) are distinct types of places in the conference domain. They are siblings under Place in their respective ontologies but denote different concepts with non-overlapping instances.

The EKAW property 'technicallyOrganisedBy' (a subproperty of 'organisedBy') relates an event to the entity that technically organises it, whereas the IASTED property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a lecture or a presentation). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

Break Event in edas is a non-academic conference event (e.g., coffee break, meal break), while Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes the conference. These are completely different categories of entities (event vs. person) with no semantic overlap.

Session in ekaw is a scientific event (e.g., conference session, demo session, poster session), while Fee in sigkdd is a monetary charge (registration fee, sponsor fee). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'is held after' links an Activity to a Time (temporal relation), while 'can stay in' links a Person to a Place (accommodation relation). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a conference session, while Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is a person who chairs a tutorial. These are distinct organizational roles in a conference: a session chair manages a paper presentation session, whereas a tutorial chair oversees a tutorial event. They are sibling-level concepts under Person/Conference Participant but denote different responsibilities, so they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Person (specifically a Conference Member who submits/writes papers). In edas, ConferenceSession is an event/session within a conference (a domain of hasRelatedDocument and relatesTo). One denotes a person, the other an event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level working event representing the entire conference, sibling to Workshop and Tutorial. In ekaw, Workshop Session is a specific session within a workshop, sibling to Conference Session, Demo Session, etc. These denote different granularities of events and do not overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'writes' property relates an Author to a Contribution (an author writes a paper). The edas 'providedBy' property relates a Sponsorship to an Organization (a sponsorship is provided by an organization). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and have no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Both classes are named Author and share the same parent Speaker in their respective ontologies, with paths rooted in Person/Delegate. They both represent conference participants who author papers. The children differ (specific subtypes like Lecturer vs. Author of paper), but the core concept of an Author as a person who writes a paper is the same in both ontologies.

Associated Chair is a person role (a conference committee member who chairs sessions), while Speaker lecture is an activity/event (a lecture session). They belong to completely different ontological categories (person vs. activity) and share no domain overlap.

These classes denote entirely different concepts. 'Two Level Conference' in edas is a type of conference (an event), while 'Registration Student' in sigkdd is a registration fee category for students. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are subclasses of Person, but they denote overlapping yet distinct concepts. ekaw's Conference Participant encompasses all conference attendees including non-organizers (e.g., Early/Late Registered Participant, Presenter, Student), while sigkdd's Organizator is specifically an organizer (with children like General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster). The ekaw ontology has separate classes such as OC Member for organizing committee members, indicating Conference Participant is broader than Organizator. They overlap (organizers are participants) but neither subsumes the other cleanly since sigkdd's hierarchy also includes Listener and Speaker as separate siblings, suggesting a different partitioning of persons.

In iasted, 'Introduction of speaker' is a subclass of Activity > Conference activity > Introduction, making it an event/activity where a speaker is introduced. In sigkdd, 'Speaker' is a subclass of Person, denoting the human role. One is an activity, the other is a person; they are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing the call for submissions, while Deadline Abstract Submission is a specific temporal deadline for abstract submission. They are different kinds of entities: one is a document/announcement, the other is a date/deadline. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Dining Place in edas is a subclass of Place, denoting a physical location where dining occurs. Conference Banquet in ekaw is a subclass of Social Event, denoting the event/activity of a banquet itself. One is a place, the other is an event, so they are not equivalent. However, a Conference Banquet typically takes place at a Dining Place, so they are related.

These properties have fundamentally different domains and semantics. In cmt, 'addProgramCommitteeMember' is an action performed by an Administrator to add a person as a Program Committee Member. In the Conference ontology, 'has_members' is a structural partitive relation from a Committee to its Committee members. The cmt property is an administrative action (domain: Administrator), while the Conference property is a membership relation (domain: Committee). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. In edas, 'relatedToEvent' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (a paper to its presentation event). In ekaw, 'listsEvent' links a Programme Brochure or Web Site (a document) to an Event it lists. The domains (Accepted Paper vs. Programme Brochure/Web Site) and ranges (Paper Presentation vs. Event) are disjoint, so these are not the same relation.

hasAuthor is an object property linking a Paper to an Author (person), while has_an_ISBN is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to a string (ISBN identifier). They relate completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated relations.

Organisation in ekaw denotes an organisational entity (e.g., Academic Institution, Proceedings Publisher) that organises events and publishes documents. Document in sigkdd denotes a written artefact (e.g., Abstract, Paper, Review) that is presented or submitted. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties relate completely different entities in different directions. In cmt, 'memberOfProgramCommittee' links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (membership relation). In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (authorship/presentation relation). They share no semantic overlap.

These properties operate in different domains and directions. 'has_a_committee_chair' links a Committee to its Chair (committee -> chair), while 'isInitiatedBy' links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the person/role who initiated it (call -> chair/TPC member). The domains (Committee vs Call) and the intended semantics (committee leadership vs call initiation) are distinct, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Both classes denote the same social event in a conference: a reception (cocktail reception). confOf places Reception under Social event alongside Banquet and Trip, while iasted places Coctail reception under Conference activity. Despite different hierarchy positions, the intended instances coincide: a welcome/social gathering event at a conference. The labels are near-synonymous (Reception vs Coctail reception), and both represent the same domain concept.

Workshop in edas is an academic event (subclass of Conference Event > Academic Event) where papers are presented and academic activities occur. Exhibitor in sigkdd is a type of sponsor (subclass of Sponzor) that exhibits at the conference. These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a sponsor/exhibitor entity. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two entities denote completely different concepts. In ekaw, Conference Session is a type of scientific event/session (a temporal occurrence in a conference programme, with siblings like Demo Session, Poster Session, etc.). In sigkdd, Organizator is a type of person who organizes the conference (with children like General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Chairman in cmt is a leadership role (parent of Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair) responsible for marking conflicts of interest. Registeered applicant in Conference is a person who has registered for a conference (parent of Paid applicant). These denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties denote completely different concepts. `has VAT` captures the value added tax (a monetary/tax amount) associated with Social/Working events, with range string. `is dated on` captures the date/time on which an Activity occurs, with range dateTime. They relate different kinds of information (tax vs. scheduling) and have different domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different entities. enableVirtualMeeting connects Administrator to Conference (an administrator enabling a virtual meeting for a conference), while is_given_by connects Presentation to Active conference participant (who gives a presentation). Different domain, different range, different semantics.

cmt:Paper is a document submitted to a conference (subclass of Document, with authors, reviewers, decisions, etc.). edas:ComputerNetworksSwitchingTopic is a specific subject-area topic (subclass of Topic) used to classify papers. They denote completely different kinds of entities: a document vs. a classification topic. No alignment relation holds.

confOf:University is a specific kind of organization (an academic institution), while ekaw:Organisation is a broader class that includes Academic Institution, Organising Agency, and Proceedings Publisher. University is a specialization of Organisation, not equivalent to it.

Organization denotes an entity such as a conference organizer, university, or company, while Currency denotes a monetary unit (e.g., USD, EUR). These are completely disjoint concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Committee member in Conference is a general class for any member of a committee (with children Chair and Co-chair, and siblings including various conference roles). SC Member in ekaw is specifically a member of the Scientific Committee (SC), a subcommittee of the Programme Committee (PC). While both denote committee members, SC Member is a narrower role within the PC/SC structure, whereas Committee member is broader and not tied to a specific committee type. They overlap but are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Location is a general class for where an Event is held (range of 'held In'). In sigkdd, Hotel is a specific kind of Place (sibling of Conference hall, Main office). A Hotel is one possible location, but the two classes do not denote the same concept: Location is more general, and Hotel is a specific venue type. They are not equivalent, and since Hotel is not a subclass of Location in ekaw's hierarchy, the safest reference relation is unrelated rather than subsumed_by.

hasFax and E-mail are distinct contact channels. Both are datatype properties on Person with range string, but they denote different attributes (fax number vs email address). No subsumption holds between them.

confOf:Conference denotes the overall academic conference event (parent Working event, siblings Tutorial and Workshop), while edas:ConferenceDinner denotes a specific social meal event during a conference (path: Non Academic Event > Meal Event > Conference Dinner). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In EDAS, PersonalPublicationHistory is a subclass of PersonalHistory, representing a record/history of a person's publications — it is a history object, not a person. In EKAW, Paper_Author is a subclass of Person, representing the actual human author of a paper. These are different kinds of entities entirely: one is a historical record/artefact, the other is a person role. They share no intended instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In ekaw, Tutorial is a scientific event—an individual presentation where a tutorial is given at a conference. In iasted, Simulating is a research activity performed before the conference (a kind of Activity, not an event). They belong to disjoint branches (events vs. pre-conference research activities) and denote completely different things, so they are unrelated.

cmt:ConferenceMember is a subclass of Person whose instances are people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). edas:Conference is the conference event/organization itself, with subclasses like SingleLevelConference and TwoLevelConference, and properties like hasCountry, paperDueOn, etc. One denotes a person, the other denotes an event/organization; they are disjoint kinds of entities.

Person in the Conference ontology denotes a human being (with email, gender, first/last name, etc.), while Activity in iasted denotes an event or activity (held in places, dated, paid for). These are completely disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property from Call to string, describing textual submission guidelines. heldIn is an object property from Event to Location, indicating where an event takes place. They have different domains, different ranges, and completely different semantics; they are not equivalent or otherwise related.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'scientificallyOrganises' has domain Academic Institution and denotes an institution organizing a scientific event (range unspecified but conceptually an Event). In sigkdd, 'presentation' has domain Speaker and range Document, denoting the document/presentation material associated with a speaker. The domains (Academic Institution vs Speaker) and the intended ranges (Event vs Document) do not overlap, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a subtype of Chairman), while Tutorial is a type of event. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (organisational role in a conference). Property B relates a Person to a Building, City, or State (physical location/occupation). They connect entirely different domain and range types and describe unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

confOf:Tutorial and ekaw:Workshop are distinct types of conference events. A Tutorial is an instructional/educational session, while a Workshop is a collaborative working event. They are siblings under different parent hierarchies (Working event vs Scientific Event) and denote different kinds of academic events. They share no overlap in intended instances.

hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (an offer to review), while hasReview relates a Paper to a Review. Bid and Review are distinct concepts in the conference domain, so these properties connect different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Contribution to its Author, while property B (reviewerOfPaper) links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and denote different relations in the conference domain.

A's 'Conference document' is a class of documents (call for papers, reviews, contributions, etc.) with properties like has_authors and date_of_issue. B's 'Conference' is a subclass of Event > Working_event, sibling to Tutorial and Workshop, denoting the conference event itself. These are completely different categories (document vs. event), so they are unrelated.

The property 'has a name' in Conference denotes a naming relation whose domain includes Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic, with range string. The property 'registration Due On' in edas denotes a registration deadline with domain Conference and range dateTime. They relate different kinds of information (a name vs. a deadline date) and have different ranges (string vs. dateTime), so they are unrelated.

`accepted By` relates a Paper to an Administrator who accepted it (part of the paper-acceptance workflow). `is given by` relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it. The domains (Paper vs Presentation) and ranges (Administrator vs Active conference participant) are different concepts, and the relations describe different aspects of the conference domain (paper acceptance vs presentation delivery). They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Conference www is a web document/resource about a conference (subclass of Conference document, has a URL), while Computer Networks Optical Topic is a subject topic within the computer networks domain. They denote completely unrelated concepts.

The property 'has authors' in Conference relates a Conference document to its authors (Person), while 'need' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they need. They have opposite domain/range directions and completely different semantics: one assigns authorship to documents, the other expresses a person's need for an item. There is no alignment relationship between these two properties.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. In cmt, 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper). In sigkdd, 'design' links an ACM SIGKDD conference to a Deadline. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

Both properties denote the relation of an event to the place where it is held, but confOf:location is a DatatypeProperty with range xsd:string (a textual address), while ekaw:heldIn is an ObjectProperty with range ekaw:Location (a class of location objects). Because their value spaces differ (literal string vs. Location resource), they cannot be equivalent in a reference alignment; they are related/overlapping in meaning.

Both are object properties with domain Author and range a paper/contribution concept (confOf Contribution ≈ edas Paper). They express the same relation: an author writes a paper. Direction is identical (Author -> Paper).

confOf 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution they have authored. ekaw 'referenced In' relates a paper to something that references it (e.g., a publication or proceedings). These are fundamentally different relations: one denotes authorship, the other denotes a citation/reference relationship. They do not share the same domain/range types or semantics.

confOf:University is an organization (subclass of Organization, sibling of Company) that is the range of the 'study At' property for scholars. iasted:Student_non_speaker is a person/role (subclass of Non speaker under Delegate) representing a student who does not give a talk. One denotes an institution, the other a person role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (paper bidding process), while has_a_publisher relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and serve different functions in the conference domain.

In confOf, Organization is a broad class with children Company and University, covering any organizational entity. In edas, NGO is a specific subclass of Organization (alongside Academia, Government, Industry). confOf's Organization corresponds to edas's Organization, not to NGO. confOf has no NGO subclass, and NGO is not equivalent to the general Organization class.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Paper' is a class representing a document submitted to a conference, with subclasses like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc. In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Deadline' is a class representing temporal deadlines for conference submissions, with subclasses like Deadline Abstract Submission and Deadline Paper Submission. These are completely different domain concepts: one is a document/artefact, the other is a temporal milestone. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

These are completely different properties. 'hasPostalCode' relates Contact Information to a string (postal/zip code), while 'has_amount_of' relates Money to an integer (monetary amount). They have different domains, different ranges, and serve entirely unrelated purposes in the conference domain.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person role - the human chair of a conference - situated under Person > Chairman. Single Level Conference (edas) is a type of event/organisation, a subclass of Conference. One denotes a person, the other an event type; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The edas `hasEmail` is a datatype property linking a Person/Contact Information to a string email address. The iasted `is_used_by` is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They have different domains, different ranges (string vs Person), and completely different meanings (contact email vs usage relation).

Property A links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (administrative/organisational relation), while property B links an Academic Institution to some scientific event/activity it scientifically organises. The domains differ (Organizing committee vs Academic Institution), the ranges differ, and the intended relations are distinct: one denotes committee-level organisation of a conference volume, the other denotes institutional-level scientific organisation. No equivalence or subsumption holds.

In EDAS, Review is a general class for all reviews (a sibling of Paper, Programme, etc. under Document). In EKAW, Neutral_Review is a specific subclass of Review (distinguished by sentiment alongside Positive_Review and Negative_Review). Thus EDAS Review is strictly more general than EKAW Neutral_Review, making the relation subsumed_by.

Regular_author in the Conference ontology is a class denoting a person who authors a conference contribution (a conference participant/contributor). Author_attendee_book_registration_fee in the iasted ontology is a class denoting a monetary fee charged to an author attendee who registers with a book. One is a person/role, the other is a financial amount; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision, representing the outcome of accepting a paper. Listener in sigkdd is a subclass of Person, representing a conference attendee who listens to presentations. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is a class denoting a written document (a camera-ready version of an accepted contribution), while entity B is a class denoting an administrative event (the reviewing procedure). They belong to disjoint hierarchies (documents vs. events) and denote completely different kinds of things in the conference domain.

A is an 'Early paid applicant' (someone who registered early and paid), while B is a 'Late Registered Participant' (someone who registered late). These are disjoint temporal categories of conference registrants; they denote mutually exclusive sets of people, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only loosely related as sibling-like registration categories.

Demo Paper in EKAW is a specific type of paper (a demonstration paper), a sibling of Regular Paper, Industrial Paper, etc. Submission in IASTED is a general document category that includes Final manuscript and Initial manuscript, alongside many other document types like Review, Form, Invitation letter. These denote different concepts: a demo paper is not the same as a submission document category, and their positions in the respective hierarchies do not overlap.

Meeting Room Place is a physical location where meetings take place, while Worker non speaker is a person (a delegate who does not give a presentation). They belong to completely different conceptual categories despite both being under Place in their respective hierarchies.

Conference Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion or outing organized during a conference), while Sponsor company house is a physical building/location (the headquarters or office of a sponsor company). They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (Event vs. Place) and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Abstract in the Conference ontology is a document (a written summary of a paper/poster/presentation), while Time in iasted is a temporal entity with children like Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties differ in both type and meaning. 'has Biography' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's biographical text. 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item, representing a person obtaining some item. They share the same domain (Person) but have different ranges (string vs Item) and denote entirely different relations.

Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion) in confOf, while Value added tax is a monetary tax concept in iasted. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no semantic overlap.

Slide Set denotes a set of presentation slides used during a talk, while Workshop Paper is a specific type of paper submitted to a workshop. They are sibling-level document categories under Document in edas vs. Paper in ekaw, with no overlap in intended instances.

Reject Rating in edas is a rating value used in paper reviews (a subclass of Review Rating, alongside Accept Rating etc.), denoting a negative evaluation score. Accepting manuscript in iasted is an organizational activity that happens before a conference (subclass of Activity, alongside Receiving/Refusing manuscript). One is a rating/score concept, the other is a workflow activity. They do not denote the same concept despite both being loosely associated with manuscript disposition.

The cmt `hasAuthor` property links a Paper to its Author, while the ekaw `hasUpdatedVersion` property links a Document to an updated version of that Document. They relate entirely different kinds of things (authorship vs. versioning) and share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and have opposite directions. In cmt, 'hasBeenAssigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review (Reviewer -> Paper). In iasted, 'is_sent_by' links an Item (e.g., a submission artifact) to the Person who sent it (Item -> Person). The domains (Reviewer vs. Item), ranges (Paper vs. Person), and intended meanings (review assignment vs. authorship/submission) are all different, so the properties are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a specific leadership role responsible for the conference, while Conference Participant (ekaw) is a broad superclass for anyone attending the conference. A chair is a participant, but the two classes do not denote the same concept; they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in the direction given.

In ontology Conference, 'Poster' is a subclass of Conference contribution, i.e., a written document/artifact (a poster paper). In ekaw, 'Poster Session' is a subclass of Session under Event, i.e., a scheduled session where posters are presented. One is a document, the other is an event/session; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship), while 'pay' links a Person to a Registration fee (payment). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; they are not equivalent, subsuming, or overlapping.

Entity A is an event class representing the administrative activity of participant registration during a conference. Entity B is a class representing a monetary fee charged for registration, with properties like price and currency, and subtypes for different member categories. One denotes an event, the other a financial charge; they are completely different concepts.

In cmt, Administrator is a specialized user role (Person > User > Administrator) responsible for administrative tasks like accepting papers, assigning reviewers, and entering conference details. In Conference, Reviewer is a person who reviews papers and can invite co-reviewers. These are distinct roles: an Administrator manages the conference system while a Reviewer evaluates submissions. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Contribution is a document/artefact (paper, poster, short paper) authored and reviewed; iasted:Person is a human agent (delegate, sponsor) who gives presentations and occupies buildings. They are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

In EKAW, Track is a thematic subdivision of a conference (e.g., Semantic Web Track), a Scientific Event with sessions and presentations. In IASTED, Plenary lecture is a lecture attended by all participants, a type of Conference activity/Lecture. A track is not a lecture; they are different kinds of conference events with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. 'has_authors' connects a Conference document to its Person authors (document -> person), while 'submit' connects an Author to a Paper they submit (author -> paper). They are not the same relation, nor is one a generalization of the other; they describe different aspects of the authorship/submission process.

Trip in confOf is a specific social event involving travel/excursion, while Coctail reception in iasted is a networking gathering. They are different kinds of conference activities with distinct purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

cmt:Paper is a document submitted for review (subclass of Document, with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties like hasAuthor, hasDecision, assignedTo). edas:ComputerNetworksMeasurementsTopic is a specific subject-area topic under Topic > ComputerNetworksTopic. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference proceedings in ontology Conference is a published document (with ISBN, volume, publisher), while Conference activity in iasted is an event or activity during a conference (children include Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Registration). They denote completely different kinds of things despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

Entity A is the Conference event itself (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while entity B is a City where a conference takes place (a subclass of City sibling of Presenter city and Sponsor city). They denote completely different categories of things—an event versus a geographic location—so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the same concept: a paper/contribution that has been rejected. In Conference, 'Rejected contribution' is a subclass of Reviewed contribution, meaning it went through review and was not accepted. In edas, 'Rejected Paper' is a subclass of Paper with siblings like Accepted Paper, indicating the same review outcome. The sibling Accepted contribution/Accepted Paper correspondence further confirms alignment. The only minor difference is that Conference models a richer hierarchy (Written > Submitted > Reviewed > Rejected) while edas places Rejected Paper directly under Paper, but the intended instances coincide.

Travel Grant in edas is a kind of Sponsorship (financial support for travel), whereas Sponzor fee in sigkdd is a kind of Fee (a payment collected from a sponsor). One is a grant/subsidy given to a recipient, the other is a fee paid by a sponsor; they denote different and unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, with subclasses like Accepted/Rejected Paper and properties like isWrittenBy and isReviewedBy. In iasted, Tip is a monetary concept (child of Money, sibling of Fee, Tax, Sponzorship) referring to a gratuity. These denote completely unrelated concepts despite no label overlap.
Conference Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion) in EKAW, while Hotel is a place/accommodation in SIGKDD. They denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in instances.

In the Conference ontology, 'Committee member' is a general class covering any committee member (with subclasses Chair, Co-chair, etc.), whereas in sigkdd 'Program Committee member' is a specific subclass of Organizator restricted to the program committee. Thus A is more general and is subsumed_by B.

`hasFirstName` relates a Person to their first name (a personal name string), while `E-mail` relates a Person to their email address. These are completely different attributes despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string). A reference alignment would not equate them.

cmt's Associated Chair is a conference role (a kind of Chairman involved in organizing/running a conference), whereas confOf's Scholar is a price-category participant who studies at a university. They occupy different positions in the domain (committee/leadership role vs. attendee registration category) and share no meaningful overlap in intended instances.

Property A links a Reviewed contribution to its Review (paper -> review), while property B links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (history -> reviewer). They connect different entity types in different directions and represent different relationships in the conference domain.

confOf:Participant is a broad superclass covering all conference participants (with subclasses Member, Regular, Student), whereas ekaw:Early-Registered_Participant is a specific subclass of Conference Participant denoting only those who registered early. The confOf class is strictly more general, so it is subsumed_by the ekaw class.

Microelectronics Topic is a subject-area topic (subclass of Topic) in the EDAS ontology, representing a research domain like antennas, CAD, or cryptography. Invited Talk Abstract is a document type (subclass of Abstract under Document) in the EKAW ontology, representing the text of an invited talk abstract. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (a role), while Closing Talk is a type of academic event/talk. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Social Event in edas is a non-academic event (e.g., Excursion, Reception, Meal), while Scientific Event in ekaw is an academic event (e.g., Conference, Session, Workshop). They are disjoint categories of events, not equivalent.

Rejected contribution is a specific conference document that was submitted, reviewed, and rejected. Personal Publication History is a history object tracking a person's publication record. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Entity A is a research topic about parallel and distributed computing, a subclass of Topic in the EDAS ontology. Entity B is a document type — a tutorial abstract — subclass of Abstract in the EKAW ontology. These are completely different concepts: one classifies subject areas, the other is a written document artifact. No overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the person chairing the entire conference, while Demo Chair (ekaw) is the person responsible for demonstration sessions. These are distinct organizational roles in a conference, neither subsuming the other.

Both classes represent social outings associated with a conference, situated under a common Social Event parent. 'Excursion' and 'Conference Trip' are synonymous in the conference domain, denoting the same kind of non-academic organized trip for conference participants.

Entity A is a class denoting a camera-ready paper (a document artefact), while entity B is a class denoting a registration deadline (a temporal entity). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (Document vs. Time) and share no instances in common.

Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper (a document) in cmt, while Bronze Supporter is a subclass of Sponsor in sigkdd. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (e.g., a paper they have a conflict with), while speak_in relates a Person to a Place or Time where they present. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and meanings.

confOf:writes links an Author to a Contribution (paper) that the author has written. edas:relatesTo links a Document to various entities (events, persons) that the document relates to. They have different domains (Author vs Document), different ranges (Contribution vs Event/Person), and different semantics (authorship vs general relatedness).

In cmt, Review is a peer-review document written by a Reviewer for a Paper, with properties like write Review and written By. In iasted, Publication is a published item (e.g., Book proceeding, Cd proceeding) that is a final published artifact. A review is an unpublished evaluation document, not a publication. They share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relationship.

cmt:User is a person who uses the conference management system (subclass of Person, with children Administrator, Author, Reviewer). edas:Social Event is a non-academic conference event such as an excursion or reception (subclass of Non Academic Event > Conference Event). These are completely different domain entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Abstract is a short summary of a paper (a subclass of Paper in cmt), while Slide Set is a collection of presentation slides (a sibling of Paper in edas). They are different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Full Version in cmt denotes a complete/long version of a paper (contrasted with Paper Abstract), whereas Workshop Paper in ekaw denotes a paper submitted/presented at a workshop (contrasted with Conference Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). These are orthogonal classifications: a workshop paper could have a full version or an abstract, and a full version could be for any venue. Their instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion, banquet, reception) under Event, denoting an organised outing during a conference. iasted:Card is a physical item (sibling of Document, Publication, Transport vehicle) with a child Credit card, denoting a card artefact. They share no domain semantics: one is an event/activity, the other a physical item. No subsumption or overlap holds.

These properties connect entirely different kinds of entities. 'is part of conference volumes' links a Conference part to a Conference volume (a structural/partitive relation between conference components), while 'is Topic Of' links a Topic to a Conference or Paper (a subject-matter relation). The domains (Conference part vs. Topic) and ranges (Conference volume vs. Conference/Paper) do not overlap, so these are unrelated relations.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a kind of Chairman), while Free Time Break is a type of non-academic conference event (a break). They share no instances and are from completely unrelated parts of the domain.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Two Level Conference' in EDAS is a type of Conference (a conference event with two levels, e.g., a main conference and workshops). 'Early Registered Participant' in EKAW is a type of Person who registered early for a conference. One is an event/conference, the other is a person/participant. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In the Conference ontology, 'Review expertise' denotes the expertise or qualification a reviewer has regarding a submitted contribution (it is linked to reviewers and submitted contributions). In confOf, 'Member PC' denotes a person who is a PC member and acts as a reviewer. One is an expertise/qualification artefact, the other is a person/role; they are disjoint kinds of entities.

The EKAW 'has Part' property denotes a mereological (part-whole) relation, while the IASTED 'sign' property denotes a relation between a Person and an Item (e.g., a person signing a document). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no indication they overlap in meaning.
A is a datatype property mapping a Person/Organization to a street string; B is an object property mapping a Person to an Item. Different domains/ranges and unrelated meanings.

In cmt, 'Program Committee Chair' is a specific person role (subclass of Person > Chairman) responsible for ending reviews. In Conference, 'Program committee' is a committee (subclass of Committee) associated with a conference volume. One denotes an individual person/role, the other denotes a committee body; they are different kinds of entities.

In ontology A, Conference denotes the overall conference event (with children like Conference volume and properties like name). In ontology B, Conference Trip is a specific social event (child of Social Event, sibling of Conference Banquet) referring to a trip associated with a conference. These are completely different concepts: one is the conference itself, the other is a social outing during it.

Conference in ontology A denotes an academic conference event (with children like Conference volume, proceedings, etc.), while Place in ontology B denotes a physical location (with children like Conference hall, Hotel, Main office). These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a physical location where events may be held.

Program Committee Chair in cmt is a leadership role responsible for overseeing the reviewing process (ending reviews), sitting under Chairman and Program Committee Member. Session chair in iasted is a Delegate who chairs a conference session, sitting under Delegate alongside attendees and presenters. These are distinct roles in conference organization with different responsibilities and different ontological contexts.

Written contribution in Conference ontology is a broad class covering any written academic submission (regular, submitted, etc.), while Publication in iasted is a physical/medium item (book proceeding, CD proceeding) that is a sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Card, Document, and Transport vehicle. They overlap in the conference domain (a written contribution can become a publication) but their intended instances do not coincide: Written contribution includes drafts/submissions that are not yet publications, and Publication includes media formats (CDs, books) that are not 'written contributions' per se.
