Thus they are related but not equivalent.

These properties are completely different in meaning, domain, and range. earlyRegistration is a datatype property indicating whether a Participant registered early (boolean), while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to the Location where it takes place. They share no semantic overlap.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'acceptsHardcopySubmissions' is a datatype property from Conference to boolean, indicating whether a conference accepts hardcopy submissions. 'listsEvent' is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event, indicating that a brochure or website lists events. They share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In EDAS, 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event (a programme is part of an event). In SIGKDD, 'holded by' links a Conference to ACM SIGKDD (the conference is organized by the SIGKDD organization). The domains (Programme vs Conference), ranges (Conference Event vs ACM SIGKDD), and intended meanings (part-of vs organizer) are all different, so the properties are not equivalent.

Conference hall denotes a room or space within a venue where conference sessions take place, whereas Hotel denotes an entire lodging establishment. Although both are subclasses of Place, they represent different kinds of locations at different granularity levels. Notably, in ontology B itself, Hotel and Conference hall are listed as distinct sibling subclasses of Place, confirming they are not intended to be the same concept.

confOf:Conference is an event (a conference gathering), sitting under Event > Working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop. iasted:Session chair is a person/role, sitting under Delegate (a person who attends the conference) alongside Listener, Speaker, etc. One denotes an event, the other a person role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific leadership role under Chairman, distinct from Program Committee Chair and Program Committee Member. Program Committee member in sigkdd is a general committee member role under Organizator. These are different organizational roles with no clear equivalence or subsumption relationship.

confOf Member PC is a PC member who reviews papers (comment says 'Reviewer', domain of reviewes -> Contribution). ekaw SC Member is a subclass of PC Member, specifically a member of the Scientific Committee. In EKAW, PC Member is the general programme-committee member class (parent of SC Member, PC Chair, etc.), so confOf Member PC aligns with ekaw PC Member rather than the more specific SC Member. Thus confOf Member PC is subsumed by ekaw SC Member's parent, making it subsumed_by SC Member in the given pair.

Social program is a conference activity (e.g., dinner, cocktail reception) in the iasted ontology, while Program Committee member is a person/organizer role in the sigkdd ontology. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

The two properties have opposite directions and relate different entity types. In iasted, 'is paid by' goes from Money to Person (Money -> Person), while in sigkdd, 'pay' goes from Person to Registration fee (Person -> Registration fee). Although they are conceptually inverse relations (a person pays money vs. money is paid by a person), inverse properties are not equivalent. The domain and range are swapped, and the range entities (Person vs Registration fee) differ, so they do not denote the same relation in the same direction.

A Paid applicant is a person who has paid registration fees to attend a conference, sitting under Person > Conference applicant > Registered applicant. An Author in sigkdd is a person who submits papers and may receive awards, sitting under Person > Speaker. The two concepts denote different roles in the conference domain: one is about registration/attendance, the other about authorship of papers. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Both properties link an event to a place, but they differ in domain and range. The iasted 'is held in' has domain Activity (more general than Conference Event) and range Place+Time (broader than just Place). Thus edas:hasLocation is subsumed_by iasted:is_held_in, since the latter covers a broader class of events and can also point to time.

The cmt 'title' property relates a Paper to its title string, while the confOf 'ends on' property relates an Event to its end date string. They have disjoint domains (Paper vs Event) and denote completely different attributes, so they are unrelated.

In the Conference ontology, Chair is a committee chair (a person who chairs a committee), sitting under Committee member with sibling Co-chair. In ekaw, Session_Chair is a person who chairs a conference session (a session moderator), sitting under Conference Participant and PC Member. These are different roles: one chairs an organizational committee, the other chairs a presentation session. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Entity A is a specific topic class about computer networks security, a subclass of Topic in the EDAS ontology. Entity B is a state class representing sponsorship status in the IASTED ontology, a subclass of State. These denote completely different concepts in different hierarchies with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are types of conference presentations, but they are not equivalent. 'Paper Presentation' in EDAS is a broad academic event category for presenting an accepted paper (with siblings like Workshop, Talk Event), while 'Video presentation' in IASTED is a specific medium of presentation (sibling to 'Power Point presentation'). A paper presentation could be delivered via video, but not all paper presentations are video presentations, and not all video presentations are paper presentations. They overlap but neither subsumes the other.

Regular Session is a type of scientific event/session (e.g., conference session, demo session, poster session), while Organizing Committee is a type of committee responsible for organizing the conference. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges. 'is Provider Of' links an Organization to a Sponsorship (indicating which organization provides a sponsorship), while 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person (indicating an item is needed for a person). They relate different kinds of entities in different contexts and are not equivalent.

confOf:Assistant is a person who assists in conference organization (sibling to Administrator, Volunteer, etc., under Person). iasted:Reviewer is a delegate-level speaker who also reviews papers (under Speaker under Delegate). These denote different roles: an organizational assistant vs. a peer-reviewing participant. No subsumption holds between them.

Conference participant (A) is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference. Activity after conference (B) is a subclass of Activity, denoting events like departures or tours that happen after a conference. One is a person, the other is an event; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a Document), with sibling Paper Full Version, suggesting it denotes an abstract or short version of a paper. Short paper in confOf is a subclass of Contribution, with siblings Paper and Poster. Both represent short written contributions to a conference, but Paper Abstract is more specifically an abstract (possibly a summary of a full paper), while Short paper is a distinct submission type. They overlap in denoting short-form works but are not equivalent.

The cmt 'assigned To' property assigns a Reviewer to a Paper (i.e., designates who reviews the paper), while the ekaw 'references' property indicates that one paper cites another. These are completely different relations in the conference domain: one links a paper to its reviewer, the other links a paper to a cited paper. They share no semantic overlap.

In edas, Workshop is a subclass of Academic Event, representing a type of conference event/session. In iasted, Tutorial speaker is a subclass of Author (under Delegate > Speaker > Author), representing a person who presents a tutorial. One is an event, the other is a person/role; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The two properties are inverses, not equivalents. In cmt, 'assignedTo' has domain Paper and range Reviewer, meaning a paper is assigned to a reviewer. In ekaw, 'reviewerOfPaper' has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper, meaning a reviewer reviews a paper. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other, they are unrelated as direct alignments.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Reviewing event in confOf is an administrative event representing the reviewing procedure. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (person vs. event) and denote unrelated concepts.

Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a conference session, sibling to Author, Reviewer, Attendee, etc. OC Chair (ekaw) is the chair of the Organizing Committee, a sub-role of OC Member. These are distinct conference roles: one chairs a session (a program/event-level unit), the other chairs the organizing committee (an organizational body). Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. `has_a_steering_committee` links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a committee that oversees the conference), while `is_signed_by` links an Item (e.g., a document or publication) to a Person who signs it. They have different domains (Conference volume vs. Item), different ranges (Steering committee vs. Person), and no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

A Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person). One conference day in iasted is a temporal unit (subclass of Conference days under Time). They denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. a time period—so they are unrelated.

Workshop Chair (ekaw) is the chair of a workshop, a specific satellite event, while General Chair (sigkdd) is the top organizer of the entire conference. These are distinct organizational roles; neither subsumes the other.

`written By` in confOf links a Contribution to its Author (paper -> author), whereas `submit` in sigkdd links an Author to a Paper (author -> paper). They have opposite domain/range directions and denote different relations (authorship vs. submission), so they are not equivalent; nor is one a generalization of the other.
detailsEnteredBy relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and in opposite directions. A's 'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (a person authors/contributes to a paper). B's 'is_occupied_by' links a Building, City, or State to a Person (a place is occupied by a person). The domains and ranges are disjoint, and the intended meanings share no overlap.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a specific subclass of Paper representing the complete/extended version of a submission, distinct from 'Paper Abstract'. In edas, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers (with subclasses like Accepted, Rejected, Published, etc.). The cmt 'Paper Full Version' denotes a particular form of a paper, not the entire category of papers. Thus cmt's Paper Full Version is subsumed by edas's Paper, but they are not equivalent.
Workshop is a conference part (academic event/session), while Van is a transport vehicle. They share no domain overlap.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, representing an individual who is a student (e.g., a conference participant or author who is a student). In sigkdd, Exhibitor is a subclass of Sponzor, representing an organization or entity that exhibits at the conference. These are completely different concepts: one is a person by role, the other is a type of sponsor/exhibitor. They share no instances and are unrelated.

Conference part in ontology A denotes a structural component of a conference event (e.g., Track, Tutorial, Workshop), whereas Conference Paper in ekaw denotes a written document submitted to a conference. These are completely different kinds of entities—one is an event/session component, the other is a document—so they are unrelated.

Both classes represent committees in the conference domain. They share the same label and have overlapping children (Organizing Committee, Program Committee). The properties in ontology A (has committee chair, has members, etc.) describe typical committee relationships that align with the concept of a committee in ontology B. The children in B (Best Paper Awards Committee, Organizing Committee, Program Committee) are all types of committees, consistent with the intended instances of Committee in A.

The property 'has the last name' relates a Person to their surname/family name, while 'has Email' relates a Person/Contact Information to their email address. These are completely different attributes with no semantic overlap, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (paper bidding in the conference review process), while hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country (geographic location). These are entirely different relations with disjoint domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

Conference document in the Conference ontology denotes documents produced for or associated with a conference (e.g., Call for paper, Review, Conference contribution), with properties like authors and date of issue. Contact Information in edas denotes personal contact details (city, email, phone, postal code, street). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

hasTitle relates a Contribution to its title string, while hasSubmissionInstructions relates a Call to submission-instruction text. They connect different domain entities to semantically different string content, so they are not equivalent.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'topic Covered By' relates a Research Topic to the Events or Papers that cover it, while 'need' relates a Person to an Item they need. They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships with no overlap.

Both denote social/leisure activities associated with a conference (e.g. tours, departures), but they are not strictly equivalent: ekaw's Conference Trip is a specific kind of social event, while iasted's Activity after conference is a broader temporal category of activity that includes departures and full-day tours. They overlap in extension but neither subsumes the other cleanly.

confOf:Scholar is a price-category person (a student/academic who gets a discounted registration, sibling to Author, Participant, etc., with a studyAt University property). iasted:Author is a sub-role of Speaker under Delegate, denoting someone who presents authored work at the conference. A Scholar in confOf is not necessarily an author/presenter, and an iasted Author is not necessarily a scholar (price category). Their intended instances do not coincide; they are orthogonal classifications of conference participants.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document for which they have a conflict of interest (e.g., authored paper they shouldn't review). 'obtain' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they receive or acquire (e.g., registration kit, proceedings). These are completely different relations despite sharing domain Person and range Document/Item.
writePaper relates an Author to a Paper they author, while pay relates a Person to Money they pay. These are completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

These properties operate in opposite directions and connect entirely different domain entities. In cmt, 'assignedByAdministrator' links a Reviewer to an Administrator (the administrator who assigned the reviewer). In Conference, 'belongs_to_reviewers' links Review expertise/Review preference to a Reviewer (indicating ownership of a preference or expertise). They share only the range class Reviewer; their domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different.

Property A denotes a person's last name (family name), while property B denotes a person's nation (country of origin). Despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they capture completely different attributes of a person and are not semantically related.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In ontology Conference, 'Regular contribution' is a subclass of Conference contribution (a document type), with children like Paper and Extended abstract. In confOf, 'Regular' is a subclass of Participant (a person type), representing a regular conference attendee. Despite the shared word 'regular', one is a document/artifact and the other is a person/role, so they are unrelated.

Meta Reviewer is a person (a special kind of Reviewer) who reads and meta-reviews papers, while Review is a document (a conference document). One is an agent, the other is an artefact; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception during a conference), while iasted:Audiovisual_equipment is a physical item (e.g., computers, projectors). They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

confOf:Conference is a conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the academic meeting itself. iasted:Trip city is a subclass of City, sibling to Conference city, Presenter city, and Sponsor city, denoting a geographical location associated with travel. These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a city.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria. In ekaw, 'hasReview' relates a Paper to a Review. They connect different entity types and describe different relationships with no overlap.

confOf:University is an organization (institution) where scholars study, placed under Organization with sibling Company. iasted:Student_lecturer is a person role—a kind of lecturer/author/speaker/delegate—placed deep in a hierarchy under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer. One is an institution, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate completely different entities. In Conference, 'has a track workshop tutorial topic' links a Conference part to a Topic (categorizing what a track/workshop/tutorial is about). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presents the document). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

Organizing committee is a committee responsible for organizing a conference (local arrangements, logistics), while Academia Organization is an organization (institution) from academia (e.g., a university or research institute). They are different kinds of entities: one is a committee role within a conference, the other is a type of institution. No overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. In cmt, readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to read/review. In sigkdd, submit relates an Author to a Paper they submit. These are distinct relations in the conference domain, not inverses, and neither subsumes the other.

In ekaw, Tutorial is a scientific event (a type of individual presentation). In iasted, Tutorial speaker is a person (a delegate/author who speaks at a tutorial). One is an event, the other is a person; they are disjoint categories, not equivalent or subsumed.

These two properties have fundamentally different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'addProgramCommitteeMember' is an administrative action where an Administrator adds a Program Committee Member (a management/operational relation). In the Conference ontology, 'was_a_program_committee_of' indicates that a Program committee was the program committee for a Conference volume (a historical/organizational association between a committee and a conference). They differ in direction, domain (Administrator vs Program committee), range (Program Committee Member vs Conference volume), and semantic intent (adding a member vs recording a committee-conference association). They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

manuscriptDueOn is a submission deadline (when authors must submit their manuscripts), while End_of_conference marks the end date of the conference event itself. Both are datatype properties on Conference with range dateTime, but they denote temporally and semantically distinct milestones in the conference lifecycle.

A 'Call for paper' is a specific conference document announcing paper submission opportunities, while a 'Mailing list' is a communication channel/document for distributing information. They serve fundamentally different purposes in the conference domain despite both being document-like entities.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome). In iasted, is_held_before links an Activity to a Time. They share no common domain or range types and express entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In Conference, 'Call for participation' is a subclass of Conference document—a published artefact inviting participation. In confOf, 'Submission event' is a temporal/administrative event representing the act of submitting contributions. One is a document, the other is an event; their instances do not coincide.

These properties differ in both domain and range and direction of meaning. A's 'has a location' is a datatype property from Conference volume to string (a conference volume has a textual location). B's 'is present in' is an object property from Person to Place/Time (a person is present at a place/time). They relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

Contribution 1th author is a specific role: the first author of a conference contribution, a subclass of Regular author. sigkdd's Author is a general class for any author of a paper, with properties like submit, obtain, and notification_until. The sigkdd Author class is more general, encompassing all authors, while Contribution 1th author is restricted to first authors only. Thus Contribution 1th author is subsumed by Author.

In ontology A, 'has tracks' links a Conference volume to its constituent Tracks (organisational sessions of a conference). In ontology B, 'has Topic' links a Working event to a Topic (subject-matter topic). A track is a structural subdivision of a conference, whereas a topic is a subject category; these are different domain concepts, so the properties are unrelated.

The cmt readPaper property has domain Reviewer and range Paper, meaning it links a person (Reviewer) to the Paper they read. The ekaw reviewOfPaper property has domain Review and range Paper, meaning it links a review document to the Paper it reviews. These are fundamentally different relations: one connects an agent to a document, the other connects a document to a document. The domains are disjoint in kind (person vs. review artefact), so the properties cannot be equivalent.

The cmt property 'virtual Meeting Enabled By' links a Conference to an Administrator who enables a virtual meeting, while the edas property 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person who is a member of it. These are distinct relations with different semantics, domains, and ranges.

A is the registration fee for an author attending with a CD (a specific author category), while B is the registration fee for a non-member. These are disjoint fee categories: an author is not a non-member, and a non-member is not necessarily an author. They share only the common parent 'Registration fee'.

Both properties link a presentation to the paper it presents, but they differ in generality. In EDAS, relatedToPaper has range Accepted Paper (only accepted papers are presented), while in EKAW, presentationOfPaper has range Abstract or Paper (broader, not restricted to accepted papers). Thus EKAW's property subsumes EDAS's more specific relation.

The two properties relate completely different things. 'belongs to reviewers' connects review expertise/preference entities to a Reviewer (i.e., a reviewer is assigned or owns that expertise/preference), whereas 'give' connects a Person to an Activity or Item (a person gives a presentation or distributes an item). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics share nothing in common.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Information for participants in Conference is a document type (subclass of Conference document). They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote different kinds of entities.

PaperFullVersion is a full paper document in the conference submission domain, while ComputerNetworksEnterpriseTopic is a specific subject topic about computer networks in the enterprise context. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference's Topic is a general class for conference topics, with properties linking it to conference parts, review preferences, and submitted contributions. EDAS's Medicine Topic is a specific subclass of Topic (a child alongside Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), representing a particular subject area. Medicine Topic is thus a strict specialization of the general Topic concept, not equivalent to it.

ekaw:writtenBy relates a Document to the Person who authored it. iasted:is_used_by relates an Item to a Person who uses it. Authorship and usage are distinct relationships; an author is not necessarily a user and vice versa. The properties have different semantics and different domain classes (Document vs Item), so they are not equivalent.

confOf:writes relates an Author to a Contribution they have authored (authorship relation). ekaw:references is a citation/bibliographic relation between documents. These are fundamentally different relations in the conference domain: one denotes authorship, the other denotes referencing/citation. They share no common semantics.

Rejected contribution and Accepted Paper are mutually exclusive disjoint states of a paper: one denotes a submission that was rejected after review, the other a paper that was accepted. They share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing and soliciting paper submissions, while Best Student Paper Award is an award given to a student paper. They are completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

A Numerical Review Question is a question (e.g., a rating criterion) used within a review, while B Review is the review document itself. They are different kinds of entities: one is a question item, the other is the review artifact. No subsumption or equivalence holds.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. cmt's 'writtenBy' links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it (Review -> Reviewer). edas's 'hasReviewHistory' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (Reviewer -> Personal Review History). They relate different entities in opposite directions and denote different relationships.

A 'Two Level Conference' in EDAS is a type of conference (a conference event with two levels of organization), while 'OC Chair' in EKAW is a person who chairs the Organizing Committee. These are completely different concepts: one is an event/conference type, the other is a person role. They share no semantic overlap despite both appearing under a hierarchy that includes Person/Conference.

confOf Student is a general student participant in a conference (Person > Participant > Student, sibling of Regular). iasted Student_lecturer is a specific kind of lecturer (a speaker/author who is a student) under a deep hierarchy (Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer > Student_lecturer). The confOf Student is any student attending the conference, while the iasted Student_lecturer is specifically a student who is also a lecturer/presenter. These are different concepts: one is a general attendee category, the other is a specialized presenter role. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other given their different ontological contexts.

Both classes denote the same concept in the conference domain: a paper submitted to a conference. In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and is the central entity for reviews, bids, and assignments. In confOf, Paper is a subclass of Contribution alongside Poster and Short paper. Despite the slightly different taxonomic contexts (Document vs. Contribution), both represent the same real-world entity—a conference paper—and share the same label and domain semantics.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In the EDAS ontology, 'Computer Networks Aapplications Topic' is a specific subject-area topic under the 'Computer Networks Topic' hierarchy, used to classify papers or submissions. In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Organizing Committee' is a type of committee responsible for organizing a conference. There is no overlap in intended instances, and neither concept subsumes the other.

Property A denotes a person's last name (family name), while property B denotes a street address. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they represent fundamentally different attributes of a person. No reference alignment would equate a surname with a street address.

These properties differ in domain, range, and meaning. `hasHomePage` is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's home page URL), while `is_used_by` is an object property from Item to Person (an item used by a person). They denote completely different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, 'hasDecision' links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome). In iasted, 'is_sent_before' links an Item to a Time, expressing a temporal deadline. They share no common domain or range types and express different relations.

Both relate a person to a written document, but submitPaper specifically denotes the act of an Author submitting a Paper (to a conference/for review), while write is a more general relation from Person to Item (authoring). Submission and authoring are distinct activities in the conference domain, so the properties overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

Both classes denote committee leadership roles (chairs) in a conference context, but they are not equivalent. In cmt, 'Program Committee Chair' is the head of the Program Committee (with siblings like 'Associated Chair' and 'Conference Chair'), while in Conference, 'Co chair' is specifically a secondary/assistant chair role (sibling to 'Chair'). A Program Committee Chair is a primary chair, not a co-chair, so the concepts overlap (both are committee chairs) but do not denote the same set of instances.

Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker), while Sponsor city is a geographic location (city) that sponsors a conference. One is a person, the other is a place; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The property 'gives presentations' (domain: Active conference participant, range: Presentation) denotes the act of presenting at a conference, while 'writes' (domain: Author, range: Contribution) denotes authorship of a paper. These are distinct relations in the conference domain: an author writes a paper, while a participant gives a presentation. The domains and ranges differ (Active conference participant vs. Author, Presentation vs. Contribution), and the two activities are conceptually independent. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:hasCountry links Organizations and Persons to a Country (a geopolitical entity), while iasted:occupy links Persons to Buildings, Cities, or States (physical/spatial locations). The ranges differ fundamentally (Country vs. Building/City/State), and the semantics differ: 'has country' denotes nationality or country-level affiliation, whereas 'occupy' denotes physical occupation of a space. There is no clear subsumption either, as Country is not a superclass of Building/City/State in these ontologies.

Conference's Topic is a general class for conference topics, with properties linking it to conference parts, reviews, and submitted contributions. edas's Performance Topic is a specific subclass of Topic (a domain-specific topic like Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), not a general topic concept. The two do not denote the same set of instances: one is the general notion of a topic, the other is a specialized subject-area topic. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship with each other.

Reviewed contribution in Conference is a written paper that has been reviewed (a document/artefact), while ReviewForm in edas is a form used to collect reviews (a template/instrument). They denote entirely different kinds of things, so they are unrelated.

confOf 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a person writes a paper). iasted 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (e.g., a presentation or session is given by a person). These are different relations with different domains and ranges: one is about authorship of a written contribution, the other about presentation/delivery of an activity. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. `hasUpdatedVersion` (ekaw) links a Document to another Document that is an updated version of it. `presentationed_by` (sigkdd) links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. They relate different kinds of entities and express different semantics, so they are unrelated.

Reception in edas is a social event (a gathering/activity) at a conference, while Invitation letter in iasted is a document. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (events vs. documents) and share no instances in common.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. `hasAttendee` links a Conference Event to a Person (the people attending the event), while `hasEvent` links an Event to another Event (a sub-event of a larger event). Their domains and ranges differ, and they denote different relations in the conference domain.

Sponsor state in iasted is a subclass of State, representing a geographical or organizational state associated with a sponsor, with siblings like Conference state and Presenter state. Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Speaker (under Person), representing a person invited to speak. These denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference contribution in ontology A is a document-like entity (child of Conference document) representing the actual academic contribution (papers, posters, talks). Academic Event in ontology B is a temporal event (child of Conference Event) with children like Workshop, Talk Event, Organizational Meeting. A contribution is not an event; these are fundamentally different categories in the conference domain.

Conference Banquet is a social event at a conference, while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation/place. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in instances.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. In cmt, 'assignedByReviewer' links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (the reviewer who assigned the external reviewer). In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). The domains (External Reviewer vs Document), ranges (Reviewer vs Speaker), and semantic meanings (reviewer assignment vs presentation authorship) are completely different.

Both classes denote the same concept: a program committee in the conference domain. They share identical labels (modulo case/spacing) and both relate to program committee members and conference volumes. The cmt ontology models ProgramCommittee with members (has Program Committee Member / member Of Program Committee), while the Conference ontology places Program_committee under Committee with siblings like Organizing committee and Steering committee, and associates it with Conference volumes. These are two modeling perspectives of the same real-world entity.
Author is a person who writes/submits papers, while Tutorial is a type of conference event/session. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). In edas, Conference Session is a type of event/session at a conference (a scheduled gathering), not a person. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote members of a conference Program Committee. In cmt, 'Program Committee Member' is a person who belongs to the PC (with properties like member Of Program Committee and has Program Committee Member linking to Program Committee). In ekaw, 'PC Member' is a subclass of Possible Reviewer and a child of Person, also denoting a program-committee member. The two labels are standard abbreviations of the same role, and the structural context (Person subclass, committee-related properties, chair subtypes) confirms they are intended to denote the same set of individuals.

confOf 'Short paper' is a contribution type (alongside Paper and Poster), while edas 'Published Paper' is a paper status (alongside Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, etc.). They classify on different axes (format vs. publication status), so their intended instances do not coincide.

In ekaw, 'Invited Speaker' is a concrete class of person (a presenter who is invited to speak at a conference). In iasted, 'Presenter state' is a subclass of 'State' (a temporal/role state, not a person), with siblings like 'Conference state' and 'Sponsor state'. These are fundamentally different ontological categories: one denotes a person, the other denotes a state or status. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

These two properties are completely different. cmt's 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who authored it (Review -> Reviewer). Conference's 'has a review expertise' links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise object representing the expertise area/level assigned for reviewing (Submitted contribution -> Review expertise). They have different domains, different ranges, and express different relationships: authorship of a review vs. expertise area associated with a contribution's review.

Both properties relate conference entities to Topics, but they differ in domain and direction of use. Property A has domain Review_preference and range Submitted_contribution or Topic, meaning it links a reviewer's preference to either a topic or a paper. Property B has domain Contribution and range Topic, meaning it links a paper to its topic. They overlap in the case where A connects a Review_preference to a Topic, but A also connects to Submitted_contributions and originates from Review_preference rather than from a Contribution. They are not equivalent and neither subsumes the other cleanly.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'is part of conference volumes' relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (indicating containment/membership in a published volume), while 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presented the document). They connect different entity types in different directions and represent unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

edas:Organization is a broad top-level class covering all kinds of organizations (academia, government, industry, NGO), while ekaw:Academic Institution is a specific subclass of Organisation restricted to academic bodies (with children University and Research Institute). The ekaw class denotes a strictly narrower set of instances, so Organization subsumes Academic Institution rather than being equivalent to it.

These properties relate completely different entities in opposite directions. 'has_an_organizing_committee' links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (conference -> committee), while 'isMemberOf' links a Person to a Conference (person -> conference). They differ in domain (Conference volume vs Person), range (Organizing committee vs Conference), and direction. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only weakly related as both concern conference organization.

Entity A is a topic class about computer networks management, a subclass of Topic. Entity B is a person role (Webmaster), a subclass of Organizator > Person. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Meta-Reviewer is a specialized role: a reviewer who consolidates other reviews and submits a meta-review, with exactly one per paper. Possible_Reviewer is a generic class of persons who could serve as reviewers (it subsumes PC Member). The former is a specific functional role; the latter is a pool of potential reviewers. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

These properties are fundamentally different. 'location Of' in ekaw is an object property with domain Location and range Event, indicating where an event takes place. 'is dated on' in iasted is a datatype property with domain Activity and range dateTime, indicating when an activity occurs. They differ in type (object vs datatype), domain (Location vs Activity), range (Event vs dateTime), and semantic meaning (spatial location vs temporal date).

In cmt, Conference Chair is a specific leadership role (a Chairman responsible for running the conference), sitting under Chairman alongside Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair, etc. In the Conference ontology, Conference participant is a broad superclass covering anyone who participates in the conference (active or passive), including committee members, contributors, reviewers, and applicants. A conference chair is a single specific official, not the entire class of participants; conversely, most participants are not the conference chair. The two classes do not have coinciding intended instances, and neither cleanly subsumes the other in the modeling of these ontologies.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference contribution' is a document (subclass of Conference document) that encompasses written contributions, posters, presentations, and invited talks. In the edas ontology, 'Paper Presentation' is an event (subclass of Academic Event / Conference Event) representing the act of presenting a paper at a venue. One is a document/artefact, the other is an event/activity; they are different categories of things despite both relating to conference papers.

Paper Abstract denotes the abstract of a paper (a short summary component), while Industrial Paper denotes a paper written by industry practitioners. They share the parent Paper but represent fundamentally different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Conference is a conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas edas:PerformanceTopic is a subject topic (subclass of Topic, sibling of Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain—an event versus a research topic—so they are unrelated.

Abstract (ekaw) is a document type representing a summary of a paper or talk, with siblings like Paper, Review, Flyer. Registration fee (sigkdd) is a monetary charge for conference attendance, with properties like Price, Currency, and payed by. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Social Event is a subclass of Event (e.g., Conference Banquet, Conference Trip), while Organizator is a subclass of Person (e.g., General Chair, Program Chair). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

These classes denote entirely different kinds of documents. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document providing logistical or practical information to attendees, sibling to calls for papers and announcements. 'Conference Proceedings' in EKAW is a multi-author volume collecting accepted papers. They share no overlap in intended instances.

Conference www in ontology Conference is a web document (a Conference document with a URL), while Conference airport in iasted is a physical place (a Building). They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different categories of entities—a digital document vs. a physical location.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (representing a type of conference event with two review levels), whereas in EKAW, 'Session Chair' is a subclass of Person/Conference Participant (representing a person who chairs a session). Despite the confusing parent listing in the prompt, the path 'Conference > Two Level Conference' confirms it is an event type, not a person role. There is no semantic overlap between a conference type and a session chair role.

cmt:Reviewer is a broad class covering any person who reviews a paper (it has subclasses like Meta Reviewer and is the range of assignedTo). ekaw:SC_Member is a specific kind of committee member (a sub-class of PC Member) under Possible Reviewer, denoting a member of the (Senior) Steering/Program committee. While an SC Member may act as a reviewer, not every Reviewer is an SC Member, so cmt:Reviewer is strictly more general than ekaw:SC_Member.

Call for participation is a conference document announcing an event and inviting people to participate, whereas Conference Paper is an academic paper presented at a conference. They are completely different concepts: one is an announcement/invitation document, the other is a scholarly work. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.

Both represent a specific edition of a conference. A's 'Conference volume' has properties like has contributions, has tracks, has committees, has important dates, and belongs to a conference, indicating it is a concrete instance/edition rather than the abstract series. B's 'Conference' is explicitly commented as 'One edition of a conference' and is a sibling of Workshop, Track, and Session under Scientific Event. The intended instances coincide.

Entity A is a person (a late paid conference applicant), while entity B is a monetary fee charged for an extra trip. They belong to completely different conceptual categories (person vs. money/fee) and share no instances.

The edas 'end Date' property applies to a Conference and records when the conference ends, while the iasted 'done till' property applies to a Deadline and records the date by which a deadline task must be completed. They have different domains (Conference vs Deadline), different ranges (dateTime vs date), and different semantics (conference end vs deadline due date).

The cmt 'title' property denotes the title (name) of a Paper, while confOf 'hasKeyword' denotes keywords associated with a Contribution. These are fundamentally different attributes: a title is the name of the paper, whereas keywords are topical descriptors. Despite both being datatype properties with domain Paper/Contribution and range string, they denote different relations and should not be aligned.
Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Coffee Break is a type of event during a conference. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Computer Architecture Topic is a subject-domain topic (child of Topic, sibling to various technical topics like Antennas, CAD, Cryptography). Organizing Committee member is a person role (child of Organizator > Person, sibling to General Chair, Program Chair). These denote completely different entities: a research subject area vs. a conference organizational role.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Document > Paper, representing the abstract content of a paper. Deadline Paper Submission in sigkdd is a subclass of Deadline, representing a temporal deadline for paper submission. One is a document artifact, the other is a time point. They share no semantic relationship in the conference domain.

Entity A is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value (the deadline for camera-ready paper submission). Entity B is an object property linking a Paper to an Individual Presentation (how/where the paper is presented). They relate completely different kinds of things in different directions; one is about a submission deadline date, the other about a presentation instance. No equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap.

confOf:Social_event is a subclass of Event with children Banquet, Reception, Trip, denoting social activities at a conference. sigkdd:Speaker is a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited_Speaker, denoting a person who gives a presentation. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Conference is an event (a conference itself, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop under Working event), while iasted:Plenary_lecture_speaker is a person role (a kind of Author/Delegate who gives a plenary lecture). One denotes an event, the other a person; they share no domain overlap.
Conference www is a web document/resource identified by a URL, while Hotel is a physical place/accommodation. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In confOf, Author is a direct subclass of Person and denotes any person who writes a contribution. In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (under Delegate), so it denotes a delegate who is also a speaker and author; it further has subclasses like Lecturer and various speaker types. Thus iasted Author is narrower, so confOf Author is subsumed_by iasted Author.

confOf:Conference is an event (a conference gathering), while sigkdd:Conference_hall is a physical place (a room/building where a conference is held). They are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a location.

Proceedings in ekaw is a document (a multi-author volume containing conference papers), while Author in iasted is a person (a delegate/speaker who authors papers). These are completely different categories — a document vs. a person — with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things: cmt's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person), while Conference's has_important_dates links a Conference volume to Important dates (temporal information). Their domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, so they are unrelated.

edas ConferenceEvent is a broad class covering any conference-related event (academic or non-academic), with children Academic Event and Non Academic Event. ekaw Conference is specifically one edition of a conference, a leaf class under Scientific Event. ekaw Conference is a specific instance/type of what edas would model as an Academic Event, which is itself a child of ConferenceEvent. Thus edas ConferenceEvent is strictly more general than ekaw Conference.

In EKAW, Evaluated_Paper is a superclass that has both Accepted_Paper and Rejected_Paper as children, meaning it denotes any paper that has received an evaluation decision. In EDAS, Accepted_Paper is specifically a paper that has been accepted. Thus EDAS Accepted_Paper is strictly narrower than EKAW Evaluated_Paper, so the relation is subsumed_by.

NGO is a sub-class of Organization (a non-governmental organization), while Organizing Committee member is a sub-class of Person (a human who serves on the organizing committee). These are completely disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

A Volunteer in confOf is a general helper role under Person, distinct from specialized committee roles. An Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a specific organizational leadership role under Organizator, alongside chairs and webmaster. The instances do not coincide: a volunteer is not necessarily an organizing committee member, and vice versa. They are different roles in the conference organization hierarchy.

finalizePaperAssignment in cmt is a specific administrative action where an Administrator finalizes paper assignments for a Conference. prepare in iasted is a general relation where a Person prepares an Item. They operate on different domain/range types (Administrator/Conference vs Person/Item) and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Property A links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation that publishes the proceedings). Property B links a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material the speaker presents). They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships with no overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In edas, 'is Topic Of' links a Topic to a Conference or Paper (indicating the subject matter of a paper or conference). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presents a document). The domains (Topic vs Document) and ranges (Conference/Paper vs Speaker) are disjoint, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'expertOn' links a PC Member to a Topic they are expert in, while 'isMemberOf' links a Person to a Conference they are a member of. They relate different entity types in different directions and denote different relationships.

Associated Chair is a specific administrative role (a vice/associate chair of the conference or program committee), sitting under Chairman in cmt. Conference contributor in the Conference ontology is a broad superclass for anyone who contributes content (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors). These are at different levels of generality and denote different concepts: one is a chairing role, the other is a contributor role. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other in a reference alignment.

These properties are completely different. hasPostalCode is a datatype property relating organizations/persons to a string postal code, while is_used_by is an object property relating items to persons. They share no domain, range, or semantic overlap.

These properties are completely different in meaning, domain, range, and type. In cmt, 'enterConferenceDetails' is an object property where an Administrator enters details for a Conference. In sigkdd, 'Start_of_conference' is a datatype property that assigns a dateTime value to a Conference. They share no semantic overlap.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Conference' denotes the conference event itself (with properties like paper due dates, country, topics, and members). In the IASTED ontology, 'Conference city' is a subclass of 'City' and denotes a geographical location where a conference takes place. These are completely different concepts: one is an event/organization, the other is a city. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated entities.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a leadership role (a Chairman responsible for the conference), a subclass of Person. In iasted, Technical commitee is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference), placed under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate. The iasted class denotes a type of attendee/delegate, not a conference leadership role. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while edas's 'Powerline Transmission Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

The two properties differ in type, domain, range, and meaning. 'done till' is a datatype property from Deadline to date, representing a deadline date. 'notification until' is an object property from Author to a 'Deadline Author notification' class, linking an author to a notification deadline. They do not relate the same kinds of entities in the same direction.

The property 'held In' in ekaw is an object property linking an Event to the Location where it takes place. The property 'Price' in sigkdd is a datatype property giving the integer cost of a Registration fee. They relate entirely different domain and range types and denote unrelated concepts.

The property writePaper in cmt has domain Author and range Paper, relating an author to the paper they write. The property isWrittenBy in edas has domain Paper and range Author, relating a paper to its author. These are inverse relations, not equivalent. Per the instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, and since they are strict inverses rather than overlapping or subsuming, the correct relation is unrelated.

confOf:University is an organization that scholars study at (e.g., an academic institution). iasted:Presenter_university is a physical building/place where a presenter is housed during a conference. Despite the shared word 'university', they denote fundamentally different things: one is an organizational entity, the other is a building. Their paths, siblings, and properties confirm this divergence.

The two properties go in opposite directions and have different domain/range types. A's 'has tracks' links a Conference volume to its Track parts (whole-to-part), while B's 'partOfEvent' links an Event to the Event it is part of (part-to-whole). They are not inverses in a formal sense because their domains and ranges differ (Conference volume/Track vs Event/Event), so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or inverse-equivalent.

confOf Participant is a subclass of Person (a human attendee), while sigkdd Registration fee is a subclass of Fee (a monetary amount). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Proceedings Publisher is an organisation that publishes proceedings, while Refusing manuscript is an activity that occurs before a conference. They share no common instances and belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies.

Program committee is a collective body (a committee) that reviews papers, while Program Chair is an individual person who leads that committee. One is an organization/group, the other is a person role; they are disjoint kinds of entities.

In cmt, Subject Area denotes a research topic or category used to classify papers (domain of 'has Subject Area' is Paper). In sigkdd, Conference denotes an academic event with properties like start/end dates, city, and name, organized by ACM SIGKDD. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Extended abstract is a type of conference document/contribution (a written artefact), while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject-area topic for classifying papers. They share no domain overlap: one is a document type, the other is a research topic category.

Sponsorship in edas denotes a sponsorship arrangement (e.g., a travel grant) provided by an Organization, with cost and currency attributes. Registration fee in sigkdd denotes a fee paid by a Person to register for an event, with subtypes for members, non-members, and students. These are distinct concepts: one is about organizational sponsorship/grants, the other about attendee registration payments. They share superficially similar properties (cost amount/price, currency) but relate to different domain processes and different participating entities (Organization vs Person).

In confOf, Conference is an event (subclass of Event > Working event), denoting the conference gathering itself. In ekaw, Proceedings is a document (subclass of Document > Multi author Volume), denoting the published volume of papers. These are fundamentally different categories of entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, ConferenceMember is a subclass of Person (an individual who is a member of a conference, with subclasses Author, Reviewer, Chair, etc.). In the Conference ontology, Committee is a group/body (with subclasses Organizing committee, Program committee, Steering committee) that has members and chairs. One denotes a person; the other denotes an organizational body. They are disjoint kinds of entities, not equivalent.

Entity A is a class representing a type of event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) in the confOf ontology. Entity B is a class representing a specific subject topic (Computer Networks Applications) in the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and domains of discourse: one is about organizational events, the other about subject-matter topics. There is no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, 'Conference part' denotes a component of a conference (e.g., Track, Tutorial, Workshop), whereas in ontology B, 'Conference' denotes one edition of a conference itself (a Scientific Event). These are different concepts at different levels of granularity: a part of a conference is not the same as a conference edition. They share no direct subsumption relationship either.

A's Author is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person/Conference Member). B's Programme is a document (subclass of Document) associated with a conference event. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Person/Conference Member who submits and writes papers. In edas, Conference is an event with properties like endDate, hasCountry, paperDueOn, etc. These are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is an organizational event. No alignment relationship exists.

A Call for paper is a conference document announcing the solicitation of papers, while an Organizational Meeting is an academic event (a meeting). They belong to disjoint branches (documents vs events) and denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

These properties go in opposite directions. In cmt, 'write Review' has domain Reviewer and range Review, meaning a reviewer writes a review. In Conference, 'has a review' has domain Reviewed contribution and range Review, meaning a reviewed contribution has a review. They relate different subject entities (Reviewer vs. Reviewed contribution) to the same object (Review). They are not inverses in a formal sense because the domains and ranges do not line up as inverse properties would (the range of one would need to be the domain of the other). They denote different relations in the conference domain.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' (cmt) relates a Conference to an Administrator who initiates the reviewer bidding process. 'invited_by' (Conference) relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer who issued the invitation. They describe different relationships between different entities with no overlap.

Travel Grant in edas is a subclass of Sponsorship, denoting a financial grant supporting travel. Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Speaker (under Person), denoting a person invited to give a talk. These are completely different concepts: one is a monetary award, the other is a role/person. No subsumption or overlap exists.

maxChoice is a datatype property from Social event/Working event to positiveInteger, representing a maximum number of choices. listsEvent is an object property from Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event, representing a listing relationship. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Registration in iasted is a conference activity (a process/event of registering for a conference), with Delegate as a child. Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives a presentation, a subclass of Person. These denote entirely different categories of entities (an activity vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

Person denotes a human agent (authors, reviewers, participants, staff) while Place denotes a physical location (conference halls, hotels, offices). They share no instances and are from disjoint domains; the only connection is that a Person can stay in a Place.

A is a Conference event class (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop), while B is a state class (subclass of State, sibling of Conference state/Sponsor state). They denote completely different kinds of entities—an event vs. a temporal/role state—with no overlap in intended instances.

Contribution 1th author is a person role (the first author of a conference contribution) in the Conference ontology, while Single hotel room is a type of accommodation/place in the iasted ontology. They belong to completely different domains (authorship vs. lodging) and share no semantic relationship.

Property 'issues' in Conference relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher publishes proceedings). Property 'coversTopic' in ekaw relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (a paper/event covers a research topic). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

Both are datatype properties with range string, but they apply to different entities. In cmt, 'title' is specifically the title of a Paper. In Conference, 'has a name' applies to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic. The Conference property is more general; cmt's 'title' (a name for a paper) is a specific case of naming, so cmt:title is subsumed_by Conference:has_a_name.

Conference Chair is a person who leads the conference organizing committee, initiates calls, and may review papers. Speaker is a person who gives a presentation at the conference. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: a conference chair need not give a talk, and a speaker need not chair the conference. They share only the common parent Person.

confOf 'Reviewing event' is a temporal event (subclass of Administrative event, sibling of Submission event, Registration event, etc.) denoting the reviewing procedure/process. edas 'Review Form' is a document/artefact used to record review content. One is an event, the other is a document; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In confOf, Conference denotes the overall academic conference event (a working event sibling to Tutorial and Workshop). In iasted, Lecture is a specific conference activity—a talk or session—whose children include Plenary lecture, Session, and Tutorial, and whose siblings include Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Registration, etc. These denote completely different levels of granularity: one is the entire conference, the other is a lecture/presentation within a conference. They are not equivalent, nor is there a subsumption relation between them.

A is a specific registration fee amount for an author attending with a CD; B is a registration category for a student. They share the parent 'Registration fee' but denote different concepts (a fee vs. a registration type) and target different participant groups.
Committee member is a person who serves on a committee, while Building is a physical place. These are disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
A is an event (a happening in the conference workflow), while B is a deadline (a point in time). They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies and do not share instances.

Tutorial is an academic event where participants learn about a topic, while Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no domain overlap.

These entities denote different concepts. In EDAS, 'Accpet If Room Rating' is a subclass of 'Review Rating' — a rating value assigned to a paper (likely meaning 'accept if there is room'). In EKAW, 'Negative Review' is a subclass of 'Review' — an actual review document with negative content. One is a rating/score, the other is a document; they are not the same kind of entity and do not overlap in intended instances.

In the iasted ontology, 'Viza' (likely a transliteration of 'visa') is a travel document under Item > Document, sibling to Review, Submission, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc. In edas, 'Review' is a peer-review document for a paper. These are completely different document types: a visa is an entry permit, not a review. They share the parent Document but denote distinct artefacts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties are completely different. In cmt, 'member Of Conference' is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference (indicating membership). In sigkdd, 'End of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime value (indicating when the conference ends). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Author information form is a document/form used in conference organization for collecting author details, while Hotel is a physical place/accommodation venue. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (Document vs Place) and share no domain overlap.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference, while Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal deadline for booking hotels. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Reception in edas is a social event (a gathering/occasion), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who presents. They belong to entirely different ontological categories (event vs. person) with no overlap in intended instances.

In confOf, 'Working event' is a broad superclass covering Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop—i.e., any non-administrative, non-social event. In edas, 'Conference' is a specific event type with properties like paper deadlines and country. Since confOf's Working event includes Conference as a child, edas:Conference is a narrower concept, making confOf:Working_event subsume edas:Conference (edas:Conference is subsumed_by confOf:Working_event).

In the Conference ontology, 'Reviewed contribution' is a class whose instances are written documents (papers) that have undergone review, sitting in the hierarchy Conference document > Conference contribution > Written contribution > Submitted contribution > Reviewed contribution. In confOf, 'Reviewing event' is a subclass of Administrative event under Event, denoting the reviewing procedure itself (an event/activity), not the artefact being reviewed. The two entities belong to disjoint branches of the domain (document vs. event), so they do not share instances and are not equivalent; nor is one more general than the other.

Conference's Paper is a general class for regular contributions (with siblings like Extended abstract), while edas's Withdrawn Paper is a specific paper state (sibling to Accepted, Rejected, Published, etc.). They do not denote the same concept: one is a broad document type, the other a narrow status-based subclass. They are not in a direct subsumption relationship across these two ontologies, so unrelated is the appropriate verdict.

Conference Chair (cmt) is an administrative/leadership role responsible for chairing the conference, sitting under Chairman and Conference Member. Plenary lecture speaker (iasted) is a type of author/speaker who presents a plenary lecture, sitting under Author and Speaker. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a conference official with organizational authority, the other is a presenter of a specific talk type. They share no common instances and neither subsumes the other.

A Meta Review is a specific kind of review document written by a meta-reviewer, whereas a Textual Review Question is a type of review question (a question in a review form that accepts textual answers). They are at different levels of abstraction: one is a review artefact, the other is a component of a review form. They share no instance overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and go in conceptually different directions. `has_a_steering_committee` links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (an organizational body associated with the conference). `isMemberOf` links a Person to a Conference (indicating membership/attendance). They do not share the same domain or range, nor do they denote the same relation in the conference domain.

The two properties denote completely different attributes: 'starts on' captures the start date/time of an Event, while 'has Name' captures the full name of a Conference. They have different domains (Event vs Conference) and different semantics, so they are unrelated.

CAD Topic is a subject-area topic for conference papers (e.g., antennas, cryptography, mobile computing), while Transport vehicle is a physical item (car, shuttle bus, taxi, van) used for logistics. They belong to completely different domains and share no conceptual overlap.

assignedByAdministrator relates a Reviewer to an Administrator (who assigned the reviewer), while writes relates an Author to a Contribution (paper). Different domains, ranges, and semantics; no overlap.

confOf:location applies to both Social event and Working event, denoting where any such event is held, while sigkdd:City_of_conference is restricted to Conference. The confOf property is strictly more general, covering a broader set of events and a broader notion of location (not limited to a city).

In iasted, Submission is a specific subclass of Document (with children like Final manuscript and Initial manuscript), representing the act/artifact of a paper submission. In sigkdd, Document is a broader class encompassing Abstract, Paper, and Review. Thus iasted's Submission is a narrower concept than sigkdd's Document, making it subsumed_by.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper), while is_sent_before relates an Item to a Time (a temporal relation). They have different domains, different ranges, and express fundamentally different relations.

In the Conference ontology, 'Review preference' is a class whose instances are review-preference objects (with a degree, a topic or submission, and assigned reviewers), used to model bidding/assignment in the review process. In confOf, 'Contribution' is the top class for submitted works (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like abstract, title, keywords, authors, and reviews. These denote completely different things—a review-assignment preference versus a submitted paper—so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting people to participate in an event, while a 'Record of attendance' is a document certifying that someone attended. They are different types of documents with different purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

Property A (has_a_name) is a datatype property that assigns a string name to entities like Conference, Publisher, and Topic. Property B (topicCoveredBy) is an object property linking a Research Topic to the Event or Paper that covers it. They have completely different domains, ranges, types (datatype vs object), and meanings.

A's Paper is a general conference paper (regular contribution), while B's Rejected_Paper is a specific paper that has been rejected after evaluation. B is a strict subclass of A: every rejected paper is a paper, but not every paper is rejected.

confOf's Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster, Short_paper) covering any paper submitted/published. ekaw's Accepted_Paper is a specific paper that has passed review and is accepted for proceedings. Every Accepted_Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is accepted, so Paper subsumes Accepted_Paper.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'is part of conference volumes' links a Conference part to a Conference volume (a document/artefact relationship). In ontology B, 'has Event' links an Event to a sub-Event (a mereological relationship between events). The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

The two properties differ in both domain and direction. In cmt, assignExternalReviewer has domain Reviewer and range External Reviewer, modeling a reviewer assigning an external reviewer. In ekaw, hasReviewer has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer, modeling a paper having a reviewer. They relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. 'Conference Hiker' in the iasted ontology is a subclass of Delegate, representing a person who attends a conference. 'Conference' in the sigkdd ontology represents the conference event itself, with properties like start/end dates, city, and name. A person attending a conference is not equivalent to, nor a subsumer/subsumee of, the conference event.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. 'has_been_assigned_a_review_reference' links a submitted contribution/topic to a review preference (i.e., assigning a reviewer preference to a paper), while 'writes' links an author to a contribution (i.e., authorship). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; there is no overlap or subsumption between them.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and express different relations. confOf:studyAt links a Scholar to a University (where the scholar studies), while ekaw:writtenBy links a Document to a Person (the author of the document). The domains (Scholar vs Document) and ranges (University vs Person) are disjoint, and the intended meanings (studying at vs authorship) are unrelated.

Both classes denote an invited talk / invited presentation at a conference. They share the same label (modulo case) and occupy analogous positions in their respective taxonomies: A's 'Invited talk' is a child of 'Presentation' under 'Conference contribution', while B's 'Invited Talk' is a child of 'Individual Presentation' under 'Scientific Event'. The intended instances—talks delivered by invited speakers—coincide, so a reference alignment would mark them equivalent.

These properties have different meanings and different ranges. 'assignExternalReviewer' relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (the act of assigning someone as an external reviewer), while 'hasReviewHistory' relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a record of reviews they have performed). They connect the same domain (Reviewer) to entirely different concepts, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.
