Review in Conference is a review document for a contribution, sibling to Conference contribution and Call for paper. Programme in edas is a conference programme/schedule document, sibling to Meal Menu and Slide Set, linked to Conference Event. They are different kinds of documents with different purposes and properties.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. In cmt, paperAssignmentFinalizedBy links a Conference to an Administrator who finalizes paper-to-reviewer assignments. In ekaw, technicallyOrganises links an Organisation to some entity it technically organises (a sub-property of organises). The domains (Conference vs Organisation), ranges (Administrator vs unspecified), and semantics (administrative finalization of assignments vs technical organisation of an event/activity) do not overlap.

Academia Organization in edas is a type of organization (e.g., a university or research institute), while Organizing Committee in sigkdd is a type of committee responsible for organizing a conference. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Meeting Room Place in edas denotes a room where meetings/sessions are held, sibling to Conference Venue Place and Dining Place. Main office in iasted denotes the primary administrative office of an organization, sibling to Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Session room. A meeting room is a space for sessions/events, whereas a main office is an administrative headquarters; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In edas, AccommodationPlace is a specific kind of Place (a sibling of ConferenceVenuePlace, DiningPlace, MeetingRoomPlace), i.e. lodging such as hotels. In iasted, Place is the general spatial concept whose children include Building, Conference hall, Hotel room, Main office, Session room. Thus iasted:Place is strictly more general than edas:AccommodationPlace, so the relation is subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

Multi-author_Volume in ekaw is a document type (a collection of works by multiple authors, parent is Document, child is Proceedings). Author in iasted is a person role (parent is Speaker, under Delegate > Building > Place). One is a publication artefact, the other is a person; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In ontology A, Conference denotes the academic event/organisation itself (with a name, proceedings, publisher, topics, and conference volumes as children). In ontology B, Conference days is a temporal concept (a subclass of Time) representing the span of days during which a conference takes place, with children such as Delegate and One conference day. These denote fundamentally different entities (an event/organisation vs. a time period), so they are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption between them.

These properties connect entirely different domain and range pairs. 'is Provider Of' links an Organization to a Sponsorship it provides, while 'location Of' links a Location to an Event held there. They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. In edas, `hasStartDateTime` applies to Conference Event and records when an event starts. In sigkdd, `Date` applies to Deadline and records the deadline date. These are distinct relations over different subject types (event start time vs. deadline date), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Track in the Conference ontology denotes a thematic session within a conference (a conference part, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). Car in the iasted ontology denotes a physical transport vehicle (sibling of Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is a specific subject topic about computer network applications within a Topic hierarchy, while Entity B is a committee type responsible for reviewing conference papers. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

Both 'PC Chair' (ekaw) and 'Program Chair' (sigkdd) denote the same role in conference organization: the head of the Program Committee responsible for overseeing the paper review process and technical program. 'PC' is a standard abbreviation for 'Program Committee', making 'PC Chair' synonymous with 'Program Chair'. Both are subclasses of organizer/participant classes, confirming they refer to the same organizational role.
City is a geographic location where organizations and persons are located, while Currency is a monetary unit. These are entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference domain.

The confOf 'location' property captures where an event is held (a string-valued venue/place), while the edas 'paperDueOn' property captures a paper submission deadline (a dateTime). They relate to completely different aspects of the conference domain (physical location vs. temporal deadline) and have disjoint domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.

Conference Venue Place in edas denotes the general location where a conference takes place (a venue), whereas Conference airport in iasted denotes an airport associated with a conference (for travel/transport). They are sibling-level concepts under Place/Building but refer to different kinds of locations: a conference venue is not an airport, and an airport is not a conference venue.

Both properties link a Paper (or conference event) to its Topic/Research Topic. The domains (Conference/Paper vs Event/Paper) and ranges (Topic vs Research Topic) are closely aligned, and both express the relationship of a paper or event covering a subject area. The slight difference in range naming (Topic vs Research Topic) does not indicate a different relation in this domain.

Property A relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it. Property B relates a geographic entity (Building, City, or State) to a Person who occupies it. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different; there is no overlap in the kinds of things being related.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Call for participation in the Conference ontology is a document type (subclass of Conference document). They denote completely different categories of entities—a role/person versus a document—so they are unrelated.

Property A (has a name) applies to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic, denoting their name. Property B (has short title) applies to Social event and Working event, denoting a short title. The domains are disjoint sets of entities, and the intended meanings (full name vs. short title) differ, so these are unrelated.

Although both are subclasses of Document, they denote entirely different artefacts. In cmt, Review is a peer-review report of a paper (with properties like written By Reviewer, write Review). In iasted, Payment document is a financial document with children Bank transfer and Cheque. They share no instances and no semantic overlap beyond being documents.

A is a person role (Presenter under Conference Participant in ekaw), while B is a document type (Brief introduction for Session chair under Document in iasted). One denotes a person, the other a document artifact, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Conference denotes the whole conference event (a top-level working event alongside Workshop and Tutorial), whereas ekaw:Industrial_Session is a specific session within a conference (a child of Conference Session). These are at completely different levels of granularity and do not share instances.

Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (assigning a chair role), while property B links a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material). They relate entirely different domain and range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Talk Event in edas is a subclass of Academic Event, denoting an event (e.g., a talk or presentation). Presenter in ekaw is a subclass of Conference Participant, denoting a person who presents. These are disjoint categories (event vs. person) with no meaningful alignment.

The property 'prepare' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they prepare, while 'holded by' in sigkdd relates a Conference to the ACM SIGKDD organization that hosts it. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and denote unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

Decision (cmt) represents an acceptance or rejection outcome for a submitted paper, with children Acceptance and Rejection. Country (confOf) represents a geographic nation, used as the range of hasCountry for organizations and persons. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. 'gives_presentations' relates Active conference participant -> Presentation (a person gives a presentation), while 'is_given_by' relates Activity/Item -> Person (a presentation/activity is given by a person). They describe the same real-world relationship but in opposite directions. Per the task instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent. They are also not subsumption-related since neither is more general than the other; they are inverses, which the task classifies as unrelated rather than equivalent.

Property A (has_a_committee_chair) relates Committee to Chair, identifying the chair of a committee. Property B (sign) relates Person to Item, indicating a person signs an item. They have different domains, different ranges, and denote entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

Talk Event in edas is a subclass of Academic Event representing a presentation/talk event (with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk). Author in sigkdd is a subclass of Speaker representing a person who writes papers. These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a person role.

The confOf 'parallel with' property denotes a symmetric relation between two administrative events that occur concurrently (side by side), whereas the ekaw 'part Of Event' denotes a meronymic relation where one event is a constituent part of another (e.g., a session within a conference). These are fundamentally different relations: parallel-with is a temporal/concurrency relation between sibling events, while partOfEvent is a structural containment relation. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The cmt 'enter Review Criteria' property has domain Administrator and range Conference, meaning an administrator enters review criteria for a conference. The iasted 'give' property has domain Person and range Activity/Item, meaning a person gives an activity or item. These are completely different relations: one is about setting review criteria for a conference, the other about giving/producing activities or items. The domains (Administrator vs Person) and ranges (Conference vs Activity/Item) do not align, and the semantics are unrelated.

confOf's 'Short paper' is a type of written contribution (a document/artifact), sibling to Paper and Poster under Contribution. edas's 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event (a session where a paper is presented), not the paper itself. One is a document, the other is an event; they do not share instances.

In cmt, Paper is a document submitted for review with authors, bids, decisions, and subject areas. In Conference, Review is a conference document that evaluates a contribution. These are distinct concepts: one is the artefact being reviewed, the other is the evaluation itself. They share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The property 'written By' in confOf relates a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper), while 'need' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they need. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person). In the Conference ontology, Conference contribution is a document/artefact submitted to a conference (subclass of Conference document, with children like Poster, Presentation, Written contribution). One denotes a person/role, the other a document/artefact; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The cmt property 'written By' relates a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it, while the sigkdd property 'presentationed by' relates a Document to the Speaker who presented it. These are different relations involving different domain and range concepts (review-writing vs. document-presentation), so they are unrelated.

Both represent oral presentation activities at a conference, but they differ in scope. Talk Event in EDAS is specifically about talks (with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk), while Lecture in IASTED is broader, including Sessions and Tutorials alongside Plenary lectures. They overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly.

Both are object properties linking a paper/contribution to its author, with matching domain (Paper/Contribution, which are themselves equivalent in the conference domain) and range (Author). 'has Author' and 'written By' express the same relation in the same direction (document -> author).

The two properties operate in completely different domains. 'is Initiated By' relates a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the committee members who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). 'is equipped by' relates a Place to an Item it is equipped with. They share no common domain or range types and denote entirely different relationships in the conference-organisation domain.

Conference:Person is a broad superclass of all people involved in the conference (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers, chairs). EKAW:Possible_Reviewer is a specific subclass of EKAW:Person denoting only those who can serve as reviewers. Every possible reviewer is a person, but not every person is a possible reviewer, so Person subsumes Possible_Reviewer.

Accommodation Place is a physical location (e.g., hotel/lodging) under Place in edas, while Worker lecturer is a person role under Lecturer in iasted. They denote completely different categories of entities.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'enterReviewCriteria' in cmt relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of entering review criteria for a conference), while 'isReviewing' in edas relates a Reviewer (or chair/TPC member) to a Paper (the act of reviewing a specific paper). They connect different entity types in different directions and represent different actions in the conference organization workflow.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'is a date of acceptance announcement' relates Important dates to a date value, capturing when paper acceptance notifications are issued. 'early Registration' relates a Participant to a boolean, indicating whether the participant registered early. They share no conceptual overlap in the conference domain.

Both are meronymic part-of relations over conference/event-like entities, but A is specific to Conference part -> Conference volume, whereas B is the general Event -> Event part-of relation. B therefore subsumes A; they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote an Administrator in the conference organization domain. In cmt, Administrator is a subclass of User (which is a subclass of Person) and is responsible for administrative tasks such as accepting papers, assigning reviewers, and entering conference details. In confOf, Administrator is a direct subclass of Person, alongside other conference roles like Author, Chair PC, Member PC, etc. The intended instances—persons who administer the conference tool/system—coincide across both ontologies. The difference in hierarchy depth (cmt has an intermediate User class) does not affect the equivalence of the Administrator concept itself.

The two properties have opposite directions and relate different entities. In cmt, readByReviewer goes from Paper to Reviewer (a paper is read by a reviewer). In Conference, reviews goes from Review to Reviewed contribution (a review reviews a contribution). They are not inverses of each other either, since readByReviewer is about reading/accessing a paper, while reviews is about the act of reviewing a contribution. The domains and ranges do not align in any equivalent or subsumption relationship.

In cmt, Paper is a specific document type (a leaf-level class with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and a sibling Review). In confOf, Contribution is a broad class that subsumes Paper, Poster, and Short paper. Thus cmt:Paper is a narrower concept than confOf:Contribution: every cmt Paper would be a confOf Contribution, but confOf also includes posters and short papers that are not cmt Papers. The two are therefore not equivalent; cmt:Paper is subsumed by confOf:Contribution.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities and express different relations. `is submitted at` links a Conference contribution (a document/artefact) to the Conference volume it appears in, i.e. a submission/publication relation. `partOfEvent` links an Event to another Event as a part-to-whole (mereological) relation. The domains and ranges differ (contribution vs. event; conference volume vs. event), and the intended meaning (submission vs. parthood) is distinct, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

Reception is a social event (e.g., a banquet or trip) in the conference organization domain, while Invited Speaker is a person who gives a talk. They are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Workshop is an event type (a kind of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Conference_Hiker is a person/role (a Delegate subtype, sibling of Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc.). One denotes an academic event, the other a person who attends a conference. They share no instances and are completely different categories.

Both classes denote the same concept: a human person involved in the conference domain. They share the same label and are top-level classes for people in their respective ontologies. The children (Agency Staff Member, Conference Participant, Paper Author, Possible Reviewer, Student vs. Listener, Organizator, Speaker) are all subtypes of conference participants, and the properties (author Of, organised By, organises, written By vs. E mail, Name, Nation, can stay in, pay, payed by) all apply to persons in the conference context. The intended instances coincide.

Registeered_applicant is a subclass of Conference_applicant (someone who applied to attend a conference), while Participant is a direct subclass of Person in confOf. They overlap in extension (a registered applicant is typically a participant), but neither subsumes the other: a Participant can exist without having registered/applied (e.g., invited speakers, organizers), and a Registeered_applicant is specifically someone who has gone through an application/registration process. The hierarchies and sibling structures differ enough that equivalence is not warranted.

hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person belonging to the conference), while hasCall links an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., a call for papers). These are entirely different relations with disjoint ranges (people vs. calls), so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing that papers are being solicited for submission, whereas a 'Camera Ready Paper' is the final, publication-ready version of a paper itself. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain: one is an announcement/invitation document, the other is a finished paper artifact. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

A Paper in cmt is a scholarly document submitted for review, with authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions. A Value added tax in iasted is a kind of tax (under Money > Tax). These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In the Conference ontology, 'Paper' is a regular contribution (a full paper as opposed to an extended abstract). In ekaw, 'Regular Paper' is a specific subclass of the more general 'Paper' class, distinguishing it from camera-ready, demo, industrial, poster, submitted, and workshop papers. The ekaw 'Paper' superclass is the broader concept that corresponds to the Conference ontology's 'Paper', while 'Regular Paper' is a narrower subtype. Thus Conference:Paper is subsumed_by ekaw:Regular_Paper is not quite right either—rather, Conference:Paper corresponds to the ekaw:Paper superclass, making it more general than ekaw:Regular_Paper. The relation is subsumes.

These properties are completely different in meaning and structure. confOf's 'ends on' is a datatype property mapping an Event to a string (representing an end date), while iasted's 'go through' is an object property mapping an Item to an Activity (representing an item undergoing some process). They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Event vs Item), range (string vs Activity), and semantic meaning.

The cmt 'max Papers' is a datatype property from Program Committee Member to int, representing the maximum number of papers a PC member can be assigned. The sigkdd 'submit' is an object property from Author to Paper, representing an author submitting a paper. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a short paper or abstract document), while Withdrawn Paper is a paper that has been removed from the review process. They denote different concepts: one is a document type, the other a submission state. Their paths, siblings, and parents confirm no overlap in intended instances.

Performance Topic is a subclass of Topic covering technical subjects like antennas, CAD, and communication theory. Program Committee is a committee type responsible for reviewing papers. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

The two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. `hasConferenceMember` in cmt has domain Conference and range Conference Member (Conference -> Conference Member), while `isMemberOf` in edas has domain Person and range Conference (Person -> Conference). A property and its inverse are not equivalent in the reference alignment.

In cmt, Program Committee Member is a specific role under Conference Member, consisting of reviewers who evaluate papers. In edas, Conference Chair is a distinct leadership role (a Person who initiates calls and can review papers). These are different conference roles: a PC member is not the same as a conference chair. They are not in a subsumption relation either, since each ontology treats them as separate sibling-level roles under Person/Conference Member.

Free Time Break is a non-academic break event (like free/unstructured time between sessions), while Conference Banquet is a specific social event (a formal dinner). They are both non-academic conference events but denote different kinds of activities with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties are fundamentally different in both type and meaning. 'organised By' in ekaw is an object property linking an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. 'Name_of_conference' in sigkdd is a datatype property linking a Conference to its name (a string). They relate different kinds of things in different directions and are not equivalent.

The cmt 'end Review' property means a Program Committee Chair finishes/ends a Review (Chair -> Review), whereas the iasted 'is given to' property means an Item is given to a Person (Item -> Person). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

Both properties denote the relation of a reviewer writing a review for a paper/contribution. The domain Reviewer (cmt) corresponds to Member PC (confOf) in the conference-review context, and the range Review (cmt) corresponds to Contribution (confOf) as the reviewed artefact. The direction is identical (reviewer -> reviewed item), so the properties are equivalent.

confOf:Workshop is an event type (a working event like a conference or tutorial), while edas:PowerlineTransmissionTopic is a subject matter topic (a sibling of Antennas Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.). They denote completely different concepts: one is a kind of academic meeting/event, the other is a research subject area. No overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Meeting Room Place in edas is a physical location (subclass of Place). They denote entirely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have different domains (Member PC vs Author) and different ranges (Contribution vs Paper), and they denote different actions: reviewing a paper vs submitting a paper. They are not equivalent and do not subsume one another.

Performance Topic is a subject-area classification (a kind of Topic, sibling to Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.), whereas Invited Talk is a type of presentation event (under Event > Scientific Event > Individual Presentation). They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a Chairman in CMT), whereas IASTED member is a type of Delegate (attendee) in the iasted ontology. They occupy completely different positions in the conference organization hierarchy and share no organizational or conceptual overlap.

A 'Reviewed contribution' is a specific conference document (a paper that has been reviewed), while B 'Personal History' is a person's history record containing publication and review histories. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

confOf's Topic is a general class for conference topics, used broadly as the range of dealsWith, expertOn, and hasTopic properties across contributions, PC members, and working events. edas's CommunicationsTopic is a specific subclass of edas's Topic, representing only communications-related subjects, with siblings like AntennasTopic, CADTopic, MedicineTopic, etc. Thus CommunicationsTopic is a strict specialization of the general Topic concept, not equivalent.

Property A (`is a full paper submission date`) has domain `Important dates` and range `date`, specifically denoting the submission deadline for full papers. Property B (`is dated on`) has domain `Activity` and range `dateTime`, a general relation assigning a date/time to any activity. Their domains differ (Important dates vs. Activity), their ranges differ (date vs. dateTime), and A is a specific deadline predicate while B is a generic temporal-annotation predicate. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same way, so they are not equivalent; nor is there a clear subsumption between a deadline-specific date property and a general activity-dating property.

A Conference applicant is someone who applies to attend a conference, whereas a Demo Chair is a specific conference role responsible for demonstration sessions. These are distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:User is a person who uses the conference management system (parent Person, siblings Chairman, Conference Member, etc.), whereas edas:TalkEvent is an academic event such as a welcome or closing talk (parent AcademicEvent, siblings PaperPresentation, Workshop). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Academia Organization in edas is a general class for academic organizations (universities, research institutes, etc.). Proceedings Publisher in ekaw is a specific role: an organization that publishes conference proceedings. While a proceedings publisher could be an academic organization, the two classes have different intended extensions: not all academic organizations publish proceedings, and not all proceedings publishers are academic organizations (e.g., Springer, IEEE are industry organizations). The classes are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear direction given the available context.

Presenter (ekaw) is a subclass of Person/Conference Participant, denoting a person who presents. Lecture (iasted) is a subclass of Activity/Conference activity, denoting an event or talk. These are disjoint categories (person vs. activity) and share no instances, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote conference leadership roles, but they are not equivalent. In the Conference ontology, Chair is a subclass of Committee member (alongside Co-chair), indicating a committee-level role. In edas, Conference Chair is a direct subclass of Person and a sibling of Session Chair, TPC Member, Reviewer, and Author, indicating a top-level conference role. The edas Conference Chair is also modeled as a potential reviewer and call initiator, roles not implied for the Conference ontology's Chair. These are distinct but overlapping concepts: a Conference Chair may also be a committee chair, but the two classes do not have identical intended instances.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different contact information: email address vs phone number. They are distinct attributes of a person and do not denote the same relation.

Meal Event is a non-academic event (e.g., conference dinner) in the event hierarchy, while Organizator is a person role (chair, committee member, etc.). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no instances.
confOf:University is an organization that scholars study at, while edas:MealMenu is a document describing meals at meal events. They share no domain overlap.

A 'Two Level Conference' in EDAS is a conference-organisation concept (a conference with two review levels), while 'Agency Staff Member' in EKAW is a person affiliated with an agency. They belong to completely different domains (event vs. person), share no semantic overlap, and their parent hierarchies confirm this divergence.

Accommodation Place in edas is a physical location (a Place) where conference participants can stay, sibling to Conference Venue Place and Dining Place. Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event/activity (under Event > Social Event), sibling to Conference Banquet. One denotes a static venue/location, the other a temporal event; their instances do not coincide.

These properties have entirely different meanings and connect different kinds of entities. 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (who wrote it), while 'updated Version Of' links a Document to a prior Document that it is an updated version of. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

The cmt `name` property relates Conference and Person entities to a string (their name), while the edas `endDate` property relates a Conference to a dateTime (its end date and time). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; one captures a name and the other a temporal endpoint, so they are unrelated.

Entity A is a class representing a published document (a paper artefact) in the edas ontology, while entity B is a class representing a person who is an author of a paper in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different categories of things: a document vs. a person. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Computer Architecture Topic is a subject-area classification (a Topic) in the EDAS ontology, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (an Abstract) in the EKAW ontology. They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

The two properties relate completely different domain and range pairs. confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author, while sigkdd's 'payed by' links a Registration fee to the Person who paid it. They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap.

Committee member in Conference is a subclass of Person (a human who serves on a committee), with children Chair and Co chair. Organization in confOf has children Company and University and is the target of employedBy (Person -> Organization). One denotes an individual person, the other an institution; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

confOf:Workshop is a kind of academic event (a working event with papers, sessions, etc.), whereas iasted:Presenter_state is a state or status of a presenter. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Event vs State) and share no domain overlap.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference gathering itself. ekaw:Conference_Proceedings is a document (subclass of Proceedings > Multi author Volume > Document), denoting the published volume of papers. One is an event, the other a document; neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. confOf:dealsWith connects a Contribution to a Topic (what the paper is about), while sigkdd:submit connects an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Co chair in Conference is a committee co-chair (child of Committee member, sibling of Chair), while ConferenceChair in edas is the overall chair of the conference (child of Person, sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.). These are distinct organizational roles: a committee co-chair is not the same as the conference chair, and neither subsumes the other in the given hierarchies.

Review expertise in Conference denotes the expertise/qualification level of a reviewer for a submitted contribution, while Paper in sigkdd denotes a written document submitted by an author. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Reviewed contribution is a subclass of Submitted contribution, meaning it is a paper that has been reviewed. Paper in edas is a more general class that includes all papers regardless of review status (e.g., Pending Paper, Withdrawn Paper, Active Paper). Thus, every Reviewed contribution is a Paper, but not every Paper is a Reviewed contribution.

confOf:City is a geographic city used as the range of hasCity for Organization and Person (i.e., where organizations/persons are located). ekaw:Location is the range of heldIn for Events (i.e., where an event takes place, which could be a venue, building, campus, or city). These denote different concepts: one is specifically a city/municipality, the other is a generic event location. They do not share the same intended instances, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the different contexts (organizational/personal address vs. event venue).

The EKAW property 'written By' specifically relates a Document to the Person who authored it. The IASTED property 'is designed for' has a broad domain (Activity, Money, Time) and range (Activity, Person), indicating a generic suitability or purpose relation. They connect different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a conference document/item to its author(s), with domain a conference document/item and range Person. The labels 'has authors' and 'is writen by' are synonymous in this domain, and the structure (document -> person) matches.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference fees' is a top-level grouping for all monetary charges associated with a conference (registration, etc.). In sigkdd, 'Fee' has children 'Registration fee' and 'Sponzor fee', making it the more general parent concept. Thus A's 'Conference fees' is subsumed by B's 'Fee' rather than being strictly equivalent, since B's Fee may also include non-conference fee contexts.

Paper Author is a subclass of Person, denoting a human who authors a paper. Registration form is a subclass of Form under Document, denoting a bureaucratic document used for conference registration. They belong to disjoint branches (person vs. document) and share no instances.

Paper Full Version is a concrete document artifact (a full-length paper submitted to a conference), while Test Only Topic is a subject-area classification topic. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Document vs. Topic) and share no instances in common.

cmt's ProgramCommitteeChair is a specific chair role (chair of the program committee), whereas Conference's Chair is a more general chair role (any committee chair). The Conference ontology models chairs generically with properties linking them to committees, while cmt specializes chairs into Conference Chair, Associated Chair, and Program Committee Chair. Thus ProgramCommitteeChair is subsumed by the more general Chair.

The property 'paper ID' in cmt assigns a numeric identifier to a Paper, while 'has amount of' in iasted assigns a monetary quantity to Money. They relate to completely different domains (papers vs. money) and carry different semantics (identifier vs. amount). No reference alignment would equate these.

Entity A is a specific registration fee for an author attending with a book, a leaf class under Registration fee in iasted. Entity B is the general Registration fee class in sigkdd, which has various registration fee subtypes as children. A is a more specific concept subsumed by B.

The property 'write' in iasted relates a Person to an Item (e.g., a person writing a paper), while 'hold' in sigkdd relates an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Free Time Break is a scheduled break during the conference program (sibling of Coffee Break, Meal Break under Break Event), i.e. unallocated time within the academic schedule. Conference Trip is a social/excursion event (sibling of Conference Banquet under Social Event), i.e. an organized outing. They are different kinds of non-academic events: one is a gap in the schedule, the other is a planned social activity. No subsumption holds between them.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Record of attendance in iasted is a document recording attendance (subclass of Document/Item). They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Security Topic is a subclass of Topic in the EDAS ontology, representing a subject area for conference papers. Tutorial Abstract is a subclass of Abstract > Document in the EKAW ontology, representing a type of document. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Place, but 'Conference Venue Place' in EDAS is a broad category covering any venue where conference events take place (including meeting rooms, dining places, etc.), while 'Conference hall' in SIGKDD denotes a specific physical hall/building. A conference hall is a type of conference venue place, so the EDAS class subsumes the SIGKDD class.

IASTED_non_member is a subclass of Delegate (a person who attends the conference but is not an IASTED member). Registration_Non-Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount charged for non-member registration). One is a person, the other is a fee; they denote completely different kinds of entities.

Property A (has_a_review) relates a Reviewed contribution to a Review, i.e., it links a document to its review. Property B (write) relates a Person to an Item, i.e., it links an author to a document they authored. They have different domains (document vs person) and different ranges (review vs item), and they express different relations (having a review vs authoring an item). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

Accommodation Place in edas is a kind of Place (e.g., a hotel or lodging venue where conference attendees stay), whereas Car in iasted is a Transport vehicle (a means of conveyance). They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote completely different concepts in the conference-organisation domain.

Bid (cmt) is a bid placed by a reviewer on a paper, while Publisher (Conference) is an entity that publishes conference proceedings. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while the confOf 'contactEmail' property denotes the contact email of a Contribution. They relate different kinds of things (name vs email) and have different domains (Conference/Person vs Contribution), so they are unrelated.

Rejected Paper is a class denoting a document (a paper that was rejected), while Deadline for notification of acceptance is a class denoting a temporal entity (a deadline). They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies (Document vs Time) and share no instances.

The property 'has a publisher' in Conference relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation that publishes the proceedings). The property 'topicCoveredBy' in ekaw relates a Research Topic to Events or Papers that cover that topic. These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and they express unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

Bid in cmt is a reviewer's bid on a paper (part of the paper assignment process), while Money in iasted represents monetary amounts such as fees, sponsorships, taxes, and tips. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The edas property 'is Member Of' specifically relates a Person to a Conference (membership relation), while the ekaw property 'part Of' is a generic mereological relation with unspecified domain and range. Although both express a 'belonging' of sorts, membership of a person in a conference is conceptually distinct from a generic part-whole relation; a person is not a part of a conference in the mereological sense. The intended semantics differ, so they are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other in this context.

A 'Call For Papers' is an announcement soliciting paper submissions, while a 'Review' is a document evaluating a submitted paper. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. confOf:writtenBy links a Contribution to the Author who wrote it, whereas edas:isMemberOf links a Person to the Conference they are a member of. They have different domains, different ranges, and express different relationships in the conference domain.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Person/Conference Member, representing a person who writes or submits papers. In edas, ConferenceEvent is a class representing events (academic or non-academic) that have locations, dates, programmes, and attendees. These are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is an event. There is no overlap in their intended instances.

hasLastName is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's surname), while is_made_from is an object property from Item to Item (what an item is made from). They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Test Only Topic is a subject-area topic (e.g., antennas, communications, cryptography) used to classify papers, while Best Research Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They belong to completely different conceptual categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are object properties with range Person, but their domains differ: ekaw:writtenBy has domain Document (e.g., papers written by authors), while iasted:is_given_by has domain Activity or Item (e.g., a presentation or lecture given by a person). They overlap in the conference domain (an item such as a paper can be both written and given by someone), but the intended relations are distinct: authorship vs. delivery/presentation. They are related but not equivalent.

In ekaw, Session Chair is a subclass of Person/Conference Participant, denoting a person who chairs a session. In iasted, Session is a subclass of Lecture/Conference activity, denoting an event/activity. These are completely different concepts: a person vs. an event.

Conference announcement is a document type (subclass of Conference document) that denotes an announcement artefact, while Lecture is an activity/event (subclass of Conference activity) denoting a talk or presentation session. They belong to disjoint branches (documents vs. activities) and share no instance overlap.

Both are subclasses of Person and both can be reviewers of papers, but they are not equivalent. Conference Chair is a specific organizational role (the chair of the conference), while Possible Reviewer is a broader category denoting anyone who could potentially review a paper. A Conference Chair may be a possible reviewer, but not every possible reviewer is a Conference Chair. They overlap in instances but have different intended extensions.

These are completely different properties. acceptsHardcopySubmissions is a boolean property indicating whether a Conference accepts hardcopy submissions, while abstract is a string property holding the abstract text of a Contribution. They differ in domain (Conference vs Contribution), range (boolean vs string), and meaning.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (authors, speakers, active participants), while Social event is a subclass of Event (banquets, receptions, trips). These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Participant is a class of people (subclass of Person) who participate in a conference, with subclasses like Member, Regular, and Student. iasted:Memeber_registration_fee is a monetary fee (subclass of Registration fee under Money) charged for member registration. One denotes a person role, the other a financial amount; they share no domain overlap.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while the edas 'hasBiography' property denotes a biographical text of a Person. These are distinct attributes with different meanings and no subsumption relationship between them.

Organizer in the Conference ontology denotes a person or organization responsible for organizing a conference, while Working_event in confOf denotes a type of event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop). These are completely different concepts: one is an agent/role, the other is an event type. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

confOf Trip is a specific kind of social event (a sibling of Banquet and Reception), whereas ekaw Social Event is the general class whose children include Conference Trip and Conference Banquet. Thus Trip is subsumed by Social Event, not equivalent to it.

The confOf 'has Keyword' is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword, while the ekaw 'has Review' is an object property linking a Paper to a Review object. They relate completely different kinds of values and represent different relations in the conference domain.

Property A (has_a_review_reference_or_expertise) relates a Reviewer to their review expertise or preferences, capturing reviewer qualifications/assignments. Property B (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution they have written. These are fundamentally different relations: one is about reviewer expertise/preferences, the other about authorship of a paper. They connect different domain and range types and serve different purposes in the conference organization domain.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a kind of Chairman), while Coffee break is a conference activity/event. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The property hasCountry in edas relates a Conference to a Country (its location country), while speak_in in iasted relates a Person to a Place or Time (where/when they speak). They have completely different domains (Conference vs Person) and different ranges (Country vs Place/Time), and they express fundamentally different relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Working_event is a kind of event (parent Event, siblings Social_event/Administrative_event, children Conference/Tutorial/Workshop) denoting academic activities. iasted:Hotel_room is a kind of place (parent Place, siblings Building/Conference_hall/Session_room, children Single/Double hotel room) denoting lodging accommodations. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In the Conference ontology, 'Information for participants' is a subclass of 'Conference document' — a document providing information to conference participants, alongside siblings like Call for paper, Review, and Conference announcement. In the edas ontology, 'Performance Topic' is a subclass of 'Topic' — a subject-matter topic for papers/sessions, alongside siblings like Antennas Topic, Computer Networks Topic, and Cryptography Topic. One is a document type, the other is a technical subject area; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The property hasDecision in cmt relates a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while obtain in sigkdd relates an Author to an Award. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and no subsumption relationship holds between them.

In confOf, Conference denotes the main conference event itself (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). In iasted, Coffee break is a specific social/schedule activity that occurs during a conference, sibling to Registration, Welcome address, Lecture, etc. They share the word 'Conference' only because the iasted path places Coffee break under 'Conference activity'; the entities denote entirely different things.

A is a person who writes a paper; B is a monetary fee charged to non-authors for registration. They denote completely unrelated concepts despite the superficial lexical overlap of 'author'/'nonauthor'.

Both classes are subclasses of Person and represent reviewers in the conference domain. The confOf ontology explicitly annotates Member_PC with the comment 'Reviewer', and the class has properties 'expert On' and 'reviewes' that align with the reviewing role. The Conference ontology's Reviewer participates in review-related properties (review expertise, review preference, inviting co-reviewers). Despite the different label, the intended instances coincide: people who serve as reviewers/programme committee members.

confOf's 'Submission event' is a specific administrative event denoting the act of submitting contributions, whereas ekaw's 'Event' is the top-level class for all conference events (scientific, social, etc.). The confOf class is a narrow subtype of the broad ekaw Event, so it is subsumed_by it, not equivalent.

These properties operate in completely different domains. 'invited by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer (the person who invited them to review), while 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (the sponsor providing financial support). They have different domains, different ranges, and describe unrelated relationships in the conference organization domain.

Both properties relate an author/person to the paper/document they have authored. The direction is identical (author -> paper). The domain and range are compatible: Author is a sub-class of Person, and Paper is a sub-class of Document. The intended meaning of both properties is to express the authorship relation between a person and their written contribution.

Both properties relate a reviewer role to a Paper in the same direction (reviewer -> paper). The edas domain (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) is a union of committee/reviewer roles that overlaps with ekaw's Possible Reviewer; the range is identical (Paper). The labels 'is Reviewing' and 'reviewer Of Paper' denote the same reviewing relation in the conference domain.

External Reviewer in cmt is a specific person assigned to review on behalf of another Reviewer but who is not themselves a Reviewer. Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a broader concept denoting anyone who could potentially review a paper (subsuming PC Member). The cmt External Reviewer is not a general candidate reviewer but a delegated non-PC reviewer; the two concepts do not share the same intended instances, and neither subsumes the other in a clear direction.

Presenter (ekaw) is a conference participant who presents (parent: Conference Participant, child: Invited Speaker), whereas Student non speaker (iasted) is explicitly a delegate who does NOT speak (parent: Non speaker). These are disjoint categories of conference participants, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or overlapping.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop), denoting the academic meeting itself. iasted:Conference_building is a physical place (subclass of Building, sibling of Conference hotel/airport/restaurant), denoting the venue structure. These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a physical location. No subsumption holds either, since a conference event is not a kind of building nor vice versa.

Conference in ontology A denotes an academic conference event (with conference volumes, proceedings, parts, topics, publishers), while Organization in confOf denotes an organizational entity (with subtypes Company and University, and properties like employedBy, hasCity, hasCountry, hasPostalCode, hasStreet). These are fundamentally different domain concepts: a conference event vs. an organization that might host or be affiliated with a conference. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

startDate denotes the beginning date/time of a conference, while End_of_conference denotes the ending date/time. They are temporally opposite attributes of the same domain entity (Conference) and range (dateTime), so they do not denote the same relation; nor is one more general than the other. They are distinct, non-overlapping properties.

Property A ('is the 1th part of') relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation, indicating a part-whole relationship where the abstract is a component of a larger work. Property B ('give') relates a Person to an Activity/Item, indicating that a person gives or presents something. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing a call for submissions, while Company is an organization type (a commercial entity). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

Author Not Reviewer in cmt is an Author who is explicitly not a Reviewer, a restriction based on role exclusion. Presenter in edas is an Author who presents a paper, a restriction based on activity. The sets do not coincide: an author who is not a reviewer may not present, and a presenter could also be a reviewer. Neither subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

The cmt 'addedBy' property records which Administrator added a Program Committee Member to the system, whereas the Conference 'was_a_committe_co-chair_of' property records which Committee a Co-chair co-chaired. They have different domains (Program Committee Member vs Co chair), different ranges (Administrator vs Committee), and describe completely different relationships in the conference-organisation domain.

The two properties relate completely different things: 'has an abstract' links a paper/poster/presentation to its Abstract, while 'is Written By' links a Paper to its Author. They have different domains and ranges and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'was a member of' links a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation), while 'organised By' links an Event to an Organisation or Person (organisational responsibility). Different domains, different ranges, different semantics.

In the Conference ontology, Person is a broad class covering all people involved in a conference (committee members, applicants, contributors, participants, reviewers, chairs). In sigkdd, Author is a specific subclass of Speaker, denoting only authors of papers. Thus Person subsumes Author: every Author is a Person, but not every Person is an Author.

Trip in confOf is a social event (e.g., excursion, banquet, reception) that occurs during a conference. Receiving manuscript in iasted is an administrative activity before the conference where submitted papers are received. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties link a Paper to its Author(s) with the same domain (Paper) and range (Author). 'has Author' and 'is Written By' are synonymous relations in the conference domain, both expressing the authorship relation from the paper's perspective.

In ekaw, Presenter is a specialized Conference Participant who presents at a conference, with Invited Speaker as a child. In sigkdd, Speaker is a direct child of Person and has broader scope: it includes Author as a child, suggesting any author who presents a paper is considered a Speaker. The sigkdd Speaker class is more general than ekaw's Presenter, since Presenter requires being a Conference Participant (a registered attendee) while sigkdd Speaker is any Person who gives a presentation. Thus ekaw Presenter is subsumed by sigkdd Speaker.

Conference applicant is a person who applies to attend a conference (subclass of Person), while Research is an activity performed before a conference (subclass of Activity). One is a person, the other is an activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption hierarchy.

The confOf 'employed By' property relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while the ekaw 'technically Organises' property relates an Organisation to something it technically organises (e.g., an event). These are entirely different relations with different domains and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a Paper to its subject area / topic. 'Subject Area' and 'Topic' are synonymous in the conference domain, and both properties have Paper as domain and Topic/SubjectArea as range. The edas property additionally includes Conference as a domain, but the Paper->Topic portion aligns directly with cmt's Paper->SubjectArea.

A is a person who writes papers (Author in cmt, under Person > Conference Member). B is a monetary fee for member registration (under Money > Fee > Registration fee). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

hasPostalCode relates Contact Information to a postal code string, while E-mail relates Person to an email address string. These are completely different attributes with different domains and different semantic meanings.

A Presenter in edas is a person (subclass of Author) who presents a paper. B Presenter house in iasted is a building/place where a presenter stays during the conference. They are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is a physical venue. No overlap in intended instances.

Delegate in iasted is a person who attends a conference (a subclass of Person), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place where conference sessions are held. These are completely different categories of entities (person vs. place) with no semantic overlap.

Both properties share the same domain (Person) and relate a person to a document-like entity (Conference document vs. Item). However, 'contributes' specifically denotes authorship or contribution of a conference document, while 'sign' denotes the act of signing an item, which is a broader and different action. The ranges differ in specificity and the relations denote different kinds of involvement, so they are related but not equivalent.

In ontology A, Conference is the top-level event/organisation concept (with child Conference volume and a name property). In ekaw, Proceedings is a kind of Document (path: Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings), i.e. the published volume of papers. A conference and its proceedings are distinct entities in the conference domain; neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Review is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a paper. In edas, ReviewQuestion is a question item in a review form (numerical or textual), not the review itself. These are different concepts with no direct overlap in intended instances.

A Registeered applicant is a person who has applied for conference registration, while a Delegate is a broader category covering all conference participants (speakers, listeners, session chairs, committee members, etc.). A registered applicant who is accepted and attends becomes a delegate, so Registeered applicant is subsumed by Delegate.

Conference contributor (A) denotes a person who contributes academic content to a conference (e.g., authors of papers, invited speakers, active participants). Its children are Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author. Organizator (B) denotes a person who handles the organizational/administrative side of running a conference. Its children are General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, and Webmaster. These are disjoint sets of roles: a contributor creates and presents content, while an organizer manages logistics and the committee structure. Although both are subclasses of Person, their intended instances do not overlap, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Property A is a datatype property mapping a Person to their last name (string), while property B is an object property mapping an Item to the Item it is made from. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

A's 'has a name' applies to multiple entity types (Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic) and denotes a general naming property, while B's 'has Title' is specific to Contribution and denotes a title. Although both are datatype properties with range string, their domains and intended meanings differ; A is more general than B.
confOf Reception is a social event (e.g., a banquet or trip), while ekaw Negative Review is a document evaluating a paper. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

Tax (e.g., Departure tax, Value added tax) is a compulsory levy imposed by a government, whereas Registration fee is a conference attendance charge. They share only the distant parent Money/Fee and have disjoint intended instances.

Wireless Communications Topic is a subject-area topic (sibling of Communication Theory Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.), while Invited Talk is a type of scientific event/presentation (sibling of Contributed Talk, Tutorial). They denote completely different things: a research topic vs. a presentation format.
Banquet is a social event (e.g., conference dinner), while Publication is an item such as a book proceeding or CD. They share no domain overlap.

The cmt 'date' property captures a temporal value (a date) associated with a Conference, whereas the Conference ontology 'has a URL' captures a string URL associated with a Conference www object. They denote completely different attributes (temporal vs. locator), so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Positive_Review is a specific subclass of Review (alongside Negative_Review and Neutral_Review), denoting only reviews with a positive verdict. In sigkdd, Review is the general class of reviews (a subclass of Document). Thus ekaw:Positive_Review is strictly more specific than sigkdd:Review, so the relation is subsumed_by.

Both relate a person to a written work they authored: Conference.contributes has domain Person and range Conference document, while edas.hasRelatedPaper has domain Author and range Paper. Author is a narrower class than Person, and Paper is a narrower class than Conference document, so hasRelatedPaper is a more specific property than contributes. They are not equivalent because contributes can apply to any Person (not only authors) and can point to any conference document (not only papers).

Scientific Event in ekaw is a kind of event (e.g., conference, session, workshop, track). Author in sigkdd is a person who submits papers and receives notifications/awards. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific leadership role (a Chairman who assists the Conference Chair), whereas Member PC in confOf denotes a regular program committee member/reviewer. They occupy different positions in the conference hierarchy and their intended instances do not coincide.

confOf:Short_paper is a type of academic contribution (a short paper submitted to a conference), sibling to Paper and Poster under Contribution. iasted:Mailing_list is a type of document (a mailing list record), sibling to Form, Invitation letter, Review, Submission, etc. under Document. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Subject Area in cmt denotes a topical category for classifying papers, while Country in edas denotes a geographical entity. They share no semantic overlap despite both being associated with a has-property.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'has_been_assigned_a_review_reference' links a submitted contribution (or topic) to a review preference, capturing the assignment of a review preference to a paper. In ontology B, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item, capturing the action of a person giving a presentation or item. The domains (Submitted contribution/Topic vs Person) and ranges (Review preference vs Activity/Item) do not overlap, and the relations denote different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf's writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper). edas's isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship it provides. These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

The property 'is submitted at' relates a Conference contribution to the Conference volume where it is submitted, while 'awarded by' relates an Award to whatever entity grants the award. These are entirely different relations involving different domain concepts (paper submission vs. award granting), so they are unrelated.

Paid applicant is a person who has paid registration fees, while Payment document is a financial document such as a bank transfer or cheque. They are completely different kinds of entities (person vs. document).

Both are conference contributions/documents, but an Extended abstract is a specific short summary document, while a Conference Paper is a full paper presented at a conference. They are sibling-level concepts in their respective hierarchies (Extended abstract is a sibling of Paper in ontology A), so they overlap as conference contributions but are not equivalent.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'has a submitted contribution' links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (i.e., what paper a reviewer is assigned to review). In ontology B, 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (i.e., who presents a document). The domains (Review expertise vs. Document) and ranges (Submitted contribution vs. Speaker) are disjoint, and the relations describe different aspects of the conference domain.

Accepted_contribution is a class representing a paper/contribution that has been accepted for publication at a conference, while Deadline_hotel_reservation is a temporal deadline for booking hotel accommodations. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

hasBiography denotes a biographical text about a person, while Name denotes the person's name. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they represent fundamentally different attributes of a person and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Property A (has_tutorials) relates a Conference volume to its constituent Tutorial parts, while property B (need) relates a Person to an Item they require. They have different domains (Conference volume vs Person), different ranges (Tutorial vs Item), and different semantics (partitive relation vs requirement relation).

A Workshop Paper is a document (academic paper) in ekaw, while a Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle in iasted. They belong to completely disjoint branches of their ontologies and share no domain overlap.

Paper Full Version in cmt denotes the complete/extended version of a paper (as opposed to a Paper Abstract), distinguishing by content completeness. Industrial Paper in ekaw denotes a paper from industry (as opposed to academic), distinguishing by authorship source. These are orthogonal classification dimensions: a paper could be both a full version and industrial, or either one without the other. Their sibling structures confirm this: cmt contrasts full version vs. abstract, while ekaw contrasts industrial vs. regular/conference/workshop/demo papers. No subsumption relationship holds between them.

Invited speaker is a conference contributor distinguished by being invited to speak, while Author of paper student is a student who authored a paper. An invited speaker need not be a student or an author, and a student author need not be an invited speaker. The two classes have distinct defining criteria and their intended instances do not coincide.

A Workshop is an academic event (a type of conference session/meeting), while Author cd proceedings included is a specific role/person (an author whose paper is included in CD proceedings). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (events vs. persons/roles) and share no instances in common.

The property 'has authors' in Conference relates a Conference document to a Person (the author of the document), whereas 'speak in' in iasted relates a Person to a Place or Time (where/when they speak). These properties have different domains, different ranges, and express completely different relationships in the conference domain.

In ontology A, 'Reviewed contribution' is a contribution (paper) that has been reviewed, sitting under Written contribution > Submitted contribution. In ontology B, 'Review' is the review document itself, sitting under Document with siblings like Paper and Flyer. These are disjoint concepts: one is the artefact being reviewed, the other is the review artefact. They are not equivalent, nor is there a subsumption relation between them.

Track in the Conference ontology is a conference part (like a session or stream of papers), while Tax in the iasted ontology is a monetary amount (e.g., departure tax, VAT). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

The two properties operate at different levels of granularity. In ontology A, 'was an organizing committee of' links an Organizing committee (a sub-organization/committee entity) to a Conference volume, representing the relationship between a committee and the conference it organizes. In ontology B, 'hold' links ACM SIGKDD (the parent organization/society) to a Conference, representing the relationship between the overarching organization and the conferences it holds. The domains differ (a committee vs. the parent organization) and the ranges differ (a conference volume vs. a conference). These are structurally and semantically distinct relationships, so they are not equivalent.

The property 'is Review History Of' in edas links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer, indicating which reviewer performed a review history. The property 'give' in iasted links a Person to an Activity or Item, indicating that a person gives/presents an activity or item. These properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions and contexts; one is about review history ownership, the other about presenting or giving activities/items. They do not denote the same relation.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference occurrence itself. edas:ConferenceVenuePlace is a physical location (subclass of Place, sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) where a conference is held. These are fundamentally different concepts: an event vs. a geographical/physical venue.

These properties operate in completely different domains. In cmt, 'has Co author' links a Paper to its Co-author (a person who co-authored the paper). In the Conference ontology, 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to a Co-chair (a person who co-chairs the committee). The domains (Paper vs. Committee) and ranges (Co-author vs. Co-chair) are entirely different concepts with no overlap in the conference organization domain.

The confOf 'employed By' property relates a Person to the Organization that employs them, while the ekaw 'publisher Of' property relates an Organisation to the documents/publications it publishes (Flyer, Multi author volume, Programme brochure, Web site). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and express entirely different relationships (employment vs. publishing), so they are unrelated.

Review and Abstract are distinct concepts in the conference domain. A Review is a document written by a reviewer evaluating a paper, while an Abstract is a summary of a paper's content. They are siblings under Document in their respective ontologies but denote different kinds of documents with different purposes.

Property A is 'has the first name' (a person's given name), while property B is 'E mail' (a person's electronic mail address). These are completely different attributes of a Person, despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string). They denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Both classes denote the same role in a conference: a person who chairs a session. They share the same label and both are subclasses of Person (edas) / Conference Participant, which is itself a subclass of Person (ekaw). The surrounding siblings in both ontologies are conference roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, TPC Member vs. PC Chair, Tutorial Chair, Workshop Chair), confirming the same intended meaning.

confOf:Student is a class denoting a person (a kind of conference participant who is a student). sigkdd:Registration_SIGMOD_Member is a class denoting a registration fee category for SIGMOD members. One is a person/role, the other is a fee/registration type; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.
confOf:hasTitle applies to Contribution (e.g., paper titles) while edas:hasName applies to Conference (full conference name). They relate to different entities and denote different concepts.

In ontology Conference, 'Conference proceedings' is a published volume (with ISBN, publisher, volume number) — a document/artefact. In ekaw, 'Conference' is a scientific event (one edition of a conference). These are completely different kinds of entities: a published book vs. an event, so they are unrelated.

A 'Paper Full Version' in CMT denotes the complete/extended version of a paper (contrasted with a 'Paper Abstract' sibling), whereas a 'Poster Paper' in EKAW denotes a paper accepted as a poster presentation (contrasted with Regular, Demo, Industrial, Workshop papers). These are orthogonal classifications: a full version could be any type of paper, and a poster paper could itself have a full version. The labels, sibling structure, and domain semantics indicate distinct concepts with no direct equivalence or subsumption.

Conference contributor (A) denotes a person who contributes to the conference by submitting a paper or presenting (children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author). Administrator (B) denotes an administrative role (confTool), not a contributor of academic content. They share only the parent Person, but their intended instances are disjoint.

In cmt, Review is a document written by a reviewer about a paper. In edas, Review Rating is a rating value (Accept, Reject, etc.) assigned to an active paper. One is a document, the other is an evaluation score; they denote completely different concepts.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length paper document in the cmt ontology (Document > Paper > PaperFullVersion), whereas MicroelectronicsTopic is a subject-area topic in the edas ontology (Topic > MicroelectronicsTopic). They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

A 'Presenter house' is a specific kind of building where a presenter stays (a lodging), whereas 'Hotel' in sigkdd is a general place for lodging/accommodation. Hotel is more general than Presenter house, so Presenter_house is subsumed_by Hotel.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges. 'technicallyOrganises' has domain Organisation and relates an organisation to something it technically organises (an event/activity). 'occupy' has domain Person and range Building/City/State, describing a person occupying a physical location. They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap.

Academic Institution in ekaw is an organization (parent Organisation, children University and Research Institute), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person (parent Person, children Author and Invited Speaker). They belong to disjoint branches of the ontology hierarchy and denote completely different categories of entities.

The property 'is Initiated By' in edas relates a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the committee members who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). The property 'is visited by' in iasted relates a geographic or built entity (Building, City, State) to a Person who visits it. These properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges and denote unrelated relationships in the conference organization domain.

A is a specific subject topic (optical computer networks) under a Topic hierarchy, while B is a type of presentation event (a contributed talk) under an Event hierarchy. They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a person role in a conference committee (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference city is a geographic location (subclass of City). They denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

hasVAT is a datatype property associating events with a string value representing value added tax, while heldIn is an object property associating events with a Location. They relate events to completely different kinds of values and have no semantic overlap.

In EKAW, Conference Participant is a broad superclass covering any person who participates in a conference (chairs, presenters, registered attendees, committee members, etc.). In IASTED, Speaker is a subclass of Delegate and specifically denotes a delegate who speaks at the conference.
