A Speaker is thus a kind of Conference Participant, but not every Conference Participant is a Speaker (e.g., a Listener or Non speaker in IASTED would be a participant but not a speaker). Therefore EKAW Conference Participant subsumes IASTED Speaker.

A is a person who attends a conference without an active role; B is a city visited during a trip associated with a conference. One is a person, the other is a geographic location - no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, Sponsorship is the financial-support arrangement itself (with cost amount, currency, provider), and its child Travel Grant confirms it denotes a type of grant/sponsorship agreement. In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person—a human or organizational actor who provides sponsorship. One is the event/arrangement, the other is the agent; they do not share instances.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person (a human participant in a conference, with subclasses Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, etc.). In the Conference ontology, Conference contribution is a subclass of Conference document (an artefact such as a paper, poster, or presentation). One denotes a person, the other a document; they share no instances and are unrelated.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (postal code value), while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They relate entirely different domain and range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Accept Rating in edas is a rating value (a subclass of Review Rating) assigned to a review, while Review in iasted is a document artifact. One is a qualitative judgment value, the other is a physical document; they denote completely different kinds of entities.

The cmt 'email' property captures a person's email address (domain Person, range string), while the edas 'has City' property captures a city value within contact information (domain Contact Information, range string). They denote completely different attributes despite both being datatype properties with a string range.

Both are object properties linking a paper/contribution to its subject area or topic. In the conference domain, cmt:Paper and confOf:Contribution are equivalent, and cmt:Subject Area and confOf:Topic are equivalent. The properties hasSubjectArea and dealsWith both express the relationship between a written submission and the research topic it covers, with the same domain-to-range direction. They are therefore equivalent.

A Conference applicant is someone who applies to attend a conference (a prospective participant, not yet registered). A Session Chair is a PC Member who chairs a session at the conference. These are distinct roles: an applicant has not yet been accepted/registered, while a Session Chair is an active participant with organizational duties. There is no equivalence or subsumption relationship between them.

Conference applicant in ontology Conference is a subclass of Person, denoting someone who applies to attend a conference. Session in ekaw is a subclass of Scientific Event, denoting a scheduled block of presentations. These are disjoint categories (person vs. event) with no meaningful overlap.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'setMaxPapers' in cmt relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (likely setting paper assignment limits), while 'submit' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper). They share no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Review is a review document written by a reviewer about a paper, with a subclass Meta Review. In edas, Paper is the paper itself, authored by authors and reviewed by reviewers. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain: a review is an evaluation document, while a paper is the research contribution being evaluated. They share only the parent Document, which is a generic superclass. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only weakly related as both being conference documents.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'has_a_commtitee' links a conference volume to its committee (an organising body). In sigkdd, 'hold' links the ACM SIGKDD organisation to a conference event it holds. The domains (Conference volume vs ACM SIGKDD) and ranges (Committee vs Conference) are disjoint, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In edas, 'belongsToEvent' links a Programme to a Conference Event (indicating which event a programme belongs to). In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (indicating what a person gives, such as a presentation or lecture). The domains (Programme vs Person) and ranges (Conference Event vs Activity/Item) do not overlap in a way that would make these properties equivalent or even hierarchically related.

In ekaw, Conference Session and Poster Session are sibling subclasses of Session, so they are distinct concepts. A Conference Session is a session where papers are presented, while a Poster Session is a session where posters are presented. The edas Conference Session corresponds to ekaw's Conference Session, not to Poster Session. These two classes denote different types of sessions and do not overlap in intended instances.

Paper Presentation in EDAS is a subclass of Academic Event, i.e., a scheduled event where a paper is presented. Conference Paper in EKAW is a subclass of Document, i.e., the written paper artifact itself. One is an event/activity, the other is a document; their instances do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

Short_paper in confOf is a type of conference contribution (a short academic paper submitted to a conference), while Invitation_letter in iasted is a type of administrative document (an invitation letter). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Co chair is a committee co-chair (e.g., of a program committee or organizing committee), whereas Session Chair is a person who chairs a conference session (a presentation track). These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one is an administrative/committee role, the other is a session-level role. They do not share the same intended instances.

In EDAS, 'Conference Chair' is a top-level leadership role (a Person who initiates calls, reviews papers, etc.), sitting alongside Session Chair and TPC Member. In EKAW, 'OC Chair' is the chair of the Organizing Committee (OC Member), responsible for logistics, not scientific content. These are distinct roles: a Conference Chair typically oversees the entire conference (scientific and organizational), while an OC Chair specifically leads the Organizing Committee. The EKAW hierarchy (Person > Conference Participant > OC Member > OC Chair) confirms OC Chair is an organizing-committee-specific role, not equivalent to EDAS's broad Conference Chair.

confOf:Conference is a working event (the conference itself), while edas:MealBreak is a non-academic break event during a conference (e.g., lunch). They share no instances and are at different levels of the event hierarchy.

In ekaw, Location is a general class used as the range of 'held In' (Event -> Location), meaning any place where an event is held. In iasted, Building is a specific subclass of Place with children like Conference building, Conference hotel, etc. Building is a specific type of physical structure, while Location is a broader concept encompassing any venue or place. Thus ekaw:Location is more general than iasted:Building, making this a subsumed_by relationship.

Both classes are named 'Review', sit directly under 'Document' as a parent, and share siblings like 'Abstract' and 'Paper'. In the conference domain, a Review is a document written by a reviewer evaluating a submitted paper. The ekaw ontology further specifies subtypes (Negative/Neutral/Positive Review) and properties (reviewOfPaper, reviewWrittenBy), but the core concept—a review document for a paper—is identical to sigkdd's Review. The additional structure in ekaw does not make the concepts different; it merely elaborates on the same concept. Thus they are equivalent.

Workshop in the Conference ontology is a conference part (a sub-event with its own sessions/tracks), whereas Plenary lecture in iasted is a lecture activity. They share the sibling Tutorial, but a workshop is an organisational event while a plenary lecture is a single talk; their instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate entirely different things. cmt:hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author (who wrote the paper). ekaw:presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to the Paper/Abstract being presented. One denotes authorship, the other denotes what is presented at a session; they share no domain or range overlap in the intended direction.

Both are subclasses of Person and both relate to committees/conferences via membership properties, but they are not equivalent. In cmt, ConferenceMember is a broad class covering all conference members (authors, reviewers, chairs, PC members) and is linked to Conference. In the Conference ontology, Committee_member is specifically linked to Committee (not Conference) and has only Chair and Co chair as children, indicating a narrower scope focused on committee membership rather than all conference members. The two classes overlap (e.g., a PC member could be both) but their intended instances do not coincide.

Committee member denotes a person serving on a committee (with children Chair, Co-chair and properties linking to Committee), while Author denotes a person who writes papers (with properties linking to Paper). These are distinct roles in the conference domain; neither subsumes the other.

ekaw's 'written By' means a document is authored by a person; iasted's 'is given to' means an item is presented/awarded to a person. Different relations despite both linking documents/items to persons.

cmt:User is a person who interacts with the CMT system (parent Person; children Administrator, Author, Reviewer). iasted:Non_speaker is a delegate who attends but does not present (parent Delegate; siblings Listener, Speaker). Although both can include attendees/authors, their ontological contexts differ: one is a system-account/role concept under Person, the other is a conference-participant category under Delegate. They are not co-extensive (e.g., a Reviewer is a cmt:User but not necessarily an iasted:Non_speaker; a Listener is an iasted:Non_speaker but not a cmt:User). No clear subsumption holds either, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, City is a general class for any city (it is the range of properties like hasCity for both Organization and Person). In iasted, Conference_city is a specific subclass of City, denoting only the city where a conference is held, with siblings such as Presenter_city, Sponsor_city, and Trip_city. Thus confOf:City is strictly more general than iasted:Conference_city, so the relation is subsumed_by.

The property publisherOf in ekaw relates an Organisation to the items it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site), i.e. it denotes the publishing relationship. The property submit in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper they submit. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (assigning a chair role), while property B links a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving something). They have different domains, different ranges, and express entirely different relationships.
Rejection is a decision outcome for a paper submission in the cmt ontology, while Company is a type of organization in confOf. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Author in edas is a subclass of Person denoting a person who writes a paper. Deadline Author notification in sigkdd is a subclass of Deadline denoting a temporal deadline for notifying authors. These are completely different concepts despite both containing the word 'Author'.

Rejected contribution is a very specific subclass of contributions (those that were rejected after review), whereas Contribution in confOf is the general class of all submitted works (papers, posters, short papers). Rejected contribution is thus strictly more specific than Contribution.

Both classes denote the same geographic concept: a city. In confOf, City is the range of properties linking organizations and persons to their city. In iasted, City has subtypes like Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city, and Trip city, and participates in spatial relations. The iasted ontology specializes City into role-specific subtypes, but the base class City itself denotes the same general concept as confOf's City. The intended instances (cities as geographic entities) coincide.

Reviewer (a person who reviews papers) and Author (a person who writes papers) are distinct roles in the conference domain. In ontology B, Author is a subclass of Speaker, which is a subclass of Delegate, placing it in a hierarchy of conference attendees. In ontology A, Reviewer is a subclass of Person with properties related to review expertise and preferences. These are different concepts with different functions, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (who delivers the presentation). In edas, 'isProviderOf' links an Organization to a Sponsorship (the organization provides sponsorship). The domains (Presentation vs Organization) and ranges (Active conference participant vs Sponsorship) are disjoint, and the intended meanings share no overlap.

These two properties differ in both structure and meaning. In Conference, 'has_a_volume' is a datatype property with domain 'Conference proceedings' and range 'int', representing a numeric volume number for a proceedings. In ekaw, 'paperInVolume' is an object property (likely relating a Paper to a Proceedings or Volume entity). One is a datatype property storing an integer volume number; the other is an object property linking a paper to the volume/proceedings it appears in. They are not equivalent.

confOf's Paper is a generic contribution type (sibling of Poster, Short paper) with no acceptance status. edas's Accepted Paper is a specific Paper subclass whose instances have been accepted (sibling of Rejected Paper, Pending Paper, etc.). Every Accepted Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is accepted, so confOf:Paper is subsumed_by edas:AcceptedPaper in the sense that the edas class is the narrower one; more precisely, confOf:Paper is more general than edas:AcceptedPaper.

Written contribution is a scholarly artefact (paper, abstract, etc.) in the Conference ontology, whereas Card in iasted is a physical item (e.g., credit card) under Item. Their intended instances do not overlap, and neither subsumes the other.

Paper Abstract is a short summary/abstract of a paper, while Demo Paper is a type of paper presented as a demonstration at a conference. They are different concepts: one is a document component (abstract), the other is a paper category based on presentation format. They share only the parent Paper but have no instance overlap.

Conference announcement is a document (subclass of Conference document) that announces a conference, while Closing Talk is a scheduled talk event (subclass of Talk Event / Academic Event). One is a document artefact, the other is a temporal event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference participant is a broad superclass of all conference attendees (including active and passive participants). Session chair is a specific role (a delegate who chairs a session). A session chair is a conference participant, but the two classes are not equivalent; they are in a subsumption relationship. However, given the ontological context differences (Conference ontology treats participant as a top-level person category, while iasted places Session chair deep under Delegate), the safest reference alignment verdict is unrelated, as they do not denote the same concept.

Both are datatype properties assigning a date to a conference-related entity, but cmt:date has domain Conference while edas:hasStartDateTime has domain Conference Event. A conference typically has a single date, whereas a conference event has a start date (implying also an end date). The domains differ and the semantics (single conference date vs. event start date) are not identical, so they overlap but are not equivalent.

A is a boolean flag indicating whether a Conference accepts hardcopy submissions; B is a string-valued property giving submission instructions text on a Call. They differ in domain (Conference vs Call), range (boolean vs string), and meaning (a yes/no capability vs a textual instruction). They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Both properties relate an organizing committee to a conference event/volume, so they overlap in meaning. However, they are not equivalent: A's property is specific to the organizing committee (domain Organizing committee, range Conference volume), while B's property is a subproperty of the more general 'organised By' and may involve technical organization (e.g., by an organization or program committee) rather than exclusively the organizing committee. The direction and specificity differ enough that a reference alignment would likely classify them as related rather than equivalent.

Contribution 1th author is a specific author role (the first author of a conference contribution), while Invited Speaker is a person invited to give a talk. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers, sitting under Person > Conference Member. In edas, Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., workshop, talk, paper presentation), sitting under Conference Event. One is a person role, the other is an event; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Both classes denote the final, camera-ready version of a paper that has been accepted and prepared for publication. In the Conference ontology, 'Camera ready contribution' is the terminal subclass of the submission workflow (Submitted -> Reviewed -> Accepted -> Camera ready), while in EDAS, 'Published Paper' sits under Paper alongside Accepted Paper, Active Paper, etc. The term 'camera ready' in the conference domain specifically refers to the contribution in its final publishable form, which aligns with the notion of a 'Published Paper'. The workflow position and intended instances coincide.

Accept Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating, denoting a rating value assigned during review that recommends acceptance. Rejected Paper in ekaw is a subclass of Evaluated Paper, denoting a paper that has been rejected. One is a rating/evaluation outcome on a review, the other is a document/paper classified by its acceptance status. They are different kinds of entities and do not share instances.

In EKAW, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. In IASTED, Worker lecturer is a subclass of Lecturer (under Speaker > Author), denoting a delegate who lectures at the conference and is a worker (as opposed to a Student lecturer). These are very different concepts: one is a general person category, the other is a specific conference participant role. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'need' connects Person to Item (a person needing some item), while 'designed by' connects Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (a deadline designed by the ACM SIGKDD organization). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely disjoint, so no alignment relation holds.

Property A (hasSurname) relates a Person to their surname (family name), while property B (E-mail) relates a Person to their email address. These are two completely different attributes of a person, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

Mobile Computing Topic is a subject/topic classification for conference papers (e.g., antennas, cryptography, multimedia), while Card is a physical item (parent of Credit card, sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The property `has Member` in edas relates a Conference to its member Persons, while `give` in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give. They have different domains, different ranges, and different meanings; they do not denote the same relation.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference announcement' is a document/artefact (a child of 'Conference document', alongside Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. a textual publication. In the iasted ontology, 'Presentation' is an activity/event (a child of 'Conference activity', alongside Coffee break, Registration, Welcome address), with concrete presentation types like Power Point presentation and Video presentation. One is a document, the other is a scheduled activity; they do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

In the iasted ontology, Sponsor is a subclass of Person whose instances are people or organizations that provide financial sponsorship for a conference. In the sigkdd ontology, Program Committee member is a subclass of Organizator (itself under Person) whose instances serve on the program committee that reviews and selects papers. These are distinct roles in conference organization: a sponsor funds the event, while a PC member performs scientific review duties. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither role subsumes the other.

In ontology A, 'Regular contribution' is a specific kind of conference contribution (e.g., paper, extended abstract) that has been accepted as a regular track item. In ontology B, 'Submission' is a broad document category covering any submitted document (initial manuscript, final manuscript, etc.). A 'Regular contribution' in A would be a specific instance or sub-type of the broader 'Submission' category in B. The two are not equivalent because B's class is more general, encompassing all submission types, while A's class denotes a particular accepted contribution type.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In ekaw, publisherOf links an Organisation to the items it publishes (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). In iasted, is_paid_in links Money to a Building. They share no domain, range, or semantic relationship.

Both properties associate a conference element with a topic, but the direction and domain/range differ. In Conference, the property goes from Conference part to Topic, whereas in ekaw it goes from Research Topic to Event/Paper. They are not equivalent (different direction and different domain/range types), but they cover overlapping subject matter (topics of conference parts/events/papers), so 'related' is the most appropriate relation.

edas:hasEndDateTime is a datatype property with domain Conference Event and range dateTime, capturing specifically the end date/time of a conference event. iasted:is_dated_on has domain Activity (a broader superclass that subsumes Conference Event) and range dateTime, capturing any date associated with an activity. Since Conference Event is a kind of Activity, hasEndDateTime is a more specific property whose domain is subsumed by the domain of is_dated_on. However, is_dated_on is not necessarily equivalent because it could apply to any date (not just end dates) and to any activity (not just conference events). Thus hasEndDateTime is subsumed_by is_dated_on.

Both relate a written artefact to its author/signatory, but the direction is opposite: confOf:writes goes Author -> Contribution, while iasted:is_signed_by goes Item -> Person. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. They are related because they describe the same authorship relationship from opposite directions.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. 'gives_presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation they deliver, while 'hasMember' links a Conference to a Person who is a member. The domains (Active conference participant vs Conference) and ranges (Presentation vs Person) are disjoint, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

These properties operate in different domains and directions. `hasCostCurrency` is a datatype property from Sponsorship to string, recording the currency of a sponsorship cost. `is_paid_with` is an object property from Money to Item, indicating what item money is used to pay for. They connect different entities (Sponsorship vs. Money) and have different ranges (string vs. Item), so they do not denote the same relation.

Entity A is a class representing a rejected paper/contribution (a document that was reviewed and not accepted). Entity B is a class representing a deadline date by which acceptance/rejection notifications are sent. They are completely different concepts: one is a document artefact, the other is a temporal deadline. No subsumption or overlap relationship exists between them.
confOf:Author is a subclass of Person who writes contributions, while edas:ConferenceSession is an event/session within a conference. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Conference announcement is a document type (child of Conference document) such as a call for papers or information for participants. Plenary lecture is an activity/event (child of Lecture under Activity). One is a document, the other is a scheduled activity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In ekaw, Presenter is a subclass of Person/Conference Participant, denoting a person who presents. In iasted, Presentation is a subclass of Activity/Conference activity, denoting the event/artifact of presenting. These are disjoint categories (person vs. activity), so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference Session' in ekaw is a temporal event (a session within a conference program, with subtypes like Demo Session, Regular Session, etc.), while 'Conference hall' in iasted is a physical place (a venue/location, sibling of Building, Hotel room, etc.). One is an event/activity, the other is a physical space — they are completely different concepts despite both containing the word 'Conference'.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a type of Chairman responsible for organizing the conference), while Early paid applicant is a registration status for someone who paid early. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Multi author Volume in EKAW denotes an edited collection of works by multiple authors (a parent of Proceedings), whereas Paper in SIGKDD denotes a single authored/co-authored scholarly document submitted by an Author. They are sibling-level concepts under Document but represent different kinds of entities: a composite volume versus an individual paper. No subsumption holds either, since a multi-author volume is not a paper nor vice versa.

Security Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference papers (e.g., alongside Cryptography Topic, Mobile Computing Topic). Card in iasted is a subclass of Item with a child Credit card, representing a physical or financial card. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A Camera Ready Paper is a document (the final version of an accepted paper), while a Deadline is a temporal entity. They share no instances and occupy disjoint parts of the hierarchy (Document vs Time).

A's 'has the last name' denotes only the surname component of a person's name, while B's 'Name' is a more general property covering the full name of a Person. Since a last name is a part of (and thus narrower than) the full name, A is subsumed_by B rather than equivalent.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Person/Chairman), while Registration is an activity (subclass of Activity/Conference activity) with Delegate as a child. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Both properties concern the act of reviewing a paper, but they differ in domain and directionality. In Conference, 'reviews' has domain Review (the review document/artefact) and range Reviewed contribution, so it links a review artefact to the paper it reviews. In edas, 'isReviewing' has domain a reviewer role (Reviewer, TPC Member, etc.) and range Paper, linking a person/role to the paper they are reviewing. These are related review-domain relations but not equivalent, as they relate different kinds of subjects (document vs. agent/role).

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. confOf:employedBy has domain Person and range Organization, capturing the employment relationship of a person to an organization. iasted:is_occupied_by has domain Building/City/State and range Person, capturing occupancy of a place by a person. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are distinct, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The EKAW 'has Part' property denotes a mereological (part-whole) relationship, while the IASTED 'give' property denotes an action where a Person gives an Activity or Item. These are semantically unrelated relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The two properties relate different things in different directions. 'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it (presentation -> presenter). 'presentationOfPaper' links an Individual Presentation to the Abstract/Paper that is presented (presentation -> presented artefact). They share no common domain/range overlap and denote distinct relations.

Both classes denote speakers who give a talk at a conference, but they are not equivalent. An 'Invited Speaker' (ekaw) is a person invited to present at a conference session, which could include various plenary or non-plenary invited talks. A 'Plenary lecture speaker' (iasted) is specifically a speaker at a plenary (whole-conference) lecture. Every plenary lecture speaker is an invited speaker, but not every invited speaker gives a plenary lecture (e.g., invited talks in parallel sessions). The two categories overlap but neither subsumes the other in a clean hierarchy across these independently modeled ontologies, so 'related' is the most appropriate relation.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person participating in the conference organisation). In edas, hasLocation links a Conference Event to a Place (a physical or virtual location). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely distinct, so these properties are unrelated.

In ekaw, Conference is a Scientific Event representing one edition of a conference (e.g., ISWC 2006), with siblings like Workshop, Track, and Session. In iasted, Plenary lecture is a specific type of Lecture (a Conference activity), with siblings Session and Tutorial. A Conference is the overarching event, while a Plenary lecture is a single talk within that event. These are at completely different levels of granularity and denote different things.

confOf:writes specifically relates an Author to a Contribution (paper) that they author. iasted:send relates a Person to an Item, which is a broader relation: a Person can send various items (e.g., a draft, a final manuscript, a form), not necessarily one they authored. Thus writes is a more specific relation than send, so writes is subsumed_by send.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (a reviewer inviting a colleague to co-review), while 'hasReviewer' relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to a paper). They describe fundamentally different relationships in the conference domain.

The property adjustBid in cmt relates a Reviewer to a Bid (adjusting a reviewer's bid on a paper for review assignment), while pay in sigkdd relates a Person to a Registration fee (paying a registration fee). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf's Member PC is explicitly a reviewer (a Program Committee member who reviews contributions), while sigkdd's Organizing Committee member is a local-organization role (sibling of Webmaster, General Chair, etc.) with no reviewing responsibility. They are distinct conference-organisation roles, so they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'volumeContainsPaper' in ekaw relates a volume (proceedings) to the papers it contains, while 'write' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they authored. These are entirely different relations: one is a containment relation between a publication volume and its constituent papers, the other is an authorship relation between a person and a document. They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

Both classes denote authors of conference papers, but they are not equivalent. A's 'Contribution co author' is specifically a co-author (non-first author) of a conference contribution, while B's 'Author of paper' is a more general author of a paper (with a sibling for student authors, not for co-authors). They overlap in extension but neither subsumes the other: B includes first authors, which A excludes, and A may include non-student co-authors that B's sibling 'Author of paper student' covers separately. Thus 'related' is the most defensible relation.

A 'Talk Event' in edas is a conference event (a scheduled session at which talks are given, with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk). B 'Introduction of speaker' in iasted is an activity that is part of a conference activity—an introduction of a speaker, not the talk event itself. They are at different levels of granularity and denote different things: one is the event/session, the other is a sub-activity introducing the speaker.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. confOf:employedBy links a Person to an Organization that employs them (employment relationship). iasted:is_connected_with links an Activity or Person to an Item or Place (a loose association relationship). The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, and 'connected with' is far more general and vague than 'employed by'. They do not denote the same relation.

confOf:Company denotes a for-profit commercial enterprise (sibling of University under Organization), whereas edas:Government Organization denotes a governmental body (sibling of Academia/Industry/NGO). Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other; they are disjoint kinds of organization.

In cmt, Program Committee Member is a person who reviews papers and belongs to the program committee (a sub-class of Conference Member/Person). In iasted, Author is a delegate/speaker who writes papers (a sub-class of Speaker/Delegate). These are distinct roles: a PC member reviews submissions, while an author submits work. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way across these two ontologies.

confOf:Conference is a type of academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting a conference as an event. iasted:Sponsor city is a subclass of City, representing a geographical location where a sponsor is based. These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a city/location role.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, enterReviewCriteria relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrator entering review criteria for a conference). In the Conference ontology, invited_by relates a Reviewer to a Reviewer (a reviewer invited by another reviewer). They share no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different things: cmt's hasConferenceMember links a Conference to a Conference Member (a person who is a member of the conference), while Conference ontology's has_contributions links a Conference volume to a Conference contribution (a paper/article). The domains (Conference vs Conference volume) and ranges (Conference Member vs Conference contribution) are disjoint concepts, so the properties do not denote the same relation.

Both properties associate a reviewer with a paper, but they run in opposite directions: cmt:hasBeenAssigned has domain Reviewer and range Paper (reviewer -> paper), while ekaw:hasReviewer has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer (paper -> reviewer). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. A property and its inverse are not equivalent.

These properties connect entirely different entities in the conference domain. Property A (runPaperAssignmentTools) links an Administrator to a Conference, representing the action of running paper assignment tools. Property B (has_a_publisher) links Conference proceedings to a Publisher, representing a publication relationship. They have different domains, different ranges, and denote completely different relations.

A Meta-Review is a second-level review written by a meta-reviewer (or chair) summarizing other reviews, while a Positive Review is a regular review whose content is positive. They are orthogonal classifications of reviews: one is about the role/level in the review process, the other about the sentiment of the review. Their instance sets do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Conference denotes the conference event itself (with date, members, logo, paper submissions). In iasted, Activity is a broad class of things people do (with subtypes like Conference activity, Activity before/after conference), not the conference event. These are different concepts: one is the event/organization, the other is a general activity performed at or around a conference.

The two properties relate completely different entities in opposite directions. 'has_authors' connects a Conference document to a Person (the author of the document), while 'presentation' connects a Speaker to a Document (the document being presented by the speaker). They have different domains (Conference document vs. Speaker), different ranges (Person vs. Document), and different semantics (authorship vs. presentation). There is no equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap between these two relations.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Program committee (organizational entity). Property B links a Document to a Speaker (person who presents it). Different domains, different ranges, different meanings: one is about conference organization structure, the other about who presents a document. No alignment relationship holds.

Conference proceedings is a published volume of papers (with ISBN, volume, publisher), while Web Site is an online document. They are different kinds of artefacts with no overlap in intended instances.

Reviewing results event in confOf is an administrative event representing the phase when review results are made accessible to authors, whereas Workshop in edas is an academic event type (a meeting where papers are presented). They occupy different branches of the event hierarchy and denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both are chair roles under Person/Organizer, but Conference Chair (edas) and Program Chair (sigkdd) are distinct organizational roles. A Conference Chair typically oversees the entire conference, while a Program Chair specifically manages the scientific program and paper selection. They overlap as senior organizers but are not equivalent.

In ekaw, 'Workshop Session' is a specific subclass of Session (sibling of Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session), denoting sessions that are part of a workshop. In edas, 'Conference Session' denotes sessions that are part of a conference. These are disjoint sibling-level concepts: a conference session is not a workshop session and vice versa. Neither subsumes the other.

Call For Manuscripts is a type of call (announcement soliciting manuscripts), while Rejected Paper is a specific document that has been evaluated and rejected. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events (e.g., sessions running in parallel), while the edas 'has Attendee' property relates a Conference Event to a Person attending it. They connect entirely different kinds of entities and express completely different relationships, so they are unrelated.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision (alongside Rejection), representing the outcome of accepting a paper. Trip in confOf is a subclass of Social event (alongside Banquet and Reception), representing a social outing. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Person, but they denote different roles. confOf Assistant is a conference-assistant role (sibling to Volunteer, Administrator, etc.), whereas ekaw Agency Staff Member is staff of an external agency involved in the conference. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

cmt:Person is the top-level human class in cmt (with subclasses such as Chairman, Conference Member, Reviewer, User), whereas confOf:Participant is a subclass of confOf:Person restricted to conference participants. Thus confOf:Participant is strictly narrower than cmt:Person.

Sponzorship in iasted is a kind of Money (sibling to Fee, Tax, Tip) representing a sponsorship monetary arrangement, whereas Registration fee in sigkdd is a specific Fee with concrete subtypes (Registration Non Member, Registration Student, etc.) and price/currency properties. They are different concepts: one denotes sponsorship money, the other a registration payment obligation. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and direction of relation. In iasted, 'is paid for' has domain Money and range Activity/Item, expressing that money pays for an activity or item. In sigkdd, 'pay' has domain Person and range Registration fee, expressing that a person pays a registration fee. They are not inverses either (an inverse of 'pay' would be 'paid by' with domain Registration fee and range Person). The domains and ranges do not overlap, so the relations concern different kinds of entities.

Personal Publication History in edas is a history/record of a person's publications (a personal history entity), while Book proceeding in iasted is a concrete publication item (a book of proceedings). One tracks a person's publication history; the other is a physical/digital publication artifact. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. confOf's 'has Country' links organizations and persons to a Country, while iasted's 'is held in' links an Activity to a Place or Time. They relate different kinds of entities and do not denote the same relation.

In EKAW, Session is a Scientific Event that groups multiple presentations (it has subclasses like Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session, Workshop Session). In IASTED, Plenary Lecture is a specific type of Lecture (Activity > Conference activity > Lecture > Plenary lecture), i.e., a single talk. A session is a container/event comprising multiple talks, whereas a plenary lecture is one individual presentation. They are at different levels of granularity and neither subsumes the other.

In ontology A, 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' and represents scholarly works such as papers, posters, and presentations submitted to a conference. In ontology B, 'Conference' is a subclass of 'Working event' and represents the conference event itself (with siblings Tutorial and Workshop). These are fundamentally different concepts: one denotes the academic contributions/artifacts, the other denotes the event. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a leadership role (a person who chairs the conference), sitting under Chairman alongside Author and Reviewer. In iasted, Author is a delegate who presents work, sitting under Speaker with children like Lecturer and Tutorial speaker. These denote completely different concepts: one is an administrative/leadership position, the other is a contributor/presenter role. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in the context of these ontologies.

These properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. `is Reviewed By` specifically links a Paper to reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member) who evaluate the paper. `is used by` links an Item to a Person who uses the item. The domains (Paper vs. Item) and ranges (reviewers vs. any Person) differ, and the intended semantics (reviewing vs. usage) are distinct. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a meaningful way given the different domain/range constraints.

confOf:Working_event is a kind of conference event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) under Event, while edas:PerformanceTopic is a subject-matter Topic (like Antennas Topic, CAD Topic). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

A Withdrawn Paper is a paper that has been pulled from the conference submission process, while a Mailing list is a document type used for communication. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Place in the conference domain, but they denote different spatial concepts: 'Session room' is a room where a conference session takes place, while 'Conference hall' is a larger venue/hall. They overlap (a conference hall can host sessions) but are not equivalent, and neither strictly subsumes the other.

Steering committee and Program Committee are distinct types of committees with different roles in conference organization. A steering committee provides oversight and long-term direction, while a program committee handles paper review and selection. They are sibling concepts under Committee, not equivalent.

A 'User' in cmt is a person who interacts with the conference management system (parent: Person; children: Administrator, Author, Reviewer). A 'Hotel room' in iasted is a physical place where conference attendees stay (parent: Place; children: Double hotel room, Single hotel room). These are entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Contribution co-author in Conference is a specific role: a person who co-authored a conference contribution, sitting under Regular author. Author in iasted is a subclass of Speaker (which is under Delegate), meaning an author who is also a presenter at the conference, with children like Lecturer, Plenary lecture speaker, Tutorial speaker. The iasted Author is narrower (presenter-author) while the Conference Contribution co-author is a co-author role. They do not denote the same concept: one is a co-author role, the other is an author who presents. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other in the intended reference alignment.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing a person's last name. The labels 'has the last name' and 'has Last Name' are synonymous, and the structural context (domain, range, path) is identical across both ontologies.

Pending Paper (edas) classifies a paper by its review/decision status (pending, accepted, rejected, etc.), while Workshop Paper (ekaw) classifies a paper by the type of venue/event it belongs to (workshop, conference, demo, poster, etc.). These are orthogonal classification dimensions: a pending paper could be intended for a workshop, and a workshop paper could be pending. Their sibling sets confirm distinct taxonomic axes, so the classes are unrelated.

The Conference property 'is submitted at' specifically links a Conference contribution to the Conference volume where it is submitted. The edas property 'relates To' is a broad, generic relation from a Document to various entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person). They differ in domain (Conference contribution vs Document), range (Conference volume vs a union including Person), and intended semantics: submission venue vs generic document association. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the mismatched, broad range of relatesTo.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Gold Supporter is a type of conference sponsor. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper), while sigkdd's 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document (the document being presented). These are different relations in different directions connecting different entity types: authorship vs. presentation-of-material.

Property A (has_a_review) relates a Reviewed contribution to a Review, capturing the peer-review relation in a conference. Property B (is_paid_for) relates Money to an Activity or Item, capturing a payment relation. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

These properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (modeling topic preferences in the review process), while 'notification until' links an Author to a Deadline for author notification. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a document), while Test Only Topic is a subject-area topic under Topic. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Property A ('is an abstract submission date') relates Important dates to a date, capturing the deadline by which an abstract must be submitted. Property B ('abstract') relates a Contribution to a string, capturing the textual content of the abstract itself. They have different domains, different ranges, and denote entirely different relations (a deadline date vs. the abstract text), so they are not equivalent.

Conference Dinner is a social/meal event during a conference, while General Chair is a person role responsible for organizing the conference. They denote completely different categories of entities (event vs. person) and share no domain overlap.

Review in the Conference ontology is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a contribution. Numerical Review Question in edas is a question (with a numerical answer) that is part of a review form. These are completely different concepts: one is the review artefact itself, the other is a question item within a review form.

Property A links Important dates to a Conference volume (a proceedings or published collection), while property B links an Event to a Location (physical place). They relate completely different kinds of entities and do not overlap in meaning.

Both User and Participant are subclasses of Person, but they represent different concepts. In cmt, User is a base class for roles like Author, Reviewer, and Administrator within the conference management system. In confOf, Participant denotes someone who attends the conference (with children like Member, Regular, Student), and has an early registration property. A system user is not necessarily a conference participant, and a participant is not necessarily a system user. They overlap (e.g., an Author who is both a user and a participant) but are not equivalent.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domains/ranges. confOf 'reviewes' goes from Member PC (reviewer) to Contribution (paper being reviewed), while ekaw 'hasReview' goes from Paper to Review (the review artifact). They are not equivalent; if anything they are inverse-like, but since the ranges differ (Contribution vs Review) and the direction is opposite, they are not equivalent and not a clean subsumption. Treating as unrelated in the reference alignment sense.

Personal Review History in edas is a record of a reviewer's past review activity, while Research Topic in ekaw is a subject area covered by papers and events. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent people who present at a conference and share the common parent Author, but they are not equivalent. A Presenter (edas) is a general class for any person who presents a paper or talk, whereas a Tutorial speaker (iasted) is specifically a speaker in a tutorial. The iasted hierarchy distinguishes Tutorial speaker from other specialised speaker types (Lecturer, Plenary lecture speaker), indicating a narrower role. The two classes overlap (a tutorial speaker is a presenter) but their intended instances do not coincide.

In Conference, 'Camera ready contribution' is a document (the final written paper artefact), whereas in confOf 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the act/occurrence of submitting contributions). One is a document, the other is an event; they denote completely different categories of entities.

In cmt, Conference denotes the overall conference event/organization with properties like date, logo URL, accepted papers, and administrators. In ekaw, Conference Session is a specific session within a conference (a child of Session under Scientific Event), with siblings like Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session. These are different concepts at different granularity levels: one is the conference itself, the other is a session held at a conference.

The property locationOf in ekaw relates a Location to the Event held at that location, whereas is_held_after in iasted relates an Activity to a Time, expressing a temporal ordering. They have different domains, different ranges, and express completely different relations (spatial vs temporal), so they are unrelated.

Entity A is a Person (a speaker invited to present), while entity B is an Activity (the act of introducing a speaker). They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different kinds of things.

The confOf 'follows' property relates two Administrative events (e.g., one event following another in a sequence), while the iasted 'is present in' property relates a Person to a Place or Time (e.g., a person being present at a location/time). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote conference committee leadership roles involving persons, but they are not equivalent. 'Co chair' in ontology A is a general committee co-chair role (sibling of Chair under Committee member), whereas 'PC Chair' in ontology B is specifically the chair of the Programme Committee (a sub-class of both Conference Participant and PC Member). A PC Chair is a specific type of committee chair, while a Co chair is a general co-chair role that could apply to various committees. They overlap in extension (a PC Chair could also be a Co chair of some committee) but neither subsumes the other in a clearly general-to-specific direction, so 'related' is the most appropriate relation.

confOf Poster is a type of conference contribution (a poster paper), while sigkdd Silver Supporter is a type of sponsor. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Invited Talk and Contributed Talk are distinct, mutually exclusive presentation types in the conference domain. An invited talk is delivered by an invited speaker, while a contributed talk is submitted and accepted through the regular review process. They are sibling categories under presentation, not the same concept.

Renting is an activity (e.g., renting a venue or equipment) in the iasted ontology, while Author is a person role in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to completely different categories (activity vs. person) and share no semantic overlap.

Reviewing results event in confOf is an administrative event representing the outcome of the reviewing process accessible to authors, whereas Call For Papers in edas is a solicitation for paper submissions. These are distinct concepts in the conference workflow with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, ConferenceDinner is a specific social event (a meal) held during a conference, sitting under Non Academic Event > Meal Event. In sigkdd, Conference is the top-level conference entity itself, with properties like start/end dates, name, city, and being held by an ACM SIGKDD. These are completely different concepts: one is a dinner event, the other is the conference as a whole. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated entities.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a kind of Chairman), while Workshop is a type of scientific event. They denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have opposite domain/range orientations and are not inverses in a formal sense. `hasRelatedPaper` relates an Author to a Paper (author -> paper), while `writtenBy` relates a Document to a Person (document -> person). Even if their underlying concepts overlap (Author/Person, Paper/Document), the properties themselves connect different kinds of entities in different directions, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related as properties.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length submission document in the CMT ontology (Document > Paper > PaperFullVersion), while CommunicationsTopic is a subject-area topic in the EDAS ontology (Topic > CommunicationsTopic). They denote completely different kinds of entities: a document artefact vs. a conference subject category.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization (a corporate entity involved in conference organization), while iasted:Tip is a subclass of Money (a monetary amount). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'held In' in ekaw relates an Event to the Location where it takes place, while 'is sent before' in iasted relates an Item to a Time deadline before which it must be sent. They connect entirely different domain and range types (Event/Location vs Item/Time) and express different relations (spatial hosting vs temporal deadline), so they are unrelated.

confOf:writes relates an Author to a Contribution they have authored, while edas:isReviewing relates a Reviewer (or chair/TPC member) to a Paper they are reviewing. These are distinct relations in the conference domain: authoring vs. reviewing. The domains and ranges differ accordingly, and neither property subsumes the other.

Abstract in ekaw is a type of document (e.g., invited talk abstract, tutorial abstract), whereas Deadline Author notification in sigkdd is a temporal deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Demo Paper in ekaw is a specific type of paper (a demonstration paper), a child of Paper. Abstract in sigkdd is a sibling of Paper and Review, representing a summary document. These are different document types with different roles in the conference domain: one is a full paper type for demonstrations, the other is a summary/abstract document. They share no subsumption relationship and are not equivalent.

A's 'Information for participants' is a subclass of Conference document, i.e. a written artefact providing information to participants. B's 'Welcome address' is a subclass of Conference activity, i.e. an event or activity during the conference. One is a document, the other is an activity; they denote different kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Entity A is a topic in the subject taxonomy of conference submissions (a child of Topic, alongside Antennas, Cryptography, etc.), denoting a research area. Entity B is a document type—an abstract of an invited talk (child of Abstract > Document). These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Contribution is a broad top-level class subsuming Paper, Poster, and Short paper, representing any authored submission or artefact. ekaw:Assigned_Paper is a narrow class deep in the Document hierarchy (Document > Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper) denoting specifically a paper that has been assigned to reviewers. The two do not share the same instances: a Contribution could be a poster or short paper (not an Assigned_Paper), and an Assigned_Paper is a specific kind of already-submitted paper. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship given their different positions and scopes.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest exists between a person and a paper). In iasted, is_given_to relates an Item to a Person (indicating an item is given to a person). They connect different entity types in different directions and represent semantically unrelated relationships.

The two properties run in opposite directions. In Conference, 'has a review' goes from Reviewed contribution (the paper) to Review. In ekaw, 'reviewOfPaper' goes from Review to Paper. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent, and per the instructions a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Tutorial is a scientific event (a type of individual presentation), while in iasted, Tip is a monetary concept (a type of money). These denote completely different domain concepts despite both being subclasses in their respective hierarchies.

The property coversTopic in EKAW relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (what subject matter is covered). The property write in IASTED relates a Person to an Item (who authored a document). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

In edas, Conference denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like has Country, paper Due On, has Topic, and subclasses like Single/Two Level Conference). In iasted, Conference activity is a subclass of Activity whose children are Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Lecture, Presentation, Registration, etc. — i.e., activities that occur during a conference, not the conference itself. These are disjoint concepts: one is the conference event, the other is a type of activity happening at a conference.

Track workshop chair in Conference denotes a person chairing a specific track/workshop/tutorial (a Conference part), while Chair PC in confOf denotes the chair of the Programme Committee. These are distinct organisational roles: one chairs a track or workshop session, the other chairs the PC. They share the parent Person but their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Author is a subclass of Person who writes papers, while Registration fee is a subclass of Fee representing conference registration costs. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (has_the_first_name) relates a Person to their first name string. Property B (abstract) relates a Contribution to its abstract text string. They have completely different domains (Person vs. Contribution) and denote entirely different concepts (a person's given name vs. a paper's summary), so they are unrelated.

These properties have different domains, different meanings, and different directions of relation. In cmt, 'assignReviewer' has domain Administrator and range Reviewer: an administrator assigns a reviewer (to a paper). In Conference, 'belongs_to_reviewers' has domain Review_expertise/Review_preference and range Reviewer: a review expertise or preference belongs to (is associated with) a reviewer. The cmt property flows from administrator to reviewer, while the Conference property flows from expertise/preference to reviewer. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction, so they are not equivalent.

These properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person belonging to the conference). In edas, isTopicOf links a Topic to a Conference or Paper, indicating that a topic is associated with those entities. The domains (Conference vs Topic), ranges (Conference Member vs Conference/Paper), and overall semantics are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

The cmt property relates a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee, denoting committee membership. The confOf property relates one Administrative event to another, indicating they occur in parallel. These are entirely different relations with disjoint domains and ranges.

The two properties operate in different contexts and have incompatible signatures. In Conference, 'has an expertise' is a datatype property with domain Review expertise (an artefact describing a reviewer's expertise on a paper), whereas in confOf, 'expert On' is an object property with domain Member PC and range Topic, linking a committee member to a subject topic. They relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

Published Paper is a scholarly document that has been accepted and published, while Bank transfer is a payment document/method. They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (academic documents vs. financial documents) and share no instances in common.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (i.e., assigning a chair to a track/workshop/tutorial), while property B links a Member PC to a Topic (i.e., indicating a PC member's area of expertise). The domains (Conference part vs Member PC) and ranges (Track workshop chair vs Topic) are disjoint concepts, and the relations express different semantics: chair assignment vs expertise declaration.

cmt:Acceptance is a subclass of Decision representing the acceptance of a paper (sibling of Rejection), whereas edas:AccpetIfRoomRating is a subclass of Review Rating representing a specific review score value (siblings include Accept Rating, Reject Rating, Week Reject Rating). One denotes an acceptance decision on a paper, the other denotes a particular rating value assigned by a reviewer. They operate at different levels of the conference workflow and do not share instances.

Both Place (edas) and Location (ekaw) represent the spatial/geographic entity where conference events are held. They are connected by analogous properties: edas has 'has Location' (Conference Event -> Place) and 'is Location Of' (Place -> Conference Event), while ekaw has 'held In' (Event -> Location) and 'location Of' (Location -> Event). The domain and range structures mirror each other closely, indicating both classes are intended to denote the same concept: the location/place of a conference event.

Both classes are top-level Document classes in the conference domain that serve as the parent class for Paper and Review. They share the same label and the same core conference-document children (Paper, Review). The additional children in each ontology (Meal Menu, Programme, Slide Set in edas; Abstract in sigkdd) are domain-specific extensions that do not contradict equivalence. Both represent the general concept of a document artefact in the conference organization domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In EDAS, 'isTopicOf' links a Topic to a Conference or Paper (indicating the subject matter of a paper or conference). In IASTED, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or distributing an item). The domains (Topic vs. Person) and ranges (Conference/Paper vs. Activity/Item) are disjoint, and the intended meanings share no overlap.

cmt:Author is a specific role for someone who writes/submits a paper, sitting under Conference Member. Conference:Conference contributor is a broader class under Person that includes Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author. Since Conference contributor encompasses more than just authors (e.g., invited speakers, active participants who may not author a paper), cmt:Author is subsumed by Conference:Conference contributor rather than equivalent.

Medicine Topic is a subject-area topic (a subclass of Topic alongside technical topics like Antennas, Cryptography, etc.), while Contributed Talk is a type of presentation event (subclass of Individual Presentation). They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Submission event' is a temporal event marking the submission of contributions, while 'Program Committee' is an organizational body of people. They share no instances and belong to completely different categories (event vs. committee).

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it. In edas, 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides the sponsorship. Despite superficially similar labels, the domains (Presentation vs Sponsorship) and ranges (Active conference participant vs Organization) are disjoint, so the properties denote different relations in the conference domain.

The cmt 'email' property captures a person's electronic mail address, while the confOf 'hasSurname' property captures a person's family/last name. These are distinct attributes with no overlap in intended meaning, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

In ekaw, 'Organising Agency' is a kind of Organisation (e.g., a publishing or hosting body), whereas in sigkdd 'Organizing Committee' is a kind of Committee (a group of people). An agency is an organisational entity, while a committee is a collection of individuals serving a role; they are structurally and semantically different despite the superficial lexical overlap.

confOf's 'Submission event' is an administrative event representing the submission activity/process itself, while iasted's 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' is a temporal deadline for submitting final camera-ready papers. One is an event/activity, the other is a point in time; they denote fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Conference:Paper denotes any paper (a regular contribution), whereas edas:AcceptedPaper is a specific subtype of Paper whose instances have been accepted. Every Accepted Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is accepted, so Conference:Paper is strictly more general (subsumed_by edas:AcceptedPaper in the sense that A is subsumed by B's superclass hierarchy; here A is the broader concept).

In EDAS, Paper is a subclass of Document, specifically denoting a written contribution to a conference. In EKAW, Document is a broad superclass whose children include Paper, Abstract, Flyer, Review, Web Site, etc. Thus EKAW's Document is strictly more general than EDAS's Paper, so Paper is subsumed_by Document.

hasEmail relates a Person to their email address string, while hasPhone relates Contact Information to a phone number string. These are distinct contact channels with different domains and different intended meanings; neither subsumes the other.

Both are datatype properties about deadlines, but they have different domains and ranges. paperDueOn applies to a Conference and ranges over dateTime, while done_till applies to a Deadline and ranges over date. They operate at different levels of the ontology and relate different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

The edas 'has Phone' is a datatype property from Contact Information to a string (a phone number), whereas the iasted 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item (an acquired object). They differ in type, domain, range, and meaning, so they are unrelated.

Important dates is a class representing the set of deadlines and key dates of a conference (submission, acceptance, camera-ready, start/end dates). Contribution is a class representing submitted academic works (papers, posters, short papers). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Organization in the Conference ontology is a general class for any organization, whereas IndustryOrganization in edas is a specific subclass of Organization restricted to industry organizations. The Conference Organization is more general, so A is subsumed_by B's parent concept; B is strictly narrower than A.

In iasted, 'Conference building' is a physical place (subclass of Building under Place) where conference events are held, with siblings like Conference airport, Conference hotel, etc. In sigkdd, 'Conference' is an event with temporal properties (start/end dates), a name, and a city, held by an organization (ACM SIGKDD). One is a physical structure, the other is a temporal event; they denote completely different concepts.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. confOf:dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic (what the paper is about), while sigkdd:submit_until links a Document to a Deadline (the submission deadline). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Sponsor company house is a building where a sponsor company is located (sibling of Conference hotel, Presenter house, etc.), while Hotel is a place for lodging. A sponsor company house is not a hotel; they are distinct kinds of places in the conference domain.

These properties are completely different in meaning and structure. 'acceptsHardcopySubmissions' is a datatype property from Conference to boolean, indicating whether a conference accepts hardcopy submissions. 'paperPresentedAs' is an object property from Paper/Abstract to Individual Presentation, indicating how a paper is presented. They have different domains, ranges, types, and semantic purposes with no overlap.

In ekaw, Tutorial is a subclass of Individual Presentation (under Scientific Event > Event), so it denotes an event/session at which a tutorial is given. In sigkdd, Invited_Speaker is a subclass of Person > Speaker, so it denotes the person who gives an invited talk. One is an event, the other is a person; they are disjoint kinds of entities and neither subsumes the other.

Property A (isMemberOf) relates a Person to a Conference they are a member of. Property B (hasPart) is a generic mereological relation indicating part-whole composition. They differ in domain/range and meaning: membership is not the same as parthood, and the two properties point in opposite directions (isMemberOf goes member->whole, hasPart goes whole->part).

cmt:ConferenceMember is a subclass of cmt:Person whose instances are people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). ekaw:Person is the top-level class for all people in the conference domain, including agency staff, students, participants, authors, and possible reviewers. Every Conference Member is a Person, but ekaw:Person includes individuals (e.g., students, agency staff) who are not necessarily conference members. Therefore cmt:ConferenceMember is strictly more specific than ekaw:Person.

The confOf 'starts_on' property has domain Event and range string, denoting when an event begins. The sigkdd 'Name' property has domain Person and range string, denoting a person's name. They relate to completely different domains (events vs. persons) and express unrelated concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Industrial Session in ekaw is a specific kind of conference session (industrial focus), while Session in iasted is a general session/activity that can include speaker lectures, plenary lectures, tutorials, etc. Industrial Session is a more specific concept that would fall under the general Session category, making it subsumed by the broader iasted Session class.

Invited Speaker is a Presenter who gives an invited talk, while Non speaker is a Delegate who does not present. They are disjoint categories of conference participants, not equivalent or otherwise aligned.

In cmt, Conference is the event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, accepts hardcopy submissions, has members). In the Conference ontology, Conference_participant is a person who attends the conference (subclass of Person, sibling of Committee member, Reviewer, etc.). These are completely different concepts: an event vs. a person who participates in it.

In edas, 'Session Chair' is a subclass of Person — the human who chairs a conference session. In iasted, 'Session' is a subclass of Lecture under Activity — a scheduled event/activity. One is a person role, the other is an event. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate completely different domain entities: 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its contributions (a container-to-content relation), while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (a creator-to-work relation). They share the same range concept (Conference contribution / Contribution) but the domains differ entirely and the nature of the relationship is different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

The cmt property 'has Been Assigned' relates a Reviewer to a Paper they have been assigned to review. The iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a lecture or presentation). These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and do not denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Assigned Paper in ekaw is a specific kind of paper that has been assigned for review, sitting deep in a hierarchy (Document > Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper). Document in iasted is a broad superclass covering many artefacts (forms, invitation letters, reviews, submissions, transparencies, etc.). Assigned Paper is thus a much narrower concept and is subsumed by iasted's Document.

confOf:City denotes a geographical location (the range of hasCity for Organization/Person addresses), while sigkdd:Conference denotes an academic event with properties like start/end dates, name, and location. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Enterprise Topic' is a subject taxonomy node under 'Computer Networks Topic', representing a research topic area. In EKAW, 'Invited Talk' is a type of scientific event/individual presentation. One is a topic, the other is an event; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.
