Conference announcement is a document type (a conference-related publication artefact), while Operating Topicsystems is a subject topic within the Topic hierarchy. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Registered applicant' is a person who has applied to attend/register for a conference, while an 'Author' is a person who submits a paper. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: an author need not be a registered applicant, and a registered applicant need not be an author. Their hierarchies and properties confirm different intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Deadline in the conference domain, but they denote different deadlines: 'Submissions deadline' in iasted is a general deadline for all submissions, while 'Deadline Abstract Submission' in sigkdd is specifically for abstract submission (a sibling of 'Deadline Paper Submission'). They overlap in that an abstract submission deadline is one kind of submissions deadline, but the iasted class also covers full paper submissions, so they are not equivalent.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'hasConferenceMember' links a Conference to its Conference Members (people who are members of the conference). In edas, 'initiates' links conference roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call (e.g., call for papers). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and serve entirely different purposes.

Published Paper (edas) classifies papers by review/decision status (accepted, rejected, pending, withdrawn, etc.), meaning a paper that has been published. Regular Paper (ekaw) classifies papers by type/format (regular, demo, poster, industrial, workshop), meaning a full-length non-special paper. These are orthogonal classification dimensions: a regular paper can be published or not, and a published paper can be regular, demo, poster, etc. Their sibling sets confirm different partition criteria, so the classes are unrelated.

Conference's Paper is a general regular contribution (encompassing both accepted and rejected submissions), whereas edas' Published Paper is a specific subtype of Paper that has been published. Published Paper is thus a proper subset of the broader Paper concept, so Paper is subsumed_by PublishedPaper's parent but not equivalent to PublishedPaper itself.

Conference document in ontology Conference is a class whose instances are documents (call for papers, reviews, conference contributions, etc.), with properties like has authors and has a date of issue. Conference Event in edas is a class whose instances are events (academic or non-academic), with properties like has location, has start/end date time, and has programme. These are fundamentally different categories of things - documents vs. events - despite both being named 'Conference' something. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

In cmt, Chairman is a general superclass with three subclasses: Associated Chair, Conference Chair, and Program Committee Chair. In edas, Conference Chair is a specific role. Thus cmt:Chairman is strictly more general than edas:Conference Chair, so the relation is subsumes.

An Excursion (in edas) is a social event involving a trip or outing, typically off-site. A Cocktail reception (in iasted) is a reception/gathering event, not an excursion. They are different types of social/conference activities; neither subsumes the other and they do not denote the same concept.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. In sigkdd, Best Student Paper Award is a subclass of Award, denoting an award given for a student paper. These are completely different concepts: one is a person, the other is an award. They share the word 'Student' but denote unrelated entities in the conference domain.

Invited speaker is a conference contributor distinguished by being invited to speak, while Student is a participant who is a student. These are disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances; being an invited speaker does not imply being a student and vice versa.
A 'Worker non speaker' is a person (a delegate who does not give a talk), while a 'Conference hall' is a physical venue. They belong to disjoint domains (person vs. place) and share no instances.

confOf:Scholar is a price-category/registration role (a student or academic who studies at a university), whereas edas:Reviewer is a functional role of a person who reviews papers. Their intended instances do not coincide: a scholar is not necessarily a reviewer, and a reviewer is not necessarily a scholar. They share only the common parent Person, which is insufficient for equivalence.

Both classes represent members of the Programme Committee under Person. confOf's 'Member PC' has the comment 'Reviewer' and is the domain of reviewes (Member PC -> Contribution), while edas's 'TPC Member' is among the domains of is Reviewing (-> Paper) and ranges of is Reviewed By (Paper ->). Both denote PC members who perform reviews, so their intended instances coincide.

Volunteer denotes a person who assists with conference logistics, while Sponsor denotes a person or entity that provides financial support. Despite both being subclasses of Person, their intended instances do not coincide.

A Program Committee (cmt) reviews papers and has Program Committee Members as members. A Steering committee (Conference) is a distinct committee type that oversees the conference series/volume. In the Conference ontology, Steering committee and Program committee are explicitly modeled as sibling classes under Committee, confirming they are different concepts. A steering committee provides strategic oversight while a program committee handles paper selection, so they do not share instances.

enterConferenceDetails is a specific action where an Administrator enters details for a Conference, while prepare is a general relation where a Person prepares an Item. The domains (Administrator vs Person), ranges (Conference vs Item), and the nature of the actions (entering conference details vs preparing items) are different, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. In sigkdd, Registration SIGKDD Member is a subclass of Registration fee, denoting a registration fee category for SIGKDD members. One is a person, the other is a fee; they are completely different kinds of entities.

hasLocation relates a Conference Event to its Place (event -> place), while locationOf relates a Location to its Event (place -> event). These are inverse directions, not equivalent. The inverse of hasLocation would be something like 'locationOf' in the same ontology, but cross-ontology these are directional inverses, not the same relation.

In EDAS, MeetingRoomPlace is a specific subclass of Place (a room where meetings happen), while in sigkdd Place is the general top-level location class with children like Conference_hall, Hotel, and Main_office. MeetingRoomPlace is thus a narrower concept subsumed by the general sigkdd Place.

In the iasted ontology, 'Initial manuscript' is a subclass of Document > Submission, representing the actual paper document submitted by an author. In the sigkdd ontology, 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a subclass of Deadline, representing a temporal point (a date/deadline) by which papers must be submitted. One is a document artifact, the other is a temporal event. They share the words 'paper' and 'submission' but denote entirely different kinds of entities (document vs. deadline), so they are unrelated.

confOf Banquet is a specific social event (a meal gathering), while ekaw Social Event is the general class whose children include Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. Banquet is thus a kind of Social Event, not equivalent to it.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference (the act of finalizing paper assignments for a conference), while parallel_with relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

confOf:writes specifically relates an Author to a Contribution they author. edas:hasRelatedDocument is a broad relation from events or persons to any related Document. The domains and ranges differ substantially, and hasRelatedDocument is not specifically an authorship relation.

Accommodation Place in edas denotes lodging (hotels, etc.) for conference participants, while Session room in iasted denotes a room where conference sessions are held. They are sibling subclasses of Place but represent different concepts with non-overlapping instances.
A is a datatype property assigning a start timestamp to a Conference Event; B is an object property linking an Event to another Event. Different types, domains, ranges, and semantics.

Week Reject Rating is a rating value (a subclass of Review Rating) used to evaluate reviews, while Rejected Paper is a document (a paper that has been rejected). One is a rating/evaluation concept, the other is a document artefact. They are in completely different parts of the ontology hierarchy and denote different kinds of entities.

Mailing list is a communication document (e.g., a list of email addresses or a mailing-list posting) used for conference correspondence, whereas Abstract is a summary of a paper. Both are subclasses of Document, but they denote different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

An invited speaker is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, while a reviewer is a person who evaluates submitted papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: an invited speaker is selected by organizers to present, whereas a reviewer is assigned to assess submissions. Neither role subsumes the other, and they are not equivalent.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level event representing the conference itself (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop under Working event). In edas, Paper Presentation is a specific academic event where a paper is presented (sibling of Organizational Meeting, Talk Event, Workshop under Academic Event). These denote completely different concepts: one is the conference as a whole, the other is a presentation session within a conference.

hasFirstName is a datatype property from Person to string capturing a person's given name, while obtain is an object property from Person to Item capturing a person obtaining an item. They differ in type, range, and meaning.

A's 'has the first name' is specifically a person's first name, while B's 'Name' is a general name property for a Person. 'Name' subsumes 'has the first name' because a full name is more general than just a first name.

The two properties have completely different meanings and ranges. hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest with a specific paper), while isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (indicating membership in a conference organization). They share the same domain (Person) but differ entirely in range and semantics.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a specific leadership role (a Chairman responsible for the conference), distinct from the Program Committee Chair. In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a member of the organizing/program committee. These are different roles: a Conference Chair oversees the entire conference, while a Program Committee member is a regular committee participant. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

`acceptedBy` in cmt links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it, capturing the acceptance decision process. `award` in sigkdd links something (unspecified domain) to an Award, capturing an accolade given. These are distinct relations: acceptance of a paper versus receipt of an award. They relate different kinds of entities and denote different aspects of the conference domain.

In the Conference ontology, Organization is a broad class covering any organizing or affiliated institution. In confOf, Company is a specific subclass of Organization (sibling of University), denoting a commercial/corporate entity. Organization is strictly more general than Company, so A is subsumed_by B.

The two properties have incompatible domains and ranges and run in opposite directions. iasted:is_paid_in has domain Money and range Building, meaning money is paid in a building. sigkdd:pay has domain Person and range Registration_fee, meaning a person pays a registration fee. They do not share the same argument structure, and even the broader notion of payment is modeled differently (location vs. fee object), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Meta Reviewer in cmt is a person (subclass of Reviewer/Person) who oversees reviews, while Review in sigkdd is a document (subclass of Document) that is the review itself. They denote completely different categories of entities—a role/person versus an artefact/document—so they are unrelated.

`reviewsPerPaper` is a datatype property with domain Conference and range int, representing the number of reviews assigned per paper. `has_a_name` is a datatype property with domain Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic and range string, representing the name of various entities. They have different domains, ranges, and meanings; they are not equivalent.

The property 'assigned By Reviewer' in cmt relates an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to a paper). The property 'presentation' in sigkdd relates a Speaker to a Document (the presentation/slides a speaker gives). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and serve different purposes in the conference organization domain.

Rejected Paper and Accepted Paper are mutually exclusive disjoint states of a paper in the conference domain. A rejected paper has been declined and will not appear in proceedings, while an accepted paper has been approved for publication. These classes share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship; they are sibling status categories representing opposite outcomes of the review process.

A Welcome Talk is a type of academic event/talk that occurs at a conference, while a Conference hall is a physical place where events are held. They are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a location.

Property `contributes` (Person -> Conference document) denotes authorship or contribution of a scholarly document, while `pay` (Person -> Registration fee) denotes a monetary payment for conference registration. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics; they share only the common domain Person.

Property A ('has a degree') has domain Review_preference and range int, representing a degree/preference level for a review. Property B ('Name') has domain Person and range string, representing a person's name. They relate to completely different entities and have different datatypes, so they are unrelated.

Multimedia Topic in edas is a subject-area topic (sibling of Antennas Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc., under Topic). Tutorial Abstract in ekaw is a document type (subclass of Abstract under Document). They denote completely different things: a conference subject area vs. a kind of abstract document.

Both properties relate conference artifacts to a Topic, but they differ in domain scope. confOf:dealsWith has domain Contribution (papers/contributions), while edas:hasTopic has domain Conference OR Paper. The edas property is more general since it applies to both conferences and papers, whereas confOf:dealsWith is restricted to contributions. Thus confOf:dealsWith is subsumed_by edas:hasTopic.

Antennas Topic is a subject-area topic (e.g., antennas, communication theory, microelectronics) used to classify papers by research area. Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award given for outstanding application papers. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a person role (a kind of Chairman under Person) in cmt, while Workshop is a type of event (under Event > Working event) in confOf. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain: one is a human committee role, the other is an academic event. There is no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Review is a document artefact produced by a reviewer (domain of writeReview/writtenBy, range of writeReview). In edas, Call For Reviews is a kind of Call (an announcement soliciting reviews), sibling to Call For Papers and Call For Manuscripts. One is the review document itself; the other is a call/announcement requesting reviews. They denote different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'Submission event' is an administrative event (a happening/activity during the conference lifecycle when contributions are submitted), while iasted's 'Registation deadline' is a temporal entity (a specific date/time point by which registration must occur). One is an event, the other is a deadline for a different activity (registration, not submission). They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Student_registration_fee is specifically a reduced fee for students, while Registration_SIGMOD_Member is a fee for SIGMOD members. These are distinct categories of registration fees targeting different groups (students vs. SIGMOD members); neither subsumes the other and they do not coincide.

These properties have completely different meanings and argument structures. 'has_workshops' relates a Conference volume to its constituent Workshop parts (a mereological/part-whole relation), while 'organisedBy' relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it (an agency/organizer relation). They connect different domain and range types and express fundamentally different relationships.

confOf:Workshop is a type of event (a working event under Conference/Tutorial), while edas:Presenter is a type of person (a subclass of Author). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'submit Paper' connects an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a manuscript), while 'is held before' connects an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering of an event). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Review Question in edas is a question item in a review form (with numerical and textual subtypes), while Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a person who may serve as a reviewer (subclass of Person). These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference announcement is a document type (a published notice about a conference), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting abstracts. They denote completely different kinds of entities (document vs. date/event), so they are unrelated.

Both properties connect a person to a conference document/item, but in opposite directions. 'contributes' goes Person -> Conference document, while 'is prepared by' goes Item -> Person. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. A reference alignment would not equate a property with its inverse.

Both are conference events involving talks/lectures, but they are not equivalent. 'Talk Event' in edas is a broad class covering any talk-based event (including closing talks, welcome talks, paper presentations), while 'Plenary lecture' in iasted is a specific kind of lecture attended by all conference participants. A plenary lecture could be considered a type of talk event, but not every talk event is a plenary lecture (e.g., paper presentations, welcome talks are typically not plenary). The two concepts overlap but are not coextensive.

A's 'Reviewed contribution' is a document (a paper that has been reviewed), while B's 'Reviewer' is a person who performs reviews. These are disjoint categories in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Dining Place in edas is a place specifically for dining (e.g., restaurants, banquet halls), a sibling of Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, and Meeting Room Place. Hotel in sigkdd is a place for lodging/accommodation. While both are subclasses of Place, a dining place and a hotel are distinct kinds of locations. A hotel may contain a dining place, but the classes do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Both properties relate documents to their authors, but in opposite directions: 'has_authors' goes from Conference document to Person, while 'write' goes from Person to Item. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent.

confOf:Trip is a social event (e.g., excursion) under Event, while iasted:Transport_vehicle is a physical item (Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item. They denote completely different categories in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a person role in the CMT ontology (a kind of Chairman involved in conference organization), whereas Technic activity is a conference activity/event in the IASTED ontology (a kind of Activity, sibling to Cocktail reception, Lecture, Registration, etc.). They denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. an activity—and share no meaningful semantic relationship.

The cmt property 'assigned By Administrator' relates a Reviewer to an Administrator who assigned them (e.g., to review a paper), whereas the iasted property 'write' relates a Person to an Item they authored. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while hasTopic links a Working event to a Topic (subject area). They relate completely different entities and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

edas:AcademiaOrganization is a broad class covering all academic organizations (universities, research institutes, etc.), while ekaw:University is a specific academic institution. ekaw:University is a proper subclass of edas:AcademiaOrganization, so the edas class subsumes the ekaw class.

The two properties have completely different meanings and signatures. In cmt, 'write Review' relates a Reviewer to the Review they author (domain Reviewer, range Review). In the Conference ontology, 'invited by' relates a Reviewer to the Reviewer who invited them (domain Reviewer, range Reviewer). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Written contribution is a broad class covering any written conference artefact (regular contributions, submitted contributions), while Initial manuscript is specifically the first version of a manuscript submitted for review. Initial manuscript is a kind of written contribution, so Written contribution subsumes Initial manuscript.

The cmt 'title' is a datatype property mapping a Paper to a string (its title text), while the ekaw 'paperPresentedAs' is an object property mapping a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation. They relate completely different kinds of values (literal string vs. presentation event) and serve entirely different purposes.

Contribution 1th author is a class representing the primary author of a conference contribution, while Double hotel room is a class representing a type of hotel accommodation. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:University denotes a degree-granting educational institution (domain of 'study At' for Scholars), whereas ekaw:Research_Institute denotes a research-focused organisation. In ekaw, University is a sibling of Research_Institute under Academic Institution, explicitly distinguishing the two. They are disjoint kinds of organisations, so neither equivalence nor subsumption holds.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and express different relations. In cmt, hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person). In the Conference ontology, was_an_organizing_committee_of links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume. The domains (Conference vs Organizing committee) and ranges (Conference Member vs Conference volume) do not align, and the relations are conceptually distinct.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'detailsEnteredBy' (domain: Conference, range: Administrator) records which administrator entered conference details, while 'hasProgramme' (domain: Conference Event, range: Programme) links a conference event to its programme. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and serve unrelated purposes.

Both properties concern authorship of a written work, but they run in opposite directions: cmt:writePaper goes from Author to Paper, while iasted:is_writen_by goes from Item to Person. A property and its inverse are not equivalent. They are related because they describe the same authorship relationship from opposite directions.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person (people who are members of a conference, such as authors, chairs, reviewers). City in iasted is a geographic location with subclasses like Conference city, Presenter city, Sponsor city, and Trip city. These denote completely different categories of entities (people vs. places) with no overlap in intended instances.

In EKAW, Flyer is a specific kind of printed/promotional document (a sibling of Paper, Review, Programme Brochure, etc.). In IASTED, Document is a broad superclass covering many item types (forms, letters, reviews, submissions, etc.). Thus EKAW's Flyer is a specific document type that would be subsumed by IASTED's Document, not equivalent to it.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the entire conference (a leadership/administrative role, under Chairman). Student lecturer in iasted is a specific kind of speaker/author who is a student giving a lecture. These denote completely different roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Final manuscript is a document submitted for publication (Item > Document > Submission > Final manuscript), while Best Applications Paper Award is an award given to a paper (Award > Best Applications Paper Award). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties are fundamentally different. `hasCostCurrency` in edas is a datatype property from Sponsorship to string, capturing the currency of a sponsorship cost. `is_paid_for` in iasted is an object property from Money to Activity/Item, indicating what a monetary amount pays for. They have different domains (Sponsorship vs Money), different ranges (string vs Activity/Item), and different semantics (currency designation vs payment relation).

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Plenary lecture is an academic activity/event (subclass of Lecture/Activity). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Cd proceening is a publication artifact (a CD containing conference proceedings) under Item > Publication, while Invited Speaker is a person role under Person > Speaker. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In iasted, Time is a general temporal class with children like Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day, serving as the range of various temporal relations. In sigkdd, ACM_SIGKDD represents the specific organization (the ACM SIGKDD conference body) that organizes the conference, sets deadlines, and searches for sponsors. One is an abstract temporal concept; the other is a concrete organizational entity. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges, and express different relationships. In edas, 'is Location Of' has domain Place and range Conference Event, meaning a place is the location of a conference event. In iasted, 'is present in' has domain Person and range Place/Time, meaning a person is present at a place or time. They are not inverses of each other either (the inverse of 'is Location Of' would be 'has location' with domain Conference Event and range Place). The domains and ranges do not overlap in a way that would make these properties equivalent or even related.

These properties have different domains and ranges and express different relationships. 'was a program committee of' links a Program committee to the Conference volume it served, while 'belongsToEvent' links a Programme (a document/schedule artefact) to a Conference Event. The domains (Program committee vs Programme) and ranges (Conference volume vs Conference Event) are distinct concepts, and the relations themselves are not semantically equivalent.

In edas, Conference is a top-level event class representing the conference itself, with properties like dates, country, topics, and members. In iasted, Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate, i.e., a type of person attending a conference. These denote completely different concepts: an event vs. a person role.

Property A ('was a steering committee of') relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume, denoting an organizational/governance relationship. Property B ('writes') relates an Author to a Contribution, denoting authorship of a paper. These are completely different relations in the conference domain with different domain and range types.

confOf:Author is a subclass of Person whose instances are people who write contributions, while ekaw:Web_Site is a subclass of Document whose instances are web pages. One denotes a human role, the other a digital artefact; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Although both properties share the domain Person and range Document, they denote completely different relations. 'hasConflictOfInterest' indicates that a person has a conflict of interest with a document (e.g., a reviewer cannot review a paper due to a conflict), while 'authorOf' indicates that a person authored a document. These are distinct relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

Rejected contribution is a class whose instances are written contributions (papers) that were not accepted for publication. Negative Review is a class whose instances are review documents expressing a negative opinion. One is the artefact being evaluated; the other is the evaluative document. They are disjoint kinds of things, not equivalent.

These properties denote different relations. 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to the people who reviewed it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member), capturing the peer-review assignment. 'is prepared by' relates an Item to the Person who authored or prepared it. Reviewing and preparing/authoring are distinct roles in the conference domain, so the properties are unrelated.

Active conference participant in Conference is a sub-class of Conference contributor, denoting someone who actively contributes to a conference (e.g., gives presentations). Presenter in EKAW is a broader class of any conference participant who presents, including invited speakers. The Conference ontology's Active conference participant is more specific because it is restricted to contributors, while Presenter covers any presenter. Thus Active conference participant is subsumed by Presenter.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In confOf, 'reviewes' connects a PC Member to a Contribution (paper) they are reviewing. In iasted, 'is used for' connects an Item to an Activity or Money, expressing what an item is used for. The domains (Member PC vs Item), ranges (Contribution vs Activity/Money), and intended meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

Although both are subclasses of Document, they denote different concepts: A's Paper is a written contribution to a conference (with children like Conference Paper, Submitted Paper, etc.), while B's Review is an evaluation document of a paper. In ontology A, Review is actually a sibling of Paper, confirming they are distinct concepts. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Conference Member in cmt is a person who is a member of a conference (parent: Person; subclasses include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member). Workshop in the Conference ontology is a conference part/event (parent: Conference part; siblings: Track, Tutorial). One denotes a person, the other denotes an event/component of a conference. They share no instances and are completely different concepts.

Conference part in ontology Conference denotes a component of a conference such as Track, Tutorial, or Workshop, with properties linking it to chairs, topics, and conference volumes. Place in sigkdd denotes a physical location such as a Conference hall, Hotel, or Main office, where a Person can stay. These are entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

has_tracks relates a Conference volume to its Track (a structural subdivision of the conference program), while hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (an individual participating in the conference). They connect completely different kinds of entities (Track vs Person) and express different relationships (structural composition vs membership).

The two properties operate on different domains and carry different semantics. `hasSubmissionInstructions` (domain Call, range string) captures textual submission instructions attached to a Call for Papers, whereas `done_till` (domain Deadline, range date) records the date by which a deadline is completed. They relate different kinds of things (instructions text vs. a due date) and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

has_tutorials (domain Conference volume, range Tutorial) is a specific part-whole relation linking a conference volume to its tutorials. hasEvent (domain Event, range Event) is a general part-whole relation linking any event to its constituent events. Since tutorials are events and a conference volume is an event, has_tutorials is a specialization of hasEvent, so it is subsumed_by hasEvent.

logoURL points to a logo image (anyURI) for a Conference, while has_a_location gives a location string for a Conference volume. They denote completely different attributes with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

These properties have completely different domains and ranges: hasName relates a Conference to a string (its full name), while has_amount_of relates Money to an int (a monetary amount). They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap.

The property 'hasAttendee' in edas relates a Conference Event to a Person who attends it. The property 'prepare' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they prepare. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics: one links events to attendees, the other links persons to items they prepare. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. 'enterConferenceDetails' relates an Administrator to a Conference (managing conference setup), while 'isMenuOf' relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (catering). Their domains and ranges are disjoint and they share no semantic overlap.

These properties operate in different domains and directions. Property A (has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution) has domain Review_preference and links a review preference to the submitted contribution or topic being reviewed/preferred. Property B (reviewes) has domain Member_PC and links a PC member to the contribution they review. A connects a preference object to a contribution; B connects a reviewer (person) to a contribution. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since their domains are disjoint kinds of entities.

authorOf is an object property relating a Person to a Document they authored, while E-mail is a datatype property relating a Person to a string email address. They have completely different ranges and meanings.

These classes denote entirely different concepts. In iasted, 'Student non speaker' is a subclass of Delegate (a person) who is a student and does not give a presentation. In sigkdd, 'Registration Non Member' is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary charge). One is a person category, the other is a fee category; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Workshop in edas is an academic event (a conference session/track where papers are presented), while Bronze Supporter in sigkdd is a type of sponsor (an organization or entity providing financial support at a particular tier). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Member_PC is a subclass of Person denoting a PC member / reviewer (domain of reviewes and expertOn). edas:AcceptRating is a subclass of ReviewRating, i.e. a specific rating value used to accept a paper. They denote completely different kinds of entities (a person vs. a rating), so they are unrelated.

Free Time Break is a temporal event (a scheduled break during a conference), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology hierarchy (event vs. place) and share no instances in common.

The cmt 'hasDecision' property links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while the iasted 'is_situated_in' property links a geographic location (Building, City, Place) to another geographic location (Building, City, Place, State). These are entirely different domain relations with no overlap in meaning.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. In edas, 'is Location Of' links a Place to a Conference Event (the place where an event happens). In iasted, 'is situated in' links a Place to another Place (e.g., a Building situated in a City, a City situated in a State), expressing spatial containment between places. They do not share the same domain/range types nor the same relational semantics.

A 'Conference part' denotes a structural component of a conference program (Track, Tutorial, Workshop), while B 'Building' denotes a physical structure (Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc.). These are entirely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'adjusted By' property relates a Bid to a Reviewer (a reviewer adjusts a bid), while the confOf 'writes' property relates an Author to a Contribution (an author writes a paper). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and they denote different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties relate fundamentally different kinds of entities. 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to its Committee (a part-of / has-component relation), while 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event (an agency / causal relation). They differ in both domain and range types and express different semantic relationships, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

These properties are completely different. 'has_the_last_name' is a datatype property mapping a Person to a string (their surname), while 'can_stay_in' is an object property mapping a Person to a Place (accommodation). They share the same domain (Person) but have different ranges and entirely unrelated meanings.

The two properties differ in both domain and range. confOf:follows relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (event-to-event ordering), while iasted:is_held_before relates an Activity to a Time (event-to-timepoint). They do not connect the same kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

A Conference Member in cmt is a person who participates in the conference (parent: Person; subclasses include Author, Reviewer, Chair). A Social Event in ekaw is an event like a banquet or trip (parent: Event). One denotes a person, the other an activity; they share no domain overlap.

Entity A is a person (Track workshop chair) who chairs a workshop track, a subclass of Person. Entity B is a Workshop, a scientific event, a subclass of Event. One is a person role, the other is an event. They are completely different categories with no overlap.

Property 'need' in iasted relates Person to Item (a person needing an item), while 'search' in sigkdd relates ACM_SIGKDD to Sponzor (an organization searching for a sponsor). Different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; no overlap in meaning.

In EKAW, Evaluated_Paper is a paper that has been reviewed and assigned a decision (parent Assigned_Paper, children Accepted/Rejected Paper). In IASTED, Submission is a general document submitted to the conference (parent Document, children Final/Initial manuscript), covering any submitted item, not specifically reviewed papers. The concepts do not coincide: an Evaluated_Paper is a reviewed paper awaiting or having a decision, while a Submission is any submitted document. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other since IASTED Submission includes non-paper documents and EKAW Evaluated_Paper is a specific reviewed-paper stage.

Communication Theory Topic is a subject-area Topic (sibling of Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), whereas Invited Talk Abstract is a kind of Document/Abstract. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

In cmt, Acceptance is a subclass of Decision, representing the act or outcome of accepting a paper. In ekaw, Rejected_Paper is a subclass of Evaluated_Paper, representing the document that was rejected. One is a decision event/outcome (acceptance), the other is a document type (rejected paper). They are not even on the same dimension (acceptance vs. rejection, decision vs. document), so they are unrelated.

confOf:Contribution is a class representing submitted works (papers, posters, short papers) with properties like abstract, title, keywords, and author relationships. edas:ReviewForm is a different concept entirely—a form used for reviewing submissions. These are distinct entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties relate completely different entities. 'was_a_committee_of' has domain Committee and range Conference volume, describing which conference volume a committee belongs to. 'isMemberOf' has domain Person and range Conference, describing conference membership of a person. The domains (Committee vs Person) and ranges (Conference volume vs Conference) are different concepts, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote unrelated relations. In EKAW, hasEvent relates an Event to a (sub-)Event, while in IASTED, need relates a Person to an Item. There is no overlap in intended meaning.

In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person, meaning a sponsoring individual. In sigkdd, Platinum Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor, which is a specific tier of sponsor (alongside Gold, Silver, Bronze). Platinum Supporter is thus a more specific concept than the general Sponsor class in iasted, making this a subsumed_by relationship rather than equivalence.

Property A relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (an abstract is a part of a paper). Property B relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper (a topic is the subject of a paper/conference). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

Property `title` in cmt assigns a title to a Paper, while property `Currency` in sigkdd specifies the currency of a Registration fee. They have different domains (Paper vs Registration fee) and denote unrelated attributes in the conference domain.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Registration_form is a document/form that attendees fill out to register. They share no instances and occupy completely different positions in their respective ontologies (event vs. document).

Paper Full Version is a complete version of a conference paper (a scholarly document), while Cheque is a payment document (a financial instrument). They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and serve entirely unrelated purposes in the conference domain.

The property 'held In' in ekaw relates an Event to the Location where it takes place. The property 'search' in sigkdd relates an ACM SIGKDD conference to a Sponzor (sponsor). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges, and there is no semantic overlap between them.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'was a committee of' connects a Committee to a Conference volume, indicating which conference a committee belongs to. 'presentationed by' connects a Document to a Speaker, indicating who presented a document. The domains (Committee vs. Document), ranges (Conference volume vs. Speaker), and intended meanings are completely different, so these properties are unrelated.

In edas, Conference Chair is a person who chairs the entire conference, distinct from Reviewer (a separate sibling class). In iasted, Reviewer is a delegate who writes reviews. These are different roles: a conference chair and a reviewer are not the same concept, and neither subsumes the other in the given ontologies.

Tutorial Chair and Program Chair denote distinct organizational roles in a conference. A Tutorial Chair is responsible for organizing tutorials, while a Program Chair oversees the overall academic program (papers, reviews, acceptance decisions). They are sibling-level chair roles under different committee structures and neither subsumes the other.

These properties denote completely different concepts. 'acceptsHardcopySubmissions' indicates whether a Conference accepts hardcopy paper submissions (boolean), while 'has_an_ISBN' indicates whether Conference proceedings have an ISBN identifier (string). They have different domains (Conference vs Conference proceedings), different ranges (boolean vs string), and capture unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Computer Networks Switching Topic' is a specific subject-area topic under the Topic hierarchy, representing a research subject related to computer networks switching. In iasted, 'Trip day' is a temporal concept under the Time hierarchy, representing a day during a trip. They share no instances, no common parent, and no semantic overlap.

confOf:Company is a commercial organization (sibling of University under Organization), denoting a corporate entity involved in conference organization. edas:Computer Networks Security Topic is a subject taxonomy node (child of Computer Networks Topic under Topic), denoting a research topic for paper classification. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A Volunteer in confOf is a person who assists with conference logistics (a helper), sibling to roles like Administrator and Assistant. B PC Chair in ekaw is the chair of the Programme Committee, a leadership role with specific authority over paper assignment and reviewing. These are distinct concepts: a volunteer is not the same as a PC Chair, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Track in the Conference ontology is a subclass of Conference part, denoting a thematic subdivision of a conference program (alongside Tutorial and Workshop). These are completely different concepts: one is a person, the other is an event/session category. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

readByReviewer relates a Paper to the Reviewer who reads it (Paper -> Reviewer), while hasReview relates a Paper to the Review artifact produced for it (Paper -> Review). The ranges differ: Reviewer (a person) vs Review (a document). These are distinct relations in the conference domain, not equivalent.

cmt:name applies to both Conference and Person and denotes the full name of a person, whereas confOf:hasFirstName applies only to Person and denotes just the first name (with the comment noting involvement of middle name). Since a first name is a part of a full name, cmt:name is more specific in value but more general in domain; the safest reference relation is that cmt:name is subsumed by the broader naming property, not equivalent.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and run in opposite directions. 'send' relates a Person to an Item (a person sends an item), while 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (a fee is paid by a person). They describe completely different relations in the conference domain and are not inverses of each other either, since sending an item is not the inverse of paying a registration fee.

Topic in the Conference ontology denotes a subject area of a conference (e.g., assigned to conference parts, associated with review preferences and submitted contributions). Place in the iasted ontology denotes a physical location (with children like Building, Conference hall, Hotel room) where activities are held and persons are present. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative sub-event dealing with participant registration (a logistical activity within a conference). ekaw's 'Conference' is the top-level scientific event representing one edition of a conference. These are completely different concepts: one is a specific administrative activity, the other is the overall conference event. They share only the generic 'Event' ancestor and have no meaningful overlap in intended instances.

Delegate in iasted denotes a conference attendee (a person who registers and attends the conference), with subclasses like Listener, Speaker, Session chair, etc. Organizator in sigkdd denotes a person who organizes the conference, with subclasses like General Chair, Program Chair, Webmaster, etc. These are disjoint sets of people: attendees vs organizers. They share only the common parent Person, which is too generic to imply any alignment.

These properties have completely different meanings. confOf's 'parallel with' is a symmetric-style relation indicating that two Administrative events occur in parallel (same time slot, different tracks). ekaw's 'organised By' indicates that an Event is organized by an Organisation or Person. They connect different kinds of entities in different directions and express unrelated concepts.

Conference Chair (edas) is the chair of an entire conference, while Workshop Chair (ekaw) is the chair of a workshop, which is a specific type of event within a conference. These are distinct organizational roles with different scopes and responsibilities. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers), while Transport vehicle is a physical vehicle (car, bus, taxi, van). They belong to entirely different domains (people vs. items) and share no semantic overlap.

In Conference, 'Submitted contribution' is a subclass of 'Written contribution' and specifically denotes a contribution that has been submitted for review (it has child 'Reviewed contribution' and properties linking it to review expertise and review preference). In confOf, 'Contribution' is a broad superclass with children Paper, Poster, and Short paper, and properties like abstract, title, keyword, and authorship. confOf's Contribution encompasses all written contributions (submitted or not), while Conference's Submitted contribution is restricted to those that have been submitted. Thus A is strictly more specific than B.

The two properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges and express different relations. In cmt, 'adjusted By' links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it, capturing a bid-adjustment relationship. In the Conference ontology, 'reviews' links a Review to the Reviewed contribution it reviews, capturing a reviewing relationship. The domains (Bid vs Review), ranges (Reviewer vs Reviewed contribution), and the nature of the relations are completely different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author (the person who wrote the paper), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review (an evaluation document). These are distinct relations with disjoint ranges (Author vs Review), so they are unrelated.

Program Committee (cmt) denotes a committee of reviewers for a conference, while Conference (sigkdd) denotes the conference event itself. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain: one is an organizational body, the other is the event. They share no subsumption relationship and are not related.

These properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (managing conference setup), while 'has Menu' relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (catering/meals). Their domains and ranges are disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended meaning.

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop — it represents academic/professional events. ekaw's 'Web Site' is a subclass of Document, a digital artefact that lists events and has publishers. One is an event type, the other is a document type; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Meta Reviewer is a person (a specialized reviewer who oversees reviews), while Paper is a document (the submitted article). They belong to completely different branches of the ontology hierarchy and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

Property A (has_an_ISBN) assigns an ISBN identifier to Conference proceedings, while property B (abstract) assigns an abstract text to a Contribution. They relate different subjects to different kinds of string values and denote unrelated relations in the conference domain.

confOf's Working_event is a kind of conference event (parent Event, siblings Social_event and Administrative_event, children Conference/Tutorial/Workshop). edas's AntennasTopic is a specific subject-area Topic (parent Topic, siblings are other technical topics like CAD, Cryptography, Mobile Computing). They belong to completely different parts of the domain hierarchy and share no intended instances.

cmt:Document is a broad class covering papers and reviews (the core scholarly documents in a conference management system). iasted:Form is a specific subclass of iasted:Document, covering administrative forms like registration forms and hotel registration forms. These are different levels of abstraction and different domain concepts: cmt:Document is about scholarly artifacts, while iasted:Form is about administrative paperwork. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

In EKAW, University is an academic organisation (subclass of Organisation > Academic Institution). In IASTED, Presenter university is modelled as a physical place/building where a presenter stays, a sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc. These denote fundamentally different things (an institution vs a lodging venue), so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the same conference-domain concept of a Tutorial. In ontology A, Tutorial is a Conference part (sibling of Track and Workshop) and is the range of 'has tutorials'. In ontology B, Tutorial is a Lecture (sibling of Plenary lecture and Session) under Activity > Conference activity. Despite the different ontology structures, the intended instances coincide: tutorial sessions held at a conference. The labels are identical and the context in both ontologies supports the same interpretation.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Non Academic Event' is a type of conference event such as a break, meal, or social event. In iasted, 'Non speaker' is a type of delegate (person) who does not give a presentation, with subtypes like Student non speaker and Worker non speaker. One is an event/activity, the other is a person/role; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Short paper in confOf is a length-based classification of a contribution (short vs. regular paper vs. poster), while Industrial Paper in ekaw is a topic/track-based classification (industrial vs. academic). These are orthogonal dimensions of paper categorization; neither subsumes the other and their intended instances do not coincide.

In confOf, Poster is a type of Contribution (a presentation artefact), sibling to Paper and Short paper. In sigkdd, Abstract is a type of Document, sibling to Paper and Review. A poster is a presentation format, while an abstract is a summary document; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The property 'for Event' in EDAS links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the Academic Event it is issued for, a specific conference-domain relation. The property 'inverse of partOf_7' in EKAW is an inverse part-whole relation whose range is Event, relating parts to their containing events. These are structurally and semantically different relations: one connects calls to events, the other connects sub-events to their parent events. They do not denote the same relation.

The cmt 'read Paper' property relates a Reviewer to a Paper they read (for reviewing purposes), while the iasted 'give' property relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a presentation or lecture). These are semantically distinct relations: reading a paper vs. giving a presentation/item. The domains (Reviewer vs. Person) and ranges (Paper vs. Activity/Item) differ, and there is no overlap in intended meaning.

cmt:User is a broad superclass covering Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—anyone with a system account. confOf:Member is a specific subclass of Participant (alongside Regular and Student), denoting a type of conference attendee. The extension of cmt:User (system users) and confOf:Member (a participant category) do not coincide, and neither clearly subsumes the other, so they are unrelated.

Associated Chair (cmt) and General Chair (sigkdd) are distinct conference roles. In cmt, Associated Chair is a subordinate to the Conference Chair, while in sigkdd, General Chair is the top-level organizer. They are not the same role, nor is one a generalization of the other; they are different committee positions with different responsibilities.

These properties differ in both structure and meaning. 'has important dates' is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates object (a container for multiple deadline-related dates). 'Start of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference directly to a single dateTime value. One is a complex relation to a date-collection entity; the other is a simple scalar date attribute. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

cmt:Person is a top-level class for all people in the system (including users, reviewers, conference members, etc.), while Conference:Committee_member is a specific subclass of Person restricted to committee members (chairs, co-chairs). They are at different levels of generality and do not share the same intended instances. cmt:Person is more general, but since they come from different ontologies with different hierarchies, the safest classification is unrelated rather than subsumes/subsumed_by.

Contact Information in edas is a class representing a person's or entity's contact details (city, email, phone, postal code, street). Conference in sigkdd represents a conference event with properties like name, start/end dates, and city. These are completely different concepts: one is contact data, the other is an academic event. They share only the incidental property of having a city attribute.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In confOf, 'follows' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (e.g., one event following another in a sequence). In ekaw, 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (i.e., who organises what event). They share no common semantics.

Paper Abstract is a document artifact (a short summary of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while NGO is a type of organization (non-governmental organization) in the edas ontology. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In EKAW, 'referenced In' indicates that something (e.g., a paper) is referenced in another document or context, whereas in IASTED, 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a presentation or lecture). They have different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Conference Venue Place in edas is a physical venue (e.g., building, room) where conference events are held, sibling to Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place. Presenter city in iasted is a city associated with a presenter, sibling to Conference city, Sponsor city, Trip city. One denotes a venue/place structure, the other a city role; they are different kinds of entities with no clear overlap or subsumption.

Form in iasted is a subclass of Document covering administrative forms (registration, hotel, author information), whereas Author in sigkdd is a subclass of Person/Speaker denoting a person who writes papers. These are completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Deadline is a general class with multiple specific subclasses (camera ready, notification, hotel reservation, registration, submission). In sigkdd, Deadline Author notification is a specific subclass of Deadline. Thus iasted's Deadline is strictly more general than sigkdd's Deadline Author notification.

Pending Paper is a document (a submitted paper awaiting decision) while Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal entity (a date by which acceptance notifications are due). They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies (Document vs Time) and share no instances.

Both classes denote a paper/contribution that has been accepted at a conference. In Conference, 'Accepted contribution' is a subclass of 'Reviewed contribution' with a sibling 'Rejected contribution', and in edas, 'Accepted Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper' with a sibling 'Rejected Paper'. The sibling structure and the position in the class hierarchy confirm that both represent the same concept: a submission that passed review and was accepted.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a kind of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while iasted:Book_proceeding is a publication item (a physical artefact, sibling of Cd_proceeding). One denotes a scientific meeting/event, the other a published document. They are completely different kinds of entities.

In the Conference ontology, Regular author is a specific kind of conference contributor that is a child of Conference contribution and has subtypes Contribution 1th author and Contribution co author, indicating it models authors of written contributions. In edas, Author is a broad subclass of Person with children like Presenter and siblings such as Attendee, Reviewer, and Conference Chair, covering any person who authors a paper. Thus edas:Author is more general than Conference:Regular author, which is restricted to authors of conference contributions.

Property A (has_a_volume) links Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while property B (City_of_conference) links a Conference to a string city name. They relate different domain entities to different range types and capture entirely unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a leadership role (a person who chairs the conference, under Chairman/Person). In iasted, Conference Hiker is a type of Delegate (a conference attendee), under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate. Despite the similar label, they denote completely different concepts: one is an administrative/leadership role, the other is a category of participant. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision (with sibling Rejection), denoting the outcome of a paper review process. Invited Talk in ekaw is a subclass of Individual Presentation under Event, denoting a type of conference presentation. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Presenter in EKAW is a conference participant who presents (a paper, demo, etc.), situated under Person > Conference Participant. Author book proceedings included in IASTED is a specific author role for someone whose paper appears in the book proceedings, situated under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Speaker > Author. The IASTED class denotes a publication-venue-specific author sub-role, not a general presenter. Their intended instances do not coincide: a Presenter need not be an author in the book proceedings, and an Author book proceedings included need not be presenting at the conference. They are neither equivalent nor in a clear subsumption relation.

A's 'Conference contributor' is a broad subclass of Person covering all kinds of contributors to a conference (authors, speakers, active participants). B's 'Worker lecturer' is a very specific subclass of Person (via Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer) distinguishing a working/professional lecturer from a student lecturer. The two classes are at very different levels of generality and do not share the same intended instances; a worker lecturer is a narrow professional category, while a conference contributor is a broad role category. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other in a way a reference alignment would record.

Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a specific conference session, evidenced by properties like 'initiates Call' and 'is Reviewed By Paper' linking to session-level activities. Program Chair (sigkdd) is a top-level organizer responsible for the entire scientific program (e.g., overseeing reviewers, accepting papers). These are distinct organizational roles: a Session Chair manages individual sessions, while a Program Chair oversees the whole program. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in the given ontologies.

Both are datatype properties on Person with range string, but `hasFirstName` captures only the first name component while `Name` in sigkdd is the full name of a person. They overlap in being name-related attributes of Person, but they are not equivalent since one is a proper part of the other.

Conference contribution (A) is a document/artefact submitted to a conference volume, with children like Poster, Regular contribution, Written contribution, and properties has contributions/is submitted at linking it to Conference volume. Conference activity (B) is a temporal activity/event at a conference, with children like Cocktail reception, Coffee break, Registration, Welcome address. One is a submitted document, the other is a scheduled activity; their instances do not coincide.

A 'Conference participant' is a person who attends a conference, while a 'Dinner banquet' is a social event/activity. One is a person, the other is an event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference document in ontology Conference is a broad container for many conference artefacts (call for papers, announcements, contributions, reviews, web pages, participant info), while Document in sigkdd is narrower, covering only Abstract, Paper, and Review. Thus Conference document subsumes the sigkdd Document class.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (a working event under Event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while iasted:Overhead_projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (under Item). They denote completely different categories of things in the conference domain—an event versus a physical device—and share no meaningful relationship.

Both classes denote the same concept in the conference domain: a tutorial as a type of instructional presentation/event. In EKAW, Tutorial is a subclass of Individual Presentation (under Scientific Event), while in IASTED it is a subclass of Lecture (under Conference activity). Despite the different hierarchy paths, both refer to tutorial sessions at academic conferences, and their intended instances coincide.

Operating Topicsystems is a subclass of Topic in the EDAS ontology, representing a subject area within the conference domain (alongside siblings like Antennas Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.). Organising Agency is a subclass of Organisation in the EKAW ontology, representing an entity that organises conferences (alongside siblings like Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher). These are completely different concepts: one is a topic/subject, the other is an organisation. They share no instances and are not related in the conference domain.

confOf Member PC is a Program Committee member who reviews papers (comment says 'Reviewer', domain of reviewes and expertOn). ekaw Agency Staff Member denotes staff of a sponsoring/agency organization, not a PC reviewer. They share only the parent Person; their intended instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. In ekaw, 'paperPresentedAs' links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (the presentation itself). In sigkdd, 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (the person presenting). One connects paper→presentation-event, the other connects document→person, so they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the person who chairs the program committee in a conference. 'Program Committee Chair' (cmt) and 'Program Chair' (sigkdd) are synonymous labels for the same role in the conference organization domain. Both are subclasses of a person/organizer hierarchy and are siblings of other chair roles (e.g., Conference/General Chair). The slight naming difference ('Program Committee Chair' vs 'Program Chair') is a common shorthand variation, not a semantic distinction.

The two properties have opposite directions: ekaw:authorOf has domain Person and range Document, while iasted:is_signed_by has domain Item and range Person. They are inverses rather than equivalent, and a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

In cmt, 'Conference' denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, accepts hardcopy submissions, has members). In the Conference ontology, 'Conference applicant' denotes a person who applies to attend a conference (subclass of Person, sibling of Reviewer, Committee member, etc.). These are completely different concepts: one is the event/organization, the other is a person role.

The two properties describe different relations and have opposite directions. In cmt, `endReview` relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review, denoting the action of ending/concluding a review. In ekaw, `reviewWrittenBy` relates a Review to a Possible Reviewer, denoting authorship of the review. They connect different entity types and express different relationships (an administrative action vs. an authorship relation), so they are not equivalent, not subsumed, and only weakly related at best.

A Workshop in confOf is a standalone working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial) where papers are presented and discussed. An Industrial Session in ekaw is a specific session within a conference program focused on industrial presentations. These are different types of events: a workshop is a full event, while an industrial session is a sub-session of a conference. Their instances do not coincide.

In ekaw, OC Chair is a specific role within the Organizing Committee (a chair who leads it), sitting under OC Member. In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is a general member of the organizing committee, not specifically a chair. The sigkdd class is more general, subsuming the ekaw OC Chair role. They are not equivalent because one denotes a chair position and the other any organizing-committee member.

Administrative event in confOf is a temporal occurrence in conference organization (e.g., submission, reviewing, registration), while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic in edas is a subject-area classification for papers. They share no instances and belong to disjoint domain partitions.

Conference participant denotes any person who participates in a conference (including attendees, speakers, etc.), whereas Organizator denotes a person involved in organizing the conference (chairs, committee members, webmaster). These are disjoint concepts: an organizer is not a participant in the same sense, and a participant is not necessarily an organizer. They share only the common parent Person.

Property A (has_a_URL) is a datatype property from Conference www to string, representing a URL. Property B (locationOf) is an object property from Location to Event, indicating where an event is located. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

hasVAT captures value added tax for social/working events, while hasEmail captures an email address for persons/contact information. They relate to completely different domains and concepts, so they are unrelated.

Conference announcement is a document type (a conference-related publication/notice), while Computer Networks Enterprise Topic is a subject domain topic in a taxonomy of computer network areas. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

Contribution co-author is a person role (a kind of author who co-authored a contribution), while Multi-author Volume is a document type (a published volume with multiple authors, e.g., proceedings). One is a person/role, the other is a document; they share only the words 'author' in different senses.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception at a conference), while edas:RejectRating is a review rating indicating a paper should be rejected. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

Both are object properties linking a topic to the things it covers. In edas, 'is Topic Of' has domain Topic and range {Conference, Paper}; in ekaw, 'topic Covered By' has domain Research Topic and range {Event, Paper}. The domains (Topic vs Research Topic) and ranges (Conference vs Event, plus Paper in both) are close synonyms in the conference domain. The two properties express the same relation (a topic is covered by / is the topic of a paper or event/conference), just with slightly different naming conventions. No inverse direction is involved. They are equivalent.

Paper Author in ekaw is a subclass of Person, denoting someone who authors a paper. Student registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Registration fee under Money, denoting a monetary amount charged for student registration. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are called Abstract and concern the conference domain, but their structural positions differ. In Conference, Abstract is a fine-grained subclass of Extended abstract under Conference contribution, and it is the object of the property 'has an abstract' (Paper/Poster/Presentation -> Abstract), suggesting it models the abstract text/component of a contribution. In sigkdd, Abstract is a direct subclass of Document alongside Paper and Review, suggesting it models a standalone document type. The intended instances overlap (abstract texts) but are not clearly the same concept, so related is more appropriate than equivalent.

Conference contributor (A) groups people who contribute papers or talks (Active participant, Invited speaker, Regular author), while OC Member (B) is an Organizing Committee member (with OC Chair as a child). These are distinct roles: contributing content vs. serving on the organizing committee. No overlap in intended instances.

Transport vehicle (Item > Transport vehicle, with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) denotes a physical vehicle used for conference logistics. Organizator (Person > Organizator, with children General Chair, Program Chair, etc.) denotes a person who organizes the conference. These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Review in the Conference ontology is a document produced by a reviewer evaluating a contribution. Review Rating in edas is an evaluation category (Accept, Reject, etc.) assigned to a paper. One is the review artefact itself, the other is the rating/score outcome; they denote completely different concepts.

confOf:Regular denotes a non-student, non-member conference participant, while iasted:Sponsor denotes a person or organization that provides financial sponsorship. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain: a regular participant pays to attend, whereas a sponsor funds the event. Their paths, siblings, and intended instances do not coincide.

The confOf property 'has short title' applies to Social event and Working event, capturing a short display title for those entities. The sigkdd property 'Name of conference' applies specifically to a Conference and denotes the full name of the conference. They have different domains and different intended meanings (short title vs. conference name), so they are not equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote different relations. In cmt, acceptPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of accepting a paper). In edas, relatedToPaper relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (a generic association between a presentation and the accepted paper it presents). They do not connect the same kinds of entities nor express the same relation.

Tutorial and Workshop are distinct types of conference events. In ontology B, Workshop and Tutorial are explicitly modeled as sibling classes under Working event, confirming they are non-overlapping concepts. In ontology A, Tutorial is a sibling of Workshop under Conference part, further confirming the distinction. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

A Meta Review is a second-level review written by a meta-reviewer or chair to synthesise the regular reviews of a paper. A Neutral Review in EKAW is one of three sentiment categories (Positive/Neutral/Negative) classifying a regular review's overall recommendation. They occupy structurally similar positions under Review, but denote different concepts: one is a review type by role/stage, the other by sentiment polarity. Their instances do not coincide.

The two properties are completely different: `hasKeyword` (confOf) associates a Contribution with a string keyword describing its topic, while `hasCostAmount` (edas) associates a Sponsorship with an integer monetary amount. They have different domains (Contribution vs. Sponsorship), different ranges (string vs. int), and different meanings, so they are unrelated.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers, active participants), subclass of Person.
