Technical commitee in ontology B is a subclass of Delegate (which is under Place > Building > Conference building), making it a type of delegate/attendee rather than a contributor. They occupy different positions in their respective hierarchies and denote different concepts.

Both classes are subclasses of Person, but they denote different scopes. In Conference, 'Committee member' is specifically a member of a committee (linked to Committee via has members / was a member of). In sigkdd, 'Organizator' is a broader organizational role whose children include General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, and Webmaster. Thus sigkdd's Organizator subsumes Conference's Committee member, since committee membership is one kind of organizational role, but they are not equivalent.

These properties connect entirely different entities in different directions. `hasReviewHistory` links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a person's review track record), while `reviewOfPaper` links a Review to the Paper it reviews. Different domains (Reviewer vs Review), different ranges (PersonalReviewHistory vs Paper), and different semantics: one is about a reviewer's history, the other about which paper a review evaluates.

Contact Information in edas is a class holding contact details (city, email, phone, postal code, street) for persons or organizations. Document in ekaw is a published or unpublished artefact (abstract, paper, review, flyer, etc.) with authors and updated versions. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper Full Version is a conference document (a full paper submission), while Audiovisual equipment is a physical item like a projector or computer. They share no domain overlap despite both descending from a generic 'Item'/'Document' root.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference in the conference-review domain, whereas 'study At' links a Scholar to a University. Their domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so they are unrelated.

Entity A is a topic in the domain of parallel and distributed computing, a subclass of Topic. Entity B is a document type, specifically an abstract for an invited talk, a subclass of Abstract under Document. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Submitted_contribution in the Conference ontology is a specific subclass of Written_contribution representing contributions that have been submitted for review. Paper in EKAW is a broad class covering all kinds of papers (submitted, camera-ready, regular, demo, etc.). Since EKAW's Paper includes subtypes like Camera Ready Paper that are no longer 'submitted', Submitted_contribution is a narrower concept than Paper. The EKAW equivalent of Submitted_contribution would be the specific child class Submitted_Paper, not the general Paper class.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization representing a corporate entity (e.g., a company sponsoring or involved in a conference). edas:Operating Topicsystems is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area within the conference's taxonomy of topics (alongside Antennas, CAD, Communication Theory, etc.). These are completely different concepts: one is an organizational entity, the other is a conference topic. No overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. 'belong to a conference volume' links Important dates to a Conference volume, whereas 'hasProgramme' links a Conference Event to a Programme. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are distinct, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise related.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'acceptedBy' links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it (paper -> administrator). In sigkdd, 'submit' links an Author to a Paper they submit (author -> paper). They are not inverses of each other either, since 'acceptedBy' relates to acceptance by an administrator, not submission by an author. They denote entirely different relations in the conference domain.

cmt:title has domain Paper and denotes the full title of a paper. confOf:has_short_title has domain Social_event or Working_event and denotes a short title for events. Different domains (papers vs events) and different intended meanings (full title vs short title), so they are not equivalent.

confOf's hasTopic links a Working event to a Topic (subject matter of the event), while ekaw's hasEvent links an Event to a sub-Event (part-whole relation between events). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In edas, 'is Initiated By' connects a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the persons who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). In sigkdd, 'presentation' connects a Speaker to a Document (the presentation material). The domains (Call vs. Speaker), ranges (persons vs. Document), and overall semantics (who initiates a call vs. what document a speaker presents) are completely different, so these properties are unrelated.

The cmt property 'paper Assignment Tools Run By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs the paper-assignment tools). The iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (a person giving a presentation or item). They have different domains, different ranges, and different meanings; no overlap in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who runs paper assignment tools). In the Conference ontology, 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publication relationship). They share no semantic overlap.

Conference participant in ontology A is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person, with active/passive participants as children). Conference Venue Place in ontology B is a physical location where a conference takes place (subclass of Place, sibling to Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). One denotes a person, the other a physical location — completely disjoint concepts despite both containing the word 'Conference'.

These properties describe completely different relationships. 'author Of' (ekaw) links a Person to a Document they authored, while 'is paid by' (iasted) links Money to a Person who pays it. The domains (Person vs Money), ranges (Document vs Person), and semantic meanings are entirely unrelated.

Welcome Talk in edas is a subclass of Talk Event (an event that takes place at a conference), whereas Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Abstract (a document). One denotes an event, the other a document artefact, so they are not equivalent.

The property `title` in cmt has domain Paper and range string, representing the title of a paper. The property `Nation` in sigkdd has domain Person and range string, representing the nationality of a person. They relate completely different kinds of entities (documents vs. people) and denote unrelated attributes, so they are not equivalent.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Computer Networks Topic' is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference papers. In the SIGKDD ontology, 'Program Committee' is a subclass of Committee, representing a group of people who review papers. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range concepts. In cmt, assignReviewer links an Administrator to a Reviewer (the act of assigning someone to review a paper). In sigkdd, presentation links a Speaker to a Document (the slides or document presented). They share no common semantics in the conference domain.

confOf Tutorial is a subclass of Working event (an Event), denoting an event/activity. ekaw Invited_Talk_Abstract is a subclass of Abstract (a Document), denoting a written artefact. They belong to disjoint branches (Event vs Document) and do not share instances.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the person chairing the conference itself (a leadership role, under Chairman). Conference_applicant (Conference ontology) is a person who applies to attend/register for a conference (parent Person, child Registered_applicant). These are completely different roles: one is an administrative leader, the other is a prospective attendee. No overlap in intended instances.
Published Paper is a conference paper that has been published, while Cheque is a payment document. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

The two properties operate in completely different contexts. In EDAS, 'is Initiated By' links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the committee members who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). In SIGKDD, 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Call vs Document), ranges (committee members vs Speaker), and the underlying semantics (initiating a call vs presenting a document) are distinct, so the properties are unrelated.

Workshop in confOf is a type of event (a working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). Program Committee in sigkdd is a type of committee (sibling of Best Paper Awards Committee and Organizing Committee). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain: one is an event that takes place, the other is a group of people responsible for reviewing papers. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. In cmt, enterConferenceDetails relates an Administrator to a Conference (the administrator entering conference details). In ekaw, organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (who organises the event). They do not connect the same kinds of entities nor express the same relation.

In confOf, Conference is a kind of working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the academic conference itself. In iasted, Trip day is a temporal concept under Time (alongside Conference days and Deadline), denoting a day on which a trip occurs. These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a time period.

Entity A is a datatype property linking an 'Important dates' object to a date value (the deadline for full-paper submissions), whereas entity B is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper). They differ in type (datatype vs. object), domain, range, and meaning; they denote different relations in the conference domain.

These properties connect entirely different entity types in different directions. 'hasRelatedPaper' links an Author to a Paper (author -> paper they authored), while 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (document -> person presenting it). The domains (Author vs Document), ranges (Paper vs Speaker), and semantic meanings (authorship vs presentation) are all different, so these are unrelated.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'belong_to_a_conference_volume' links Important dates to a Conference volume, while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution. They have disjoint domains and ranges and denote unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

Property A (has_parts) relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts, i.e., the structural components of a published volume. Property B (hasProgramme) relates a Conference Event to its Programme, i.e., the schedule of activities. These are different relationships: one is about the composition of a publication, the other about the programme of an event. The domains and ranges differ accordingly, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

In EDAS, Session Chair is a subclass of Person, denoting the person who chairs a session. In EKAW, Session is a subclass of Scientific Event, denoting the event/session itself (e.g., a conference session, demo session, poster session). One is a person role, the other is an event; they denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

A Tutorial is an academic lecture/activity in the iasted ontology (subclass of Activity > Conference activity > Lecture), while an Exhibitor is a type of sponsor in the sigkdd ontology (subclass of Sponzor). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In Conference, Tutorial is a subclass of Conference part, a sibling of Track and Workshop, and the range of 'has tutorials' from Conference volume — it denotes an event/session. In ekaw, Tutorial Abstract is a subclass of Document > Abstract, a sibling of Invited Talk Abstract — it denotes a written document summarising a tutorial. An event and its abstract document are different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalisation of the other.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing that paper submissions are being solicited; it is a sibling of 'Call for participation', 'Conference announcement', etc. B's 'Paper' is the actual scholarly submission itself, with children like Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper and properties like 'is Written By' (Author) and 'is Reviewed By' (Reviewer). These are completely different concepts: one is an announcement document, the other is the research artifact being submitted. They share no instance overlap.

reviewerOfPaper in EKAW specifically relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review, while write in IASTED broadly relates any Person to any Item they author. Writing a paper is a more specific act than the general authorship relation, and reviewing is distinct from authoring. The general 'person writes item' relation subsumes the narrower reviewer-paper assignment.

Both classes denote a workshop as a type of conference event/part. In the Conference ontology, Workshop is a Conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial), while in edas it is an Academic Event (sibling of Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, Talk Event). Despite the different taxonomic positions, the intended instances coincide: both represent workshop events within a conference. The structural differences reflect modeling choices rather than semantic divergence.

confOf:Member PC is a person who serves on the Programme Committee and acts as a reviewer (subclass of Person, domain of reviewes/expertOn). edas:Review is a document artefact (subclass of Document, sibling of Paper/Programme/Slide Set). One denotes the reviewer (a person), the other the review document itself; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The cmt 'title' property captures the title of a Paper, while the edas 'hasPhone' property captures a phone number of Contact Information. They have disjoint domains (Paper vs. Contact Information) and denote completely different attributes, so they are unrelated.

Personal Review History in EDAS is a history/record object associated with a reviewer, not a person. Possible Reviewer in EKAW is a subclass of Person who can serve as a reviewer. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one is an information artefact, the other is a person role.

hasTopic relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject classification), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (bestowing or presenting). Different domains, ranges, and meanings; no overlap.

The property hasStreet in edas relates Contact Information to a string (a street address), while has_amount_of in iasted relates Money to an int (a monetary amount). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Organizing committee is a committee (a group of people) responsible for organizing a conference, while Administrative event is a temporal event (with children like Registration, Submission, Reviewing events). They are disjoint categories: a committee is not an event.

cmt:Conference denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, members, administrators), while Conference:Conference_document denotes documents produced for a conference (children include Call for paper, Review, Conference www, etc.). These are completely different concepts despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

confOf:Regular is a subclass of Participant (a person who regularly attends a conference), whereas ekaw:Regular_Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document type). These are completely different categories of entities—a person versus a document—so they are unrelated.

A 'Conference contributor' is a person who contributes to a conference (e.g., authors, speakers), while a 'Presenter house' is a building/place where a presenter resides or is hosted. One is a person role, the other is a physical location; they share no domain overlap.

A's Presentation is a broad class covering any conference presentation (including invited talks, posters, regular contributions), serving as a super-class for various presentation types. B's Power Point presentation is a specific format of presentation (a sibling of Video presentation under Presentation). These are at different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept: one is the general category, the other is a specific medium/format. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since A's Presentation is a different ontology's general class while B's PowerPoint presentation is a leaf node representing a particular presentation type.

Attendee (in edas) denotes a person who attends a conference, while Sponsor (in iasted) denotes a person or organization that provides financial support. These are distinct roles in the conference domain; an attendee is not necessarily a sponsor and vice versa. They share only the common parent Person, which is insufficient for equivalence.

In cmt, Subject Area is a topic or category that a Paper can be classified under (via 'has Subject Area'). In ekaw, Location is a physical place where an Event is held (via 'held In'). These are completely different concepts: a subject area is an abstract topic, while a location is a physical venue. There is no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person (range string), while the edas 'start Date' property denotes the start date and time of a Conference (range dateTime). They relate to completely different attributes of a conference and share no semantic relationship.

These properties operate in opposite directions and connect different entity types. 'is Initiated By' links a Call (a document/announcement) to the people who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). 'send' links a Person to an Item they send. While both involve people and documents, the direction is reversed: in A the document is the subject and the person is the object, while in B the person is the subject and the item is the object. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since their domains and ranges are disjoint.

Both properties link a presentation to a paper, but they run in opposite directions: edas:relatedToPaper goes from Paper Presentation to Accepted Paper, while ekaw:paperPresentedAs goes from Paper to Individual Presentation. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. They are related because they concern the same association between papers and presentations.

The two properties are completely different in meaning and structure. 'has a volume' is a datatype property from Conference proceedings to an integer (likely a volume number), while 'publisher Of' is an object property from an Organisation to various publication artefacts (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). They have different domains, different range types (datatype vs object), and different semantics.

Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement soliciting paper submissions), while Conference hall is a physical place where conference sessions are held. They belong to entirely different domains (documents vs. places) and share no conceptual overlap.

confOf:Social event is a non-academic gathering such as a banquet, reception, or trip, with properties like location and VAT. ekaw:Evaluated Paper is a paper that has been assigned and reviewed. These denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Contribution 1th author in Conference ontology is a specific author role: the first/primary author of a conference contribution, subclass of Regular author. Lecturer in iasted is a person who delivers a lecture at a conference, subclass of Author (under Speaker). These are different concepts: being a first author of a paper is about authorship order, while being a lecturer is about presenting at the event. A first author may not present, and a lecturer may not be the first author. No subsumption holds between them.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has_a_steering_committee' links a Conference volume to a Steering committee, while 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event. They do not share a domain, range, or semantic role.

Property A ('has a name') assigns a string name to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic. Property B ('start Date') assigns a dateTime representing the start date and time of a Conference. They have completely different meanings, domains, and ranges (string vs dateTime). There is no overlap in what these properties express.

Conference:Organization is a broad class for any organization, while ekaw:Organising_Agency is a specific subtype of organization (under Organisation, with siblings like Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher). Organization subsumes Organising_Agency, but they are not equivalent because the former is more general.

Rejected contribution in Conference is a terminal state of a reviewed paper that was not accepted. Active Paper in edas is a broad category encompassing papers that are active in the system (including accepted, pending, published, rejected, and withdrawn papers). The sibling Rejected Paper in edas corresponds to Rejected contribution, not Active Paper. The two classes have disjoint intended instances: Rejected contribution is strictly rejected papers, while Active Paper includes all non-withdrawn papers in various states. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a way that would be recorded as a reference alignment.

Workshop in the Conference ontology is a conference part (an academic event/session), while Taxi in the iasted ontology is a transport vehicle. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

An Organizational Meeting in EDAS is a meeting held to organize or plan conference activities (e.g., committee or planning meetings), not a scientific event where papers are presented. A Track in EKAW is a thematic session within a conference program containing scientific presentations. They serve different purposes: organizational/administrative vs. scientific/academic content delivery. Their sibling structures confirm this distinction—Organizational Meeting sits alongside Paper Presentation and Talk Event as event types, while Track sits alongside Conference and Session as program-structure elements.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and describe different actions. 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to the Conference volume where it appears (submission destination), with domain Conference contribution and range Conference volume. 'prepare' links a Person to an Item they prepare (authorship/preparation action), with domain Person and range Item. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so no equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful overlap holds.

Multi-author Volume in ekaw denotes a published collection of works (e.g., proceedings), while Form in iasted denotes administrative forms (registration, hotel, author info). They share the parent Document but represent disjoint document categories with no overlap in intended instances.

In the edas ontology, 'Programme' is a subclass of Document (a printed or digital programme/schedule artefact for a conference event), with siblings like Paper, Review, and Slide Set. In the sigkdd ontology, 'Program Committee' is a subclass of Committee (a group of people who review papers), with siblings like Best Paper Awards Committee and Organizing Committee. One is a document, the other is a committee of people; they denote completely different concepts despite both containing the word 'Program(me)'.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, detailsEnteredBy links a Conference to an Administrator (who enters conference details). In ekaw, organises links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

Subject Area in cmt denotes a research topic or thematic category that a Paper can be classified under (domain of has Subject Area is Paper, range is SubjectArea). Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who gives a presentation, with subclasses Author and Invited Speaker. These are completely different concepts: one is a topic/category, the other is a human role. No overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'study At' property relates a Scholar to a University, representing the institution where a person studies. The iasted 'obtain' property relates a Person to an Item, representing possession or acquisition of an item. These are fundamentally different relations: one connects a person to an educational institution, the other connects a person to a physical or abstract item. There is no overlap in meaning.

Research Topic in ekaw denotes a subject area or theme covered by events and papers (e.g., a research field like 'machine learning'), while Conference in sigkdd denotes an academic event with properties like start/end dates, city, and name. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have opposite domains and ranges and different semantics. In Conference, 'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (a person authors/contributes a document). In iasted, 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person (an item is needed for a person). They do not relate the same kinds of entities in the same direction, and there is no indication of overlap or subsumption.

In iasted, Building is a broad superclass of many venue types (Conference building, Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, etc.), while in sigkdd, Main office is a specific sibling of Conference hall and Hotel under Place. They are at different levels of generality and denote different things: a general building vs. a specific office. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other since Main office is not listed as a child of Building in iasted.

PaperFullVersion in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a document submitted to a conference), whereas CryptographyTopic in edas is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

In cmt, Document is a top-level class whose instances are papers and reviews—artifacts produced or used in the paper-reviewing process. In iasted, Card is a subclass of Item with child Credit card and siblings such as Audiovisual equipment and Transport vehicle, denoting physical items used at the conference venue. These are completely different categories: cmt's Document is a textual artefact, while iasted's Card is a physical object like a credit card. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Conference contribution is a document-type entity (paper, poster, presentation) submitted to a conference volume, while Tax is a monetary amount (departure tax, VAT). They belong to completely different domains (academic contributions vs. money/fees) with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person, denoting people who contribute to a conference (authors, speakers, participants). Non Academic Event is a subclass of Conference Event, denoting events like breaks, meals, and social activities. These are completely different categories: a person role vs. an event type.

The two properties are of different types and have incompatible ranges. 'obtain' is an object property relating a Person to an Item they obtain, while 'Name' is a datatype property relating a Person to a string representing their name. They denote completely different relations.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In cmt, 'run Paper Assignment Tools' is an action performed by an Administrator on a Conference (managing paper-assignment tooling). In ekaw, 'paper Presented As' links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (how/where a paper is presented). They share no common domain, range, or semantic meaning.

The two properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, readByReviewer has domain Paper and range Reviewer, expressing which reviewer(s) read/reviewed a paper. In the Conference ontology, invited_by has domain Reviewer and range Reviewer, expressing that one reviewer was invited by another reviewer. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Entity A is a specific research topic about computer network security, a subclass of Topic in the EDAS ontology. Entity B is an Organizing Committee, a subclass of Committee in the SIGKDD ontology, representing a group of people who organize a conference. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Talk Event in edas is a broad class for spoken academic events (including closing talks, welcome talks, paper presentations), while Workshop Session in ekaw is a specific session type within a workshop. They are at different levels of granularity and serve different purposes: one is a general talk/presentation event, the other is a session within a workshop. Their instance sets do not meaningfully coincide.

Submitted Paper is a paper submitted for review at a conference, while Payment document is a document related to payment (bank transfer, cheque). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain despite both being subclasses of Document.

The cmt property 'review Criteria Entered By' links a Conference to an Administrator (who enters review criteria), while the iasted property 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., a person giving a presentation or item). They have different domains, different ranges, and express entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

In cmt, Review is a specific document type (a peer-review of a paper), subclass of Document. In iasted, Document is a broad superclass covering many artefacts (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc.). The iasted Document class is strictly more general than the cmt Review class; in fact, iasted even lists Review as a child of Document. Thus cmt:Review is subsumed_by iasted:Document.

confOf:Author is a person who writes a contribution (a paper author), while iasted:Reviewer is a delegate/speaker who performs reviews. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: an author submits work, a reviewer evaluates others' work. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in the general case.

The cmt hasDecision property links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while confOf follows links one Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal/sequential ordering). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

`Information for participants` is a conference document (e.g., informational material distributed to participants), while `Modelling` is a research activity performed before a conference. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and share no semantic overlap.

Submitted Paper is a specific academic document type (a paper submitted to a conference for review), while Card is a physical item (with a Credit card subclass) used in the IASTED ontology for registration/payment purposes. They belong to completely different domains and share no instances.

has_the_last_name is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's surname), while authorOf is an object property from Person to Document (relating a person to a paper they authored). They relate completely different kinds of things and serve entirely different purposes.

Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while OperatingTopicsystems is a specific subject topic (like Antennas, Cryptography, etc.) under Topic. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

Bank_transfer is a payment document (a financial instrument) in the iasted ontology, while Paper is a research document in sigkdd. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. In edas, 'isMemberOf' links a Person to a Conference (person belongs to conference). In iasted, 'is_given_by' links an Activity/Item to a Person (activity/item is presented by person). They have different domains and ranges, and are not inverses of each other since the ranges/domains do not correspond (Person-Conference vs Activity/Item-Person).

The property `deals With` in confOf relates a Contribution to a Topic (the subject area of the paper), while `has Rating` in edas relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (the score assigned by a reviewer). These are entirely different relations connecting different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

The property `writes` in confOf relates an Author to a Contribution (the author writes the paper). The property `hasReview` in ekaw relates a Paper to a Review (the paper has a review). These are completely different relations with different domains and ranges, and they do not overlap in meaning.

Associated Chair is a person who co-chairs a conference (path: Person > Chairman > Associated Chair), while Industry Organization is a type of organization (path: Organization > Industry Organization). One is a human role, the other is an organizational entity; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

A's Paper is a general conference contribution (sibling to Extended abstract, parent Regular contribution), while B's Workshop Paper is a specific subtype of Paper in ekaw. A's Paper is more general, so it is subsumed by B's broader Paper concept but not equivalent to the narrower Workshop Paper.

These properties relate different entities in different directions. 'belongsToEvent' links a Programme to a Conference Event (a programme is part of an event). 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event (an agent organises an event). The domains (Programme vs Organisation/Person) and the nature of the relationship (part-of/membership vs agent-of-organisation) are fundamentally different, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

These properties have different domains and different meanings. `writtenBy` (domain: Review, range: Reviewer) indicates who authored a review, while `invited_by` (domain: Reviewer, range: Reviewer) indicates who invited a reviewer to serve on a committee. They relate different entities in different directions and capture distinct relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate fundamentally different kinds of things. confOf:employedBy has domain Person and range Organization, modelling a person's employment at an organization. ekaw:organisedBy has domain Event and range Organisation or Person, modelling which agent organises a conference event. The domains (Person vs Event) and the intended semantics (employment vs event-organisation) are distinct, so these are not the same relation.

Multi-author Volume is a document type (e.g., proceedings) published by an organisation, while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors of acceptance. They share no domain overlap.

The cmt Administrator is a system-level user role responsible for managing the conference system (accepting papers, assigning reviewers, entering review criteria, enabling virtual meetings). The confOf Scholar is a price-category person who studies at a university. These are completely different concepts: one is an administrative/system role, the other is an academic/registration category. They share no common instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Both properties have identical domain (Author) and range (Paper), and both represent the action of an author submitting a paper in the conference domain. The labels 'submit Paper' and 'submit' are synonymous in this context, and the structural position (Author -> submit -> Paper) matches exactly.

Demo Session is a type of scientific event/session where demonstrations are presented, while Organizing Committee is a committee responsible for organizing a conference. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings: 'has_the_first_name' applies to Person and records a person's first name, while 'hasStreet' applies to Contact Information and records a street address. They relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

These properties are completely different. A's 'name' is a datatype property mapping Conference/Person to a string (the name of the entity). B's 'is used by' is an object property mapping Item to Person (indicating a usage relationship between an item and a person). They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain, range, and semantic meaning.

Both are object properties linking a written contribution to its author. In confOf, 'written By' has domain Contribution and range Author; in iasted, 'is prepared by' has domain Item and range Person. Contribution and Item are the conference artefacts being authored, while Author and Person overlap as the agents who write them. The direction is identical (work -> author), and the labels are synonymous in this domain.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event (a trip/activity), while Conference restaurant in iasted is a building/place. One is an event, the other is a physical location; they denote completely different concepts despite the shared word 'Conference'.

Property A links a submitted contribution/topic to a Review preference (expressing a preference for a reviewer), while property B links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (assigning a reviewer). They differ in both the object type and the relation semantics: preference vs. assignment.

The property hasRelatedPaper in edas links an Author to a Paper (the paper they authored or are related to), while obtain in sigkdd links an Author to an Award. These are fundamentally different relationships: one connects authors to their written works, the other connects authors to awards they received. The ranges (Paper vs Award) are disjoint concepts, and the semantics of the relations are entirely different.

hasCity relates an Organization or Person to a City (a location), while hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (a participant). They connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Paper is a general class for any paper contribution (siblings include Poster and Short paper), whereas edas:RatedPapers is a specific subclass of Active Paper restricted to papers that have received a rating. Every Rated Paper is a Paper, but not every Paper is rated, so confOf:Paper is subsumed by edas:RatedPapers in the sense that the edas class is narrower; here confOf:Paper is the more general concept and edas:RatedPapers the more specific, making the relation subsumed_by for A relative to B.

Contact Information in edas is a data container class for address/contact details (city, email, phone, postal code, street), while Person in sigkdd represents conference participants (listeners, organizers, speakers) with properties like name, nation, registration payment. They are fundamentally different concepts: one is contact data, the other is a human actor. Though both can have email, the classes themselves do not overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent events occurring at a conference. They share similar structural properties: both have location-related properties (hasLocation/heldIn, isLocationOf/locationOf), both have sub-classes distinguishing academic/scientific events from non-academic/social events, and both serve as the top-level event concept in their respective ontologies. The minor differences in associated properties (e.g., attendees, programme, dates) reflect modelling granularity rather than conceptual divergence.

A Conference Chair is the person who chairs the conference (organizational/administrative role), while an Invited Speaker is a presenter invited to give a talk. These are distinct roles in a conference: a chair organizes/oversees, whereas an invited speaker delivers a presentation. Their instance sets do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

cmt:Paper is a single submitted paper with authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions. ekaw:Multi author Volume is a collection of works by multiple authors (e.g., proceedings), with Paper as a sibling rather than a child. They denote different kinds of entities and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. In cmt, 'run Paper Assignment Tools' connects an Administrator to a Conference (the administrator runs paper-assignment tools for the conference). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' connects a Document to a Speaker (the document is presented by the speaker). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely disjoint, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Workshop Paper is a specific kind of paper presented at a workshop, a full document type. In sigkdd, Abstract is a sibling of Paper and Review, denoting a summary document, not a full paper. These are distinct document categories with different intended instances.

Camera Ready Paper is a finalized, accepted paper ready for publication (a specific subtype of Paper in ekaw), while Abstract in sigkdd is a summary document that is a sibling of Paper and Review. These are distinct document types: a camera-ready paper is a complete accepted paper, whereas an abstract is a brief summary. They do not share instances, and neither subsumes the other.

The iasted 'is designed for' is an object property relating activities/money/time to activities/persons, while the sigkdd 'Name' is a datatype property relating a person to a string (their name). They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

Entity A is a subclass of Person (a late-paying conference applicant), while entity B is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount charged to non-members). One denotes a person, the other a fee; they are in disjoint hierarchies and do not overlap.

In cmt, `name` is a datatype property of Conference and Person whose range is a string, representing the full name of a person or conference. In the Conference ontology, `has the last name` is a datatype property of Person whose range is a string, representing specifically the last name (surname) of a person. A full name subsumes a last name (a last name is a part of a full name), so `name` is more general than `has the last name`; hence `name` is subsumed_by `has the last name` is incorrect direction-wise—rather, `has the last name` is subsumed by `name`. The correct relation is that `name` subsumes `has_the_last_name`, i.e., `name` is more general. Therefore the relation is `subsumes` (A subsumes B).

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'hasPostalCode' relates Contact Information to a string (postal code), while 'is_sent_after' relates an Item to a Time. They share no semantic relationship in the conference domain.

Both are subclasses of Person in the conference domain, but they denote overlapping yet distinct concepts. cmt's Conference Member is a broad category covering authors, chairs, PC members, and reviewers (anyone with a formal membership role in the conference). Conference's Conference contributor is specifically about people who contribute content (active participants, invited speakers, regular authors). A Reviewer in cmt is a Conference Member but would not typically be a Conference contributor, while a Regular author in Conference would be a Conference Member in cmt. They overlap significantly but are not coextensive.

Submitted_contribution in the Conference ontology is a specific subclass of Written_contribution, denoting a contribution that has been submitted for review (it has child Reviewed_contribution and is linked to review expertise/preference). Document in sigkdd is a broader class covering Abstract, Paper, and Review—any document artefact in the conference. A submitted contribution is a kind of document, so Submitted_contribution is subsumed by Document, but the two are not equivalent because Document includes abstracts and reviews that are not themselves submitted contributions.
readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper they review, while writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author. They differ in domain, range, and meaning; they are not inverses of each other either.

Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (Item > Transport vehicle > Shuttle bus) in the iasted ontology, while Listener is a person (Person > Listener) in the sigkdd ontology. These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

In ontology A, 'Conference contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference document' and has children such as 'Poster', 'Presentation', 'Regular contribution', and 'Written contribution', denoting the artefacts or works contributed to a conference. In ontology B, 'Event' denotes occurrences (scientific or social) that are held at a location, organised by agents, and listed in brochures. A contribution is not an event; it is the content or document submitted, whereas an event is an activity. The two classes have disjoint intended instances.

Both classes represent deadlines in the conference domain. They share the same label and intended meaning: temporal points by which certain conference-related actions must be completed. Both have similar children (submission deadlines, notification deadlines, camera-ready deadlines) and both are associated with date/dateTime properties. The specific subtypes differ slightly across ontologies but the core concept of a deadline is identical.

These properties are completely unrelated. confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper). edas's 'initiates' links committee roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call (e.g., call for papers). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

These properties relate different entities in different directions. 'relatedToPaper' in edas links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (the paper being presented). 'presentationed_by' in sigkdd links a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). They connect different domain/range types and express different relationships: one associates a presentation with its paper, the other associates a document with its presenter. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Pending Paper in EDAS denotes a paper whose review status is pending (a workflow state, sibling to Accepted/Rejected/Withdrawn), whereas Conference Paper in EKAW denotes a paper presented at a conference (a venue/type classification, sibling to Workshop Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). They classify papers along orthogonal dimensions (review status vs. venue/presentation type), so their intended instances do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'has a degree' relates a Review preference to an integer (likely a preference rating degree), while 'has First Name' relates a Person to a string (a person's given name). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Both properties relate a person to a written document, but they are inverses: ekaw:authorOf has domain Person and range Document (Person -> Document), while iasted:is_writen_by has domain Item and range Person (Item -> Person). A property and its inverse are not equivalent.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and denote different concepts. In cmt, 'acceptedBy' links a Paper to an Administrator who accepted it, indicating paper acceptance. In the Conference ontology, 'invited_by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer, indicating an invitation relationship between reviewers. The domains (Paper vs Reviewer), ranges (Administrator vs Reviewer), and intended meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

The edas Attendee is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person, siblings include Author, Reviewer, etc.). The iasted Nonmember registration fee is a monetary amount charged for registration (subclass of Fee > Registration fee). One is a person role, the other is a financial concept; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Reject Rating is a rating value indicating paper rejection, while Positive Review is a review with positive content. These are opposite concepts: a reject rating corresponds to a negative review, not a positive one. They also differ in kind (rating vs. document).

confOf Workshop is a working event (a conference-like event with papers, sessions, etc.), while edas Welcome Talk is a specific talk event (a single presentation). They are at very different granularity levels and denote different concepts in the conference domain.

Wireless Communications Topic is a subject-area topic (sibling of Communication Theory Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.) under Topic in the edas ontology. Transport vehicle is a physical item (with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van) under Item in the iasted ontology. These denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties operate on completely different domains and ranges with different semantics. Property A links a submitted contribution (or topic) to a review preference, indicating what kind of review a paper should receive. Property B links a document to a speaker, indicating who presents it. The domains (Submitted contribution/Topic vs. Document), ranges (Review preference vs. Speaker), and intended meanings are entirely distinct with no overlap in the conference domain.

The two properties are completely different in domain, range, and meaning. `hasFirstName` is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's first name), while `is_used_by` is an object property from Item to Person (indicating which person uses an item). They share no semantic relationship.

Review expertise in the Conference ontology denotes the level or area of expertise a reviewer has regarding a submitted contribution, functioning as a qualification metric. Document in sigkdd is a general container for textual artefacts (Abstract, Paper, Review). These are fundamentally different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Committee member denotes a person serving on a conference committee (with subtypes Chair, Co-chair), while Sponsor denotes a person or entity that provides financial sponsorship. Despite sharing the parent Person, their intended instances do not coincide: a committee member is not necessarily a sponsor and vice versa. They are distinct roles in the conference domain.

Sponsor (iasted) is a Person who provides financial support to a conference, while General Chair (sigkdd) is an Organizator responsible for running the conference. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are named 'Paper', sit directly under 'Document', and represent the same concept in the conference domain: a submitted paper. They share the same structural position (Document > Paper) and the same siblings (Review, Abstract). The edas ontology adds specialized subclasses (Accepted, Rejected, etc.) and richer properties, but the core denotation of the class Paper is identical in both ontologies.

The two properties have completely different meanings: confOf's 'max Choice' captures a maximum number of choices for a social/working event, while sigkdd's 'Start of conference' captures the start date/time of a conference. They have different domains (Social event/Working event vs. Conference), different ranges (positiveInteger vs. dateTime), and no semantic overlap.

Chairman in cmt is a leadership role (parent Person, with children like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair) responsible for marking conflicts of interest. Speaker in iasted is a Delegate who presents (parent Delegate, sibling of Listener, Non speaker). These are distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string (postal code), while obtain is an object property linking Person to Item. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

The property 'is Reviewing' in edas specifically relates reviewers/committee members to Papers they are reviewing. The property 'give' in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a presentation or lecture). Although both connect a person to something they provide, the range types differ (Paper vs Activity/Item) and the intended semantics are distinct: reviewing a paper is not the same as giving an activity or item.

In edas, Reviewer is a subclass of Person—the agent who performs reviewing. In iasted, Review is a subclass of Document—the written review artefact itself. These denote fundamentally different categories (person vs. document) with no overlap in intended instances, so they are unrelated.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics. In ekaw, 'location Of' has domain Location and range Event, meaning it relates a location to the event held there (a location is the location of an event). In iasted, 'is situated in' has domain Building/City/Place and range Building/City/Place/State, meaning it relates a place to the place it is situated in (e.g., a building situated in a city, a city situated in a state). The ekaw property connects locations to events, while the iasted property connects places to containing places. They denote different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In confOf, hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (e.g., organizing a conference event). In sigkdd, obtain links an Author to an Award. The domains (Working event vs Author) and ranges (Administrative event vs Award) are disjoint, and the intended meanings share no overlap.

In Conference, Review is a document written by a reviewer about a contribution, sibling to Conference contribution. In edas, Paper is the submitted article itself, with Review appearing as a distinct sibling under Document. These are different concepts: a review is not a paper.

Numerical Review Question is a type of review question (a question with a numerical answer used in reviewing), while Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper). They belong to completely different parts of the conference domain hierarchy and share no instances.

The two properties operate in completely different domains and ranges. confOf:reviewes relates a PC Member to a Contribution (paper being reviewed), while iasted:is_paid_for relates Money to an Activity or Item (payment relationship). They share no semantic overlap.

Both are non-academic social events involving food, but a Banquet is a specific evening social event (a conference dinner), while a Meal Break is a scheduled break during the academic program for eating. They overlap in theme but are distinct event types in a conference.

Conference Chair in cmt is a leadership role (a person who chairs the conference, under Chairman > Conference Member), while Worker non speaker in iasted is a type of delegate/attendee who does not give a presentation (under Non speaker > Delegate > Conference building > Building > Place). These are completely different concepts: one is the head of the conference, the other is a non-presenting attendee. They share no meaningful semantic overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. `has Attendee` links a Conference Event to a Person (the attendees of the event), while `hold` links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference (the conference it organizes). They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning; one is about participation, the other about organization/holding of an event.

Property A (has_a_location) associates a Conference volume with a location (string), while property B (hasName) associates a Conference with its full name. They relate different kinds of things (location vs. name) and have different domains (Conference volume vs. Conference), so they are unrelated.

These two properties denote different relations in the conference domain. 'is Reviewed By' (edas) relates a Paper to the people who reviewed it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member). 'is writen by' (iasted) relates an Item to the Person who authored it. Reviewing and authoring are distinct relationships; a paper's reviewers are generally not its authors, and the properties connect different role sets. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

cmt:Author is specifically a person who writes/submits papers, sitting under Conference Member with siblings like Reviewer and Administrator. ekaw:Conference Participant is a broad class covering anyone who participates in a conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, OC members, etc.), and it has a sibling Paper Author that corresponds more closely to cmt:Author. The two classes have largely disjoint intended instances: an Author need not be a conference participant, and a Conference Participant need not be an author. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

Registration form in iasted is a document/form that participants fill out (subclass of Form, sibling of Hotel registration form). Registration Non Member in sigkdd is a fee amount charged to non-members (subclass of Registration fee, sibling of Registration Student). One is a document, the other is a monetary fee; they denote completely different concepts despite sharing the word 'registration'.

These properties relate different entities in different directions. Property A (has_a_review_expertise) links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (capturing the expertise level assigned to a review). Property B (reviewes) links a Member PC to a Contribution (capturing which paper a PC member reviews). They have different domains, different ranges, and represent different relationships: one is about expertise classification of a review, the other is about the reviewing assignment itself.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event (e.g., an excursion or outing during a conference), whereas Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place where conference activities occur. They are disjoint categories (event vs. place) with no overlap in intended instances.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking Person/Contact Information to a string (email address), while send is an object property linking Person to Item (sending an item). They differ in type (datatype vs object), range (string vs Item), and meaning (possessing an email address vs sending an item). No alignment relation holds.

Both are social/leisure activities associated with a conference, but a Conference Trip is a broad category of social event (sibling to Conference Banquet), while a Full day tour is a specific type of post-conference activity. A conference trip could include various excursions, not limited to full-day tours, and a full-day tour is a specific kind of trip. They overlap but are not equivalent.

minChoice is a confOf datatype property with domain Social event/Working event and range positiveInteger, representing some numeric choice/option count. hasEndDateTime is an edas datatype property with domain ConferenceEvent and range dateTime, representing the end timestamp of an event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range types: cmt's runPaperAssignmentTools has domain Administrator and range Conference (an administrator running paper-assignment tools on a conference), whereas Conference's issues has domain Publisher and range Conference proceedings (a publisher issuing proceedings). The participants and the intended action are different, so the properties are unrelated.

In the Conference ontology, Person is a broad superclass with children including Committee member, Conference applicant, Conference contributor, Conference participant, Reviewer, and Track workshop chair. In confOf, Author is a subclass of Person (alongside Administrator, Chair PC, Member PC, Participant, etc.). Thus Person in Conference is strictly more general than Author in confOf; the two are not equivalent.

A 'Two Level Conference' in edas is a type of conference (a conference event/organization), while 'Sponsor state' in iasted is a state (status) associated with a sponsor. They denote completely different concepts—a conference type versus a sponsorship status—with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote members of a program committee. confOf's 'Member PC' (with comment 'Reviewer' and properties like 'reviewes Contribution') and sigkdd's 'Program Committee member' (under Organizator) refer to the same role in conference organization. The label 'Member PC' is an abbreviation of 'Program Committee member', and both are subtypes of Person in their respective ontologies.

In the EDAS ontology, 'Reviewer' is a subclass of Person, denoting a human agent who writes reviews. In the EKAW ontology, 'Review' is a subclass of Document, denoting the review artefact itself (with children like Negative Review, Positive Review). These are fundamentally different entities (agent vs. document), so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference restaurant in iasted is a physical place/building where conference events occur. They share the word 'Conference' but denote completely different categories of entities.

These two properties are completely different in meaning and structure. 'written By' in ekaw is an object property relating a Document to the Person who wrote it. 'Nation' in sigkdd is a datatype property relating a Person to a string representing their nationality. They have different domains, different ranges (object vs datatype), and denote entirely unrelated concepts.

Contribution 1th author is a subclass of Regular author, representing a person who is the first author of a conference contribution. Author information form is a subclass of Form (a document), representing a form that authors fill out. One is a person/author role, the other is a document/form. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf Contribution is a broad class covering Paper, Poster, and Short paper, while edas Paper is specifically a paper (a subclass of Document). Contribution thus subsumes Paper: every Paper is a Contribution but not vice versa (posters and short papers are not Papers).

Conference Chair in edas is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Person, sibling of Attendee, Author, Reviewer, etc.), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office). One is a human role, the other is a location; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties differ in both domain and range and in the direction of the relation. In iasted, 'prepare' relates Person -> Item (a person prepares an item such as a document or presentation). In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' relates Document -> Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). They are not inverses in a clean sense either, since the domain/range types (Person/Item vs Document/Speaker) do not align well across the two ontologies. There is no clear equivalence or subsumption.

Property A links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the entity that publishes the proceedings), while property B links a Contribution to an Author (the person who wrote it). They relate completely different kinds of things in the conference domain and have no semantic overlap.

Accommodation Place in edas is a geographic/venue location where conference participants stay (a Place subclass, sibling of Conference Venue Place and Dining Place). Worker non speaker in iasted is a person role—a delegate who does not give a talk and is a worker—nested under Person > Delegate > Non speaker. One is a place, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are unrelated.

Both classes represent non-scientific social/leisure activities associated with a conference (e.g., banquets, trips, departures), but they are not strictly equivalent: ekaw:Social Event is specifically a social gathering during the conference, while iasted:Activity_after_conference is temporally restricted to activities occurring after the conference ends. The two extensions overlap (e.g., a post-conference tour is both a social event and an after-conference activity) but neither subsumes the other, since a conference banquet is a Social Event that is not after the conference, and a Departure is an after-conference activity that is not typically a social event.

In cmt, 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author specifically denoting authors who are not reviewers. In edas, 'Reviewer' denotes persons who review papers. These are disjoint categories: one excludes reviewers, the other is exactly reviewers. They share no instance overlap and neither subsumes the other.

Reviewing results event in confOf represents the event where review results are made accessible to authors, while Call For Manuscripts in edas represents a call soliciting manuscript submissions. These are distinct concepts in the conference workflow: one is an outcome/announcement event, the other is a solicitation call. They do not share instances or a subsumption relationship.

The two properties connect entirely different entities. 'belongs to reviewers' links review expertise or review preference to a reviewer, while 'presentation' links a speaker to a document. They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relations in the conference domain.

In ontology Conference, 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who applies to attend or participate in a conference. In confOf, 'Conference' is a subclass of Working_event, denoting the conference event itself. These are completely different concepts: one is a person (an applicant), the other is an event. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf:Conference denotes the main academic conference event (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas iasted:Activity_after_conference denotes post-conference activities such as Departure and Full day tour. They occupy different positions in their respective hierarchies and refer to disjoint kinds of things.

In ekaw, Presenter is a person who presents at the conference (a Conference Participant who gives a presentation). In iasted, Non_speaker is a Delegate who does NOT speak/present. These are complementary, not equivalent: a Presenter is someone who does present, while a Non_speaker is someone who does not. They are disjoint categories of participants, so they are unrelated (not equivalent, not subsuming one another).

Conference proceedings is a published document (with ISBN, volume, publisher), while Time is a temporal entity whose children include Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day. These are completely disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

contactEmail relates a Contribution to a contact email address (string), while hasSubmissionDeadline relates a Call to a submission deadline (dateTime). They connect different domain entities to different kinds of values and denote unrelated relations.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. `has_a_name` assigns a string name to entities like Conference, Publisher, and Topic. `minChoice` assigns a positive integer (likely a minimum number of choices) to Social event and Working event. They share no semantic relationship.

Government Organization is a type of organization (e.g., a government body that may sponsor or participate in a conference), whereas Sponzorship is a monetary concept (a financial sponsorship arrangement). They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Organization vs Money) and denote different kinds of entities.

Mobile Computing Topic is a subject-area topic under Topic in the edas ontology (siblings include Communication Theory, Computer Networks, etc.), denoting a research subject. Transport vehicle is a concrete physical item under Item in iasted (children: Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a senior conference committee role (a Chairman who assists in running the conference), while Listener is a Delegate who attends but does not present. They are completely different concepts: one is an organizational leadership role, the other is a passive attendee. No overlap in intended instances.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In EKAW, 'scientificallyOrganisedBy' relates an event to the Academic Institution that scientifically organises it (a sub-property of 'organised By'). In IASTED, 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a talk or a lecture). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so the properties are unrelated.

`Conference fees` in the Conference ontology denotes monetary charges associated with attending a conference, while `Conference` in edas denotes the conference event itself (with children like Single Level Conference, properties like has Country, paper Due On, etc.). These are completely different concepts: one is a fee/charge, the other is an academic event. They share the word 'Conference' but do not overlap in meaning.

In ekaw, Conference_Paper is a specific kind of paper accepted/published at a conference, sitting under Paper alongside Camera_Ready_Paper, Regular_Paper, etc. In sigkdd, Abstract is a sibling of Paper and Review under Document, denoting the summary text of a submission. A conference paper is a full document, not an abstract; the two classes have disjoint intended instances.

The confOf 'written By' property links a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper), whereas the sigkdd 'presentationed by' property links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). Authorship and presentation are distinct roles in the conference domain, and the domains/ranges (Contribution/Author vs Document/Speaker) do not coincide.

Rejected contribution is a written paper that has been reviewed and rejected, while Reception is a social event at a conference. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no domain overlap.

In cmt, Reviewer is a concrete role: a person assigned to review a paper (with properties like assignedTo, readByReviewer, adjustBid). In ekaw, Possible_Reviewer is a more general class denoting anyone who could potentially review a paper; its subclass PC_Member is the concrete reviewer role. Thus cmt:Reviewer is narrower than ekaw:Possible_Reviewer.

Topic in edas denotes a subject area of a conference or paper (e.g., Antennas, Cryptography, Mobile Computing), while Time in iasted denotes a temporal entity such as a conference day, deadline, or trip day. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Review Question in EDAS is a question item within a review (e.g., a numerical or textual question posed to a reviewer), whereas Review in EKAW is the entire review document (with children like Positive/Negative Review). A review question is a component of a review, not the review itself; the two classes denote completely different kinds of things.

The edas Conference Chair is a subclass of Person (a human role), while the iasted Brief introduction for Session chair is a subclass of Document (an artefact). They denote completely different kinds of entities despite the shared phrase 'Session chair'.

These entities are unrelated despite superficially similar labels. In ekaw, 'Conference Session' is a scientific event/session (e.g., a talk or session at a conference), while in iasted, 'Conference state' is a temporal/logical state of a conference (e.g., before, during, after). They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Event vs. State) and denote different concepts.

The property 'is Written By' in edas relates a Paper to its Author, while 'design' in sigkdd relates an ACM SIGKDD conference to a Deadline. They connect completely different domain and range types and denote unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

confOf:follows relates one Administrative event to another (e.g., an event following another in a sequence), whereas ekaw:eventOnList relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (i.e., the event is listed on that document/site). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.
Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while ParallelAndDistributedComputingTopic is a subject-area topic. They share no domain overlap.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person who applies to attend/register for a conference (a prospective participant before acceptance/registration), while a 'Tutorial Chair' is a specific organisational role responsible for chairing a tutorial. They denote different concepts in the conference domain: one is an applicant status, the other is a chair role. Their instance sets do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different entities. `has_an_ISBN` associates a Conference proceedings with its ISBN string identifier, while `hasBiography` associates a Person with a biographical text string. They have different domains (Conference proceedings vs. Person), different meanings, and no overlap in the kinds of things they relate.

In cmt, Paper is a conference paper submitted for review, with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer. In ekaw, Programme Brochure is a document listing events in a programme, with properties lists Event and publisher Of Organisation. They share the parent Document but denote completely different artefacts in the conference domain.

Accommodation Place in edas is a specific kind of place (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) denoting lodging. Building in iasted is a more general class whose children include Conference hotel, Conference restaurant, Conference building, Presenter house, etc. Accommodation Place is thus a narrower concept subsumed by Building, not equivalent.

A Conference applicant is a person who applies to attend/register for a conference (a prospective participant), whereas a PC Member is a member of the Programme Committee who reviews papers and makes acceptance decisions. Their instances do not coincide, and neither class subsumes the other: an applicant is not necessarily a reviewer/PC member, and a PC member is not necessarily an applicant. They are therefore unrelated in the conference domain.

Both properties relate a conference participant/paper to a presentation, but the domains differ: A's domain is Active conference participant (a person), while B's domain is Abstract/Paper (a document). They connect different kinds of subjects to presentations, so they overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. `isMemberOf` links a Person to a Conference (membership relation), while `organisedBy` links an Event to an Organisation or Person (organisational responsibility). Their domains and ranges do not coincide, and they express semantically distinct relationships.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference volume' is a specific child of 'Conference', representing a particular edition or volume of a conference series (it has parts, tracks, committees, contributions, important dates). In the EDAS ontology, 'Conference' is the general concept with subtypes like Single Level Conference and Two Level Conference. The Conference ontology's 'Conference volume' corresponds to a specific conference instance/edition, which is more specific than the general 'Conference' class in EDAS. Thus, Conference_volume is subsumed_by Conference.

The two properties relate different kinds of documents to different kinds of agents. `isWrittenBy` in edas links a Paper to its Author, while `reviewWrittenBy` in ekaw links a Review to a Possible Reviewer. Since the domains (Paper vs Review) and ranges (Author vs Possible Reviewer) denote distinct entities in the conference domain, the properties do not denote the same relation.

The two properties relate completely different attributes: 'has an ISBN' captures the ISBN identifier of conference proceedings, while 'City of conference' captures the geographic location of a conference. They have different domains (Conference proceedings vs Conference) and no semantic overlap.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. 'belongs to reviewers' links Review expertise/Review preference to a Reviewer (i.e., which reviewer has that expertise or preference), while 'reviewer Of Paper' links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (i.e., which paper a reviewer reviews). The domains and ranges differ, and the intended semantics are distinct.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level human-agent class in their respective conference ontologies. They share overlapping properties (e.g., Person -> Place, Person -> Registration fee / Money) and their children (Delegate, Sponsor vs. Listener, Organizator, Speaker) are all subtypes of people involved in a conference. The intended instances coincide: any person participating in or associated with a conference.

Both classes concern presentations at a conference, but they differ in scope and structure.
