EKAW's Individual Presentation is a scientific event where a paper is presented (with subtypes like Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial), while IASTED's Presentation is a conference activity (sibling to Coffee break, Registration, etc.) with subtypes like Power Point presentation and Video presentation. They overlap in denoting presentation activities but are not equivalent due to different organizational contexts and sibling structures.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference, indicating a topic's association with a review preference. In ontology B, 'is given to' links an Item to a Person, indicating an item is given to a person. The domains (Topic vs Item), ranges (Review preference vs Person), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only trivially related by being object properties.

The cmt 'name' property names conferences and persons, while the edas 'hasCostCurrency' property specifies the currency of a sponsorship. They relate to completely different entities and serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain.

Author Not Reviewer is a conference member who authored a paper but is not assigned as a reviewer (cmt ontology, path Person > Conference Member > Author > Author Not Reviewer). Worker non speaker is a delegate attending a conference who is a worker (non-academic) and not giving a presentation (iasted ontology, path Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Non speaker > Worker non speaker). These denote completely different concepts: one is about authorship/reviewing roles in paper management, the other about delegate employment type and speaking status at a conference venue.

TPC Member in edas is a person who serves on the Technical Program Committee (reviews papers, initiates calls), a subrole of Person. IASTED member in iasted is a subrole of Delegate (a conference attendee), not a committee role. The two ontologies use 'member' differently: edas denotes a program-committee member, iasted denotes a member of the IASTED organization attending the conference. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The iasted 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item (e.g., a talk or presentation) to the Person who gives it, while sigkdd 'awarded by' relates an Award to the entity that grants it. They connect different kinds of subjects to different kinds of objects, so they do not denote the same relation.

In EDAS, 'Paper' is a broad class with subclasses like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, Published Paper, etc., covering all papers regardless of submission or acceptance status. In EKAW, 'Regular Paper' is a specific subclass of 'Paper' (distinguished from Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Industrial Paper, etc.). Thus EDAS Paper is more general than EKAW Regular Paper, making the relation 'subsumes'.

The cmt property 'hardcopyMailingManifestsPrintedBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who prints hardcopy mailing manifests. The iasted property 'write' relates a Person to an Item they have written (e.g., a paper or document). These are entirely different relations: one is about an administrative printing task for conference mailing manifests, the other is about authorship of items. They share no common domain or range types and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers, sitting under Person > Conference Member. In ekaw, Organisation is an institutional entity (universities, agencies, publishers) that organises events or publishes materials. One is a human role, the other is an organisation; they share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

Both classes denote a person who reviews papers in a conference. They share the same label and occupy a parallel position under Person in their respective hierarchies. The properties associated with each (assigning reviewers, reading papers, inviting co-reviewers) are all activities characteristic of a reviewer role in the conference domain. The difference in intermediate parent (Conference Member vs. direct child of Person) reflects modelling granularity, not a difference in intended instances.

The two properties are completely different in type, domain, range, and meaning. 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item, representing a person obtaining an item. 'Name of conference' is a datatype property from Conference to string, representing the name of a conference. They share no semantic relationship.

In iasted, 'Conference building' is a broad venue that includes subtypes like hotels, airports, and restaurants, and even has 'Delegate' as a child, suggesting a very general place concept. In sigkdd, 'Conference hall' is a specific room or auditorium where conference sessions take place, a direct child of Place. These denote different concepts: a building versus a hall/room within a building. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the differing hierarchies.

In confOf, Conference denotes the overall conference event (a Working event sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). In iasted, Plenary lecture denotes a single lecture activity within a conference (a Lecture sibling of Session and Tutorial). These are different kinds of entities: one is the whole conference event, the other is a specific talk/activity inside it. They do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Workshop in ekaw is a type of scientific event. These are completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Welcome Talk and Contributed Talk are distinct types of conference presentations. A Welcome Talk is an opening/welcome address, while a Contributed Talk is a presentation of a submitted paper. They share the parent concept of a talk/presentation but denote different kinds of events with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent academic/scientific events within a conference context. They share similar hierarchical positions (children of a general Event class), have overlapping children (Workshop, Paper Presentation/Individual Presentation), and both contrast with non-academic/social events. The terms 'Academic Event' and 'Scientific Event' are near-synonyms in the conference domain, and their intended instances (conferences, workshops, talks, sessions) substantially coincide.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a conference document (e.g., logistical information for attendees), while 'Signal Processing Topic' in edas is a subject-area topic for categorizing papers. They share no domain overlap.

These properties differ in type, domain, and range. confOf:remark is a datatype property from Contribution to string (a textual comment/note on a paper). iasted:obtain is an object property from Person to Item (a person receiving/obtaining an item). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. cmt:hasAuthor links Paper to Author (indicating authorship of a paper), while sigkdd:obtain links Author to Award (indicating an author receiving an award). They share no common domain or range types and denote completely different relations in the conference domain.

In the iasted ontology, Sponsor is a general class of person who provides sponsorship, with no tier distinction. In sigkdd, Bronze Supporter is a specific tier of supporter (a subclass of Sponzor, alongside Gold, Silver, Platinum, etc.). Thus Bronze Supporter is a strictly more specific concept than the general Sponsor, so Sponsor is subsumed by Bronze Supporter's parent category; Bronze Supporter is subsumed by Sponsor.

confOf:Scholar is a subclass of Person representing a conference attendee who is a scholar (e.g., a student), with a property 'study At' linking to University. sigkdd:Sponzor fee is a subclass of Fee representing a sponsorship fee. These are completely different domain concepts: one is a person role, the other is a monetary fee. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Participant in confOf is a general class for conference attendees (with children Member, Regular, Student), while Sponsor in iasted is a specific role: a person or organization that provides financial support. A sponsor is not a kind of participant, and a participant is not a kind of sponsor. They share only the parent Person, which is too generic to imply any alignment.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing the call for submissions, while Short paper is a type of contribution (a short research paper). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event whose children are Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop—i.e., it denotes the programmatic/academic events of a conference. iasted:Conference_days is a subclass of Time whose children are Delegate and One conference day—i.e., it denotes a temporal period (a day or set of days) during which the conference takes place. One is an event/activity type, the other is a time interval; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Both are subclasses of Person and relate to conference participation, but they denote different concepts. cmt's ConferenceMember is defined by membership (has member/member of relations from Conference), with children like Author, Reviewer, and Committee Members—people who are part of the conference organization or submission process. ekaw's ConferenceParticipant is defined by actual attendance/registration, with children like Early/Late Registered Participant, Presenter, and Session Chair. A ConferenceMember (e.g., an Author who submitted but did not attend) need not be a ConferenceParticipant, and a ConferenceParticipant (e.g., a student attendee) need not be a ConferenceMember. They overlap significantly but are not equivalent.

These properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. In cmt, 'write Review' has domain Reviewer and range Review, modeling the act of a reviewer writing a review. In the Conference ontology, 'belongs to a review reference' has domain Topic and range Review preference, relating topics to review preferences. They connect different entities and represent different relationships in the conference organization domain.

Extended abstract is a specific contribution type (short document distinct from a full Paper), while Published Paper denotes a paper by publication status. Their instances do not coincide: an extended abstract is not necessarily a published paper, and a published paper is typically a full paper rather than an extended abstract. They differ in both classification dimension and intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different entities in different directions. In cmt, 'has Been Assigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Reviewer vs Document), ranges (Paper vs Speaker), and the underlying relations (review assignment vs presentation authorship) are all distinct, so these properties are unrelated.

The cmt 'name' property denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while the confOf 'remark' property denotes a remark attached to a Contribution. They have different domains (Conference/Person vs. Contribution), different semantics (naming vs. commenting), and no overlap in the kinds of things they relate.

The two properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. `adjustBid` in cmt relates a Reviewer to a Bid (the reviewer adjusts a bid for a paper), while `invites_co-reviewers` in Conference relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (a reviewer invites co-reviewers to help review a submission). They describe completely different relations in the conference domain.

The iasted class 'Author book proceedings included' is a specialized subclass of Author (under Author > Author book proceedings included) denoting authors whose work is included in book proceedings. The sigkdd 'Author' class is the general Author concept (Person > Speaker > Author) with children like 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student'. The iasted class is thus a specific kind of author subsumed by the general sigkdd Author class, not equivalent to it.

Invited Talk Abstract is a document (an abstract text for an invited talk), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for paper submissions. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies (Document vs. Deadline) and share no instances.

The two properties relate completely different entities. 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who sponsors an event), while 'written By' links a Document to a Person (who authored the document). They have different domains, different ranges, and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

In ontology A, 'Conference' denotes the conference event/organisation itself, with a child 'Conference volume' and properties linking to conference parts, proceedings, publishers, and topics. In ontology B, 'State' denotes a geographic or administrative state (a place), with children like 'Conference state', 'Presenter state', 'Sponsor state' and properties about being occupied by, situated in, or visited by persons and other places. These are entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events (e.g., sessions or tracks running in parallel), while the edas 'is Topic Of' property relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper. They have completely different domains and ranges, and denote entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

cmt:Paper is a general class for any paper submitted to the conference system, with subclasses like Paper Full Version and Paper Abstract. ekaw:Regular_Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw:Paper, denoting only regular papers as opposed to demos, posters, industrial papers, etc. Thus cmt:Paper is more general and is subsumed_by ekaw:Regular_Paper in the sense that every Regular Paper is a Paper, but not vice versa.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person (e.g., an item required by a person), while 'designed by' links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (e.g., a deadline created by the SIGKDD organization). Their domains and ranges are disjoint concepts, so they cannot denote the same relation.

These properties are completely different. 'has_the_last_name' is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's surname. 'is_used_for' is an object property from Item to Activity/Money, describing what an item is used for. They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Conference proceedings is a published volume containing collected papers (has publisher, volume, ISBN), while Contribution is an authored submission (paper, poster, short paper) with abstract, keywords, and authors. These are disjoint concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes describe conference participants who registered early, but they come from different classification hierarchies. 'Registeered applicant' in Conference is a subclass of 'Conference applicant' and has a child 'Paid applicant', focusing on the registration/application status. 'Early Registered Participant' in ekaw is a subclass of 'Conference Participant' alongside various committee roles and presenter types. While there is clear semantic overlap (both denote early-registered attendees), the ontologies model them within different conceptual structures (applicant vs. participant), and neither subsumes the other. A reference alignment would likely mark them as related rather than equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'hasRelatedPaper' links an Author to a Paper they authored, while 'updatedVersionOf' links a Document to another Document that is a prior version. They relate different kinds of entities and express different relationships.

Textual Review Question is a type of review question (a question asked in a review, with sibling Numerical Review Question), while Abstract is a document type (sibling of Paper and Review). These are completely different concepts: one is a question used in reviewing, the other is a summary document accompanying a paper.

Conference Trip (ekaw) is a social event—an activity attendees participate in—while Fee for extra trip (iasted) is a monetary charge for such a trip. One is an event, the other is a fee; they denote completely different categories of things.

CMT's 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of Author specifically excluding reviewers, while SIGKDD's 'Author' is the general author class. 'Author Not Reviewer' is strictly more specific than SIGKDD's 'Author', so it is subsumed_by it.

In cmt, Paper is a concrete submitted document that is reviewed, accepted/rejected, assigned to reviewers, and has authors. In Conference, Regular contribution is a broader category that subsumes Extended abstract and Paper, so it is more general than a single paper artefact. The cmt Paper corresponds more closely to the Conference Paper child of Regular contribution, making cmt:Paper subsumed_by Conference:Regular_contribution.
Program committee is a group of people who review conference submissions; Building is a physical structure/place. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (the act of an author submitting a paper), while is_sent_after relates an Item to a Time (expressing a temporal ordering). They have different domains, different ranges, and express fundamentally different relations.

The two properties differ in both domain and meaning. A's 'was an organizing committee of' specifically links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume, denoting the administrative body responsible for organizing a conference. B's 'technically Organises' is a sub-property of 'organises' with domain Organisation, referring to technical organization (e.g., technical sponsorship or program committee duties) rather than the organizing committee's administrative role. The domains (Organizing committee vs. Organisation) and the intended semantics (administrative organization vs. technical organization) do not coincide, so the properties are not equivalent, nor is there a clear subsumption or overlap.

In edas, 'Break Event' is a general class covering Coffee Break, Free Time Break, and Meal Break. In iasted, 'Coffee break' is a specific leaf activity. Thus edas:BreakEvent is strictly more general than iasted:Coffee_break, so the relation is subsumes.

Conference contributor denotes a person who contributes a paper or talk to the conference (parent of Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author), whereas Listener denotes a non-contributing attendee who only listens. Their intended instances are disjoint rather than overlapping, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or related.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (who wrote the paper), while 'pay' links a Person to Money (a payment action). They share no semantic relationship in the conference domain.

The cmt 'has Been Assigned' property links a Reviewer to a Paper they have been assigned to review. The ekaw 'references' property links papers that cite/reference other papers. These are completely different relations: one connects a person (reviewer) to a document (paper) for review assignment, the other connects documents to documents for citation. They share no common domain or range types and denote unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

Both classes denote a co-author of a paper/contribution. In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of Author and is linked via 'co write Paper' to Paper. In Conference, 'Contribution co author' is a subclass of Regular author (which is a subclass of Conference contribution's author hierarchy) and is paired with 'Contribution 1th author' as a sibling. The structural positions align: both represent the co-author role within the author hierarchy of a conference paper/contribution. The label and structural correspondence strongly support equivalence.

A 'One day presenter' in iasted is a specific kind of Delegate who presents at the conference for one day, sitting among siblings like Speaker, Listener, and Session chair. B 'Organizator' in sigkdd is a Person who organizes the conference, with children such as General Chair, Program Chair, and Webmaster. A presenter is not an organizer; these denote disjoint roles in the conference domain, so they are unrelated.

Both are conference events involving presentations, but they are not equivalent. A Talk Event in EDAS is a specific academic event where talks are given (including closing/welcome talks), while a Conference Session in EKAW is a scheduled block within a conference that can contain multiple talks or presentations of various types (industrial, demo, poster, regular). A Conference Session subsumes or overlaps with Talk Event but they are not the same concept.

confOf Workshop is a specific event type (sibling of Conference, Tutorial under Working event). edas Organizational Meeting is a distinct academic event type (sibling of Workshop, Paper Presentation, Talk Event). They are different event categories in the conference domain; an organizational meeting is not the same as a workshop.

The property 'adjusted By' in cmt relates a Bid to a Reviewer (the reviewer who adjusted the bid), while 'updated Version Of' in ekaw relates a Document to another Document (indicating a document version relationship). These properties operate on entirely different domain and range types and describe unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

Both classes describe papers that have progressed beyond initial submission in the review workflow, but they capture different stages: 'Rated Papers' denotes papers that have received ratings/reviews, while 'Assigned Paper' denotes papers assigned to reviewers for evaluation. An assigned paper may not yet be rated, and a rated paper is typically already assigned. They overlap in extension but are not equivalent.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Contribution to its Author, while property B (providedBy) links a Sponsorship to its providing Organization. They relate completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain and have no overlap in intended meaning.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a type of Chairman responsible for organizing the conference), while Early Registered Participant is a person who registered early for the conference. They denote completely different concepts: one is an organizational/committee role, the other is a registration status. Their paths, siblings, and intended instances do not overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and express different relations. In cmt, 'rejectedBy' links a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it. In iasted, 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they give. The domains (Paper vs Person), ranges (Administrator vs Activity/Item), and meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

In iasted, Document is a broad superclass covering many artefacts (submissions, reviews, forms, invitation letters, etc.). In sigkdd, Abstract is a specific document type (a sibling of Paper and Review under Document). Thus iasted's Document is strictly more general than sigkdd's Abstract; the two are not equivalent.

In edas, Document is a broad top-level class covering academic artefacts (Paper, Review, Programme, Slide Set, Meal Menu). In iasted, Document is a subclass of Item and covers a much wider range of conference organisational artefacts (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, records of attendance, visas, etc.) in addition to reviews and submissions. The iasted Document is therefore more general than the edas Document, whose instances are a subset of the organisational and academic documents found in iasted.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In cmt, memberOfProgramCommittee links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee. In edas, hasMember links a Conference to a Person (member). They are not inverses of each other either, since the domains and ranges do not match: cmt's property is specifically about program committee membership, while edas's hasMember is about conference membership generally. The concepts are distinct in the conference domain.

A Conference Dinner is a social meal event during a conference, while B Conference is a scientific event representing one edition of a conference. They denote completely different concepts despite sharing the word 'Conference'.

Call for paper is a conference document (a publication/announcement soliciting papers), while Main office is a physical place. They share no instances and belong to completely different domains (document vs. place).

Both properties connect a Paper to a Reviewer (cmt Reviewer ~ ekaw Possible Reviewer) and express that a paper has been assigned to / read by a reviewer. The direction is identical (Paper -> Reviewer), and the intended relation in the conference domain is the same.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. `hasRating` links an Active Paper to its Review Rating (a score/evaluation), while `reviewOfPaper` links a Review to the Paper it reviews. They do not share the same domain or range, nor do they connect the same kinds of things, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event during a conference (e.g., a trip or excursion organized for attendees), while Departure in iasted is an activity after the conference (leaving/departing). They denote different concepts: one is a social outing, the other is the act of leaving. Their paths and siblings confirm distinct meanings.

Call for participation is a document (subclass of Conference document) that invites people to participate in a conference. Registration of participants event is an administrative event representing the act of registering participants. One is a document/artefact, the other is an event/process; they denote completely different categories of things.

In ontology A, 'Conference participant' is a broad class under Person with children Active/Passive conference participant and siblings including various roles. In ontology B, 'Tutorial Chair' is a specific role under Conference Participant. A tutorial chair is a kind of conference participant, so A subsumes B. They are not equivalent because B denotes a specific chair role, not the general participant class.

In EKAW, SC_Member is a subclass of PC_Member (Programme Committee member), distinct from the sibling class Session_Chair. In EDAS, Session_Chair is a direct subclass of Person. The EKAW class corresponding to EDAS Session_Chair is the sibling 'Session_Chair', not SC_Member. SC_Member denotes a programme-committee sub-reviewer role, not the person chairing a session, so the two classes do not share instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. In cmt, memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (i.e., a person's membership in a conference). In the Conference ontology, was_a_member_of links a Committee member to a Committee (i.e., a person's membership in a specific committee). These are distinct relationships in the domain: being a member of a conference is not the same as being a member of a committee, and the ranges (Conference vs Committee) are different concepts.

In Conference, 'Accepted contribution' is a specific stage in the workflow: a reviewed submission that has been accepted (with sibling 'Rejected contribution' and child 'Camera ready contribution'). In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a broad document type sibling to Abstract and Review, covering any paper artifact. Thus sigkdd:Paper is more general than Conference:Accepted_contribution; the latter is a specific kind of paper (one that passed review), so the relation is subsumed_by.

confOf 'Working event' groups the main organizational events of a conference (Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) and is a sibling of 'Administrative event' and 'Social event'. iasted 'Lecture' is a sub-activity of 'Conference activity' whose children are Plenary lecture, Session, and Tutorial—i.e. specific presentation/session formats within a conference. The two classes sit at different levels of granularity and cover different extensions: a Conference or Workshop is a Working event but is not a Lecture, while a Plenary lecture is a Lecture but not a Working event. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

These two classes denote completely different concepts. In ekaw, 'Conference Banquet' is a social event (a meal/gathering) under Event > Social Event. In iasted, 'Conference days' is a temporal entity under Time, representing the days on which the conference takes place. One is a social gathering, the other is a time period; their instances do not coincide.

The confOf 'abstract' property relates a Contribution to its abstract text, while the edas 'hasPostalCode' property relates Contact Information to a postal code string. They have different domains (Contribution vs Contact Information) and denote completely different attributes in the conference domain, despite both being datatype properties with range string.

Entity A is a Conference (an academic event with volumes, proceedings, publishers, topics). Entity B is a Conference Hiker, a person (subclass of Delegate) who attends a conference. These are completely different concepts: one is an event/organization, the other is a type of attendee. No subsumption relation holds between them.

The property 'assigned To' in cmt relates a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assigned to reviewer for review), while 'searched by' in sigkdd relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD (sponsor searched by ACM SIGKDD). These properties connect entirely different domain and range entities and represent different relationships in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Presenter is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant). In iasted, Presenter state is a state/status (subclass of State), not a person. These denote completely different kinds of entities.

Student registration fee denotes a discounted fee for students, while Registration Non Member denotes the full fee for non-members. These are disjoint categories of registration fees; neither subsumes the other and they do not overlap.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. In confOf, expertOn links a Member PC to a Topic they have expertise in. In sigkdd, obtain links an Author to an Award they receive. The domains (Member PC vs Author), ranges (Topic vs Award), and intended meanings (expertise assignment vs award receipt) are entirely different, so the properties are unrelated.

`enter Conference Details` in cmt is an administrative action where an Administrator inputs/edits conference details (domain: Administrator, range: Conference). `organises` in ekaw denotes an Organisation or Person organising an Event. The domains (Administrator vs Organisation/Person), ranges (Conference vs Event), and semantics (data-entry action vs organisational responsibility) are distinct, so the two properties are unrelated.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person (e.g., authors, reviewers, chairs). In sigkdd, Place is a physical location (conference hall, hotel, office). These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

edas:RejectedPaper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that was rejected), while ekaw:Paper is the general class of all papers. ekaw:Paper subsumes edas:RejectedPaper, so the relation is subsumed_by.

confOf:Contribution is a class representing submitted academic works (papers, posters, short papers) with properties like abstract, keywords, title, authors, and reviews. sigkdd:ACM_SIGKDD represents the ACM SIGKDD organization itself, which holds conferences, designs deadlines, and searches for sponsors. These are completely different concepts: one is a type of academic submission/artifact, the other is an organizing body. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Call for participation is a conference document (e.g., an announcement or informational text inviting people to participate in a conference), while Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. One is a document/artefact, the other is an activity. They share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

cmt:assignedTo assigns a Reviewer to review a Paper. ekaw:technicallyOrganisedBy (a subproperty of organisedBy) indicates the agent responsible for the technical organisation of an event or activity. These properties relate different kinds of things (paper-reviewer vs. event-organiser) and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Reviewer' and denote the same concept in the conference domain: a person who reviews papers. In ontology A, Reviewer is a subclass of Person with review-related properties (review expertise, review preference, inviting co-reviewers). In ontology B, Reviewer is a subclass of Speaker (which is a subclass of Delegate, ultimately under Person), with Author as a sibling. The iasted ontology models conference participants under a Place/Building hierarchy, but the intended instances of Reviewer coincide: people serving as reviewers. The different structural positioning reflects ontology modeling differences, not conceptual divergence.

Conference participant is a broad class covering all persons who participate in a conference (including passive participants like listeners and active participants like speakers). Speaker is a specific type of delegate who gives a presentation. Every speaker is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is a speaker (e.g., listeners, reviewers who don't present). Thus Conference participant subsumes Speaker.
University is an organization where scholars study, while Textual Review Question is a type of review question used in paper reviews. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. enterConferenceDetails links an Administrator to a Conference (entering conference details), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (who presented the document). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Conference applicant is a person who applies to attend a conference, while Conference Venue Place is a physical location where a conference takes place. One is a person, the other is a place; they share no instances and are not related in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations. 'gives_presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation they deliver, whereas 'relatesTo' links a Document to various entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person) it is related to. There is no overlap in intended meaning.

Both are subclasses of Paper representing papers not yet accepted, but they are not equivalent. 'Pending Paper' in EDAS denotes a paper awaiting a decision (a workflow state), while 'Submitted Paper' in EKAW denotes any paper that has been submitted (a submission act), which is broader and includes papers that may already be assigned or reviewed. Their sibling structures differ: EDAS uses acceptance-status siblings (Accepted, Rejected, etc.), while EKAW uses paper-type siblings (Demo, Poster, Regular, etc.). They overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so 'related' is the best fit.

Co-author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Publisher is an organization/entity that publishes conference proceedings. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Demo Chair (ekaw) is a person who chairs a demo session, while Session chair (iasted) is a person who chairs a regular session. These are distinct organizational roles in a conference: a demo chair oversees demonstrations, whereas a session chair oversees presentation sessions. They are sibling-level roles under Conference Participant / Delegate respectively, not the same concept.

Property A 'has authors' relates a Conference document to a Person (the author of the document), while property B 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (a member/participant of the conference). These are different relations with different domains (document vs. conference event) and different semantics (authorship vs. membership).

The cmt property 'virtual Meeting Enabled By' relates a Conference to an Administrator who enables a virtual meeting. The iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., a lecture or item). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics; they do not denote the same relation.

The property `is Written By` in edas relates a Paper to its Author (authorship of a written document). The property `is given by` in iasted relates an Activity or Item to a Person (presentation/delivery of an activity or item). These are distinct relations in the conference domain: authorship of a paper vs. delivery/presentation of an activity or item. They do not share the same domain or range types, and they denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

These two datatype properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. `siteURL` (domain: Conference, range: anyURI) captures the web address of a conference, while `earlyRegistration` (domain: Participant, range: boolean) indicates whether a participant registered early. They share no semantic overlap.

Property A (written By) links a Contribution to its Author, while property B (award) links something to an Award. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

confOf:Company is a type of organization (an entity like a corporation), while iasted:Main_office is a type of place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote different concepts: one is an organizational actor, the other is a physical space.

Review expertise in the Conference ontology denotes an expertise/preference record associated with a reviewer and a submitted contribution (it is the object of 'has a review expertise' and has properties linking it to reviewers and submitted contributions). Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a subclass of Person denoting a person who could review a paper. One is an expertise artefact/record, the other is a person role; they do not share instances and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, `name` is a general datatype property applying to both Conference and Person, representing the full name or general name of an entity. In confOf, `has Surname` is specifically the surname (family name) of a Person. A general name property and a surname property are not equivalent; they relate different levels of naming granularity, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way.

Co-author in cmt is a person who co-writes a paper, sitting under Person > Conference Member > Author. Memeber registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee for member registration, sitting under Money > Fee > Registration fee. These denote completely unrelated concepts (a person vs. a monetary amount).

A is a person who attends but does not actively participate in a conference; B is a social event (a banquet) held during a conference. They are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member (cmt) is a person who is a member of a conference (parent: Person; subclasses include Author, Reviewer, etc.). Hotel fee (iasted) is a monetary charge for hotel accommodation (path: Money > Fee > Hotel fee). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'was a committee chair of' links a Chair to a Committee they presided over, while 'is signed by' links an Item (e.g., a document) to a Person who signed it. They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relations in the conference domain.

The cmt property 'has Bid' relates a Paper to a Bid (an offer to review), while the iasted property 'is paid in' relates Money to a Building (where payment is made). These are completely different domain relations with no overlap in meaning.

Property A (belongs_to_a_review_reference) links a Topic to a Review preference, indicating a topic's association with a review preference. Property B (submit) links an Author to a Paper, indicating the act of an author submitting a paper. These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. In cmt, readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper they read (for reviewing). In edas, relatedToPaper relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper it is about. The domains (Reviewer vs Paper Presentation) and ranges (Paper vs Accepted Paper) are disjoint concepts, and the intended meanings (reviewer reading a paper vs presentation being associated with a paper) are distinct.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference, but cmt's 'date' is a generic conference date while edas's 'paperDueOn' is specifically the paper submission deadline. 'date' is more general than 'paperDueOn', so 'date' is subsumed_by 'paperDueOn' in the sense that paperDueOn is a more specific date property.

confOf:Organization denotes an organizational entity (e.g., Company, University) that employs people and has contact details (address, city, country). edas:Place denotes a physical location (e.g., Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) where conference events are held. These are disjoint concepts: an organization is an institutional actor, while a place is a spatial/venue entity. Their child classes and associated properties confirm no overlap in intended instances.

A Program committee is a group of people appointed to review submissions for a conference, whereas an Academic Institution is an organization such as a university or research institute. They belong to disjoint branches of the ontology (committee vs. organisation) and share no instances.

These two properties are completely different in meaning. In cmt, 'reviewsPerPaper' is a datatype property with domain Conference and range int, representing the number of reviews required per paper (a count). In ekaw, 'reviewOfPaper' is an object property with domain Review and range Paper, linking a review to the paper it reviews. They differ in domain, range type, and semantic intent: one is a cardinality/count, the other is a relational link from a review to a paper.

Property A (has_a_committee_co-chair) relates a Committee to a Co chair (a person role), while property B (heldIn) relates an Event to a Location. They connect completely different domain and range types and describe unrelated aspects of the conference domain.

Personal History in edas is a record of a person's activities (publications, reviews), while Document in sigkdd is a concrete artefact (abstract, paper, review) submitted or presented at a conference. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Paper is a class representing a conference contribution document, while Deadline Author notification is a class representing a temporal deadline by which authors are notified. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. Registration Non Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee, denoting a fee category for non-member registration. These are completely different kinds of entities (a person vs. a monetary fee), so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with range string that assign a name, but their domains differ substantially. A's 'has a name' applies broadly to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic, while B's 'Name' is restricted to Person. Thus A is strictly more general than B, so A subsumes B rather than being equivalent.

The two properties have opposite directions. In Conference, 'is given by' has domain Presentation and range Active_conference_participant (presentation -> presenter). In iasted, 'give' has domain Person and range Activity/Item (presenter -> presentation). They are inverses rather than equivalent, and an inverse relationship is not considered equivalent in the reference alignment.

Both properties represent submission deadlines for papers, but they differ in specificity and domain. Property A specifically captures the submission date for full papers (a subset of all submissions), while property B captures the general submission deadline for any call (which may include full papers, short papers, posters, etc.). They overlap in the case of full paper submissions but are not equivalent since B is more general than A.

The cmt 'title' property captures the title of a Paper, whereas the confOf 'remark' property captures a remark on a Contribution. These are semantically distinct attributes of a document; a title is the name of the paper, while a remark is a comment or note about it. They do not denote the same relation.

In the iasted ontology, Sponzorship is a subclass of Money, meaning it denotes a financial amount or monetary contribution associated with sponsorship. In the sigkdd ontology, Sponzor denotes the agent/entity that provides sponsorship (an organization or company), as evidenced by its subclasses (Bronze Supporter, Gold Supporter, etc.) and properties like 'Name of sponsor'. One is a monetary amount, the other is the sponsoring agent; these are disjoint concepts.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different attributes: `email` captures a person's electronic mail address, while `hasFirstName` captures a person's given name. They are distinct concepts and neither subsumes the other.

Rejected_contribution is a class representing a written paper/contribution that has been rejected after review. AccpetIfRoomRating is a class representing a specific review rating value (a borderline accept contingent on room availability). One is a document artefact, the other is a rating enumeration value; they denote completely different kinds of things.

In cmt, User is a broad superclass of Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—a general user of the conference management system. In iasted, Reviewer is a specific subclass of Speaker (under Delegate), denoting a person who reviews papers. These are at different levels of generality and serve different roles: cmt's User encompasses all system users (including administrators), while iasted's Reviewer is a specific conference participant role. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a straightforward way given the different modeling contexts.

In edas, Active Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that is being actively reviewed, with a Rating). In sigkdd, Paper is the general class of all papers. Thus Active Paper is subsumed by sigkdd's Paper.

In edas, Accepted Paper is a specific paper status (a paper that has been accepted for publication/presentation), sitting under Paper > Document. In iasted, Document is a broad superclass covering many kinds of conference artefacts (forms, letters, reviews, submissions, etc.). An accepted paper is not a document in the broad iasted sense; rather, it would be a specific submission artefact. The intended instances do not coincide, and neither class subsumes the other in a way that would be recorded as a reference alignment.

Both classes denote a conference event/edition in the conference-organisation domain. EDAS Conference has properties like paperDueOn, hasName, hasCountry, and hasTopic, and children such as Single/Two Level Conference, indicating a concrete conference edition. EKAW Conference is a Scientific Event with siblings like Workshop, Session, Track, and its comment explicitly says 'One edition of a conference.' The intended instances coincide.

Meta Review in cmt is a subclass of Review (a Document), representing a type of review artifact. Reviewer in edas is a subclass of Person, representing a human role. These are completely different categories of entities: one is a document/artifact, the other is a person. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf's Person is a broad top-level class covering all people in the conference domain (authors, chairs, participants, volunteers, etc.). ekaw's Student is a specific subclass of Person denoting only students. Thus Person subsumes Student; they are not equivalent.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations. In cmt, 'enterConferenceDetails' connects an Administrator to a Conference (an administrator entering conference details). In confOf, 'follows' connects an Administrative event to another Administrative event (one event following another). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so they are unrelated.

The cmt 'name' property assigns a string name to a Conference or Person, while the confOf 'early Registration' property is a boolean flag indicating whether a Participant registered early. They have different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.
paperID is a numeric identifier for a Paper, while remark is a textual comment on a Contribution. They have different domains, ranges, and intended meanings.

In EDAS, 'Textual Review Question' is a specific type of review question (a question with a free-text answer, sibling to 'Numerical Review Question'), not a review document. In EKAW, 'Review' is a Document (the review artifact itself, with children like Positive/Negative/Neutral Review and properties linking it to Paper and Possible Reviewer). A textual review question is a component/question within a review form, not the review document; the two do not share instances.

Slide Set denotes presentation slides used during a talk, while Abstract denotes a summary of a paper. Both are subclasses of Document, but they are distinct document types with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Workshop is an event (a kind of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Student_lecturer is a person role (a kind of Lecturer, under Speaker/Author/Delegate). They denote completely different entities in the conference domain: an event vs. a person.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In edas, 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (i.e., listing conference members/participants). In iasted, 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (i.e., a person preparing some item such as a document or presentation). They connect different entity types in different directions and denote different relations.

Rejected Paper in edas is a document (a paper artifact that has been rejected), while Receiving manuscript in iasted is an activity (the process of receiving manuscripts). They belong to fundamentally different categories: one is a document type, the other is an activity type. They do not denote the same concept.

Plenary lecture is a type of academic/ conference activity (a talk or presentation), while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology (Activity vs. Committee) and denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Company denotes a for-profit commercial organization, while ekaw:University denotes an academic institution. They are sibling-level distinctions under Organization/Organisation and share no instance overlap. A company is not a university and vice versa, so they are unrelated (neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relation).

The two properties relate entirely different domains to Person. In Conference, 'has_authors' links a Conference document to the Person(s) who authored it. In iasted, 'is_occupied_by' links a Building, City, or State to a Person who occupies it. They share only the range Person; the domains and intended meanings are completely different, so they are unrelated.

A's memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference they belong to (membership), while B's organises links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. These are different relations: being a member of a conference is not the same as organising an event, and the domains/ranges differ accordingly.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Document > Paper, representing a short summary or abstract of a conference paper. In edas, 'Communications Topic' is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject-area topic within the communications engineering domain (e.g., antennas, networks, cryptography). These are completely different concepts: one is a document artefact, the other is a subject classification. No subsumption or overlap relationship exists.

In cmt, 'write Paper' specifically relates an Author to a Paper (academic writing). In iasted, 'sign' relates a Person to an Item, which is broader (signing any item, not necessarily writing a paper). The cmt property is more specific than the iasted 'sign' property, so cmt's writePaper is subsumed_by iasted's sign.

Both are committee roles for persons, but a Conference Chair is the single head of the whole conference, whereas a Co chair is a secondary/supporting role on a committee (sibling of Chair). They overlap conceptually as leadership roles but are not equivalent.

Organizing committee and Program Committee are distinct committee types in conference organization. The organizing committee handles logistics (venue, registration, local arrangements), while the program committee handles paper review and selection. In ontology B (sigkdd), they are explicitly modeled as sibling classes under Committee, confirming they are different concepts. In ontology A (Conference), Organizing_committee is also a sibling of Program_committee under Committee, further confirming the distinction.

In iasted, 'Conference restaurant' is a subclass of Building under Place, denoting a physical dining venue associated with a conference. In sigkdd, 'Conference' is an event with properties like start/end dates, city, and name, and is held by an organization (ACM SIGKDD). These denote completely different categories—a physical place versus a temporal event—so they are unrelated.
logoURL points to a logo image URL for a conference, while hasName gives the full name string of a conference. They denote different attributes with different datatypes and semantics.

In ekaw, Session is a scientific event (a time-slot block of talks). In iasted, Session chair is a person (a delegate who chairs a session). They denote completely different categories of entities—an event vs. a person—so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs a conference, sitting under Person > Chairman. Presenter university (iasted) is a physical place/building where a presenter is affiliated, sitting under Place > Building. One is a human role, the other is a location; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Dining Place is a location where meals are served (a subtype of Place), while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle (a subtype of Item). They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Although both properties share a similar name ('written By' / 'is Written By'), they operate on different domains and ranges. In cmt, 'writtenBy' relates a Review to a Reviewer (who wrote the review), whereas in edas, 'isWrittenBy' relates a Paper to an Author (who wrote the paper). These are distinct relations in the conference domain: one concerns authorship of a review, the other concerns authorship of a paper. They do not share the same domain or range, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and have different domains and ranges. confOf:reviewes connects a Member PC to a Contribution (a PC member reviews a paper), while iasted:is_used_by connects an Item to a Person (an item is used by a person). The direction, domain, range, and intended meaning are all different, so they are not equivalent.

Conference contributor (A) is a subclass of Person, denoting people who contribute to a conference (e.g., authors, invited speakers, active participants). Social Event (B) is a subclass of Event, denoting social activities like banquets and trips. These are completely different categories: one is a person role, the other is an event. No overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, External Reviewer is a subclass of Person — a human agent who reviews a paper on behalf of another Reviewer. In Conference, Review is a subclass of Conference document — the written review artefact itself. One denotes a person, the other a document; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The property `contributes` in Conference relates a Person to a Conference document (the artefact they author or contribute to), whereas `employedBy` in confOf relates a Person to an Organization that employs them. The domains coincide (Person), but the ranges are entirely different (Conference document vs. Organization), and the relations themselves denote different real-world connections: authorship/contribution versus employment. There is no subsumption or overlap between these two properties.

The cmt 'hasCo-author' property links a Paper to its Co-author (Paper -> Co-author), indicating authorship of a paper. The iasted 'write' property links a Person to an Item (Person -> Item), indicating a person writes an item. These are different relations with different domains and ranges: one captures co-authorship of papers specifically, the other captures a person writing any item. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

Accommodation Place in edas is a physical location (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). Registration form in iasted is a document (subclass of Form > Document > Item). One denotes a physical venue, the other a paperwork artefact; they share no semantic overlap.

Published Paper in edas is a document artefact (subclass of Paper under Document), representing the actual published paper. Refusing manuscript in iasted is an activity (subclass of Activity before conference), representing the action of refusing a manuscript. One is a document, the other is an event/action; they denote completely different categories of entities.

Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution they author, while property B (reviewerOfPaper) relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper they review. These are distinct relations in the conference domain: authoring vs. reviewing. They connect different domain/range types and represent different roles, so they are unrelated.

confOf Tutorial is an event (subclass of Working event), while ekaw Tutorial Chair is a person role (subclass of Conference Participant). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relationships. 'hasRelatedPaper' links an Author to a Paper they authored, while 'hasUpdatedVersion' links a Document to an updated version of that Document. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and do not denote the same relation.

cmt:AuthorNotReviewer is a subclass of cmt:Author, specifically denoting authors who are not reviewers. confOf:Author is the general author class. The cmt class is strictly more specific than the confOf class, so it is subsumed_by it.

Both classes are named 'Organization' and represent organizations involved in the conference domain. confOf specializes Organization into Company and University, while edas specializes it into Academia Organization, Government Organization, Industry Organization, and NGO. The differing subclass partitions reflect different modeling granularities (e.g., University maps to Academia Organization, Company maps to Industry Organization), but the intended instances of the superclass itself coincide: both denote the general concept of an organization. The additional properties in each ontology (contact details in confOf, sponsorship roles in edas) are compatible extensions rather than indicators of different concepts. Thus, a reference alignment would treat these as equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing the solicitation of submissions, whereas a 'Poster Paper' is a specific type of paper submitted/presented as a poster. They denote completely different things in the conference domain.

Session Chair (ekaw) is a person who chairs a session, a sub-class of Conference Participant and PC Member. IASTED member (iasted) is a delegate who is a member of the IASTED organization. Although Session chair appears as a sibling of IASTED member in iasted, the two classes denote different concepts: one is a role in a session, the other is a membership status in an organization. Their intended instances do not coincide.

Conference contribution is a document type (paper, poster, presentation) submitted to a conference volume, while Award is a prize given to authors/papers. They share no instances and occupy different positions in the domain hierarchy.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume (organizational containment). Property B is a datatype property giving the end date/time of a Conference. They have different domains, different range types (object vs dateTime), and denote completely different relations.

confOf:Working_event is a subclass of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) denoting a kind of conference event, while edas:CommunicationsTopic is a subclass of Topic denoting a subject area. They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote entirely different concepts.

In Conference ontology, 'Information for participants' is a subclass of Conference document, i.e. a textual artefact providing information to attendees. In confOf, 'Tutorial' is a subclass of Working event, i.e. an academic event/session. They denote completely different categories of entities (document vs event) with no overlap in intended instances.

Contribution 1th author is a class denoting a person/role (the first author of a conference contribution), situated under Regular author. Multi author Volume is a class denoting a kind of document (a volume with multiple authors), situated under Document. One is an author role, the other is a publication artefact; they share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs a session, a subclass of Person with siblings like Attendee, Author, Reviewer. Poster Session (ekaw) is a type of event/session, a subclass of Session under Event. One denotes a person role, the other an event type; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In EKAW, 'OC Chair' is the chair of the Organizing Committee (OC), responsible for organizing the conference logistics. In IASTED, 'Session chair' is a delegate who chairs a specific conference session (e.g., a paper presentation session). These are distinct roles: an OC Chair handles organizational matters, while a Session Chair handles a single session. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties are inverses of each other: edas:isTopicOf has domain Topic and range Conference/Paper (Topic -> Conference/Paper), while ekaw:coversTopic has domain Event/Paper and range ResearchTopic (Event/Paper -> ResearchTopic). They relate the same kinds of entities but in opposite directions. Per the task instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, and since neither subsumes the other, the correct relation is unrelated.

The two properties go in opposite directions: 'is Written By' relates a Paper to its Author (Paper -> Author), while 'write' relates a Person to an Item they author (Person -> Item). They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. In OAEI alignment, a property and its inverse are not considered equivalent.

A's Reviewer is a Person who reviews papers; B's Neutral Review is a Document (a review with neutral sentiment). They are completely different entities (person vs. document artifact) with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'has Call' in edas relates an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., a call for papers), whereas 'part Of Event' in ekaw relates an Event to another Event of which it is a part. These are entirely different relations: one associates an event with a call-for-papers document/artefact, while the other expresses mereological containment between events. They do not share the same domain/range types nor the same intended meaning.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a broad superclass of authors, invited speakers, and active participants—people who contribute content to a conference. Webmaster in ontology B is a specific organizational role (a subtype of Organizator) responsible for the conference website. A webmaster is not a content contributor, and a contributor is not an organizer; the two classes denote disjoint categories of conference participants.

`assigned To` relates a Paper to a Reviewer (paper-reviewer assignment), while `has an abstract` relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract. They connect completely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote conference participants who give presentations, but they are not equivalent. ekaw:Presenter is a broad class covering any conference participant who presents (with Invited Speaker as a child), while iasted:Plenary_lecture_speaker is a specific kind of speaker (one who gives a plenary lecture), subclassed under Author. A plenary lecture speaker is a type of presenter, but not every presenter gives a plenary lecture. The two overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly given their different ontology structures, so 'related' is the most appropriate relation.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference (enabling a virtual meeting capability), while gives_presentations relates an Active conference participant to a Presentation (the act of presenting). They share no semantic overlap.

confOf:Working_event is a working/academic event (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while ekaw:Social_Event is a social event (parent of Conference_Banquet, Conference_Trip). They are disjoint sibling categories under Event, not equivalent.

A 'Conference participant' is a person who attends a conference, while a 'Social Event' is an event like a banquet or trip. These are completely different categories (person vs. event) with no meaningful overlap.

Conference Chair is a specific organizational role (the person chairing the conference), while Early Registered Participant is a person who registered early for the event. They denote different concepts: one is a leadership/committee position, the other is a registration status. Their instance sets do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The cmt property 'hasProgramCommitteeMember' links a Program Committee to its members (PC members). The confOf property 'reviewes' links a Member PC to the Contribution (paper) it reviews. These are different relations with different domains and ranges: one associates a committee with its members, the other associates a reviewer with a paper.

Both properties associate a paper/contribution with review-related information, but they differ in what they point to: A points to a Review expertise (the reviewer's expertise level assigned to a review), while B points to a Review (the review document itself). The ranges are different concepts, so the properties are not equivalent; they are related through the review process.

The cmt property 'memberOfConference' relates a Conference Member to a Conference, expressing membership of a person in a conference. The edas property 'isLocationOf' relates a Place to a Conference Event, expressing that a place hosts an event. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types (person-to-conference vs. place-to-event) and express fundamentally different relationships (membership vs. location). They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only trivially related by both being object properties in the conference domain.

A Conference announcement is a document/artefact (subclass of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), whereas a Trip is a social event (subclass of Event > Social event, sibling of Banquet and Reception). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

The two properties relate different domain entities to Paper. In cmt, 'has Been Assigned' connects a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. In sigkdd, 'submit' connects an Author to a Paper they have authored/submitted. These are distinct relations with different domains (Reviewer vs Author) and different semantics (assignment vs submission), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or otherwise overlapping.

In the edas ontology, 'Paper' is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, with children like Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper and properties like 'is Reviewed By' and 'is Written By'. In the iasted ontology, 'Viza' (a transliteration likely meaning 'Visa') is a sibling of administrative documents like 'Invitation letter', 'Payment document', and 'Record of attendance' — it denotes a travel visa document, not a research paper. Despite both being subclasses of Document, they denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a document (written scientific contribution) with authors, reviews, and acceptance decisions. In ekaw, Individual Presentation is a scientific event (a talk/presentation session) at which a paper is presented. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities: one is a document, the other is an event. The ekaw property 'paper Presented As' explicitly links papers to individual presentations, confirming they are distinct concepts rather than equivalent or even overlapping ones.

A Tutorial is an instructional/educational session at a conference, while an Organizational Meeting is a meeting for organizational/administrative purposes. These are distinct types of conference events with different purposes, instances, and roles.

The confOf 'parallel with' property relates two Administrative events (e.g., sessions or tracks running in parallel at a conference). The ekaw 'technically Organises' property relates an Organisation to something it technically organises (e.g., a conference or event). These are entirely different relations: one is a temporal/scheduling relation between events, the other is an organisational relation between an organisation and an event. They share no common semantics.

confOf's Topic is a general conference topic class (domain of dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic). edas's CADTopic is a specific subclass of Topic (a sibling of AntennasTopic, CommunicationTheoryTopic, etc.), denoting topics in the CAD (Computer-Aided Design) domain. The general Topic subsumes the specific CADTopic, but they are not equivalent.

In EDAS, 'Programme' is a document containing the conference program (schedule of events), linked to ConferenceEvent via hasProgramme/belongsToEvent. In EKAW, 'WebSite' is a web page or online resource published by an organisation and listing events. Despite both being subclasses of Document, they denote different artefacts: a programme document vs. a website. EKAW also has a separate 'ProgrammeBrochure' sibling which is closer to EDAS's Programme, further indicating that WebSite is not the same concept.

confOf:Scholar is a price-category role (a student/discounted attendee who studies at a university), not a paper author. Its siblings (Administrator, Assistant, Volunteer, Science Worker) and its property 'study At -> University' confirm it denotes a discounted participant type. edas:Author is a person who writes papers (has Related Paper -> Paper). An author need not be a scholar and a scholar need not be an author; the concepts have no necessary overlap.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad superclass encompassing authors, chairs, PC members, and reviewers—i.e., people with active organizational or authorial roles in the conference. In the Conference ontology, a Passive conference participant is specifically a non-active participant (e.g., an audience member), contrasted with Active conference participant. The cmt Conference Member includes many active roles (Author, Reviewer, Chair), so it does not align with the passive participant category. The two concepts have different intended extensions with no clear overlap.

PC Chair is the chair of the whole Programme Committee, a senior organisational role, whereas Session chair is a person chairing a single session. They are distinct roles in conference organisation, so they are not equivalent; nor is one a generalisation of the other.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'end Review' relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (the chair ending/managing a review). In Conference, 'belongs to a review reference' relates a Topic to a Review preference (a topic belonging to a review preference). They connect entirely different entity types and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

In edas, Attendee is a broad class covering any person who attends the conference (sibling to Author, Reviewer, Session Chair, etc.). In iasted, One day presenter is a specialized Delegate who presents for a single day. Every one-day presenter is an attendee, but most attendees (e.g., authors who only co-author, listeners, session chairs) are not one-day presenters. Thus Attendee subsumes One day presenter.

Property A (has_an_organizing_committee) links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee, denoting that a conference has an organizing committee. Property B (writes) links an Author to a Contribution, denoting that an author writes a paper. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics; they share no overlap in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (under Chairman/Conference Member in cmt), while One day presenter is a type of Delegate/attendee in iasted. These denote completely different concepts: one is an administrative/organizational role, the other is a presenter attending for a single day. Their instances do not coincide.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event (an activity/trip organized as part of a conference), while Taxi in iasted is a transport vehicle (a physical item used for transportation). They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies (Event vs. Item) and denote fundamentally different kinds of entities.

submitPaper relates an Author to the Paper they submit, while notification_until relates an Author to a Deadline for author notification. These are different relations connecting different kinds of objects (a submitted paper vs. a notification deadline), so they are unrelated.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a Social Event (an activity/trip that happens during a conference), while Conference hotel in iasted is a Building/Place where conference participants stay. One is an event, the other is a physical location; they denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes denote the same concept in the conference domain: a review of a submitted paper. In cmt, Review is a Document written by a Reviewer for a Paper. In Conference, Review is a Conference document related to a Reviewed contribution via 'has a review' / 'reviews'. Despite minor structural differences (e.g., cmt distinguishing Meta Review as a subclass), the intended instances coincide.

confOf:Conference is a scientific conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), denoting the conference itself as an event. edas:MeetingRoomPlace is a physical place/room where meetings occur (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference Venue Place, Accommodation Place, Dining Place). One is an event, the other is a physical location; they denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a short summary of a conference paper (a scholarly artefact), while Mailing list in iasted is an administrative document/item used for conference organisation. They share no instances and belong to completely different conceptual categories despite both being subclasses of Document.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range types and denote unrelated actions: cmt's enterReviewCriteria has domain Administrator and range Conference (an administrator entering review criteria for a conference), while iasted's need has domain Person and range Item (a person needing an item). There is no overlap in meaning, direction, or the kinds of entities they connect.

Trip in confOf is a social event (e.g., an excursion organized during a conference), whereas Car in iasted is a transport vehicle. They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different kinds of entities.

Accepted Paper denotes a paper that has passed review and been accepted, while Submitted Paper denotes a paper that has been submitted (typically pending review). These are distinct, non-overlapping statuses in the paper lifecycle; an accepted paper is no longer merely submitted, and a submitted paper has not yet been accepted. They share the parent Paper but represent different stages, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or subsuming.

Both are datatype properties with range 'date', but they have different domains and different semantics. In cmt, 'date' applies to a Conference (the conference date), while in iasted, 'done till' applies to a Deadline (the date by which a deadline must be met). These are distinct relations: one records when a conference occurs, the other records the cutoff date for a deadline. They do not relate the same kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The iasted property 'is connected with' has domain {Activity, Person} and range {Item, Place}, making it strictly broader than the sigkdd property 'can stay in', which has domain Person and range Place. The sigkdd property is a specialization of the iasted property, relating a subset of the domain (Person) to a subset of the range (Place). They are not equivalent because the iasted property also covers Activity-to-Item and Activity-to-Place connections.
