The two properties are completely different: 'has_the_first_name' is a datatype property from Person to string capturing a person's first name, while 'is_paid_with' is an object property from Money to Item describing how money is paid. They share no domain, range, or semantics.

These properties differ in both domain and range and represent different relationships. In confOf, 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (a reviewer reviewing a paper). In edas, 'has Rating' links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a paper having a rating value). They are not the same relation: one connects a person to a paper, the other connects a paper to a rating.

The confOf property writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author, while the ekaw property reviewOfPaper relates a Review to the Paper it reviews. They connect completely different domain and range types and express different relations (authorship vs. review subject), so they are unrelated.

Property A ('is the 1th part of') relates an Abstract to the Paper/Poster/Presentation it is part of, expressing a part-whole relationship. Property B ('write') relates a Person to an Item they author, expressing an authorship relationship. These are fundamentally different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In ekaw, paperPresentedAs links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (the presentation event/session). In sigkdd, presentation links a Speaker to a Document (likely the presentation slides/file). The domains (Paper vs Speaker), ranges (Individual Presentation vs Document), and overall meaning differ significantly, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumer of the other.

Both are subclasses of Paper, but they classify papers along different dimensions. 'Published Paper' denotes a paper that has been published (a status/lifecycle stage), while 'Workshop Paper' denotes a paper presented at a workshop (a venue/track type). A paper can be both published and a workshop paper, but neither concept subsumes the other: a published paper could be a conference paper (not a workshop paper), and a workshop paper could be unpublished (e.g., submitted). Thus they overlap without equivalence or subsumption.

hasFax and hasEmail are distinct datatype properties capturing different contact channels (fax number vs email address). They share the same domain (Person) and range (string), but denote different relations; neither subsumes the other.

confOf's defaultChoice is a positiveInteger property on Social event/Working event representing a default choice value, while edas's hasEndDateTime is a dateTime property on ConferenceEvent representing when an event ends. They have different domains, different ranges (positiveInteger vs dateTime), and completely different meanings.

The ekaw property 'organised By' relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. The sigkdd property 'presentation' relates a Speaker to the Document they present. These properties connect entirely different domain/range pairs and express different relationships, so they are unrelated.

The confOf 'has Topic' property relates a Working event to a Topic (the subject area of the event), whereas the iasted 'obtain' property relates a Person to an Item (something the person receives or acquires). They have completely different domains, ranges, and intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Both Decision and Review Rating represent evaluation outcomes for papers (with overlapping children like Acceptance/Accept Rating and Rejection/Reject Rating), but they are distinct concepts: Decision is the final accept/reject determination made by an organizer/decision-maker, while Review Rating is a reviewer's rating on a scale. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

Property A (has_a_name) assigns a string name to entities such as Conference, Conference part, Publisher, and Topic, while property B (Start_of_conference) assigns a dateTime representing when a conference starts. They have different domains, different ranges (string vs dateTime), and denote completely different relations.

confOf:Company is a kind of organization (e.g., a sponsoring or industry entity), whereas iasted:Car is a transport vehicle (Item > Transport vehicle > Car). They denote completely different categories in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A relates an Abstract to the Paper/Poster/Presentation it is part of, while property B relates a Contribution to its Author. They connect completely different kinds of entities and express different relationships (part-whole vs. authorship).

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (a publication/announcement), while 'One conference day' is a temporal entity (a day in a conference). They belong to completely different hierarchies (documents vs. time periods) and share no semantic overlap.

These properties denote completely different relations. In cmt, 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria (a meta-level relation about who configured the review process). In edas, 'isReviewing' links a Reviewer/Chair/TPC Member to a Paper they are reviewing (the actual review assignment relation). They have different domains (Conference vs. Reviewer roles), different ranges (Administrator vs. Paper), and different semantics (who set up review criteria vs. who is reviewing a paper).

The property hasAttendee in edas relates a Conference Event to a Person attending it, whereas holded_by in sigkdd relates a Conference to the organization ACM SIGKDD that hosts it. They connect different kinds of entities and express different relations (attendance vs. organizational ownership), so they are unrelated.

Both are object properties linking a Person to a document, but they are not equivalent. In Conference, 'contributes' specifically means a Person contributes to a Conference document (e.g., authoring). In edas, 'hasRelatedDocument' is a broader relation whose domain includes not only Person but also Academic Event, Conference, and Conference Session, and whose range is the more general Document. Thus 'contributes' is a narrower/specialized version of 'hasRelatedDocument', making it subsumed_by.

In confOf, 'Regular' (under Participant, alongside Member and Student) denotes a regular/non-student/non-member conference participant, i.e. a regular attendee. In edas, 'Attendee' (under Person) is the general conference attendee. Both denote the same set of persons who attend the conference without special roles, so they are equivalent.

Both properties denote the relation of a person writing a document. In confOf, Author writes Contribution; in iasted, Person write Item. Author is a sub-class of Person and Contribution is a sub-class of Item, so the domain and range types are compatible. The relation direction is the same (author -> paper), and the labels are morphological variants (writes/write). A reference alignment would treat these as equivalent.

The cmt 'title' is a datatype property from Paper to string, representing the title of a paper. The iasted 'obtain' is an object property from Person to Item, representing a person obtaining an item. They have different domains, different ranges, different property types, and different semantics.

Speaker lecture in iasted is a subclass of Session/Activity, denoting an event or lecture activity. Organizator in sigkdd is a subclass of Person, denoting a human role. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Activity vs Person) and share no instances.

Contribution in confOf is a submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper) authored by persons and reviewed by PC members. ConferenceSession in edas is a scheduled event/session at a conference, related to documents and academic events. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain: one is an artefact/work, the other is a temporal event slot.

A's 'Information for participants' is a conference document (sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), i.e. informational material published for attendees. B's 'Contact Information' is a data object with fields like city, email, phone, postal code, and street, used to capture contact details for persons or locations. These denote completely different things: a published document vs. structured contact data.

Power Point presentation is a subclass of Presentation (an Activity) in iasted, denoting a type of presentation artefact/event. Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person, denoting a human who gives a presentation. One is an activity/document, the other is a person; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In EDAS, Meal Event is a specific subtype of Non Academic Event, distinct from Social Event (a sibling). In EKAW, Social Event is a broad category encompassing Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. Since a meal event (e.g., Conference Dinner) is a kind of social event, EKAW's Social Event is more general, making EDAS Meal Event subsumed by EKAW Social Event.

Both classes denote the same concept of a conference event in the conference-organisation domain. In ontology A, Conference is a top-level class with children such as Conference volume and properties like hasName, indicating it represents the conference itself. In ontology B, Conference is a subclass of Working event (under Event), alongside Tutorial and Workshop, which is consistent with it being a specific kind of academic event. The labels match exactly and the contextual information (siblings, properties, children) supports that both refer to the same real-world concept of an academic conference.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations. 'event On List' (ekaw) relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (i.e., the event is listed on a brochure or website). 'give' (iasted) relates a Person to an Activity or Item (i.e., a person gives an activity or item). There is no semantic overlap between these two relations.

Paper Full Version in cmt denotes a complete/full-length paper as opposed to a Paper Abstract, i.e., a distinction by completeness of content. Demo Paper in ekaw denotes a paper accompanying a demonstration, a distinction by paper type/track. These are orthogonal classifications: a demo paper could be a full version or an abstract, and a full version could be a regular or demo paper. They share the parent Paper but denote different concepts.

`has an ISBN` assigns an International Standard Book Number to Conference proceedings (a bibliographic identifier for published proceedings), while `has Name` assigns the full name of a Conference itself. They have different domains (Conference proceedings vs. Conference) and denote different attributes (ISBN code vs. conference name), so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Active_conference_participant in Conference denotes a person who actively participates (e.g., gives presentations), while OC_Member in ekaw denotes an Organizing Committee member. These are distinct roles in conference organization; an active participant is not necessarily an OC member, and vice versa. They share only the general ancestor Person/Conference Participant.

The two properties have opposite directions and different domain/range pairs. `has_authors` relates a Conference document to the Person(s) who authored it (document -> person), while `prepare` relates a Person to an Item they prepare (person -> item). They are not inverses in a formal sense either, since the ranges/domains differ (Conference document vs. Item, Person vs. Person). They denote different relations in the conference domain.

Associated Chair in cmt is a type of Chairman involved in conference leadership, while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a logistics/organization role. These are distinct roles in conference organization with different responsibilities, not equivalent or subsuming.

Break Event in edas denotes a scheduled break during a conference (e.g., coffee break, meal break, free time), whereas Registration in iasted denotes the activity of registering for the conference. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is a class denoting a person who chairs a track/workshop (a role, subclass of Person), while entity B is a class denoting a Workshop event itself (subclass of Working event). One denotes a person/role, the other an event; they are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Submitted contribution in the Conference ontology is a written paper/manuscript submitted to a conference (a document artefact, parent Written contribution, child Reviewed contribution). ReviewQuestion in edas is a question item within a review form (with numerical/textual subtypes). These denote completely different things: a submitted paper versus a question asked during reviewing. No overlap in intended instances.

A Government Organization is a public-sector organization (e.g., a government body), while a Proceedings Publisher is an organization that publishes conference proceedings. These are disjoint intended extensions: a government organization is not by definition a proceedings publisher, and vice versa. They share only the broad parent Organization/Organisation, which is insufficient for equivalence or subsumption.

In edas, Reviewer is a person who reviews papers (subclass of Person, with review-related properties). In iasted, Author is a speaker who writes papers (subclass of Speaker under Delegate). These are distinct roles in the conference domain: a reviewer evaluates submissions while an author produces them. They are sibling concepts in iasted, not the same concept.

Both classes denote authors of conference papers, but they are not equivalent. In cmt, AuthorNotReviewer is a specific subclass of Author whose instances are explicitly excluded from being reviewers (a constraint-driven partition of authors). In ekaw, Paper_Author is a direct subclass of Person representing any author of a paper, with no such exclusion. The cmt class is thus a proper subset of ekaw's Paper_Author in terms of intended instances, but the two ontologies model authorship at different levels of granularity and with different structural roles, so a reference alignment would more likely record them as related rather than strictly subsumed.

In cmt, Conference Chair is the person who administrates the conference, a leadership role. In iasted, Worker lecturer is a sub-class of Lecturer (which descends from Author/Speaker/Delegate), i.e. a presenter who is a worker rather than a student. These denote completely different concepts: a conference administrative head vs. a type of lecturer by employment status. They share no intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has tracks' links a Conference volume to its constituent Tracks (structural part-whole relation), while 'expert On' links a Member PC to a Topic they are knowledgeable about (expertise relation). Their domains and ranges are disjoint, and they express different relations in the conference domain.

In the edas ontology, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (an event), despite having Person and TPC Member listed as parents (likely due to ontology modeling peculiarities). In the iasted ontology, 'Delegate' is a subclass of Person (a person who attends a conference). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a type of conference event, the other is a type of person/attendee. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

A TPC Member is a person who serves on the programme committee (subclass of Person), while a Registration fee is a monetary amount charged for conference attendance (subclass of Fee). They belong to entirely different domains (people vs. money) and share no semantic overlap.

The property 'isMemberOf' in edas relates a Person to a Conference (membership in a conference organization), while 'prepare' in iasted relates a Person to an Item (preparing an item such as a document or presentation). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and meanings.

cmt:Document is a written artefact (parent of Paper and Review, range of hasConflictOfInterest), while ekaw:Organisation is an institutional entity (parent of Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher). These denote completely disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Reviewed_contribution is a submitted paper that has gone through the review process (with children Accepted/Rejected), while sigkdd Paper is a general document authored by someone. They overlap in extension (a reviewed paper is a paper), but neither subsumes the other: not all papers are reviewed contributions, and not all reviewed contributions are necessarily papers in the sigkdd sense. They are related but not equivalent.

Rejection is a decision outcome for a paper submission in the conference review process, while Van is a type of transport vehicle. These classes denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties relate a document-like entity (Paper/Item) to a person who authored/signed it, but they are not equivalent: cmt's hasAuthor specifically links Paper to Author, while iasted's is_signed_by links Item to Person. The domains (Paper vs. Item) and ranges (Author vs. Person) differ in scope, and 'signed by' may include non-author signatories (e.g., reviewers, editors), making the properties related but not equivalent.

Tutorial Abstract is a document type (subclass of Abstract under Document) representing the abstract text of a tutorial. Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline (subclass of Deadline) representing the due date for submitting abstracts. These are completely different kinds of entities: one is a written artefact, the other is a temporal milestone. No subsumption relationship exists between them.

A Workshop is an academic event/session type (a gathering or meeting around a topic), whereas a Video presentation is a specific mode of presenting content. These are disjoint kinds of entities in the conference domain: a workshop is an event that may contain presentations, while a video presentation is a presentation format. They share no instance overlap.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. In cmt, enterConferenceDetails relates an Administrator to a Conference (entering conference details). In ekaw, eventOnList relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (listing an event on a brochure or website). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

edas Accommodation Place is a specific subclass of Place (a place where people stay, sibling to Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). sigkdd Place is the general location concept whose children include Conference hall, Hotel, and Main office. Accommodation Place is thus narrower than (subsumed by) the general Place class, not equivalent to it.

The two properties have incompatible domains and ranges and go in opposite directions. In cmt, 'assigned By Reviewer' has domain External Reviewer and range Reviewer, expressing that an external reviewer is assigned by (some) reviewer. In ekaw, 'has Reviewer' has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer, expressing that a paper has a reviewer. They do not share the same domain/range types, and even conceptually they are not inverses (one is about reviewer-to-reviewer assignment, the other about paper-to-reviewer assignment).

In ontology A, 'Conference contribution' is a broad class covering all types of contributions to a conference, including talks, posters, presentations, and written contributions. In ontology B, 'Conference Paper' is specifically a kind of Paper (a written document). Thus B's Conference Paper is a narrower concept, corresponding to the Written contribution subclass of A's Conference contribution, making A subsumed_by B is incorrect; rather A is more general, so B is subsumed_by A. Wait—A is broader, so A subsumes B. Correcting: relation is 'subsumes'.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a broad superclass covering all persons who contribute to a conference (authors, invited speakers, active participants). Conference Chair in ontology B is a specific role: the person chairing the conference, who initiates calls, reviews papers, etc. The former is a general contributor category; the latter is a specific leadership role. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear direction.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers, sitting under Person/Conference Member. In edas, Organization is an entity like academia, government, industry, or NGO that provides sponsorships. One denotes a human author, the other an organizational body; they share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The property hasMenu in edas relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu (catering/menu of meals), whereas presentationed_by in sigkdd relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). They connect entirely different domain and range types and express unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. In Conference, 'has_contributions' links a Conference volume to the Conference contributions (papers/articles) it contains. In sigkdd, 'presentation' links a Speaker to the Document they present. The domains (Conference volume vs. Speaker) and ranges (Conference contribution vs. Document) are disjoint concepts, and the relations capture different aspects of the conference domain (publication content vs. presentation material). They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Conference Chair in cmt is the chair of the entire conference (a leadership role), while Assistant in confOf is a general assistant role. They are distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

An Organizational Meeting is a type of event (a meeting that takes place), while a Program Committee is a group of people (a committee). They are different kinds of entities entirely—one is an event/activity, the other is a committee/body of people. Despite the superficial lexical similarity between 'Organizational' and 'Organizing Committee', these classes do not overlap in their intended instances.

A Tutorial in EKAW is an instructional session (path: Individual Presentation > Tutorial, siblings Contributed Talk, Invited Talk), while a Video presentation in IASTED is a presentation delivered via video (path: Presentation > Video presentation, sibling Power Point presentation). These denote different kinds of activities: a tutorial is a teaching session, whereas a video presentation is a delivery medium. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In edas, Place is a general class with children Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place. In sigkdd, Hotel is a specific subclass of Place (a kind of accommodation). Thus edas:Place is strictly more general than sigkdd:Hotel, so the relation is subsumes.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In confOf, 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author. In sigkdd, 'searched by' links a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. They share no common domain or range, and no meaningful overlap in the conference domain.

In ontology Conference, 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing the solicitation of papers, whereas in ekaw 'Conference Paper' is an actual paper presented at a conference. One is an announcement/call, the other is the submitted/published artefact; they denote completely different things despite the word overlap.

In Conference ontology, Poster is a specific type of contribution (a poster presentation), distinct from Regular contribution and Written contribution. In confOf, Paper is a full-length written paper, a sibling of Poster and Short paper. These are disjoint subtypes of contribution, not equivalent.

In cmt, Meta Review is a specialized subclass of Review (a higher-level review of other reviews, typically written by a meta-reviewer). In the Conference ontology, Review is the general class of review documents. Thus cmt's Meta Review is a more specific concept than Conference's Review, making it subsumed_by.

hasConflictOfInterest in cmt relates a Person to a Document for which the person has a conflict of interest (e.g., author cannot review their own paper). is_used_for in iasted relates an Item to an Activity or Money, indicating what the item is used for. These are completely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference participant is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person), while Session is an activity/event (subclass of Activity > Conference activity > Lecture). One denotes a human participant, the other a scheduled lecture session. They share no instances and are from completely different branches of their respective ontologies.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ekaw, 'topic Covered By' links a Research Topic to the Events or Papers that cover it. In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Research Topic vs Document), ranges (Event/Paper vs Speaker), and overall semantics (topic coverage vs authorship/presentation of a document) do not coincide, so they are unrelated.

Country in edas denotes a geographical entity (nation), used as the range of 'has Country' for conferences. Research Topic in ekaw denotes a subject area covered by events and papers. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Paper in the Conference ontology is a document (a written contribution), while Paper_Author in ekaw is a person who writes a paper. These are disjoint categories (document vs. person), so they are unrelated.

cmt:co-writePaper has domain Co-author (a specialization of Person) and range Paper (a specialization of Item), while iasted:write has domain Person and range Item. Thus co-writePaper is narrower: it specifically captures co-authorship of papers, whereas write covers authorship of any item by any person. The direction is the same (author -> written artifact), so co-writePaper is subsumed by write, not equivalent.

logoURL is a datatype property from Conference to anyURI, representing the conference logo's web address. heldIn is an object property from Event to Location, representing where an event takes place. They relate different domain/range types and denote completely different concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'parallel with' in confOf relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel (same domain and range: Administrative event). 'organises' in ekaw relates an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. They connect different entity types in different directions and express fundamentally different relationships with no overlap.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'has a review' links a Reviewed contribution to a Review (a paper has reviews). 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (a reviewer has a history of their reviewing activity). The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, so the properties are not equivalent, subsumed, or even meaningfully related.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Introduction in iasted is a conference activity/event (subclass of Conference activity/Activity). They denote completely different categories of entities—a person vs. an activity—with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is a conference document providing information for participants (e.g., logistics, venue details), while entity B is a specific topic within computer networks (switching) used to classify papers by subject area. They belong to completely different parts of their respective ontologies and denote entirely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Poster Paper in ekaw is a type of academic document (a poster presentation paper), while Bronze Supporter in sigkdd is a type of conference sponsor. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Reviewer is a person who evaluates submitted papers, characterized by review expertise, preferences, and co-reviewer invitation properties. Invited_Speaker is a person invited to give a talk at the conference, a subclass of Speaker. These are distinct roles in a conference: reviewing submissions vs. delivering an invited presentation. Their instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Participant is a broad class covering all conference attendees (with children Member, Regular, Student), while iasted:Lecturer is a highly specific role nested under Speaker > Author > Delegate. A Lecturer is a specific kind of participant who gives a lecture, not equivalent to the general Participant class. The iasted ontology has no general Participant class at this position, and the two concepts do not overlap sufficiently to be equivalent or subsuming in either direction.

Student lecturer in iasted is a person who is both a student and a lecturer (a speaker/author presenting at the conference), situated under Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer. Best Student Paper Supporter in sigkdd is a type of sponsor (under Sponzor) that financially supports a best student paper award. These are completely different concepts: one is an academic role/person, the other is a financial sponsor category. They share the word 'Student' but denote unrelated entities in the conference domain.

Submission in iasted is a document type (subclass of Document) representing a submitted paper/manuscript, with children like Final manuscript and Initial manuscript. Committee in sigkdd is a group of people organizing the conference, with children like Program Committee and Organizing Committee. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Topic denotes a subject area of a conference (e.g., a research topic), as shown by properties like 'deals With' (Contribution -> Topic) and 'expert On' (Member PC -> Topic). sigkdd:Document is a written artefact with subtypes Abstract, Paper, and Review, and properties like 'submit until' (Document -> Deadline). These are completely different concepts: a subject area vs. a document type. They share no instances and are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a short summary or abstract document of a paper, a sibling of 'Paper Full Version'. In edas, 'Published Paper' is a paper that has been published, a sibling of acceptance-state classes like 'Accepted Paper', 'Rejected Paper', etc. These denote completely different concepts: one is a document part/type (the abstract), the other is a publication-status category of a paper. They share only the parent 'Paper'.

Steering committee is a committee that oversees a conference volume, while Academic Institution is an organization like a university or research institute. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, 'Programme' is a conference programme/schedule document (child of Document, sibling of Meal Menu, Slide Set, etc., linked to Conference Event via hasProgramme). In sigkdd, 'Paper' is an academic paper (child of Document, sibling of Abstract, Review, target of submit from Author). These denote completely different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'topic Covered By' (ekaw) relates a Research Topic to the Events/Papers that cover it, while 'submit' (sigkdd) relates an Author to the Paper they submit. They connect different entities in different directions with no overlap in intended semantics.

In the iasted ontology, Document is a broad superclass covering many kinds of documents (forms, invitation letters, mailing lists, payment documents, reviews, submissions, transparencies, visas, etc.). In the sigkdd ontology, Paper is a specific subclass of Document, denoting a written contribution submitted by an author. Since iasted's Document subsumes sigkdd's Paper (a paper is one kind of document), the correct relation is subsumes, not equivalent.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document they have a conflict with, while has_authors relates a Conference document to its Person authors. They connect different entity types in opposite directions and represent semantically distinct relationships.

confOf's 'Short paper' is a contribution type (a paper format/length category, sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution). ekaw's 'Assigned Paper' is a submitted paper that has been assigned to reviewers (a workflow state, parent of Evaluated Paper). They denote different concepts: one classifies the nature of the contribution, the other tracks review-assignment status. Their instances do not coincide.

Conference part (Track, Tutorial, Workshop) is a structural subdivision of a conference, while Person is a human actor (Author, Reviewer, Attendee, etc.). They denote completely disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Short_paper in confOf is a type of conference contribution (a short paper submission), while CryptographyTopic in edas is a subject-area topic under Topic. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain: one is a document type, the other is a research topic. No alignment relation holds.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'acceptPaper' relates an Administrator to a Paper, representing the acceptance decision. In edas, 'relatedToEvent' relates an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation, representing an association between a paper and its presentation event. They do not share the same domain, range, or semantic intent.

Early Registered Participant denotes a conference attendee who registered early, while Program Committee member denotes a person serving on the program committee. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote a conference event in the academic domain. They share the same label and both have a name property. The differences in their additional properties (e.g., dates, city, conference volume) reflect modeling granularity differences rather than different intended extensions.

Regular contribution in the Conference ontology is a broad category covering any non-invited written contribution, including both submitted and accepted papers (its children are Extended abstract and Paper). Submitted Paper in EKAW specifically denotes a paper that has been submitted for review. A submitted paper is a kind of regular contribution, but not every regular contribution is necessarily in the submitted state (e.g., an accepted/extended abstract). Thus Regular contribution is more general, subsuming Submitted Paper.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote completely different attributes: hasFax captures a person's fax number, while hasLastName captures a person's surname. They are distinct relations over the same domain and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Both are social activities within a conference, but Trip in confOf is a specific kind of social event (an excursion or outing), while Social_program in iasted is a broader category of conference activity that includes Dinner banquet as a child. They overlap in domain (social events at conferences) but are not equivalent: Social_program is more general, potentially subsuming Trip, but the hierarchies don't align cleanly enough to assert subsumption with confidence.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range string, representing the name of a conference. The edas property is explicitly commented as 'Conference Full Name', and the sigkdd property is labeled 'Name of conference'. They relate the same concept (Conference) to the same datatype (string) in the same direction, denoting the same relation.

TPC Member is a program committee member who reviews papers and initiates calls, while Speaker is a person who gives presentations. These are distinct roles in a conference; a TPC member need not be a speaker and vice versa. They share only the parent Person.

The cmt property acceptedBy relates a Paper to an Administrator who accepted it, denoting the decision-making role in the acceptance process. The ekaw property scientificallyOrganisedBy relates an unspecified entity to an Academic Institution responsible for scientific organisation of an event. These properties concern different relationships (paper acceptance vs. scientific organisation of an event), different domains (Paper vs. event-like entity), and different ranges (Administrator vs. Academic Institution). They do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a full-length submission document in the cmt ontology, while Registration SIGMOD Member is a registration fee category for SIGMOD members in the sigkdd ontology. These denote completely different concepts (a document vs. a fee type) with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Paper is a broad class covering all papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version), and it is the domain of many properties like hasDecision, assignedTo, hasBid, etc. In ekaw, Evaluated_Paper is a specific subclass in the hierarchy Document > Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper > Evaluated Paper, representing papers that have already been evaluated (with children Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper). The cmt Paper class is more general than ekaw Evaluated_Paper, as it includes papers that may not yet be submitted, assigned, or evaluated. Thus cmt:Paper is subsumed_by ekaw:Evaluated_Paper in terms of specificity, but they are not equivalent since their intended instances do not coincide.

Workshop in Conference is a standalone conference part (sibling of Track and Tutorial, with Conference volume having workshops), denoting a self-contained scientific event. Industrial Session in ekaw is a specific type of Conference Session within an event, focused on industrial rather than academic content. A workshop is not a session type, and an industrial session is not a workshop; their instances do not coincide.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Gold Supporter is a type of sponsor. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Workshop is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial), i.e., a type of meeting/session. ekaw:Workshop Chair is a person (subclass of Person > Conference Participant > PC Member), i.e., the chair of a workshop. These are completely different kinds of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Associated Chair is a specialized chairman role (a conference leadership position, sibling of Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair). In confOf, Assistant is a helper/staff role (sibling of Volunteer, Administrator). Despite superficial label similarity, these denote different concepts: a co-chair vs. a support assistant. They share only the common parent Person, which is too general to establish any meaningful alignment.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and denote different relations. `locationOf` in ekaw relates a Location to an Event (i.e., a location hosts an event). `can_stay_in` in sigkdd relates a Person to a Place (i.e., a person can stay at a place). They share no common semantics.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'expertOn' in confOf relates a PC Member to a Topic they have expertise in, while 'publisherOf' in ekaw relates an Organisation to published materials (Flyer, Multi author Volume, Programme Brochure, Web Site). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

confOf Participant is a specific role (Person who participates/registers for a conference), situated as a child of Person alongside Author, Chair PC, etc. edas Person is the general class of all people, with children Attendee, Author, Reviewer, etc. Thus confOf Participant is a narrower concept subsumed by edas Person.

confOf:Contribution is a broad class covering all submission types (Paper, Poster, Short paper) at any stage, while edas:RatedPapers is a narrow subclass in the hierarchy Document > Paper > Active Paper > Rated Papers, denoting specifically papers that have already received reviews/ratings. Every Rated Paper is a Contribution, but not every Contribution is a Rated Paper, so Contribution is subsumed_by RatedPapers.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference' denotes the conference itself (with a name, proceedings, publisher, topics), whereas in confOf 'Event' is a broad superclass of Administrative event, Social event, and Working event. A Conference is a specific kind of Event, not equivalent to the general Event category.

Conference www in ontology Conference is a web page (a Conference document with a URL), while Conference Paper in ekaw is a written academic paper. One is a web resource, the other is a scholarly document; they do not coincide.

These properties relate entirely different concepts. Property A links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (indicating chairing of a track/workshop), while property B links a Call to organizers who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are completely different.

In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (Person > Author > Presenter), meaning a Presenter is a specific kind of Author who presents. In sigkdd, Author is a broader class (Person > Speaker > Author) with children like 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student'. The sigkdd Author class appears more general, encompassing all paper authors, while edas Presenter is specifically an author who presents. Thus Presenter is subsumed by Author.

Associated Chair is an administrative/leadership role in conference organization (a type of Chairman), while Plenary lecture speaker is a type of author who presents a plenary lecture. These are completely different concepts: one is a conference governance role, the other is a presentation role. They share no meaningful semantic overlap in the conference domain.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. cmt:detailsEnteredBy links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered conference details), while ekaw:listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. The domains (Conference vs. Programme Brochure/Web Site), ranges (Administrator vs. Event), and intended meanings are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

Property A ('has a date of issue') applies to a Conference document and records the date the document was issued. Property B ('End of conference') applies to a Conference itself and records when the conference ends. They have different domains (document vs. conference event) and different meanings (publication/issue date vs. conference end date), so they are not equivalent, subsumed, or otherwise related.

markConflictOfInterest in CMT marks a conflict of interest between a person (Author/Chairman/Reviewer) and a Paper, preventing the reviewer from bidding on or reviewing that paper. submit in SIGKDD is the act of an Author submitting a Paper. These are entirely different relations: one declares a conflict, the other performs a submission. They share no semantic overlap despite both linking an Author to a Paper.

Both classes are subclasses of Person and represent conference participants who attend to listen rather than to present or organize. 'Attendee' and 'Listener' are near-synonyms in the conference domain, and their sibling structure (Author, Reviewer, Chair vs. Organizator, Speaker) confirms they denote the same role: a non-presenting, non-organizing participant.

Property A (has_an_abstract) relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract (a document part). Property B (write) relates a Person to an Item they author. These are different relations with different domains and ranges: one connects a written work to its abstract component, the other connects a person to something they write. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

An Invited speaker is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, while a Presenter is any person who presents (a paper, a poster, etc.). The two classes overlap—an invited speaker is typically a presenter—but they are not equivalent: a regular author presenting their own paper is a Presenter but not an Invited speaker, and an invited speaker may not be an Author (the parent of Presenter in edas).

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In cmt, writtenBy links a Review to the Reviewer who wrote it. In the Conference ontology, belongs_to_a_review_reference links a Topic to a Review preference. The domains (Review vs Topic), ranges (Reviewer vs Review preference), and overall semantics are entirely different, so the properties are unrelated.

The two properties operate in opposite directions and relate different domain/range pairs. `has parts` goes from a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (a mereological, container-to-contained relation), whereas `belongsToEvent` goes from a Programme to a Conference Event (a membership/belonging relation). They are not inverses of each other because the participating entities differ (Conference volume vs Programme, Conference part vs Conference Event), so there is no equivalence, subsumption, or clear overlap.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things. In edas, 'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to reviewers/chairs (the reviewing relationship). In iasted, 'is occupied by' links a Building, City, or State to a Person (occupancy of a place). They share no domain or range overlap and denote unrelated relations.

The cmt 'rejected By' property relates a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while the iasted 'write' property relates a Person to an Item they authored. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A's property links a Committee to its Chair (a specific role within a committee), while B's property links an Event to its organising entity (Organisation or Person). They relate different kinds of subjects and objects and express different relationships.

Chair PC in confOf is a Person who chairs the program committee, while Reviewer in iasted is a subrole of Speaker (a Delegate) who writes reviews. A PC chair is an administrative/leadership role, not a reviewer role; their instance sets do not coincide and neither subsumes the other.

markConflictOfInterest relates an Author/Chairman/Reviewer to a Paper to declare a conflict of interest, preventing assignment. isReviewedBy relates a Paper to a reviewer who reviewed it. They have opposite domain/range directions and denote completely different relations (conflict declaration vs. review assignment).

In confOf, Conference is the top-level event that hosts the whole conference (a sibling of Workshop and Tutorial under Working event). In ekaw, Conference is also a top-level event, but the candidate B here is Session, which is a sub-event within a conference (e.g. a conference session, demo session, poster session). A Conference is not a Session; they are at different levels of the event hierarchy and their intended instances do not coincide.

Country denotes a nation (domain of hasCountry, range Conference -> Country), while Location denotes a place where an event is held (range of heldIn: Event -> Location). A country is not the same as a location; a location could be a venue, city, or building, and a country is a geopolitical entity. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for people involved in a conference. Their children (Committee member, Reviewer, Conference participant vs. Listener, Organizator, Speaker) are all subtypes of conference participants, and their properties (email, name) overlap. They denote the same concept: a person in the conference domain.

Both properties concern the relationship between a reviewer and a paper, but they are inverses of each other. `isReviewing` goes from reviewer roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to Paper, while `hasReviewer` goes from Paper to Possible Reviewer. A property and its inverse are not equivalent; they are related.

External Reviewer in cmt is a person who reviews papers on behalf of another reviewer; Paper in sigkdd is a document submitted to a conference. They are completely different kinds of entities (person vs. document) with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'belongs to reviewers' in Conference links Review expertise/Review preference to a Reviewer, indicating which reviewer is associated with a review expertise or preference. The property 'writes' in confOf links an Author to a Contribution, indicating authorship of a paper. These properties relate entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships in the conference domain.

Entity A is a class denoting a person role (Track workshop chair), a subclass of Person, with properties linking it to Conference part. Entity B is a class denoting a document (Brief introduction for Session chair), a subclass of Document, with siblings like Form, Review, Submission. One is a person, the other is a document; they share no common instances and are unrelated.

Workshop in Conference is a conference part denoting a workshop event itself, while Demo Session in ekaw is a session where demonstrations are presented. They are different kinds of entities: a workshop vs. a demo session. They share no subsumption relationship and their instances do not coincide.

confOf:Trip is a general social event covering excursions or outings, while iasted:Dinner_banquet is a specific kind of social program activity (a banquet/dinner). A dinner banquet is a specific type of social event but not equivalent to the broader concept of a Trip. Thus Trip subsumes Dinner_banquet, meaning Dinner_banquet is subsumed_by Trip.

A Registeered applicant is a person who has applied/registered for a conference (with a subclass Paid applicant), whereas a TPC Member is a person serving on the programme committee who reviews papers and initiates calls. These denote completely different roles in the conference domain, with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A relates a Program Committee to its members (general PC members), while property B relates a Committee to its chair (a specific leadership role). They connect different kinds of entities and express different relationships; one is not a generalization of the other.

Property A (accept Paper) relates an Administrator to a Paper that is accepted for publication. Property B (write) relates a Person to an Item they author. These are completely different relations in the conference domain: one denotes acceptance of a submission, the other denotes authorship. They share no semantic overlap.

A Closing Talk is the final/concluding talk of a conference, while an Introduction of speaker is the act of introducing a speaker before their talk. These are distinct conference activities with different purposes and temporal positions in the program.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and have opposite directions. confOf:studyAt links a Scholar to a University (a person studies at an institution). iasted:is_visited_by links a Building, City, or State to a Person (a place is visited by a person). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics do not coincide, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Both classes denote the same concept: a reception as a specific type of social event within a conference. They share identical labels, identical positions in their respective hierarchies (both are children of a Social event/Social Event class), and both ontologies model conference organization where a Reception is a social gathering event. The sibling classes (Banquet, Trip in confOf; Excursion in edas) are all social event types, confirming the same domain context. No evidence suggests different intended meanings.

cmt:Paper is a conference paper (a written contribution submitted for review), with properties like hasAuthor, hasDecision, assignedTo reviewers, etc. edas:MealMenu is a menu for a meal event, with properties hasMenu/isMenuOf relating it to MealEvent. Despite both being subclasses of Document, they denote completely different things: a scholarly paper vs. a meal menu. No overlap in intended instances.

These properties have opposite directions and different semantics. In cmt, 'readPaper' relates a Reviewer to a Paper they read (Reviewer -> Paper). In Conference, 'belongs_to_reviewers' relates a Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer (Review_expertise/preference -> Reviewer). They connect different entity types in different directions and represent different relationships: one denotes the act of reading a paper, the other denotes assignment/ownership of expertise or preference to a reviewer.

In edas, Paper is a document authored and submitted to a conference, with subclasses like Accepted/Rejected/Published Paper. In iasted, Publication is a physical item (sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Card, Transport vehicle) with subclasses Book proceeding and Cd proceeding. These denote different concepts: an academic paper vs. a physical publication medium. Their extensions do not overlap.

confOf:Conference is an event (a conference gathering), sitting under Working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop. iasted:Hotel_presenter is a person role—a Delegate who presents at a hotel—sitting under Delegate alongside Speaker, Listener, etc. One is an event, the other is a person; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Call for participation is a Conference document (a text artefact issued to invite participants), while Organizational Meeting is an Academic Event (a scheduled gathering). One is a document, the other is an event; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

These properties denote different relations. cmt:endReview relates a PC Chair to a Review (the act/artefact of reviewing) and represents the chair ending or finalising the review process. edas:isReviewing relates a reviewer (or chair/TPC member) to a Paper and represents the reviewer actively reviewing that paper. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings differ: one is an administrative action on a Review, the other is a reviewing-role assignment to a Paper. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. 'has_the_first_name' applies to Person and captures a person's first name, while 'hasName' applies to Conference and captures the full name of a conference. They relate to different entity types and do not denote the same relation.

Decision (cmt) represents the outcome of reviewing a paper (acceptance/rejection), while Organisation (ekaw) represents entities like academic institutions, organising agencies, and publishers. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The cmt 'date' property represents the date of the Conference itself (the event date), while the edas 'registrationDueOn' property represents the registration deadline date and time. These are distinct concepts: one denotes when the conference takes place, the other denotes a deadline for registering to attend. They relate different kinds of temporal information about the conference and are not equivalent.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Computer Networks Topic' in EDAS is a subject-area topic for conference papers (subclass of Topic, with children like security, switching, sensor network topics). 'Card' in IASTED is a physical item (subclass of Item, sibling of Audiovisual equipment, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle, with child Credit card). No semantic overlap exists between a research topic and a physical card.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and oddly also listed under Person/TPC Member), representing a type of conference event. In IASTED, 'Non speaker' is a subclass of Delegate, representing a conference attendee who does not give a presentation. One is a conference type, the other is a person/attendee role; their instances do not coincide.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of Paper, representing the complete version of a submitted paper, distinct from the Paper Abstract. In sigkdd, 'Abstract' is a direct subclass of Document, representing a standalone document type alongside Paper and Review. These are different concepts: one is the full version of a paper, the other is an abstract document. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf Scholar is a price-category class (discounted registration) for any academic attending the conference, as shown by its comment 'price category - scholar' and siblings like Participant, Volunteer, Science Worker. ekaw Paper_Author is the role of a person who authored a paper. A scholar (student/academic) need not have authored a paper, and a paper author need not be a scholar (e.g., a senior researcher paying full registration). Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Paper Full Version is a full conference paper (a specific contribution type), while Flyer is a promotional document. They are both documents but denote completely different artefacts with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Two Level Conference' in edas is a type of conference (an event), while 'General Chair' in sigkdd is a person who organizes the conference. These are completely different categories of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

In ontology A, 'Invited talk' is a subclass of Conference contribution and Presentation, meaning it denotes an event/activity (the talk itself). In ontology B, 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Person > Speaker, meaning it denotes a person who gives an invited talk. These are fundamentally different types of entities (event vs. person), so they are unrelated.

An Organizing committee is a collective body (a Committee) responsible for organizing a conference volume, whereas a Sponsor is an individual Person who provides financial support. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology hierarchy (Committee vs. Person) and have no overlap in intended instances.

Conference days (iasted) represents the days on which a conference takes place, with children like Delegate and One conference day. Deadline Paper Submission (sigkdd) is a specific deadline for submitting papers. These are entirely different concepts: one denotes temporal intervals of the conference event, the other denotes a submission cutoff date. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

The two properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges. In cmt, 'assigned By Reviewer' links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer an external reviewer was assigned by). In Conference, 'has been assigned a review reference' links a Submitted contribution (or Topic) to a Review preference. These are fundamentally different relations with no overlap in the kinds of entities they connect.

Rejected contribution is a reviewed paper that was rejected, while Abstract is a document type (sibling of Paper and Review). These are different concepts: one is a submission status, the other is a document kind. They share no instances.

hasPhone captures a person's telephone number while E-mail captures a person's email address; both are datatype properties on Person with range string, but they denote distinct contact attributes, not the same relation.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. In cmt, 'written By' links a Review to the Reviewer who authored it. In Conference, 'belongs to reviewers' links a Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer, indicating which reviewer an expertise/preference belongs to. They relate different kinds of things and do not denote the same relation.

confOf:Banquet is a specific kind of social event (a banquet), whereas edas:MealEvent is a broader category covering any meal-related event, with Conference Dinner as a child. A banquet is a meal event, but not every meal event is a banquet, so Banquet is subsumed by MealEvent.

In ekaw, 'Paper Author' is any person who authored a paper, a broad role under Person. In iasted, 'Author' is a narrow subclass of Speaker (under Delegate) restricted to conference participants who present authored work (e.g., Lecturer, Tutorial speaker). Thus ekaw's Paper Author is more general, subsuming iasted's Author.

hasStreet is a datatype property from Contact Information to a string (street address line), while locationOf is an object property from Location to Event (indicating which event a location belongs to). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

Chair is a specific role within a conference committee (a person who chairs a committee), whereas Possible_Reviewer is any person who could review a paper. A chair might be a possible reviewer, and a possible reviewer might be a chair, but the intended instances do not coincide: many possible reviewers are not chairs, and many chairs are not acting as possible reviewers. The concepts denote different roles in the conference domain.

In cmt, Associated Chair is a specialized conference leadership role (a Chairman who assists the Conference Chair). In confOf, Administrator is a separate administrative role under Person, distinct from the conference leadership roles (Chair PC, Member PC). These denote different responsibilities in conference organization.

A Conference in confOf is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), while a Hotel registration form in iasted is a document (subclass of Form, sibling of Author information form and Registration form). These denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain: an event versus a document. There is no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. A's 'is the 1th part of' has domain Abstract and range Paper/Poster/Presentation, expressing that an Abstract is part of a Paper/Poster/Presentation. B's 'presentation Of Paper' has domain Individual Presentation and range Abstract/Paper, expressing that a presentation is of/about a paper or abstract. The domains and ranges are disjoint (Abstract vs Individual Presentation), and the relations are conceptually different (part-of vs presentation-of).

These properties are fundamentally different. 'has an email' is a datatype property relating a Person to a string (their email address), while 'send' is an object property relating a Person to an Item (something they send). They have different ranges (string vs Item) and different semantics (possessing an email vs sending an item).

A Conference Paper in EKAW is a scholarly written contribution submitted to a conference, whereas a Record of attendance in IASTED is an administrative document certifying that someone attended an event. They are completely different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (has_a_URL) associates a Conference with a URL string, while property B (hasTitle) associates a Contribution with its title string. They relate different subject types (Conference vs. Contribution) and express different attributes (URL vs. title), so they are unrelated.

Property A captures a person's first name, while property B captures a street address. They denote completely different attributes despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

Registeered_applicant in the Conference ontology is a subclass of Person > Conference applicant, denoting a person who has registered for a conference. Fee in the sigkdd ontology is a class whose children are Registration fee and Sponzor fee, denoting a monetary charge. One is a person role, the other is a financial concept; they share no instances and are unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a broad class covering all paper types (it has children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and is the domain of properties like hasBid, hasDecision, assignedTo that apply to papers in general). In ekaw, Submitted_Paper is a specific subclass of Paper, distinguished from Camera_Ready_Paper and other paper types. The cmt Paper class is more general, encompassing any paper, while ekaw Submitted_Paper refers specifically to papers that have been submitted (but not yet accepted/camera-ready). Thus cmt:Paper subsumes ekaw:Submitted_Paper.

In the Conference ontology, 'Paper' is a broad class covering regular conference contributions (with sibling 'Extended abstract'), making it a general paper concept. In ekaw, 'Conference Paper' is a specific subclass under 'Paper' alongside more specialized types like 'Regular Paper', 'Demo Paper', 'Poster Paper', etc. Thus ekaw's 'Conference Paper' is more specific than Conference's 'Paper', which denotes the general notion of a paper contribution.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing a person's last name/surname. 'has the last name' and 'has Surname' are synonymous in the conference domain, and both connect Person to a string value in the same direction.

confOf:Workshop is a type of event (a working event where conference activities occur), whereas ekaw:Late-Registered_Participant is a person who registered late for the conference. These are disjoint categories—an event vs. a person—with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Review is a document written by a reviewer about a paper. In edas, Call For Papers is a type of Call (announcement) soliciting paper submissions. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Author, making Author the more general concept. edas Author corresponds to the broader iasted Author class, not to the more specific Lecturer subclass. Therefore edas Author is subsumed by iasted Lecturer's parent, and the two entities are not equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities and express different meanings. confOf's 'parallel with' is a symmetric scheduling relation between Administrative events (e.g., two sessions running at the same time). ekaw's 'topic Covered By' links a Research Topic to the Events or Papers that cover it. They share no domain, range, or semantic overlap.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'assigned To' relates a Paper to a Reviewer (the system or chair assigns a reviewer to a paper). In iasted, 'write' relates a Person to an Item (a person writes/authorship of an item). One is about reviewer assignment, the other about authorship. They are not equivalent, nor in a subsumption relation.

A is 'Memeber registration fee' (a specific registration fee for members), while B is 'Registration fee' (the general class with children for member, non-member, and student fees). A is strictly more specific than B, so A is subsumed_by B.

Meeting Room Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where meetings are held, while Hotel fee is a monetary amount (subclass of Fee > Money) charged for hotel accommodation. They belong to completely different domains (spatial location vs. financial cost) and share no semantic overlap.

Rejected_Paper is a paper that has been evaluated and turned down, so it is not published or included in the proceedings. Final_manuscript is the final version of a submission that is accepted and sent for publication. These are disjoint outcomes of the review process, not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In edas, Sponsorship is a financial support concept (e.g., Travel Grant) with properties like cost amount, currency, and provider organization. In iasted, Sponsor state is a subclass of State (alongside Conference state, Presenter state), representing a phase or status in a sponsorship lifecycle, not the sponsorship itself. These are fundamentally different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Publisher (Conference ontology) denotes an organization that publishes conference proceedings, while Country (edas ontology) denotes a geographical entity. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'finalizePaperAssignment' relates an Administrator to a Conference, indicating the admin finalizes paper assignments for the conference. 'presentationOfPaper' relates an Individual Presentation to an Abstract/Paper, indicating which paper is being presented. They connect different entity types in different directions and serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain.

The property 'is given by' specifically relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it. The property 'hasAttendee' relates a Conference Event to any Person attending it. Since a Presentation is a kind of Conference Event and an Active conference participant is a kind of Person, 'is given by' is a more specific relation than 'hasAttendee' (every presenter is an attendee, but not every attendee is a presenter). Therefore 'is given by' is subsumed by 'hasAttendee'.

A Session chair is a Delegate who presides over a single conference session, while a Program Chair is an Organizator responsible for the overall academic program of the conference. These are distinct roles with different scopes and responsibilities; neither subsumes the other.

Organizing committee in Conference is a specific committee (sibling of Program committee, Steering committee) composed of people who organize a conference volume. Organisation in ekaw is a broad class including academic institutions, organising agencies, and publishers. An organizing committee is not an organisation in the same sense; they are different kinds of entities with no clear overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. In edas, 'for Event' links a Call to an Academic Event (a call-for-papers is issued for a particular conference event). In iasted, 'need' links a Person to an Item (a person needs some item). The domains (Call vs. Person), ranges (Academic Event vs. Item), and the intended meanings are completely different, so they are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and not meaningfully related.

In EKAW, Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents (a role based on activity at the conference). In IASTED, IASTED non member is a Delegate who is not an IASTED member (a membership status classification). These are orthogonal dimensions: a presenter could be a member or non-member, and a non-member could be a speaker or non-speaker. The classes do not share instances by definition.

Property A (has_authors) links a Conference document to a Person (authorship), while property B (hasCountry) links an Organization or Person to a Country (geographic location). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express completely different relationships.

Rejected contribution is a written contribution that was reviewed and rejected, while Textual Review Question is a type of review question (e.g., a free-text question in a review form). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, NGO is a subclass of Organization, denoting a non-governmental organization (e.g., an institution that might sponsor or participate in a conference). In iasted, Modelling is a subclass of Research (under Activity before conference), denoting a research activity. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In ontology A, 'issues' connects a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher issuing proceedings). In ontology B, 'lists Event' connects a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (a document/web resource listing events). The domains (Publisher vs. Programme Brochure/Web Site) and ranges (Conference proceedings vs. Event) do not overlap, and the relations describe different actions in the conference domain.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities in different directions. 'has Member' links a Conference to a Person (conference membership), while 'sign' links a Person to an Item (a person signing an item). Their domains and ranges are disjoint in role, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of things. cmt:hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Member (a person who is a member of the conference), while edas:hasRelatedDocument links various entities (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person) to a Document. The domains overlap only on Conference, but the ranges are disjoint (Conference Member vs. Document), and the intended semantics are completely different: one denotes membership of a person in a conference, the other denotes association of a document with an entity.

The two properties relate completely different things: 'has tracks' links a conference volume to its tracks (sessions/topics), while 'has Country' links a conference to a country (geographic location). They share no semantic overlap despite both being object properties with domain Conference/Conference volume.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision (alongside Rejection), representing the outcome of accepting a paper. Van in iasted is a subclass of Transport vehicle, representing a physical vehicle used for transportation. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

edas PaperPresentation is a specific academic event where an accepted paper is presented (linked to AcceptedPaper via properties). iasted Presentation is a broader conference activity covering any presentation format (PowerPoint, video, etc.). PaperPresentation is a kind of Presentation, but Presentation includes non-paper presentations, so PaperPresentation is subsumed by Presentation.

In ekaw, Student is a person who is a student (a sub-class of Person, sibling to Paper Author, Participant, etc.). In sigkdd, Best_Student_Paper_Supporter is a type of Sponsor (sibling to Bronze/Gold/Platinum/Silver Supporter and Exhibitor), i.e., an entity that financially supports a best student paper award. These denote completely different kinds of things: a student person vs. a sponsor organization/role. They share the word 'Student' only because the sponsor supports a student paper award, not because the sponsor itself is a student.

Conference part in ontology A denotes a structural component of a conference (e.g., Track, Tutorial, Workshop), while Speaker in ontology B denotes a person who gives a presentation. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is a Conference Proceedings, a document/publication volume produced by a conference, sitting under Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings. Entity B is a Conference building, a physical place/venue where a conference is held, sitting under Place > Building. One is an information artefact, the other is a physical structure; their intended instances do not coincide at all.

Accepted Paper (edas) classifies papers by acceptance status (sibling to Rejected Paper, Pending Paper, etc.), while Regular Paper (ekaw) classifies papers by type/length/category (sibling to Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Industrial Paper, etc.). These are orthogonal classification dimensions: a regular paper can be accepted or rejected, and an accepted paper can be regular or a demo/poster paper. Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

confOf:Author is a person who writes a contribution (a subclass of Person). sigkdd:Deadline_Author_notification is a temporal deadline by which authors are notified. One is a human role, the other is a date/deadline; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In cmt, Author is a broad class covering all authors of a paper (the domain of 'submit Paper' and 'write Paper' is Author -> Paper). In the Conference ontology, Contribution_co-author is a specific subclass of Regular_author that denotes only co-authors (as opposed to the 1st author). Thus cmt:Author is more general and subsumes Conference:Contribution_co-author.

In ekaw, 'Paper Author' is a subclass of Person, denoting a human who authors a paper. In sigkdd, 'Best Student Paper Award' is a subclass of Award, denoting a prize given for a paper. These are completely different domain concepts (a person vs. an award) with no overlap in intended instances.

Early paid applicant is a person who registered early and paid for a conference; Renting is an activity (e.g., renting equipment/venue) performed before the conference. One is a person, the other is an action — no overlap in intended instances.

These properties relate completely different concepts. hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic/field), while has_an_abstract links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (summary text). The domains partially overlap (Paper) but the ranges are entirely different concepts (Subject Area vs Abstract), so these are unrelated relations.

In the iasted ontology, 'Computer' is a subclass of 'Audiovisual equipment' (alongside LCD projector, Overhead projector, Video cassette player), denoting a physical device used in conference presentations. In the sigkdd ontology, 'Organizator' is a subclass of 'Person' (alongside Listener, Speaker), denoting a human role in conference organization. These are completely different concepts: a physical device vs. a person/role. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop), denoting the conference gathering itself. iasted:Book_proceeding is a publication artefact (subclass of Publication, sibling of Cd_proceeding), denoting the printed proceedings. These are fundamentally different categories of entities in the conference domain — an event vs. a document — so they are unrelated.

The property 'written By' in ekaw relates a Document to the Person who authored it, while 'pay' in iasted relates a Person to Money. They have different domains and ranges and denote completely different relations.

A Meta Review is a second-level review written by a meta-reviewer, whereas a Negative Review is a review whose content is negative. These are orthogonal classifications of reviews (by role vs. by sentiment), so their intended instances do not coincide.
