There is no overlap in meaning or in the kinds of things they relate.

These are entirely different properties. 'acceptsHardcopySubmissions' is a boolean property indicating whether a conference accepts hardcopy submissions, while 'hasName' is a string property holding the full name of a conference. They have different ranges (boolean vs string) and completely different semantics.

A Withdrawn Paper is a paper that has been pulled from the review process, while a Submitted Paper is one that has been sent in for consideration. These are distinct, non-overlapping lifecycle states: a withdrawn paper is no longer under consideration, whereas a submitted paper is. Neither subsumes the other.

Property A links Conference part to Conference volume, denoting that a part (e.g., a paper) belongs to a published conference volume/proceedings. Property B is an inverse-partOf relation whose range is Event, suggesting it links some entity to an Event (e.g., an event being part of another event). The domains and ranges differ substantially: one concerns conference volumes (publications) and the other concerns events. These are structurally and semantically different relations in the conference domain.

Meal Break and Coffee break are distinct subtypes of break events. A meal break is a scheduled break for eating a meal, while a coffee break is a short refreshment break. They are sibling-level concepts under a common break-event category, not equivalent. Neither subsumes the other since they are disjoint subtypes.

Bid in cmt is a class representing a reviewer's bid on a paper, with properties tying it to Reviewer and Paper. ACM_SIGKDD in sigkdd is the organization/conference series itself, with properties tying it to Deadline, Conference, and Sponsor. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference applicant (Person > Conference applicant) denotes a person who applies to attend a conference, while Accommodation Place (Place > Accommodation Place) denotes a physical location for lodging. They share no instances and belong to disjoint branches (people vs. places).

In ekaw, Event is a conference-domain event (scientific event, social event) that is organized, held in a location, and covers topics. In iasted, Place is a physical location (building, conference hall, hotel room, etc.) where activities are held. These are fundamentally different concepts: one denotes an occurrence/activity, the other a physical space. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Decision is an abstract class representing the outcome of the paper review process (Acceptance or Rejection), with hasDecision linking Paper to Decision. In the Conference ontology, Submitted_contribution is a subclass of Written_contribution representing a document that has been submitted for review, with properties related to review expertise and review preferences. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a decision/outcome, the other is a document/artefact. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

cmt:Paper is a specific kind of document (a written contribution with authors, reviews, decisions, etc.), whereas iasted:Item is a broad superclass encompassing documents, publications, equipment, cards, and transport vehicles. Paper is thus a strict subclass (subsumed_by) of Item, not equivalent.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'location Of' in ekaw relates a Location to an Event (where something takes place), while 'searched by' in sigkdd relates a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (a specific sponsorship/search relationship). They share no conceptual overlap in the conference domain.

Both classes denote people who attend a conference. 'Conference Participant' in EKAW and 'Delegate' in IASTED are synonyms in the conference domain. The IASTED ontology places Delegate under multiple parents (including Person), and its children (Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc.) are all types of conference participants, matching the EKAW hierarchy where Conference Participant has children like Presenter, Session Chair, etc. The structural overlap in children and the shared parent Person support equivalence.

In cmt, Co-author is a subclass of Author, representing a specific role of an author who co-writes a paper. In confOf, Author is the general class of persons who write contributions. Thus cmt:Co-author is strictly more specific than confOf:Author, making it subsumed_by.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (and Person), representing a type of conference organizational structure. In IASTED, 'One conference day' is a temporal entity under Time > Conference days, representing a single day within a conference. One is a conference type/structure, the other is a time period. They share no semantic overlap.

In EKAW, 'Regular Session' is a specific subtype of Session (a normal conference session), while in EDAS, 'Conference Session' is the general class for sessions within a conference. EKAW even lists 'Conference Session' as a sibling of 'Regular Session', confirming that Conference Session is more general. Thus EDAS Conference Session subsumes EKAW Regular Session.

The two properties relate completely different domain and range types and describe different activities. In cmt, 'enter Review Criteria' is used by an Administrator to specify review criteria for a Conference. In confOf, 'writes' is used by an Author to produce a Contribution (paper). There is no overlap in meaning, direction, or the kinds of entities involved.

Conference participant in ontology A is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference (with children like Active/Passive conference participant). Conference Dinner in ontology B is a subclass of Meal Event under Conference Event, denoting a social dining event. These are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is an event. No overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a specific subclass of Paper (a short abstract of a paper submitted for review), whereas in iasted, Document is a broad class covering many administrative and logistical artefacts (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, records of attendance, etc.). These are at very different levels of generality and serve different purposes. Paper Abstract is not a super- or subclass of the broad iasted Document, and the two do not overlap in intended instances.

Conference_participant in ontology Conference is a subclass of Person, denoting people who participate in a conference (with children like Active/Passive conference participant). Conference in ekaw is a subclass of Scientific Event, denoting one edition of a conference event. These are completely different concepts: one is a person role, the other is an event. No subsumption or overlap relationship applies.

Both Subject Area and Topic denote thematic categories in the conference domain, but they are not strictly equivalent. In cmt, Subject Area is a property of a Paper (via 'has Subject Area'), representing the subject areas a paper belongs to. In the Conference ontology, Topic is a broader concept that can belong to conference parts (tracks, workshops), be assigned review preferences, and be topics of conference parts. Topic appears to be a more general organizational concept covering conference structure, while Subject Area is specifically tied to paper classification. They overlap in meaning but their intended instances and structural roles do not fully coincide.

Individual Presentation is an event (subclass of Scientific Event) where a paper is presented; Speaker is a person who gives a presentation. One is an event, the other is a person — disjoint categories in the conference domain.

Government Organization denotes a governmental body (with siblings like NGO, Industry Organization, Academia Organization), while Organising Agency denotes an entity that organizes a conference (with siblings like Academic Institution, Proceedings Publisher). These are different concepts: not all government organizations organise conferences, and not all organising agencies are government organizations. They share the parent Organisation but have distinct intended instances.

The cmt property 'has Been Assigned' (Reviewer -> Paper) denotes the assignment of a reviewer to a paper for reviewing purposes, i.e., the system/program committee assigns a paper to a reviewer. The iasted property 'write' (Person -> Item) denotes the act of a person writing/authoring an item (e.g., a paper). These are fundamentally different relations: one is about review assignment, the other about authorship. They have different domains (Reviewer vs Person), different ranges (Paper vs Item), and different semantics. They are not equivalent, not in a subsumption relationship, and only weakly related at best.

These properties operate at different levels of granularity and in different directions. In cmt, memberOfProgramCommittee links an individual person (Program Committee Member) to the committee they serve on (Program Committee). In Conference, was_a_program_committee_of links the entire Program committee entity to the Conference volume it serves. The cmt property is a membership relation from person to committee; the Conference property is an affiliation relation from committee to conference. They do not relate the same kinds of entities in the same direction, so they are not equivalent.

The cmt property 'hardcopyMailingManifestsPrintedBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who printed hardcopy mailing manifests, while the sigkdd 'submit' property relates an Author to a Paper being submitted. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings; one is about printing manifests, the other about submitting papers.

Property A (is_a_topis_of_conference_parts) is an object property linking Topic to Conference part, representing which topics belong to conference parts. Property B (Name_of_conference) is a datatype property linking Conference to string, representing the name of a conference. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

reviewsPerPaper in cmt is a property of Conference with range int, representing how many reviews are assigned per paper. maxChoice in confOf is a property of Social event and Working event with range positiveInteger, representing a maximum choice count for events. They have different domains (Conference vs. Social/Working event), different semantics, and no overlap in meaning.

confOf:Reception is a social event (a reception/gathering), while iasted:Refusing manuscript is an administrative activity of rejecting a submitted paper. They share no domain overlap and are not in comparable parts of the hierarchy.

Associated Chair is a conference leadership role (a chair who assists in organizing the conference), while Invited Speaker is a presenter invited to give a talk. They occupy completely different branches of the conference-organization hierarchy: one is an administrative/organizational role, the other is a presentation role. Their instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a specific subclass of Paper (a short version of a paper submission, sibling to Paper Full Version). In ekaw, Abstract is a broader document class that includes various presentation abstracts (Invited Talk Abstract, Tutorial Abstract) and is a sibling of Paper, not a child of it. The cmt Paper Abstract is a more specific concept (an abstract associated with a paper) that is subsumed by the broader ekaw Abstract class, but they are not equivalent since their extensions differ significantly.

Car in iasted is a transport vehicle (Item > Transport vehicle > Car), an inanimate physical object used for transportation. Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes a conference (Person > Organizator), with subtypes like General Chair, Program Chair, etc. These are completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

The property hasCountry in edas relates a Conference to a Country (the country where the conference is held), while heldIn in ekaw relates an Event to a Location (a venue or place where an event is held). These are different relations with different domains and ranges: Conference vs Event, and Country vs Location. A country is not the same as a location, and a conference is not the same as an event in these ontologies. They do not denote the same relation.

Activity in iasted is a broad temporal/organizational concept (with children like 'Conference activity', 'Activity before conference') denoting things people do at a conference. Award in sigkdd is a specific honor/prize given to authors for papers. An award is not a kind of activity, nor is an activity a kind of award; their instances do not coincide and there is no subsumption relationship.

Conference Chair is a person who chairs a conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Presenter city is a geographic city where a presenter is located. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'contributes' in Conference ontology relates a Person to a Conference document (a person contributes a document to a conference). The property 'obtain' in sigkdd ontology relates an Author to an Award (an author obtains an award). These are entirely different relations: one is about contributing documents, the other about receiving awards. They do not share the same domain, range, or semantic meaning.
Coffee Break is a temporal event (a scheduled break during a conference), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They share no common instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both classes denote conference participants who give presentations, but they are not equivalent. 'Invited speaker' in the Conference ontology is a specific role based on how the speaker was invited, while 'One day presenter' in iasted is a delegate classification based on registration duration. An invited speaker could be a one-day presenter or a multi-day attendee, and a one-day presenter could be an invited speaker or a regular presenter. They overlap but neither subsumes the other.

Both classes denote the same top-level concept of a human person in the conference domain. They share the identical label 'Person' and both serve as the general superclass for conference-related human roles (e.g., Author/Attendee in edas, Delegate/Sponsor in iasted). The structural position and intended instances coincide despite differences in specific sub-roles and associated properties.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a committee chair), while Coctail reception is a social activity/event. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (Person/Chairman vs Activity/Conference activity) and denote entirely different kinds of entities.

A is a subject-matter topic (Powerline Transmission) under Topic, while B is a type of presentation event (Invited Talk) under Individual Presentation. They denote completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

The two properties differ in both type and granularity. `has_important_dates` is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates object (a collection of deadlines), while `hasEndDateTime` is a datatype property linking a Conference Event to a single dateTime value. They relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. confOf:studyAt links a Scholar to a University (where the scholar studies), while edas:relatesTo links a Document to an Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, or Person. The domains (Scholar vs Document) and ranges (University vs Event/Person) do not overlap, so these are not the same relation.

Both classes denote the same concept: a person involved in the conference domain. They share identical labels, overlapping children (Reviewer, Author/Conference contributor, Attendee/Conference participant, committee members), and common properties (has email, has first name, has last name). The structural and semantic evidence strongly supports equivalence.

Both are subclasses of Person, but they denote overlapping yet distinct concepts. cmt:User is a broad class covering any person who uses the system (Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while Conference:Conference_contributor is specifically someone who contributes to a conference (Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author). A User such as an Administrator may not be a contributor, and a Conference contributor such as an Invited speaker may not be a system User. They overlap in instances like authors and reviewers, but their intended extensions do not coincide.

Accepted_contribution is a specific stage in the review workflow (a contribution that passed review), while Submission in iasted is a broad document category covering any submission-related document (including initial manuscripts, final manuscripts, reviews, forms, etc.). Accepted_contribution is thus a narrower concept subsumed_by the general Submission class.

PaperFullVersion is a full-length submission document in cmt, while ComputerNetworksManagementTopic is a subject-area classification in edas. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Document vs Topic) and denote unrelated kinds of entities.

Co chair is a generic role for any committee co-chair (path: Person > Committee member > Co chair), while General Chair is a specific organizing role (path: Person > Organizator > General Chair). They are distinct conference roles at different levels of specificity and do not share the same intended instances.

The cmt property 'memberOfProgramCommittee' links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee, denoting committee membership. The iasted property 'sign' links a Person to an Item (e.g., a document or artefact they sign). These are different relations with different ranges (Program Committee vs. Item) and different semantics (committee membership vs. signing an item). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

A 'Conference participant' is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person), while a 'Social Event' is a non-academic event such as an excursion or reception (subclass of Conference Event). One is a person, the other is an event; they share no semantic overlap.

A 'Workshop Session' in EKAW is a temporal event (subclass of Session under Scientific Event), whereas a 'Session room' in IASTED is a physical place (subclass of Place). They denote completely different categories of entities—an event versus a location—so they are unrelated.

These two datatype properties are completely unrelated. `has_a_URL` has domain `Conference www` and range `string`, representing a web address. `has_amount_of` has domain `Money` and range `int`, representing a monetary quantity. They differ in domain, range, and intended meaning.

cmt:Conference denotes the overall academic conference event/organization that has administrators, members, dates, and accepts submissions. ekaw:Conference_Trip is a specific social event (a trip organized as part of a conference), subclass of Social Event and sibling of Conference Banquet. These are completely different concepts: one is the conference itself, the other is a social outing during a conference. No subsumption relation holds between them.

Both properties relate a presented item to the person presenting it, but the domains differ: A's domain is Presentation (the event/act) while B's domain is Document (the artefact). The ranges also differ: Active conference participant vs Speaker. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

cmt:User is a broad superclass covering Administrator, Author, and Reviewer—any person who interacts with the CMT system. iasted:Speaker is a specific kind of Delegate who presents at a conference. A Speaker is not a system user of CMT, and a CMT User (e.g., an Administrator) is not necessarily a conference delegate or presenter. The two classes denote different concepts in different modelling contexts with no clear overlap.

Conference document in ontology Conference denotes written artefacts (calls for papers, reviews, contributions, announcements, web pages), while Event in ekaw denotes occurrences (scientific events, social events). They share no instances and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties have different domains and ranges that do not overlap. In edas, 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (i.e., who sponsors an event). In iasted, 'is given by' links an Activity or Item to a Person (i.e., who presents or gives an activity/item). These are semantically distinct relations: sponsorship provision vs. presentation/giving, with different participant types (Organization vs. Person).

Hotel_presenter in iasted is a subclass of Delegate, i.e., a person (presenter staying at a hotel), whereas Hotel in sigkdd is a subclass of Place, i.e., a physical building. These are entirely different categories (person vs. place) and are unrelated.

The two properties denote completely different relations in the conference domain. 'is a date of acceptance announcement' is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value, representing when acceptance notifications are issued. 'location Of' is an object property linking a Location to an Event, indicating where an event takes place. They have different domains, ranges, and types, and share no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Paper is a Document (a written artefact submitted for review) with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties like has Author, assigned To, has Decision. In iasted, Research is an Activity (not a document) under Activity before conference, with children Modelling and Simulating, and siblings like Accepting manuscript, Receiving manuscript, Renting. These denote completely different things: one is a document/artefact, the other is a research activity/process. No subsumption holds between a document class and an activity class.

These are two distinct deadlines in the conference timeline. 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' is the deadline for submitting the final, accepted version of a paper (after acceptance), while 'Deadline Paper Submission' is the deadline for initial paper submissions (before review). They occur at different stages and are siblings under Deadline rather than the same concept.

Entity A is a class representing an event/talk (Invited talk), a kind of conference contribution or presentation. Entity B is a class representing a person (Plenary lecture speaker), a kind of author/speaker/delegate. One denotes an event, the other a person; they are in different ontological categories and do not overlap.

SC Member is a person who serves on the conference's program committee (a sub-class of PC Member under Person), while Sponzorship is a financial concept (a sub-class of Money). They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract is a document (a short version of a paper) in the cmt ontology, while Double hotel room is a physical place (a hotel room type) in the iasted ontology. They belong to completely different domains (academic documents vs. accommodation) and share no semantic relationship.
Car is a transport vehicle in iasted, while Listener is a person (conference attendee) in sigkdd. They denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Both denote conference presentation activities, but they are modeled at different levels of generality. 'Invited talk' in ontology A is a specific kind of conference contribution (a document/presentation artefact), while 'Speaker lecture' in ontology B is a session-level activity under Lecture > Session. They overlap in intended instances (an invited talk may be a speaker lecture) but are not equivalent due to different structural roles and modeling contexts.

Property A (has a program committee) links a conference volume to its Program committee (the organizing/reviewing committee of people). Property B (hasProgramme) links a conference event to a Programme (the schedule/list of sessions and events). These are structurally similar (both connect a conference-level entity to a sub-entity) but denote completely different relations: one assigns a committee of people, the other assigns a programme/schedule of activities. Their ranges (Program committee vs Programme) are distinct concepts, so the properties are unrelated.

Review Rating in EDAS is a rating value assigned to a paper (e.g., Accept, Reject), serving as the range of the 'has Rating' property. Positive Review in EKAW is a kind of Review document whose content is positive. One is an evaluation score/rating, the other is a document. They denote different categories of things and are unrelated.

A's Abstract is a generic abstract of a paper/poster/presentation, while B's Tutorial Abstract is a specific abstract for a tutorial. They are at different levels of generality and do not share a common parent in the merged hierarchy, so they are not equivalent, subsumed, or related.

confOf 'Science Worker' is a subclass of Person (alongside Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc.), denoting a person with a scientific role. iasted 'Worker non speaker' is a subclass of Delegate > Non speaker, denoting a conference delegate who does not give a talk. The two classes are in entirely different hierarchies (Person vs Delegate) and capture different notions; there is no evidence their instances coincide.

Meta Review in cmt is a specific type of review document (a meta-review of a paper), while Personal History in edas is a container class for personal publication and review histories of a person. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.
A is a subject-area topic (CAD) under Topic, while B is a kind of document (an abstract for a tutorial) under Abstract. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

Both properties link a Conference to a person involved in it, but cmt:hasConferenceMember has range Conference Member (a specific role/subclass of Person), while edas:hasMember has the broader range Person. Thus cmt:hasConferenceMember is more specific and is subsumed by edas:hasMember.

An Accepted Paper is a paper that has been accepted for presentation/publication at a conference, while an Invitation letter is a document sent to invite someone (e.g., a speaker or participant). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain despite both being subclasses of Document.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a specific kind of social event (a trip/excursion associated with a conference), whereas Conference activity in iasted is a broad superclass encompassing all conference activities (lectures, presentations, registration, coffee breaks, social programs, etc.). The two are at very different levels of generality and do not denote the same concept. They are not in a simple subsumption relation either, since a Conference Trip is a social event (not an arbitrary conference activity like a lecture or registration), and Conference_activity is a broad category that does not subsume Conference_Trip in the same hierarchy.

Conference document in ontology Conference is a broad class covering many kinds of conference-related documents (Call for paper, Conference contribution, Review, etc.). Call in edas is a specific type of document focused on soliciting manuscripts, papers, or reviews. Since Call corresponds to one of the children of Conference document (Call for paper), Call is more specific and is subsumed by Conference document.

In the edas ontology, 'Presenter' is a class of persons (a kind of Author who presents a paper). In the iasted ontology, 'Presenter university' is a class of places/buildings (the university where a presenter is based). These are completely different categories of entities — one denotes a person, the other a physical location — so they are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a specific subpart of a Paper (a sibling of 'Paper Full Version'), denoting the abstract component of a paper. In ekaw, 'Paper' is the general class of papers (with subclasses like Conference Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). A paper abstract is a constituent part of a paper, not the paper itself, so cmt's Paper Abstract is more specific than (subsumed by) ekaw's Paper. They are not equivalent.

Non Academic Event in edas is a conference event such as a break, meal, or social event. Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes the conference. These are completely different kinds of entities (event vs. person) with no overlap in intended instances.

Rejected_contribution in Conference is a leaf class specifically for contributions that were rejected after review. Evaluated_Paper in ekaw is a broader class covering papers that have been evaluated, with children Accepted_Paper and Rejected_Paper. Thus Evaluated_Paper subsumes Rejected_contribution, but they are not equivalent since Evaluated_Paper also includes accepted papers.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'assigned To' links a Paper to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to review a paper). In iasted, 'is paid by' links Money to a Person (who paid the money). They relate different kinds of entities and describe unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference Chair is a specific committee role (a Person who chairs the conference). In iasted, Delegate is a participant category whose path goes through Conference building, and it has children like Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc. These denote different concepts: a chair role vs. a conference attendee/participant type. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given their disjoint structural contexts.

edas Talk Event is a broader category encompassing any talk-type event at a conference (including closing talks, welcome talks, paper presentations), while ekaw Contributed Talk is specifically a presentation of a contributed paper, as opposed to invited talks or tutorials. Talk Event subsumes Contributed Talk since a contributed talk is one kind of talk event, but not all talk events are contributed talks.

Committee_member in Conference is a specific subclass of Person (a person who is a member of a committee), while Person in confOf is the general top-level class for all people. Committee_member is subsumed by confOf's Person, but they are not equivalent since confOf's Person also includes authors, participants, administrators, scholars, and others who are not necessarily committee members.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a gathering/activity), while Fee for extra trip is a monetary charge. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies (Event vs Money) and denote different kinds of entities.

In ekaw, 'Conference Session' is a specific session within a conference event (e.g., a talk or presentation session), sitting under Session > Scientific Event > Event. In sigkdd, 'Conference' is the top-level conference event itself (e.g., ACM SIGKDD conference), with properties like start/end dates, city, and name. A session is a part of a conference, not the conference itself; these are at different levels of granularity and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

confOf:Conference is a top-level conference event (a whole conference), sibling to Workshop and Tutorial under Working event. ekaw:Regular_Session is a session within a conference (sibling to Demo Session, Poster Session, Workshop Session under Session). A conference and a regular session are different kinds of events at different granularity levels; neither subsumes the other.

Conference in ontology A denotes the conference event/organization itself (with a name, proceedings, publisher, topics), while Place in edas denotes a physical location (with subclasses like Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). These are completely different concepts: one is the academic event, the other is a physical venue where events may occur.

Conference contributor in ontology Conference is a broad class covering any person who contributes to a conference, with subclasses including Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author. Paper Author in ekaw is specifically a person who authored a paper. Since authoring a paper is one way of being a conference contributor, Conference contributor subsumes Paper Author, but they are not equivalent because Conference contributor includes non-paper contributors such as invited speakers and active participants.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In cmt, hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document for which that person has a conflict of interest (e.g., authorship or affiliation). In sigkdd, submit relates an Author to a Paper they are submitting. The domain/range overlap (Person/Author, Document/Paper) is incidental; the intended semantics are distinct and there is no subsumption relationship between them.

These properties have incompatible domains and ranges and denote different relations. 'is held before' (domain Activity, range Time) describes when an activity/event takes place relative to a time point. 'submit until' (domain Document, range Deadline) describes the deadline by which a document must be submitted. They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different semantics.

confOf Person is a broad class covering all people in the conference domain (authors, committee members, participants, volunteers, etc.). ekaw Conference_Participant is a specific subclass of ekaw Person restricted to those who participate in the conference. Thus confOf Person is strictly more general than ekaw Conference_Participant.

These properties denote completely different relations. `paperDueOn` is a datatype property from Conference to dateTime representing a submission deadline, while `paperPresentedAs` is an object property from Abstract/Paper to Individual Presentation representing how a paper is presented. They share the word 'paper' but have different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Conference contributor in ontology A is a broad class of persons who contribute to a conference (including active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors), covering any author or presenter of accepted work. Presenter in ekaw is specifically a person who presents at the conference (a subset of conference participants). Every Presenter is a conference contributor, but not every contributor (e.g., a regular author who does not present) is a Presenter. Thus Conference contributor subsumes Presenter.

These classes are from different conceptual hierarchies. 'Late paid applicant' in Conference ontology is a person who registered late and paid, sitting under Person > Conference applicant > Registered applicant > Paid applicant. 'Registration Student' in sigkdd is a registration fee category (under Fee > Registration fee), representing a fee amount for student registrants, not a person. One denotes a person, the other a fee/price, so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Scholar is a price-category role (a person eligible for a reduced registration fee, e.g., a student or academic), evidenced by its comment 'price category - scholar' and its sibling roles such as Administrator, Volunteer, and Participant. In sigkdd, Author is a sub-class of Speaker and denotes a person who submits a paper and may obtain an award. The two classes occupy different positions in their respective taxonomies and denote different concepts: a registration price category versus an authorship role. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a way a reference alignment would record.

edas:TalkEvent is a specific kind of academic event (a talk, with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk, and siblings like Paper Presentation, Workshop). ekaw:Event is the top-level event class, with children Scientific Event and Social Event, and properties covering all events (organised by, held in, part of, etc.). A Talk Event is a strict subtype of the general Event concept, not equivalent.

max Choice is a datatype property on Social event / Working event with range positiveInteger, representing a maximum number of choices (e.g., for event options). done till is a datatype property on Deadline with range date, representing a deadline date. They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; there is no overlap in meaning.

The two properties relate completely different entities. confOf:employedBy has domain Person and range Organization, denoting a person being employed by an organization. ekaw:writtenBy has domain Document and range Person, denoting a document being authored by a person. They differ in domain, range, and meaning.

confOf:Workshop is an academic working event where papers are presented, sibling to Conference and Tutorial. edas:CoffeeBreak is a non-academic break event (sibling to Free Time Break and Meal Break). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a type of Chairman/Conference Member), while Conference restaurant is a physical place/building where conference events occur. They belong to completely different hierarchies (Person vs Place) and share no semantic overlap.

hasHomePage points to a person's home page URL, while E-mail points to an email address. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote different contact information attributes. They are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

Organization in edas denotes an institution (with subtypes Academia, Government, Industry, NGO) that can provide sponsorships. Committee in sigkdd denotes a group of people responsible for specific conference tasks (Best Paper Awards, Organizing, Program). These are disjoint concepts: an organization is an institutional entity, while a committee is a working group of individuals. No subsumption holds either.

External Reviewer in cmt is a person assigned to review a paper on behalf of another Reviewer but is explicitly NOT a Reviewer themselves. PC Member in ekaw is a Program Committee member who serves as a possible reviewer and includes roles like PC Chair, Session Chair, etc. These are distinct concepts: an External Reviewer is outside the program committee, while a PC Member is inside it. They denote different roles in the conference organization.

In cmt, Paper is a document submitted for review with authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions. In sigkdd, Award is a prize given to papers/authors (e.g., Best Paper Award). These are distinct concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

A Conference Chair is a leadership role responsible for overseeing the conference, while a Speaker is a delegate who presents at the conference. These are distinct roles in the conference domain; a Conference Chair is not a kind of Speaker and vice versa. Their hierarchies and sibling contexts confirm they denote different concepts.

Both are datatype properties of Conference, but cmt:date is a generic date (range xsd:date) while edas:startDate is specifically the conference start date and time (range xsd:dateTime, comment 'Conference Start Date and Time'). startDate is a more specific subproperty of date, so date subsumes startDate; equivalently, date is subsumed_by startDate in the sense that startDate is the narrower concept.

Research Institute (ekaw) is an organization under Organisation > Academic Institution, with sibling University. Review (sigkdd) is a document under Document, with siblings Abstract and Paper. One is an institution (an organization), the other is a review artifact (a document). They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Both are datatype properties named 'hasPhone' with range xsd:string, used to store a phone number for a person or contact-information object in the conference domain. The domain classes (confOf:Person and edas:ContactInformation) are closely related, and the intended meaning of the property—recording a phone number—coincides across the two ontologies.

Property 'writes' in confOf relates an Author to a Contribution (i.e., who authored a paper). Property 'volumeContainsPaper' in ekaw relates a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. These are entirely different relations: one connects a person to a document they authored, the other connects a container (volume) to the papers inside it. They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relationships in the conference domain.

These properties have completely different meanings. 'maxPapers' in cmt specifies the maximum number of papers a Program Committee Member can be assigned, with domain Program Committee Member and range int. 'paperDueOn' in edas specifies the paper submission deadline date/time for a Conference, with domain Conference and range dateTime. They relate different entities (person vs. conference), have different ranges (int vs. dateTime), and serve entirely unrelated purposes.

Conference Chair is a leadership role (a person who chairs the conference), while Student non speaker is a type of delegate (a student attendee who does not present). They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties link a conference entity to a Topic, but their domains differ: confOf:hasTopic has domain Working event (e.g., a conference session), while edas:hasTopic has domain Conference or Paper. They share overlapping semantics (assigning topics) but do not relate the same kinds of things in the same way, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Presenter (ekaw) is a conference participant who presents a paper or talk, situated under Person > Conference Participant. A Conference Hiker (iasted) is a subclass of Delegate under Place > Building > Conference building, and its siblings (Non speaker, Listener, Speaker, etc.) suggest it denotes a delegate who attends multiple conferences or moves between sessions, not specifically someone who presents. The two concepts have different intended instances and no clear subsumption relationship.

The cmt 'write Paper' property relates an Author to a Paper they have authored. The ekaw 'topic Covered By' property relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper that covers that topic. These are completely different relations with different domains (Author vs. Research Topic) and different semantics (authorship vs. topic coverage).

Both classes denote the published proceedings of a conference. In ekaw, Proceedings is a multi-author volume (a document) that is the parent of Conference Proceedings. In iasted, Book proceeding is a publication (a physical item) that is a sibling of CD proceeding. Despite the slight difference in modeling (document vs. physical item), both represent the same concept: the bound collection of papers from a conference.

Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (an item), while Organizator is a person who organizes a conference. They belong to completely disjoint domains (physical object vs. person) and share no conceptual overlap.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Fee in iasted is a subclass of Money, denoting monetary charges such as registration fees, hotel fees, and tips. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate different concepts in different directions. 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the entity responsible for publishing), while 'written By' links a Document to a Person (the author). The domains (Conference proceedings vs Document) and ranges (Publisher vs Person) differ, and the relations themselves denote distinct roles (publishing vs authoring).

In cmt, Paper is a document (subclass of Document) with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and it is the subject of reviewing/acceptance properties. In edas, PaperPresentation is an event (subclass of AcademicEvent > ConferenceEvent) representing the presentation of a paper at a conference. These are fundamentally different entities: one is a written document/artifact, the other is a scheduled academic event. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties differ in type, domain, range, and meaning. `is situated in` is an object property relating places (Building, City, Place) to other places (Building, City, Place, State), expressing spatial containment. `City of conference` is a datatype property with domain Conference and range string, providing the name of the conference's city as text. They do not denote the same relation.

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while edas's 'Computer Architecture Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different parts of the conference domain hierarchy with no overlap in intended instances.

Information for participants is a conference document providing logistical details to attendees, while Abstract is a summary of a paper. They denote different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

Decision in cmt is a specific outcome of paper review (Acceptance/Rejection), while Activity in iasted is a general event/action with temporal and spatial properties. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference participant in ontology A is a broad class covering any person who participates in a conference, with children Active conference participant and Passive conference participant. Presenter in ekaw is a specific kind of conference participant who presents (e.g., gives a talk), with child Invited Speaker. A presenter is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is a presenter (e.g., attendees, committee members). Thus Conference participant subsumes Presenter.

confOf:Social event is a subclass of Event with children like Banquet, Reception, and Trip, denoting social activities in a conference. iasted:Document is a subclass of Item with children like Review, Submission, and Form, denoting textual or administrative artefacts. These classes have disjoint intended instances and no overlap.

confOf:Member_PC is a person who serves on a programme committee (reviewer), with domain properties expertOn and reviewes. edas:TwoLevelConference is a type of conference (a conference event/organisation), not a person. They belong to completely different branches of their ontologies and denote unrelated entities.

The property 'occupy' in iasted relates a Person to a Building, City, or State (i.e., a person occupying/located at a place). The property 'payed by' in sigkdd relates a Registration fee to a Person (i.e., a fee paid by a person). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings; they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Both classes are subclasses of Deadline in the conference domain, but they denote different deadline events. 'Registation deadline' in iasted concerns the deadline for registration, while 'Deadline Author notification' in sigkdd concerns the deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance. They share the common parent Deadline but their intended instances do not coincide, so they are related (both are conference deadlines) but not equivalent.

confOf's Event is a broad superclass covering Administrative event, Social event, and Working event, whereas ekaw's Social_Event is a specific subtype of Event (with children like Conference Banquet and Conference Trip). confOf:Event therefore subsumes ekaw:Social_Event rather than being equivalent to it.

Property A (has_an_organizing_committee) links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee, a specific committee. Property B (organisedBy) links an Event to an Organisation or Person, indicating the general organizer. They differ in direction (A goes from event to committee; B goes from event to organizer), domain (Conference volume vs Event), and range (Organizing committee vs Organisation/Person). They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the structural differences.

confOf:Student is a class denoting a person (a kind of conference participant) who is a student. sigkdd:Registration_Non-Member is a class denoting a registration fee category for non-members. One is a person type, the other is a fee/registration type; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. In cmt, memberOfProgramCommittee links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (member -> committee). In Conference, has_a_program_committee links a Conference volume to a Program committee (conference -> committee). They are not inverses of each other (one is about a person's membership, the other about a conference having a committee), and they do not share the same domain or range types. They denote different relations in the conference domain.

In EDAS, 'Session Chair' is a person who chairs a session (a track/event session), distinct from 'Conference Chair' which is the overall conference organizer. In EKAW, 'PC Chair' is the head of the Programme Committee, responsible for the scientific program and paper selection. These are different organizational roles: a session chair manages a single session, while a PC chair leads the entire programme committee. EKAW even has a separate 'Session Chair' class as a sibling of 'PC Chair', confirming they are distinct concepts. The two ontologies use different terminology for different roles, and there is no subsumption relationship between them.

`parallel with` in confOf is a symmetric relation between two Administrative events (e.g., sessions running in parallel). `belongsToEvent` in edas links a Programme to a Conference Event, expressing membership/containment. They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings; neither subsumes the other.

Attendee in edas is a general class for any person attending a conference (a participant), while Invited Speaker in ekaw is a specific role: a presenter who was invited to give a talk. An invited speaker is an attendee, but the two classes do not denote the same concept; they are in a subsumption relationship (Attendee subsumes Invited Speaker) rather than equivalence. Since the options require one relation and they are not equivalent, 'unrelated' is the closest available choice, though 'subsumes' would be more precise.

Paper Full Version in cmt is a concrete full-text submission of a paper, while Call for paper in Conference is a document announcing the conference and inviting submissions. They are completely different kinds of conference documents with no overlap in intended instances.

edas 'Dining Place' is a specific kind of place (a restaurant or dining venue) under the general 'Place' class, alongside accommodation, conference venue, and meeting room places. sigkdd 'Place' is a broad class with children like Conference hall, Hotel, and Main office. The sigkdd Place is more general and subsumes the edas Dining Place, but they are not equivalent since Dining Place denotes only dining-specific locations.

A Workshop is a distinct academic event type focused on a specific topic, typically with its own papers and program. An Industrial Session is a conference session featuring industry presentations. These are different kinds of events: a workshop is not a type of industrial session, nor vice versa. They share only the general ancestor of conference event/session.

Both classes denote conference participants who attend but do not actively present or speak. 'Passive conference participant' in Conference ontology contrasts with 'Active conference participant', indicating non-presenting attendees. 'Worker non speaker' in iasted is a non-speaker delegate who is a professional (worker) rather than a student. The core concept—conference attendee who does not give a talk—coincides. The iasted ontology further distinguishes worker vs. student among non-speakers, but both classes target the same set of non-presenting professional attendees. Minor structural differences (iasted places it under Delegate via Non speaker) reflect modeling style rather than semantic divergence.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has a commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so the properties are unrelated.

These classes denote entirely different concepts. In Conference, 'Call for participation' is a document (subclass of Conference document) — a written announcement inviting participation. In confOf, 'Reviewing results event' is an event (subclass of Administrative event) where review outcomes are communicated to authors. One is a document artefact, the other is a scheduled event; their instances do not coincide.

The two properties have different domains and different meanings. `has Street` in confOf applies to Organization and Person, capturing a street address. `City of conference` in sigkdd applies to Conference and captures the city where the conference takes place. They relate different kinds of entities and denote different address/location concepts, so they are not equivalent.

Talk Event in edas is a subclass of Conference Event/Academic Event, i.e., a scheduled oral presentation event (with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk). Tutorial Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Document > Abstract, i.e., a written summary document for a tutorial. One is an event, the other is a document; they share no intended instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Committee member denotes a person serving on a committee (with specialized sub-roles Chair and Co-chair), while Participant denotes a person attending the conference (with sub-roles Member, Regular, Student). Their instance sets do not coincide: a committee member need not be a participant, and a participant need not be on any committee. They are sibling subclasses of Person in their respective ontologies with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Sponzorship is a subclass of Money representing sponsorship money, with siblings Fee, Tax, Tip. In sigkdd, Fee is a broader class with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee. The two concepts overlap (sponsorship fees fall under both), but they are not equivalent: Sponzorship is specifically about sponsorship, while Fee is a broader category covering registration and sponsorship fees. They are related but neither subsumes the other cleanly since Sponzorship includes non-fee sponsorship money and Fee includes non-sponsorship fees.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Management Topic' is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for papers. In EKAW, 'Conference Session' is a subclass of Session under Event, representing a scheduled time slot at a conference. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

These properties have different domains (Call vs Item), different ranges (dateTime datatype vs Time object), and different semantics: 'has Submission Deadline' specifies when a call's submissions are due, while 'is sent after' indicates a temporal relationship for when an item is sent. They denote different relations in the conference domain.

Conference in ontology Conference denotes an academic/scientific conference event (with conference volumes, proceedings, publishers, topics), while Building in iasted denotes a physical structure (parent Place, with subtypes like Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc.). These are entirely different concepts: an event vs. a physical location. No subsumption or overlap exists.

The two properties have incompatible domains and ranges. In iasted, 'is paid for' links Money to Activity/Item (money pays for an activity or item). In sigkdd, 'payed by' links Registration fee to Person (a registration fee is paid by a person). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and do not denote the same relation.

The two properties have opposite domain/range directions. In ekaw, 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (the author who wrote it). In iasted, 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (the person signs the item). They are not inverses of each other either, since writing a document and signing an item are different actions in the conference domain.

confOf:Paper is a class whose instances are written documents (subclasses of Contribution, siblings Poster and Short_paper). sigkdd:Author_of_paper is a subclass of Person whose instances are people who author papers. One denotes a document, the other a person; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

In the Conference ontology, Organization is a general class for any organization. In edas, NGO is a specific subclass of Organization (a sibling of Academia Organization, Government Organization, and Industry Organization), denoting non-governmental organizations specifically. Therefore Organization (A) is strictly more general than NGO (B), so A is subsumed_by B in the sense that A's concept is broader; the relation from A to B is subsumed_by (A is subsumed by B as the more general concept is narrower in scope). More precisely, A subsumes B, but since the question asks the relation of A to B and B is a child of Organization, A is the parent. The correct relation is that A subsumes B.

Publisher is an organization that issues conference proceedings, while City is a geographic location where organizations or persons are located. These are completely disjoint concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have different domains and ranges and serve different purposes. 'has_contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (i.e., the papers published in that volume). 'relatesTo' links a Document to various entities it is related to (Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, Person). The domain of A is Conference volume while the domain of B is Document; the ranges are also disjoint in meaning. They do not denote the same relation.

The two classes denote completely different concepts. In EKAW, Conference_Proceedings is a subclass of Document/Proceedings, i.e. a published volume of conference papers. In IASTED, Author_book_proceedings_included is a subclass of Author (via Speaker), i.e. a person who authored something included in book proceedings. One is a document, the other is a person; they share no instances and are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations. In ontology A, 'is a topis of conference parts' links a Topic to a Conference part (a topic belongs to a conference part). In ontology B, 'need' links a Person to an Item (a person needs an item). There is no overlap in the kinds of things being related or the meaning of the relation.

The property 'rejected By' in cmt relates a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while 'presentationed by' in sigkdd relates a Document to a Speaker who presented it. These are completely different relationships in the conference domain: one concerns paper rejection, the other concerns document presentation. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Member_PC is a subclass of Person denoting a PC member / reviewer (a human role), whereas edas:PersonalReviewHistory is a subclass of Personal History recording a reviewer's review history (a data object). They denote completely different categories of entities.

Coffee Break is a short refreshment break during conference sessions, while Conference Banquet is a formal social meal event. They are distinct types of non-academic/social events with different purposes and scope; neither subsumes the other.

Both properties relate a reviewer to another reviewer in the context of an invitation/assignment, but they differ in domain scope and direction of generality. In cmt, 'assignedByReviewer' has domain External Reviewer and range Reviewer, indicating that an external reviewer is assigned by an (internal) reviewer. In the Conference ontology, 'invited_by' has domain Reviewer and range Reviewer, covering any reviewer invited by any reviewer. The Conference property is thus more general in domain, but the two are not straightforwardly equivalent because 'assigned' and 'invited' can denote different relationships (assignment to review vs. invitation to be a reviewer). They overlap but are not certain to coincide.

Property A relates a committee member to the committee they belong to, while property B relates a PC member to the contribution they review. These are different relations connecting different kinds of entities.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has parts' links a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (e.g., tracks or sessions within a volume), whereas 'is Member Of' links a Person to a Conference they are a member of. The domains (Conference volume vs Person) and ranges (Conference part vs Conference) are disjoint, so these properties denote different relations in the conference domain.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In EDAS, 'Computer Networks Management Topic' is a subject-area topic for paper classification, sitting under 'Computer Networks Topic' alongside other subtopics like security, sensors, and switching. In IASTED, 'Computer' is a physical piece of audiovisual equipment (an item), sibling to LCD projector and overhead projector. One is an abstract topic/subject category; the other is a physical device. They share the word 'computer' but have no semantic overlap.

Paper Full Version in cmt is a full-length paper (a complete written document), sibling to Paper Abstract, under Paper. Poster in confOf is a poster presentation (a distinct contribution type), sibling to Paper and Short paper under Contribution. A full paper and a poster are different types of contributions; neither subsumes the other.

Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing a paper submission deadline, while WirelessCommunicationsTopic is a subject-area topic. They share no instances and occupy unrelated branches of their ontologies.

In cmt, `name` is a general datatype property with domain Conference AND Person, covering names of both conferences and people. In sigkdd, `Name_of_conference` is specifically for conference names only (domain: Conference). The cmt `name` property is more general (applies to more entity types), so it subsumes the sigkdd property. They are not equivalent because their domains differ: cmt's `name` also applies to Person instances, while sigkdd's is restricted to Conference.

Cryptography Topic is a subject-area classification under Topic in the edas ontology, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a child) under Item in the iasted ontology. They denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Company (subclass of Organization) denotes a corporate entity, while Hotel (subclass of Place) denotes a physical lodging venue. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Organization vs Place) and do not share instances in the conference domain.

These properties differ in both type and semantics. A's 'date' is a datatype property with domain Conference and range date, representing a date value directly. B's 'has important dates' is an object property with domain Conference volume and range Important dates, linking to a class that aggregates important deadline dates. They operate at different levels of abstraction and have different domains.

confOf:Member_PC is a regular program-committee member / reviewer (comment says 'Reviewer', siblings include Chair_PC which is the chair). sigkdd:Program_Chair is the head of the program committee (a distinct, more specific role). The two roles do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

Property A (is_given_by) relates a Presentation to the Active conference participant who presents it. Property B (hasMember) relates a Conference to a Person who is a member of that conference. They connect different domain and range types (Presentation->Active conference participant vs. Conference->Person) and represent different relationships: giving a presentation vs. being a member of a conference. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

Personal Review History in edas is a record of a reviewer's past review activity, linked to a Reviewer via hasReviewHistory/isReviewHistoryOf. Paper in sigkdd is a document submitted by an author. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference contribution is a document-like entity (papers, posters, presentations) submitted to a conference volume, while Building is a physical place (hotels, airports, halls). They share no domain overlap despite both being conference-related.
Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Hotel is a physical accommodation place. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Both properties relate a presentation/speaker to a presented document, but they differ in domain (Individual Presentation vs Speaker) and range (Abstract/Paper vs Document). They overlap in meaning but are not equivalent.

The property attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event they attend, while prepare relates a Person to an Item they prepare (e.g., a paper or presentation). These are distinct relations with different ranges and meanings; attending an event is not the same as preparing an item.

Rejected contribution denotes a paper that was reviewed and rejected, while Withdrawn Paper denotes a paper that was withdrawn (typically by the authors before a decision). These are mutually exclusive terminal states of a submission's lifecycle, so the classes do not overlap.

confOf Trip is a social event (e.g., banquet, reception) that occurs during the conference, while iasted Activity_after_conference groups activities like departures and post-conference tours that happen after the conference ends. They differ in temporal positioning and purpose: Trip is a social event during the conference, whereas Activity_after_conference is explicitly a post-conference activity. The intended instances do not coincide.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. In cmt, 'acceptedBy' links a Paper to the Administrator who accepted it (paper -> administrator). In edas, 'relatedToPaper' links a Paper Presentation to the Accepted Paper it is about (presentation -> paper). They have different domains (Paper vs Paper Presentation), different ranges (Administrator vs Accepted Paper), and express fundamentally different relationships.

In EKAW, 'Scientific Event' is a broad class subsuming conferences, sessions, tracks, workshops, and individual presentations—i.e., the scientific/academic gatherings themselves. In IASTED, 'Presentation' is a specific conference activity (a talk or delivery of material) with children like 'Power Point presentation' and 'Video presentation', and siblings like 'Coffee break', 'Registration', and 'Welcome address'. These denote different kinds of entities: one is an event/gathering, the other is an activity/performance within a conference. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other in the intended domain modelling.

The edas property belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event, expressing that a programme belongs to an event. The ekaw property technicallyOrganisedBy (a subproperty of organisedBy) expresses that something is technically organised by some agent or organisation. These relations differ in both the kinds of entities they connect and their intended meaning: one is about a programme's association with an event, the other about technical organisation of an entity by an organiser. They do not denote the same relation.

confOf 'Working event' is a subclass of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) denoting a type of conference activity. edas 'Cryptography Topic' is a subclass of Topic, a subject-matter classification for papers. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Entity A is a document/form (a form that authors fill in to provide information), sitting under Item > Document > Form alongside registration forms. Entity B is a person role (an author who submits papers and receives notifications), sitting under Person > Speaker > Author. One is an artefact, the other is a person; they share only the word 'author' in their labels but denote completely different categories of entity.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee, while property B links two Administrative events that run in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings in the conference domain.

These two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. In edas, 'is Location Of' has domain Place and range Conference Event, meaning Place -> Conference Event (a place is the location of an event). In iasted, 'is held in' has domain Activity and range Place/Time, meaning Activity -> Place (an activity is held in a place). They relate the same two kinds of entities but in opposite directions. A property and its inverse are not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person and includes roles like Author, Reviewer, and Program Committee Member—people who participate in the conference. In iasted, Non speaker is a subclass of Delegate (which descends from Place > Building > Conference building), making it a spatially-located category of delegates who do not present. The two classes occupy entirely different ontology branches and do not share the same intended instances.

confOf:City is a general class for cities, serving as the range of properties from Organization and Person. iasted:Presenter_city is a specific subclass of iasted:City, restricted to cities associated with presenters (a sibling of Conference_city, Sponsor_city, Trip_city). The general City subsumes the more specific Presenter_city; they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, 'Invited Speaker' is a specific kind of presenter—one who was invited to give a talk (e.g., a keynote or invited talk). In iasted, 'Speaker' is a broad class subsuming Author, Reviewer, and various other delegate types who speak at the conference. Thus iasted:Speaker is more general than ekaw:Invited Speaker; every invited speaker is a speaker, but not every speaker is an invited speaker.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. `has a publisher` links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (the organisation that publishes proceedings), while `presentationed by` links a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents it). The domains (Conference proceedings vs. Document), ranges (Publisher vs. Speaker), and semantics (publication vs. presentation) are disjoint, so these properties are unrelated.

Proceedings in ekaw is a document (a multi-author volume containing conference papers), while Author in sigkdd is a person who writes papers. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf Reviewing event is an administrative event representing the reviewing procedure for submitted contributions, whereas edas Call For Papers is a call soliciting paper submissions. One is a process/event during which reviews are handled; the other is an announcement requesting submissions. They denote different concepts in the conference domain and neither subsumes the other.

The cmt 'name' is a datatype property mapping Conference/Person to a string (a name/label). The iasted 'obtain' is an object property mapping Person to Item (a person obtaining an item). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings; they are not equivalent.

A 'Conference Participant' in ekaw is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person), while 'Registration fee' in iasted is a monetary amount charged for registration (subclass of Money > Fee). These are completely different concepts: one denotes a human participant, the other a financial charge. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad superclass encompassing all persons affiliated with a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, committee members). Co-chair in Conference is a specific role within a committee, a sibling of Chair. The former is a general category of conference participants; the latter is a narrow committee role. They do not share instances, and neither subsumes the other (Conference Member is not a committee role, and Co-chair is not a superclass of all conference members).

confOf's 'Submission event' is an administrative event marking the act of submitting contributions, while iasted's 'Deadline for notification of acceptance' is a specific temporal deadline for notifying authors of acceptance decisions. They refer to different concepts (an event vs. a deadline) at different stages of the conference workflow.

Property A (reviews) has domain Review and range Reviewed contribution, meaning a Review reviews a Contribution. Property B (writes) has domain Author and range Contribution, meaning an Author writes a Contribution. These are different relations with different domains (Reviewer vs. Author) and different directions of action relative to the contribution.

In iasted, Submission is a broad class covering all submitted documents including initial and final manuscripts, reviews, and other items. In sigkdd, Paper is a specific document type that is submitted by an author. Paper is a kind of submission, so iasted:Submission is more general and subsumes sigkdd:Paper, making Paper subsumed_by Submission.

Committee member in Conference is a person who serves on a committee, with children Chair and Co-chair. IASTED member in iasted is a delegate who is a member of the IASTED organization, placed under Delegate with siblings like Listener, Speaker, Session chair. One denotes committee membership; the other denotes membership in the IASTED association. These are different concepts despite both involving the word 'member'.

Published Paper (edas) denotes a paper that has been published, a status/lifecycle concept, as shown by siblings like Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn. Poster Paper (ekaw) denotes a paper submitted for a poster presentation, a type/category concept, as shown by siblings like Demo Paper, Regular Paper, Workshop Paper. These are orthogonal dimensions: a poster paper could be published or not, and a published paper could be a regular paper or a poster paper. They share only the parent Paper.

Conference announcement is a specific document type (a formal announcement about a conference), while Mailing list is a communication channel/distribution list. They are different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

confOf:Workshop is a type of event (a working event where papers are presented), while iasted:Introduction_of_speaker is a specific conference activity (a speech act introducing a speaker). They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

These properties relate different entities in different directions. confOf:employedBy connects Person to Organization (a person is employed by an organization). iasted:is_given_by connects Activity/Item to Person (an activity or item is given by a person). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different: one is about employment affiliation, the other about authorship/presentation attribution. They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Talk Event in edas is an academic event (parent: Academic Event) with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk. Silver Supporter in sigkdd is a type of sponsor (parent: Sponzor) at a sponsorship tier. These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap.

Tip (a gratuity, sibling of Fee, Sponzorship, Tax under Money) and Registration fee (a conference attendance fee with member/non-member/student subtypes) denote different financial concepts in the conference domain; they share only the broad ancestor Money/Fee.

confOf:Conference is a specific kind of working event (a conference itself), situated as a sibling of Tutorial and Workshop. edas:ConferenceEvent is a broad top-level class that encompasses both academic and non-academic events, with properties covering any event with attendees, locations, and programmes. Thus confOf:Conference is a narrower concept (a specific academic conference) that falls under the more general edas:ConferenceEvent, making the relation subsumed_by rather than equivalent.

Conference_proceedings in ontology Conference is a document (the published book of conference papers), evidenced by properties such as has ISBN, has volume, has publisher. Proceedings_Publisher in ekaw is a subclass of Organisation, i.e. the entity that publishes proceedings. One is a document, the other is an organisation/agent; they are disjoint kinds of things, so they are not equivalent, nor is there a subsumption relation.

Paper Full Version is a conference document (a full paper submission) in the cmt ontology, while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment in the iasted ontology. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In Conference, Workshop is a kind of conference part/event (sibling of Track and Tutorial), while in ekaw, Workshop_Paper is a document/paper type (child of Paper). One denotes an academic event, the other a written artefact submitted to such an event. They are disjoint kinds of things, not equivalent or subsumed.

Conference Venue Place in edas denotes a place where a conference is held (e.g., a building or meeting room), whereas Presenter house in iasted denotes the residence or lodging of a presenter. They occupy different positions in their respective hierarchies and do not share the same intended instances.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Conference airport in iasted is a physical location (subclass of Building/Place). They denote completely unrelated concepts despite both containing the word 'Conference'.

In EDAS, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (a type of event/organisation), despite appearing alongside person-related classes in the hierarchy. In EKAW, 'OC Member' is a subclass of Conference Participant, i.e. a person who serves on the Organising Committee. One denotes a conference structure, the other a person role; they share no instances.

Regular contribution in Conference is a specific academic contribution type (parent: Conference contribution; children: Extended abstract, Paper) representing written scholarly works submitted to a conference. Document in iasted is a broad administrative container (parent: Item; children include Form, Payment document, Mailing list, Viza, etc.) covering many non-academic artefacts.
