Their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other: Regular contribution is not a kind of administrative Document, and Document includes many things that are not contributions.

cmt's `date` is a general conference date (domain Conference, range date), while edas's `hasSubmissionDeadline` is specifically the submission deadline for a Call (domain Call, range dateTime). A general conference date is not the same relation as a submission deadline; they connect different domain entities and denote different concepts.

hasPhone and hasEmail are distinct datatype properties capturing different contact information (phone number vs email address). They share the same domain (Person) and range (string), but denote different relations. A reference alignment would not consider them equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Both denote the same kind of social gathering event at a conference: a banquet / conference dinner. In confOf, Banquet is a Social event (alongside Reception and Trip), and in edas, Conference Dinner is a Meal Event under Non Academic Event. A 'banquet' and a 'conference dinner' are synonymous in the conference-organisation domain, referring to the same intended instances.
Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a subject area/topic. They share no semantic relationship.

Call_for_paper in the Conference ontology is a conference document announcing a call for papers, while TestOnlyTopic in edas is a subject topic used for testing. They belong to completely different hierarchies (document vs. topic) and denote unrelated concepts.

The two properties relate completely different entities. In ekaw, 'written By' links a Document to the Person who authored it. In iasted, 'is present' links a Person to a Time (presumably indicating when a person is present). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Cryptography Topic is a subject-area classification (child of Topic, siblings are technical domains like Communications Topic, Computer Networks Topic). Best Applications Paper Award is a conference award (child of Award, siblings are Best Research Paper Award, Best Student Paper Award). They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasEmail relates a Person to their email address string, while hasFirstName relates a Person to their first name string. These are distinct attributes with no overlap in intended meaning.

Entity A is a topic within a conference topic taxonomy (Computer Networks Security Topic), representing a subject area for papers or sessions. Entity B is a physical piece of audiovisual equipment (Computer) used at a conference venue. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes are named Conference and concern the conference domain, but they model different aspects. In cmt, Conference is the concrete conference event with administrative properties (submissions, dates, members, logo). In the Conference ontology, Conference is a more abstract concept that has conference volumes as parts and is linked to proceedings, publishers, and topics. They overlap but their intended instances do not fully coincide.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'assigned By Administrator' (domain: Reviewer, range: Administrator) denotes the assignment of a reviewer to a paper by an administrator, relating a reviewer to an administrator. 'reviewer Of Paper' (domain: Possible Reviewer, range: Paper) denotes that a reviewer is reviewing a particular paper, relating a reviewer to a paper. They connect different entity types in different directions and are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

The property 'held In' in EKAW relates an Event to the Location where it takes place. The property 'is equipped by' in IASTED relates a Place to an Item that equips/furnishes it. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties have different domains and different intended meanings. In cmt, 'reviewsPerPaper' is a datatype property on Conference specifying how many reviews each paper receives. In the Conference ontology, 'has_a_degree' is a datatype property on Review preference specifying a degree value for a review preference. They relate different kinds of entities and do not denote the same relation.

Entity A is the class of persons who perform reviewing (a Reviewer), while entity B is the class of documents that contain a review (a Review). They denote completely different things (a role/person vs. an artefact), so they are unrelated.

Invited_speaker is a person (subclass of Conference contributor) who speaks at a conference, while Conference_city is a geographic location (subclass of City) where a conference takes place. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and denote different kinds of entities.

Single Level Conference in EDAS is a type of academic conference (a conference with one review level), whereas Conference Trip in EKAW is a social event during a conference. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'was a committe co chair of' connects a Co chair to a Committee (a role-to-group relation), while 'is signed by' connects an Item to a Person (an artefact-to-signatory relation). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Welcome address is an activity/event (a speech or session welcoming conference participants), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue where conference activities occur. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Activity vs Place) and denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In iasted, Tutorial speaker is a highly specific subclass of Speaker (via Author), denoting only those who give tutorials. In sigkdd, Speaker is the general class of all presenters (with subclasses Author and Invited Speaker). Thus sigkdd:Speaker is strictly more general than iasted:Tutorial_speaker, so the relation is subsumed_by.

In Conference ontology, 'Information for participants' is a subclass of Conference document — it denotes a document providing information to conference participants. In confOf, 'Camera Ready event' is a subclass of Administrative event — it denotes an event (a temporal occurrence) in the conference lifecycle when camera-ready papers are prepared. One is a document, the other is an event; they are different categories of things with no overlap in instances.

cmt:Person is a broad class covering all people in the system (chairs, committee members, reviewers, users), while ekaw:PC_Member is a specific role under Possible Reviewer. cmt:Person subsumes ekaw:PC_Member because every PC member is a person, but not vice versa.

These properties operate in completely different domains and ranges. cmt:paperAssignmentFinalizedBy relates a Conference to an Administrator, indicating that the paper assignment process has been finalized by that administrator. sigkdd:presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker, indicating who presented the document. They connect different entity types (Conference vs. Document, Administrator vs. Speaker) and describe different relationships (assignment finalization vs. presentation authorship). There is no meaningful overlap.

University in ekaw is an academic institution (organisation), while Simulating in iasted is a research activity that occurs before a conference. These are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf 'Camera Ready event' is a subclass of Administrative event (an event in the conference timeline), whereas ekaw 'Camera Ready Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a document). One denotes a temporal event, the other a written artefact; they do not share instances.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In cmt, Conference Chair is a person who chairs the conference (a role under Person > Chairman). In edas, Welcome Talk is an academic event (a talk under Conference Event > Academic Event > Talk Event). One is a person/role, the other is an event, so they are unrelated.

Review in the Conference ontology is a document (subclass of Conference document) — the actual review artefact written by a reviewer. Reviewing event in confOf is a temporal/administrative event (subclass of Administrative event > Event) representing the reviewing procedure/phase. One is a document, the other is an event; their instances cannot coincide.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. In confOf, expertOn links a Member PC to a Topic (indicating expertise). In ekaw, writtenBy links a Document to a Person (indicating authorship). They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings.

A 'Conference Session' in EKAW is a scientific session within a conference (e.g., demo, poster, regular, workshop sessions) where papers are presented. A 'Conference activity' in IASTED is a broad category encompassing all conference-related activities including cocktail receptions, coffee breaks, registration, and social programs. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a specific scientific presentation session, the other is a general activity category. They share no clear subsumption relationship either, as EKAW sessions are not a subset of IASTED conference activities in any meaningful way.

In ontology A, 'Regular author' is a specific kind of conference contributor who writes conference contributions, sitting under 'Conference contribution' and 'Conference contributor'. In ontology B, 'Author' is a broader role placed under 'Speaker' (a delegate who presents), with children including various speaker subtypes (Lecturer, Plenary lecture speaker, Tutorial speaker) and authors of different proceedings formats. B's Author encompasses presenting authors and speakers, making it more general than A's Regular author, which is specifically a contributor who authors written work. The hierarchies and sibling contexts differ enough to preclude equivalence.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing a short version or abstract of a conference paper. Multimedia Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic representing a subject-matter classification for papers (multimedia). These denote completely different concepts: one is a document type, the other is a topic category. No overlap in intended instances.

In EKAW, Industrial_Session is a specialized subclass of Conference_Session (a session with industrial/paper presentations). In EDAS, Conference_Session is the general class for any conference session. These are not equivalent: EDAS's Conference_Session corresponds to EKAW's Conference_Session (the parent), not to Industrial_Session. Industrial_Session is a specific type of session that has no direct counterpart in EDAS, so the two classes are unrelated rather than in a subsumption relationship.

hasHomePage links a Person to their home page URL (a string), while Nation links a Person to their country of nationality/origin. Despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string), they denote completely different attributes with no overlap in intended meaning.

`accept Paper` in cmt is a specific administrative action where an Administrator accepts a Paper (decision in a review process). `give` in iasted is a general action where a Person gives an Activity or Item. They differ in domain, range, and meaning; neither subsumes the other in a way a reference alignment would record.

The confOf 'abstract' property captures the abstract text of a Contribution, while the sigkdd 'Currency' property captures the currency of a Registration fee. They relate to completely different domain concepts (paper abstracts vs. payment currency) and have disjoint domains (Contribution vs. Registration fee), so they are unrelated.

A is a person who writes papers (cmt Author, path Person > Conference Member > Author, with properties submit Paper, write Paper). B is a physical location (edas Place, with children Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place, and properties has Location/is Location Of relating to Conference Event). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Trip is a social event (e.g., an excursion organized as part of a conference), whereas Hotel fee is a monetary fee for accommodation. They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies (Event vs. Money) and denote completely different kinds of entities.

Extended abstract and Regular Paper denote different types of conference contributions. An extended abstract is a short summary document, while a regular paper is a full-length paper. They are sibling categories under contribution/paper hierarchies, not the same concept.

The two properties are inverses of each other, not equivalent. In cmt, 'assignedTo' goes from Paper to Reviewer (paper assigned to reviewer). In edas, 'isReviewing' goes from Reviewer to Paper (reviewer is reviewing paper). A reference alignment would not treat a property and its inverse as equivalent; they relate the same entities but in opposite directions.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. confOf:parallel_with links two Administrative events (e.g., sessions running in parallel), while edas:isInitiatedBy links a Call to the persons who initiate it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). They share no domain, no range, and no semantic overlap.

Registeered applicant is a person who has registered for a conference (subclass of Conference applicant > Person), while Credit card is a payment instrument (subclass of Card > Item). They belong to entirely different branches of their ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

Workshop in edas is an academic event (a type of conference session), while Worker lecturer in iasted is a person role (a lecturer who is a worker). They share the substring 'work' but denote completely different categories: an event vs. a person.

Paper Full Version is a complete version of a submitted paper, while Tutorial Abstract is a summary of a tutorial talk. They are different document types in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A denotes a first name (given name) of a Person, while property B denotes a last name (family name/surname) of a Person. These are distinct attributes that do not overlap; neither subsumes the other.

The two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges and express different relations. `is needed for` (iasted) has domain Item and range Person, indicating that some item is needed for a person. `presentation` (sigkdd) has domain Speaker and range Document, linking a speaker to the document they present. The domains (Item vs. Speaker) and ranges (Person vs. Document) do not coincide, and the intended meanings are unrelated.

These properties denote different relations. cmt:assignedTo assigns a Reviewer to review a Paper, while confOf:writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author. The domain and range differ (Paper/Reviewer vs Contribution/Author), and the semantics are distinct: assignment of a reviewer vs authorship attribution.

Conference Proceedings in EKAW is a multi-author volume collecting conference papers, while Abstract in SIGKDD is a short summary document sibling to Paper and Review. They denote completely different document types with no overlap in intended instances.

edas:Paper is a general class for all papers (with subclasses like Accepted, Rejected, Published, etc.), while ekaw:Workshop Paper is a specific subclass of ekaw:Paper. edas:Paper is strictly more general than ekaw:Workshop Paper, so the relation is subsumes.

The cmt 'email' property captures a person's email address, while the edas 'has Last Name' property captures a person's surname/family name. These are distinct attributes with no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated.

confOf's 'ends on' applies to Event and records when an event ends (e.g., a conference end date), while iasted's 'done till' applies to Deadline and records the date by which a deadline task must be completed. These are different relations: one marks the end of an event, the other marks a due date for a submission or task. Their domains (Event vs Deadline) and intended meanings do not coincide.

Tutorial in iasted is a type of academic activity/lecture (a session or event where a tutorial is given), situated under Activity > Conference activity > Lecture. Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes the conference, situated under Person with children like General Chair, Program Chair, etc. One is an event/activity, the other is a person role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

These properties connect entirely different domain/range pairs. 'hasRating' links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (assigning a review score to a paper), while 'is_used_for' links an Item to an Activity or Money (indicating what an item is used for or its monetary value). They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Modelling is a research activity (e.g., building mathematical or computational models), while Organizing Committee member is a person role in conference organization. They belong to completely different domains (activity vs. person) and share no semantic overlap.

Entity A is a class representing an accepted paper/contribution (a document artifact that passed review). Entity B is a class representing a specific review rating value ('Accept If Room') used by reviewers to rate submissions. They belong to entirely different categories: A classifies the contribution itself, while B classifies a rating assigned during the review process. Despite the superficial similarity of 'accept' in their names, they denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Venue Place in edas is a subclass of Place denoting a physical location where a conference is held. Hotel presenter in iasted is a subclass of Delegate, denoting a person (presenter staying at a hotel). One is a place, the other is a person/role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

iasted:Deadline is a general class for all kinds of deadlines (camera ready, notification, hotel reservation, registration, submission), while sigkdd:Deadline_Abstract_Submission is a specific deadline for abstract submission. The iasted:Deadline class subsumes the sigkdd:Deadline_Abstract_Submission class, as the latter is a specific instance/subclass of the former's broader concept.

Submitted Paper is a research paper submitted for review at a conference, while Bank transfer is a payment document representing a financial transaction. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Full day tour is a leisure activity held after a conference, while Conference hall is a physical place where a conference takes place. They belong to disjoint domains (activity vs. place) and share no instances.

Committee member (Conference) denotes a person serving on a conference organizing or program committee, with children like Chair and Co-chair, and properties linking to Committee. Agency Staff Member (ekaw) denotes staff of an external agency (e.g., sponsoring or partner organization), not a conference committee role. Despite both being subclasses of Person, their intended instances are disjoint: one is internal to the conference organization structure, the other is external agency personnel.

Conference Chair (cmt) is an administrative/leadership role responsible for overseeing the conference, whereas Presenter (ekaw) is a functional role for someone who presents a paper or talk. A Conference Chair need not present anything, and a Presenter need not chair the conference. Their instance sets do not meaningfully coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The cmt property `adjustBid` relates a Reviewer to a Bid (the reviewer adjusts their bid on a paper), whereas the ekaw property `reviewerOfPaper` relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (indicating that the reviewer is assigned to or reviews that paper). These are different relations: one concerns bidding behaviour, the other concerns the reviewer-paper assignment/review relation. They do not denote the same concept.

In cmt, Author is a person who submits and writes papers, a subclass of Person/Conference Member. In iasted, Form is a document type (subclass of Item > Document) with children like registration forms and author information forms. These are completely different categories—a person role versus a document artifact—with no overlap in intended instances.

cmt:User is a broad superclass covering all system users (Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while iasted:Lecturer is a highly specific subclass of Speaker/Author representing someone who gives a lecture at the conference. A Lecturer is a narrow role; a User is a general category. They do not share instances in the same way, and neither subsumes the other (not all Users are Lecturers, and a Lecturer in iasted is not necessarily a cmt:User since iasted models them as delegates/speakers, not system users).

confOf:Company is an organization (e.g., a corporate entity like a sponsor or employer), while edas:CommunicationTheoryTopic is a subject-area topic for paper classification. They share no instances and no semantic relationship.

A is 'Contribution 1th author' (first author of a conference contribution), a specific role within Regular author. B is 'Author of paper student' (a student author of a paper). These are not equivalent: A restricts by author order (first author), B restricts by author status (student). A's instances (first authors) may or may not be students, and B's instances (student authors) may or may not be first authors. B's parent 'Author' is more general than A, so A is subsumed by B's broader Author concept, but the two classes themselves have different restriction criteria and do not share the same intended instances.

confOf Administrative event is a broad organizational event category (subtypes: camera ready, reviewing, submission, registration of participants), while iasted Registration is a specific activity whose instances are delegates registering. They do not share instances: one is an event type, the other a registration act/participant record. No subsumption holds because Administrative event is not a kind of Registration nor vice versa.

Regular contribution in Conference is a written document (subclass of Conference document / Conference contribution) whose instances are papers or extended abstracts. Paper Presentation in edas is an academic event (subclass of Conference Event) at which a paper is presented. One is a document/artefact, the other is an event; their instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent.
Property A relates a Chair to a Committee they chaired, while property B relates a Contribution to the Author who wrote it. They connect completely different entities and express different relations.

In confOf, Participant is a broad class covering all conference attendees (with children Member, Regular, Student), while Author is a sibling of Participant under Person. In edas, Author is a specific role for a person who writes papers. A confOf Participant is more general than an edas Author: an Author is a kind of participant, but not every Participant is an Author. The two ontologies model the hierarchy differently (confOf places Author as a sibling of Participant, edas treats Author as a leaf role), so they are not equivalent. confOf's Participant subsumes edas's Author.

confOf:Country denotes a geographic entity (a country), used as the range of properties like hasCountry for Organization and Person. sigkdd:Person denotes a human participant in a conference (with subclasses Listener, Organizator, Speaker). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

TextualReviewQuestion in edas is a specific type of review question (a question posed to reviewers requiring a textual answer), sibling to NumericalReviewQuestion under ReviewQuestion. Review in iasted is a document artefact (a review document), child of Document, sibling to various conference documents like forms, invitation letters, and submission records. One is a question, the other is a document; they denote completely different things.

In ontology A, Conference denotes the actual conference event (with children like Conference volume and properties such as has a name). In ontology B, Conference state is a subclass of State, with siblings like Presenter state and Sponsor state, indicating it represents a state or phase of a conference rather than the conference itself. These are fundamentally different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf's Member is a participant registration category (sibling to Regular and Student), denoting a fee/discount status. ekaw's OC Member is an Organizing Committee member (with child OC Chair and siblings like PC Chair, Session Chair), denoting a functional role. These are different dimensions of conference participation, so they are not equivalent.

cmt:Paper is a document submitted for review (a written contribution with authors, reviewers, bids, decisions). edas:Call is a call for submissions/reviews (with deadlines, instructions, initiated by chairs). These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties are completely different. `hasLastName` is a datatype property from Person to string, capturing a person's surname. `is_used_by` is an object property from Item to Person, indicating that an item is used by a person. They have different domains, different ranges (string vs Person), different types (datatype vs object), and no semantic overlap.

The cmt 'hasDecision' property links a Paper to a Decision (acceptance/rejection outcome), while the iasted 'is_made_from' property links an Item to another Item (composition relation). These are completely different relations in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference part to a Conference volume (part-whole relation within a publication volume). Property B links a Place to a Conference Event (spatial location relation). They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and represent different relations (part-of vs. location-of), so they are unrelated.

In EKAW, Evaluated_Paper is a paper that has been reviewed and assigned a decision (parent Assigned_Paper, children Accepted/Rejected Paper). In SIGKDD, Abstract is a sibling of Paper and Review under Document, denoting the summary text of a submission. These are different kinds of entities: one is a paper in a specific workflow state, the other is a document type (the abstract artefact). They do not share instances, and neither subsumes the other.

Paper Presentation in edas is a subclass of Conference Event / Academic Event, denoting a presentation session where a paper is presented. Paper in sigkdd is a subclass of Document, denoting the written document itself. One is an event, the other is a document; they are disjoint kinds of entities, not equivalent, not in a subsumption relation, and only weakly related by association.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper (a document), representing the abstract portion of a conference paper. Test Only Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference submissions. These are completely different concepts: one is a document type, the other is a subject classification. No overlap in intended instances.

PC Member in ekaw is a committee member who reviews papers (path: Person > Possible Reviewer > PC Member, with children like PC Chair, Session Chair). Author in iasted is a person who writes papers (path through Delegate > Speaker > Author, with children like Lecturer, Tutorial speaker). These are distinct roles: a PC Member reviews papers, while an Author writes them. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear hierarchy.

Pending Paper (edas) classifies a paper by its review status (not yet processed), while Regular Paper (ekaw) classifies a paper by its type/content (a standard full paper as opposed to a demo, poster, or industrial paper). These are orthogonal classification dimensions: a regular paper can be pending, and a pending paper can be a regular paper. Their sibling sets confirm this—edas siblings are status-based (Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, etc.) while ekaw siblings are type-based (Demo, Poster, Industrial, Workshop, etc.). They do not denote the same concept.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. 'issues' connects a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a publisher publishes proceedings), while 'written By' connects a Contribution to an Author (who wrote the contribution). They share no common domain or range types and denote entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Both classes involve reviewing activities, but they are not equivalent. In cmt, Reviewer is a specialized role under Conference Member with specific review-assignment properties and a child Meta Reviewer. In edas, TPC Member is a broader committee role under Person that includes reviewing but also initiates calls and has Two Level Conference as a child. The edas ontology separately has a Reviewer class as a sibling of TPC Member, indicating TPC Member is not simply the same as Reviewer. The two overlap in reviewing function but differ in scope and hierarchy.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'employed By' links a Person to an Organization they work for, while 'is held before' links an Activity to a Time. They share no domain or range overlap and denote different relations in the conference domain.

These properties are completely unrelated. 'held In' is an object property relating an Event to its Location, while 'has amount_of' is a datatype property relating Money to an integer value. They have different domains, different ranges (object vs datatype), and serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain.

confOf:Conference is a top-level conference event (a whole conference), while ekaw:Poster_Session is a specific session within a conference where posters are presented. They are at different levels of granularity and denote different kinds of events.

confOf's Administrative event is a specific subtype of Event (covering camera-ready, registration, reviewing, submission events), whereas ekaw's Event is the top-level class for all events (scientific and social). Administrative event is strictly narrower than Event, so it is subsumed_by Event.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'rejected By' (domain Paper, range Administrator) indicates which administrator rejected a paper. 'submit' (domain Author, range Paper) indicates an author submitting a paper. They relate different entities in different directions and represent unrelated relationships in the conference domain.
Possible Reviewer is a person who can review papers (subclass of Person), while Value added tax is a monetary tax concept. They share no domain overlap whatsoever.

confOf:University is an organization that scholars study at, while iasted:Sponzorship is a monetary concept (child of Money, sibling of Fee/Tax/Tip). These denote completely different things with no overlap.

confOf Participant is a broad class covering all conference attendees (with subclasses Member, Regular, Student), while ekaw Presenter is a specific role for those who present papers. Every Presenter is a Participant, but not vice versa, so Participant subsumes Presenter.

These two properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. confOf:minChoice applies to Social event/Working event with range positiveInteger (likely a minimum number of choices or participants), while iasted:done_till applies to Deadline with range date (a completion date). They share no conceptual overlap in the conference domain.

confOf Contribution is a broad class covering papers, posters, and short papers, making it more general than ekaw Paper, which is a specific subclass of Document with specialized subtypes like Conference Paper, Demo Paper, etc. The two are not equivalent because Contribution includes non-paper items like posters, while ekaw Paper is strictly a paper document.

The property 'issues' in Conference relates a Publisher to the Conference proceedings it publishes, while 'held In' in ekaw relates an Event to the Location where it takes place. They connect completely different domain and range types and express different relations (publication vs. venue), so they are unrelated.

Conference www in ontology Conference is a document (subclass of Conference document) representing a conference website/URL. Conference days in iasted is a temporal entity (subclass of Time) representing the days on which a conference takes place, with children like Delegate and One conference day. One is a web document, the other is a time period; they share the word 'conference' but denote completely different concepts.

Tutorial in the Conference ontology is a conference part (an educational session), while Tip in iasted is a kind of Money (a financial amount). They belong to completely different domains and share no conceptual overlap.

confOf:Workshop is a type of academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Author_book_proceedings_included is a role/person (subclass of Author, sibling of Lecturer and various speaker types). One denotes an event, the other a person role; they share no instances and are not related.

In iasted, Publication is a kind of Item (a document/artefact like a book proceeding or CD proceeding). In sigkdd, Author is a person (under Person > Speaker) who writes papers and submits them. One is a published document, the other is a person who authors documents; they share no instance overlap and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The property 'done till' in iasted has domain Deadline and range date, representing the date by which a deadline is completed. The property 'End of conference' in sigkdd has domain Conference and range dateTime, representing when a conference ends. These properties relate to entirely different kinds of entities (a deadline vs. a conference) and capture different concepts, so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

Property A (has an organizing committee) links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee, while property B (technically Organises) links an Organisation to an event it technically organises. They differ in both domain and range types, and in directionality: A connects a conference to a committee, B connects an organisation to an event. They do not relate the same kinds of things in the same direction.

Personal History in edas is a container for an individual's past publications and reviews (a person-level record). Submission in iasted is a document submitted to a conference (with children like Final/Initial manuscript). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Paper is a written contribution submitted to a conference (subclass of Contribution, sibling of Poster and Short paper). edas:AntennasTopic is a subject-area classification (subclass of Topic, sibling of many other technical topics like CAD Topic, Cryptography Topic). They denote completely different kinds of things: a document versus a research topic.

In cmt, Acceptance is a Decision (the outcome of accepting a paper), whereas in iasted, Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal Deadline by which authors must be notified. One denotes a decision/outcome, the other a date; they do not share instances.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person, denoting people who are members of a conference (e.g., authors, reviewers, chairs). In the Conference ontology, Conference part is a structural component of a conference (with children Track, Tutorial, Workshop), not a person. These are completely different concepts despite the superficially similar labels.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and represent different concepts. In cmt, 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (the administrator finalizes paper assignments). In sigkdd, 'submit' links an Author to a Paper (the author submits a paper). The domains (Conference vs Author) and ranges (Administrator vs Paper) are disjoint, and the relations denote different actions in the conference workflow.

Entity A is a conference document providing information for participants (e.g., logistics, venue, accommodation), while entity B is a subject topic in the domain of security. They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote unrelated concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. In cmt, 'detailsEnteredBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details. In iasted, 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item they prepare. These are different relations with no overlap in the conference domain.

Communication Theory Topic is a subject-area topic for conference papers (a subclass of Topic alongside Communications Topic, Computer Networks Topic, etc.), while Transport vehicle is a physical item (subclass of Item with children Car, Shuttle bus, Taxi, Van). They denote completely different categories with no overlap in the conference domain.

Property A (has_parts) goes from Conference volume to Conference part, expressing that a volume has parts. Property B (partOfEvent) goes from Event to Event, expressing that an event is part of another event. They operate in opposite directions (whole-to-part vs part-to-whole) and over different entity types (Conference volume/part vs Event/Event). They are not equivalent, and since one is not a generalization of the other, they are unrelated.

These properties are completely different. hasSurname is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's family name). is_used_by is an object property from Item to Person (indicating a person uses an item). They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Session Chair is a person who chairs a session (organizational/administrative role), while Speaker is a person who presents a talk. These are distinct conference roles: a session chair moderates a session, whereas a speaker delivers content. They do not coincide in intended instances, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of things: ekaw:writtenBy links a Document to the Person who authored it, while sigkdd:pay links a Person to a Registration fee. They have no overlap in domain, range, or meaning.

In cmt, Co-author is a Person (subclass of Author) who co-writes a Paper. In the Conference ontology, Regular_author is a subclass of Conference_contribution (a document), not a person. The two entities belong to fundamentally different ontological categories: one is a person/agent, the other is a document/artifact. Despite the superficially similar label, they do not denote the same concept.

Associated Chair is a person role in a conference committee (subclass of Chairman/Person in cmt), while Presenter university is a physical place/building where a presenter is affiliated (subclass of Building/Place in iasted). They belong to entirely different hierarchies (person vs. place) and share no instances.

A is a class denoting a contribution (paper) that has been accepted, while B is a class denoting a review rating value indicating rejection. They are from entirely different parts of the domain hierarchy and do not share instances.

Committee member is a subclass of Person denoting people who serve on committees, with children Chair and Co chair. MeetingRoomPlace is a subclass of Place denoting physical locations. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap.

Entity A is a datatype property linking 'Important dates' to a 'date' value, representing the deadline for camera-ready paper submission. Entity B is an object property linking 'Author' to 'Paper', representing the act of an author submitting a paper. They have different domains, different ranges (date vs. Paper), and different meanings (a deadline date vs. a submission action). They are unrelated.

Chairman in cmt is a person who leads a committee or conference (subclass of Person, with children like Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair). Deadline in iasted is a temporal entity (subclass of Time) representing submission/registration deadlines. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are conference events involving presentations, but they are not equivalent. A 'Talk Event' in EDAS is a specific kind of academic event focused on talks (with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk, Paper Presentation), while a 'Session' in EKAW is a broader organizational unit of a conference (with children like Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, Regular Session, Workshop Session). A Session is a time-slot container that may contain multiple talks/presentations, whereas a Talk Event is the individual presentation event itself. They overlap conceptually in the conference domain but denote different levels of granularity — a Session subsumes or relates to Talk Events rather than being equivalent to them.

confOf:Regular is a class representing a person/participant who is a regular (non-student, non-member) attendee, sitting under Person > Participant. sigkdd:Registration_SIGKDD_Member is a class representing a registration fee category for SIGKDD members, sitting under Fee > Registration_fee. One denotes a type of person, the other a type of fee. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The property 'held In' in ekaw specifically relates an Event to the Location where it is held. The property 'is connected with' in iasted is a much more general relation connecting Activities or Persons to Items or Places. They differ in domain (Event vs Activity/Person), range (Location vs Item/Place), and intended meaning. 'held In' denotes a specific spatial hosting relation, while 'is connected with' is a broad, generic association. They are not equivalent, and neither clearly subsumes the other given the mismatched domain/range sets.

Entity A is a specific research topic (Satellite and Space Communications) under Topic, representing a subject area for conference submissions. Entity B is an award (Best Applications Paper Award) under Award, representing a prize given at a conference. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties operate on different domains and ranges. In EDAS, 'is Initiated By' links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to organizers (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). In IASTED, 'is given by' links an Activity or Item to a Person. A Call is not the same as an Activity or Item, and the sets of possible range values (specific committee roles vs. generic Person) differ. The intended meaning of each property does not coincide, so they are not equivalent; nor is there a clear subsumption relationship.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has_a_commtitee' links a Conference volume to a Committee, while 'write' links a Person to an Item (e.g., a paper). They have different domains, different ranges, and different meanings in the conference domain.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities in different directions. 'author Of' (ekaw) links a Person to a Document they authored (Person -> Document), while 'is needed for' (iasted) links an Item to a Person who needs it (Item -> Person). They do not share the same domain, range, or semantic meaning; one is about authorship, the other about a requirement/need relation.

A Presenter is a conference participant who presents (a paper, demo, etc.); it is a sub-class of Person. B Worker non speaker is a sub-class of Non speaker, which is a sub-class of Delegate, and the whole chain is under Place > Building > Conference building, so it is a kind of delegate who does not give a talk. The two classes are almost disjoint in meaning (presenter vs. non-speaker) and also live under very different hierarchies (Person vs. Place/Delegate).

Paper Abstract in cmt is a summary of a research paper submitted for review, while Hotel registration form in iasted is an administrative form for hotel booking at a conference venue. They share the distant ancestor Document but denote completely different artefacts with no overlap in intended instances.

hasCostCurrency is a datatype property from Sponsorship to string (the currency of a sponsorship cost), while heldIn is an object property from Event to Location (where an event takes place). They relate entirely different domain/range pairs and denote completely different relations.

The cmt 'reject Paper' property relates an Administrator to a Paper that is being rejected, while the sigkdd 'presentationed by' property relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics; one concerns paper rejection and the other concerns presentation authorship.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (indicating when an activity occurs relative to some time point). 'notification until' relates an Author to a Deadline (Author notification) (indicating the notification deadline for an author). They connect different entity types in different directions and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

The confOf 'remark' property attaches an arbitrary comment or note to a Contribution (a submitted paper), whereas the edas 'has Submission Instructions' property attaches procedural submission instructions to a Call (a call for papers). They have different domains (Contribution vs Call), different intended meanings, and do not overlap in the conference domain.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the chair of the entire conference, a specific leadership role, while Organizing Committee member (sigkdd) is a member of the organizing committee. These are distinct roles: a conference chair is not the same as an organizing committee member, and neither subsumes the other in a clear hierarchy.

Company in confOf is a type of organization (e.g., a corporate entity), while Renting in iasted is an activity that occurs before a conference. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Reviewed contribution is a written academic paper that has been peer reviewed, while Money is a financial entity with subclasses like Fee, Tax, and Tip. They belong to completely different domains (academic documents vs. financial resources) and share no conceptual overlap.

The two properties are completely different in nature and purpose. 'has_short_title' is a datatype property from confOf that assigns a string-valued short title to social/working events. 'go_through' is an object property from iasted that relates an Item to an Activity (indicating that an item goes through some activity). They differ in type (datatype vs. object property), domain (Social_event/Working_event vs. Item), range (string vs. Activity), and semantic meaning. There is no alignment relationship between them.

A Conference participant is a person who attends a conference (subclass of Person), while an Excursion is a social event (subclass of Conference Event). One is a person, the other is an event; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

The confOf 'writes' property links an Author to a Contribution (the paper they authored), while the sigkdd 'obtain' property links an Author to an Award. These are different relations in the conference domain: authoring a paper is not the same as obtaining an award, and their ranges (Contribution vs Award) are distinct concepts.

In cmt, Review is a peer-review document written by a Reviewer for a Paper, with properties like write Review and written By. In iasted, Submission is a document submitted to organizers (e.g., Final manuscript, Initial manuscript), not a review. The iasted ontology has a separate sibling class 'Review' for that concept. These are structurally and semantically different: one is a review document, the other is a submitted manuscript. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Conference Venue Place in edas denotes a physical place where conference events are held (a venue), sibling to accommodation, dining, and meeting-room places. Trip city in iasted denotes a city associated with a trip (e.g., a city visited during a trip), sibling to conference city, presenter city, and sponsor city. One is a venue/place, the other is a city tied to a trip; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither subsumes the other.

The confOf 'abstract' is a datatype property from Contribution to string, representing the abstract text of a contribution. The ekaw 'heldIn' is an object property from Event to Location, representing where an event takes place. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The property 'writes' in confOf relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'pay' in sigkdd relates a Person to a Registration fee. These are completely different relations in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Both classes represent a Workshop in the conference domain. Despite different positions in their respective class hierarchies (confOf places it under 'Working event' alongside Conference and Tutorial, while edas places it under 'Academic Event' alongside Organizational Meeting, Paper Presentation, and Talk Event), both denote the same concept: a workshop event at a conference. The different sibling structures reflect different modeling choices for event taxonomies, not different intended meanings of Workshop itself.

The two properties have incompatible domains and ranges and describe different relations. In iasted, 'is paid with' goes from Money to Item (money is used to pay for an item). In sigkdd, 'pay' goes from Person to Registration fee (a person pays a registration fee). They are not inverses of each other either, since the iasted property relates Money to Item, not Person to Fee. No clear equivalence, subsumption, or overlap holds.

Author in cmt is a person who writes or submits papers, a subclass of Person/Conference Member. Place in sigkdd is a physical location such as a conference hall, hotel, or office. These denote completely different categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A (cmt:date) is a datatype property with domain Conference and range date, representing when a conference takes place. Property B (Conference:has_a_location) is a datatype property with domain Conference volume and range string, representing the location of a conference volume. These denote completely different relations (temporal vs. spatial), so they are unrelated.

These properties have different domains and ranges and represent different relationships. In cmt, 'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer is assigned to review the paper). In sigkdd, 'submit' links an Author to a Paper (indicating the author submits the paper). They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

Property 'reviews' in the Conference ontology relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution (a reviewer reviewing a paper), while 'is paid in' in the iasted ontology relates Money to a Building (the currency in which a fee is paid at a venue). These are completely different relations with disjoint domains and ranges, and no semantic overlap.

Tutorial is a conference part where participants receive instruction, while Plenary lecture is a lecture delivered to all attendees. They are distinct concepts: a tutorial is not a plenary lecture and vice versa. In the iasted ontology, Tutorial is even a sibling of Plenary_lecture under Lecture, confirming they are different types of activities.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. Silver Supporter in sigkdd is a subclass of Sponzor, denoting a sponsor at a particular support level. These are disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate Paper to fundamentally different things: 'accepted By' links a paper to the Administrator who accepted it (an acceptance decision/agent), while 'has Review' links a paper to a Review artifact. They connect Paper to disjoint ranges (Administrator vs Review) and represent different relationships in the conference workflow.

In confOf, Poster is a subclass of Contribution, i.e., a type of submitted scientific artefact (a poster paper). In ekaw, Poster_Session is a subclass of Session under Event, i.e., a scheduled conference session where posters are presented. One denotes a document/contribution type, the other denotes an event/session; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

A's 'Registration fee' is the general fee for conference registration (parent of various attendee-type fees). B's 'Registration Student' is a specific student registration fee. They are at different levels of generality and do not coincide in intended instances.

In cmt, 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of 'Author' that specifically excludes reviewers, making it a narrower concept than edas 'Author', which is a general author class (parent of Presenter, sibling of Reviewer). The cmt class denotes a proper subset of authors—those who are not also reviewers—so it is subsumed by the edas Author class.

Conference volume in the Conference ontology denotes a conference edition/event with committees, contributions, tracks, and important dates. Building in iasted is a physical structure (place) where people stay or meet. These are fundamentally different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (i.e., the set of papers accepted into a proceedings volume). Property B links a Paper to its Reviews. These are different relations: one connects a container/volume to its constituent papers, the other connects a paper to its reviews. The domains (Conference volume vs. Paper) and ranges (Conference contribution vs. Review) are distinct, and the relations themselves denote different things.

Paper Full Version is a full-length manuscript submitted for review, while Best Applications Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in instances.

In edas, Reviewer is a subclass of Person — the human who performs reviewing. In sigkdd, Review is a subclass of Document — the written review artefact itself. These are fundamentally different categories (agent vs. artefact), so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

Although both classes share the label 'Presentation', they denote different concepts. In the Conference ontology, Presentation is a subclass of Conference contribution (a document/artefact like a paper or poster) and is something an active participant gives. In the iasted ontology, Presentation is a subclass of Conference activity (an event/activity like a cocktail reception, coffee break, or lecture). One is a contribution/document, the other is a scheduled activity; their instances do not coincide.

The property 'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'has Email' captures a person's email address. Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, but they denote completely different attributes of a person and do not coincide.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations. 'need' (iasted) links Person to Item, indicating something a person requires. 'presentationed by' (sigkdd) links Document to Speaker, indicating who presented a document. The domains (Person vs Document), ranges (Item vs Speaker), and intended meanings are disjoint, so no equivalence, subsumption, or overlap holds.

Paper Author is a person who writes a paper, while Best Student Paper Supporter is a sponsor who supports a best student paper award. They belong to disjoint hierarchies (Person vs Sponzor) and denote completely different roles in the conference domain.

Review in Conference is a document containing reviews of contributions, while Programme Brochure in ekaw is a promotional document listing conference events. They are different kinds of conference documents with no overlap in intended instances.
Program committee is a committee that reviews conference papers, while University is an educational organization. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

cmt's ConferenceMember is a broad superclass encompassing authors, chairs, PC members, and reviewers—any person with a formal conference role. confOf's Member sits under Participant and has only Regular and Student as subclasses, suggesting it denotes a narrower category of conference attendee (e.g., a registered participant with a membership tier). Thus ConferenceMember is more general than Member; they are not equivalent.

Contribution 1th author is a class representing the first author of a conference contribution (a person role), while Two Level Conference is a class representing a type of conference event. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes represent types of conference speakers, but they denote different roles. 'Tutorial speaker' in iasted is a specialized author who presents a tutorial, while 'Invited Speaker' in sigkdd is a speaker invited to give a talk. A tutorial speaker may or may not be an invited speaker, and vice versa. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

ekaw:Location is a geographic/physical place where an Event is held (domain of heldIn/LocationOf). sigkdd:ACM_SIGKDD is the organizing body (a committee/association) that designs deadlines, holds conferences, and searches for sponsors. One is a place, the other is an organization; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

The property 'has Call' in edas relates an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., Call for Papers), whereas 'hold' in sigkdd relates ACM SIGKDD to a Conference it holds. These are different relations: one is about issuing a call, the other about organizing/holding a conference. They do not denote the same relation in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a document submitted to a conference with authors, reviewers, bids, and decisions. In iasted, Money is a financial entity with fees, sponsorships, taxes, and tips, paid by persons for activities/items. These classes share no instances and occupy completely different parts of the domain (academic documents vs. financial amounts).

These properties operate in completely different domains. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference (paper-review domain), while 'is held after' links an Activity to a Time (event-scheduling domain). They share no semantic overlap.

The ekaw 'references' property denotes a relation where one document cites or refers to another document, while the iasted 'give' property denotes a Person presenting or giving an Activity or Item. These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and share no semantic overlap.

Taxi is a transport vehicle (Item > Transport vehicle > Taxi) in the iasted ontology, while Listener is a person who attends a talk (Person > Listener) in the sigkdd ontology. They belong to completely disjoint domains (vehicles vs. conference attendees) and share no instances.

In the sigkdd ontology, Abstract and Paper are sibling classes under Document, meaning they are distinct concepts: an Abstract is a summary of a paper, while a Paper is the full document. In edas, Paper is the main document class with subclasses like Accepted/Rejected Paper. Since sigkdd explicitly separates Abstract from Paper, they denote different things and are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Submission in iasted is a class representing a submitted document (a subtype of Document with children like Final manuscript and Initial manuscript). Deadline Abstract Submission in sigkdd is a temporal deadline concept (subtype of Deadline) representing the date by which abstracts must be submitted. One denotes a document/artefact, the other a point in time; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee (organizational structure), while property B links an Author to a Contribution (authorship). They relate completely different domain and range types with no semantic overlap.

confOf 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (the author writes a paper). ekaw 'presentationOfPaper' links an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract (the presentation presents a paper). These are entirely different relations: one connects authors to their written works, the other connects presentation events to the papers being presented. No subsumption or overlap.

Paper Abstract is a short textual summary of a paper (a document artefact), whereas Cd proceening is a publication medium (a CD containing proceedings). They belong to different branches of their ontologies and denote different kinds of entities.

In iasted, 'Payment document' is a specific document type (parent: Document; children: Bank transfer, Cheque) used for payment-related artefacts. In sigkdd, 'Document' is a general class with children Abstract, Paper, Review, tied to presentations and deadlines. The iasted 'Payment document' is a leaf-level specialisation, not the same as the sigkdd general 'Document' class, and there is no evidence the sigkdd Document encompasses payment documents. They denote different concepts at different levels of generality with no clear overlap in intended instances.

Both properties relate a person-like entity to a written artefact, but they are not equivalent. In cmt, co-writePaper specifically links a Co-author to a Paper, whereas in ekaw, authorOf links a Person to a Document. The ekaw authorOf is broader in both domain (Person vs Co-author) and range (Document vs Paper), and it denotes primary authorship rather than co-authorship. They overlap in extension but neither subsumes the other cleanly (a Co-author is a Person, but a Paper is a Document, so the properties are cross-cutting), making 'related' the most accurate relation.

CAD Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference papers (e.g., antennas, communication theory, computer architecture). Card in iasted is a subclass of Item, representing a physical or financial item like a credit card. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties operate in completely different domains. In Conference, 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (i.e., a review document is about a paper). In sigkdd, 'searched by' links a Sponzor to ACM SIGKDD (i.e., a sponsor is searched/identified by the ACM SIGKDD organization). The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different, so the properties are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains and meanings: 'has the last name' applies to a Person and records a surname, while 'has Phone' applies to Contact Information and records a phone number. They do not relate the same kinds of things and are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

In ekaw, Session Chair is a person who chairs a session, a role under Conference Participant/PC Member. In iasted, IASTED non member is a delegate who is not an IASTED member, a membership-status classification under Delegate. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a functional role, the other is a membership status. They do not share instances in the intended interpretation and neither subsumes the other.

An Organizational Meeting is a type of event (a meeting that takes place), while an Organizing Committee is a group of people. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities despite both relating to conference organization.

confOf's Science Worker is a broad category of persons (sibling to Author, Scholar, Participant, etc.), while iasted's Worker lecturer is a highly specific subclass of Lecturer under Speaker > Author. They occupy very different positions in their respective hierarchies and do not denote the same concept.

Credit card in iasted is a financial instrument (Item > Card > Credit card), while Author of paper in sigkdd is a person role (Person > Speaker > Author > Author of paper). These denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Trip in confOf is a social event (e.g., excursion) under Event > Social event, while Tax in iasted is a monetary amount (e.g., departure tax, VAT) under Money. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest exists between a person and a document), while hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (assigning a rating to a paper). They connect different entity types in different directions and serve entirely unrelated purposes in the conference domain.

cmt's Preference is a value class representing a bid/interest level (e.g., want to review, do not want to review), not a person. ekaw's Possible_Reviewer is a subclass of Person who could serve as a reviewer. They denote entirely different concepts: one is a preference value, the other is a person role.

Conference Member in cmt is a person who belongs to a conference (subclass of Person, with subclasses like Author, Reviewer, Chair). Place in iasted is a physical location (with subclasses like Building, Conference hall, Hotel room). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference announcement is a document type (child of Conference document, sibling of Call for paper, Review, etc.), while Full day tour is an activity (child of Activity after conference). One is a textual artefact, the other is a social/event activity; they share no instances and no subsumption relationship.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a person who chairs the conference, sitting under Person > Chairman. Program Committee (sigkdd) is a committee (a group/organization), sitting under Committee. One is an individual role/person, the other is a collective body. They share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Early paid applicant is a person who registered early and paid for conference attendance. Program Committee is a committee organizing the conference program. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization, denoting a corporate entity (e.g., a sponsoring company). iasted:Sponsor_company_house is a subclass of Building under Place, denoting a physical building/location associated with a sponsor. One is an organization, the other is a building; they denote different categories of things and are not equivalent.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In ontology A, 'has_been_assigned_a_review_reference' links a submitted contribution (or topic) to a review preference, capturing the assignment of a review preference to a paper. In ontology B, 'is_given_by' links an activity or item to a person, indicating who performs or provides that activity/item. The domains and ranges are disjoint in meaning, and the relations denote different aspects of the conference domain.

Camera Ready event is a temporal/administrative event in the conference workflow (preparing final versions of accepted papers), while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They denote completely different categories of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In cmt, hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject), while in Conference, has_a_publisher links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. They share no common domain or range, and no subsumption or overlap exists.

The cmt property 'enter Conference Details' has domain Administrator and range Conference, representing an administrator entering conference details. The sigkdd property 'presentation' has domain Speaker and range Document, representing a speaker presenting a document. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (has_an_abstract) links a paper/poster/presentation to its Abstract. Property B (presentationOfPaper) links an Individual Presentation to a Paper or Abstract. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions: A connects a written work to its abstract, while B connects a presentation event to the paper/abstract it presents. These are distinct relations in the conference domain.

A Plenary lecture is a type of academic lecture/session activity at a conference, while Best Research Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

cmt:Acceptance is a Decision (acceptance vs rejection of a paper), while edas:WeekRejectRating is a Review Rating (a weak reject rating). They belong to different hierarchies and denote different concepts: one is a decision outcome, the other is a review score category.

Both are datatype properties indicating when something begins, but they differ in domain and range: confOf starts_on applies to Event with range string, while edas startDate applies specifically to Conference with range dateTime. They overlap in meaning but are not equivalent.

confOf:follows relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (event-to-event ordering), while iasted:is_held_after relates an Activity to a Time point (event-to-time). They differ in both the range type and the nature of the relation: one orders two events, the other anchors an event in time. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties relate entirely different entities. 'is submitted at' links a Conference contribution to the Conference volume where it is submitted, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present. They differ in domain, range, and meaning; neither subsumes the other.

Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing a person's email address. The labels 'has an email' and 'E mail' are synonymous in the conference domain, and the structural context (Person -> email -> string) is identical.

The two properties relate completely different entities in opposite directions. In cmt, 'member Of Conference' links a Conference Member to a Conference (person -> conference). In sigkdd, 'holded by' links a Conference to ACM SIGKDD (conference -> organization). They do not denote the same relation.

The cmt `title` property relates a Paper to its title string, while confOf `hasVAT` relates Social/Working events to a value-added-tax string. They concern completely different domains (document metadata vs. taxation of events) and have disjoint domains, so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Acceptance is a Decision (a subclass of Decision, sibling of Rejection) representing the outcome of accepting a paper. In iasted, Receiving manuscript is an Activity before conference (sibling of Accepting manuscript, Refusing manuscript, etc.) representing the administrative act of receiving a submitted manuscript. These are different concepts: one is a decision outcome, the other is a pre-conference activity. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

These properties have different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'rejectedBy' (cmt) links a Paper to the Administrator who rejected it, while 'relatedToPaper' (edas) links a Paper Presentation to the Accepted Paper it is about. They connect different entity types in different directions for different purposes.

Late Registered Participant (ekaw) denotes a conference participant who registered late, characterized by registration timing. Program Committee member (sigkdd) denotes a person serving on the program committee, characterized by a specific organizational role. These are distinct concepts: one is about registration status, the other about committee membership. They share only the general ancestor Person and have no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Scholar is a price-category person (a student/academic scholar, sibling of Author, Participant, etc., with property studyAt -> University). iasted:Reviewer is a delegate who reviews papers, a subclass of Speaker under the Person hierarchy. A scholar (student) and a reviewer are different roles; neither subsumes the other.

Test Only Topic is a subject-area topic under Topic in the EDAS ontology, while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award under Award in the SIGKDD ontology. They denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

In edas, 'Paper Presentation' is a conference event (subclass of Academic Event) where an accepted paper is presented. In iasted, 'Power Point presentation' is a document/artefact (subclass of Presentation under Activity > Conference activity), not the event itself. They denote different categories of things: an event vs. a presentation material/format.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. A's 'belong to a conference volume' links Important dates to a Conference volume, while B's 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are disjoint, so they are unrelated.

In Conference, Organization is a general class for organizations. In confOf, University is a specific kind of organization (a subclass of Organization). Every university is an organization, but not every organization is a university (e.g., companies, institutes). Thus Organization is more general than University, so Organization is subsumed_by University in the sense that the Conference class is broader. The relation is subsumed_by.

Sponzorship in iasted is a monetary concept (child of Money, sibling of Fee, Tax, Tip), representing the financial support arrangement itself. Silver Supporter in sigkdd is a specific sponsor category/role (child of Sponzor, sibling of Gold/Bronze/Platinum Supporter), representing an entity that provides sponsorship at a particular tier. One is a financial transaction/amount, the other is a sponsor role; they denote different kinds of things.

The two properties relate completely different entities in different directions. 'was a committee chair of' links a Chair to a Committee they presided over, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presented it. They share no common domain or range types and denote unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

Property A (reviews) has domain Review and range Reviewed contribution, meaning it links a review to the paper it reviews. Property B (reviewerOfPaper) has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper, meaning it links a reviewer to the paper they review. These are different relations: one connects a review document to a paper, the other connects a person to a paper. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumer of the other.

Slide Set in edas denotes presentation slides, a distinct artefact from Paper in ekaw which represents a written academic contribution. They share the parent Document but have different intended instances, different siblings, and no overlap in meaning.
Review is a conference document (peer review of a paper), while Value added tax is a monetary tax. They share no domain overlap whatsoever.

Meeting Room Place in edas denotes a place where meetings are held (e.g., conference sessions, committee meetings), a sibling of Conference Venue Place, Accommodation Place, and Dining Place. Double hotel room in iasted is a specific type of hotel room (a lodging/accommodation). A meeting room is not a hotel room; they serve different purposes. The two classes do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

confOf 'Submission event' is an administrative event representing the overall submission process/activity, whereas sigkdd 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a specific deadline date for abstract submissions. One is an event/activity, the other is a temporal deadline; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting a paper to a conference), while expertOn relates a Member PC to a Topic (the expertise area of a program committee member). They share no semantic overlap.

These properties have completely different domains and meanings. In cmt, 'assignReviewer' relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (the act of assigning a reviewer to a paper). In edas, 'isReviewHistoryOf' relates a PersonalReviewHistory object to a Reviewer (linking a review history record to the reviewer it belongs to). They connect different kinds of entities and represent different relationships, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

In edas, 'Conference' denotes the academic conference event itself (with properties like paper due dates, topics, members, countries, and subtypes like Single/Two Level Conference). In iasted, 'Conference hotel' is a physical building (a Place > Building) where conference attendees stay. These are completely different concepts: one is an academic event, the other is a lodging venue. They share the word 'Conference' but denote unrelated entities in the domain.

Both properties express the authorship relation: confOf's 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author, while iasted's 'is writen by' links an Item to a Person. In the conference domain, Contribution and Item are closely overlapping document/artefact concepts, and Author is a sub-type of Person. The relation direction is identical (document -> author/person), and the labels are near-synonymous ('written By' vs 'is writen by'). The slight domain/range narrowing on the confOf side (Author vs Person) is not enough to block equivalence of the relation itself.

Entity A is a topic about computer networks switching (a subject classification under Topic), while entity B is a physical computer device (an audiovisual equipment item). They denote completely different concepts despite both containing the word 'Computer'.

The cmt 'submit Paper' property relates an Author to a Paper (an author submits a paper artifact). The sigkdd 'submit until' property relates a Document to a Deadline (a document has a submission deadline).
