Mobile Computing Topic is a subject-area topic under Topic in edas (alongside Antennas, Cryptography, etc.), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of Award in sigkdd. They belong to completely different conceptual hierarchies and denote entirely different things in the conference domain.

Topic in the Conference ontology denotes a subject area or theme (e.g., a research topic), as evidenced by properties linking it to conference parts, tracks, and review preferences. Individual Presentation in EKAW is a scientific event where a paper is presented (parent: Scientific Event; children: Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The property `initiates` in edas relates conference roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call (e.g., call for papers), while `heldIn` in ekaw relates an Event to a Location where it takes place. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships in the conference domain.

Property A relates a Committee to the Conference volume it was a committee of, while property B relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give. The domains (Committee vs Person), ranges (Conference volume vs Activity/Item), and overall semantics are completely different, so these properties do not denote the same relation.

In ontology A, Presentation is a Conference contribution (a talk/event where someone presents), with children like Invited talk and siblings like Poster and Regular contribution. In ontology B, Document is a written artefact with children Abstract, Paper, and Review. A Presentation is an oral delivery event, not a document; the two classes have disjoint intended instances.

The cmt 'adjusted By' property links a Bid to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer adjusted a bid), while the sigkdd 'pay' property links a Person to a Registration fee (indicating payment of registration). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics; they share no meaningful overlap in the conference domain.

In EDAS, 'Conference' is the top-level conference event with properties like paper deadlines, country, topics, and members, and it has subtypes like Single/Two Level Conference. In EKAW, 'Conference_Session' is a specific session within a conference (a child of Session, sibling of Demo/Poster/Regular/Workshop sessions). These are at very different levels of granularity: a conference vs. a session within a conference. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Paper (a document artefact, the abstract of a paper), whereas in edas 'Radio Communications Topic' is a subclass of Topic (a subject-area classification such as antennas, CAD, cryptography). They belong to disjoint hierarchies and denote completely different kinds of entities, so they are unrelated.

A is the class Event (conferences, sessions, social events) in ekaw, with properties like heldIn, organisedBy, partOfEvent. B is the class Speaker (a person who presents) in sigkdd, a subclass of Person with children Author and Invited_Speaker. These are completely different domain concepts: an event vs. a person role. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.

Property A (has_a_review) relates a reviewed contribution to the Review it receives (domain: Reviewed contribution, range: Review). Property B (hasReviewer) relates a Paper to the Possible Reviewer assigned to review it (domain: Paper, range: Possible Reviewer). They connect different kinds of entities in different directions: one points to the review artefact, the other to the reviewer person. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

cmt:Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference (subclass of Document, with authors, reviewers, bids, decisions). confOf:Social_event is a non-academic gathering such as a banquet, reception, or trip (subclass of Event, with location, VAT, title). These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The cmt 'assignedTo' property assigns a Reviewer to a Paper for review. The Conference 'is_the_1th_part_of' property relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation as a constituent part. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Both classes represent the same concept: a published volume of papers from a conference. In ontology A, 'Conference proceedings' is a top-level class with properties like publisher, volume, ISBN, and name — all hallmarks of a proceedings publication. In ontology B, 'Conference Proceedings' is a subclass of Proceedings > Multi author Volume > Document, which is the standard classification for such publications. The labels are identical (modulo case), and the structural context (publisher, ISBN, volume properties in A; document hierarchy in B) confirms they denote the same entity in the conference domain.

Extended abstract is a short summary of work (a brief document type, sibling of Paper under Regular contribution), while Poster Paper is a full paper associated with a poster presentation. They are distinct document categories in the conference domain: an extended abstract is not a poster paper and vice versa. They share no clear subsumption relationship either.

Conference Event in edas denotes an event (academic or non-academic) with attendees, start/end dates, a location, and a programme. Building in iasted is a physical place (a subtype of Place) such as a conference hall, hotel, or airport. One is an event/activity, the other is a physical structure/location; they do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Session Chair in edas is a person role (subclass of Person) who chairs a session, while Workshop Session in ekaw is an event (subclass of Session). One is a person, the other is an event — they denote completely different things despite both containing the word 'Session'.

These are unrelated datatype properties. `has_a_degree` applies to a Review preference and takes an integer (likely a preference degree/rating), while `hasSurname` applies to a Person and takes a string surname. They relate different kinds of entities and have different ranges and meanings.

Author is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person), while Individual Presentation is a scientific event (subclass of Event) at which a paper is presented. They denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the person chairing the entire conference, while Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is the person chairing a tutorial event. These are distinct roles with different scopes in the conference organization domain; neither subsumes the other.

A Conference in confOf is an academic event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), whereas Presenter city in iasted is a geographic location (subclass of City, sibling of Conference city, Sponsor city, Trip city). These denote completely different categories of entities in the conference domain.

Review and Abstract are distinct document types in the conference domain. In ontology A, Review is a Conference document specifically for reviewing contributions, with properties linking it to Reviewed contribution. In ontology B, Abstract is a sibling of Review and Paper under Document, representing a summary of a paper. They denote different concepts: a review is an evaluation document, while an abstract is a summary document. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

Member registration fee is a specific registration fee for members attending the conference, while Sponzor fee is a fee paid by sponsors. These are distinct categories of fees in the conference domain - one is paid by attendees for registration, the other by sponsors for sponsorship. They share only the common parent Fee but denote different financial concepts.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'belong to a conference volume' links Important dates to a Conference volume, while 'need' links a Person to an Item. They share no common domain or range types and denote completely different relationships in the conference domain.

The cmt 'has Decision' property links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject), while the iasted 'is held in' property links an Activity to a Place or Time. They relate completely different kinds of entities in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

The two properties denote completely different relations. In confOf, 'expertOn' links a Program Committee member to a Topic they have expertise in. In sigkdd, 'notification_until' links an Author to a Deadline for author notification. They have different domains (Member PC vs. Author), different ranges (Topic vs. Deadline), and different intended meanings.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'has_authors' links a Conference document to a Person (the author of the document). In sigkdd, 'obtain' links an Author to an Award (an author receiving an award). They share no common domain or range types and denote different relations in the conference domain.

Conference www is a web document/resource identified by a URL, while Research Institute is an academic organisation. They denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Both classes denote the same concept of a Person in the conference domain. They share identical labels, overlapping properties (email, first name, last name), and their children represent various conference roles (authors, participants, committee members, reviewers, chairs). The children sets are complementary role specializations rather than evidence of different intended meanings, so the instances of both classes coincide.

The two properties operate in completely different parts of the conference domain. `addedBy` in cmt relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (indicating who added the PC member), while `parallel_with` in confOf relates two Administrative events (indicating scheduling overlap). They have different domains, different ranges, and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Extended abstract is a short conference contribution type (a document genre), while Assigned Paper is a paper that has been assigned to reviewers (a workflow state). They occupy different positions in their hierarchies and denote different concepts: one is about content type, the other about review-process status. No subsumption holds between them.

Committee member is a specific kind of person who serves on a committee, while Person in iasted is the general class of people (with children Delegate, Sponsor). Committee member is thus subsumed by Person.

hasSurname is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's family name), while writtenBy is an object property from Document to Person (indicating authorship of a document). They have different domains, ranges, types, and meanings, so they are unrelated.

cmt:assignedTo relates a Paper to the Reviewer it is assigned to for review. ekaw:hasPart is a generic mereological relation indicating that something has a part. These are fundamentally different relations: one is about assignment of papers to reviewers, the other is about part-whole relationships. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

logoURL is a datatype property from Conference to anyURI (a web address for a conference logo), whereas is_present_in is an object property from Person to Place/Time (indicating where/when a person is present). They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and meanings.

Student registration fee in iasted is a specific subclass of Registration fee (for students). Registration fee in sigkdd is the general class with children including Registration Student. So A is strictly more specific than B, hence subsumed_by.

Property A (has a name) applies to Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic, denoting the name of those organizational entities. Property B (has First Name) applies to Person and denotes a person's first name. The domains are disjoint and the intended meanings differ, so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other in the conference domain.

hasFirstName relates a Person to their first name (a given name), while E-mail relates a Person to their email address. These are distinct attributes with no overlap in intended meaning, despite both being datatype properties with domain Person and range string.

In ontology A, 'Review' is a general class of review documents (a subclass of Conference document). In ontology B, 'Neutral Review' is a specific subclass of 'Review' that sits alongside 'Positive Review' and 'Negative Review'. Thus A's Review is more general than B's Neutral Review, making A subsumed_by B is incorrect — rather B's Neutral Review is subsumed by A's Review. The correct relation is that A (Review) subsumes B (Neutral Review), i.e., B is subsumed_by A.

cmt:Paper is a scientific paper submitted for review and publication, with properties like has Author, has Decision, assigned To Reviewer, and children Paper Abstract / Paper Full Version. iasted:Mailing_list is a document type (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Payment document, etc.) representing a communication channel/list, not a scholarly paper. Despite both being subclasses of Document, they denote completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'is Written By' in edas specifically relates a Paper to its Author (authorship relation). The property 'is used by' in iasted relates an Item to a Person, which denotes usage rather than authorship. These are distinct semantic relations: one is about who wrote a document, the other about who uses an item. They do not coincide as the same relation in the conference domain.

Reception is a social event (e.g., welcome reception, banquet), while Full day tour is a post-conference excursion activity. They are different types of non-academic conference events with distinct purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties operate on completely unrelated domains and ranges. confOf:hasKeyword links a Contribution to a string keyword, while iasted:has_amount_of links Money to an integer amount. They share no conceptual overlap.

In cmt, Program Committee is an organizational body (committee) that has program committee members. In confOf, Scholar is a type of Person representing a price category (a scholar/discounted attendee). These are completely different concepts: one is a committee entity, the other is a person role. No overlap in intended instances.

Committee_member in the Conference ontology is a specific role a Person can hold (a member of a Committee), with siblings such as Reviewer, Conference participant, etc. Person in ekaw is the top-level class for all people. Every committee member is a person, but not every person is a committee member, so Committee_member is subsumed_by Person.

Multimedia Topic is a subject-area classification (a Topic) for conference submissions, while LCD projector is a physical audiovisual equipment item. They belong to entirely different parts of the domain hierarchy and share no instances.

Both classes denote speakers who give invited/plenary talks at a conference, so their instances overlap. However, a Plenary lecture speaker is a specific kind of invited speaker (one giving a plenary/keynote at the main conference), while an Invited Speaker is a broader category that could include speakers at sessions, tutorials, or other events. Neither class subsumes the other in the given hierarchies, so the best relation is related.

Both classes denote a conference event in the conference-organisation domain. In confOf, Conference is a subclass of Working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while in sigkdd it is the main conference object with properties like city, start/end dates, name, and a relation to ACM SIGKDD as organizer. Despite differences in modelling granularity, the intended instances coincide: both represent the conference event itself.

Reception is a social event (e.g., a gathering or party) in the conference organisation domain, while Speaker is a person who gives a presentation. They denote completely different categories of entities—an event versus a person—so they are unrelated.

Author is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person in edas), while Tax is a monetary amount (subclass of Money in iasted). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

has_a_URL is a datatype property from Conference www to string, recording a web address. heldIn is an object property from Event to Location, recording where an event takes place. They relate different kinds of things in different directions and have no overlap in intended use.

The two properties differ in both domain/range and direction. In EDAS, hasCountry links a Conference to a Country (the country where the conference is held). In EKAW, locationOf links a Location to an Event, expressing which event takes place at a location. They relate different kinds of entities (Country vs Location, Conference vs Event) and run in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other.

The property 'is Written By' in edas relates a Paper to its Author (paper -> author), while 'has Updated Version' in ekaw relates a Document to another Document (document -> document). They connect entirely different kinds of entities and express completely different relationships: authorship versus versioning. There is no overlap in meaning.

Double hotel room is a specific type of accommodation room within a hotel, while Hotel is the entire lodging establishment. They denote different kinds of entities at different granularity levels, and neither subsumes the other in the given hierarchies.

confOf:Conference is a class representing a conference event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). iasted:Author_cd_proceedings_included is a class representing a specific type of author (one whose paper is included in CD proceedings), nested deep under Person > Delegate > Speaker > Author. These denote completely different concepts: an event vs. a person role.

Property A (has_authors) links a Conference document to a Person (authorship). Property B (employedBy) links a Person to an Organization (employment). They have different domains, different ranges, and express completely different relationships with no overlap.

confOf:Workshop is a standalone working event (a full workshop, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). ekaw:Poster_Session is a session within an event where posters are presented, sibling of Workshop_Session and Demo_Session. They denote different kinds of scientific events and do not overlap in intended instances.

These properties differ in both structure and meaning. Property A ('is paid with') is an object property from Money to Item, indicating what item is used to make a payment. Property B ('Currency') is a datatype property from Registration fee to string, representing a currency name as a string value. They have different domains (Money vs Registration fee), different range types (object vs datatype), and different semantics: one links to a payment item object while the other holds a string label for currency.

In EKAW, Student is a subclass of Person, denoting a specific kind of person (a student). In SIGKDD, Person is the general class of all people (with subclasses Listener, Organizator, Speaker). Thus EKAW Student is strictly more specific than SIGKDD Person, so Student is subsumed_by Person.

confOf:Conference is an event (a conference event itself), while iasted:Worker_lecturer is a person role (a lecturer who is a worker). They are completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a leadership role responsible for overseeing the conference, sitting under Chairman. Invited speaker (Conference) is a person invited to give a talk, sitting under Conference contributor. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances: a conference chair is not necessarily an invited speaker, and vice versa.

Camera Ready Paper is a document (a finalized paper), while Submissions deadline is a temporal entity (a deadline). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

The two properties relate completely different concepts. In ontology A, 'has a review reference or expertise' links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference. In ontology B, 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present. The domains (Reviewer vs Speaker), ranges (Review expertise/preference vs Document), and overall semantics are entirely disjoint, so no equivalence, subsumption, or meaningful relation holds.

The iasted property 'is situated in' relates places (Building, City, Place) to other places (including State), expressing a spatial/location relationship. The sigkdd property 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper, expressing a submission action. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics; they share no overlap in the conference domain.

Registration form in iasted is a document (subclass of Form) that attendees fill out to register for a conference. Registration fee in sigkdd is a monetary amount (subclass of Fee) that a person pays to register. One is a physical/digital document, the other is a financial charge; they share the word 'registration' but denote completely different concepts.

confOf:Workshop is a scientific event (a type of working event, sibling of Conference and Tutorial). iasted:Presenter_house is a physical building where a presenter lives (child of Place > Building, sibling of Conference hotel, Conference airport, etc.). One is an event, the other is a physical location; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person, denoting a person who is a student. Best Applications Paper Award in sigkdd is a subclass of Award, denoting a specific award given for an applications paper. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf:Company is an organization (a company as a corporate entity), sibling of University under Organization. iasted:Bank_transfer is a kind of payment document (a financial instrument), sibling of Cheque under Payment document. One denotes a corporate organization, the other a payment document; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relationship.

Important dates is a specific container class for conference deadlines and milestone dates (abstract submission, camera-ready, acceptance, start/end), tied to a Conference volume. Time in iasted is a general temporal concept whose children include Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day, used as a range for when activities are held or items sent. The former is a structured set of conference-specific dates, not a general temporal entity; their intended instances do not coincide, and neither clearly subsumes the other.

Communication Theory Topic is a subject-area topic (a subclass of Topic, alongside Communications Topic, Cryptography Topic, etc.), while Organizing Committee is a committee role (a subclass of Committee, alongside Program Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee). These denote completely different concepts in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have different domains: A's 'has a location' applies to Conference volume (a publication/proceedings), while B's 'location' applies to Social event and Working event (physical gatherings). They relate location to fundamentally different kinds of entities, so they are not equivalent.

confOf's 'Short paper' is a type of conference contribution (a document submitted to a conference), while sigkdd's 'Best Student Paper Award' is an award given to a paper. They belong to completely different hierarchies (Contribution vs. Award) and denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

These properties relate different things in different directions. 'has Location' (edas) links a Conference Event to the Place where it occurs. 'holded by' (sigkdd) links a Conference to the organizing body ACM SIGKDD. The ranges differ (Place vs. ACM SIGKDD), and the relations are conceptually distinct: one denotes a venue/location, the other denotes an organizer/holder. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subsumption of the other.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In EDAS, hasMember links a Conference to a Person (conference membership). In SIGKDD, presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). The domains (Conference vs. Document), ranges (Person vs. Speaker), and intended meanings are distinct, so they are not equivalent, subsuming, or meaningfully related.

In the Conference ontology, 'Conference' denotes the main academic conference event/organization, with a child 'Conference volume' and a name property. In confOf, 'Social event' is a specific kind of Event (alongside Administrative event and Working event) with children like Banquet, Reception, and Trip, and properties about VAT, location, and choice limits. These denote completely different things: an academic conference vs. a social gathering within a conference. They share no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties have different domains and ranges and denote different relations. In cmt, 'addedBy' means an Administrator added a Program Committee Member (e.g., to the conference system or committee). In ekaw, 'writtenBy' means a Document was written by a Person. They relate different kinds of entities and express different actions (adding vs. authoring), so they are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

These properties operate on completely different domains and ranges. 'written By' links a Contribution to its Author, while 'is paid by' links Money to a Person. They denote different relations in the conference domain with no overlap in meaning.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'setMaxPapers' in cmt relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (likely setting a paper assignment limit for that PC member). 'is given to' in iasted relates an Item to a Person (indicating an item is given to someone). They connect different entity types in different directions with no semantic overlap.

The two properties operate in opposite directions and connect different domain/range pairs. Property A (has_a_track-workshop-tutorial_topic) goes from Conference part to Topic, while property B (isTopicOf) goes from Topic to Conference/Paper. They are not inverses of each other either, since A's domain is 'Conference part' (not Conference) and its range is only Topic, whereas B's range includes Paper in addition to Conference. The mismatch in both direction and the entities involved means these properties do not denote the same relation.

A Plenary lecture is a type of academic lecture/activity at a conference, while a Best Paper Awards Committee is a committee that selects best paper awards. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The confOf 'written By' property links a Contribution to its Author (paper -> author), while the sigkdd 'obtain' property links an Author to an Award (author -> award). They have opposite domain/range structures and denote completely different relations: authorship vs. award receipt.

Multimedia Topic is a subject-area classification (a kind of Topic) used to categorize papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing a conference. These are entirely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Review preference in the Conference ontology denotes a reviewer's preference for reviewing a particular topic or submission (with properties like degree, topic, reviewer), not a document. Review in iasted is a subclass of Document, i.e. an actual review artefact. These are different concepts with no direct alignment.

The cmt 'added By' property relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (a membership-tracking relation). The Conference 'has a program committee' property relates a Conference volume to its Program committee (an organizational-structure relation). They have different domains, different ranges, and denote entirely different relationships in the conference organization domain.

These properties denote completely different concepts. In cmt, 'reviewsPerPaper' is a datatype property with domain Conference and range int, representing the number of reviews required per paper. In confOf, 'reviewes' is an object property with domain Member PC and range Contribution, representing the relation that a PC member reviews a contribution. They differ in arity (datatype vs object property), domain, range, and intended meaning.

Paper Abstract in cmt is the abstract of a submitted Paper (sibling of Paper Full Version under Paper), whereas Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is the abstract of an Invited Talk (sibling of Tutorial Abstract under Abstract). They describe abstracts of completely different kinds of conference items, so they do not coincide.

The EKAW property 'technicallyOrganisedBy' (subproperty of 'organisedBy') relates an event to the organising entity (e.g., a person or organisation that technically organises it). The SIGKDD property 'presentationed_by' relates a Document to a Speaker (the person presenting it). These are different relations: one is about who organises an event, the other about who presents a document. They connect different kinds of subjects and objects with different semantics, so they are not equivalent, nor is one a subrelation of the other.

Organizer in the Conference ontology denotes a person or committee member who organizes the conference, whereas Organization in edas denotes an institutional entity (with subclasses like Academia Organization, Government Organization, Industry Organization, NGO) that can provide sponsorships. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an individual/role, the other is an institution/organization type.

The property 'occupy' in iasted relates a Person to a Building, City, or State (i.e., where the person is located or occupies), while 'pay' in sigkdd relates a Person to a Registration fee (i.e., a financial transaction). These are entirely different relations with disjoint ranges and unrelated semantics.

Entity A is a class denoting a conference document providing information for participants, sibling to Call for paper, Review, etc. Entity B is a specific topic (Cryptography) under a Topic hierarchy in the edas ontology. They belong to completely different hierarchies and denote entirely different concepts: one is a document type, the other is a subject-area topic. No subsumption or overlap relationship holds.

In EDAS, Workshop is a specific subclass of Academic Event (a leaf class with siblings like Paper Presentation and Talk Event). In EKAW, Scientific Event is a broad superclass whose children include Conference, Session, Track, and Workshop. Thus EKAW's Scientific Event is strictly more general than EDAS's Workshop, so Workshop is subsumed_by Scientific Event.

Both classes are top-level Event classes in the conference domain. confOf's Event has children Administrative event, Social event, Working event; ekaw's Event has children Scientific Event, Social Event. The overlap in children (Social event) and the shared role as the root event concept in a conference ontology indicate the same intended extension. The differing subtypes reflect modelling granularity rather than a different denotation.

confOf:Conference is an event (subclass of Working event, sibling of Tutorial/Workshop), whereas iasted:Presenter_house is a physical building (subclass of Place > Building, sibling of Conference hotel/airport). One denotes a conference event, the other a building where a presenter stays; they share no instances.

Entity A is a class denoting a written artefact (a contribution that has been accepted), while entity B is a class denoting an administrative event (the act/occurrence of submitting contributions). One is a document-like object, the other is an event; their instances do not coincide.

These properties denote completely different concepts. In cmt, 'reviewsPerPaper' is a datatype property with domain Conference and range int, representing the number of reviews assigned per paper. In the Conference ontology, 'reviews' is an object property with domain Review and range Reviewed contribution, linking a review to the contribution it reviews. They differ in type (datatype vs. object), domain, range, and intended meaning.

These properties differ in domain, range, and meaning. In EKAW, 'scientificallyOrganisedBy' links an event to the Academic Institution that scientifically organizes it. In SIGKDD, 'hold' links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference it holds. The domains (unspecified event vs. ACM SIGKDD), ranges (Academic Institution vs. Conference), and direction of the relationship are incompatible, so they are not equivalent.
hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (an offer to review), while hasTopic relates a Conference/Paper to a Topic (subject area). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Call for paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while CAD Topic is a subject-area topic (like Computer-Aided Design) used to classify papers. They share no instances and occupy entirely different positions in their respective ontologies.

A Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event involving travel (e.g., excursions or outings), while a Coctail reception in iasted is a reception/gathering activity. They are different kinds of conference activities with distinct purposes, and neither subsumes the other.

An External Reviewer in CMT is a person assigned to review a paper on behalf of another Reviewer, but who is not themselves a Reviewer. A Paper Author in EKAW is a person who authors a paper. These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one performs reviews, the other writes papers. They share only the common parent Person, but their intended instances do not coincide.

In confOf, Social event is a broad category of Event with children Banquet, Reception, and Trip. In edas, Reception is a specific leaf subclass under Social Event. Thus confOf:Social_event is strictly more general than edas:Reception, so the relation is subsumes.

Both are subclasses of Deadline, but they denote distinct points in the conference timeline. 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' is the deadline for submitting the final, accepted manuscript, while 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is the deadline for submitting an abstract prior to full paper submission. They occur at different stages and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Workshop in edas is a subclass of Academic Event, i.e. an event that takes place at a conference. Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a subclass of Document/Multi-author Volume/Proceedings, i.e. a published artefact. They denote completely different things (an event vs. a document), so they are unrelated.

Individual Presentation in EKAW is a scientific event where a paper is presented (e.g., Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial). Item in IASTED is a physical or informational object (Audiovisual equipment, Document, Publication, Transport vehicle, etc.). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

In ekaw, Proceedings is a document class (a multi-author volume containing conference papers). In iasted, Author_cd_proceedings_included is a subclass of Author (a person role), specifically an author whose work is included in CD proceedings. One denotes a document/artefact, the other a person/role; they share no instances and are not in a subsumption relation.

Property A (has Street) captures a street address, while property B (Nation) captures a country/nationality. They denote different attributes of a person/organization with no overlap in meaning, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or subsumed.

Pending Paper is a paper awaiting review/decision in the conference submission workflow, while Bank transfer is a payment document representing a financial transaction. They belong to completely different domain areas (paper review status vs. payment method) and share no meaningful semantic relationship.

Both classes denote conference participants who give talks, but they are not equivalent. In ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a direct subclass of 'Conference contributor' and specifically denotes a person invited to speak. In ontology B, 'Lecturer' is a subclass of 'Author' (itself under 'Speaker') and has subclasses like 'Student lecturer' and 'Worker lecturer', suggesting a broader category of any person who delivers a lecture at the conference, not necessarily one who is invited. The two concepts overlap (an invited speaker may be a lecturer) but their intended instances do not coincide.

The cmt property 'written By' relates a Review to the Reviewer who authored it, while the sigkdd property 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document they present. These properties connect entirely different domain and range types and express different relationships (authorship vs. presentation material), so they are unrelated.

Both classes denote the person who chairs the Organizing Committee (OC) of a conference. In cmt, 'Conference Chair' sits under Chairman and Conference Member, and in ekaw, 'OC Chair' (Organizing Committee Chair) sits under OC Member and Conference Participant. The cmt ontology uses 'Conference Chair' to refer to the chair of the conference's organizing body, which aligns with ekaw's 'OC Chair'. Both are specific roles for persons responsible for chairing the conference organization, and their hierarchical positions (subtypes of Person/Conference Participant) are consistent.

Banquet is a social event in confOf, while Audiovisual equipment is a physical item in iasted with children like Computer and LCD projector. These denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The cmt property hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Member (i.e., a person who is a member of the conference). The ekaw property inverse_of_partOf_7 is an inverse-part-of relation whose range is Event, relating events to their containing events. These are completely different relations: one denotes membership of a person in a conference, the other denotes mereological (part-whole) relationship between events. They share no semantic overlap.

Poster Paper is a type of document (a paper presented as a poster) in the ekaw ontology, while Registation deadline is a temporal concept (a deadline for registration) in the iasted ontology. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties differ in both domain and range: A's domain is Conference volume with range string (a textual location), while B's domain is Conference Event with range Place (an object). They relate different kinds of entities to different kinds of values, so they are not equivalent.

Property A captures the starting date of an important date (e.g., conference start), with domain Important dates and range date. Property B captures whether a participant registered early, with domain Participant and range boolean. They relate different entities and have incompatible ranges (date vs boolean), so they denote completely different relations.

The two properties relate different entities in different directions. `hasReviewer` links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (someone assigned to review the paper), while `presentationed_by` links a Document to a Speaker (someone presenting the document). Reviewers and speakers are distinct roles in the conference domain, and the relations capture different semantics.

Chair PC in confOf is a person chairing the Program Committee, whereas Webmaster in sigkdd is a specific organizing-role responsible for the conference website. These are distinct conference roles with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are datatype properties named 'hasEmail' with domain Person and range string, representing the same relation of associating an email address with a person in the conference domain. The additional domain (Contact Information) in edas is a related construct that does not change the core semantics of the property.

Mailing list in iasted is a specific kind of document (a communication channel/announcement list), while Paper in sigkdd is a scholarly submission document. They share the parent Document but denote completely different concepts in the conference domain. A mailing list is not a paper, nor is one more general than the other.

The ekaw property 'paper In Volume' relates a paper to a volume/proceedings in which it appears, while the iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., giving a presentation or item). These properties connect entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations, so they are unrelated.
Call_for_paper is a conference document announcing paper submissions, while AntennasTopic is a subject-area topic in EDAS. They denote completely unrelated concepts.

Conference:Paper denotes any regular contribution paper (encompassing accepted, rejected, etc.), while edas:RejectedPaper is a specific subclass of Paper whose instances have been rejected. Every rejected paper is a paper, but not every paper is rejected, so Conference:Paper is strictly more general than edas:RejectedPaper.

The two properties have incompatible domains, ranges, and directions. In edas, 'relates To' links a Document to an Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, or Person. In sigkdd, 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document. They connect entirely different kinds of entities and do not denote the same relation.

The cmt 'accept Paper' property relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of accepting a paper for publication). The Conference 'issues' property relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (the act of publishing proceedings). These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and denote different processes in the conference domain.

These classes denote completely different concepts. In edas, 'Powerline Transmission Topic' is a subclass of Topic, representing a subject area for conference papers (alongside other topics like Antennas, Cryptography, etc.). In iasted, 'Power Point presentation' is a subclass of Presentation (under Activity > Conference activity), representing a type of presentation format at a conference. One is a topic/subject classification; the other is a presentation method. They share no semantic relationship despite both containing the word 'Power'.

Property A (hasFirstName) relates a Person to their first name (a string), while property B (Currency) relates a Registration fee to its currency (a string). They have different domains (Person vs Registration fee) and denote completely different attributes in the conference domain; there is no overlap in meaning.

Submitted Paper is a document type (a paper submitted for review), while Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal deadline for booking accommodation. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Document vs. Time) and share no semantic relationship.

Review Rating in edas is a rating value (Accept/Reject/etc.) assigned to a paper, while Review in ekaw is a document written by a reviewer. They denote completely different concepts: a qualitative score vs. a written review document.

Both classes are named 'Place' and serve as the top-level spatial location concept in their respective conference ontologies. Both have subclasses representing specific conference-related locations (venues, rooms, accommodations, etc.) and both are used as the range of properties linking activities/events to their locations. The children differ in specificity but the intended instances (physical places where conference activities occur) coincide, making them equivalent in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. confOf:dealsWith relates a Contribution to a Topic it covers, while iasted:obtain relates a Person to an Item they receive. There is no overlap in the kinds of things being related or the direction of the relation.

Both denote the published proceedings of a conference. EKAW's 'Conference Proceedings' (a specialization of Proceedings > Multi author Volume > Document) and IASTED's 'Book proceeding' (a specialization of Publication > Item) represent the same concept: the bound collection of conference papers. The different positions in their respective document hierarchies reflect ontology design choices, not a difference in intended meaning.

A is a fee (money amount) charged to non-members for registration, while B is a registration category for students. One is a monetary fee, the other is a registration type; they denote different kinds of things despite both being under a Registration fee hierarchy.

The cmt property reviewCriteriaEnteredBy relates a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria, whereas the iasted write property relates a Person to an Item they wrote. These are different relations with different domains and ranges, and they do not overlap in meaning.

Property A (cmt:title) has domain Paper and range string, representing the title of a paper. Property B (confOf:hasFirstName) has domain Person and range string, representing a person's first name. They relate to completely different entities (documents vs. people) and denote different concepts, so they are unrelated.

Paper Full Version is a full paper document in the CMT ontology, while Registration Student is a student registration fee in the SIGKDD ontology. They belong to completely different domains (documents vs fees) and share no conceptual overlap.

confOf:Social event is a subclass of Event with children like Banquet, Reception, and Trip, denoting social activities at a conference. iasted:Fee is a subclass of Money with children like Hotel fee and Registration fee, denoting monetary charges. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Currency in iasted denotes a monetary unit (e.g., a fee currency), while Person in sigkdd denotes a human participant (Listener, Organizator, Speaker). These are completely disjoint concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. confOf:remark is a string-valued property on Contribution (likely for review remarks or notes), while iasted:has_amount_of is an integer-valued property on Money (representing a monetary amount). They share no semantic overlap.

In iasted, 'Registration fee' is a specific subclass of Fee (under Money > Fee), with children like Author/Nonauthor/Student registration fees. In sigkdd, 'Fee' is the general class with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee. Thus iasted's Registration fee is strictly narrower than sigkdd's Fee, which covers all fee types.

Active conference participant is a broad class covering any person who actively participates (e.g., gives presentations), including authors, speakers, etc. Author in sigkdd is specifically a person who submits papers and can obtain awards. An Author is a kind of active participant, but the two classes are not equivalent: Active conference participant subsumes Author, yet the sigkdd Author hierarchy (with children like Author_of_paper_student) and its properties (submit, obtain Award) indicate a narrower role. Given the structural differences and that Active_conference_participant includes non-author roles, the safest reference alignment relation is 'related' (overlap without strict equivalence).

Both are types of talks at academic conferences, but a Welcome Talk is an opening/welcome address while an Invited Talk is a presentation by an invited speaker. They overlap (a welcome talk could be given by an invited speaker) but neither subsumes the other and they are not equivalent.

Both classes denote the same concept: a paper/contribution that has been reviewed and rejected. The hierarchy paths are parallel (Reviewed contribution / Evaluated Paper, with sibling Accepted contribution / Accepted Paper), and the labels are synonymous in the conference domain.

Property A links Conference parts to Conference volumes (organizational/document structure), while property B links Persons to Items (needs/requirements). Different domains, different ranges, and different semantics; no overlap in the conference domain.

Property A denotes the date of acceptance announcement (when paper acceptances are communicated), while property B denotes the registration deadline (when attendees must register). These are distinct conference deadlines with different purposes, domains, and ranges; they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Presenter is a broad class (any conference participant who presents) and has Invited Speaker as a subclass. In sigkdd, Invited Speaker is a specific kind of speaker. Thus ekaw:Presenter subsumes sigkdd:Invited_Speaker, but they are not equivalent since Presenter also covers non-invited presenters.

The two properties relate different entities in opposite directions. In Conference, 'has members' goes from Committee to Committee member. In edas, 'isMemberOf' goes from Person to Conference. They are not inverses of each other either, since one is about committee membership and the other about conference membership.

confOf:Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception at a conference), while ekaw:Neutral_Review is a document representing a neutral-toned paper review. They belong to completely different branches of their respective ontologies (social events vs. review documents) and share no instances.

Entity A is a person (a late-paid conference applicant) under the Person hierarchy, while entity B is a monetary fee for hotel accommodation under the Money/Fee hierarchy. They denote completely different kinds of things with no overlap in intended instances.

confOf Poster is a type of conference contribution (sibling of Paper, Short paper), while iasted Mailing list is a document type (sibling of Form, Invitation letter, Review, etc.). These denote completely different things: a poster presentation vs. a mailing list document.

An Invited speaker is a conference contributor who presents a talk by invitation, while a Listener is a person who attends to listen. These are disjoint roles in a conference; an invited speaker is not a listener and vice versa.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In Conference, 'has contributions' links a Conference volume to the Conference contributions it contains (i.e., a publication/proceedings container to its papers). In edas, 'for Event' links a Call (e.g., a call for papers) to the Academic Event it is issued for. The domains (Conference volume vs. Call) and ranges (Conference contribution vs. Academic Event) do not coincide, and the relations describe different aspects of the conference domain (contents of a proceedings vs. target event of a call). They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

confOf Reception is a social event (sibling of Banquet and Trip), whereas iasted Presentation is a conference activity with specific subtypes like Power Point and Video presentation. They denote different kinds of things in the conference domain.

A 'Conference participant' in ontology A denotes a person who attends a conference (with children like Active/Passive conference participant), while 'Agency Staff Member' in ekaw denotes a staff member of an agency (e.g., a sponsoring or organizing agency). These are different concepts: one is about conference attendance, the other about agency employment. They share the parent 'Person' but have different intended instances.

Both properties express that an event is held at/by a location or organization, but they differ in generality. ekaw's heldIn has domain Event and range Location, covering any event held at any location. sigkdd's holded_by has domain Conference (a specific kind of event) and range ACM_SIGKDD (a specific organization/venue). Thus holded_by is a more specific case of heldIn, making heldIn subsume holded_by (holded_by is subsumed_by heldIn). They are not equivalent because their domains and ranges are at different levels of generality.

OC Member in ekaw is an Organizing Committee member (a conference participant with organizational duties, parented by Conference Participant). Speaker in iasted is a Delegate who presents (parented by Delegate, with children Author and Reviewer). These are distinct concepts: an OC member performs organizational/administrative roles, while a Speaker is someone who gives a presentation. Their hierarchies and sibling contexts confirm different intended meanings.

confOf 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (the act of authorship). ekaw 'paperInVolume' relates a paper to a published volume (publication containment). They connect entirely different kinds of entities and represent different relations, so they are unrelated.

Meeting Room Place in edas denotes a room where meetings/sessions are held (a conference facility), while Single hotel room in iasted denotes a private accommodation room for one person. They are disjoint kinds of places: one is for collective events, the other for individual lodging. Neither subsumes the other.

Property A (has_the_first_name) has domain Person and range string, representing a person's first name. Property B (remark) has domain Contribution and range string, representing a remark about a contribution. They have different domains (Person vs Contribution) and completely different semantics (personal name vs comment on a paper). They are unrelated.

Conference document is a broad document superclass (call for papers, contributions, reviews, etc.), while Award is a specific recognition given to authors. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

Conference Chair is a leadership role (a Person who initiates calls, reviews papers, etc.), while Speaker is a Delegate who presents at the conference. A Conference Chair is not necessarily a Speaker, and a Speaker is not necessarily a Conference Chair; the two concepts occupy different positions in the conference organisation hierarchy and have no clear overlap.

Both classes concern sponsorship-related money in a conference setting, but they are structurally different: in iasted Sponzorship is a kind of Money (alongside Fee, Tax, Tip), whereas in sigkdd Sponzor fee is a kind of Fee (alongside Registration fee). The former denotes the sponsorship arrangement/amount itself, while the latter denotes a specific fee paid by a sponsor. They overlap in domain but are not equivalent.

The ekaw property 'reviewerOfPaper' specifically relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the reviewing relationship). The iasted property 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., giving a presentation or distributing an item). These are different relations in the conference domain: one is about reviewing a paper, the other about giving/delivering an activity or item. They do not share the same domain/range types or the same intended meaning.

hasSurname is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's family name), while obtain is an object property from Person to Item (a person obtaining an item). They relate different kinds of things in different ways and share no semantic overlap.

These classes denote different kinds of documents. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a general informational document sent to conference participants (sibling to Call for paper, Conference announcement, etc.). 'Hotel registration form' in the iasted ontology is a specific fillable form for hotel booking, a subclass of Form alongside Author information form and Registration form. One is general participant information, the other is a specific hotel booking form; neither subsumes the other in a clear way.

Associated Chair is a person role in conference organization (a type of Chairman/Conference Member), while Conference hotel is a physical place/building where a conference is held. They belong to completely different domains (person roles vs. physical locations) with no overlap in intended instances.

A 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a specific introductory document for session chairs, while B 'Paper' is a research paper submitted by authors. Despite both being subclasses of Document, they denote completely different kinds of documents with no overlap in intended instances.

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members, while 'held In' links an Event to the Location where it takes place. They have different domains (Committee vs Event) and different ranges (Committee member vs Location), and there is no overlap in meaning.

NGO is a non-governmental organization (a type of organization by sector), while Organising Agency is an organization that handles conference organization. These are orthogonal classifications: an NGO could be an organising agency, but most NGOs are not, and most organising agencies are not NGOs. Their instances do not coincide.

Entity A is a class denoting a person who registered late and paid (a paid applicant), while entity B is a class denoting a specific monetary fee amount for an author attendee with CD registration. One is a person, the other is a fee/money concept; they share no domain overlap.

Accepted contribution is a document/artefact (a paper that has been accepted), while Receiving manuscript is an activity (the act of receiving a manuscript). They belong to disjoint branches of their respective ontologies (document vs activity) and denote fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Both classes denote persons who chair a workshop, but they are not equivalent. In ontology A, 'Track workshop chair' is a single class covering chairs of tracks, workshops, and tutorials (as shown by the property 'was a track workshop chair of' mapping to Conference part, which includes tracks, workshops, and tutorials). In ontology B, 'Workshop Chair' is specifically the chair of a workshop, with 'Tutorial Chair' as a separate sibling class. Thus A's class is broader (encompassing tutorial and track chairs too), while B's is narrower (workshop-only). They overlap but neither cleanly subsumes the other given differing organizational models, so 'related' is the best fit.

`Conference fees` in the Conference ontology denotes monetary charges associated with attending a conference, whereas `Workshop` in confOf is a type of working event (a scientific meeting). These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person, representing people who are members of a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Non Academic Event in edas is a subclass of Conference Event, representing events like breaks, meals, and social activities. These are completely different categories: one is a person role, the other is an event type. There is no overlap in their intended instances.

A Paid applicant is a person who has paid registration fees to attend a conference, sitting under a hierarchy of applicants and registrants. A TPC Member is a person serving on the program committee who reviews papers and initiates calls. These denote completely different roles in the conference domain with no overlap in intended instances.

Both properties associate a conference event/part with a Topic, but they are inverses of each other. In ontology A, the property goes from Topic to Conference part (domain: Topic, range: Conference part), while in ontology B it goes from Working event to Topic (domain: Working event, range: Topic). Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, the best relation is 'related'.

The cmt property hasCo-author relates a Paper to its Co-author (domain Paper, range Co-author), whereas the sigkdd property submit relates an Author to a Paper they submit (domain Author, range Paper). They connect different entities in opposite directions and represent different relations, so they are unrelated.

Video presentation in iasted is a subclass of Presentation (an Activity), denoting a type of conference presentation format. Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person, denoting a human role who delivers presentations. One is an event/activity, the other is a person; they are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Organization in edas denotes an institution (with subclasses like Academia, Government, Industry, NGO) that provides sponsorships. Person in sigkdd denotes an individual human (with subclasses like Listener, Organizator, Speaker) who has email, name, nationality, pays fees, etc. These are disjoint categories with no overlap in intended instances.

Both are datatype properties named 'has Postal Code' with range string, but their domains differ. In confOf the domain is Organization or Person, while in edas the domain is Contact Information. Since Contact Information is a more general concept that can apply to persons and organizations, the edas property is more general (subsumes the confOf one). They are not equivalent because the confOf property is restricted to Organization/Person, whereas the edas property applies to any Contact Information.

Conference Chair in cmt is a leadership role (a Chairman responsible for the conference), while Author cd proceedings included in iasted is a specific type of author whose paper is included in the CD proceedings. These are completely different concepts: one is an administrative/organizational role, the other is a contributor classification based on publication medium. They share no instances in common.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. In edas, hasLocation links a Conference Event to the Place where it occurs. In iasted, is_equipped_by links a Place to an Item that the place is equipped with. They have different domains (Conference Event vs Place), different ranges (Place vs Item), and express different relations (location of an event vs equipment of a place). They are not equivalent, nor is one a generalization of the other.

Committee member is a person who serves on a committee, while Dining Place is a physical location for dining. They belong to disjoint branches of their ontologies (Person vs Place) and share no instances.

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs a committee or conference, while Social program in iasted is a conference activity like a dinner or reception. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.
Conference contributor is a person who contributes to a conference (parent: Person), while Hotel room is a physical place (parent: Place). They denote completely different concepts with no overlap.

hasCity is a datatype property from Contact Information to a string (the name of a city), while locationOf is an object property from Location to Event (relating a place to the event held there). They have different domains, different ranges (string vs Event), and different semantics: one gives a city name as text, the other links a Location object to an Event object. They are not equivalent, nor is one more general than the other.

In edas, Workshop is a subclass of Academic Event (a kind of conference event where papers are presented). In iasted, Author book proceedings included is a subclass of Author (a person who is included in book proceedings). These are completely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a role/person. They share no instances and are not related in the conference domain.

In EDAS, Accommodation Place is a specific kind of Place (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) where people stay during a conference. In EKAW, Location is a more general concept used as the range of 'held In' (Event -> Location), meaning any place where an event is held. Location subsumes Accommodation Place since an accommodation place is a specific type of location, but they are not equivalent.

Both properties share the same local name 'writtenBy' and relate a written artefact to its author. In confOf the domain is Contribution and range is Author; in ekaw the domain is Document and range is Person. Contribution is a kind of Document and Author is a kind of Person in the conference domain, so the two properties denote the same relation (a work written by a person). The slight domain/range specialisation does not make them different relations, so a reference alignment treats them as equivalent.

These properties are completely unrelated. 'hasTitle' assigns a string title to a Contribution, while 'hasSubmissionDeadline' assigns a dateTime deadline to a Call. They have different domains, different ranges, and represent entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Workshop (in Conference) and Track (in EKAW) are distinct concepts in the conference-organisation domain. A Workshop is a type of conference part/event focused on a specific theme, often with its own programme, whereas a Track is a thematic subdivision of a conference programme. In EKAW, Workshop and Track are explicitly siblings under Scientific Event, confirming they are not the same thing. The two ontologies use different labels for different concepts, so they are unrelated rather than equivalent or in a subsumption relation.

The two properties relate entirely different entities and in different directions. cmt's hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area (domain Paper, range Subject Area), while sigkdd's submit links an Author to a Paper (domain Author, range Paper). They share no common domain or range and denote different relations in the conference domain.

The cmt 'assigned To' property assigns a Reviewer to a Paper, indicating who will review it. The Conference 'has_been_assigned_a_review_reference' property links a Submitted contribution (or Topic) to a Review preference, which is a different concept (a preference rather than the reviewer themselves). The domains and ranges differ significantly, and the relations they express are distinct.
Co-author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Personal ReviewHistory is a history of reviews given by a reviewer. They denote completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The confOf 'abstract' property attaches an abstract string to a Contribution (i.e., the abstract of a paper). The edas 'has Submission Instructions' property attaches submission instructions to a Call for papers. These are completely different relations: one describes a document artifact, the other describes procedural instructions for a call. They share only the string range.

Reception in edas is a social event (a reception/gathering), while Technic activity in iasted is a technical conference activity. They are in different branches of the event hierarchy and denote different kinds of things. Notably, iasted has a separate sibling 'Coctail reception' that would correspond to edas Reception, confirming that Technic activity is a distinct concept.

In the Conference ontology, 'Paper' is a general class of regular contributions (alongside Extended abstract). In edas, 'Active Paper' is a specific subclass of 'Paper' that is still under consideration (as opposed to Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, etc.). Thus the Conference 'Paper' is more general than the edas 'Active Paper', so the relation is subsumed_by.

Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they denote different attributes: 'has an email' captures a person's email address, while 'has Last Name' captures a person's surname. They do not relate the same information, so they are unrelated.

The two properties relate entirely different kinds of entities. 'belong to a conference volume' links Important dates to a Conference volume, while 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person. The domains (Important dates vs. Item) and ranges (Conference volume vs. Person) are disjoint, so the properties cannot be equivalent or even in a subsumption relationship.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings. 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (e.g., an item required by a person), while 'searched by' relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD (e.g., a sponsor searched by the organization). There is no overlap in the kinds of things they relate or the direction of the relation.

Both relate a person to a document in a conference setting, but they differ in scope and direction of intent. 'contributes' links any Person to a Conference document (authorship or contribution), while 'presentation' specifically links a Speaker to a Document they present. A presented document is one kind of contribution, but not every contribution is a presentation, and the domain restrictions differ (Person vs Speaker).

The two properties relate completely different kinds of entities. 'has_workshops' connects a Conference volume to its constituent Workshops (a part-whole relation), while 'obtain' connects a Person to an Item (an acquisition/possession relation). Their domains (Conference volume vs Person) and ranges (Workshop vs Item) are disjoint, and the intended meanings share no overlap.

These classes denote completely different concepts. 'Information for participants' in the Conference ontology is a type of conference document (e.g., logistical information, travel details, accommodation info) intended for conference attendees. 'Computer Networks Management Topic' in the edas ontology is a subject topic used to classify papers submitted to a conference. One is a document/artifact, the other is a subject classification. They share no instances and have no subsumption relationship.

confOf's 'Submission event' is a temporal/administrative event (subclass of Event > Administrative event) denoting the submission phase or deadline, whereas iasted's 'Final manuscript' is a concrete document artefact (subclass of Item > Document > Submission). One is an event/activity, the other is a physical document; their instances do not coincide, so they are not equivalent. They are also not in a subsumption relation (an event is not a document), so they are unrelated.

`assigned To` in cmt specifically assigns a Reviewer to review a Paper, a workflow role-assignment relation. `is signed by` in iasted indicates authorship/signing of an Item by a Person. These are different relations: one is about review assignment, the other about signing/authorship. The domains (Paper vs Item) and ranges (Reviewer vs Person) also differ in meaning, and there is no indication the relations overlap in the conference domain.

In EDAS, ConferenceVenuePlace is a specific kind of Place (a sibling of Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place) denoting the venue where a conference is held. In SIGKDD, Place is a general class with children Conference hall, Hotel, and Main office. The EDAS ConferenceVenuePlace is thus narrower than the SIGKDD Place, corresponding more closely to SIGKDD's Conference hall subclass than to Place itself.

Track workshop chair in Conference. denotes a person chairing a track (a session/programme track within a conference), while Demo Chair in ekaw denotes a person chairing demonstrations (a specific event type). These are distinct conference roles: one manages a programme track, the other manages demos. They share the general parent Person/Participant but are not the same role, and neither subsumes the other.

The two properties are completely different: 'has a date of issue' is a datatype property linking a conference document to a date, while 'topic Covered By' is an object property linking a research topic to events or papers. They share no domain, range, or semantic overlap.

The property 'is Written By' in edas relates a Paper to its Author, while 'is equipped by' in iasted relates a Place to an Item. These are completely different domain/range pairs and denote unrelated relationships in the conference organisation domain.

The property 'read Paper' in cmt relates a Reviewer to a Paper they read (for reviewing purposes), while 'write' in iasted relates a Person to an Item they write. Reading and writing are distinct, even opposite relations; they connect different domain/range types and have no overlap in meaning.

In EDAS, 'Social Event' is a specific subclass of 'Non Academic Event' (itself under 'Conference Event'), with children like Excursion and Reception. In EKAW, 'Event' is the top-level class that subsumes both 'Scientific Event' and 'Social Event'. Thus EKAW's Event is strictly more general than EDAS's Social Event, so the relation is subsumed_by.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts. In edas, 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to the Organization that provides it. In sigkdd, 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Sponsorship vs Document), ranges (Organization vs Speaker), and overall semantics (sponsorship provision vs presentation delivery) are disjoint, so these properties are unrelated.

confOf's Paper is a general contribution type (sibling of Poster, Short paper) representing any paper submitted to the conference. edas's Withdrawn Paper is a specific paper status (a paper that has been withdrawn from consideration), sitting under Paper alongside Accepted, Rejected, Pending, etc. The confOf Paper class is strictly more general, subsuming the narrower Withdrawn Paper concept.

Paid applicant is a person who has paid registration fees, while Activity before conference is an organizational activity occurring before the event. They share no instances and no hierarchical relationship.

The confOf 'remark' property attaches a textual string remark to a Contribution, whereas the edas 'hasCostAmount' property attaches an integer monetary amount to a Sponsorship. They have disjoint domains, disjoint ranges, and completely different intended meanings.

Chairman in cmt is a person who chairs a committee or conference, while Video presentation in iasted is a type of presentation activity. These are completely different domain concepts with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties have different domains and ranges despite sharing the Reviewer domain. 'assigned By Administrator' relates a Reviewer to an Administrator (who assigned the reviewer), while 'has Review History' relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History (the reviewer's review history). They denote different relationships with different target types.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman > Person), while Main office in sigkdd is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They denote completely different categories of entities: a human role vs. a location.

The two properties have different domains and ranges: 'has a date of issue' applies to Conference documents and yields a date, while 'has Start Date Time' applies to Conference Events and yields a dateTime. A document's date of issue is not the same concept as an event's start date/time, so they are unrelated.

Submissions deadline (iasted) is the deadline by which authors must submit their papers/manuscripts. Deadline Author notification (sigkdd) is the deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance/rejection, as confirmed by its sibling structure (Abstract Submission, Paper Submission are separate siblings) and the property 'notification until' (Author -> Deadline Author notification). These are temporally and functionally distinct events in the conference lifecycle: submission comes before notification. They share the parent Deadline but denote different deadline types.

These properties are completely different. 'has a degree' is a datatype property from Review preference to int, representing a degree/preference value. 'hasReview' is an object property from Paper to Review, linking a paper to its reviews. They have different domains, different ranges (datatype vs object), and different semantics.

In EDAS, Non Academic Event is a broad category covering Break, Meal, and Social events, whereas in EKAW, Social Event is a specific kind of event (with children like Conference Banquet and Conference Trip). Thus EDAS Non Academic Event is strictly more general than EKAW Social Event.
Assigned Paper is a conference paper that has been assigned for review, while Credit card is a payment instrument. These denote completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Conference Chair' is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman/Person). In iasted, 'Sponsor state' is a state (subclass of State), not a person. These denote completely different kinds of entities with no overlap in intended instances.

These properties operate in opposite directions and connect different entity types. In cmt, 'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer (indicating which reviewer is assigned to review a paper). In the Conference ontology, 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (indicating the relationship between a review document and the paper it reviews). They differ in domain/range structure, directionality, and the nature of the relationship (assignment vs. act of reviewing).

The property 'author Of' in ekaw relates a Person to a Document they authored, while 'give' in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item they present or provide. These are distinct relations in the conference domain: authoring a paper is not the same as giving a presentation or providing an item.

hasHomePage is a datatype property from Person to string (a person's home page URL), while writtenBy is an object property from Document to Person (authorship). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and have no semantic overlap.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor/exhibitor at a conference. These are completely different concepts with no overlap in instances.

The two properties relate different kinds of entities. confOf:hasCity links Organizations and Persons to a City (where they are located), while iasted:is_situated_in links Buildings, Cities, and Places to Buildings, Cities, Places, or States (a more general spatial-containment relation). The domains and ranges are disjoint (Organization/Person vs. Building/Place), and the intended semantics differ: one assigns a city to an actor, the other expresses spatial situatedness among places. They are not equivalent, and neither subsumes the other.

The cmt 'date' property captures the date of a conference (a temporal value), while sigkdd 'Name_of_conference' captures the name of a conference (a string label). These are completely different attributes of a conference entity, so they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Session is a scientific event (subclass of Event > Scientific Event) with children like Conference Session, Demo Session, Poster Session, etc. In iasted, Hotel room is a physical place (subclass of Place) with children like Single hotel room and Double hotel room.
